chapters.title: 第1章
chapters.source_text:
暴雨如注，狂风吹得雨水斜飞，树浪翻涌。
白光一闪，雷声惊骇。
黝黑山洞中，草窝里的林楸骤然惊醒。
车祸导致的剧烈疼痛贯穿五脏六腑，灵魂震荡，脑子里嗡嗡作响。电闪雷鸣之中，林楸在草窝里挣扎许久，才找回身体的支配权。
“没死。”那双冷眸里闪过一道失望。
闪电映着青年湿透的侧脸，他面颊苍白，像从地狱里爬出来的恶鬼。
手下的触感有些奇怪，没等他打量周围的环境，胃里一阵痉挛。像烈火烧灼，又被利器撕扯。
饥饿叫嚣着，林楸眼前阵阵发黑。
身体迫切渴求食物，林楸借着闪电的光看到角落里放着个罐子，里头装着水。
他根本来不及思考，抱起罐子往肚里猛灌。
直到那股饿得要晕厥过去的感受消失，林楸虚脱得滑坐在地。
外面狂风怒号，雷声惊天，洞内时不时被闪电映得亮如白昼。
林楸恹恹地靠在刚刚睡觉的草窝边，捂着肚子，像回光返照一般，再次昏睡过去。
*
雨后初晴，天空澄蓝。
水滴已经在洞口蓄积出一个小水洼。
阳光照入洞穴之中，带来一丝暖意，唤醒草窝边昏睡的林楸。
他手指动了动，长睫掀开来。底下那双眸子极漂亮，像坚冰覆盖下的湖泊，清透而平静。
林楸支撑着身体坐起，目光触及身上的兽皮裙，动作一顿。
手指捻住只到大腿一半的兽皮，干硬粗糙，有些像牛皮。
林楸眉微蹙，缓慢舒展着僵躺了一夜的四肢，将自己挪到最近的草窝之中。
他此刻处在一个山洞中。
洞口用石头封住，只余顶上留出半臂高的空隙，阳光就是从那里进来的。
洞内面积不大，十几平米，靠里侧放着他坐着的这个草窝。靠草窝边，就是昨晚他喝了水的那个罐子。
林楸盯着那粗糙得在爷奶乡下家里都少见的豁口陶罐，凝视许久。
再右边墙壁下，放着一堆干木头，除此之外什么都没有。
胃部依旧饥饿，林楸窝在草堆里，无精打采。照着办公室里那些同事爱看的小说中的设定，他多半是穿了。
林楸伸出手，看着食指上的薄茧，还有虎口处的一点小痣，身体好像是自己的，但及肩长发却是他穿来之前没有的。
林楸疲惫地合眼，手抵着肚子，收敛思绪。
挺好，换一种活法。
昏昏沉沉中，不知多久。在林楸坦然接受自己要再一次饿死的时候，洞口外传来了脚步声。
很轻。
但环境太过安静，林楸注意到了。
洞口的大石头被挪开，林楸面对洞口卧着，刚一睁眼，便被洞外那辽阔无边的原始森林震撼住了。
山洞的位置不低，目之所及林木参天，树根虬结。密林随着山峦起伏，各种植物厮杀掠夺，那蓬勃的生命力，一眼惊心。
夕阳西落，他看不见悬在天边的硕大红日，只瞧见洞口上端框住的一缕彩霞尾巴。
自然尽情泼墨，橘红泛金，满是炫技般的调色。
这原始而粗犷的景色，极少出现在人类能深入的区域。
从市区到原始森林，林楸这下确定，真穿了。
他没来得及多欣赏，就被来人挡住。
是个很高的野人，预估一米九往上，全身上下同样只腰间围着兽皮。黑色短发，高眉骨，眼窝很深，身高腿长，乍一看像T台上的男模。
不过太瘦，肋骨清晰可见。
这野人态度也不怎么好。
他连看都懒得看林楸一眼，嫌恶地将手上的东西往洞里一放，出了山洞。
林楸：“水。”
野人一顿，看了眼角落里的破烂陶罐，抓着出去。
天快黑了，好在洞口的石头被移开，洞内明亮一些。
林楸看着地上芭蕉叶一样大的叶片包裹着东西，他闻到了肉的味道。
想是给他的食物，林楸打开，里头只一把蔫巴青草，一个烤糊的肉块，也只他巴掌大。
实在是饿得在晕倒的边缘徘徊，林楸哪有心思思考，将大叶片挪近了点儿，先将那青草往嘴里塞。
青草种类多，有植物的嫩尖，有根茎，不过多是叶子。吃着泛苦，说不上什么好味道。
待到林楸草吃了一半，刚拿了肉块，打水的野人回来了。
林楸感觉到一股略显灼热的视线，他转了转身子，那目光依旧追着他的手。
再一侧，那人哼了声，放下罐子出去。
人没走，就守在洞口。
“不是不吃。”
林楸听见了。
说的不是他，应该是原来的“他”。
入乡随俗，又不知能活多久，他也尝尝这里的特产。
林楸一口咬下，嘎嘣脆。
他只眉头蹙了蹙，平静地咀嚼，苦涩的糊味在口腔蔓延，烤得过了，喇嗓子。
肉没处理好，像是血都没放干净，腥气十足。
值得高兴的是，自己的牙口好像不错。
林楸看着肉上的豁口，再默默多啃了几口。
非常难吃。
不知哪个野人的手艺，林楸看着扑簌往叶片上掉的糊肉碎屑……瞧刚刚野人馋他手里肉块的模样，这烤法，纯属浪费资源。
不知明天有没有下一顿，林楸将食物都留了一半放着。又灌了点水，这才像活了过来。
借着最后一点天光，他听着外面的野人吸溜口水，影子从洞口移开。
石头重新封好了洞口，林楸等他走了，试图挪一挪，结果纹丝不动。
他回到草窝边坐着，抓过罐子喝了一口水。
这下细细抿了下，水清冽而甘甜，像是山泉水。
目光与水中的视线相接，是他自己的脸。但像极了古代那种逃难的人，蓬头垢面，骨瘦如柴。
再晒一晒能当干尸。
*
残阳落尽，山洞彻底暗了下来。
林楸回到草窝里，闭眼睡觉。
他没有关于这里的一切记忆，脑子还是原来那个被用得只剩疲惫的脑子。
他那一对外人眼里的高知父母，自他幼儿园开始就开始鸡娃。后头两人离婚，他妈变本加厉，病态控制，把一切归咎到他身上。
他反抗，但他妈用生命威胁。
等他看着两人吵来吵去，期间不可不免都要拉他出来遛一遛，林楸渐渐麻木……结果在他二十六岁这一年，他两个又甜甜蜜蜜复婚且再次有了爱的结晶。
林楸：想死。
他也确实死了，但没死彻底。
这下成了野人，没了糟心的父母，他该学会享受一下当野人的日子。
独独属于他自己的日子。
后头几天，林楸意识到自己是在“坐牢”。
几句试探，便明白怎么一回事了。
这地方极端天气频繁，食物严重不足。野人……不对，是兽人，他亲眼见到那守门的野人变成了一头黑狼，体型极大，根本不是正常狼。
食物不足就算了，“他”却跟其他部落的兽人一起偷走部落食物，好死不死，被自己人当场抓获。
现在人家没弄死他，已经是手下留情。
林楸每日在草堆里窝着，啃着蔫巴青菜跟糊肉块儿，安安分分，实际上已经饿得两眼发昏。
再一次看到兽人进来送食物时，林楸收起淡淡的死感，从草堆里爬起来。
他做不来野人，他要改善生活。
见兽人防备地看着他，林楸道：“下一次能直接送鲜肉吗？不用烤。”
兽人看他一眼，赶紧出去将洞口堵上，生怕他跑了。
没说能，也没说不能。
林楸就当他能了。
林楸照旧先吃了一半的食物垫垫肚子，接着开始考量下一次鲜肉来了怎么吃。
他这里有木柴、陶罐，能煮能烤，但缺的是刀跟火。
林楸在草堆下摸了摸，掏出几块垫在最底下的石块儿。选了几个大小合适的，往地上摔。
叮叮咚咚的响声叫外面的兽人探头往里看，见林楸从地上捡起个薄薄的石头片，兽人恶狠狠警告：“你别想什么歪主意。”
林楸有气无力，“我想做个石刀。”
兽人不再说话，再次隐在洞外。
摔了几块石头，林楸累得双手发颤，肚子又开始叫嚣。
还是太饿了。
选了几片能用的，林楸用装肉块的叶片试了下，挺锋利的。接下来就是火。
钻木取火林楸第一次尝试。
选取一块干木头，用石刀刮掉树皮，等会儿引火星子。再在木头上深刻出一道凹痕方便固定。
又选一根长木棍，一端削尖，然后搓……
搓——
搓得林楸手心火辣辣的，最后双手控制不住地颤，差点带他飞出去。
林楸倒地，双手血红。
兽人站在外头，脑袋杵在洞口顶端的空隙外，目光盯着那叶子上的一半烤肉。
兽人咽了咽口水，“不吃肉我吃。”
林楸眼珠缓缓转动，望着洞口那脑袋问：“有火种吗？”
兽人恶声恶气地问：“要火种干什么？”
“烤肉。下一次我要生肉。”他强调。
兽人离开洞口缝隙，洞内又亮了几分。
林楸听到他远去的脚步声，眉心微动。下一次过来，应该能如他所愿。
兽人看着凶，挺好说话。
*
天色黑尽，远空透着一抹青白色。
狼莫给林楸送完了食物，慢慢跑回狼山。
他们是狼部落，黑白灰狼都有。狼王叫岩，兽形是一头威风凛凛的黑狼。
如今冬天极寒，夏天极热，兽人们一般都住在狼山中间的最大的山洞中。
狼莫回到山洞时，其他兽人都已经啃完自己分到的食物，这会儿躺在自个儿窝里一动不动。
这近百年间，猎物越来越少，捕猎也困难。
兽人们这是趁着刚刚吃了食物，肚里有东西垫着赶紧睡，免得过会儿饿了就睡不着了。
狼莫往大山洞里面走，瞧见靠近火堆旁、挨着山洞墙壁的黑狼睁开一双灰色的眼睛看来。
他脚步放缓，磨磨蹭蹭走到跟前。
“王。山洞那边，狼楸想要生肉跟火种。”
狼岩蹙眉，“他愿意吃了？”
“愿意，每次都没剩的了。”说着，狼莫咽了咽口水。
狼岩看他一眼，“明天给他，你先去吃。”
“嗷！”狼莫捂着肚子，立即离开。
狼岩想起这个自关起来就不停叫骂，最后不得已被关到离狼山远一点位置的亚兽人，眉头深深地皱紧。
chapters.translated_text:
The rain poured down like a waterfall, the gale-force winds whipping the rain into slanted sheets and sending waves of trees surging.

A flash of white light, followed by a terrifying crack of thunder.

In the pitch-black cave, Lin Qiu woke up with a start in a nest of grass.

The intense pain from the car accident pierced through his internal organs, his soul felt shaken, and his head was buzzing. Amidst the lightning and thunder, Lin Qiu struggled in the grass nest for a long time before he finally regained control of his body.

"Not dead." A flash of disappointment crossed those cold eyes.

The lightning illuminated the young man's soaked profile; his cheeks were pale, making him look like an evil ghost crawling out of hell.

The sensation under his hands was strange. Before he could examine his surroundings, his stomach spasmed. It felt like it was being seared by fire and torn by sharp blades.

Hunger clamored, and black spots danced before Lin Qiu's eyes.

His body was desperately craving food. By the light of the lightning, Lin Qiu saw a jar in the corner containing water.

He didn't have time to think; he grabbed the jar and gulped the water down.

Only when the feeling of starving to the point of fainting subsided did Lin Qiu slide to the ground, exhausted.

Outside, the wind howled and thunder roared, the cave illuminated as bright as day by the flashes of lightning.

Lin Qiu leaned listlessly against the edge of the grass nest where he had just been sleeping, clutching his stomach, and drifted back into a faint, as if experiencing a final burst of energy before death.

*

The rain cleared, and the sky turned a clear blue.

A small puddle had accumulated at the cave entrance.

Sunlight shone into the cave, bringing a hint of warmth that woke the sleeping Lin Qiu by the grass nest.

His fingers twitched, and his long lashes lifted. The eyes beneath were extremely beautiful, like a lake covered in solid ice—clear and calm.

Lin Qiu propped himself up to sit, his movements pausing when his gaze fell upon the animal skin skirt he was wearing.

His fingers pinched the animal skin that reached only to mid-thigh; it was dry, hard, and rough, somewhat like cowhide.

Lin Qiu frowned slightly, slowly stretching his limbs, which had been stiff from lying still all night, and moved himself into the nearest grass nest.

He was currently in a cave.

The entrance was sealed with stones, leaving only a gap half an arm's length high at the top, which was where the sunlight was streaming in.

The cave wasn't large, maybe ten square meters or so. The grass nest he was sitting in was placed against the inner wall. Beside the nest was the jar he had drunk water from last night.

Lin Qiu stared at the chipped pottery jar—so crude it would be rare even in his grandparents' rural home—and gazed at it for a long time.

Against the wall to the right was a pile of dry wood; other than that, there was nothing.

His stomach was still hungry. Lin Qiu huddled in the grass, listless. Based on the tropes in the novels his office colleagues loved to read, he had most likely transmigrated.

Lin Qiu stretched out his hand, looking at the thin calluses on his index finger and the small mole on the web of his thumb. The body seemed to be his own, but the shoulder-length hair was something he hadn't had before he transmigrated.

Lin Qiu closed his eyes wearily, his hand pressed against his stomach, gathering his thoughts.

That's fine, a different way to live.

In his drowsy state, he didn't know how much time had passed. Just as Lin Qiu was calmly accepting that he was about to starve to death again, footsteps sounded outside the cave.

Very light.

But the environment was so quiet that Lin Qiu noticed.

The large stone at the entrance was moved aside. Lin Qiu was lying facing the entrance, and the moment he opened his eyes, he was stunned by the vast, boundless primeval forest outside.

The cave was situated quite high up. As far as the eye could see, there were towering trees and tangled roots. The dense forest rose and fell with the mountains, various plants fighting and preying on each other. The exuberant vitality was breathtaking at a single glance.

The sun was setting. He couldn't see the massive red sun hanging in the sky, only the tail end of the colorful clouds framed by the top of the cave entrance.

Nature was painting with abandon, orange-reds blending with gold in a display of masterful color-mixing.

This primitive and rugged scenery rarely appeared in areas accessible to humans.

From the city to the primeval forest—Lin Qiu was now certain he had truly transmigrated.

He didn't have time to admire it further before he was blocked by the person who had arrived.

It was a very tall savage, estimated to be over 1.9 meters, wearing only animal skin around his waist. He had short black hair, a high brow ridge, deep-set eyes, and long legs; at first glance, he looked like a male model on a runway.

However, he was too thin, his ribs clearly visible.

This savage didn't have a very good attitude, either.

He didn't even bother to look at Lin Qiu, disgustedly placing the things in his hand into the cave before leaving.

Lin Qiu: "Water."

The savage paused, glanced at the broken pottery jar in the corner, grabbed it, and went out.

It was getting dark, but fortunately, the stone at the entrance had been moved, making the cave a bit brighter.

Lin Qiu looked at the items wrapped in leaves as large as banana leaves; he smelled the scent of meat.

Assuming it was food for him, Lin Qiu opened it. Inside were only a handful of wilted green grass and a piece of burnt meat, only the size of his palm.

He was truly hovering on the edge of fainting from hunger, so Lin Qiu had no heart to think. He pulled the large leaves closer and stuffed the green grass into his mouth first.

There were many types of grass, including tender plant tips and roots, but mostly leaves. It tasted bitter and couldn't be called good.

By the time Lin Qiu had eaten half the grass and just picked up the piece of meat, the savage who had gone to fetch water returned.

Lin Qiu felt a slightly burning gaze; he turned his body, and that gaze continued to follow his hand.

To one side, the man snorted, put down the jar, and went out.

He didn't leave; he stood guard at the entrance.

"Not that he doesn't eat."

Lin Qiu heard it.

It wasn't about him; it must have been about the original "him."

When in Rome, do as the Romans do. Since he didn't know how long he could live, he might as well try the local specialties.

Lin Qiu took a bite—crunchy.

He only frowned slightly, chewing calmly. The bitter, burnt taste spread in his mouth; it was overcooked and scratched his throat.

The meat wasn't prepared well, as if the blood hadn't been drained properly, and it was extremely gamey.

What was worth being happy about was that his teeth seemed to be in good shape.

Lin Qiu looked at the bite mark on the meat and silently took a few more bites.

It was terrible.

He didn't know whose handiwork it was. Lin Qiu watched the burnt meat crumbs falling onto the leaves... Looking at how the savage had been craving the meat in his hand earlier, this way of roasting was a pure waste of resources.

Not knowing if there would be a next meal tomorrow, Lin Qiu saved half of the food. He drank some more water, and only then did he feel like he had come back to life.

By the last bit of daylight, he listened to the savage outside slurping his saliva, and the shadow moved away from the entrance.

The stone was used to seal the entrance again. Lin Qiu waited for him to leave and tried to move it, but it didn't budge.

He returned to the grass nest and sat down, grabbing the jar to take a sip of water.

This time, he took a careful sip; the water was clear and sweet, like mountain spring water.

His gaze met the reflection in the water—it was his own face. But it looked just like those refugees in ancient times, disheveled and skin and bones.

If he were to be sun-dried, he could pass for a mummy.

*

The setting sun faded, and the cave went completely dark.

Lin Qiu returned to the grass nest and closed his eyes to sleep.

He had no memories of this place; his brain was still the same one that had been used until only exhaustion remained.

His parents, who were considered highly educated by outsiders, had started "chicken-parenting" him since kindergarten. Later, when the two divorced, his mother became even worse, exercising pathological control and blaming everything on him.

He resisted, but his mother threatened him with her life.

After watching the two of them argue back and forth, inevitably dragging him out to be paraded around during the process, Lin Qiu gradually became numb... In the end, in his twenty-sixth year, the two of them happily remarried and had another "fruit of love."

Lin Qiu: I want to die.

And he had indeed died, but not completely.

Now that he had become a savage, without those troublesome parents, he should learn to enjoy the days of being a savage.

Days that belonged solely to him.

Over the next few days, Lin Qiu realized he was "in prison."

After a few probes, he understood what was going on.

This place had frequent extreme weather and a severe shortage of food. The savage... no, the beastman—he had seen with his own eyes that the savage guarding the door turned into a black wolf, huge in size, not a normal wolf at all.

It wasn't enough that food was scarce, but "he" had stolen tribal food with beastmen from other tribes and, unfortunately, was caught red-handed by his own people.

The fact that they hadn't killed him yet was already an act of mercy.

Lin Qiu huddled in the grass every day, gnawing on wilted greens and burnt meat, behaving himself, though in reality, he was already dizzy from hunger.

When he saw the beastman come in to deliver food again, Lin Qiu put away his faint sense of death and climbed up from the grass pile.

He couldn't be a savage; he had to improve his life.

Seeing the beastman looking at him defensively, Lin Qiu said, "Can you bring fresh meat next time? No need to roast it."

The beastman glanced at him and quickly went out to block the entrance, afraid he would run away.

He didn't say he could, nor did he say he couldn't.

Lin Qiu took it as a yes.

Lin Qiu ate half the food as usual to pad his stomach, then began to consider how to eat the fresh meat when it arrived.

He had firewood and a pottery jar; he could boil or roast, but he lacked a knife and fire.

Lin Qiu felt around under the grass pile and pulled out a few stones that were at the very bottom. He chose a few of suitable size and smashed them against the ground.

The clanging sound made the beastman outside peek in. Seeing Lin Qiu pick up a thin stone flake from the ground, the beastman warned him fiercely, "Don't get any crooked ideas."

Lin Qiu said weakly, "I want to make a stone knife."

The beastman didn't speak again and hid outside the cave once more.

After smashing a few stones, Lin Qiu was so tired his hands were trembling, and his stomach began to clamor again.

Still too hungry.

Choosing a few usable pieces, Lin Qiu tested them on the leaf that had held the meat; they were quite sharp. Next was fire.

This was Lin Qiu's first attempt at drilling wood for fire.

He selected a piece of dry wood, used the stone knife to scrape off the bark to catch sparks later, and carved a deep groove into the wood to make it easier to fix.

He then chose a long wooden stick, sharpened one end, and started rubbing...

Rubbing—

It rubbed Lin Qiu's palms until they were burning, and in the end, his hands couldn't stop trembling, almost sending him flying.

Lin Qiu fell to the ground, his hands blood-red.

The beastman stood outside, his head poked past the gap at the top of the cave entrance, his gaze fixed on the half-eaten roasted meat on the leaf.

The beastman swallowed his saliva, "If you're not eating the meat, I will."

Lin Qiu's eyes slowly turned to look at the head at the entrance and asked, "Do you have fire?"

The beastman asked fiercely, "What do you want fire for?"

"To roast meat. Next time, I want raw meat," he emphasized.

The beastman left the gap, and the cave became a bit brighter.

Lin Qiu heard his retreating footsteps, his brows twitching slightly. Next time he came, he should be able to get his wish.

The beastman looked fierce, but he was quite easy to talk to.

*

The sky turned completely dark, with a hint of blue-white in the distance.

Lang Mo finished delivering food to Lin Qiu and slowly ran back to Wolf Mountain.

They were the Wolf Tribe, with black, white, and gray wolves. The Wolf King was named Yan, and his beast form was a majestic black wolf.

Nowadays, winters were extremely cold and summers were extremely hot, so the beastmen generally lived in the largest cave in the middle of Wolf Mountain.

When Lang Mo returned to the cave, the other beastmen had already finished their share of food and were lying motionless in their own nests.

In the last hundred years, prey had become increasingly scarce, and hunting had become difficult.

The beastmen were taking advantage of the food they had just eaten to fall asleep quickly, so they wouldn't be unable to sleep once they got hungry later.

Lang Mo walked into the depths of the large cave and saw the black wolf lying against the cave wall near the fire pit open a pair of gray eyes to look at him.

He slowed his pace and shuffled over to him.

"King. At the cave, Lang Qiu wants raw meat and fire."

Lang Yan frowned, "He's willing to eat?"

"Willing, he hasn't left any for a while now." As he spoke, Lang Mo swallowed his saliva.

Lang Yan glanced at him, "Give it to him tomorrow. You go eat first."

"Awoo!" Lang Mo clutched his stomach and left immediately.

Lang Yan thought of this sub-beastman who had been cursing non-stop since he was locked up and was eventually forced to be moved to a location further away from Wolf Mountain, his brows furrowing deeply.

chapters.title: 第10章
chapters.source_text:
或许山坡太陡，又夜能视物，林楸放任自己从走变成了跑。
风声呼呼从身旁掠过，林楸一下奔过狼岩去。
火堆重新燃起。
另一张他没收走的兽皮被小心折叠好，放在圆木上。
这木头是狼石跟狼莫给他搬来的，他们还用狼爪子帮着去了皮。
石锅里放着他那一份肉，用大叶子盖着。
林楸将两张兽皮叠放在腿上，轻轻抚过。
他跟他们就是陌生人，他不应该在意。但才相处多久，他就已经做不到无视。
面前伸过来一只手，很大，手指极长，指腹都是厚实的茧子。
上面放着一把小刀。
精致小巧，是用黑曜石做的，泛着光泽的黑色，玻璃质感。
林楸双手搭在兽皮上，仰头看着兽人，脖颈修长又脆弱。
狼岩扫过一眼，道：“拿着。”
林楸：“送给我？”
“嗯。”
林楸：“我没有东西交换。”
狼岩：“不用。”
林楸攥着小刀刀柄，上面还用兽皮缠着。他划了下圆木，留下一道深痕。
林楸看着往山洞去的背影，想不明白。
他没有遮掩，狼岩只要不傻都应该看出来了，他到底是怎么打算的？一直把他拘在狼山吗？
林楸晚饭吃得晚了些，回到山洞，兽人们几乎都睡熟了。
他捧着兽皮跟刚刚用刀子切割下来的兽皮条，回到草窝里，开始给自己做衣服。
他拿着兽皮在身上比划。
以前没做过这事儿，有些生疏。
狼岩趴在窝里，闭着眼，竖着耳朵听着旁边的动静。
林楸好不容易确定了怎么裁剪，小心割破兽皮，费了一点功夫，随后开始用刀尖打孔。
瞥见旁边毛绒绒的狼耳动了动，林楸知道他没睡着。
他一边缝兽皮，低声道：“我能跟你们一起去捕猎吗？”
狼岩睁眼，映着火光的眸子藏着星河。
“不能。”
还是一样的答案，林楸移开眼。
狼岩：“你要听从祭司安排。”
林楸手上一错，骨针扎在指腹。他疼得眼睫一扇，悄然在兽皮上搓了搓。
狼岩扫过他指腹，道：“睡觉的时候刀不要放窝里……安分一点。”
他转过头，背对林楸。
林楸忙了会儿，注意到狼岩始终竖着耳朵。想是自己弄出声音他睡不着，林楸默默将东西一裹，放在草窝外。
他掀开兽皮往草窝里一躺，有一丝丝的恼。
他闭着眼想，他还要怎么安分。
夜里又是雨，林楸还不习惯这里的天气，翻个身的功夫，兽皮被他裹在身前，整个后背露了出来。
睡着冷，当幼崽再一次爬窝里，林楸直接将他搂紧。
狼岩：“……”
算了。
他目光擦过林楸后背，瞧着他裹着兽皮不算好睡姿，还知道冷了往他这边缩。
狼岩拎着兽皮一角，将他连带幼崽一起盖住。
不一会儿，狼果寻过来。
看幼崽缩在林楸脖子上，瞪圆了眼，见狼岩什么都不说，又气咻咻地回去。
雪总不听话，他不想管了。
*
连续几天的好运后，这一天，狩猎队空手而归。
得益于植物繁多，生长旺盛，采集队依旧带回来不少野菜。
林楸还好，肉干混着野菜能沾个肉味儿，其他兽人就只能干嚼野菜。
他穿着自己做的兽皮马甲，腿上兽皮裙换成了兽皮短裤。
匀出来的兽皮也不浪费，做了两个长长的袖笼，在室外呆着的时候就戴上，热的时候取掉。
兽人们趴在地上，往跟前的野菜堆里一栽。狼口大张，犬牙尖锐，嗷呜一下满满一大口的野菜。
林楸看着，唇角掀了掀。
兽人苦兮兮，眼睛直往林楸的锅里瞧，又见他身上的兽皮稀奇，一时间看不过来。
并非每日都有肉吃。
后头几日，林楸起来时，狩猎队并没出发。
他上午去祭司那边帮忙，问过才知道领地里没兽群了。虽然祭司告诉他兽人们不会坐以待毙，狼岩已经派了几个兽人出去寻找，但林楸觉得希望渺茫。
林楸：“既然没有兽群，为什么不迁徙？”
老祭司笑，像看幼崽一样看林楸，眼里尽是沧桑。
他声音里是耗尽气力的疲惫，仿佛只含着一口气，再波折不得。
“我们部落已经迁徙了三次，从中央大陆一直到东边大陆，哪里都一样。”
“我们已经没有再迁徙的能力了。”
只能等死。
一瞬间冒出来的想法，祭司无尽恐慌，狠狠将其压下去。
他们狼部落的兽人生来斗争，不可能由着生命逝去。
林楸看着祭司，“你们还有别的办法吗？”
老祭司一恼，抓着手杖敲了他腿一下，“什么你们，我告诉你，你狼楸也是狼部落的！”
“就算以前不懂事，错了改正。还真想着跟那绿眼兽人跑了？妄想！”
部落存亡时刻，谁都别想逃过。
林楸：“疼。”
老祭司：“哼！”
疼才好，不疼不长记性。
亚兽人被送过来的时候已经挨了一顿收拾，看他阿父跟看仇人一样。先前还喜欢嚷嚷，现在这个样子才像真的长大了。
可惜性子太独，不把部落当部落。
这个时候，只能团结，他们才可能熬过去。
老祭司也没什么力气，那兽皮敞开时，两条腿瘦如骷髅，只有骨头连着皮。
部落弥漫在没有食物的灰暗中。
林楸出了山洞，瞧着狼果正在给幼崽煮野菜。
部落只两口陶锅，大的在祭司那里，小的归狼果管，专门用来给幼崽煮糊糊。
见林楸看着，狼果哼了声，背对他去。
大的小的都是这个德行。
林楸将他留下来的那些肉干取出来，交给狼果。
他看着年纪还小，什么情绪都浮现在那双冰蓝色的眼睛里。
这会儿看着林楸手上的肉，分明馋，脑袋一偏咕哝：“别以为这样就能讨好我。”
林楸：“不是讨好你的。”
狼果脖子跟脸立马红透。
林楸：“给幼崽的。”
他放下肉干，不叫这个快把兽皮裙抠烂的兽人为难。
肉干不多，混着青菜煮熟总归有点肉香。狼果等肉汤冷却，赶紧抱着进了山洞。
幼崽稍微还有点吃的垫垫，其他狼兽人就没有那么好运了。
狼莫趴在地上，从爪子下翻出一株草来。
林楸看着他往嘴巴里放，那草他在祭司那里看过，吃完立马晕。
“不能吃。”他疾步过去阻止。
狼莫没什么力气抬头，虚着眼睛看了眼林楸，“没事的，是圈圈草。”
吃完能看见好多圈圈，然后就睡着了。
他一口咬住，嚼吧嚼吧吞进去。
脑袋一歪，含糊道：“好饿……”
林楸抓住他狼毛，用了些力气，“吐出来。”
“咳……呕！”
旁边狼西不动，早已经先一步吃了。
狼石看在眼里，下巴搭在草地上，四条腿窝着压住肚皮。他道：“没事，睡一会儿就好了。我们饿狠了经常吃。”
“不怕醒不过来！”林楸急了，声音略大，脸上一阵薄红。
狼石被凶得舔了舔鼻尖，略显心虚道：“不会。”
奇怪，怎么楸冷脸跟王一样可怕。
林楸甩开狼莫的脖子，见其他兽人看来，才觉自己失了态。
狼果捧着罐子里剩下一点出来，见林楸着急那一下，又看族人们吃了圈圈草躺下地上，心里闷闷的。
“给，你吃。”狼果将罐子给林楸。
林楸：“不用。”
他脸还绷着，在亲眼见到兽人为了忍受饥饿吃毒药，震惊不已，随即而来的是满心的惶恐。
他深刻地认识到，这个地方缺少食物已经到了什么地步。
狼果以为他害怕。
他也怕过，缺乏食物的恐惧从出生就伴随着他们。
他们从上一任祭司开始就在不停努力，这一任祭司也从没放弃过。但他们兽人的数量还是从百年前的上千人，到如今分作两个部落，加起来也不过两百多个兽人。
这其中，老兽人几乎没有。
幼崽……多的时候十几个，少的时候四五个。
起码有一半，养到后头养不活。
狼果自懂事之后就跟在他阿爸身边帮忙看管幼崽，阿爸离开，换他接任。
兽人饥饿，没有奶水。
他也亲眼见到好多幼崽生下来没多久就去世。
肉糊糊虽然尽可能的多给幼崽，但还是要保证狩猎的兽人能够活动。他就是见得太多，所以对于楸曾经做过的事深恶痛绝。
起初他恨不得楸去死，可现在，他心里不知是个什么滋味。
狼果看着林楸，“只要你不再做那事，你想去哪里，王他们不会拦着。”
大家都在努力活着，狼楸也必须与部落共同进退。
林楸看着狼果。
这事他真的不知道怎么解释。
狼果撇过头，“你放心，时间到了，肉虽然不够，但大家会一起种植尾巴草，也比野菜能填饱一点肚子。”
尾巴草？
林楸头一次从狼果这里听说。
他没开口问，也没在祭司那里看到过，想必是极重要的东西。
既然要种，早晚能看见。
今天狼山外面处处趴着巨大的狼，白狼少些，灰狼跟黑狼数量差不多。
林楸不想待在阳光下，便去祭司山洞。
不过这次山洞里不只有老兽人，还多了个忙忙碌碌的白狼兽人。
是个漂亮少年，也是老祭司口中的下一任祭司。
chapters.translated_text:
Perhaps because the slope was too steep and he could see in the dark, Lin Qiu let himself transition from walking to running.

The wind whistled past his ears, and Lin Qiu quickly ran past Wolf Rock.

The campfire had been rekindled.

Another animal skin that he hadn't taken away was carefully folded and placed on the log.

These logs had been brought over for him by Lang Shi and Lang Mo, and they had even used their wolf claws to help strip the bark.

His share of the meat was in the stone pot, covered with large leaves.

Lin Qiu placed the two animal skins on his lap, gently stroking them.

He was a stranger to them; he shouldn't care. But after spending just this short time together, he could no longer remain indifferent.

A hand reached out in front of him—very large, with extremely long fingers and thick calluses on the pads.

Resting on it was a small knife.

Exquisite and compact, made of obsidian, with a glossy black, glass-like texture.

Lin Qiu rested his hands on the animal skin, looking up at the beastman, his neck slender and fragile.

Lang Yan glanced at him briefly and said, "Take it."

Lin Qiu: "For me?"

"Mn."

Lin Qiu: "I have nothing to exchange for it."

Lang Yan: "No need."

Lin Qiu gripped the handle of the small knife, which was wrapped in animal skin. He scratched the log with it, leaving a deep mark.

Lin Qiu looked at the retreating figure heading toward the cave, unable to make sense of it.

He hadn't hidden it; anyone with half a brain like Lang Yan should have figured it out by now—what on earth was his plan? Did he intend to keep him confined to Wolf Mountain forever?

Lin Qiu had dinner a bit late. When he returned to the cave, almost all the beastmen were fast asleep.

Clutching the animal skin and the strips of hide he had just cut with the knife, he returned to his grass nest and began making clothes for himself.

He held the animal skin up to measure it against his body.

Having never done this before, he felt somewhat clumsy.

Lang Yan lay in his nest, eyes closed, ears pricked to listen to the movement next to him.

After finally figuring out how to cut the pattern, Lin Qiu carefully sliced the animal skin, putting in quite a bit of effort, and then began punching holes with the tip of the knife.

Catching a glimpse of the furry wolf ears twitching nearby, Lin Qiu knew he wasn't asleep.

As he sewed the animal skin, he asked in a low voice, "Can I go hunting with you guys?"

Lang Yan opened his eyes. His fire-lit pupils seemed to hold a starry river.

"No."

It was the same answer as before. Lin Qiu looked away.

Lang Yan: "You must follow the priest's arrangements."

Lin Qiu's hand slipped, and the bone needle pricked his fingertip. He winced, his eyelashes fluttering as he quietly rubbed his finger against the animal skin.

Lang Yan glanced at his fingertip and said, "Don't keep the knife in the nest when you sleep... Behave yourself."

He turned his head, with his back to Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu worked for a while, noticing that Lang Yan's ears remained pericked the whole time. Figuring that he was making noise and keeping him awake, Lin Qiu silently bundled his things up and placed them outside the grass nest.

He pulled back the animal skin and lay down in the nest, feeling a tiny trace of irritation.

He closed his eyes and thought, how much more well-behaved was he supposed to be?

It rained again during the night. Lin Qiu still wasn't used to the weather here. In the middle of turning over, the animal skin ended up wrapped around his front, leaving his entire back exposed.

It was cold to sleep that way, so when the cub climbed back into the nest, Lin Qiu pulled it tightly into his arms.

Lang Yan: "..."

Forget it.

His gaze swept across Lin Qiu's back, taking in his awkward sleeping posture wrapped in the animal skin, yet knowing enough to curl up toward him when he was cold.

Lang Yan picked up a corner of the animal skin and draped it over both Lin Qiu and the cub.

Before long, Lang Guo came searching.

Seeing the cub curled up against Lin Qiu's neck, his eyes went wide with anger. Seeing that Lang Yan wasn't saying anything, he huffed and went back.

Snow was always disobedient; he didn't care anymore.

*

After several days of good luck, today the hunting party returned empty-handed.

Thanks to the abundant and thriving plant life, the gathering party still brought back plenty of wild vegetables.

Lin Qiu was doing all right; dried meat mixed with wild vegetables allowed him to get a taste of meat, while the other beastmen had to chew dry wild vegetables alone.

He was wearing a vest made of animal skin that he had made himself, and the animal skin skirt on his legs had been replaced with animal skin shorts.

The leftover animal skin wasn't wasted either; he had made two long sleeves that he wore when staying outdoors and took off when it got hot.

The beastmen lay on the ground, burying their faces right into the pile of wild vegetables before them. With their wolf mouths wide open and sharp canine teeth, *ao-wu*, they took massive bites of wild vegetables.

Watching this, the corners of Lin Qiu's lips twitched.

The beastmen looked miserable, their eyes constantly peeking into Lin Qiu's pot, while also finding the animal skins he wore too novel to stop staring.

They didn't have meat to eat every day.

Over the next few days, when Lin Qiu woke up, the hunting party didn't set out at all.

He went to help out at the priest's place in the morning, and only after asking did he learn that there were no herds left in the territory. Although the priest told him the beastmen wouldn't sit and wait for death, and Lang Yan had already sent a few beastmen out to search, Lin Qiu felt the hope was slim.

Lin Qiu: "Since there are no herds, why don't you migrate?"

The old priest smiled, looking at Lin Qiu like he was a cub, his eyes full of the vicissitudes of life.

His voice was exhausted from having spent all his strength, as if he were holding onto just one last breath, unable to withstand any more twists and turns.

"Our tribe has already migrated three times, all the way from the Central Continent to the Eastern Continent, and everywhere is the same."

"We no longer have the ability to migrate again."

We can only wait to die.

A thought that suddenly popped up filled the priest with endless panic, and he fiercely suppressed it.

The beastmen of their Wolf tribe were born to fight; it was impossible to just let life slip away.

Lin Qiu looked at the priest. "Do you have any other way?"

The old priest grew annoyed, grabbing his walking stick and rapping Lin Qiu on the leg. "What do you mean 'you'? Let me tell you, you, Lang Qiu, are also of the Wolf tribe!"

"Even if you didn't know better before, mistakes are meant to be corrected. Were you really thinking of running off with that green-eyed beastman? Delusional!"

At a time of tribal life and death, no one was allowed to escape.

Lin Qiu: "It hurts."

The old priest: "Hmph!"

It was good that it hurt; without pain, one wouldn't learn their lesson.

When the demi-human had been sent over, he had already received a beating, looking at his father as if he were an enemy. Before, he liked to make a fuss, but now this demeanor made him seem truly grown up.

It was a pity his temperament was too solitary; he didn't treat the tribe like a tribe.

At a time like this, only through unity could they possibly pull through.

The old priest didn't have much strength either. When his animal skin robe parted, his two legs were as thin as a skeleton's, with only skin clinging to bone.

The tribe was shrouded in the gloom of lacking food.

Lin Qiu walked out of the cave and saw Lang Guo boiling wild vegetables for the cub.

The tribe only had two pottery pots; the large one was with the priest, and the small one belonged to Lang Guo, used exclusively for boiling mush for the cubs.

Seeing Lin Qiu watching, Lang Guo let out a huff and turned his back to him.

Big and small, they all had this exact attitude.

Lin Qiu took out the dried meat he had saved and handed it to Lang Guo.

Lang Guo still looked young, all his emotions floating right there in his icy-blue eyes.

At this moment, looking at the meat in Lin Qiu's hand, he was clearly tempted, yet he tilted his head and muttered, "Don't think this means you can win me over."

Lin Qiu: "I'm not trying to win you over."

Lang Guo's neck and face instantly turned beet red.

Lin Qiu: "It's for the cub."

He put down the dried meat, unwilling to make things difficult for this beastman who was practically shredding his own animal-skin skirt out of awkwardness.

There wasn't much dried meat, but boiling it with greens always brought out a bit of meaty aroma. Waiting for the meat soup to cool down, Lang Guo hurriedly picked it up and rushed into the cave.

The cubs at least had a little something to pad their stomachs, but the other wolf beastmen weren't so lucky.

Lang Mo lay on the ground, digging a plant out from beneath his paws.

Lin Qiu watched him put it into his mouth. He had seen that grass at the priest's place; whoever ate it would immediately pass out.

"You can't eat that," he hurried over to stop him.

Lang Mo didn't have much strength to lift his head. He squinted tiredly at Lin Qiu and said, "It's fine, it's loop grass."

After eating it, you see lots of loops, and then you fall asleep.

He bit down on it, chewed it up, and swallowed it.

Tilting his head, he mumbled vaguely, "So hungry..."

Lin Qiu grabbed his wolf fur and used some force. "Spit it out."

"Cough... ugh!"

Nearby, Lang Xi didn't move; he had already eaten it a step ahead.

Lang Shi watched from the side, resting his chin on the grass, his four legs tucked under his belly. He said, "It's fine, just sleep for a while and it'll pass. When we get too hungry, we eat this often."

"Aren't you afraid you won't wake up?!" Lin Qiu panicked, his voice slightly raised, a faint flush appearing on his face.

Being yelled at, Lang Shi licked the tip of his nose and said with a somewhat guilty conscience, "We won't."

Strange, how could Qiu's cold face be as terrifying as the King's?

Lin Qiu let go of Lang Mo's neck, and seeing other beastmen looking over, he realized he had lost his composure.

Lang Guo came out holding what little was left in the pot. Seeing Lin Qiu's anxiousness just now, and then seeing the clansmen lying on the ground after eating the loop grass, he felt a heavy weight in his chest.

"Here, you eat it." Lang Guo handed the pot to Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu: "No need."

His face remained taut. Witnessing firsthand beastmen eating poison just to endure hunger had shocked him deeply, immediately followed by a heart full of panic.

He deeply realized just how severe the lack of food was in this place.

Lang Guo thought he was scared.

He had been scared too; the fear of food shortages had accompanied them since birth.

They had been trying continuously since the previous priest, and the current priest had never given up either. Yet their numbers as beastmen had still dropped from over a thousand a century ago to now being split into two tribes, adding up to barely over two hundred beastmen.

Among them, there were almost no old beastmen.

As for cubs... sometimes a dozen, sometimes just four or five.

At least half of them couldn't be raised to adulthood.

Ever since he understood things, Lang Guo had been by his dad's side helping take care of the cubs. When his dad left, he took over the role.

The beastmen were starving and had no milk.

He had also witnessed with his own eyes many cubs passing away not long after birth.

Although the meat mush was given to the cubs as much as possible, they still had to ensure the hunting beastmen could function. Because he had seen too much, he had harbored a deep hatred for what Qiu used to do.

At first, he wished Qiu would just die, but now, he didn't know what kind of feeling was in his heart.

Lang Guo looked at Lin Qiu. "As long as you don't do that stuff anymore, the King and the others won't stop you wherever you want to go."

Everyone was striving to live, and Lang Qiu must also face hardships together with the tribe.

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Guo.

He really didn't know how to explain that matter.

Lang Guo looked away. "Rest assured, when the time comes, even though the meat won't be enough, everyone will plant tail grass together. It's still more filling than wild vegetables."

Tail grass?

It was the first time Lin Qiu had heard of this from Lang Guo.

He didn't ask about it out loud, nor had he ever seen it at the priest's place; it must be something extremely important.

Since they were going to plant it, he would see it sooner or later.

Today, huge wolves were lying everywhere outside Wolf Mountain—fewer white wolves, while the numbers of gray and black wolves were roughly equal.

Lin Qiu didn't want to stay out in the sunlight, so he went to the priest's cave.

This time, however, the cave didn't just hold the old beastman; there was also a busy white wolf beastman.

He was a pretty youth, and also the next priest mentioned by the old priest.

chapters.source_text:
这会儿，狼山这边从连廊到草地，躺满了兽人。
大家花了一天的时间将尾巴草收回来，狼兽人们悬着半年的心终于落了下来。
大伙儿虽累，心是轻盈的，这不一躺就睡着了。
成年兽人干活只管莽，但脱粒的小狼有限，一时半会儿没弄完。
祭司便叫小狼把狼山所有空着的山洞清扫出来，剩下的尾巴草全放山洞里摊开着，等明天再慢慢弄。
这会儿大家精疲力尽，包括黑羽兽人在内，大部分已经闭眼打起了呼噜。
晚饭是狼贝带着采集队几个兽人做的。骨头汤的味道一出来，睡梦中的兽人拧着眉头，鼻子嗅闻着，脑袋像指南针一样冲着灶台这边偏转，挣扎着似要醒来。
林楸跟狼岩回来得正好，灶台前空荡荡。
以前争抢着吃饭的兽人都累瘫了，倒是头一次让他们占了先。
他两个盛了肉汤，后头狼果则带着一溜幼崽来。
幼崽喂养得好，长得就快。看着胖墩墩的，胳膊腿儿蹦着极有力。
兽人们收尾巴草忙了一天，幼崽就你追我赶疯跑了一天。这会儿各个面颊透红，浑身冒着汗，闻起来一股小狗崽子的香臭味道。
林楸看过去，幼崽就冲着他笑。
眼看要凑上来，叫狼果一手逮一个，立在原地。
“吃肉了！”狼贝等着他们打完肉汤，吆喝一声。
兽人惊坐起，又龇牙咧嘴地捂住后腰瘫倒下去。
“嗷！！！”狼莫哀嚎，“怎么会这么累！腰、断了嗷！”
狼西脚下发颤，撑着他肩膀勉强站起来，又疼得狼莫捂腰痛呼。
狼西颤颤巍巍，“明年不干了，宁愿打猎。”
兽人正儿八经干农活的时候很少，垦地用兽形，两爪子扒拉就成，跟玩儿似的。
播种就随意一撒，更是轻松。
费劲儿一点的就是运鸟粪。
后头的除草可以蹲着，割尾巴草蹲又蹲不住，站起来又够不着，兽形不好操作，只能人形弯着腰忙活。
他们长得又高，这么弯折一天，能活蹦乱跳才奇怪了。
兽人头一次体会到农忙的累，此时又困又饿。肚子打了几次鼓了，愣是爬不起来。
狼贝又叫了几声，才陆续有兽人撑着后腰，苦哈哈地往灶台这边挪。脚步沉重，一下下走得闷响，跟灌了铅似的。
狼兽人动了，黑羽兽人却坐在一起，显得有些拘谨和茫然。
狼雨路过，招呼：“走啊，吃了赶紧睡觉。”
黑羽兽人打起精神，跟在狼雨后头。
“今晚肯定睡得好。”
黑羽兽人连连点头。
狼雨：“睡好了，明天继续。”
黑羽兽人一下蔫了。
羽涯跟在羽山后头，边上羽乐也回到队伍里，垂头丧气的，叫羽涯看了，忍不住哑着嗓子道：“他们欺负你了？”
来时还活泼的羽涯，此刻就跟水洼里晒了一天的鱼，也蹦跶不起来了。
羽乐看他一眼，确认是在跟自己说话，本来就小的声音更是低得听不清，“没有。”
羽涯耷拉着脑袋，头重脚轻往前栽，也没继续问。
羽乐以前跟他们也玩儿不到一块儿，没话说。
不过这狼部落简直不是兽人待的地方，他下次说什么都不来了！
黑羽兽人吊在队伍尾巴，前面动，他们就跟着挪。一个个肩膀微塌，目光呆滞，行尸走肉一样只知道动作，说不出话来。
没一会儿，前头有兽人过来。
“伸手。”
黑羽兽人想也不想，老实伸手。
手中一沉，硕大一个饭盆差点摔下去，吓得兽人慌忙抱住，也不呆了。
一个陶器要他们干活一个月才换得来，像今天这样的活儿，可不想再干了……
狼雨：“饭盆抱稳了，没了今晚只能用手抓着吃。”
黑羽兽人照旧由羽山打头，离灶台越近，那股肉汤的味道越香浓。
不是黑羽兽人在大泽那边吃惯了的鱼汤，是今天狼部落狩猎队带回来的弯角兽肉汤。
弯角兽不好捕捉，黑羽兽人碰运气一年才能吃个两三次。
当亲眼看见狼兽人连肉带汤，舀了三大勺倒进碗里，饭盆被占满一大半，兽人还有些恍惚。
来不及惊讶，边上的狼兽人又用两个细木棍挑了一大堆的野菜过来，还问：“放汤里还是放叶子上？”
羽山想到狼兽人都分开的，立马道：“放叶上。”
狼兽人赞许地看过来一眼，会吃，跟他们一样！
羽山捧着碗站立在一旁，看着自己伴侣、族人，哪怕是羽涯跟羽乐两个小兽人，分得的肉汤依旧跟他们的没什么两样，羽山不禁道：“你们够吗？”
狼贝见他咽口水，抡起勺子问：“要不再添点儿？”
羽山摇头，赶紧招呼羽千跟两个小狼，找地方坐去了。
其他黑羽兽人自发找过来，围成一圈，头碰头，面面相觑。
羽山：“还不饿？”
话落，旁边一大声吸溜声。
羽涯：“嘶！”
“怎么了？！”兽人手紧紧扣着碗沿，想吃，但怕有毒。
羽涯忙着吸溜冷气，道：“烫。”
羽山：“放心，他们都吃了。”黑羽兽人现在跟狼兽人没有仇了，不至于下毒毒死他们。
说罢，他早忍不住，埋头吃得香。
“狼兽人原来吃这么好？”羽涯呼噜呼噜往嘴里灌，烫得吐舌头还舍不得放了嘴里的肉。
他一边吃，一边嘀嘀咕咕。刚刚还没精神，这会儿恨不能将整个陶碗往肚里塞。
兽人们埋头苦吃，吭哧吭哧吃下肚一半的肉汤，才放慢速度。
羽千抿掉唇角沾染的肉沫，浑身透着热气儿。
他肩膀挨着羽山，身体舒展开来。
他扫了一圈围拢的族人们，见一个个养得头发也亮了，脸也红润，心情更加明朗。
目光转到附近，见羽乐细胳膊细腿儿的，依旧孱弱，慢慢皱起眉头。
小兽人捧着比脸大的陶盆，小口小口吃着。毛绒绒的脑袋垂下来，好像这么久了，一句话也没听他说。
羽千：“乐。”
小兽人抬起头，眉间有郁色，但依旧柔软乖巧。
“阿千叔。”
“是不是累了？”
羽乐乖乖点头，“只有一点点。”
羽千摸摸小兽人脑袋，“累了就休息，只要认真做，黑狼兽人不会说什么。”
羽乐：“嗯。”
小兽人就抬着脑袋看着他，圆眼清澈，像初生的幼崽。羽千对他的怜惜更甚。
“快吃吧。”
羽乐又低下头去。
不论是部落以前那些食物，还是狼部落的肉汤，羽乐都吃得慢吞吞。饭量也小，看着没有一点食欲。
兽人都觉得幼崽只要能吃，就好养。
狼部落的食物是他们吃过最好吃的，但羽乐还这样，羽千有些犯愁。
余下那一半肉汤塞进肚子，没一会儿，兽人陆续起来，学着狼兽人去溪边洗了碗，狼雨就过来带他们去睡觉。
走着走着，面上接着几滴雨。
狼雨道：“幸好尾巴草收完了。”
单只今天小狼们脱粒的尾巴草都已经装了大半陶罐，已经比原来一块地所有的尾巴草都多。都能匀出来给支部落送上一些。
尾巴草还没脱粒完呢，待到所有陶罐装满，今年雪季就不用愁了。
想到这儿，狼雨脚步更加轻快。
羽山跟羽千落在后头一步，休息了会儿，肚子也饱了，脑子也灵活了。
他两个看着狼部落战一天囤下来的食物，就不免想到自家部落。
羽山很想问问尾巴草的事……但这会儿开口，显得黑羽兽人觊觎人家食物似的。
狼雨给他们带到地方，兽人离开，本来疲惫的黑羽兽人却没有一个睡下。
大家围着洞中的微弱火堆，心里沉甸甸的。
“也不知道部落开始囤雪季的食物没有？”
“有祭司就是好，狼部落食物都吃不完，还能分给我们吃肉呢……”
说者无心，角落里蜷缩着的小兽人却一僵，抱着膝盖，脑袋深深埋下去。
羽涯：“阿山叔，咱们要不再跟他们交换尾巴草种子？”
羽山手按着隐隐作痛的腿，火光映在他脸上，将他眼角的皱纹刻得更深。
“食物珍贵。”
之前交换的都是器物，两个部落间的关系也在交往中慢慢亲密起来。若提起交换食物，万一成仇……
羽山声音微沉道：“再想想。”。
狼兽人有这样的能力，他们不得不更加慎重。
羽千轻轻挪开他按在腿上的手，垂眸给他捏着，一下一下，力道正合适。
羽山手掌盖在他手背，紧了紧。
羽千温声道：“就按一会儿，不累。”
羽山低头，蹭了蹭自己伴侣的额角。
其他族人沉默着，心中急切，但也知道这事儿不能出岔子。
羽涯：“不就开个口的事儿？”
才说完，就挨了旁边兽人一下，“你当狼兽人是你阿爸？要什么开个口就是。”
羽涯：“就问一问，又没硬要！”
“行了。”羽山看着一脸不服气的小狼，压着眉头道，“涯，这里不是我们部落，说话别不过脑子。”
“这需要过什么脑子。”羽涯扬起下巴，一脸无所谓。
羽山胸口起伏了下，“这要换做我们部落，有兽人开口问你交换辛辛苦苦种出来的食物，你怎么想？”
“他想打架！”羽涯脱口而出，随即两眼一鼓，愣住。
边上兽人重重拍了拍他肩膀，“说话，过脑子，记住了！”
羽涯脸憋得青白，哑了许久，脑袋一耷，“知道了……”
chapters.title: 第100章
chapters.translated_text:
At this moment, the area from the corridor to the meadow on Wolf Mountain was covered with resting orcs.

Everyone had spent the day harvesting the foxtail grass, and the weight that had been hanging over the wolf orcs' hearts for half a year finally lifted.

Although everyone was exhausted, their hearts were light, and they fell asleep as soon as they lay down.

The adult orcs were reckless when working, but there were only a few wolf cubs to do the threshing, so it wasn't finished in a short time.

The priest then told the wolf cubs to clear out all the empty caves on Wolf Mountain and spread the remaining foxtail grass inside to be dealt with slowly tomorrow.

By now, everyone was drained, including the Black Feather orcs, and most had already closed their eyes and started snoring.

Dinner was prepared by Lang Bei and a few orcs from the gathering team. As the scent of bone soup wafted out, the sleeping orcs frowned, sniffing the air, their heads turning toward the stove like compass needles, struggling as if to wake up.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan returned just in time; the area in front of the stove was empty.

The orcs who usually scrambled for food were paralyzed with exhaustion, so for once, they were able to get ahead.

The two of them ladled out meat soup, and behind them, Lang Guo arrived with a line of cubs.

The cubs were well-fed and growing fast. They looked chubby, and their arms and legs were bouncy and full of energy.

The orcs had been busy harvesting foxtail grass all day, and the cubs had been chasing each other and running wild all day. Now, their cheeks were flushed, their bodies were sweating, and they smelled like the sweet-stinky scent of little puppies.

Lin Qiu looked over, and the cubs smiled at him.

Seeing them about to crowd around, Lang Guo caught one in each hand, keeping them in place.

"Time to eat!" Lang Bei shouted after they finished ladling the soup.

The orcs sat up in shock, then grimaced and clutched their lower backs as they collapsed back down.

"Awoo!!!" Lang Mo wailed, "Why is it so tiring! My back... it's broken, awoo!"

Lang Xi’s legs trembled as he leaned on his shoulder to stand up, only for the pain to make Lang Mo wail while holding his back again.

Lang Xi said shakily, "I'm not doing this next year. I'd rather go hunting."

Orcs rarely did serious farm work; they used their beast forms to plow the land, just scratching with their paws, which was like playing.

Sowing was just a casual scatter, which was even easier.

The most strenuous part was transporting bird droppings.

The later weeding could be done while squatting, but they couldn't squat while cutting foxtail grass, and they couldn't reach it while standing. Their beast forms weren't suitable for the task, so they had to work in human form while bent over.

They were tall, so it would be strange if they could still jump around after bending over like that all day.

The orcs experienced the exhaustion of farm work for the first time, and they were both sleepy and hungry. Their stomachs had rumbled several times, but they simply couldn't get up.

Lang Bei called out a few more times before the orcs gradually supported their lower backs and trudged bitterly toward the stove. Their footsteps were heavy, thudding with every step as if their legs were filled with lead.

The wolf orcs moved, but the Black Feather orcs sat together, looking somewhat reserved and bewildered.

Lang Yu passed by and called out, "Let's go, eat and then go to sleep."

The Black Feather orcs gathered their spirits and followed behind Lang Yu.

"We'll definitely sleep well tonight."

The Black Feather orcs nodded repeatedly.

Lang Yu said, "Sleep well, we'll continue tomorrow."

The Black Feather orcs wilted instantly.

Yu Ya followed behind Yu Shan, and Yu Le also returned to the group, looking dejected. Seeing this, Yu Ya couldn't help but ask in a raspy voice, "Did they bully you?"

Yu Ya, who had been lively when they arrived, was now like a fish left in a puddle all day, unable to jump around anymore.

Yu Le glanced at him, confirming he was talking to him, and his already soft voice became even lower, "No."

Yu Ya hung his head, swaying as he walked forward, and didn't ask any further.

Yu Le hadn't been able to play with them before, so they had nothing to say to each other.

Besides, this Wolf Tribe was simply no place for an orc to stay; he wouldn't come back next time no matter what!

The Black Feather orcs hung at the back of the line, moving only when the front moved. Their shoulders were slightly slumped, their eyes dull, moving like zombies, unable to speak.

Before long, an orc came over from the front.

"Reach out your hands."

The Black Feather orcs reached out honestly without thinking.

Their hands sank as a large rice bowl was placed in them, nearly dropping it. Startled, the orcs hurriedly hugged the bowls, no longer looking dull.

A piece of pottery took them a month of hard work to trade for; they didn't want to do work like today's ever again...

Lang Yu said, "Hold your bowls steady. If you lose them, you'll have to eat with your hands tonight."

The Black Feather orcs, led by Yu Shan as usual, got closer to the stove, and the scent of the meat soup became richer.

It wasn't the fish soup the Black Feather orcs were used to eating in the Great Swamp, but the curved-horn beast meat soup brought back by the Wolf Tribe's hunting team today.

Curved-horn beasts were hard to catch; the Black Feather orcs were lucky if they could eat it two or three times a year.

When they saw the wolf orcs ladle three large scoops of meat and soup into their bowls, filling them more than halfway, the orcs were still in a daze.

Before they could be surprised, the wolf orc next to them used two thin sticks to pick up a large pile of wild vegetables and asked, "In the soup or on the leaves?"

Yu Shan remembered that the wolf orcs kept them separate, so he immediately said, "On the leaves."

The wolf orc gave an approving look; they knew how to eat, just like them!

Yu Shan stood to the side holding his bowl, watching his partner, his clansmen, and even the two little orcs, Yu Ya and Yu Le, receive the same amount of meat soup as theirs. Yu Shan couldn't help but ask, "Is this enough for you?"

Seeing him swallow, Lang Bei raised his ladle and asked, "Want some more?"

Yu Shan shook his head and quickly called Yu Qian and the two little wolves to find a place to sit.

Other Black Feather orcs spontaneously gathered around, forming a circle, heads touching, looking at each other.

Yu Shan asked, "Not hungry yet?"

As soon as he spoke, there was a loud slurping sound nearby.

Yu Ya: "Hiss!"

"What's wrong?!" The orc gripped the edge of his bowl tightly, wanting to eat but fearing it might be poisoned.

Yu Ya was busy sucking in cold air and said, "It's hot."

Yu Shan said, "Don't worry, they all ate it." The Black Feather orcs no longer had a grudge against the wolf orcs, so they wouldn't poison them to death.

After saying that, he couldn't hold back any longer and buried his head to eat deliciously.

"The wolf orcs eat so well?" Yu Ya gulped it down, his tongue sticking out from the heat, yet he couldn't bear to let go of the meat in his mouth.

He muttered while eating. He had been listless just a moment ago, but now he wished he could stuff the entire pottery bowl into his stomach.

The orcs buried their heads and ate, and only after finishing half of the meat soup did they slow down.

Yu Qian wiped the meat foam from the corner of his lips, his whole body radiating heat.

His shoulder brushed against Yu Shan's, and his body relaxed.

He scanned the gathered clansmen, seeing that everyone's hair looked brighter and their faces were rosy, and his mood became even brighter.

His gaze turned nearby, and seeing Yu Le’s thin arms and legs, still frail, he slowly frowned.

The little orc held a pottery bowl larger than his face, eating in small bites. His fluffy head hung down; it seemed he hadn't heard him say a word for a long time.

Yu Qian: "Le."

The little orc looked up, his brows furrowed with melancholy, but he remained soft and obedient.

"Uncle Yu Qian."

"Are you tired?"

Yu Le nodded obediently, "Only a little bit."

Yu Qian patted the little orc's head, "Rest if you're tired. As long as you work diligently, the Black Wolf orcs won't say anything."

Yu Le: "Mm."

The little orc looked up at him, his round eyes clear, like a newborn cub. Yu Qian felt even more pity for him.

"Eat up."

Yu Le lowered his head again.

Whether it was the food from their old tribe or the meat soup of the Wolf Tribe, Yu Le ate slowly. His appetite was small, and he looked like he had no appetite at all.

Orcs always felt that as long as a cub could eat, it was easy to raise.

The Wolf Tribe's food was the best they had ever eaten, but Yu Le was still like this, and Yu Qian was a bit worried.

After stuffing the remaining half of the meat soup into their stomachs, the orcs gradually stood up, learned from the wolf orcs to wash their bowls by the stream, and Lang Yu came to take them to sleep.

As they walked, a few drops of rain fell on their faces.

Lang Yu said, "Luckily, the foxtail grass is all harvested."

Just the foxtail grass threshed by the little wolves today already filled more than half a pottery jar, which was more than all the foxtail grass from the original plot. They could even spare some to send to the branch tribe.

The foxtail grass hadn't even been fully threshed yet; once all the jars were full, they wouldn't have to worry about the snow season this year.

Thinking of this, Lang Yu's steps became even lighter.

Yu Shan and Yu Qian lagged a step behind. After resting and filling their stomachs, their minds were clearer.

Looking at the food the Wolf Tribe had hoarded in one day of fighting, they couldn't help but think of their own tribe.

Yu Shan really wanted to ask about the foxtail grass... but speaking up now would make the Black Feather orcs look like they were coveting someone else's food.

Lang Yu led them to their place and left. Although they were exhausted, not a single Black Feather orc fell asleep.

Everyone gathered around the faint fire in the cave, their hearts heavy.

"I wonder if our tribe has started hoarding food for the snow season yet?"

"It's good to have a priest. The Wolf Tribe has more food than they can eat, and they can even share meat with us..."

The speaker didn't mean anything by it, but the little orc curled up in the corner stiffened, hugging his knees, his head buried deep.

Yu Ya: "Uncle Yu Shan, should we trade for some foxtail grass seeds with them?"

Yu Shan pressed his aching leg, the firelight reflecting on his face, carving the wrinkles at the corners of his eyes even deeper.

"Food is precious."

They had only traded artifacts before, and the relationship between the two tribes was slowly becoming closer through their interactions. If they brought up trading for food, what if it turned into enmity...

Yu Shan's voice was low as he said, "Let's think about it."

The wolf orcs had such capabilities, so they had to be even more cautious.

Yu Qian gently moved his hand away from his leg and lowered his eyes to massage it, one stroke after another, the pressure just right.

Yu Shan placed his palm on the back of his hand and tightened it.

Yu Qian said warmly, "Just massaging for a while, it’s not tiring."

Yu Shan lowered his head and rubbed against his partner's forehead.

The other clansmen were silent, feeling anxious in their hearts, but they also knew that this matter couldn't go wrong.

Yu Ya: "Isn't it just a matter of asking?"

As soon as he finished speaking, he was hit by the orc next to him, "Do you think the wolf orcs are your father? You can just ask for whatever you want."

Yu Ya: "I'm just asking, I'm not forcing them!"

"Enough." Yu Shan looked at the defiant little wolf and frowned, "Ya, this isn't our tribe, don't speak without thinking."

"What is there to think about?" Yu Ya raised his chin, looking indifferent.

Yu Shan's chest heaved, "If this were our tribe, and an orc asked to trade for food you worked so hard to grow, what would you think?"

"He wants to fight!" Yu Ya blurted out, then his eyes widened, and he froze.

The orc next to him patted his shoulder heavily, "Think before you speak, remember that!"

Yu Ya's face turned pale, and after a long silence, he hung his head, "I know..."

chapters.source_text:
夜风卷着细雨往大山洞里吹，洞口湿了一片。
忙碌一天的兽人睡得熟，只零星几个小狼还在说着悄悄话。
明天地里没活儿，黑羽兽人在，后头也用不着小狼继续脱粒。
狼金这会儿正安排明天抓圆鼻兽割毛做牙刷的事，这是王之前交代的任务，他还没做。
山洞更里面，窸窸窣窣的声儿不断。
林楸翻个身，手捂着耳朵，那声儿才停了。
狼岩脑袋搭在草窝边缘，尾巴垂着，眼也不眨地看着睡熟的林楸。
爪子不小心搁在两个草窝中间挡着的干草上，又不小心抓了一把下来，塞到两个草窝的缝隙当中……
视线没了阻挡，狼岩静静看了会儿林楸，阖眼睡觉。
雨下了半夜，早晨就停了。
尾巴草收割过后，狼兽人便分开来，继续做自己的事儿，脱粒跟脱壳的事儿交给黑羽兽人。
林楸醒得晚，睁眼时，看着两个草窝中间的格挡，有些疑惑地伸手摸了摸。
好像矮了。
林楸坐起来，山洞早空了。
他不经意瞧见两个草窝中间的缝隙，见塞得满满当当的干草，面上空白一阵，随后牵起唇角。
他道昨晚是哪个老鼠在作怪。
林楸只当没看见，将长发拢在一处简单梳了梳，扎做个高马尾，起身出去。
早饭过后，黑羽兽人分散在几个山洞里忙。
林楸打算去看看昨天兽人们带回来的咩咩兽，又顺带捡了背篓石镰，去大河边割些草来喂。
狼岩从祭司山洞下来，一眼定在河边躬身割草的林楸身上。
脚步一转，往那边靠近。
雨季过后，大河水位降了下去，岸边一部分砂石裸露，那绑着鱼笼的草绳也露了出来。
兽人们捕鱼捕得勤，早前做的那几十个鱼笼坏得快，如今也不过剩下二三十个。这河里的鱼精了，不敌以前好抓，兽人们只得空闲时多做些网来，追着鱼群跑。
河边刚割下的青草漫着清新的香气。
河水慢吞吞前行，蓝天白云也躺在那水流中，悠然自得。
微风卷起林楸衣角，单薄的麻布衣服贴近身体，勾勒出清瘦的腰，笔直的腿。
听到动静，林楸割下最后一把草，握着石镰回看。
视线对上，林楸弯眼。
狼岩扬起唇角。
他身上就一条麻布短裤，还算宽松，半身赤着，打猎练出来的腱子肉紧实而不夸张。
这么闲闲走过来，跟度假似的。
林楸一时恍惚，好似还在从前的世界，只不过去了个草原上旅行，身边多了个陪伴的人。
眼前一暗，林楸回神。
他问：“刚刚跟祭司商量什么呢？”
狼岩握住伸过来的手，手指细长，指缝两侧的软肉更是柔软细腻，他忍不住捏了捏，再抓紧。
“去支部落的事。”
林楸抬眼，望入灰眸中。
狼岩：“尾巴草收上来了，比往年收得多，可以匀出一点。雨季支部落没过来，我们也不知道那边情况。雪季之前还要忙着囤食物，现在过去正合适。”
林楸：“什么时候去？”
狼岩：“就这几天的事。”
林楸：“那你去吗？”
狼岩一下攥得林楸手有些紧，就怕他说也想回去。
“还没定，但我应该不去。”
“好。”林楸应了声，就没继续再问。
狼岩自然也不再提。
他拎着背篓，一手牵着林楸，随他去西边林子。
另抓的两头咩咩兽先单独养在栅栏外面，兽人用绳子将它们绑在树上，依旧按照先前喂养咩咩兽的方式喂养。
带回来的咩咩兽一公一母，若是养得好，没准明年就能再添几头。
狼岩去喂栅栏里的红鸟，林楸就站在外头，打量这刚到的成员。
咩咩兽在林楸看来就跟羊似的，或许跟岩羊有些像，但皮毛却白且厚实。
部落里那些厚皮子，好些都是咩咩兽的。
看了会儿，狼岩喂完出来，林楸就得去祭司山洞坐坐了。
今天已经够晚，少不得叫祭司说上几句。
狼岩过来这一程，就好像陪他遛了个弯儿。
*
黑羽兽人在，第一批脱粒的尾巴草装了十个兽皮袋。
这期间，去支部落的兽人也选好了。
狼岩不去，由狼火带队过去。
这次过去，不仅要带尾巴草，还有之前多做的陶锅、陶罐、渔网，连梳子都塞了十几把。又捎带上些鱼干、菜干、果干、蘑菇干，一部分是给狼火他们路上吃，余下一点交给支部落。
就那么几个兽皮袋的食物，也不是为了让他们饱腹，而是让支部落的兽人见了、尝了，再趁着空闲多做些这东西。
虽抵不过肉，但总能饿的时候垫一垫肚子，好熬过冬季。
去支部落要半个月，来回就是一个多月。
为了保证兽人路上安全，狼火带的兽人不全是第二狩猎队的，狼岩还从另外的采集队、狩猎队挑了些兽人出来。
兽人挑好了，东西也收拾妥当，祭司选了日子，狼火便带着二十兽人的小队出发了。
路途遥远，板车不好运送，兽人们都是变做兽形两边挂着兽皮袋走。
林楸去送，跟着往前走了几步，忽然被狼岩拉住手腕往回带。
林楸退回来，不明所以看着他。
狼岩长得高大，肩膀宽阔，立在林楸身侧能将他整个挡住。就是凑近了得仰头才能看见他脸，有些费脖子。
林楸分明不矮，怪狼岩太高。
他光洁的下巴抬着，叫狼岩轻轻勾了下，逗猫似的。
“回去了。”
林楸痒，在他肩上狠蹭了下。
“我送一送他们。”
狼岩顺势圈住林楸后腰，手掌扣紧，带着他往回走，“他们自己找得到地方，不用送。”
林楸一脸奇怪地看他。
狼岩面不改色，只一味将林楸抓紧。
林楸看着他锋利的眉压着，有些琢磨出味儿来，他笑，“你不会是怕我跟着跑了吧？”
狼岩：“你答应我了。”
狼兽人的伴侣是不会分开的。
林楸笑得脑袋轻轻撞他肩膀，又被他圈住腰，动不得。
他趴在狼岩肩头笑声轻颤，分明那么个冷峻的兽人，怎么这事儿上这么大反差。
“祭司都不让我走，你怕什么？再说，我跑得过你吗？”
狼岩：“嗯。”
他下巴搭在林楸头顶，望着山洞的方向，还有些愁。
旁的兽人答应成为伴侣后就住一个窝，可楸好像一点没有这个意识。他也不提，狼岩又不好说，怕逼急了吓到他……
狼兽人有了伴侣，那就是一辈子只这一个，所以确定关系之后，便会亲密无间。他不知道楸怎么想，只能悄悄动作。
狼岩抱了他一会儿，林楸就道：“我要去祭司那儿了。”
狼岩松开，看着林楸转头就往狼山走。
他看了会儿，正要提步跟上，林楸停下，忽的转身撞上他怀抱。
他踮起脚，圈住狼岩脖子，飞快亲了他嘴角一下。没等狼岩反应过来，立马跑了。
狼岩眸光一软。
浑身的焦躁不安没了，整个兽人变得积极向上，稳重严肃。
林楸跑了一段，改为慢慢走。他略喘着气，回头看，狼岩还看着他。
他笑容明媚起来，心里前所未有的踏实。
“瞧瞧狼雪，都比你认真……”才上到祭司山洞，祭司一个小陶罐塞过来。
林楸听着自己都能一字不差重复的念叨话，将罐子口打开，鼻子嗅了嗅，药膏的味道沁凉。
“祭司，这是什么？”
老祭司没说完叫他打断，吹胡子瞪他一眼，没好气道：“能是什么，擦晒红的皮的。”
林楸疑惑地看过来。
老祭司：“王让做的，你脸跟脖子都要晒得脱皮了，不知道？”
嘀嘀咕咕着，又来一句，“其他兽人晒多久都不像你，也不知你阿父怎么给你养的……”
林楸笑盈盈的，指节蹭了下下巴，似还残留着狼岩手指留下的粗糙触感，又对祭司温声道：“谢谢祭司。”
他长得好，又白净，卖乖的时候格外招人疼。
那双雪似的眸子被融化在温暖的关怀中，连笑意都逐渐多了起来。倒比从前那独来独往的，瞧着顺眼多了。
“哼！”
老兽人再不理他，做药膏去了。
山洞除了祭司，还有个白狼幼崽狼雪在。
幼崽跟着祭司也学了几个月了，认真得很，这会儿坐在狼起做的小板凳上分草药。
幼崽皮肤稍嫩，虫子就爱盯着他们咬。
狼雪身上涂了些草药汁，腰间系着麻布小短裤的绳子，看背影，像脱了皮刚出锅的小芋头。
水水嫩嫩的，一看就软糯。
幼崽跟前摆着的草药堆跟当初林楸刚来那会儿一样，不过里头多是杂草。
他心无旁骛，还有肉窝窝的小手在草堆里挑选，弄得手上满是泥。
他也不像狼冰那样有点脏污就一脸烦闷，捡得格外认真。
林楸没去打扰，而是坐在角落慢慢将药膏涂抹好，再洗干净手，跟着祭司做药膏。
如今简单的药膏他已经能上手，一些药方也能调配。像幼崽那一堆的野草里，有哪些草药他也一眼能认出来。
林楸想，这些天的努力并未白费。
以后要是出门，随意将他扔个地方，他也不至于两眼摸瞎。
想到这儿，林楸唇角微扬。
察觉到旁边幽幽递过来的目光，他唇角抿平，收拢心神，加紧速度帮忙。
chapters.title: 第101章
chapters.translated_text:
The night wind carried a fine drizzle into the large cave, dampening the entrance.

The beastmen, exhausted from a busy day, were fast asleep; only a few scattered wolf cubs were still whispering to each other.

There was no work in the fields tomorrow, and with the Black Feather beastmen around, the wolf cubs wouldn't need to continue threshing.

Lang Jin was currently busy organizing the task of catching round-nosed beasts to harvest their hair for toothbrushes—a mission the King had assigned earlier that he hadn't yet completed.

Further inside the cave, there was a constant rustling sound.

Lin Qiu turned over, covering his ears with his hands, and the sound finally stopped.

Lang Yan rested his head on the edge of his grass nest, his tail drooping, staring unblinkingly at the sleeping Lin Qiu.

His claw accidentally rested on the dried grass used as a partition between the two nests, and he inadvertently pulled a handful down, stuffing it into the gap between them...

With his view no longer obstructed, Lang Yan watched Lin Qiu quietly for a while before closing his eyes to sleep.

The rain fell for half the night and stopped by morning.

After the tail-grass was harvested, the wolf beastmen split up to continue their own tasks, leaving the threshing and husking to the Black Feather beastmen.

Lin Qiu woke up late. When he opened his eyes and looked at the partition between the two nests, he reached out and touched it with some confusion.

It seemed lower.

Lin Qiu sat up; the cave was already empty.

He caught sight of the gap between the two nests and saw it stuffed full of dried grass. His expression went blank for a moment, then the corners of his lips curled up.

He wondered which little mouse had been up to mischief last night.

Lin Qiu pretended not to notice, gathered his long hair together to comb it simply, tied it into a high ponytail, and got up to leave.

After breakfast, the Black Feather beastmen were busy in several different caves.

Lin Qiu planned to go see the "baa-baa" beasts the beastmen had brought back yesterday, and while he was at it, he picked up his basket and stone sickle to go to the big river to cut some grass to feed them.

Lang Yan came down from the priest's cave, his gaze immediately locking onto Lin Qiu, who was bent over cutting grass by the river.

He changed his direction and headed toward him.

After the rainy season, the water level of the big river had dropped, exposing some of the sand and gravel on the banks, along with the grass ropes tied to the fish traps.

The beastmen fished diligently, and the dozens of traps they had made earlier wore out quickly, leaving only twenty or thirty remaining. The fish in the river had become smarter and were not as easy to catch as before, so the beastmen had to make more nets in their spare time to chase the schools of fish.

The freshly cut grass by the river gave off a refreshing fragrance.

The river flowed sluggishly, and the blue sky and white clouds lay within the water, looking leisurely and carefree.

A light breeze caught the hem of Lin Qiu's clothes, the thin linen fabric clinging to his body, outlining his slender waist and straight legs.

Hearing movement, Lin Qiu cut the last handful of grass and turned back, holding his stone sickle.

Their eyes met, and Lin Qiu’s eyes curved.

Lang Yan raised the corners of his lips.

He was wearing only a relatively loose pair of linen shorts, his upper body bare, his muscles—honed by hunting—firm and not overly bulky.

Walking over so leisurely, it was as if he were on vacation.

Lin Qiu felt a momentary trance, as if he were still in his old world, just traveling on a grassland with someone by his side.

The light in front of him dimmed, and Lin Qiu snapped back to reality.

He asked, "What were you discussing with the priest just now?"

Lang Yan held the hand that reached out; the fingers were slender, and the soft flesh on the sides of his finger joints was even more delicate. He couldn't help but squeeze them before gripping them tighter.

"About going to the branch tribe."

Lin Qiu looked up, gazing into those gray eyes.

Lang Yan said, "The tail-grass has been harvested, and we have more than in previous years, so we can spare a little. The branch tribe didn't come over during the rainy season, and we don't know their situation. We have to be busy stocking up on food before the snow season, so now is the perfect time to go."

Lin Qiu asked, "When are you leaving?"

Lang Yan replied, "Within these next few days."

Lin Qiu asked, "Are you going?"

Lang Yan gripped Lin Qiu's hand a little tighter, afraid he might say he wanted to go back too.

"It's not decided yet, but I probably won't go."

"Okay." Lin Qiu responded and didn't continue to ask.

Naturally, Lang Yan didn't bring it up again.

He carried the basket, holding Lin Qiu's hand, and followed him to the forest in the west.

The two newly caught baa-baa beasts were kept separately outside the fence for now. The beastmen had tied them to trees with ropes and were feeding them in the same way as before.

The baa-baa beasts brought back were one male and one female; if they were raised well, perhaps they could add a few more next year.

Lang Yan went to feed the red birds in the enclosure, while Lin Qiu stood outside, observing these new members.

To Lin Qiu, the baa-baa beasts looked like sheep, perhaps similar to bighorn sheep, but their fur was white and thick.

Many of the thick hides in the tribe were from these baa-baa beasts.

After watching for a while, Lang Yan finished feeding and came out, and Lin Qiu had to go to the priest's cave to sit for a bit.

It was already late enough today that the priest would inevitably have a few words to say.

Lang Yan's walk over here felt just like accompanying him on a stroll.

*

With the Black Feather beastmen there, the first batch of threshed tail-grass filled ten animal-skin bags.

During this time, the beastmen to go to the branch tribe had also been selected.

Lang Yan was not going; Lang Huo would lead the team.

This time, they would take not only the tail-grass but also the extra pottery pots, jars, and fishing nets they had made, and even stuffed in a dozen combs. They also brought along dried fish, dried vegetables, dried fruit, and dried mushrooms; some were for Lang Huo and his team to eat on the road, and the rest were to be given to the branch tribe.

Those few bags of food weren't meant to fill them up, but to let the beastmen of the branch tribe see and taste them, so they could make more of these things in their spare time.

Although it couldn't replace meat, it could at least cushion their stomachs when they were hungry, helping them survive the winter.

It would take half a month to reach the branch tribe, making the round trip over a month.

To ensure the safety of the beastmen on the road, the beastmen Lang Huo took were not all from the Second Hunting Team; Lang Yan also selected some from other gathering and hunting teams.

Once the beastmen were chosen and the supplies packed, the priest picked a date, and Lang Huo set off with a team of twenty beastmen.

The journey was long and the carts were difficult to transport, so the beastmen transformed into their beast forms, carrying the animal-skin bags on their sides as they traveled.

Lin Qiu went to see them off and followed them a few steps forward, only to be suddenly pulled back by his wrist by Lang Yan.

Lin Qiu stepped back, looking at him in confusion.

Lang Yan was tall and broad-shouldered; standing beside Lin Qiu, he could block him completely. It was a bit of a neck-straining effort to look at his face when they were close.

Lin Qiu clearly wasn't short; it was just that Lang Yan was too tall.

His smooth chin was lifted, and Lang Yan gently hooked it, as if teasing a cat.

"Let's go back."

Lin Qiu felt ticklish and rubbed hard against his shoulder.

"I'm seeing them off."

Lang Yan took the opportunity to wrap his arm around Lin Qiu's lower back, his palm firm, leading him back. "They can find the place themselves; no need to see them off."

Lin Qiu looked at him with a strange expression.

Lang Yan remained calm, only focused on holding Lin Qiu tighter.

Lin Qiu watched his sharp brows knit together and began to catch on. He laughed, "You aren't afraid I'll run off with them, are you?"

Lang Yan replied, "You promised me."

Wolf beastmen's mates never separate.

Lin Qiu laughed, his head gently bumping against his shoulder, but he was held by the waist and couldn't move.

He leaned on Lang Yan's shoulder, his laughter trembling slightly. Such a cold and stern beastman, how could there be such a contrast when it came to this?

"Even the priest doesn't stop me from leaving, what are you afraid of? Besides, can I even outrun you?"

Lang Yan said, "Hmm."

He rested his chin on the top of Lin Qiu's head, looking toward the cave, still feeling a bit worried.

Other beastmen lived in the same nest after becoming mates, but Qiu didn't seem to have any awareness of this at all. He didn't bring it up, and Lang Yan didn't know how to say it, fearing he might scare him if he pushed too hard...

Once a wolf beastman had a mate, they only had one for life, so after confirming the relationship, they would be inseparable. He didn't know what Qiu was thinking, so he could only act quietly.

Lang Yan held him for a while, then Lin Qiu said, "I need to go to the priest's place."

Lang Yan let go and watched as Lin Qiu turned and headed toward Wolf Mountain.

He watched for a moment, and just as he was about to follow, Lin Qiu stopped, suddenly turned around, and bumped into his embrace.

He stood on tiptoe, wrapped his arms around Lang Yan's neck, and quickly kissed the corner of his mouth. Before Lang Yan could react, he ran off.

Lang Yan's gaze softened.

All his restlessness vanished, and the beastman became positive, steady, and serious.

Lin Qiu ran for a distance before slowing to a walk. Slightly out of breath, he looked back and saw Lang Yan still watching him.

His smile became bright, and he felt a sense of security in his heart like never before.

"Look at Lang Xue, he's more diligent than you..." As soon as he reached the priest's cave, the priest shoved a small pottery jar at him.

Lin Qiu listened to the nagging he could already repeat word for word, opened the jar, and sniffed; the scent of the ointment was cool and refreshing.

"Priest, what is this?"

The old priest didn't finish his sentence before being interrupted, blew his beard at him, and said crossly, "What could it be? It's for rubbing on skin that's been sunburned."

Lin Qiu looked over in confusion.

The old priest said, "The King had me make it. Your face and neck are about to peel from the sun, didn't you know?"

Muttering to himself, he added, "Other beastmen don't look like you no matter how long they're in the sun. I don't know how your father raised you..."

Lin Qiu smiled, rubbing his chin with his knuckles, as if the rough sensation of Lang Yan's fingers still lingered there, and said gently to the priest, "Thank you, Priest."

He was good-looking and fair-skinned, and when he acted cute, he was particularly endearing.

That pair of snow-like eyes melted into the warm care, and even his smiles gradually increased. He looked much more pleasant than the loner he used to be.

"Hmph!"

The old beastman ignored him and went back to making medicine.

Besides the priest, there was also the white wolf cub, Lang Xue, in the cave.

The cub had been learning from the priest for a few months and was very diligent, currently sitting on a small stool made by Lang Qi, sorting herbs.

The cub's skin was tender, and insects loved to bite them.

Lang Xue had some herbal juice applied to his body and a small linen rope tied around his waist; from the back, he looked like a small, peeled taro just out of the pot.

Tender and soft, he looked squishy.

The pile of herbs in front of the cub was the same as when Lin Qiu first arrived, though it contained mostly weeds.

He was focused, his chubby little hands picking through the pile, getting his hands covered in mud.

Unlike Lang Bing, who would look annoyed at the slightest bit of dirt, he was picking through them with extreme care.

Lin Qiu didn't disturb him, but sat in the corner, carefully applying the ointment, then washed his hands and joined the priest in making medicine.

He could now handle simple ointments and mix some prescriptions. He could recognize at a glance which herbs were among the weeds in the cub's pile.

Lin Qiu thought that all his efforts these days hadn't been in vain.

If he were to go out in the future and be dropped in some random place, he wouldn't be completely blind to his surroundings.

Thinking of this, the corners of Lin Qiu's lips curled up slightly.

Noticing the faint gaze directed at him from the side, he pressed his lips into a thin line, gathered his focus, and sped up his work to help.

The orcs of Wolf Mountain lived their lives in an orderly, routine fashion.

Lang Huo, meanwhile, led a small team and set out on a long journey.

They departed before the morning dew had evaporated, reached the eastern part of the Great Marsh by midday, filled their stomachs, rested for a while, and began skirting around the Great Marsh in the afternoon.

Half a day was not enough to travel outside the territory of the Wolf Tribe.

The Great Marsh could not be crossed directly; just skirting around the southeast side of the marsh took the orcs three or four days.

After passing the Great Marsh, they continued onward.

The location of the branch tribe was in the direction the great river flowed, so everyone followed it without worrying about getting lost.

The orcs climbed mountains and crossed ridges, trying their best to avoid other orc tribes along the way.

Watching the vegetation change before their eyes, the thickets grew denser, the moss became increasingly damp, and even the poisonous insects crawling underfoot grew larger.

The moisture in the forest was visible to the naked eye; Lang Huo felt his skin itching from the humidity and knew they were almost there.

In the southwest of the Eastern Continent, mountains and plains intermingled, the temperature was high, and the snow season was slightly shorter.

There were no impassable mountain ranges here, the variety of plants was extremely rich, and it was abundant in various wild fruits and vegetables, which was why there were many small and medium-sized orc tribes.

The territory of the branch tribe was less than half the size of the one at Wolf Mountain. It was surrounded by mountains on three sides, with an open flat land in the middle, and lakes scattered like pearls, clear and emerald green.

Lang Huo had specifically arranged to rest a night early, setting out the next morning, expecting to arrive before the midday meal.

As they neared their destination, the orcs relaxed their vigilance somewhat.

The giant wolves carried massive animal-hide bags, bulging with unknown contents, but enough to make any orc green with envy.

Nowadays, most orcs on the Beast God Continent could not get enough to eat, and many died of starvation.

The way the Wolf Tribe ate three meals a day now was an exception among exceptions.

Driven by hunger, orcs were capable of desperate acts.

The supplies brought this time were more than all the previous ten-plus years combined; the twenty orcs who came each carried something on their backs.

Pottery was fragile, so the orcs ran as carefully as they possibly could.

As they walked, Lang Huo suddenly looked up.

A sound of wind being broken emerged from the forest.

In the blink of an eye, sharpened sticks came flying toward the team from all directions.

Lang Huo shouted, "Dodge!"

The wolf orcs bristled, immediately dodging, but forgetting they were carrying burdens; the hide bags slammed to the ground, and the miscellaneous items in the wicker baskets spilled out directly.

The messy items inside clattered and clanged, and the pottery shattered all over the ground.

Lang Huo’s expression turned cold and grim, "Drop the supplies, take cover!"

The orcs instantly dropped to the ground, shifted into human form, and used the bags as cover to confront the orcs hiding in the bushes who dared not show their faces.

Lang Huo’s jaw was tight, his reddish hair standing on end.

He quickly ran through the tribes in this area in his mind; they came here often and everyone knew they were delivering supplies to the Wolf Tribe, so few orcs dared to provoke them.

Daring to hide but not come out—Lang Huo stared into the deep forest, and his mind was made up.

Using the hide bags as cover, he signaled with a gesture.

Listening quietly for the sound of something cutting through the air again, he raised his hand, and at that opening, half of the wolf orcs charged out.

There was a flurry of panic in the forest, mixed with the sound of flapping wings.

Looking at those green feathers, a fire crackled and popped in Lang Huo’s heart.

He kicked off the ground, leaped up, and hooked a claw, knocking the orc already in mid-air down.

"I knew it was you, Green Eye Tribe." Lang Huo gritted his teeth, stepping forward as if to crush the orc and grind him into the mud.

The Feather-tribe orc fell to the ground and shifted into human form. He tried to scramble up impatiently, but a wolf claw pinned his back down.

He let out a cry of pain, looking back in terror.

Lang Huo scanned the Green Eye Tribe orcs being chased around and sneered.

Cowardly orcs who only dared to use underhanded tricks and didn't dare to fight head-on!

Just as Lang Huo was about to hook the orc by the neck and lift him up, a sharp whistle sounded outside; the pursuing orcs went quiet and retreated rapidly in unison.

Lang Huo glanced at the fleeing orcs and strode out.

Seeing the wolf orcs left behind were fine, he noticed rustling movements in the jungle.

Another team of orcs was charging toward them from the front.

Lang Huo listened quietly for a moment, then looked up and slapped the orc who had just whistled on the forehead.

"Those are from the branch tribe! You can't even tell the difference?"

Lang Shun gasped, "I... I was just anxious..."

"If the King were here, he’d lock you up again! It’s one thing to mess up checking a salt mine, but you can’t even recognize your own tribe members!" Lang Huo was furious; looking at the shattered pottery pot on the ground, he swiped a claw at a nearby tree in a fit of temper.

The claw marks were deep, and wood chips flew.

Lang Shun pulled in his ears and moved toward the hide bags to minimize his presence.

Looking back into the forest, there was no sign of the Green Eye Tribe left.

Before long, the wolf orcs who had come to scout the situation emerged from the deep green forest.

"Huo!" The black wolf, Ye, landed before them with a light, floating step.

He was truly floating; his feet were unsteady, and he was so gaunt from hunger that he looked like a wandering ghost.

His nose twitched, he scanned the forest again, and his voice was so weak it was about to dissipate, "The Green Eye Tribe again."

Lang Ye, the captain of the hunting team for the branch tribe. He was the same age as Lang Huo, and they were orcs who had slept in the same grass nest since they were little.

He draped his arm over Lang Huo’s shoulder, turned his head, and was about to speak, but seeing Lang Huo’s chubby face and feeling the muscles under his arm, he shoved Lang Huo away.

"Are you really Lang Huo?"

Lang Huo rolled his eyes, "Are you blind or just stupid from hunger?"

Lang Ye: "No, how did you get so fat?"

Lang Huo let out a lukewarm laugh.

Seeing he still had his old attitude, Lang Ye confirmed it was him, leaned in again, and said, "Why did you come? Is life at Wolf Mountain better now, so you brought us food too?"

Lang Huo pushed his hand away, angry, "How are you patrolling? The Green Eye Tribe orcs almost reached your territory."

Lang Ye’s stomach rumbled with hunger; he couldn't help but look at the things they brought, saying, "It’s different here than at Wolf Mountain."

Although there were many plants, the prey was just average, and with orcs crowded together, everything had to be fought for.

Their tribe was right next to the Green Eye Tribe, and they had fought several times for hunting in each other's territory.

He was excitedly wondering what good things they had brought.

Even the wolves were fat!

Could it be that the prey in the north had increased?

Lang Ye began to sniff, and as he looked, he noticed the shattered pottery.

"Pottery?"

Lang Huo: "Heh, it’s broken."

A wasted trip!

Lang Ye pushed Lang Huo aside and stood straight. Just a moment ago he had been as weak as a withered seedling, but now he was like a sharp blade, his eyes filled with malice, his pupils dark and deep.

There were few pottery pieces in the tribe to begin with; they hadn't even brought one when they left, so this was likely something the orcs had scraped together from the tribe.

He stood tall and said, "You guys go ahead."

With a wave of his hand, the wolf orcs who had followed stopped their reminiscing and chased after the direction the Green Eye orcs had disappeared.

That was pottery that couldn't be replaced!

There were only so many at Wolf Mountain; the Priest must have had a great use for them when he gave them out, and now they were broken!

These green-haired birds were simply asking for death!

Lang Shun felt a gust of wind blow past, and a few black wolf hairs drifted and landed on the tip of his nose. He blew, and the dry, straw-like hair floated away.

He looked at Lang Huo, who was standing to the side.

"Huo, are we going?"

Lang Huo thought of the appearance of those wolf orcs just now; their fur couldn't hide their thin bodies, and their waists were so narrow they looked like they would snap.

"Wait," Lang Huo said.

It was easy to guess that life at the branch tribe was also bad. The orcs were so hungry that finding food was already difficult; where would they have the energy to guard this place every day?

The orcs at Wolf Mountain were well-fed now and had grown stronger, and it was precisely because of this that seeing Ye and the others like this made him realize how terrifying hunger was.

Had they also looked this half-dead before?

He was afraid that the orcs who had just run out would faint halfway.

This wait lasted until the sun was directly overhead.

Lang Huo had originally planned to arrive at the branch tribe's living area just in time for a meal, but then he slapped his own head.

"Tsk! I’m getting senile!"

The wolf orcs looked over with wide eyes.

"Set up the pots, light the fire."

Lang Shun: "Didn't you say we were going to eat at the branch tribe?"

Lang Huo looked at him like he was a fool, "Do you think they are like Wolf Mountain, eating three meals a day?"

The orcs suddenly realized.

The sound of them slapping their own heads rang out a dozen times.

They had brought plenty of dried fish, but the orcs didn't like eating it. They were well-fed now and had become picky. Along the way, they caught prey whenever they encountered it, and if they ate fish, they would cast nets into the river several times to catch fresh ones.

Therefore, except for the dried fish left for the branch tribe, their own rations had hardly been touched.

The orcs were all skilled at setting up stoves, lighting fires, and making soup.

Several orcs from the gathering team spoke to Lang Huo and started looking for wild vegetables in the vicinity.

There were many plants here; they didn't touch the ones they didn't recognize and only looked for the ones they had eaten before.

By the time Lang Ye and his group returned, tongues lolling and legs trembling with exhaustion, the meat soup in the pot was already cooked. The soup had dried fish mixed with wild vegetables; although the presentation was a bit poor and it tasted a bit bad...

"Bad?!"

The exclamation startled the birds into flight; Lang Ye and the group of branch tribe wolf orcs held their pottery bowls, staring at them with extreme resentment and grievance.

Looking at these orcs from Wolf Mountain, each one strong and sturdy, as if they could flick them away with one hand, they were filled with sour envy.

"You guys are eating and drinking well and forgot about us!"

"The Priest is biased!"

"Woo... Awoo, it’s delicious! Woo... I’m going to tell Chi!"

Amidst the resentful complaints mixed with evaluations of the food, Lang Huo watched them eat without lifting their heads, not even willing to spit it out when it burned their mouths. The witty remarks he had prepared rolled around in his mouth, but his smile froze on his face, and he couldn't say a word.

Without the cover of their wolf-form fur, if not for the fact that orc skeletons were naturally large, they would surely have been thin as paper.

He felt his throat tighten; he couldn't let out a breath, and the stifling feeling in his heart was unbearable.

Thinking this, he slapped Lang Ye on the head.

"Woo!" Lang Ye was still guarding his food, holding the bowl and turning his back.

Lang Huo laughed in anger, just squatting beside him without saying anything.

These pots were originally cooked for everyone to eat together, but at this moment, none of the orcs from Wolf Mountain moved.

They only watched as the branch tribe orcs finished one bowl, then reluctantly added a little more, and when they asked for more, they didn't give any.

Lang Ye’s eyes were red, as if he would cry if they didn't give him more.

Lang Huo’s heart felt heavy, his voice strained: "You’ve been hungry for too long, you can’t eat too much."

Only then did Lang Ye wipe his face and return to his senses, though his eyes were complex. He looked at Lang Huo, a thousand words in his heart, but for a moment he didn't know what to ask, or how to ask.

What exactly happened at Wolf Mountain?

From after the snow season until now, these orcs had all changed. And the things they brought were more than double what they were in previous years...

That tiny glimmer of hope was right before him, but he didn't dare to confirm it.

狼山的兽人们按部就班地生活着。
狼火则带着小队，出发远行。
早晨露水未散就出发，一个上午到达大泽东部，填饱肚子休息一阵，下午开始绕行大泽。
半日的时间不足以走出狼部落。
大泽不能直接穿过去，单是从东南边绕开大泽，兽人们就花了三四日的时间。
过大泽，继续前行。
支部落的位置就在大河流淌的方向，大家顺着走，不用担心跑丢。
兽人们翻山越岭，一路还要尽量避开其他兽人部落。
眼看着眼前的植物慢慢变化，树丛更加茂密，苔藓也愈发湿润，就连脚下爬过的毒虫都更大了。
林子里的水汽肉眼可见，狼火感觉到皮肤被闷得发痒，就知道快到了。
东部大陆西南边，山峦与平原交错，气温高，雪季也稍短些。
这里没有天堑似的山脉，植物种类极其丰富，且盛产各种野果野菜，是以中小型兽人部落不少。
支部落的领地比狼山那边小一半多。三面环山，中间是开阔的平地，湖泊如珍珠散落，清透碧绿。
狼火特意提前一晚上修整好，第二天早晨出发，预计午间饭前到达。
快到地方了，兽人们有些放松警惕。
巨狼驮着硕大的兽皮袋，里头鼓鼓囊囊不知塞的是什么，但也足够令兽人眼红。
如今兽神大陆上大部分兽人可是吃不饱的，饿死不在少数。
狼部落如今那一天三顿的样子，也是特殊中的特殊。
兽人饥饿之下，能做出拼了命的事。
这次带来的物资比前头十多年的都多，来的二十个兽人，各个背上都背着东西。
陶罐这些易碎，兽人们跑得小心得不能再小心。
走着走着，狼火忽然抬头。
一股破风的声音从林子传出。
眨眼间，四面八方削尖的棍子冲着队伍而来。
狼火大喝：“躲开！”
狼兽人狼毛一竖，当即避开，却不想身上驮着东西，一时忘了顾忌，兽皮袋砸在地上，藤筐装着的零碎东西更是直接倒了出来。
里头乱七八糟的东西叮叮当当响，陶器碎了一地。
狼火表情一冷，阴森森的，“放下东西，掩藏！”
