The two tribes were neighbors; they could be trusted a little, but they also needed to be guarded against. Given the current relationship, it didn't matter if Lang Bing told Yu Le about some common herbs for minor ailments.

It just so happened that if the Black Feather beastmen were sensible, they would know to get along well with them instead of coveting things in secret.

As a priest of a tribe, he naturally hoped for the tribe to be well.

Lin Qiu: "As long as the priest knows what's going on."

...

The houses in the western forest were being built quickly; in just a few days, the walls had already been laid.

After finishing his work at the priest's cave, Lin Qiu went down the mountain and saw the beastmen holding a large pottery jar, splashing water on the walls. The livestock pen was next to the small river where they used to soak hemp grass, making it convenient to fetch and use water.

When working, the beastmen didn't like to wear those hemp clothes, only wrapping a tattered animal skin around their waists, leaving their upper bodies and long legs bare, very much in the style of a primitive tribe.

Once the walls were built, it was time to prepare for the roof beams and sealing.

Lin Qiu went in to look around; this house was built small, with only one small window and one door for entry and exit.

Building a brick house for the first time, the beastmen relied entirely on their own exploration. Their construction experience was limited to those few sheds.

Lin Qiu intended to let them practice first, fearing they would have to build more in the future.

Then again, having gone to such great lengths just for the red birds and bleat-beasts to survive the snowy season, Lin Qiu was a bit worried they wouldn't succeed in the end.

He vaguely sensed the beastmen's urgency for meat.

Eating too much fish didn't help them gain weight, and the prey caught by the hunting team was hit-or-miss; eating fish could only temporarily solve their hunger.

Lin Qiu racked his brains; in the current situation, this was the only way to obtain a stable source of meat.

Lin Qiu's brows knitted into a knot; if meat wasn't an option, then other food would have to do.

"Qiu!"

Hearing a beastman call from outside, Lin Qiu let out a soft breath, hiding all his worries.

He answered, and before he could go out, Lang Qi came in.

The middle-aged beastman had a serious face, a rolled-up piece of tree bark tucked under his arm, and a half-burnt wooden stick in his hand, an aura of an old pedant rushing toward him.

He was only missing a pair of round-framed glasses on his face.

"Qiu, hurry and see where to build the kang." He got straight to the point, with no intention of delaying at all.

Lin Qiu: "Against the inside, don't face the door."

The two of them discussed for a few sentences, determined the location for the kang, and drew a diagram with a charcoal pencil.

Lin Qiu said: "Uncle Qi, I'll have to trouble you with the window and door frames."

Lang Qi: "Alright."

The older generation was just that straightforward.

After looking around here, Lin Qiu thought of his own Wolf King. He searched for him on Wolf Mountain, looked up, and his gaze landed on the top of Wolf Mountain.

Looking down from the top of the mountain, everything was clear, but looking up didn't work.

Lin Qiu thought about what he wanted to do, his lips curled up, but he didn't go up to find him.

There was still some sunlight, so Lin Qiu simply went into the large cave, dismantled his and Lang Yan's nest, and took out the dry grass to sun it.

He didn't want his original grass nest anymore, just moved Lang Yan's nest further in.

Lin Qiu was busy, and other beastmen saw this and learned from him, dismantling their nests to sun them as well.

For a time, grass scraps flew in the cave, little bugs ran around, and it was a mess. Lang An came out of the weaving cave to rest for a while, and upon seeing this, he simply directed the beastmen to move all the nests and thoroughly clean the inside.

Every corner, including the cub nest area and the storage places, had everything moved out for cleaning.

Lin Qiu checked the animal skins inside, and they were all fine.

Lang An was just about to go to the priest's to get some insect repellent, and seeing this, he said: "Qiu, sun the animal skins too."

Lin Qiu said: "Alright."

With all this tossing, he didn't know if they could sleep in the cave tonight.

The big ones were busy, and the cubs also ran over to help. Lin Qiu handed the task of sunning the animal skins to them, and Lang Sheng patted his chest and promised: "Don't worry, Uncle Qiu, we will sun them until they smell fragrant."

Lin Qiu patted the cub's head and got a handful of stinky sweat.

Lin Qiu went into the cave to help clean; there was a lot of dust, and the wolf beastmen couldn't stop sneezing.

Lang Guo even carried the cubs out, not letting them go inside.

Lin Qiu simply used the hemp fabric scraps used for making clothes to make a few simple masks. The beastmen wore them over their mouths and noses, and now they felt slightly more comfortable.

The beastmen's grass nests weren't built once a year.

Under the grass nest were stones and wooden sticks; some single male beastmen weren't particular, and when the wood under the nest rotted and collapsed, they just added new wood on top. This repeated, and he didn't know how many years it hadn't been cleaned.

Lin Qiu took a look, and it was all wood shavings eaten by bugs.

Insect repellent was used a lot every year, but it wasn't used under the grass nest, and over time, it completely became a bug nest.

Seeing this, Lang An put his hands on his hips and scolded Lang Shi, who had come in to move the grass nests: "Look at how careless you are, the bottom of the grass nest is rotten and you still don't change it. With so many bugs, aren't you afraid of being itchy when you sleep at night!"

"One or two of you are so sloppy, and you still want to find a mate? Even in your dreams, no one would want you!"

Lang Shi was scolded so hard he didn't dare to move, his eyes innocent.

He had changed it...

"What are you still standing there for? Call a few more who are free to come and move them!"

Lang Shi stumbled and ran out immediately. He pulled over Lang Mu and the others, and unsurprisingly, they were pointed at and scolded by Lang An again.

If the priest worried about the health of the beastmen, and the Wolf King worried about the food and safety of the beastmen, then Lang An often stayed on Wolf Mountain, equivalent to the housekeeper of Wolf Mountain.

He asked about everything in the home, and the beastmen dared not disobey.

Lang Mu and the others were scolded until their ears buzzed, as if bugs had crawled into them.

A few wolf beastmen looked at Lang Shi with resentment, but Lang Shi pretended not to see and did whatever he was told.

Lang An: "What are you standing there for! Move quickly! If you don't shovel out all this dust, are you keeping it to put in the meat soup?!"

It was the first time Lin Qiu had seen Lang An get angry, so he stayed far away from him.

Seeing the beastmen as obedient as quails, he couldn't help but curl his lips, not feeling that this matter had anything to do with him at all.

He was just sunning his own grass nest, he didn't do anything.

Look at how clean it was under their King's grass nest; what did that have to do with him?

Wolf Mountain was noisy all afternoon, and Lang Yan heard it all from the mountain top.

He twitched his ears, watching Lin Qiu come out, his face covered with a piece of hemp cloth, his clear eyes faintly smiling, clearly gloating.

Watching those little cubs running and jumping on the animal skins, all dirty, making it so the animal skins wouldn't be good to use in the winter.

He got up and went down to help.

In the cave, there was a whole basket of wood shavings just from cleaning, and there were little bugs crawling inside. Lin Qiu felt itchy all over just looking at it.

Seeing Lang Yan come down, he hurriedly pulled him away.

"It's a mess, don't go in yet."

"Helping."

"It's almost done, you don't need to."

After Lin Qiu finished speaking, seeing the cubs looking over, he rewarded them with a pocket of fruit one by one and told them to go play.

Lang Yan followed Lin Qiu to spread the animal skins flat again and carefully counted them; there were about 140 animal skins in total.

There were many from bleat-beasts, and they looked a bit newer. There were also a few types Lin Qiu hadn't seen before.

Most of the animal skins were very large, enough to cover from head to toe, about the same size as the one in Lin Qiu's grass nest.

Lin Qiu thought of the snowy season and asked: "Are these enough?"

There were over a hundred beastmen in the tribe; if everyone had one, the remainder wouldn't be distributed evenly.

Lang Yan said: "If we squeeze, it's enough."

Lin Qiu: "Were these all saved up from the past?"

Lang Yan: "Mm. Saved for a long time."

Originally, when there was plenty of prey, the tanning of animal skins had good and bad, and if they were bad, the beastmen would just throw them away.

Later, it wasn't possible; there was little prey, and few animal skins.

Gradually, the beastmen began to figure out how to improve their craftsmanship, and they tried their best to keep every animal skin.

As he spoke, his gray eyes were a bit gloomy.

It was a pity that those old beastmen with the best craftsmanship had died in the long hunger.

"King..." Lin Qiu hugged his waist tightly and looked up at him.

Lang Yan: "I also want to thank Qiu."

Lin Qiu: "What are you thanking me with?"

Seeing that he was really asking, Lang Yan lost his sadness and began to think carefully.

Lin Qiu smiled, stood on tiptoe, and quickly kissed his chin, "I have something I want."

"What?"

"You."

Lang Yan laughed, hugged his mate, and lowered his head...

"Aww!!!" A group of little cubs who had just run away stood on the side like bamboo shoots, their hands covering their eyes, their mouths grinning to their ears.

Lin Qiu was embarrassed, but his movements were domineering.

He hooked his arms around Lang Yan's neck, pressed his face against his, and said to the group of cubs: "What are you 'aww-ing' about? My mate, can't I kiss him?"

Lang Yan was helpless, seeing him being serious with the cubs, and fearing he would be tired from standing on tiptoe, he supported his back and said to Lang Sheng: "Has Lang Jin come back yet?"

The cubs shook their heads obediently.

Lin Qiu let go of his hand, leaned against Lang Yan, and hummed triumphantly.

Childish!

The cubs quietly stuck their tongues out at him.

Lang Yan: "When they come back, tell them to take you to catch red birds. You're big enough, it's time to start learning to hunt."

The cubs weren't unhappy; instead, they all puffed out their chests.

"Understood, King! We will definitely learn well!"

The cubs ran away, and Lin Qiu's feet were tired too.

He loosened his hands, rested them on Lang Yan's chest, and relied on the arm around his waist to support his body.

He looked at those little radishes, with their short legs, "Can you let them go into the forest?"

Lang Yan: "Nearby is not afraid, it's time to learn."

Lin Qiu didn't think it was inappropriate; look at Lang Xue—the biggest little white wolf in this litter had been following the priest to learn about herbs for a long time.

Seeing that he wasn't deliberately making things difficult for the cubs for his own sake, Lin Qiu curved his eyes.

Their King was so fair.

"Right!" Lin Qiu let go of Lang Yan, grabbed his hand and said, "I thought of another kind of food."

"What?"

"Lotus roots." There were so many lakes and marshes in the south, and wild lotus roots were everywhere. If they dug them out, wouldn't there be another kind of food for the snowy season?

And eating lotus roots at this time was just right; they were definitely softer and waxier than when they dug them before, and also larger.

Lang Yan: "I'll arrange it."

Lin Qiu: "Digging lotus roots isn't easy; it's hard for beastmen to cross that swamp..." As he spoke, his eyes lit up and fell on the group of Black Feather beastmen who were still working in front of Wolf Mountain.

The Black Feather beastmen felt a chill down their backs.

Lang Yan looked over and said: "It's feasible."
chapters.title: 第107章

chapters.translated_text:
Night fell, and Langshan, which had been bustling all afternoon, fell silent.

All the orcs in the large cave had their grass nests relaid. Enduring Lang An’s chilly gaze, they hunched their bodies and obediently shuffled inside.

The hay in the fresh nests had been drying all afternoon. The rotten wood beneath the nests had been used as firewood and replaced with new logs, so it wouldn't feel lumpy while sleeping like before.

A wolf-orc rolled around happily, but caught a glimpse of Lang An still standing at the cave entrance with his claws raised, and froze.

Lang An let out a "humph."

The wolf-orc immediately lay down properly.

Lang An: "If I catch you being this sloppy again, go roll to another cave to sleep!"

He wondered why the bugs in the cave were endless; it was all because of this bunch of lazy bums.

The orcs pressed their ears against their heads, not daring to disobey.

*

Lang Yan made a quick decision regarding the lotus root digging and told Yu Shan about it that evening while eating meat soup.

Yu Shan agreed as well.

However, they had to leave a bit quickly; they would be departing tomorrow.

Yu Shan told his tribesmen, and Yu Qian panicked, grabbing his partner's hand and asking, "Then what about the matter of exchanging for tail-grass? Did you mention it?"

Yu Shan: "Not yet."

Yu Ya: "Uncle A-Shan, are you afraid? If so, let me go say it."

This young orc was just reckless. An adult orc next to him hooked his neck and said, "Save some energy and don't cause trouble."

Yu Le sat inside, hugging his knees with both hands, his chin resting on his arms, watching the orcs discuss things quietly and obediently.

Between the end of the rainy season and the beginning of the snowy season lies a long, mild season when fruits ripen. Orcs usually wait until halfway through this period before slowly starting to store food for the snowy season.

Firstly, if they stored it too early, it would spoil before the snowy season arrived, which would be a waste.

Secondly, the food the orcs hunted daily was barely enough to eat. The snowy season was hard to endure, so they had to eat as much as possible and hoard a little meat to survive the bitter cold.

Right now, the ripening season should be just over halfway through. The Black Feather orcs watched as the wolf-orcs harvested tail-grass, dried fish, and even various dried vegetables they had dried during the rainy season... The cave where the wolf-orcs stored their food was likely full, but they didn't know the situation at their own tribe.

The Black Feather tribe had fewer orcs than Langshan, and the snowy season was the time when they needed orcs the most to store food, so everyone was naturally anxious.

Yu Le's thoughts raced. He gripped his knees tightly, gathered his courage, and thought: What if he went to say it...

But as soon as he imagined the scene, he felt terrified, curled himself up, and wanted to hide immediately.

After a long while...

"Uncle A-Shan, are we exchanging for seeds?"

The voice was very small. It was only because no one was talking at that moment that everyone heard it. Turning their heads, they saw it was Yu Le speaking.

A flash of surprise appeared in everyone's eyes.

In the past, this young orc would avoid speaking whenever possible, wishing he could dig a hole to hide himself in.

Yu Qian, however, was delighted.

It was indeed the right decision to bring the young orc along; at the very least, he dared to take the initiative to speak now.

He said gently to the young orc, "It would be best if we could exchange for seeds."

Yu Le lowered his head. After a while, just when the orcs thought he wouldn't speak again, he added cautiously, "But Uncle A-Shan, Lang Bing said their tail-grass has been cultivated for many, many years, and even the branch tribe doesn't have any..."

Hearing this, Yu Shan's brow twitched.

"Even the branch tribe doesn't have any?"

Everyone looked over, and Yu Le was so scared he curled himself up tighter. He said softly, "That's what A-Bing said. It was only because this year's tail-grass harvest was a little bit better than previous years that they sent some over."

Seeing the timidity in the young orc's eyes, Yu Qian felt a pang of heartache. He went over, hugged him, and patted his head.

"Thanks to Yu Le, this information is very important."

Yu Le buried his head on Yu Qian's shoulder, his eyelashes trembling non-stop, and he let out an "Mm."

The orcs fell silent.

Yu Qian sighed inwardly, knowing that the matter of exchanging for seeds was likely not going to happen.

Feeling the young orc in his arms tense up, Yu Qian stroked his back to comfort him: "Don't be afraid. Everyone is discussing things together; in the future, Yu Le can say whatever he wants to say."

Yu Ya, sitting nearby, curled his lip when he saw this.

He couldn't even speak properly; he was so stupid.

*

The large cave.

In the grass nest, Lin Qiu rested his head on Lang Yan's arm, his feet stepping on Lang Yan's instep, his thoughts drifting far away.

The Great Marsh was vast. It would be best if the Black Feather orcs, who could fly, crossed the marsh to get near the wild lotus roots. They could also bring the wolf-orcs in to dig, then have them transport the roots to the shore, and finally send them to Langshan.

Lin Qiu stepped on Lang Yan's instep, "King, are our orcs going to the Great Marsh?"

Lang Yan: "Yes."

Lin Qiu looked up, his cheeks very close to Lang Yan's. "I want to go too."

"To dig lotus roots?"

Lin Qiu's eyes brightened, "Yes, there are loaches and swamp eels in the mud; we can catch some meat to eat."

Lang Yan: "And big long snakes."

Lin Qiu shuddered, immediately thinking of the python the wolf-orcs had caught near the Great Marsh. He stomped hard on Lang Yan's instep, "Don't mention it."

Lang Yan pressed his chin against Lin Qiu's soft hair and curled his lips, "Still want to go?"

Lin Qiu frowned, "If that's the case... there should be a lot of them in the Great Marsh. What if they are poisonous and the orcs get bitten?"

Lang Yan: "Bring insect repellent, and bring more antidotes."

Lin Qiu still wanted to go dig for lotus roots.

It was about time to start preparing food for the snowy season. There were many snakes in the Great Marsh, so they might as well have the orcs catch more, dry them into jerky, which was faster than hunting other four-legged prey.

Thoughts by day, dreams by night.

Lin Qiu dreamed all night that he was rolling in a mud pit, holding a huge, fat wild lotus root while being chased by a python. He couldn't bear to throw it away, and he woke up in a cold sweat.

When he opened his eyes, it was rarely still dark.

There was a little sweat on his forehead. Lin Qiu stared at the water stains on the cave ceiling, still feeling a lingering fear.

Lang Yan woke up as soon as he felt the slight movement.

The breathing by his ear sounded a bit off. Lang Yan cradled Lin Qiu's face to look at him, wiped the sweat from his forehead, and pulled him closer into his arms, "Had a nightmare?"

Lin Qiu buried his face in the crook of his neck, "Chased by a big snake."

Lang Yan: "Then we won't go."

Lin Qiu shook his head, only squeezing tighter into his arms.

Breakfast was porridge made from tail-grass. The golden grains were thrown into a pottery pot with a full pot of water, and cooked until the rice paste was thick; then it was ready to eat.

Ever since Lin Qiu taught the orcs to make fish traps to catch fish, for the first time in so long, they didn't have fish for breakfast.

The rice porridge had no meaty flavor at all, just some yam cut into it.

Half a bowl per orc.

The orcs ate from basins, so half a bowl was quite a lot.

Lang Mo and Lang Xi held their portions, placed them on the table, sat on small stools with their legs spread wide, and impatiently pursed their lips to slurp from the edge of the bowl.

As soon as their lips touched it, they pulled away quickly, afraid of being burned.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan sat opposite them and asked, "How is it?"

Lang Mo licked his lips, "A bit..."

Lang Xi: "Grassy."

"Grassy?" Lin Qiu thought for a while before he understood what the orcs meant. "Too plain?"

Without meat, it was only natural for it to be plain.

The porridge in the bowl was still bubbling when it was served, steaming hot. Lin Qiu stirred it slowly, watching the two orcs in front of him grimacing as they drank the porridge.

"How did you eat tail-grass before?"

Lang Mo's mouth was burned red, and he said with a thick tongue, "There wasn't this much before; we just roasted it and ate it dry."

Lang Xi added, "Two handfuls per orc a day, enough to last half a snowy season."

Two handfuls, eaten dry—what good could that do?

Mixed with some wild fruits and wild vegetables, it was at most enough to not starve to death.

Anyway, after every past snowy season, every orc that came out of the cave was skin and bones, looking no different from the dead.

Lang Mo slurped a big mouthful of porridge, burning his mouth so much he moved it from left to right, but he couldn't bear to spit it out.

Lin Qiu: "It's too hot and will hurt your throat. You won't be able to eat anything good in the future."

As soon as he said that, Lang Mo gulped and swallowed it straight down.

He was burned so badly he jumped, knocked over his stool, and ran to the stove like his butt was on fire, grabbing a fruit-shell ladle to scoop water and pour it into his mouth.

Lang Yan frowned, "If you don't know how to eat, then don't eat."

He was such a big orc, yet he acted like a cub.

Lang Xi lowered his head, silently held his bowl tighter, and slowed down his pace a little.

The tail-grass seeds boiled with water didn't scatter around the mouth like when eaten dry; the texture was soft and glutinous, with a hint of sweetness. The rice porridge retained the most simple flavor of food, and the yam was soft and mushy. One mouthful gave a thick sense of fullness.

This taste was what sub-orcs and cubs liked.

The male orcs also held their bowls carefully, blowing on them, and slurping them into their mouths bit by bit.

This was something they had grown themselves.

From selecting seeds to raising seedlings, they guarded those weak little sprouts just like they guarded their cubs. They pulled weeds, thinned the seedlings, transplanted them, fertilized them, watered them, and finally harvested them, removing the husks bit by bit, until it became what it was now.

Thinking of this, the orcs were all dazed.

They remembered how many seeds the priest had taken out at the beginning—just that one bag made of animal skin. But that one bag, after the rainy season and before the snowy season, had turned into dozens of bags...

The orcs were trembling with excitement. They hurriedly looked at the old priest, who was drinking porridge while clutching his beard, and asked, "Priest, let's eat a little less. If we plant dozens of bags next year, won't we never have to go hungry again?"

The old priest calmly put down his beard, smoothed it out, and said in a flat tone, "Aren't you afraid of being worked to death?"

"We aren't afraid of being tired."

They were more afraid of hunger—very afraid.

When they were hungriest, the orcs would tighten their stomachs with animal skin strips. Some couldn't take it and would jump off the mountain...

They weren't afraid of being tired; they were afraid of having no food to eat.

At this moment, truly holding this bowl of porridge and looking at the tail-grass seeds piled up in the cave, the orcs realized how great the effect of what Lin Qiu had asked them to do was.

The orcs' hands were trembling slightly.

In the past, they had done the same planting and the same harvesting, but what they got in return was only a little bit more than the seeds they had planted.

There weren't even many plump ears that could be selected as seeds.

Therefore, even the priest was cautious, not daring to distribute the few seeds to the branch tribe, fearing that they would be even worse at planting and would waste the seeds.

How could the old priest not understand what the orcs were thinking?

He said irritably, "Eat. Enough seeds have been saved. Don't complain about being tired when you plant next year."

What the orcs could think of, the old priest could naturally think of as well.

He not only saved enough seeds for next year, but he saved five times the amount of this year's seeds.

Even if the branch tribe came back, they would have to be put to work in the fields.

They were afraid of not having enough to eat, but the old priest was only more afraid than they were. What he was thinking about was the livelihood of the two tribes. If the branch tribe didn't manage to grow anything, he would have to send some over from here.

This was the disadvantage of having a branch tribe. As a priest, he was only one person, and he was old; he couldn't look after this side and that side at the same time.

But he couldn't give up on either side...

He might as well be worked to death.

The wolf-orcs could eat porridge made from tail-grass seeds, so the Black Feather orcs naturally had to have a share.

Compared to the wolf-orcs' habits, the Black Feather orcs felt as if they had eaten something that touched their hearts upon their first taste of this porridge.

The rice grains were fine and soft, and the taste was fragrant, which was very much to the Black Feather orcs' liking.

Most of this year's tail-grass had been husked by them. Now that they were eating it for the first time, and thinking that the jar full of rice porridge only contained one ladle of grass seeds, the Black Feather orcs found it even harder to sit still.

"A-Shan."

"Uncle A-Shan..."

They had thought about it for a long time last night. It was definitely impossible to shamelessly ask for tail-grass seeds, but what if they only exchanged for some edible tail-grass?

They wouldn't take it to plant, just to eat. They wondered if that would work.

Yu Shan held his pottery bowl, the steam filling the air, blurring his slightly weathered brows and eyes.

Tail-grass was precious. If they exchanged for it, it would likely take longer than the labor time for the pottery and fishnets.

Yu Shan wasn't afraid of coming to work for the Wolf tribe again; he was just worried about not being able to look after his own tribe.

They couldn't always rely on exchanges to get food and stay in the Wolf tribe without leaving.

He had come here several times and understood that Langshan could eat their fill now because the whole tribe was working together. But the Black Feather tribe? The orcs were not united, and they were all old, weak, sick, or disabled. Who would rack their brains to think of ways to increase food?

If he wasn't there, and with the old chief in that condition, the orcs were probably still busy fighting to be the chief...

As Yu Shan's partner, Yu Qian knew what he was thinking.

He placed his hand on the back of Yu Shan's hand and squeezed it tightly.

"A-Shan, nothing is more important than food." Only with food could they survive the snowy season and have a future.

Yu Shan's gaze fell on the group of wolf-orcs under the shed through the hazy steam. They were visibly stronger and more energetic than his own tribesmen, and there was hope in their eyes.

Their snowy season would definitely not be as hard to endure as before.

Yu Shan finally nodded, though his voice sounded a bit weary.

"Alright, I'll go ask."

*

"You want tail-grass?"

Just after washing the bowls, Lang Yan was stopped by Yu Shan. The orc seemed a bit hesitant, and after brewing for a while, he finally stated his purpose.

Yu Shan said: "Yes, we want to exchange for tail-grass."

These words were difficult to say, as if his mouth was glued shut, and he had to summon all his strength to speak.

Yu Shan knew that exchanging labor for things was a transaction between two tribes and was fair; they shouldn't feel guilty.

But in the current Orc God Continent, one could imagine how precious food was. Even if you did a lot of work in your own tribe, the Orc God wouldn't distribute food to you.

Again and again, Yu Shan's pride had been worn away.

Seeing the middle-aged orc lower his head while speaking, Lang Yan understood that they were forced to bow their heads for food.

But as things stood, apart from the lotus root digging, the tribe could do all the remaining work themselves.

Why should they feed twenty extra mouths?

Whose food came for free?

Lang Yan: "After the tail-grass was harvested, we sent quite a bit to the branch tribe. I'm afraid we can't spare any more."

Yu Shan looked up and smiled, the corners of his mouth lifted as if with great effort, but there was no smile in his eyes, only bitterness.

"...I know, we are being greedy."

Lang Yan: "The previous exchanges were voluntary; there is no such thing as greed."

Yu Shan suppressed his dejection and returned to the group of Black Feather orcs.

Everyone gathered around and asked in low voices: "What happened? Did they agree?"

"Can we exchange for a lot? We can work for as long as it takes."

"Yes, as long as it takes."

Yu Le pursed his lips into a straight line and looked at Yu Shan with worry.

He knew it hadn't worked.

"It didn't work."

As expected.

The tribesmen were still discussing in low voices, seemingly not having understood Yu Shan's words.

Yu Shan raised his voice: "It won't work. The Wolf King said they have already distributed a lot to the branch tribe, and what's left is barely enough for themselves."

The orcs were stunned.

The air was quiet for a moment, and then the orcs began to chatter again.

"We, we should have said something earlier."

"I said we should ask earlier, but Shan, you kept saying 'wait a bit, wait a bit.' Look now, you waited until they..."

Yu Qian took a deep breath, "Enough!"

The orcs fell silent.

Yu Qian: "Pack your things. We're going to the Great Marsh soon."

The orcs were dejected and didn't make another sound.

Previously, the Wolf tribe had readily agreed to exchange pottery with them, so they had taken it for granted that this time would also work. The Wolf King looked fierce, but he was easy to talk to.

But who would have thought he wouldn't give them anything at all.

Among the twenty orcs, most felt disappointed after knowing the result, but there were a few who felt resentment.

They lowered their heads, almost breaking the chopsticks in their hands, their voices barely audible.

"Maybe they just want us to beg them. It's not like they have that much food..."

"Not necessarily. They must think we're losing out by exchanging labor. Maybe they're eyeing something else."

Yu Qian was sensitive and told Yu Shan about it afterward.

Yu Shan didn't dare to wallow in the sorrow of not being able to exchange for tail-grass anymore; he directly grabbed a few orcs into the sleeping cave and gave them a stern warning.

If they caused trouble in the Wolf tribe, they could forget about ever wanting to exchange for anything from the Wolf tribe again.

It was fine for a few orcs to complain about him, but if they dared to ruin the relationship between the two tribes, even killing them wouldn't be enough to atone for their sins!

Yu Shan had a premonition that to be full, they had to follow the Wolf tribe's lead.

*

The orcs going to the Great Marsh were still the same group as Lang Huo's, and they were already familiar with what to bring.

Lang Huo hitched up the wooden cart, packed the tools needed for eating, called Lang Yu and Lang Hong, the two sub-orcs responsible for cooking, and set off for the Great Marsh.

The Black Feather orcs ran for a distance and then flew with their wings.

The Black Feather orcs had eaten a lot of food at Langshan, and these twenty orcs were not weak at all like before. They were energetic; the wolf-orcs arrived at the Great Marsh in the morning, and they arrived at the same time, even having the energy to lay out their nests.

This time, Lin Qiu and Lang Yan came together.

Lin Qiu intended to train his running speed and endurance. He would run for a while, and when he really couldn't run anymore, he would ask Lang Yan to carry him to catch up with the main force.

After resting enough on Lang Yan's back, Lin Qiu would get down and continue running.

The orc world was not peaceful; one couldn't lose the ability to save one's own life.

The two of them arrived a little later than the main force. When they walked out of the forest, the Black Feather orcs had already set up their nests, Lang Huo had led the orcs to catch fish, and Lang Yu and Lang Hong had set up the pottery pot, just waiting for the ingredients to be added.

Lang Huo heard the movement and glanced toward the shore.

The orcs were standing in the shallow water in linen shorts, catching fish in their hands, the sunlight falling into the water, shimmering.

Lang Huo grinned, his hair, tied up messily with an animal skin strip, showing a dark red luster, full of vitality: "Qiu, why are your legs shaking?"

Lin Qiu ignored him, grabbed Lang Yan's fur, slid off his back, and sat down on the grass with a thud.

Lang Yan glanced at Lang Huo.

The orc shut his mouth and stared at the big fish.

Anyone who didn't know would think he was counting how many scales the fish had.

Lin Qiu spread his limbs, having no strength left at all.

"I've been less active lately and haven't been running outside much."

Lang Yan lay down beside him, flicked his tail, and wrapped it around Lin Qiu's side.

Orcs passing by nearby saw this and immediately took a wide detour.

Orcs with partners were all the same—they were protective of their food.

Lin Qiu didn't notice; he just had no strength left and lay on Lang Yan's back. The wolf fur was thick, and Lang Yan had gained some weight, so lying on him was like lying on a mattress that was just the right firmness, and it had even more support.

He moved his hands to Lang Yan's forehead and shook it, and a few strands of wolf fur flew up.

"King, you're shedding again..."

Lang Yan: "It's almost the snowy season; it's time to change fur."

Lin Qiu smiled: "Just in time to make another fur jacket."

Lang Yan: "Alright."

Any orc would be happy if their partner was willing to wear clothes made of their fur and be stained with their scent.

The Great Marsh was vast, and the wind had nothing to block it, rushing around wantonly.

Not far from the shed where the orcs were staying, the wild grass that had been harvested before had already grown back. The leaves of the wild grass were faintly yellow, swaying in the wind, with waves of grass rolling.

Lin Qiu rested his hands on Lang Yan's head.

Seeing those fluffy big ears twitch twice, he suddenly grabbed them with both hands.

Lang Yan's tail tightened suddenly, and Lin Qiu's leg felt as if it had been bound by a hemp rope.

Lin Qiu pinched his ears tightly and wouldn't let go; the soft, bouncy feel was so comfortable. He rested his chin on Lang Yan's forehead, turned his head, and followed his gaze to the patch of wild grass.

"King, what are you looking at?"

Lang Yan tried to move his ears but felt his partner pinching them as if playing a prank.

A flash of helplessness crossed Lang Yan's eyes: "Nothing."

Lin Qiu pulled his hands away a little and looked at the furry ears. He supported himself on Lang Yan's back with his palms, moved closer and closer, and breathed onto those ears.

As if on purpose, he exhaled heavily.

Lang Yan turned over, pulled him directly into his chest, and pressed him tightly.

Lin Qiu ended up lying on his back, smiling at Lang Yan.

"King, ears aren't meant to be touched..."

Seeing the orcs nearby sneaking glances, Lang Yan leaned down, and the long fur around his neck directly buried Lin Qiu.

Lang Yan's ears twitched, and he heard the playful laughter coming from under the fur.

"They can be touched."

Lin Qiu buried his head in the wolf fur, like burrowing into a haystack, and messed up his own hair too.

The circle of orcs by the water looked as if they had eaten a dozen green fruits in a row, feeling both sour and uncomfortable. Lang Shun muttered: "Huo, when do you think we'll be able to find a partner?"

Lang Huo: "Go ask the King."

He was sour too.

There were few sub-orcs of age in the tribe to begin with, and even if you added the branch tribe together, there were at most twenty sub-orcs and female orcs who hadn't found partners.

If they wanted to find one, it would be faster to dream.

Lang Shun flicked his hand, and the fish that was almost caught in the net fell into the water and ran away.

Lang Huo: "Lang Shun! If you can't do it, don't do it!"

Lang Shun: "I, I... don't be fierce, the net was loose."

"It wouldn't be loose if you didn't flick your hand!"

"Don't be so hot-tempered."

"My name is Lang Huo, how can I not be hot-tempered!"

*

They had porridge made from tail-grass seeds in the morning, and back to fish at noon. Not just the wolf-orcs, but the Black Feather orcs also felt a bit uncomfortable.

Barely filling their stomachs, the orcs lay in the shed, smacking their lips, trying to taste a hint of tail-grass seed flavor from the mouthful of fish.

After trying for a while, the orcs were disheartened.

Sighs kept coming from under the shed where the Black Feather orcs were sleeping.

Thinking of Yu Shan's failed exchange with the Wolf King this morning, they felt as if their hearts were being stirred by a stick, making them feel even worse.

Yu Shan: "Stop sighing, get some sleep, or you won't have the strength later."

After resting at noon, they prepared to go into the water.

Lotus roots were easy to identify. They didn't know how many years they had been growing in the Great Marsh; even if there was only one cluster of lotus roots at the beginning, they could now cover the whole area.

Almost all the shallow muddy bottoms were covered with this stuff.

The orcs were going into the Great Marsh for the first time, and fearing they would sink in, they had specially brought wooden boards.

The Black Feather orcs took the lead, bringing the wooden boards down first. Then they came back to bring the wolf-orcs over.

Lin Qiu, covered in the smell of insect repellent, lay on Yu Qian's back, bypassed the marshes, and was carried to the middle of the Great Marsh.

He sat on a thin wooden board and saw that Lang Huo had already left the board and was slowly descending into the mud.

The clear water bubbled up with mud bubbles, making a gurgling sound. A smell of mud wafted out, and Lang Huo said: "Hold the rope tight! Don't let go!"

Lang Shun leaned his body on the wooden board, staring at him, "I'm holding it, I'm holding it!"

The other orcs didn't move; Lang Huo was the first to go down and try.

Just in case, two orcs stayed on the wooden board, each holding a rope tied to his waist. A Black Feather orc was also flying in the sky, with a rope tied to his claws as well.

Most of the orcs hadn't come over yet; they all held their breath, looking at this side from afar.

Lang Yan stood next to Lin Qiu, watching intently.

They had chosen a shallow water area, but the water still slowly submerged Lang Huo's thighs, his waist, until it reached his chest.

Seeing this, Lang Yan's face became slightly stern, "Pull."

Lang Huo grabbed the rope in a hurry, "King! Wait a minute! It seems it won't sink anymore!"

The orcs tensed their arm muscles, watching under the water.

Lin Qiu had measured with a wooden stick that the water here was shallow. From the surface of the mud to the surface of the water, the deepest part could reach the orcs' waists.

The orcs were all tall and big, and their upper bodies were still high enough. If they didn't get close to the deep parts, there shouldn't be a big problem.

Lang Yan: "Where is the mud?"

Lang Huo moved and found he couldn't pull his feet out, "Up to my thighs."

"Is it solid?"

Lang Huo nodded, "The mud underneath isn't as soft as the top."

"Try a few more steps."

Lin Qiu: "Lift your feet slowly. The more anxious you are, the harder it is to pull them out."

In front of all the orcs, Lang Huo walked a few more steps, guided by the three ropes on his waist. Lang Huo walked from the edge of the lotus leaf cluster to the middle and back again. He pushed aside the disc-like lotus leaves, grabbed two or three withered lotus seed pods, and brought out a burst of fragrance.

"King! It's fine!" After reporting the situation, he raised the lotus seed pod in his hand and asked, "Qiu, can this be eaten?"

Lin Qiu: "It can be eaten, but the one in your hand seems to be rotten."

Lang Huo was about to walk out of the lotus cluster when he suddenly stopped in his tracks and said "Eh."

Lang Yan immediately looked around vigilantly, but Lang Huo bent down and started searching in the water. The water wet his shoulders and neck, and he had to lift his chin so he wouldn't drink the muddy water.

Lin Qiu frowned, "What did you step on?"

Lang Huo: "Wait!"

He grabbed something and tried to pull it up, and the water surface rippled along with it. He pulled for a while but couldn't move it, so the orc gritted his teeth and pulled it up violently.

With a splash, black muddy water splattered everywhere.

Lang Huo fell into the water with a thud.

He scrambled up, shook his hands in the water, and looked at the white, tender lotus root joint, his gaze dazed.

Realizing what it was, he held the lotus root high, his face full of surprise.

"There is!"

The lotus root was complete and half a body long.

Lin Qiu stared at it closely and found that this wild lotus root was about the same size as the lotus roots he had seen.

One section was actually as long as a forearm!

Lin Qiu muttered: "We've hit the jackpot..."

He had originally thought that the quality of the wild lotus roots would be uneven, and it would be good enough to dig out some, but he didn't know they could grow this fat!

Lang Yan: "What?"

Lin Qiu grabbed Lang Yan's hand, "King! Dig, the more the better!"

Lotus roots grew in the mud and were the hardest to dig. Now that it was getting colder every day, they had to hurry.

If Lin Qiu's previous suggestion to dig for wild lotus roots was just to add a little vegetable to the tribe, the lotus roots they were digging now could definitely be eaten as a meal.

The output of one acre of lotus root field was about two thousand catties. In this Great Marsh, the lotus leaves, deep and shallow, were endless.

Lin Qiu hadn't found many when he came before the rainy season; the lotus roots were just growing leaves then, so it was normal not to find them. Looking at it now, the lotus leaves were dense and thick; there was enough for the orcs to eat for years.

They could also make lotus root starch, which not only used up the lotus roots but could also be stored for a long time.

Lin Qiu was excited and forgot to let go of Lang Yan for a while.

Lang Yan covered his hand and said to the Black Feather orcs in mid-air: "You can bring them down now."

Yu Shan in the sky nodded and whistled. The Black Feather orcs waiting on the shore began to bring the wolf-orcs closer one by one.

The orcs landed and were about to ask what had just happened when they saw that only Lang Huo's head was left above water.

His body was tilted in the water, like a rice seedling thrown directly into a paddy field, or as if he was entangled by something. The orcs panicked and rushed toward him.

"Huo, is it a long snake!"

Lang Yan glanced over and said: "He's fine, dig for lotus roots."

Lin Qiu reminded: "Try not to break them. Reach your hands into the mud, and once you grab a lotus root joint, slowly dig away the mud along it. It's best to bring the whole thing out. Otherwise, it's hard to clean the mud out of the holes."

Hearing this, the orcs stopped running.

They realized belatedly that they were already stepping in the mud, so they hurriedly plucked a few lotus leaves, crushed them, waited nervously for their feet to step firmly, and listened to Lin Qiu's words, clumsily reaching their hands into the mud.

This work was like digging for clay by the river, but the important thing wasn't to dig up the mud, but to find the things hidden inside.

It was dirty in there, and there were really those white, clean things...

"I found one!" an orc said in surprise.

"I have one here too!"

"Dig!" Lang Huo pulled out another one, shook it in the water, slapped it hard, and laughed loudly, "We've lived here for so many years, and this is the first time we've known that the Great Marsh hides such good treasures!"

Lin Qiu: "Be careful not to splash mud into your mouth."

Lin Qiu was supporting himself on Lang Yan's arm to go into the water. He wasn't afraid of snakes anymore; with so many orcs here and such a big commotion, any snakes would have run away long ago.

Yu Ya glanced at this side, moved to Yu Shan's side, and grabbed a leaf to block in front of him.

"Uncle A-Shan, does our tribe have this?"

Yu Shan had traveled all over the Black Feather tribe's territory. He recalled it for a while, sighed, and shook his head.

There were lakes, but they were deep lakes, and this stuff couldn't grow there.

Yu Ya said sourly: "How come all the good things grow in their tribe..."
chapters.title: 第108章
chapters.source_text:
入夜了，热闹一下午的狼山沉寂下来。
大山洞里所有兽人的草窝重新铺好，兽人们顶着狼安冷飕飕的眼神，缩着身体，乖乖往里面挪。
新鲜草窝里的干草晒了一下午，草窝底下腐朽的木头都当了柴火，又重新用木头铺好，一点不会像以前一样硌着睡觉。
狼兽人美滋滋打个滚儿，瞥见还在洞口站着的狼安，举着爪僵硬。
狼安“哼”了声。
狼兽人立马规规矩矩躺好。
狼安：“再叫我发现你们这么邋遢，以后滚别的山洞睡去！”
他说怎么洞里的虫子杀不尽似的，全赖着群懒货。
兽人耳朵扣在脑门上，哪敢不听。
*
挖藕的事，狼岩很快做了决定，当天晚上吃肉汤的时候跟羽山说了。
羽山也答应下来。
不过离开得有点快，明日就要走。
羽山将这事儿告诉族人，羽千一慌，抓着伴侣手道：“那交换尾巴草的事，你说没有？”
羽山：“还没有。”
羽涯：“阿山叔，你是不是怕啊，要不然我去说。”
这小兽人就是莽，旁边成年兽人勾住他脖子道：“你省点心吧，别捣乱。”
羽乐坐在里面，双手抱膝，下巴落在胳膊上，乖巧安静地看着兽人们商讨。
雨季结束到雪季开始，中间是漫长温和的果子成熟季。兽人通常会在这段时间过半后，才慢慢开始储藏雪季的食物。
一来要是存早了，还没到雪季就坏掉，浪费。
二来，兽人每日打猎的食物都不够吃，雪季难熬，怎么都要先让自己尽量多吃，囤一点肉，才能撑过严寒。
这会儿成熟季应该刚刚过一半，黑羽兽人眼睁睁看着狼兽人一下收割了尾巴草，晒了鱼干，有些甚至还是雨季晒的各类菜干……狼兽人储物的山洞怕是放满了，可他们部落那边不知情况。
黑羽部落兽人本就比狼山少些，每年雪季储存食物又是最需要兽人的时候，大家自然着急。
羽乐心思百转，手指紧扣住膝盖，鼓起勇气想：要不他去说……
可一想到这种情景，立马害怕似的，团着自己，想立刻藏起来。
许久……
“阿山叔，我们是换种子吗？”
这声儿很小，得亏这会儿没兽人说话，大家才听见。侧头一看，原来是羽乐在说话。
大家眼中讶异一闪。
以往这小兽人可是能不说话就不说，恨不能挖个洞把自己藏起来。
羽千却欣喜。
果然带小兽人来没错，至少，他敢主动开口了。
他冲着小兽人温和道：“能换种子最好。”
羽乐低下头，过了会儿，兽人们以为他不会说话时，他又小心翼翼道：“可是阿山叔，狼冰说他们的尾巴草培育了好多好多年，连支部落都没有……”
闻言，羽山眉心跳了下。
“支部落也没有？”
大伙儿都看过来，羽乐吓得将自己团得紧了紧。他轻轻道：“是阿冰说的。今年尾巴草的收成才比往年多一点点，他们才送过去。”
羽千见小兽人眼里带着怯意，心里一酸，过去将他搂住，摸摸他脑袋。
“多亏羽乐，这消息很重要。”
羽乐埋头搭在羽千肩膀，睫颤个不停，“嗯”了声。
兽人们沉默了。
羽千心中叹气，知道换种子的事多半不成。
感受着怀中小兽人的绷紧，羽千抚着他后背安抚道：“不用怕，大家都是一起商量事，以后羽乐想说什么也可以说。”
羽涯坐在旁边，看了撇撇嘴。
说个话都不敢，真笨。
*
大山洞。
草窝里，林楸枕在狼岩手臂，脚踩着他脚背，思绪飘到远处去。
大泽宽阔，黑羽兽人会飞，越过沼泽靠近野藕最好不过。还可以带狼兽人进去挖，再由他们运到岸边，最后送到狼山。
林楸脚下踩了踩狼岩脚背，“王，咱们的兽人去大泽吗？”
狼岩：“去。”
林楸仰头，脸颊与狼岩挨得极近，“我也想去。”
“挖藕？”
林楸眼睛发亮，“嗯，泥里还有泥鳅、黄鳝，能摸到些肉吃。”
狼岩：“还有大长虫。”
林楸一个激灵，顿时想到了之前狼兽人在大泽那边抓的蟒蛇。他狠踩了下狼岩脚背，“别提。”
狼岩下巴贴在他软发上，勾起唇角，“还去吗？”
林楸眉头皱起，“这样的话……大泽里面应该会有很多，万一有毒，兽人们被咬了怎么办？”
狼岩：“带驱虫药，再多带点解毒的。”
林楸还是想去摸藕。
差不多该开始准备雪季的食物，大泽长虫多，干脆叫兽人们多抓些，晒干做成肉干，比抓其他四个蹄子的猎物来得快点。
日有所思，夜有所梦。
林楸一晚上梦见自己在泥潭打滚儿，抱着一根硕大肥胖的野藕被蟒蛇追，他又舍不得扔了，吓得他出了一身冷汗。
睁开眼时，难得天还没亮。
他额头出了一点汗，林楸盯着洞顶的水痕，心有余悸。
狼岩感觉到一点动静就醒了。
耳边的呼吸有些不对劲，狼岩托着林楸的脸看了看，擦掉他额上的汗，将他往怀里拢了拢，“做噩梦了？”
林楸埋在他颈窝，“被大蛇追。”
狼岩：“要不然就不去。”
林楸摇头，只往他怀里挤。
早上喝的是尾巴草做的粥，金黄色的米粒儿扔陶锅里，加上满满一锅的水，煮得米浆粘稠，便可以吃了。
自从林楸教兽人们做了鱼笼捕鱼后，这么久了，终于有一早上没有吃鱼。
米粥里没有半点荤腥味道，只切了些山药进去。
一个兽人半碗。
兽人们用盆吃饭，半碗也不少。
狼莫、狼西捧着自己那份儿，往桌上一放，大马金刀坐在小凳上，迫不及待地撅着嘴巴往碗沿吸溜一口。
唇刚沾上一点，嘴撇开得飞快，生怕被烫了。
林楸跟狼岩坐他俩对面，见状，问：“怎么样？”
狼莫舔舔唇，“有点……”
狼西：“草。”
“草？”林楸想了一会儿才明白兽人的意思，“素了？”
没放肉，素也是应该。
碗里的粥盛出来时还在鼓泡泡，热气腾腾的，林楸慢慢搅拌，看着面前两兽人龇牙咧嘴地喝粥。
“你们以前怎么吃的尾巴草？”
狼莫嘴巴烫红了一圈，大着舌头道：“以前没这么多，烤一烤干吃。”
狼西补充道：“一天一个兽人两把，能吃半个雪季。”
两把，干吃，能顶什么用。
混着些野果、野菜吃，最多不饿死罢了。
反正以往雪季过后，哪个兽人出山洞不是形销骨立，看着跟死了没区别。
狼莫吸溜了一大口粥，烫得他左边倒右边，硬是舍不得吐出来。
林楸：“太烫伤到喉咙，以后有好吃的都吃不着。”
话落，狼莫咕噜一下，愣是直着脖子咽了下去。
他烫得跳脚，凳子叫他撞倒，火烧屁股似的飞快跑到灶边，抓着果壳瓢舀水就往嘴里灌。
狼岩蹙眉道：“不会吃就别吃。”
多大的兽人了，还跟幼崽一样。
狼西低下脑袋，默默捧紧了自己的碗，速度放慢一点点。
加水煮过的尾巴草籽不像干吃那样满口乱窜，口感软糯，有一点点的清甜。米粥保留着食物最朴素的味道，山药也软烂，一口下去浓浓的饱腹感。
这种味道是亚兽人跟幼崽喜欢的。
雄兽人也小心捧着碗，吹一吹，一点点往嘴里吸溜。
这是他们自己种出来的。
从选种，到育苗，他们跟守护幼崽一样守护着那弱小的苗苗。有了草就拔掉，还间苗，移栽，又施肥，浇水，最后再收割回来，一点一点去掉壳，最后变成现在这样。
这样一想，兽人们都恍惚。
他们记得当初祭司拿出来的种子有多少，就那个兽皮袋一袋。但那么一袋，经过雨季，到了雪季前，就变成了几十袋……
兽人惊颤，忙看向一旁抓着胡子喝粥的老祭司道：“祭司，咱们少吃点，明年种个几十袋，是不是就不用挨饿了？”
老祭司镇定地放下胡子，顺带捋一捋，语气淡淡：“也不怕累死。”
“我们不怕累。”
更怕饿，很怕。
最饿的时候，兽人用兽皮条勒紧肚子。有的受不了了，就从山上跳下去……
他们不怕累，怕没食物吃。
此刻真真切切捧着这一碗粥，看着山洞里堆满了的尾巴草籽，兽人才意识到，林楸叫他们做的事，作用多大。
兽人们手都有些哆嗦。
以往他们同样的种植，同样的收割，换来的，不过比下去的种子多那么一点点。
甚至能挑选出来的，能用来做种子的饱满穗子都不多。
是以，连祭司都小心翼翼，不敢将为数不多的种子分一些去支部落，怕的，就是他们更加不会种，浪费这种子。
老祭司怎么不懂兽人们想什么。
他没好气道：“吃吧，种子留够了的，明年种的时候你们不要喊累。”
兽人们能想到的，老祭司自然能想到。
他不仅足足地留下了明年的种子，还留得是今年种子的五倍。
就是支部落回来了，也得拉来种地。
他们怕吃不饱，老祭司只会比他们更怕。他心里想的是两个部落的生计，万一支部落那边没种成，还得这边送去。
这就是分部落的坏处了，他这个当祭司的只有一个，又一把年纪了，能顾到这边顾不到那边。
但哪一边又都不能放弃……
累死他算了。
狼兽人能吃尾巴草籽做的粥，黑羽兽人自然也得分一份。
比起狼兽人的习惯，黑羽兽人初尝一口这粥，仿佛吃到心坎儿上了。
米粒细软，味道清香，非常符合黑羽兽人的口味。
今年这尾巴草大多是他们脱壳的，如今头一遭吃到，想到那一罐子满满当当的米粥也不过放了一瓢的草籽，黑羽兽人更是难以静心坐下来。
“阿山。”
“阿山叔……”
他们昨晚想了许久，要尾巴草种子肯定是不能厚着脸皮要了，但如果只交换一些能吃的尾巴草呢。
他们不拿去种，只吃，不知道行不行。
羽山捧着陶碗，水汽弥漫，模糊了他略显沧桑的眉眼。
尾巴草珍贵，要是交换，应该只会比那陶罐渔网交换的劳动时间更长。
羽山倒是不怕再来狼部落做事，只是担心顾及不到部落那边。
他们总不能一直依靠交换获取食物，待在狼部落不走。
他来了这么几次，也看明白了狼山如今能吃饱，离不开整个部落齐心发展。可黑羽部落呢，兽人心不齐，又尽是些老弱病残的，谁会绞尽脑汁去想什么增加食物的办法。
他不在，老族长又那个身体，兽人们怕是还忙着争当族长呢……
羽千作为羽山伴侣，知道他想什么。
他手搭在羽山手背，抓着他紧了紧。
“阿山，什么都比不过食物。”只有食物他们才能度过雪季，才有未来。
羽山目光隔着朦胧水汽，落到棚子底下那群狼兽人身上。他们肉眼可见的比自家兽人壮实，有精神，眼里也有希望。
他们的雪季必定不会像以前那么难熬。
羽山终于点头，只声音有些疲惫。
“好，我去问问。”
*
“你们想要尾巴草？”
方才洗了碗，狼岩就被羽山叫住。兽人似乎有点难以启齿，酝酿了会儿，才说明来意。
羽山道：“是，我们想交换尾巴草。”
这话说得艰难，像嘴巴被黏住，鼓了劲儿才能开口。
羽山知道用干活换取东西是两个部落间的交易，是公平的，他们本不该心虚。
可如今兽神大陆，食物的珍贵可想而知，就是在自家部落做再多的活儿，哪有兽神分食物给你。
再一再二再三，羽山有点骨气也磨没了。
狼岩见中年兽人自个儿说着就低下头，也明白他们为了食物折腰，也是不得已。
可照目前来看，除开那挖藕一事，部落如今剩下的活儿都可以自己做。
他们何必再养额外的二十张嘴？
谁的食物是白来的？
狼岩：“尾巴草收回后，我们送了不少给支部落，剩下的怕是匀不出来。”
羽山抬头笑起来，嘴角像用了大力气提起来的，眼里却没一点笑意，充斥着苦涩。
“……我知道，是我们贪心。”
狼岩：“先前的交易，你情我愿，不存在什么贪心。”
羽山强忍落寞，回到黑羽兽人堆里。
大伙儿围上来，小声道：“怎么了？他们答应了吗？”
“能换得多吗？干多久的活儿都行。”
“对，多久都行。”
羽乐唇抿成直线，担忧地看着羽山。
他知道，不成。
“不成。”
果然。
族人还在小声讨论，似乎没听明白羽山的话。
羽山加重了声音道：“不行，狼王说，他们已经分出不少给支部落，剩的也只勉强够他们自己。”
兽人呆滞。
空气安静了瞬间，兽人又七嘴八舌地议论起来。
“就、就应该早点说。”
“我之前就说了问问，可山你总说等一等，等一等，看吧，等到现在人家都……”
羽千深吸一口气，“好了！”
兽人噤声。
羽千：“收拾东西，等会儿就去大泽那边了。”
兽人垂头丧气，不再吭声。
先前狼部落爽快同意跟他们交换陶器，他们想当然的就觉得这次应该也能成。狼王看着凶，但好说话。
可谁知，竟一点不给。
二十个兽人当中，大都知道结果后心里失落，但也有几个，生出怨怼。
他们低下头，差点折断手上筷子，声音微不可闻。
“怕不是想让我们求他们，不就是食物多点……”
“也不一定，肯定是觉得我们用干活交换亏了，说不准惦记其他什么。”
羽千细腻，注意到之后跟羽山说了说。
羽山哪里还敢沉浸在交换不来尾巴草的忧愁中，直接抓了几个兽人进睡觉的山洞，好生警告了一番。
要叫他们在狼部落惹出事儿，以后再想跟狼部落换点东西，那更是想都别想。
几个兽人说他两句可以，但敢坏了两部落间的关系，弄死他们，都难赎罪！
羽山有预感，要吃饱，必须得跟着狼部落的步子走。
*
要去大泽的兽人依旧是狼火那一批，要带什么兽人已经熟门熟路了。
狼火将板车一套，收拾好吃饭用的家伙什，叫上狼雨跟狼虹俩负责做饭的亚兽人，出发前往大泽。
黑羽兽人跟着跑了一段，再用翅膀飞。
黑羽兽人在狼山吃了不少食物，这二十个兽人一点不像之前一样弱唧唧的。能折腾，狼兽人一上午到大泽，他们同时到，甚至还有力气给自己铺窝。
这次过来，林楸跟狼岩同行。
林楸有意锻炼自己跑步速度跟耐力，他跑一段，实在跑不动再叫狼岩背着追上大队伍。
在狼岩背上休息够了，林楸又下来接着跑。
兽人世界并不安宁，保命的东西不能丢。
他俩比大部队稍晚一点到，走出林子时，黑羽兽人已经把自己窝搭好，狼火带着兽人把鱼捞起来了，狼雨跟狼虹也把陶锅架起，就等着食材入锅。
狼火听见动静，往岸边瞧了眼。
兽人穿着麻布短裤站在浅水中，手上正逮了条鱼，阳光落入水中，波光粼粼。
狼火龇牙笑，胡乱用兽皮带扎高的头发透出暗红光泽，朝气蓬勃的，“楸，你怎么腿儿在打哆嗦？”
林楸不理他，抓着狼岩毛毛从他背上滑下来，一屁股坐在草上。
狼岩瞧了狼火一眼。
兽人嘴巴一闭，捧着大鱼盯住。
不知道的还以为在数鱼有几片鳞。
林楸摊开四肢，一点力气都没有了。
“最近活动少了，都没怎么往外跑。”
狼岩在他旁边趴坐下，尾巴一甩，围在林楸身侧。
附近兽人路过，瞧这样子，立马绕得远远的。
有了伴侣的兽人都一个德行，护食。
林楸没察觉，只没了力气，往狼岩背上一趴。狼毛厚实，狼岩又长了些肉，趴着就像趴在软硬适度的床垫子上，还更有支撑性。
他双手挪到狼岩脑门，晃了晃，几缕狼毛飞起。
“王，你又掉毛了……”
狼岩：“要到雪季，该换毛了。”
林楸笑：“正好再做一件毛褂子。”
狼岩：“好。”
伴侣愿意穿自己毛毛做的衣服，沾染上自己的气味，是个兽人都乐意。
大泽辽阔，风没什么阻挡，肆意乱窜。
兽人们落脚的棚子不远处，之前收割过的蛮草早已经重新长了出来。蛮草叶片隐隐见黄，随风摇曳，草浪叠动。
林楸双手搭在狼岩脑袋上。
瞧着那毛绒绒的大耳朵弹动两下，忽的两手抓去。
狼岩尾巴猝然收紧，林楸腿上如同被勒了一根麻绳。
林楸捏紧他耳朵不放，软弹的手感，可舒服了。他下巴搭在狼岩脑门，脑袋一转，顺着他看向那片蛮草地。
“王，看什么？”
狼岩试图动耳朵，却感受到自家伴侣恶作剧似地捏住。
狼岩眼里闪过无奈，“没看什么。”
林楸撤开一点手，看着那毛耳朵。他手心撑着狼岩背上，挪着挪着靠近，鼻息喷洒在那双耳朵上。
像故意的，剧烈吐息。
狼岩一翻身，直接将他拢在胸口，压得紧紧的。
林楸变成仰躺，笑看着狼岩。
“王，耳朵摸不得啊……”
狼岩见旁边兽人悄摸摸看来，俯身垂下，颈侧一圈长毛直接将林楸埋起来。
狼耳颤动，又听到毛毛底下传来的撒欢儿似的笑。
“能摸。”
林楸脑袋往狼毛里扎，钻草垛似的，把自己头发也弄得乱糟糟。
水边一圈兽人看得像连啃了十来个青皮果，又酸又难受，狼顺嘀咕：“火，你说咱什么时候才能找到伴侣啊？”
狼火：“你问王去。”
他还酸呢。
部落适龄的亚兽人本来就少，就算把支部落加在一块儿，没找伴侣的亚兽人跟雌性兽人最多也就二十个。
他们要找，做梦比较快。
狼顺一甩手，网里差点就捞上来的鱼一下落水跑了。
狼火：“狼顺！你要不行就别干！”
狼顺：“我、我……你别凶嘛，是网松了。”
“你不甩手能松！”
“别那么大火气。”
“我叫狼火，火气能不大！”
*
早上吃的尾巴草籽做的粥，午间又吃回了鱼，不只狼兽人，黑羽兽人都觉得有点难受。
勉强垫了肚子，兽人们趴在棚子里，咂摸着嘴巴试图从一嘴鱼味儿中品出一点尾巴草籽味儿。
努力了会儿，兽人灰心丧气。
黑羽兽人睡的棚子底下更是连连传出叹气声。
想到早上羽山找狼王的交换没成功，心里跟棍子乱搅一样，更难受了。
羽山：“别叹了，睡会儿，不然等会儿没力气。”
中午休息了会儿，就准备下水了。
莲藕好辨认，大泽里的不知生长了多少年，就是最开始只有一丛藕，现在也能铺满开来。
凡是水较浅的淤泥底，几乎遍布这东西。
兽人们头一次下大泽，害怕陷进去，还专门带了木板来。
黑羽兽人打头，先把木板带下去。接着再回来带狼兽人过去。
林楸满身驱虫的药味儿，趴在羽千背上，绕过那些沼泽，被他背到了大泽中间。
他坐在薄木板上，看到狼火已经离开木板，慢慢往泥地里下。
清澈的水鼓出淤泥泡泡，咕噜咕噜响。一股泥腥气溢散，狼火道：“抓紧绳子！别放啊！”
狼顺身体倾倒在木板上，紧盯着他，“抓着呢，抓着呢！”
其他兽人们都没动，狼火是第一个下去尝试的。
以防万一，木板上呆着两个兽人，手上各拿一根绳子绑在他腰间。天上还飞着个黑羽兽人，爪子上同样绑着绳子。
大多兽人还没过来，都屏住呼吸，远远眺望着这边。
狼岩挨着林楸，定定看着。
他们选的是浅水地方，但水还是慢慢没过狼火的大腿，腰侧，直到胸口。
狼岩见状，面上微肃，“拉。”
狼火急得抓住绳子，“王！等一下！好像不会下陷了！”
兽人绷紧手臂肌肉，注视着水下。
林楸用木棍测量过，这里的水浅，从淤泥表面到水面，最深的地方能到兽人们的腰处。
兽人都长得人高马大的，上半身高度依旧足够，不往深处靠近，应该没大问题。
狼岩：“泥到哪儿了？”
狼火动了动，发现脚拔不出来，“到大腿。”
“踩实了？”
狼火点点头，“底下泥没上面软。”
“多试几步。”
林楸：“慢慢抬脚，越急越难拔。”
当着众兽人的面，狼火又走了几步，腰上三根绳子牵引着，狼火从荷叶丛边缘走到中间又走回来，他拨开圆盘一样的荷叶，抓着三两枯败的莲蓬，带出一身清香。
“王！没事！”报告完情况，又举起手中莲蓬问，“楸，这个能吃吗？”
林楸：“能吃，不过你手上那个好像坏了。”
狼火正要走出这片莲丛，忽然停在原地，“咦”了声。
狼岩顿时警惕看向四周，狼火却弯下腰就开始在水里寻摸。水打湿肩膀，脖颈，他得抬着下巴才不会喝到淤泥水。
林楸蹙眉，“你踩到什么了？”
狼火：“等等！”
他抓着东西，试图往上拉，水面也跟着涌动。拉了会儿拉不动，兽人一咬牙，直接暴力往上扯。
只听哗啦一声，黑色的淤泥水四溅。
狼火一屁股栽水里。
他连忙爬起来，手在水中晃了晃，看着那白白嫩嫩的藕节，目光呆了呆。
反应过来，他将手上的莲藕高高举起，一脸惊喜。
“有！”
那莲藕完整，有半身长。
林楸紧紧盯着，发现这野藕跟他见过的菜藕大小相当。
一截竟有小臂长！
林楸喃喃：“发了……”
他本来以为野藕的质量参差不齐，能挖出来些就不错了，哪知道还能有长这么胖的！
狼岩：“什么？”
林楸抓住狼岩的手，“王！挖，越多越好！”
藕生长在淤泥里，最是难挖。现在一天比一天冷，他们必须赶快。
要是林楸之前提议挖野藕只是想给部落添一点菜，现在挖出来的藕就妥妥的能当饭吃。
一亩藕田的产出约在两千斤，这片大泽，深深浅浅的荷叶根本望不到边。
林楸雨季前来没发现多少，那会儿藕正长叶，没发现才正常。这会儿一看，藕叶密密麻麻，兽人们吃几年都够了。
还可以做藕粉，消耗掉莲藕不说，也能长时间储存。
林楸激动，抓着狼岩一时间忘了放。
狼岩捂住他手，对半空的黑羽兽人道：“可以带他们下来了。”
天上的羽山点头，呼啸一声，岸边等候的黑羽兽人开始一个个带着狼兽人往这边靠近。
兽人落地，正想问问刚刚发生了什么，就看见狼火已经只剩个脑袋在外面。
他半个身体歪斜在水中，像直接被丢进水田里的秧苗，又像被什么缠住似的。兽人一慌，急急忙忙往他那边跑。
“火，是不是长虫！”
狼岩斜过去一眼，道：“他没事，挖藕。”
林楸提醒：“尽量不要挖断，手往淤泥里探，抓到藕节了慢慢沿着它把淤泥挖掉，最好整个带出来。不然孔洞进了泥不好清洗。”
兽人一听，不跑了。
他们后知后觉自己已经踩在泥里，忙手上薅着几张荷叶，掐烂了，紧张等着脚下踩实，听着林楸的话生疏地将两只手往泥巴里探。
这活儿就跟当初在河边挖黏土似的，但重要的不是把泥巴挖上来，而是找里面藏着的东西。
这里头脏兮兮的，真有那白白净净的……
“有了！”兽人惊讶。
“我这边也有！”
“挖啊！”狼火又掏出来一个，晃一晃水，猛拍了一下，哈哈大笑，“咱在这边住了这么多年，头一次知道，大泽还藏着这么好的宝贝！”
林楸：“小心泥点溅嘴巴里。”
林楸这会儿撑着狼岩手臂往水里下。他不怕蛇了，这地儿兽人一多，闹出这么大动静，有蛇也早跑了。
羽涯冲着这方看一眼，挪到羽山旁边，抓过一个叶片挡在跟前。
“阿山叔，咱部落有这个吗？”
羽山是走遍了黑羽部落领地的，他回想一番，叹气摇头。
湖泊倒是有，但都是深湖，长不出来这东西。
羽涯酸道：“怎么什么好东西都长在他们部落……”

chapters.title: 第109章
chapters.translated_text:
The water temperature in the lake was just right, but as his feet sank deeper into the silt, the chill made him shiver.

Lin Qiu clung to Lang Yan’s shoulders, slowly submerging into the water.

Once his feet were firmly planted, he tried pulling one leg out to ensure he could walk, then patted the large hand tightly gripping his waist, "Alright, you can let go now."

Lin Qiu caught the nearest large lotus leaf and traced the stem downward; the water was still a bit deep, so he had to tilt his waist to reach his hand into the silt.

As the lake water rose to his shoulders and neck, Lin Qiu tilted his head back slightly, frowning, "The water is a bit deep."

Lang Yan gently supported his chin with his hand.

Lin Qiu was stunned for a moment, then smiled at him.

"Thank you, King."

Lang Yan: "Just playing around is enough."

Lin Qiu buried his arm into the silt and finally felt something along the stem. His eyes lit up, and he leaned his body downward.

The now-murky lake water was reaching his chin, and Lang Yan frowned as he watched.

"Let me."

"I felt it," Lin Qiu said, looking up, "Wait a second."

Lang Yan’s hand was still supporting his chin, and since he couldn't stand steadily in the silt, Lin Qiu simply grabbed his hand to steady himself.

Lang Yan took the opportunity to hold him, using a bit of force to support him slightly.

Lin Qiu dug for a while before finally pulling out the deeply buried lotus root. After shaking it twice in the water, most of the silt clinging to it fell away, revealing white, slender segments.

Lin Qiu: "They aren't all as fat as the ones Lang Huo found."

"Hmm." Lang Yan’s hand had already submerged into the water, supporting his waist again, "You’ve dug it up, so stop playing now."

Lin Qiu set the lotus root aside and pushed off his arm to pull his foot up, "I’m not a cub."

When his foot wouldn't budge, Lin Qiu patted Lang Yan’s arm, "King, give me a lift."

Lang Yan closed his palm, gripped Lin Qiu’s waist tightly, and lifted him up like a child, placing him directly onto the wooden board he had been sitting on earlier.

Lin Qiu washed his feet clean, stood up shakily on the board, and observed the lake.

Most of the deep parts of the Great Marsh were in the middle and southeast; at this time of year, the water level dropped, revealing large stretches of mudflats along the edges.

Their current location was the nearest shallow lake after crossing the swamp.

The shallow lake faced the central lake island across the water, with slightly higher terrain on the periphery and patches of exposed silt all around.

After looking around, Lin Qiu lowered his head, seeing only the crown of Lang Yan’s hair.

Water was splashed onto his legs bit by bit, and the silt on them had already been washed away by Lang Yan. Lin Qiu said, "They’ll just get dirty again."

Lang Yan: "It will itch if you stay in it too long."

Lang Yan checked his fair, slender legs, finding no red marks from insect bites. He pinched the soft calves with his palms and looked up at him.

"Let's go back."

Lin Qiu: "Not yet, there’s still something to do."

He nimbly got back into the water, pulled Lang Yan along, and said, "Let’s see if we can drain the water out a bit more."

Lang Yan looked at the back of his neck and had no choice but to follow him wading through the water.

The beastmen were already busy, occasionally howling as they held up the lotus roots they had just dug. Some were competing to see who could dig the biggest and longest ones, splashing the water loudly.

Lin Qiu walked from the east side to the west side, where the water was already up to his chest.

He stopped moving forward and instead circled toward the south.

The water level gradually dropped, receding to his calves. When he looked back, he and Lang Yan were already standing on the mudflats.

This patch of silt was raised, but the height difference from the water surface was at most one meter.

Lin Qiu: "King, let’s dig a trench here."

If not for this slightly higher patch of silt blocking it, the lake where the beastmen were digging lotus roots would have been nearly half dry.

Lang Yan clearly understood his intention. He looked around for a while but didn't see any suitable tools. Not wanting to shift into his beast form and get his fur wet, he signaled the Black-Feathered beastmen flying overhead to bring some bone shovels.

The surface silt was quite soft, and one scoop made a pit.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan dug here for a long time until the bottom of the pit was level with the water surface. With a little more effort, the silt was washed away by the water, like a broken bowl, and all the water surged into this spot.

After the pit was dug a bit larger, they moved to a few other places.

Where they were afraid of water spreading in, they piled up the silt. Where they could drain water, they dug pits.

After walking a full circle, the effects slowly began to show.

"Eh? I don't seem to be swallowing water anymore," Lang Shun spat twice.

Standing next to him was Lang Chou, who was diligently bending over and struggling with a lotus root.

"A-Chou, did you notice?"

Lang Chou gestured for him to look into the distance. The King and Lin Qiu had been digging for so long, yet this fool was as blind as if he had no eyes.

Lang Shun: "Hehe, Qiu is still the most thoughtful one."

Perhaps during the dry season, the marshes of the Great Marsh were not connected. Lotus roots mostly grew in shallow water areas, and now most of them were exposed.

Digging lotus roots in just this one spot wasn't enough, so Lin Qiu pulled Lang Yan along, draining water where they could and building dams where they could in the areas they planned to dig later.

After finishing the circle, Lin Qiu stood at the edge of a lotus patch and looked around.

Catching a glimpse of a beastman landing on the lake island and grabbing a python, Lin Qiu immediately looked away. Lang Yan shifted his body, blocking his view.

Seeing Lin Qiu watching intently, Lang Yan noticed the mud spots on his face had dried.

Lang Yan wiped them off for him.

Lin Qiu: "King, are there any large tribes like ours to the south of our tribe?"

Lin Qiu only knew that beyond the Great Marsh was the White Sparrow Tribe, but what about further south?

Lang Yan: "No."

"What about other directions?"

Lang Yan shook his head, "Few."

"When the tribe chose this location, they specifically avoided large tribes." In the current situation, if two large tribes dared to be close to each other, it would mean a fight to the death.

The Wolf Tribe couldn't afford such turmoil, and neither could other tribes.

"King, do you want to grow lotus roots?" Lin Qiu leaned against him, and Lang Yan took the opportunity to pull him into his arms.

Lang Yan: "There are many here."

Lin Qiu: "In the long run, we won't just dig here once or twice; we will need to grow them ourselves later. We need to renovate this place so that irrigation and drainage aren't restricted. Then we can build some roads, and by then, even without the Black-Feathered beastmen, we can come to this marsh."

Lang Yan: "I'm afraid we don't have the energy for that right now."

This place was full of pits and bumps; to plant them like tail-grass on a large, flat piece of land would likely take ten times the effort.

Plus, since the tail-grass planting was successful this year, after this snow season, the Priest would definitely plant more. By then, the tribe would only be busier.

Besides, it wasn't easy to clear a good piece of land in a marsh.

Lin Qiu: "I didn't say right now. We need to have a long-term vision and make a five-year or ten-year plan for our tribe."

"I don't want to keep eating fish forever."

Lang Yan looked at his partner nestled in his arms, lowered his head, and touched his nose against his.

"Okay."

Lin Qiu beamed, "Then we'll include this in our considerations?"

Lang Yan: "Hmm."

With his gray eyes fixed on Lin Qiu’s smile, Lang Yan lowered his gaze and gently touched the corner of his lips.

Lin Qiu was stunned for a moment and said, "King, I'm talking to you about serious business."

Lang Yan stroked Lin Qiu’s hair, his expression relaxed, a faint smile playing on his lips, looking incredibly handsome.

Lin Qiu’s eyes changed; he hooked his neck, stood on tiptoe, and rushed forward...

With such beauty before him, he wasn't a saint.

*

Lang Yan, bearing a small tooth mark on his lip, carried his partner out of the water and then used the Black-Feathered beastmen to get to the shore.

The arrangements for the Great Marsh were already made; they had only come to check on the situation.

They planned to return in the evening. The tribe was building houses, burning charcoal, and setting up heated beds; Lin Qiu had to be there to oversee it.

The first batch of dug lotus roots was already piled on the stove, washed, trimmed of segments, and packed into two large basins.

Seeing Lin Qiu come up, Lang Yu grabbed him and asked, "Qiu, should we stew this too?"

It wasn't early, and Lin Qiu and Lang Yan planned to eat before heading back.

Thinking that the beastmen hadn't eaten this often before, Lin Qiu simply washed his hands and helped Lang Yu with the cooking.

Tonight's meat was snakes caught by the beastmen. Lin Qiu didn't see the whole creatures; the meat on the cutting board was already processed.

He told Lang Yu to slice the meat and picked out some tender lotus root tips, asking Lang Hong to slice those as well.

It wasn't about the quantity, just teaching the beastmen a few dishes.

Besides stir-fried lotus root with meat, they made lotus root and meatball soup, stewed lotus root, and cold-tossed lotus root. Four methods were just right; after this, the Great Marsh side should eat lotus root often, and by rotating the styles for a month, the beastmen would get the hang of it.

From far away, the beastmen in the lotus fields tied up the dug roots, and the Black-Feathered beastmen transported them up.

The beastmen mastered the technique after digging for a while, and their speed was fast. Besides the lotus roots Lang Yu washed for eating, there was a small mountain of them piled on the shore.

Seeing it was about time, Lin Qiu started the fire and heated the oil, added the simply marinated meat slices, stir-fried them until cooked, removed them, added a little more oil, and sautéed green onions and ginger until fragrant.

Then he added the lotus root slices, stir-fried them, and finally added the meat back in, sprinkling with salt.

A simple and quick dish of stir-fried lotus root with meat was ready.

Lang Yu and Lang Hong were both experienced cooks; this method was no different from how they usually cooked wild vegetables, and they learned it after watching once.

Lin Qiu stepped aside and left the rest to them.

There wasn't much oil in the tribe, and the beastmen had only brought one jar.

Using it sparingly, just a hint of oil flavor was enough.

Even so, this first meal of lotus root was quite sumptuous.

With so many beastmen, they rarely ate such stir-fried dishes, and the mere aroma made them stop their work.

"Qiu, is it ready to eat?" a beastman shouted from far away.

Lin Qiu: "Almost."

By the time the four dishes were done, it was dark.

As soon as the beastmen heard they could eat, they pulled themselves out of the mud like radishes. By now, the water in that shallow beach had been drained by half, and the beastmen were covered in mud like mud dolls.

After running a few steps, the beastman in front suddenly cried out.

The other beastmen looked over, breaking into a cold sweat.

They quickly dropped to the ground. The beastman had been running fast, went off course, and one step into what looked like flat ground caused the mudflat to act like flowing water, quickly swallowing him down.

In just that short moment, he had sunk to his thighs.

Lang Huo: "Don't move! Lie down!"

A Black-Feathered beastman happened to be coming to bring the beastmen back to shore; seeing this, he flew down and dropped a wooden board beside the beastman.

Several beastmen carefully pulled him out, their hearts still racing with fear.

They had almost forgotten that the edge was full of man-eating mud.

The Black-Feathered beastman landed, "Grab on."

The beastmen, still shaken, hurriedly grabbed their claws and were carried flying toward the shore.

As soon as they landed, they met Lang Yan’s dark, stern eyes.

The beastman lowered his head, not daring to make a sound.

Lang Yan: "If there’s a next time, stay on Wolf Mountain and don't come out."

Don't look at it as just a small sinking; if he had been any faster and run into the deep swamp, it wouldn't have been just a matter of sinking a foot.

Beastman: "I will remember, King."

Lang Yan withdrew his gaze and looked at Lang Huo.

"Keep a close watch."

Lang Huo nodded, then secretly glared at the beastman next to him.

The lotus root was fragrant, the tender ones were crisp, and the old ones were soft and waxy if stewed long enough. It was a delicacy suitable for all ages.

A basin of sour, spicy, and crisp cold-tossed lotus root, half a basin of stir-fried lotus root with meat, a pottery jar of meatballs, and a pottery jar of lotus root stew.

The beastmen had never eaten this well even on Wolf Mountain.

Drooling, the beastmen surrounded the stove.

Lang Huo rubbed his hands anxiously, "Qiu, can we eat, can we eat!"

Lin Qiu was surrounded and couldn't get out, saying helplessly: "You keep asking if you can eat, but where are your bowls? It's so hot, are you going to eat with your hands?"

The beastmen swallowed their saliva and ran off quickly to get their bowls.

Lin Qiu finally squeezed out from beside the stove and stood next to Lang Yan.

When the beastmen returned, they lined up, and Lang Yu and Lang Hong served them.

Once the beastmen got their food, they sat on the ground and shoved a large piece of meat into their mouths. They picked and chose, eating the meat quickly before finally picking up the lotus root.

Lin Qiu listened to the crunching sounds from all directions and glanced at the meat in Lang Yan’s bowl, quickly looking away.

Lang Yan: "Want some?"

Lin Qiu: "No."

He only had a bowl of cold-tossed lotus root; the other three dishes contained snake meat, which he didn't really want to eat.

Lang Yan: "Try it, it's good."

Lin Qiu turned his head away, his cheeks moving as he chewed the crunchy lotus root.

Lang Yan smiled, didn't ask again, and finished his meal quickly.

The leaves rustled, and a crescent moon hung in the sky. A few stars twinkled, and the night was quiet...

In the deep wild grass, a long ear quietly poked out from the blades.

It sniffed rapidly, but upon smelling the scent of the wolf beastmen and Black-Feathered beastmen mixed in the aroma, it pulled its ear back in fright and quickly vanished into the darkness.

Lang Yan glanced at the wild grass.

Lin Qiu: "What are you looking at?"

Lang Yan: "There was movement."

Lin Qiu stood up, intending to go take a look. Lang Yan grabbed his wrist, "Let Lang Huo handle it, we should head back."

...

By the time they rushed back to the Wolf Tribe under the stars, Lin Qiu was already fast asleep on Lang Yan’s back.

The Black-Feathered beastmen left, and Lang Yan carried Lin Qiu directly up the mountain into a cave at the very top.

The cave was of moderate size and kept clean inside.

The large grass nest placed in the innermost part had its base raised significantly with stones, and the nest itself was made thick.

There was no fire in the cave. A wolf beastman who heard the movement came up to check, and seeing it was Lang Yan, ran back down the mountain to curl up in his own grass nest.

Lin Qiu was groggy, feeling Lang Yan put him down.

He closed his eyes, found the beastman’s shoulder, touched his face, and leaned his head against his shoulder again, breathing steadily.

Lang Yan gently rubbed his nose against his cheek, tucked him in, and closed his eyes to sleep.

Lin Qiu woke up and realized he was already in the tribe.

The cave was unfamiliar, and the animal skin covering him wasn't the one from before; it was larger and thicker, enough to cover another person.

The skin was heavy, pressing down on him, making Lin Qiu break into a sweat.

Lin Qiu pushed the skin away and sat up, leaning against the edge of the nest, his long hair spilling over his shoulders. His cheeks were flushed, his breath hot, and the long-sleeved linen shirt he was wearing was already soaked with sweat and wrinkled.

He was alone in the cave. Lin Qiu undressed while listening to the footsteps outside, staring at the cave entrance.

"Are you hungry?"

Lang Yan entered holding a pottery jar. Seeing Lin Qiu was awake, he poured some water from the jar and brought it to Lin Qiu’s lips.

Lin Qiu drank half a bowl in one breath and kicked the animal skin still covering his legs, "It's not the snow season, why cover me with such a thick skin?"

Lang Yan put the bowl down and set the skin aside.

"Hot!" Lin Qiu threw the clothes he had taken off into his arms, his lips bright red, his forehead damp. Pushing away the skin seemed to have exhausted him, and he was panting slightly.

Lang Yan tidied up the clothes and placed them on his lap.

"I'll go get a basin of water for you to wipe down," he said, then added, "Should I wash your pants?"

Lin Qiu hesitated for a moment, took them off, and threw them to him.

Seeing the fair skin that had been hidden under the clothes, Lang Yan’s eyes darkened. Lin Qiu pushed his chest, "Go on."

Lang Yan’s Adam’s apple bobbed, and the veins on his forehead pulsed.

He grabbed Lin Qiu’s wrists, lifted him up, and sat him on his lap.

Lin Qiu was bare, having taken off his pants to be washed. But sitting on his partner like this, even the thickest skin couldn't handle it.

The breath on his neck was scorching, and Lin Qiu turned his head away, his earlobes red as blood.

"Go on, hurry."

Lang Yan bit down, and Lin Qiu shivered, collapsing limply into his arms.

"Do you think I'm blind?"

Lin Qiu muttered, "That's not it, we're partners. Taking off clothes in front of a partner is perfectly normal... mmph."

The cave was their private one, and no other beastmen came by.

Lang Yan sat sideways into the grass nest, back to the entrance, wrapping the bare Lin Qiu tightly. Standing at the entrance and looking in, one could only see a pair of arms weakly clinging to his broad shoulders, like a kitten's paws with little strength, trying to push Lang Yan away.

"I'm all sweaty, I need to wash... mmph..."

Lang Yan tightened his arms and kissed him even more fiercely.

Feeling comfortable from the kisses, Lin Qiu grabbed Lang Yan’s long hair and tilted his head to meet him.

Like a lazy cat, he slowly stretched out his long legs and wrapped them around Lang Yan’s waist. His arms hung around Lang Yan’s neck, and with no clothes to grab, he unconsciously tugged at his thick, long hair.

The wheat-colored palms grabbed his fair ankles and tucked them back in.

Lin Qiu kicked him, humming, "Uncomfortable..."

Lang Yan kissed him for a long time, looked down at the tears hanging in the corners of Lin Qiu’s eyes, and couldn't help but bite the soft flesh on his cheek.

"Wash..."

He was still thinking about it.

Lang Yan took a deep breath, pressed his nose tightly against his cheek, and patted his restless bottom.

"Alright, wash."

He waited a while, took Lin Qiu’s clothes and pants down, and after a while, brought up a basin of water.

When he sat on the edge of the grass nest, Lin Qiu moved over, straddled his lap, and leaned against him lazily.

Lang Yan was helpless.

It was daytime, and the beastmen were all awake and active down the mountain...

He could only endure it, wrung out the cloth, and wiped Lin Qiu clean.

"King." Lin Qiu lowered his head, stepped on his feet, and looked at him blankly, "Good..."

Lang Yan’s hand trembled; he hugged him tightly with one arm, not letting him move.

Lin Qiu leaned on his chest and whispered in his ear, "Will it hurt?"

Although he was a sub-beastman now and theoretically it should be possible, it was his first time.

The veins on Lang Yan’s forehead pulsed, and he couldn't help but bundle him up, "You'll know tonight."

Lin Qiu buried his head in his shoulder and laughed, his shoulders shaking.

His cheeks were flushed, but his actions were very bold.

Lin Qiu laughed, looking up, his eyes soft and moist, veiled in a hazy shimmer.

Lang Yan met his gaze, and his heart suddenly trembled.

He could feel Lin Qiu’s wholehearted trust and attachment to him, which made his heart ache even more compared to the prickly sub-beastman he once was.

Lang Yan quickly finished wiping him down and put his clothes on.

He didn't let go, just kept holding him.

Lin Qiu fussed for a while, then lay on his shoulder. His long hair, combed smooth by Lang Yan, flowed down like a waterfall, softly resting on Lang Yan’s shoulder.

Lin Qiu moved, his hands still holding him tightly.

He pried at Lang Yan’s fingers and said weakly, "King, how much longer are you going to hold me... I'm hungry."

Lang Yan paused, "Sorry."

He had forgotten.

Last time, he was so tired after kissing that he fell asleep, and now he hadn't eaten yet; Lang Yan was afraid he would faint.

He even forgot to take the water used for wiping down, and hurried down the mountain.

After finally getting Lin Qiu to eat his brunch, Lang Yan started tidying up the cave. He poured out the water, washed the clothes, and moved his partner’s daily items up the mountain.

Seeing him busy back and forth, Lin Qiu jumped up and hung on his back.

Lang Yan stopped, and Lin Qiu wrapped his legs around his waist.

"Carry me."

Lang Yan supported him from behind, his eyes soft, "Do you want to go down?"

Lin Qiu yawned, "Hmm."

There weren't many beastmen on Wolf Mountain; the hunting and gathering teams were all out. Lang An and a few middle-aged sub-beastmen were weaving, and the rhythmic sound of the loom came out.

Lang Qi had pulled Lang Mu’s team to work on the heated beds and wanted to take the opportunity to make a large stone mill.

Only Lang Shi was on patrol for the guard team.

The rest of Lang Mo’s team was busy, half responsible for building houses and half for burning bricks, tiles, and charcoal.

On the flattened ground in front of Wolf Mountain, only Lang Guo was basking in the sun with the cubs.

Lang Sheng, that little thing, had sturdy arms and legs, tanned dark by the sun, looking like a little coal boy. Behind him followed a group of cubs, tumbling into the grass.

Lin Qiu slid off Lang Yan’s back, and feeling the sun, lazily sat down next to Lang Guo. The four cubs who couldn't shift into human form immediately crawled toward him.

Lin Qiu pinched a cub’s little paw, "Do I have milk cakes or meat bones on me?"

Lang Guo laughed, "You have the King’s scent on you."

As he spoke, Lang Yan sat down, and the cubs running around gathered around him.

Lang Yan: "Sit."

The cubs sat obediently in front of Lang Yan.

"Lang Sheng and Little Fatty in one group, Lang Hua and Lang Wu in one group..."

As he spoke, the cubs automatically adjusted their positions and sat in pairs.

Lang Yan: "Fight for me to see."

The cubs looked at each other, immediately scrambled up, and pounced on their partners.

The wolf cubs were very fierce. Lin Qiu held a cub, his eyes wide. The little ball in his arms clawed at his hand, whining and wanting to go down.

Lang Guo: "Come on, you guys go too."

Lin Qiu hesitated, "Won't they get hurt?"

Lang Guo: "Don't worry, they can't get hurt, their teeth haven't hardened yet."

Once released, the cubs whimpered low, and the four gray-black balls immediately started a chaotic fight.

The cubs had short legs, and with a slight touch, they would fall over, their fighting method being to bite.

After biting a mouthful of fur, they would have to stick their tongues out to spit it out.

Lin Qiu laughed as he watched.

There were sixteen cubs in total, and Lang Xue was also there today. Excluding the four who couldn't shift, the other twelve were fighting fiercely in pairs.

Lang Yan watched, occasionally saying, "Don't pull hair, do you rely on pulling fur when you hunt?"

"Don't bite to kill!"

"A prey’s weakness is the throat; as long as you find the right moment to bite the throat, you can kill with one blow. But likewise, a prey’s hooves and horns are their weapons; learn to avoid them."

"Awoo!" The cubs listened carefully and tested it one by one on their companions.

After fighting for a long time, the cubs’ eyes turned red.

Whimpering low, threatening each other, they shifted into their beast forms to have another round.

Lang Yan didn't stop them, just watched the cubs to ensure they didn't hurt each other.

Lin Qiu watched intently, and seeing the four cubs in front rolling into a ball, with the one underneath unable to get up, he reached out to help lift it.

The cub bit him; it didn't hurt, but it was itchy.

Lang Guo pulled the tail of a cub that was still pressing down, and asked Lin Qiu, "How is it over at the Great Marsh?"

Lin Qiu pinched the tail of the cub beside him, "There are many lotus roots; we won't have to worry about food during the snow season after digging them back."

Lang Guo was surprised, "It didn't look like much when the beastmen dug them last time."

Lin Qiu: "The Great Marsh is so big, we can only stay at the edge and look; how would we know if there are more elsewhere?"

Lang Guo: "That’s true."

The cub underneath had already climbed up and pounced back. Lang Guo and Lin Qiu let go, letting them continue their fight.

Lin Qiu sat there for a while, then climbed up.

He patted the dust off his body, walked past Lang Yan, and asked, "King, let's go check the brick kiln."

Lang Yan looked up and reached out.
