Now that Yu Shan was away and the chief had difficulty moving, Yu Hua truly thought the tribe belonged to him, spending all day leading a group of orcs lying around in their nests waiting to be fed.

Summoned over this time, Yu Hua and several other orcs were yawning continuously, their hair disheveled, looking as if they had just gotten out of their nests.

"At a time like this, other tribes have already started preparing for the snow season. Look at you all, what on earth are you doing?" The old chief suppressed his anger, but his hands couldn't stop trembling.

Yu Hua stretched out his legs, pointing them straight at the old chief.

Falling just a palm's width short of landing on the chief, he slung his arm lazily over the edge of the nest and said, "Chief, isn't it raining today?"

"So what if it's raining? Aren't you going to eat?"

"Isn't it just a matter of casting a net a few times? Just tell a couple of orcs to go, do we all need to go?"

"Exactly, we need to save our energy for hunting."

"Hunting!" The old chief was so angry he almost couldn't catch his breath.

Yu Jiang couldn't bear to watch any longer. He kicked Yu Hua's foot away, blocked the front of the chief, and frowned. "Yu Hua, don't anger the chief."

Yu Hua sneered, "How on earth did I anger the chief?"

Yu Jiang: "Yu Shan will be back soon. Do you think he'd tolerate you acting like this?"

At the mention of Yu Shan, Yu Hua, who had just been slouching carelessly, stood up instantly, his face as dark as a raincloud.

"Yu Jiang, don't use Yu Shan to scare me. Even if he comes back, do you think I'm afraid of him?"

"Ha," Yu Hua chuckled. "Don't forget, during the days Yu Shan hasn't been here, I'm the one who led everyone to cast nets and catch fish so you all could eat your fill."

Yu Jiang: "That was also because Yu Shan led everyone to work together and trade for those things!"

Yu Hua's face turned livid.

"Yu Shan, Yu Shan, Yu Shan, everything is Yu Shan! So what if his legs are crippled, you still want him to be the chief of the Heiyui Tribe? You aren't even looking at whether he can win people's allegiance!"

"Yu Hua! The chief is still right here!"

Yu Hua sneered. "Fine! Since you all keep thinking of Yu Shan, then wait for him to come back. I'm not caring anymore."

He flicked his sleeves and walked away. The remaining orcs looked at each other in dismay, thought for a moment, and simply followed him away.

"Y-Yu Hua!" The old chief's voice was hurried, frightening Yu Jiang into turning around immediately to soothe his breathing.

"Chief..." Yu Jiang lowered his head. "Chief, I'm sorry, I should have spoken properly just now."

The old chief closed his eyes and panted for a long time before his strength drained away, collapsing limply.

"Blame me... It's all my... my fault..."

It was his teaching that had gone wrong.

Yu Shan had a good personality since childhood and could consciously accomplish whatever was asked of him. Yu Hua had a mischievous temperament, so the chief had been a bit stricter with him. But as time passed, Yu Hua thought the chief was biased, breeding resentment toward both him and Yu Shan.

He had originally thought of training Yu Hua well too, so that at least after he passed on, Yu Hua could help Yu Shan shoulder the tribe together.

But Yu Hua's heart was too small, and his temper was no good either.

In the end, Yu Hua couldn't bear to see him show the slightest bit of protection toward Yu Shan. The old chief had thus given up that idea and focused solely on nurturing Yu Shan. Yet he never expected that Yu Shan would have an accident while hunting and suffer severe injuries.

Alas!

The old chief said, "A-Jiang..."

"Chief." Yu Jiang sat down, guarding by the old chief's side.

"The snow season... the food for the snow season must... must start being prepared. Yu Hua can't be relied upon. You take those young orcs and go gather first..."

"Chief, if I leave, then what about you?"

The old chief couldn't do without an orc by his side now.

The old chief: "It's fine, I won't die."

"But..."

The old chief raised a hand and grasped him tightly. "A-Jiang, listen to me."

Yu Jiang met those cloudy yet determined eyes, his eye sockets burning as he couldn't help lowering his head.

His lips remained pale, his hand habitually clutching his stomach. Tears swirled in his eyes as his lips trembled, fighting to hold back that wave of soreness.

If his belly hadn't been punctured by a beast's horn back then, he wouldn't have been left without cubs, nor would his body be in such poor condition.

Only when driven to absolute desperation would the chief be asking him to go.

The tribe is in such a state now that Yu Jiang is afraid—afraid that they won't even make it halfway through the snow season.

"A-Jiang..."

Yu Jiang lowered his eyes. "Alright. Patriarch, I will go."

*

Daze.

Yu Le, busy digging lotus roots, suddenly felt a palpitation. He instinctively looked toward the direction of his own tribe, but could see nothing.

"Le, what's wrong?" Yu Qian asked from the side.

Yu Le’s hands were covered in mud, and he was still clutching a plump, white lotus root.

The little beastman had been out with them, staying with everyone, eating his fill, and working without pause; his complexion looked much better than before.

"Uncle A-Qian, I’m worried about my grandfather."

Yu Qian replied, "We’ll be able to go back soon. Don’t be afraid. Before we left, I entrusted your Uncle A-Jiang to look after the Patriarch."

Yu Le set the lotus root down. "Uncle A-Qian, after everyone leaves, will they come back to the Wolf Tribe?"

Yu Qian asked, "You still want to come?"

The little beastman hung his head, looking a bit wilted.

"I discussed it with A-Bing and the others; I asked him to teach me a little bit about medicinal herbs."

Yu Qian’s spirits lifted.

They had brought Yu Le here with that very intention, but they hadn't dared to ask the Wolf Tribe. They had only hoped he would watch and learn enough to make the trip worthwhile, even if it was just a tiny bit.

He never expected that he would actually pull it off!

Lang Bing was the successor to the Wolf Tribe’s old priest and the next priest of the tribe. The little wolf usually looked cold and ignored other beastmen, but he was always leading a group of wolf pups out to gather herbs.

Every time Yu Qian saw that, he felt incredibly envious.

In their tribe, they couldn't even name many herbs, let alone gather them.

Now, it was great—if Yu Le could learn from Lang Bing, even just a little, it would be better than the little beastman sitting in their own tribe staring blankly every day.

Yu Qian quickly glanced at the surrounding wolf beastmen and lowered his voice to confirm, "Is it true?"

Yu Le nodded.

Yu Qian asked, "Does the Wolf Tribe’s old priest know about this?"

After the excitement passed, he calmed down.

It would be best if Lang Bing was willing to teach, but he feared this was just a secret agreement between the two beastmen.

The inheritance of a priest was a confidential matter. If the old priest didn't know, and this came to light later, it would be even worse than when Yu Ya led the theft of the Wolf Tribe’s salt.

Just thinking about it made Yu Qian break out in a cold sweat.

Yu Le said, "The old priest knows. He agreed."

Yu Qian’s eyes widened, and he even leaned in closer to look at the little beastman. He acted as if he hadn't heard clearly; he was so excited that he didn't know where to put his hands and feet.

"Re-really? The old priest agreed?"

His speech was incoherent. He stared intently at the little beastman’s face, and the moment he saw him nod, Yu Qian’s eyes grew sore, and tears splashed into the water.

"Good, good..."

"Uncle A-Qian..." Yu Le was startled.

Yu Qian lowered his head, forgetting his hands were covered in mud, and hugged the little beastman tightly.

"It’s so good, so good. Uncle A-Qian is fine, Uncle A-Qian... I’m going to tell your Uncle A-Shan."

Yu Qian let go of Yu Le and moved so hurriedly that his feet hadn't even pulled out of the mud before he fell to his knees.

He choked on a mouthful of muddy water, but he was too happy to care. He pushed himself up with his hands in the mud, stood up, and stumbled forward.

Remembering something, he turned back, his eyes filled with a bit of trepidation as he looked at Yu Le: "Does the Wolf King know about this?"

Yu Le shook his head. "I don't know."

Yu Qian took a deep breath. "Don't panic, don't panic. I'm going to tell your Uncle A-Shan."

He didn't know who he was telling not to panic; he was only a few meters away from Yu Shan, yet he walked unsteadily.

His legs went weak several times, causing him to sit in the muddy water, his hair soaked and his body covered in black silt. His eyes were gradually brimming with tears, yet they were extremely bright.

Yu Le watched Yu Qian’s back and lowered his head. "Plop, plop"—

Two tears also fell quietly.

Yu Le hadn't lied; the reason he had held back until now was that he was afraid of disturbing their peace of mind.

He knew this matter was very, very important, which was why they should work even harder for the Wolf Tribe.

But that sudden palpitation earlier had made him think of his grandfather, and he had just said it naturally.

The only thing he worried about now was that the old priest had said he could learn from Lang Bing, but he also required that he must stay in the Wolf Tribe and not leave until he had learned well.

Lang Bing was currently teaching Lang Xue the most basic herbal knowledge; teaching one more wouldn't be a burden.

The old priest viewed the study of herbs as more important than anything else.

Once agreed upon, it could not be interrupted by other matters.

It was the same for Lang Bing, the same for Lang Xue, and even Lin Qiu, during the time he first started learning from the priest, had gone every single day without fail.

After this, he would almost never be able to see his grandfather.

But his grandfather’s health...

Yu Le stood still in the water for a while, watching the water surface gradually calm down, and the worry on his face faded away.

The little beastman remained silent, working hard to reach his hand into the mud to find the white lotus roots.

His grandfather had told him to come, and he had come.

If his grandfather knew of this result, he would surely be very, very happy.

The rain was getting heavier, and Lang Yu on the bank shouted, "Come back! No more digging today!"

The black-feathered beastmen began to fly to the bank, their claws clutching lotus roots tied with hemp rope, transporting them in batches.

"A-Qian, you said the Wolf Tribe agreed to teach Yu Le?"

Yu Shan stood on the mudflat, supporting his body on one leg; if you didn't look closely, you wouldn't notice his leg trembling slightly.

Beastmen who stayed in the water for too long, especially on a rainy day, would suffer from leg cramps.

He had been enduring it, not wanting the wolf beastmen to notice, nor wanting his partner to worry.

Yu Qian wept with joy, using the rain to hide his tears. Looking up and seeing the dazed look in Yu Shan’s eyes, he could no longer hold back; he lowered his head and hugged his partner’s waist, burying his face in his chest to calm his surging emotions.

But the moment he embraced him, he felt a bone-chilling cold.

His hands trembled slightly, and Yu Qian traced his arm down to his leg. He didn't dare move anymore and cried, "Go up quickly, go up quickly!"

Yu Shan smiled, genuinely happy from the bottom of his heart.

He patted his partner’s back and said, "I knew that little beastman Yu Le was obedient; he’s the easiest to make people’s hearts soften."

"Go up! We'll talk later," Yu Qian urged anxiously.

Yu Shan wiped the corners of his reddened eyes—how could he not see that he was crying?

"Don't cry, don't cry, it's a happy thing. I'm going up now."

All the black-feathered beastmen went ashore, washed their bodies clean, and sat under the shed around the fire.

Lang Yu and Lang Hong stood by the stove, smashing the lotus roots and chopping them into pieces. "This rain is definitely going to last for a few days."

Lang Hong sighed, "It's like this before every snow season."

"It’ll probably be cold in the water."

"You're right. Let's not make cold dishes; let's make more hot soup."

As the two beastmen discussed the meal, Yu Qian leaned against Yu Shan, his hand unable to resist resting on his leg again.

Yu Shan held his partner’s hand and smiled. "It's fine."

Yu Qian frowned in distress. "Why didn't you say anything before?"

It was his own fault for not noticing; he should have boiled some hot water every night for him to soak in.

The beastmen listened to the sound of the rain and chatted while leaning against the low wall.

No one noticed them, except for Yu Le, who slowly moved over, looking at Yu Shan with concern.

"Uncle A-Shan, is your leg hurting?"

Yu Shan patted the little beastman’s head. He and Yu Qian’s own cub hadn't survived, so they treated this sickly, endearing cub as their own.

Although he was physically weak, he hadn't been perfunctory or lazy these days, working even more diligently than some adult beastmen.

The two of them saw it all, and their hearts only grew more fond of him.

Yu Shan solemnly patted the little beastman’s shoulder twice. "Uncle A-Shan is happy for you."

Yu Le lowered his head. He didn't know what to say, but suddenly he saw the gruesome scar on Yu Shan’s leg.

His leg had once been injured by the horn of a prey animal, leaving a long, deep gash. Even after it healed, the scar remained uneven, and the color of the skin was different from the rest, looking like a worm crawling on it.

Yu Le was stunned.

Yu Shan moved, hiding the scar on his leg.

"Scared, aren't you? It's fine, let's not look at it."

Yu Le shook his head and gathered the courage to lift his head. "Uncle A-Shan, don't worry, I will definitely learn well."

He would make sure Uncle A-Shan’s leg wouldn't hurt like this anymore.

The little beastman’s words made both adult beastmen laugh, their eyes filled with gratification.

"Good, learn well," Yu Qian also patted his head and said.

This rain did indeed last a long time; it rained continuously for three days, then intermittently for another two. As soon as the rain stopped, the beastmen clearly felt the temperature drop.

The wind blew against their skin, raising goosebumps.

The temperature in the water would only be lower.

On rainy days, Lang Yu and Lang Hong didn't call for the black-feathered beastmen to go into the water, to avoid them getting sick and needing to go back for herbs.

With the delay of these few days, Lang Huo had also returned, bringing members of the little wolf hunting team.

There wasn't much time left to work, so everyone didn't dare to delay. They were afraid that the water would become bone-chillingly cold later, which would be unbearable.

Qiu said they had to dig up the lotus roots quickly and head back early, as they still had to prepare other things for the snow season.

The little wolves had endless energy once they were fed, which was perfect for digging lotus roots.

After digging for another four or five days, two batches of lotus roots were transported back to Wolf Mountain, and the little wolves were exhausted.

Lang Huo watched them dawdling and, after thinking about it, simply gave the little wolves a day off.

It was a good chance for them to roam around and see if they could catch some prey.

They had caught plenty of long-worms in Daze to make into jerky, but they hadn't eaten any; although there were enough lotus roots every day, the beastmen couldn't keep their spirits up without eating meat.

When the little wolves heard this, how could they refuse?

So, the next day, they slept until the sun was high, ate breakfast, and went off to look for prey.

They ran around all day, didn't encounter any deer-beasts, but caught some miscellaneous small animals.

There wasn't much meat, but it was edible.

The little wolves headed back excitedly, just happening to pass through the patch of wild grass on the east side.

Thinking that the grass was deep and there should be long-worms inside, the little wolves cautiously and slowly stepped into the wild grass.

As the wind picked up in the afternoon, there was a rustling sound in the grass.

Lang Jin in front suddenly raised his hand, and Leopard Xiu beside him, along with the other little wolves, quietly crouched down.

Lang Jin signaled: There’s movement ahead.

He then pointed to the left and right: Flank them.

The little wolves dispersed with tacit understanding, restrained their presence, and slowly approached the western side of the wild grass in a semi-encirclement.

Closing in, all the little wolves pounced forward at once.

"Awoo!"

"Caught it!!!" The feeling in their palms wasn't slippery—it wasn't a long-worm?

Lang Jin lifted his hand to look, and the little wolves gathered around.

"A beastman?"

"A rabbit beastman?"

Lang Jin held the creature by its two long ears, while the other little wolves poked at its rabbit paws. The captured Tu Luo was so terrified that he went stiff, his body trembling.

Lang Jin said, "Bring him back."

The little wolves circled Lang Jin, looking at the rabbit beastman in his hand with excitement.

Tu Luo seemed to see his own future.

The wolf beastmen would throw him into that bubbling pot of water, boil him, and eat him!

Help, help, help!

But at this moment, he couldn't make a sound.

"This rabbit beastman is quite bold, daring to run into our tribe? Isn't he afraid we'll eat him?"

The little wolves bared their teeth on purpose, and seeing the rabbit beastman’s pupils shrink in fear, they became even more excited.

"Yeah, yeah, I wonder how he’d taste best—cold-tossed or in a soup?"

Tu Luo rolled his eyes back, and his four legs went limp.

The little wolves said, "Oh! Did he faint?"

Lang Jin grinned. "What a coward."

The little wolves returned with a pile of miscellaneous small animals—red birds, round-nosed beasts, and more. After bringing them back, Lang Yu immediately told them to process them.

The two sub-beastmen were discussing how to eat them when they turned and saw what Lang Jin had brought before them...

"A rabbit beastman!!!" Lang Yu was shocked.

Lang Hong looked over, holding a ladle, and said, "They’ve come back again?"

"Looks like it. Only saw this one? Oh my! Why did you catch him?" Lang Yu asked.

Lang Jin set him down. "We thought it was a long-worm."

Lang Yu and Lang Hong squatted down and poked the rabbit beastman. He had gray fur, softer than their wolf fur.

Lang Yu thought of the sweater he had recently knitted with wolf fur; if it were made of rabbit beastman fur, it would probably be even more comfortable.

Tu Luo was already fainted, but he still couldn't help shivering.

"What should we do with him?" Lang Yu asked.

The Wolf Tribe was large, and Daze was located on the southern edge of the tribe. Beastmen rarely came here in the past, and it was only recently, because of digging bird droppings and lotus roots, that they had started coming more frequently.

They also knew there was a rabbit beastman tribe in the south.

In the eyes of the wolf beastmen, the rabbit tribe mostly ate plants and were the kind of tribe anyone could bully. They were weak and timid, and since the wolf beastmen didn't come this way often, they hadn't given them much thought.

But now that they were all here, this group of rabbits dared to come back.

Did they not take them seriously?

Regardless, since they had caught one, they had to have a good talk.

Lang Yu signaled for Lang Jin to put the rabbit beastman down, so as not to break his ears.

Lang Jin asked, "Yu, should we tie him up?"

Leopard Xiu squatted down and stared at the ball of fur.

"Rabbit tribe, they usually know how to farm."

There were rabbit tribes on the Central Continent too. Don't look at them as weak; they were prolific.

They also knew how to farm, and because they mostly ate wild vegetables, in the current situation, they were actually the most surviving race among all the tribes.

"Farming?!" Lang Jin’s eyes lit up. "What do they grow?"

Leopard Xiu replied, "I don't know either. Why don't we wait for him to wake up and see?"

Lang Jin said, "Then we wait."

His glowing wolf eyes scanned the wild grass again; these rabbit beastmen were the best at digging holes, and he wondered where their nest was hidden.

This wait lasted until the beastmen finished digging lotus roots and went ashore, and the meat soup in the pot was ready. The little wolves were holding their bowls, surrounding the rabbit beastman, when they finally saw the rabbit beastman’s feet twitch twice.

"He’s awake!"

Lang Jin glared at the little wolf beside him. "Keep your voice down, don't scare him into fainting again."

Turning his head, he saw the rabbit beastman suddenly scramble up, curl into a ball, his fur standing on end, and his eyes rolling back again.

Lang Jin immediately said, "You are not allowed to faint!"

Tu Luo was so scared he trembled, pitifully hugging himself, his tears instantly wetting his fur.

He didn't even dare to faint.

He saw the wolf beastmen holding precious pottery, and smelled the meaty aroma coming from that pottery.

Tu Luo shivered violently.

Was it his arm or his leg...

He was trembling, wishing he could just faint again.

Lang Jin casually found a wooden stick and poked him. "Why aren't you talking?"

Leopard Xiu looked at the poked rabbit. "He must be scared silly."

Lang Jin asked, "You, what’s your name?"

Tu Luo opened his mouth, too scared to speak.

Lang Jin asked, "Are you a mute?"

Leopard Xiu said, "Could it be a disabled beastman abandoned by his tribe?"

"Tu... Tu Luo." His voice was thin and weak, and he almost fainted again.

Lang Jin twitched his ears and nodded. "I’m Lang Jin."

"Leopard Xiu."

Tu Luo turned his head and saw a black leopard.

His eyes rolled back, and he fainted again.

"Oh my! Why is he such a coward?"

"He didn't get scared to death, did he?"

The little wolves surrounded him, chattering. Lang Yu couldn't watch anymore and said, "Alright, let's wait for his tribe’s beastmen to come looking for him."

That rabbit beastman looked young, likely not even an adult. The Wolf Tribe had their bottom line; they didn't harm other people’s cubs.

Lang Jin felt bored.

He threw the stick away, held his pottery bowl, and went to the side to drink meat soup.

The meat soup tonight was fragrant; it would be even better if they could continue eating meat tomorrow.

Slowly, the sky turned completely dark.

In the dense forest, in a burrow hidden underground, a gray rabbit beastman hurried through the maze-like tunnels to a large nest dug in the center.

"Pat-Patriarch! Tu Luo is missing!"

The young rabbit patriarch’s hand loosened, and he looked up with a dazed face; the plant roots he had just half-filled dropped to the ground.

Immediately after, a burst of terrified screams erupted in the nest:

"Tu Luo?!?"

"Did he go near the wolf beastmen again!!!"

chapters.source_text:
天色漆黑，大泽旁的两个草棚外，兽人升起火堆。
火堆旁，已经醒来的兔萝身子趴地，将自己团成一个球。
火光昏暗，树影绰绰。
狼兽人来来往往，嘴里叼着根木头，眼睛油绿，像埋伏在这里等着猎物自投罗网的凶兽。
东边蛮草丛中，窸窣一阵响动。
一只尖端白色的兔爪悄悄拨开蛮草，远远看着棚子的方向。待看清那火堆边的兽人，爪子一颤，吓得一屁股坐在地上，都忘了隐藏。
“族、族长……兔兔兔兔萝真的被抓了。”
兔族长颓丧地垂下两个长耳朵，一哆嗦，揪下身上一大戳毛。
“藏不住了。”
兔族长强迫自己镇定，飞快道：“兔艾，你赶紧回去，收拾东西带上族人们离开。”
兔艾：“族长……”
兔族长长叹了一声，摇了摇头，“快去。”
兔艾紧咬着唇，看了那火堆旁的兽人一眼，真恨不能把他抓回来打一顿！
分明族长之前就叮嘱过，不要靠近狼兽人！不要靠近狼兽人！
可兔萝就是不听！
他们本来就在人家部落，上次已经被发现过，狼王放了他们纯属运气。这次送到手上，想想，不死也……
兔艾咬得唇角出血，才没忍住拉上族长一起。
这兔萝！
兔艾狠狠抹了一把眼睛，快速离开。
兔族长软着腿，蹲在蛮草中，看着那火堆边来往的狼兽人。
怎么办……怎么办呢？！
“雨！都这会儿了，兔部落的兽人还没来。”狼金叼着牙刷，瞧着那趴地上的蠢兔子，有些不耐烦了。
兽人领地意识都强，狼兽人只会更强。
先前容忍他们，一是没精力，二是算体谅弱小，再有，他们没招惹到狼兽人跟前来。
现在都送上门，被他们抓了，但凡懂点事儿的，也该派个兽人来好好道个歉。
狼金还烦呢，一想到这群兔兽人藏在他们部落，心安理得享受他们的庇护，心里就不得劲。
他都困了！
再不来，他把这蠢兔子扔大泽里。
狼雨：“你先去睡吧，明天还忙呢。”
狼金看着兔萝，哼了声。
他去水边漱了口，拿着牙刷回来。走了两步，目光一利，抬起头盯着蛮草那边。
试图走出来的兔族长吓得定在原地，被狼金看了个准。
狼金：“来了。”
风吹得火堆扑哧响，地面上映出两个弱小的长耳朵兽人的影子。
兔族长被请到火堆前，手脚僵硬地刚一坐下，趴在地上沾了一身泥灰的兔萝扑进他怀里。
兔族长被他撞得一口气差点没上来，他余光小心注意着狼兽人，嘴角僵硬地抬了抬，笑得像要哭出来。
还没睡的几个狼兽人都出来了，坐在火堆边，身形高大，显得两个保持原型的兔兽人更是弱小。
狼火抱臂，旁边坐的是狼顺。
他一抬眼，目光微凉，“灰兔一族？”
不知道是不是远古血脉的影响，看到狼兽人，兔族长也忍不住想要团成一团。
可抱着他的兔萝还往他身上挤，撕都撕不下来。
兔族长不敢抬头，小心道：“是、是灰兔。”
“藏在我们部落挺久了吧。”狼火有种地盘被兽人染指的感觉，心里不爽，面上自然也没好态度。
兔族长心肝发颤，头垂得更低。
狼雨看了狼火一眼，示意他别这么冲。
狼火白眼一翻，沉声一通问道：“你们部落有多少兽人？老的多少？幼崽多少？青壮年多少？你们什么时候来的？巢在什么地方？说！”
话一落，两个兔兽人一抖，心也凉到了谷底。
还好，还好……
族长庆幸，刚刚叫兔艾赶紧带着族人离开。
“别想着跑，我现在能好好跟你说话，你就好好回答。要是跑了？”狼金冷笑，“我想，你不想知道那个后果。”
兔族长一个冷颤。
兔萝闭着眼睛，忍不住再往兔族长怀里钻，恨不能将自己藏进去。
兔族长被好几双眼睛盯着，一个没忍住，红着眼睛一口冲着兔萝耳朵咬去！
死兔崽子！
叫你不听话！
“呜……阿爸，疼。”
狼火皱眉，面上不耐烦。
兔族长不敢去想狼兽人的手段，在全是凶兽的大部落面前，他们只有听话的份儿。
他不得已，声音嘶哑，一点一点把话从喉咙挤出来：“我们、我们一共有二十七个兽人，没、没老兽人，幼崽两个，其他都成年了……”
他们是三年前从南边来的，当时的部落在距离狼部落很远的一个大湖旁，本来他们住得好好的，但遇到一支专门抢食物的流浪兽人队伍，族人被抓的抓，吃的吃……
后来他们往北逃难，进入了狼部落，才彻底安全。
兔族长带着族人在狼部落边缘忐忑地藏了一段时间，后头发现他们并没有过来，就起了悄悄藏在狼部落的心思。
这一藏，就是三年。
之前雨季遇到一次狼兽人，他们吓得搬了出去，可经历了之前的噩梦，兔兽人不敢在外面呆着，这又回来。
原本，他们就是藏在东边那一片蛮草后头。
蛮草深，又没什么用，兽人不会越过蛮草往东边去，很安全。但谁知道前不久，狼兽人开始收割蛮草，兽人们也吓得立马往更偏僻的地方搬。
现在住的，是往东南边的一处密林的地下。
平常的入口是一个树洞，还有另外几个洞口，分别在蛮草这边，东南边，还有北边。
狼金拎着兔族长，让小狼将几个洞口都堵了。
他们来得极快，族长想拖延，可再一想若是最后沦落到被狼部落追杀，那就连活命都难了。
兔艾急着回来召集族人，要搬家，或许以后再也不会回来。
他们的种子、食物，这些年积攒的东西全部要带走。快雪季了，不带走，他们怕是过不了雪季。
就这么耽搁一阵，一阵青烟从北边跟东南两个方向涌入到中部的巢中，兔艾腿一软，瘫坐下来。
完了，都完了。
“咳！咳咳！怎么回事？”
“咳咳，快离开！”
“不！不能出去！”兔艾一把抓住族人的手。
“不出去就要死了！”族人心一狠，大致知道外面一定有兽人守着了。与其出去当一辈子奴隶，也不要死在里面。
不一会儿，狼金开始清点这些套了一串的兔兽人。
“族长……”兔艾绝望地看着目光呆滞，一言不发的兔族长。
寄生在别人的部落，早知道该有这下场的。
狼金看他们哭哭啼啼，手一挥，道：“带走。”
按照兔族长说的数量，一个不少。
本该是休息时间，还得出来加班，狼兽人一个个冷着脸，看着比当初追杀兔部落的流浪兽人还要可怕。
被抓的兔兽人直接吓晕了不少。
大泽边。
一串儿兔兽人被弄到一处，狼金打个哈欠，赶紧钻棚子里睡觉去。
狼火看了眼，就在旁边坐着，闭目睡觉。
狼雨跟狼虹对视一眼，什么都没说，也离开了。
这火堆附近一下或趴或躺十来个狼兽人，胆子小的兔兽人眼睛一翻，又晕了几个。
兔艾动了动被麻绳套起来的爪子，红着眼睛，刚想动嘴啃，叫兔族长抓住。
他轻轻摇头。
现在还摸不清狼兽人的底细，万一是个阴狠性子，见他们主动把这东西解开，肯定避免不了一顿收拾。
先等等，看他们到底想干什么。
兔艾看了眼他怀中的兔萝一眼，无声叹了口气，倒在火堆旁，眼泪顺着眼角流下来。
兔萝是族长的幼崽，刚出生时就遇上他们被流浪兽人抓捕，亲眼见多了那些流浪兽人抓着他们族人就啃，脑子就有点问题。
他不怎么爱说话，分明在狼兽人过来之前，他很乖。
可狼兽人来了，他像看见个什么好玩的，总喜欢悄悄看着他们。
为此，族长也说过、打过，这下终于是被发现了。
兔艾不知道心里是个什么想法，怨吧，也怨。但提心吊胆在狼部落里住着，这些年找食儿都小心翼翼，连他们最喜欢的菜都没种过了。
这下被抓起来，倒又还有一种尘埃落定的感觉。
这一晚，兔兽人们晕的晕，哭的哭，反正都不敢发出一点声音。
只要看到那不远处趴着的巨狼，就恨不能刨个坑将自己藏起来。余光瞥见那狼嘴，又想到那些流浪兽人一口一个族人脑袋……
兔兽人一晚上没几个能睡着，闭上眼睛，都是噩梦连连，惊出一身冷汗。
伴着狼兽人的呼噜声，大家几乎是熬了一夜。
熬到眼睛干涩，身体保持着一个姿势连动都不敢动，浑身血液凝住，身体早没了知觉。
伴随着一个哈欠声，兔兽人齐齐哆嗦。
一凝神，才发现天已经亮了。
狼金扫了眼这些颓靡的兔兽人，心里总算舒服了点儿。
真当他狼部落的地儿白住的！
狼金怨气散了些，面上还是那冷淡样子，只轻飘飘看了一眼这些个兔兽人，溜溜达达去洗漱。
狼雨跟狼虹睡了个整觉出来，立马开始收拾锅灶。
注意到那一群他们醒来后绷紧身体的兔兽人，也没说什么，手上继续忙着。
兔族人的情况要告诉王跟祭司，具体怎么安排，还得王拿主意。
虽说狼兽人并不欺负弱小，但这群兽人运气不好，正面撞上他们了，如果不处置，传出去还当他们狼部落随意进出呢。
不过，等王那边的消息也得几天后。
这一批莲藕还没挖好，狼火他们肯定不着急回去。
这群兔兽人也不能扔这儿不管，总归还是得叫狼火给安排一下。
正想着，狼火收拾完自己，脸上挂着些水珠，清清爽爽回来了。
只见他往兔族长身边一蹲，手搭在膝上，道：“变个人形看看？”
狼雨一愣，抄起菜板上一快刚切下来的藕节扔过去，“你说什么呢？！”
狼火偏头躲开，意识到自己这话不妥，忙往后摆手，“雨，我就是看看他们人形什么样？”
这兽形缩起来跟个球一样，怕是一截藕都抱不住。
兔族长低下头，旁边兔艾一下挡在他面前，怒得胡须直颤，弹腿踢来。
狼火一把逮住兔耳朵，道：“行，那你变。”
兔艾：“你、你要杀就杀，为什么还要侮辱我们！”
兔族长是失去了伴侣的亚兽人！
叫亚兽人当着雄兽人的面变人形，打的什么心思！
狼火眉心跳了跳，“随便你们，反正出来一个兽人，我看看。”
话落，一个雄兽人出来，低着头变成人身。
兽人人形也受兽形体型大小的影响，像象兽人兽形大，人形基本上也是兽人中最大的，往往人形都两米往上。
而小型兽人，比方说白雀兽人，兔兽人就会矮小一些。
狼岩看着到自己下巴的兔族雄兽人，点点头，“还行。”
他盘腿坐下来，示意几个还炸着毛的兔兽人也坐。看他们还绷着身体怒目瞪来，也无所谓道：“你们的事，得交给我们我们王来定。”
兔兽人一听，跌坐下来，失了精神。
狼火：“回一趟狼山太麻烦，所以我不打算现在走。我们还要在大泽这边留三天，这三天也不能把你们放了，但也不能不管你们。”
“这样，咱们商量商量。”
“这三天我先不追究你们跑到我们部落来的事情，这期间你们给我们干活，交换食物，怎么样？”
狼火说完了，可这群兔兽人跟木头一样，呆呆傻傻，看眼神，一点没把他的话听进去。
狼火“啧”了声。
兔兽人肩膀齐齐一缩。
狼火：“行不行？给句话？”
兔葵，也就是兔族长搂着自己的幼崽，紧着声音道：“做什么活？”
狼雨跟狼虹也停下刀，看着这边。
兔兽人的身体不算弱，看起来比他们当初还要好一点，挖藕也能挖。
但小狼不是在这儿，也不缺兽人。
“捡绒毛。”
狼雨眸光一闪，一下想起林楸当初说的保暖的法子。小狼甚至听了绒羽，专门跑黑羽部落去抢了一番。
兔兽人还懵着，狼雨道：“鸟都飞走了，哪里还有绒。”
“鸟飞走了，绒又没跟着飞走。湖心岛上那么多鸟窝，总不能一点找不出来。”
雨季时候湖心岛多少鸟筑巢，那鸟毛到处都是，路边随处一丛草上都挂着绒朵。
他们忙着挖藕，没空，这不刚好兔兽人撞上来了。
狼雨没继续说，他觉得狼火这主意够聪明。
狼火再问兔葵：“同不同意？”
兔葵被盯着，心脏收紧，搂住幼崽点了下头。
都被抓了，只要不威胁到生命，还有什么不同意的。何况捡个鸟绒而已。
狼火就这么妥帖地将一群兔兽人安排好了。
湖心岛很大，兔兽人自己过不去，得由黑羽兽人把他们带过去。而湖心岛周围的水又深，就算兔兽人会打洞，放在那岛上，他们也跑不掉。
这样既不用兽人盯着，还能叫他们干点活儿，狼兽人想想都忍不住给狼火背上拍一巴掌。
不愧是当队长的兽人！脑子转得就是快！
*
今天天阴，小风吹得湖心岛上的荒草摇曳。
兔兽人全被运了过来，站在岛上，看着黑羽兽人振翅远离。
兔艾搓了搓胳膊，有些冷，“族长，大泽很多长虫，这岛上是不是也有……”
兔葵牵着自家幼崽的手，目光在湖心岛上晃了一圈。
岛上没什么高大树木，只有些灌丛，多数是快要干枯的荒草。雨季时候，这大泽边的鸟群盛景他们也亲眼见过，只这会儿荒草长出来，鸟窝也都藏在草丛中了。
“天冷了，应该都藏起来了。快找吧。”
狼兽人已经跟他们描述过找什么样的绒羽，兔葵叫兽人分散开，仔细着找。
兽人都应下，垂着个脑袋，找了木棍扒拉。
兔兽人身形偏纤细，但胳膊腿儿却有力。因着刨洞，手臂上都是薄薄一层肌肉轮廓。
昨晚被抓得仓促，吃的用的一个没带出来。这会儿变成人形，腰上围着的都是草裙。
湖心岛上的风又没个遮挡，兔兽人常年藏在地下窝里，昨晚熬了一晚，再这么吹上一会儿，不少兽人开始打喷嚏。
兔葵捏着狼兽人给的兽皮兜，想到了雪季。
“阿爸！毛！”
身边兔萝已经蹲下，认认真真地翻出个鸟窝。
稀泥堆砌的鸟窝底部已经干透开裂，里头垫着草，干草当中，一团被自家幼崽掏出来的灰色绒羽叫风一吹，轻轻动了动。
兔葵忙蹲下抓住。
绒羽，陶锅，鸟粪，还有莲藕……
这就是大部落的厉害。
他们比小部落知道得更多，也会制造和挖掘更多的生存资源。
他们现在已经没了退路，要想活下去，最好的办法就是依附于狼部落。
而显然，狼部落也不养闲兽人。
兔葵手指捻着那轻飘飘的一小团绒羽，在兔萝的注视下，放进了兽皮袋里。
他摸一摸自家幼崽的额发。
幼崽额头贴近他手心，瞧着他露出个傻笑来。
兔葵轻声问：“阿萝为什么喜欢看狼兽人？”
兔萝：“他们有吃的。”
“阿爸，他们有好多吃的。”兔萝双手在空中画了个圈，眼神晶亮，兔葵在身边，他就不那么怕狼兽人了。
兔葵心一酸，眼神逐渐变得坚定。
比起从前的流离失所，这何尝不是一次机会呢？
一次给他们自己博一个稳定生活的机会！
*
下雨过后降了温，预示着雪季更进一步。
多数部落已经开始准备雪季的食物，白雀部落的雀二白也收拾收拾，在族人的目送中，准备前往狼部落。
走前，雀二白紧了紧背上的包袱，目光哀戚看着白雀族长。
“族长，我走了啊。”
白雀族长挥一挥翅膀，目光殷切，“你可要好好说话，最好多换一点药回来。”
雀十二白：“二白叔……”
“诶！”雀二白停下，眼里湿漉漉。
“你看路。”
雀二白抬手，“你，就没什么想跟叔说的？”
雀十二白想了想，道：“叔，你快点回来。慢点也没关系。”
雀二白夸张地长叹：“叔年纪大了！背着这些东西肯定走不快，到时候腰酸腿疼的，影响跟狼族祭司交易。你年轻，要不然你帮叔去一趟？”
雀十二白转身，背对洞口。
“族长，我出去捕猎了啊！”
说着不等雀二白开口，飞快蹿上天去。
雀二白忙喊：“十二白啊！看在咱名字里都有个二的面上……”
“你到底走不走了！”白雀族长吼道。
他不想跟他演了。
“雀大白！要是我死在狼山……”
“屁！你都去几次了，没见你死过！赶紧的，部落事儿还多着呢，回来帮忙！”
“雀大白！”
“你走不走！”白雀族长举起石头威胁。
雀二白哼哼唧唧，一甩肩上的兽皮袋，不情不愿地挪步。
呸！
自己怕还让他去！
就是因为一个窝里的，什么累活坏活都让他干！
雀二白骂骂咧咧，带着后头两个小辈走了。
白雀兽人兽形小，速度虽快，但负重实在不行。
这次去狼部落交换，他们带的依旧是几样老祭司曾经指定的草药，还有部落里攒下来的一点肉干。
三个兽人一人一大包，得用人形扛在肩上走。
兽皮袋大得像后背长了个瘤子，坠得三个兽人走路都有些晃悠。
跟大部落交换，他们不敢敷衍。
可步行去狼山，这就慢了。
他们以往都是从东南边绕行，但今年狼兽人直接从北边开辟了一条路，雀二白出来前跟白雀族长商量过，就干脆直接走北边的路。
要是刚好出部落遇到狼兽人，托他们带一截，还能省事儿。没遇到他们就自己走，也能快一点。
就是这一脚踏入人家部落，总瘆得慌。
又不能在部落边缘等着他们来，谁知道要等多久。
雀二白缩着脖子，跟着两个小辈慢吞吞往北边挪。
走了四天，终于，看到了大泽边的狼兽人，还有一群在天上飞来飞去，爪子上不知道抓着什么东西黑羽兽人。
怪说没看见黑羽兽人挖鸟粪，原来被弄来搬东西了。
那东西瞧着是大泽里挖出来的，不知道这狼部落又找到什么好玩意儿。
这会儿狼兽人的气息就在跟前，雀二白不敢掉以轻心。他没敢偷偷摸摸，而是主动走出林子，先隔着远远的，跟那棚子底下的狼兽人打个招呼。
“是狼部落的吗？我们是白雀部落的，想跟你们祭司交换雪季的药！”
大泽当中，几个狼兽人收回锋利的眼神，继续埋头干活。
狼雨擦了擦手，跟狼虹对视一眼，笑着往西侧去。
“雀二。”
“狼雨，我叫雀二白，不是雀二。”
雀二是他阿父跟前头那几辈兽人的名字，从一二三排列下去……后头老一辈兽人们觉得排太长了，干脆在最后加个白，再从一二三开始排，这样就不会串名。
狼雨将三个兽人引到棚子下，雀二白见周围就他两个亚兽人，那哆嗦的心肝儿一下缓和了不少。
他蹲好，两个手臂习惯性拢在腿侧，“我们还打算换药。”
狼雨点头，“今年怎么没走东南？”
雀二白被狼雨眼睛盯着，总觉得下一刻要被拔了毛，宰了吃。
他咽了咽口水，好歹打过几次交道了，不怕不怕。
“我们之前看见你们在那边挖鸟粪，想着近一点，万一在大泽遇见你们，能、能少走点路。”雀二白高高翘起嘴角笑，尽力给狼兽人一个友好的形象。
后头两个兽人也学着咧嘴。
狼雨笑道：“正好狼火他们要回去，你们是跟着一起？还是留在这里？”
雀二白犹豫。
他打心眼里不想靠近狼山，那狼窝里的气息闻一下能噩梦一个月。可雀二白又想着多换一些药，那最好还是自己亲自去跟狼部落祭司商量。
他搓搓酸疼的腿儿，想到部落里那些小崽子，一咬牙，道：“去狼山。”
狼雨：“行，你们歇会儿。等最后一点装了就走。”
雀二白：“那你忙，我们等着。”
雀二白表现得很规矩，不敢多看，也不敢多问，只安安分分地等。后头两个小辈就直接抱着东西，脑袋低着，不敢说话。
稍稍有动静，身体都得绷紧了。
狼雨看在眼里，心里满意。
也就雀兽人这个态度，才叫狼雨放心让他们坐过来。
chapters.title: 第112章
chapters.translated_text:
The sky was pitch black. Outside the two grass sheds by the Great Marsh, the wolf-beastmen lit a bonfire.

Beside the fire, the rabbit-beastman Tu Luo, who had already woken up, lay on the ground, curled into a ball.

The firelight was dim, and the shadows of the trees danced.

Wolf-beastmen walked back and forth, carrying sticks in their mouths, their eyes glowing with a greasy green light, like fierce beasts lying in ambush, waiting for prey to walk right into their trap.

In the wild grass to the east, there was a rustling sound.

A rabbit paw with a white tip quietly parted the wild grass, looking toward the sheds from afar. When it caught sight of the beastmen by the bonfire, the paw trembled, and it sat down on the ground in fright, forgetting even to hide.

"Ch-Chief... Tu Luo really has been caught."

The Rabbit Chief let his two long ears droop in despair, shuddered, and plucked a large tuft of fur from his body.

"We can't hide anymore."

The Rabbit Chief forced himself to stay calm and said quickly, "Tu Ai, hurry back, pack your things, and take the tribespeople away."

Tu Ai: "Chief..."

The Rabbit Chief sighed heavily and shook his head, "Go quickly."

Tu Ai bit his lip tightly, glancing at the beastmen by the fire, wishing he could drag him back and give him a beating!

The Chief had clearly warned them before: do not go near the wolf-beastmen! Do not go near the wolf-beastmen!

But Tu Luo just wouldn't listen!

They were already in their territory; they had been discovered once before, and the Wolf King letting them go was pure luck. Now that they had delivered themselves to his doorstep, just thinking about it, if they didn't die, they would...

Tu Ai bit his lip until it bled, only then managing to hold back from dragging the Chief along with him.

This Tu Luo!

Tu Ai wiped his eyes fiercely and left quickly.

The Rabbit Chief, his legs weak, crouched in the wild grass, watching the wolf-beastmen moving about by the fire.

What to do... what to do?!

"Yu! It's already this late, and the rabbit-beastmen still haven't come." Lang Jin, chewing on a toothbrush, looked at the stupid rabbit lying on the ground, feeling impatient.

Beastmen all have strong territorial instincts, and wolf-beastmen even more so.

They had tolerated them before, first because they lacked the energy, second out of pity for the weak, and third, because they hadn't provoked the wolf-beastmen directly.

Now that they had delivered themselves and been caught, anyone with a bit of sense should have sent a beastman to offer a proper apology.

Lang Jin was annoyed; the thought of these rabbit-beastmen hiding in their territory, enjoying their protection with peace of mind, made him feel uneasy.

He was sleepy!

If they didn't come soon, he would throw this stupid rabbit into the Great Marsh.

Lang Yu: "You go to sleep first; we're busy tomorrow."

Lang Jin looked at Tu Luo and snorted.

He went to the water's edge to rinse his mouth and came back with his toothbrush. After two steps, his gaze sharpened, and he looked up toward the wild grass.

The Rabbit Chief, who had been trying to walk out, was frozen in place, caught right in Lang Jin's sight.

Lang Jin: "They're here."

The wind made the bonfire crackle, casting the shadows of two weak, long-eared beastmen onto the ground.

The Rabbit Chief was invited to the fire. As soon as he sat down, his limbs stiff, Tu Luo, who had been lying on the ground covered in mud and ash, threw himself into his arms.

The Rabbit Chief was hit so hard he almost lost his breath. He carefully kept an eye on the wolf-beastmen, his mouth stiffly lifting into a smile that looked like he was about to cry.

The few wolf-beastmen who hadn't slept yet all came out, sitting by the fire. Their tall, imposing figures made the two rabbit-beastmen, who remained in their original forms, look even weaker.

Lang Huo sat with his arms crossed, with Lang Shun sitting beside him.

He raised his eyes, his gaze cold, "The Gray Rabbit tribe?"

Perhaps due to the influence of their ancient bloodline, upon seeing the wolf-beastmen, the Rabbit Chief couldn't help but want to curl into a ball.

But Tu Luo, who was hugging him, kept pressing into him, impossible to peel away.

The Rabbit Chief dared not look up and said cautiously, "Y-yes, we are Gray Rabbits."

"You've been hiding in our territory for quite a while, haven't you?" Lang Huo felt as if his territory had been tainted by other beastmen. He felt unhappy, and naturally, his expression wasn't pleasant.

The Rabbit Chief's heart trembled, and he lowered his head even further.

Lang Yu glanced at Lang Huo, signaling him not to be so aggressive.

Lang Huo rolled his eyes and asked in a deep voice, "How many beastmen are in your tribe? How many old ones? How many cubs? How many able-bodied adults? When did you arrive? Where is your nest? Speak!"

As soon as he finished speaking, the two rabbit-beastmen shivered, their hearts sinking to the bottom.

Thankfully, thankfully...

The Chief was glad he had just told Tu Ai to take the tribe and leave quickly.

"Don't think about running. I can talk to you properly now, so you answer properly. If you run?" Lang Jin sneered, "I think you don't want to know the consequences."

The Rabbit Chief shivered.

Tu Luo closed his eyes, unable to stop himself from burrowing further into the Rabbit Chief's arms, wishing he could hide inside him.

With several pairs of eyes staring at him, the Rabbit Chief couldn't help it; with red eyes, he bit down on Tu Luo's ear!

You damn rabbit brat!

I told you not to be disobedient!

"Wuu... Dad, it hurts."

Lang Huo frowned, looking impatient.

The Rabbit Chief dared not think about the wolf-beastmen's methods; in front of a large tribe full of fierce beasts, they only had the option of being obedient.

He had no choice, his voice hoarse, squeezing the words out of his throat bit by bit: "We, we have twenty-seven beastmen in total, no, no old beastmen, two cubs, the rest are all adults..."

They had come from the south three years ago. Their tribe at the time was by a large lake far from the Wolf tribe. They had been living well, but they encountered a group of wandering beastmen who specialized in stealing food. Their tribespeople were captured or eaten...

Later, they fled north and entered the Wolf tribe's territory, only then becoming truly safe.

The Rabbit Chief had led his tribe to hide on the edge of the Wolf tribe's territory in trepidation for a while. Later, when they realized the wolf-beastmen didn't come over, they got the idea to hide quietly within the Wolf tribe.

They had been hiding like this for three years.

They had encountered wolf-beastmen once during the rainy season and were so scared they moved out, but after experiencing the nightmare before, the rabbit-beastmen didn't dare stay outside, so they came back.

Originally, they were hiding behind that patch of wild grass to the east.

The wild grass was deep and useless, and the beastmen wouldn't cross the wild grass to go east, so it was safe. But who knew that not long ago, the wolf-beastmen started harvesting the wild grass, and the beastmen were so scared they immediately moved to a more remote place.

They were currently living underground in a dense forest to the southeast.

The usual entrance was a tree hole, and there were several other exits located on the side of the wild grass, to the southeast, and to the north.

Lang Jin grabbed the Rabbit Chief and had the young wolves block all the exits.

They moved extremely fast. The Chief wanted to stall, but then he thought that if they ended up being hunted by the Wolf tribe, they wouldn't even be able to survive.

Tu Ai was in a hurry to return and gather the tribespeople to move; perhaps they would never come back.

Their seeds, food, and everything they had accumulated over the years had to be taken. The Snow Season was coming; if they didn't take it, they probably wouldn't survive the season.

Just as they were delayed for a moment, a cloud of blue smoke poured into the central nest from the north and southeast directions. Tu Ai's legs went weak, and he collapsed.

It's over, it's all over.

"Cough! Cough, cough! What's going on?"

"Cough, cough, hurry and leave!"

"No! We can't go out!" Tu Ai grabbed his tribesman's hand.

"If we don't go out, we'll die!" The tribesman steeled his heart, knowing roughly that there must be beastmen guarding outside. Rather than going out to be slaves for life, he would rather not die inside.

Before long, Lang Jin began to count these rabbit-beastmen who were tied in a string.

"Chief..." Tu Ai looked desperately at the Rabbit Chief, who was staring blankly and not saying a word.

Parasitizing someone else's tribe, they should have known this would be the outcome.

Lang Jin saw them crying and wailing, waved his hand, and said, "Take them away."

According to the number the Rabbit Chief gave, not a single one was missing.

It should have been rest time, but they had to work overtime. The wolf-beastmen all had cold faces, looking even more terrifying than the wandering beastmen who had hunted the Rabbit tribe back then.

Many of the captured rabbit-beastmen were scared into fainting.

By the Great Marsh.

A string of rabbit-beastmen were brought to one place. Lang Jin yawned and hurried into the shed to sleep.

Lang Huo glanced at them, sat down nearby, and closed his eyes to sleep.

Lang Yu and Lang Hong exchanged a look, said nothing, and left as well.

With a dozen wolf-beastmen lying or crouching around the fire, the timid rabbit-beastmen rolled their eyes and fainted again.

Tu Ai moved his paws, which were tied with hemp rope, his eyes red. Just as he was about to chew through them, the Rabbit Chief grabbed him.

He shook his head gently.

They didn't know the wolf-beastmen's bottom line yet. If they were the cruel type, seeing them untie this on their own would definitely lead to a beating.

Wait a bit and see what they really want to do.

Tu Ai glanced at Tu Luo in his arms, sighed silently, and collapsed by the fire, tears streaming down his face.

Tu Luo was the Chief's cub. When he was born, they encountered the capture by wandering beastmen. Seeing those wandering beastmen grab their tribespeople and chew on them, his mind was a bit affected.

He didn't like to talk much, but clearly, before the wolf-beastmen came, he was very well-behaved.

But when the wolf-beastmen came, he seemed to see something fun and always liked to watch them quietly.

For this, the Chief had scolded and hit him, and now they had finally been discovered.

Tu Ai didn't know what he was feeling. Resentment? Yes, there was resentment. But living in the Wolf tribe with constant fear, they had been careful about finding food all these years, not even planting their favorite vegetables.

Now that they were caught, there was a strange sense of finality.

That night, the rabbit-beastmen either fainted or cried, but none dared to make a sound.

Whenever they saw the giant wolves lying not far away, they wished they could dig a hole to hide in. A glimpse of those wolf mouths reminded them of the wandering beastmen who ate their tribespeople head by head...

Few of the rabbit-beastmen could sleep all night; closing their eyes brought endless nightmares, breaking out in cold sweat.

Accompanied by the snoring of the wolf-beastmen, everyone stayed up almost all night.

They stayed up until their eyes were dry, their bodies kept in one position without daring to move, their blood feeling frozen, and their bodies long since numb.

Accompanied by a yawn, the rabbit-beastmen shivered in unison.

Focusing their minds, they realized it was already dawn.

Lang Jin glanced at these listless rabbit-beastmen, and his heart finally felt a bit better.

They really thought they could live in his Wolf tribe's territory for free!

Lang Jin's resentment dissipated a bit, but his expression remained cold. He just glanced lightly at these rabbit-beastmen and strolled off to wash up.

Lang Yu and Lang Hong woke up after a full night's sleep and immediately started cleaning up the stove.

Noticing the rabbit-beastmen who stiffened their bodies after waking up, they didn't say anything and continued with their work.

The situation with the rabbit-beastmen had to be reported to the King and the Priest; the King would have to make the final decision on how to arrange them.

Although the wolf-beastmen didn't bully the weak, these beastmen were unlucky to run into them head-on. If they weren't dealt with, word would get out that the Wolf tribe could be entered and exited at will.

However, it would be a few days before they got news from the King.

This batch of lotus roots hadn't been finished yet, so Lang Huo and the others certainly weren't in a hurry to go back.

These rabbit-beastmen couldn't be left here unattended, so they would have to let Lang Huo arrange something.

Just as he was thinking about it, Lang Huo finished cleaning himself, came back fresh with water droplets on his face.

He squatted down beside the Rabbit Chief, hands on his knees, and said, "Change into human form and let me see?"

Lang Yu was stunned, picked up a piece of lotus root just cut on the cutting board, and threw it over, "What are you saying?!"

Lang Huo tilted his head to dodge, realizing his words were inappropriate, and waved his hands back, "Yu, I just want to see what they look like in human form?"

In beast form, they curled up like a ball; they probably couldn't even hold a piece of lotus root.

The Rabbit Chief lowered his head, and Tu Ai immediately blocked him, his whiskers trembling with anger, kicking his legs.

Lang Huo grabbed his rabbit ears and said, "Fine, then you change."

Tu Ai: "You, if you want to kill us, then kill us, why do you have to insult us!"

The Rabbit Chief was a sub-beastman who had lost his mate!

Asking a sub-beastman to change into human form in front of male beastmen, what kind of intention was that!

Lang Huo's brow twitched, "Whatever, just have one beastman come out, I'll take a look."

As soon as he finished, a male beastman came out, lowered his head, and changed into human form.

The human form of a beastman is also affected by the size of the beast form. Like elephant-beastmen, whose beast forms are large, their human forms are basically the largest among beastmen, often over two meters tall.

And small beastmen, such as White Sparrow beastmen or rabbit-beastmen, would be shorter.

Lang Yan looked at the rabbit-beastman who reached his chin and nodded, "Not bad."

He sat cross-legged and signaled the few rabbit-beastmen who were still bristling to sit down too. Seeing them still tense and glaring, he said indifferently, "Your matter must be decided by our King."

When the rabbit-beastmen heard this, they collapsed, losing their spirit.

Lang Huo: "Going back to Wolf Mountain is too much trouble, so I don't plan to leave now. We will stay by the Great Marsh for three more days. We can't let you go during these three days, but we can't ignore you either."

"How about this, let's discuss it."

"For these three days, I won't hold you accountable for running into our tribe. During this time, you work for us, and we exchange food, how about that?"

Lang Huo finished speaking, but these rabbit-beastmen were like wood, dull and stupid. Looking at their eyes, they hadn't taken in a word he said.

Lang Huo "tsk"ed.

The rabbit-beastmen's shoulders shrank in unison.

Lang Huo: "Yes or no? Give me an answer?"

Tu Kui, the Rabbit Chief, hugged his cub and said in a tight voice, "What work?"

Lang Yu and Lang Hong also stopped their knives and looked over.

The rabbit-beastmen's bodies weren't weak; they looked even better than they had back then, so they could dig lotus roots too.

But the young wolves weren't here, and they weren't short of beastmen.

"Gather down."

Lang Yu's eyes flashed, and he immediately remembered the method for keeping warm that Lin Qiu had mentioned. The young wolf had even heard about down feathers and specifically ran to the Black Feather tribe to snatch some.

The rabbit-beastmen were still confused. Lang Yu said, "The birds have all flown away, where would there still be down?"

"The birds flew away, but the down didn't fly away with them. There are so many bird nests on the island in the middle of the lake; there must be some to be found."

During the rainy season, so many birds nested on the island in the middle of the lake; bird feathers were everywhere, and down tufts were hanging on bushes along the road.

They were busy digging lotus roots and didn't have time, and now the rabbit-beastmen had just happened to run into them.

Lang Yu didn't continue, thinking Lang Huo's idea was clever enough.

Lang Huo asked Tu Kui again: "Do you agree?"

Tu Kui was stared at, his heart tightening, and he hugged his cub and nodded.

They were already caught; as long as it didn't threaten their lives, what else could they disagree with? Besides, it was just gathering bird down.

Lang Huo had arranged for the group of rabbit-beastmen so neatly.

The island in the middle of the lake was very large; the rabbit-beastmen couldn't get there themselves and had to be taken by the Black Feather beastmen. And the water around the island was deep, so even if the rabbit-beastmen knew how to dig holes, they couldn't run away once they were on the island.

This way, they didn't need beastmen to watch them, and they could still get them to do some work. The wolf-beastmen couldn't help but want to pat Lang Huo on the back.

As expected of a beastman who is a captain! His brain turns fast!

*

It was cloudy today, and a light breeze made the wild grass on the island in the middle of the lake sway.

All the rabbit-beastmen were transported over and stood on the island, watching the Black Feather beastmen flap their wings and fly away.

Tu Ai rubbed his arms, feeling a bit cold, "Chief, there are many long worms in the Great Marsh, I wonder if there are any on this island..."

Tu Kui held his cub's hand, his gaze sweeping across the island.

There were no tall trees on the island, only some shrubs, mostly wild grass that was about to wither. During the rainy season, they had seen the spectacular sight of bird flocks by the Great Marsh with their own eyes, but now that the wild grass had grown, the bird nests were hidden in the grass.

"It's cold, they should all be hidden. Let's hurry and find them."

The wolf-beastmen had already described to them what kind of down feathers to look for. Tu Kui told the beastmen to spread out and search carefully.

The beastmen all agreed, lowering their heads and using wooden sticks to poke around.

The rabbit-beastmen were slender, but their arms and legs were powerful. Because of digging holes, their arms had a thin layer of muscle definition.

They were caught in a hurry last night, and they didn't bring any food or supplies. Now that they were in human form, they were all wearing grass skirts around their waists.

The wind on the island had no shelter, and the rabbit-beastmen had lived in underground nests for years. After staying up all night, and now being blown by the wind for a while, many beastmen started sneezing.

Tu Kui pinched the animal skin pouch given by the wolf-beastmen and thought of the Snow Season.

"Dad! Feathers!"

Beside him, Tu Luo had already squatted down and was earnestly turning over a bird nest.

The bottom of the bird nest, built of mud, had dried and cracked, lined with grass inside. Among the dry grass, a tuft of gray down feathers that his cub had dug out moved gently in the wind.

Tu Kui hurriedly squatted down and grabbed it.

Down feathers, pottery pots, bird droppings, and lotus roots...

This is the power of a large tribe.

They knew more than small tribes and could manufacture and excavate more survival resources.

They had no way back now; if they wanted to survive, the best way was to attach themselves to the Wolf tribe.

And clearly, the Wolf tribe didn't keep idle beastmen.

Tu Kui twisted the light tuft of down feathers with his fingers and, under Tu Luo's gaze, put it into the animal skin bag.

He stroked his cub's forehead hair.

The cub pressed his forehead against his palm, looking at him with a silly smile.

Tu Kui asked softly: "Why does A-Luo like to watch the wolf-beastmen?"

Tu Luo: "They have food."

"Dad, they have so much food." Tu Luo drew a circle in the air with his hands, his eyes bright. With Tu Kui by his side, he wasn't so afraid of the wolf-beastmen anymore.

Tu Kui's heart ached, and his eyes gradually became firm.

Compared to their previous displacement, wasn't this an opportunity?

An opportunity to fight for a stable life for themselves!

*

The temperature dropped after the rain, signaling that the Snow Season was getting closer.

Most tribes had already started preparing food for the Snow Season. Que Erbai of the White Sparrow tribe also packed up and, amidst the farewells of his tribespeople, prepared to head to the Wolf tribe.

Before leaving, Que Erbai tightened the bundle on his back, looking at the White Sparrow Chief with a sorrowful expression.

"Chief, I'm leaving now."

The White Sparrow Chief flapped his wings, his gaze earnest, "You must speak well, and it would be best to exchange for more medicine."

Que Shierbai: "Uncle Erbai..."

"Yeah!" Que Erbai stopped, his eyes wet.

"Watch the road."

Que Erbai raised his hand, "You, don't you have anything else to say to your uncle?"

Que Shierbai thought for a moment and said, "Uncle, come back quickly. It's okay if you're slow."

Que Erbai sighed dramatically: "Your uncle is old! Carrying these things, I definitely won't be able to walk fast. By then, my waist will ache and my legs will hurt, which will affect the trade with the Wolf tribe's Priest. You're young, why don't you help your uncle go?"

Que Shierbai turned around, back to the cave entrance.

"Chief, I'm going out to hunt!"

Saying this, without waiting for Que Erbai to speak, he quickly darted into the sky.

Que Erbai hurriedly shouted: "Shierbai! For the sake of us both having 'Er' in our names..."

"Are you leaving or not!" the White Sparrow Chief roared.

He didn't want to act with him anymore.

"Que Dabai! If I die on Wolf Mountain..."

"Bullshit! You've been there several times, and I haven't seen you die! Hurry up, there's still a lot to do in the tribe, come back and help!"

"Que Dabai!"

"Are you leaving!" The White Sparrow Chief raised a stone in threat.

Que Erbai grumbled, swung the animal skin bag on his shoulder, and moved reluctantly.

Pfft!

He's afraid himself and makes him go!

Just because they were from the same nest, he makes him do all the tiring and bad work!

Que Erbai cursed and grumbled, taking the two juniors behind him and leaving.

White Sparrow beastmen have small beast forms; although they are fast, their load-bearing capacity is really not good.

This time, when going to the Wolf tribe to exchange, they still brought a few medicinal herbs specified by the old Priest, as well as a little dried meat saved by the tribe.

The three beastmen each had a large bag, which they had to carry on their shoulders in human form.

The animal skin bags were so large they looked like tumors growing on their backs, making the three beastmen walk a bit unsteadily.

They didn't dare to be perfunctory when exchanging with a large tribe.

But walking to Wolf Mountain was slow.

They used to go around from the southeast, but this year the wolf-beastmen had opened a road directly from the north. Before Que Erbai left, he had discussed it with the White Sparrow Chief, so they decided to just take the northern road.

If they happened to run into wolf-beastmen when leaving the tribe, they could ask them to carry a part of it, which would save effort. If they didn't run into them, they would walk themselves, which would also be faster.

It was just that stepping into someone else's tribe always made one feel uneasy.

And they couldn't wait on the edge of the tribe for them to come; who knew how long they would have to wait.

Que Erbai shrank his neck and followed the two juniors, moving slowly toward the north.

After walking for four days, they finally saw the wolf-beastmen by the Great Marsh, as well as a group of Black Feather beastmen flying back and forth in the sky, holding something in their claws.

No wonder they hadn't seen the Black Feather beastmen digging bird droppings; it turned out they had been brought to move things.

That thing looked like it was dug out of the Great Marsh; I wonder what good stuff this Wolf tribe had found again.

At this moment, the scent of the wolf-beastmen was right in front of them, and Que Erbai didn't dare to be careless. He didn't dare to sneak around, but instead took the initiative to walk out of the forest, first greeting the wolf-beastmen under the shed from a distance.

"Are you from the Wolf tribe? We are from the White Sparrow tribe and want to exchange with your Priest for medicine for the Snow Season!"

In the Great Marsh, several wolf-beastmen withdrew their sharp gazes and continued to bury their heads in their work.

Lang Yu wiped his hands, exchanged a look with Lang Hong, and smiled as he walked toward the west side.

"Que Er."

"Lang Yu, my name is Que Erbai, not Que Er."

Que Er was the name of his father and the generations of beastmen before him, arranged in order from one, two, three... Later, the older generation of beastmen felt the list was too long, so they simply added 'Bai' at the end and started from one, two, three again, so the names wouldn't get mixed up.

Lang Yu led the three beastmen to the shed. Seeing that there were only two sub-beastmen around, Que Erbai's trembling heart calmed down a lot.

He squatted down, his two arms habitually folded at his sides, "We still want to exchange for medicine."

Lang Yu nodded, "Why didn't you go from the southeast this year?"

Que Erbai was stared at by Lang Yu's eyes, always feeling that he would be plucked and slaughtered for food in the next moment.

He swallowed his saliva; at least they had dealt with each other a few times, so don't be afraid, don't be afraid.

"We saw you digging bird droppings over there before, and thought it would be closer. In case we ran into you at the Great Marsh, we could, could walk less." Que Erbai raised the corners of his mouth high and smiled, trying his best to give the wolf-beastmen a friendly image.

The two beastmen behind him also learned to grin.

Lang Yu smiled: "It just so happens that Lang Huo and the others are going back. Are you going with them? Or staying here?"

Que Erbai hesitated.

He didn't want to go near Wolf Mountain from the bottom of his heart; the scent in that wolf den could give him nightmares for a month. But Que Erbai also wanted to exchange for more medicine, so it would be best to discuss it with the Wolf tribe's Priest in person.

He rubbed his aching legs, thought of the little cubs in the tribe, gritted his teeth, and said, "Go to Wolf Mountain."

Lang Yu: "Okay, you guys rest for a while. We'll leave once the last bit is loaded."

Que Erbai: "Then you go ahead and get busy, we'll wait."

Que Erbai behaved very properly, not daring to look more or ask more, just waiting quietly. The two juniors behind him just held their things, heads lowered, not daring to speak.

Even the slightest movement made their bodies tense up.

Lang Yu saw it in his eyes and was satisfied.

It was only with this attitude from the Sparrow beastmen that Lang Yu felt at ease letting them sit over.

chapters.title: 第113章
chapters.translated_text:
Just past mid-morning, all the newly dug lotus roots were brought ashore.

Many beastmen came this time; the Black Feather beastmen and the young wolves dug for lotus roots, while the members of the second hunting squad went around catching long worms to make into jerky. The supplies brought back this time filled ten flatbed carts.

The rabbit beastmen had relied on gathering downy tufts to trade for food over the past few days. By accumulating little by little, they had actually managed to fill an entire animal skin bag.

However, Lang Huo did not intend to bring the rabbit beastmen along; he would wait until he returned and asked the King before making any arrangements.

Lang Huo tied the animal skin bag filled with downy tufts tightly and placed it directly into the cart he was pulling.

These things were light and airy, making them exceptionally warm when spread out in a grass nest. After getting familiar with the Black Feather beastmen, the wolf beastmen had even specifically run into their nests to roll around and experience it for themselves.

Lang Huo told the rabbit beastmen to hurry up and find more, the more the better.

On the return journey, three White Sparrow beastmen followed along.

The items they brought were placed directly on the flatbed carts, while they themselves flew alongside the wolf beastmen.

Lang Huo and the beastmen were rushing back to have that midday meal, flying without stopping, until the wings of Que Erbai and the others were almost broken.

Finally, with Wolf Mountain in sight, the breath they had been holding was released, and the three White Sparrow beastmen fell straight down.

Lang Huo instinctively caught one in each claw, scaring the two little White Sparrow beastmen so much that they couldn't catch their breath and fainted with their heads tilted to the side.

Lang Huo gave a flick of his hand, passing the two fainted little White Sparrows to Que Erbai, who was swaying in mid-air like a drunkard. "I didn't do anything."

Que Erbai flapped his heavy wings. "I-I know."

Seeing a group of cubs staring at them, Lang Huo waved his hand, and the cubs ran over in a swarm.

Lang Huo: "Take them to the Priest."

The cubs looked at what he was holding and then looked up. "Uncle Huo, are we eating them?"

Que Erbai shuddered.

Lang Huo: "Stop joking, can't you see they're about to be scared to death?"

Lang Sheng giggled, grabbed the two little White Sparrows, then grabbed Que Erbai and shoved him into the hands of a nearby cub. "Go! Find the Priest!"

Que Erbai's throat tightened, and he rolled his eyes back, sticking out his tongue.

The cub hurriedly let go.

He watched the White Sparrow's wings stretch backward and asked, "What do you want?"

Que Erbai's legs twitched. "The things we brought..."

Lang Huo: "Don't worry, I'll have the young wolves deliver them."

The cubs ran off in a flurry, and Que Erbai felt as if his brain had been shaken into a mush. By the time he was placed on the platform in front of the Priest's cave, his legs were wobbling, and he flopped onto the ground with a thud.

Wolf beastman cubs... bullying, bullying a bird too much!

*

"King! Qiu! We're back!" Before they even arrived, Lang Huo shouted toward Wolf Mountain several times.

Lang An and Lin Qiu came out of the weaving cave; they had just been taking inventory of the linen to see how many tops they could make.

Hearing this, Lin Qiu said, "The King went hunting, he's not here."

Seeing Lang Huo's excitement, Lang An laughed, "He must have brought back good things."

Lang Huo opened the sack filled with downy feathers, and a few tufts floated out; he hurriedly grabbed them and stuffed them back in.

Lin Qiu: "Where did these come from?"

Lang Huo: "Found them."

Lang Jin leaned over, "We caught some rabbit beastmen and had them gather them."

Lang An touched the fluffy tufts, not daring to breathe too heavily. "Didn't the rabbit beastmen leave? How did they come back?"

Lang Jin hummed, "Our tribe has a good life, that's why."

While the beastmen were talking, Lin Qiu grabbed a handful of the down, shielding it from the wind to inspect it.

The bird down was fluffy and light as air, without any weight. Perhaps because it had been shed for a while, there wasn't much of a smell.

The colors were white and gray, all large tufts of down, mostly very clean with no impurities inside.

These rabbit beastmen had gathered them quite carefully.

"Qiu, how is it?" Seeing a few tufts blown away, Lang Huo hurriedly held his breath and reached out to catch them back.

Lin Qiu carefully put them back and tied the mouth of the animal skin bag tight. "Very good."

Lang Huo: "It's a pity there isn't much now. These were found by twenty-something rabbit beastmen over several days. The heart of the lake island has almost been completely turned over by the beastmen."

Lin Qiu: "The tribe's animal skins are barely enough; we'll take whatever we can find."

Lang An lifted the skin bag to test its weight and nodded. "We still have so much wolf fur, it's enough to pad the nests."

The downy feathers would be stored for now, and the matter of the rabbit beastmen would have to wait until Lang Yan returned.

The beastmen who had just run back from the Great Marsh started clamoring that they were hungry. Lang An called a few sub-beastmen to cook for them, while Lin Qiu took inventory of the items brought back.

There was a little bit of lotus root left from the last trip, so Lang An cooked it for them to eat.

The newly transported lotus roots filled eight flatbed carts; the remaining cart contained jerky, and another had various plant tubers, all found by Lang Yu and Lang Hong when they had free time.

Don't let the amount fool you; if a hundred or so beastmen ate to their hearts' content, it wouldn't last many meals.

Once the items were put away, Lin Qiu came out and saw Lang An beckoning to him.

"Qiu, go to the Priest's cave and take a look, the White Sparrow beastmen are here."

"I still have to cut grass..."

"Oh! Forget the grass." Lang An pushed him. "The King isn't here, you go and keep watch, don't let the Priest be coaxed by the White Sparrows into giving away too much."

Lin Qiu laughed, "Alright, I'll go."

Lang An also laughed, "You are the King's partner, this is how it should be."

Lin Qiu climbed up to the Priest's cave, and as soon as his feet touched the ground, he heard the old Priest calling him inside.

"Been waiting for you for a long time, why did you just come up?" The old Priest told him to sit.

Lin Qiu: "What were you waiting for me for?"

"What do you think?" The old Priest glared at him.

The Wolf Tribe was special; the Wolf King was the leader of the entire tribe, and once he had a partner, the two beastmen would govern the tribe together.

The things Lin Qiu had done earlier were already part of his participation in building the Wolf Tribe, and the beastmen listened to him, having long ago accepted them as a pair.

Now that they were openly together, with Lang Yan away, Lin Qiu had to be there when it involved matters between the two tribes.

This was the second time Lin Qiu had seen the White Sparrow beastmen.

They were still fluffy fur balls, about the same size, and the two fur balls were lying on a grass mat with their eyes closed. The other one remained in human form, sitting on a stool beside the grass mat, looking slightly restrained.

The White Sparrow beastman in human form looked much shorter than the wolf beastmen; the one in front of him probably only reached his shoulder.

Lin Qiu: "What's wrong with the two of them?"

Que Erbai smiled weakly, "They're young and inexperienced, they were just... just..."

"Lang Huo caught them, they got a fright and fainted, nothing serious," the old Priest said casually.

Lin Qiu: "Sorry."

Que Erbai hurriedly waved his hands and shook his head, "No, no, it's their own fault for being timid."

Seeing the chapped skin on the corners of his mouth, Lin Qiu stood up and poured him a cup of water.

The Priest was also a bit of a glutton; the water was infused with the jam they had made earlier, and it tasted sweet and sour.

"Drink some, rest for a bit."

Seeing that Lin Qiu looked easy to talk to, Que Erbai carefully took it and took a sip.

The sweetness filled his mouth, and Que Erbai couldn't help but gulp down a large mouthful.

The old Priest watched with a pained heart; he only had the last small jar of jam left.

After Que Erbai rested and caught his breath, the two White Sparrow beastmen lying on the ground also woke up. The old Priest's remaining sweet water didn't survive; it was all given to the other two beastmen.

Little Wolf brought all the things the White Sparrow beastmen had brought to the cave. Que Erbai remembered the main business, licked his lips with lingering desire, and hurriedly straightened his expression.

"Wolf Priest, we came this time to exchange for medicine for the Snow Season again."

The old Priest stood up and walked toward the animal skin bag the White Sparrows had brought. "Let me see what you've brought?"

Que Erbai stood up, and the other two White Sparrow beastmen helped untie the animal skin bags.

Lin Qiu also went over and heard Que Erbai introduce, "The medicinal herbs you wanted took us half a year to find this many; they are all washed clean and dried."

The old Priest grabbed a handful to look and nodded.

Lin Qiu: "Are these Joint Grass and Mist Flower Grass?"

The old Priest: "Yes."

The White Sparrow beastmen lived in the Stone Forest, and some medicinal herbs liked to grow there. Joint Grass was a straight stalk that grew like bone joints and could treat broken bones; Mist Flower Grass had blossoms as hazy as white mist and could neutralize toxins.

"According to what we discussed before, one animal skin bag of herbs for one jar of ointment."

"Wolf Priest, we also have..." Que Erbai looked behind him, and the two little White Sparrows hurriedly brought up the animal skin bag filled with jerky.

"Jerky, can we trade this?"

The White Sparrows' animal skin bag was half the size of the Wolf Tribe's, about as high as Lin Qiu's thigh, and could hold twenty or thirty catties of jerky.

The little White Sparrows were afraid it wouldn't sell, so they picked two large pieces and handed them to Lin Qiu and the old Priest with eager eyes.

White Sparrow beastmen had round eyes, and looking at people so cautiously made one's heart soften.

Que Erbai said, "The jerky is made from good meat. We dried it well and added salt, so it can be preserved until the Snow Season."

Lin Qiu flipped through the jerky to inspect it; it was indeed dried well, with no burnt parts. The saltiness was a bit light, but it was evenly applied.

The Wolf Tribe used to roast jerky this way too, but this year was different. Under Lin Qiu's guidance, the beastmen would marinate it with spices like Sichuan peppercorns and spicy grass, making the flavor much better.

Regardless of the taste, this was meat, rare meat.

The old Priest looked at Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu nodded, "It's acceptable."

Que Erbai's tense nerves relaxed, and he revealed a smile.

The old Priest said, "How about this, for the two types of herbs earlier, I can give you one jar for coughs and one jar for preventing frostbite. This bag of jerky can also be traded for one jar. Which one do you want?"

Lin Qiu had also participated in making the old Priest's ointment. One jar of ointment was only the size of a palm, but it was extremely costly in terms of herbs.

A beastman would eat one spoonful at a time, enough for twenty or thirty doses, and common illnesses would be cured after a few doses.

Medicine should be potent, not plentiful, and Que Erbai clearly thought the same.

He asked, "Is there anything that makes it less easy to get sick during the Snow Season?"

The old Priest thought for a moment and nodded, "That would be for dispelling cold, but there's no ointment for that, only raw herbs for now."

"Raw herbs are fine too!" Que Erbai said, slightly eager.

He was afraid the old Priest wouldn't give it to them.

Seeing the old Priest look over, Lin Qiu raised an eyebrow, "You aren't talking about the ginger planted in the ground, are you?"

The old Priest: "Look, the wild ginger in my cave is all used up."

Compared to trading for a small jar of ointment, trading for raw herbs could get them much more.

The old Priest and Que Erbai went back and forth, and finally, they settled on one bag of jerky for half a bag of ginger.

The ginger was especially fresh and had to be dug up on the spot.

Hearing that they needed to dig ginger, the free beastmen in the tribe all came out with bone shovels.

Since the wild ginger had been transplanted, it had grown from a single root to a cluster, and the leaves were already a bit withered.

The ground was usually managed by the beastmen, so there were no weeds, and the soil was very loose. There was no need for bone shovels; they could just grab the stalks and pull, and it would come out by the roots.

A strong, pungent smell of ginger made the beastmen sneeze repeatedly.

Que Erbai, with the two little White Sparrows, followed closely behind Lin Qiu. They watched as the beastmen grabbed the pulled-up wild ginger and tapped it; the mud fell away, revealing yellowish ginger chunks.

Just pulling a few clusters was enough for half an animal skin bag.

The three White Sparrow beastmen opened their eyes wide as they looked at the row of straight ginger leaves, extending from right in front of them to the east end, as long as several collapsed stone forests put together.

If they harvested it all, they could at least fill ten of their animal skin bags!

So, so much!

Lang Rong was responsible for looking after these plants; he recorded the fertilizing and weeding on animal skins. These herbs growing so well was partly his credit.

When the ginger was first planted, the beastmen had seen with their own eyes a piece the size of a palm being buried in the soil. In the blink of an eye, this pull yielded a piece the size of a rice bowl.

The beastmen were delighted and got into the rhythm of pulling.

"Qiu! Why don't we harvest it all together!"

Lin Qiu: "That works."

This was the time for harvesting wild ginger anyway.

The beastmen forgot all about the White Sparrows and pulled away with enthusiasm.

In front of the White Sparrow beastmen, Lin Qiu picked out some of the older ginger, shook off the dirt, and neatly placed it into their animal skin bag.

"Ginger dispels cold. If you catch a chill or are about to go to a cold place, take a palm-sized piece, slice it, and boil it in water. Don't use too much water. Drinking it can slightly prevent illness. However, the most important thing during the Snow Season is keeping warm, otherwise, no amount of herbs will be useful."

After Lin Qiu finished speaking, he looked up and saw two pairs of watery eyes looking at him.

It was the two little White Sparrows.

White Sparrow beastmen had a youthful appearance, and their adult form was also a fluffy ball of white feathers.

They seemed afraid to take human form in the Wolf Tribe; they had only changed for a moment in the cave, and now they had shrunk back into fluffy balls.

Lin Qiu probed, "How about staying for a meal?"

Que Erbai looked at Lin Qiu, secretly pondering his status in the Wolf Tribe.

The two little White Sparrows didn't dare to nod.

Que Erbai thought of the scene where they were surrounded by wolf beastmen and their food was shared away, swallowed hard, and hurriedly shook his head. "No need! We'll just take the herbs and go."

They hadn't brought much, so they could fly away in one go.

Seeing this, Lin Qiu didn't say anything more.

The old Priest said, "Call Lang Huo to see you off."

The wolf beastmen naturally wouldn't watch the White Sparrows fly alone in their own tribe. Lang Huo and the squad of beastmen ate their fill and flew them all the way to the Great Marsh in one go, and Lang Huo stayed there to continue digging lotus roots.

The herbs were seeding and the wild ginger was mature, so the beastmen simply harvested all the herbs that could be picked.

They kept enough seeds for next year and dried the rest to store in the caves.

The sky grew dark, and clouds gathered again.

On the stove, the clay pot was steaming, and the fresh fragrance of lotus root permeated the air.

It was already the usual time for dinner, but the beastmen who had gone out hunting and gathering hadn't returned. Lang couldn't wait and ran to the top of Wolf Mountain to check.

The evening chill was heavier, and Lin Qiu rubbed his arms, walked under the shed, and found a sheltered spot to sit.

The beastmen were more cold-resistant than him, most still wearing only a pair of shorts. They squatted under the shed and urged Lang Mo and the others: "The house is built, it's time to build the shed."

"It needs to be windproof for the Snow Season, otherwise it's cold when drinking soup."

"If only we could build a heated bed..."

Lang Mo jumped up and scolded: "Why don't you say you want to build a heated bed in your own nest!"

The beastman thought about it, as if imagining something wonderful, and laughed foolishly: "That's not impossible."

Seeing Lin Qiu there, Lang Mo pulled him over and said, "Qiu, how should we build it?"

Lin Qiu looked up at the grass roof and said, "The roof needs to be changed."

"Change it!"

"How thick is the snow in the Snow Season?"

The beastman: "Very thick! Just at our cave entrance, if you jump down, you can bury an entire beastman."

Lin Qiu looked at the waist-high low wall. "The rainy season is wet and hot, sealing it completely won't work."

"Then what should we do..."

Lin Qiu: "How about this: reinforce the shed with bricks, keep the low wall at this height, and weave some grass curtains to hang. Block the snow when it snows, and block the rain when it rains."

"Alright, let's do that!"

The group of beastmen in front of him all nodded, their sun-tanned faces grinning to reveal white teeth.

Lin Qiu changed his tone and said, "If you want to seal it, leaving windows like the ones in the house on the west side is also fine."

The beastmen thought about it and slapped their thighs, "That works too!"

Lin Qiu laughed, "Then you all consider it and see which one is suitable."

The beastmen formed a group, raising their voices to discuss it.

Feeling cold, Lin Qiu simply went to sit by the stove.

There were no stars tonight, and Lang An and a few other beastmen were sitting by the stove, sorting out the herb seeds they had dug up today.

Lin Qiu came over, saw there was fire in the stove, rummaged through a rattan basket, found a few broken yams, and buried them directly in the ashes with the embers.

Seeing him shivering, Lang An touched his hand. "Why are your hands so cold?"

Lin Qiu looked at the sub-beastmen who were also only wearing shorts and laughed helplessly: "It's cold."

Lang An frowned, "The sweater will be ready soon. I'll work harder and get it done for you sooner."

Lin Qiu: "Then thank you, An."

Lang An grabbed his hand and hurriedly pulled him toward the stove opening. "The King and the others are busy hoarding meat for the Snow Season, so they'll be back later than before. If you can't stay outside, go to the cave; there's no wind inside, it's warmer."

Lin Qiu: "It's fine, it's warm here too."

"The Snow Season is coming, it's always like this, the weaker beastmen always feel the cold first," a middle-aged sub-beastman next to him said.

Lang An nodded, "Fortunately, it looks like we won't freeze this year."

Lin Qiu leaned against the low wall, his gaze lowered, feeling a bit drowsy while waiting.

"What did everyone do during the Snow Season before?"

"Sleeping, starving through the days, couldn't do anything," Lang An said with emotion.

Chatting and waiting for a while longer, the beastmen finally returned.

Lang An called them to eat, and the beastmen put down their prey and hurried over.

The intensity of hunting before the Snow Season was several times higher than usual; the beastmen not only had to catch enough for the day but also hoped for leftovers.

Today, the two hunting squads were busy separately, but the results weren't necessarily great.

Lin Qiu stood up, watched Lang Yan wash his hands by the stream and come over, and hurriedly took the bowls and chopsticks to line up first.

Lang Yan saw Lin Qiu at a glance and walked toward him with his long legs.

The light under the shed was a bit dim; Lin Qiu's eyes curved into a smile, and when he got close, he stepped aside to let him stand next to him.

"Where did you go today?"

Lang Yan took the bowl from his hand and, taking advantage of the darkness, draped his arm around Lin Qiu's waist. "Went to the southeast."

"We'll definitely have to go there again later, so we'll be back even later." Lang Yan's arm pressed against Lin Qiu's body, feeling a bit cold, so he pulled Lin Qiu into his arms and let him lean against him. "Tell An and the others not to wait, you all eat first."

Lin Qiu was indeed cold, and he felt comfortable only after pressing against Lang Yan's hot body.

"Was there much prey?"

Lang Yan rested his chin on Lin Qiu's shoulder, his eyelids drooping, feeling a bit lazy. "Scattered, not much."

Lin Qiu: "I saw the red bird eggs have hatched. I'll try to see if I can use a heated bed to hatch some more and try to raise more."

There should only be two months left until the Snow Season, and red bird eggs need more than twenty days to hatch. As long as the chicks can grow a bit larger, they can survive the winter.

The winter lasts four or five months; if there isn't enough food in the end, they can also kill some red birds to eat.

Lang Yan tightened his grip on his waist and took a few steps forward, following the beastmen moving in front. "Take your time with the red birds, no rush."

Lin Qiu turned to look at Lang Yan. "The White Sparrow beastmen came today to exchange for herbs with the Priest."
