Coming back to his senses, Lang Yan watched the beastmen hurriedly holding their bowls, already reaching their claws into the meat soup pot.

On the ginger soup side, not a single beastman had come over.

Lang Yan: "Didn't you hear what Qiu said?"

The beastmen went silent for a moment, looking dejected. They peeked at Lang Yan, and seeing he was still staring at them, they could only drag their feet and walk obediently toward the ginger soup one by one.

Lang Yan noticed a beastman who only scooped half a ladle of ginger soup and said coldly, "Two ladles each; if you don't finish it, don't eat the meat soup."

"Achoo!"

"Blech!" A beastman covered his mouth and spat.

"So gross."

"Qiu poisoned us!"

"Tsk tsk tsk, tsk tsk tsk..." A beastman smacked his lips, "It's delicious!"

The beastmen complained: "What kind of taste is that!"

The beastman gulped down the ginger soup in one breath, his tongue burning, and he swallowed it desperately before quickly scooping up meat soup to soothe the heat.

Lang Yan frowned at the sight, turned his head away, and ignored them.

After eating the meat soup, the beastmen came back to life.

They lay down casually under the corridor, in a mess, without leaving a path in the middle.

Lang Yan went to check the two prey they had brought back, a large and a small curved-horn beast, just a male and a female.

After checking, Lang Yan confirmed they were tied up, then went to the stream to take a bath before heading to the cave.

As soon as he entered the cave, he saw his partner draped in fur, sitting cross-legged in the grass nest. He had changed his long pants into sleeping shorts, revealing straight calves and white knees.

Seeing him enter, Lin Qiu looked up and smiled with his eyes curved.

His cheeks were rosy and fair, his brows filled with joy, like a bird that had flown to a branch early on a sunny day after a full meal.

He realized that Lin Qiu was smiling more and more.

Lang Yan walked slowly to his side, lowered his head, and kissed his partner on the forehead.

Lin Qiu's eyelashes fluttered, and he knelt up.

"You should have come back earlier today."

Lang Yan hugged Lin Qiu and lifted him up, melting him into his arms, "We chased two curved-horn beasts far away today."

"Did you catch them?"

Lang Yan held his hands, kneading and rubbing them, his chin resting on his shoulder, and said, "Caught them, alive, only a few minor injuries."

Lin Qiu was slightly surprised, "Are you going to raise them?"

Lang Yan: "I just came to ask you if you want to try."

Lin Qiu nodded, "Let's try."

Curved-horn beasts are large, and catching them alive is extremely difficult. Lin Qiu had previously thought about raising sheep-beasts because they were the right size and traveled in herds.

"What if they don't survive?"

"If they don't survive, we'll just have fresh meat for the snow season."

Lin Qiu turned his head to rub against his face, getting quite wet. Lin Qiu got down from him, found a cloth, told Lang Yan to sit on the wooden stool, and gathered his long hair to wipe it.

"It's night, why are you washing your hair?" Lin Qiu frowned.

Lang Yan pulled the person behind him to the front, his forehead against his waist and abdomen, circling him like he was marking territory.

"It got wet in the rain, let's just wash it together."

"Light the fire, let's dry off before sleeping."

"Hmm." Lang Yan closed his eyes and leaned close to his partner, his nose tip couldn't help but press against his soft waist and abdomen; it was too soft, and he couldn't help but press and grind against it.

Lin Qiu's abdomen tightened, and he heard Lang Yan laughing lowly.

Lin Qiu reached down and touched his chin, "Don't mess around."

Lang Yan rubbed the corner of his clothes with his nose bridge, his breath hot, and looking at his blushing partner, he opened his mouth and bit it right in front of him.

A pain on his head, Lang Yan said hoarsely, "It's not dry yet, keep wiping."

Lin Qiu bit his lower lip, his hands gripping his long hair tightly, and he continued to gather the cloth with trembling hands.

Lang Yan's hair was thick, and after changing the linen cloth once, he continued wiping for a long time. Lin Qiu's legs were weak from standing, and finally, he was hooked by Lang Yan and lay limply on his lap.

He looked up weakly, watching Lang Yan lick his tongue; even after eating a sugar cake, he had to savor the taste. Lin Qiu twitched like a fish on a cutting board, his whole body flushed red.

Lang Yan touched Lin Qiu's face, supported his back, and lifted him up a bit.

Lin Qiu hugged his shoulders, burying his head tightly in his neck and not coming out.

"Sleepy." Lang Yan bit his ear.

Lin Qiu hummed twice, his hand stroking his hair, still a bit damp, "Hair."

Lang Yan: "Right away."

A fire was lit in the cave, and Lang Yan had made a straw curtain. At this time, the straw curtain was half-lowered, leaving only the top part for ventilation.

The cave was warm.

Lang Yan covered Lin Qiu with fur, looked down at his sleepy face, and held his feet tightly with his large palms.

This period had been extremely busy, and he had to go out again early tomorrow morning.

Lang Yan dried his hair, held Lin Qiu, and lay down in the grass nest, closing his eyes to sleep.

The rain continued until the next morning, finally stopping.

The sky cleared, and mist rose from the mountains, spreading over the ranges like a waterfall.

Lin Qiu had just walked to the cave entrance when he saw layers of steps extending down the mountain.

Stepping on them, they were steady and firm.

Their King went out early and returned late, yet still had time to do this; he didn't know how long he had slept last night.

In front of the large cave, Lin Qiu smelled a medicinal scent as soon as he stepped in.

Yu Le was guarding the stove, and on the stove was a small pot specifically used for boiling medicine. The little beastman was guarding it seriously, his eyes never leaving it.

Lin Qiu deliberately made some noise, but Yu Le shrank to the side, leaving room for him.

Lin Qiu said, "Is the old patriarch awake?"

Yu Le recognized Lin Qiu's voice and stood up in a hurry, looking much more spirited than yesterday.

"Uncle Qiu." He followed the little wolves in calling him that.

"Grandpa woke up last night and just fell asleep again."

Lin Qiu pressed his shoulder, told him to sit down, and placed the pottery bowl in his hand on the table, "It's good that he woke up. Have you eaten?"

The little beastman nodded, "I've eaten."

The meat soup was kept warm in the pot, and as soon as the lid was lifted, the familiar scent of lotus root wafted out.

Lin Qiu knew the beastmen's habits well; once they found something delicious, they would eat it until they were sick of it, and they would probably be eating lotus root for a while.

Fortunately, he liked it too, so Lin Qiu scooped some up and moved to the table to eat.

Recently, the little wolves had also been going out and had no free time. Lin Qiu looked at the little beastman who had sat down obediently again; it would probably be until the snow season before Lang Bing had time to teach him.

The Black Feather patriarch would most likely not stay here for long, and the little beastman would definitely go back with him.

He didn't know what it would be like when they came back next time.

After breakfast and washing the bowls, Lin Qiu first checked the meat hung up last night.

He didn't make roasted meat this time; the jerky was hung to air-dry for a few days, and then Lin Qiu planned to smoke it and make it into cured meat.

When the time came, stir-frying it with dried vegetables would also be a good dish.

After checking, Lin Qiu strolled into the large cave.

His wine should be ready; the beastmen had waited so long that no one had come to urge him anymore.

The large cave was full of beast-women busy making clothes.

Lang Guo was dizzy from taking care of the cubs; when Lin Qiu entered, the cubs ran to his feet and raised their claws to climb onto him.

Lang Guo was happy and just lay in the grass nest without moving.

Lin Qiu picked up the four chubby cubs, and they were surprisingly heavy.

He bounced them and said, "Just like little piglets."

The cubs wagged their tails and called to him in milky voices: "Awoo awoo awoo..."

Lin Qiu: "I didn't say you were fat, I said you were growing well."

Lin Qiu played with them for a while before putting them back into Lang Guo's grass nest.

Lang Guo reached out, "Don't, keep playing for a while."

Lin Qiu: "I'm going to check the wine."

Lang Guo sat up with a start, squatting in the corner in front of the three large pottery jars lined up before Lin Qiu could.

The innermost jar was the one Lin Qiu made first, and the other two were made later because the beastmen were greedy and urged the gathering team to find new grapes.

Lin Qiu lifted the mud lid, and underneath were layers of dried leaves, with a layer of linen cloth tied with rope at the very bottom.

As soon as the mud lid was removed, the fragrance of wine wafted out.

Lang Guo took a deep breath and quickly went to get a few pottery cups. The cubs chased him out and then chased him back, almost being stepped on by a beastman.

Lang Yu was frightened and hurriedly shooed them into the grass nest, and in a moment, Lin Qiu completely removed the lid.

The beast-women making clothes twitched their noses and, by unspoken agreement, put down their work and approached Lin Qiu.

There were tables and chairs in the large cave, and the beast-women sat down consciously.

Lin Qiu scooped out a little wine and poured it into the cup Lang Guo had eagerly brought over.

The wine was much clearer, the aroma more mellow, with the fruity taste of grapes; not to mention the other beastmen, even Lin Qiu was tempted.

Lang Guo held the cup with both hands and gulped it down without hesitation.

Lin Qiu didn't have time to warn him before he saw Lang Guo cough, smack his lips, and extend the cup again with extremely bright eyes.

Lin Qiu: "Don't be in such a hurry."

He scooped out a cup, sealed the lid again, and turned his head to see the beast-women waiting with smiles on their faces.

Lang An was also among them; he looked outside and pushed the cup he had just brought over forward.

"Hurry up, if those outside smell it, they'll snatch it again."

Lin Qiu couldn't help but laugh; each beastman only got two or three sips.

Who knew that all the wolf-beastmen were the same, heroically grabbing their cups and gulping it down in one go.

Lin Qiu: "That's not how you drink it..."

Beastmen would get dizzy even from eating old fruit, this wine...

Thump, Lin Qiu turned his head in fright.

He saw Lang Guo had already fallen into the grass nest, giggling foolishly.

Looking at the other middle-aged beast-women, except for two or three whose cheeks were a bit red, the rest had clear eyes and shouldn't be drunk.

Lang An saw his worry and laughed, "Don't worry, we've been eating fruit that went bad during the snow season for years; we can handle it better than the young ones."

Seeing this, Lin Qiu didn't dare to pour them any more.

He sat by the table, holding the cup with both hands, took another small sip himself, and narrowed his eyes.

"Is it good?" Lin Qiu asked.

Lang An tapped his fingers on the table, looking at his cup, "A little more."

Lin Qiu: "You can't be greedy."

"What do you call greedy if I finish it in one sip? Give me some more." Lang Yu also pushed his cup forward.

"Awoo! What delicious food are you eating behind our backs!"

A roar came from the cave entrance, and Lin Qiu's hand shook.

Fortunately, there wasn't much left in the cup.

Lang Mo led the beastmen in aggressively, and Lin Qiu looked away, holding his cup, calm and composed.

He was just checking if the wine was drinkable, he had nothing to feel guilty about.

"Qiu!"

Lin Qiu: "Keep your voice down, I can hear you. What do you want?"

The beastmen said resentfully: "Where's ours?"

Seeing this, Lang An moved like the wind and was out of the cave in an instant.

Lin Qiu's hand moved slightly, these beastmen! No sense of justice!

"Qiu! You're biased!"

Lin Qiu: "I was just checking if it was drinkable, how am I biased?"

The wolf-beastmen sniffed at Lang Guo and then picked up the cups on the table to smell them, their eyes moist, as if they had been deceived in a major way.

Lin Qiu silently put down the cup, feeling a little bit guilty.

No, it couldn't be that bad...

"Awoo awoo awoo!!!"

The beastmen cried for him to see on the spot.

It was that bad!

How could it not be!

Food is a matter of the utmost importance.

Even if it’s just water, it’s delicious water!

The wolves are fuming!

They aren't angry about not being able to drink the purple-skinned fruit wine; they’re angry that Qiu secretly ate it with a group of beastmen behind their backs!

Couldn't he have at least saved them a sip?!

The beastmen didn't care about face or pride; they only knew that Lin Qiu was playing favorites, and they howled loud enough to shake the heavens.

If it were just one beastman howling, it would be fine, but a whole crowd of wolf-beastmen were blocking Lin Qiu, howling so hard he could see down their throats.

"Alright, alright..."

"Awoo-ooo-ooo! Awoo-ooo-ooo-ooo!!!"

Lin Qiu closed his eyes, finally understanding why his King always refused to open his eyes when facing this pack of wolves.

"Enough!"

"This is my fault. I shouldn't have been so weak-willed. When the uncles asked, I gave it to them. I should have finished tasting it alone, put it away, and then shared it with everyone together."

"Awoo!"

Lin Qiu looked up.

Lang Mo fiercely shoved the beastman who had "awooed": "You still dare to howl! Be careful, or you won't get any!"

Lin Qiu: "How about this: tonight, when the hunting and gathering team returns, everyone can have a taste. Is that okay?"

Lang Mo wanted to laugh, but he forcibly suppressed the corners of his mouth from curling up.

Lang Xi coughed lightly, looking as if he had forgiven Lin Qiu, "Fine, that's fine."

Lin Qiu: "If it's fine, why are you still blocking the way?"

Seeing that Lin Qiu looked like he was about to get angry, the beastmen tucked their tails and bolted out of the cave in an instant.

Lin Qiu felt exhausted and sat down slowly, leaning against the table.

He thought about how his King was always used to keeping a cold face in front of the beastmen; most of the time, one glance was enough to make them behave.

Isn't that a way to save energy?

Lin Qiu felt his ears still buzzing. He felt something rubbing against his feet, and when he looked down, the cubs had their paws on his legs, looking up with bright, round eyes.

Lin Qiu’s mouth set into a flat line, "Don't even think about it."

Lin Qiu sat in the cave for a while, watching Lang Guo, who was still groggy and didn't know when he would wake up.

He picked up his basket, originally intending to take the four cubs out to cut grass.

The light in front of him dimmed, and when he turned his head, he saw the few sub-beastmen who had just slipped away returning. Lin Qiu didn't even look at their ingratiating smiles; he put the cubs into their grass nest and headed out with his basket on his back.

"Oh my, Qiu is angry," Lang Yu said softly.

Lang An: "I'll go coax him."

The sub-beastmen laughed. Upon reflection, this was probably the first time Qiu had acted like this in front of them. Instead of being angry, they were actually a bit happy.

"It’s better when Qiu is like this. Always being so polite doesn't feel like we're beastmen of the same tribe."

"Pfft—" a nearby beastman laughed, "You guys probably forgot, when Qiu first arrived, he pointed at our King's nose and scolded him; he wasn't very polite then either."

Lang Yu: "Look, he wasn't polite to the King back then, and now how great their relationship is."

"Haha, so that means we should scold him more."

The beastmen chatted and laughed, but Lang Shuang suddenly said: "I always feel like Qiu has become a different beastman."

The lively cave suddenly went quiet, with only the sound of the cubs rummaging in the grass nest.

The cave was silent for two or three seconds. Lang Yu reached out and pressed down on a cub's head, and the cub sat down obediently, looking dazed.

Lang Yu coughed lightly and whispered: "Didn't the Priest say he bumped his head?"

"Even if he bumped his head, he wouldn't know so much... I just feel like Qiu must be able to communicate with the Beast God."

"Hiss... don't say that out loud!"

Seven or eight sub-beastmen shut their mouths, their eyes full of hope.

Clearly, they had all thought of the same thing.

Lang Yu: "Let's not talk about this. Let's think about whether An can coax Qiu."

Everyone laughed again, their cheeks slightly flushed.

They really hadn't acted right in this matter.

*

The curved-horn beasts the beastmen caught last night were being kept on the west side, and Lin Qiu hadn't gone to see them yet.

Lin Qiu found a place to cut grass, and seeing Lang An following behind, he smiled helplessly and said: "An, I'm not angry."

How could he not know why An was following him?

Lang An: "I didn't say you were angry. I saw you cutting grass, so I'm helping to cut some too."

Now that the tribe was raising more wild beasts, just the grass for the ten bleating-beasts required several baskets.

Lang An: "You have a lot to do every day. The beastmen only remember to cut grass when they think of it to feed them. Sometimes they feed them seven or eight times a day, and sometimes they forget. Why don't we just have a few beastmen specifically watch over this area?"

Lin Qiu: "No, I have to watch it myself."

Lang An grabbed a handful of grass, cut it with his stone sickle, and tossed the slightly withered yellow grass into the basket.

"It's not that I'm stopping you from coming. With several feedings a day, cutting grass, feeding, and watering, it's better to have specific beastmen do it. You can come whenever you want to check, which saves you trouble and lets you focus on other things."

Lin Qiu considered it for a while and agreed.

At first, Lang Mo and the others always came to watch the breeding area, but Lang Mo had his own tasks, so it would be better to arrange a few beastmen to focus on it.

"Does An have any beastmen to recommend?"

"I still have to think about that."

There weren't many idle beastmen in Wolf Mountain, and this breeding business was a big deal. Don't look at it as just feeding grass and changing water; it was still physically demanding.

It also required care; if anything happened to them, they needed to inform Lin Qiu or the Priest in time.

Lang An cut grass while thinking about the available beastmen in the tribe.

On the grassland, Lang Sheng was running around with a group of cubs, making a racket. Seeing Lin Qiu and Lang An cutting grass from afar, they immediately rushed over.

The cubs sat on the grass, observed for a while, and then started grabbing and pulling at the grass with their paws.

Lang An watched without stopping them.

Cubs at this age were the most energetic, able to run and jump, playing after they were full, with no worries.

Seeing them huddled in the grass like mushrooms, Lin Qiu had a thought and whispered to Lang An: "Uncle An, do you think the cubs could do it?"

Lang An was so startled he almost dropped his stone sickle.

"How could the cubs do it?!"

Lang Sheng sat on the ground, his paws grabbing at the grass beside him rapidly. Hearing the two adult beastmen talking in low voices, he quietly pricked up his ears.

"No, the cubs are too small, not even as tall as the bleating-beasts. They can't even cut grass, let alone look after these animals."

Lin Qiu: "I just had a sudden thought."

There were over a dozen cubs; if each grabbed half a basket of grass, that would be enough for the livestock for a day.

But thinking about it carefully, it wouldn't work.

Lang An: "How about this? Lang Rong is staying in the tribe now. He watches over the few radishes the rabbit-beastmen planted, and he's mostly free. Otherwise, let's call him."

Lin Qiu: "Can he handle it?"

Lang An: "I'll go ask him."

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

The cubs grabbed a few handfuls of grass and ran off.

Once they reached a place where Lin Qiu and the others couldn't hear, Lang Sheng beckoned, and everyone sat down, their clear eyes fixed on Lang Sheng.

They had all grown up in the same nest, were about the same age, and had slept together since before they could transform into human form; it was a tacit understanding from childhood.

Lang Sheng: "I just heard Qiu-Qiu say he wanted us to raise red birds and bleating-beasts."

Beside him, Lang Yuan’s voice was soft, naive, and childish: "Let's raise them."

Lang Sheng spread out his two little legs, "But An said no."

Little Fatty on the side sighed, "My Dad must think we're too small..."

The three cubs spoke seriously like little adults, while the other cubs couldn't sit still and were already rolling on the ground after a few words.

Lang Sheng fell backward, arms spread out, his little black arms looking sturdy and strong.

"Sigh! We're still too small."

Lang Yuan rested his chin on his knees, his chubby little face squished, and his eyes curved like crescent moons when he smiled, "Oh! Don't rush, we'll grow up."

Little Fatty shook his head and lay down on the grass too.

Forget it, forget it, thinking about things is too complicated, I won't think about it.

The cubs next to them rolled until the surrounding grass was flattened, bumping into them and rolling all the way to Lang Sheng’s side, including Little Fatty.

Lang Sheng kicked his little legs and immediately bumped back aggressively.

Little Fatty was caught in the middle, "Ouch, ouch! I'm being squashed!"

In the distance, Lin Qiu stood up with a full basket. Hearing the cubs playing, he couldn't help but look over and smile.

Lang An: "Wolf Mountain is never quiet when they're awake."

Lin Qiu: "That's how it should be."

The cubs weren't grown up yet; as long as they were fed and slept well, that was enough.

Lang An felt a momentary sadness in Lin Qiu, but when he looked, Lin Qiu was smiling. He thought he was overthinking it and said: "Let's hurry and feed them. After that, I'll go find Lang Rong."

The Priest's cave.

Lang Rong was free, so he stayed in the Priest's cave.

On one side, the old Priest was teaching Lang Xue about herbs, while he was alone, using the juice of the longevity grass to carve the planting points he had organized onto animal hide.

He was hunched over the Priest's medicine-making table, so busy he had blocked out all surrounding sounds.

Lang An entered the cave and had even walked up beside him to watch for a while, but he still didn't know.

Lang An nodded as he watched; Lang Rong and his older sister Lang Qing were both steady-natured.

Priest: "Why did you run up here?"

Lang An: "I saw that there are more animals being raised, so I discussed it with Qiu to find a beastman to be specifically responsible for that. I thought Lang Rong should be free, so I came to ask him."

Priest: "He's the one."

Lang An was taken aback and said with a smile: "At least ask him; just him alone won't work."

"Why would you need to ask? On that animal hide, he not only recorded planting tail-grass, herbs, and radishes, but he also specifically recorded how to raise red birds and bleating-beasts."

What red birds eat, how many eggs they lay, how long the eggs take to hatch, what the hatched red birds eat, how long until the little red birds leave the nest... he remembered it more carefully than anyone.

Otherwise, with those few radishes, could he still be hunched over here working?

Lang An felt very relieved after hearing this.

That steady attitude sounded reliable.

"Fine! If he's willing, then it's him. But he can't do it alone."

"Then tell him to designate two little wolves himself."

The two beastmen decided on this matter just like that. Lang Rong was completely immersed in his records throughout, and when he finished, he saw Lang An beckoning him over with a smile.

As soon as Lang Rong heard he was being asked to be responsible for breeding, he agreed without the slightest hesitation.

Lang An looked at the little wolf who had grown to his shoulder height, patted his shoulder, and said: "It's almost the cold season now. The radish planting you have on hand isn't too busy, so you'll be responsible for the breeding first. After the cold season..."

"I can do it after the cold season too."

It was called planting, but actually, he was just responsible for recording the fertilization and growth of various plants; it was just a matter of moving his hands.

When it really came time to plant, all the beastmen worked together, and he couldn't exert much strength.

Breeding was different. Although the adult beastmen hadn't said it, he vaguely knew this was very important. So, in his spare time, he explored it himself, recording the growth of red birds and bleating-beasts just like he recorded the tail-grass.

He understood the changes in these animals; he recorded the increases and decreases in numbers, the animals' appetites, and the types of food in great detail.

No beastman was more suitable than him.

"Uncle An, I'm willing to do this."

Lang An looked at the persistence in the little wolf's eyes and tightened his grip on his shoulder, "Good, then do it."

The little wolf smiled. Usually honest and dull, he looked a bit more lively now.

Lang Rong had a quiet nature and was always overlooked by the beastmen.

He had two good friends: one was the captain of the little wolf hunting team, and the other was the captain of the little wolf gathering team and the next Priest. He hung out between them, often running back and forth, and didn't have a fixed task.

Seeing that he was genuinely happy, Lang An felt relieved.

He stood up, patted the little wolf’s head and said: "You can find two companions to be responsible with you. Qiu also keeps an eye on that side, and the King and the Priest also value this matter. You must be careful; if any problems arise, the first thing you must do is tell Qiu."

"I'll remember that." Lang Rong’s delicate cheeks were flushed with excitement, and seeing that, Lang An couldn't help but feel happy along with him.

"As long as you remember."

"Then I'll go find Qiu!"

Saying that, he ran down the mountain before Lang An, and just looking at him, one could tell this matter suited his heart.

The Priest withdrew his gaze and said: "Anything else?"

Lang An: "No."

The Priest: "If not, then hurry up and leave; I still have to teach Lang Xue."

What a temper! He didn't even want to come anyway.

Lang An left the cave decisively.

Lang Rong ran to Lin Qiu in one breath, standing there like a little sapling, looking up at Lin Qiu with eager eyes.

After the excitement, Lang Rong became shy. He stood properly and said: "Qiu, Uncle An said to let me follow you to raise red birds."

Lin Qiu: "You agreed?"

Lang Rong nodded heavily.

Lin Qiu: "Fine, then from now on, you'll be responsible for this side, not just the red birds, but also the bleating-beasts and the curved-horn beasts."

"Okay!"

Lin Qiu: "Can you handle the planting side?"

"I can! I only need to record things over there," Lang Rong said eagerly, afraid that Lin Qiu wouldn't agree.

"Then it's settled."

"Mm!"

Lin Qiu couldn't help but smile, giving him some instructions, and the little wolf kept nodding. Lin Qiu was worried he would shake himself dizzy.

With someone specifically responsible for breeding, Lin Qiu didn't have to keep worrying about the trivial matters of cutting grass and changing water.

After observing for a few more days, if Lang Rong and the two little wolves didn't make any mistakes, he would feel safe handing it over to him.

The beastmen were busy hoarding food, and Lin Qiu also told the little wolves to start hoarding grass for the bleating-beasts to get through the winter when they had time.

Those two curved-horn beasts were too large and aggressive, and the beastmen didn't dare to get close, so they just left the grass for them to eat.

Lin Qiu wandered around Wolf Mountain, and wherever he went, beastmen were watching him.

After being watched like that for a day, it was finally evening.

Today, Lang Yan and the others changed their hunting grounds, and the team split into small groups, each looking for prey.

Lang Yan returned earlier. When the first hunting team arrived at Wolf Mountain, the horizon was a bluish-green, not yet completely dark.

In the evening, Lang An stewed soup with the sharp-horned beasts brought back by the first hunting team. Before the cold season, the beastmen needed to accumulate fat and couldn't always rely on lotus roots and fish.

Seeing Lang Yan return, Lin Qiu decisively followed behind him like a tail.

Now, whenever the beastmen stared, Lin Qiu would shift behind Lang Yan.

By the stream, Lang Yan had just washed his hands when he saw Lin Qiu sticking to his side.

Lang Yan grabbed his wrist; his palms were large and rough, and they felt a bit itchy when they brushed against his skin.

He pulled Lin Qiu to the front, directly blocking the other beastmen's view.

With doubt in his gray eyes, Lin Qiu smiled and rested his forehead on his shoulder.

"What are they looking at?"

"Waiting for me to distribute the wine. I opened it today to taste it and shared some with An and the others. They found out and started crying in front of me, shouting that I was playing favorites."

Lang Yan frowned, "They need to be disciplined."

Lin Qiu shook the wrist he was holding, "Loosen up a bit, King. I'm not the one who needs to be disciplined."

Lang Yan lifted Lin Qiu’s wrist to look; it was a bit pinched and red. He rubbed it with his thumb, but it just made it redder, so he rubbed it with the tip of his nose and kissed the side of Lin Qiu’s wrist.

Lang Yan: "Don't spoil them."

Lin Qiu: "How am I spoiling them? It just so happens that a jar of wine can be opened, so let everyone have a taste first. If they like it, I'll make more next year."

Lang Yan held both of Lin Qiu’s hands, lowering his eyes, looking as if he wasn't very happy.

If this isn't called spoiling, what is?

After waiting a little longer, the other two hunting teams and the little wolves returned. Lang An called the beastmen to eat meat, but the beastmen lined up with their bowls, their movements not as active as before.

The beastmen's eyes kept drifting toward Lin Qiu, but when Lang Yan glanced over, they immediately lowered their heads, burying them in their bowls.

The beastmen looked dejected.

Did Qiu forget something?

Lin Qiu hadn't forgotten; he still remembered that the beastmen could pass out from eating fermented fruit before.

Even their King hadn't been able to hold up.

Wine was easier to get drunk on than the bad fruit the beastmen gnawed on, and he was worried that if he brought it out too early, the beastmen would drink it, pass out, and not be able to eat the meat soup.

The beastmen dawdled, their eyes constantly glancing at Lin Qiu, but with Lang Yan by his side, no one dared to come up.

Everyone thought they wouldn't get to drink tonight and were even eating the meat soup absent-mindedly. Lang An couldn't stand it anymore and tapped each of the beastmen on the head with a small stick.

"If you're eating meat soup, eat it properly. Looking around like that, are you dissatisfied with my cooking? Then let's just stick to fish soup from now on!"

"Not dissatisfied, not dissatisfied!"

Once they heard they might only be able to eat fish soup, the beastmen didn't dare to be distracted anymore, slurping their bowls and drinking more than half the soup in one breath.

After the beastmen had finished eating and washed their bowls one after another, they saw Lin Qiu still hadn't moved.

The beastmen felt aggrieved, dejected, and moved silently toward the large cave.

They moved and looked back, looking crestfallen.

The beastmen from the teams that weren't at Wolf Mountain today were dazed.

What happened?

Lin Qiu saw Lang Mo walk to the entrance of the cave and called out: "Mo, bring out that jar of wine from the very back!"

Lang Mo’s ears pricked up instantly.

When Lin Qiu looked, the pointed wolf ears were already out.

He patted Lang Yan’s leg beside him and said: "Look, they were still thinking about it; if I didn't give them any, they definitely wouldn't sleep well tonight."

Lang Yan didn't speak, only tightened his grip on Lin Qiu’s hand, his thumb rubbing the soft flesh of his palm.

His partner’s skin was tender, but his palms felt rougher than before.

A jar of wine didn't look like much, but it wasn't full, at most only two-thirds full.

There were over a hundred beastmen, including the rabbit-beastmen; if each got a small sip, it could be finished completely.

The beastmen had their own cups, all kinds of shapes and sizes. They were all because they had seen Lin Qiu make cups, and they followed suit, having Lang Mo and the others mold some when they fired pottery.

Lang Mo carefully held the jar and came out, not daring to take big steps.

He grinned, his eyes crinkling into lines.

"Looks exceptionally stupid."

Lin Qiu looked up, surprised to hear that from their King.

He poked Lang Yan, his hand landing right on his waist and abdomen.

Lin Qiu poked and poked, "King, you can't be jealous, can you?"

Lang Yan’s eyes were dark, "What does it mean to be jealous?"

Lin Qiu lightly scratched his abs, "Just the way you look at the beastmen..."

Lang Yan: "I've always looked at them like that."

Lin Qiu curled his lips, not saying much, just waiting for Lang Mo to set it down. Just as he was about to go up and distribute it to the beastmen, Lang Yan gripped him and wouldn't let go.

Lang An had already walked up excitedly; if he had sleeves, he would definitely have rolled them up.

"Qiu, how do we distribute it?"

"Use a spoon, two spoons per beastman."

"That's only one mouthful," the beastmen muttered.

The other beastmen didn't care if it was one mouthful or two; knowing it was good stuff, they quickly found their dusty cups, washed them, and lined up.

As the wine was stirred, the beastmen’s noses were sharp, and the scent entered their lungs; just smelling it made them intoxicated.

Lin Qiu also took some for himself.

He first brought it to Lang Yan’s lips and said: "King, you have a taste."

Lang Yan took a sip. His ears were filled with slurping sounds; the beastmen couldn't bear to drink it all at once, so they pursed their lips and sipped. It was like mice entering an oil vat, cheering with their paws raised, sounding increasingly annoying.

The rabbit-beastmen also got some. They were cautious, holding their large bowls and first touching it to their lips. They licked it, savored the taste, and Tu Ai’s eyes widened.

"It’s hitting my mouth!"

"My throat is so hot!"

"Did the wolf-beastmen poison it..."

Tu Kui saw the wolf-beastmen’s cherished appearance and knew it was good stuff. Some beastmen could drink it, while others took a sip and immediately looked for water.

Tu Kui took another sip and looked at the cub lying in his arms, who was watching eagerly.

He covered the cub’s eyes and said gently: "Qiu said that cubs who aren't grown up can't drink it."

"Dad... Dad..." Tu Luo grabbed his hand and shook it gently, acting spoiled with a soft voice.

Tu Kui thought for a moment, dipped a chopstick in it, and let him lick it.

Tu Luo bit the chopstick in one gulp, using a bit too much force, and broke the chopstick.

"Hey! Spit out the chopstick."

Tu Luo: "Ptoo, ptoo, ptoo!"

His two long ears puffed up, and he stuck out his tongue, trying to rub it against Tu Kui.

Tu Kui quickly pinched his chin; although it was his own cub, he still disliked having his saliva smeared all over him.

"Tu Ai! Water."

"So spicy, so spicy, so spicy!!! I want water too!"

The rabbit-beastmen were in chaos, while the wolf-beastmen were holding their cups, lazily curling up, taking a sip, then another.

Their wolf bodies slowly went limp, their heads dizzy, as if they saw the Beast God dancing in a fur skirt.

The beastmen had almost never drunk alcohol; those with low tolerance just fell to the ground and started snoring after two sips.

The gluttonous ones drank it cherishly, then glanced at the jar with red faces.

Lang An leaned against the counter, a cup in one hand, took another sip, and looked sideways at the beastmen. "The jar has been washed with water twice already, it's gone."

"Thump—" the beastmen lay on the ground, limbs spread out.

It's gone, wuu...

I haven't had enough, awoo.

*

The scent of wine permeated the corridor.

The beastmen who drank the wine like juice were still wanting more, washed up as usual, and lay down in their grass nests. They just closed their eyes and fell asleep in no time.

Lin Qiu was worried the beastmen wouldn't adapt, so he checked them one by one, and only felt relieved when he found no problems.

Many beastmen were lying in the corridor. Lin Qiu went around them, walked to the inner side, and squatted down in front of Lang Yan, who was sitting against the low wall.

Lin Qiu touched Lang Yan’s face; it was a bit hot.

"King, let's go back to the cave."

Lang Yan opened his eyes, only feeling his eyelids were incredibly heavy. He hooked his smiling partner in front of him into his arms, hugged him with extreme possessiveness, rested his head on his shoulder, and closed his eyes again.

Lin Qiu touched Lang Yan’s hair; it was a bit coarse and hard, "King, it's a bit tight, I can't breathe."

As the words fell, the restraint on his body loosened.

But it only loosened a little; Lin Qiu couldn't break free.

The nearby beastmen had all fallen, and even Lang An and the others had returned to their caves. Lin Qiu let him hold him for a while, then tried to stand up.

The next instant, the hand behind his waist tightened again.

Lin Qiu patted his arm helplessly, "King, it's cold sleeping outside."

Lang Yan’s voice was tight: "It's not cold."

Lin Qiu: "I'll get sick."

Lang Yan rubbed against him slowly and sat up. Lin Qiu quickly helped him toward the large cave.

Who knew that before they reached the cave entrance, Lang Yan smelled the messy scent of the beastmen and, hooking Lin Qiu, insisted on going up the mountain.

Lin Qiu: "King... can you climb up?"

Lang Yan squinted at Lin Qiu for a while, and just when Lin Qiu thought he was going to fall asleep again, his vision suddenly flipped, his stomach hit something hard, and he was directly carried on Lang Yan’s shoulder.

"King!" Lin Qiu was so scared he braced himself against Lang Yan’s back, "Put me down quickly."

A drunkard was carrying him; what if he fell and broke his head?

Lang Yan stopped and then squatted down.

Lin Qiu’s feet landed on the ground, and he breathed a sigh of relief.

He lifted Lang Yan’s face and touched it; it was still burning hot.

"I won't let you drink anymore."

Lang Yan kissed Lin Qiu’s palm, his eyes never leaving his face. Seeing this, Lin Qiu curled his lips into a beautiful smile.

"Then let's go back to the cave on the mountain; you hold onto me, don't fall."

Lang Yan thought for a while and nodded.

Lin Qiu first took him to the stream and wiped his face with cool water. Lang Yan avoided it, burying his face in Lin Qiu’s neck.

Smelling the scent he liked, he couldn't help but lick it.

Lin Qiu shivered, quickly finished washing up, and then pulled him up the mountain.

Passing by the Priest’s cave, he went to check on the old Priest.

The old beastman knew how to enjoy himself better than them; in front of him were some dried meat, fruit, and a little bit of wine. Drinking wine with dried meat, the old beastman hummed an unknown tune comfortably.

It was like a sacrificial song, distant and mysterious.

His hand was tugged, and Lin Qiu looked up.

Lang Yan said with a stiff face: "Let's go back."

Lin Qiu: "Are you awake?"

Lang Yan didn't say anything, leaned over to pick up his partner, and walked toward the cave.

In the warm grass nest, Lin Qiu lay on Lang Yan, his back being gently stroked, and he had a good dream.

Lang Yan pressed the tip of his nose against the soft flesh of Lin Qiu’s neck, sniffing deeply.

Compared to wine, he preferred the scent on his partner.
