萝卜苗移栽后，一个坑三两株，又是施肥又是除草，兔艾跟兔藤几乎天天往地里跑。
如今萝卜长成，叶片嫩绿，郁郁葱葱。
只隔着零星缝隙，才能瞧见藏在底下的胖萝卜。
还是早晨，叶上缀着露珠。
林楸只在边缘走了一圈，摘了十来个个头均匀的，拎着藤筐回去。
溪水彻底冻手了。
林楸洗完萝卜，手红得像萝卜。
萝卜叶叫他剁碎了，狼溶立马跑来拿走喂牲畜，等着萝卜晾干水分的时候，林楸又从山洞里抱了个大肚罐子出来。
罐子矮胖，才到膝盖高。
里头洗干净，用灶上的开水烫过，倒扣着阴干。
狼溶那边将萝卜往食槽里一倒，红鸟争相抢食。他又喂了咩咩兽，它们也乐意吃。
不过弯角兽却不好养，这大家伙挑嘴，脾气也暴躁，养了这么久都没有养熟。
狼山剩下的兽人不多，骨头汤只炖了两锅。
计划是早上一锅，中午一锅。
又用熏肉炒的萝卜叶，还凉拌了小半盆萝卜缨，除了切去的根须跟削皮的几个萝卜，没一点剩下。
肉汤好了，炒菜的味道远远就勾得外面忙碌的兽人聚集起来。
林楸肚子咕咕响，也唤了一声狼溶跟幼崽他们，回来吃饭。
萝卜炖骨头汤，汤色是清透的白，不如鱼汤那么浓厚，也不像藕汤带着点红。看着就跟萝卜肉一样，晶莹可口。
兽人们捧着碗，喝着带点甜味的肉汤喟叹。
兔艾跟兔藤吃了很多萝卜，但没尝试过炖汤，刚一入口，便被惊艳。
汤居然是鲜甜的！
一点不腻，也没有生吃萝卜的呛。
萝卜也好软，抿一下就化了。就算牙口不好的兽人吃着，也不费力气。
老祭司端着自个儿的碗，就是这么美滋滋想的。
比起莲藕炖汤，他更喜欢萝卜。
莲藕要炖许久才软，兽人们牙口大多都好，也都赶时间，多数时候差不多了就行了，不像现在手头这个。
骨头汤虽然没什么肉，但只吃萝卜，也足够满足。
幼崽更别说，要不是太烫，脑袋都钻入碗里去了。
“这个好！咱们以后多种点。”狼莫吃着连连点头，藕汤吃多了，换个口味，没想到同样好吃。
兔艾：“还剩下些种子，这个适合凉快的时候种，只能等明年了。”
“你们还会种什么？”
“萝卜一样的，可以热的时候种的有吗？”
“要多留一点种子，种子够吗？”
一顿萝卜，就叫狼兽人把两个兔兽人围起来了。兔艾看着狼兽人大开的嘴巴，挪着往兔藤身后缩。
也不是怕，是应付不来。
兔藤还是那副温和模样，兽人问什么，他就回答什么。
狼安看着，道：“兔藤脾气真好。”
换做是他，早收拾狼了。
狼雨：“要不说让他带幼崽呢。”
腿坏了只是一方面，人家以前腿好着的时候，也专门负责带幼崽的。
何况兔兽人能生，幼崽不知多少，他能带也是一种能耐。
狼兽人团结，好东西也不吃独食。
萝卜先做来尝尝味儿，中午吃的也是早上多煮的那一锅汤，晚间等其他兽人们回来了，再多弄些花样。
晚间萝卜又拔了不少。
这一天，少说就吃了四五十斤的萝卜，但地里看着却没怎么少。
狼山前又重新燃起了篝火。
火焰丈高，踏着夜色回来的兽人将猎物一扔，绕着篝火躺倒在地。
他们已经忙活了两个月，早出晚归，都没空清理自己。兽人鼻子灵，现在也不爱躺在廊下，因为兽人挤着臭。
加上换毛，又没空梳理，狼毛挂在身上一坨一坨的，看着跟陈年老垢一样，兽人自己都嫌弃自己。
狼岩比兽人们好些，他爱干净，林楸也会给他梳毛。
是以，这么多狼兽人当中，还是狼王最好看。
黑毛透着金属一样的冷光，蓬松粗硬，换毛后脖颈一圈毛毛又极长，显得更加威风。
兽人们等着吃饭，躺在篝火旁闭目养神。
闲不住的，用棍子串了两条巴掌大的小鱼，先烤着尝尝。
灶下的人多，也用不着林楸。
他有些冷了，瞧着篝火那边，晃晃悠悠就走了过去。找准趴在地上最漂亮、体型最大的那头黑狼，坐下去，背靠在它身上。
狼岩挪了挪，摊开温暖腹部，将自家伴侣圈着。
狼岩道：“地上冷，去山洞里。”
“这么大的火，不冷。”林楸侧身趴在狼岩背上，两手摸到狼岩耳朵，“呐，你试试。热乎着呢。”
狼岩眼里闪过无奈。
“毛脏。”
“我不嫌弃你。”
“我不嫌弃你……”兽人酸溜溜地小声学他。想到这寒风瑟瑟，大雪将临，自己只能独自一个兽人窝在草窝里，寒冷孤独……
狼呜的一声，抱头痛嚎。
林楸吓了一跳。
狼岩按住自己伴侣，爪子抓地，夯实的土面上落下一道深痕。
有时候真的很想揍兽人一顿。
“趴稳。”他起身，林楸趴在他背上，下巴垫在狼脑袋上，脸颊左右是软乎的狼耳朵。
“嗯？不烤火了？”
“怕他们受不了。”
“刚刚嚎是因为这个？”
“嗯。”
林楸叹息，鼻尖去蹭狼耳朵。耳朵轻弹，林楸张嘴抿住，狼岩身体一僵，停在原地不动。
偏偏林楸还在思索，没注意，叼着耳朵轻轻地磨。
像幼崽牙痒痒时候的样子。
狼岩无奈，忍着耳上的痒，继续往前走。
他不知道为什么自家伴侣这么喜欢他的耳朵。
“王，狼兽人能找其他兽人当伴侣吗？”
“能找。”
“那不是不同物种吗？”
狼岩知道他什么意思，他已经习惯了自家伴侣不懂这些常识性的东西。狼岩温声道：“都是兽人。”
“那生下来的幼崽……”
“都有可能。兽人们就算找异族，一般也会找体型相差不大的种族，但比起找同族，找异族的不那么容易生崽。”
林楸一手攀住狼耳朵，无意识地揉了揉。
狼岩尾巴倏地僵直，又停了下来。
林楸：“嗯？怎么不走了？”
狼岩不动声色地放松肌肉，“踩着石子了。”
“兽形也会硌脚吗？”
“嗯。”
廊下，狼岩找了个地方重新趴下。
林楸从他背上滑下来，转过身，面对狼岩坐着，两手往狼岩胸口下的毛毛里揣。
他柔韧性好，身体前曲着，额头靠在狼岩大脑袋上，眼睛与那双灰眸对视。
“王。”
“嗯。”狼岩鼻尖碰了碰他的脸，林楸便双手环抱住他脑袋，手掌刚好落在耳朵上。
狼岩：哎……
林楸保持头碰头的姿势，“王，要下雪了，咱们搬下来不？”
狼岩：“现在还不着急。”
最冷的时候没到。
狼岩尾巴一扫，圈在林楸小腿上，“明天开始，不出去捕猎了。”
“抓够了？躺部落了？”
“去洗澡。”
“洗澡？”
*
“洗澡啊？王说的洗澡，那肯定是往西边走了。”狼莫捧着萝卜汤，呼噜噜灌了一大口，舔了舔嘴。
这个时候，兽人都吃上肉汤了，廊下坐满了兽人。
不坐不知道，一坐进来，臭烘烘的味道混着肉汤味，还能听到有兽人打哕。
狼安他们都端着碗出去吃了。
林楸也有些不适应，挪到外面，跟着狼岩一起。
狼西：“在山里面，有几个地方水一直是热的，我们每年雪季之前就会去那边洗澡。洗得干干净净，没臭味儿了，才好一起窝在山洞里过雪季。”
“而且祭司说了，那水洗了好，身上不长痘痘，不生虫。”
林楸：“听着像温泉。”
“温泉？”狼莫品了品，这个名字倒是合适。
林楸中午吃得饱，顺手将碗里的拳头大小的肉夹给了狼岩。全程陪着伴侣吃饭，没有说话的狼王抬起头。
林楸靠着他，轻轻打个饱嗝，“我吃不下了。”
狼岩皱眉，目光掠过林楸肚子。
但他穿得厚，看不出来。
林楸笑着道：“我真吃不下了，好大一碗呢。”
他的饭量已经比以前增长不少，但在兽人们眼里，还是少。
狼莫哼哼吃出猪叫，头也不抬，“晚上饿了可没吃的。”
狼西：“就是就是。”
林楸：“晚上再说。”
狼岩将伴侣分来的肉吃下，看他碗里剩的肉汤，也一并解决了。
饭后，兽人打着喷嚏，不情不愿地往山洞里走。
太呛人了，以前雪季也是这么忙过来的，怎么没觉得兽人这么臭呢？
兽人这么想着，不自觉嘀咕了出来。
狼安翻个大大的白眼，“那是你们以前本来就不爱干净。”
兽人反驳：“明明是饿得没力气了，哪里顾得上这个！”
“就是，就算不洗澡，我们也洗了爪子洗了脸，比其他部落好多了。”
狼安不跟他们争，他现在还记得兽人草窝底下掏出的不知积攒了多少年的腐朽木头。
还有那一窝起码传了十八代的虫！
怕不是十几年前草窝一搭好就没换过。
狼安道：“明天正好有空，去洗澡之前，再把大山洞好好收拾收拾。”
“嗷。”兽人们懒懒回道。
明天洗白白，窝进山洞，啃着肉干每天吃饱了睡，睡饱了吃，兽人从来没有一刻觉得雪季这么舒坦。
兽人们期待着，连梦里都忍不住发出桀桀笑声。
亚兽人听得不耐，抄起边上一个果子扔过去。
兽人尾巴一扫，打掉。
翻个身，继续做大梦去！
chapters.translated_text:
Before the snow season, it is the busiest time of the year for the beastmen.

White frost appears on the ground more and more frequently, and the water in the puddles is gradually drying up, leaving only the paw prints of cubs who ran past in a hurry.

The cubs who used to squat by the puddles to play with ice are now busy cutting grass.

The leaves on the mountains are withering, and the cold wind blows wantonly, scattering fallen leaves everywhere in front of Wolf Mountain.

The ripe fruits are also gradually falling, being gnawed on by animals under the trees or rotting in the ground.

Wooden doors have been installed on the caves of the Wolf Tribe.

Inside the doors are the fresh fruits, fresh vegetables, and various root vegetables that the beastmen gathered in the last bit of time before the snow season.

Thanks to the efforts of the beastmen, dried fish has accumulated in two caves, and dried meat has barely filled another.

As the weather gets colder, the beastmen have begun to store whole animal carcasses directly, waiting only for the freeze to preserve them for the entire snow season.

Lin Qiu has recently developed the habit of getting up early with Lang Yan.

When Lang Yan moves beside him, Lin Qiu, still groggy, tightens his arms around his neck, letting him pull him up as he sits.

Lang Yan gathers the animal skin to wrap him tightly, "Sleep a little longer."

Lin Qiu barely opens his eyes, his hand pinching the animal skin blanket and pushing it away—

Cold air rushes in, and he is instantly awakened by the chill.

Lang Yan frowns, about to wrap him up again.

Lin Qiu yawns, pressing his palm against his chest and pushing lightly, "Not sleeping anymore."

In the eyes of the beastmen, the snow season begins when snow is seen, but Lin Qiu feels that it has already entered winter.

He wraps himself in a layer of linen long sleeves that are wrinkled but much softer, puts on an animal skin vest over it, and then wraps a layer of light fur coat made of soft fleece on the outside.

The linen trousers on his legs have been replaced with animal skin trousers, and he wears a pair of animal skin boots on his feet.

Lin Qiu combs his hair and ties it up with an animal skin rope.

After getting himself ready, he looks back to see that Lang Yan's upper body is still bare, having only changed his previous linen shorts into an animal skin skirt.

Lang Yan sees the envy in his partner's eyes, steps forward, takes the comb from his hand, and puts it away.

"Going down?"

Lin Qiu lowers his head and touches his waist and abdomen.

Lang Yan's breathing hitches as he looks at Lin Qiu, his voice restrained: "I have to hunt, not now, how about tonight?"

Lin Qiu's ears turn red, "I was just checking if you were cold."

Lang Yan is still looking at him, "A little."

He holds Lin Qiu's hand, leaves the cave, and walks down the mountain.

His partner has just left the bed, so his hands are still warm. However, when he returns at night, he won't have this warm feeling.

The east is already turning white, with brighter light than the past few days.

Lin Qiu thinks it's a rare warming, but when he looks to the west, the peaks of the towering mountains are already covered with a layer of white snow.

Lin Qiu: "King, it's snowing."

Lang Yan follows his gaze; high on the mountains, sporadic white spots look like frost flowers.

He says calmly: "The mountain tops are earlier."

The old priest stands on the platform in front of the cave, holding his gorgeous staff hung with stones and shells, looking at the distant horizon. Hearing the voices, he turns his head and says: "Yan, it will snow the day after tomorrow."

Lang Yan: "I know."

For these two months, the wolf beastmen have worked almost every day without rest, whether they were hunting and gathering or staying behind to guard the tribe; even the cubs were busy with things for the snow season.

The snow season is too hard to endure. Even though the beastmen have visibly more food stored this year, the panic of so many years cannot dissipate at once.

Down at the foot of the mountain, most of the beastmen have come out.

Lang An also called two beastmen to bring over two baskets of dried fish and lotus roots, placing them at the edge of the team. The beastmen consciously take a little from a basket and put it into the animal skin pouches tied to their waists.

The rabbit beastmen arrived early; their physical strength is not as good as the wolf beastmen, and their appetites are smaller.

Standing here early, they eat some dried fish or lotus root while waiting. Seeing Lang Yan come down, they put the leftovers into their pouches, knowing it's time to go.

Each team counts their beastmen and sets off into the morning light.

Lin Qiu watches them leave.

In front of several stoves burning with red light, steam fills the air.

Lin Qiu walks to the stove and sits down to help with the fire.

Lang An is deboning meat; there is still some shredded meat left on the ribs, red and fresh. The sub-beastman finds the fragile joint, twists it with both hands, and the animal bone is completely separated.

Lin Qiu: "An, the priest said it's going to snow."

Lang An is unhurried, "Look at the mountains on the Black Feather Tribe's side, they already have some snow; it's about this time."

"Will the first snow be very heavy?"

"It's different every year. Last year it was very heavy; in one night, everything was white."

Lang An thinks Lin Qiu is afraid and hands him the bones to put into several clay pots, "Don't worry, we've survived previous snow seasons with not much food. This year we have food in several caves, what is there to fear?"

Lin Qiu: "I know."

It's just his first year, he's unsure and always on edge.

The rainy season was bad enough, and from what the beastmen say, it gets tens of degrees below zero outside during the snow season, which would freeze people to death. Even the beastmen don't dare to walk outside the cave, which shows how hard it is.

Thinking of this, Lin Qiu says nervously: "An, should we hoard some water? And firewood!"

Lang Hong passes by holding radishes just harvested from the field, on his way to wash them in the stream. Lin Qiu's words are carried by the wind to his ears, and he laughs: "Qiu, relax."

The snow season is right in front of them, and the beastmen see the caves full of food, so their panic has lessened, but Lin Qiu has become more and more nervous, to the point that even they can feel it.

Lin Qiu: "I'm just afraid of missing something."

Ever since he finished counting the food last time and found that so much was only enough to last half the snow season, Lin Qiu became anxious.

Lang An: "Don't worry, it's been so many years, we might miss anything, but we won't miss firewood."

Lang Mo has burned quite a bit of charcoal, but the beastmen have also cut a lot of firewood; just the thick logs alone fill two large caves, not to mention the hay and branches.

The charcoal Lang Mo burned also fills a whole cave.

Several caves are large, and the firewood is plentiful.

As for water...

"We used to just dig up snow and put it in jars, and roasting it by the fire makes water. It will be very cold then, and if we fill jars now, it will freeze into ice, which is hard to take."

This is the life experience of the beastmen.

There is no air pollution here, so the snow is naturally clean.

However, after the beastmen mentioned it, he did feel that he was a bit too tense.

Just then, when Lang Hong came back with a basin, Lin Qiu saw the radishes in his basin.

"The radishes are ready?" Lin Qiu asked.

The radishes in the basin are large, with the smallest weighing at least a pound. They have all been washed by the beastmen, with the leaves in one pile and the radishes in another.

Tu Ai and Tu Teng finished cleaning the field, washed their hands, and slowly came to the veranda.

Hearing Lin Qiu's words, Tu Ai said: "They grow fast."

The radishes came at the right time; they are the rabbit beastmen's own winter food.

The radishes weren't called this name at first; according to the rabbit beastmen's heritage, it was the name given to them by the Beast God's messenger hundreds of years ago.

And the original radishes weren't this big; they were improved and optimized by the rabbit beastmen generation after generation.

It can be said that this is one of the most impressive types of plants grown by the rabbit beastmen.

"Tu Ai, is it okay to put them in bone soup?" Lang An asked.

The radishes were brought by the rabbit beastmen, so he subconsciously asked the expert.

Tu Ai: "Yes."

Everything can be stewed in bone soup.

The purpose is not to make the bone soup taste good, but to let the bland vegetables get some meat flavor. The meat-loving beastmen still have preferences.

The radishes aren't peeled either; Lin Qiu watches as Lang An raises his knife and starts chopping.

It's really a bit rough, without any order; after a few random chops, the radishes become pieces of different sizes.

Perhaps he is used to chopping lotus roots and hasn't handled this round, chubby thing before.

Lin Qiu gets up and takes his small knife, "Peel them?"

Lang An's hand pauses, the knife embeds into the radish, and the cutting board shakes.

"Need to peel?"

Tu Ai is organizing the radish leaves. He looks up, his eyes also confused, "We just gnaw on them directly; the skin is a bit pungent."

But food is precious, and the skin isn't inedible.

Lin Qiu: "How about trying to peel a pot? The skin can be chopped up and given to the red birds."

He just wants to improve the food for his red birds and sheep-beasts.

And after peeling, the texture is a bit better.

Lang An naturally has no objections.

Lin Qiu stands next to him, takes a radish, peels it, and cuts it into rolling pieces. Then he takes another radish, peels it, cuts it in half, and then cuts it into neat pieces.

Lang An watches, and slowly the radishes under his hands become uniform in size.

Lin Qiu's lips curl up, he stops working and turns to look at the radish leaves in Tu Ai's hands.

"How do you eat these?"

Tu Ai blinks, "Eat them raw."

They know the Wolf Tribe has many tricks, but they didn't have clay pots before.

The rabbit beastmen have tried other methods, such as roasting them, but it always felt strange and not as good as eating them raw.

Lin Qiu: "How about trying to stir-fry them, or mix them with seasoning? Pickled radish also sounds good."

At the thought of pickled radish, Lin Qiu's mouth waters.

Isn't this a coincidence? They have radishes, they have clay pots, and they definitely don't lack salt.

Lin Qiu: "An, radish leaves can be stir-fried with smoked meat, preferably with a mix of fat and lean."

As for stir-frying, the beastmen are already very familiar with it.

It just so happens that today is the first time eating radishes, so according to habit, they will try various cooking methods, and whichever is delicious, they will stick to that one in the future.

These sub-beastmen all know how to do it, but Lin Qiu is thinking about pickled radish.

"Tu Ai, can we pull a few more radishes?"

Lin Qiu certainly knows they can be pulled, but in the eyes of the beastmen, radishes are grown by the rabbit beastmen; how would a wolf beastman know?

Tu Ai nods, "Just look for the big ones."

This batch they picked are the largest ones, and the smaller ones will continue to grow.

But the snow season is coming, so it's best not to leave them in the ground, otherwise they will be hard to dig. Unless buried deep in the soil, they will rot.

Lin Qiu: "I'll try a few first."

"Try what?" the middle-aged beastmen ask, looking over.

If Lin Qiu makes food, it must be delicious.

Lin Qiu: "Pickled radish."

"Like pickled meat?" Tu Ai doesn't understand either and asks in a low voice.

Tu Teng is carefully organizing the radish leaves, "I don't know either."

Lang An: "We don't know either, Qiu always has many methods we can't think of."

In the field to the east, Lin Qiu carries a rattan basket to pull radishes.

Don't look at the fact that the beastmen only cultivated a small patch of seedlings at first, but the beastmen didn't discard a single seedling.

After the radish seedlings were transplanted, there were two or three plants in one hole, and they were fertilized and weeded; Tu Ai and Tu Teng ran to the field almost every day.

Now that the radishes have grown, the leaves are tender green and lush.

Only through sporadic gaps can one see the fat radishes hidden at the bottom.

It is still morning, and the leaves are dotted with dew.

Lin Qiu walks around the edge, picks ten or so of uniform size, and carries the rattan basket back.

The stream water is completely freezing to the hands.

After Lin Qiu washes the radishes, his hands are as red as the radishes.

He chops the radish leaves, and Lang Rong immediately runs over to take them to feed the livestock. While waiting for the radishes to air-dry, Lin Qiu takes a big-bellied jar out of the cave.

The jar is short and fat, reaching only to his knees.

It is washed clean, scalded with boiling water from the stove, and turned upside down to dry in the shade.

Lang Rong pours the radishes into the trough, and the red birds scramble for food. He also feeds the sheep-beasts, and they are happy to eat them too.

However, the curved-horn beasts are not easy to raise; these big guys are picky and have a bad temper, and they haven't been tamed after being raised for so long.

There aren't many beastmen left on Wolf Mountain, so only two pots of bone soup were stewed.

The plan is one pot in the morning and one pot at noon.

They also used smoked meat to stir-fry the radish leaves and made a small basin of cold-dressed radish tops. Except for the roots that were cut off and the few radishes that were peeled, nothing was left.

The meat soup is ready, and the smell of the stir-fried vegetables draws the busy beastmen outside to gather.

Lin Qiu's stomach growls, so he calls Lang Rong and the cubs to come back to eat.

The radish and bone soup has a clear white color, not as thick as fish soup, nor as red as lotus root soup. It looks just like the radish meat, crystal clear and delicious.

The beastmen hold their bowls, drinking the sweet-tasting meat soup and sighing with satisfaction.

Tu Ai and Tu Teng ate a lot of radishes, but they had never tried stewing them in soup. As soon as they took a bite, they were amazed.

The soup is actually fresh and sweet!

It's not greasy at all, and doesn't have the pungency of raw radishes.

The radishes are also very soft, melting with a sip. Even beastmen with bad teeth can eat them without effort.

The old priest holds his own bowl, thinking exactly this.

Compared to lotus root soup, he prefers radishes.

Lotus root takes a long time to stew until soft, and most beastmen have good teeth and are in a hurry, so most of the time it's just "good enough," unlike the one in his hands now.

Although the bone soup doesn't have much meat, just eating the radishes is satisfying enough.

Not to mention the cubs; if it weren't too hot, they would have buried their heads in the bowls.

"This is good! Let's grow more in the future." Lang Mo nods repeatedly while eating. He had eaten too much lotus root soup, so changing the flavor was unexpectedly delicious.

Tu Ai: "There are still some seeds left. This is suitable for planting when it's cool, so we have to wait until next year."

"What else can you grow?"

"Is there anything like radishes that can be planted when it's hot?"

"Need to save more seeds, are there enough seeds?"

A meal of radishes makes the wolf beastmen surround the two rabbit beastmen. Tu Ai looks at the wolf beastmen's open mouths and shrinks behind Tu Teng.

It's not fear, it's just that he can't handle it.

Tu Teng is still his gentle self, answering whatever the beastmen ask.

Lang An watches and says: "Tu Teng has a really good temper."

If it were him, he would have already dealt with the wolves.

Lang Yu: "That's why we let him take care of the cubs."

His leg being broken is only one aspect; even when his legs were fine, he was specifically responsible for taking care of the cubs.

Besides, rabbit beastmen are fertile and have countless cubs; his ability to take care of them is a skill in itself.

The wolf beastmen are united and don't eat good things alone.

They made the radishes to taste them first, and they ate the same pot of soup at noon that was cooked in the morning. In the evening, when the other beastmen return, they will make more varieties.

More radishes were pulled in the evening.

On this day, they ate at least forty or fifty pounds of radishes, but the field didn't look like it had decreased much.

The bonfire was lit again in front of Wolf Mountain.

The flames are high, and the beastmen returning through the night throw down their prey and lie on the ground around the bonfire.

They have been busy for two months, leaving early and returning late, without time to clean themselves. Beastmen have sharp noses, and now they don't like lying on the veranda because the beastmen are smelly when crowded together.

Plus, they are shedding their fur and don't have time to groom, so the wolf fur hangs on their bodies in clumps, looking like old dirt, and the beastmen themselves are disgusted.

Lang Yan is better than the other beastmen; he loves cleanliness, and Lin Qiu also grooms him.

Therefore, among so many wolf beastmen, the Wolf King is still the best-looking.

His black fur has a cold, metallic sheen, fluffy and coarse. After shedding, the fur around his neck is extremely long, making him look even more majestic.

The beastmen wait for food, lying by the bonfire with their eyes closed to rest.

Those who can't sit still use sticks to skewer two small fish the size of a palm and roast them to taste first.

There are many people under the stove, so Lin Qiu doesn't need to help.

He is a bit cold, so he looks at the bonfire and wanders over. He finds the most beautiful and largest black wolf lying on the ground, sits down, and leans his back against it.

Lang Yan moves, spreads his warm abdomen, and circles his partner.

Lang Yan says: "The ground is cold, go to the cave."

"With such a big fire, it's not cold." Lin Qiu lies on his side on Lang Yan's back, his hands touching Lang Yan's ears, "Here, you try. It's warm."

A flash of helplessness crosses Lang Yan's eyes.

"The fur is dirty."

"I don't mind you."

"I don't mind you..." the beastman mimics him in a small, jealous voice. Thinking of the cold wind, the heavy snow about to come, and himself having to curl up in a grass nest alone, cold and lonely...

The wolf lets out a howl, holding his head in pain.

Lin Qiu is startled.

Lang Yan presses down on his partner, his claws gripping the ground, leaving a deep mark on the solid earth.

Sometimes he really wants to beat the beastman up.

"Hold on tight." He stands up, and Lin Qiu lies on his back, his chin resting on the wolf's head, his cheeks flanked by soft wolf ears.

"Hmm? Not roasting by the fire anymore?"

"Afraid they can't stand it."

"Was that why you howled just now?"

"Yeah."

Lin Qiu sighs, rubbing his nose against the wolf's ears. The ears flick, and Lin Qiu opens his mouth to nibble on them. Lang Yan's body stiffens, stopping in place.

But Lin Qiu is still thinking and doesn't notice, gently grinding his teeth on the ears.

Like the way cubs do when their teeth are itchy.

Lang Yan is helpless, enduring the itch on his ears, and continues to walk forward.

He doesn't know why his partner likes his ears so much.

"King, can wolf beastmen find other beastmen as partners?"

"They can."

"Isn't that a different species?"

Lang Yan knows what he means; he is already used to his partner not understanding these common-sense things. Lang Yan says warmly: "They are all beastmen."

"Then the cubs born..."

"Anything is possible. Even if beastmen find other races, they generally find races with similar body sizes, but compared to finding the same race, it's not as easy to have cubs with other races."

Lin Qiu climbs onto the wolf's ears with one hand, rubbing them unconsciously.

Lang Yan's tail suddenly stiffens, and he stops again.

Lin Qiu: "Hmm? Why did you stop?"

Lang Yan relaxes his muscles calmly, "Stepped on a pebble."

"Does the beast form also get sore feet?"

"Yeah."

On the veranda, Lang Yan finds a place to lie down again.

Lin Qiu slides off his back, turns around, sits facing Lang Yan, and sticks his hands into the fur under Lang Yan's chest.

He has good flexibility, bending his body forward, his forehead resting on Lang Yan's big head, his eyes meeting those gray eyes.

"King."

"Yeah." Lang Yan touches his face with his nose, and Lin Qiu hugs his head with both hands, his palms landing just right on the ears.

Lang Yan: Sigh...

Lin Qiu maintains the head-to-head posture, "King, it's going to snow, are we moving down?"

Lang Yan: "No rush yet."

The coldest time hasn't arrived.

Lang Yan sweeps his tail, circling Lin Qiu's lower legs, "Starting tomorrow, we won't go out hunting."

"Caught enough? Lying in the tribe?"

"Go take a bath."

"Take a bath?"

*

"Take a bath? If the King says take a bath, he must be going to the west side." Lang Mo holds the radish soup, gulps down a big mouthful, and licks his lips.

At this time, the beastmen have all eaten the meat soup, and the veranda is full of beastmen.

You wouldn't know until you sat down; once you sit in, the smelly odor mixed with the meat soup smell is overwhelming, and you can even hear some beastmen retching.

Lang An and the others all took their bowls outside to eat.

Lin Qiu is also a bit unaccustomed to it, so he moves outside, following Lang Yan.

Lang Xi: "Inside the mountain, there are a few places where the water is always hot. We go there to bathe every year before the snow season. Only after we are clean and have no smell can we huddle together in the cave to spend the snow season."

"And the priest said that the water is good for washing; it prevents pimples and insects on the body."

Lin Qiu: "Sounds like a hot spring."

"Hot spring?" Lang Mo tastes the name, it's quite fitting.

Lin Qiu ate his fill at noon, so he hands the fist-sized meat in his bowl to Lang Yan. The Wolf King, who has been accompanying his partner to eat without speaking, looks up.

Lin Qiu leans against him, burping gently, "I can't eat anymore."

Lang Yan frowns, his gaze sweeping over Lin Qiu's stomach.

But he is dressed thickly, so he can't see it.

Lin Qiu says with a smile: "I really can't eat anymore, it's such a big bowl."

His appetite has increased a lot compared to before, but in the eyes of the beastmen, it's still small.

Lang Mo grunts while eating, not looking up, "There won't be food if you're hungry at night."

Lang Xi: "That's right, that's right."

Lin Qiu: "We'll talk about tonight later."

Lang Yan eats the meat his partner shared, and finishes the remaining meat soup in his bowl as well.

After the meal, the beastmen sneeze and walk into the cave reluctantly.

It's too pungent; they've been busy through the snow season before, why didn't they feel the beastmen were so smelly?

The beastmen think so and mutter it out unconsciously.

Lang An rolls his eyes, "That's because you didn't like to be clean before."

The beastmen retort: "It's clearly because we were too hungry and had no strength, how could we care about that!"

"That's right, even if we didn't take a bath, we washed our paws and faces, much better than other tribes."

Lang An doesn't argue with them; he still remembers the rotten wood dug out from under the beastmen's grass nests that had accumulated for who knows how many years.

And that nest of insects that had been passed down for at least eighteen generations!

It's probably been there since the grass nest was built over a decade ago and never changed.

Lang An says: "Tomorrow happens to be free, before going to bathe, let's clean up the big cave properly."

"Awoo," the beastmen reply lazily.

Tomorrow they will wash clean, curl up in the cave, gnaw on dried meat, eat and sleep every day; the beastmen have never felt the snow season was so comfortable.

The beastmen look forward to it, and can't help but let out cackling laughs even in their dreams.

The sub-beastmen are impatient and pick up a fruit from the side and throw it over.

The beastman sweeps his tail and knocks it away.

He turns over and continues to have his big dream!
chapters.title: 第119章

chapters.source_text:
林楸睡了一会儿，清醒得差不多，去溪边捧着水洗了洗脸。
短短半日，兽人们已经翻出一大块地，自狼山西部一直蔓延开，一片漆黑。
狼累得倒地，胸腹、爪子黢黑。
而另一边，十几个兽人拎着肥硕的鱼，浑身湿漉漉地靠近狼山。
那鱼各个快一米甚至超过一米长，几十斤重，上辈子也就禁渔多年的江河才养得出来。
这不是有肉吃？
兽人吃鱼依旧是烤，狼莫抖着黑漆漆的四条腿儿来问：“楸，你还要新鲜鱼还是烤好的？”
林楸：“自己烤。”
狼莫蔫蔫点头，又拖着步子回去。
林楸干脆跟着他，自己去拿。
兽人杀鱼也跟杀野兽一样，开膛破肚，鳞片刮掉，不过鱼鳃保留着。
鱼肚子里内脏太腥，兽人们一吃就吐，实在下不去口才扔了。
林楸依旧分了巴掌大的一块鱼肉，他拿去小溪边冲洗几遍，内里也收拾得干干净净。
这鱼肉看着极好，颜色淡粉，肉晶莹剔透。
林楸先煎一半煮鱼汤，另一半直接烤。
狼岩送的小刀切鱼肉跟切豆腐一样，林楸用得很趁手。鱼片片得薄薄的，几下就煎出香味儿。
灶上炖鱼汤的时候，林楸将烤得外焦里嫩的鱼肉撕着吃。肉质细嫩，能吃到鱼肉的纤维感，还有些软弹。
只放了几颗盐的鱼肉也不腥，只有木柴的香。
这么好吃，要是河里多，尽可以多捞些。
林楸心里有了些想法。
几下就吃完烤鱼，远远看着兽人们吃一口吐两下，面上艰难，还有被鱼刺卡着拼命咳嗽的。
吃个鱼，兽人们如临大敌。
早有聪明的，摸到了楸这边。看看他吃干净了烤鱼肉，再瞧瞧他锅里奶白色的鱼汤，瞪圆了眼，满脸惊奇。
狼莫抓着自个儿也没烤的鱼，扭捏道：“楸，你怎么做的，教一教我们可不可以？”
一码归一码，他可以用下一顿的肉换。
狼西胳膊挂在狼莫肩上，两条腿无力垂着，也飞快点头。
身边围着四五个兽人。
远远的，又见着几个偷偷摸摸往这边靠近。
林楸：“好。”
烤鱼并不难，只是兽人们不讲究，将肉往火堆里一扔，等自己觉得肉差不多熟透了，再把肉刨出来。
这就导致他们烤出来的肉糊的占一大部分。
至于为什么不守着烤，因为又困又饿又累，坐在火堆旁边没一会儿就闭着眼睛脑袋直点，一不小心被燎了毛的事很常见。
林楸叫他们把鱼肉用木棍串好，就围着他那小火堆烤。
鱼皮卷曲滋滋冒油了，再换面。
这对兽人们来说麻烦，这手拿着棍子没一会儿，就想把鱼肉往火堆里一架。
林楸：“要糊了，翻面。”
兽人齐刷刷的一翻，已经无聊得耷拉眼皮时，忽然闻到一阵焦香。
鼻子使劲儿耸了几下，几个狼兽人开始咽口水。
林楸：“撒点盐，均匀一点，多了咸。”
兽人你看我，我看你，没带。
林楸直接将自己那一小包拿出来。
有的兽人一抓半把，林楸木棍抵着他手背，“多了。”
亚兽人严肃的时候面色略冷，像雪天似的，直冒冷气。
兽人们也不知道怎么了，乖乖听话。
不过抓个盐都得调整好几次，生怕盐少了。怪不得之前吃的糊肉块一会儿极咸一会儿淡的。
鱼肉烤得很快，林楸一说好，兽人们立马撤回木棍。呼哧呼哧在鱼肉上吹了两口，张开嘴巴争先恐后咬住。
咔哧咔哧的声音酥脆，很悦耳。
呼呜！
好吃，好好吃！
林楸见差不多，也把自己鱼汤的火撤了。一转头，好几个脑袋凑在这边。
“吸溜……”狼莫收回分泌过多的口水。
林楸看他们木棍上空荡荡，还有兽人在咬棍子上的那点肉，问：“吃完了？”
那么大块肉，跟没嚼一样，一口吞了。
“吃完了。”狼莫道。
兽人们点头。
眼睛只盯着林楸的石锅，没心眼似的，很憨。
嘴里残留着烤鱼的香味，兽人忍不住舔了下嘴巴，咂摸着，有些没吃够。
味儿都没尝到呢，鱼肉就没有了。
而且刺不扎舌头，脆脆的诶！
林楸看着他们闪亮的眼睛，道：“没有多的。”
兽人失望，脚步像灌了铅，一步一沉重地离开。
林楸轻轻一叹。
他将自己锅里的鱼汤倒了一半在巴掌大的小木桶里，这是他的饭碗，余下的就交给狼果。
狼果：“幼崽有吃的。”
林楸：“我吃不完。”
狼果接过，哼也不哼了，不知怎么面对林楸，赶紧先去喂幼崽。
狼果一左一右两口锅，抱得格外轻松。
锅里的汤晃动，对比自己陶锅里泛着一股腥味的肉糜，楸那白色的鱼汤闻着格外香，看着也好吃。
狼果也看到了刚刚那些兽人围着楸，他也有些想知道怎么做的。
……
种子才下地，夜里就又下起了雨。
白日出太阳温度正合适，但晚上风吹就冷。洞口没封，风直接灌到底，就是边上有狼岩挡着也有些冷。
林楸蜷着蜷着，不断后退。
两个草窝挨着，这一退，狼岩兽形本就高处草窝一大截，林楸后背直接贴在了狼岩的背上。
深长的毛发似最暖和的绒毯，林楸又觉得后背漏风，迷糊间往后摸了摸，拽着东西搭在身上。
狼岩尾巴一僵，毛沿着脊骨炸开，耳朵竖得笔直。
他浑身僵硬，尾巴迅速往回撤。
林楸翻身一滚，落入草窝，人懵懵地坐起来，与狼岩眼瞪眼。
狼岩眼珠不动。
林楸闭眼往草窝里一倒，拽着兽皮昏睡。
狼耳动得厉害，狼岩晃了下尾巴，翻个身，往草窝边缘睡去。四肢落在草窝外悬空，离滚下去不远。
许久，狼耳又一哆嗦。
*
一觉天明。
山洞里安静，浮尘在光束下飘动。
兽人们又出去找猎物了。
昨儿鱼吃完了，肉干又给了幼崽，林楸也只能挨饿到兽人们回来。
上午依旧干活，不过这次要处理的植物起码少了一半。
正觉轻松，祭司又叫他吃药糊糊。
林楸抿紧嘴角，脖子往后，直抵着木架子没了退路。
“不吃能不能行？”
他自我感觉挺好。
老祭司：“要我把你阿父叫来部落？”
林楸：“我还有阿父？”
“吃！”祭司气得，木杖上的石头晃得叮当响。
连自己还有阿父都不知道了！
林楸怕自己把老兽人气出个好歹，只能捏着鼻子往下灌。祭司盯着，吃得一口没剩。
这下饥饿的肚子一下饱了。
林楸半死不活，靠着木架子闭目。
祭司看不过眼，塞了他一片叶子叫他嚼烂。
林楸：“不行……”
呕！
祭司直接塞他嘴里。
林楸：甜的？
他嚼吧嚼吧咽了，“还有没有？”
祭司：“没了。”
当什么草都能吃！
都成年两年了，还当自己是幼崽？！
中午照旧睡了一觉，全是祭司那一大碗药糊糊的作用。等林楸晕晕乎乎醒来，天都黑了。
后脑有些胀痛，林楸缓了一会儿才爬起来。
外出的兽人也回来了。
今日抓到猎物数量多，但个头小，像鸡又像鸟，林楸分到一条腿儿。
采集队带回来的各类能吃的植物依旧不少，惊喜的是还有浆果。
指头大小，林楸尝了一个，酸酸甜甜，脆脆的。口味像蓝莓那一类。
肉少，兽人们没凑过来学艺。都是自己囫囵嚼吧嚼吧，再啃几口草赶紧回山洞睡觉。
林楸把腿儿上的肉剔下来，切成小块儿，直接炖了汤。
随着炖煮的时间越长，鸡汤似的香味儿愈浓。
那味儿甚至比烤鱼的味道还要霸道，随着风一阵吹进山洞，洞里兽人们噌的一下竖起耳朵，眼冒绿光。
“好香好香好香……”
狼莫爪子捂住鼻子，嫌堵不住，一头扎入狼西的毛毛里。闷闷的声音传出，“肯定是楸。”
“一口能吞的肉，怎么弄得这么香嗷呜……要是我们有大大的陶锅就好了，全部肉一起煮，喝汤我都愿意！”
狼西馋得啃了一口狼莫的耳朵，“没有，只有中央大陆的丘山部落会做。”
部落的陶锅都是他们先辈还在中央大陆的时候交换来的。
“王！要不咱们像楸那样挖个大石锅吧，多挖几个。”山洞里有兽人喊道。
“王不在洞里。”
林楸吃完晚饭，看了眼才刚刚从祭司山洞出来的狼岩，慢慢往大山洞里走。
狼岩腿长步子大，不一会儿就跟到林楸后头。
正以为他要走到前头去，发觉他压着步子，离自己不远不近的位置。
“楸。”沉静的夜里，他叫得突兀。
“嗯？”林楸下意识转头。
狼岩看着他的脸像观察什么，过会儿，越过他离开。
林楸停在原地，敛下睫。
怀疑我了？
林楸心跳急促了些，追着狼岩进山洞，窝进草窝里，余光注意着兽人。
狼岩何其敏锐。
他一下化作狼形，耳朵抖了下。
林楸皱眉，拉高兽皮，将自己陷入草窝。
“你可以靠近大河，也可以进林子。”狼岩说完，往草窝另一侧挪了挪，闭上眼睛不再说话。
林楸：“好。”
不怀疑，还自由了。
这是祭司跟狼岩商量的结果，楸依旧需要每天半日去祭司那里，但可行动的范围扩大。
不过仍旧继续有兽人盯着他。
老祭司说，太拘着楸不好，影响他身体恢复。
狼岩略想了想，便同意了。
chapters.translated_text:
Lin Qiu slept for a while, and once he was mostly awake, he went to the stream to cup some water and wash his face.

In just half a day, the beastmen had already cleared a large plot of land, spreading out from the west side of Wolf Mountain, leaving the ground pitch black.

The wolves were so exhausted they collapsed to the ground, their chests, bellies, and paws covered in black dirt.

On the other side, a dozen or so beastmen approached Wolf Mountain, soaking wet and carrying fat, plump fish.

Those fish were each nearly a meter or even longer, weighing dozens of catties; in his past life, only rivers that had been closed to fishing for many years could produce such specimens.

Doesn't this mean there's meat to eat?

Beastmen still roasted their fish. Lang Mo, shaking his pitch-black legs, came over to ask, "Qiu, do you want fresh fish or roasted ones?"

Lin Qiu: "I'll roast them myself."

Lang Mo nodded listlessly and dragged his feet back.

Lin Qiu simply followed him to go get some himself.

Beastmen killed fish the same way they killed wild beasts—gutting them and scraping off the scales, though they kept the gills.

The internal organs in the fish belly were too fishy; the beastmen would vomit as soon as they ate them, so they only threw them away when they truly couldn't stomach them.

Lin Qiu still took a palm-sized piece of fish meat, took it to the stream to rinse it several times, and cleaned the inside thoroughly.

This fish meat looked excellent; it was a pale pink color, and the flesh was translucent.

Lin Qiu pan-seared half of it to make fish soup and roasted the other half directly.

The small knife Lang Yan had given him cut the fish meat like tofu, and Lin Qiu found it very handy. He sliced the fish thinly, and it didn't take long for it to start smelling fragrant as it seared.

While the fish soup simmered on the stove, Lin Qiu tore off pieces of the fish meat, which was charred on the outside and tender on the inside, to eat. The texture was delicate and tender; he could feel the fibers of the meat, and it was slightly soft and springy.

Even with only a few grains of salt, the fish wasn't fishy at all, possessing only the aroma of the firewood.

It was so delicious; if there were plenty in the river, he could catch a lot more.

Lin Qiu had some ideas in mind.

He finished his roasted fish in a few bites, then looked over at the beastmen in the distance, who were taking a bite and spitting twice, their faces pained, some coughing desperately as they got stuck with fish bones.

Eating fish was like facing a formidable enemy for the beastmen.

Some of the smarter ones had already made their way over to Qiu. Seeing him finish his roasted fish, then looking at the milky-white fish soup in his pot, their eyes widened in amazement.

Lang Mo clutched his own unroasted fish and said bashfully, "Qiu, how did you make that? Could you teach us?"

Business was business; he could trade his next meal's meat for it.

Lang Xi, with his arm draped over Lang Mo's shoulder and his two legs dangling limply, nodded rapidly as well.

Four or five beastmen were gathered around him.

In the distance, he saw a few more sneaking toward them.

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

Roasting fish wasn't difficult, but the beastmen were careless; they would throw the meat into the fire and wait until they felt it was cooked through before digging it out.

This resulted in most of the meat they roasted being burnt.

As for why they didn't watch it while it roasted, it was because they were so sleepy, hungry, and tired that they would start nodding off while sitting by the fire, and it was common for them to accidentally singe their fur.

Lin Qiu told them to skewer the fish meat with wooden sticks and roast them around his small fire.

When the fish skin curled and started sizzling with oil, they were to flip it.

This was troublesome for the beastmen; after holding the stick for a while, they would want to just prop the fish meat right into the fire.

Lin Qiu: "It's going to burn, flip it."

The beastmen flipped in unison, and just as they were getting bored and drooping their eyelids, they suddenly smelled a charred fragrance.

Their noses twitched hard, and the wolf beastmen started to salivate.

Lin Qiu: "Sprinkle some salt, keep it even, too much and it'll be salty."

The beastmen looked at each other; they hadn't brought any.

Lin Qiu took out his own small pouch.

Some beastmen grabbed half a handful, but Lin Qiu pressed his wooden stick against the back of their hand, "Too much."

When the sub-beastman was serious, his expression was slightly cold, like a snowy day, radiating a chill.

The beastmen didn't know what came over them, but they obeyed obediently.

However, they had to adjust their salt-grabbing several times, terrified of using too little. No wonder the burnt meat chunks they ate before were sometimes extremely salty and sometimes bland.

The fish meat roasted quickly. As soon as Lin Qiu said it was ready, the beastmen immediately pulled back their sticks. They blew on the meat a few times and then opened their mouths, scrambling to take a bite.

The crunching sound was crisp and pleasant.

Whoo!

Delicious, so delicious!

Seeing that it was about time, Lin Qiu also removed the fire from his fish soup. Turning his head, he saw several heads crowding around.

"Slurp..." Lang Mo retracted his excessive saliva.

Lin Qiu looked at their empty sticks, and at the beastmen still biting the bits of meat off the sticks, and asked, "Finished?"

Such a large piece of meat, they swallowed it in one bite as if they hadn't even chewed.

"Finished," Lang Mo said.

The beastmen nodded.

Their eyes were fixed solely on Lin Qiu's stone pot, looking as simple-minded as could be.

With the lingering taste of the roasted fish in their mouths, the beastmen couldn't help but lick their lips, savoring it, feeling like they hadn't eaten enough.

They hadn't even tasted the flavor before the fish was gone.

Plus, the bones didn't prick their tongues; they were crunchy!

Lin Qiu looked at their shining eyes and said, "There isn't any more."

The beastmen were disappointed, their footsteps heavy as if filled with lead as they left.

Lin Qiu sighed softly.

He poured half of the fish soup from his pot into a palm-sized wooden bucket—his own bowl—and left the rest for Lang Guo.

Lang Guo: "The cubs have food."

Lin Qiu: "I can't finish it."

Lang Guo took it, stopped grunting, and not knowing how to face Lin Qiu, hurried off to feed the cubs.

Lang Guo held the two pots, one in each hand, with surprising ease.

The soup in the pot sloshed; compared to the fishy-smelling minced meat in his own clay pot, Qiu's white fish soup smelled exceptionally fragrant and looked delicious too.

Lang Guo had also seen those beastmen surrounding Qiu earlier, and he was also curious about how it was made.

...

The seeds had just been sown when it started raining again at night.

The temperature was just right when the sun was out during the day, but the wind was cold at night. The cave entrance wasn't sealed, so the wind blew straight to the back, and even with Lang Yan blocking the side, it was still a bit cold.

Lin Qiu curled up, constantly backing away.

The two grass nests were side by side, and as he retreated, Lang Yan's beast form was already much taller than the nest, so Lin Qiu's back pressed directly against Lang Yan's back.

The long, thick fur felt like the warmest velvet blanket. Lin Qiu felt a draft on his back, and in his daze, he reached back and pulled something over himself.

Lang Yan's tail stiffened, his fur bristled along his spine, and his ears stood straight up.

His whole body went rigid, and his tail quickly retracted.

Lin Qiu rolled over, fell into the grass nest, sat up in a daze, and stared eye-to-eye with Lang Yan.

Lang Yan's eyes didn't move.

Lin Qiu closed his eyes, fell back into the grass nest, and drifted off to sleep while clutching the animal skin.

His wolf ears twitched violently; Lang Yan flicked his tail, turned over, and slept on the edge of the grass nest. His limbs hung over the edge of the nest, not far from rolling off.

After a long while, his wolf ears twitched again.

*

Morning came.

The cave was quiet, and dust motes floated in the beams of light.

The beastmen had gone out to find prey again.

The fish from yesterday was gone, and the dried meat had been given to the cubs, so Lin Qiu could only go hungry until the beastmen returned.

He worked in the morning as usual, but this time the plants that needed processing were at least half as many.

Just as he was feeling relieved, the priest called him to eat the medicinal paste.

Lin Qiu pursed his lips, his neck pressed back against the wooden frame with no room to retreat.

"Can I not eat it?"

He felt perfectly fine.

The old priest: "Do you want me to call your father to the tribe?"

Lin Qiu: "I still have a father?"

"Eat!" The priest was so angry that the stones on his wooden staff rattled.

He didn't even know he still had a father!

Lin Qiu was afraid of giving the old beastman a heart attack, so he had to pinch his nose and gulp it down. The priest watched him until he didn't leave a drop.

Now his hungry stomach was suddenly full.

Lin Qiu felt half-dead, leaning against the wooden frame with his eyes closed.

The priest couldn't stand to watch, so he shoved a leaf into his hand and told him to chew it up.

Lin Qiu: "No..."

Ugh!

The priest shoved it directly into his mouth.

Lin Qiu: It's sweet?

He chewed it and swallowed, "Are there any more?"

The priest: "No more."

As if every grass can be eaten!

He's been an adult for two years, does he still think he's a cub?!

He took a nap at noon as usual, all thanks to that big bowl of medicinal paste from the priest. By the time Lin Qiu woke up feeling dizzy, it was already dark.

The back of his head throbbed, and it took a while for Lin Qiu to crawl up.

The beastmen who had gone out had also returned.

They had caught a lot of prey today, but they were small, looking like chickens or birds, and Lin Qiu was given a leg.

The gathering team had brought back plenty of edible plants, and to his surprise, there were berries too.

They were the size of a finger; Lin Qiu tasted one, and it was sweet and sour, and crunchy. The flavor was like blueberries.

There was little meat, so the beastmen didn't crowd around to learn his cooking skills. They all chewed their food down, gnawed on some grass, and hurried back to the cave to sleep.

Lin Qiu stripped the meat off the leg, cut it into small pieces, and stewed it into soup.

As it simmered longer, the chicken-like aroma grew stronger.

That smell was even more overpowering than the roasted fish; as it drifted into the cave with the wind, the beastmen in the cave perked up their ears, their eyes glowing green.

"So fragrant, so fragrant, so fragrant..."

Lang Mo covered his nose with his paws, but feeling it wasn't enough, he buried his head into Lang Xi's fur. A muffled voice came out, "It must be Qiu."

"How can meat that you can swallow in one bite smell so good? Awoo... If only we had big clay pots, we could boil all the meat together; I'd even drink the soup!"

Lang Xi was so tempted he took a bite of Lang Mo's ear, "We don't have any; only the Qiu Mountain Tribe in the Central Continent knows how to make them."

The tribe's clay pots were all traded for when their ancestors were still in the Central Continent.

"King! Why don't we dig a big stone pot like Qiu did? Let's dig a few more," a beastman shouted in the cave.

"The King is not in the cave."

After finishing his dinner, Lin Qiu glanced at Lang Yan, who had just come out of the priest's cave, and walked slowly toward the large cave.

Lang Yan had long legs and a long stride; it wasn't long before he was following behind Lin Qiu.

Just as Lin Qiu thought he would walk past him, he noticed Lang Yan slowing his pace, staying at a distance neither too close nor too far.

"Qiu." In the quiet night, his voice sounded abrupt.

"Hmm?" Lin Qiu turned his head instinctively.

Lang Yan looked at his face as if observing something, and after a while, he walked past him and left.

Lin Qiu stopped in his tracks and lowered his eyelashes.

Does he suspect me?

Lin Qiu's heart beat a little faster. He followed Lang Yan into the cave, curled up in his grass nest, and kept an eye on the beastman.

How sharp Lang Yan was.

He immediately transformed into his wolf form, his ears twitching.

Lin Qiu frowned, pulled up the animal skin, and buried himself in the grass nest.

"You can go near the big river, or you can go into the forest," Lang Yan said, then moved to the other side of the grass nest, closed his eyes, and said no more.

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

Not suspected, and he was free.

This was the result of the discussion between the priest and Lang Yan; Qiu still needed to spend half a day at the priest's place, but his range of movement had expanded.

However, there were still beastmen watching him.

The old priest said that keeping Qiu too restricted wasn't good and would affect his recovery.

Lang Yan thought about it for a moment and agreed.
chapters.title: 第12章

chapters.translated_text:
The wind howled, and the night was even colder than the day. The moonlight faded, and it was so dark outside that one could not even see their own hand.

Inside the cave, separated by a grass curtain, a fire was burning quietly.

A new wooden table had been placed in a corner of the cave, adorned with lifelike little clay puppets. An earthenware jar was filled with hot water, and the clay cups beside it were set out in pairs.

The ground was covered with flat, clean, and tidy straw mats.

In the sheltered area at the back, the grass nest was dry. The spread-out animal skins were fluffy, reflecting the warm, soft glow of the firelight.

Lin Qiu lay in the grass nest, his arms wrapped around Lang Yan's neck. His partner covered him, a large animal skin draped over his waist.

"King..." Lin Qiu's eyes were watery, and sweat trickled down his cheeks.

Lang Yan lowered his head, pulled Lin Qiu to sit on his lap, and hurriedly tucked the animal skin around him, wrapping him up tightly.

Lin Qiu let out a muffled groan, pushing weakly against him, his sweat-dampened forehead resting on Lang Yan's broad arm as he squirmed aimlessly.

"Hot..."

Lang Yan touched his back, finding a light sheen of sweat. "Stay covered."

"No... mmph."

Lang Yan tightened his arms, effectively cutting off his words. Lin Qiu hummed, responding head-on, his tongue captured and savored until he felt dizzy and muddled.

Half-intoxicated and stimulated to the point of fainting, he still thought to himself that he couldn't let the King hold back for too long, or he wouldn't be able to handle it.

The fire died down. Lang Yan took a look, carefully wrapped the animal skin around Lin Qiu so no air could get in, and stepped out of the grass nest.

He felt the jar; the water was still warm.

His partner loved cleanliness, so Lang Yan took a basin and a cloth from under the table, poured some water, and carried it to the edge of the grass nest.

Lin Qiu regained a sliver of consciousness; he half-opened his eyes, feeling too lazy to move a muscle.

After being cleaned up, Lang Yan sat up, and Lin Qiu slowly rolled over to lie on his chest.

Lang Yan patted his back.

Lin Qiu mumbled, "King... are you still getting up early tomorrow?"

Lang Yan pulled him closer into his embrace. Sensing the leg draped over him and the arms wrapped around him, he lowered his head and rubbed his nose against his partner's cheek. He was so soft that he couldn't help but take a small bite.

"Not getting up early. Sleep."

Lin Qiu touched his chest and drifted into a deep sleep.

Lin Qiu slept very comfortably. He vaguely heard Lang An urging the beastmen and thought it must be dawn.

He tried to get up, but he felt like he was hugging a giant heater; it was too warm under the covers. As soon as he moved, his back was gently stroked, and he drifted back into a drowsy sleep.

Lin Qiu had a full, satisfying sleep.

The grass curtain was still hanging in the cave, and it was dim inside. When Lin Qiu opened his eyes, he found himself sprawled on top of Lang Yan, using him as a meat cushion.

Lin Qiu lifted his head, still feeling a bit dazed.

Seeing him awake, Lang Yan pulled the animal skin blanket up to cover his shoulders and tucked the long hair at his temples behind his ears.

Lin Qiu tilted his head, pressing his cheek against Lang Yan's palm.

"King, what time is it?"

Lang Yan pinched the soft flesh on his face. "Time for the second meal."

Lin Qiu: "..."

"We didn't go down all morning?"

"Mm."

"You didn't go down either?"

"I promised to stay with you."

Lin Qiu buried his head in the crook of Lang Yan's neck and stopped moving.

A soft chuckle came from above, and Lin Qiu grabbed his large hand and covered his own head with it.

He didn't want to see anyone.

The grass curtain opened, and a cold wind rushed in.

Wrapped up tightly, Lin Qiu followed behind Lang Yan down the mountain.

He looked composed, but after a few steps, his legs were truly weak and his waist sore, so he hardened his heart and simply climbed onto Lang Yan's back.

He was his own partner, and they were just living a normal married life; what was there to be ashamed of in front of the other beastmen!

Besides, the beastmen definitely wouldn't gossip about this!

"Qiu, did you and the King make cubs last night?"

The first beastman they saw upon descending the mountain made Lin Qiu lose his composure.

"Nonsense! We just got up late." Lin Qiu's cheeks turned burning red. He was on Lang Yan's back, and he didn't know whether to get down or stay put.

"Eh? That's not right..." The beastman twitched his nose, his gaze shifting between Lin Qiu and Lang Yan. "You're covered in the King's scent."

Lin Qiu poked Lang Yan's shoulder.

Lang Yan: "Uncle Di, that's enough."

The beastman laughed. "Alright, alright, I won't say anything else."

"Making cubs is a big deal, I'd be happy if..."

"Cough!"

"Fine, fine, I won't say it!" The beastman chuckled and walked away with his hands behind his back.

The beastman's name was Lang Di, one of the brothers from the old Wolf King's generation. He had served the old Wolf King alongside Lang Chi and could be considered a close elder to Lang Yan.

He had always been active with the third hunting squad, sleeping when he was free, and rarely mingled with the younger beastmen.

Like Lang Chi, he was specifically left by the old Wolf King to help Lang Yan manage the tribe's beastmen.

But Lang Yan did such a good job that he focused solely on hunting to ensure the beastmen were well-fed.

Now that he was older, combined with years of fatigue, his body was not what it used to be. Hunting already exhausted his strength, and upon returning to the tribe, he mostly lay in a corner to recover.

Now that the tribe was getting better and better, it was foreseeable that they would have a decent winter.

Lang Di had rested all night and was in good spirits. Seeing the Wolf King and his partner only just coming down the mountain, he thought the beastmen would surely be happy about the prospect of new cubs.

With a future for the tribe, his heart felt light.

Ah!

Lang Di felt content. Seeing Lin Qiu's thin skin, he thought of his father, Lang Chi—his old brother whom he hadn't seen in many years.

He wondered how he was doing now.

Thinking this, Lang Di walked away happily.

Lang Yan couldn't control his elders, but the other beastmen feared him.

Lin Qiu held his stomach, walking slowly behind Lang Yan.

The beastmen had just finished tidying up the cave and, seeing the two of them sitting at the table for lunch, they gave a sneaky smile.

Before they could finish smiling, Lang Yan swept a glance their way. The beastman was so scared he hiccuped and hurriedly scurried away to avoid Lang Yan's gaze.

The King is petty!

He clearly hadn't done anything!

Lin Qiu ate lunch with the beastmen, filled his stomach, and then lay limply on Lang Yan, feeling weak all over.

Lang An passed by, glanced at them, and shook his head secretly.

This won't do. Qiu couldn't even hold up for one night. With the winter season being so long, Qiu might just fall apart!

Lang An thought he should give Lin Qiu some extra nourishment.

After the cave was tidied, the beastmen ate their fill and lay down to rest for a while.

Lin Qiu thought about the radishes that hadn't been pickled yet, but when he tried to get up, his legs went soft and he fell back down.

Forget it, he wouldn't push himself.

"An, check if those radishes and the jar are dry. If they are, put them in the jar. Use cold boiled water, mix in half a cup of salt, and pour it in. Just make sure the radishes are submerged."

Lang An waved his hand. "Got it, you just rest."

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan.

Lang Yan brushed the stray hair from his face. "What's wrong?"

Lin Qiu: "Do they all know?"

Lang Yan's Adam's apple bobbed. He leaned in and touched his nose to Lin Qiu's cheek. "Mm."

Lin Qiu gritted his teeth.

Just as Lang Yan was about to tell him not to be angry, his hand was suddenly grabbed by his partner, and he saw his eyes burning with fierce determination.

Lin Qiu: "I want to train!"

"Hm?" Lang Yan supported his palm and squeezed it. "Train what?"

Lin Qiu glanced downward, and Lang Yan's waist tightened.

"Are the sub-beastmen really not as weak as me?"

Lang Yan thought for a moment and said diplomatically, "It usually doesn't affect much, we don't have to compare."

When beastmen had enough to eat, sub-beastmen and female beastmen actually had good stamina; the sub-beastmen and female beastmen of the Wolf Tribe even participated in hunting.

Their tribe practiced monogamy, and since the beastmen didn't have much else to do, they just made cubs in the nest at night.

Thinking about it carefully, it didn't seem to affect the beastmen at all; some sub-beastmen even enjoyed it and would pester their partners to do it whenever they had time.

In other tribes, where sub-beastmen and female beastmen were equally scarce, they would have one sub-beastman paired with multiple male beastmen. If that sub-beastman or female beastman didn't have the stamina, they mostly wouldn't dare to find more.

Lang Yan stroked Lin Qiu's back. His partner was different.

He had been born prematurely, and their generation of beastmen had grown up in an environment where they were never full, so it was normal that his physique hadn't been built up.

Thinking this, Lang Yan considered being more restrained in the future.

But his partner was still looking up, exposing his slender, delicate neck, and saying to him, "Let's train more."

Lang Yan felt his throat go dry. He touched his partner's face tenderly. Was this something you could train?

He said he was shy; other beastmen would want to hide when this topic was brought up.

But he was also bold. If he hadn't been pestering him last night, and if he hadn't lacked self-control, he wouldn't have let things get out of hand just because of a little provocation.

Lang Yan lowered his head, touched his forehead to his, and didn't know what to do with him.

"King, what do you say?" He was still being stubborn.

Lang Yan looked at those eyes that held the stars and laughed helplessly. "Alright..."

Lin Qiu rested for a while, but he still couldn't stop worrying about his radishes.

He went to check; Lang An had already mixed the salt water, and the radishes were just submerged. Lin Qiu took the lid, covered it, and poured a circle of water around the rim.

"That's it?" Lang An and a few other sub-beastmen gathered around, wanting to learn; they hadn't expected it to be so simple.

Lin Qiu: "That's it. Just make sure the water around the rim doesn't dry out. Keep it in a cool place, and it'll be ready to eat in ten days or so."

The beastmen were half-understanding. Lang An asked, "How is this different from radishes rubbed with salt?"

Lin Qiu: "Um... sour? Does that count?"

"Sour radish and old duck soup is delicious."

"What kind of soup?"

The name alone sounded delicious!

Lin Qiu: "Sour radish stewed meat soup, it's good."

Though there were no old ducks, maybe they could catch some wild ducks. They'd see later; maybe stewing red birds would work too.

The beastmen had rested enough, and Lang Yan gave the order to prepare to leave.

Wolf Mountain couldn't be left without beastmen, so they split into two groups. Lang Yan took half the beastmen first. There were Lang An and the others, Lang Guo and the cubs, the little wolves, and the entire guard team.

Even the old priest was carried by a beastman.

This group consisted of the old, the weak, and the young; the second group would be the dirty hunting squad.

The hot spring in the west was hidden in the mountains, not far from Wolf Mountain. At the pace of the wolf beastmen, it took about an hour to walk there, mostly involving crossing one or two small hills; running would naturally be faster.

Lin Qiu sat on Lang Yan's back, watching the beastmen bypass Wolf Mountain and head toward the back of the mountain.

The whole way was small hills and canyons. Once they entered the forest and climbed up along the deep gullies carved by the stream, they soon went deep into the mountains and saw pools of various sizes flowing down step by step on the flat land in front of the mountain.

The pools were steaming with white mist, the water exceptionally clear, with a faint smell of sulfur.

The beastmen went into the water one by one. The little wolves were the fastest, jumping into the water with "woo-hoo" cries, splashing water everywhere and causing the beastmen to dodge.

Lang Sheng and his group of little cubs followed Lang Mo and the others, cautiously approaching the pool. When they tested the water with their bare, dark feet, they were so shocked their eyes went round.

"It's hot!"

Lang Mo laughed: "It's hot. You guys sit on the edge and adapt first, don't rush in."

It was safer for the little beastmen to be with the adult beastmen.

The old priest didn't need any help. He skillfully found a small pool that wasn't too hot, took off his animal skin robe, and slowly entered the water.

There were stones in the water, which allowed him to sit.

The beastmen found their own spots. Lang Yan looked at the cub in Lang Guo's arms. "They won't go in the water."

Lang Guo: "King, I brought a basin."

Lang Yan nodded and, carrying the curious Lin Qiu on his back, walked to a pool further away from the other beastmen and sat down.

The steam rose, and the pool water was a deep blue.

This pool was flat, looking as if it had been trimmed.

The pool was surrounded by mountains, though only a little greenery remained.

Lang Yan entered the water first; his thick wolf fur floated up and didn't get soaked immediately. Lin Qiu laughed at the sight, squatted down to test the water temperature, and then began to take off his clothes.

Wearing only his undergarments, Lin Qiu sat on the edge, his two white legs dangling into the water. His ankles were rosy, and his calves were covered in red marks, as if bitten by insects.

Lang Yan held his breath, dove into the water, and once his fur was soaked, he swam slowly to Lin Qiu's side.

Lin Qiu bent over, hugged his neck, and slid into the water as well.

The water reached his chest, and Lin Qiu was startled. "It's so deep."

Lang Yan: "Climb on my back."

"Not climbing." He found a place to steady himself and paddled his hands on the water's surface. "King, come here, I'll wash your fur."

Lang Yan rested his two paws on the edge and looked at him.

Lin Qiu looked at him and burst into laughter.

The wet wolf head turned, and his nose rubbed against his cheek.

Lin Qiu hugged his head and took a bite of his wolf ear.

Lang Yan: "..."

The beastmen had brought a plant that could create bubbles, called bubble grass, specifically for washing fur.

Lin Qiu learned from the beastmen to pound the bubble grass into a pulp with a stone at the edge of the pool. He wrapped the bubble grass in a small linen bag and scrubbed it against the wet wolf fur.

He applied it once, scrubbed it with his hands, and then combed it with a comb.

By the time he finished washing it once, his hands were almost cramping.

Lang Yan finished washing in the pool, transformed into human form, and pulled his exhausted partner over.

"I'll wash you." He patted Lin Qiu's lower back. "Beast form."

Lin Qiu rarely used his beast form, mainly out of habit; unless he was practicing running or exercising outside, he was always in human form.

He transformed into a wolf. His size wasn't small, but Lang Yan could hold him up with one hand.

Seeing that he had already started putting bubbles on his fur, Lin Qiu rested his chin on his shoulder and asked lazily, "Aren't you tired?"

Lang Yan: "Not tired."

In every pool, large and small, the beastmen were like an assembly line, scrubbing fur for each other. Even the smallest cubs were squatting in basins, covered in bubbles.

A beastman glanced over. "Hey! The cubs are all gray bubbles, so dirty!"

"Awoo!" The cub stomped the water indignantly!

Lang Guo swept a glance at the beastman next to him, who was dripping water, and said with disgust, "Why don't you look at the color of the water you're washing off?"

"The priest's medicinal paste looks cleaner than your bathwater!"

The priest in the distance looked up and snorted. Comparing his medicinal paste to the beastmen's bathwater!

It seemed they weren't drinking enough of it!

The pool water was flowing, but it couldn't be helped that some beastmen's bathwater was too dirty.

The beastmen looked at the pool with the little wolves. The little wolves were grabbing their feet and scrubbing vigorously. The first pass didn't bubble, so they smashed a few more bubble fruits to wash a second time.

After scrubbing, they had to break it open and smell it.

Around the pool, there were also little wolves with soaked fur being surrounded and washed by their companions.

The little wolves were strong, like they were killing prey, grabbing handfuls of wolf fur and pulling so hard that the little wolf underneath felt their scalp tighten and whimpered.

In that clean pool, gray-black bubbles floated on the surface, wrapped in quite a bit of wolf fur that should have been shed long ago.

As another batch of little wolves went ashore, the black water flowed continuously.

After the beastmen finished their first wash, they hurried to the pools further upstream.

Lin Qiu was lulled to sleep by the scrubbing, and with Lang Yan massaging him, it was just too comfortable.

When the two changed pools, Lin Qiu plopped and hung naked on Lang Yan.

His cheeks were flushed from the steam, and his whole body was a bit pink.

Lang Yan hugged his waist, his fingertips tracing the tooth marks on his collarbone, and he lowered his head to take another bite.

Lin Qiu raised his hand, bringing up some water droplets, and covered Lang Yan's face.

"King, I'm sleepy."

You couldn't stay in the hot spring for too long. Lin Qiu leaned on Lang Yan, washed for a while longer, and then they both went up.

After drying their bodies and wrapping themselves in animal skin clothes, Lin Qiu felt refreshed all over.

He had never taken such a comfortable bath.

As he dried his hair, he watched the beastmen climbing up with limp hands.

Especially the little wolves; their fur was hard to wash, and after soaking for so long, they barely managed to climb up, their two hind legs still dangling in the water.

Lin Qiu: "Don't soak for too long."

The wolf beastmen crawled by the pool and nodded slowly.

Dizziness.

The old priest had already gotten up. He looked at the useless beastmen and said, "I told you, none of you listen."

"Priest, we're being good!" Lang Jin shouted, leaning on Bao Xiu.

Lang Rong rested his head on Lang Jin, opened his mouth, and took a deep breath—it was all the little wolves' fault for being so dirty.

The wolf beastmen went ashore one after another, shook themselves a few times, and the fur on their bodies was half-dry.

After running for a while on the way back, their bodies would be almost completely dry.

The beastmen had come slowly, but on the way back, they were frolicking and howling in the forest, running back excitedly.

Lang Yan walked unhurriedly at the back, Lin Qiu wearing his animal skin boots, walking with him. The two beastmen walked as if they were strolling; Lin Qiu had to stop every few steps to look at the surroundings.

They rarely came to the back mountain; even the beastmen didn't really come this way for gathering.

Lin Qiu watched as the beastmen suddenly stopped in front of a tree, their claws digging into something on it.

Just as he was about to look, there was a crunch under his feet.

Lin Qiu moved his foot, and a round nut cracked open.

"Walnut?"

Lin Qiu picked up the broken nut, removed the shell, and took out the clean walnut kernel inside. He tasted it, then pinched half and put it into Lang Yan's mouth.

Lin Qiu confirmed: "It's a walnut."

Lang Yan: "A bit bitter."

Lin Qiu nodded. "The shell is thick, too."

He looked around, and Lang Yan asked: "Want some?"

Lin Qiu: "Good stuff, it's good for the brain."

Lang Yan's eyes flickered; his own beastman probably needed it very much.

The beastmen rummaged around, ran ahead, and were back to digging at something on a tree.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan stopped and, using this spot as a center, searched everywhere.

The walnuts of this season had all fallen; the outer green skin had rotted away, exposing the nut in the middle.

Unfortunately, the little animals liked to eat them too. After searching for a long time, they only found a dozen or so.

Lang Yan looked up, confirmed what the tree that bore these fruits looked like, and committed it to memory.

"We'll find more next year."

Lin Qiu held the walnuts and smiled, "Okay."

He looked at the King, feeling that his beastman needed to supplement his brain.

Lang Yan and Lin Qiu walked slowly; before they even reached Wolf Mountain, they saw the second group of beastmen heading their way.

Several hunting team leaders were leading the group. Seeing Lin Qiu holding something, they walked forward while tilting their heads to look behind him.

Lin Qiu couldn't help but laugh, and he shared a few with them.

"Walnuts; you can pick them if you see them."

The beastmen stopped immediately and ran over happily to take them.

"Qiu, can these be eaten?"

Lin Qiu: "Yes."

As soon as he finished speaking, they saw Lang Huo pinch his hand, and the only walnut he held cracked open.

Lin Qiu: "Impressive."

Lang Huo cracked another one open with one hand, *clack, clack*, looking smug.

Before he could get too cocky, he suddenly felt a chill on the back of his neck. He followed that cold sensation and looked over, meeting the King's indifferent gaze, and immediately stood up straight.

Lang Yan: "Let's go."

He held Lin Qiu’s wrist, watching his footing, and led him around the beastmen.

The walnuts were small with thick shells and not much meat. Lin Qiu ate two, and Lang Yan took the rest.

Hearing a *crack*, Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan’s palm.

He was confused: "I'm not eating anymore."

Lang Yan loosened his hand, and the walnut was crushed into crumbs.

Seeing him not move, Lin Qiu raised his eyes, looking at his own reflection in those gray pupils. There seemed to be a sense of competitiveness, but upon closer inspection, it was still cold and indifferent.

In a flash of inspiration, Lin Qiu remembered something and let out a chuckle.

He praised, "The King is still the most impressive."

Only then did Lang Yan discard the shells and hold the fruit meat to Lin Qiu’s lips. Watching him finish it, he said, "Don't praise other beastmen so much."

Lin Qiu: "I won't."

His King was jealous.

Back in the cave, Lin Qiu didn't feel cold after walking that mountain path. His long hair was still a bit damp, so he was pulled by Lang Yan to sit by the fire to dry it.

Lin Qiu looked at the grass nest in the large cave; he and Lang Yan’s nest had been tidied up, surely by An and the others.

After bathing, his whole body felt two taels lighter.

The beastmen had all gone back to their nests to lie down comfortably. Although it wasn't time to sleep yet, they weren't working today, so it was a rare rest.

Lin Qiu dried his hair in the large cave, then shifted into his beast form to continue drying it.

As they were killing time like this, they suddenly heard a "crunch, crunch" sound in the cave.

Lin Qiu looked over and saw the beastmen’s mouths moving.

He didn't know what they were eating, but it looked like they were cracking sunflower seeds.

Perhaps Lin Qiu’s gaze was too direct; Lang Yun, in the grass nest diagonally opposite, reached out, opened his palm, and asked, "Want some?"

Lin Qiu: "What is it?"

Lang Yan brought some over for him, and as soon as Lin Qiu saw them, he hurriedly pushed Lang Yan’s hand away.

"No, no!"

Those weren't seeds at all; they were clearly insect larvae. They had crunchy shells and liked to live on pear and plum trees—the stinging caterpillars, also known as *bajiaoding*.

Lin Qiu remembered how the beastmen used to chop firewood to find the fat worms inside and said, "Is there nothing else to eat?"

Lang Yan returned the things, and Lang Yun said, "It's delicious."

Lin Qiu: "Then you eat more."

He knew that since the beastmen hadn't had much to eat before, they had to taste everything; they could even eat poisonous plants, let alone protein-rich insects.

"Food is still too scarce."

Not only was the staple food scarce, but as Lin Qiu calculated, the beastmen had almost no snacks.

Not to mention snacks, sometimes when he had a craving, he had to think twice before roasting a yam. He always felt it wasn't right to just take food gathered by the tribe.

Everyone ate from the big pots, and there was no portion they could distribute themselves...

It was difficult!

Lin Qiu slumped onto Lang Yan’s back.

"King, we still have to work hard."

Lang Yan: "Okay."

Lin Qiu lay on Lang Yan’s back, whispering into his ear about many foods Lang Yan didn't understand. By the time he counted enough to make himself hungry, he buried his head in the fur on Lang Yan’s chest, wrapped in a faint plant scent, and began his afternoon nap.

When he woke up, the beastmen in the grass nests were all gone.

Going outside, he saw the beastmen pulling garlic sprouts and radishes in the field to the east.

Lin Qiu: "Why pull them now?"

Lang Yan: "The Priest said it will snow tonight."

Lin Qiu glanced to the west; there was more snow accumulated than yesterday. It wasn't the scattered specks from before, but a solid sheet.

The sky was gloomy, with gray tones everywhere.

Aside from the sounds of the wolf-beastmen moving, no other animal activity could be heard.

There was a silence before a heavy snowfall.

The beastmen hurried back and forth in front of Wolf Mountain. Lang An brought out all the clothes the rabbit-beastmen had made with them. Lin Qiu went to help, and as he approached, Lang An grabbed two thick sweaters and placed them in his arms.

"These are for you and the King."

"I made one for you too," he said, bringing over a down jacket.

The clothes were made large, and Lin Qiu’s vision was slightly blocked as he held them.

He simply sent them up to the mountain. On his way down, he passed the Priest’s cave and heard Lang Bing inside teaching Lang Xue, while the old Priest sat at the cave entrance watching the sky.

"Priest, do you have to go down to live tonight?"

The old Priest: "Yes, I have to go down."

"Do you need help moving things?"

"You busy yourself; some beastmen are coming." As he finished, he watched Lang Shi bring the guard beastmen up.

Lang Mo grinned at Lin Qiu: "Qiu, An told you to go down."

"Okay."

Lin Qiu went down the mountain and met Lang Rong with the little wolves: "Qiu! The curved-horn beasts won't go into the shed!"

Lin Qiu said: "If they won't go in, let them be. I think the curved-horn beasts are still hard to raise; most will be eaten during the snow season. Rong, check the roofs and windows; don't let the snow collapse them."

"Got it!"

Returning to the corridor, he saw Lang An shouting in the east field. Lin Qiu hurried over, watching the beastmen carry baskets of radishes into the cave.

"Qiu, how should we store the garlic sprouts?"

Lin Qiu: "The same as the radishes."

It was too late to dig a cellar now, and since the snow here was heavy and deep, a cellar wouldn't hold much, and it was troublesome to open and close it every time.

"Then we'll just put them in the room."

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

He looked at the base of the garlic sprouts; to eat the garlic, they would have to wait until next year. Eating just the sprouts now wouldn't yield much, and the beastmen would use up a lot in just one stir-fry.

Everything left outside began to be packed into the caves. The beastmen checked the caves containing food again and again.

In the corridor, Lang Qi was setting up a ladder to check the tiles above.

"Qiu! Should we bring back the fish traps outside?" a beastman shouted from far away by the riverbank.

The beastmen mostly used nets to catch fish, rarely using fish traps, and many of these were broken.

Lin Qiu replied: "The river surface shouldn't freeze over very quickly, so leave them for now. We can still eat fresh fish if we pull them up every day."

"Okay!" The beastman hurried to collect the nets first, catching enough for tonight.

Lin Qiu paced back and forth in front of Wolf Mountain, while Lang Yan checked the prey that hadn't been put in the caves. After a snowfall tonight, the prey would freeze and wouldn't spoil.

The beastmen walked back and forth in front of Wolf Mountain. By the time the other group of beastmen finished bathing and returned, everything was settled, and Lang An began preparing the meat soup for the evening.

*

South of Wolf Mountain, five or six days' journey away.

On the winding mountain, Lang Chi was leading a team of beastmen, including Lang Ye, running down the mountain.

The further north they went, the colder the beastmen felt.

Lang Chi’s thick, long wolf fur was blown backward. Facing the wind, he felt the cold seeping through the gaps in his fur.

Lang Ye looked worriedly at the dim sky and said, "Chief, I'm afraid it's going to snow."

Lang Chi: "It's not much further."

The branch tribe didn't have a priest, so they couldn't be sure exactly when it would snow. Lang Chi had arranged things for the branch tribe before leaving with the little wolves.

Worried about encountering snow on the way, they hadn't brought much, only some dried fish and dry rations.

They had hurried all the way, but were still a bit slow.

Fortunately, they were near the Great Marsh. Although taking a detour would take time, there were plenty of fish in the Great Marsh, so food wouldn't be an issue.

*

Wolf Mountain.

The sky turned dark in no time. The beastmen had eaten a full meal, their hands and feet feeling soft, and they lay down in their warm grass nests, their faces flushed as if they had finished drinking wine.

If it snowed tonight, they should still be able to go out for the first few days.

The beastmen had finished making the sweaters. Everyone climbed up, pulled out the clothes they had been sitting on, and tried putting them on over their heads.

A sweater alone wasn't enough; they still had to drape a fur blanket over themselves.

Fur was limited, so the beastmen didn't make full-body fur clothes like Lin Qiu’s, but just draped them. When sleeping, they would unfold them to use as blankets.

Wrapped in the sweaters, the beastmen felt uncomfortable, as if they had fleas.

After wearing them for a while, they took them off immediately.

The sweaters were too tight; they weren't used to it.

However, they had seen the beastmen make them stitch by stitch, which was very troublesome. Not one beastman complained; they all laid them out nicely to pad the bottom of their grass nests, then lay down on their sides, waiting to wear them when it got cold.

The Priest had already moved down to the cave, and the faint light that usually shone on the path up the mountain dimmed.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan walked up the mountain.

He tugged on Lang Yan’s index finger, walking and stopping, and couldn't help but say, "I always feel a chill on my back."

Lang Yan stopped, "Are you cold?"

Lin Qiu: "Maybe it's the wind."

In the cave, Lin Qiu lit the oil lamp.

The tribe didn't have much oil, and the oil in this lamp was used for cooking, so it had a smell when burning.

By the light of the lamp, Lang Yan lowered the grass curtain.

The curtain was made thick, but it would still let in drafts. Lang Yan asked, "It’s hard to walk on the mountain after it snows; do you want to move down?"

Lin Qiu bumped his forehead against Lang Yan’s back, "This is the second time you've asked."

Lang Yan: "I'm worried it's cold up here."

Lin Qiu: "We'll see tomorrow; if it's cold, we'll go down."

The oil lamp was blown out. Lin Qiu snuggled against his wolf king, initially wanting to practice a bit, but as soon as he touched the grass nest, he became drowsy.

Lang Yan didn't remind him; he lay quietly, waiting until Lin Qiu was fast asleep before curling his lips and rubbing his chin against the top of his head.

He listened to the sounds outside, closed his eyes, and fell asleep as well.

In the middle of the night, there was a rustling sound.

Lang Yan held Lin Qiu, tucking the fur tightly around him. He looked out through the gap in the grass curtain; it was bright outside—it had snowed.

It was fine inside the cave; not much wind could get in, and the fur was tight.

He looked at the sleeping Lin Qiu in his arms, ensured he wasn't cold, and closed his eyes to sleep again.

In the early morning, Lin Qiu woke up.

He looked outside immediately, seeing only the exceptionally bright daylight through the gap in the grass curtain.

He turned over, lay on Lang Yan, and kept staring outside.

"King, did it snow?"

Lang Yan hurriedly pulled the fur to wrap him up, "It snowed heavily; it's already white outside."

Lin Qiu: "I'm going out to look."

Lin Qiu wrapped himself up tightly and poked his head out.

The cave was high up, so he could see far.

He saw the distant mountains dyed white, a silence like ink wash painting. The nearby treetops were also covered in snow; it hadn't reached the point of being completely white, but some had accumulated.

The air was chilly; Lin Qiu had only poked his head out for a moment, and the tip of his nose was already frozen red.

Lang Yan put on his sweater and wrapped himself in fur, then hurriedly grabbed him back.

"It's cold outside."

Lin Qiu looked up, letting Lang Yan adjust his fur clothes. With warm, large hands pressed against his neck, Lin Qiu blinked.

Lang Yan said, "Something is missing on your neck."

Lin Qiu sniffled; in just that short time, he had a runny nose.

He followed Lang Yan into the cave and watched him take out a long, wide strip of fur with soft down.

Lin Qiu stood still, watching him wrap it around his neck a few times.

With half his face hidden under the fur, his face looked even smaller.

He curved his eyes, "Warm."

Lang Yan touched his head, "Does your head hurt?"

Lin Qiu shook his head.

"Don't let the wind blow on you too much; even if we go out for a while, we'll get a headache."

Lin Qiu: "Then let's make fur hats."

Lang Yan covered his reddened ears with both hands, then moved the heels of his palms to press against his slightly cool face.

"Like a straw hat?"

Lin Qiu raised his head, touching his nose tip to his, "With a smaller brim, deeper, so it can cover the ears directly."

Lang Yan: "The tribe has some scrap fur; we'll go down and look later."

The grass curtain opened, and all the cold air rushed in.

Lin Qiu walked down the mountain, and the exposed skin was soon stung by the wind. Seeing him walk slowly, Lang Yan bent down and picked him up, walking down the mountain as if on flat ground.

Lin Qiu sat on his arm, his hands curled against his chest.

The wind made his face hurt.

"This is different from what I imagined."

"How is it different?"

"It shouldn't be gradual and gentle? Snowing isn't cold, melting snow is cold; why is it like this on the first day?"

Lang Yan: "If we live up there in the future, we have to come down to eat every day."

Lin Qiu buried his face in his neck, muffled, "Stop talking, I'll just come down to sleep."

Lang Yan rubbed his face, "I'm just worried."
