When the beastmen first migrated to Wolf Mountain, they lived there for a few years, and it wasn't until the old Wolf King couldn't hold on anymore and passed away that he told them to split up.

"When the snow season is over and the chief and the others return, maybe we can go over for a trip."

"Eat quickly! It'll get cold once the wind blows."

Inside the cave, the beastmen were wrapped in gray, rough animal skins, their hair braided and draped over their shoulders. Their large feet were bare, and they squatted on the ground, surrounding the pitch-black pottery pot to eat meat soup.

The sound of slurping soup in the cave was loud and lively.

The beastmen held their warm bowls, feeling warm on their bodies, and glanced at the snowflakes drifting outside, unable to help but grin foolishly.

This year, they would be able to drink hot meat soup every day during the snow season.

*

On Wolf Mountain, after hearing this "show-off" from the beastmen, Lang Ye really wanted to howl at the Wolf King.

Why could they eat such delicious food every day, but they couldn't come back!

Lang Ye wanted to come back so much he could barely sleep!

Lang Chi was also a bit dazed; was meat something they could eat every day?

Even fish meat had to be saved with all their might, and it could only be eaten until full when mixed with many wild vegetables and boiled.

When it was Lang Chi's turn in line, seeing that the bowl contained both meat bones and strange plants with many holes, he poked it with his chopsticks and couldn't help but pull Lang Di aside to ask: "What is this again?"

"Lotus root, don't you have it on your side?"

Lang Chi: "Isn't it grown by the rabbit beastmen?"

Lang Di patted his shoulder, "We discovered it ourselves. Qiu said it was edible, so we tried it. Let me tell you, it's everywhere in the Great Marsh; we've been digging for a month and still haven't finished. We even invited the Black Feather beastmen to help; they dig every day, and there's still more."

"You invited the Black Feather beastmen but didn't look for us!"

"Oh, it's not an invitation, it's an exchange. They work with us in exchange for our pottery pots and fishing nets. Both of these were brought to you, don't be envious."

Lang Chi recalled, "Do we have this on our side?"

"There should be." Lang Yu walked over carrying a cub's bowl and said casually.

"This thing grows in the water; the leaves are round, and the lotus root hides in the mud under its leaves, which is very hard to dig."

There were many deep lakes on the branch tribe's side, but it wasn't like there were no shallow lakes and lake beaches.

As soon as Lang Yu said this, Lang Chi immediately had an impression.

"How come when you guys came..."

Lang Yu: "We only just discovered it too."

They didn't know until they came to Wolf Mountain; once they arrived, they found many new things.

Lang Chi told Lang Ye and the others to keep a close eye out and look for it when they went back.

Lotus root meat soup—the branch tribe beastmen who had never eaten good things were dizzy with pleasure again. Their posture was similar to that of the Wolf Mountain beastmen at the beginning, wishing they could lick the bowl clean.

At a long table in the corner, the rabbit beastmen sat on stools, holding appropriately sized pottery bowls and eating.

This batch of pottery bowls was fired for them by Lang Mo later on.

Lang Ye looked at them with curiosity, his gaze undisguised.

The beastmen who were eating seriously slowly pricked up their ears, secretly took a glance, and then suddenly turned their heads back.

The little fluff on their arms stood up to the tips of their ears, and the beastmen's legs tensed.

"Chief, he's looking at us," Tu Ai said carefully.

Tu Kui cautiously turned his head; Lang Ye was holding his rice basin and had even moved a few steps closer.

Tu Kui nodded.

Lang Ye: "My name is Lang Ye."

Upon hearing this, the rabbit beastmen breathed a sigh of relief in their hearts. He wasn't looking to start a fight...

The few rabbit beastmen nearby introduced themselves one after another, their voices a bit small; they were still reserved in front of the strange wolf beastmen.

Lang An glanced at them and didn't say anything.

Lang Ye wouldn't do anything to harm the rabbit beastmen.

Just when Tu Kui thought Lang Ye had only come over to say hello and would leave, Lang Ye said directly: "After the snow season, why don't you come with us to the branch tribe to plant radishes?"

Tu Luo blinked and said happily: "Radishes!"

"We are in the same tribe as the Wolf Mountain beastmen. Wolf Mountain planted them, so we have to plant them on our side too. So..."

"So shut your mouth," Lang Guo appeared from somewhere and tugged on Lang Ye's ear, "Radishes can't be planted now. They still have to plant other things with us."

Lang Ye looked up, "Guo?"

Lang Guo let go and warned: "They are just getting used to it here, don't think about taking them away."

Tu Kui said gently: "Going to the branch tribe is out of the question, but we can teach you how to plant them."

Lang Ye: "That's really! Great!"

"Forget it, you haven't even started planting tail grass yet; plant the tail grass well first."

"One more radish won't hurt."

"You've got a big mouth."

"Your mouth is the one that stinks!"

Lang Guo narrowed his eyes and suddenly kicked him. He snorted, shook his head, and walked away.

Lang An watched the two of them with a smile; it was quite good, they were still bickering as soon as they met.

This showed that even after more than a dozen years, their relationship remained good.
chapters.title: 第122章

chapters.source_text:
晚饭过后，兽人们抱着碗筷去溪边洗。
溪水比以往浅了些，兽人碰了碰水面，对着水中的倒影龇牙。
“王，水好冷！”
狼岩捧着两个碗，在溪水边放下。他薅了一把干草，将碗放入水中，干草往碗里搅合搅合，再拿起来看了看。
“以前没见你们喊过冷。”狼岩道
“以前雪季又不用天天摸冷水。”兽人嘟囔。
林楸拿了陶杯跟牙刷来，等狼岩洗完，递给他道：“是不能一直摸冰水，手会冻伤开裂。我看山洞的火堆也空着，不如架上几口锅，烧点热水。”
这样兽人们要喝热水，也不用单独在灶台那边占一口锅。
兽人多了，五口锅的肉汤还不一定够。
边上兽人眼睛一亮，“好主意！”
等到兽人洗完碗，大家开始收拾卫生。
睡前洗漱已经成了习惯，连兔兽人也人手一把小狼做的牙刷，蹲在溪水下游，龇牙刷刷刷。
狼赤看着，忽然叫狼安也塞了一把牙刷。
“没多的陶杯了，你们先用碗装水。”
狼夜瞧着一根儿小拇指粗细的木头，一端方正，打了孔，穿着些兽毛。兽毛摸着粗糙微硬，又嗅了嗅，脸一皱。
圆鼻兽的毛。
这种小兽最喜欢钻土里。
“嫌弃什么，小狼处理过的，用这个沾牙粉刷牙。注意点别咬断，部落没剩几把了。”狼安道
狼安担心他们不会，还抓了一旁认认真真刷牙的幼崽过来给他们示范。
幼崽听话，刷牙不会偷懒。不像某些成年兽人，图快，囫囵一刷就叮铃哐啷敲杯子洗牙刷了。
幼崽自觉接受了重任，十几个幼崽对二十几个成年兽人，龇牙教得格外认真。
林楸离他们有点远，听着，忍不住翘起唇角。
旁边“嘶呀”叫唤，林楸被吸引注意。
狼兽人嘴里包着一口溪水要吐不吐，看着难受。
“好冰好冰好冰……”兽人一口吐了水，忍不住摸了摸自己牙齿。
林楸看着自己陶杯里兑了温水的水，道：“陶锅里还有热水。”
话落，两边兽人跑了个空。
洗漱完，狼夜捧着自己陶碗跟牙刷，不停地用舌尖跟嘴皮蹭牙，感觉可干净了，涩涩的，一时间还有些不自在。
“楸的花样真多。”
经过跟幼崽的一番交流，狼夜他们也知道了，这事儿又是楸告诉兽人的。
狼赤沉默走在前面，远远看了眼与狼岩并肩而行的林楸，与有荣焉。
他的幼崽好了。
还得了兽神眷顾，当阿父的心中慰贴。
虽然现在幼崽还与他有些生疏，但那不是记不得以前的事，他反正要在这边待过雪季，再慢慢相处就是。
实际幼崽与亲生父母生疏在兽人部落也是常事，但总有些兽人，过于疼爱幼崽罢了。
回到山洞，就有兽人琢磨往火堆上架陶罐。
幼崽玩儿了一天，这会儿打着哈欠，互相抓着前面幼崽的衣摆，由狼生带领着，慢慢往最里面的草窝走。
路过比他们高许多，像巨人一样的成年兽人，狼生爪子扒拉过去。
成年兽人低头看。
幼崽噙着泪，困顿道：“让开，让开。”
兽人们会心一笑，往旁边让出位置。
小火车开到了山洞拐角，成年兽人看不见了，大幼崽与小幼崽分了窝。
他们四五个一堆，直接往草窝里一栽，倒下去片刻眼睛就彻底睁不开。还有直接跪趴在草窝边，来不及进去就已经睡着了。
狼果坐在最里面的草窝，刚看顾着四个没变人形的幼崽睡着。然后起身，挨个儿给大幼崽调整姿势，趴外面的抱进草窝里，再拉上兽皮盖着。
一路走到最外面的草窝，狼果甩着胳膊腿儿继续往外走。
小崽子们终于睡着了，这会儿是他难得的空闲时间。
拐角出去，最近的就是狼岩跟林楸的草窝。
就这一块儿空余的位置大，置了几张长桌，长凳。
火堆要再稍稍往外一点，为了防止柴跑出来烧到其他地方，火堆处往下挖了半臂深。
此时兽人们围着那地方商量怎么把陶锅搭上去。
狼果往长桌边一坐，手撑着脑袋，歪歪扭扭靠在上面。
林楸看他一身疲惫，捧起旁边的罐子，给他倒了一杯还温热的白开水。
狼果斜了眼，“我要喝酒。”
林楸冲着狼岩抬了抬下巴，示意跟他去说。
狼果也是真的渴了，抄起杯子，一口气灌到底。
“王，雪季又没什么事，喝点呗。”
狼岩视线落在远处，看着跟狼云挤一个草窝的狼赤。兽人察觉到目光，看了过来，哼了一声又侧过头去。
狼岩：“赤他们还没尝过。”
狼果拍桌站起，“我去抱来！”
兽人被狼果的动静吸引，正试图往火堆边放砖头的兽人分神，手指被燎了一下。
他“嗷”的一叫，正要控诉，却看狼果搬了酒来。
兽人立马甩开砖头，屁颠屁颠往那边跑。
“嗷！”旁边干活的同伴捂脚跳。
兽人缩脖子，一下挤进兽人群中，几下就逮不住了。
狼赤正跟兽人说着话呢，身边的几个草窝一下就空了。只留他跟狼夜这群兽人，又是一脸迷惑地望着他们。
不过狼夜这次学聪明了，先不问，也跟着兽人跑里面去。
狼安走到里头长桌旁，看着狼果在擦罐子上的灰尘，他来了兴趣。
“可以喝了？”
狼果得意一笑，“能，王同意了的。”
“我来分。”狼安手里已经拿了自己杯子来，林楸往旁边让一让，留个空位给狼安。
狼夜几个睡在靠外面的位置，动作再快，也没狼山的兽人快。
等他们靠近，早落在兽人后头，连兽人们围着什么东西都看不见。
直到一股奇特的香味传出来……
“什么味道？”
“酒。”狼地端着杯子，慢悠悠从兽人堆里挤出来，将一小杯葡萄酒递给狼赤，“王说先给你尝尝，试试。”
“酒又是什么？”狼赤不解。
“嘿！”狼地看他疑惑，越觉得楸过来是他们捡了便宜，“这酒啊，跟咱们雪季放坏了的果子差不多……”
“那怎么能吃？”
有好的不吃，吃坏的，雪季后期吃坏果子那是不得已。
“只是差不多，又不是一样。”
按照狼地理解，葡萄酒也是楸把紫皮果，就是楸叫葡萄的这东西捏烂了装罐子里，还装了挺久，那不就是烂果子做的。
但是这最后出来的不是稀烂的果肉，而是干净澄澈，颜色格外漂亮的水。
这水吧，味道复杂。
喝着却又觉得有些上瘾，不过喝了两口，兽人就醉醺醺的了。
“喝不死的，你先尝尝。”
狼赤跟着他往后走，坐在了没兽人的空地上。
狼夜只能眼巴巴看着，自己还没有呢。
陶杯粗糙，也不知道谁捏的，口大腰细，中间收窄的地方刚刚好一个手掌印。
狼赤看了眼，颜色很奇怪。想到是自家幼崽做的，一点不再怀疑，一口就闷。
“哎哟！你别一下喝完！”
狼赤咽下，眉心一皱，呛咳着有些龇牙。
好奇怪的味道。
狼地心疼，看了眼他杯子，一滴不剩。
“你、你真是不会喝！这个啊，得慢慢品。一小口一小口，诶！那才叫享受！”
狼赤闷声咳嗽，嘴里充斥着酒味。
起初的不适应过后，咂摸着嘴，居然又想再试一试。喉咙有些烫，身体好像也更加热。
狼赤看了一眼狼地，试图伸手，叫狼地躲过去。
“一个兽人两勺！这是我的。”
旁边，狼雨捧着一大杯，给兔兽人那边送过去。见状，笑着问：“赤，你觉得怎么样？”
狼赤看着他，甩了甩头，怎么眼前一下就雾蒙蒙的。
“哟！醉了。”
狼雨笑呵呵的，赶紧给兔兽人送去。
狼地看狼赤靠在草窝，也慢慢靠上去，抿一口小酒，面颊上多了一丝红。
“现在你放心了……”
狼赤眯了眯眼，甩头。
这种不清醒的状态让狼警惕，但身体却像不受控制一样。狼赤声音沉着，道：“喝多了不好。”
“可不，所以我们这才喝第二次。”
狼赤双手搭在草窝边缘，叹息一声，隔着那重重兽人，看不到里面。
“我看狼山在养咩咩兽。”
“养了有一段时间了。”
狼赤为身体的不适皱了皱眉，可此刻，精神却是前所未有的放松。
“我们也该回来了……”
狼地：“那你什么打算？”
“岩还没跟我说，最多明年雪季前……”
支部落的情况其实比狼山还要难，那边除了鱼，已经找不出什么猎物。
吃鱼是能撑一段时间，但最多半年，鱼也补充不了兽人们的能量。
到时候只有两个选择——
要么再一次迁徙，要么回到狼山。
狼赤当初带兽人走，就是为了在食物有限的情况下，给狼山的年轻狼兽人们留下生机。如今狼山跟支部落的兽人稍稍能吃饱，比起以前好得太多，自然他们可以考虑要不要回来。
何况狼部落的发展，需要他们。
起初，狼赤觉得兽人们已经在绝望边缘，最多五年，狼部落也得覆灭。
但否极泰来，野外的猎物几乎不可能再恢复到从前时，狼山找到了另一条路。
且看着，是极其可行的路。
种植尾巴草，养殖动物，配合着狩猎采集，只要发展成了规模，那狼部落就能慢慢恢复生气。
狼赤很期待那一天，也自然想参与进来。
洞内充斥着醉人的香，狼兽人鼻子灵，那香气更是成倍的，仿佛闻一闻都能晕过去。
狼赤从没有一刻像这么放松过，跟着老伙计闲聊，暂且不用操心雪季是否食物不够，也不用担忧是否有兽人会熬不过去……肚里饱胀，身体轻飘飘的，像卧在云朵里，不知不觉就睡了过去。
狼赤睡熟了，起了鼾声。
狼地冲着对面草窝招手，年轻狼兽人笑嘻嘻过来，将他搬进窝里。
这期间他都没动一下，不像之前狼莫叫他吃饭时那般警惕。
兽人们看着咧嘴，可笑着笑着，狼顺忽然道：“我们要是哪一天都喝了酒，别的兽人偷袭，我们是不是也弄不醒？”
放下狼赤的一圈兽人站起，恰逢一阵冷风吹进山洞，兽人晕乎乎的脑子顿时清醒。
回想狼顺那随口一句话，惊出一身冷汗。
狼火打个哆嗦，“有这个可能。”
狼地笑呵呵撑着草窝爬起来，晃晃悠悠往自己草窝走，“所以王的要求是对的，这东西，还真不能随便喝。”
不说其他，看看此刻山洞里倒下的一大片狼兽人，就知道这东西的威力。
林楸倒没醉，也没兽人们联想那么多。
他喝了两口，坐在草窝里，侧身靠着狼岩肩头。
手指被狼岩捏着，林楸看向睡得不省人事的阿父，“王，你是不是故意的？”
狼岩：“嗯？”
装傻是吧。
“那边山洞还没弄好，你就先把狼赤弄醉了。”
狼岩并不否认，也不承认。
不过放眼整个山洞，还是睡熟了的兽人安分些。
林楸：“只剩最后一罐了。”
狼岩：“存着。”
兽人这样子，轻易不能沾这东西。
时候不早，兽人也无心再弄那陶锅。
洞口的草帘放下来，留的缝隙足够，兽人就胡乱往草窝里一倒，各自睡去。
林楸照旧靠着狼岩，手顺着他胸膛往上摸，直捏到狼岩耳朵，再踏实地放任自己沉入梦乡。
狼岩看着怀中伴侣，往他鼻尖咬了一下。
不捏他耳朵是不是睡不着？
“唔。”
林楸往他脖子埋，手也没松。
狼岩搂着他，轻拍两下，也跟着一起睡去。
雪季半个月，兽人们几乎每天都是睡醒了吃，吃了再睡。又下了几场大雪，洞外银装素裹，彻底一片白。
另一个山洞早已经收拾好，狼赤跟狼夜他们都搬了过去。
狼山前，除了照看牲畜，以及巡逻的兽人偶尔出来，几乎不见什么兽人。
终于，今天雪停了。
天上厚实的云散开，金色的光束照亮了昏暗的山洞。兽人舒展身体，去往廊下趴着。
林楸裹足了兽皮，浑身毛绒绒的，看着有些笨重。
他掀开草帘出去，避开乱趴的兽人，一口气走到灶台那边，欣喜地对着阳光伸出手。
不消片刻，手上冰冷，林楸又哆嗦着揣回来。
“一点不暖。”
狼安几个忙活做早饭，笑道：“雪季就是这样的，陶锅这边暖和，来这里坐。”
林楸：“我先去看看红鸟跟咩咩兽。”
雪堆积起来，狼山前只见雪，不见草。积雪松软，林楸一脚踩下去，直接陷了半个小腿。
狼岩本来跟在他后头，见状立马调换位置，自己走到他前头去。
兽人没清扫路面的习惯，从廊下到西边，只有狼溶带着小狼们早上喂红鸟时踩出来的脚印。
狼岩在前，林楸就拽着他衣角，踩着他的脚印走。
白雪沙沙响，少许落进兽皮靴里，林楸忙拽着狼岩停下，将靴里的雪倒出来。
“兽人们有空，可以把廊道附近的雪清一清，不然积高了得把廊道都淹了。”
狼岩手撑着林楸，“回去就叫他们做。”
林楸笑了声，跺跺脚，示意他继续往前走。
才一会儿，林楸手指露在外面红了。等离廊道远一点，就探入狼岩兽皮衣服下，勾着他穿在里面的毛衣上。
毛衣挨着温热的身体，隔着薄薄一层，能感觉到狼岩腰侧的肉紧实，硬邦邦的。
狼岩还贴心地帮他压着外头，怕漏风。
走到西边，小狼正在清理房顶跟棚子上的积雪。
林楸叫了声狼溶，小狼直接从房顶上跳下来，“楸！红鸟跟咩咩兽都喂了。”
“炕烧着没？”
“嗯！不过……你进去看看吧。”
小狼一脸为难，林楸以为出什么事了，忙松开狼岩，推开草帘进屋。
一下进入昏暗中，眼前模糊了下。
林楸站定，缓了缓，脚下直接被咩咩兽撞了一下。
“楸？”
林楸正想把咩咩兽赶进去，一抬头，见原本做给咩咩兽的炕上，挤满了大大小小的狼兽人。
林楸哑然，好半晌才道：“……你们跑这儿来干什么？”
狼兽人迷糊坐起，手上还强制抱了个咩咩兽，“我们昨晚就是在这里睡的啊。”
狼岩掀着草帘，看着里头，蹙眉。
光落进屋里，兽人们看清狼岩，立马笑着爬起来。
“王，你怎么来了？”
兽人局促地搓着手，像遇到天敌的小兽般，怂着往角落里缩。他们身上还沾着草屑。黑色头发上，咩咩兽的白毛也格外显眼。
亏得咩咩兽不在屋里拉屎拉尿，不然可想而知得有多臭。
狼岩：“山洞没地方给你们睡？”
兽人连忙摇头。
瞧狼岩还盯着自个儿，兽人低头，忙松开抱着的咩咩兽。
咩咩兽一甩头，冲着他叫了声，混入族群。
林楸无奈，“快出来。”
“楸，里面真暖和。”
“对！你放心楸，我们专门守在这里，就是为了看着咩咩兽。”
狼岩额角青筋隐隐跳动，“没事做把山洞到这边的路清理出来。”
兽人：“哦。”
大伙儿不敢再贫，一个个扭扭捏捏绕过狼岩，还有往窗户那边翻出去的。
林楸大概一数，十来个兽人。
也不知道这么点地儿怎么挤上去的。
林楸回头问狼岩：“真有那么冷？”
狼岩：“他们吃饱了。”
林楸：“我就说，睡在大山洞里其实也还好。”
不知道是不是身边躺了个暖炉的原因，林楸每晚上都睡得很好。
其他狼兽人现在多保持着兽形，睡觉也用兽形，那毛才换过，应该也不会特别冷。
现在才雪季半个月，没到最冷的时候。
去到红鸟那边，好在就没跟红鸟抢地方的兽人了。
红鸟不像咩咩兽，它们屋里屋外都拉，每天都得清理，不然根本下不了脚。
即便这样，屋里也有味道。
这边窗户开着，通着风。外面雪映着，室内还算亮堂。
房子内，小狼也给红鸟做了窝。屋里头暖和，每天总能捡到些蛋。
靠火炕角落，倒扣着一个破旧藤筐。
狼溶跟着进来，将红鸟赶到一边去，揭开藤筐给林楸看。
“楸，这些都是能孵小红鸟的。”
林楸：“点个灯来。”
林楸蹲炕上去，打眼一扫，十来个红鸟蛋。
他伸手探了探底部，比体温高一些。
见是狼岩端着油灯来，狼溶乖乖跟在他身后，林楸冲小狼招了招手，问：“都是什么时候捡的？”
狼溶也跟着蹲过去，点了个青色的鸟蛋，“最久的是七天前，就是这两个。”
林楸示意狼岩把油灯放炕上，他拿了红鸟蛋挨个来看。
小狼学着他，立马开始检查其他的。
狼岩走到林楸身边，微微弯腰，看着自家伴侣手中的蛋。
林楸转了一圈，油灯的光线还是不那么方便，看得不明。
林楸又凑近看了好一会儿，确认那蛛丝一样的血线更多了，是个成功受精的蛋，且孵化有效。
林楸：“王，里头小红鸟在长。”
狼溶是每天都要来记录，一天的时间几乎都耗在这里，自然也知道红鸟蛋的变化。
他也觉得里面小红鸟在长，但不敢确定。直到听到林楸亲口说，才抿了抿唇，露出个腼腆笑来。
狼岩：“火炕也能孵蛋？”
林楸：“应该可以。”
不过这还只是小狼开始在试验，参照鸡蛋，不同阶段温度还有变化。
这红鸟又不一样，具体如何，还得慢慢琢磨。
林楸不确定能不能成，但不能打击小狼的积极性。而且如果掌握了火炕孵蛋，对狼兽人来说百利无一害。
狼岩看着那窝里的红鸟蛋，跟狼溶道：“要是成功，以后红鸟跟咩咩兽都交给你。”
狼溶手一紧，呆呆地看着狼岩。
狼岩：“觉得不行？”
狼溶鼓起勇气，道：“王！我会好好做的！”
狼岩点头。
他看着伴侣蹲在草窝边，一一检查完毕，又小心放回去，翻了翻面，将藤筐盖好。
狼岩伸手，林楸撑着跳下火炕。
“不着急，我们慢慢摸索。”
狼溶：“好！”
小狼谨慎，目光更加坚定。
要孵蛋，屋里的火炕得早晚都烧着。
这半个多月都是狼溶带着同伴照料，连幼崽都会悄悄往这边跑。
林楸不把他们当什么都不懂的幼崽，在养殖这件事上，狼溶做得比他更加认真和用心。
有这个态度跟毅力，火炕孵化红鸟蛋是迟早的事。
林楸一身轻松，出去也帮着把圈里收拾收拾。见时候差不多，叫上小狼一起，先回去吃早饭。
早上熬的是小米粥，也就是尾巴草籽。
六口锅里都是金黄色的尾巴草籽，熬得浓稠，面上都飘着一层米油。
锅里除了尾巴草籽，还放了些植物块根，有的还创新性地扔了些菜干进去。
林楸闻着味儿，还没吃过煮菜的。
除了尾巴草粥，好像今早没其他吃的。林楸想着自己泡的萝卜应该好了，赶紧去捞了一个出来。
为了方便腌制，大萝卜都破开两半。
表皮颜色褪了些，水成了胭脂一样红。一揭开盖子，酸香味儿冲鼻。
旁边好奇探头的狼莫忙避开，打个喷嚏，又迅速跑回来占据林楸身边位置。
“楸，能吃了吗？”
林楸：“应该可以。”
他用干燥筷子捞起来一块，放菜板上，用刀切成指头大小的块儿。
狼莫闻着那味儿就忍不住流口水，纯粹是酸的。
林楸：“来点儿？”
狼莫试探夹走一块，一入口，当即五官皱紧，不停吐舌头。
“好酸！”
林楸笑着提醒：“再来一口粥。”
狼莫立即转头找自己的碗，咕噜来了一口，这才压下去味道。他盯着菜板，抿了抿嘴巴，又觉得还能接受。
“楸，我再来一块？”
“来吧。”
狼莫再夹，这次就着粥吃。酸萝卜嚼着脆脆的，也不觉得没肉的粥味道寡淡了。
狼莫越嚼越香，“楸，再来点儿。”
“你们吃独食呢！”桌上坐着的兽人控诉。
狼安忙着打饭，闻言，跟林楸道：“楸，多切一点，让兽人都分一点尝尝。”
林楸点头，酸菜下稀饭，他爷奶早饭标配。
又切了三个萝卜，案板上已经堆起来。
林楸自个儿往碗里弄了一点，提醒后面的兽人：“不能多了，不然酸。”
兽人们点头，等林楸一走，当即一大筷子下去。
还没刨到碗里，狼安抄起小棍打在兽人手背。
“嗷！”
狼安冷飕飕道：“听不见楸的话？”
狼兽人瘪嘴，“我、我又不吃一个兽人吃，我分给其他兽人呢。”
“他们要吃不知道自己来，滚蛋！”
兽人立马灰溜溜走了。
狼安大声警告：“就这么点！别想贪多，好吃还有萝卜，再做就是！”
兽人们点头，鄙夷地看了眼灰溜溜的兽人。
兽人不服，悄悄道：“你敢说，你们忍得住！”
狼兽人面无表情，转回头。
哼！
他以为谁都跟他一样呢！
他们最多最多，就多弄那么一点点。
廊下两边矮墙，还有中间的一排长桌上，都放满了兽人的大陶碗。大家或站或坐，幼崽也混在兽人堆里。兔兽人照旧坐在最角落的桌子旁。
分了酸萝卜的兽人夹起来一点，先试探着闻一闻，不自觉地皱鼻子。
这味道像青皮果，酸味十足，可酸得又不一样，跟以前楸做的食物很是不同。
兽人总感觉，这酸萝卜应该不怎么好吃。
大小兽人第一口先直接吃，不出意料，全跟狼莫一样急着找粥。
然后一口粥，一口酸萝卜，正品一品味道呢，筷子往粥里一搅——
诶？
怎么没了。
兽人下意识看向旁边同伴，又忍不住被嘴里残留的酸味勾得又喝了两口粥。
脆脆的，酸酸的，比寻常的菜要咸一点。
“但没有生萝卜的辣味，下这个叫粥的食物很合适。要是混着肉吃，应该也不错。”兔艾点评道。
兔葵：“楸这个做法好，还能放很久。”
兔艾：“对，萝卜放到后头里头就空了，不好吃。这样能保存，我等会去跟楸说一声。”
兔葵：“不用。吃不了多久的。”
兔艾看着那群还央求着狼安再弄点萝卜的狼兽人，默默道：“好像也是……”
那一堆萝卜，换他们，要慢慢分配着吃一个雪季呢。
chapters.title: 第123章
chapters.translated_text:
After dinner, the orcs carried their bowls and chopsticks to the creek to wash them.

The creek water was shallower than usual; an orc touched the surface and bared his teeth at his reflection in the water.

"King, the water is so cold!"

Lang Yan held two bowls and set them down by the creek. He grabbed a handful of dried grass, put the bowls into the water, swirled the grass inside them, and then picked them up to inspect them.

"I haven't heard you complain about the cold before," Lang Yan said.

"We didn't have to touch cold water every day during the snow season before," the orc muttered.

Lin Qiu brought over a pottery cup and a toothbrush. After Lang Yan finished washing, he handed them to him and said, "You really shouldn't keep touching icy water; your hands will get frostbitten and crack. I see the fire pits in the cave are empty, so why not set up a few pots and boil some hot water?"

This way, if the orcs want hot water, they won't have to occupy a pot at the cooking stove separately.

With so many orcs, five pots of meat soup might not even be enough.

An orc nearby’s eyes lit up, "Great idea!"

Once the orcs finished washing their bowls, everyone began to tidy up.

Washing up before bed had become a habit; even the rabbit-kin orcs each had a toothbrush made by the young wolves, squatting downstream in the creek, brushing their teeth with a "brush-brush-brush" sound.

Lang Chi watched, then suddenly called Lang An over and shoved a toothbrush into his hand.

"There are no more pottery cups, you guys use bowls to hold water for now."

Lang Ye looked at a piece of wood the thickness of a pinky finger, square at one end, with holes drilled in it and animal hair threaded through. The hair felt coarse and slightly hard; he sniffed it and wrinkled his nose.

Round-nosed beast hair.

These small beasts loved to burrow into the dirt.

"What are you complaining about? The little wolves processed it. Use this to dip in tooth powder and brush your teeth. Be careful not to bite it in half; there aren't many left in the tribe," Lang An said.

Worried they wouldn't know how, Lang An grabbed a cub who was brushing his teeth earnestly nearby to demonstrate for them.

The cubs were obedient and didn't slack off when brushing. Unlike some adult orcs who, wanting to be quick, would just give it a rough scrub and then clatter their cups and brushes around.

The cubs consciously accepted the heavy responsibility; a dozen cubs were teaching twenty-something adult orcs, baring their teeth and being exceptionally serious.

Lin Qiu was a bit far from them, but hearing this, he couldn't help but curl his lips into a smile.

A "hiss" sound came from nearby, and Lin Qiu’s attention was drawn.

A wolf-orc had a mouthful of creek water he was struggling to spit out, looking uncomfortable.

"So cold, so cold, so cold..." The orc spat out the water and couldn't help but touch his teeth.

Lin Qiu looked at the warm water mixed in his own pottery cup and said, "There is still hot water in the pottery pot."

As soon as he finished speaking, the orcs on both sides ran off empty-handed.

After washing up, Lang Ye held his pottery bowl and toothbrush, constantly rubbing his teeth with his tongue and lips. It felt very clean, astringent, and he felt a bit uncomfortable for a moment.

"Qiu really has so many tricks."

After some interaction with the cubs, Lang Ye and the others also learned that this, too, was something Qiu had told the orcs.

Lang Chi walked in front in silence, glancing from afar at Lin Qiu, who was walking shoulder-to-shoulder with Lang Yan, feeling a sense of reflected glory.

His cub was doing well.

And he had received the favor of the Beast God; his fatherly heart felt comforted.

Although the cub was still a bit distant from him now, it wasn't because he didn't remember the past. He was going to stay here through the snow season anyway, so they could just get along slowly.

In reality, it was common for cubs to be distant from their biological parents in orc tribes, but some orcs were just overly doting on their cubs.

Back in the cave, some orcs were figuring out how to set up pottery pots over the fire.

The cubs had played all day, and now, yawning, they grabbed the hem of the cub in front of them and, led by Lang Sheng, walked slowly toward the grass nests in the back.

Passing by the adult orcs, who were much taller than them like giants, Lang Sheng’s claws reached out.

The adult orcs looked down.

The cub, with tears in his eyes, said sleepily, "Move, move."

The orcs smiled knowingly and moved aside to make space.

The little train arrived at the corner of the cave, the adult orcs were out of sight, and the older cubs and younger cubs separated into their nests.

They flopped into the grass nests in groups of four or five, and within moments of lying down, their eyes were completely shut. Some even knelt and slumped at the edge of the nest, falling asleep before they could even get inside.

Lang Guo sat in the innermost grass nest, having just watched over the four cubs who hadn't shifted into human form as they fell asleep. Then he got up, adjusted the positions of the older cubs one by one, carried those who had fallen asleep outside into the nests, and pulled animal skins over them.

Walking all the way to the outermost nest, Lang Guo shook his arms and legs and continued walking outward.

The little ones were finally asleep, and this was his rare moment of free time.

Turning the corner, the closest place was the grass nest of Lang Yan and Lin Qiu.

This was the only place with enough space, where a few long tables and benches had been set up.

The fire pit needed to be moved slightly further out, and to prevent firewood from rolling out and burning other things, the fire pit area had been dug half an arm’s length deep.

At this moment, the orcs were gathered around that spot, discussing how to set up the pottery pot.

Lang Guo sat by the long table, resting his head on his hand, leaning crookedly against it.

Lin Qiu saw his exhaustion, picked up the jar beside him, and poured him a cup of still-warm boiled water.

Lang Guo slanted his eyes, "I want to drink alcohol."

Lin Qiu tilted his chin toward Lang Yan, signaling him to go talk to him.

Lang Guo was truly thirsty; he grabbed the cup and gulped it down in one go.

"King, there’s nothing to do during the snow season, let us have some."

Lang Yan’s gaze landed in the distance, watching Lang Chi, who was squeezed into a grass nest with Lang Yun. The orc noticed the gaze, looked over, snorted, and turned his head away.

Lang Yan: "Chi and the others haven't tasted it yet."

Lang Guo slapped the table and stood up, "I'll go get it!"

The orcs were attracted by Lang Guo’s movement, and the orc who was trying to place bricks by the fire was distracted, his finger getting singed.

He let out an "Ow!" and was about to complain, but then saw Lang Guo carrying the wine over.

The orc immediately dropped the bricks and ran over there happily.

"Ow!" A companion working nearby clutched his foot and jumped.

The orc shrank his neck and squeezed into the crowd of orcs, disappearing from sight in a few seconds.

Lang Chi was talking to the orcs, and the grass nests beside him suddenly emptied. Only he and Lang Ye’s group of orcs remained, looking at them with confusion.

However, Lang Ye was smarter this time; he didn't ask first and followed the orcs inside.

Lang An walked to the long table inside and saw Lang Guo wiping the dust off the jar; he became interested.

"Can we drink it?"

Lang Guo smiled triumphantly, "Yes, the King agreed."

"I'll do the pouring." Lang An already had his cup in hand; Lin Qiu moved aside to leave a space for Lang An.

Lang Ye and the others slept in the outer positions, so no matter how fast they moved, they weren't as fast as the Lang Shan orcs.

By the time they got close, they were already behind the orcs, unable to even see what they were gathered around.

Until a peculiar fragrance wafted out...

"What is that smell?"

"Wine." Lang Di held a cup, slowly squeezed out of the crowd of orcs, and handed a small cup of wine to Lang Chi, "The King said to let you taste it first, give it a try."

"What is wine?" Lang Chi was puzzled.

"Hey!" Lang Di saw his confusion and felt even more that Qiu coming over was their gain, "This wine is about the same as the fruit that goes bad during our snow season..."

"Then how can you eat it?"

When there is good food, you don't eat it; eating spoiled food is only a last resort late in the snow season.

"It’s just similar, not the same."

According to Lang Di’s understanding, the wine was also made by Qiu mashing up the purple-skinned fruit—the thing Qiu called grapes—and putting it in a jar for a long time. Isn't that just made from rotten fruit?

But what came out in the end wasn't mushy fruit pulp, but clean, clear water with an exceptionally beautiful color.

This water had a complex taste.

Yet, drinking it made one feel a bit addicted. However, after only two sips, the orcs were already tipsy.

"It won't kill you, just try it."

Lang Chi followed him to the back and sat in an empty space where there were no orcs.

Lang Ye could only watch longingly; he didn't have any yet.

The pottery cup was rough, and he didn't know who had made it; it had a wide mouth and a narrow waist, with the narrowed part in the middle just right for a palm print.

Lang Chi took a look; the color was very strange. Thinking it was made by his own cub, he didn't doubt it anymore and downed it in one gulp.

"Ouch! Don't drink it all at once!"

Lang Chi swallowed, his brows furrowed, choking and coughing, baring his teeth a little.

Such a strange taste.

Lang Di felt pained, looked at his cup, and saw not a drop left.

"You, you really don't know how to drink! This thing, you have to savor it slowly. One small sip at a time, hey! That’s what you call enjoyment!"

Lang Chi coughed muffledly, his mouth filled with the taste of alcohol.

After the initial discomfort, he smacked his lips and actually wanted to try it again. His throat felt a bit hot, and his body seemed to feel warmer too.

Lang Chi glanced at Lang Di and tried to reach out, but Lang Di dodged.

"Two spoonfuls per orc! This is mine."

Nearby, Lang Yu held a large cup and sent it over to the rabbit-kin side. Seeing this, he asked with a smile, "Chi, what do you think?"

Lang Chi looked at him and shook his head; why was everything in front of him suddenly foggy?

"Yo! He's drunk."

Lang Yu laughed and hurriedly sent the wine to the rabbit-kin.

Lang Di saw Lang Chi leaning against the grass nest and slowly leaned back too, sipping the wine, a hint of red appearing on his cheeks.

"Now you can rest easy..."

Lang Chi squinted and shook his head.

This state of being unclear made the wolf vigilant, but his body felt as if it were out of his control. Lang Chi’s voice was deep as he said, "Drinking too much is bad."

"Of course, that's why this is only our second time drinking it."

Lang Chi rested his hands on the edge of the grass nest and sighed, unable to see inside through the layers of orcs.

"I see Lang Shan is raising sheep-beasts."

"They've been raising them for a while now."

Lang Chi frowned at the discomfort in his body, but at this moment, his spirit was more relaxed than ever before.

"We should come back too..."

Lang Di: "Then what are your plans?"

"Yan hasn't told me yet, at the latest before next year's snow season..."

The situation in the branch tribe was actually even harder than in Lang Shan; apart from fish, they couldn't find any other prey there.

Eating fish could sustain them for a while, but at most for half a year; fish couldn't replenish the orcs' energy.

At that time, there would only be two choices—

Either migrate again or return to Lang Shan.

Lang Chi had taken the orcs away back then to leave a chance of survival for the young wolf-orcs of Lang Shan when food was limited. Now that the orcs of Lang Shan and the branch tribe could eat a little better, it was much better than before, so naturally, they could consider whether to return.

Moreover, the development of the Wolf Tribe needed them.

At first, Lang Chi felt that the orcs were already on the edge of despair, and at most in five years, the Wolf Tribe would be destroyed.

But things turned around; when it was almost impossible for wild prey to recover to what it once was, Lang Shan found another path.

And looking at it, it was an extremely viable path.

Planting tail-grass, raising animals, combined with hunting and gathering—as long as it developed to a certain scale, the Wolf Tribe could slowly recover its vitality.

Lang Chi was looking forward to that day and naturally wanted to participate.

The cave was filled with an intoxicating fragrance. Wolf-orcs had sharp noses, and the aroma was multiplied; it felt as if they could faint just from smelling it.

Lang Chi had never felt so relaxed; chatting with his old friend, he didn't have to worry about whether there would be enough food for the snow season, nor did he have to worry about whether any orcs would not make it... His belly was full, his body felt light and airy, as if he were lying on a cloud, and he fell asleep without realizing it.

Lang Chi was fast asleep and started snoring.

Lang Di waved at the grass nest opposite, and a young wolf-orc came over with a grin and moved him into the nest.

During this time, he didn't move at all, unlike the vigilance he showed when Lang Mo called him to eat earlier.

The orcs looked on and grinned, but as they laughed, Lang Shun suddenly said, "If one day we all drink alcohol and other orcs attack, wouldn't we be unable to wake up?"

The circle of orcs who had put Lang Chi down stood up, just as a cold wind blew into the cave, and the orcs' dizzy brains suddenly cleared.

Recalling Lang Shun’s casual remark, they broke out in a cold sweat.

Lang Huo shivered, "That’s possible."

Lang Di laughed as he propped himself up from the grass nest and wobbled toward his own nest, "So the King’s requirement is right; this thing really shouldn't be drunk casually."

Not to mention anything else, just looking at the large number of wolf-orcs collapsed in the cave right now, one knew the power of this stuff.

Lin Qiu wasn't drunk, nor did he associate as much as the orcs.

He had two sips, sat in the grass nest, and leaned his side against Lang Yan’s shoulder.

With his fingers being pinched by Lang Yan, Lin Qiu looked at his father, who was sleeping soundly, "King, did you do this on purpose?"

Lang Yan: "Hmm?"

Playing dumb, are we?

"The other cave isn't ready yet, and you already got Lang Chi drunk."

Lang Yan neither denied nor admitted it.

However, looking at the entire cave, the sleeping orcs were more well-behaved.

Lin Qiu: "There's only one jar left."

Lang Yan: "Save it."

With the orcs like this, they shouldn't touch this stuff easily.

It was getting late, and the orcs had no heart to mess with the pottery pot anymore.

The grass curtain at the cave entrance was lowered, leaving enough of a gap, and the orcs just flopped into their grass nests and went to sleep.

Lin Qiu leaned against Lang Yan as usual, his hand tracing up his chest until he pinched Lang Yan’s ear, and then he let himself sink into a dream.

Lang Yan looked at his partner in his arms and bit the tip of his nose.

Can’t you sleep without pinching his ear?

"Mmm."

Lin Qiu buried himself in his neck, his hand not letting go.

Lang Yan held him, patted him lightly, and fell asleep as well.

For the half-month of the snow season, the orcs spent almost every day eating after waking up and sleeping after eating. It snowed a few more times, and outside the cave, everything was silver-clad and completely white.

The other cave had long been tidied up, and Lang Chi, Lang Ye, and the others had moved over.

In front of Lang Shan, apart from the orcs tending to the livestock and patrolling, almost no orcs were seen.

Finally, the snow stopped today.

The thick clouds in the sky dispersed, and golden beams of light illuminated the dim cave. The orcs stretched their bodies and went to lie down under the corridor.

Lin Qiu was wrapped in animal skins, looking fluffy and a bit cumbersome.

He lifted the grass curtain and went out, avoiding the scattered orcs, and walked in one breath to the cooking stove, happily stretching his hands toward the sunlight.

Before long, his hands were cold, and Lin Qiu shivered and tucked them back in.

"Not warm at all."

Lang An and the others were busy making breakfast and laughed, "The snow season is just like this. It’s warm by the pottery pot; come sit here."

Lin Qiu: "I’ll go check on the red birds and the sheep-beasts first."

Snow had piled up, and in front of Lang Shan, only snow could be seen, no grass. The snow was soft, and Lin Qiu stepped into it, sinking half a calf deep.

Lang Yan had been following behind him, and seeing this, he immediately switched positions and walked in front of him.

The orcs didn't have the habit of clearing the road; from the corridor to the west, there were only the footprints left by Lang Rong and the little wolves when they went to feed the red birds in the morning.

With Lang Yan in front, Lin Qiu grabbed his hem and walked in his footprints.

The white snow crunched, and a little bit fell into his animal-skin boots. Lin Qiu hurriedly pulled Lang Yan to a stop to pour the snow out of his boots.

"When the orcs have time, they can clear the snow near the corridor; otherwise, if it piles up too high, it will bury the corridor."

Lang Yan supported Lin Qiu, "I’ll tell them to do it when we get back."

Lin Qiu smiled, stomped his feet, and signaled for him to continue walking forward.

After only a while, Lin Qiu’s fingers, exposed to the air, turned red. Once they were further from the corridor, he reached under Lang Yan’s animal-skin clothes and hooked onto the sweater he was wearing inside.

The sweater was against his warm body, and through the thin layer, he could feel the muscles on Lang Yan’s waist, firm and hard.

Lang Yan also thoughtfully pressed his outer clothes down to keep the wind out.

When they reached the west side, the little wolves were clearing the snow from the roof and the shed.

Lin Qiu called out to Lang Rong, and the little wolf jumped directly from the roof, "Qiu! The red birds and sheep-beasts have all been fed."

"Is the heated bed burning?"

"Yeah! But... you should go in and see."

The little wolf looked troubled. Lin Qiu thought something had happened, so he hurriedly let go of Lang Yan and pushed open the grass curtain to enter the room.

Entering the dimness, his vision blurred for a moment.

Lin Qiu stood still, waited for a moment, and was immediately bumped by a sheep-beast at his feet.

"Qiu?"

Lin Qiu was just about to drive the sheep-beast in, but when he looked up, he saw that the heated bed originally made for the sheep-beasts was crowded with large and small wolf-orcs.

Lin Qiu was dumbfounded, and it took a long while before he said, "...What are you guys doing running in here?"

The wolf-orcs sat up groggily, still forcibly holding a sheep-beast in their arms, "We slept here last night."

Lang Yan lifted the grass curtain, looked inside, and frowned.

Light fell into the room, and when the orcs saw Lang Yan, they immediately climbed up with a smile.

"King, why are you here?"

The orcs rubbed their hands awkwardly, shrinking into the corners like small beasts encountering a natural enemy. They were still covered in grass clippings. On their black hair, the white fur of the sheep-beasts was also particularly conspicuous.

It was fortunate that the sheep-beasts didn't poop or pee in the room, otherwise, one could imagine how smelly it would be.

Lang Yan: "Is there no place for you to sleep in the cave?"

The orcs shook their heads hurriedly.

Seeing Lang Yan still staring at them, the orcs lowered their heads and hurriedly let go of the sheep-beasts they were holding.

A sheep-beast shook its head, bleated at him, and merged into the herd.

Lin Qiu was helpless, "Come out quickly."

"Qiu, it’s really warm inside."

"Right! Don't worry, Qiu, we are specifically guarding here just to watch the sheep-beasts."

The veins on Lang Yan’s forehead pulsed slightly, "If you have nothing to do, clear the road from the cave to here."

The orcs: "Oh."

Everyone dared not joke anymore, one by one they awkwardly bypassed Lang Yan, and some even climbed out through the window.

Lin Qiu counted roughly; there were a dozen orcs.

He didn't know how they managed to squeeze into such a small space.

Lin Qiu turned back to ask Lang Yan: "Is it really that cold?"

Lang Yan: "They are full."

Lin Qiu: "I was just saying, sleeping in the big cave is actually fine."

Perhaps because there was a heater lying beside him, Lin Qiu slept very well every night.

Other wolf-orcs mostly kept their beast forms now, and they used their beast forms to sleep, and since their fur had just been changed, it shouldn't be particularly cold.

It had only been half a month of the snow season, not the coldest time yet.

Going to the red bird side, fortunately, there were no orcs fighting for space with the red birds.

Red birds weren't like sheep-beasts; they pooped both inside and outside the room, and it had to be cleaned every day, otherwise, one couldn't even step inside.

Even so, there was still a smell in the room.

The windows here were open for ventilation. With the snow reflecting outside, the room was still quite bright.

Inside the house, the little wolves had also made nests for the red birds. It was warm inside, and they could always find some eggs every day.

In the corner against the heated bed, an old rattan basket was turned upside down.

Lang Rong followed him in, drove the red birds to the side, and uncovered the rattan basket to show Lin Qiu.

"Qiu, these are the ones that can hatch little red birds."

Lin Qiu: "Bring a lamp."

Lin Qiu squatted on the heated bed and took a look; there were a dozen red bird eggs.

He reached out and touched the bottom; it was a bit warmer than body temperature.

Seeing Lang Yan bringing the oil lamp, with Lang Rong obediently following behind him, Lin Qiu beckoned to the little wolf and asked, "When were they all collected?"

Lang Rong also squatted over and pointed to a cyan bird egg, "The oldest one was seven days ago, these two."

Lin Qiu signaled Lang Yan to put the oil lamp on the heated bed, and he took the red bird eggs one by one to examine them.

The little wolf learned from him and immediately started checking the others.

Lang Yan walked to Lin Qiu’s side, bent down slightly, and looked at the eggs in his partner’s hands.

Lin Qiu turned them around, but the light from the oil lamp wasn't very convenient, and he couldn't see clearly.

Lin Qiu leaned in closer and watched for a long while, confirming that the spiderweb-like blood vessels were more visible; it was a successfully fertilized egg, and the incubation was effective.

Lin Qiu: "King, the little red bird inside is growing."

Lang Rong came to record every day, and almost all his time was spent here, so naturally, he knew the changes in the red bird eggs.

He also felt that the little red bird inside was growing, but he wasn't sure. Only when he heard Lin Qiu say it himself did he purse his lips and reveal a shy smile.

Lang Yan: "Can a heated bed also hatch eggs?"

Lin Qiu: "It should be possible."

However, this was just the little wolves starting to experiment. Referring to chicken eggs, the temperature at different stages would change.

These red birds were different, and the specifics would have to be figured out slowly.

Lin Qiu wasn't sure if it would work, but he couldn't dampen the little wolves' enthusiasm. Moreover, if they mastered hatching eggs on a heated bed, it would have a hundred benefits and no harm for the wolf-orcs.

Lang Yan looked at the red bird eggs in the nest and said to Lang Rong: "If it succeeds, from now on, the red birds and sheep-beasts will be handed over to you."

Lang Rong’s hands tightened, and he looked at Lang Yan blankly.

Lang Yan: "Don't think you can do it?"

Lang Rong gathered his courage and said, "King! I will do it well!"

Lang Yan nodded.

He watched his partner squatting by the grass nest, finishing the inspection one by one, putting them back carefully, turning them over, and covering the rattan basket.

Lang Yan reached out, and Lin Qiu supported himself and jumped off the heated bed.

"Don't worry, we'll figure it out slowly."

Lang Rong: "Okay!"

The little wolf was cautious, his gaze even more determined.

To hatch eggs, the heated bed in the room had to be burned morning and night.

For the past half-month, Lang Rong had been leading his companions to take care of it, and even the cubs would sneak over here.

Lin Qiu didn't treat them as cubs who didn't understand anything; in terms of animal husbandry, Lang Rong did it more seriously and attentively than he did.

With this attitude and perseverance, hatching red bird eggs on the heated bed was only a matter of time.

Lin Qiu felt lighthearted and went out to help tidy up the pen. Seeing that it was about time, he called the little wolves to go back and have breakfast.

They were having millet porridge in the morning, which was tail-grass seeds.

The six pots were filled with golden tail-grass seeds, boiled thick, with a layer of rice oil floating on top.

Besides the tail-grass seeds, some plant roots were added to the pots, and some innovatively threw in some dried vegetables.

Lin Qiu smelled the aroma; he hadn't eaten boiled vegetables before.

Apart from the tail-grass porridge, it seemed there was nothing else to eat this morning. Lin Qiu thought that the radishes he had pickled should be ready, so he hurriedly went to fish one out.

To facilitate pickling, the large radishes were split in half.

The skin color had faded a bit, and the water had turned as red as rouge. As soon as the lid was lifted, the sour aroma rushed to his nose.

Lang Mo, who was curiously poking his head over, hurriedly avoided it, sneezed, and then quickly ran back to occupy the position beside Lin Qiu.

"Qiu, can we eat it?"

Lin Qiu: "It should be ready."

He used dry chopsticks to fish out a piece, put it on the cutting board, and used a knife to cut it into finger-sized chunks.

Lang Mo couldn't help but drool when he smelled that scent; it was purely sour.

Lin Qiu: "Want some?"

Lang Mo tentatively picked up a piece, and as soon as it entered his mouth, his facial features immediately scrunched up, and he kept sticking out his tongue.

"So sour!"

Lin Qiu smiled and reminded him: "Take another bite of porridge."

Lang Mo immediately turned his head to find his bowl, gulped down a mouthful, and only then suppressed the taste. He stared at the cutting board, smacked his lips, and felt it was acceptable.

"Qiu, can I have another piece?"

"Go ahead."

Lang Mo picked up another piece, this time eating it with the porridge. The sour radish was crunchy, and the porridge without meat didn't taste bland anymore.

Lang Mo chewed and found it more and more delicious, "Qiu, give me some more."

"You guys are eating alone!" an orc sitting at the table complained.

Lang An was busy serving food, and hearing this, he said to Lin Qiu: "Qiu, cut a bit more, let the orcs share and taste it."

Lin Qiu nodded; pickles with porridge were his grandparents' standard breakfast.

He cut three more radishes, and they were already piled up on the cutting board.

Lin Qiu put a little in his own bowl and reminded the orcs behind him: "Not too much, otherwise it will be too sour."

The orcs nodded, and as soon as Lin Qiu left, they immediately reached out with large chopsticks.

Before they could even get it into their bowls, Lang An picked up a small stick and hit the orcs on the back of their hands.

"Ow!"

Lang An said coldly: "Didn't you hear what Qiu said?"

The wolf-orc pouted, "I, I’m not eating it all by myself, I’m sharing it with other orcs."

"If they want to eat, they should come get it themselves, get lost!"

The orc immediately walked away dejectedly.

Lang An warned loudly: "Just this much! Don't think about being greedy, if it’s good, there are more radishes, we can make more!"

The orcs nodded and looked at the dejected orc with disdain.

The orc was unconvinced and whispered: "You dare say you can resist it!"

The wolf-orc remained expressionless and turned his head back.

Hmph!

He thought everyone was like him!

At most, at most, they would just take a tiny bit more.

On the low walls on both sides of the corridor, and on the row of long tables in the middle, were filled with the orcs' large pottery bowls. Everyone was either standing or sitting, and the cubs were mixed in with the orcs. The rabbit-kin orcs were still sitting at the table in the corner as usual.

The orcs who got the sour radish picked up a little, tentatively smelled it first, and wrinkled their noses unconsciously.

This smell was like green-skinned fruit, very sour, but it was sour in a different way, very different from the food Qiu had made before.

The orcs always felt that this sour radish shouldn't taste very good.

The large and small orcs ate the first bite directly, and as expected, they were all in a hurry to find porridge like Lang Mo.

Then a bite of porridge, a bite of sour radish, just as they were savoring the taste, they stirred their chopsticks into the porridge—

Eh?

How come it’s gone.

The orc subconsciously looked at the companion beside him and couldn't help but be hooked by the lingering sour taste in his mouth, drinking two more mouthfuls of porridge.

It was crunchy, sour, and a bit saltier than ordinary vegetables.

"But it doesn't have the spiciness of raw radishes, and it’s very suitable for this food called porridge. If it were mixed with meat, it should also be good," Rabbit Ai commented.

Rabbit Kui: "Qiu’s method is good, and it can be kept for a long time."

Rabbit Ai: "Right, radishes become hollow if left until later, and they don't taste good. This way it can be preserved; I’ll go tell Qiu later."

Rabbit Kui: "No need. It won't last long."

Rabbit Ai looked at the group of wolf-orcs who were still begging Lang An to get more radishes and said silently: "Seems so..."

That pile of radishes, if it were up to them, they would have to distribute it slowly to eat for a whole snow season.

chapters.title: 第124章
chapters.translated_text:
The tribe’s salt reserves were originally quite sufficient, but a significant amount was used for curing meat and fish before the snowy season. It is feared that the salt originally expected to last until next year's rainy season will be exhausted shortly after the snowy season ends.

But it doesn't matter; this should be enough to get through the snowy season.

Besides salt, although the wolf beastmen didn't stockpile a huge amount of prey, they have a wide variety of stored food and a considerable quantity.

By boiling these together into a thick, soupy mixture, the beastmen can eat their fill at every meal, and the food is sufficient.

At this moment, while the wolf beastmen are haggling over how many more radishes to pickle, the days for the neighbors of the Wolf Tribe are not so easy.

To the west, the Black Feather Tribe.

The Black Feather beastmen built their nests high atop the mountains. Although the mountains are safe, snow accumulated there early on.

Because of the incident with Yu Hua, the Black Feather Tribe was distracted and disorganized during the time they should have been busy stockpiling food. Later, after the old patriarch was sent to the Wolf Tribe, Yu Shan returned to handle the tribe's affairs, causing another period of turmoil.

The result of that turmoil was that the tribe split in two, and Yu Hua took away at least half of the tribe's strong and healthy beastmen.

The Black Feather Tribe suffered a severe blow to its vitality as a result.

Where Yu Hua went, Yu Shan does not yet know. He dared not delay a single moment, quickly arranging for the beastmen to forage for food and make dried fish.

Later, once the tribe regained some calm, Yu Shan went to bring the old patriarch back.

It has been more than half a month since the first snow.

In the cave at the highest point of the mountain, the beastmen are all huddled together.

The old patriarch's nest was moved to the innermost, wind-sheltered area. Yu Le guards him day and night, but the old patriarch is rarely conscious and mostly remains in a stupor.

The mountain winds are raging, and the beastmen, learning from the wolf beastmen, have used grass curtains to block off most of the cave entrance.

The light inside the cave is dim; a single beam of light falls in, revealing only floating dust.

The beastmen lie in their nests, which are filled with downy feathers, in a half-asleep state, enduring the hunger in their bellies.

They were late in stockpiling food, and with the tribe originally having only about eighty beastmen—including twenty or so who were weak or disabled, seven little beastmen, and the twenty or so strong ones that Yu Hua took away—it could almost be said that half of the tribe's hunting party was gone.

No matter how hard the remaining beastmen try, even if they dive into the river every day, the fish caught must be rationed to last through the long snowy season, requiring them to eat sparingly every day.

Fortunately, although they only have two meals a day, each meal is enough to barely stave off hunger, which is much better than the previous one meal a day where they still went hungry.

The beastmen don't feel it's unbearable; the snowy season is cold, and they have nothing else to do anyway.

It has been light for a while now, and Yu Jiang has set up a pottery pot to boil fish soup.

When the beastmen split up, some of the pottery pots and jars were taken by Yu Hua. The beastmen huddled in their nests, watching, and couldn't help but whisper: "I wonder where Yu Hua and the others went? Will they regret it?"

Nearby, Yu Qian is using warm pebbles to press and rub against Yu Shan's leg, trying to make his partner feel a bit better.

The snowy season is cold, and for beastmen who have been injured, it is even harder to endure.

Yu Shan said: "Yu Hua has a stubborn temper, but his abilities are not weak. With the few beastmen following him, as long as they find a place to settle and prepare food early, they will be able to get by."

Yu Qian sits cross-legged beside Yu Shan, and at the thought of Yu Hua, he can't help but let out a soft huff.

"You were even willing to share the pottery pots and jars with him; if he still can't make it, the other beastmen won't respect him either."

Yu Hua had that fight with Yu Shan back then, left, and not long after, came back aggressively.

Yu Qian thought he had calmed down, but it turned out he was just there to demand things.

His partner had rushed to send the old patriarch to Wolf Mountain and rushed back, not even having time to catch his breath, only to be met with Yu Hua righteously demanding the fishing nets and pottery they had exchanged for through their own labor.

Yu Shan tried to persuade him to stay, but he just sneered, saying that now they knew they couldn't survive without him.

Bah!

It wasn't that they couldn't survive without him; it was clearly Yu Shan being worried!

With his impulsive nature and disregard for the big picture, even if he took most of the strong young beastmen, it’s not certain they could safely survive the snowy season.

Before, when the old patriarch was in good health, he could still manage the tribe's affairs. Later, when the old patriarch couldn't, it was all his partner putting in the effort.

The tribe hadn't been in chaos for years, and even the respite they got before the snowy season was because Yu Shan took the initiative to lead the beastmen to Wolf Mountain to trade their labor.

And they, on the other hand, took the things they traded for to fatten themselves up, and once they had strength, they started bickering over the position of patriarch.

They didn't even look at the old patriarch's condition; he might have been able to survive the snowy season, but now, looking at him...

Sigh!

Yu Qian touches the long scar on his partner's leg.

Yu Shan is single-mindedly devoted to the tribe; as long as the tribe is well, anything is fine. If it weren't for the fact that Yu Hua is unreliable, what would it matter if the patriarch position were given to him?

But he doesn't understand; he only knows that the old patriarch was biased toward him...

When the Black Wolf Tribe split up, it was to feed more beastmen. But them? Right before the snowy season, they made such a joke of themselves.

The more he thinks about it, the more he feels the tribe is finished.

Yu Qian repeats the motion with his hands, but his mood is quite low.

Yu Shan notices and places his hand on the back of his, saying, "It will get better."

After surviving the snowy season and building a good relationship with the Wolf Tribe, Yu Shan is confident he can make the tribe better.

The fish soup is ready, and Yu Jiang dishes some out first and sets it aside.

The beastmen get up, tiptoeing past the old patriarch's nest, collect their portions, and return to their own nests to eat.

Yu Qian places the pebbles he was holding by the fire and squats down beside the dazed little beastman.

He pats his shoulder lightly, points toward Yu Jiang, and says in a low voice: "Go eat first. You'll only have the strength to guard him if you're full."

Yu Le lowers his head and slowly shuffles away.

Yu Shan stands to the side, looking at the little beastman who only reaches his chest, and presses his shoulder, "Go talk to Yu Ya and the others. You've been back for so long, and I haven't seen you speak much."

Yu Le walks straight toward Yu Ya.

By the pottery pot, Yu Jiang sees him looking like a lost soul and reaches out to stop him.

"Meat soup, hold the bowl steady."

Yu Ya and the others are all holding their bowls, heads down, shuffling to the side to make room for him.

Yu Ya and these other little beastmen are all males; they are usually quite mischievous, while Yu Le is quiet and timid, so they don't really play together.

In the past, whenever Yu Ya saw Yu Le, he would always tease him a bit.

But with the old patriarch's condition... Yu Le is even more silent than before, looking so pitiful that Yu Ya can't bring himself to say anything.

Yu Le walks over, sits down beside him, lowers his head, and drinks the fish soup little by little. Yu Ya glances at him, hesitates, and thinks for a while before coming up with a topic.

"Weren't you going to learn herbs from the wolf beastmen? When are you going?"

"I don't know."

"Are you going alone? If not, I'll go with you."

Yu Le’s eyes are vacant, staring at Yu Shan and Yu Qian helping his grandfather up and feeding him soup.

"Hey! I said I'd go with you."

In the past, Yu Le would have shrunk back at his tone, but now he just remains dull and foolish, shaking his head.

"I don't know."

Yu Jiang, keeping an eye on them, sees Yu Le like that and can't help but turn away, quickly wiping the corner of his eye.

When Yu Shan returned from the Wolf Tribe, he didn't tell the tribe members what the wolf priest had said. But even without him saying it, everyone had their own judgment.

The old patriarch rarely wakes up now, and he has to be fed by both Yu Shan and Yu Qian.

They are all walking on eggshells, and the atmosphere in the cave is very gloomy.

Yu Le, who was raised by him, feels it even more deeply.

He guards the old beastman day and night; sometimes when they wake up in the middle of the night, they see the little beastman sitting bolt upright.

They are all afraid; the old patriarch is so old that if he were to pass away, they could accept it. They are just afraid that the little beastman won't be able to hold on—he is already frail, and if something were to happen...

Everyone is anxious, and consequently, Yu Ya and the others look worried too.

But this matter is simply unsolvable.

*

The cold wind is biting. Southwest of the Black Feather Tribe, Yu Hua leads his companions and has found a valley here to settle in.

The reason he chose the valley is that there is a spring at the bottom.

The water gushing from the spring is warm, and in the icy world, it still emits wisps of heat. Right now, both banks are covered in snow, but the small stream formed by the spring has not frozen over.

This location is quite good, and since those who followed him are capable beastmen, they have been busy for over a month and have managed to save up some food.

In the past, Yu Hua would have been lying in a grass nest hibernating by now. But not anymore; he has become the leader of this group of beastmen, and there are many things that require him to make decisions.

Yu Hua picks up the pottery pot soaking in the stream and can't help but look toward the direction of the Black Feather Tribe.

Even though he is deep in the mountains and cannot see the high mountain where the Black Feather Tribe lives, his eyes are full of resentment.

He wants to prove to that old beastman that he is bound to be better than that useless Yu Shan! He also wants to show Yu Shan that without him, the Black Feather Tribe simply won't make it!

...

Directly south of the Wolf Tribe, the White Sparrow beastmen have transformed into round, fluffy beast forms, huddled in their nests, passing the winter safely.

The beastmen of the tribe are almost all skilled with bows and arrows. They are small in size, but their success rate in catching prey is high. Their food intake is at least half that of the wolf beastmen.

Every snowy season, the White Sparrow beastmen just huddle in their caves like this, sleeping and eating, and the days pass in a daze.

Outside the stone forest, Sparrow Twelve-White, who had just finished patrolling, rushed into the cave and charged straight at the patriarch, his claws gripping the nest to brake, but his body still tilted from momentum, landing with a "splat" on the patriarch.

The White Sparrow patriarch, who is a size larger, kicks his legs, impatiently shoving Sparrow Twelve-White away.

"Can you stop using me as a cushion!"

"Patriarch! Something's up!" Sparrow Twelve-White rolls over, stands up, and leans toward the patriarch with his wings behind his back.

"If you have something to say, say it!" Sparrow One-White is annoyed to death; why are all the little sparrows the same?

Reckless!

Idiots!

Not like the wolf beastmen, who look intimidating just by standing there.

"To our west, a group of Black Feather beastmen has arrived."

The White Sparrow patriarch flaps his wings, flies up to stand on the edge of the nest, and says condescendingly: "You already said that before!"

"Oh, I forgot." Sparrow Twelve-White rubs his head with his wing.

"But... why haven't they gone back yet?" The White Sparrow patriarch squats down, his downy feathers covering his yellowish claws, "Did you see what they were doing?"

"No."

The White Sparrow patriarch rolls his eyes.

A bunch of idiots!

But that place is already outside the Black Feather Tribe's territory. To the east of there is their territory, and to the west, there don't seem to be any large tribes.

"Could it be they want to expand their territory?"

"Probably not." Sparrow Two-White jumps beside the White Sparrow patriarch and says with certainty.

"You know?"

Sparrow Two-White triumphantly presses his wing on the White Sparrow patriarch's head, only to be grabbed by the armpit and shoved, causing Sparrow Two-White to tumble into the nest.

He kicks his legs, pinning Sparrow Twelve-White, unable to get up.

Seeing no beastman coming to save him, he simply spreads his wings and stares at the cave ceiling: "That group of large-bodied feather-folk always likes to build nests in the highest places."

This is a residual habit from the evolution of the feather-folk, including them, the small-bodied feather-folk, who also like to live on top of the stone forest.

"They are heading toward the valley, maybe because it's warmer there and they can find food. Or maybe they had a falling out with the Black Feather Tribe."

The White Sparrow patriarch nods, thinking that makes some sense.

"Since that's the case, keep an eye on them. If they don't move, we won't bother them. If they dare to come and grab territory, notify the wolf beastmen."

After all, the Wolf Tribe values stability, and both sides are friendly neighbors of the Wolf Tribe; if they start trouble, the Wolf Tribe won't be at peace either.

Having decided, the White Sparrow patriarch jumps into the grass nest.

"Chirp!" Sparrow Two-White is stepped on, stretches out his legs, tilts his head, and pretends to faint.

The White Sparrow patriarch kicks him out of his nest in disgust, settles down comfortably, and glances at the other beastman.

Sparrow Twelve-White quickly hops away.

*

Tens of thousands of miles west of the Wolf Tribe, the Central Continent has also entered the snowy season.

With the decrease in prey and the migration of large tribes, the Wilderness Tribe is now the only dominant power in the middle of the Central Continent.

Long before the snowy season, all the tribes that offer food to the Beast God had already come. But the return journey is long, and some had left too little time for the return trip; now, with the heavy snow, they are still struggling on the road.

And in the Wilderness Tribe, where stone houses are everywhere, the beastmen are huddled in their own homes, spending the snowy season in warmth.

The Wilderness Tribe is large enough, with nearly six thousand beastmen.

They live in family units, each family having a stone house, arranged in an arching formation that surrounds the stone houses of the priest and the patriarch in the center.

At this moment, behind the two-story high stone house in the center of the tribe, in the large square where the beastman altar is located, there is not a speck of snow.

On the stone-paved square, there are animal skin bags of all sizes.

Every animal skin bag is clean and intact, and they are packed full. The animal skin bags are placed in circle after circle around the statue of the Beast God, occupying almost half of the square.

By now, today's food offering has been completed.

The beastmen in charge of the four districts—east, west, south, and north—of the Wilderness Tribe are brought in by Hu Xiaowei, accompanied by the two hundred beastmen brought by these captains to be responsible for transporting the Beast God's bounty.

They are all strong and tall, and there are both herbivorous and carnivorous beastmen.

Hu Xian stands at the door of the only small stone house in the square, wearing an animal skin robe that reaches his ankles. His eyelashes and hair are both white, and he stands in the wind like an immortal.

His eyes look at the Beast God statue in the center of the square, his gaze ethereal.

Several captains approach, and upon seeing Hu Xian, they subconsciously hold their breath, as if they had seen the Beast God descend once again.

Their patriarch looks sixty percent like the portrait of the Beast God.

Hu Xiaowei: "Patriarch, they are here."

Several captains immediately bow respectfully toward him and say in unison: "Patriarch."

Hu Xian's gaze shifts over the captains, and he says faintly: "Go ahead, remember to thank the Beast God for his bounty."

Neither the captains nor Hu Xiaowei dare to disturb him further. Having received permission, they first step back and then quickly walk to the center of the square, only then daring to issue orders for the beastmen to carry the items away.

The food offered to the Beast God is naturally the best: sturdy meat jerky, carefully selected roots of uniform size, and high-quality buzz-insect honey...

Hu Xiaowei holds his booklet, counting bit by bit according to the number of beastmen in each district, and after confirming everything is correct, he tells the beastmen to carry it away.

Their patriarch likes quiet, so the beastmen only dare to speak in low voices.

When they do speak, they glance at the small stone house to confirm the patriarch isn't paying attention before continuing.

Hu Xiaowei and the captains act quickly; once the items are counted, the captains immediately lead their teams away in an orderly fashion.

The beastmen carrying the large and small bags of food are full of joy, the weight of the food pressing down on them.

Having finished his work, Hu Xiaowei also intends to leave. Before leaving, he looks at the small stone house and, seeing the patriarch lift his eyes toward him, immediately tucks away the booklet and hurries over.

"Patriarch."

Hu Xian is still standing at the door; he is thin and slightly tall. Although the animal skin robe is large, it is inevitable that some wind will leak in.

It is not warm at the door, and Hu Xian's skin has always been pale; Hu Xiaowei looks at his face and for a moment cannot tell whether he is cold or not.

Hu Xian: "What is the High Priest doing?"

"Seeing patients." Hu Xiaowei immediately recovers and bows his head respectfully.

"There are many beastmen with coughs and runny noses during the snowy season, as well as those with burns from roasting meat, or injuries from fighting..."

Their tribe has too many beastmen, and the High Priest is only one person, so sometimes he is overwhelmed. Not to mention that beastmen from other tribes come to seek medical treatment, and the High Priest never turns anyone away.

Hu Xian: "Tell him to train a successor."

Hu Xiaowei scratches his head, "Patriarch, isn't Yun Cong, who follows him, already doing that?"

Hu Xian: "One is not enough."

"Who was sent for the Black Feather Tribe matter before?"

"Snow Eagle Tribe beastman, Xue Xiao. The Black Feather Tribe is too far away, and Xue Xiao flies the fastest. They are beastmen from the snowy lands, so they can adapt to the snowy season."

Hu Xian knows what he wants to know and glances at Hu Xiaowei.

Hu Xiaowei knows there is nothing left for him to do and leaves immediately.

The large square suddenly becomes empty and silent. Hu Xian looks at the statue on the altar, and after a long time, his voice sounds like light mist: "I am doing this for my own people; you should understand."

At a time when every tribe is struggling, the beastmen of the Wilderness Tribe are spirited, listening to the cheerful rhythmic beating.

"Father! The tribe is distributing food again." Little beastman Hu Li, huddled in his father's arms, hears the sound, hugs his big tail, and looks up to rub against him.

Nearby, the beautiful red fox beastman gets up, first pulls the animal skin to cover both the big and small ones, and smiles: "Father is going out; you watch over Father and don't let him get down."

"I will definitely watch him well!" The little beastman climbs onto the male beastman's shoulder and wraps himself around his neck like a scarf.

The male beastman chuckles, burying his head to rub against the cub's soft fur, looking at his partner tenderly.

"My leg is already healed."

Hu Jing raises his eyebrows and glares at him, "The High Priest said you can't get down yet, be obedient."

"Okay, Hu Jing, come back quickly."

Hu Jing leaves the house and sees the neighbors nearby scrambling to leave their stone houses, lining up to collect the food belonging to their families.

A neighbor sees him and waves happily: "Hu Jing! You're here, there's buzz-insect honey today! You better hurry."

"Okay!" Hu Jing thinks of the scarcity of buzz-insect honey and can't help but quicken his pace.

The Wilderness Tribe has many stone houses, and the layout is not messy, but distributed along both sides of roads arranged in a grid pattern.

Although the roads are not paved with stone, every household is responsible for clearing the road in front of their own door, so there is no snow in the middle of the road.

When Hu Jing reaches the captain's house, he sees the captain, Xiong Ke, waving at him.

"Captain."

Xiong Ke waves his hand, and immediately a beastman behind him hands over the prepared food.

Xiong Ke's voice is deep and somewhat deafening, "Hu Chang was injured while hunting, so the tribe gave extra food; tell him to recover well."

Hu Jing takes the animal skin bag, his smile widening.

"I will tell him, thank you, Captain."

Xiong Ke nods and continues to get busy.

On the way, Hu Jing glances at the food in the animal skin bag; there are two arm-length pieces of dried meat, not thin strips, but as thick as a beastman's calf. There are also dried vegetables, fruits, and long roots, and a small jar of buzz-insect honey.

This is enough for them to eat for three days.

Hu Jing takes the food home in high spirits. As soon as he enters the house, his cub, lying on his father's shoulder, looks up and says obediently: "Father, I watched over Father well."

Hu Jing hands the animal skin bag to his partner to see and touches the cub, "You're a good boy."

Hu Chang looks at the meat jerky and can't help but smile.

"The tribe is really good to us."

"The High Priest said it's the Beast God favoring our tribe."

Hu Chang's smile suddenly fades a bit, "But... those tribes that sent food, do they not get any of this..."

Hu Jing sighs: "Since they also offered food to the Beast God, next year, there should be more prey in their territories."

"That's true, that's right." Hu Chang breathes a sigh of relief, watching his partner start to arrange a fire and roast meat.

While other beastmen are skin and bones, the beastmen of the Wilderness Tribe can be considered strong and healthy.

However, the tribe doesn't have much pottery, unlike the Wolf Tribe, which can use pottery to boil meat soup.

The beastmen just gnaw on meat jerky and eat some roots, and they can fill their bellies solidly.

*

Wolf Mountain.

After breakfast, the beastmen start using brooms made of tree branches to sweep the snow from the front of the mountain and the top of the corridor.

The beastmen have great strength, and these days, having eaten their fill, they just lie in the caves with nowhere to expend their energy; their washboard-like bellies have grown a bit of fat.

As the brooms sweep out, the snow spray scatters like salt particles.

The snow Lin Qiu has seen is the snow of the south, gentle and rare. Seeing the beastmen working hard, he finds a place without any beastmen and reaches out to grab a handful of snow.

As soon as he lets go, seeing Lang Yan coming over, he immediately throws the snow at his feet.

Lang Yan stops, a bit stunned.

Lin Qiu squats down, quickly digging at the snow, trying to pack it together.

Lang Yan hurries over, and Lin Qiu hands the snow ball to him, "Pack it bigger."

Lang Yan: "It's cold."

Lin Qiu's knuckles are frozen red; he quickly rubs his hands, hides them in his animal skin clothes, and looks at Lang Yan expectantly.

Lang Yan looks at Lin Qiu from head to toe, confirms he isn't freezing, and quickly does as he asked. Before he finishes, he sees Lin Qiu, having warmed his hands, reaching out to touch it again.

Lang Yan immediately says: "Is this okay?"

Lin Qiu glances at it and hands him another one from his hand.

Lang Yan frowns, "Your hands are red."

Lin Qiu immediately shrinks into his sleeves, "Just a moment, it'll be done soon."

Lang Yan has no choice but to continue helping.

With Lang Yan's help, Lin Qiu makes a snowman half a person tall. The snowman's eyes are made of black dried fruit, its nose is made of leftover lotus root tips, and it is holding a broom.

Lin Qiu claps his hands and nods.

Before he can admire it for long, Lang Yan says: "Qiu, go into the cave."

"In a minute." Lin Qiu is studying where else needs modification, looking like he doesn't want to leave.

Lang Yan is silent, his lips pressed tight.

He steps forward, suddenly lowers his body, lifts Lin Qiu, and walks straight toward the corridor.

"Hey! Wait a minute!"

"Don't move, or we'll both fall."

"You... how are you so unreasonable? I haven't finished yet."

Lang Yan's brows press even tighter, his arms wrapping around Lin Qiu's legs like pliers, saying nothing.

From afar, Lang Chi sees them and huffs.

Although he doesn't like it, he thinks Lang Yan is doing the right thing.

It's so cold, is snow something you can just play with like that?!
chapters.source_text:
部落存盐本来还算足，但雪季前腌肉跟腌鱼干用了不少，原本预计能吃到明年雨季的盐，怕是雪季过后就要耗尽。
但没关系，这不是能吃过雪季么。
除开盐，狼兽人虽然囤的猎物不算多，但存粮的种类多，数量也可观。
这样混杂着煮熟，弄成汤汤水水的样子，兽人们每顿吃饱，食物也是够的。
此刻，就在狼兽人们为着再腌多少萝卜而讨价还价时，狼部落的邻居们日子就没那么好过了。
西边，黑羽部落。
黑羽兽人的巢建在高山之上，山上虽然安全，却早早积了雪。
因着羽哗一事，黑羽部落在本该忙着囤食物的时候，兽人心不齐，耽搁了一阵。后头老族长被送去狼部落，羽山回去处理黑羽部落的事，又闹了一阵。
闹过的结果，就是部落一分为二，羽哗带走了部落至少一半身强体壮的兽人。
黑羽部落也因此元气大伤。
羽哗去哪儿了，羽山暂且不知。他不敢耽搁一点时间，快速安排兽人们寻找食物，制作鱼干。
后来，等部落恢复平静，羽山才去将老族长接了回来。
距离第一场雪已经过去半个多月。
山上最高处的山洞中，兽人们都窝在一起。
老族长的窝被搬到最里面避风处，羽乐日日守着，但老族长也是清醒的时候少，昏沉的时候多。
山风肆虐，兽人们学着狼兽人那样，用草帘挡了大半洞口。
洞里光线暗淡，一缕光束落进来，只有灰尘浮动。
兽人们各自趴在铺满了绒羽的窝里，似睡非睡，忍受着肚里饥饿。
他们囤食物晚了些，加之部落原本仅有八十来个兽人，其中二十多个身体虚弱或有残缺的兽人，七个小兽人，羽哗又带走了二十多个身强体壮的，几乎可以说带走了部落半个狩猎队。
剩下的兽人再如何努力，就算天天扎进河里，捕捞到的鱼分摊到漫长的雪季，一天也必须节省着吃。
好在一天虽也两顿，每顿勉强垫垫肚子，但比从前一天一顿还吃不饱好了太多。
兽人们不觉得不能忍受，雪季寒冷，他们也没别的事情做。
这会儿已经天亮了一会儿，羽江架起陶锅煮鱼汤。
兽人分家，陶锅陶罐也叫羽哗带走了些，兽人们窝在巢里看着，忍不住小声道：“不知道羽哗他们去哪儿了？会不会后悔。”
旁边，羽千正用温热的鹅卵石压在羽山腿上刮蹭，让伴侣好受一些。
雪季冷，受过伤的兽人们更是难熬。
羽山道：“羽哗脾气倔，但能力不弱。跟着他的兽人少，只要他们早点找到地方落脚，准备食物，也能过去。”
羽千盘腿坐在羽山身边，想起羽哗就忍不住轻哼一声。
“你都愿意分他陶锅陶罐了，他要再不行，兽人也不服他。”
羽哗当时跟羽山打了那一架，走了，没多久又气势汹汹回来。
羽千还以为他消了气，结果是来要东西的。
他家伴侣匆匆把老族长送到狼山，又匆匆回来，来不及喘一口气，就看着羽哗理直气壮地要他们靠劳动交换回来的渔网跟陶器。
羽山劝他留下，他还嗤笑，说现在知道离了他不行了。
呸！
哪里是离了他不行，分明是羽山担心！
凭他一时意气，不顾全大局的样子，就算他带走了大部分青壮兽人，也不一定能安稳度过雪季。
从前老族长身体好，部落的事他还能安排一二。后头老族长不行，可都是他伴侣费心费力。
部落几年没乱，甚至雪季前得到的那一阵喘息，都是羽山主动带着兽人去狼山交换了劳动换回来的。
他们倒好，拿着换的东西给自己养肥了，有力气了，计较起族长的位置来。
也不看看老族长身体怎么样，原本兴许能熬过雪季去，可现在看着……
哎！
羽千摸着自己伴侣腿上长长的疤痕。
羽山一心一意都是部落，部落好，怎么样都行。要不是羽哗靠不住，就是那族长位置让给他，又如何呢。
可他不懂，他只知道老族长偏心待他……
人家黑狼兽人部落分开，却是为了养活更多的兽人。他们倒好，临了雪季，还闹出这么个笑话来。
越想，越觉得部落好像完了。
羽千重复着手上动作，情绪却有些低落。
羽山察觉，手贴上他的手背，“会好的。”
熬过雪季，跟狼部落交好，羽山有信心让部落变好。
鱼汤好了，羽江先盛了点出来放在一边。
兽人们爬起来，轻手轻脚路过老族长的窝，领了自己那份儿，又回自己窝边去吃。
羽千将手中鹅卵石放在火堆旁，蹲在发呆的小兽人身边。
他轻拍他肩，指了指羽江那边，低声说：“先去吃，吃饱了才有力气守着。”
羽乐低下头，慢慢往外挪。
羽山站在一旁，看着才到他胸口高的小兽人，按了按他肩膀，“跟羽涯他们说说话去，都回来这么久了，没见你开几次口。”
羽乐就径直往羽涯那边走。
陶锅边，打汤的羽江看他跟失了魂一样，伸手将他拉住。
“肉汤，端稳了。”
羽涯几个各个抱着碗闷头往边上挪一挪，留出个位置来。
羽涯这几个小兽人都是雄兽人，寻常就比较皮，羽乐话少，胆儿小，跟他们玩儿不到一起去。
以往羽涯见了羽乐，怎么都要怼几句。
可老族长这情况……羽乐比从前更沉默的模样，可怜兮兮的，叫他也说不出话来。
羽乐走过来，在他旁边坐好，低下头，一点一点喝着鱼汤。羽涯看了他一眼，犹豫着，想了一圈才想起个话题。
“你不是要去跟狼兽人学草药，什么时候去？”
“不知道。”
“你一个兽人去吗？要不然，我跟着你一起。”
羽乐双目无神，盯着对面羽山跟羽千将他阿爷扶起来，配合着喂汤。
“喂！我说我跟你一起去。”
换做以前，羽乐该被他的语气吓得一缩，可现在还是呆呆傻傻的，摇头。
“我不知道。”
羽江关注着这边，看羽乐那样，忍不住背过身，迅速抹了下眼角。
羽山从狼部落回来，并没把狼族祭司说的话告诉族人。但他不说，大家心里也有判断。
老族长现在醒来的时候很少很少，吃东西都得羽山跟羽千两个兽人喂。
他们都提心吊胆的，山洞里的气氛很低迷。
被他带着长大的羽乐感受只会更真切。
他日日守着老兽人，有时候他们半夜醒来，都看着小兽人直挺挺坐着。
他们都怕，老族长这么大年纪了，要是走了也能接受。就怕小兽人撑不住，本就体弱，要是万一出了事……
大伙儿着急，连带着，羽涯几个看着也急。
可这事，简直无解。
*
冷风瑟瑟，黑羽部落西南方向，羽哗带领着同伴，在这边找了一处山谷落脚。
之所以选山谷，原是这谷底有泉眼。
泉眼涌出来的水温热，冰天雪地里，还冒着丝丝缕缕的热气。这会儿两岸积雪覆盖，那条泉水汇成的小溪流也没有结冰。
这位置还算好，加之跟来都是有能力的兽人，他们忙碌了一个多月，也攒下些食物。
换做以往，羽哗这会儿也该躺在草窝里猫冬了。但现在不行，他成了这群兽人的头儿，好多事需要他拿主意。
羽哗捡起泡在溪水里的陶锅，忍不住望了眼黑羽部落的方向。
即使身处重重山中，看不见黑羽部落居住的高山，他眼中也满是怨意。
他要向那老兽人证明，他势必比得过那个废了的羽山！他也要叫羽山看看，没了他，黑羽部落根本不行！
……
狼部落正南边，白雀兽人化作圆滚滚的兽形，挤在巢里，安稳过冬。
部落兽人几乎都擅长弓箭，他们体型小，捕捉猎物的成功率却高。他们的食量比起狼兽人，也起码小了一半。
每年雪季，白雀兽人就这么窝在山洞里，睡着、吃着，恍恍惚惚日子就过去了。
石林外，刚在外面巡逻一圈的雀十二白冲入山洞，又一下冲到族长跟前，爪子紧抓着窝刹住，身体还是跟着惯性倾斜，吧唧一下压在族长身上。
体型大了一圈的白雀族长蹬腿儿，不耐烦地将雀十二白踢开。
“能不能不要把我当缓冲的垫子！”
“族长！有事！”雀十二白翻个身，站起，背着翅膀往族长面前凑了凑。
“有事说事！”雀一白都烦死了，小雀怎么都一个德行。
莽撞！
笨蛋！
不像狼兽人一样，看着就唬兽人。
“咱们西边，来了一群黑羽兽人。”
白雀族长拍了下翅膀，飞上去站在窝边缘，居高临下道：“你之前已经说过了！”
“哦，我忘了。”雀十二白翅膀蹭脑袋。
“不过……他们怎么还没回去？”白雀族长蹲下，绒毛遮住鹅黄色的爪子，“你看见他们在干什么了吗？”
“没有。”
白雀族长翻个白眼。
全是些笨蛋！
不过那地方已经出了黑羽部落的领地。那边往东，就是他们的领地，往西，好像也没什么大部落在。
“难不成他们想扩大领地？”
“应该不会。”雀二白跳到白雀族长旁边，肯定道。
“你知道？”
雀二白得意地用翅膀压了压白雀族长的脑袋，被他往咯吱窝一抓，雀二白一头栽进窝里。
他蹬了蹬腿，压着雀十二白，起不来。
看没兽人救他，索性翅膀一摊，盯着洞顶道：“那群体型大的羽族，总喜欢往最高的地方搭窝。”
这是羽族进化中残留的习性，包括他们这些体型小的羽族，不也是喜欢住在石林顶上。
“他们往山谷走，可能是那里暖和，能找找食物。也可能跟黑羽部落闹掰了。”
白雀族长点点头，觉得有那么点道理。
“既然如此，那就先盯着，他们不动，也就不管。他们敢过来抢地盘，就通知狼兽人。”
毕竟狼部落重视稳定，两边可都是狼部落的友好邻里，他们闹起来，狼部落也不安生。
想好了，白雀族长往草窝里一跳。
“啾！”雀二白被踩了下，伸直了腿，脑袋一歪，装晕。
白雀族长嫌弃地将他踹出自己的窝，舒舒服服往下团了团，瞥一眼另一个兽人。
雀十二白赶紧蹦跳着离开。
*
自狼部落往西边而去，数万里之遥，中央大陆也同样步入了雪季。
伴随着猎物减少，大部落迁徙离去，中央大陆中部如今只有原野部落一家独大。
早在雪季前，所有给兽神供奉食物的部落已经来过了。只回程路漫漫，有些回程预留的时间短了，如今大雪，依旧在路上挣扎。
而石屋遍布的原野部落，兽人们各自窝在自己家中，温暖过雪季。
原野部落规模足够大，兽人近六千。
他们以家庭为单位，一家一座石头房子，呈拱卫状，将祭司与族长的石屋包裹在中心。
此时，部落中心两层高大石屋后头，兽人祭坛所在大广场中，不见一点积雪。
石板铺平的广场上，放着大大小小的兽皮袋。
每一个兽皮袋都干净、完好，里面也装得鼓鼓囊囊。兽皮袋绕着兽神的雕像放了一圈又一圈，几乎占据半个广场。
这会儿，今天的食物已经供奉完毕。
原野部落东南西北四个片区的分管兽人被狐小尾带着进来，同行的，还有这几个队长带来负责搬运兽神恩赐的两百个兽人。
他们皆是身强体壮，身量高大，食草兽人、食肉兽人都有。
狐弦站在那广场上唯一一座小石屋门口，披着长至脚踝的兽皮袍。他眼睫、发色皆白，如仙人一般，随风站立。
那双眼看着广场中心的兽神像，目光虚幻。
几个队长近前来，看到狐弦下意识屏息，仿佛看到了兽神再一次降临。
他们的族长，跟兽神画像，像了六分。
狐小尾：“族长，他们来了。”
几个队长立即恭恭敬敬冲着他低头，齐声道：“族长。”
狐弦目光在几个队长身上一转，淡淡道：“去吧，记得要谢谢兽神的恩赐。”
队长跟狐小尾都不敢多打扰他，得了准许，先是后退一步，随后快步走到广场中央，这才敢出声命令兽人搬走东西。
供奉兽神的食物自然挑的最好的，有结实的肉干，有粗细均匀特意挑选过的块根，也有上好的嗡嗡虫蜜……
狐小尾捏着他那本册子，一点一点按照片区兽人的数量，清点无误之后，叫兽人扛走。
他们族长喜静，兽人说话都只敢低声。
开口时还要往那小石屋看上一眼，确认族长没在意，才继续说。
狐小尾跟几个队长的动作快，东西清点完，队长立马带队有序离开。
那些食物大包小包叫兽人扛着，沉甸甸的，压得专门来搬食物的兽人满脸欣喜。
狐小尾事情办完，也打算离开。走前看了小石屋一眼，见族长冲着他抬了下眼，立马揣好册子，赶紧上前。
“族长。”
狐弦还是站在门口，他身形偏瘦，身量略高。兽皮袍子虽然大，但难免会漏风。
这门口并不暖和，狐弦的皮肤一直都白，狐小尾看了下他的脸，一时间分不清他到底是冷不冷。
狐弦：“大祭司在做什么？”
“看病。”狐小尾立马回神，低头恭敬道。
“雪季咳嗽跟流鼻涕的兽人很多，还有烤肉被烧伤的，打架不小心弄伤的……”
他们部落兽人太多了，大祭司就一个兽人，有时候总会忙不过来。更别说还有外面其他部落的兽人过来求医，大祭司都来者不拒。
狐弦：“叫他培养下一任大祭司。”
狐小尾挠挠头，“族长，他身边跟着的云丛不就是嘛。”
狐弦：“一个不够。”
“之前黑羽部落的事，派去的是谁？”
“雪鹰部落的兽人，雪啸。黑羽部落那边太远了，雪啸飞得最快，他们本来就是雪地的兽人族，也能适应雪季。”
狐弦知道了自己想知道的，看了狐小尾一眼。
狐小尾知道没自己事儿了，立马离开。
偌大的广场一下空寂，狐弦看着那祭坛上的雕像，许久，声似轻雾：“我都是为了自己的族人，您应该理解。”
在这个各个部落都苦熬的时候，原野部落的兽人听着那欢快的敲击声，精神振奋。
“阿父！部落又分食物了。”小兽人狐栗窝在他阿父怀里，听到声音，抱着大尾巴仰头去蹭。
旁边，漂亮的红狐兽人起身，先拉了拉兽皮给一大一小盖好，笑道：“阿爸出去，你看着阿父，别让他下来。”
“我一定好好看着！”小兽人爬到雄兽人肩膀，将自己像围脖一样，围在他脖子上。
雄兽人闷笑，埋头蹭了蹭幼崽柔软的毛，温柔看着伴侣。
“我腿都好了。”
狐镜竖眉瞪他，“大祭司都说了还不能下来，你听话。”
“好，阿镜快去快回。”
狐镜离开屋，便看到附近的邻居争先恐后离开石屋，排队领回了属于自己家的食物。
邻居见了他，高兴挥手道：“阿镜！你来了，今天有嗡嗡虫蜜！你赶紧去。”
“诶！”狐镜想到嗡嗡虫蜜的稀缺性，也忍不住加快了步子。
原野部落有很多石屋，石屋布局并不乱，而是沿着呈井字形的道路两边分布。
路上虽然没有铺石头，但每家每户都要负责清理自己门口的路，所以这一路走来，中间并没有积雪。
狐镜到了队长家门口，就看到队长熊壳冲他招手。
“队长。”
熊壳一挥手，后头立马有兽人将准备好的食物递过来。
熊壳声音浑厚，有些震耳，“狐常狩猎受伤，部落给了多的食物，叫他好好养伤。”
狐镜接过兽皮袋，笑容大了些。
“我会告诉他的，谢谢队长。”
熊壳点头，又继续忙去。
路上，狐镜看了眼兽皮袋中的食物，里面有两条手臂长的干肉块，并非细长一条，而是有兽人小腿粗。还有干菜，果子，以及长长的块根，嗡嗡虫蜜也有一小罐。
这些足够他们吃三天。
狐镜拿了食物喜气洋洋回家，刚一进屋，自家幼崽就趴在他阿父肩膀，仰起头，乖乖道：“阿爸，我有看好阿父哦。”
狐镜将兽皮袋递给自己伴侣看，顺手摸了摸幼崽，“真乖。”
狐常看着那肉干，也忍不住笑。
“部落对我们可真好。”
“大祭司说了，是兽神眷顾我们部落。”
狐常笑容忽然收敛了些，“可……那些送食物来的部落，是不是就分不到这些……”
狐镜叹道：“他们既然也给兽神供奉了食物，来年，领地里应该会有更多的猎物。”
“是这样，没错。”狐常松了口气，看着伴侣开始安排着生火，烤肉。
在其他兽人都骨瘦如柴的情况下，原野部落的兽人可以算得上是身强体壮。
不过部落的陶器不多，不像狼部落那样能用陶器煮肉汤来吃。
兽人们只是啃肉干，吃些块根，就能把肚子填得扎扎实实的。
*
狼山。
吃过早饭，兽人们开始拿着树枝做的扫帚，清扫山前跟廊顶上的积雪。
兽人们力气大，这些天吃饱了就往洞里趴，无处消耗精力，搓衣板似的肚子上，隐隐长了些肉。
那扫帚一挥出去，雪沫子散开，盐粒子似的。
林楸见过的雪是南方的雪，温温柔柔，还难得一见。见兽人们吭哧吭哧忙起来，他找了处没兽人的地方，先伸手捏了一把雪。
手一松，见狼岩过来，立马将雪扔他脚下。
狼岩停下，有些愣住。
林楸蹲下来，飞快将雪刨了刨，试图团起来。
狼岩忙走过来，林楸将雪团往他手上一送，“团大一点。”
狼岩：“冷。”
林楸指节冻红了，他忙搓了搓手，藏在兽皮衣里，期待地看着狼岩。
狼岩从头到脚看了一眼林楸，确认他没冻着，赶紧按照他要求做。他还没弄好，又看见捂热了手的林楸又上手摸。
狼岩立即道：“这个可以了吗？”
林楸扫了眼，又将手上的另一个递给他。
狼岩蹙眉，“手红了。”
林楸立即往袖口里缩了缩，“就一会儿，马上就好。”
狼岩只好继续帮忙。
林楸借着狼岩的手，搓了个半人高的雪人出来。雪人眼珠子用黑黢黢的果干做的，鼻子用吃剩的藕尖做的，还抱着一把扫帚。
林楸拍手，点点头。
还没欣赏一会儿，狼岩：“楸，进山洞去。”
“马上。”林楸研究着还有哪里需要修改的地方，看着是不想走。
狼岩默了默，唇角绷直。
他上前，忽然矮身将林楸扛起，直接往廊道上走。
“诶！等会儿！”
“别动，等会儿一起摔。”
“你……怎么不讲理，我还没弄完。”
狼岩眉头压得更紧，手臂跟钳子似的环抱林楸的腿，不吭声了。
远远的，狼赤看到他俩，哼一声。
虽然看不惯，但也觉得狼岩做得对。
这么冷，雪是能这么玩儿的吗？！

The orcs were clearing the area in front of the mountain. The old priest, bundled up like a ball, came out carrying a whole piece of wild ginger he had grown earlier.

"An, slice this up and boil it into soup for the orcs to drink later."

Wolf An watched as the old priest placed the wild ginger on the stove, then leaned on his cane and leisurely returned to his cave to nest.

The wild ginger was as large as two palms. Usually, it was used as a seasoning, with at most a palm-sized piece used at a time. The tribe didn't have much of it, so using it felt like a waste.

The wild ginger was washed, sliced, and thrown into the water to boil.

Wolf An watched as Wolf Yan carried Lin Qiu back, smiling more kindly than he did when seeing his own cubs.

"Oh my, Qiu's face is frozen red. Come over here and sit for a while."

Lin Qiu was already being carried by Wolf Yan, and upon hearing Wolf An's voice, he deflated, his ears turning even redder.

He couldn't help but pinch Wolf Yan's lower back, but he couldn't even make a dent.

Did he have no dignity?

Not until Wolf Yan placed him on the stool in front of the stove did Lin Qiu secretly glance at the low-pressure Wolf King and silently move his legs away.

There were some embers in the stove, so Lin Qiu stuffed a handful of dry grass inside to ignite the fire.

Smelling the strong scent of ginger, Lin Qiu looked at the stove and said, "Isn't this too much?"

Wolf An: "The priest brought it, so don't worry about it. A stronger brew should be more effective as medicine."

He glanced at Wolf Yan, who had pulled up a stool to sit beside Lin Qiu and keep watch, and couldn't help but laugh.

The King protected Qiu like the apple of his eye.

The orcs of the tribe were happy to see the Wolf King having a good relationship with his mate.

The scent of the wild ginger was heavy; just from slicing it, Lin Qiu, sitting in front of the stove, felt it stinging his nose.

Wolf Yan guarded him for a while and then held his hand. Lin Qiu scratched his palm in confusion, "What's wrong?"

His hands were warm.

"You go to the cave, I'll do the cooking."

Lin Qiu rubbed his nose and said with a smile, "It's nothing, it's comfortable sitting here."

As the boiling time grew longer, a continuous sound of sneezing came from all around; wolf noses were just too sensitive.

Lin Qiu looked up, "Who climbed up to the roof?"

A head poked out from the edge of the eaves.

"Achoo!"

"It's me, Qiu. What are you guys cooking? The smell is way too strong!"

Seeing it was Wolf Jin, Lin Qiu said mysteriously, "Something delicious."

The little wolf was hanging upside down from the roof, which was very dangerous.

Wolf Yan glanced up, stood up, and Wolf Jin immediately retracted his head.

The King who was watching him had finally left, so Lin Qiu stretched out his legs and spread his hands in front of the stove to warm them slowly.

With many orcs, the work was fast. The road was cleared, and everyone pretended not to see the stuff on the stove, carrying their brooms as if they still had work to do, and headed straight to the west.

Wolf Yan: "Come back."

The orcs froze, one foot raised, standing like snowmen, not daring to move.

Wolf Yan: "Do I need to say it a second time?"

"Awoo! King, I don't want to drink that!" the orc howled, carrying his broom back in a huff, extremely reluctant.
