林楸无奈，怕他们太闲了捣乱，又跟小狼安排事情：“回去帮狼安，水烧好了兑水弄得不能太烫，然后送来。”
“嗷！”
小狼欢快地抱着空了一半的罐子跑了。
加上后头来的羽哗，需要紧急救治的兽人一共八个。
送这些伤患过来的黑羽兽人同样受了凉，喝完姜汤还哆嗦。
好在灶台上还有祭司治疗羽涯他们的草药，匀一点出来，赶紧给他们喝了。末了，又叫他们转移到另一个小山洞，先烤火让身体缓和过来。
而这边山洞中，狼冰接骨，林楸递药，顺带包扎。
小小的狼雪抓着药罐子，小脸绷着，认认真真给兽人不严重的伤口上撒药。
老祭司则对着兽人刺破皮肤的骨头，拧死了眉头。
“这腿保不了了，得截了。不截你必死，截了也不一定能活。你自己选一个。”
林楸看了眼老祭司对着说话的兽人。
人家脸都烧红了，哪里能说什么话。
祭司显然也意识到了，转头沉声问：“谁能拿主意？”
林楸：“我去问问。”
“截！”洞口，急匆匆赶来的六个小兽人道。
羽涯闻到浓厚的血腥味，偏过头，深吸一口外面的冷气，再坚定地走进来。
“截吧。”
老祭司皱眉，“去问成年兽人。你们不是该休息？别让我的药白费。”
“老祭司，我们就是担心，过来看看。”羽涯没了底气，低着头不敢看兽人。
林楸点了个兽人匆匆去问，问完回来，黑羽兽人也跟了过来。
为首的兽人郑重道：“祭司，一切都看你的方法来，要是他们活不过来，是他们自己不行。”
“行，这可是你们自己说的。”

chapters.title: 第127章
chapters.translated_text:
The valley.

The orcs barely managed to get some sleep in the cave.

Since it wasn't their own territory, they never felt truly at ease. The wolf orcs sat up, yawning with exhaustion, and slumped crookedly against their companions.

Lang Yan’s ears twitched; he opened his eyes, his gray pupils clear and alert.

He looked outside the cave and stood up to head over.

The few fur-balls that had just tried to approach puffed up into spheres instantly, letting out a sharp, startled "chirp" and nearly fainting from fright.

Lang Yan lowered his head, looking at the White Sparrow orcs, whose beast forms were not even as tall as his lower leg.

"Something up?"

Que Shierbai shook his head rapidly, took a dozen steps back with a clatter, pressed his wings against his thumping chest, and said, "No, nothing, we just came over to take a look."

"Eh? Little white sparrows!"

The wolf orcs swarmed out and squatted down, though their line of sight was still higher than the fluffy white sparrow orcs.

Facing a large group of wolf orcs, Que Shierbai swallowed hard and quietly shuffled his claws backward again.

A long, thin trail of claw marks was left on the snow at the cave entrance.

The little white sparrow explained, "We saw that the Snow Eagle orcs were gone."

"Oh, they were killed by the Black Feather orcs. There’s one left, locked up; don't know if he's dead or not," Lang Shun said enthusiastically.

Que Shierbai gasped in fright; the air was too cold, and he choked on it.

"The Black Feather orcs fought the Snow Eagle orcs and won?" His bean-like eyes widened, and he gripped a handful of snow under his claws, looking as if he couldn't believe it.

Yu Lie squeezed through the gap, lowered his head, and said in a deep voice, "You still dare to look down on us?"

"Hey!" Que Shierbai shrank back. "That’s... that’s just what our patriarch said."

The little white sparrow sold out his patriarch without hesitation.

It was cold standing at the cave entrance, and Lang Yan didn't intend to chat with the White Sparrow orcs; he signaled the other orcs to eat and prepare for the return journey.

There was still a lot of food in the cave, which Yu Hua and the others had stored for the snow season, and it needed to be taken away as well.

A dozen or so dumpling-like White Sparrow orcs looked up at Lang Yan as he entered the cave.

Que Shierbai watched too, then tilted his head, his bean-like eyes spinning in circles.

Had he forgotten something?

His back was poked.

A companion whispered a reminder: "Uncle Erbai..."

Oh, right! The patriarch told them to come and ask about this!

Que Shisan hurriedly asked, "What happened to the orcs from our tribe who went to the Wolf tribe to report the news? They haven't come back yet."

Lang Huo: "They got frostbite."

The dozen or so White Sparrows were shocked again, and the sound of choking coughs continued.

Lang Huo, having succeeded in his prank, grinned and said, "But with our priest there, they won't die."

Que Shierbai said honestly, "Thank you."

Lang Huo watched him hop outward. "Are you leaving?"

Que Shierbai: "It's cold, we have to go back quickly." Otherwise, it wouldn't be good if they ended up with frostbite like Que Erbai.

They didn't have a priest.

Que Shierbai felt dejected and timidly waved his wings at the orcs at the cave entrance, the arc of his movement extremely small. "W-we’re leaving."

The White Sparrow orcs looked bulky and round, but it was actually all feathers.

They flew fast; with a 'whoosh,' like a thrown snowball, they disappeared from the valley in a moment.

A group of wolf orcs watched them, unable to stop themselves from grinding their claws.

Seeing these little things made their claws itch.

They were like little wolf-fur balls.

There was a lot to bring back for the return trip, so Yu Lie took charge and directly divided half of the food in Yu Hua's cave among the wolf orcs. It wasn't payment for this trip, but just a way to express their gratitude.

The wolf orcs didn't decline and took it decisively.

Yu Lie wanted to take his orcs back to the tribe first to report the news and bring the food back. The wolf orcs would travel with them for a stretch before parting ways.

The wolf orcs valued their lives, so as usual, they bundled themselves up with animal skins before carrying the food on their backs.

Lang Yan and Yu Lie walked at the back. There were still patients from the Black Feather tribe at Wolf Mountain, so Yu Lie would have to make another trip later.

This had been agreed upon with Lang Yan beforehand to avoid barging into someone else's tribe and breaking the rules. Delivering news and transporting patients were special circumstances, so that went without saying.

Before leaving, all the supplies in the cave were cleared out.

A Black Feather orc slapped his head. "Almost forgot, there's still an orc in the next cave."

They pushed away the rocks blocking the cave entrance, revealing Xue Xiao, who was covered in blood inside.

The orc was unconscious, his chest rising and falling slightly; he was still alive.

Their tribe had few orcs capable of hunting to begin with, and this loss was devastating. The Black Feather orcs hated the Snow Eagle orcs to the bone.

Leaving this one alive wasn't because they wanted him to live, but to take him back for their tribesmen to see, giving those who had lost partners or fathers a way to vent.

Besides, letting him die like this would be letting him off too easily.

Yu Lie’s hands clenched with a cracking sound; if he hadn't forced himself to hold back, he would have torn him apart yesterday!

He went in, pulled out a grass rope found in the cave, and tied the orc up to ensure he couldn't fight back even if he had the strength.

Then, he transformed into his beast form, grabbed Xue Xiao with his claws, and flew toward the sky.

The wolf orcs were eager to return home and ran at full speed.

After traveling for half a day, it was time to part ways, and the wolf orcs headed toward their own tribe.

Yu Lie, clutching the grass-rope-bound Xue Xiao, nodded at them and led his orcs toward the north.

The cold wind was biting, cutting into their bodies like blades.

Xue Xiao woke up.

He opened his eyes wearily, seeing only the vast, white, snowy plains beneath the high sky, which looked like his homeland.

It seemed he had been away from the Northern Continent for too long; he had thought he had forgotten what the tribe looked like.

Turns out he still remembered.

There wasn't much prey left in the Northern Continent either. He had brought his tribesmen out to make a living and seek a way to survive. The food of the Wilderness tribe was sucked from other tribes; they had lived well following them for so many years, but that had come to an end.

His tribesmen were gone.

Xue Xiao looked calmly at the boundless snow and used his last bit of strength to twist and break free.

With a loud bang—

The wolf orcs, who hadn't gone far, all stopped and looked back.

The Black Feather orcs flying in the sky paused their flapping wings, staring blankly at the ground.

A cluster of what looked like intensely vibrant blood flowers bloomed on the pure white snowfield.

Yu Lie looked at his claws; the grass rope made by his tribesmen was of poor quality.

But it wasn't a problem with the rope.

He slowly flapped his wings, moved toward the wolf orcs, and glided to a landing.

"What just happened..."

"Xue Xiao broke free himself and fell to his death."

"Didn't hold him tight enough?" the wolf orc wondered.

Lang Yan, thinking of the orc who should have been a match for him in a fight, said calmly, "He must have done it willingly."

Orcs value their tribe and their people. This battle was tragic, and with only him left, he didn't want to live alone.

Yu Lie nodded, looking somewhat silent.

"He broke free himself."

Knowing it was death, he chose to embrace it.

Although they stood on different sides, in this regard, he was an orc worthy of respect for his tribesmen.

Lang Yan: "Let's go."

Lang Huo actually felt it was a bit of a pity. After the Black Feather orcs flew away, he carried his prey over to Lang Yan and said, "King, do you think if the Snow Eagle orcs had joined us in the beginning, we wouldn't have to fear other Feather tribes?"

He had watched the Snow Eagle orcs fight; if they hadn't been exhausted by the Black Feather orcs twice earlier, they could have suppressed the Black Feather orcs.

Lang Yan jumped down the hillside, the snow reaching his belly.

He said unhurriedly, "Do you think, with us eating one meal a day and starving to the point of chewing on bugs, he would have joined us?"

Lang Huo: "..."

Seems like that's true.

The disappointment lasted only a moment, and Lang Huo shook the prey on his body.

"Hehe, let's go back and find Qiu! Didn't expect to be able to bring food back this time; let Qiu make us something delicious."

Lang Yan didn't respond, just silently increased his speed.

*

Wolf Mountain.

The priest, Lang Bing, and Lin Qiu had been busy from morning until noon. Even Lang Xue couldn't stand and had to sit down to help; only then were all the orcs treated.

Lin Qiu sat in the corner, watching Lang Bing tidying up the obsidian flakes the old priest had used, still feeling a bit dazed.

He had known since he was first released from the cave that the tribe's medical level wasn't bad.

At least, it didn't quite fit with this purely primitive tribe.

The more he learned from the priest, and the more he understood about the person who had single-handedly achieved a leap in medical progress on the Beast God Continent, the more Lin Qiu felt that the Beast God Continent was full of hidden talents and could not be underestimated.

Until this morning, when he saw the old priest use herbs to anesthetize the orcs, use crude obsidian flakes to cut open flesh, clean bone fragments, stitch, apply medicine, and bandage...

If he weren't still in a cave, Lin Qiu would have thought he was on a modern operating table.

The old priest had rested for a while; he propped himself up and took two steps. He couldn't walk further and said to the little wolf at the door, "Help me!"

The little wolf immediately came in, looked curiously at the sleeping orc, and then skillfully carried the old priest on his back.

"Priest, are they going to be okay?"

"Depends on their fate."

As the old and young left, Lin Qiu rubbed his sore arms, watching Lang Bing’s beautiful braids, which were always kept clean and neat, stained with blood.

He sat on the ground, no longer showing any signs of his former cleanliness obsession.

Lin Qiu: "Bing, do you know how to do this?"

Lang Bing: "Not really, I've only practiced on prey... but none of them survived."

The little wolf looked up, his clean face also splattered with blood, but there was no disgust in his eyes.

Lin Qiu: "In our environment, it's extremely difficult."

Lang Bing looked at him, sensing that he knew something.

Lin Qiu smiled: "Need a sterile environment, alcohol? Or antibiotics?"

Lang Bing: "Don't understand."

Lin Qiu: "I don't either. Since the old priest knows how, maybe he knows a little bit."

Lang Bing shook his head dejectedly. "I've seen the priest's inherited notes; they aren't complete."

Lin Qiu thought, and for some reason, his eyelids twitched; a doubt rose in his heart, and he said slowly, "Then there should be a complete set."

The little wolf: "Don't know."

That healer who benefited the Beast God Continent, since they could achieve this, must have considered the related circumstances.

Perhaps they were truly the Beast God descended, or perhaps they were in the same situation as him, in which case there must be a solution.

Even if there wasn't, just based on how smart their little wolf was, as long as he was given enough time, Lin Qiu believed they could figure it out.

Lin Qiu stood up, looked at the somewhat confused little wolf, and gently smoothed his beautiful long hair. "Let's go, let's go clean up; you're dirty."

Lang Bing carried the animal skin bag containing the obsidian flakes, holding onto the hem of Lin Qiu's clothes with one hand.

"Didn't the Beast God tell you?"

Lin Qiu laughed. "Maybe he did, but I was distracted and didn't learn it."

Fine, now all the orcs in the tribe thought he had met the Beast God.

The little wolf wrinkled his nose, glanced at him, and couldn't help but hum.

"How could you be distracted!"

It seemed he really wanted to know; his eyes even carried a hint of accusation.

Lin Qiu: "Wait a bit longer, let's see if I can dream of the Beast God again someday."

Alcohol could actually be made by hand, but there was nothing in the tribe. He could only pick up a few grapes for fermented wine, let alone grain brewing.

Right now, the priority was to solve the orcs' food and clothing needs.

When the tribe developed, perhaps one day, these things would be researched.

Perhaps it wouldn't be him, but this group of little wolves who loved to study.

*

The wolf orcs didn't return to the tribe until the next morning.

They were carrying things, so they walked slower.

At this time, Lin Qiu and Lang Bing hadn't slept all night.

Fortunately, orcs had strong recovery abilities, and with the herbs Lang Yan and the others brought over, the rescue was timely. Currently, only Yu Hua hadn't woken up; all the other orcs had pulled through.

Yu Hua’s body was still very hot.

He had been running a high fever since he arrived, and it had persisted until now; the situation wasn't very optimistic.

When Lang Yan returned, he looked around and couldn't find his partner. When he asked the orcs and finally found him, he saw Lin Qiu wiping the body of the lying Yu Hua.

Lang Yan stared fixedly at Yu Hua’s neck.

Lang Mo, who was nearby, jumped in fright and immediately snatched the cloth from Lin Qiu’s hand to wipe it himself.

Scared the life out of an orc!

The priest had spent so much energy saving him; he better not get his neck slashed by the King!

Lin Qiu seemed to sense something, turned around, and couldn't help but greet him with surprise.

"King? You're back."

He walked up to Lang Yan, feeling happy, only to see Lang Yan grab his hand and rub it twice with his thumb.

Lin Qiu opened his palm, puzzled: "It's not dirty."

Lang Yan: "Hmm."

He led Lin Qiu out, went to the corridor, and specifically fetched a basin of water.

Lin Qiu sat beside him, watching Lang Yan grab his hand and scrub each finger twice, not missing the gaps between them.

Lin Qiu slowly realized.

The King was jealous again.

Lin Qiu didn't mention it, leaning his shoulder against his, his posture relaxed like a lazy cat.

He asked about what happened in the valley.

That group of Black Feather orcs had been there for two days, but they were still drowsy and hadn't told them about what happened over there.

"Did our orcs get hurt?"

"No."

Lang Yan wasn't in a hurry to speak; he washed the bird-smell off Lin Qiu’s hands, dried them, and then led him into the large cave.

Sitting by the fire, Lin Qiu felt the cave was lively.

The returned orcs were already telling everyone about the valley.

"You don't know how dangerous it was! Yu Shan was lying on the ground, and Xue Xiao’s claws were aiming right for his neck! If I hadn't jumped down immediately and stomped Xue Xiao flat, Yu Shan would have been dead!"

"The Black Feather orcs could still fight even when crippled; they were originally beating the Snow Eagle orcs to the point where they wanted to retreat, but who knew the Snow Eagle orcs were so stubborn and wouldn't leave."

"Hey! They followed a bad tribe and got many orcs killed; they deserved to die."

The orcs were talking all at once, one after another, and Lin Qiu couldn't follow the story.

Lang Yan: "I'll tell Qiu."

Lin Qiu leaned against him; he had been working around the clock for the past two days taking care of those orcs and hadn't rested at all last night, so he was a bit tired.

Lang Yan asked: "Do you know about the Wilderness tribe?"

Lin Qiu: "Don't know."

Lang Yan spread out his partner’s hand, rubbing his thumb against it as he slowly began to speak:

"In the Central Continent, where prey was once countless, many tribes were born. Our Wolf tribe, Big Cat tribe, Black Panther tribe, and Feather tribe were all large tribes, while the Wilderness tribe at that time was just a medium-sized tribe living on the wilderness north of the Central Continent."

"They were composed of multi-racial orcs, including the Rabbit tribe, Sheep tribe, Deer tribe, and Fox tribe, and at that time, their tribal leader was from the Sheep tribe, which had the most orcs. But the only ones who could fight were the Fox tribe."

However, in the eyes of orcs like them, the Fox tribe was completely insignificant.

The Wilderness tribe had mixed orcs and weak strength, but their reproductive ability was strong.

The more orcs they had, the more territory they occupied on the northern wilderness of the Central Continent, eventually becoming the largest tribe on the northern wilderness.

Later, the Wilderness tribe migrated to the center of the Central Continent.

Later still, prey decreased, and several large tribes in the center of the Central Continent began to fight for territory, especially fiercely.

But after fighting back and forth, everyone eventually realized that although they had annexed more territory, there still wasn't enough to eat.

Gradually, everyone had the intention to migrate.

Before the Wolf tribe left, the large tribes of the Central Continent had long lost their former glory. Most of those large tribes had left, but the Wilderness tribe insisted on staying.

Once they left, regardless of strength or the number of orcs, the Wilderness tribe became the largest in the Central Continent.

Later on, it was that Great Priest who announced that he could treat any orc who came to him for help.

Orcs had long suffered from having no priest to treat their illnesses.

As orcs flocked there, the Great Priest appeared in the orcs' field of vision again, and his reputation resounded throughout the entire Beast God Continent.

Just then, Yun Du declared that the reason for the decrease in prey was that these orcs had angered the Beast God, and only tribes that offered sacrifices could survive.

The wolf orcs thought he was talking nonsense.

But small tribes rarely had priests; they revered the Beast God and feared the Beast God, so they listened to the Great Priest.

Thus, on the surface, they were offering sacrifices to the Beast God, but in reality, all the food they obtained was supplied to the Wilderness tribe.

At a time when other tribes were short of food and orcs were constantly starving to death, they kept their own orcs strong and healthy.

"With food, they attracted more orcs to join, and the Wilderness tribe grew further. The Snow Eagle orcs of the Northern Continent were so arrogant before, but they joined them for food just the same..."

The Snow Eagle orcs were among the most powerful orcs in the Northern Continent. They lived in extremely cold places, were cold-resistant, fierce, and fast, naturally becoming the enforcers of the Wilderness tribe.

Lin Qiu yawned, feeling that their King’s voice was very hypnotic.

Seeing this, Lang Yan ended the long background introduction, carried his partner into the grass nest, and covered him with animal skins.

"Do you want me to keep talking?"

Lin Qiu rubbed against his chest, his voice muffled: "You haven't gotten to the point yet."

Lang Yan’s hand under the animal skin held his partner’s waist, pulling him closer into his arms.

"The team of Snow Eagle orcs that came had thirty-three in total, and the leader was called Xue Xiao. Currently, it's unknown how many Snow Eagle orcs are left in the Wilderness tribe."

"The battle took place in the valley south of the Black Feather orcs. Because earlier in the Black Feather tribe, Yu Hua led the orcs to split from Yu Shan, they settled in the valley and discovered the Snow Eagle orcs first, which led to the notification to us..."

His partner was sleepy.

Lang Yan held Lin Qiu’s supple waist, his voice becoming even softer.

Lin Qiu relaxed, his eyelids heavy, and finally, unable to hold on any longer, he fell asleep leaning against him.

Lang Yan pressed his nose against his partner’s cheek and couldn't help but kiss him.

The orcs who had been running for two days were all tired; the excited chatter in the cave lasted for a while, followed immediately by the thunderous snoring of the orcs.

In the innermost grass nest, the cubs were jumping around wanting to play with Lin Qiu, but were caught by the ears by Lang Guo and chased away.

"The King and Qiu are both tired; wait until they wake up to play with them."

The cubs stood on tiptoes, looking over Lang Guo’s arm to confirm that both orcs had their eyes closed, before leaving unwillingly.

Outside Wolf Mountain, Lang Hong and Lang Yu, who were on cooking duty today, began to get busy.

The group of wolves who had just returned said that today they were going to eat the prey they brought back—they wanted lots of meat, they wanted fragrant roasted meat!

*

West of Wolf Mountain, the Black Feather tribe.

Yu Lie and his orcs arrived at the tribe half a day earlier than the wolf orcs, arriving at dawn.

The Black Feather orcs had been hiding in the mine cave at the foot of the mountain, waiting in agony for two days, finally waiting for their tribesmen to return.

Yu Lie circled in the sky and called out; the orcs in the mine cave crawled out, a dark mass, and hurriedly flew up the high mountain.

"Where are Yu Shan and the others?"

"Where is Yu Hua?"

"How come only you guys came back?"

Yu Lie said quickly: "They are being treated at the Wolf tribe and are fine now. Let the tribesmen move up first, and I'll tell you the rest slowly."

The remaining Black Feather orcs were anxious.

Landing in the cave, they saw that the returned orcs were all shivering, with snow piled on their feathers. Seeing this, everyone didn't dare to ask in a hurry and quickly got the fire started.

Yu Jiang went to boil the herbs he had previously given Yu Yi to drink.

After a flurry of activity, the orcs from below moved up one after another.

Everyone laid out their nests, sat down, and looked at Yu Lie, as well as the group of orcs sitting by the fire who had barely recovered after drinking the herbs.

Seeing the ones they wanted to see, the stone in some orcs' hearts fell.

But when they counted again, their hearts went cold.

"Twenty-nine of our orcs died." Yu Lie clenched his fists, lowering his head in grief.

This couldn't be hidden, and it shouldn't be hidden; eventually, the tribesmen had to be told.

Upon hearing this, the orcs felt dizzy.

Yu Qian hurriedly braced himself against the rock wall; his forced composure shattered, his heart twisted with pain, and he couldn't catch his breath, unable to even stand steady.

Yu Le looked carefully at his grandfather, who was sleeping and hadn't woken up.

"...That’s half the hunting team!" The orc looked panicked, staring at Yu Lie, hoping with trepidation that he was joking.

Yu Lie didn't dare to look into the orcs' eyes.

He sat cross-legged by the fire, the snow on his eyelashes melting, mixing with something, and the ground in front of him became soaked.

"The Snow Eagle orcs were too powerful; if Yu Hua hadn't led the orcs to fight them for a long time first, we might not have been able to come back. Of those twenty-plus orcs, only four were saved."

Of the eight seriously injured orcs at the Wolf tribe, four were orcs who had followed Yu Shan later.

"Then, then who else is alive?" The tribesman’s voice trembled, his eyes filled with despair.

Yu Lie moved his lips, not even daring to speak again.

But with the old patriarch there, they didn't dare to be too emotional.

Even crying had to be done outside, crying outside the cave.

Twenty-nine orcs!

Twenty-nine young and strong men!

When they followed Yu Hua, they left, and at least they were alive, but now they were suddenly gone!

Although they argued and fought, they were their companions and relatives who had grown up together and spent days and nights with them!

The orcs covered their mouths, biting their lips hard, sobbing in agony.

Clearly, the tribe was about to get better; why did it have to be like this!

Yu Le sat beside the old patriarch, his head lowered, his eyes dazed as he watched crystal-clear tears fall.

The old orc beside him wasn't peaceful even in his sleep, his brows deeply furrowed.

Yu Le wiped his tears quickly, but they wouldn't stop and continued to fall.

Yu Le was the weakest among the group of little orcs; since he was a cub, he had almost been protected by these uncle-generation orcs as he grew up.

His uncles often argued over a bite of food, but they would use food to coax him. They told him to grow up well and become a priest, so they could have him treat them later.

But they hadn't even seen him do that yet; how, how could they be gone...

Yu Le’s tear-blurred eyes saw his body, which had become even thinner since the snow season, bent deeply.

Woo...

What exactly should they do?

How could his grandfather get better, how could he become a good priest, and how would the tribe get better?

The Wilderness tribe was still there, the Snow Eagle orcs were dead, but other orcs would come; what exactly should they do...

山谷。
兽人们在山洞中勉强睡了一觉。
不是自己的地盘，睡得始终不安心。狼兽人们坐起来，困乏地打着哈欠，又歪歪扭扭压在同伴身上。
狼岩耳朵动了动，睁开眼，灰眸清醒。
他看向洞外，起身过去。
刚试着靠近的几个毛团直接炸成球，吓得发出“啾”的一声刺耳尖叫，险些晕过去。
狼岩低头，看着兽形还没他小腿高的白雀兽人。
“有事？”
雀十二白飞快摇头，噔噔噔往后退了十几步，翅膀压着扑通扑通的胸口，道：“没有，没有，我们就是过来看看。”
“诶？小白雀！”
狼兽人涌出来，蹲下来，视线还是比雪绒绒的白雀兽人高些。
面对一大群狼兽人，雀十二白狠狠咽了咽口水，又悄悄挪着爪子，往后退了退。
洞口的雪面上，留下一条细长的爪子印。
小白雀解释：“我们看到雪鹰兽人不在了。”
“哦，他们被黑羽兽人弄死了。还剩一个，关着呢，不知道死没死。”狼顺热心道。
雀十二白吓得吸了一口凉气，太凉了，惊得呛咳。
“黑羽兽人打雪鹰兽人，赢了？”豆豆眼睁大，爪子下抓握起一撮雪，仿佛难以置信。
羽猎插着缝隙出来，低头沉声道：“你们还敢小看我们？”
“嘿！”雀十二白瑟缩，“那不是，我们族长说的嘛。”
小白雀转手将自己族长卖了。
站洞口冷，狼岩不打算跟白雀兽人闲聊，他招呼兽人，吃过东西准备回程。
山洞里还有很多食物，都是羽哗他们存着过雪季的，也要带走。
十几个汤圆似的白雀兽人仰头看着狼岩进山洞。
雀十二白也看着，然后歪头，豆豆眼里打圈圈。
他是不是忘了什么？
后背被戳了戳。
同伴小声提醒：“二白叔……”
对哦！族长叫他们来问这个的！
雀十三忙问：“我们部落去狼部落报信的兽人怎么样了？他们还没回来。”
狼火：“冻伤了。”
十几个白雀再一惊，呛咳声不断。
狼火恶作剧得逞，龇牙笑道：“不过有我们祭司在，死不了。”
雀十二白实诚道：“谢谢。”
狼火看他往外跳了跳，“你们要走了？”
雀十二白：“冷，我们要赶紧回去。”不然像雀二白一样冻伤了就不好了。
他们没有祭司。
雀十二白失落，冲着洞口的兽人们怯怯地挥舞下翅膀，弧度极小，“我、我们走了。”
白雀兽人看着笨重，圆滚滚的，其实都是羽毛。
他们飞起来快，嗖的一下，像抛出去的雪球，一会儿就消失在山谷。
一群狼兽人目光注视着，忍不住磨了磨爪。
这小玩意儿看着，爪子痒痒。
跟狼毛球似的。
回程要带的东西多，羽猎做主，直接将羽哗山洞中的一半食物分给狼兽人。也不是他们这一趟过来的报酬，只是表达一下感激。
狼兽人毫不谦虚，果断拿了。
羽猎要带着兽人先回一趟部落报信，顺带把食物带回去。狼兽人与他们同行一段路，然后再分开。
狼兽人可惜命，照旧先把自己捆好兽皮，再背上食物。
狼岩跟羽猎走在后头。黑羽部落还有病患在狼山，羽猎到时候还得去一趟。
这事先跟狼岩说好，免得到时候直接闯进人家部落，失了规矩。递消息跟送病患的情况特殊，那就不多说了。
离开前，洞内所有存货被搜罗一空。
黑羽兽人一拍脑袋，“差点忘了，隔壁山洞还有个兽人。”
他们将堵住洞口的石头推开，露出里面满身血污的雪啸。
兽人昏迷，胸口微微起伏，还活着。
他们部落能狩猎的兽人本来就少，这一下损失大半。黑羽兽人对雪鹰兽人恨之入骨。
留下这一个，也不是想让他活，而是带回去让族人看看，让失去伴侣或者阿父的兽人们有个发泄途径。
再者，这么死了，太便宜他。
羽猎手捏得噼啪响，要不是强忍着，昨天都直接把他生撕了！
他进去，扯了山洞里翻出来的草绳将兽人绑好，确保他就算还有力气也不能反击。
随后他变作兽形，爪子抓住雪啸，冲着天空飞去。
狼兽人一心归家，跑得飞快。
行了半天，差不多该分道了，狼兽人往自家部落方向走。
羽猎爪子抓着被草绳绑起来的雪啸，冲着他们点头示意，也带着兽人往北。
寒风凛冽，如刀片一般割得身上生疼。
雪啸醒了。
他疲惫地睁开眼，只看到高空之下，仿若家乡所在的雪原，白茫茫一片。
离开北部大陆好像太久了，他都以为他忘了部落的样子。
原来还记得。
北大陆的猎物也不多了，他带着族人出来，是谋生，求一个活路。原野部落的食物是从其他部落吸的血，他们跟着好吃好喝，这么多年，也到头了。
族人没了。
雪啸平静地看着那一望无垠的雪，用尽最后的力气，反身挣脱开来。
砰的一声巨响——
还没走远的狼兽人全部停下回头。
天空飞行的黑羽兽人拍动的翅膀停滞，呆呆看着地面。
一团仿佛极致艳丽的血花，盛开在纯白雪原。
羽猎看了眼自己爪子，自家兽人做的草绳质量不好。
可并非草绳问题。
他慢慢拍着翅膀，往狼兽人的方向靠近，滑翔落地。
“刚刚什么情况……”
“雪啸自己挣脱，摔死了。”
“没抓稳？”狼兽人纳闷。
狼岩想着那个跟他对打应该能打个平手的兽人，面上平静道：“他应该是自愿的。”
兽人重部落、重族人，这一场战斗惨烈，只留他一个，他不愿意独活。
羽猎点头，看着有些沉默。
“他自己挣脱的。”
明知是死，主动向死。
他们虽然立场不同，但这一点上，他于他的族人，是个值得敬佩的兽人。
狼岩：“回吧。”
狼火其实觉得有点可惜，等黑羽族人飞走，他驮着猎物跑到狼岩身边，道：“王，你说要是雪鹰兽人当初投奔的是我们，我们是不是就不怕其他羽族？”
他也是看了雪鹰兽人打架的，要不是前期被黑羽兽人消耗了两次，能压着黑羽兽人打。
狼岩跃下山坡，积雪到了肚腹。
他不紧不慢道：“你觉得，我们一天吃一顿，饿得都啃虫子的情况下，他能投奔我们？”
狼火：“……”
好像也对。
失落只是一瞬间，狼火晃了晃身上的猎物。
“嘿嘿，咱回去找楸！没想到这次还能带食物回去，让楸给我们做好吃的。”
狼岩不回应，只默默加快速度。
*
狼山。
祭司、狼冰还有林楸从早上忙到中午。连狼雪都站不住，要坐下来帮忙了，兽人才全部治疗完毕。
林楸坐在角落，看着狼冰正在收拾老祭司用过的黑曜石薄片，还有些恍惚。
他从刚被放出山洞时就知道，部落的医术水平不差。
至少，跟这个纯原始的部落是有些不搭的。
跟祭司学的越多，了解到那个曾凭一己之力让兽神大陆医术实现跨越式提高的人后，林楸越发觉得兽神大陆藏龙卧虎，不可小觑。
直到这个上午，青烟看到老祭司用草药将兽人麻醉，用简陋的黑曜石薄片划开兽人的皮肉，清理碎骨，缝合、上药、包扎……
要不是还身处山洞中，林楸都要以为他上现代手术台了。
老祭司已经休息了一会儿了，他撑着腿起来，走了两步。走不动，对着门口小狼道：“扶我一把！”
小狼立马进来，好奇地看一眼睡着的兽人，再熟练将老祭司背起来。
“祭司，他们好了吗？”
“看命。”
一老一少离开，林楸捏着酸软的手臂，看着狼冰从来保持着干净整齐的漂亮辫子染了血污。
他坐在地上，哪里还有以前洁癖的样子。
林楸：“冰，你会吗？”
狼冰：“不怎么会，我只在猎物身上练过手……但是没有一头活下来。”
小狼抬头，干净的脸上也是血点子，他眼里却没嫌弃。
林楸：“咱们这个环境，是极难。”
狼冰看他，直觉他知道些什么。
林楸一笑：“需要无菌环境、酒精？或是抗生素？”
狼冰：“听不懂。”
林楸：“我也不懂。老祭司既然会，那他或许知道一点。”
狼冰失落摇头，“我看过祭司传承的手札，不全。”
林楸一想，不知怎么眼皮跳了跳，心中涌起一点怀疑，他慢慢道：“那应该有完整的。”
小狼：“不知道。”
那一位造福兽神大陆的医者，既然能做到这方面，相关的情况大概是有考虑的。
或许他真是兽神降世，又或者真的是如他一般的情况，那么必定有解法。
就算没有，就凭他们小狼这么聪明，只要给足他时间，林楸相信，他们也能做出来。
林楸起身，看着有些迷茫的小狼，轻轻理顺他的漂亮长发，“走吧，去收拾收拾，身上脏了。”
狼冰拎着装黑曜石片的兽皮袋，一手拽住林楸衣摆。
“兽神没有告诉你吗？”
林楸失笑，“或许告诉了，但我走神了，没学会。”
好了，现在部落所有兽人都认为他见过兽神了。
小狼皱了皱鼻子，瞥他一眼，又忍不住哼了声。
“你怎么走神呢！”
看来真想知道，眼神都带点控诉了。
林楸：“再等等吧，看我哪天做梦能不能再梦到兽神。”
酒精其实能手搓，但部落里什么都没有。他连发酵酒都只能捡点葡萄，更别提粮食酿造了。
眼前，是要先解决兽人温饱。
待到部落发展，或许有那么一天，这些东西也会研制出来的。
兴许靠的还不是他，而是这群喜欢钻研的小狼呢。
*
狼兽人们是第二天上午才回到部落的。
他们带着东西，走得慢一些。
此时，林楸跟狼冰一夜未眠。
庆幸的是，兽人恢复能力强，加上狼岩他们带了草药过去，救助及时。目前只有羽哗还没醒过来，其他的兽人都熬了过来。
羽哗身体依旧很烫。
从他来时就已经高烧，持续到现在，情况不怎么乐观。
狼岩回来，找了一圈没找到伴侣，问了兽人才找过来时，就看见林楸在给躺着的羽哗擦身体。
狼岩一下盯住羽哗脖子。
边上狼莫一个激灵，立马抢了林楸手上的帕子，自己来擦。
吓死个兽人！
祭司费尽精力救治的，可别被王一爪子割破脖子！
林楸似有所感，回头，忍不住惊喜迎上去。
“王？你们回来了。”
他走到狼岩面前，正高兴呢，就看狼岩抓着他的手，用指腹擦了两下。
林楸掌心摊开，有些疑惑：“不脏啊。”
狼岩：“嗯。”
他牵着林楸出去，到了廊下，专门打了一盆水过来。
林楸坐在他旁边，看狼岩抓着他手，一根一根手指都得搓两遍，指缝都没错过。
林楸慢慢反应过来。
王又醋了。
林楸不提，肩膀抵着他肩膀，懒猫一样姿态放松。
他问起山谷那边的事。
那群黑羽兽人来了两天，都还昏昏沉沉，没跟他们讲过那边的事。
“咱们兽人没有受伤吧？”
“没有。”
狼岩没急着说，将林楸手上的鸟臭味洗干净，擦干，然后带着他进大山洞里。
在火堆边坐下，林楸才觉山洞热闹。
回来的兽人已经跟大家讲起山谷那边的事了。
“你们不知道当时多凶险，羽山躺在地上，雪啸爪子冲着他脖子就去！要不是我立马跳了下去，一脚踩扁了雪啸，羽山都没命了！”
“黑羽兽人瘸了还能打，本来打得雪鹰兽人都想退了，但谁知道雪鹰兽人认死理，又不走了。”
“哎！跟了个坏部落，弄死了不少兽人，死了也是应该。”
兽人七嘴八舌，你一句我一句，林楸听得都不连贯。
狼岩：“我给楸讲。”
林楸往他身上一靠，这两天连轴转着照顾那些兽人，昨晚一晚没歇，他也有些累。
狼岩问：“知道原野部落吗？”
林楸：“不知道。”
狼岩摊开伴侣的手，指腹一边蹭着，缓缓道来：
“在曾经猎物数不胜数的中央大陆，孕育出许多部落。我们狼部落、大猫部落、黑豹部落、羽族部落都是大型部落，而当时的原野部落还只是居住在中央大陆以北的荒原上一支中型部落。”
“他们由多种族兽人构成，包括兔族，羊族、鹿族、狐族，而当时，他们的部落首领还是由兽人数量最多的羊族担当。但里头能打的，只有狐族。”
不过狐族在他们这些兽人眼里，完全不够看。
原野部落兽人混杂，实力弱小，但繁殖能力强。
兽人越多，他们在中央大陆北部原野上占据的领地也越来越大，最后更是成了北部荒原上最大的部落。
之后的原野部落，就迁徙到中央大陆中部。
再后来，猎物减少，中央大陆中部的几个大部落开始争夺领地，尤为激烈。
可斗来斗去，最后大家发现吞并的领地虽然多了，依旧不够吃。
渐渐的，大家有了迁徙的意向。
狼部落离开前，中央大陆的大部落早没了以前的辉煌。那些大部落走得差不多了，原野部落却坚持留下。
等他们一走，不论实力，还是论兽人数量，原野部落就成了中央大陆之最。
再后头，就是那大祭司放话，可以给任何求上门的兽人治病。
兽人苦没有祭司治病已久。
随着兽人涌去，大祭司再次出现在兽人们的视野中，名声更是响彻整个兽神大陆。
就在这时，云渡宣称，猎物减少的原因是他们这些兽人惹怒了兽神，只有供奉祭品的部落才能存活下来。
狼兽人当他放屁。
可小部落少有祭司，他们崇敬兽神，也畏惧兽神，便听了那大祭司的话。
如此，明面上是供奉兽神，实际得来的食物全部供养给了原野部落。
在其他部落食物紧缺、兽人不断饿死的关口，他们却把自家兽人养得身强体壮。
“有了食物，又吸引更多兽人投奔，原野部落进一步壮大。北部大陆的雪鹰兽人以前那么高傲，一样为了食物加入了他们……”
雪鹰兽人是北部大陆的兽人中武力数一数二的。他们生活在极寒之地，耐寒，凶猛，速度快，自然而然地成了原野部落的打手。
林楸打个哈欠，觉得他们王的声音好催眠。
狼岩见状，结束这长长的背景介绍，将伴侣抱进草窝，盖好兽皮。
“还要讲吗？”
林楸蹭了蹭他胸口，声音含糊：“你还没说到重点呢。”
狼岩兽皮底下的手握住伴侣的腰，将他往怀里搂了搂。
“来的一队雪鹰兽人一共三十三个，为首的叫雪啸。目前不知道原野部落还有多少雪鹰兽人。”
“战斗的地方在黑羽兽人南边的山谷。因为之前黑羽部落里，羽哗带领兽人跟羽山分家，他们落脚在山谷，先一步发现雪鹰兽人，才有了后头的通知我们的事……”
伴侣困了。
狼岩搂着林楸柔韧的腰身，声音更加轻缓。
林楸放松下来，眼皮发沉，最后实在撑不住，靠着他睡着了。
狼岩鼻尖贴着自家伴侣侧脸，没忍住亲了一下。
跑了两天的兽人都累了，山洞里兴奋的说话声持续了一段时间，紧接着就是兽人们震耳的呼噜声。
最里头的草窝里，幼崽蹦蹦跳跳要找林楸玩儿，叫狼果逮住耳朵，驱赶到一边儿去。
“王跟楸都累了，你们等他们醒了再找他们玩儿。”
幼崽隔着狼果手臂，踮脚看了看，确认两个兽人都闭着眼睛，才不情不愿地离开。
狼山外头，今日轮着做饭的狼虹跟狼雨开始忙活起来。
那群刚回来的狼说了，今天要吃他们带回来的猎物，要多多的肉，要香喷喷的烤肉！
*
狼山西边，黑羽部落。
羽猎带着兽人到部落的时间比狼兽人早了半天，早上天亮时到的。
黑羽兽人藏在山下矿洞，煎熬地等了两天，总算等到族人回来。
羽猎在天空盘旋，叫了一声，矿洞的兽人们钻出来，乌压压的，急急地飞上高山。
“羽山他们呢？”
“羽哗呢？”
“怎么就你们回来了？”
羽猎快速道：“他们在狼部落治疗，现在没事了。先叫族人搬上来吧，剩下的事我慢慢说。”
留守的黑羽兽人心急如焚。
落到山洞，才看到归来的兽人各个瑟瑟发抖，羽毛上堆了雪。大伙儿见状也不敢急着问，赶紧把火堆生起来。
羽江又重新抓了之前给羽逸喝的草药来煮。
一通忙碌，山下的兽人也陆陆续续搬上来。
大家铺好窝，坐定，都看着羽猎，还有那一群坐在火堆边喝了草药勉强缓过来的兽人。
见到想见的，部分兽人心中石头落地。
可再一数，心凉了半截。
“我们的兽人，死了二十九个。”羽猎握紧双拳，低头沉痛道。
这事儿瞒不住，也不能瞒，终究是要告诉族人的。
听到这话，兽人眼前阵阵发晕。
羽千连忙撑住岩壁，强制的镇定被打散，心中绞痛，一口气喘不上来，站都站不稳了。
羽乐小心看了眼他阿爷，昏睡着，没醒。
“……那可是半个狩猎队！”兽人目色仓惶，看着羽猎，忐忑地希望他说的是个玩笑话。
羽猎不敢看兽人们的眼睛。
他盘坐在火堆旁，眼睫上的雪消融，混着什么，跟前的地面洇湿一团。
“雪鹰兽人太厉害，要不是羽哗先带兽人跟他们打了很久，我们去了，都不一定能回来。他们那二十多个兽人，只救下来四个。”
狼部落那重伤的八个兽人，其中四个还是后头跟着羽山去的兽人。
“那、那还有哪些活着？”族人声音颤抖，眼神绝望。
羽猎动了动嘴皮，甚至不敢再开口。
偏偏老族长在，他们不敢太过激动。
连哭都得冲出去，在山洞外面哭。
二十九个兽人！
二十九个青壮年！
当初他们跟着羽哗走了就走了，至少还有命，可现在突然没了！
他们虽然也吵，也打架，那可是他们日夜相处，一同长大的同伴跟亲人啊！
兽人捂住嘴，死咬着唇，嘶声泣血。
明明部落都要变好了，为什么会这样！
羽乐坐在老族长身边，低着头，迷茫睁着双眼，看着晶莹的眼泪掉落。
边上老兽人睡着了也不安稳，眉头深深皱紧。
羽乐飞快擦了把眼泪，可止不住，又继续往下掉。
羽乐是一群小兽人中最弱的，从幼崽时起，他几乎就是被这些叔叔辈的兽人护着长大的。
阿叔们经常为了一口食物吵架，可会拿食物哄他。他们告诉他要好好长大，成为祭司，以后他们还得找他看病呢。
可这还没看呢，怎么、怎么就没了呢……
羽乐泪眼模糊，雪季以来更加单薄的身躯深深地弯了下去。
呜……
到底要怎么办。
阿爷怎么样才能好起来，他要怎么成为一个好祭司，部落要怎么样才会变好。
原野部落还在那里，雪鹰兽人死了，还有其他的兽人会来，到底要怎么办……

chapters.translated_text:
Lin Qiu hadn't slept well for several days, and with Lang Yan back, he finally relaxed and slept until evening.

He faintly heard some noise and, remembering the injured beastmen in the tribe, suddenly woke up and sat up.

Lang Yan was talking to Lang An, and seeing this, he immediately wrapped Lin Qiu in an animal skin.

"King, how is Yu Hua?"

Lang Yan's gaze turned cold instantly.

Lang An sighed, and seeing the dark circles still under Lin Qiu's eyes, went to pour him a cup of warm water.

"I was just talking to the King about this. Yu Hua is still burning up; the priest said if the fever doesn't break tonight, he might not make it..."

Lin Qiu threw off the animal skin blanket and prepared to get up, saying, "There are no beastmen wiping him down to lower his temperature..."

"We are wiping him, we are, don't worry." Fearing he would catch a cold after just waking up, Lang An quickly signaled Lang Yan to hold him down.

"Drink some water first," Lang An said.

Lin Qiu took the cup, realizing he was a bit thirsty. He drank it in one go and asked, "What about the medicine? Can he swallow it?"

"We fed him, but he's clenching his teeth and won't take it." It was frustrating; half a bowl of medicine would be wasted. The priest said many herbs couldn't be replaced now, so every bit used was a bit less left.

Lang An naturally didn't want this medicine to be used on his own tribe's beastmen later, but it was always good to have some in reserve.

Lin Qiu: "The priest is old and shouldn't be pushed too hard. What about the ice? Has he rested?"

Seeing Lang An shake his head, Lin Qiu pulled away Lang Yan's hand and hurriedly wrapped himself in an animal skin to go out.

Lang An caught the expression on their Wolf King's face, which looked as if he had a grudge against the beastman, and couldn't help but say, "King, that is a life, after all."

Lang Yan said indifferently, "Has Yu Lie come over? What did Yu Shan say?"

After Lin Qiu left, he also stood up and headed out.

Lang An followed behind, sighing for who knows how many times today, "Yu Lie is here, and he has a few beastmen guarding over there. As for Yu Shan... he is only begging the priest to try again."

As long as a beastman still has breath, no one is willing to give up.

Lang Yan: "I'll go take a look."

Walking quickly, Lang Yan suddenly stopped and said to Lang An, "Cook their meat soup as well."

"Understood," Lang An said in a low voice.

Their tribe had stored plenty of food for the snow season this year. Even though times were hard now, they could still spare a few mouthfuls.

From the corridor to the cave where the Black Feather beastmen were settled, the snow on the path had been trampled flat by the beastmen. Lang Yan followed behind Lin Qiu and soon ducked into the cave.

"Hmph!"

Lang An heard the sound from behind, turned his head, and saw Lang Chi staring in that direction with a dark expression.

Lang An: "I'm telling you, Chi, if you don't like the King's actions, then don't look. Hmphing all day long—you're at your age, don't hmph yourself into an illness."

Lang Chi: "If we have extra food, wouldn't it be better to share it with the branch tribes? Why raise a bunch of birds that have nothing to do with us?"

"Keep your voice down!" Lang An glared at him. This beastman kept his composure in front of the younger ones, but only those of his own age knew he had always had a foul temper.

Lang Chi: "Was I wrong?"

Lang An: "Pah, didn't you take so many cattails, pottery pots, and fishing nets earlier? Did you get those for free?"

Lang Chi choked, unable to retort in time.

Lang An rolled his eyes, not wanting to deal with this beastman who had been acting strange ever since he found out Qiu and the King had become mates.

He's got issues!

The King is such a good beastman—good-looking, strong, a great hunter, and considerate to his mate—yet he still doesn't like him.

Can't he see how good their relationship is? He just has to act like he's got worms crawling all over him, unhappy with everything!

If they really had a falling out, he'd only be the one getting angry.

Lang Chi was stifled, and knowing that an angry Ya-beastman was not to be trifled with, he gloomily turned back to his cave.

Lang An instructed the beastman in charge of the meat soup today to prepare a little more, then took a basin, scooped up some water, and carried it into the cave.

Some beastmen had been cleared out of the cave where the Black Feather beastmen were lying, including those who had woken up later, who were sent to other caves.

At this moment, only Yu Shan, Lang Bing, Lin Qiu, and the following Lang Yan were in the cave.

Yu Hua was still lying in the grass nest, covered with animal skins. Even on his dark skin, one could see he had burned to a deep red.

Most of his body was exposed, and Lang Bing kept dipping a spoon into wine to rub his palms and soles.

At this point, it didn't matter if the wine could be used or not. If his temperature didn't drop, he would be a fool even if he woke up.

Lin Qiu saw the little wolf working until his neck was strained, his eyes full of bloodshot veins, and said, "I'll do it, you go get some sleep first."

Lin Qiu reached for the spoon, but Lang Bing dodged.

"I'm fine, I don't want to leave."

"If you don't sleep, what will you do if you get sick too? Be obedient, go to sleep."

Lang Bing raised his head, "Qiu, I've grown up this big, and this is the first time I've seen the priest do this for a beastman. I want to watch."

Whether he can be saved or not, it's all experience.

In this regard, what he lacks is experience. He doesn't want the one lying here in the future to be a beastman from his own tribe while he is powerless to help.

The little wolf had a stubborn streak, his eyes full of persistence.

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan, hoping he would persuade him.

In this freezing weather, if he really keeps going like this, and if something happens...

Lang Yan: "Staying up for a few nights is no problem."

Lin Qiu gritted his teeth in secret and glared at him.

Lang Yan stared at Lin Qiu's hand and glanced at the lying beastman, his eyes cold and indifferent. He didn't even notice his mate's chilly gaze.

With the Wolf King's indulgence, Lang Bing continued to stay up with full confidence.

Lin Qiu told him to rest and that he would do it himself.

Lang Yan faintly bared his fangs. When Yu Shan came to talk to him, he quietly restrained himself.

"Yan, don't worry, we remember all the help you've given the Black Feather tribe. We will repay it."

Lang Yan: "What will you use to repay it?"

Yu Shan was not embarrassed; in the beastmen's understanding, this was only right.

When beastmen ask a priest from another tribe for medical treatment, they have to exchange things. Not to mention that the Wolf tribe's priest had treated so many of their beastmen—it was they who were taking advantage.

Thinking of his own tribe's current situation, with the wound throbbing with pain, Yu Shan said in a deep voice, "If you don't mind, our beastmen will continue to come to your tribe to help with work, no matter how long it takes. We will also try our best to gather twenty curved-horned beasts for you, though I'm afraid we can't give them all at once."

Curved-horned beasts were rare and hard to catch.

Based on the number of beastmen the Black Feather tribe could currently hunt with, this was equivalent to selling their tribe to the Wolf tribe.

The Black Feather tribe couldn't take this for granted just because the Wolf tribe didn't ask. If they did that, who would associate with their tribe in the future?

It would be bitter, but as long as the beastmen could survive, the tribe would get better after enduring this.

After this incident, Yu Shan solidified his determination to follow the Wolf tribe.

Of course, Yu Shan wasn't making decisions recklessly. He knew that having his beastmen work for the Wolf tribe wouldn't result in them being exploited to death, and furthermore, those in his tribe who couldn't hunt or gather could also be arranged for.

This incident was a huge blow to them; even if he hadn't gone back, he could imagine the despair of the beastmen after they learned of this.

If he didn't get them out to do something, he was afraid the beastmen would have problems.

Lang Yan glanced at the side from the corner of his eye.

Yu Shan thought he was dissatisfied and gritted his teeth, "Thirty, thirty curved-horned beasts."

Seeing Lin Qiu stop, Lang Yan looked at Yu Shan, his expression softening just a little.

"No need, just twenty."

"Alright!" Yu Shan said.

After this was settled, Yu Shan felt more at ease. Their beastmen were eating, drinking, and getting medical treatment in the Wolf tribe; if it were them, they would also be impatient.

"There is one more thing."

Before he could bring it up, Lang Yan said, "The two caves here are temporarily left for your use. Heal your wounds first; we don't know when the Wilderness tribe will send beastmen again."

Yu Shan smiled bitterly, "Yes."

Lang Yan watched Lin Qiu wipe his hands clean and asked casually, "How did you offend them?"

Yu Shan: "In previous years, we always went there to exchange salt. Just this year, we didn't go..."

Why they didn't go, both beastmen knew clearly in their hearts.

Without this previous incident, the two tribes would have had no connection at all.

"Just this?"

Yu Shan: "Just this."

Lang Yan: "Still as petty as ever. You should be careful; there will definitely be a second time."

Yu Shan looked at the unconscious Yu Hua, his eyes dim, "Okay."

He actually held a fluke, thinking the Central Continent was too far away, and wanted to gamble on that small possibility. But the Wolf tribe came from there, and if the Wolf King said so, it couldn't be fake.

Lang Yan looked at him and added, "If you want to migrate, you have to pay it back before you leave."

Yu Shan: "You can rest assured about that..."

Lang Yan glanced at his injured area, his gaze deep, and before Yu Shan could notice, he slowly withdrew it.

He had wanted to let the Black Feather beastmen practice with the Wolf beastmen, but given their current situation, it wasn't a good time to bring it up. He would wait and see.

The cave was filled with the fragrance of wine.

Lang Shan only had one last jar of wine left, and most of it was used on this beastman.

Soon, they were called to eat in the large cave.

Lang Yan and Lin Qiu left, taking the little wolf who refused to leave with them. Yu Lie took a few beastmen who could walk and went to line up, taking care of his own beastmen.

Yu Shan was still sitting in Yu Hua's cave. Seeing Yu Lie come in, he asked, "Does the old chief know about this?"

Yu Lie placed the bowl in front of him and said, "Don't worry, the chief doesn't know. He... hasn't woken up for days."

Yu Shan took the chopsticks with his only good hand and said after a long while, "Not waking up is also fine."

"Tell everyone to keep it a secret, and don't tell him either."

The old chief had been muddled recently, and he was already awake for only short periods. Let him be kept in the dark and go to meet the Beast God in peace.

"I've already told everyone."

Yu Shan nodded and said nothing more.

Yu Lie wasn't in a hurry to eat; he went out again and brought over Yu Hua's medicinal soup.

The beastman wouldn't take the medicine; his teeth were locked tight.

One beastman had to pry his mouth open while another poured it in. It looked pitiful. Yu Shan heard the commotion next to him, turned his head away, and stared blankly at the meat soup in his bowl.

Perhaps it was his fault; he shouldn't have had such a big argument with Yu Hua before the snow season.

If he wanted to be the chief, he could have let him be. At worst, he could have kept a closer eye on him. At least, at least...

Yu Shan put down his chopsticks and leaned against the grass nest, feeling weak all over.

The Wilderness tribe's beastmen would come again, and when that time came, they couldn't keep relying on the Wolf beastmen to step in...

"Hua!"

The beastman exclaimed, and Yu Shan looked up sharply to see clearly.

Yu Hua had spat out the medicine that had just been poured in.

Any movement tugged at Yu Shan's wounds, but he didn't change his expression. He forced his trembling hand down and said, "Pour it again, you must get it down him!"

Yu Lie lowered his head, told the beastman to wipe him clean, and walked out in a hurry.

Once out of the cave, he wiped his face hard.

Thinking of Xue Xiao, who had escaped from his claws, he wished he could piece him back together and chop him into pieces!

Walking to the corridor, the Wolf beastmen saw him coming over with an empty medicine bowl and were not surprised.

Lang An made some space and said, "We saved some for you, hurry and eat, or it will get cold."

Yu Lie nodded silently, went to the stove to pour the medicinal soup, and left again.

Lang An kept watching until he entered the cave entrance.

He said softly, "Are we really out of options?"

Lin Qiu was eating his meat soup and saw Lang Bing's head almost falling into his bowl, so he quickly reached out to support his chin.

Lang Yan frowned, "Finish eating and go to sleep."

Lang Bing's body stiffened, and his sleepiness flew away, "I..."

Lang Yan: "If you don't want to sleep, then eat properly."

Lang Bing didn't dare to speak anymore, forced himself to perk up, and ate the meat soup in his bowl mouthful by mouthful.

Lin Qiu then turned back and answered Lang An's previous question: "There's nothing else to do; everything that could be done has been done."

Lang An nodded, which was also within his expectations.

Lang Yu, who was beside them, said, "Then what are the plans for the Black Feather tribe? Are you taking him back?"

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan, "King?"

Lang Yan: "No plans."

The Black Feather tribe wouldn't give up easily, and if the beastman died in the Wolf tribe, it didn't matter.

When a beastman dies, in the eyes of the beastmen, they are just going to meet the Beast God. Digging a hole to bury the body is fine, as long as it isn't dug up and eaten by wild beasts, anything goes.

In the corridor, the stove fire flickered in the cold wind.

After eating, the beastmen hurriedly washed up with the warm water in the large cave and then rolled into their grass nests.

If they couldn't sleep, they would chat with the beastmen in the nearby nests, or otherwise mess around.

West of Lang Shan, the Rabbit beastmen also hurriedly hopped into their cave, shook off the snow on their bodies, and sat by the fire to warm up.

Compared to the rowdiness of the Wolf beastmen, the Rabbit beastmen were much quieter.

Tu Kui was a bit sleepy.

He held his cub, touched its soft fur, and nestled in the nest with a relaxed posture. His gaze fell vaguely on the orange-red flames, feeling drowsy.

"Chief," Tu Ai squeezed over and squatted into a grass nest, "Are those Black Feather beastmen not leaving?"

As soon as he asked, the beastmen in the nests along the stone wall all pricked up their long ears.

The Rabbit tribe had a slight sense of comparison toward the Black Feather beastmen who had worked for the Wolf tribe before.

They were now an affiliated tribe of the Wolf tribe and were afraid that if the Black Feather beastmen figured things out and joined the Wolf tribe, they would have no use.

There was also competition between affiliated tribes.

Tu Kui was the tribe chief and was more sensitive than the beastmen; he felt that the current Wolf tribe placed particular importance on planting.

As long as they had this skill, they were useful, so he wasn't panicked.

Even if they took out all their seeds and taught the Wolf tribe, given the character of the Wolf beastmen, the result for the Rabbit tribe wouldn't be bad.

Of course, he wasn't stupid. They could only hand over all their seeds when both sides completely trusted each other and merged into one.

Tu Kui wasn't sure if that time would ever come.

In the cave, the Rabbit beastmen huddled in twos and threes in a grass nest, leaning against each other for warmth.

Everyone spoke in low voices, their stomachs full, and the cave was warm; they had already habitually relaxed and fallen into a deep sleep while smelling the scent of firewood.

And in the cave where Yu Hua was, the light leaking through the gaps in the grass curtain remained bright.

Yu Lie was guarding here, and both Lang Bing and Lin Qiu were there.

Lin Qiu and Lang Bing understood medicine, so the two beastmen took turns guarding. By midnight, Yu Hua started talking nonsense, and when Lin Qiu touched him, he was burning hot.

Lang Bing immediately ran over, and the two beastmen cooperated to start wiping him down again.

Yu Lie crowded around, anxious and spinning in circles. Lin Qiu said, "Go heat up the medicinal soup and keep feeding it to him."

Yu Lie panicked, "Okay, okay! I'm going."

The commotion woke up the next room, and Yu Shan was helped over by a beastman.

He stood at the cave entrance, listening to the intermittent sounds from Yu Hua's mouth, and was shocked to the spot.

"It wasn't me..."

"It wasn't, Shan, it wasn't... I didn't... Why don't you believe me! I didn't push him! It wasn't, it wasn't..."

The old injury on his leg suddenly throbbed with heart-piercing pain!

The old injury on Yu Shan's leg was the pain in his heart.

Before the injury, he was the tribe's designated next chief; after the injury, he was decadent for a long time and didn't ask about tribe affairs.

Only when he accepted that his leg was crippled and came out did he faintly hear rumors in the tribe that his leg was caused by Yu Hua.

But this injury was clearly his own carelessness.

He had just thought those words were something the clansmen said casually, but now, listening to Yu Hua's words, could it be that the chief also suspected him?

Yu Shan understood everything in an instant.

No wonder, after he came out, Yu Hua went from his previous small antics to becoming unreasonable, opposing him everywhere. Before, they could barely have a proper conversation, but after that, it was all barbs and insults, faintly carrying hatred.

Yu Shan was in so much pain he couldn't stand, and watching the beastman who was struggling so much that even Yu Lie couldn't hold him down, he felt unbearable grief.

Lin Qiu rubbed his elbow, which had been knocked against the wall by the beastman, and looked at Yu Shan: "Be prepared, he is like this..."

Lin Qiu didn't say the rest, but everyone understood.

Yu Shan seemed to have aged a lot all of a sudden, hunching his back, still slowly moving forward.

He looked at the beastman who was trapped in that incident like a trapped animal, his heart twisting with pain, and he almost knelt by Yu Hua's grass nest.

He had grown up in the same nest as Yu Hua; they ate together and slept together.

He treated him like his own biological younger brother.

At that time, Yushan thought there was no other orc whose relationship with him was better than the one he shared with Yuhua.

Until they left the nest, the two of them caught the clan chief's eye and were taken by his side to be taught.

At first, both of them were outstanding.

Because Yuhua had a slightly better physique and performed better than him during combat training, Yuhua even received praise from the clan chief.

Back then, the little cub naively said that he would train hard to protect the tribe and protect him in the future.

But later, as they grew older, the clan chief told him that Yuhua's temperament was too rash and too competitive, and letting him manage the tribe might lead to a major disaster in the future. Yushan could only work even harder, hoping to protect him in return.

The clan chief was strict. As he grew older, the tasks on his shoulders became heavier. There were fewer and fewer times when the two brothers could sit down and have a proper talk.

During training, the clan chief always liked to compare them, always saying that he was steady and attentive, while saying that Yuhua was deeply envious, narrow-minded, and incapable of managing the tribe.

Hearing this too often, Yuhua gradually became unconvinced and, out of competitiveness, dragged him along to compete. When he couldn't win, he would secretly train more by himself; when he won, he still refused to relax.

As the years and months piled up, their relationship changed from brothers who told each other everything into competitors, and eventually to adversaries.

At this moment, upon hearing Lin Qiu's words, resentment toward the clan chief welled up in him as well.

Why did he always use harsh words to hurt people? Why did he never trust him? Why did he always compare the two of them together? Why... did he himself follow the clan chief's words in his thinking!

Couldn't he have been a bit more firm, given in to him a little, cared more about his thoughts, and sat down to have a proper chat with him? Couldn't he have made the clan chief say a little less...

This brother of his was someone he watched grow up side by side!

How could it—how could it have come to this point...

Yushan lay prone beside Yuhua, weeping bitterly.

The orc in the grass nest was similarly struggling in a deep, muddy swamp, tears hanging at the corners of his eyes, repeatedly saying, "It wasn't me, why won't you believe me."

Looking at this sight, Lin Qiu was at his wit's end.

Lang Bing stood beside him, tensed like a drawn bowstring.

"Qiu..." Lang Bing felt somewhat uneasy.

Lin Qiu stroked the little wolf's head, his gaze falling on Yuhua's face.

He must have suffered a lot of grievances during his growth as well...

Lin Qiu sighed silently, "Let's go outside."

Lang Bing looked at him, "Shouldn't we try a bit harder?"

Lin Qiu: "The Black Feather orcs are here, look."

Several more orcs had entered. While pinning Yuhua down, they were learning to cool him down just like they had done earlier.

Yulie had even brought back medicine; it needed to be given to him to drink.

But the orc seemed to have lost all will to live...

Lin Qiu ultimately left with the little wolf.

Lang An, who had been lingering at the door, also put down his basin and left.

Perhaps Yushan needed an environment with only Black Feather orcs. He wondered if they would be able to talk things through.

...

"Hua!"

In the middle of the night, the cave of the Black Feather tribe was pitch black. Outside the grass curtain, the fierce wind wailed as the old clan chief, who had been lying down for many days, suddenly woke up.

"Grandpa!" Yule, who was guarding him, grabbed the old orc's hand in pleasant surprise. Before he could even speak, his eyes turned red first.

"Clan chief! The clan chief has woken up! Quick, bring some meat soup!" Qian hurriedly scrambled up, and before he could make arrangements, he heard the old clan chief ask again: "Where is Yuhua?"

"Where is Hua?"

Qian's heart tightened. Trying his utmost to hide his emotions, he said, "Clan chief, didn't Hua leave with the orcs? But don't worry, they should be back. He was just throwing a momentary tantrum..."

"Hua!"

"I want to see Hua!"

Yule was close by, and he sensed that his grandpa was very different right now.

He was full of energy, his grip on Yule's hand was very strong, and he was even able to stand up by himself.

Qian's heart skipped a beat. Wanting to say something more, he met the clan chief's all-seeing eyes, closed his eyes, and said, "Alright, I'll have the orcs take you to see him."

It was snowing again.

The wind blew fiercely, and along the road to the Wolf tribe, the orcs had a very hard time.

Yet the old clan chief lay on an orc's back, constantly murmuring Hua's name—from a voice full of vitality to one that grew smaller and smaller, weaker and weaker...

Yule closely followed alongside, his teeth chattering from the cold, never daring to stop.

"Grandpa, Grandpa... don't sleep!" he said with a crying tone.

The Black Feather orc carrying the old clan chief sped up, struggling to fly forward.

By the time they reached Wolf Mountain, they were utterly exhausted and crashed headfirst into the snow.

The Wolf Mountain orcs heard the commotion and rushed out, only to see a group of Black Feather orcs frantically helping an orc and digging another orc out of the snow.

Lang Yan saw clearly who it was and pointed the way for them, "The cave with the lit fire."

The Black Feather orcs immediately carried the old clan chief inside.

Lang Yan looked up at the sky; the snowflakes were huge. He reached out, and pure white snow fell into his palm, gradually dissolving.

That group of Black Feather orcs surrounded that cave, standing there until they were numb.

Lang Yan didn't leave, and more and more wolf orcs also came out, standing far away in the corridor, watching quietly.

Over on the rabbit orcs' side, a few orcs gradually poked their heads out.

Everyone seemed to have anticipated something.

After a long time—or perhaps it hadn't been long—the snow reflected the clear sky, and the sunlight came out...

"Grandpa—"

With a heaven-shattering cry of grief, the old clan chief of the Black Feather tribe, Yupuo, concluded his long and arduous life.

...

Day broke, and the wind seemed to have stopped as well.

On the back mountain of the Wolf tribe, there was an extra mound of earth—it belonged to the old Black Feather clan chief.

When an orc died, their soul returned to the Beast God, and their body returned to the land that nurtured them.

The death of a tribe's chief was always deeply sorrowful. Fortunately, Yuhua, who had looked like he was perishing and was the meritorious hero who protected the tribe, miraculously survived through the night.

Although he hadn't woken up yet, the old shaman said he was out of danger.

The wolf orcs didn't know what had happened in that cave full of Black Feather orcs, nor did they plan to ask around.

But to them, the fact that Yuhua could still survive after having his legs severed by the shaman was already something that brought joy to the orcs.

This time escorting the old clan chief over had mobilized almost all the orcs of the Black Feather tribe.

Everyone had anticipated the old clan chief's passing.

With so many orcs, it was impossible to eat and drink for free at the Wolf tribe. The Black Feather orcs were just planning to take their companion back to recover from his injuries when they were grabbed and cursed at for half a day by the old shaman!

The orc he had managed to save with great difficulty by spending a massive amount of herbs was already physically weak right now. If he caught a cold on the road and started running a fever like Yuhua, wouldn't all his effort go to waste?!

The old shaman detested orcs who didn't respect the fruits of his labor the most!

The Black Feather orcs were scolded so badly they didn't dare step out of the cave, while the idle wolf orcs bared their big white teeth and watched the spectacle with schadenfreude.

The final result: the injured stayed behind, two orcs to take care of the injured stayed behind, Yule also stayed behind, and the rest—including those who had previously caught a cold—could roll back where they came from!

Of course, this didn't include Que Erbai and the others, who had faintly lowered their presence and were living a wonderful life in the Wolf tribe.

Although he was somewhat afraid of the wolf orcs, didn't the tribe have quite a few weak little rabbit orcs? He had companions!

He wasn't afraid!

For the sake of a bite to eat, he wasn't afraid at all!

Considering that he had truly risked his life to deliver the message, the wolf orcs turned a blind eye and let him muddle along in the Wolf tribe for the time being.

*

The weather was clear with hardly any clouds.

The trees on the back mountain of Wolf Mountain were covered in rime, like a world formed of ice crystals.

The front of the mountain was bustling, but the back mountain only had the sound of snow piles occasionally falling from the trees.

Yule stood before the newly turned earth, his eyes vacant, a lone orc lost in a daze.

After the old clan chief passed away, he cried for a long time, until his eye sockets were red, swollen, and stinging, and his throat was hoarse and unable to speak. Yet there would never again be a pair of aged hands gently stroking his head and telling him Grandpa was there.

He thoroughly understood that crying was useless.

Crying couldn't make Grandpa's illness heal, couldn't make him stay, nor could it make him become the tribe's shaman to treat Uncle Yuhua's illness...

Yule stood on the mountain for a while. He knew he couldn't stay outside for long; his constitution was weak, and getting sick would just be a burden.

Yuhua blinked his stinging eyes, silently whispered "Grandpa," and then sluggishly walked down the mountain.

Upon reaching the foot of the mountain, he saw Lang Bing.

His hair had been re-braided, and neat, pretty white hair braids rested on one side of his shoulders. Seeing him come down, Lang Bing hesitated for a moment before walking up to meet him.

The little wolf had never spoken soft words in front of his peers, but this weak little orc was always bursting into tears over nothing, leaving them not even daring to speak harshly to him.

At first, they all disliked him and didn't want to take him along, but they had no choice-they had to listen to Qiu's words.

After hanging out together for a long time later on, they also knew he didn't do it on purpose; he just had shallow tear ducts and would shed tears at the slightest emotional wave.

Lang Bing had spent half a day at the foot of the mountain thinking of words to comfort someone, but he still didn't know how. Seeing him come down now, he could only awkwardly blurt out, "Let's go back, it's time for breakfast."

Yule didn't move. With trembling lips, seeing the little wolf's worried gaze, he couldn't help but bump into him.

Lang Bing instinctively moved to defend himself, but realizing who it was, he immediately relaxed his strength and was instead bumped back two steps by Yule.

His arms stiffened. Although he often hooked shoulders and linked backs with the little wolves, none of them had ever dared to drill into his arms like this.

While feeling at a loss, he heard Yule say in a hoarse voice, "I don't have a grandpa anymore."

Lang Bing paused, and his hand fell onto Yule's back.

"He went to see the Beast God. When you see the Beast God in the future, you'll definitely be able to see him again..." After saying this, Lang Bing bared his teeth—what kind of nonsense was he saying!

Yule wept bitterly, his voice cracking.

For the last time, he allowed himself to be this weak for the very last time!

From now on, he would never cry again.

When the call for dinner finally rang out before Wolf Mountain, Lang Bing glanced at his damp shoulder and walked along with Yule with a wooden expression.

Near the Black Cave at the back mountain—the place where orcs used to be locked up—the little wolves heard the commotion and quickly poked their heads out.

Yule just blankly followed behind Lang Bing. When Lang Bing stopped, Yule bumped right into him.

Lang Bing had anticipated it and didn't move this time. Looking at Lang Jin in front of him, he asked, "What are you guys here for?"

Lang Jin: "You can come, why can't we?"

The little wolves stealthily observed Yule, terrified that he might do something foolish. Yule raised his head, looking at them with eyes as red as ripe fruit.

Lang Jin averted his gaze. The thought of those tear-filled eyes made his hair stand on end, and he hurriedly said, "Hurry up, hurry up, it's time to eat."

Yule pressed his dry, peeling lips together and lowered his head, "Thank you."

He knew everyone had come to accompany him.

Wolf ears were sharp; everyone heard those barely audible words.

The little wolves scratched their heads, feeling awkward. When were they ever this sensitive? It was just that seeing Lang Bing heading over, they had quietly followed along.

"Aigoo! Hurry up, hurry up, or it'll all be grabbed!"

There was no such thing as food being grabbed; the Wolf tribe always made meat soup according to the number of orcs, so the little wolves were just making conversation. Warmth welled up in the bottom of Yule's heart, and his nose felt sour.

Fearing that he would cry again—he was already freezing outside until his head hurt, let alone Yule—Lang Bing urged,

"Hurry and walk!"

The little wolves immediately swished forward. After taking two steps, they couldn't help but stealthily look back again.

Lang Bing rolled his eyes and led Yule to the front.

For once, the little wolves didn't go to snatch food from the adult orcs. Lagging behind, they openly watched.

He should be fine, right? Look, he wasn't crying, was he?

Cry he didn't, but not long after finishing the meat soup, Yule threw up. At that time, there were hardly any Black Feather orcs left in the tribe, and seeing this, they immediately reacted like they were triggered, stumbling and running to find the old shaman.

Upon looking, the old shaman declared that he had caught a cold and, compounded with emotional shock, had fallen ill.

The wolf orcs all knew Yule's physical constitution and temperament; with the old clan chief gone, this matter was simply insoluble.

The old shaman handed over some calming herbs and told him to get a good sleep. Given his current condition, sleeping was far better than being awake.

The Wolf tribe had witnessed the entire affair concerning the Black Feather tribe—it was just a helpless struggle to survive, and nobody could be blamed.

After this commotion lasted for several days, the Wolf tribe smelled of medicinal soup every day. The orcs choked on it from time to time, and their bodies were permeated with the scent of medicine.

Yet this time, not a single orc complained. Everyone behaved themselves obediently, finishing their meals and rolling straight back into their nests.

After the Black Feather orcs left, only a few injured orcs and the ones taking care of them remained in the tribe.

Wolf Mountain remained gloomy for two days before gradually returning to its usual state.

The wolf orcs still had a bit too much surplus energy. Trapped within a single side of the cave, they ate their fill and slept; sleeping too much left them with exceptionally high spirits.

At first they could still tease the cubs to pass the time, but later the cubs got annoyed by them and avoided them altogether.

The wolf orcs began pondering games to play, simply making a few large fur balls and kicking them back and forth in the cave all day long.

The air inside the cave was foul, and the veins on Lang Yan's forehead were throbbing violently.

However, he couldn't drive the orcs out to gather mushrooms this time. Feeling pent-up for a long time as well, Lang Yan simply seized an opportunity, pinned the orcs down, and started a brawl.

At that time, Lin Qiu was still with the old shaman in the Black Feather orcs' cave changing bandages for the orcs. Yuhua hadn't woken up yet, but the shaman said it looked like he would wake up in the next couple of days.

Just as he was wrapping gauze around an orc, a cub ran out in a flurry, taking advantage of the fact that everyone wasn't paying attention.

"A fight broke out! Qiu, the King is fighting with them!"

Lin Qiu wasn't paying attention for a split second and applied force with his hands.

"Ugh!" The orc's wound was tightened, his facial features scrunched up tightly, but he didn't dare utter a sound.

Why did the wolf orcs start a fight?

Did they quarrel because of their affairs?!

Lin Qiu hurriedly apologized, handed the bandaging task over to Lang Bing, grabbed a cub, and sprinted toward the cave. As he ran, he couldn't help but fiercely jab the cub on the forehead.

"Who told you guys to come out!"

The cub played dumb, "Hehe..."

Lin Qiu: "Who's 'hehe' with you? Go back and have Lang Guo discipline you lot!"

"Awoo..."

Burning with anxiety, Lin Qiu ran to the cave, put the cub down, and lifted the curtain to take a look—

Wolf fur was drifting like willow catkins, the grass nests were overturned, and the wolf orcs were engaged in a melee from the cave entrance all the way to the very back, leaving the ground in absolute disarray.

Lang Guo stood at the corner, shielding the cubs behind him, coldly watching this group of orcs beating each other up!

He had found them an eyesore for a long time!

Lin Qiu had never seen wolf orcs in a free-for-all brawl before. The giant wolves used their claws and teeth to suppress one another, charging and crashing around with such immense force that he could only hear loud thuds. Low, resonant wolf howls threatened each other, and they were fighting tooth and nail.

Lin Qiu didn't dare go in at all. He pulled the cub back and stayed put.

Seeing him arrive, Lang An slowly walked over, leaning against the stone wall. Passing two orcs locked in a grapple, he couldn't resist delivering an extra kick.

He placated Lin Qiu, saying, "It's fine. They're just too full and need to vent."

Lin Qiu noticed one particular black wolf who was especially eye-catching.

His fur was glossy, fluffy, and imposing. While the other orcs attacked in a group, he alone managed to suppress them unilaterally. His claws made the giant wolves' heads buzz, and the other orcs couldn't even touch his tail.

Lang Yan shook the wolf fur off his claws and coldly glanced over.

Confirming there had been no provocation, Lin Qiu breathed a sigh of relief.

"How long is this fight going to last?"

Lang An: "It's going to be a while."

It was rare for the King to make a move, and the orcs were itching for a beating. After fighting their companions, they couldn't help but go provoke Lang Yan. Until they got beaten until they howled, they wouldn't settle down.

"Atishoo!"

There was too much wolf fur flying around, and Lin Qiu didn't want to get mixed up in it.

He still had work to do.

Handing this group of escaped cubs over to Lang An, he hurriedly rushed back to help at the other cave.

Seeing Lin Qiu leave, Lang Yan withdrew his gaze, kicked away the orc pinning him down, and with a fierce expression, launched even heavier blows.

The commotion inside the cave lasted all morning. In the end, the wolf orcs were chased and beaten by Lang Yan until they howled; even when they didn't want to fight anymore, they were pinned down and beaten further.

Finally, battered, bruised, and twitching in pain on the ground, Lang Yan shook his fur, looked at the chaotic mess of the large cave, and ordered the orcs to clean it up.

"If it's not cleaned up before I get back, you can all roll outside to sleep tonight."

The giant wolves tucked their tails and whimpered.

It hurt!

But their whole bodies felt refreshed!

They definitely wouldn't dare provoke Lang Yan again anytime soon.

The demi-orcs had also chipped in. While Lang Yan ordered the orcs to tidy up the cave, they silently took the cubs over to the rabbit orcs' side.

Lang Yu had a bruised, dark-blue corner of his mouth. Seeing the wolf cubs playing in a pile with the rabbit cubs, and meeting the rabbit orcs' worried gazes, he wanted to smile but it hurt so much he bared his teeth instead. Waving his hand, he said, "It's nothing, everyone was just playing around."

The rabbit orcs shivered.

It was fortunate they hadn't played like that with them, otherwise they wouldn't have been able to withstand even a single claw from a wolf orc.
