Half an hour ago.

A tuft of down was plucked from Lang Sheng’s clothes by Lang Jin. After failing to catch and bite Lang Jin, he was called over by Lang Guo and had no choice but to lead the group of cubs back to the grass nest.

As soon as Lang Guo left, Lang Sheng scrambled up, looking at the spot where Lang Jin had just pulled out the down.

The little gray wolf sat in the very center, with Lang Yuan on his left, Lang Pang on his right, and two rows of companions surrounding him.

The grass nest was large enough for the dozen or so cubs to sit comfortably.

Everyone looked curiously at Lang Sheng’s clothes, using their little chubby paw pads to press on the spots where the tips of the feathers were poking out.

"Sheng, it’s coming out again."

Xiao Pang hooked at it with his claw, pulling a thread from the linen fabric, and immediately retracted his paw.

Lang Sheng looked around and saw white specks on all the cubs' clothes, exclaiming, "You have them too!"

The cubs lowered their heads one after another, pressing their paw pads against the protruding down. Not only could they not push it back in, but it also made their paws itch.

"If you pull it out, it’ll be gone."

I don't know which cub said it, but as soon as everyone heard this, their ears twitched happily, and they immediately used their claws to hook at their clothes.

But it wasn't convenient to do it themselves, so Xiao Pang suggested, "Sheng! We’ll do yours first."

Lang Sheng nodded and lay down in the grass nest.

"Come on."

The cubs immediately crowded over, surrounding him in a circle. As they hooked away with their claws, they discovered that more and more tips of down were poking out.

Lang Sheng’s nose itched, and he sneezed. Turning his head to look, he saw his clothes were covered in pulled threads.

He immediately said, "Stop, stop it."

He got up too quickly, and the cubs didn't have time to retract their claws. With a loud rip, the linen was completely torn open by the cubs.

Most of the down was exposed, feathers flying everywhere, and the cubs froze.

Lang Sheng was both shocked and angry; he pouted and lunged at the cubs.

"Give me back my clothes!"

"I didn't do it on purpose!"

The cubs didn't dare to yell loudly and attract Lang Guo. With Lang Sheng’s lunge, all the down flew up into the air.

"Wow—"

Lang Yuan stretched out his little wolf paw, watching the down drift onto his paw pad. He blew on it, and the down flew high up again.

The cubs’ playfulness was ignited. Seeing them fighting, they stuck their butts in the air, eager to join in.

After getting his paw stepped on, a cub excitedly joined the melee.

The chubby down-filled clothes instantly went flat, down flew everywhere, and the cubs ended up in a chaotic brawl, biting whoever they could catch!

In the middle of the scuffle, Lang Sheng suddenly transformed into his human form.

He squeezed out from under the cubs’ bellies. Seeing him like this, everyone immediately sat down, tucked their paws in tight, and placed them obediently in front of them.

Before anyone could speak, they saw Lang Sheng pick up a tooth from the grass nest.

His eyes were filled with tears, on the verge of crying, glaring at everyone as if looking for the culprit.

The cubs were as quiet as chickens, nervously rubbing their paws.

When Lin Qiu and Lang Guo walked in, this was the scene they saw.

"Who did this!" Lang Guo scooped up Lang Sheng and hurriedly wrapped him in animal hide.

Seeing the blood all over his mouth, Lin Qiu was frightened and quickly pulled Lang Guo, "Take him to the priest first."

"Waaaaah!!!"

One started crying, and they all started crying.

Lin Qiu’s ears were stinging, and he didn't know how to comfort them. Lang Yan came over upon hearing the noise, and the cubs flocked to him like they had found a pillar of support, squeezing against him.

"King! A-Sheng’s tooth fell out!"

"King, it wasn't me."

"Awoooo... it’s all my fault, I was picking the fluff off him, and my claws tore his clothes!"

"King, will A-Sheng not be able to eat meat anymore..." The cub cried as if the sky had collapsed.

Lin Qiu picked up Lang Yuan, who was pursing his little mouth, on the verge of tears. The other cubs rubbed their heads against Lang Yan’s legs, smearing tears all over him.

Lang Yan didn't mind; he sat down and beckoned with his hand.

The cubs immediately crowded over, leaning on him dependently.

Lang Yan: "Who wants to tell me, from start to finish, what happened?"

Lin Qiu held Lang Yuan, watching the four cubs on the other side sit up with wide eyes, and hurriedly sat down, petting each of their heads in turn.

In the line of cubs, Lang Xiao Pang stood up and stumbled through his words: "We were playing, Lang Jin was pulling the fluff on A-Sheng’s clothes, we came back, there was still fluff on A-Sheng’s clothes... we helped pull it, it tore, and then we started fighting..."

In the corner of the cave, the cubs’ voices were childish.

The Wolf King listened quietly, with the other cubs nestled beside him. Feeling secure, their emotions calmed down.

Lin Qiu put Lang Yuan down as well. Lang Yuan leaned over obediently, sticking to his companions, and placed his paw pads on their King as well.

Lin Qiu left quietly to find Lang Guo.

The tooth the cub lost was a canine, the sharpest one.

When Lin Qiu arrived, the blood on Lang Sheng’s face had been cleaned off, and he was sitting obediently in front of the priest, opening his mouth wide for him to see.

The priest touched his other teeth; they weren't loose.

"Every little wolf changes teeth at different times, but it’s usually before they change into human form. You’ve already changed once, this tooth might not grow back..."

"Wuu—"

The old priest knocked him on the forehead and said sternly, "Quiet."

Lang Sheng licked the hole where the tooth was missing, unable to help himself, tears streaming down.

"Without sharp teeth, how will I hunt in the future..."

Wolf beastmen’s greatest weapons were their claws and sharp teeth. Now that he was missing one, he couldn't even bite through a prey’s throat... Lang Sheng thought about it and felt his life was hopeless.

"I was the most powerful cub, now I’m not..."

He was truly heartbroken. Lin Qiu felt bad seeing this, glanced at the little tooth in his hand, and took it.

"The priest didn't say it definitely wouldn't grow back, what if it does?"

Lang Guo patted his forehead like he was patting a melon, "The priest must have a way."

The old priest: "It just depends on whether it grows back on its own."

Lang Sheng lowered his head. He was the most powerful little wolf among the cubs; when he grew up, he would definitely be a captain of the hunting team like Uncle Huo.

But now, he had lost a tooth.

There was no hunting team captain who didn't have a full set of teeth.

Lang Yan: "Wolf beastmen don't just use their mouths to hunt."

Lin Qiu planned to clean the little wolf’s tooth, drill a hole in it, and have him wear it around his neck as a form of mental comfort.

Hearing Lang Yan speak, he turned back to see a dozen cubs following obediently behind him.

Lang Yan sat down, and the cubs approached one by one to apologize to Lang Sheng.

Lang Sheng was still listless.

Lang Yan: "We are beastmen; hunting relies on strength, but also on brains. If you just bite every prey you catch, you might be able to bite, but we can't."

"But they can all bite, and in the future, I’ll be the only one who can't..."

The adult beastmen also heard about the situation and walked over, each taking a cub away.

Lang Jin was among them, saying disdainfully, "You don't even find the prey dirty. That fur hasn't been washed clean in a lifetime, rolled in mud, rolled in feces—if you can bring yourself to bite..."

Lang Jin’s words immediately scared the cubs.

Lang Sheng said in horror, "No! I won't bite anymore!"

Lin Qiu smiled and silently went to find Lang Qi.

The little wolf’s tooth was small, and drilling a hole was delicate work; it was best to find Lang Qi.

Lang Qi was still in the cave where he did his woodworking; the large stone mill wasn't finished yet, so Lang Qi had his hands full.

The Lang Mu team was also called over to help; no matter how cold it was, they had to work while keeping the fire going.

Lin Qiu found some hemp grass to twist into thin ropes nearby. Lang Qi looked at the little tooth and said, "I was wondering what the cub was crying about; so it’s just a lost tooth."

"Does it affect hunting?" Lin Qiu asked.

Lang Mu said: "A little. We all rely on claws and teeth, but usually a small team hunts together, so as long as there are beastmen with good teeth, it’s fine."

Lin Qiu immediately remembered what Lang Jin had just said.

He frowned, "How about we make some tools?"

He hadn't thought about it before, but now that he thought about their King catching prey with his mouth and then kissing him when he returned... Lin Qiu’s brow furrowed so tightly a mosquito could be crushed.

"What kind of tools?" Lang Qi became interested.

Lin Qiu: "You drill the hole first, I’ll draw them out."

Lin Qiu had also watched the beastmen hunt many times; they usually hunted in small teams, relying on their claws and their own weight to suppress the prey, then breaking the throat.

Sometimes beastmen would grab a wooden stick or a stone to smash the prey, but it was rare.

"White Sparrow beastmen use bows and arrows; we could actually make those," Lin Qiu said in a low voice.

Lang Mu: "Those are feather thorns; they hurt a lot when they pierce the body."

Lang Qi: "Those are made from the thorns of a beast in their territory; that kind of beast is rare now."

Lang Mu nodded, "We can't make them either."

Lin Qiu: "Let’s try other methods."

Bows and arrows, spears, slings, bolas... they were all simple and easy-to-make hunting tools.

It wasn't difficult for wolf beastmen to hunt; the difficulty was not being able to find prey, which was why Lin Qiu hadn't thought in this direction before.

He handed the hemp thread to Lang Mu to twist and found a charcoal pencil to draw.

The beastmen had seen the White Sparrow beastmen’s bows and arrows. After generations of effort, the White Sparrow tribe’s bow and arrow craftsmanship had reached the top level of the Beast God Continent.

Since Que Erbai was in their tribe, he could see if he could ask him to provide some advice.

If there was no animal fur suitable for arrowheads, then stone could be used as a substitute; it would work just as well.

Spears were used for throwing; a long piece of wood with a sharp tip was simple and convenient.

Slings and bolas weren't much different. A sling was made of animal hide woven into a strip with a pouch at the end, which could hold a stone to strike prey.

Stones thrown through a sling had more force and caused more damage than throwing them directly.

Bolas had pouches on both ends of the animal hide strip, each holding a stone ball, which could be used to strike or trip the prey, making it easier to capture.

There were various tools, and Lin Qiu drew and labeled them all.

Which one was suitable would only be known after the beastmen practiced.

As soon as Lin Qiu finished drawing, Lang Qi took them.

The beastmen took one look, and without even asking Lin Qiu, they already had an idea in their minds.

Lin Qiu: A veteran craftsman.

The tools were left for Lang Qi to study slowly. But no matter how many tools there were, if the number of prey didn't increase, feeding the tribe would still be difficult.

Thinking of this, Lin Qiu felt the urgency of expanding the scale of animal husbandry even more.

He temporarily pushed this thought aside, strung the drilled little wolf tooth with a thread, tied a knot, and added a few beautiful round beads.

Returning to the large cave, the cubs were still unhappy.

Although the wolf beastmen favored the cubs in everything they ate and used, they didn't know how to coax children.

The Beast God Continent was very realistic; cubs of any tribe understood that survival was difficult. Wolf cubs also practiced hunting from a young age and understood that losing a canine meant losing a bit of aggressiveness.

This was a big blow to Lang Sheng.

The adult beastmen had all dispersed, and only Lang Sheng was sitting facing the stone wall, his head pressed against it, silent.

Lang Yan sat nearby, and the other cubs squatted beside Lang Yan, all looking at Lang Sheng with longing eyes.

The cubs didn't feel good either, huddled together and not daring to speak.

If they hadn't fought, A-Sheng’s tooth definitely wouldn't have fallen out...

Lin Qiu walked over and squatted beside Lang Yan.

"Haven't coaxed him yet?"

Lang Yan moved a grass cushion over and placed it beside him.

Lin Qiu didn't sit, but placed the necklace in Lang Yan’s hand.

The cubs’ eyes widened, and they stretched out their paws to touch it.

"Pretty..."

"Qiu, we want one too."

Lin Qiu smiled: "There are no more teeth."

The cubs licked their teeth with the tips of their tongues and shook their heads, reluctant. They looked at Lang Sheng again, pouted, and wondered why they felt a little envious...

Lang Yan glanced at the wolf cub lying face to the wall and said slowly, "There’s only one string. If Lang Sheng doesn't want it..."

A gray shadow flashed before their eyes, and Lang Yan’s hand was empty.

Seeing Lang Sheng lying with his back to them again, fiddling with the newly made necklace, his tail wagged slightly.

It seemed he had been coaxed a little.

The little wolf looked back silently, and Lin Qiu lowered his head, pretending not to see.

After a long while, Lang Sheng gathered his courage and walked up to Lin Qiu, looking up and handing him the necklace.

"I, I want to wear it."

Lin Qiu took it, looked at the cub’s arched head, and put it on him.

The little wolf tooth hung on the gray fur, with three symmetrical pine-green beads on each side—simple, but beautiful.

"Thank you, Qiu." Lang Sheng fiddled with it with his paw, sat down, and moved forward a bit.

He rested his chin on Lin Qiu’s leg, looking at Lin Qiu’s gentle expression. He still couldn't help it; his mouth pouted, and he turned his head and bumped into Lang Yan’s arms.

"King! I lost my tooth, I can’t be a little captain of the hunting team anymore..." The little wolf’s paws pressed against Lang Yan’s arm, still with quite a bit of strength.

Lang Yan: "Being a captain isn't about teeth."

"Then what is it about?"

"It’s about who is better at fighting."

"But I’m missing a tooth..."

"It’s also about brains."

Lang Sheng finally sniffled, looked up, and looked seriously at their King: "My head is big, my brain must be good."

Lin Qiu pursed his lips, holding back a laugh, and turned his head away.

Lang Yan touched the little wolf’s ears, "It is quite big."

"Heh—"

With snot bubbles hanging from his nose, the little wolf was finally better.

Lin Qiu watched their King quietly. He was handsome, but his temperament was cold; who knew he was a beastman who could coax cubs and had so much patience.

The matter of the cub losing his tooth passed for now, and Lang Sheng could jump around with his companions again, and even had the mood to show off his unique little necklace.

Lin Qiu watched, and as soon as he sat down, his hand was grabbed by Lang Yan.

Lin Qiu hooked his fingers and said with a smile: "King, I asked Uncle Qi to try making some hunting tools; shall we try them out later?"

Lang Yan checked his fingers, and seeing there were no injuries, said: "Okay."

*

The forest was lonely and quiet, with deep snow.

The branch tribe’s wolf beastmen directly cut a small path in the snow. The path was deeply embedded in the snow, with high snow walls on both sides.

The leading wolf was wrapped in two layers of animal hide, his mouth, nose, and ears all covered, revealing only a pair of eyes. The other wolf beastmen followed closely in his footsteps; no beastman spoke, only the soft sound of paw pads stepping on the snow.

The Green Eye tribe was very good at hiding their nests; they had wings and rarely left traces on the ground.

In the past, the Wolf tribe hadn't failed to look for their lair, but the dense forest made it impossible to find.

Now that the snow covered everything, it was all white, and the places where the Green Eye beastmen were active were easier to find than at other times.

The line of wolf beastmen walked toward the heart of the Green Eye tribe.

Not only did they not patrol their territory during the snow season, but the Green Eye beastmen didn't either.

Their treehouses were built magnificently and exquisitely; being in the trees made them targets. Plus, with that green plumage, it was hard not to notice them.

When the wolf beastmen found the Green Eye beastmen’s treehouses, they didn't delay at all, and after confirming there were no ambushes, they directly surrounded them.

Green Moon was Green Jiao’s partner; they had been together for less than two years, and this year’s rainy season had just hatched two cubs.

Not all cubs could grow up; Green Moon knew this because he had just lost the smaller one.

The cub was still lying in his nest, quiet, with no rise or fall in his chest. Green Moon’s body trembled slightly, his lips pale, and he cut his own wrist, trying to send blood into the cub’s mouth.

His cub was just calling for hunger, why wasn't he eating now?

"Dad, Dad..." The other cub woke up smelling the blood. Green Moon hurriedly hid his hand behind his back and picked him up with the other.

The cub was very thin; Green Moon held him, and he was as light as a withered leaf, and he could feel rows of bones.

The number of Green Eye beastman cubs was among the best in the southern tribes; they could give birth, which was why they could fight for so much territory and have more food.

But the cubs born were just there to suffer.

Green Moon lowered his head, tears dripping onto the cub’s feathers.

"Dad, I’m hungry..." The cub, who had just changed his downy feathers and whose new feathers hadn't fully grown, said weakly, "When will Father come back?"

Green Moon’s throat rolled, and he forced back a sob, stroking the cub’s back to comfort him: "Soon, your Father will be back soon."

The cub couldn't hear the sound of his nest-mate brother, and his neck turned weakly, wanting to find him.

"Dad, is brother asleep again?"

Green Moon’s hand shook, his voice strained: "...Yes, he’s asleep."

"Dad, I’m so sleepy too."

Green Moon hugged the cub tightly, almost begging: "Don't sleep, A-Kong, be good, don't sleep..."

Green Moon was about to collapse; he carefully hid the dead cub into his belly so the older one wouldn't see.

The cub was weakly crying of hunger. His hand trembled, and looking at the cub who couldn't even hold up his neck, he reached out to cover his eyes and took out the hand he had hidden behind his back.

"Drink some water, drink it and have a sleep, and Father will be back."

...

The door of the treehouse was kicked open violently, and Lang Xing’s claws went straight for Green Moon’s neck. But when he saw the scene before him, his whole body shook.

Green Moon was dizzy with hunger, his reaction slow.

The moment he saw the wolf beastman, he was stunned, and the faint hope in his eyes was completely extinguished. He lifted his neck, closed his eyes, and tears streamed down his cheeks.

Failed.

They had endured one snow season after another; since he had consciousness, he had lived a life of hunger. His cubs were the same, never having eaten their fill for a single day.

He was truly, fed up.

Lang Xing looked at his bleeding wrist and the cub who was drinking blood in small sips, and within a few breaths, he hid the pity in his eyes.

This was the upper treehouse; the beastmen below had already been captured.

Lang Xing: "What are you doing?"

Green Moon bit his lips, his arms hugging the cub tightly. He looked stubbornly at the wolf tribe member who was also a sub-beastman, and said: "You saw it."

Lang Xing took out a rope and tied him up.

Green Moon bit his lips until they bled, and said in despair: "You might as well kill me."

Lang Xing said coldly: "Kill you? And then what? Help you raise the cub?"

Green Moon completely collapsed, "You might as well kill me! Kill me!"

Lang Xing just thought he was starved crazy, and grabbed the beastman with one hand, leaving the grass nest.

When he heard something slide into the grass nest, he looked down and saw it was a cub that had already died.

Lang Xing’s body stiffened, and he looked away, unable to bear it.

He looked at the sub-beastman who was almost strangling the other cub in his arms, forcibly held his hand, and peeled the cub away.

"Kill me!"

"I told you to kill me!" Green Moon cried out in collapse, his voice like weeping blood.

The cub lying in his palm was drawn by his father’s crying and moved twice. But having been strangled too tightly just now, he fainted and couldn't wake up.

Lang Xing tucked the cub into the animal hide on his chest and carried Green Moon for two steps.

But as a sub-beastman with cubs himself, he thought of the lonely, forever-sleeping cub in the grass nest, and couldn't take another step.

"The one left, you..."

There was a weight on Lang Xing’s shoulder, and he realized Green Moon had fainted.

Lang Xing also had cubs, and he couldn't bear this...

In the end, he sighed, turned back, and wrapped the deceased cub in animal hide. He then carried Green Moon down, dug a hole under the big tree, and put the cub in.

His companions came down one after another; they had already searched the entire place where the Green Eye beastmen lived.

Seeing Lang Xing digging a hole, they paused, and one after another took out similar small things wrapped in animal hide or dry grass from their bosoms. Some were big, some were small; the largest was as big as the pottery jar they drank water from—it was a cub that had already been able to transform into human form.

"Xing, dig the hole bigger."

Small animal hides were placed before his eyes one after another, and Lang Xing even smelled a stench.

His jaw tightened, and he lowered his head, digging a new hole next to it. Seeing this, the other wolf beastmen simply dug with him.

The Green Eye beastmen had all been brought down from the treehouses; most of them were sub-beastmen with cubs and female beastmen.

There were almost no old beastmen.

There were very few male beastmen, and when they broke in, they just sat in the treehouses without moving.

The wolf beastmen grabbed them, only to see under the animal hides that the beastmen either had broken legs or injured stomachs. The wounds had already festered, and a foul smell permeated the air.

This trip was not at all as triumphant as imagined, but rather stifling.

Now they had sub-beastmen, cubs, and injured male beastmen in their hands, all of whom were so hungry they couldn't stand, and even after being caught, they looked like they had no desire to live.

Even Lang Cang felt it was tricky.

"Cang, this... what should we do?" The beastman dug a paw full of mud while helping Lang Xing fill the hole, feeling extremely at a loss.

He could be sure that they were indeed looking for trouble for themselves.

If there were prey in this little place of the Green Eye tribe, would they need to run to the Wolf tribe to rob? If they hadn't come, these beastmen would have died if they died...

Oh my!

The beastman scratched his head in anxiety; he shouldn't have come if he had known!

All the Green Eye beastmen were here; it was cold outside, and their treehouses weren't necessarily warm. At this moment, they all had numb expressions, sitting on the ground wrapped in animal hides, looking half-dead.

Lang Cang closed his eyes, thinking that if Lang Chi came back, he would probably scold him.

But now that it was done, could they go back empty-handed?

This...

Hey!

Troublesome! Truly a troublesome matter!

This was the first time the wolf beastmen had robbed territory and encountered this; even Lang Cang couldn't keep his cool.

The pit was filled, and Lang Xing went to rub his paws in the snow, stood up, and looked at this group of sub-beastmen and cubs.

In this situation, the Green Eye tribe still had so many sub-beastmen and could still give birth; that was a kind of ability.

He said: "Take them back. We can't raise them, it just depends on whether their own partners are willing to raise them."

They came to occupy the territory; even if there was little prey in the territory, having one was a profit.

Lang Cang: "Take them away."

It was already done, was there any room for regret?

The wolf beastmen thought they would have to fight a battle here, but it was effortless. Everyone was blowing in the cold wind, shrinking their paws, and still had to carry this group of beastmen who were too hungry to walk back.

Only they could be debt collectors to this extent.

Claw Mountain.

The remaining wolf beastmen estimated the time and made hot fish soup, waiting for the beastmen to return.

Lang Wan looked around on the mountain for a while, and saw the beastmen returning in a long line in the white snow.

He hurriedly went down the mountain, and when he saw the beastmen carried on the backs of the wolf beastmen, he froze in place.

Lang Cang looked at him gloomily, bypassed him, and threw the beastman on his back directly into the wooden house.

Other beastmen followed suit, finding an empty wooden house to throw the beastmen into.

Lang Wan said: "Did you go to occupy territory, or to rob sub-beastmen?"

Although occupying territory and robbing sub-beastmen often went together, the Wolf tribe hadn't robbed other tribes before, nor had they done this kind of immoral thing.

"What are you talking about!" Lang Cang said angrily, "What occupying territory, there wasn't a single beastman who resisted."

"Oh, so it turned into saving beastmen?"

Lang Wan had a headache just thinking about it; dozens of male beastmen already had no food, why bring more sub-beastmen and cubs? Were they doing charity?

Lang Cang had nothing to say.

He shook his paws irritably and went back to the cave gloomily.

The sub-beastmen were locked into the wooden houses, and Green Moon happened to be locked in with Green Jiao.

He woke up, opened his eyes, and looked for the cub first. The moment he saw Green Jiao holding the cub, he crawled over crying and collapsed silently in Green Jiao’s arms.

Green Jiao only saw this one cub and knew the situation.

He endured the severe pain in his chest, hugged his partner with difficulty, and placed the cub between them to keep warm.

"I’m sorry."

Green Moon grabbed him, trembling constantly.

Green Jiao saw the dried blood on his wrist, felt a pain in his heart, and hugged his partner tighter.

It was their incompetence that made their partners and cubs suffer.

"I’m sorry..."

Lang Wan listened to the crying coming from each wooden house, irritably rolled up a snowball, and threw it at the distant lake.

The Wolf tribe wouldn't give them food!
