"Everyone isn't used to them yet; they always miss their aim, and sometimes they even accidentally hurt their companions."

"Tell them to go to the fields and practice on the squeak-beasts."

Lang You was stunned for a moment, then nodded.

It was a good idea; the orcs could see at night anyway.

"After that, tell them to take turns guarding the fields, five orcs to a group. Don't stop until the squeak-beasts are fewer and their aim is accurate."

"Understood."

Lang You took a long stride and immediately went to make the arrangements.

Lang Yu stirred the wild vegetable soup and couldn't help but laugh: "The King always has so many ideas."

"Practicing archery at night..." Lin Qiu hesitated.

Lang Yan: "Don't worry, they won't go blind."

Lin Qiu laughed, his shoulders shaking. It was like Lang Yan was a roundworm in his stomach; how did he know what he was thinking?

Lang Yan watched him and suddenly pinched his cheek.

Lin Qiu: ?

Lang Yan calmly withdrew his hand and said nothing.

After dinner, the cubs and the orcs with bows and arrows ran to the fields.

A crescent moon hung in the sky, its light clear and bright. Looking at it, Lin Qiu always felt as if he were still in his original world.

But looking closely, the moon was different. It was larger, brighter, and when it was full, the moon at the edge of the sky felt within reach.

Lin Qiu was lost in thought when his face suddenly felt warm.

"Let's go back to the cave."

Lin Qiu narrowed his eyes and held the hand pressed against his cheek. "Are you going out tomorrow, King?"

"I'll go take a look. Does Qiu want to go too?"

Lin Qiu shook his head. "In a few days. Wolf Mountain is too busy right now."

It was time to sleep.

Accompanied by the sparse chirping of insects, Lin Qiu curled up beside his mate and slept soundly through the night.

The next day, just as it was getting light, Lang Yan got up, and Lin Qiu sat up with him.

"It's still early." Lang Yan brushed the hair from Lin Qiu's forehead and said gently.

Lin Qiu looked at the gap above the wooden door; a sliver of rosy light was already visible, like the tail of a ribbon.

"I'm not sleeping anymore."

After descending the mountain, most of the orcs in the large cave were awake and sitting in the corridor eating breakfast.

Seeing Lin Qiu come down at this hour, the orcs looked surprised. Lang Mo even waved at him and said, "Qiu, are you going out with the King and the others too?"

"Not for now."

"Then why are you down so early?"

"Early to bed and early to rise makes a person healthy."

"Going to bed early is boring, and getting up early is because you're hungry; how is that healthy?" Lang Mo curled his lip and tilted his head back to gulp down a large mouthful of soup.

His jaw tightened, and with a *crunch*, he chewed up the bone.

Lin Qiu smelled that the soup didn't smell right. "Was there leftover prey from last night?"

"No."

Lang An held up a ladle, intending to serve soup to the orcs. "Squeak-beast meat soup. The orcs caught them; there were so many."

Lin Qiu immediately took a step back, staring fixedly at the pottery pot.

Lang Yan placed his palm on Lin Qiu's back and said, "There's other food. If you don't like it, don't eat it."

Lang An smiled gently, his slightly curly hair swaying. He said, "I knew you wouldn't eat it."

Never mind the squeak-beasts; even delicious prey like long-worms, Qiu didn't like.

Lin Qiu: "I'll just gnaw on some dried fish."

Lin Qiu ladled out some soup that only had wild vegetables in it, took a piece of dried fish, and sat in the corner.

Lang Mo and Lang Xi shifted their positions to share a table with Lin Qiu.

"Did you catch a lot of squeak-beasts last night?" Lin Qiu asked.

Lang Mo: "A lot, half a basket."

"Half a basket!" Lin Qiu thought to himself that cleaning them one by one would take a lot of time.

"Who told them to steal our seeds?" Lang You said that because of catching squeak-beasts, the orcs' archery accuracy had improved.

Lin Qiu took a bite of the fresh wild vegetables and nodded slightly.

If it was this effective, then there was no need to worry about the squeak-beasts in the fields.

*

After breakfast, most of the orcs went out to hunt and forage.

Lin Qiu watched a group of giant wolves mixed with a few small rabbit-orcs leave. The procession was massive, and the ground vibrated faintly as they ran.

After the orcs left, he first went to check on the ewe-beast cub born yesterday. Seeing that it was fine, he went to the fields to check on the cages he had set yesterday.

The cages were crudely made, but they were strong enough, wrapped in two or three layers of vines.

Lin Qiu checked a few; the mechanisms weren't set up quite right, the fish paste inside was gone, and no squeak-beasts had been caught.

"Qiu, we've already cleared the cages." Tu Kui also came over with a stone sickle, ready to continue weeding.

"Did you catch many?"

"Six, but many of the cages were bitten to pieces."

Lin Qiu now knew that setting cages wasn't very effective.

"Don't worry, the orcs caught quite a few last night."

Lin Qiu nodded.

Tu Kui came to the fields diligently; almost as soon as weeds sprouted, they were pulled. With the Black Feather orcs helping, Lin Qiu didn't stay in the fields to work.

He went to the shed where the bird droppings were kept, pushed aside the hay covering them, and turned them over slightly with a wooden stick; they were still steaming inside.

There were many fields this year, and this little bit of fertilizer was far from enough.

Lang Huo and the others had gone to the Great Marsh to haul bird droppings; he didn't know when they would be back.

Just as he was busy, Lang Mo found him.

The orcs were generally tall with long legs; it seemed like he reached him in just a few steps.

"Qiu! Where should the houses be built?"

The orcs in Lang Mo's squad were busy making bricks, their faces covered in dirt, like they were wrapped in a shell of mud.

"Didn't the King say?"

"The King went hunting and told us to ask you and the priest."

"What did the priest say?"

"The priest said he doesn't care about this."

Lin Qiu: "..."

"I'll discuss it with the King tonight. But we definitely need to build quite a few houses, so make as many bricks and tiles as possible."

"We know. You guys hurry up and discuss it then."

After Lang Mo finished speaking, he wandered around the fields twice more before running back to work.

Lin Qiu left the fields, washed his hands by the stream, and returned to the cave to think about how to build these houses.

Judging by the Wolf Tribe's current development, they likely wouldn't be moving again.

If houses were built, one for each household, with nearly three hundred orcs including wolf-orcs and rabbit-orcs, it would be like a large village.

First, they needed a sufficiently large open space.

The east was now large fields, with no room for houses. The terrain in the west rose slowly, and there were brick kilns and pottery kilns there, along with many loose stones, so it wasn't a good location.

The best location was right in front of the mountain—backed by the mountain, facing the river, with flat terrain. But during the rainy season, the river would rise, and being too close to the bank would definitely lead to flooding, unless the river embankment was raised.

Then they would have to push it a bit further north.

Houses could be built sporadically in front of the mountain, but to form a settlement, the area north of Wolf Mountain was the most suitable.

However, this involved the future when there would be hundreds of houses; they had to see what the King and the priest thought first. Simply building a canteen and a few houses for orcs with mates could actually be done in front of Wolf Mountain.

Lin Qiu looked at the drawings he had made on the ground with an unburnt stick, leaving them for now to show Lang Yan when he returned.

In the evening, the orcs returned.

Lin Qiu immediately pulled Lang Yan into the cave.

Lang Yan looked at his mate, his gaze deep and seemingly shimmering with light. Lin Qiu didn't notice.

Once inside the cave, Lang Yan had just wrapped his arms around Lin Qiu's waist when he was tapped on the arm, signaling him to look at the ground.

Lang Yan: "About building the houses?"

"Yes." Lin Qiu was puzzled. "What else would you be thinking about?"

Lang Yan lowered his head to bump Lin Qiu's forehead, then rested his chin on his shoulder, lazily saying, "Nothing."

"Then should I tell you what I'm thinking?"

"Hmm."

Both orcs sat on low stools. Lin Qiu leaned forward, pointing at the ground with a stick. Lang Yan's chest pressed against Lin Qiu's back, his chin resting on his shoulder, listening quietly.

Lin Qiu finished in one breath and asked, "What do you think is suitable?"

Lang Yan: "In front of Wolf Mountain."

"But it will flood during the rainy season."

"The wind is very strong during the snow season. Even if the houses are built behind the mountain and the *kang* is warm, the roofs can be blown off by the strong wind; it's neither safe nor warm. Besides, this is a large grassland, which is perfect for grazing the ewe-beasts later."

"As for the flooding, we can raise the foundation like the corridor, or we can just raise the river embankment."

When the tribe first stayed here, they chose this area in front of Wolf Mountain because it was sheltered from the wind, close to the river for water, and the terrain was flat—the open space in front of the mountain was enough for the orcs to frolic.

"Raising the river embankment is very troublesome."

Lin Qiu was still worried and turned to look at him.

They were very close; when Lang Yan lowered his head slightly, their noses touched.

"Don't worry. At Lang Mo and the others' current speed, they can't build that many houses all at once. The river won't rise this high every year, and even if we have to move later, we'll have time."

"Alright then, in front of the mountain it is."

"Hmm." Lang Yan kissed the tip of Lin Qiu's nose.

The location was chosen: right in front of Wolf Mountain.

The packed-earth area in front of the mountain would remain as the orcs' activity plaza. A little to the west, they would build small houses for orc mates. In the east, they would renovate the canteen where the stove was, trying not to dismantle the stove itself.

Lang Yan only went out with the orcs for two or three days before staying back at Wolf Mountain to keep watch.

Lang Mo came over from time to time to discuss the houses, and it was half a month later when the first brick came out of the kiln.

The temperature gradually rose, and the heavy beast-skin coats were no longer needed.

The orcs also began to shed their fur.

Wolf fur drifted everywhere on Wolf Mountain; it could be seen on grass leaves, and in the corners of corridors and stone walls, there were balls of wolf fur mixed with dust.

This time, without Lin Qiu having to ask, the orcs combed the fur off themselves and saved it.

The cubs had just finished combing their fur and were running wild in front of Wolf Mountain.

The cubs were well-fed, their fur sleek and shiny, looking extra fluffy and soft when they ran.

As they ran, they saw Lang Huo's squad pulling a cart and jumped directly onto it.

"Get down," Lang Huo said.

"Uncle Huo, are you going to the Great Marsh again? Take us with you!" Lang Sheng took the lead, jumped onto the cart, and then climbed onto the giant wolf's back, resting his little head on the big one, eyes looking into eyes.

"Take us with you!" the other cubs shouted excitedly, scratching at the thick fur of the adult wolf orcs.

They were tired of running around Wolf Mountain; they had explored every inch of the mountain and the foot of the mountain, and they knew exactly where every squeak-beast hole was.

"We want to go out too!"

"We can help!"

Now that Rong and the others were grazing the ewe-beasts, they didn't need them to cut grass. The squeak-beasts in the fields were used by the adult orcs for archery practice, so they didn't even need to catch them for training anymore.

The tribe didn't need them anymore; the cubs wanted to go out!

Lang Huo shook his head, and the cubs slid down a bit, quickly grabbing his ears with their claws.

"You want to go out?" Lang Huo asked.

"Yes!" the cubs said expectantly.

"Go find the King. If the King agrees, I'll take you out to see."

"Uncle Huo! Wait for us, we're going to find the King right now!" Lang Sheng took the lead, sliding down the giant wolf's head and landing on the ground, his soft flesh bouncing.

In the fields, the vegetables planted by the rabbit-orcs had sprouted, and they were busy transplanting them.

Lin Qiu squatted beside the green, velvet-like clover, helping to apply some fertilizer.

Lang Yan was patrolling the tail-grass meadow. After the orcs' day-and-night patrols and hunting, the number of squeak-beasts in the fields had decreased significantly, and the germination rate of the tail-grass was very encouraging.

Hearing the cubs shouting for the King from afar, the orcs in the fields put down their work, thinking something had happened.

Lang Yan walked out of the fields, listened, and said to Lin Qiu, "They want to go to the Great Marsh."

"It's so far, how can they?"

"Qiu Qiu! We're going with Uncle Huo! We won't run around!" The cubs heard Lin Qiu say this as they ran up and hurriedly looked at Lang Yan.

They hugged Lang Yan's legs and tried to climb up.

"King! We want to go! We've never left Wolf Mountain! Uncle Huo isn't going hunting; we'll sit on the cart, be good, just let us go see!"

"King... let us go."

The cubs looked at Lang Yan with wet eyes, hugging his legs and shaking them, but Lang Yan stood firmly and didn't fall for it at all.

He lowered his eyes and flicked the cubs on the forehead.

"No."

"Wuu—"

"Don't cry." Lang Yan pinched the cubs' cheeks.

The cubs slid down, falling to the ground pitifully.

The rabbit-orcs watched from the side, almost pleading for them. But seeing Lang Yan's stern expression, their reason returned.

The Wolf King's decision was correct; the cubs were fragile and would get hurt if they weren't careful.

The journey to the Great Marsh was so long that even if they sat on the cart, they would be jolted the whole way.

"Ah Sheng? Are you coming or not? If not, we're leaving!" Lang Huo's voice came from in front of the mountain.

Several cubs surrounded Lang Yan, their heads against his legs, aggrievedly pawing at him from time to time.

Lang Yan: "When you're a little bigger, you can go wherever you want."

The cubs remained motionless.

Lin Qiu just watched and laughed from the side; he wasn't going to help coax the cubs.

Lang Yan lowered his head, looking at the little furry heads. When he moved his leg, the cubs hurriedly hugged it tighter.

"It's warm now, and there are starving stray orcs everywhere. They don't just eat animals; they eat orcs too. They love tender cubs the most... The Great Marsh is so far. If Uncle Huo and the others run into them, they can run away, but if you follow, you can't fight and you'll just be a burden."

The cubs were stunned by his words, their eyes wide, forgetting to close their mouths.

Lang Sheng was the oldest and a bit smarter; he lunged at Lang Yan's leg and hung on tightly. "King! You're lying to the cubs! Uncle Huo and the others have been there so many times and never met any!"

"We have," Tu Kui said softly.

The cubs looked at him. A trace of hidden pain flashed in Tu Kui's eyes, and although he smiled gently, he looked sad.

"We met them before."

"If we hadn't met them, we wouldn't have fled to the Wolf Tribe."

Tu Luo hopped out of the hole he had just dug, watching the cubs vigilantly.

Tu Kui touched his long ears, and Tu Luo suddenly pressed tightly against him.

Suddenly, he said in terror: "Eaten, eaten!"

"Ah Peng was eaten!"

Tu Kui was startled and hurriedly hugged the cub in front of him to comfort him. He stroked those two long rabbit ears and said, "Don't be afraid, don't be afraid."

Lang Sheng and the others quieted down, curling their claws and leaning tightly against Lang Yan in fear.

Lang Yan lowered his eyes and said, "If you're bored, go to Uncle Qi's place. It's been so long, hasn't he chosen a cub to learn carpentry with him yet?"

Lang Sheng shook his head, his eyes fixed on the somewhat strange Tu Luo, his bottom almost sitting on Lang Yan's feet.

Why, why would orcs eat orcs...

*

Southern part of the Black Feather Tribe.

Yu Lie and the hunting party were chasing a group of prey.

They flew high, and the prey looked like beans, but the Black Feather orcs could still see them clearly.

The Black Feather Tribe's territory was vast, with the core being the western mountain range where they lived. To the west was an endless plain. To the south was a position slightly north of the valley where they had previously encountered the Snow Eagle orcs.

To the north, there wasn't much prey, so the Black Feather orcs hadn't occupied it.

Yu Lie was focused on chasing the prey. Just as he was about to dive, a companion's wing brushed against his.

"Lie! Look!"

Yu Lie squinted and saw orcs that had appeared from nowhere in the south, chasing directly after their prey.

"They actually dare to come into our territory to catch the prey we're hunting!"

"Lie! Could it be the Yuanye Tribe..."

"Look at how thin they are; do they look like it?"

The previous Snow Eagle orcs were all plump and sturdy, as if they had written "I can eat my fill every meal" on their faces.

Yu Lie scanned them and guessed, "They might be stray orcs."

Being beaten by the Yuanye Tribe was a small tribe against a large one, a matter of insufficient strength. But against a few stray orcs, what was there to fear?

Yu Lie's feathers shone with a dark green luster, his beak sharp, his claws keen, and he flew directly toward the orcs.

There were five orcs in total: two from the Feather clan, one from the Black Bear clan, and two from the Cat clan.

Yu Lie's sharp claws went straight for the head of the leading orc.

The leading orc saw this, immediately hugged his head and crouched down, screaming: "We are a tribe that just migrated nearby! We didn't know this was your prey!"

Yu Lie's claws missed, and he flew high, his sharp eyes fixed on them.

"A tribe that just migrated?"

"Yes, we migrated from the west and only arrived a few days ago. You... your territory border has no markings; we didn't know this was your territory."

Usually, orcs would patrol their territory and leave their own scent where they walked.

If orcs had marked their territory for a long time and neighbors were fixed, everyone would know the location of the other's territory and wouldn't easily intrude.

But strange orcs wouldn't know.

Therefore, they usually relied on markers left during patrols to distinguish them—some were stones arranged in rules, some were scents, and some were claw prints or hoof prints.

The Black Feather orcs had been worried about one thing throughout the snow season and even now, so they hadn't patrolled much, making it possible that the orcs didn't know this was their territory.

Yu Lie landed, and the other Black Feather orcs stopped behind him.

Both sides sized each other up.

Yu Lie looked from the orcs' thick, black feet to their tattered beast-skin skirts, and then to their messy, mud-caked hair that was falling out in clumps.

They looked like they had migrated.

He asked in a rough voice, "Where is your tribe located?"

The other side became defensive.

Yu Lie: "If your tribe is nearby, then it's still in our territory."

The Black Bear orc's gaze swept over Yu Lie's wings, and he said dully, "We will move away immediately."

Seeing that their attitude was sincere enough, Yu Lie said, "There's no room left here. To the east is the Wolf Tribe; you can only go south."

"Wolf?"

Yu Lie didn't say much more, only adding, "They aren't easy to provoke. If you intrude into their tribe like this, you won't even be able to say a word before you lose your lives."

The Black Bear orc: "We understand."

There was still some distance from the border line, so Yu Lie naturally had to watch them leave his tribe's territory.

Because of this, he wouldn't be able to return today.

Yu Lie left five orcs to continue hunting and report back, while he took the remaining orcs to watch them leave.

These orcs looked like they had been hungry for a long time, and their running speed was very slow.

Yu Lie followed from a distance until he saw a group of orcs of different races emerge from the bushes where they were hiding, confirming that they were a tribe, not stray orcs living everywhere.

There were nearly fifty of these orcs, mostly from the Bear clan, with a few from the Feather clan, as well as cubs and sub-orcs.

They wore tattered beast skins around their waists, skin wrapped around bone, looking like they hadn't eaten for a long time.

Yu Lie landed on a treetop and saw the cubs in the procession rush out, hugging the Bear orcs' legs and shouting:

"Father!"

That little cub was not from the Bear clan.

But it wasn't uncommon for orcs of different races to form mates; this was a normal thing in orc tribes.

The Bear orc should be the chief of this tribe. He spoke to his tribesmen, and then everyone disappeared into the jungle, looking like they were going to pack up.

Not long after, the orc procession assembled and began to walk south.

The Bear orc looked at the tree, his gaze landing on Yu Lie's wings.

"I want to ask, is there any suitable place around here that can be used as a territory?"

Yu Lie looked at the cub still hugging the Black Bear orc's leg, its eyes bulging from hunger, staring straight at him, as if it were swallowing its saliva.

Yu Lie didn't have any food on him.

"I've never left the tribe, so I don't know. You'll have to find it yourselves."

The Bear orc nodded, had no choice but to carry the cub with one hand, and followed the procession.

The orcs must have been very hungry; not long after they started walking, some cubs and sub-orcs collapsed. But the Black Feather orcs said nothing and kept following behind.

They couldn't even protect themselves; where would they find the compassion?

From dawn to dusk, Yu Lie finally stopped. Through the last bit of light, they looked at the few low mountains at the end of the sky.

That was the valley.

It was still some distance from the edge of their tribe. If this group of orcs could find their way there, there was warm water even in the snow season, and as long as they found food, they could barely survive in the future.

Yu Lie didn't follow anymore.

But Xiong Chen and the others couldn't stay here.

These Feather orcs looked different from them; they were well-fed, and they definitely couldn't defeat them.
chapters.source_text:
狼山前热闹，兽人们还专门燃起篝火，围成圈绕着火堆玩儿。
今天猎物不多，但兽人们挖了些能吃的块根，狼安拿出来，叫他们自己先烤着吃。
黑羽兽人坐在一旁，有些羡慕地看着狼兽人们。
羽千想起今天生了幼崽的咩咩兽，忍不住看向西边。
本来，最开始羽山挑选来狼部落的兽人时没有想到他，是他主动要来的。
他们得罪了原野部落，大家都不知道几个月后等待他们的将会是什么。但羽千想，倘若他们这次能活，那跟着狼部落干活学到的东西，将是部落能继续存在下去的关键。
所以抱着那么一点微小的希望，他过来了。
雪季后，羽千跟着狼兽人一点一点忙活过来，兽人们并没有藏私，他便也知道了地是怎么种的，咩咩兽是怎么喂养的，能吃的野菜其实有很多种，烹饪食物的法子也有很多……
听到自己族人羡慕狼部落的声音，羽千觉得，其实有这么一个邻居在已经是他们幸运了。
换作别的部落，大概也会羡慕他们的。
要是能度过这次危机，他想，他们黑羽部落也将会有更好的发展。
篝火被风吹得猎猎作响，宝塔一样搭起来的木柴让火焰烧得比兽人还高。猩红的火星飘向夜空，像烟花一样璀璨。
黑羽兽人们安静待在一角，他们被狼兽人的喜悦感染，脸上刚扬起笑意，却又抿平了嘴角，忐忑地祈求着那场危机不要到来。
今天兽人们没抓到大型猎物，所以没多少肉吃。
林楸还在帮忙添柴烧火，看狼莫他们在篝火那边烤吱吱兽，不免跟狼岩说起地里吱吱兽的情况。
“……地太宽了，到处都是洞。我放了点笼子，果跟祭司说让幼崽抓吱吱兽，不知道管不管用……”
“笼子放了多少？”
“十个，我打算再做些出来。”
十个远远不够，说不定一次下来还没幼崽抓得多。
狼岩想着，招招手，叫幼崽去把狼游叫来。
天还有些冷，狼游身上只穿着一件兽皮马甲，胸前敞开的，之前捕猎受伤愈合的疤痕格外明显。
“王。”
“兽人们弓箭用得怎么样？”
“大家还不习惯，总瞄不准，有时候还会误伤同伴。”
“叫他们去地里对着吱吱兽练。”
狼游愣了愣，点头。
是个好主意，反正兽人们晚上看得见。
“之后叫他们轮流守地，五个兽人一组。什么时候吱吱兽少了，箭头准了，什么时候停止。”
“好。”
狼游长腿一迈，立刻去安排。
狼雨搅拌着野菜汤，忍不住笑道：“还是王主意多。”
“晚上练箭……”林楸欲言又止。
狼岩：“放心，不会瞎。”
林楸颤着肩膀笑了两声，跟他肚子里的蛔虫似的，他想什么怎么狼岩都知道？
狼岩看着，忽然捏了捏他脸颊。
林楸：？
狼岩淡然收回手，什么都没说。
吃过晚饭，幼崽跟有弓箭的兽人就跑地里去了。
天上一轮弯月，清辉明朗。林楸看着，总感觉自己好像还在原来的世界。
可细看，月是不一样的。更大，光辉更盛，圆月时，天尽头的月亮仿佛触手可及。
林楸出神看着，忽然脸上一热。
“回山洞了。”
林楸弯眼，握住贴在脸侧的手，“王明天出去吗？”
“去看看。楸也想去？”
林楸摇头，“再过几天，现在狼山忙不过来。”
该睡觉了。
伴着寥寥虫鸣，林楸窝在伴侣的身边一夜酣眠。
第二天天刚亮，狼岩起身，林楸也跟着坐起来。
“还早。”狼岩撩开林楸眼前的头发，温声道。
林楸看了眼木门上方的缝隙，已经能看到一丝霞光，像一截彩带尾巴。
“不睡了。”
下了山，大山洞里的兽人差不多都醒了，正坐在廊道里吃早饭。
林楸这会儿下山，兽人们诧异看着，狼莫还冲着他挥挥手道：“楸，你也要跟王他们一起出去？”
“暂时不去。”
“那你下来这么早？”
“早睡早起身体好。”
“早睡是无聊，早起是饿醒的，哪里什么身体好。”狼莫撇撇嘴，又抱着碗仰头灌了一大口汤。
他腮帮子一紧，咔嚓一声，嚼碎了骨头。
林楸闻着汤味道不对，“昨晚有剩的猎物没吃？”
“没啊。”
狼安举着勺子，打算给兽人打汤，“吱吱兽肉汤，兽人们抓的，可多了。”
林楸立刻后退一步，紧盯那陶锅。
狼岩手掌贴着他后背，道：“有其他的，不喜欢就不吃。”
狼安温柔笑起来，微卷的发尾轻轻摇晃，他道：“就知道你不会吃。”
吱吱兽也就罢了，长虫那么好吃的猎物楸也不喜欢。
林楸：“我啃鱼干就好。”
林楸盛了一点只有野菜的野菜汤，又拿了一块鱼干坐到角落里去。
狼莫跟狼西挪了挪位置，跟林楸一张桌子。
“昨晚吱吱兽抓了很多？”林楸问。
狼莫：“多，半筐呢。”
“半筐！”林楸想了想，一只一只处理干净都得花好多时间。
“谁叫它们要偷我们的种子呢？”听狼游说，为了抓吱吱兽，兽人们射箭的准头都高了。
林楸咬了一口鲜嫩的野菜，微微点头。
这么有效果，那地里的吱吱兽就不用操心了。
*
吃过早饭，大部分兽人要出去狩猎采集。
林楸目送一群巨狼混着几个体型颇小的兔兽人离开，队伍浩浩荡荡，奔跑中地面都隐隐震动。
兽人走后，他先去看了看昨天刚出生的咩咩兽幼崽，瞧着没什么事，再去地里看看昨天放的笼子。
笼子做得粗糙，胜在用藤蔓缠了两三层，足够结实。
林楸看了几个，机关做得不太到位，里头鱼糜没了，吱吱兽也没抓到。
“楸，笼子我们清理过了。”兔葵也拿着石镰过来，准备继续除草。
“抓得多吗？”
“有六只，但是好多笼子都被咬烂了。”
林楸这下知道下笼子效果不大了。
“你不用担心，昨晚兽人们抓了不少。”
林楸点头。
兔葵来地里来得勤快，几乎杂草一冒头，就被他们扯了。有黑羽兽人帮忙，林楸也没继续蹲在地里干活。
他去放鸟粪的棚子底下，鸟粪上盖着的干草扒开，稍稍用木棍翻了下，里头还冒着热气。
今年地多，这点肥料远远不够。
狼火他们去大泽那边拉鸟粪了，不知道什么时候回来。
正忙着，狼莫找了过来。
兽人普遍高，腿也长，好像随便迈了几步就走到了跟前。
“楸！房子建在哪里啊？”
狼莫小队的兽人此刻在忙着做砖，一个个灰头土脸的，像裹了一层泥壳。
“王没说吗？”
“王捕猎去了，让我们问问你跟祭司。”
“祭司怎么说？”
“祭司说他不管这事儿。”
林楸：“……”
“我晚上跟王商量商量。但肯定是要建不少房子的，砖瓦尽量多弄点。”
“我们知道，那你们赶紧商量吧。”
狼莫说完，又去地里晃悠了两圈，再跑回去忙。
林楸离开地里，去溪边洗了手，然后回山洞先自己琢磨琢磨这房子怎么建。
按照狼部落现在的发展来看，他们大概率以后不会再搬家了。
那房子建造起来，一户一间，狼兽人加上兔兽人接近三百口兽人，相当于一个大型村落。
首先，需要一块足够大的空地。
东部现在是大片的田地，没地方建房子。西部地势缓慢抬高，那边分布着砖窑陶窑，乱石又多，位置不算好。
最好的位置就是山前这一块，背靠山，前靠河，地势平坦。但雨季时河道涨水，离河岸太近肯定会被淹，除非加高河堤。
那就只能往北推一点。
山前可零星建屋，要形成聚落，还是狼山北边那块地方最合适。
不过这涉及到以后几百间屋子的时候了，要先看王跟祭司怎么想的。单纯的建食堂和有伴侣的兽人居住的几间房子，其实狼山前就可以。
林楸看着地上被他用没烧完的木棍画出来的东西，暂且没擦，等狼岩回来再让他看看。
晚间，兽人们回来了。
林楸第一时间把狼岩拉到山洞里。
狼岩看着自己伴侣，目光深邃似有光芒闪烁。林楸没注意到。
进了山洞，狼岩刚搂住林楸的腰，就被他拍了拍胳膊，示意他看地上。
狼岩：“建房子的事？”
“对啊。”林楸疑惑，“不然你想的什么事？”
狼岩低头磕了一下林楸脑袋，顺势枕在他肩膀，懒洋洋道：“没什么。”
“那我给你讲一讲我怎么想的？”
“嗯。”
两个兽人都坐在矮凳上，林楸身子前倾，拿着木棍点着地上。狼岩半个胸口贴在林楸后背，下巴挨着他肩，静静听他说。
林楸一口气讲完，道：“你说怎么样合适？”
狼岩：“狼山前。”
“可是雨季会涨水。”
“雪季风很大，房子建在山后火炕烧得再暖和，房顶也能被大风掀开，不安全也不暖和。而且这边正好是个大草原，以后用来放咩咩兽再好不过。”
“至于涨水，可以像廊道这样加高地基，再不然咱们就加高河堤。”
当初部落留在这里，看中的就是狼山跟山前这一片位置，防风，近河取水也方便，而且地势平坦，山前的空地足够兽人们撒欢。
“加高河堤可是很麻烦的。”
林楸还有些担忧，转头看着他。
他们挨得很近，狼岩稍微一低头，鼻尖就贴上林楸鼻尖。
“放心，按照目前狼莫他们的速度，一下子建不起来那么多房子。河水不会年年涨这么高，就算以后要搬，我们也来得及。”
“那好吧，就山前。”
“嗯。”狼岩亲了下林楸鼻尖。
位置选定，就在狼山前。
山前夯实的那块地不变，把这里当做兽人们的活动广场。往西边一点，直接建造兽人伴侣居住的小房子。东边就在灶台的这个地方改建食堂，尽量不把灶台拆了。
狼岩只跟着兽人们出去了两三天，就又留在狼山守着。
狼莫时不时跑来商量房子的事，等到第一砖出窑，已经是半个月后了。
气温逐渐上升，兽皮大衣穿不住。
兽人们也开始换毛。
狼山到处飘着狼毛，草叶上随处可见，廊角、石壁角都是混着灰尘滚落过去的狼毛团。
这次不用林楸招呼，兽人们自己就先把狼毛梳下来存着。
幼崽刚梳完毛，在狼山前疯跑。
幼崽养得好了，皮毛油光水滑的，跑起来格外蓬松柔顺。
跑着跑着，看到狼火小队拉着板车过来，他们起身一蹦，直接跳到了板车上。
“下来。”狼火道。
“火叔，你们是不是又要去大泽？带我们一起去吧。”狼生带头，跳上板车后直接跑到巨狼背上去，小脑袋搭在大脑袋上，眼睛看着眼睛。
“一起去吧！”其他幼崽激动得刨着成年狼兽人厚实的狼毛道。
他们在狼山都跑腻了，山上山脚哪里没有被他们探索过，哪里有吱吱兽洞他们都知道得一清二楚。
“我们也想出去！”
“我们可以帮忙！”
现在溶他们养咩咩兽直接放牧，用不到他们割草。地里吱吱兽被成年兽人们用来练箭，他们都不用抓吱吱兽训练了。
部落已经用不上他们，幼崽要出去！
狼火晃了晃脑袋，幼崽身体往下滑了一点，赶紧用爪子抓住他耳朵。
“想出去？”狼火问。
“想！”幼崽期待道。
“找王去，要是王同意了，我就带你们出去看看。”
“火叔！你等等我们，我们现在就去找王！”狼生带头，一下沿着大狼脑袋滑下去，落在地上，身上软肉还弹了弹。
地里，兔兽人们种的菜都长出苗了，兔兽人们正在移栽。
林楸蹲在那绿绒毛似的三叶草旁边，帮忙施点肥下去。
狼岩在尾巴草地巡逻，经过兽人们日夜巡逻抓捕，地里吱吱兽少了很多，尾巴草发芽率也很喜人。
远远听着幼崽着急喊王，地里的兽人都放下手里的活儿，还以为出什么事了。
狼岩从地里走出来，听了听，跟林楸道：“他们想去大泽。”
“那么远，怎么行？”
“楸楸！我们跟着火叔一起去！不会乱跑的！”幼崽跑到跟前就听到林楸这样说，又急吼吼地去看狼岩。
他们抱住狼岩的腿，还试图往上爬。
“王！我们想去！我们从来没有出过狼山！火叔又不是去捕猎，我们坐在板车上，乖乖的，就让我们去看看吧。”
“王……让我们去吧。”
幼崽湿漉漉的眼睛望着狼岩，抱着他的腿摇啊摇，偏偏狼岩站得稳稳当当，也一点不吃这一套。
他垂眸，弹了下幼崽脑门。
“不行。”
“呜——”
“不许哭。”狼岩捏住幼崽腮帮子。
幼崽滑落，可怜兮兮跌坐在地。
兔兽人们在一旁看着，险些给他们说情了。但一看狼岩冷峻的脸色，理智回归。
狼王的决定没错，幼崽脆弱，稍有不慎就会受伤。
这边去大泽的路途那么远，就算是他们坐在那板车上，也要一路颠簸。
“阿生？行不行啊？不行我们走了！”山前，狼火声音传来。
几个幼崽围了狼岩一圈，脑袋抵着他腿，委屈地时不时用爪子扒拉他。
狼岩：“等你们再大一点，想去哪儿去哪儿。”
幼崽依旧一动不动。
林楸只在一旁笑看着，他可不帮忙哄幼崽。
狼岩低头，看着一个个毛乎乎的小脑瓜子。腿一动，幼崽就连忙抱紧他。
“现在暖和了，到处都是饿得发慌的流浪兽人，他们不仅吃动物，还吃兽人。幼崽细皮嫩肉的，他们最喜欢……大泽那么远，你们火叔他们遇上了还能跑，你们跟着，打又打不过，还拖后腿。”
幼崽被他唬得一愣一愣的，睁大眼睛，下巴都忘了合上。
狼生最大，聪明一点，他一下扑住狼岩的腿把自己紧紧挂在上面，“王！你骗幼崽！火叔他们都去了那么多次了从来没有遇到过！”
“有的。”忽然，兔葵轻声说了一句。
幼崽看向他，兔葵眼里闪过一丝隐痛，面上温柔笑着，看起来却是难过的样子。
“我们以前就遇到过。”
“要不是遇到他们，我们就不会逃到狼部落。”
兔萝蹦蹦跳跳钻出自己刚挖的洞，警惕看着幼崽们。
兔葵摸摸他的长耳朵，兔萝忽然紧紧贴在兔葵身上。
忽然，他惊恐道：“吃、吃掉了！”
“阿蓬被吃掉了！”
兔葵惊了一下，赶紧将幼崽搂在身前安抚，他顺着那两个长长的兔耳朵道：“不怕，不怕。”
狼生他们安静下来，蜷缩着爪爪，害怕得紧紧往狼岩身上靠。
狼岩垂眸道：“要是无聊，就去起叔那里，这么久了，他还没选出跟他一起学木工活的幼崽？”
狼生摇摇头，眼睛一直盯着有些奇怪的兔萝，屁股几乎坐在狼岩脚背。
兽人、兽人为什么要吃兽人……
*
黑羽部落南部。
羽猎带着狩猎队正追赶着一群猎物。
他们飞得高，猎物如豆小，黑羽兽人依旧看得清清楚楚。
黑羽部落领地广阔，核心部分就是他们居住的西部山脉处。往西，是一望无际的平原。往南，就是之前遇到雪鹰兽人的山谷再靠北一点的位置。
往北部，没多少猎物，黑羽兽人便没有继续占领。
羽猎一心追逐着猎物，眼看近了，正要俯冲而下，身边同伴忽然翅膀擦过他翅膀。
“猎！你看！”
羽猎眯眼看去，却见南边不知哪蹿出来的兽人，直接冲着他们的猎物追去。
“居然敢跑到我们领地来抓我们正在追捕的猎物！”
“猎！会不会是原野部落……”
“你看那瘦得，像吗？”
之前那些雪鹰兽人，一个个长得膘肥体壮，就差把我能顿顿吃饱写在脸上了。
羽猎打眼一扫，猜测道：“可能是流浪兽人。”
他们挨原野部落的打，那是小部落对上大部落，实力不济。对上几个流浪兽人，哪还有怕的。
羽猎羽毛闪着青黑的光，鸟喙尖锐，利爪锋利，直接冲着那几个兽人而去。
一共五个兽人，其中两个羽族的，一个黑熊族，两个猫族。
羽猎利爪自冲着兽人脑袋去。
为首的兽人一看，立马抱头蹲下，惊叫道：“我们是附近刚刚迁徙过来的部落！我们不知道这是你们的猎物！”
羽猎一爪落空，直接飞高，锐眼盯着他们。
“刚迁徙来的部落？”
“对，我们是西边迁徙过来的，才过来几天。你、你们领地边界没有标记，我们不知道这是你们的领地。”
一般兽人会在领地巡逻，走过的地方会留下自身的气味。
如果兽人划出领地的时间够长，附近邻居固定，也都知道对方领地位置，不会轻易侵扰。
但陌生兽人就不知道了。
所以它们一般靠兽人巡逻过程中留下的标记来分辨，这些标记有些是规则排列的石头，有些是味道，有些是爪印、蹄印之类的。
黑羽兽人整个雪季乃至现在都愁着一件事，也没怎么巡逻，所以兽人不知道这是他们领地也有可能。
羽猎落下地，其他黑羽兽人也停在他身后。
双方互相打量着。
羽猎从兽人粗黑的大脚看到破破烂烂的兽皮裙，然后是乱糟糟裹着泥一撮一撮掉着的头发。
看着像是迁徙来的。
他粗声问道：“你们的部落在什么位置？”
对方顿时防备。
羽猎：“要是你们部落在附近，那就还是在我们领地里。”
黑熊兽人目光从羽猎的翅膀划过，闷声道：“我们立刻搬走。”
看他们态度还算诚恳，羽猎便道：“这边已经没有位置了，再往东边是狼部落，你们只有往南走。”
“狼？”
羽猎没多说，只道：“他们不好招惹，你们要是像这样闯入他们部落，话都说不了一句，怕就没命了。”
黑熊兽人：“我们知道了。”
这边离边界线还有点距离，羽猎自然是要看着他们离开自家部落的。
这样一来，今天是回不去了。
羽猎留五个兽人继续抓捕猎物，顺带回去报信。他则带着剩下的兽人盯着他们离开。
这几个兽人像饿了很久，奔跑的速度很慢。
羽猎远远跟着，直到看到一群不同种族的兽人从藏身的树丛出来，才确定他们应当是一个部落，而不是四处为家的流浪兽人。
这些兽人有近五十个，熊族的兽人最多，有几个羽族，还有幼崽跟亚兽人。
他们腰间围着破败的兽皮，皮包着骨，看起来很久没吃饭了。
羽猎停落树梢，就看见队伍里的幼崽冲出来，抱着熊兽人的腿喊道：
“阿父！”
那个小崽子并不是熊族。
但不同种族结成伴侣的兽人不是没有，这在兽人部落是很正常的一件事。
熊兽人应当是这个部落的族长，他跟族人们说了说话，随后大家又消失在丛林中，看样子是去收拾东西了。
没多久，兽人队伍集结，开始往南边行走。
熊兽人看向树上，目光又落在羽猎翅膀上。
“我想问一问，这边还有没有合适的地方可以当领地？”
羽猎看着还抱着黑熊兽人腿的幼崽，眼睛饿得有些凸出，直勾勾地看着他，像是咽了咽口水。
羽猎身上可没有食物。
“我没出过部落，也不知道，你们自己找找吧。”
熊兽人点点头，只好单手拎着幼崽，跟上队伍。
兽人们应当很饿，没走多久，就有幼崽和亚兽人倒下。但黑羽兽人什么都没说，一直在后面跟着。
他们自身不保了，哪有那么多同情心。
从天亮走到天黑，羽猎最终停下来，隔着最后一丝光线，他们看着天尽头的几座矮山。
那边就是山谷了。
离他们部落边缘还有一段距离，要是这群兽人能找到那边去，那里雪季都有温热的水，只要再找到食物，以后勉强能度日。
羽猎没再跟了。
但熊沉他们不能在这里停留。
这几个羽族看起来跟他们不一样，是吃饱了的状态，他们肯定不敌。
chapters.title: 第142章

chapters.source_text:
狼山。
兽人们各司其职，忙到中午，狼安叫兽人们吃饭的吆喝声又响起。
大伙儿去溪边洗手，随后自己拿碗，打汤吃饭。
狩猎采集队不在，兽人们中午这一顿就随便吃点垫垫肚子。没什么猎物，午间就是白水煮菜，里头混着些河虾。
河虾与林楸从前所见的河虾略有不同，它们个头偏大，大的有一掌长。现在这个时候虽没到最肥的时候，但“春嫩夏肥”，这个时候的河虾滋味也不差。
水煮菜里只撒了几颗盐，吃的是个食物本味。
兔兽人吃着欢喜，青菜本来就是他们喜欢的，那虾肉也嫩甜，煮出来的汤格外的鲜。
狼兽人却不喜欢这刮油的食物，可肚里饥饿，只得闷头往肚里刨。
林楸见状，去弄了点蘸料来。
兽人们眼睛发亮，纷纷挪着靠近。林楸分了他们大半，自己剩下一个碗底的，用虾肉蘸着吃。
河虾并不腥，又是刚捞上来的，最是新鲜。
林楸先直接吃了一个，肉质弹牙，格外鲜甜。又蘸酱，虾肉就多了一股浓烈的香草味道，但也盖不过那点鲜甜。
林楸挺喜欢，他剥开一个蘸了料送到狼岩嘴边。
狼岩偏头叼过，就见自己伴侣一双眼睛看着他。
“好吃吗？”林楸问。
“好吃。”狼岩道。
“要是有豆子就好了，可以做点酱油出来，做菜做蘸料都方便。”
“什么样的豆子？”狼莫倾身靠来，迫不及待地问。
林楸：“根须长得像有瘤子，豆荚扁扁的，半指长，有绒毛。成熟后是黄色。”
狼兽人们绞尽脑汁，也没想出个匹配的。
林楸：“也可能不长这样。”
狼兽人们垂头丧气，“吃不到。”
楸说的这些好吃的，都吃不到。
狼岩一直没开口，等将几个剥了壳的虾放到林楸碗里，才道：“兽神大陆很大，或许就长在某一个地方。”
楸既然从兽神那里见过这个东西，那大陆上肯定会有，只看他们找不找得到。
“要是集市还开着就好了……”狼安也叹道。
集市开着，他们兴许还能问问其他部落还有其他几个大陆上的兽人。
林楸：“没准以后猎物多了又重开了。”
狼安失笑道：“那我们或许看不到了。”
兽人们不再言语，快速吃完碗里的食物，随后洗了碗往地上一躺，休息一会儿再出去干活。
林楸跟狼岩打算上小山洞小憩一会儿，还没走，狼安道：“王，是不是该挖些盐了，后头雨季要储存点食物，又要忙着种植和建房子，兽人们都没空。”
年初备好盐，一年就不用担心盐不够用。
今年还得多多的准备，雪季前支部落要回来，楸腌肉腌鱼也需要很多的盐。
狼岩：“等狼火回来。”
狼岩得保证至少有两个狩猎队狩猎。
狼安说了这事，也进山洞休息去了。
大山洞里，狼雪还趴在木桌上分草药苗，狼冰晚上回来要种。
羽乐把这些天狼冰小队采集回来的草药分类，自己先处理一遍，放在筐里。
老祭司躺在草窝里似睡非睡，草窝靠墙那边放着他那象征祭司身份的木杖。
有了狼起做的拐杖，他像是很久没用过那个了。
山洞里安静，兽人们呼吸绵长。
狼兽人一天只要吃饱就能睡好。
今天阳光只出来了一会儿，下午便阴了。老祭司说要下雨了，几个亚兽人一醒，就先把廊道上的帘子放下来，免得上面还没晒干的鱼被打湿。
林楸也只睡了一会儿，去溪边洗了脸，清醒了，就开始了他的训练。
部落现在还算稳定，狼岩便按照先前所说，专门带着他训练。
不仅仅是练习奔跑，还有抓捕猎物，应对敌人。
林楸先跟在狼岩身后绕着狼山前奔跑，热热身。人形一圈，兽形两圈。
跑到西边，狼莫跟狼溶都出来看。
跑到东边，兔兽人们冲着他笑，还有些好奇。
到了山前，狼安他们干脆把织布机搬出来，一边看他们训练，一边织布。
林楸盯着自家伴侣的尾巴，“我感觉我像猴儿。”
“不像。”狼岩一本正经道，“猴兽人没有狼兽人好看。”
“不是这个意思……”
“那也不像。”
跑完，林楸站在夯实了的地面。
他许久没跑了，这才三圈下来就有些呼吸不匀。反观狼岩，就跟刚刚散了个步一样，整个兽人看着还更轻松了。
林楸看自家狼王拧起的眉头，有些不好意思道：“要不我每天都绕着狼山跑一跑？”
“要跑。现在先休息休息。”
“这就休息了？”
林楸也看过兽人们的训练，当时狼岩可不是这样要求的。是不是对他太过放松了？
狼岩：“休息。”
林楸直接往地上一坐，深吸一口气再吐出来。
对比自家这些狼兽人，甚至是兔兽人，他真的好弱。
林楸搞不明白，到底是原身体弱本就锻炼少了，还是他原来那个身体跟着过来了。
他以前运动量也少，学习忙，上班也忙，但身体还算健康。可到了这里，他完全就是个拖后腿的。
林楸胡思乱想着，下巴被轻托起来。
他看着狼岩半跪在他面前。
“别乱想，我会让你跟上兽人的。”
“那就靠你了，王。”
狼岩摸摸他的脸，“好。”
从这天开始，狼岩就带着林楸训练。
先慢慢跑，把体能练上去，等绕狼山跑个十圈跑得轻松了，再加上捕猎跟打斗练习。
兽人们从刚开始的看热闹，慢慢也习惯了楸总在狼山前跑跳。连幼崽也被王逮了去，跟着楸一起训练。
有时候狼岩不在，林楸就按照他教的那一套自己训练。幼崽监督他，他也监督幼崽。
不过白日里忙，林楸有时是早早起来练，有时是接近傍晚才练。
正是金乌西落，红日半醉。
林楸刚练完，滚了一身尘土，坐在地上看着汗珠一颗颗往下掉。
狼溶满脸欣喜地从北边跑回来，喊道：“楸！又有咩咩兽有幼崽了！”
林楸用手背将眼角的汗水擦去，撑着地站起来。
“有几个？”
“两个！”
狼溶寻常都是安静样子，一激动，难得声音大了些，连山洞里忙活的狼起跟狼安他们都听见了。
兽人一喜，立马放下手中的事跟着林楸一起过去。
幼崽追在后面，一个蹦跳蹿远，那原地还留下一团灰尘轻轻散去。
现在咩咩兽已经适应每天出来放牧了，小狼们也不用每一个都待在这边。
有时甚至不需要小狼跟着，只时不时来看看就行。咩咩兽早上放出来，到了天黑前，它们自己都能回圈。
快天黑了，咩咩兽在往回走。
狼溶就是赶着它们回来的时候发现的，他本来就是随手一摸，哪想到真摸到了，就立马来通知林楸。
可等他们刚跑过去，却看见咩咩兽在地里啃菜。
“诶！菜！”狼溶吓得魂飞，要知道地里的作物可是部落最重要的东西。
兔兽人们又不在，地里没看守的兽人。
狼溶狂奔过去，嘴上吆喝着，那咩咩兽却头也不抬，啃食得更快了。
等把它们赶出来，菜地都秃了一块。
狼溶像犯了错，僵硬地立在咩咩兽的身边，满脸无措地看着林楸跟一众过来的狼兽人们。
林楸摸摸小狼脑袋，“不怪你。”
狼溶脑袋垂得更低，自责不已。
在兽人们心中，地里的东西是兽人们辛辛苦苦种出来的，花了好大的精力。
大家守了这么久都没出错，可偏偏就是他赶咩咩兽回来时半途离开，才发生了这事。
那块菜地，原本长得格外茂盛，昨天还听葵念叨着说今天能收割了，结果却被咩咩兽啃得七零八落，稀稀拉拉。
“都怪我。”狼溶极小声哽咽道。
狼安几个亚兽人见状，纷纷上来先安慰小狼。
林楸则先检查了咩咩兽，确认小狼没摸错，再去检查地里。
兔兽人那边听到呼喊声，也急急忙忙跑了过来，看到地里那一瞬，心都漏跳一拍。
又发现小狼眼眶发红，立马敛了失落，一起来安慰他。
“都是菜，没事，还能长出来。”兔葵道。
兔藤也杵着拐杖，拍着小狼肩膀道：“只是三叶草吃得最多，这个可以割好多次，越割越长，没事的。”
咩咩兽被兽人们围着，还有些蠢蠢欲动。
林楸看在眼里，又看看地里的菜。他蹲下来，摸了摸差点被啃秃了的三叶草。
“葵，三叶草的种子还有吗？”
“有，这个好长，不用补种。”
“那现在这一片先收割，给咩咩兽吃好不好？”
兔葵一愣，想到咩咩兽啃成那样子，确实不好下口，他点头道：“好。”
眼看着又一头咩咩兽钻空子跑进那三叶草地，低头就啃，兽人们似乎明白了什么。
“楸！你想种这个给咩咩兽吃？”兔葵问。
林楸点头道：“或许咱们可以自己种牧草。”
“为什么还要专门种？草原上那么多草。”兔艾低声道。
他其实有些可惜，三叶草也是他们辛辛苦苦培育出来的，专门给咩咩兽吃……总感觉好像有些浪费。
林楸：“只是先试试看。”
林楸看着这群越来越健壮的咩咩兽，跟兽人们解释道：
“现在草原上的草虽然多，看着是够吃，但我们才十一头咩咩兽。要是以后养到几十头、几百头甚至上千头，大家还觉得够吗？”
“而且咩咩兽的养殖事关兽人们能不能长久生存下去，我们不能完全靠它们自己采食，也需要培育专门的牧草，以防万一。”
“现在正好遇到他们喜欢的，咱们不如试一试，看看这是否能作为合适的牧草来用？这不比专门再培育牧草省事？”
“要是能成，我们以后养再多的咩咩兽，都不怕它们没有草吃。”兔葵喃喃，已经明白了林楸的意思，也明白，狼兽人们的目标远远不止养那么几十头咩咩兽。
他们要的是靠着养殖和种植能完全养活部落，甚至以后不用出去采集捕猎，且能永久定居在一个地方。
兔葵想明白了，当即同意。
其他兽人同样明了，眼中迸发出惊人的光芒。
“几百头，几千头！”
“那、那要吃多久才吃得完啊……”兽人们有些飘飘然，仿佛看到了以后天天吃肉，顿顿吃肉的美好日子。
“种！”狼安坚定道，“兽人够不够，要不要我们帮忙？”
兔葵笑着摇头，“有黑羽兽人了。”
虽然他们现在去给狼莫打下手去了。
兔艾站在兔葵身后，看一会儿咩咩兽，再看一下菜地，就在林楸以为他还纠结时，他激动道：“族长，我现在就去把种子拿过来！”
咩咩兽被狼溶赶了回去，小狼走的时候还是个木讷样子。
不是咩咩兽把菜啃坏了吗？
怎么又变成种牧草了？
那些菜到底是给他们吃的还是咩咩兽吃的啊？
牧草合不合适，得先用这一批咩咩兽试一试。需要的时间漫长，且慢慢看吧。
脸上一凉，林楸抬头望天。
“又下雨了。”
这边天还亮着，东边已经昏黑。乌云慢慢靠拢过来，西边还未落下的红日更加绚烂。
雨势渐渐变大。
兽人们急忙躲进廊下。
“狩猎队他们还没回来呢。”狼安甩了甩胳膊上的雨水道。
话刚落，就看着树丛里跑出来几个狼兽人。
狼安笑：“真是说不得。”
“下雨了下雨了！”兽人们嚷嚷着，一下冲进廊道。四个爪子一曲，乌龟一样趴在地上，还往前滑了一点。
他们本就从雨势大的地方回来，这么呲溜一滑，地面都是水。
西边烧砖的狼莫小队也跑回来了，他们一身泥灰，被水一冲刷，脸甚至还干净了点儿。
今天狩猎队难得的捕猎到三头猎物，两头尖角兽，一头弯角兽。
兽人们狂喜，远远就盯着那落在后头驮着猎物的兽人身上。
“今天怎么这么多！”兽人们激动地嚎。
狼岩在入口抖一抖毛，甩掉身上的雨水，走到廊道上，一条帕子就搭在脑门上。
他抬起头，鼻尖贴了贴自己伴侣的手心。
“今天运气好，本来是抓尖角兽，回来的路上又遇到一头弯角兽。正好，两头弯角兽先留着，看能不能养。”
说起这个，林楸一边给他擦毛毛，一边高兴道：“今天我们发现咩咩兽喜欢吃三叶草。”
“其他菜它们应该也喜欢。”
“但三叶草快被它们吃光了。”
“什么？！”狼云嚎，“我们还没吃到！”
大家都等着兔兽人种出来的菜呢！
去年雪季前那个萝卜多好吃啊！
被他吼了声震到耳朵的狼莫给了他一拳，随即箍着他脖子给他叨叨牧草的事儿。
听到什么百头、千头的咩咩兽，狼兽人傻兮兮地笑了起来。
“牧草好，多种，多种！”
外出的兽人们身上都湿了，老祭司看了眼，直接叫他们进山洞把毛烤干。
这会儿还没到能淋雨不管的时候，万一生病，部落草药都不够。
忙碌一天的狩猎采集队的兽人们进大山洞里休息，留守狼山的兽人们就要开始准备晚饭了。
狼石照例带着几个兽人出来去杀猎物。
兽人专门把盆带上，狩猎队为了抓活的费了好大的劲儿，血自然也得留着。
几个亚兽人则分工，有负责生火的，有负责洗野菜的，还有准备配菜跟调味料的。
“楸，还是炖肉汤吗？”狼安顺嘴一问。
林楸想着咩咩兽身上大多是瘦肉，肥油都没多少，他道：“尖角兽不能动，弯角兽尽量能吃两天，骨头明天再炖，不如煮个肉片汤，再炒个野菜炒肉。”
林楸看了，那些野菜里有野葱野蒜，正好能增香。
“行。”
肉有限，为了以后，兽人们只能省着吃。
雨慢慢下大了，雨声清脆，听着像给耳朵按摩一样舒服。
林楸依旧守着两口锅的柴火，就是往灶孔里递柴时有些不方便。他看向身边趴坐着、大脑袋搭在他腿上的大黑狼。
他狠狠摸了一把狼脑袋，道：“这里灰多。”
狼岩闭着眼睛一动不动，反正就是不走。
林楸捏他耳朵一下，低声道：“无赖。”
几个亚兽人看着只是笑，手上更为麻利。只忙着快点做好晚饭，好叫在外面奔波一天的兽人们吃完早点休息。
檐下的水如珠帘成串，吹进来的风带着水汽，还有淡淡的草木香。林楸喜欢这个味道，忍不住深吸一口气，似乎还闻到了甜甜的花香。
好久没吃甜的了……
部落的蜂蜜不禁吃，原先那点雨季里做做冷饮，冬季里混着热水喝一点，再不然就是做饭的时候用一点，不知不觉就用完了。
现在林楸回忆起那味道，竟有些馋了。
他咽了下口水，忍不住手指勾着那软软弹弹、绒毛柔密的毛耳朵搅了搅。
狼岩尾巴甩动，嗅着伴侣的气息打盹。
没多久，狼石先拎着一大块有肥油的肉跟两条瘦肉回来。都是洗干净的，可以直接切了烹煮。
后头，狼木端着一盆血回来。
盆上盖着大叶片，他自己头上满是雨水，这血倒是护得好好的。
血就留着明天早上吃，亚兽人们先忙今晚的。
狼石跟狼木放下东西，又出去了。
现在他们知道猎物的内脏都能吃，得好好处理。都是肉，扔一点都可惜。
林楸远远看着他们回到溪边，皱了皱眉。
“溪边也得搭个棚子。”
“是，明天要是不下雨，叫狼木他们搭一个。”狼安道。
想起狼木他们手里的事儿，他又说：“不知道起那边的大石碾做好了没有？”
现在狼木他们不仅要负责巡逻狼山，也得给起帮忙。
狼莫那边更是走不开。
护卫队……说来好笑，护卫队就剩狼石天天往山头跑。
“起叔还得多做点农具呢，哪里忙得过来。”
“兽人少了。”他俩同时叹道。
林楸拨弄着狼岩的毛毛，让火烤得均匀些，瞧他一直不说话，动作又轻了轻。
看来猎物不好抓，今天他们肯定跑了很远。
原来部落那一头尖角兽也适应了圈养生活，比之前的弯角兽好养。
现在这两头一来，不知道尖角兽能不能像咩咩兽一样习惯圈养生活，然后产仔。
其实要是弯角兽也能驯化，对兽人们来说是最好的。
弯角兽体型大，大一点的，有咩咩兽三个那么大。
可惜，脾气太倔。
林楸现在暂且不考虑驯养弯角兽，但他也没打算放弃，只能以后再看看有没有机会。
咩咩兽现在养得还好，暂时没什么问题。
但只一种也不行，还要先试试尖角兽。就是尖角兽也少，要养成群不知道得抓到什么时候去。
*
炒菜费油，但那香味就是霸道。
炝炒的油香钻进大山洞，片刻，廊下兽人拿着碗就排起了长队。
狼安看着，只能加快翻炒的速度。
煮整个部落的食物不容易，亚兽人们原来吃不饱还体虚，现在抡勺子都给自己抡出一身肌肉。
林楸看了看排着的队伍，又瞧着腿上趴着的黑狼脑袋。
他轻轻扯了下狼胡子，道：“吃饭了。”
狼岩耳朵动了动，脑袋往林楸肚子上埋了埋。
林楸眸光清润，带着一丝笑意，像夹着雨丝的风，清清爽爽的，又有着看家人一般的柔和。
吃过晚饭，兽人们各自洗漱睡觉。
大家正陆陆续续往山洞走，忽然听到林子里咯吱咯吱的动静。
兽人机警，盯着树林。
狼火好不容易在下雨天拉着鸟粪回来，浑身狼狈不堪，就指着吃上晚上狼山那顿晚饭的信念撑着。
哪知道到了狼山，看着空荡荡的锅，嗅着空气中残留的肉香，狼火郁闷地捂住鼻子趴下。
“饿……”
狼安见状，只好给他们做了晚上同样的肉片汤跟炒菜。
也幸好是捕的一头弯角兽，换做其他猎物，早没肉了。
狼岩看他回来，本来打算安排一队兽人明天去采盐。但看他们累，最后还是让狼火小队休息一天，后天再说。
*
黑羽部落。
兽人们从雪化之后就开始捕猎，忙到现在，猎物也抓了一些，但是承诺给狼部落的弯角兽目前只抓到两头。
黑羽兽人本来打算先关着养一养，等攒得差不多再送去。
结果弯角兽脾气暴躁，还不愿意吃食物，眼看着越来越瘦，羽山干脆派了羽涯他们几个将这两头弯角兽先送过去。
这几天下雨，等雨一停，羽涯几个小兽人立马行动。
走之前，羽长拉着自己的幼崽叮嘱：“这两头弯角兽是部落好不容易抓来的，路上别看丢了。走得慢没关系，带上点鱼干，路上饿了吃。”
没办法，越是接近雪化后的第三个月，黑羽部落的氛围越紧张。
成年兽人不能走，也不敢走，只能让小兽人去一趟。
都是快成年的小兽人了，要是这事都办不好，其他的成年兽人就更不放心交给他们。
羽涯听着自家阿爸啰嗦了一会儿，同伴也准备好了。
他们跟羽山打了个招呼，背着鱼干，飞往山下。
弯角兽养在山脚洞中，这会儿被羽猎套了绳子，强制牵出来，交给几个小兽人。
“去了那边，问问你羽千叔他们需不需要什么东西，要是有兽人干不下来活儿，你们就跟他们替一下。”
“我们？”
“嗯，你们，是族长说的。”
羽涯想到去年那枯燥的磨尾巴草籽的日子，一脸抗拒，但嘴上没说着拒绝。
经过之前那事，小兽人也懂事不少，像往常那种莽撞去狼部落偷盐的事，现在是做不出来了。
“走吧，最好早点到狼部落，没准还能蹭上一顿饭。”羽猎笑道。
小兽人嘴一撇，走了。
chapters.title: 第143章
chapters.translated_text:
Wolf Mountain.

The orcs were busy with their respective duties until noon, when the sound of Lang An calling everyone to eat rang out again.

Everyone went to the stream to wash their hands, then grabbed their own bowls to serve soup and food.

Since the hunting and gathering team was away, the orcs just ate something simple for lunch to fill their stomachs. There wasn't much game, so lunch was just boiled vegetables with some river shrimp mixed in.

These river shrimp were slightly different from the ones Lin Qiu had seen before; they were on the larger side, with the biggest ones being a palm's length. Although it wasn't their fattest season yet, there is a saying that "spring is for tenderness, summer is for fatness," so the flavor of the river shrimp at this time was not bad at all.

The boiled vegetables were seasoned with only a few grains of salt, highlighting the natural flavor of the food.

The rabbit orcs ate happily; they liked green vegetables to begin with, and the shrimp meat was tender and sweet, making the resulting soup exceptionally fresh.

The wolf orcs, however, didn't like this "grease-stripping" food, but since they were hungry, they just buried their heads and shoveled it into their mouths.

Seeing this, Lin Qiu went to prepare some dipping sauce.

The orcs' eyes lit up, and they moved closer one after another. Lin Qiu shared most of it with them, keeping only a bowl-bottom's worth for himself to dip the shrimp meat in.

The river shrimp didn't taste fishy, and since they were freshly caught, they were at their freshest.

Lin Qiu ate one directly first; the meat was firm and bouncy, exceptionally fresh and sweet. Then he dipped it in the sauce, and the shrimp meat took on a strong herbal flavor, though it didn't overpower that hint of sweetness.

Lin Qiu liked it quite a bit. He peeled one, dipped it in the sauce, and held it to Lang Yan's lips.

Lang Yan turned his head to take it, seeing his mate watching him with a pair of bright eyes.

"Is it good?" Lin Qiu asked.

"It's good," Lang Yan replied.

"If only we had beans, we could make some soy sauce. It would be convenient for both cooking and as a dipping sauce."

"What kind of beans?" Lang Mo leaned over, asking impatiently.

Lin Qiu: "The roots look like they have nodules, the pods are flat, half a finger long, and have fine hairs. They turn yellow when ripe."

The wolf orcs racked their brains, but couldn't think of anything that matched the description.

Lin Qiu: "They might not look exactly like that, either."

The wolf orcs hung their heads in disappointment, "We can't eat them."

All these delicious things Qiu talked about, they couldn't eat.

Lang Yan hadn't spoken, but after placing a few peeled shrimp into Lin Qiu's bowl, he said, "The Beast God Continent is very large; perhaps they grow in some place."

Since Qiu had seen this thing from the Beast God, it must exist on the continent; it was just a matter of whether they could find it.

"If only the market were still open..." Lang An sighed as well.

If the market were open, they might have been able to ask other tribes or orcs from other continents.

Lin Qiu: "Maybe it will reopen once there is more game."

Lang An laughed helplessly: "We might not live to see that."

The orcs stopped talking, quickly finished their food, washed their bowls, and lay down on the ground to rest for a while before going out to work again.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan planned to go to the small cave for a nap, but before they could leave, Lang An said, "King, shouldn't we dig for some salt? We need to store food for the rainy season ahead, and we'll be busy with planting and building houses, so the orcs won't have time."

If they prepared salt at the beginning of the year, they wouldn't have to worry about running out for the rest of the year.

This year, they needed to prepare even more; the branch tribe would be returning before the snow season, and Qiu would also need a lot of salt to cure meat and fish.

Lang Yan: "Wait for Lang Huo to return."

Lang Yan had to ensure that at least two hunting teams were out hunting.

After Lang An mentioned this, he also went into the cave to rest.

In the large cave, Lang Xue was still lying on the wooden table sorting herb seedlings that Lang Bing would plant when he returned in the evening.

Yu Le sorted the herbs that Lang Bing's team had collected over the past few days, processed them himself, and placed them in baskets.

The old priest lay in the grass nest, half-asleep, his wooden staff—the symbol of his status—resting against the wall near the nest.

Since Lang Qi made him a cane, it seemed he hadn't used that staff in a long time.

The cave was quiet, and the orcs' breathing was long and steady.

Wolf orcs only needed to be full to sleep well.

The sun had only come out for a little while today, and it turned overcast in the afternoon. The old priest said it was going to rain, so as soon as the few sub-orcs woke up, they lowered the curtains on the corridor to prevent the fish that hadn't dried yet from getting wet.

Lin Qiu had only slept for a little while; he went to the stream to wash his face, and once he was awake, he began his training.

The tribe was relatively stable now, so Lang Yan followed through on what he had said earlier and personally took him to train.

It wasn't just practicing running, but also catching prey and dealing with enemies.

Lin Qiu first followed behind Lang Yan, running around the front of Wolf Mountain to warm up. One lap in human form, two laps in beast form.

When they ran to the west side, Lang Mo and Lang Rong came out to watch.

When they ran to the east side, the rabbit orcs smiled at him, filled with curiosity.

By the time they reached the front of the mountain, Lang An and the others had simply moved their looms out to weave while watching them train.

Lin Qiu stared at his mate's tail, "I feel like a monkey."

"You don't," Lang Yan said solemnly, "Monkey orcs aren't as good-looking as wolf orcs."

"That's not what I meant..."

"Then you don't look like one either."

After finishing the run, Lin Qiu stood on the packed earth.

He hadn't run in a long time, so after just three laps, his breathing was uneven. In contrast, Lang Yan looked as if he had just taken a stroll, appearing even more relaxed.

Lin Qiu looked at his wolf king's furrowed brows and said with some embarrassment, "How about I run around Wolf Mountain every day?"

"You should run. But rest for now."

"Resting already?"

Lin Qiu had seen the orcs' training before, and Lang Yan hadn't demanded that back then. Was he being too lenient with him?

Lang Yan: "Rest."

Lin Qiu sat directly on the ground, took a deep breath, and let it out.

Compared to these wolf orcs, or even the rabbit orcs, he was really weak.

Lin Qiu couldn't figure out if his original body was just weak from lack of exercise, or if his old body had followed him here.

He hadn't exercised much in the past either, busy with studies and work, but he was still healthy. Yet here, he was a complete burden.

Lin Qiu was lost in thought when his chin was gently lifted.

He looked at Lang Yan, who was kneeling in front of him.

"Don't overthink it, I will help you keep up with the orcs."

"Then I'm counting on you, King."

Lang Yan touched his face, "Okay."

From that day on, Lang Yan began training Lin Qiu.

They started with slow runs to build up his physical fitness, and once he could run ten laps around Wolf Mountain easily, they would add hunting and fighting practice.

The orcs, who had initially just watched for the fun of it, gradually got used to Qiu running and jumping in front of Wolf Mountain. Even the cubs were caught by the King to train alongside Qiu.

Sometimes when Lang Yan wasn't around, Lin Qiu would train according to the routine he had taught. The cubs supervised him, and he supervised the cubs.

However, since they were busy during the day, Lin Qiu sometimes trained early in the morning, and sometimes near dusk.

It was just as the golden sun was setting, the red sun half-intoxicated.

Lin Qiu had just finished training, covered in dust, sitting on the ground watching beads of sweat roll down.

Lang Rong ran back from the north, his face full of joy, shouting: "Qiu! Another baa-baa beast has cubs!"

Lin Qiu wiped the sweat from the corners of his eyes with the back of his hand and stood up, bracing himself against the ground.

"How many?"

"Two!"

Lang Rong was usually quiet, but he was so excited that his voice was unusually loud, and even Lang Qi and Lang An, who were busy in the cave, heard him.

The orcs were delighted and immediately put down what they were doing to follow Lin Qiu over.

The cubs chased behind, one leaping far away, leaving a puff of dust that gently dissipated in their wake.

Now that the baa-baa beasts had adapted to being grazed outside every day, the little wolves didn't all have to stay there.

Sometimes they didn't even need the little wolves to follow them, just coming to check on them occasionally. The baa-baa beasts were released in the morning, and by nightfall, they could return to their enclosure on their own.

It was almost dark, and the baa-baa beasts were heading back.

Lang Rong had discovered the cubs while driving them back; he had just touched one by chance, and never expected to actually feel them, so he immediately came to inform Lin Qiu.

But just as they ran over, they saw the baa-baa beasts munching on the vegetables in the field.

"Hey! The vegetables!" Lang Rong was terrified; he knew the crops in the field were the most important things to the tribe.

The rabbit orcs weren't there, and there were no orcs guarding the field.

Lang Rong sprinted over, shouting, but the baa-baa beasts didn't even lift their heads, chewing even faster.

By the time they drove them out, a patch of the vegetable field was bald.

Lang Rong stood stiffly beside the baa-baa beasts like a wrongdoer, looking at Lin Qiu and the crowd of wolf orcs who had come over with a look of utter helplessness.

Lin Qiu patted the little wolf's head, "It's not your fault."

Lang Rong hung his head even lower, filled with self-reproach.

In the hearts of the orcs, the things in the field were grown by the orcs with great difficulty and effort.

Everyone had guarded them for so long without a mistake, yet it happened just when he left halfway through driving the baa-baa beasts back.

That vegetable patch had been growing exceptionally lushly, and just yesterday he had heard Kui mentioning that it could be harvested today, but now it was chewed into a mess, sparse and ragged.

"It's all my fault," Lang Rong sobbed in a very low voice.

Seeing this, Lang An and the other sub-orcs came up to comfort the little wolf first.

Lin Qiu checked the baa-baa beasts first to confirm the little wolf hadn't been mistaken, then went to check the field.

Hearing the shouting, the rabbit orcs also rushed over, and the moment they saw the field, their hearts skipped a beat.

Seeing the little wolf's red eyes, they immediately put aside their own disappointment and joined in to comfort him.

"They're just vegetables, it's fine, they can grow back," Rabbit Kui said.

Rabbit Teng also leaned on his cane, patting the little wolf's shoulder and saying: "It's just the clover that got eaten the most, but that can be harvested many times; the more you cut it, the more it grows, it's okay."

The baa-baa beasts were surrounded by the orcs, still looking a bit restless.

Lin Qiu saw this and looked at the vegetables in the field. He squatted down and touched the clover that had been nearly chewed bald.

"Kui, are there any clover seeds left?"

"Yes, this grows well, no need to replant."

"Then let's harvest this patch now and give it to the baa-baa beasts, shall we?"

Rabbit Kui was stunned, thinking about how the baa-baa beasts had chewed it into such a state that it was indeed hard to eat, so he nodded: "Okay."

Watching another baa-baa beast find a gap and run into the clover field to start munching, the orcs seemed to understand something.

"Qiu! Do you want to grow this for the baa-baa beasts to eat?" Rabbit Kui asked.

Lin Qiu nodded: "Perhaps we can grow our own pasture."

"Why grow it specifically? There's so much grass on the prairie," Rabbit Ai said in a low voice.

He actually felt a bit regretful; the clover was something they had painstakingly cultivated, and to use it specifically for the baa-baa beasts... it felt a bit wasteful.

Lin Qiu: "It's just to try it out for now."

Lin Qiu looked at this group of increasingly robust baa-baa beasts and explained to the orcs:

"Although there is plenty of grass on the prairie now and it looks like enough to eat, we only have eleven baa-baa beasts. If we raise dozens, hundreds, or even thousands in the future, do you all still think it will be enough?"

"Moreover, the raising of baa-baa beasts is related to whether the orcs can survive for a long time. We cannot rely entirely on them foraging for themselves; we also need to cultivate specialized pasture as a precaution."

"Since we've just happened upon something they like, why don't we try it and see if it can be used as suitable pasture? Isn't that less trouble than cultivating specialized pasture?"

"If it works, we won't have to worry about them having no grass to eat no matter how many baa-baa beasts we raise in the future," Rabbit Kui murmured, having understood Lin Qiu's meaning, and also realizing that the wolf orcs' goal was far beyond just raising a few dozen baa-baa beasts.

What they wanted was to be able to fully support the tribe through animal husbandry and agriculture, and perhaps in the future, not have to go out to forage or hunt, and be able to settle permanently in one place.

Rabbit Kui understood and immediately agreed.

The other orcs understood as well, and a stunning light erupted in their eyes.

"Hundreds, thousands!"

"Then, then how long would it take to finish eating all that..." The orcs felt a bit lightheaded, as if they could see the wonderful days ahead of eating meat every day, every meal.

"Plant it!" Lang An said firmly, "Are there enough orcs? Do you need our help?"

Rabbit Kui shook his head with a smile, "We have the Black Feather orcs."

Although they were currently helping Lang Mo.

Rabbit Ai stood behind Rabbit Kui, looking at the baa-baa beasts for a while, then at the vegetable field. Just when Lin Qiu thought he was still struggling, he said excitedly: "Chief, I'll go get the seeds right now!"

The baa-baa beasts were driven back by Lang Rong, who still looked dull as he walked away.

Didn't the baa-baa beasts ruin the vegetables?

How did it turn into planting pasture?

Were those vegetables for them to eat or for the baa-baa beasts?

Whether the pasture was suitable or not would have to be tested with this batch of baa-baa beasts. It would take a long time, so they would just have to wait and see.

Feeling a chill on his face, Lin Qiu looked up at the sky.

"It's raining again."

It was still bright here, but the east was already dark. Dark clouds slowly gathered, and the red sun that hadn't set yet in the west became even more magnificent.

The rain gradually grew heavier.

The orcs hurriedly hid under the corridor.

"The hunting team hasn't returned yet," Lang An said, shaking the rainwater off his arms.

No sooner had he spoken than he saw several wolf orcs running out of the bushes.

Lang An laughed: "Speak of the devil."

"It's raining, it's raining!" the orcs shouted, rushing into the corridor. They bent their four paws and slid forward on the ground like turtles.

They had just returned from an area with heavy rain, and with that slide, the ground was covered in water.

Lang Mo's team, who were burning bricks in the west, also ran back. They were covered in mud and ash, and after being washed by the rain, their faces were even a bit cleaner.

Today, the hunting team had rarely managed to catch three pieces of game: two sharp-horned beasts and one curved-horned beast.

The orcs were overjoyed, staring from afar at the orcs who were lagging behind carrying the game.

"Why so much today!" the orcs howled excitedly.

Lang Yan shook his fur at the entrance, shedding the rainwater, and walked onto the corridor, a cloth draped over his forehead.

He lifted his head and pressed his nose against his mate's palm.

"Good luck today. We were originally catching sharp-horned beasts, but on the way back, we encountered a curved-horned beast. It's perfect; we'll keep the two curved-horned beasts first and see if we can raise them."

Speaking of this, Lin Qiu, while wiping his fur, said happily: "Today we discovered that the baa-baa beasts like to eat clover."

"They should like other vegetables too."

"But the clover is almost eaten up by them."

"What?!" Lang Yun howled, "We haven't eaten any yet!"

Everyone was waiting for the vegetables the rabbit orcs grew!

How delicious that radish was before the snow season last year!

Lang Mo, whose ears were ringing from his roar, gave him a punch, then wrapped his arm around his neck and chattered on about the pasture.

Hearing about the hundreds or thousands of baa-baa beasts, the wolf orcs laughed foolishly.

"Pasture is good, plant more, plant more!"

The orcs who had been out were all wet, and the old priest looked at them and told them to go into the cave to dry their fur.

It wasn't the time to be careless about getting rained on; if they got sick, the tribe wouldn't have enough herbs.

The orcs of the hunting and gathering team, who had been busy all day, went into the large cave to rest, and the orcs guarding Wolf Mountain began to prepare dinner.

Lang Shi, as usual, took a few orcs out to slaughter the game.

The orcs specifically brought the basin; the hunting team had gone to great lengths to catch them alive, so the blood naturally had to be saved.

The sub-orcs divided the work: some were responsible for starting the fire, some for washing the wild vegetables, and others for preparing side dishes and seasonings.

"Qiu, is it meat soup again?" Lang An asked casually.

Lin Qiu thought about how the baa-baa beasts were mostly lean meat with very little fat, so he said: "We can't touch the sharp-horned beasts, and we should try to make the curved-horned beast last two days. Let's save the bones for tomorrow's soup, and instead make a meat slice soup and stir-fry some wild vegetables with meat."

Lin Qiu had checked, and among the wild vegetables were wild onions and garlic, which would be perfect for adding flavor.

"Alright."

Meat was limited, so for the sake of the future, the orcs had to eat sparingly.

The rain grew heavier, the sound crisp and clear, feeling as comfortable as a massage for the ears.

Lin Qiu continued to watch the firewood for the two pots, though it was a bit inconvenient to feed wood into the stove. He looked at the big black wolf lying beside him with its large head resting on his lap.

He gave the wolf's head a firm rub and said: "It's dusty here."

Lang Yan kept his eyes closed and didn't move; he wasn't leaving, no matter what.

Lin Qiu pinched his ear and whispered: "Rascal."

The few sub-orcs just laughed, their hands moving even more nimbly. They were just busy trying to finish dinner quickly so the orcs who had been running around all day could eat and rest early.

The water under the eaves hung like strings of pearls, and the wind blowing in carried moisture and a faint scent of grass and trees. Lin Qiu liked this smell and couldn't help but take a deep breath, seemingly catching a whiff of sweet floral fragrance.

It had been a long time since he'd eaten anything sweet...

The tribe's honey didn't last; they had used some for cold drinks during the rainy season, mixed a little with hot water during the winter, or used a bit while cooking, and it had been used up without them realizing it.

Now, as Lin Qiu recalled the taste, he actually felt a bit greedy.

He swallowed, and couldn't help but hook his fingers into the soft, bouncy, and velvety fur of the ears, stirring them.

Lang Yan's tail flicked, and he dozed off while sniffing his mate's scent.

Not long after, Lang Shi returned with a large piece of fatty meat and two strips of lean meat. They were all cleaned and ready to be cut and cooked.

Behind him, Lang Mu brought back a basin of blood.

The basin was covered with large leaves, and although his own head was covered in rainwater, the blood had been well protected.

The blood would be saved for tomorrow morning; the sub-orcs would focus on tonight's meal first.

Lang Shi and Lang Mu put the things down and went out again.

Now they knew that the internal organs of the game could be eaten, so they had to be processed carefully. It was all meat, and it would be a shame to throw any of it away.

Lin Qiu watched them return to the stream from afar and frowned.

"We need to build a shed by the stream too."

"Yes, if it doesn't rain tomorrow, I'll tell Lang Mu and the others to build one," Lang An said.

Thinking of the things Lang Mu and the others had in their hands, he added: "I wonder if the large stone mill over at Qi's place is finished yet?"

Now Lang Mu and the others not only had to be responsible for patrolling Wolf Mountain, but also had to help Qi.

Lang Mo's side was even more tied up.

The guard team... it was funny to say, but the guard team was down to just Lang Shi running to the mountain peaks every day.

"Uncle Qi still has to make more farm tools, he can't keep up with everything."

"There are too few orcs," they both sighed at the same time.

Lin Qiu poked at Lang Yan's fur to let the fire roast it evenly, and seeing him not speaking, he moved more gently.

It seemed the game wasn't easy to catch; they must have run very far today.

The sharp-horned beast the tribe had before had also adapted to life in captivity, and was easier to raise than the previous curved-horned beasts.

Now that these two had arrived, he wondered if the sharp-horned beasts could adapt to life in captivity like the baa-baa beasts and produce offspring.

Actually, if the curved-horned beasts could also be domesticated, it would be best for the orcs.

The curved-horned beasts were large; the bigger ones were three times the size of a baa-baa beast.

Unfortunately, their temper was too stubborn.

Lin Qiu wasn't considering domesticating the curved-horned beasts for now, but he didn't intend to give up either; he would just have to see if there was an opportunity later.

The baa-baa beasts were being raised well for now, and there were no problems for the time being.

But one type wasn't enough; they still had to try the sharp-horned beasts. It was just that there were so few sharp-horned beasts, and he didn't know how long it would take to catch enough to form a herd.

*

Stir-frying used oil, but the aroma was overbearing.

The scent of the stir-fried oil drifted into the large cave, and in a moment, the orcs under the corridor lined up with their bowls.

Seeing this, Lang An could only speed up his stir-frying.

Cooking food for the entire tribe wasn't easy; the sub-orcs used to be weak from not eating enough, but now they had built up muscles from wielding the ladles.

Lin Qiu looked at the queue, then at the black wolf head resting on his lap.

He gently tugged on the wolf's whiskers and said: "Time to eat."

Lang Yan's ears twitched, and he buried his head deeper into Lin Qiu's stomach.

Lin Qiu's eyes were clear and bright, carrying a hint of a smile, like the wind carrying raindrops—fresh, crisp, and with the gentleness of looking at family.

After dinner, the orcs washed up and went to sleep.

Everyone was walking toward the cave one after another when they suddenly heard a creaking sound in the woods.

The orcs were alert, staring at the forest.

Lang Huo had finally managed to bring back bird droppings on a rainy day, looking disheveled and miserable, and had been sustained solely by the belief of eating that dinner at Wolf Mountain.

Who knew that when he arrived at Wolf Mountain, looking at the empty pots and smelling the lingering aroma of meat in the air, Lang Huo depressedly covered his nose and lay down.

"Hungry..."

Seeing this, Lang An had no choice but to make them the same meat slice soup and stir-fry they had for dinner.

It was fortunate that they had caught a curved-horned beast; if it had been any other game, there would have been no meat left.

Lang Yan saw him return and had originally planned to arrange a team of orcs to go collect salt tomorrow. But seeing how tired they were, he finally decided to let Lang Huo's team rest for a day and talk about it the day after.

*

Black Feather Tribe.

The orcs had been hunting since the snow melted, and they had been busy until now. They had caught some game, but they had only caught two curved-horned beasts that they had promised to the Wolf Tribe.

The Black Feather orcs had originally planned to keep them in captivity for a while and send them over once they had accumulated enough.

As it turned out, the curved-horned beasts had a violent temper and refused to eat, and seeing them getting thinner and thinner, Yu Shan simply sent Yu Ya and the others to deliver these two curved-horned beasts first.

It had been raining for the past few days, and as soon as the rain stopped, Yu Ya and the other young orcs immediately took action.

Before leaving, Yu Chang pulled his cub aside and exhorted: "These two curved-horned beasts were hard for the tribe to catch, don't lose them on the way. It doesn't matter if you walk slowly, take some dried fish to eat if you get hungry on the road."

There was no help for it; the closer they got to the third month after the snow melted, the more tense the atmosphere in the Black Feather Tribe became.

The adult orcs couldn't leave, and didn't dare to, so they could only let the young orcs make the trip.

They were all young orcs who were almost adults; if they couldn't even handle this, the other adult orcs would be even less at ease leaving things to them.

Yu Ya listened to his father's nagging for a while, and his companions were ready too.

They greeted Yu Shan, shouldered their dried fish, and flew down the mountain.

The curved-horned beasts were kept in a cave at the foot of the mountain, and at this moment, they were roped by Yu Lie and forcibly led out to be handed over to the young orcs.

"When you get there, ask Uncle Yu Qian and the others if they need anything. If there are any orcs who can't finish their work, you can take their place."

"Us?"

"Yes, you, it's what the Chief said."

Yu Ya thought of the tedious days of grinding tail-grass seeds last year and looked resistant, but he didn't refuse out loud.

After the previous incident, the young orcs had become much more sensible, and the kind of reckless stealing of salt from the Wolf Tribe they used to do was no longer something they would do.

"Go on, it's best to get to the Wolf Tribe early; you might even be able to get a meal," Yu Lie laughed.

The young orc curled his lip and left.

Yu Ya and his companions had just finished the arduous task of driving two curved-horn beasts to the Wolf Mountain territory, not far from the salt cave, when they heard the clinking and clanking of hammering.

"Are there thieves?" the young orc subconsciously thought someone was stealing salt.

The orcs inside the cave walked out, looked at the two curved-horn beasts, and said with a grin, "Where would thieves come from?"

"You guys are here! Then this curved-horn beast..."

Lang Qiao waved his hand, "Take them to Wolf Mountain yourselves; we won't be going back yet."

"You have to go back eventually anyway."

Lang Qiao said nothing more and went back into the cave.

Yu Ya stared at the dark, gloomy cave, curled his lip, and continued driving the curved-horn beasts forward.

His companion behind him asked, "Are we still going?"

"Of course, or should we just leave them here?"

"That... that's so much trouble."

...

"It's no trouble," Lang Qiao said to his fellow orcs inside the cave.

When they first arrived here, the orcs of the Black Feather tribe had already noticed them.

At that time, Yu Shan had come down directly and told them to let a few young orcs stay in their tribe for a few days, and exchange them for a few adult orcs to return.

Lang Qiao still clearly remembered the troubled look in his eyes at that time.

Lang Qiao also understood that this was the Black Feather orcs preparing for the attack from the Wilderness tribe.

It was obvious that they wanted to use the Wolf tribe to keep these young orcs safe, but they didn't want to tell the young orcs directly.

It just so happened that the adult orcs had been working on their side for some time, so it was reasonable for the young orcs to come over and swap with the adult orcs who were tired from working.

Moreover, it wasn't as if the Wolf tribe hadn't accepted young orcs to work before, so they wouldn't be suspicious.

After hearing this, the wolf orcs stopped asking.

Dead curved-horn beasts were hard to transport, and live ones were hard to drive, but the work was the Black Feather orcs' job anyway; they would just focus on digging salt.

The tribe needed a lot this time, so they would have to keep digging here for a long time.

When they came, the King had even told them to bring the pots, almost as if he were telling them to stay here and boil the salt before returning.

Of course, boiling it here was impossible.

The conditions here were too primitive; it was better to go through the trouble of transporting it back to Wolf Mountain.

The orcs remaining at Wolf Mountain could handle the salt boiling; they were the hunting team, and the tribe's food supply depended on them. Working away for a short time was fine, but a long time definitely wouldn't work.

After the young orcs left, Yu Lie, who had been following behind watching, flew down and walked to the entrance of the cave where the wolf orcs were digging salt.

The wolf orcs glanced at him and then buried their heads back into digging salt.

Lang Yun said bluntly, "Are you really planning to just wait for death?"

Lang Qiao gave the little white wolf a slap on the forehead, "If you can't speak well, don't speak."

Didn't he see that Yu Lie's expression was ugly?

Yu Lie didn't have to go out today, so he simply walked into the cave and found a place to sit down.

He even had the mood to say, "If we die, those orcs guarding the south will just happen to occupy our tribe. Then you'll have new neighbors."

"Southern tribe? White Sparrow?"

"What White Sparrow, it's the Black Bear tribe."

"Black Bear?" Lang Qiao clawed the rock salt into powder, his expression becoming more serious.

"How big is the tribe, how many orcs? When did they come?"

Yu Lie looked at him for a long time, moved his mouth, but in the end, didn't say what he wanted to say.

He smiled nonchalantly, picked up the bow and arrows the orcs had left to the side to fiddle with, and said, "How big could they be? About two hundred orcs. Black Bears make up half, and there are Feather clans and Cat clans too."

Lang Qiao stared at him for a while, then turned his head and continued digging.

"You don't believe me?"

"Really don't believe me? I don't tell lies."

There was only the sound of digging salt in the cave.

"Heh, as expected, I can't fool you."

Yu Lie looked at the sturdy wolf orcs in the cave and said in a daze, "Don't worry, they can't threaten you. It's just a small tribe, but they do have all the orcs I mentioned."

Lang Qiao: "If you're free, why don't you help out?"

Yu Lie stood up and walked out.

"I'm busy too, I'm leaving."

Lang Qiao gave a scoff and continued working.

After Yu Lie left, Lang Yun asked, "Captain, is what Yu Lie said about the orc tribe true or false?"

"Regardless of whether it's true or false, if they dare to run to our tribe, we'll just dig a hole and bury them."

Lang Yun gave two sinister laughs.

"I'm good at digging holes."

*

South of the Black Feather tribe, in a valley.

Xiong Chen led the orcs all the way south until they reached this place to settle down.

They searched the entire valley and only found two caves. They cleaned them out, with the cubs and sub-orcs in one cave, and the rest of the orcs in the other.

Inside the cave, Xiong Chen found many black feathers, all belonging to the Feather clan.

He sniffed the scent and threw them far away.

At this moment, the orcs were gathered together; the sub-orcs and cubs were not in this cave.

Xiong Chen looked at the two gray-winged orcs in front of him who were so hungry they were licking their lips, and said, "Did you scout it out?"

The two gray-winged orcs nodded.

"In the stone forest nearby are the White Sparrow orcs."

"To their north is the Wolf tribe."

"There are only these few tribes in the vicinity."

The gray-winged orcs were smaller in size than the Black Feather orcs.

Their feathers were grayish-white, and their speed was incredibly fast. Their weapons were also sharp claws and beaks, but with the added speed, even the Black Feather orcs had to be careful when fighting them.

The two gray eagle orcs were named Hui Zuo and Hui You, and they were brothers from the same nest.

Xiong Chen: "Didn't you find out how many orcs the Wolf tribe has?"

The two orcs shook their heads.

Hui Zuo said, "South of that body of water to the east, there is a team of twenty or so wolf orcs digging things there."

"Digging what?"

Hui Zuo hesitated, "...It looks like bird droppings."

"Bird droppings?" Xiong Chen frowned, looking disgusted.

The wolf orcs had actually fallen to this point.

"Should we go to their tribe and take a look?" Hui Zuo asked tentatively.

The cave was dim, and dozens of pairs of eyes were glowing as they looked over.

Xiong Chen said, "Didn't you hear what those Feather clan members said earlier?"

*

Yu Ya and the others drove the curved-horn beasts from their tribe to Wolf Mountain, stopping and starting along the way, struggling with the beasts.

What should have been a half-day flight took an entire day of walking.

It was dark, and the Wolf Mountain hunting team hadn't caught any decent prey today, only several nests of red birds, both big and small.

If they ate them, there was little meat;

If they didn't eat them, they felt uncomfortable without meat.

Lin Qiu looked at the red birds, all with chicks, and simply told Lang Rong to keep them, deciding to continue eating the curved-horn beast from yesterday tonight.

They hadn't touched much of the remaining meat during the day, only making blood tofu and organ soup in the morning. In the evening, they made soup with the remaining bones and made meatballs with the rest of the meat.

But with this way of eating, the meat was all used up.

The orcs ate until they were satisfied, their bellies full, and suddenly they had no worries at all.

As for whether they could catch prey tomorrow, they would worry about that tomorrow.

The first batch of salt hadn't been transported back yet. After dinner, Lang An and the others didn't rush to sleep, but first went to take out the clay pots and jars used for boiling salt to clean them.

The shed by the creek had also been built, so they just put them in there to dry after washing.

After cleaning up, the orcs planned to go back.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan were walking up the mountain when they suddenly stopped.

Other orcs who were still washing looked over, their eyes widening, and they grinned, making the orcs' hair stand on end.

"Yu Ya, why did you guys come over?" a Black Feather orc asked as he flew over directly.

Yu Ya was exhausted, leaning on a wooden stick at the edge of the forest, looking at the orcs from afar, not wanting to move a step.

The wolf orcs were proactive, quickly driving the two curved-horn beasts back. They also grabbed the young orcs and brought them over.

They even kindly asked, "Have you eaten yet?"

Yu Ya: "Not yet."

Lang An was just about to get them something to eat when Yu Qian immediately walked out with his tribesmen. He said gently, "An, you guys go rest, I'll get it for them."

Yu Qian directly told his tribesmen to go catch fish.

He had watched the wolf orcs make meat soup many times and wanted to try to see if he could make it himself.

The young orcs were lying on the ground, so hungry they had no strength left; the dried fish had been eaten on the road, so they weren't picky now.

The wolf orcs weren't in a hurry to sleep either, excitedly surrounding the two curved-horn beasts and looking at them again and again.

"They're just a bit thin."

"Should we raise them for a while before eating?"

"Forget it, it's not like we haven't raised them before; the more we raise them, the thinner they get."

Looking at the state of the curved-horn beasts, the Black Feather orcs must have raised them for a while after catching them before sending them over. If they couldn't raise them well, why bother raising them more?

The orcs discussed how to eat the curved-horn beasts. Lang Rong glanced at them and threw some grass that the baa-baa beasts ate in front of the curved-horn beasts.

Seeing that they didn't eat at all, he was used to it and just used a broken jar to put some water next to them.

Wolf Mountain was lively for a while, then everyone was chased to sleep by Lang Yan.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan also left, and for a time, only the Black Feather orcs were left under the corridor.

Yu Le was also there, sitting in a corner, quietly listening to Yu Ya and the others talk about things in the tribe.

His life in the Wolf tribe was very regular; every day when the hunting team woke up, Yu Le woke up too.

Afterward, he would eat with everyone, and after eating, he would complete the tasks left by Lang Bing every day. In the evening, when Lang Bing came back, Yu Le would learn from him for a while before sleeping.

Listening to his companions' voices, he folded his hands on the table, and before he knew it, his head rested down, and he gradually closed his eyes amidst the fading sounds.

Yu Qian looked at Yu Le, who looked like he was asleep, and then at Yu Ya.

He had grown sensible, knowing how to look out for his companions.

When the tribe matters were finally discussed, he heard Yu Ya ask, "Uncle Qian, do you have any orcs who are tired from working? Uncle Shan told us to swap with you."

Yu Qian's hand, which was filleting fish, paused, his eyelashes drooping to hide the change in his eyes.

How could he not understand his partner's meaning?

He said softly, "There are quite a few orcs. But the Wolf tribe has a lot of work, and there's never a moment of rest, can you handle it?"

Upon hearing this, Yu Ya looked at the uncles sitting in front of the fire.

They all had hunched shoulders, looking extremely tired. He clenched his fists, gritted his teeth, and said, "Don't worry, I can do it."

"We can too," the other young orcs said.

Yu Ya and the other young orcs had already started hunting with Yu Lie and the others in the tribe, but they weren't as capable as the adult orcs; they didn't fly fast, nor did they fly far. Often, the adult orcs would have to stop and wait for them after flying for a distance.

Since the snow melted, Yu Ya and the others had been going out with Yu Shan or Yu Lie. Such days were very different from before, and very tiring, but they all persisted.

And their small team could catch prey on their own now!

Yu Qian, however, appeared hesitant and said, "You need to think clearly; once the other orcs go back to rest, there will be no orcs to swap with you. The work here cannot be delayed."

"We have thought it through," Yu Ya said earnestly.

Yu Qian looked intently at these young orcs and smiled with relief, "That's good. I'll talk to Qiu and the others tomorrow to see if they agree."

Yu Ya glanced at the sleeping Yu Le, "Is Le not going back either?"

Yu Qian's eyes grew even softer, as if carrying a faint hope, gently enveloping Yu Ya and the other young orcs.

"Yes, he still needs to continue learning."

*

The next morning, after breakfast, Yu Qian went directly to ask Lang Yan.

Having obtained the Wolf King's consent, Yu Qian selected six adult orcs to swap with the young orcs.

The remaining four adult orcs stayed here to watch over the young orcs and, if necessary, stop them from returning to the Black Feather tribe.

Once the orcs who were leaving were determined, Yu Qian went with them to pack their things.

Before leaving, he looked at the young orcs following behind and smiled, "Listen to your other uncles in the Wolf tribe. Don't just bury your heads in work; learn and observe more. It will be good for you in the future."

"We know, Uncle Qian, don't worry, we will definitely work hard."

If he said anything more, he would give the game away. Yu Qian finally patted Yu Le's head, "Uncle Qian is leaving, don't be afraid, Yu Ya and the others are here."

"Mm." Yu Le's eyes were clear, his voice tinged with a sob.

Yu Qian took one last look at this young orc who seemed to understand everything, turned, and left with the orcs.

Yu Le watched blankly, his lips trembling. When he turned back to face Yu Ya and the others, he had already suppressed all his emotions.

He couldn't always cry; only by learning things well could he protect the tribe.

Yu Le went into the cave; he still had to complete the tasks Lang Bing had given him.

Yu Ya and the others didn't think about playing either; they followed behind the remaining four adult Black Feather orcs and did whatever needed to be done.

The other young orcs who had just arrived at the Wolf tribe were still a bit curious, looking around as they walked, their eyes never leaving the sights.

Yu Ya was silent, feeling that something was a bit strange, but he couldn't put his finger on what.

"Ya! The Wolf tribe is so different from our tribe... what are they growing in that big patch of land over there?"

Yu Ya's train of thought was interrupted. He glanced in the direction the young orc was pointing and said, "Tail grass."

"That's tail grass!"

Their chief was still talking about it when he went back; the Wolf tribe had cultivated a plant that could fill their stomachs, so it turned out to be this.

Wolf Mountain had a lot of work. Besides following the rabbit orcs to work in the fields, the Black Feather orcs spent the rest of their time helping Lang Mo make bricks and tiles in the west. Sometimes they had to weave cloth, or help catch fish...

The young orcs saw how tiring it was on their first day of work.

They grumbled in their hearts; no wonder they were asked to come and swap; the weak uncles couldn't handle it.

It had to be them; they could sleep after being tired and be full of energy again the next day.

*

It was still early, and the hunting and gathering team gathered in front of Wolf Mountain after breakfast. This time, Lin Qiu was also in the team.

He had been training for some days and needed to put it into practice.

Most of the tribe's affairs were on the right track, and there were captains in charge of everything. The priest was also there, so it wouldn't be a problem if he left for a while.

Today they were going south, and Lin Qiu planned to go see the Great Marsh.
