The sunlight was a bit dazzling; he watched the little wolves busy laying bricks, their hair tied up casually with animal skin strips or tree bark, dripping with sweat, their bodies shining as if coated in oil.

After another while, Lang Yan had finished a basket of mushrooms and felt his knee being lightly scratched again.

He looked down and saw his partner’s eyes looking as if they were covered in mist, moist and hazy.

Lang Yan frowned, curling his knuckles to brush across the corner of his eye.

"Are you uncomfortable?"

Lin Qiu grabbed his finger, his voice soft: "King... how are cubs born?"

Lang Yan’s breath hitched.

Lin Qiu climbed up from his fingers, grabbing his wrist, pulling on his arm, and then sat up himself.

He leaned close to Lang Yan’s ear, his breathing slightly ragged, the corners of his eyes flushed red, looking extremely embarrassed.

Lang Yan’s Adam’s apple bobbed; one hand hovered behind Lin Qiu’s waist, and he felt his breathing turn hot. He tilted his head slightly and said, "I don't really know either."

Lin Qiu buried his head in the crook of his neck, rubbed against it hard twice, and then sat up straight.

"Scared?" Lang Yan gripped Lin Qiu’s wrist.

"No."

For a moment, neither of them spoke.

It was so quiet between them that only the sound of bricks being hammered next door remained.

"Okay, maybe a little," Lin Qiu said.

"I'll go ask."

"Don't!" Lin Qiu grabbed his hand, the flush spreading from his neck to his cheeks. Although shy, his eyes were soft, bright, and clear, showing he had his own ideas.

"Wait until I'm ready."

Lang Yan looked at his partner’s flushed but serious face, and suddenly, he lowered his head and pressed against him.

"I only hope you are well; I haven't considered anything else."

He had seen sub-beastmen pregnant; over the years, beastmen had little food, and if a sub-beastman had a cub, it would be very obvious.

They were very thin, so a belly that was only slightly larger was very noticeable.

It was like a monster parasitizing the beastman’s belly, absorbing the sub-beastman’s nutrients; often, after giving birth to one cub, they would become gaunt and unrecognizable.

Some would even die.

Either the sub-beastman, or the cub, or both.

The more Lang Yan thought, the more afraid he became.

He couldn't help but press his palm against the back of Lin Qiu’s neck, bringing his face even closer.

"Don't think about those things."

"Cough!"

Lin Qiu was startled and instinctively tried to dodge. Lang Yan anticipated it and supported his back, not letting him twist too much.

Lang An: "What are you thinking about? You look like you're about to cry."

Lin Qiu was embarrassed; laughing, he reached for the knife Lang Yan had just used and tried to continue cutting mushrooms.

Lang Yan and Lang An exchanged a look, and Lang Yan asked, "Are the mushrooms nearby all picked?"

Lang An: "Just about, they'll grow again soon. Qiao and the others should be here by now..."

"They must be here." It was Lang Huo’s voice.

Seeing Lang Huo and the others return, Lang An said happily, "Did you meet Qiao? How is the branch tribe?"

Lang Huo sat down with a thud, lying on the ground.

"We met them, the branch tribe is doing just fine."

Having caught his breath, Lang Huo remembered the important matter and immediately climbed up.

"King, was our tribe ambushed by wandering beastmen?"

"Yes."

"I felt something was wrong with those two Black Bear Tribe beastmen from the start. Did they run away? I'll go catch them!"

"Enough, you should get some rest; it's already over."

Lang Huo sat up abruptly, wanting to ask more, but the King ignored him, and Qiu looked...

"Qiu! Are your injuries bad?" Lang Huo leaned in, only to be blocked by a yam held by Lang Yan against his chest.

Lang Huo: "King! I'm anxious, can you tell me carefully?"

The members of Lang Huo’s team behind him also nodded, their eyes full of anger.

Lang Yan glanced at his partner.

Lin Qiu: "I'll tell you."

He was bored and had time.

Lin Qiu recounted the situation that day, and sounds of indignant beastmen came from the corridor from time to time.

Yu Ya brought a few small Black Feather beastmen to move bricks, looked inside, and said, "Lang Huo is back."

"Then their branch tribe’s beastmen will be back soon too," a companion said.

"Ya, when are we going back?" another small Black Feather beastman asked.

Although they ate and lived well in the Wolf Tribe, they missed their own tribe.

Yu Ya put down the bricks, and before he could answer, Lang Xi, who was busy laying walls, said, "Yu Ya, send some bricks over here!"

"Coming!"

He touched the red wall in front of him and said to his companion, "Have you forgotten what Uncle A-Shan and the others said?"

They were here to work, and also to learn.

The tribe had lost many uncles; they were grown up now and couldn't always rely on them. They had to learn things from the Wolf Tribe so that when they returned, they could make their own tribe better.

The Black Feather beastmen returned to the busy work of building houses, while the other few Black Feather beastmen followed the rabbit beastmen to work in the fields.

From sowing to harvesting, the beastmen came to look at the fields almost every day.

Tu Kui was patrolling the fields, taking the opportunity to set down another batch of traps for squeaky-beasts. Now that the archer team was rotating guard duty in the fields, the number of squeaky-beasts had decreased significantly.

The tail-grass in the fields was growing extremely well, already calf-high and flowering and setting seeds.

When the wind blew, the tail-grass rustled, the emerald green grass waves rising and falling.

Tu Kui felt a great sense of accomplishment looking at it.

He carefully walked through the entire tail-grass field and circled back from the riverbank.

In this field near the riverbank, hemp grass was planted on the far east side.

Now the hemp grass was taller than the beastmen. The rabbit beastmen managed it by referencing the wild growth environment, ensuring enough fertilizer and water, and with no weeds competing for nutrients, this first year of planting looked more uniform than the wild ones.

But it was only uniform, not particularly high-yielding.

Tu Kui pinched the palm-sized leaves, which were soft and fuzzy.

He snapped it from the tip and saw the skin attached; it wasn't as tender as before, so it should be ready for harvest.

For the first year of sowing, not having a total crop failure was a good result.

Tu Kui and the others were experienced in planting and naturally knew that cultivating high-quality crops required year after year of selection.

This couldn't be rushed and needed careful exploration.

This hemp grass field was enough to prove that the rabbit beastmen’s planting skills were not bad; he could guarantee that if other beastmen planted it, it wouldn't be half as good as theirs.

Tu Kui estimated the time until the rainy season and ran toward the corridor.

Passing the tall hemp grass field, a little further on were the vegetable plots and the experimental pasture field where seeds had been re-sown.

Tu Kui had looked at these over and over again, so he was naturally very familiar with them.

He ran forward, his eyes catching a particularly different seedling on the edge of the field, and a second later, he was out of the field.

Under the corridor, Lin Qiu had just finished talking about the tribe’s affairs and was holding the water cup Lang Yan handed him.

Lang Huo, who wanted to start a fight after hearing the story, was pinned down by Lang Yan, grumbling and kicking the air in frustration before rolling away to find a place to catch up on sleep.

Tu Kui rushed over.

"Qiu, King, the hemp grass is ready for harvest."

"I'll go take a look." Lin Qiu said, preparing to rise.

Lang Yan supported his arm, making him move a bit slower.

Arriving at the field, Lin Qiu looked at the hemp grass that was taller than him and muttered, "It's already this tall..."

He hadn't been here for just half a month, and the hemp grass had changed completely.

Lin Qiu snapped off a top section, saw it was mature, and said, "It can be harvested."

"Then I'll call the beastmen," Tu Kui said immediately.

He was the type to do things immediately, but Lin Qiu stopped him: "Kui, leave a portion to seed, and harvest one batch first; don't dig up the roots."

He wanted to see how many batches of hemp grass could be harvested from the field.

Since it was time to harvest, Tu Kui called over several adult Black Feather beastmen, first having them use long poles to knock off the hemp grass leaves so that the harvested hemp grass could be directly soaked in water for processing.

The rabbit beastmen were shorter, so the harvesting work fell to them.

Holding the base of the hemp grass with their left hand, they used a stone sickle with a clever flick to cut it, and the hemp grass fell over. They bundled it into armfuls and tied it directly using a few pieces of hemp grass laid horizontally as rope.

Lin Qiu had just finished watching, and the field was already bustling with activity.

Standing there was in the way, so he walked slowly toward the vegetable plots.

The vegetables in the plots had been eaten several times and were exceptionally tender, tasting great whether in soup or stir-fried. Anything these rabbit beastmen cultivated was top-notch.

Lin Qiu walked slowly along the edge of the land, his gaze sweeping over the harvested clover.

This was what Rong and the others had cut for the baa-baa beasts to eat.

The clover was planted too sparsely and didn't grow as fast as the baa-baa beasts ate it. Next year, they would have to choose a location specifically to plant this pasture.

As Lin Qiu thought while walking, he suddenly noticed a new leaf sprouting in the corner.

The sugarcane had sprouted!

Lin Qiu walked quickly toward it, but before he could take two steps, Lang Yan circled his waist and frowned: "Walk slowly."

He didn't need to lie down all day like before, but he couldn't walk too fast either.

"I know..."

In the blink of an eye, Lin Qiu stood before the crisp sugarcane seedling.

Tu Kui passed by with a bundle of hemp grass and stopped, "The sugarcane has sprouted."

Lin Qiu turned and smiled at him: "Just one."

"There will be more and more in the future."

Tu Kui said this and walked ahead; he was crisp and efficient in his work in the fields, which didn't match his gentle personality at all.

A huge bundle of hemp grass pressed on his back; he had to stop every few steps to adjust it so it wouldn't slip. The beastman’s back was bent, and he could only lift his head halfway to look at the road ahead.

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan: "King, there’s a lot to do in the tribe; don't always follow me."

Lang Yan: "Be good."

Lin Qiu smiled, his appearance handsome and refined.

"Then go ahead, I promise not to move around."

The scorching sun was dazzling, and the golden, scale-like ripples on the river surface attracted the cubs to throw stones into it.

Lang Guo drove the cubs away from the riverbank, his shouts long and drawn out.

Bundle after bundle of hemp grass was placed on a cart, and a giant black wolf pulled it, passing in front of Wolf Mountain and delivering it to the small river on the west side.

The cubs had found a new source of fun.

They scrambled to jump onto the cart, crawled over the hemp grass, climbed onto the big black wolf’s back, and hung themselves on their King like opossum cubs.

The cubs were chubby, and with a dozen of them clustered together, they weren't light.

Yet their King indulged them, not driving them away, and took the cubs on trip after trip.

Lin Qiu sat under the corridor, and every time Lang Yan passed by, he had to look inside.

Lin Qiu raised his paw and waved twice at him, then turned his head to continue cutting mushrooms.

The sun reached its zenith, and Lang Yu and the other sub-beastmen returned. The sub-beastmen were drenched in sweat, and as soon as they put down their baskets, they couldn't wait to wash their faces by the stream.

The stream water was cool, making it the most comfortable thing to soak in right now.

After washing, everyone sat in a circle, started the stove, boiled the wild vegetables, scooped them out into rattan-woven sieves, and moved them into the sunlight to dry.

The sliced mushrooms were also laid out flat in the rattan sieves, red and green colors creating a vibrant display. The mushroom caps were wide and the stalks were plump; the large ones weighed several pounds, while the small ones had just poked out of the mud, chubby and round like cubs.

Spread out outside the corridor, they would be completely dry in just two days.

Lin Qiu helped cut for a while, but Lang An took his knife away.

Lin Qiu was helpless, looking at Lang An, and seeing him watching him with caution, he couldn't help but laugh: "I'm fine, why is everyone treating me like a cub?"

He was an adult; didn't he know his own physical condition?

"Still fine? Look, I'm already healed, but you're not," Lang An said.

Beastmen should recover very quickly; this was something they had evolved over thousands of years, but Qiu was different. Even the priest said his foundation was poor, so he recovered slowly.

Lin Qiu couldn't argue with the beastman and lay listlessly in the grass nest, lost in thought.

He had finally found the point.

Even though his wounds had scabbed over, why were the beastmen still watching him like he was fragile? It turned out it was because his recovery speed was slow.

It was almost noon, and it was time to cook.

The sub-beastmen sped up, finishing the wild vegetables and mushrooms collected today.

Their movements were skillful; they used the thin stone knife blades like iron knives, cutting a mushroom in a few quick motions.

Lang An stood up, washed the pottery pot used to boil the vegetables, and added fresh water to boil.

The tribe was currently scrambling to gather prey for the Green Eye Tribe, so the last half-month had been tight.

Fortunately, the remaining five sharp-horned beasts had been gathered, leaving only two curved-horned beasts.

Today at noon, there were only the animal bones left from yesterday; Lang An picked a few, washed them, and started boiling the soup. Then he told the sub-beastmen still under the corridor to watch the fire while he went to check if there were any fish in the traps set by the river.

Several sounds of flapping wings came from the sky, and the beastmen on Wolf Mountain looked up.

A huge shadow swept across the mountains, and in the sunlight, the grey-black feathers of the Black Feather beastmen shone; they had come to deliver the curved-horned beasts again.

Yu Lie glided to the ground, and the curved-horned beast, which two beastmen were holding together, was gently set down.

The curved-horned beast, its hooves tied, struggled immediately, but being tightly bound, it could only let out a weak cry.

Lang Shi led the patrol team quickly from behind Wolf Mountain to the front, and Yu Lie and the others were already surrounded by wolf beastmen.

Lin Qiu also walked out slowly.

Lang Yan pulled the cart over, and the beastmen automatically stepped aside.

"Wolf King, Qiu."

Yu Lie greeted them first, though he looked a bit awkward.

Lin Qiu understood as soon as he saw the two curved-horned beasts on the ground, which were still cubs.

Lang Yan put down the cart and walked slowly to Lin Qiu’s side. He rubbed his neck against Lin Qiu’s shoulder and then looked at Yu Lie.

"Curved-horned beast cubs?"

Yu Lie’s ears turned red.

He said embarrassedly: "We haven't caught any large curved-horned beasts recently, so the chieftain asked me to come and ask if two curved-horned beast cubs could count as one large curved-horned beast?"

The wolf beastmen looked at each other.

They generally didn't eat prey cubs, and if they caught a mother with cubs, they would let them go.

Even though the curved-horned beast cubs were as big as baa-baa beasts now, they could still grow. The meat of a large curved-horned beast was several times that of a cub.

They wouldn't give up more meat for a little bit of meat right now.

Lang Yan looked at the uncomfortable Black Feather beastmen in front of him and said, "We’ll discuss it."

Yu Lie nodded, and seeing his own little beastman trying to crowd over, he quickly lowered his voice: "It’s okay if you can't; it just means you might have to wait a bit longer."

"Everyone get back to work," Lang Yan said.

The beastmen dispersed, but Yu Ya and the other little beastmen were still walking toward Yu Lie.

They looked at Yu Lie and ran up with a smile, "Uncle Yu Lie!"

Yu Lie looked at the height of the little beastmen and said in surprise, "You’ve grown taller."

"Have we?"

"Yes, and stronger." Yu Lie pinched his own cub’s arm, "Whoa! The muscles are much firmer."

The wolf beastmen were much better at raising cubs than they were.

The Black Feather beastmen caught up, and the beastmen from Lang Huo’s team had slept enough and came out yawning.

They glanced at Yu Lie, greeted him, and then shoved their heads into the ropes in front of the cart, replacing Lang Yan to pull the hemp grass.

Inside the cave, Lang Yan, Lin Qiu, and the priest gathered together.

The old priest held a mortar, grinding medicine powder: "Curved-horned beasts are hard to catch; those few are probably all they could catch in their tribe."

If they wanted to catch more, they would have to wait for other curved-horned beasts to walk into their tribe, or leave their territory and look elsewhere.

Lin Qiu: "Let's just take these two cubs."

Lang Yan: "If you want to raise them, cubs might be easier."

Lin Qiu shook his head, "The rainy season is coming, and it’s been incredibly busy with the baa-baa beasts lately. I can't watch them, and Rong and the others have no time."

Besides, he had seen the temperament of curved-horned beasts; they were very stubborn.

Whether they could be raised well wasn't certain.

If they caught cubs now and didn't have the energy to care for them, wouldn't it be a pity if they died?

He did want to raise them, but he had to be prepared first. Moreover, with the rainy season approaching, the scale of the baa-baa beasts depended on how many they could catch this season.

That was the top priority.

After discussing it, Lang Yan went to find Yu Lie.

Seeing them accept the two cubs, Yu Lie’s face flushed red: "We really haven't caught any large curved-horned beasts recently. Our chieftain knows you raise baa-baa beasts, so he brought them over for you to see."

"Does your tribe have many curved-horned beast cubs?"

"Not many, just these two."

He didn't know if they had been too aggressive in hunting them, but the curved-horned beasts in the tribe were migrating away, making them even harder to find now.

These two cubs counted as one large one; they had already delivered five, and it was unclear how long it would take to catch the remaining fourteen.

Yu Lie had one more thing to ask: whether Lang Yan had thought of his request yet.

The curved-horned beasts were sent because of the valley incident, and Lang Qiao’s help later had to be calculated separately.

Who knew Lang Yan would say directly: "I haven't thought of it, but you can give me fewer."

"What?"

"The rainy season is coming. Use the curved-horned beasts to trade for your tribe’s saltpeter; one beast for one cart, four carts for now. If you agree, just bring them next time."

Yu Lie nodded blankly, "Okay, I’ll go back and ask the chieftain."

Regardless, his business here was done.

Yu Lie and a few clansmen had a meal at the Wolf Tribe and flew back.

As the days grew longer, the hammering sounds of the canteen construction never stopped. They hammered by day and by night, and the beastmen went from covering their ears to sleep to gradually adapting.

Finally, the canteen was roofed and finished just before the rainy season.

The house, built of red bricks and grey tiles, was spacious and square, with the main entrance facing the rammed-earth square in the middle and a side door attached to the corridor, allowing direct access from the large cave.

From now on, regardless of wind or rain, the beastmen could sit in the canteen and eat comfortably.

However, it wasn't quite ready yet.

Although the door and window frames were installed, there was nothing inside.

The stove that had originally collapsed halfway was included, and the rest was still being repaired.

The canteen was planned with a dining area in the front and a cooking and serving window in the back, but for now, it remained in the planning stage and hadn't been started.

So, the entire canteen was currently just an empty room with a few stoves.

Whether they would have chairs to sit on and tables to place food on depended on whether Lang Qi was busy.

But these were not important for now; as long as the house was ready, the returning branch tribe beastmen wouldn't have to worry about having nowhere to sleep.
chapters.source_text:
天气炎热，时不时下一阵雨，林子里和草原上的蘑菇逐渐多了起来。
雨季即将来临，支部落的兽人还要回来一部分，狼山这边的兽人都在加紧储存一些能吃的食物，以免饿肚子。
最近这段日子，林楸只能趴着养伤。
他看着狼安他们布也不织了，一有空闲就钻林子里采集。但凡是能吃的，蘑菇、嫩叶、野果、块根……只要入了他的眼，就没跑了的。
部落里的蘑菇小山似的堆起来。
林楸出不去，就专门待在只剩半截的廊道下帮忙处理各种野菜蘑菇，晒成干儿以便储存。
旁边不远，狼莫带着小狼他们忙着建食堂。
一批又一批的砖运过来，兽人们就在旁边整天敲敲打打。甚至为了赶工，自发开始日夜轮班。
这样做的好处就是，短短半月，房子建了半人高。坏处也显而易见，狼兽人们都瘦了。
狼莫小队还得负责巡逻，连睡懒觉的时间都没有。
小狼们精神好，但也禁不住这么熬，一旦休息就是趴在地上睡觉。
林楸看在眼里，心里急，手上也急。
锋利的小刀险些擦过掌心。
坐在他身边的狼岩眼疾手快，一把抓住他手腕，夺了他的刀。
林楸瞧着掌心破开的大蘑菇，动了动手指，试图把刀拿回来。
狼岩把小刀放在自己另一边，道：“休息一会儿。”
林楸：“不用，我不累。”
狼岩就盯着他，不说话了。
林楸脑袋往他肩膀上一磕。
如今兽人们都只穿兽皮裙或短裤，上半身赤裸，狼岩也不例外。
林楸额头贴上去，就感觉像撞了墙一样，还挺滑溜。
“我刚刚只是走神了。”
狼岩小心护住他后背，下颌绷紧。
“休息。”
他刚刚说要动一动，狼岩让他动了会儿了，该继续趴着了。
林楸叹一口气，趴了下来。
他受伤之后，狼岩就没有再出去过，整日就守着他，盯着他，跟看犯人似的。
偏偏部落的其他兽人还默认，当伴侣的就该这样，就算狼王也不例外。林楸想找借口让狼岩出去都不行。
“我的伤应该要好了。”
“嗯。”狼岩声音发紧。
林楸的衣服薄，趴下后就能看得见背上的伤。
最严重的地方是几个嵌入脊骨附近的爪印，深可见骨，起初每天都得用草药水冲洗。
现在快半个月，附近的肉没有溃烂，慢慢结痂了。
余下地方伤口早已经愈合，有些地方结痂掉了，新长出来的红肉绕着脊骨蜿蜒而下，有些凸起，那是兽人爪印深深划过的痕迹，看着很是碍眼。
狼岩每每看见，都暗恨自己没考虑周全。
狼岩轻轻把林楸后衣摆往下拉了拉，遮住露出来的一截腰身，然后收敛心绪，继续干活。
连廊里的蘑菇野菜堆成小山，檐下以及旁边的空地上则挂满了处理好的鱼。
一眼望去，密密麻麻，仿若置身在某个渔村旁边。
兽人们为雨季做足了准备。
大伙儿都在忙，就林楸无聊得不行。
连兔艾他们都恢复得差不多了，现在吊着个手臂，还能忙着地里的事。
林楸无聊地揪着草窝边缘的干草，目光悠悠晃晃，落到一旁继续切蘑菇的狼岩身上。
欣赏了会儿狼王的英武酷帅，林楸忍不住拽了拽他裤腿。
狼岩垂眸，顺手将厚薄均匀的蘑菇片放进旁边的藤筐中。
他手背碰了下林楸发红的耳朵，道：“祭司说了，差点伤到骨头，要养。”
林楸：“你要不捡几个红鸟蛋给我孵？”
他好无聊！
林楸随意一句玩笑，却没想到狼岩看了他许久。
半晌，狼岩低头，粗硬的长发滑落肩膀，发尾扫在林楸脸上。痒痒的，林楸伸手去摸。
可下一瞬，狼岩的话让他呆若木鸡。
“想要幼崽了？”
林楸甚至不小心一下攥紧狼岩的头发，拉得笔直。
狼岩只看着他在墨发下衬得更加白皙漂亮的手指，微微弯腰。
他手撑着草窝，近距离观察着自己的伴侣。
脸上不见喜色，只有呆。
傻傻的，眼珠都不动一下，直愣愣地只知道看着他。
狼岩嘴角勾起一抹笑意，不过也没打扰林楸，而是侧头继续切蘑菇。
过了好一会儿，眼前的一堆蘑菇少去大半。
狼岩膝上有些痒，他看过去，就见他的伴侣一截手指搭在他腿上，挠啊挠，挠得他心乱。
“渴了？还是饿了？”
林楸摇摇头，看着狼岩的脸。
他要是有幼崽，一定又酷又帅。
不过林楸不是说这个，他道：“那建好的两座房子，还没分呢。”
狼岩：“部落有伴侣的兽人不多，等支部落那边的兽人来了，让他们一起抽签吧。”
虽说分开多年，但在他们心里，狼部落始终是一个部落，不好厚此薄彼。
林楸收回手，垫在自己下巴处。
阳光有些灼眼，他看着小狼们忙着砌墙，头发随意用兽皮条或者树皮扎着，大汗淋漓，身上仿佛涂了一层油似的发亮。
又过了会儿，狼岩已经切好一筐蘑菇，又感觉到膝上被轻轻挠了挠。
他垂眸看去，自家伴侣眼睛像蒙了一层雾，湿润朦胧。
狼岩蹙眉，曲着指节擦过他眼尾。
“不舒服了？”
林楸抓住他手指，声音温吞：“王……幼崽要怎么生啊？”
狼岩呼吸一滞。
林楸从他手指攀着往上，抓着他手腕，扒着他胳膊，然后自个儿坐起来。
他凑近狼岩的耳边，呼吸微乱，眼尾霞红，像不好意思极了。
狼岩喉结滚了滚，一手虚扶着他后腰，感觉呼吸都烫了起来。他微微偏头，道：“我也不太清楚。”
林楸闷头藏进他颈窝，狠狠蹭了两下，然后板板正正坐直。
“害怕？”狼岩握住林楸手腕。
“没有。”
一时间，他俩都没说话。
两人之间安静得只剩下隔壁传来的咚咚敲砖的声音。
“好吧，有一点。”林楸道。
“我去问问。”
“别！”林楸抓住他的手，红润从脖子蔓延到脸颊，虽有些羞赧，但目光柔亮清澈，自有主意。
“你等我准备好。”
狼岩看着伴侣红润但认真的脸，忽然，低头贴了上去。
“我只希望你好好的，其他的事，我没考虑过。”
亚兽人怀崽他见过，这些年，兽人们本就没什么食物，亚兽人要是有了幼崽就会很明显。
他们很瘦，所以只微微大一点的肚子就很明显。
那像一个寄生在兽人肚子上的怪物，吸收亚兽人的营养，往往生一个幼崽，他们会瘦脱了相。
有些还会死。
或者是亚兽人，或者是幼崽，或者他们一起。
狼岩越想，越有些怕了。
他忍不住掌心贴着林楸后颈，将脸贴得更近。
“别想那些了。”
“咳！”
林楸一惊，下意识要躲开。狼岩提前预判，扶着他的后背，没叫他扭得太过。
狼安：“想什么呢？看着都要哭了。”
林楸不好意思，笑着笑着就摸到狼岩刚刚用过的小刀上，又试图继续切蘑菇。
狼岩与狼安对视一眼，道：“附近蘑菇捡完了？”
狼安：“差不多，过不了多久又要长。乔他们应该到了吧……”
“肯定到了。”是狼火的声音。
狼安见狼火他们回来了，高兴道：“你们遇到乔了？支部落那边怎么样？”
狼火一屁股坐下来，躺在地上。
“遇到了，支部落那边好着呢。”
才喘了口气，狼火想起正事，立即爬起来。
“王，咱们部落遭流浪兽人偷袭了？”
“嗯。”
“我当初看那两个黑熊部落的兽人就觉得不对劲，他们跑了没？我去抓！”
“行了，你还是好好休息吧，早没事了。”
狼火一骨碌坐起来，想仔细问问，可王不搭理他，楸看着……
“楸！你伤得重不重啊？”狼火凑近，就被狼岩拎着一根山药抵住胸口。
狼火：“王！我急，你们仔细跟我说说呗？”
狼火后头的小队成员们也点点头，眼里充满怒意。
狼岩看了自己伴侣一眼。
林楸：“我跟你们说。”
他无聊，正好有空。
林楸把那天的情况说了一遍，廊道上时不时传出来兽人愤懑的声音。
羽涯带着几个小黑羽兽人搬砖过来，往里头看一眼，道：“狼火回来了。”
“那他们的支部落的兽人也快回来了。”同伴道。
“涯，咱们什么时候回去啊？”另一个小黑羽兽人道。
虽然在狼部落吃好喝好，但是他们想部落了。
羽涯将砖块放下，还没来得及回答，忙着砌墙的狼西就道：“羽涯，送些砖来这边！”
“来了！”
他摸摸面前这一堵红墙，跟同伴道：“忘记阿山叔他们说的话了吗？”
他们是来干活的，也是来学习的。
部落没了好多阿叔，他们大了，不能总想着依靠阿叔们了。他们要学些狼部落的东西，等回去，才能让自己的部落更好。
黑羽兽人又投入忙碌的建房当中，另几个黑羽兽人则跟着兔兽人下地干活。
从播种到收割，兽人们几乎每天过来看一眼。
兔葵这边正沿着地里巡视，顺带又放下一批捕吱吱兽的笼子。如今地里有弓箭队的兽人轮守，吱吱兽少了许多。
地里尾巴草长得极好，已经小腿高，在扬花结穗了。
风一吹，尾巴草沙沙而动，翠绿色的草浪高低起伏。
兔葵看着心中极有成就感。
他仔细走完了一整块尾巴草地，又从河岸那边绕回来。
靠河岸这块地，最东边种的是麻草。
如今麻草比兽人高，兔兽人们参考麻草野外的生长环境对麻草进行管理，肥水足够，又没有野草抢占营养，今年头一次种比野外的看着要均匀一点。
但也就是长得匀称，并不丰产。
兔葵捏着那巴掌大的叶片，软绒绒的。
又从尖端折断，看上面连着皮，没之前那么嫩了，应当可以采收了。
头一年播种，没有颗粒无收就是好结果。
兔葵他们是种植的老手，自然知道要培育优质的作物，需要一年又一年的选育。
这事急不来，也需得仔细摸索摸索。
这片麻草地，已经能证明他们兔兽人的种植手艺不差，换其他兽人，他敢保证麻草种出来没他们的一半好。
兔葵估摸了下雨季到的时间，往廊道下跑。
路过高高的麻草地，再过去一点，就是菜地，还有重新撒播种子的牧草试验地。
这些兔葵看了一遍又一遍，自然再熟悉不过。
他往前奔跑，眼中只掠过土地边一株格外不同的苗子，下一秒就出了地里。
廊道下，林楸刚说了一通部落的事，正捧着狼岩递过来的水杯喝水。
听完这事想打一架的狼火被狼岩摁住了，哼哼唧唧又不服气地对着空气拳打脚踢，然后滚到一边找个地方补觉去了。
兔葵急匆匆过来。
“楸，王，麻草可以采收了。”
“我去看看。”林楸说着要起。
狼岩扶着他的手臂，带得他慢了些。
到了地里，林楸看着那些比他还高的麻草，喃喃：“都这么高了……”
他不过半个月没来，麻草就大变样了。
林楸折了顶端一截，瞧着老了，便道：“可以收了。”
“那我叫兽人来。”兔葵立即道。
他也是个有事就立马做的性子，林楸忙叫住他，道：“葵，留一部分结种子，一部分先割一茬，别挖根。”
他想看看，地里的麻草能收几茬。
要收麻草了，兔葵把几个成年黑羽兽人叫来，先让他们把麻草叶子用长杆打掉，这样采收后的麻草可以直接泡水处理。
兔兽人们矮些，收割的活儿就归他们。
左手把住麻草根部，用石镰带着巧劲儿一割，麻草顺势放倒。一抱弄成一捆，用横放的几根麻草当绳子直接绑好。
林楸这边刚看完，地里就忙活起来。
他站在这边碍事儿，就往菜地那边慢慢走。
菜地里的菜吃过几次了，格外鲜嫩，不论做汤还是清炒味道都好。这些兔兽人专门培育出来的菜就没有差的。
林楸沿着土地边慢慢走，目光掠过被收割过的三叶草。
这是溶他们割去给咩咩兽吃了。
三叶草种得太少，长得不如咩咩兽吃得快。等明年，还得选个位置，专门种一种这牧草。
林楸边想边走着，忽然注意到角落里冒出的新叶。
甘蔗发芽了！
林楸快步靠近，没走两步，狼岩圈住他腰身，蹙着眉头道：“慢慢走。”
现在不用像之前那样一整天都得趴着，但也不能走得太快。
“知道了……”
转眼，林楸就站在了那脆生生的甘蔗苗前。
兔葵背着一捆麻草路过，又停下来，“是甘蔗发芽了。”
林楸转身，冲他笑着道：“就一个。”
“以后会越来越多的。”
兔葵说着就走到前面去，他忙起地里的事来干脆利落，跟他温柔的脾性很不相像。
硕大一捆麻草压在他背上，走几步要停下来掂一下，免得滑落。兽人背脊压弯，只能半抬起头，看着眼前的路。
林楸看向狼岩，“王，部落里事多，你别总跟着我。”
狼岩：“乖一点。”
林楸扬唇一笑，模样清俊漂亮。
“那你去吧，我保证不乱动。”
烈日刺目，河面上金鳞一般的波光吸引着幼崽往里扔石头。
狼果驱赶幼崽远离河边，吆喝声悠长。
一捆一捆的麻草被放在板车上，巨大黑狼拉着板车，经过狼山前，送到西边小河。
幼崽找到了新的乐趣。
他们争先恐后跃上板车，爬过麻草，爬上大黑狼的背上，将自己如同负鼠幼崽一样挂在他们王的身上。
幼崽胖墩墩的，十几个扎堆，分量不轻。
偏偏他们的王纵容着，也不驱赶，带着幼崽走了一趟又一趟。
林楸就在廊道下坐着，狼岩每每路过，都得往里看一眼。
林楸举起爪子冲着他招了两下，转头就继续切蘑菇。
日头走到正中央，狼雨几个亚兽人也都回来了。亚兽人们满头大汗，放下藤筐就迫不及待地去溪边洗了把脸。
溪水沁凉，这会儿泡着最舒服。
洗完回来，大家围坐一块，把灶火生起来，将野菜煮水后捞起来，放藤条编织的筛子里，搬到阳光下晒。
切好的蘑菇片也一一平摊在藤筛中，红红绿绿的颜色，五彩斑斓。菌伞宽大，菌柄肥硕，大的蘑菇有几斤重，小的刚钻出泥地，跟幼崽似的胖墩墩一个。
将它们摊放在廊道外，只两天就能干透。
林楸帮着切了一会儿，狼安也收了他的刀子。
林楸无奈，看着狼安，见他防备瞧着自己，哑然失笑：“我没事，怎么都把我当幼崽了？”
他一个成年人了，难道还不知道自己的身体情况吗？
“还没事？你看我都好了，你还没好。”狼安道。
兽人恢复速度应该很快，这是他们千百年来进化过来的，但楸不一样，祭司都说他身体底子差，恢复得慢。
林楸拗不过兽人，无力趴在草窝中发呆。
他算是找到重点了。
明明他伤口都结痂了，为什么兽人们还把他当个易碎品一样盯着，原来是他伤口恢复的速度慢了。
快中午了，要忙着做饭。
亚兽人们加快速度，将今天采集回来的野菜跟蘑菇收拾完。
他们动作熟练，薄薄的石刀片被他们用得像铁刀，几下就是一个蘑菇。
狼安起身，把煮完野菜的陶锅洗干净，重新加水煮。
部落里现在紧着凑齐给绿眼部落的猎物，最近这半个月日子过得紧巴巴的。
好在剩下的五头尖角兽已经凑齐了，只差两头弯角兽。
今天午间只有昨天剩下的兽骨，狼安捡了几根洗净，先熬上汤。然后叫还在廊道下的亚兽人看着火，自己又去看看河边放下去的笼子里有没有鱼。
天空传来几声震翅的声音，狼山的兽人们抬头看。
巨大的阴影掠过山间，阳光下，黑羽兽人灰黑色的羽毛发亮，他们又来送弯角兽了。
羽猎滑落地面，两个兽人一同抓着的弯角兽被轻轻放了下来。
被套住蹄子的弯角兽顿时挣扎起来，无奈被绑得严实，只能无力嘶叫。
狼石带着巡逻队快速从狼山后头绕到前面来，羽猎他们已经被狼兽人围住了。
林楸也慢慢走了出去。
狼岩拉着板车过来，兽人们自动让开。
“狼王，楸。”
羽猎先打招呼，不过看起来有些扭捏。
林楸一看地上那两头还是幼崽的弯角兽，就明白过来了。
狼岩放下板车，缓步走到林楸身边。他脖子蹭了下林楸的肩膀，随后看向羽猎。
“弯角兽幼崽？”
羽猎耳朵红了。
他不好意思道：“最近我们没抓到大弯角兽，族长让我过来问问，可不可以两头弯角兽幼崽抵一头大弯角兽？”
狼兽人面面相觑。
他们一般不吃猎物幼崽，抓到带崽的母兽还会放了。
别看弯角兽幼崽体型跟咩咩兽一般大了，但还能长呢。大弯角兽的肉是弯角兽幼崽的好几倍。
他们可不会为了当前一点肉，放弃更多的肉。
狼岩瞧着面前几个不自在的黑羽兽人，道：“我们商量商量。”
羽猎点头，见自家小兽人也要凑过来了，赶紧压低声音道：“不行也没事，就是你们可能要再等一等了。”
“都忙去吧。”狼岩道。
兽人散去，羽涯几个小兽人还在往羽猎身边走。
他们看着羽猎，笑着冲上去，“阿猎叔！”
羽猎看着比划了下几个小兽人的身高，惊奇道：“长高了。”
“高了吗？”
“高了，还壮了。”羽猎捏着自家幼崽的胳膊，哟！肉都紧实了不少。
狼兽人可比他们会养幼崽。
黑羽兽人叙旧，狼火小队的兽人也睡够了，这会儿打着哈欠出来。
他们瞅了一眼羽猎，打了招呼，随后一脑袋拱到板车前的绳条中，代替狼岩去拉麻草。
山洞内，狼岩、林楸还有祭司凑在一块。
老祭司抱着研钵，磨着药粉道：“弯角兽不好抓，那几头怕是把他们部落有的都抓完了。”
要想再抓，只有等其他弯角兽走到他们部落里来，不然就是离开部落领地，去其他地方寻找。
林楸：“这两头幼崽就算了，我们收下。”
狼岩：“要是想养，幼崽或许容易一点。”
林楸摇头，“快雨季了，最近咩咩兽那边忙得不行，我又不能盯着，溶他们根本没空。”
而且弯角兽的脾气他也算见识过了，很倔。
能不能养好还不一定呢。
幼崽现在抓来，他们又没精力照料，养死了岂不可惜。
他是要养，但要做好准备再说。何况快雨季了，咩咩兽的规模能扩大多少就看这次雨季能抓回来多少咩咩兽。
这个才是重中之重。
商量过后，狼岩便去找了羽猎。
羽猎看他们收下这两头幼崽，脸上臊红，“实在是最近没抓到大弯角兽，我们族长知道你们养咩咩兽，所以带过来让你们看看。”
“你们部落弯角兽幼崽很多？”
“不多，也就这么两头。”
不知道是不是他们抓弯角兽抓得太狠了，部落里的弯角兽都往外迁，现在更不好找了。
这两个弯角兽幼崽抵一头大的，之前已经送了五头，余下的十四头弯角兽还不知道要抓到什么时候呢。
羽猎来还有一件事，就是问问狼岩想好要求没有。
送弯角兽是因为山谷那事，狼乔后头帮了他们，还得另算。
哪知道狼岩直接说：“没想好，但是可以少几头。”
“什么？”
“快雨季了，用弯角兽换你们部落的硝石，一头换一车，暂时换四车，如果你们同意，下次直接送来就行。”
羽猎愣愣点头，“好，我回去问问族长。”
不管怎么样，他来这边的事儿办完了。
羽猎带着几个族人蹭过狼部落一顿饭，又飞回去了。
日影渐长，廊道前修建食堂的叮叮当当声就没停下来过。日也敲，夜也敲，兽人们从捂耳朵睡觉到逐渐适应。
终于，食堂上梁封顶，赶在雨季前建完。
红砖灰瓦砌成的房子，修得宽敞方正，大门冲着中间夯实过的广场，侧门贴着廊道，可以直接从大山洞里顺着廊道进去。
以后不论刮风下雨，兽人们都可以清清爽爽坐在食堂里吃饭。
不过现在还不成。
虽说门框窗框已经装好，但里面什么东西都没有。
原来坍塌一半的灶台被囊括进去，余下的还在修。
食堂规划了前面吃饭的地儿，后头做饭以及出餐的窗口，但目前也只停留在规划阶段，还没动工。
所以整个食堂，目前来说就是一个空空荡荡只有几个灶台的屋子。
要想有椅子坐，有桌子放，还要看狼起忙不忙得过来。
但这些暂且不重要，只要房子好了，回来的支部落的兽人就不愁没地方睡觉了。
chapters.title: 第151章

chapters.translated_text:
Thunder rumbled, and lightning writhed like silver dragons within the dark clouds.

The clouds hung extremely low, and the rain that had been gathering all day was about to pour down.

All the dried fish and vegetables that needed to be brought back into the caves had been retrieved. The old priest stood at the entrance of the newly built canteen, clutching his staff, his eyes sharp as he stared toward the southeast.

Logically, Lang Qiao should have returned with the branch tribe's beastmen days ago, but there was still no sign of them.

Lang Yan had even instructed the hunting parties to keep an eye out for them, but no beastman had spotted them.

"Could something have happened on the way?" Lang An stared at the rolling dark clouds, gripping his hands tightly in nervousness.

Once this heavy rain started, it would last for ten days or half a month; the rainy season had arrived.

The beastmen of Langshan had recently taken to sitting in the canteen; the ground had been rammed solid and was perfectly flat, and the room was swept so clean of dust that it felt very cool to sit on.

The canteen had replaced the corridors as the beastmen's favorite place to lounge.

Some beastmen stood at the entrance, while others lay by the windows. Because the sky was overcast, the room was dim today, making the dozens of wolf eyes look eerie, as if they were glowing with a faint green light.

"King, should we go out and look?"

Several team leaders gathered around Lang Yan. They hadn't said much these past few days, but in reality, each of them was worried about the others.

Lang Yan: "Wait a little longer."

There were many returning beastmen; this relocation was equivalent to a migration, and the beastmen had to bring all their belongings with them.

With so many beastmen, they had to fill their stomachs on the road, and carrying only dry rations certainly wasn't enough. Moving and stopping like this was definitely not as fast as a single small team traveling.

Besides, they were all wolf-beastmen, and their numbers were significant. Other beastmen would only hide upon seeing them; they wouldn't dare approach to seek death, so there were no safety concerns.

Everything that needed to be prepared on the Langshan side was already ready.

After the breeding season before the rains, there were now nearly a hundred red birds. However, Lang Rong was still pondering the matter of using heated beds to hatch eggs, which seemed to need a bit more time.

The other three sheep-beasts that were pregnant during the snow season had also given birth, and the tribe now had fourteen sheep-beasts.

Adding the few others that had mated and conceived before the rainy season, they should have twenty sheep-beasts once the rainy season passed.

Not only that, during the rainy season, the sheep-beasts would go down to the northern grasslands to give birth, and they could catch more to expand the tribe's herd.

In this way, the farming of sheep-beasts in the tribe would approach stability.

They could occasionally eat a few red birds now, but the sheep-beasts were off-limits; the tribe's stored dried fish and vegetables were at least enough to go around.

It wasn't as if they couldn't go out at all during the rainy season; they would occasionally hunt and forage, so by eating a mix of various foods, they wouldn't have to worry about going hungry.

Thunder shook the earth, and the heavy rain poured down.

At that moment, the sound of wolf howls echoed from the distant forest.

Without waiting for Lang Yan's order, all the beastmen surged out of the house and headed straight for the dense forest in the pouring rain.

Lightning flashed brightly, illuminating the excited expressions of the beastmen.

Lin Qiu subconsciously followed them out.

Lang Yan wrapped his arms around his waist, swung him up onto his back, and immediately transformed into his beast form to dash forward.

Lin Qiu held onto his neck, burying his head in his fur, his back stinging from the heavy rain.

He shouted: "We need to come back quickly; it's not good to stay under the trees when it's raining."

The beastmen responded with howls, kicking up their feet and running even faster.

The rain fell like a river pouring from the sky; the beastmen could barely open their eyes as they sprinted. The wind raged, the treetops swayed, and the lightning crackled, illuminating the dim sky from time to time.

In this apocalyptic scene, the wolf-beastmen were so excited that they howled as they ran, their eyes shining with startling intensity.

"Awoo!"

"Awoooo—"

The closer they got, the more frequent the calls became.

The beastmen shouted and responded, their voices remaining clear amidst the howling storm.

They were close.

Getting closer and closer.

Lin Qiu only heard a series of excited long howls in his ears as the beastmen rushed over. He looked up, through the blurred curtain of rain, watching the beastmen collide, laughing and playing, rolling into a ball.

The excitement of the wolf-beastmen infected Lin Qiu.

He sat quietly on Lang Yan's back, watching him move forward and touch noses with the beastmen from the branch tribe.

Lin Qiu also began to smile.

"Awoo, awoo, awoo!"

The procession was long, and the beastmen were in a sorry state, but in the rainstorm, they were like crops finally receiving water after a long drought, full of vitality.

Lin Qiu smiled, his eyes crinkling, but feeling uncomfortable from the rain, he couldn't help but lower his head to wipe his face.

Suddenly, the back of his hand was touched.

Lin Qiu touched the big black wolf's head, his wet hair draped over his body, hiding the skin that was faintly showing, and he asked with a smile: "What is it?"

Lang Yan signaled for him to lower his head.

Lin Qiu leaned in to listen.

Feeling a wet touch on his cheek, he widened his eyes and covered his face.

Lang Yan: "We're back!"

"Back! We're back at Langshan!" The beastmen howled excitedly, helping to carry things; seeing old guys like Lang Jiao, the Lang Mu team laughed and simply hoisted the beastmen up and ran.

"We're back, we're back, we're back at Langshan!"

"Back at Langshan!"

The forest was damp, and thunder rumbled from time to time, making Lin Qiu anxious.

It was common knowledge not to walk under trees when it was raining.

Fortunately, the beastmen didn't delay; they helped carry the goods and then sprinted toward Langshan.

Throughout the run, the excited, strange howls never stopped.

At the entrance of the red-brick, grey-tiled house, the old priest had changed his staff at some point.

He leaned on that wooden staff covered in gems and beads, standing quietly in front of the remaining cubs and old beastmen, watching the beastmen arriving from the branch tribe.

The laughing and shouting stopped.

The beastmen from the branch tribe also slowly slowed their pace, looking at the incredibly aged priest, and in an instant, their eyes filled with tears.

"Priest!" Lang Jiao stepped forward and grabbed the old priest's hand tightly.

The old priest looked at him, his hand trembling slightly, and he patted the back of Lang Jiao's hand heavily, "How come you look even older than me?"

Lang Jiao gritted his teeth, unable to hold back, and suddenly hugged the old priest tightly.

"Uncle Chun."

"Priest!!!" In an instant, the beastmen from the branch tribe crowded around, hugging the old priest tightly.

To them, the old priest was a grandfather, an uncle, and the spiritual pillar they had believed in even while far away in the southeast branch tribe. He made medicine, sent medicine, and even at his age, he still had to worry about them.

To put it bluntly, in the days when the tribe was so difficult, he couldn't afford to die even if he wanted to.

The responsibility on his shoulders was heavy as a thousand pounds.

Now, there was only this one old beastman left in the tribe.

Originally there was Lang Gu, but Gu was gone too.

The beastmen didn't cry when they heard the Wolf Tribe's life had improved, didn't cry when they knew they could eat their fill, and didn't cry when they knew they could return to the Wolf Tribe.

But at this very moment, amidst the wind and rain, seeing the old priest standing at the door to welcome them, holding the priest's staff and wearing his solemn, wide ceremonial robes, they wailed.

They felt so aggrieved!

No wolf-beastman wanted to be separated from the tribe; without the Wolf King, without the priest, they were like duckweed without roots, with nothing to rely on.

Food was scarce, and they never knew if they would continue to drift.

In the dead of night, everyone had even thought a thousand times if they would never be able to return to Langshan before they died.

But now, they were back...

They were back!

All their grievances had a place to pour out.

Furthermore, seeing the elder they once relied on had become so white-haired and frail after all these years, their hearts ached unbearably.

Everyone wished they could vent all the bitterness of the past dozen years at once.

Lin Qiu watched these elderly uncles crying around the priest, feeling a heavy weight in his heart. He hugged Lang Yan's neck, his head buried in his fur, never lifting it.

His back was no longer being rained on, and the crying sounds were fading behind him.

Lin Qiu was set down.

He sat on a stool, watching his partner adjust the animal skin around his waist while bringing over a cloth and clean clothes.

Lin Qiu pressed his chin against his stomach.

"It's hard as a rock," Lin Qiu muttered.

The corners of his eyes were gently touched, Lin Qiu's eyelashes trembled, and the red at the corners of his eyes looked exceptionally beautiful.

"Did you cry?"

"No." Lin Qiu buried his head, hiding directly against Lang Yan's abdominal muscles.

Lang Yan quickly changed him into a new set of clothes, then gathered his hair and wiped it carefully for him.

Lin Qiu couldn't help but look outside the big cave again; across the long corridor, at the end, was the spacious red house.

It was crowded with people, and the noise was deafening.

"Aren't you going over?"

Lang Yan touched his earlobe, "No rush."

Although he was the Wolf King, he was also a junior. If he went over now, those uncles would feel uncomfortable crying while holding the priest.

The beastmen had been suppressed for too long and needed a release.

Lin Qiu looked at his lowered eyes, grey and very gentle. He couldn't help but turn his head and press his cheek against Lang Yan's palm.

Perhaps because no one could accommodate his attachment in his past life, he couldn't help but want to be close to Lang Yan.

Lin Qiu was becoming increasingly accustomed to such clingy behavior.

Lang Yan touched the soft flesh on his face, simply sat down, held his neck to bring him closer, and kissed him gently on the lips.

Lin Qiu's breath hitched.

Lang Yan looked into his eyes, gradually deepening the kiss.

He wanted to thank his partner.

Thank him for allowing the Wolf Tribe to reunite.

But some things would seem too polite if said too often; Lang Yan cherished and cared for him, hoping only that he would be carefree and healthy.

*

The red house was boisterous. Lin Qiu lay in Lang Yan's arms, listening to his steady heartbeat, gradually calming down.

He looked at Lang Yan and found that Lang Yan was also looking at him.

Lin Qiu felt the swelling on his lips, couldn't help but purse them, and pressed his chin against Lang Yan's chest.

His partner wasn't very talkative, and his emotions were rarely shown on the outside.

The return of the branch tribe's beastmen must have made him excited too. Otherwise, with so many beastmen outside, he wouldn't have held him and kissed him for so long in the past.

"We should go over," Lin Qiu said.

Lang Yan touched his face and pinched his earlobe, as if holding a small thing he liked very much. Lin Qiu couldn't help but smile again.

He hooked his hand into Lang Yan's and said, "Let's go."

If they kept touching, something would happen.

In the red house, the beastmen were still reminiscing.

A beastman brought over a stool and helped the old priest sit down, while other beastmen from the branch tribe surrounded him to talk.

In the corner, Lang Qi sat on the ground.

In front of him, Lang Jiao and a group of old guys were staring at him.

"What? Haven't seen me in over ten years and you don't recognize me anymore?"

Lang Qi patted the wood shavings off his hands; his whole body smelled of wood.

He had also just come from the cave side and had been watching for a long time. He was reserved in his emotions; it wasn't that he didn't recognize them, but he was too excited and choked up, unable to speak for a moment.

Lang Jiao knew him well and understood his temperament. He looked him up and down and said, "You've been living better than us, at least."

Lang Qi said in a muffled voice: "The tribe needs beastmen to help."

"You say this to me as soon as I get back?"

Lang Qi's Adam's apple bobbed, his hands trembling as he slapped Lang Jiao's arm.

The force wasn't light, making Lang Jiao's face wrinkle in pain.

"Old guy! Want to fight!"

Only then did Lang Qi smile, crystal-clear tears flashing in his eyes, murmuring: "It's good to be back, it's good to be back..."

Lang Jiao looked at his equally wrinkled face and also showed a sentimental smile.

The house suddenly quieted down.

Lang Jiao turned his head and saw their young Wolf King and the Wolf King's partner coming out.

They stood up one after another and said: "King."

Lang Yan nodded: "Sit."

Except for the Lang Ye team, the other beastmen who had just returned from the branch tribe were a bit reserved.

Most of them had been busy in the branch tribe; the task of sending things back and forth between the two tribes was usually done by Lang Ye and his team.

They truly hadn't returned for sixteen years.

The little Wolf King, whose face was still somewhat tender when they left, had grown into a young man, handsome and heroic, commanding respect without anger.

The beastmen felt a bit like strangers, but they obediently sat down.

Compared to Lang Yan, they were more familiar with Lin Qiu.

Lang Chi's cub, who used to be a disobedient cub. But they heard he had fallen and hit his head and changed for the better. Now, looking at Lin Qiu standing beside Lang Yan, not losing to the Wolf King, they almost didn't recognize him.

How could the change be so great!

The sub-beastman who used to have resentment in his eyes and was full of thorns now had a calm temperament and gentle features, looking like a qualified Wolf King's partner.

Lang Yan knew the beastmen were sizing them up.

He held Lin Qiu's hand, sat down with him, and let them continue to look.

"Since you're back, you won't leave Langshan again. Live here with peace of mind. There is a lot to do in the tribe; everyone should rest first, and then we'll get busy."

After Lang Yan finished speaking, a beastman said full of energy: "King, we don't need to rest; we came back to work anyway."

Lang Yan: "No rush, there's plenty of work; just don't complain about being tired later."

Lang Huo and the other team leaders laughed cheekily, hooking their arms around the necks of the beastmen beside them, "We're all one family, help each other out in the future."

"Right, work together when there's work to do!" The beastmen laughed foolishly.

Life was still long, and fearing that the beastmen would get sick from the rain, Lang Yan didn't say much more and told them to go clean themselves up.

By now, the meat soup was almost ready.

Lang An told the beastmen to eat something to pad their stomachs first, and they would make more in the evening.

Several team leaders left with the beastmen, and Lang Yan called Lang An and the other sub-beastmen over to discuss matters.

Lin Qiu sat next to Lang Yan, suppressing his smile, listening to them talk about serious business.

"The meat soup from the six pots isn't enough now; we need to add two more pots. The stoves are enough, but can you nine beastmen handle it?"

"Don't worry, it's just two more pots," Lang An said.

"Kill two sharp-horned beasts tonight, have less soup, and let every beastman eat more meat."

They had already sent the remaining sharp-horned beasts to the Green-Eyed Tribe, leaving only two curved-horned beasts. The hunting teams had been out hunting for the past few days, and after sending five away, they could spare three more sharp-horned beasts.

"Okay," Lang An agreed.

"From now on, you arrange the daily food; try to have one meal of meat a day. Let Lang Shi's side help with slaughtering the prey."

"The beastmen staying at Langshan will continue to dry fish and vegetables. As long as we ensure enough food every day, dry as much as you can of the rest."

"I understand," Lang An said.

The sub-beastmen all knew this was in preparation for the snow season.

……

It only took a few days for the branch tribe's beastmen to integrate into Langshan.

Everyone ate and slept together, exchanged information, and in just a few days, everyone had found their own work.

They didn't even need Lang Yan to arrange it; the team leaders automatically divided up the branch tribe's beastmen.

Without a doubt, Lang Jiao's group of beastmen was taken by Lang Qi.

They had been taken to his cave on the very day they arrived.

Now that his cave was large and had been modified by the rabbit-beastmen last year, it could be lived in during the rainy season, so Lang Jiao and his group simply brought their belongings and moved in directly.

Once they arrived, the Lang Mu team could let go.

These guard team beastmen were so excited they ran all over the mountain, looking like they had just been released from a dark cave.

Besides Lang Jiao's team, the other beastmen who came were members of the hunting and gathering teams with combat capabilities.

There were two hunting teams: one was the young beastman team led by Lang Ye, and the other was the team of slightly older beastmen led by Lang Kuo.

Lang Kuo was a black wolf-beastman in his prime; the hunting team he led had a steady temperament and consisted of handsome and determined uncles.

These uncles were in their thirties or forties, and many were bachelors; it was mostly the male beastmen who stayed in the branch tribe who had partners.

The Lang Ye team now hung out with Lang Huo.

Their hunting teams worked in pairs, with one group in one direction when hunting, which increased the chances of catching prey.

Lang Kuo and his team didn't go hunting but joined Lang Mo's construction team directly.

They were very interested in how mud was burned into bricks and how bricks were built into houses.

The remaining gathering team, the only one without a leader who came over, was even more proactive. The dozen or so beastmen followed Lang An's arrangements and had already divided their tasks.

They took turns learning to wash hemp, weave cloth, cut fabric to make clothes, cook, stir-fry, feed livestock, and plow land to grow vegetables.

When they had free time, they joined Lang Bei's gathering team to go out and learn about the edible wild vegetables around Langshan.

Not one of them was idle.

Lang Yan saved time on arrangements; as soon as they arrived, there were more hands everywhere, and finally, no beastman asked Lang Yan for people.

It took a few days for the branch tribe's beastmen to adapt.

The allocation of the two houses was also put on the agenda.

Lang An handled this; he directly picked some leaves of similar size, made marks on two of them, threw them into a basket, and had the beastmen draw lots through a layer of cloth.

Although only beastmen with partners could draw, it didn't stop everyone from watching the fun.

In the canteen, Lang An put down the rattan basket.

The beastmen with partners all sent representatives out. Lin Qiu counted and found that only twenty-four beastmen had partners.

It was shockingly few.

Excluding cubs and underage young wolves, half of the beastmen had no partners, including "old bachelors" like Lang Kuo and his group.

Lin Qiu stood in the line, unable to help but look back at Lang Yan.

Lang Yan looked at him inquiringly, and Lin Qiu took a step back, about to speak to him.

"Hey! Qiu, every beastman with a partner must participate," Lang An said immediately.

Regardless of whether they were old or young, what mattered was fairness.

The beastmen in the room looked over.

Lin Qiu immediately stepped forward.

After drawing a leaf, Lin Qiu saw that his leaf was blank and immediately returned to sit beside Lang Yan.

"King, don't you think there are too few beastmen in our tribe who have formed partnerships?"

"Did you want to ask this just now?"

Behind Lin Qiu and Lang Yan, the wolf-beastmen who hadn't gone up quietly pricked up their ears to listen to them.

Lin Qiu: "Most of the beastmen in our tribe are adults. Not to mention the younger ones, look at Uncle Kuo's team; they are all bachelors!"

Lang Yan's eyelids twitched at this description, and he barely managed to say: "Some of them used to have partners."

"That was in the past."

"Does Qiu have a good idea?" Lang Yan asked, hooking Lin Qiu's wrist.

Lin Qiu looked around; the wolf-beastmen behind them suddenly lifted their heads, staring intently at the beastmen drawing lots in front.

Lin Qiu withdrew his gaze, shifted, and leaned closer to Lang Yan.

He lowered his voice and said: "Didn't the beastmen ask you before, and you said you would think about it?"

Lin Qiu thought their King would have a way.

Lang Yan also replied in a low voice: "I haven't thought of one."

There were few sub-beastmen and female beastmen in the tribe, and there were no other wolf-beastmen nearby; what could he do?

Lin Qiu's eyes widened slightly.

The wolf-beastmen behind them drooped their furry ears, looking dejected.

"Sigh!"

A very loud sigh drew the attention of other beastmen.

Lang Yun slid smoothly from his stool to the ground, listless, looking longingly at the beastmen who had partners.

Lin Qiu was startled by him.

Turning his head, he saw that the beastmen behind were lying in a crooked row.

The rabbit-beastmen pricked up their long ears, shuffling and shuffling until they reached Lin Qiu's side.

Tu Kui touched Lin Qiu's arm.

Lin Qiu: "Kui?"

"I know of a place that has a Wolf Tribe."

"Hmm?"

"Hmm!!!" The wolf-beastmen behind sat up in a row.

The beastmen drawing lots in front also looked over anxiously.

Lang An held the rattan basket and asked urgently: "Which Wolf Tribe?"

How come they hadn't heard anything about it?

"It's called the Chishan Tribe, but I don't know if they are still there."

"It's okay, Kui, tell us quickly," Lin Qiu said.

The place where the rabbit-beastmen originally lived was further south; it would take at least a month to travel from the Wolf Tribe. At the rabbit-beastmen's pace, it was even further; they had run for more than two months on their way here.

The location of the Rabbit Tribe was called Green Lake, a jade-green lake like a gemstone.

And those wolf-beastmen lived at the source of the Green Lake's water, in a vast mountain range called Chishan.

From Green Lake to Chishan, one had to travel west for a few more days.

The rabbit-beastmen had never been there and didn't dare to go.

However, Chishan was easy to identify; a type of tree grew there, and every year before autumn, the whole mountain range would turn fiery red, as if the entire mountain range were burning.

Tu Kui had almost no contact with them, only a few times when they came down from the mountain to chase prey and reached the riverbank.

The rabbit-beastmen happened to be fetching water and saw those beastmen who were fiercer than them.

"Their Wolf King is a sub-beastman, a red wolf."

Tu Kui still remembered how that red wolf caught prey outside their tribe with a single strike.

Fresh blood splashed onto him, but it wasn't as bright and eye-catching as his own wolf fur.

"A red wolf?"

"Don't they usually hide and never see other beastmen?" Lang Guo asked.

Tu Kui: "That tribe isn't all red wolves; they are just like you."

"More than a month..." the beastmen murmured.

Although finding a partner was a major event for beastmen, and it was common to travel for half a year to find a partner at the market in the past, there was too much to do in the tribe now; how could they dare to leave?

"Awoo, awoo, awoo, awoo!" Lang Mo rolled on the ground.

The other beastmen looked longingly at Lang Yan.

"King..."

Lang Yan: "We'll talk after the rainy season."

It was a good thing that there was a Wolf Tribe nearby; the wolf-beastman race was naturally close, and compared to other races, they trusted beastmen of the same wolf-beastman race more.

It was very far away, and perhaps they had things the tribe didn't have.

Being able to find time to go there and communicate with each other was the long-term plan for development.

"Awoo, awoo..."

"Shut up!" Lang Yan frowned.

The beastmen covered their muzzles with their paws, rolling on the ground happily.

As for the wolf-beastmen who drew the houses, no one paid any attention to them anymore.
chapters.source_text:
天雷滚滚，闪电如银龙在乌云中翻腾。
云层压得极低，积攒了一天的雨水即将倾泻而下。
该收回山洞的鱼干、菜干都收回来了，老祭司站在新建的食堂门口，手捏着拐杖，目光炯炯，盯着东南的方向。
按理说，早几天前狼乔就该带着支部落的兽人回来了，可现在还没个影。
狼岩都让狩猎队外出时多注意那边，也没兽人看到他们。
“别不是路上出事了吧。”狼安盯着那翻滚的乌云，有些紧张地握紧双手。
这大雨一下就是十天半月的，雨季来了。
狼山的兽人们最近都喜欢坐在食堂里，地面夯实过，平平整整的，屋子里又打扫得一点灰尘都没有，坐在上面很凉快。
食堂已经代替连廊，成为兽人们最喜欢趴的地方。
兽人们有的站在门口，有的趴在窗边，因为天阴，今天屋里还有些暗沉，衬得那好几十双狼眼幽幽，好似泛着绿光。
“王，要不然我们出去看看？”
几个队长围在狼岩身边，这几天他们嘴上不说什么，其实一个个都牵挂着那边。
狼岩：“再等等。”
回来的兽人多，这次搬迁相当于迁徙，兽人们要把自己的全部家当带上。
这么多兽人，路上也要填饱肚子，只带些干粮肯定不够。这样走走停停，肯定没有单独一小队行进的速度快。
又都是狼兽人，数量不少，其他兽人看见只有躲的份儿，不可能凑上去找死，没有安全隐患。
狼山这边该准备的已经都准备好了。
红鸟经过雨季前的繁殖，如今有近百只。不过狼溶现在还在琢磨火炕孵蛋的事，看着还需要一点时间。
雪季怀胎的另外三头咩咩兽也下了崽，部落已经有十四头咩咩兽了。
加上另外几头雨季前才交配怀崽的咩咩兽，等雨季一过，他们应该会有二十头咩咩兽。
不仅如此，雨季期间，咩咩兽下到北部草原生崽，他们可以多抓些回来壮大部落的咩咩兽族群。
如此，部落的咩咩兽的养殖便趋近于稳定了。
红鸟现在可以偶尔吃几只，咩咩兽还不能动，部落里储存的鱼干菜干至少管够。
雨季也不是一直不能出去，他们也会偶尔捕猎采集，这样各种食物混着吃，不怕饿肚子。
雷声惊天震地，大雨倾盆而至。
那一瞬间，远处的林子里有狼嚎声传出。
不用狼岩下令，兽人们全部涌出屋中，直奔大雨中的密林而去。
闪电骤亮，映着兽人们兴奋的表情。
林楸下意识跟了出去。
狼岩拥住他腰身，将他一甩，背在身上，随即变成兽形往前奔去。
林楸抱住他脖子，脑袋埋在他毛毛里，背上被雨水打得生疼。
他大喊道：“要赶紧回来，下雨天待在树下不好。”
兽人们嗷呜叫着回应，撒着脚丫子跑得更快。
雨水如天河倒灌，兽人们狂奔中，几乎睁不开眼。狂风肆意，树冠摇晃，闪电噼啪而下时不时照亮昏沉的天空。
末世一般的景象中，狼兽人们却兴奋得边跑边嚎，目光亮得惊人。
“嗷！”
“嗷呜——”
离得越近，叫声越发密集起来。
兽人们一边高喝，一边回应，声音在狂风暴雨中依旧清晰。
近了。
越来越近了。
林楸只听到耳边一阵激动的长啸，兽人们奔了过去。他抬起头，隔着模糊的雨幕，看着兽人们碰在一起，嬉笑打闹，滚成一团。
狼兽人的兴奋感染了林楸。
他静静坐在狼岩背上，看着他往前，与支部落过来的兽人碰了碰鼻子。
林楸也笑了起来。
“嗷呜嗷呜嗷呜！”
队伍很长，兽人们很狼狈，但暴雨中，兽人们仿佛久旱逢甘霖的作物，满是活气。
林楸弯眼笑起来，被雨水打得难受，又忍不住低头抹了抹脸。
忽的，手背被碰了一下。
林楸摸摸大黑狼的脑袋，湿发披在身上，藏住隐隐约约显露的肌肤，他笑问：“干什么？”
狼岩示意他低下头。
林楸侧耳倾听。
脸颊上湿漉漉的一下，他瞪大双眼捂脸。
狼岩：“回了！”
“回了回了！回狼山了！”兽人们兴奋地乱嚎，帮驮东西的驮东西，瞧着狼狡这些个老家伙，狼木小队嘿嘿笑着，干脆把兽人扛起来就跑。
“回了回了，回狼山了！”
“回狼山了！”
山林很潮，雷声时不时响起，林楸提心吊胆。
下雨不往树下走，这是常识。
好在兽人们没耽搁，帮忙拿好东西，然后往狼山狂奔。
奔跑中，兴奋的怪叫声就没停过。
红砖灰瓦的房子门口，老祭司不知道什么时候换了拐杖。
他拄着那一把挂满了宝石珠子的木杖，静静站在留下的幼崽和老兽人前头，看着支部落过来的兽人。
笑闹声停下来了。
支部落的兽人们也慢慢放缓脚步，看着苍老不已的老祭司，一瞬间，热泪盈眶。
“祭司！”狼狡上前，紧紧抓住老祭司的手。
老祭司看着他，手微微颤抖，他重重地拍了拍狼狡的手背，“怎么看着比我还老了。”
狼狡忍得牙齿紧扣，没忍住，猛地将老祭司抱住。
“春叔。”
“祭司！！！”一瞬间，支部落的兽人凑上来，把老祭司拥得严严实实。
对他们而言，老祭司是阿爷，是阿叔，是他们远在东南支部落也信仰着的精神支柱。他制药，送药，一把年纪了还得牵挂他们。
说句难听点的，以前部落那么难的日子，他想死都不能死。
他身上的责任千斤重。
如今部落里就剩下这么一个老兽人了。
原本还有狼古，可古也走了。
兽人们听到狼部落的日子变好了没哭，知道能吃饱了没哭，知道能回狼部落了还是没哭。
可此时此刻，在风雨飘摇中，看到拿着祭司权杖，穿着宽大肃穆的祭祀袍，站立在门口迎接他们的老祭司，他们嚎啕大哭。
他们委屈啊！
没有哪个狼兽人愿意与部落分开，狼王不在，祭司不在，他们就像没根的浮萍，没有依托。
食物紧缺，总不知道还会不会继续漂泊。
夜深人静时，大家甚至想过千百次，是不是到死都回不去狼山。
可是现在，回来了……
他们回来了！
所有的委屈有了倾泄处。
再加上兽人看到曾经依靠的长辈这么多年已然白发苍苍，垂垂老矣，也心痛难忍。
大家恨不能将这十几年的酸楚一并发泄了。
林楸看着这些一把年纪的阿叔们围着祭司哭成这样，心里闷闷的，他抱着狼岩脖子，脑袋埋在他毛毛里一直没抬起来。
后背没有淋雨了，哭声也在身后远去。
林楸被放了下来。
他坐在凳子上，看着自家伴侣一边围好腰间兽皮，一边拿了帕子跟干净衣服过来。
林楸下巴贴在他肚子上。
“硬邦邦的。”林楸咕哝。
眼尾被轻轻点了点，林楸睫毛轻颤，眼尾那抹红格外漂亮。
“哭了？”
“没有。”林楸埋头，直接藏在狼岩腹肌上。
狼岩给他快速换了一身衣服，然后拢起他的头发，细细给他擦拭。
林楸忍不住又往大山洞外看了一眼，隔着长长的廊道，尽头是宽敞的红房子。
里边人头攒动，声音震耳。
“你不去吗？”
狼岩摸摸他耳廓，“不着急。”
他虽是狼王，但也是小辈。这会儿过去，那些阿叔们抱着祭司哭得该不自在了。
兽人们压抑太久，需要一场发泄。
林楸看着他垂着的眼眸，灰色的，很温柔。他忍不住偏头，将脸颊贴在狼岩掌心。
兴许上辈子没有人能安放他的依恋，所以遇到了狼岩，他总忍不住亲近。
这样黏糊的姿态，林楸愈发习惯了。
狼岩摸摸他脸上的软肉，干脆坐下来，捧着他后颈贴近，轻轻吻在他唇上。
林楸呼吸一颤。
狼岩与他对视着，渐渐加深了吻。
他要感谢他的伴侣。
谢谢他，让狼部落重逢。
但有些话说多了就会显得客气，狼岩珍重他，也爱护他，只希望他无忧无虑，健康无虞。
*
红房子里喧嚣，林楸趴在狼岩怀里，听着他沉稳的心跳，渐渐平复过来。
他看着狼岩，发现狼岩也正看着他。
林楸感受到唇上的肿胀，忍不住抿了抿嘴，下巴抵着狼岩胸口压了压。
他的伴侣话不算多，情绪也鲜少外露。
支部落的兽人回来，他想必也是激动的。不然外面还有那么多兽人呢，换做以前他可不会抱着他亲这么久。
“该过去了。”林楸道。
狼岩摸摸他的脸，又捏捏他的耳垂，像揣着个分外喜欢的小东西，林楸看着又忍不住笑。
他勾住狼岩的手，道：“走了。”
再摸下去，会出事。
红房子里，兽人们还在叙旧。
有兽人搬来个凳子，扶着老祭司坐下，其他支部落的兽人就围在他身边跟他说话。
角落，狼起坐在地上。
他面前，狼狡带着一群老家伙，跟他大眼瞪小眼。
“怎么？十几年没见，还认不出我来了？”
狼起拍拍手上的木屑，浑身是木头腌透了的木香。
他也刚从山洞那边过来，围观了许久，他情绪内敛，哪里是认不出人，是太激动，一时哽咽说不出话来。
狼狡跟他熟得很，知道他性子，他上上下下打量他，道：“倒是比我们日子过得滋润。”
狼起闷声闷气道：“部落缺兽人帮忙。”
“我一回来你就跟我说这个？”
狼起喉结滚了滚，手哆嗦着，一把拍在了狼狡胳膊上。
那手劲儿不小，疼得狼狡脸都皱了。
“老家伙！想打架！”
狼起这才笑起来，眼中闪动着晶莹泪花，喃喃道：“回来就好，回来就好……”
狼狡看着他同样长满皱纹的脸，也露出个感慨的笑来。
房子里忽然安静下来。
狼狡回头，就看他们年轻的狼王跟狼王伴侣出来。
他们纷纷站起来，道：“王。”
狼岩颔首：“坐。”
除开狼夜小队，其他刚从支部落回来的兽人都有些拘谨。
他们大多在支部落奔波，来回两个部落之间送东西的事一般都是狼夜他们去跑。
他们是真正的十六年没有回来过了。
当初离开时，面庞还有些稚嫩的小狼王已经长成青年，英俊神武，不怒自威。
兽人们有些陌生，但却听话地坐下来。
比起狼岩，他们对林楸更熟悉些。
狼赤的幼崽，还是个不听话的幼崽。可听说摔了脑袋，变好了，现在他们看着站在狼岩身边不输狼王的林楸，差点还没认出来。
变化怎么会这么大！
以前那个眼中总是怨恨，满身尖刺的亚兽人，如今气质淡然，眉目柔润，像一个合格的狼王伴侣了。
狼岩知道兽人们在打量他们。
他牵住林楸的手，与他一同坐下，也由着他们继续看。
“既然回来了，以后就不会再离开狼山，你们安心住着。部落的事情很多，大家先休息休息，之后就得忙起来了。”
狼岩话落，就有兽人干劲十足道：“王，我们用不着休息，本来就是回来干活的。”
狼岩：“不着急，有的是活干，你们以后不要喊累就行。”
狼火几个队长笑得贱兮兮，哥俩好地勾住旁边兽人的脖子，“都是一家的兽人，以后多帮帮忙。”
“对，有活一起干！”兽人傻兮兮笑起来。
日子还长，怕淋雨的兽人生病，狼岩没说几句话，就让他们去收拾自己。
这会儿，肉汤已经快好了。
狼安让兽人们先吃着垫垫肚子，晚上再做好的。
几个小队队长带着兽人们离开，狼岩招呼狼安几个亚兽人过来，要商量事情。
林楸挨着狼岩坐着，敛了笑，听着他们说正事。
“现在六口锅的肉汤不够了，还要加两口锅。灶倒是够了，你们九个兽人忙不忙得过来？”
“放心，不就是多两口锅的事。”狼安道。
“晚上杀两头尖角兽，汤少一点，让每个兽人多吃点肉。”
他们已经把剩下的尖角兽给绿眼部落送过去了，只差两头弯角兽。这几天狩猎队都在外面捕猎，送走五头，还能多出三头尖角兽。
“好。”狼安应下。
“以后每天的食物你看着安排，尽量一天能吃一顿兽肉，宰杀猎物这些事还是让狼石那边帮忙。”
“留守狼山的兽人继续晒鱼干菜干，只要保证每天有足够的食物，剩下的能晒多少尽量晒多少。”
“我知道了。”狼安道。
亚兽人们都知道，这是在为雪季做准备。
……
支部落的兽人融入狼山，只需要几天的时间。
大家同吃同睡，交换两边的信息，短短几天，各自已经找好了自己的活儿。
甚至都不用狼岩安排，几个队长就自动瓜分了支部落的兽人们。
毫无疑问，狼狡这一群兽人被狼起要去。
早在刚来的当天他们就被狼起带去了自己的山洞。
现在他那山洞大，去年经过兔兽人修改了一通，雨季也能住人，狼狡他们干脆带着自己的家当，直接住那边了。
他们一来，狼木小队就可以放手了。
这群护卫队的兽人当时激动得满山跑，看着像刚刚从黑山洞里放出来。
除了狼狡这一队兽人，另外来的兽人都是些有战斗力的狩猎队跟采集队成员。
狩猎队有两个，一个是狼夜带领的年轻兽人队伍，一个是狼阔带领的稍微长一辈的兽人队伍。
狼阔是黑狼兽人，正值壮年，他带领的狩猎队气质沉稳，都是些帅气坚定的阿叔们。
这些阿叔们年纪三四十岁，好多都是光棍，留在支部落的雄兽人才是大多都有伴侣的。
狼夜小队现在跟着狼火混。
他们狩猎队两个小队一组，捕猎的时候一组一个方向，捕到猎物的几率也大些。
狼阔他们就不去捕猎了，而是直接加入了狼莫的建筑队。
他们对泥巴烧成砖块、砖又建成房子很感兴趣。
而剩下的一个采集队，也是唯一一个没有队长跟过来的队伍，他们就更积极了，十几个兽人听从狼安的安排，早已经分好了任务。
他们轮流去学洗麻织布，裁布做衣，做饭炒菜，喂养牲畜还有耕地种菜。
有空闲了，便加入狼贝的采集队，出去认识认识狼山这边能吃的野菜。
没一个空闲的。
狼岩省了安排的时间，他们一来，哪一处都多了人手，总算没有兽人问狼岩要人了。
花了几天的时间，支部落的兽人适应下来。
那两个房子的归处也提上了日程。
这事儿狼安去办的，他直接摘了些大小差不多的叶片，拿两片弄出点痕迹，然后扔筐里，隔着一层布让兽人们自己抽签。
虽然只有有伴侣的兽人可以抽，但不妨碍大家看热闹。
食堂里，狼安把藤筐放下。
有伴侣的兽人都派了代表出来，林楸一清点，发现仅有二十四个兽人有伴侣。
少得有点吓人。
排除幼崽和没成年的小狼，还有半数兽人没伴侣，包括狼阔他们那样的“老光棍”。
林楸此时站在队伍中，忍不住回头看了一眼狼岩。
狼岩目光询问，林楸退后一步正要跟他说话。
“诶！楸，每个有伴侣的兽人都必须参与。”狼安立即道。
管他老的小的，要的是公平。
一个屋子的兽人看过来。
林楸立即往前一步。
待到抽了叶片，林楸看着自己叶片上是光溜溜的，立马回到狼岩身边坐着。
“王，你没觉得咱们部落的兽人结成伴侣的太少了吗？”
“刚刚就想问这个？”
林楸和狼岩后头，没上去的狼兽人悄悄竖起耳朵听他俩说话。
林楸：“咱们部落的兽人大部分都是成年的兽人，年轻一点的先不说，你看阔叔他们那队伍，居然全是光棍！”
狼岩听着这形容，眼皮跳了一下，勉强道：“有些曾经还是有伴侣的。”
“那是曾经。”
“楸有好主意吗？”狼岩勾着林楸手腕道。
林楸看了看周围，后头的狼兽人一下抬起头，目不转睛盯着前面抽签的兽人看。
林楸收回目光，挪了挪，与狼岩靠得更近。
他压低声音道：“之前兽人们不是问了你，你说你想想？”
林楸以为他们的王会有办法的。
狼岩同样低声回：“没想到。”
部落里亚兽人跟雌性兽人少，附近又没狼兽人，他能怎么办？
林楸双目微睁。
后头的狼兽人们毛耳朵一耷拉，垂头丧气。
“哎！”
极大的一声叹气，引得其他兽人们看来。
狼云丝滑地从凳子上滑到地面，无精打采，眼巴巴地看着那些有伴侣的兽人们。
林楸被他吓得一激灵。
一回头，才看见后面的兽人歪歪扭扭趴了一排。
兔兽人们竖起长长的耳朵，挪啊挪，挪到林楸身边。
兔葵碰了碰林楸手臂。
林楸：“葵？”
“我知道一个地方有个狼部落。”
“嗯？”
“嗯！！！”后头的狼兽人坐起来一片。
前头抽签的兽人们也急着看来。
狼安撑着藤筐，急问：“哪个狼部落？”
他们怎么一点消息都没有？
“叫赤山部落，不过我不知道他们还在不在。”
“没事，葵你快说。”林楸道。
兔兽人们原来居住的地方在比较靠南的位置，从狼部落过去，起码得走一个月的时间。按照兔兽人的脚程就更远了，他们一路过来跑了两个多月。
兔部落所在的位置叫绿湖，那是一片宝石一样的碧绿湖泊。
而那群狼兽人，则居住在绿湖的水源源头，一个叫赤山的辽阔山脉当中。
从绿湖到赤山，要一路往西再走几天。
兔兽人从没去过，也不敢去。
不过赤山很好辨认，那边生长了一种树，每到秋季前，漫山遍野一片火红，就像整座山脉燃烧起来一样。
兔葵与他们几乎没有接触，只有几次他们从山上下来，追猎物追到了河边。
兔兽人当时正巧取水，看见了那些比他们凶猛的兽人。
“他们的狼王是亚兽人，是红狼。”
兔葵至今记得，那头红狼就在他们部落外面追捕猎物一击必中的样子。
鲜血溅落在他身上，却没有他一身狼毛鲜艳夺目。
“红狼？”
“他们不是经常藏起来，都不见兽人的吗？”狼果道。
兔葵：“那个部落也不全是红狼，像你们一样。”
“一个多月啊……”兽人们喃喃。
虽说找伴侣是兽人的大事，以前走半年为了在集市上找伴侣的事也很常见，但现在部落里事多，哪里敢离开。
“嗷嗷嗷嗷嗷！”狼莫在地上打滚。
其他兽人眼巴巴地看着狼岩。
“王……”
狼岩：“雨季过后再说。”
附近有狼部落是好事，狼兽人一族天然亲近，比起其他种族，他们更信任同为狼兽人一族的兽人。
那边很远，兴许还有些部落没有的东西。
能抽空过去一趟，互相交流，这才是发展的长久之计。
“嗷嗷嗷……”
“闭嘴！”狼岩皱眉。
兽人们爪子捂住嘴筒子，高兴地在地上滚来滚去。
至于抽到房子的狼兽人，也没哪个兽人关注了。
chapters.title: 第152章

chapters.translated_text:
Once the housing distribution was finished, the orcs dispersed.

Lang Jiao followed Lang Qi back to the cave to continue the woodworking they hadn't finished.

From the very first day they arrived at Wolf Mountain, Lang Qi had brought them to this cave right after lunch.

Back then, the old guy had thrown a few pieces of wood at them to plane, then buried his head in his own work, hammering and tapping away at some pre-cut timber.

Lang Jiao had cursed him for fooling around, but Lang Qi just looked up blankly and said, "Don't be lazy, get to work."

Lang Jiao was left speechless, choked by his own frustration.

He had assumed Lang Qiao only brought them over out of pity for a bunch of old guys like them, but it turned out there was actual work to be done.

And so, from that first day, Lang Jiao and the others began planing wood.

Right now, they had just returned to the cave.

Lang Qi sat on his grass mat, which had a noticeable depression in the center from all the sitting.

Lang Jiao and the others habitually picked up the wood they hadn't finished planing, but before they could start, Lang Qi said, "Hold on. Let’s divide up the tasks; it's time to start for real."

Lang Jiao held his wood and stared at him blankly.

"What do you mean 'start for real'? Are you saying we’ve just been playing around these past few days?"

Beside Lang Jiao, Lang Pi said, "Uncle Qi, tell us."

Lang Pi was the youngest among the group of orcs unable to hunt, just over thirty. He wasn't unable to hunt due to injury, but because he had eaten so little for years to save food for his mate that his body had broken down.

His mate was Lang Xing.

Lang Qi didn't waste words and laid out the work that needed to be done.

"For the canteen, we need to make fifty sets of tables and stools; the doors and windows for Lang Mo’s new houses need to be embedded during construction, so we have to hurry; the materials for the bows and arrows the orcs want need to be collected and processed; tanning animal hides is also our job; An says there aren't enough looms, so we need to make a few more; not to mention repairing farm tools and weapons, we'll just do those as we go..."

Lang Qi finished in one breath, but heard no response.

He looked at the orcs, paused, and asked, "Which ones do you want to do?"

Lang Jiao pressed his left hand over his right, both hands trembling.

They had spent days just planing a single table leg, yet Lang Qi needed to make fifty sets of tables and chairs, plus all that other stuff...

Lang Jiao felt dizzy; he finally understood why Lang Mu had been so insanely happy a few days ago.

"All... all for us to do?"

Lang Qi nodded affirmatively.

Lang Jiao took a deep breath. "You arrange it."

They were a group of orcs who couldn't hunt; now that they had finally found something to do after being idle for so long, what was the harm in being busy?

It was just that what Lang Qi said sounded so terrifying to the orcs.

"So you'll all listen to me?"

"Hurry up."

"Do these have to be finished this year?"

"My claws are going to be worn down to nothing!"

"These stone shards aren't good enough!" the other orcs chimed in, having recovered from their shock.

Lang Qi: "We have to do it quickly anyway; surely more work will keep coming in later."

Lang Qi had experience in this area.

Qiu would come up with some novel thing at any moment, like the plowshare. And it was always urgent, forcing them to push back whatever they were currently working on. Because of this constant delay, his large stone mill took from last year until this year to finish.

Since only a few plowshares had been made this year, Lang Qi thought for a moment and added, "We also need to make a few more plowshares."

The amount of land being cultivated now was so vast that even if Qiu didn't ask now, they would have to make them for next year's plowing anyway.

"It seems like there aren't enough carts either..."

"Alright, stop talking and just arrange it." Lang Jiao was afraid that if he kept talking, they would never finish.

Lang Qi nodded and began assigning tasks.

In the past, Lang Mu and the others didn't like to use their heads, so Lang Qi was responsible for assigning tasks while they just planed the wood.

He even had to draw the diagrams for them, which was exhausting.

Now he had gotten smarter; he didn't just let Lang Jiao and the others plane wood.

He brought out the diagrams, taught them how to make each item once, and made the orcs use their brains. Whoever did the best job would be assigned that task.

Including himself, there were twenty orcs in the cave. Five orcs per group, working on one thing.

Everyone discussed it together; none of them were stupid, and these orcs who previously felt useless were now happy to do the work, so the efficiency naturally increased.

Lang Qi watched the orcs in the cave start discussing and sighed comfortably.

Lang Jiao and the others finally didn't have to keep asking him questions like Lang Mu did, and he could focus on his work.

Little did he know, just as he was immersed in the scent of wood, Lang Jiao spoke up: "Qi, Qiao said the tribe was attacked by wandering orcs. What was that about?"

Lang Qi looked up and scratched the wood fiercely.

"It’s just that the wandering orcs snatched the cubs, the orcs went out to find them, and they ran to Wolf Mountain."

"You need to be more detailed!"

Lang Qi moved his lips and sighed inwardly.

Why so many questions...

Can't you just be quiet for a moment?

Doesn't planing wood require focus?!

Facing the gazes of the old guys, he had no choice but to speak and tell the story from beginning to end.

Finally, just as he thought he could return to his woodworking, Lang Pi asked again: "So the beast-people and cubs locked up in the tribe haven't recovered yet?"

Lang Qi endured it and said, "I haven't paid attention."

"You're at Wolf Mountain and you don't pay attention... what a waste of being an old wolf!"

Lang Qi couldn't take it anymore: "Can you, can you all just focus on your work!"

Lang Jiao planed a claw mark into the wood, leaving deep grooves. "Aren't we working?"

Lang Qi: "..."

He wanted to work alone even more.

They really talked too much!

Lang Jiao didn't understand Lang Qi's frustration; they hadn't seen each other in so many years, and this old guy was complaining that he talked too much?

That wouldn't do!

They came from the same litter and were the closest of orcs. If they hadn't been separated, they would have been close partners in the same hunting team by now.

If he wasn't allowed to talk here, and he went to talk to the young ones, they couldn't relate to each other anyway.

*

However, speaking of the three beast-people and the cub brought back from the valley, the orcs had been so busy that no one had paid attention to them for a long time.

Only Lang Bing and the other little wolves, who guarded the cave and were responsible for delivering their food, knew their situation.

In the evening, the heavy rain that had been falling for days finally stopped.

The hunting and gathering team left Wolf Mountain under the cover of night to begin hunting for the rainy season.

The rest of the orcs walked out of their caves, stepping on the wet grass to collect fish traps, patrol Wolf Mountain, and dig up mushrooms popping up in the grass...

The cubs had been cooped up in the cave for a long time, wearing only little shorts, smelling of herbs, and swinging their legs as they frolicked around.

Lang Guo was about to follow them out when he heard a scream from the grass nest. He looked back and saw another cub had turned into human form.

Startled, he ran back and picked the cub up from the nest.

The other three cubs, who had been stepped on by him, shook their heads, looked at him aggrievedly, and flattened themselves like pancakes in the nest.

After this delay, Lang Sheng had already led the cub squad on a tour of the canteen.

Just as they crawled out of the house, they saw Lang Bing leaving a cave on the west side from a distance.

The cubs had never been to that cave, so once Lang Bing was far away, they immediately chased each other and approached it.

The door of the cave was closed.

But it could be pushed open.

As soon as the cubs approached, the nearby busy orcs noticed. They didn't stop them, just kept an eye on them while continuing their work.

Lang Sheng squatted at the entrance, and the other cubs gathered around.

Tu Yuan squatted beside Lang Yuan and whispered, "Yuan, the bad orcs are locked in here."

Lang Yuan held her hand and replied in a small voice, "Don't be afraid, Ah Sheng is here."

Lang Sheng puffed out his chest and nodded.

His claws were already touching the door.

Even though he didn't use much force, the door made of wooden planks creaked and slowly opened.

The cubs were startled and instantly squeezed behind Lang Sheng.

Lang Sheng’s feet were lifted off the ground by their pushing, and he had to grab the door frame to keep from falling.

He backed up, but the cubs pushed him forward.

"Hey! Stop moving!" Lang Sheng said anxiously.

The cubs froze.

They pricked up their ears and listened for a while; there was no strange movement in the cave.

But looking up, the dark cave seemed like a beast with its mouth wide open, and the cubs shivered, remembering how Lang Sheng had been kidnapped.

Lang Sheng finally managed to stand steady.

He backed up while keeping a wary eye on the inside of the cave.

This cave was located very low, with the entrance at the very bottom of Wolf Mountain.

It was dim inside, and the cubs stared for a while before they could make out the scene.

There was some dry grass spread inside, and in an inconspicuous corner, three beast-people were curled up together, motionless.

As soon as their eyes met, the cubs jumped back in fright.

The three beast-people also buried their heads, their bodies tense.

Lang Sheng didn't dare to go inside.

He scanned the area again and noticed a wooden stump in the corner. Upon closer inspection, he realized it was that cub.

The cub looked over timidly, and Lang Sheng let out an "Eh."

All the cubs behind him poked their heads out.

"Ah Sheng?"

Lang Sheng waved at the cub.

The cub didn't move.

Lang Sheng rummaged through the animal skin pouch hanging on his body and pulled out a piece of dried fish he hadn't finished at lunch. He looked at the bite mark on it—it was one he had taken a bite of and didn't like.

But it didn't matter; it was all food.

Lang Sheng held it out, shook his little fleshy hand, and whispered, "Here, for you."

In an instant, the cub rushed over, grabbed the dried fish, and stuffed it into his mouth.

He was extremely fast, and the cubs were so startled that they scattered immediately.

Only Lang Sheng stood where he was, clearly seeing the cub take his dried fish and swallow it whole.

Lang Sheng tentatively asked, "Do you want to play with us?"

The cub turned back into a wooden stump, shrinking into a corner and saying nothing.

Lang Sheng felt around his body again, but there was no more food.

He looked at his companions who had gathered back, stretched out his little chubby hand, curled his fingers, and said, "Do you guys have any dried fish?"

The cubs reached into their pouches one after another.

The cubs' pouches were small, only the size of an adult orc's palm, specially made by Lang An and the others.

When the cubs went out to play, they liked to sling their pouches over their shoulders and stuff them with leftover dried fish, pretty stones they picked up, or sour-enough-to-make-your-teeth-fall-out fruit...

Before long, a mess of chewed-on dried fish, dried vegetables, and wrinkled fruit was placed in his hands.

Lang Sheng couldn't hold it all and had to cup his hands.

He squatted down, looked at the wet grass, and told a companion to pick a large leaf.

He placed the food on the large leaf, then picked through it, choosing a piece of dried fish that looked meaty.

He shook it at the cub in the cave again.

"Do you want to eat this?"

The next instant, the food was snatched away again.

The cub inside moved so fast he left an afterimage.

The wolf orc cubs didn't run this time, exclaiming in surprise, "He's so fast!"

Everyone felt like they had found something fun and picked up the food on the large leaf. "Do you want to eat this?"

"Wow!"

"Do you want to eat this one?"

"Awooo!"

"How about this one?"

"Wah-woo!"

The cubs' exclamations grew louder and louder.

The nearby wolf orcs saw them squatting at the entrance acting suspiciously, frowned, and approached.

This cave held those beast-people and the cub; they had been kept in the tribe for almost a month, but they still always huddled inside and wouldn't come out.

They couldn't even get a word out of them.

If it weren't for Lang Bing saying the orcs were getting better and slightly reacting to the outside world, they wouldn't be feeding them for free.

These little cubs didn't know what they were "wowing" about; if they irritated those orcs... it would be a waste of effort.

The adult orcs stopped, staring in astonishment as their own cubs teased the cub in the cave as if it were a wild animal.

Everyone felt a throbbing pain in their temples and grabbed their cubs.

"What are you doing?"

"They are sick orcs!"

"Are you feeding a wild beast?!"

The cubs were picked up, looking at the adult orcs in confusion.

Especially the leader, who blinked his big eyes innocently, "We're feeding him meat."

The adult orc followed the cub's claw and looked at the cub inside, who was clutching his stomach and rolling his eyes.

They were so scared they dropped their own cubs, immediately scooped up the one inside, and rushed to find the priest.

Lang Sheng rolled on the ground and climbed up.

"What's wrong with them?"

Lang Yu slapped his head directly. "Dummy! He ate too much! Who told you to feed him like that!"

The cubs took off running, following closely behind the adult orcs who were going to find the priest.

"Don't die!"

"Wuwuwu... do you die if you eat too much?"

Lang Yu looked at the beast-people in the cave, sighed, and closed the door again.

The beast-people inside listened to the noise outside disappear, and after a long while, they moved their bodies and slowly relaxed.

Under the veranda, after Lin Qiu recovered, he began dyeing cloth again.

After many experiments, he finally found a suitable raw material for dyeing—a plant the orcs called "bitter thorn grass."

However, to dye the color well, the bitter thorn grass had to be soaked in water for several days to get the dye.

The color dyed by the bitter thorn grass was greenish-gray, like the gray stones covered in moss in the forest. In short, it was a dull, grayish color, not very pretty.

The orcs took a few looks and lost interest.

But Lin Qiu's actions gave them inspiration, and some beast-people began trying to dye their own clothes with flower juice, fruit juice... they didn't care about the material, just picked whatever was brightly colored.

However, it didn't last long after dyeing; it looked good at first, but then turned yellow.

At this moment, the orcs were surrounding Lin Qiu to discuss how to fix the color when they saw Lang Shi rushing toward the big cave holding a cub.

A group of cubs followed behind Lang Shi.

Their shorts were falling down as they ran, and they were grabbing them clumsily with their hands while snot and tears streamed down their faces, howling at the top of their lungs, which made the beast-people wince and look away in disgust.

"What's wrong?" Lang An put down the cloth and stood up to ask.

The orc holding the cub had already entered the cave, and Lang Yu, who followed behind, said hurriedly:

"These little wolf cubs ran to the west cave and teased that clouded leopard cub with their leftover food. That little cub doesn't know if he's ever been full, so he ate whatever they gave him, and now he's got a stomachache!"

As soon as he finished speaking, several beast-people also rushed toward the cave.

Lin Qiu walked in front, not even having time to wipe the water off his hands.

As soon as he entered the cave, he saw the cub placed in front of the priest.

The cub was young and had been raised in the tribe for a month, but he was still skinny. His limbs were slender, making his bloated stomach look especially large.

Lin Qiu frowned as he looked.

He walked quickly to the cub's side, and the old priest had already placed his hand on his stomach to induce vomiting.

Lang Bing was picking herbs on the side, with Yu Le and Lang Xue helping, looking like they were going to boil them for the cub.

Lin Qiu: "Do you need help?"

Lang Bing had a good grasp of the herbs and was picking quickly from the sorted herbs. He shook his head and said, "Almost done."

Just as he said this, a sound of vomiting was heard.

In a blink of an eye, the cub who had been crying his eyes out just a moment ago hurriedly backed away. The clouded leopard cub was lying on Lang Shi's arm, clutching his hair with one hand, and vomiting all over the ground.

Lang Shi patted his back, looking at the pile of vomit.

There was unchewed dried fish, dried shrimp, fruit peels, and... bugs?

Lang Shi's firm face looked a bit dark, which was very intimidating to the cubs.

The culprits stood together blankly, clutching their pant legs with their little hands, too scared to come forward.

"W-we didn't feed him bugs."

After he finally finished vomiting, Lang An brought clean water for him to rinse his mouth.

Who knew the cub would hold the cup and gulp it down as soon as he opened his mouth.

He seemed to have never been full, and his gluttony shocked the beast-people.

Lang Shi hurriedly pinched the cub's cheeks, and Lang An managed to take the cup away.

"This kid..." he said in a low voice, his brows furrowed, his words filled with pity.

It was now confirmed that the three beast-people and this cub had been snatched from other tribes by the Black Bear tribe. They hadn't done anything bad, but had been abused by the Black Bear tribe all along.

Lang An tried to touch the cub's head to comfort him.

But he shivered in fright and hurried to squeeze into Lang Shi's arms. His shoulder blades protruded, and the whole cub was dark and skinny, with not much meat on his body.

Lang An's hand paused and he pulled it back.

Lang Yu buried the filth on the ground with wood ash and then cleaned it out.

Lin Qiu brought another basin of hot water, intending to wipe the cub's face. As soon as he moved, the cub looked frightened again and tried to burrow into Lang Shi's arms.

Lang Shi felt like he was holding a fish, it was so slippery.

Lin Qiu watched and didn't dare to move.

The old priest said: "Don't make him so agitated."

Lin Qiu simply walked a little further away, looking at the huddled wolf cubs, among whom was a rabbit cub.

He waved, and the cubs came forward obediently.

"Why did you think to feed him?"

"We wanted to play with him?" Lang Yuan held Lin Qiu's finger, and seeing he wasn't disgusted, leaned his little body against him and pressed his cheek against Lin Qiu's palm.

Those watery eyes looked at Lin Qiu softly, melting his heart.

Lang Sheng: "Qiuqiu, we were wrong."

Lin Qiu pinched his cheek with his other hand. "You admit your mistakes pretty fast."

The cub nodded as if in agreement. "If you do something wrong, you have to admit it, and if you admit it, you don't get beaten."

Hearing the second half of the cub's sentence, the bit of comfort in Lin Qiu's heart vanished completely.

"Heh..." he sneered.

The cubs' skin tightened, and even Lang Yuan let go of his hand and stood obediently behind Lang Sheng.
