幼崽的哭声中满是惶惶不安。
山洞中的兽人被惊得一激灵，连山洞拐角的幼崽都急忙跑出来，吓得脑袋毛都炸了。
大山洞的狼兽人坐起，红房子里睡觉的兽人也跑来，连兔葵他们都被惊得出了山洞来看。
狼石抱着浑身都是骨头的幼崽，放也不是，不放也不是。
他手足无措，祈求般看向有幼崽的亚兽人们。
林楸抹了把脸，最先反应过来。
“你抱住他，抱好。”
狼石连忙照做。
他昨晚半夜才巡逻回来，睡了才一会儿，就被刺破耳膜的哭声惊醒。
要不是外面天亮了，狼石怕是要把怀里的幼崽抡出去。
他粗壮的胳膊收拢，像个巢穴一样，完完整整地将幼崽包裹起来。
顿时，幼崽如同倦鸟归巢，片刻只剩抽泣。
山洞里的狼兽人们全都松了一口气。
狼莫忍不住掏了掏耳朵，想说两句，瞧着狼石那大块头抱着幼崽跟哄自家崽子似的，撇了撇嘴，最后什么都没说。
幼崽闹过，大家也都睡不着了。
兽人们纷纷离开山洞，去溪边蹲了两排，叼着牙刷洗漱。
林楸跟狼岩并肩走在后头，身旁是狼安和狼莫，后头还跟了一大群狼崽子们。
“我看刚刚那一下哭得好，神找回来了。”狼安道。
“哭得惨。”
狼莫只觉心脏被紧捏了一下，现在还有点难受。
换做他们的幼崽遭了这大难……狼莫只要一想，就恨不得把作恶的兽人剁成肉酱！
幸好绿眼部落救得及时，狼圆跟狼生回来了。比起幼崽的命，那十头尖角兽跟两头弯角兽都不算什么。
林楸远远看着那个乖乖趴在狼石肩膀的云豹幼崽。
狼石肩膀很宽，幼崽又小个，安安静静把脸颊贴在上面，小手也把狼石脖子抱得紧紧的。
只看着，仿佛他俩是真父子一般。
幼崽眼神不是之前那样木木呆呆的样子，灵动了些，看着是像安说的那样，神回来了。
“也不知道他梦到了什么。”
兽人们说着闲话，走到溪边，就看到狼石蹲下来，把云豹幼崽放在腿上，一手固定他，另一只手往水里晃了晃，往幼崽脸上一抹。
劲儿大了，抹得幼崽脑袋乱歪。
可偏偏小家伙不知道躲，等狼石手撤开，云豹幼崽脸都红了一大片。
“哎呀！你动作轻点儿！”狼安快步走过去道。
林楸面上带笑，余光瞧见一个人影一闪而过。定睛一看，发现是西边亚兽人出来过。
林楸立马扯了下狼岩的手。
狼岩看过去一眼，道：“看着像要好了。”
幼崽哭不仅是自己回神，也刺激了那几个亚兽人。
林楸：“是好事。”
*
今天闷热得厉害，上午太阳就被云遮住，看着又免不了一场雨了。
天空发亮，万物皆静，有种风雨欲来的味道。
晾晒在廊下的麻布垂落，一动不动。
布早干了，林楸去收起来。
这些布都是之前做完裤子的碎布，被兽人们弄来染色，如今染色成了，颜色各异。
“变颜色了！”
狼果凑上来，随手抽了一条细看。
支部落的亚兽人们路过，也纷纷从林楸手中抽走些布条。林楸垂眸一看，手中只剩下自己染色的那些。
尽是些放在林子里不起眼的颜色。
林楸：“这个不好看吗？”
狼果瞥一眼，“不好看。”
另外几个亚兽人没狼果这么直白，只是对林楸笑笑，然后就研究手中的布去了。
麻草做的布不好着色，颜色都偏淡。
林楸手上的那个灰绿灰绿的，其他兽人手中的就五彩缤纷，跟漫山遍野的花丛似的。
“楸，这些好看，我们以后的衣服能不能也弄成这个颜色？”狼果晃了晃手中黄色的布条道。
“应该可以。”
“那我们……”
“先别急，还不知道这颜色能保持多久，再等一段时间。”
“那好吧。”
狼果直接顺走布条遛幼崽去了。
林楸看着眼前支部落来的亚兽人，轻轻吸了一口气，道：“潭。”
狼潭点点头，目光从手中的布条挪到林楸脸上，“长大了，现在这样就挺好。”
林楸：“不小了，早该长大的。”
狼潭笑了笑，眼角的皱纹加深，看着很和蔼。
“你阿爸应该会很高兴。”说罢，他就领着亚兽人们先忙去了。
支部落的兽人回来后，林楸与他们接触却不多。他们像狼部落找来的长工，都忙着干活，跟林楸都说不上几句话。
大多数时候，支部落的兽人都只悄悄观察着林楸。
楸与在支部落的时候完全不一样，如同换了一个兽人。在狼潭看来，他现在的样子，很像他的阿爸。
那个像溪水一样干净清澈的亚兽人。
长相像，性格也像。
狼潭曾经与狼楸的阿爸玩儿得最好，看到林楸就想起那个早早逝去的亚兽人。
要是他还在，幼崽变成这样，也该是欣慰的。
支部落的兽人们比狼山的兽人寡言些，他们只埋头苦干，仿佛要把之前没干过的活补回来。
可惜太阳一出来，别说烧砖，连砌房子都难受；下雨更是不方便，所以雨季后，狼莫他们也闲下来。
无事可做，狼莫又带着兽人背起藤筐，去林子里捡蘑菇。
林楸没跟着去，而是留在部落。
他一边染布，空闲时候就盯着西边山洞，时不时给那边送个饭，再观察一下云豹幼崽。
兽人多了，现在没他的活儿。
林楸坐在廊道下，摇着扇子，远远看着西边。
正看得出神，扇子被抽走，一阵凉风袭来，林楸眯了眯眼。
他侧头，下巴微微仰着。
长发被他拢在肩侧，用布条扎拢，随着风轻荡。
狼岩一边扇着风，一边低头，拉近距离。
林楸脑袋一歪，看了眼廊道四处，随后脸颊上痒痒。
林楸顺着狼岩手指看去——
一根狼毛。
“你的？”
狼岩眼中含笑，“嗯，我的。”
林楸侧过身，趴在矮墙上，又看着西边。
王的手劲儿很大，扇的风一阵一阵的，吹得林楸很舒服。
“看什么？”
“西边山洞。”
林楸守了一会儿，瞥见狼石想把幼崽交出去巡逻，送了几个狼兽人，幼崽现在要哭不哭的。
狼石看过来，林楸正以为他要送来，结果狼石抱着幼崽往西边山洞走。
等再过一会儿，他就一个兽人回来了。
“交出去了？”
狼石擦着身上的汗，林楸一瞧，他脖子跟胸口都捂出一片痱子！
“你别抓，去找祭司拿点药！”
狼石：“那小崽子太粘我了。”说着嘴角翘起来，不知是高兴还是嫌弃。
“那你怎么交出去了？”
“那不是让他跟那几个亚兽人说说话，告诉他们，我们狼部落不坏。让他们早点把事情说清楚，早点回部落。”
“幼崽会听？”
“肯定会。”
也不知道他哪里来的这个自信。
西边山洞中。
云豹幼崽回到熟悉的环境，看到三个亚兽人后，向着里面跌跌撞撞走去。
为首的亚兽人看着他，确保他完好无损，又收回目光。
云豹幼崽也不说话，只挤在他们中间，然后蹲下来。
山洞又恢复安静，狼石的期望并没有实现。
云豹幼崽呆呆看着昏暗的洞口中间，仿佛又回到了当初在黑熊部落的时候。
他埋下头，轻轻发颤。
恐惧席卷全身，他仿佛看到了满口鲜血的黑熊兽人，看到了遍地的兽人骨头，看到了一个一个被当猎物宰杀的幼崽……他哆嗦得痉挛，惊叫一声，直直冲了出去。
他不怕痛似的直接用身体撞开门，哭得凄惶，好像狼石把他抛弃了。
林楸心惊，还没来得及上前，狼石就顶着一身草药味道，跑了出来。
林楸看着一大一小重新抱在一起，道：“看来是分不开了。”
狼岩：“挺好，狼石多一个幼崽，部落多一个兽人。”
林楸忍不住用手肘撞了他一下。
狼岩撩起他颈侧的头发，放到身后去。摸了摸他下巴的汗，一边扇风一边道：“回山洞里去吧。”
*
闷热了一上午，下午又开始下雨了。
采蘑菇的兽人们火急火燎从林子里钻出来，顶着一头湿发，腰间围着兽皮裙，光着大脚丫，一副野人模样往狼山跑。
路过西边那房子，一下蹿进去。
正在布置房子的狼夜被吓了一大跳。
狼莫甩甩头上的水，看看他的脸，又看看他手上干草。
“你在干什么？”
“做窝啊。”
“你做什么窝？”
“我的房子我为什么不做？”
“你的？”
狼夜有些纳闷，“是我的啊，我抽签抽到的。”
“可王不是说只有有伴侣的兽人……”
狼夜笑起来，酷帅的脸一下变得有些憨傻，“我有啊。”
“你有？！”
*
砰的一声——
狼莫跑到食堂，扔下背篓，盯着一旁打盹的狼果看。
狼果白了他一眼。
狼莫：“啧。”
他坐下，又起身。在屋里绕了绕圈，又坐下，然后又起身。
林楸坐在一旁帮忙收拾蘑菇，被他转得眼晕。
“莫！你被虫子咬了吗？”
狼莫扑通往他身边一坐。
“楸！”
“我在。”林楸侧头在旁边狼岩的肩膀上蹭了蹭耳朵，“我没聋，听得见。”
“果跟夜什么时候成伴侣了？”
“我怎么……你说什么？”
“果跟夜！结成伴侣了！”狼莫道，“还抽到了房子。”
林楸手里的刀子抖了一下，被狼岩及时抽出去。
“果？”
虽然早有预料，但这两个兽人不声不响就在一起了？
狼果：“这有什么？”
林楸有点没反应过来，他看着雨幕中回来的狼夜，再看看一旁的狼果，然后转头看着他们的王。
狼岩捏捏他的脸，“傻了？”
“王，你知道吗？”
“嗯。”
“不需要祭司主持一下什么仪式吗？”
“如果他们需要的话。”
“凑合着过。”狼果同时道。
林楸：“可别瞎凑合。”
“知道了知道了……”狼果躺地上翻个身，两手捂住耳朵。
旁边趴着的幼崽吭哧吭哧往他身上爬，找到舒服的位置，趴下来，冲着林楸奶呼呼地嗷了一声，然后闭上眼睛开始打盹。
林楸看了狼崽一会儿，狼生又带着一大群幼崽冲进来，他们围着狼岩和林楸端正坐好，像在等着什么。
林楸闻到了一股浓烈的幼崽身上的酸臭味儿。
眼前幼崽一个个浑身湿汗，昨天才洗过澡，今天身上又裹了一层泥壳，头发也成一缕一缕的了。
臭得都有些呛鼻子！
林楸忍不住偏头压在狼岩肩膀呼吸，狼岩一边扇风，一边手指戳了下幼崽后背。
狼生回头，一本正经道：“王，阿石叔说有重要的事情要说，你们不要着急。”
狼岩：“嗯，坐远一点，有点热。”
“嗷。”幼崽乖乖往前挪。
林楸脑袋藏在狼岩肩膀闷声笑。
笑了一会儿，看幼崽频频转头，他坐直身体，只眼中残留着一点笑意。
幼崽脏兮兮的，连狼圆都滚了一身泥灰。
幼崽看来时，林楸立即移开眼。
这会儿就不要对上视线了，万一幼崽要他抱，他怕他的嫌弃伤了幼崽的心。
没坐多久，狼石就抱着云豹幼崽大步进来。
“王，阿枝告诉我他是哪个部落的了。”
“阿枝？”
林楸目光落在那云豹幼崽身上。
这么快就把名字问出来了？
“对，他叫豹枝。”
狼石坐下来，把幼崽放自己腿上坐着。
幼崽看了看眼前的一片兽人，蜷缩着往后挤，扭着脖子也要将自己藏在狼石怀里。
狼石看他这样子，两手一掐小崽子的腋窝，将他拎起来换了个方向。
幼崽顺势抱住他脖子，挂在他身上，只给他们留一个圆圆的后脑勺。
“说说。”狼岩拿起蘑菇，一边切一边道。
“他们部落就叫云豹部落，在中央大陆南部。部落里有座猫头山，长得像大猫脑袋。”
狼岩垂着眼，刮掉蘑菇脚上的泥，等了会儿，没声了。他抬起头看着狼石问：“没了？”
狼石：“没了。”
“中央大陆南部有多大，光靠个猫头山，找得到？”
不说找不找得到，他们从中央大陆出来都走了半年，从现在的狼山找过去，又要走多久？
狼部落不可能为了一个幼崽，去那么远的地方。
狼石有些为难地看着挂在自己身上的幼崽，叹道：“那怎么办？”
这几天幼崽黏着他都不愿意下地，他真成带崽的兽人了？
狼岩：“养着，什么时候真去那边了，就什么时候送去。不然等他长大了，自己找回去。”
狼崽们扭着身子回头看来。
“王，那他是不是可以跟我们玩儿了？”
狼岩捏着幼崽的脸，“玩儿什么玩儿，训练了吗？”
“训练……”幼崽眼神飘忽。
狼岩捏得用力了些，幼崽立马吱吱哇哇叫起来，溜出了食堂。
狼石抱着云豹幼崽，听他小声在自己耳边喊着阿爸。
“我不是你阿爸。”
“阿爸……”幼崽又含着哭腔，看着要哭。
“至少喊个阿父啊。”
“阿爸呜……”
狼石立马抱他起来，一边拍着幼崽后背，一边哄道：“阿爸在，阿爸在……”
狼石哄着幼崽出去了。
林楸跟狼岩都顿了下，林楸忍不住噗嗤笑出声来。
“石这个阿爸看来要当一段时间了。”
狼岩：“我看他挺乐意。”
两个兽人坐在蘑菇山后头，熟练地给蘑菇去掉泥脚，清理干净，然后切片，放入盆中。
不知不觉，等这一堆蘑菇山下去一半，林楸揉着脖子抬起头，就见狼果不知什么时候走了。
他起身活动一下，这边大门正对着隔了一个广场的小房子。狼果跟狼夜在房子那边，进进出出往里面搬东西。
林楸收回目光，又往后厨去。
雨季最多的就是蘑菇。
兽人们把蘑菇炒、煮、炸、煎、烤来来回回地做，好在蘑菇滋味好，吃起来像肉，兽人们也没吃腻。
后厨做了一排大灶，一个兽人能负责两口锅，还专门分配了一个烧火的兽人。
如今做饭不缺锅不缺灶，也不缺兽人。
林楸还没往里走几步，就被狼安赶了出来。
“楸，去地里摘点香草回来。”
“都要？”地里香草有好几种。
“都要。”
林楸找了个大叶片顶在头上，然后转身出去。
狼岩看过来，林楸道：“王，我出去摘香草。”
外面下着雨，才一会儿，草地吸饱了水，一不小心就踩进一个水洼。
好在林楸穿的是草鞋，也不怕打湿。
地里，兔葵他们顶着大叶片在忙。
他们把晒干的大叶片用麻线缝起来，一层叠一层，看着就像蓑衣一样，不过更轻便些。
兽人有兽人的巧思。
“楸？”兔葵正在疏通尾巴草地里的排水沟。
现在尾巴草穗已经全部抽出，等过了雨季，就该收割了。
“我来摘点香草。”
“要留种子的香草我标记出来了，你注意别掐到了。”
“好。”
习惯了狼部落的食物，兔葵也知道这些香草的重要性。
他想留好种，所以提前把要留种的香草挑选出来，把刚好染了色的碎布条撕成一缕一缕的，松松垮垮地系上。
这样一株一株选，很费力气，但兔兽人耐得住性子。
他们在地里经年累月地观察、筛选，不然哪能有那些好菜种。
地里香草有姜、蒜、辣草、甜草还有其他带有特殊香味的香草，连带野葱，虽然不是这个季节的，兽人们也移栽了些种在这边。
林楸走进去，蹭了一腿的雨水。
鞋底沾着泥，不一会儿就重得慌，走着还打滑。
林楸赶紧摘完出来。
身旁甘蔗叶片被雨水打得飘摇，林楸扫过一眼，注意到旁边多出的几根嫩芽，心中惊喜。
他仔细数了数，一共五株甘蔗苗。再等等，说不定雨季后就可以吃了。
怀揣着这样的期待，林楸赶紧把香草洗干净拿回去。
负责做饭的兽人动作都麻利，他这边递过去，就听到案板上切香草的声音。
林楸本来想看看，又被赶了出来。
他只好回到狼岩身边，继续处理蘑菇。
挨到中午，吃完饭，兽人们各自躺窝里睡了一觉。醒来后，兽人们又钻林子找食物。
现在多囤点蘑菇，雪季就多一样食材。去年雪季兽人们吃到最后，蘑菇都省着吃，只觉今年要囤更多一点。
空闲的兽人，便都坐在食堂里的蘑菇山前，把没吃完的收拾出来，放在灶上烘干。
忙到傍晚，蘑菇山没少，反而更多。
这里头不仅有狼莫他们从附近林子里采的，还有采集队带回来的。
怕蘑菇放坏，更多的兽人加入进来，一边挑选一些洗净切好，晚上煮了吃；一边就只简单处理，烘干保存。
食堂里亮着油灯，光线微弱。
部落能剩下来的油不多，兽人们炒菜都省着用，油灯里的油自然也没多少。
大家赶着吃完晚饭，绕着蘑菇山继续忙碌。
忙到半夜，四周只剩嘈杂虫鸣，大伙儿才打着哈欠散去。不想走的，直接倒头就睡，不一会儿，整个屋子里鼾声四起。
这雨要下一段时间，狩猎采集队也不用出远门。
这次带回来的咩咩兽多，一共五头，能吃五天。混着鱼干、野菜吃，能吃得更久一些。
不仅如此，在小狼们的努力下，现在红鸟已经超过百数，现在红鸟圈小了，需要扩建一番。
红鸟暂且不能继续扩大规模，免得红鸟饲养密度大了生病，所以部落也会时不时杀几只来吃。
有了红鸟作为补充，要是兽人们没抓到猎物，也不用像以前那样只能等着饿肚子。
*
第二天一早，兽人们手上没多少事可做，便睡了个懒觉才起。
近两百个兽人，洗漱完就往食堂里钻。
大伙儿呼啦啦的如一群被长杆赶跑的鸭子，边跑还嚷嚷着饿。
狼起的桌椅还没做完。他那山洞放不下那么多东西，做好一根凳子，也会往食堂里搬。
算上以前放在廊道的那些桌凳，食堂里现在有桌子六张，凳子十条。
兽人来得早，能抢到位置就坐凳子上，抢不到的，就在地上铺个大叶片，碗放上去，坐在地上就开吃。
林楸跟狼岩进来得晚，走进食堂，就看到靠墙那一排盘腿坐在地上的兽人们。
他们抱着比脸还大的陶碗，仰头往嘴里倒。
吃完，再打一个长长的饱嗝，抹一把嘴，舒服地靠在墙上，像软面条一样滑坐在地上躺着。
林楸：“真能吃啊……”
小盆一般的陶碗，一天三顿，每一顿都吃得干干净净。
狼岩：“走了。”
狼岩打了肉汤往桌边走，林楸跟在他后面，手里拿着筷子。
路过兽人，大伙儿咧嘴招呼：“王，楸。”
狼岩颔首，林楸也点了下头。
早上吃的骨头蘑菇汤，里面混着鱼肉、野菜，反正有什么食材就往里面加什么食材。
兽人多了，支部落的兽人回来的日子也久了，没了新鲜感。
安重新懒了下来，也不耐烦做什么花样出来。
林楸喝着那看起来难看，但滋味透着一股蘑菇鲜跟骨头香的肉汤，味道还是不差的。
正吃着，早已经吃完的狼莫急匆匆往他俩对面一坐，一屁股挤掉已经吃得差不多的兽人。
“王，雨季房子建不了。”
林楸：“你们可以适当休息。”
难得有空闲，等雨季一过，狼莫他们想休息都没空。
狼莫：“闲不住？”
雨季又闷又热，兽人很容易烦躁。现在还没到最热的时候，但狼莫已经想挑衅狼王了。
他想打架！
想发泄！
想像去年那样，打累了，身上疼，力气也没了，舒舒服服睡个一天一夜，那才叫舒坦！
不过只是想想，一对上他们王冷冰冰的眼神，理智一下就回来了。
林楸不了解他的变态想法。
但狼岩看着他，狼莫也看着他，看来是想叫他给安排事儿了。
林楸想了想，还真想到了。
“起叔那边的兽皮不知道鞣制好了没有，你们试试做些水壶出来。上次出去想喝点水都要找地方。”
兽人们时常外出，不能总喝生水，带上水壶从部落里灌点热水进去也方便。
“什么水壶？”
林楸手摸到窗边，沾了一点雨水，然后在桌面给狼莫画了个图。
“肚大口小，装水不漏。”
狼莫看一眼，就差不多知道了。
“我去找起。”
要让兽皮不漏水，还不那么好做。狼莫打算先让狼起做一个试试，然后他们再跟着做。
chapters.title: 第155章
chapters.translated_text:
The cub's crying was filled with overwhelming anxiety.

The orcs in the cave were jolted awake, and even the cubs in the corner of the cave scrambled out, so frightened that their fur stood on end.

The wolf orcs in the main cave sat up, the orcs sleeping in the red houses ran over, and even Tu Kui and the others were startled enough to come out of their caves to see what was happening.

Lang Shi held the bony cub, not knowing whether to put him down or keep holding him.

He was at a loss, looking pleadingly at the sub-beasts who had cubs of their own.

Lin Qiu wiped his face, being the first to react.

"Hold him, hold him tight."

Lang Shi hurriedly did as he was told.

He had only returned from patrol in the middle of the night and had barely slept when he was awakened by the ear-piercing cries.

If it weren't for the fact that it was already dawn outside, Lang Shi might have tossed the cub in his arms away.

His thick arms curled inward, wrapping the cub completely like a nest.

Suddenly, the cub was like a weary bird returning to its nest, and within moments, only soft sobs remained.

The wolf orcs in the cave all breathed a sigh of relief.

Lang Mo couldn't help but pick at his ear, wanting to say something, but seeing the big guy Lang Shi holding the cub as if he were soothing his own child, he curled his lip and ultimately said nothing.

Once the cub had made such a scene, everyone was wide awake.

The orcs left their caves one after another, squatting in two rows by the stream, brushing their teeth.

Lin Qiu walked side-by-side with Lang Yan in the back, with Lang An and Lang Mo beside them, and a large group of wolf cubs following behind.

"I think that cry just now was good; his spirit has returned," Lang An said.

"It was a miserable cry."

Lang Mo felt as if his heart had been tightly squeezed; he still felt a bit uncomfortable.

If it were their own cubs who had suffered such a disaster... just thinking about it made Lang Mo want to mince the evil orcs into meat paste!

Fortunately, the Green Eye tribe rescued them in time, and Lang Yuan and Lang Sheng were back. Compared to the cub's life, those ten sharp-horned beasts and two curved-horned beasts were nothing.

Lin Qiu looked from afar at the Cloud Leopard cub obediently lying on Lang Shi's shoulder.

Lang Shi's shoulders were very broad, and the cub was small, pressing his cheek quietly against them, his little hands clutching Lang Shi's neck tightly.

Just looking at them, it was as if they were true father and son.

The cub's eyes were no longer as dull and vacant as before; they were a bit more lively, looking just as Lang An had said—his spirit had returned.

"I wonder what he dreamed about."

As the orcs chatted, they walked to the stream and saw Lang Shi squat down, placing the Cloud Leopard cub on his lap, steadying him with one hand while shaking his other hand in the water and wiping it on the cub's face.

He used too much force, causing the cub's head to wobble wildly.

Yet the little guy didn't know how to dodge, and by the time Lang Shi pulled his hand away, the Cloud Leopard cub's face was bright red.

"Oh my! Be gentler!" Lang An said, walking over quickly.

Lin Qiu smiled, his peripheral vision catching a figure flashing by. Looking closely, he realized it was the sub-beasts from the west side coming out.

Lin Qiu immediately tugged on Lang Yan's hand.

Lang Yan glanced over and said, "Looks like they're getting better."

The cub's crying wasn't just him recovering his spirit; it also stimulated those sub-beasts.

Lin Qiu: "That's a good thing."

*

It was stiflingly hot today; the sun was obscured by clouds in the morning, and it looked like another rain was inevitable.

The sky was bright, everything was still, and there was a sense of a storm brewing.

The linen cloth hanging under the corridor was motionless.

The cloth was already dry, so Lin Qiu went to collect it.

These cloths were scraps left over from making pants, which the orcs had dyed; now that the dyeing was done, they were all different colors.

"It changed color!"

Lang Guo leaned in and grabbed a strip to look at it closely.

The sub-beasts from the branch tribe passed by and also snatched some cloth strips from Lin Qiu's hands. Lin Qiu looked down and saw that only the ones he had dyed himself remained in his hands.

They were all colors that were inconspicuous in the forest.

Lin Qiu: "Are these not good-looking?"

Lang Guo glanced at them, "Not good-looking."

The other sub-beasts weren't as blunt as Lang Guo; they just smiled at Lin Qiu and then went back to studying the cloth in their hands.

Cloth made from hemp grass was hard to dye, so the colors were all quite pale.

The gray-green one in Lin Qiu's hand was dull, while the ones in the other orcs' hands were colorful, like a field of flowers.

"Qiu, these are pretty. Can we make our future clothes this color too?" Lang Guo asked, shaking the yellow cloth strip in his hand.

"It should be possible."

"Then we..."

"Don't be in a hurry. We don't know how long these colors will last yet, let's wait a while."

"Alright then."

Lang Guo took the cloth strips and went off to look after the cubs.

Lin Qiu looked at the sub-beasts from the branch tribe in front of him, took a soft breath, and said, "Tan."

Lang Tan nodded, his gaze shifting from the cloth strip in his hand to Lin Qiu's face, "You've grown up, and you're doing just fine now."

Lin Qiu: "I'm not small anymore; I should have grown up long ago."

Lang Tan smiled, the wrinkles at the corners of his eyes deepening, looking very kind.

"Your father would have been very happy." After saying this, he led the sub-beasts away to get back to work.

Since the orcs from the branch tribe returned, Lin Qiu hadn't had much contact with them. They were like long-term laborers hired by the Wolf tribe, busy working and rarely having a chance to talk to Lin Qiu.

Most of the time, the orcs from the branch tribe just quietly observed Lin Qiu.

Qiu was completely different from when he was in the branch tribe, as if he were a different orc. To Lang Tan, he looked very much like his father now.

That sub-beast who was as clean and clear as a mountain stream.

They looked alike, and their personalities were similar too.

Lang Tan used to be best friends with Lang Qiu's father, and seeing Lin Qiu reminded him of that sub-beast who had passed away so early.

If he were still here, he would surely be comforted to see the cub turn out like this.

The orcs from the branch tribe were more taciturn than the orcs of Wolf Mountain; they just buried themselves in hard work, as if trying to make up for all the work they hadn't done before.

Unfortunately, once the sun came out, let alone firing bricks, even building houses was miserable; and it was even more inconvenient when it rained, so after the rainy season, Lang Mo and the others were also idle.

With nothing to do, Lang Mo took the orcs and carried their rattan baskets to the forest to pick mushrooms again.

Lin Qiu didn't follow; he stayed in the tribe.

While dyeing cloth, he would stare at the western cave in his spare time, occasionally sending food over and observing the Cloud Leopard cub.

With more orcs around, there was no work for him to do.

Lin Qiu sat under the corridor, fanning himself, looking far toward the west.

Just as he was lost in thought, the fan was snatched away, and a cool breeze hit him, making Lin Qiu squint.

He tilted his head, his chin slightly raised.

His long hair was gathered to the side of his shoulder, tied with a cloth strip, and swayed gently with the wind.

Lang Yan fanned him while lowering his head, closing the distance between them.

Lin Qiu tilted his head, glanced around the corridor, and then felt an itch on his cheek.

Lin Qiu followed Lang Yan's finger—

A wolf hair.

"Yours?"

Lang Yan's eyes held a smile, "Mm, mine."

Lin Qiu turned his body, leaning on the low wall, and looked toward the west again.

The King's strength was great, and the breeze from the fan came in waves, making Lin Qiu feel very comfortable.

"What are you looking at?"

"The western cave."

Lin Qiu watched for a while and caught a glimpse of Lang Shi trying to hand the cub over to go on patrol, sending him to a few wolf orcs; the cub was on the verge of tears.

Lang Shi looked over, and just as Lin Qiu thought he was going to bring him over, Lang Shi walked toward the western cave with the cub.

After a while, he returned alone.

"Did you hand him over?"

Lang Shi wiped the sweat from his body, and Lin Qiu noticed that his neck and chest were covered in heat rash!

"Don't scratch it, go find the priest and get some medicine!"

Lang Shi: "That little cub is just too clingy." As he spoke, the corners of his mouth curled up, not knowing if it was out of happiness or annoyance.

"Then why did you hand him over?"

"I wanted him to talk to those sub-beasts and tell them that our Wolf tribe isn't bad. Let them clear things up early and return to their tribe sooner."

"Will the cub listen?"

"He definitely will."

Who knows where he got that confidence.

In the western cave.

The Cloud Leopard cub returned to the familiar environment, and upon seeing the three sub-beasts, he stumbled toward them.

The leading sub-beast looked at him, ensured he was unharmed, and then looked away.

The Cloud Leopard cub didn't speak either, just squeezed between them and squatted down.

The cave returned to silence; Lang Shi's expectations were not met.

The Cloud Leopard cub stared blankly at the dim entrance of the cave, as if he had returned to the time he was at the Black Bear tribe.

He buried his head and trembled slightly.

Fear swept through his entire body; he seemed to see the blood-stained mouths of the Black Bear orcs, the orc bones scattered everywhere, the cubs being slaughtered like prey... he shivered in a spasm, let out a scream, and rushed straight out.

As if he didn't fear pain, he crashed through the door with his body, crying miserably, as if Lang Shi had abandoned him.

Lin Qiu was startled, and before he could step forward, Lang Shi ran out, smelling of medicinal herbs.

Lin Qiu watched the big and small figures hugging each other again and said, "Looks like they can't be separated."

Lang Yan: "That's good, Lang Shi has one more cub, and the tribe has one more orc."

Lin Qiu couldn't help but nudge him with his elbow.

Lang Yan brushed the hair from the side of his neck to his back. He touched the sweat on his chin and said while fanning him, "Let's go back into the cave."

*

After a stifling morning, it started raining again in the afternoon.

The orcs picking mushrooms scrambled out of the forest in a hurry, their hair wet, wearing only animal skin skirts around their waists, their big feet bare, looking like wild men as they ran toward Wolf Mountain.

Passing by that house on the west side, they darted inside.

Lang Ye, who was decorating the house, was given a huge fright.

Lang Mo shook the water off his head, looked at his face, and then at the dry grass in his hands.

"What are you doing?"

"Making a nest."

"What kind of nest are you making?"

"Why wouldn't I make a nest in my own house?"

"Yours?"

Lang Ye was a bit puzzled, "It's mine, I drew the lot for it."

"But didn't the King say only orcs with partners..."

Lang Ye laughed, his cool, handsome face suddenly becoming a bit silly, "I have one."

"You have one?!"

*

With a bang—

Lang Mo ran to the cafeteria, threw down his basket, and stared at Lang Guo, who was dozing off to the side.

Lang Guo rolled his eyes at him.

Lang Mo: "Tsk."

He sat down, then stood up again. He paced around the room, sat down again, and then stood up once more.

Lin Qiu was sitting nearby helping to clean mushrooms, feeling dizzy from watching him.

"Mo! Were you bitten by a bug?"

Lang Mo plopped down beside him.

"Qiu!"

"I'm here." Lin Qiu tilted his head and rubbed his ear against Lang Yan's shoulder, "I'm not deaf, I can hear you."

"When did Guo and Ye become partners?"

"How would I... what did you say?"

"Guo and Ye! They've become partners!" Lang Mo said, "And they even drew a house."

The knife in Lin Qiu's hand shook, and Lang Yan took it away just in time.

"Guo?"

Although he had expected it, these two orcs got together without a sound?

Lang Guo: "What's the big deal?"

Lin Qiu hadn't quite reacted yet; he looked at Lang Ye returning through the rain, then at Lang Guo, and then turned to look at their King.

Lang Yan pinched his cheek, "Are you stunned?"

"King, did you know?"

"Mm."

"Doesn't the priest need to preside over some ceremony?"

"If they need one."

"We're just making do," Lang Guo added at the same time.

Lin Qiu: "Don't just 'make do' blindly."

"Got it, got it..." Lang Guo lay on the ground, rolled over, and covered his ears with both hands.

The cub lying nearby crawled onto him, found a comfortable spot, lay down, let out a milky "ao" at Lin Qiu, and closed his eyes to doze off.

Lin Qiu watched the wolf cub for a while, then Lang Sheng rushed in with a large group of cubs; they sat upright around Lang Yan and Lin Qiu, as if waiting for something.

Lin Qiu smelled a strong, sour, musty odor coming from the cubs.

The cubs in front of him were all covered in wet sweat; they had just bathed yesterday, but today they were covered in a shell of mud again, and their hair was in clumps.

It was so smelly it was almost choking!

Lin Qiu couldn't help but turn his head and press it against Lang Yan's shoulder to breathe; Lang Yan fanned him while poking the cub's back with his finger.

Lang Sheng looked back and said seriously, "King, Uncle A-Shi said there's something important to say, don't be impatient."

Lang Yan: "Mm, sit a bit further away, it's a bit hot."

"Ao." The cub obediently moved forward.

Lin Qiu hid his head on Lang Yan's shoulder and laughed muffledly.

After laughing for a while, seeing the cubs turning their heads frequently, he sat up straight, though a hint of a smile remained in his eyes.

The cubs were filthy, and even Lang Yuan was covered in mud and dust.

When the cubs looked over, Lin Qiu immediately looked away.

It was better not to make eye contact right now; in case the cubs wanted him to hold them, he was afraid his disgust would hurt their feelings.

They hadn't been sitting long when Lang Shi walked in with the Cloud Leopard cub in his arms.

"King, A-Zhi told me which tribe he's from."

"A-Zhi?"

Lin Qiu's gaze fell on the Cloud Leopard cub.

He asked for his name so quickly?

"Yes, his name is Bao Zhi."

Lang Shi sat down and placed the cub on his lap.

The cub looked at the orcs in front of him, curled up and squeezed backward, twisting his neck to hide himself in Lang Shi's arms.

Seeing this, Lang Shi pinched the little cub's armpits with both hands and lifted him up to change his direction.

The cub took the opportunity to hug his neck, hanging on him, leaving them only a round back of his head.

"Tell us," Lang Yan said, picking up a mushroom and slicing it.

"Their tribe is called the Cloud Leopard tribe, in the southern part of the Central Continent. There is a Cat-Head Mountain in the tribe that looks like a big cat's head."

Lang Yan lowered his eyes, scraped the mud off the mushroom stem, and waited for a while, but there was no more sound. He looked up at Lang Shi and asked, "That's it?"

Lang Shi: "That's it."

"How big is the southern part of the Central Continent? Can you find it just by a Cat-Head Mountain?"

Not to mention whether they could find it, it took them half a year to get out of the Central Continent; how long would it take to find it from the current Wolf Mountain?

The Wolf tribe couldn't go to such a far place for one cub.

Lang Shi looked at the cub hanging on him, feeling troubled, and sighed, "Then what should we do?"

The cub hadn't been willing to get off him for the past few days; had he really become an orc who raises cubs?

Lang Yan: "Raise him. When we actually go there, we'll send him back. Otherwise, when he grows up, he can find his own way back."

The wolf cubs twisted their bodies and looked back.

"King, then can he play with us now?"

Lang Yan pinched the cub's face, "Play? What play? Did you finish your training?"

"Training..." The cub's eyes drifted.

Lang Yan pinched harder, and the cub immediately squeaked and scrambled out of the cafeteria.

Lang Shi held the Cloud Leopard cub, listening to him whisper "A-Ba" in his ear.

"I am not your A-Ba."

"A-Ba..." The cub said with a crying tone, looking like he was about to cry.

"At least call me A-Fu."

"A-Ba, woo..."

Lang Shi immediately picked him up, patted the cub's back, and coaxed, "A-Ba is here, A-Ba is here..."

Lang Shi coaxed the cub and went outside.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan both paused, and Lin Qiu couldn't help but burst into laughter.

"Looks like Shi is going to be an A-Ba for a while."

Lang Yan: "I think he's quite happy about it."

The two orcs sat behind the mushroom mountain, skillfully removing the muddy stems, cleaning them, slicing them, and putting them into a basin.

Without realizing it, after half of the mushroom mountain was gone, Lin Qiu rubbed his neck and looked up, only to see that Lang Guo had left at some point.

He stood up to stretch, and the main gate here faced the small house across the plaza. Lang Guo and Lang Ye were at the house, moving things in and out.

Lin Qiu withdrew his gaze and went to the back kitchen.

Mushrooms were the most abundant thing in the rainy season.

The orcs stir-fried, boiled, deep-fried, pan-fried, and roasted them over and over again; fortunately, mushrooms tasted good, like meat, so the orcs didn't get tired of them.

The back kitchen had a row of large stoves, one orc could be responsible for two pots, and a special orc was assigned to tend the fire.

Now there was no shortage of pots, stoves, or orcs for cooking.

Lin Qiu hadn't walked a few steps inside before he was chased out by Lang An.

"Qiu, go to the field and pick some herbs."

"All of them?" There were several kinds of herbs in the field.

"All of them."

Lin Qiu found a large leaf to put on his head and turned to go out.

Lang Yan looked over, and Lin Qiu said, "King, I'm going out to pick herbs."

It was raining outside, and after just a moment, the grass was soaked with water, and one could easily step into a puddle.

Fortunately, Lin Qiu was wearing straw sandals, so he wasn't afraid of getting them wet.

In the field, Tu Kui and the others were busy with large leaves on their heads.

They sewed the dried large leaves together with hemp thread, layer by layer, looking like a straw raincoat, but lighter.

The orcs had their own ingenuity.

"Qiu?" Tu Kui was clearing the drainage ditch in the tail-grass field.

Now that all the tail-grass ears had sprouted, it would be time to harvest after the rainy season.

"I'm here to pick some herbs."

"I've marked the herbs that need to be kept for seeds, be careful not to pinch them."

"Okay."

Having gotten used to the food of the Wolf tribe, Tu Kui also knew the importance of these herbs.

He wanted to save good seeds, so he picked out the herbs for seeds in advance and tied them loosely with strips of dyed cloth.

Selecting them plant by plant was very laborious, but the rabbit orcs were patient.

They observed and screened in the fields year after year; otherwise, how could they have such good vegetable seeds?

The herbs in the field included ginger, garlic, spicy grass, sweet grass, and other herbs with special fragrances; even wild onions, although not in season, had been transplanted by the orcs.

Lin Qiu walked in, getting his legs covered in rainwater.

His shoe soles were covered in mud, and soon they felt heavy and slippery.

Lin Qiu quickly finished picking and came out.

The sugarcane leaves beside him swayed in the rain, and Lin Qiu glanced over, noticing a few new shoots, feeling pleasantly surprised.

He counted carefully; there were five sugarcane seedlings in total. Wait a little longer, and maybe they could be eaten after the rainy season.

Carrying this expectation, Lin Qiu quickly washed the herbs and took them back.

The orcs in charge of cooking were quick; as soon as he handed them over, he heard the sound of herbs being chopped on the cutting board.

Lin Qiu wanted to take a look, but he was chased out again.

He had no choice but to return to Lang Yan's side and continue processing mushrooms.

By noon, after eating, the orcs each went to their nests to sleep. After waking up, they went into the forest to find food again.

Storing more mushrooms now meant one more ingredient for the snowy season. Last snowy season, the orcs had to ration their mushrooms by the end, so they felt they should store more this year.

The idle orcs sat in front of the mushroom mountain in the cafeteria, cleaning up what hadn't been eaten and drying them on the stove.

By evening, the mushroom mountain hadn't shrunk; instead, it had grown.

This included not only what Lang Mo and the others had picked from the nearby forest but also what the gathering team had brought back.

Afraid of the mushrooms spoiling, more orcs joined in, picking some to wash and slice for dinner, while simply processing the rest for drying and storage.

The cafeteria was lit by oil lamps, the light dim.

There wasn't much oil left in the tribe, and the orcs used it sparingly for cooking, so naturally, there wasn't much in the oil lamps.

Everyone hurried to finish dinner and continued to work around the mushroom mountain.

It wasn't until midnight, when only the noisy chirping of insects remained, that everyone dispersed with yawns. Those who didn't want to leave just flopped down and fell asleep, and soon, snoring filled the entire room.

This rain would last for a while, so the hunting and gathering teams didn't need to go far.

This time they brought back many Baa-Baa beasts, five in total, which could last for five days. Mixed with dried fish and wild vegetables, they could last even longer.

Not only that, thanks to the efforts of the little wolves, there were now over a hundred red birds, and the red bird pen was too small and needed to be expanded.

The scale of the red birds couldn't be expanded for the time being, to avoid illness from high density, so the tribe would kill a few to eat from time to time.

With the red birds as a supplement, if the orcs didn't catch any prey, they wouldn't have to wait around hungry like before.

*

The next morning, the orcs didn't have much to do, so they slept in.

Nearly two hundred orcs rushed into the cafeteria after washing up.

Everyone swarmed in like a group of ducks chased by a long pole, shouting that they were hungry as they ran.

Lang Qi hadn't finished making the tables and chairs. His cave couldn't hold so many things, so whenever he finished a stool, he would move it to the cafeteria.

Counting the tables and stools previously placed in the corridor, there were now six tables and ten stools in the cafeteria.

The orcs who arrived early grabbed seats on the stools, and those who couldn't spread large leaves on the ground, placed their bowls on them, and ate while sitting on the floor.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan came in late, and upon entering the cafeteria, they saw the orcs sitting cross-legged on the floor along the wall.

They held ceramic bowls bigger than their faces, tilting their heads to pour the contents into their mouths.

After eating, they would let out a long, satisfied burp, wipe their mouths, and lean comfortably against the wall, sliding down to lie on the floor like soft noodles.

Lin Qiu: "They really can eat..."

Ceramic bowls the size of small basins, three meals a day, and every meal was eaten clean.

Lang Yan: "Let's go."

Lang Yan ladled some meat soup and walked toward the table, with Lin Qiu following behind, holding chopsticks.

Passing by the orcs, everyone grinned and greeted, "King, Qiu."

Lang Yan nodded, and Lin Qiu nodded as well.

They were eating bone and mushroom soup in the morning, mixed with fish and wild vegetables; whatever ingredients they had, they just added them in.

With more orcs around and the branch tribe having been back for a while, the novelty had worn off.

An had become lazy again and didn't bother to make anything fancy.

Lin Qiu drank the meat soup, which looked unappealing but tasted of mushroom freshness and bone broth; it wasn't bad at all.

Just as he was eating, Lang Mo, who had already finished, hurried over and sat opposite them, squeezing out an orc who had almost finished eating.

"King, we can't build houses during the rainy season."

Lin Qiu: "You can take a proper rest."

It was rare to have free time; once the rainy season was over, Lang Mo and the others wouldn't have time to rest even if they wanted to.

Lang Mo: "Can't stay idle?"

The rainy season was stuffy and hot, and orcs were easily irritable. It wasn't the hottest time yet, but Lang Mo already wanted to provoke the Wolf King.

He wanted to fight!

He wanted to vent!

He wanted to be like last year, fighting until he was tired, his body aching, his strength gone, and then sleeping comfortably for a day and a night—that was what you called comfort!

But that was just a thought; as soon as he met their King's cold eyes, his reason returned instantly.

Lin Qiu didn't understand his twisted thoughts.

But Lang Yan was looking at him, and Lang Mo was also looking at him; it seemed he wanted him to arrange something to do.

Lin Qiu thought for a moment and actually came up with something.

"I don't know if the animal skins at Uncle Qi's place have been tanned yet; you guys should try making some water bottles. Last time we went out, we had to look for places whenever we wanted to drink water."

The orcs often went out and couldn't always drink raw water; carrying a water bottle filled with hot water from the tribe would be convenient.

"What kind of water bottle?"

Lin Qiu reached the window, dipped his finger in some rainwater, and drew a diagram for Lang Mo on the table.

"Big belly, small mouth, so water won't leak."

Lang Mo took one look and understood.

"I'll go find Qi."

Making animal skins leak-proof wasn't easy. Lang Mo planned to have Lang Qi make one first, and then they would follow suit.

chapters.title: 第156章
chapters.translated_text:
When Lang Mo took his squad members to find Lang Qi, the two couples who had been assigned houses were busy decorating their new homes.

The houses were small but sturdy. Each house had two rooms, one large and one small; considering that they would eventually have cubs living with them, an extra small room had been built.

Since Lang Guo had to keep an eye on the cubs, that room was decorated slowly by Lang Ye himself.

The house next door was assigned to the orcs from Lang Shan's side.

The male orc was named Lang Li, and the sub-orc was named Lang Yu.

Lang Li was an orc from the first hunting squad, and Lang Yu was from the gathering squad. Neither of them was young; they were already in their early thirties.

They had both struggled through the hard times with the tribe. They had had cubs before—twice, in fact—but neither had survived.

The two orcs had become afraid, and for many years after that, they hadn't dared to have any more.

When the houses were being assigned, the King had required every orc with a partner to draw lots.

Lang Li and his partner hadn't intended to have cubs, but they hadn't expected to be chosen.

They knew this house was a perk for couples who wanted cubs. They weren't prepared and were afraid of being hurt again, so they thought about giving the spot to other orcs.

However, An said that since they had drawn it, it was theirs and couldn't be given away.

The two orcs had been dragging their feet. Now that they finally had some rest and saw the young couple next door decorating their house, they decided to move in as well.

Lang Mo and the others had worked so hard to build them; they couldn't just leave them empty, or it would be a waste.

The sound of rain was like scattered beans, clattering crisp and clear against the roof.

Lang Yu stood in the empty room, looking up at the tiles arranged like fish scales, lost in thought for a moment.

He had spent years following the gathering squad, and his skin was a beautiful wheat color. His slightly long hair had a bit of a wave and was a lovely silver-gray.

Unlike most sub-orcs in the tribe who had slightly heroic features, Lang Yu’s eyes were round, and his face was round. Now that his health was better than before, he looked a bit younger than his actual age.

Yet, those eyes held the weariness of someone who had seen much of life.

When Lang Li came in carrying a wooden stump while holding a large leaf over his head, he saw his partner staring blankly at the ceiling.

"A-Yu."

Lang Yu snapped out of it, stepped forward, took the large leaf from his partner's head, and placed it under the eaves.

He smoothed his partner's black hair, brushing off the rainwater that had clung to it.

Lang Li put down the wooden stump and straightened up.

He was half a head taller than his partner and broader in build; when he leaned down, he could wrap his arms around his partner and hide him completely.

"There are too many orcs in the cave. We'll tidy this place up and live here from now on."

"Otherwise, maybe we should still give it to an orc who wants..."

Lang Li held Lang Yu's hand. Even on such a hot day, his partner's hands were ice cold.

He couldn't help but use some force, pulling him toward the back of the room.

"The past is in the past. Let's not think about it anymore."

But as soon as the comforting words were spoken, tears welled up in Lang Yu's eyes, filled with the helplessness and pain of someone trapped in a quagmire.

"How can you say it's easy to forget?"

"A-Yu..."

Lang Yu rested his head on his partner's shoulder, weeping silently.

His cubs, his two cubs...

When they were young, they had cubs not long after getting together. Although they didn't have much food back then, they were young and full of spirit, unafraid of hardship. But who would have thought that the cubs would be gone not long after they were born.

For the two years that followed, Lang Yu would dream of them every time he had a nightmare.

Lang Li was afraid he would suffer too much and that his health would fail, so he had him join the gathering squad. He was busy every day, and as time passed, it seemed he had forgotten.

Later, they had another cub.

This time, the couple was extremely careful. Although all the tribe's cubs were raised together, they would go to check on theirs every day when they returned.

After finally raising the cub to three years old, it had successfully transformed into human form and could run and jump. Just as they were about to breathe a sigh of relief, the cub didn't make it through an illness.

This time, the couple suffered an even greater blow. Compared to the first cub who left shortly after birth, they had watched the second cub grow day by day, watched him learn to call them 'Baba' and 'Father,' watched him run and jump, and heard him clamoring to learn hunting from the King...

Yet, he was still gone.

Since then, they never dared to mention the word 'cub,' and even seeing the group of cubs in the tribe made them want to avoid them.

If it weren't for the house assignment this time, they wouldn't have thought about this.

Just now, as Lang Yu stood in the room lost in thought, he realized with a start that it had already been eight years since the second cub left.

Eight years—if his two cubs were still here...

Lang Yu leaned into his partner's arms, sobbing uncontrollably.

He didn't dare to think about it, and he didn't dare to have another one.

Lang Li's eyes were also red. He bit his lip, his hands trembling, and only then did he suppress his emotions, focusing on comforting his partner.

"Don't think about it, A-Yu, let's not think about it."

Lang Li helped Lang Yu sit on the wooden stump and squatted at his feet, his rough hands carefully wiping his partner's face, brushing away the tears.

He gripped Lang Yu's hands and said, "Since the house is assigned, we'll live in it. If the King wants it back later, we'll just move out. Stop crying, or your eyes will hurt again."

Lang Yu lowered his head and gave a miserable smile.

Lang Li's heart ached to see this; he knelt halfway to meet him, pressing his head against his own shoulder.

He quickly wiped the corners of his own eyes, waiting for his partner to calm down.

After a long while, Lang Yu said hoarsely, "Just tidy it up simply."

Lang Li immediately replied, "Okay. There's a heated brick bed inside; I'll put some dry grass on it, and we can bring the animal skins over to sleep."

Lang Yu nodded, having no energy to do anything else.

If they were to live here, they would live here. As his partner said, if the King wanted it back, they would just move out.

Lang Li continued to work, and Lang Yu stood up, moving the wooden stump to the corner.

The tribe didn't have chairs, so many orcs used wooden stumps instead; there were plenty of them in the tribe anyway.

He rarely thought about the cubs now.

But every time he did, it took a long time to recover. That heart-wrenching pain felt as if it had crushed him entirely, only for him to be pieced back together bit by bit.

Lang Yu closed his eyes, leaning against the wall, his heart filled with endless exhaustion.

Food was scarce, the weather was extreme, and it was hard for cubs to survive.

The Lang tribe looked as if the clouds had cleared after the rain, but every one of those dead cubs was like a thorn stuck in the hearts of their parents.

It wasn't that they didn't want them; it was that they didn't dare to.

They were afraid.

*

The rainy season was hard to endure, but fortunately, as the weather got hotter, the orcs began to use ice, and Lin Qiu made quite a few iced drinks, which made the orcs feel a bit better.

The houses were tidied up, and the two orc couples had already moved in.

At first, the other orcs were curious and would peek around the door whenever they passed by, but after being pelted with things by the occupants a few times, they gradually understood that these houses were like small caves and couldn't be entered easily.

Inside the houses, the orcs could do their own things.

Their belongings didn't have to be piled up by the grass nests anymore. The space was sufficient for two orcs, so they could arrange it however they liked.

Once the orcs realized the benefits of the houses, their indifferent attitude changed instantly.

In order to get a house assigned as soon as possible, the orcs started pestering the members of Lang Mo's squad.

They couldn't fire bricks or build houses during the rainy season, so the orcs, having nothing better to do, could prepare the brick blanks in advance.

That way, once the rainy season was over, they wouldn't have to wait and could fire them immediately for use.

Lang Mo was pestered until he had no choice. He slapped the animal skin water bottle onto the orcs, handed the task over to them, and after checking with Lang Yan, went to live in the cave on the west side.

Time flew by, and the rainy season was halfway over.

This time when the hunting squad went out, they caught another curved-horn beast. Adding it to the one they had caught before, they had two, and the Lang tribe planned to go and pay off their debt first.

Just in case, Lang Yan picked a hunting squad to go and deliver them.

Lin Qiu wanted to go along, and the little wolf gathering squad led by Lang Bing was also going.

It wasn't easy to make a trip to the south. Most of the medicinal herbs sent by Bai Que were from their territory, and the Lang tribe still didn't have enough.

Now that the market wasn't open, they could only look for them themselves and try to gather as much as possible.

They set off at night as usual.

The weather was hot, so they traveled at night and rested during the day.

Lin Qiu kept up with the run; after exercising for so long, he could now keep up with the squad.

The orcs left after dinner. The curved-horn beasts walked slowly, and the orcs also pulled carts and carried rattan baskets.

They would cut some wild grass and hemp grass from the south, bring back some bird droppings, catch some prey, or pick some lotus pods... anyway, since they were going so far, they couldn't return empty-handed.

The moon was bright and the stars were sparse, and the path in the forest was faintly visible.

Lang Huo's squad was driving the curved-horn beasts in front, while Lin Qiu and the little wolves walked behind, with Lang Yan at his side.

Lang Bing had even brought Yu Le with him this time.

Since they would be away for a long time, he wanted to teach Yu Le to recognize medicinal herbs while letting him see their growth environment in the field.

That was how the priest had taught him, and he had his own way of teaching Yu Le.

As they jogged along, Lang Bing spoke about the tribe's medicinal herbs.

"Before, when the King and the others went to the valley to help the Black Feather orcs, the orcs used up most of the life-saving pills, and the tribe no longer has the herbs to make them."

"Besides that, there aren't enough herbs for heatstroke, and there are no herbs for muscle regeneration, or for treating broken bones... many are gone."

Lin Qiu hadn't been to the priest's place for a long time and hadn't paid attention to the herbs. Hearing Lang Bing mention it, he frowned and said, "Doesn't the branch tribe still send some?"

"Only a few types; it's not enough to make up for the shortage."

Medicinal herbs were an important resource for a tribe. Although some of the herbs the priest had on hand had been stored for years and had lost their potency, having some was better than having none.

Now that they were exhausted, the priest was a bit panicked and repeatedly warned the orcs going out not to get injured.

Because there was no medicine to use.

"With no market, does that mean we can only look for them ourselves?" Lin Qiu murmured.

Lang Yan: "Tribes with priests all gather medicinal herbs, but they aren't circulating to our side right now."

"Then what should we do?"

"Once the tribe is stable, we should make a trip out."

Lang Bing: "King, I have to go too."

Lang Yan nodded.

Lin Qiu: "How long will this trip take?"

"A few months, half a year, a year... it's all possible."

The herb crisis hadn't just appeared now; it had existed before, but the orcs were barely getting enough to eat, so they couldn't worry about this.

"I'm going too."

"Wait a little longer."

The orcs from the branch tribe hadn't fully arrived yet, and the tribe couldn't support so many orcs just by hunting; they couldn't leave yet.

For now, they could only look around the vicinity; going out for ten days or half a month to find herbs would also work. They would gather as much as they could, and then they could use it to trade with the priests of other tribes.

The forest was heavy with moisture. The deeper they went, the more dew accumulated on the wolves' fur, making it feel heavy.

From Lang Shan to the valley, it took two days after the snow season passed. The Green Eye tribe was located further south of the valley, and the journey was longer. If they didn't take a detour, it would take two and a half to nearly three days.

Now that the orcs were driving the curved-horn beasts, resting during the day and traveling at night, it took them a full four days to reach the border of the Green Eye tribe, where the Grey Wing orcs had previously built their nests.

The Green Eye tribe's wooden houses were built right by this lake.

As soon as the wolf orcs arrived with the curved-horn beasts, a head poked out from a tree on the other side of the lake.

Lang Yun shouted: "We've brought you the curved-horn beasts!"

The Green Eye orc on sentry duty in the tree was delighted. He just called out a few times into the forest, and Green Ren led his clansmen out from the woods behind the wooden houses.

They didn't just live by the lake; they also lived in treehouses in the forest.

The two curved-horn beasts had their necks tied with grass ropes by the wolf orcs.

Several Green Eye orcs flew across the lake, landed on the two trees leaning over the water, and then slid down to stand in front of them.

"Wolf King."

Lang Yan: "Two curved-horn beasts, all here."

Green Ren looked at the curved-horn beasts. They were both adult beasts, fat and sturdy, full of meat.

The Green Eye orcs couldn't help but swallow, and under Green Ren's command, they drove the curved-horn beasts into the tribe.

With the task completed, Lang Yan planned to leave.

However, Green Ren said: "The tribe is making meat soup, why don't you stay and eat?"

The wolf orcs looked at him strangely.

You have to know, when the Green Eye orcs ambushed the branch tribe, some of their orcs had been killed by the wolf orcs.

They weren't holding a grudge, and they were even trying to make amends with the Lang tribe—was there something wrong with their heads?

Green Ren: "Consider it me returning a meal to you."

The wolf orcs curled their lips. Was this to be even, and then settle the score later?

Lang Yan: "Then I'll trouble you."

"Eh?" The wolf orcs stared at the back of their Wolf King's head.

Why did he agree?

The lake wasn't big, and the orcs walked around the shore to the rows of wooden houses on the other side.

Looking at the clear, beautiful lake water under the sunlight, they finally understood why the Green Eye orcs chose this place to build their houses.

It was a good place!

The scenery was beautiful, the view was open, and it was convenient to get water.

However, the wolf orcs stared at the meat soup in the pottery pot.

Lang Huo said: "You used the water from the lake?"

There were orc bones in the lake.

Green Ren pointed to the small river flowing into the lake, and only then did the wolf orcs feel at ease and sit down.

The Green Eye tribe had dealt with the branch tribe, but they didn't have much contact with the orcs from Lang Shan.

Only that one time they saved the cubs and sent them back, which was exchanged for ten sharp-horn beasts and two curved-horn beasts.

There were no tribes nearby like the branch tribe that they could steal food from.

They didn't think much of the food from the Bai Que tribe to the northeast, they didn't dare go to Lang Shan in the north, and they couldn't beat the Black Feather tribe to the northwest...

They were used to stealing and robbing when they were crowded in the south. When they first moved here, they were lost and huddled in the tribe, going hungry for several days.

Coincidentally, the prey sent by the wolf orcs helped them get through that time.

Now that the tribe had rebuilt its wooden houses and treehouses, they started to support themselves and go hunting in their territory.

Misfortune and fortune are interdependent. Because the branch tribe left the south, they thought they would be displaced. But arriving here, they accidentally saved the wolf cubs, got prey, and learned how to survive from then on.

From confirming the territory boundaries and leaving marks, to discovering prey in their territory time and time again, they wept with joy.

The north had its own advantages; the land was vast and there were few tribes. Although there was less prey, it wouldn't be like the south where you couldn't even find a single red bird feather.

So the Green Eye orcs didn't hate the wolf orcs.

They had long since understood the previous matter... it was they who had used the wrong method and brought it upon themselves.

Fortunately, they could correct it in time now.

This row of neat wooden houses was situated on the grassy bank by the river, built on stilts. The shade of the trees covered the houses, and the wind blew slowly, making the wolf orcs feel refreshed in body and mind.

These Green Eye orcs really knew how to pick a location.

The meat soup was ready, and Green Yue led the orcs to scoop it into wooden bowls and distribute it to the wolf orcs.

The other Green Eye orcs held their own wooden bowls and waited, quiet and still, looking at the wolf orcs who were much sturdier than them.

Lin Qiu saw the white-haired orc hiding in the back at a glance.

Bai Song quickly lowered his head.

Lin Qiu's vision darkened.

He looked at the lines on Lang Yan's palm, curled his lips, and let go of Lang Yan's hand.

Lang Yan's expression was a bit cold. Lin Qiu didn't let go of his hand but leaned in and whispered something in his ear.

Lang Yan's expression softened instantly. He took the wooden bowl from the Green Eye orc and placed it in Lin Qiu's hand.

Bai Song was terrified, but the wolf orcs acted as if they were in their own tribe, eating the meat soup clean without any hesitation.

After finishing and wiping their mouths, they proposed to leave.

Green Ren stood up to see them off. After walking a few steps, he couldn't help but cough twice.

Lang Yan stopped and looked at their exquisite wooden houses, saying: "If you have something to say, just say it directly."

Green Ren smiled and sighed.

The leaders of the two tribes walked ahead, while the other orcs lagged behind.

Lin Qiu faintly heard Green Ren say:

"The Green Eye tribe did a lot of wrong things in the past and suffered the consequences... now that we've moved here to start over, can the matter between the two tribes..."

Lang Huo gave a low hum.

Lang Yun picked at his ear, looking unwilling on the surface.

Lin Qiu looked around at his own orcs and said: "He wants to be on good terms with our tribe?"

"Which tribe doesn't want to be on good terms with our tribe?" Lang Yun said with a cheeky grin.

The little wolves stood beside Lin Qiu.

Led by Lang Bing, he stood quietly by Lin Qiu's side, his voice sounding as if it had been dusted with frost.

"When there are more good things, it makes other orcs jealous."

Lin Qiu patted the little wolf's shoulder, "Don't be so absolute. Turning hostility into friendship and mutual benefit is the long-term plan."

Lang Bing: "Don't understand."

Lin Qiu had been thinking about the medicinal herbs all the way here, so he said: "Are there any medicinal herbs here that our tribe doesn't have?"

Lang Bing understood.

"No," he said petulantly.

Lin Qiu couldn't help but laugh, "So that means there are."

The little wolf turned his head away, his long white braid sweeping through the air; it must have hurt when it hit his body.

"I was just asking, why are you getting angry?"

Lang Bing: "No."

Before long, Lang Yan finished talking with Green Ren.

They left the Green Eye tribe's territory and headed north. Lang Yan asked: "Are there many useful medicinal herbs around here?"

Obviously, he had also heard the conversation between Lin Qiu and Lang Bing just now.

"Don't know, have to see," Lang Bing said stubbornly.

Lin Qiu curled the corners of his mouth. After waiting a while, he heard the little wolf say reluctantly: "Just looking at the lakeside and the forest on the opposite bank earlier, there are a few types."

In the Lang tribe's territory, medicinal herbs had been gathered year after year. Even though they were careful to leave seeds, there weren't as many as in other tribes.

Herbs that were rare in their tribe were like wild grass, growing in clumps in other tribes.

Lang Yan: "Let's forget it for now."

Lang Bing felt relieved and went off with the little wolves, running and looking for herbs. Couldn't they find them themselves without relying on the Green Eye tribe?

This area didn't belong to any tribe, so they could look wherever they wanted.

The little wolves ran far away, leaving only Lin Qiu and Lang Yan behind.

They didn't plan to travel during the day, just heading north and stopping when they found a suitable place to stay.

Lin Qiu walked beside Lang Yan. As they walked, looking at the ponytail swaying behind the Wolf King, he couldn't help but reach out.

Before he could touch it, his hand was held by Lang Yan.

His palm was large and his fingers were long, directly closing around Lin Qiu's wrist.

Lin Qiu squinted, feeling the breeze in the forest, leaning his shoulder against Lang Yan's, and asked: "King, what did you just talk about?"

"They want to be on good terms with the Lang tribe."

"The two sides are still quite a distance apart, and they don't usually interact, so can't they just go about their own business?"

"That's not what you said in front of Lang Bing."

Lin Qiu's smile was light and faint, like the breeze passing by at this moment, bringing a hint of coolness to the sweltering heat.

"They are still young."

The little wolves' likes and dislikes were too direct and too sharp. The affairs between tribes weren't just black and white. They hadn't grown up yet, and sometimes they needed guidance.

Just like the two cubs, Lang Sheng and Lang Yuan; if it weren't for the Green Eye tribe, who knows where they would be now.

The sun was getting a bit scorching, so the orcs found a giant tree with lush branches and leaves in the forest and stopped.

The canopy of this tree was huge; a single trunk was enough for an orc to lie down and sleep.

These towering ancient trees, which Lin Qiu had only seen in primeval forests in his past life, were everywhere here.

They hadn't been to this place much. Lin Qiu left two little wolves to tidy up the area under the bushes, covering it with dry grass and fallen leaves, and driving away insects. Those who wanted to sleep in the tree could go up, and those who wanted to sleep under the tree had a place to lie down.

Lang Bing and Lang Huo and the others went out for a turn and came back with their animal skin pouches half full.

"King, let's stay here for two days; there are quite a few medicinal herbs here," Lang Bing said.

Lang Yan nodded, sat beside Lin Qiu, leaned against the big tree, and closed his eyes to sleep.

The other orcs found places one after another, and in a moment, they were fast asleep.

The nearby orcs had patrolled, and there were no orcs or wild beasts, so everyone slept until the afternoon.

Lin Qiu woke up feeling hungry, not knowing when he had fallen asleep on Lang Yan's lap.

He sat up, covered in sweat.

Other orcs were half-awake, not present at the moment, and most of the little wolves were still sleeping.

Lang Yan waved a fan, fanning him.

Lin Qiu felt weak all over and leaned against his partner again to clear his head.

"Huo and the others went hunting, and Lang Bing went with them."

Lin Qiu pressed against Lang Yan's shoulder and rubbed around until his sleepiness dissipated, then climbed up.

"Let's go out for a turn too."

Lang Yan saw that the little wolves were all awake, nodded, and went to gather things in the forest with Lin Qiu.

Going out in the rainy season wasn't like the snow season; there was no need to fear going hungry. As long as you knew some wild vegetables and mushrooms, you could pick a large basketful at will.

The remaining little wolves followed Lin Qiu and the others, picking herbs when they saw them and mushrooms when they saw them; anyway, you couldn't have too much food.

They had brought a pottery pot, and Lin Qiu had taken the opportunity to find a water source on this trip, so he didn't wander in the forest with the little wolves anymore.

He went back to get the pottery jar, fetched water, and returned to start making dinner.

Lang Yan helped him, cutting vegetables and tending the fire; he could do a bit of everything.

Once a pot of hot water was boiled, it was poured into the jar first, and some herbs for heatstroke were thrown in, waiting for the orcs to drink when they returned.

When water was added to the pot again, the orcs who had gone out had almost all returned.

Almost everyone had a rattan basket in hand; some were brought from the tribe, and some were made on the spot.

The rattan baskets were piled high with fruits, wild vegetables, and mushrooms; there were a full dozen baskets in front of them.

Lin Qiu was just thinking about what dish to make when Lang Bing ran in front of him, placed the rattan basket in front of him, and lifted his chin slightly, looking a bit proud.

Lin Qiu looked closely and saw a full basket of purple-skinned fruits, which were wild grapes.

"Where did you find them?"

"In the east, there are still many."

Lin Qiu sat upright in front of the stove, looking at the little wolf.

"Wash them and eat."

Lang Bing lowered his chin, staring at Lin Qiu, but just wouldn't speak.

Lin Qiu chuckled: "Got it, I remember."

It was just a small jar of wine for each orc; he would brew it.

Fortunately, they brought a few jars, otherwise, if they waited until these grapes were brought back, they would have spoiled long ago.

"Eat first, we'll go pick more after eating."

The corners of Lang Bing's mouth curled up slightly, and he moved the rattan basket away.
