浓烟滚滚，位置离狼山挺远。
那一处烟雾看着很小。
狼山的兽人们惊得全部跑上狼山，远远看着南面。可惜狼山不算高，只能估摸着火点。
狼岩表情凝重，道：“大泽以南，应该烧不到我们这边。”
林楸被阳光晃得眼晕，极力眺望，也看不出个什么。
他听着狼岩的话，还没来得及松口气，又听他道：“有部落要遭难了。”
黑羽兽人如离弦的箭冲出去，打探情况，另有两个黑羽兽人被狼部落叫回去告知黑羽部落。
烈日下，兽人们紧紧盯着那一处浓烟，心神焦灼。
“回去。”狼岩迅速离开山顶。
兽人们回到屋中，气氛有些沉凝。
狼岩道：“狼游、狼火、狼乔，你们带队，沿河以北，把大河河岸附近的树枝全部砍下来。”
“是！”
“狼石，你带护卫队，把狼山上西侧的树截断。”
“其余兽人，以狼山为中心，清理所有干草、枯树。”
下完命令，兽人们顶着烈日，戴了草帽迅速出去干活。
*
羽山来了。
他飞落狼山，就看到草割得光秃秃的狼山，他心中庆幸，赶紧去找狼岩。
两边坐下，羽山迅速道：“昨晚上开始，我们部落南边有一个起火点，今早上我们发现时，已经烧到山谷了。”
“起火点正好在绿眼部落西边。”
林楸瞳孔一缩。
“那他们……”
“目前还不知道情况，我已经派兽人去看了。你们这边南部也有一个。”
羽涯回来了。
他急急地冲进屋里，就看到他们族长来了。
“阿山叔！着火了！”
狼岩看向他，小兽人立马冷静下来，飞快道：“着火的地方就是大泽南边。”
林楸精神一松，道：“山，你们那边尽快弄出一个隔离带。”
“我们……我本来是想请你们帮忙的。”他们的兽人已经在努力了，可是进度太慢，又没趁手的工具。
狼岩迅速盘算了下部落的兽人，道：“我让狼贝他们过去。”
“诶！那我就先回去了。”
狼岩直接把狼贝叫来，狼贝道：“光我们一小队怕是不够。”
“我们也去。”狼阔站出来道。
部落有百多个兽人，前头大河够宽，他们把北边的树清理干净，只是以防万一。
狼贝和狼阔两个小队过去，留下的兽人够了。
黑羽部落离他们近，那边虽有大河经过，但大河从山脉直嵌而下，河道窄，随便飘几个火星子都能烧起来。
到那时候，他们这边即便做好准备，也怕他们那边烧过来。
狼岩点头，兽人们立刻离开。
羽山只带了一个兽人过来，他留下兽人给狼贝他们带路，自己又往回赶。
狼山收拾得很快，草早被割得差不多了，大伙儿就聚在一起砍树。
虽然工具不趁手，但他们兽人多，四五个兽人围着一棵树，砍树干不容易就砍更细一点的树枝，他们就不信，没了叶子，隔着这么宽的河，它还能轻易烧起来。
“祭司，后头几天有没有雨？”林楸匆匆找到祭司询问。
老祭司看向没有丝毫云朵的蓝天，声音又低又沉：“现在看，没有。”
林楸心里担忧，忍不住道：“那这么烧起来，半个月都不带停。”
老祭司：“不会的……大泽挡着……但，白雀他们那边就不一定了。”
*
狼山南部。
山火以极快的速度蔓延开来，在兽人们发现的时候就已经来不及了。
绿眼兽人离起火的位置最近，火浪滔天，以巨兽吞噬之态迅速蔓延至他们部落境内。
火起时是晚上，他们发现时，已经能看见火光。
绿眼兽人慌慌张张飞上树梢查探，被呛咳得差点摔下来。他眼中映着那一片橘红，炽热的温度仿佛能将他灼烧。
“族长！来了，已经来了！快跑！”
绿眼兽人们惊恐，纷纷闯入木屋收拾东西。
绿壬隔着隐隐树木，看到那通红的光。整片空间到处都是吹来的火灰，呼吸都是烫的。
他甚至看到一点火星就落在附近。
绿壬头皮发麻，大喝：“走！快走！东西别收了！”
兽人们急着哭嚎：“可东西没了，我们雪季怎么活！”
“走！！！”
绿壬撕心裂肺喊着族人，绿皎紧紧搂着幼崽，抓着伴侣，甩开那沉重的行李。
“皎！”绿月惊恐，眼中含泪。
“走。”绿皎一咬牙，猛地带着伴侣和幼崽离开木屋。
“啊！”后头留恋行李的兽人惊叫，转瞬，火舌吞噬而来。
分明刚刚那火还在百米开外。
绿皎跟绿壬同时将手上的族人往湖里一扔，扑了过去。
“族长！”
“皎！”
木屋后头的林子里，响起令人牙酸的咯吱声。木头燃烧着，一片连成一片，霎时，整个绿眼部落成了火海。
兽人们仓皇往北飞。
“族长，我们去哪儿？”兽人吸了几口烟雾，呛咳得厉害，一边奋力往前飞，一边忍不住回头看。
绿眼兽人飞得高了。
他们看着那片火海以极快的速度吞噬掉他们的木屋，兽人们双眼赤红，落下泪来。
没了，又没了……
什么都没了！
他们来不及怨，茫然又无措地往北飞。
直到与白雀兽人在空中相撞。
绿眼兽人沉默，看着他们雪白的羽毛黑灰一片。两边互相看了一眼，齐齐往前，最后不约而同地落在了狼部落的大泽。
方一落下，湖心岛上成群的候鸟被惊飞。
它们在天空绕行，叫声嘈杂，似乎注意到南边的不详，直接往北而去。
一时间，飞羽纷纷而落，湖心岛上只有白雀与绿眼部落两方兽人。
两边分开，各自占据湖心岛上一角。
大泽四周，水面相连成片。细细一看，那水上竟也飘落不少黑灰。
两个羽族的兽人仰头看着南边滚滚浓烟，带着一身的灰尘，在烈日下蜷缩起来，头疼欲裂。
傍晚了，天边火红一片。
不是晚霞，是火海。
狼岩带着兽人过来查看情况，刚钻出林子，看到的就是湖心小岛上躺了一片的兽人。
“羽涯，把他们带过来。”
部落里十个黑羽兽人飞过去，一个爪子拎着一个，将他们往岸边转移。
林楸带来了草药，挨个儿检查过去，才发现他们大多是中暑了。
他们只带了狼金的小狼队和黑羽兽人过来。
林楸是唯一一个会治病的。
他架起陶锅，迅速往里添加草药。又示意小狼们取水，先给他们擦身降温。
一个又一个兽人被带上来。
雀二白晕乎乎的，他看着眼前忙碌的小狼们道：“麻烦你们……”
“你们那边什么情况？”狼金抓着他胳膊，一边往他腋窝下用沾了水的帕子擦，一边问。
“我们、我们跑得早，没什么事，那火从南边起的。”
狼金把一条湿帕子扔他脑袋上，雀二白顿时喟叹一声，身体瘫软了去。
小狼在病患中穿梭，忙得脚不沾地。
林楸熬药需要一段时间，他便教小狼们给兽人刮痧降温。
太阳依旧晒，晒得兽人身上脱皮。
小狼来来回回取水，身上晒得发红，全是汗珠。
林楸赶紧招来他们歇一歇。
狼兽人们带了水壶来，里头提前灌了解暑的茶。小狼往地上瘫坐，靠在棚子的墙面，咕噜噜往嘴里灌水。
这下半点不嫌苦，一口气喝完半壶。
“楸，他们说火烧到他们部落去了。”狼金道。
豹休道：“火是从更南边起的，正从东边和西边围上来。”
狼岩过来就听到豹休这话，他道：“所以着火点不是两个。”
“对，雀十二他们最先发现，去看了的。”
不然他们身上怎么会有这么多灰，还中暑了。
林楸看向南边那片天空，昏黑一片，空气中都闻得到燃烧木头的味道。
他攥紧手，眼底深处藏着担忧，道：“祭司说，这几天没雨。”
兽人无能为力，只能让它烧。
大火烧了三天三夜，直接从绿眼部落西边，白雀部落南边蔓延上来，朝着北部的狼山以及黑羽部落包围过来。
好在狼山南部有大泽阻拦，山火就算绕过大泽，往东南边上来，也有大河阻拦。
而黑羽部落那边，火势更快。
好在兽人们反应及时，他们依傍河道，拓宽的隔离带也起了效果。
不过他们的部落却是被烧了一半。
三天后，附近的山火烧无可烧，渐渐变小，但更南边，火势却更旺。
天空灰蒙蒙的，四处是飘散的尘埃。
兽人们不停呛咳，最后听林楸的，取了麻布捂住口鼻才好受一些。
猎物北逃，狼兽人守着大泽南段，趁机抓了不少猎物。
狼岩就带着队伍，一直在这边守着，一直没敢离开。
直到火势渐小。
中暑的兽人好了，只来得及逃离部落的绿眼兽人不像白雀兽人那样反应及时，什么家当都没带出来。
白雀兽人已经缓和过来。
他们却像受了极大的打击，萎靡不振。
狼山的兽人这几天严阵以待，沿着河岸尽量砍树，累死累活好多天，见到火势小了，终于停下来。
他们发现狼王走了几天没回来，又急匆匆找过来。
“王！”狼游蹿出林子。
狼岩看了他们一眼，早有预料，他问：“还没有雨吗？”
“祭司说要再等等。”
“部落什么情况？”
“部落没事。”
说完，狼游注意到待在他们棚子底下的白雀和绿眼兽人。
“王，他们怎么办……”
“火熄了再说。”
*
狼山。
狼王不在，兽人们日夜观察着南边的情况，担惊受怕，夜不敢眠。
前往黑羽部落帮忙的狼贝带着兽人们回来了，她刚到狼山西边，就被山顶上的兽人叫住。
“贝，那边怎么样了？”
“熄了。”
“没兽人受伤吧？”
“没有。”狼贝说着往狼山走。
她身后跟着狼阔的狩猎队，大伙儿跑到黑羽部落就开始干活，昼夜不歇忙了几天，这些个阿叔们眼下挂着重重的黑眼圈。
大火烧了几天，无数草木化作黑灰。
天空被这一层黑灰遮掩，阳光倒不显得那么晒人了。
狼贝一边回应着同伴，一边匆匆往狼山走。狼阔他们则匆匆回到屋中，往地上一趴，闭眼就能熟睡。
“王呢？”狼贝问。
“王不在。”
狼贝停下脚步，“王在哪儿？”
“你们走后当晚，王就带着兽人去大泽了。这几天一直没回来。”
“我过去一趟。”
狼贝调转脚步，没在部落停留，带着采集队直接去大泽。
越往南，灰尘越重。
狼贝带领采集队一口气跑到大泽，兽人们看到棚底下正好在打汤，径直过去排队。
“王，阿嚏！”狼贝重重打了个喷嚏，她揉了揉鼻子，继续道：“黑羽部落那边的情况不太好。”
同伴端来肉汤，狼贝摸了下陶碗，有点烫。
“黑羽部落被烧了一半的领地，有些动物没逃出来，直接烧没了。他们说，今年应该给不了弯角兽了。”
不仅如此，黑羽兽人自己今年雪季都难熬。
狼岩：“火灭了？”
“那边是灭了。”
“今年没有就没有吧。”
狼贝点头，然后再摸了摸陶碗。她实在饿极，端起来就要往嘴里灌。
林楸看她碗里还在冒烟，那豪放样子，不把喉咙烫伤才怪。
林楸眼皮一跳，忙将自己的碗推过去。
“我的凉了，还没吃。”
狼贝看了眼，果断将自己的碗放在林楸面前，端起眼前这个猛吃。
她实在是饿狠了。
黑羽部落自己都过得拮据，而且还要忙着建隔离带，所以这几天他们饿了就吃鱼。
可光吃鱼还不顶饿，身上的油水都快被鱼给刮没了。
他们才去几天，大伙儿都瘦了。
狼贝今天又赶路回来，一天没吃了，就等着自家部落这一顿。
骨头汤炖藕，虽然骨头上没一点肉，但汤上飘着油花，还有点肉味儿，也好比生啃鱼肉来得好。
林楸看她那饿极了的样子，忍不住道：“慢点吃，不够再做。”
狼岩垂着眼，一边勾着林楸衣摆，将上面的褶皱细细抹平，一边想着几个部落的事。
南边那一片，怕全烧没了。
猎物能跑的早跑了，没跑的也烧死了，现在怕是连一根能吃的草也找不到。
白雀兽人和绿眼兽人捡回来一条命，接下来就该想想怎么填饱肚子。
正好，大泽需要兽人。
这几天，狼山过来的兽人们一边照顾病患，一边下水摸鱼，附近水域被大家摸清楚了。
择日不如撞日，现在就可以开始修整大泽。
狼岩手掌扶了下自家伴侣腰间，低声跟他说了句。
林楸眼睛骤亮，他连忙点头，狼岩便起身去找两个部落的族长商量。
此时，两个族长窝在树下，唉声叹气的，看得狼兽人们都远远绕着他们走。
狼岩过来，两个族长立马敛了愁容。
狼岩：“想好怎么办了？”
白雀族长：“我们还是不打算迁徙，等火彻底灭了，回去看看再说。”
他们住的石林，里头树少，倒也能继续住下去。
但怪就怪在一场大火下来，该烧的都烧没了，他们没有食物。
好在这边离狼部落的大泽近，要是狼部落允许，他们想让他们管一口饭，自家兽人先像之前黑羽兽人那样给他们做事。
就是不知道狼部落还有没有事让他们做。
绿壬则脑袋垂着，连摇头都显得无力，像没了心气儿。
部落一而再再而三遭难，好不容易安定下来，又遇到这个事情。
不仅绿眼兽人们迷茫了，连绿壬都在怀疑是不是兽神在惩罚他们。
雀二白蹲在白雀族长一旁，看他们又不说话了，不停地戳着他后背。
白雀族长被他戳得烦，一把将他甩开。
“狼王。”
狼岩灰眸看过来。
白雀毕竟是弱小部落，对上狼部落，没多少底气。白雀族长这一辈子，莫说面对狼王，连狼兽人都没见过几次。
他忐忑地将自己的想法说了出来。
狼岩颔首：“可以。”
白雀族长愣了下。
这么干脆？
狼岩：“还有什么要求？”
“没、没有，没有了！”
白雀族长长长地吁了一口气。
“只要熬过这几个月，火烧后的林子绿得很快，之后就不缺吃的。”
他们部落的兽人食量较小，到时候问狼部落借一下渔网，就是吃鱼，这雪季他们也得熬过去！
白雀族长说完，还看了一眼绿壬。
可这绿眼族长跟耳朵聋了一样，跟个石头似的坐靠在树前，听不懂他的暗示。
白雀族长想起他们跟狼部落的仇怨，还是决定不帮他说话。
狼岩：“既然休息好了，那就从今晚开始。”
白雀族长瞪大眼睛。
狼岩：“不行？”
“行！行！”白雀族长没顾虑了。
他们这几天相当于在狼部落吃白饭，还免费接受狼部落的治疗，换小气一点的部落，哪里还会跟他们谈什么交换，有事直接甩给他们做就行了。
他瞥了一眼绿壬。
这兽人怎么要死不活的，不就一个山火，这辈子没见过十次也有八次了。虽然不是每次都烧过来，但只要兽人没事，那日子还不是照常过。
甚至地更肥，草更绿，野菜更好吃。
这话虽也是苦中作乐，反正再如何，还不是要吃要喝要睡觉，想开点不好？
狼岩看绿壬现在的颓靡样子，知道他没心思拿主意了。
他目光往绿眼兽人堆里扫了一圈，见绿皎在喂自己幼崽，精神头还好。
这个应该可以做主。
绿皎察觉到狼岩视线，将碗递给伴侣，走了过来。
“狼王。”
“有个事，跟你们商量一下。”
绿皎看了一眼他们族长，兽人蓬头垢面，精神萎靡，他心中一痛。
绿皎咬紧牙，面向狼岩点头道：“你说。”
“我们想把大泽改一改，你们帮忙，我们管食物。”
绿皎猛地抬起头，眼中注入光亮。
他强压下激动，但说话还是快了些：“我要问问族人。”
族长现在这个样子受打击太严重，他不能做决定，族人要是同意，那这事儿就可以。
“尽快。”
狼岩说完，回到林楸身边。
林楸肉汤喝了一半，看他坐过来，往他那边侧了一下，肩贴着肩，是亲昵的姿态。
“他们答应了吗？”
“白雀答应了，绿眼兽人要商量一下。”
“多半要答应。”
其实林楸本来打算等雨季过了，这水位再降一降才干活。反正他们部落的兽人还没吵明白。
但哪想到直接就撞上了山火的事儿，两个部落的兽人无家可归。
这现成的人力，不能浪费。
部落管两百来号兽人的饭虽然麻烦了点，但这会儿兽人们也挑不到哪里去，就是顿顿吃鱼，这饭也能管下去。
当然，狼部落也不是那抠搜的部落，要人家干活，伙食肯定尽量做好。
才说着话，绿皎就来了。
他代表族人同意了，这事儿便要马上安排起来。
目前，大泽这边的兽人有狼贝的采集队，十个黑羽兽人，狼金的小狼狩猎队，还有绿眼部落以及白雀部落的全部兽人。
部落还有那么多兽人要吃要喝，所以狼游是要回去的。
狼岩让狼游回去后叫狼安派一些做饭的亚兽人过来，数量得够，能管好两百兽人吃饭的事。
白雀兽人和绿眼兽人是干活的主力，天气炎热，为了防止兽人中暑，只能让他们晚上干活，半夜还要保证吃一顿饭。
狼岩便先安排狼贝依旧采集，狼金小队捕猎。
林楸、狼岩以及黑羽兽人则跟两个部落的兽人一起忙。
按照狼部落的规划，要利用水底淤泥建造垛田，也就是水上农田。
到时候田里可种植，水里可养殖，一举两得。
话虽好说，但落在这实际的事情上，却要一点一点将水底的淤泥挖上来垒成田地，不是一日之功。
夜色宁静，大泽中虫鸣蛙叫四起。
要把河里淤泥捞上来，水浅的区域好办，像那几米深的水下，总不能让兽人们钻到水下去捞，所以还需工具。
晚上也热，但比白天好受一些。
这会儿，林楸让白雀族长和绿皎从自家兽人中挑出来十个手巧的兽人，帮忙做工具。其他兽人则跟着狼岩，先在浅水区域干着活。
头一天晚上，兽人们没干过这些事儿，不论是岸上的还是水里的兽人，都有些忙乱。
但兽人的适应能力极强，动手能力也不差。
大伙儿磕磕绊绊地砍木头，削木头，四处扒拉着找合适的石头、藤条，把附近能用的材料全部找了过来。
水里的兽人则刨泥、堆泥，从不敢下手，到扔了木棍改用手捧。
一晚混乱过去，天明时，天空依旧灰蒙蒙的。
兽人熬了一晚上，困得脑子发晕，一看天上，还以为要下雨了，激动地爬起来欢呼。
可自个儿呼到一半，看那天上纷纷扬扬落下的灰尘，又连忙用麻布捂住口鼻，蹲在地上装蘑菇。
没下雨，是那黑灰把太阳遮住了。
好在做饭的兽人们昨晚早早赶来，现在已经做好了早饭，兽人们吃过，便闭眼昏睡过去。
天空阴沉，处处飘着黑灰，附近的树木也被连续数天的烈日烧得叶片卷曲，草木发蔫。
每个兽人都很疲惫。
大伙儿甚至没来得及清洗自己，带着一身泥泞睡去。
林中时不时传出些不适的咳嗽声，兽人们捂住口鼻，蜷缩起来睡觉。
白雀族长躺在树上，看着比他高一些树枝上，蹲了一排灰白色的毛球，一口吹走落下的黑灰，无声笑了笑。
他看得开些，兽人在，部落就在。
再者，有狼部落这样的邻居，他们就算是借些食物，也能熬过这次苦难。
只要这群小崽子们好，累点也没什么。
chapters.translated_text:
Thick smoke billowed, far away from Wolf Mountain.

That patch of smoke looked quite small from here.

The beastmen of Wolf Mountain were startled and all ran up to the mountain to look toward the south. Unfortunately, Wolf Mountain wasn't very tall, so they could only estimate the location of the fire.

Lang Yan’s expression was grave as he said, "South of the Great Marsh; it shouldn't be able to burn over to our side."

Lin Qiu felt dizzy from the glare of the sun; he tried his best to peer into the distance, but he couldn't make anything out.

He listened to Lang Yan’s words, and just as he was about to let out a sigh of relief, he heard him add, "A tribe is in trouble."

The Black Feather beastmen shot out like arrows released from a bow to scout the situation, while two other Black Feather beastmen were called back by the Wolf Tribe to inform the Black Feather Tribe.

Under the scorching sun, the beastmen stared intently at the thick smoke, their hearts anxious and burning.

"Go back." Lang Yan quickly left the mountaintop.

The beastmen returned to their houses, the atmosphere heavy and somber.

Lang Yan said, "Lang You, Lang Huo, Lang Qiao, take your teams along the north side of the river and cut down all the branches near the banks of the Great River."

"Yes!"

"Lang Shi, you take the guard team and cut down the trees on the west side of Wolf Mountain."

"The rest of the beastmen, center yourselves around Wolf Mountain and clear away all dry grass and withered trees."

After giving the orders, the beastmen braved the scorching sun, put on their straw hats, and quickly went out to work.

*

Yu Shan had arrived.

He flew down to Wolf Mountain and saw that the mountain had been cleared bare of grass. Feeling relieved, he hurried to find Lang Yan.

Once they sat down, Yu Shan said quickly, "Starting last night, there was a fire point south of our tribe. By the time we discovered it this morning, it had already burned to the valley."

"The ignition point was right to the west of the Green Eye Tribe."

Lin Qiu’s pupils constricted.

"Then they..."

"I don't know the situation yet; I’ve already sent beastmen to check. There is also one to the south of your side."

Yu Ya had returned.

He rushed into the house in a hurry and saw that their patriarch had arrived.

"Uncle A-Shan! There’s a fire!"

Lang Yan looked at him, and the young beastman immediately calmed down, saying quickly, "The place that caught fire is just south of the Great Marsh."

Lin Qiu felt a weight lift from his mind and said, "Shan, you should get an isolation belt set up on your side as soon as possible."

"We... I actually wanted to ask for your help." Their beastmen were already trying, but their progress was too slow, and they lacked proper tools.

Lang Yan quickly calculated the number of beastmen in his tribe and said, "I’ll have Lang Bei and the others go over."

"Great! Then I’ll head back first."

Lang Yan called Lang Bei over immediately, and Lang Bei said, "I'm afraid our small team alone won't be enough."

"We'll go too," Lang Kuo said, stepping forward.

The tribe had over a hundred beastmen; the Great River in front was wide enough, and they had cleared the trees on the north side just as a precaution.

With Lang Bei and Lang Kuo’s two teams going over, there would be enough beastmen left behind.

The Black Feather Tribe was close to them; although the Great River passed by there, the river flowed directly down from the mountain range, making the riverbed narrow. A few drifting sparks could easily ignite it.

By then, even if they were prepared on their side, they feared the fire would spread over from there.

Lang Yan nodded, and the beastmen left immediately.

Yu Shan had only brought one beastman with him; he left the beastman to guide Lang Bei and the others while he hurried back himself.

Wolf Mountain was cleared very quickly; the grass had already been cut, so everyone gathered together to chop down trees.

Although their tools weren't ideal, they had many beastmen. Four or five of them would surround a tree; if the trunk was hard to cut, they would cut the thinner branches. They didn't believe that without leaves, and with such a wide river in between, it could still easily catch fire.

"Priest, will there be rain in the next few days?" Lin Qiu hurried to find the priest to ask.

The old priest looked at the cloudless blue sky, his voice low and heavy: "As it looks now, no."

Lin Qiu was worried and couldn't help but say, "If it burns like this, it won't stop for half a month."

The old priest: "It won't... the Great Marsh is blocking it... but, it might not be the same for White Sparrow and the others."

*

South of Wolf Mountain.

The wildfire spread at an extremely fast speed; by the time the beastmen discovered it, it was already too late.

The Green Eye beastmen were closest to the ignition point; the fire waves were monstrous, spreading rapidly into their tribe's territory like a giant beast devouring everything.

The fire started at night, and by the time they discovered it, they could already see the glow.

A Green Eye beastman flew up to the treetops in a panic to investigate and was choked by the smoke, nearly falling down. His eyes reflected that patch of orange-red, the scorching temperature feeling as if it could burn him.

"Patriarch! It’s here, it’s already here! Run!"

The Green Eye beastmen were terrified and rushed into their wooden houses to pack their belongings.

Green Ren saw the crimson light through the trees. The entire space was filled with blowing fire ash, and even breathing felt hot.

He even saw a spark land nearby.

Green Ren’s scalp went numb, and he shouted, "Go! Run! Don't pack anything!"

The beastmen cried out in distress: "But if our things are gone, how will we survive the snow season!"

"GO!!!"

Green Ren screamed at his tribesmen with all his might. Green Jiao held her cub tightly, grabbed her mate, and threw away the heavy luggage.

"Jiao!" Green Yue cried out in terror, tears in her eyes.

"Go." Green Jiao gritted her teeth and suddenly dragged her mate and cub away from the wooden house.

"Ah!" A beastman who was reluctant to leave his luggage screamed; in an instant, tongues of fire engulfed him.

Clearly, the fire had been a hundred meters away just a moment ago.

Green Jiao and Green Ren simultaneously threw their tribesmen into the lake and dove in after them.

"Patriarch!"

"Jiao!"

In the forest behind the wooden houses, a teeth-gritting creaking sound echoed. The wood burned, one piece after another, and in an instant, the entire Green Eye Tribe became a sea of fire.

The beastmen fled north in a panic.

"Patriarch, where are we going?" The beastman inhaled some smoke and coughed violently; while struggling to fly forward, he couldn't help but look back.

The Green Eye beastmen flew higher.

They watched as the sea of fire devoured their wooden houses at an extremely fast speed; the beastmen’s eyes were red, and tears fell.

It was gone, everything was gone again...

Nothing was left!

They didn't have time to complain, flying north in a daze and at a loss.

Until they collided with the White Sparrow beastmen in the air.

The Green Eye beastmen fell silent, looking at their white feathers covered in black ash. Both sides looked at each other, flew forward together, and finally landed unanimously at the Great Marsh of the Wolf Tribe.

As soon as they landed, flocks of migratory birds on the lake island were startled and flew away.

They circled in the sky, their cries noisy, seemingly noticing the ominous signs to the south, and flew directly north.

For a time, feathers fell one after another; only the beastmen of the White Sparrow and Green Eye tribes remained on the lake island.

Both sides separated, each occupying a corner of the lake island.

Around the Great Marsh, the water surfaces were connected. Looking closely, a lot of black ash was actually floating on the water.

Two Feather-tribe beastmen looked up at the billowing thick smoke to the south, covered in dust, curling up under the scorching sun, their heads throbbing with pain.

It was evening, and the horizon was a fiery red.

It wasn't the sunset; it was a sea of fire.

Lang Yan brought his beastmen over to check the situation, and just as they emerged from the forest, what they saw was a group of beastmen lying all over the small lake island.

"Yu Ya, bring them over."

Ten Black Feather beastmen from the tribe flew over, each grabbing one and transferring them to the shore.

Lin Qiu brought medicinal herbs and checked them one by one, only to find that most of them were suffering from heatstroke.

They had only brought Lang Jin’s small wolf team and the Black Feather beastmen over.

Lin Qiu was the only one who knew how to treat illnesses.

He set up a clay pot and quickly added herbs to it. He also signaled the little wolves to fetch water to wipe their bodies and lower their temperatures.

One beastman after another was brought up.

Que Erbai was dizzy; he looked at the busy little wolves in front of him and said, "Sorry to trouble you..."

"What’s the situation on your side?" Lang Jin grabbed his arm, asking while wiping his armpits with a water-soaked cloth.

"We, we ran early, so we're fine. The fire started from the south."

Lang Jin threw a wet cloth onto his head, and Que Erbai let out a sigh, his body going limp.

The little wolves moved among the patients, busy and unable to stop.

It would take some time for Lin Qiu to decoct the medicine, so he taught the little wolves to perform scraping to lower the beastmen's temperatures.

The sun was still scorching, making the beastmen’s skin peel.

The little wolves went back and forth fetching water, their bodies red from the sun and covered in sweat.

Lin Qiu quickly called them over to take a break.

The wolf beastmen had brought water bottles filled with heat-relieving tea. The little wolves slumped on the ground, leaning against the wall of the shed, gulping down the water.

They didn't complain about the bitterness at all, finishing half a bottle in one breath.

"Qiu, they said the fire burned to their tribe," Lang Jin said.

Bao Xiu said, "The fire started further south and is closing in from the east and west."

Lang Yan came over and heard Bao Xiu’s words; he said, "So there wasn't just one ignition point."

"Right, Que Shier and the others discovered it first and went to look."

Otherwise, why would they have so much ash on them and be suffering from heatstroke?

Lin Qiu looked at the sky to the south, which was pitch black; the smell of burning wood could be smelled in the air.

He clenched his hands, worry hidden deep in his eyes, and said, "The priest said there won't be rain these few days."

The beastmen were helpless and could only let it burn.

The wildfire burned for three days and three nights, spreading directly from the west of the Green Eye Tribe and the south of the White Sparrow Tribe, surrounding the northern Wolf Mountain and the Black Feather Tribe.

Fortunately, there was the Great Marsh blocking the south of Wolf Mountain, and even if the wildfire bypassed the Great Marsh and came up from the southeast, there was the Great River to block it.

As for the Black Feather Tribe, the fire was faster.

Fortunately, the beastmen reacted in time; they relied on the river channel, and the widened isolation belt also had an effect.

However, half of their tribe had been burned.

Three days later, the nearby wildfire had nothing left to burn and gradually diminished, but further south, the fire was even more intense.

The sky was gray, and dust was scattered everywhere.

The beastmen coughed incessantly, and finally, they listened to Lin Qiu and used linen cloth to cover their mouths and noses, which made them feel a bit better.

The prey fled north, and the wolf beastmen guarded the southern section of the Great Marsh, taking the opportunity to catch a lot of prey.

Lang Yan led his team to guard this side, never daring to leave.

Until the fire gradually subsided.

The beastmen with heatstroke recovered. The Green Eye beastmen, who had only managed to escape their tribe, hadn't reacted as quickly as the White Sparrow beastmen and hadn't brought any belongings out.

The White Sparrow beastmen had already recovered.

But they were hit hard and were listless.

The beastmen of Wolf Mountain had been on high alert for the past few days, cutting trees along the riverbank as much as possible. After working themselves to the bone for many days, they finally stopped when they saw the fire subsiding.

They realized the Wolf King had been gone for days and hadn't returned, so they hurried over to find him.

"King!" Lang You rushed out of the forest.

Lang Yan looked at them, having expected this, and asked, "Still no rain?"

"The priest said we have to wait a bit longer."

"What’s the situation in the tribe?"

"The tribe is fine."

After saying this, Lang You noticed the White Sparrow and Green Eye beastmen staying under their sheds.

"King, what should we do about them..."

"Wait until the fire is out."

*

Wolf Mountain.

With the Wolf King gone, the beastmen observed the situation in the south day and night, living in fear and unable to sleep at night.

Lang Bei, who had gone to help the Black Feather Tribe, returned with the beastmen. She had just arrived at the west side of Wolf Mountain when she was stopped by the beastmen on the mountaintop.

"Bei, how is it over there?"

"It’s out."

"No beastmen injured, right?"

"No." Lang Bei said as she walked toward Wolf Mountain.

Following behind her was Lang Kuo’s hunting team. They had started working as soon as they arrived at the Black Feather Tribe, working day and night for several days; these uncles had heavy dark circles under their eyes.

The wildfire had burned for several days, turning countless plants into black ash.

The sky was obscured by this layer of black ash, so the sun didn't feel as scorching.

Lang Bei responded to her companions while hurrying toward Wolf Mountain. Lang Kuo and the others rushed back to their houses, flopping onto the ground and falling into a deep sleep as soon as they closed their eyes.

"Where is the King?" Lang Bei asked.

"The King is not here."

Lang Bei stopped in her tracks. "Where is the King?"

"The night after you left, the King took the beastmen to the Great Marsh. He hasn't returned in these few days."

"I’ll go over there."

Lang Bei turned around, not stopping in the tribe, and took the gathering team directly to the Great Marsh.

The further south they went, the heavier the dust became.

Lang Bei led the gathering team in one breath to the Great Marsh. Seeing that soup was being made under the shed, they went straight over to line up.

"King, A-choo!" Lang Bei sneezed heavily. She rubbed her nose and continued, "The situation at the Black Feather Tribe is not very good."

A companion brought over meat soup; Lang Bei touched the clay bowl, and it was a bit hot.

"Half of the Black Feather Tribe’s territory was burned. Some animals didn't escape and were burned to death. They said they probably can't provide curved-horn beasts this year."

Not only that, but the Black Feather beastmen themselves would have a hard time surviving this snow season.

Lang Yan: "Is the fire out?"

"It’s out over there."

"If there isn't any this year, then so be it."

Lang Bei nodded and touched the clay bowl again. She was truly starving and picked it up to gulp it down.

Lin Qiu saw that her bowl was still steaming, and with that bold way of eating, it would be a miracle if she didn't burn her throat.

Lin Qiu’s eyelid twitched, and he hurriedly pushed his own bowl over.

"Mine has cooled down; I haven't eaten yet."

Lang Bei glanced at it, decisively placed her bowl in front of Lin Qiu, and picked up the one in front of her to eat ravenously.

She was truly starving.

The Black Feather Tribe was living frugally themselves and had to be busy building isolation belts, so they had been eating fish for the past few days.

But eating only fish wasn't enough to satisfy their hunger, and the fat on their bodies was almost scraped away by the fish.

They had only been gone for a few days, and everyone had lost weight.

Lang Bei had rushed back today and hadn't eaten all day, just waiting for this meal from her own tribe.

Bone soup stewed with lotus root—although there wasn't a bit of meat on the bones, the soup had oil floating on top and a bit of meat flavor, which was much better than eating raw fish.

Lin Qiu looked at her starving appearance and couldn't help but say, "Eat slowly, we'll make more if it's not enough."

Lang Yan lowered his eyes, hooking Lin Qiu’s hem and smoothing out the wrinkles, while thinking about the affairs of the several tribes.

That area to the south was likely all burned away.

The prey that could run had long since fled, and those that couldn't had been burned to death; now, they probably couldn't even find a single edible blade of grass.

The White Sparrow and Green Eye beastmen had saved their lives, and now they had to think about how to fill their stomachs.

As it happened, the Great Marsh needed beastmen.

These past few days, the beastmen from Wolf Mountain had been taking care of the patients while going into the water to catch fish, and the nearby waters had been thoroughly explored by everyone.

There’s no time like the present; they could start renovating the Great Marsh now.

Lang Yan placed his hand on his mate’s waist and whispered something to him.

Lin Qiu’s eyes brightened, and he nodded quickly; Lang Yan then stood up to find the patriarchs of the two tribes to discuss it.

At this time, the two patriarchs were huddled under a tree, sighing, which made the wolf beastmen walk around them from a distance.

Lang Yan came over, and the two patriarchs immediately restrained their sorrow.

Lang Yan: "Have you decided what to do?"

White Sparrow Patriarch: "We still don't plan to migrate; we'll wait until the fire is completely out and go back to see."

The stone forest they lived in had few trees, so they could continue to live there.

But the problem was that after a wildfire, everything that should have been burned was gone, and they had no food.

Fortunately, this place was close to the Wolf Tribe’s Great Marsh; if the Wolf Tribe allowed it, they wanted them to provide a meal, and their own beastmen would work for them just like the Black Feather beastmen did before.

It was just that they didn't know if the Wolf Tribe still had things for them to do.

Green Ren hung his head, even shaking it felt weak, as if he had lost his spirit.

The tribe had suffered disaster again and again, and just when they had finally settled down, they encountered this.

Not only were the Green Eye beastmen confused, but even Green Ren was wondering if the Beast God was punishing them.

Que Erbai squatted beside the White Sparrow Patriarch, and seeing that they weren't talking again, he kept poking his back.

The White Sparrow Patriarch was annoyed by his poking and shoved him away.

"Wolf King."

Lang Yan’s gray eyes looked over.

After all, the White Sparrow was a weak tribe, and they didn't have much confidence when facing the Wolf Tribe. In his entire life, the White Sparrow Patriarch hadn't seen wolf beastmen many times, let alone face the Wolf King.

He nervously stated his thoughts.

Lang Yan nodded: "Okay."

The White Sparrow Patriarch was stunned.

So straightforward?

Lang Yan: "Any other requirements?"

"No, no, none!"

The White Sparrow Patriarch let out a long sigh of relief.

"As long as we get through these few months, the forest after a fire turns green very quickly, and there won't be a shortage of food after that."

Their tribe’s beastmen had small appetites; when the time came, they would borrow fishing nets from the Wolf Tribe, and even if they just ate fish, they would survive this snow season!

After the White Sparrow Patriarch finished speaking, he glanced at Green Ren.

But this Green Eye Patriarch was like he was deaf, sitting against the tree like a stone, unable to understand his hints.

The White Sparrow Patriarch remembered their enmity with the Wolf Tribe and decided not to speak for him.

Lang Yan: "Since you've rested well, let's start from tonight."

The White Sparrow Patriarch’s eyes widened.

Lang Yan: "No?"

"Yes! Yes!" The White Sparrow Patriarch had no more concerns.

They had been eating for free at the Wolf Tribe for these few days and receiving free treatment; if it were a stingier tribe, they wouldn't even talk about exchange, they would just throw work at them directly.

He glanced at Green Ren.

Why was this beastman so half-dead? It was just a wildfire; he had seen it eight or ten times in his life. Although it didn't burn over every time, as long as the beastmen were fine, life would go on as usual.

The land would even be more fertile, the grass greener, and the wild vegetables better.

Although this was finding joy in bitterness, no matter what, they still had to eat, drink, and sleep, so wouldn't it be better to think positively?

Lang Yan looked at Green Ren’s current listless state and knew he had no heart to make decisions.

He scanned the group of Green Eye beastmen and saw Green Jiao feeding her cub, her spirit still good.

She should be able to make the decision.

Green Jiao noticed Lang Yan’s gaze, handed the bowl to her mate, and walked over.

"Wolf King."

"There’s a matter I want to discuss with you."

Green Jiao looked at their patriarch; the beastman was disheveled and listless, and her heart ached.

Green Jiao gritted her teeth, nodded to Lang Yan, and said, "Tell me."

"We want to renovate the Great Marsh; you help, and we provide the food."

Green Jiao raised her head abruptly, light filling her eyes.

She suppressed her excitement, but her speech was still a bit fast: "I need to ask my tribesmen."

The patriarch was too devastated to make a decision; if the tribesmen agreed, then this could work.

"As soon as possible."

After Lang Yan finished, he returned to Lin Qiu’s side.

Lin Qiu had finished half of his meat soup; seeing him sit down, he leaned toward him, shoulder to shoulder, in an intimate posture.

"Did they agree?"

"White Sparrow agreed; the Green Eye beastmen need to discuss it."

"They will most likely agree."

Actually, Lin Qiu had originally planned to wait until the rainy season passed and the water level dropped further before starting work. Anyway, the beastmen of their own tribe hadn't finished arguing about it yet.

But he never expected to run into the wildfire, leaving the beastmen of the two tribes homeless.

This ready-made labor couldn't be wasted.

Although it was a bit troublesome for the tribe to feed two hundred beastmen, the beastmen couldn't be picky right now; even if they ate fish every meal, they could still manage the food.

Of course, the Wolf Tribe wasn't a stingy tribe; if they wanted people to work, they would try their best to provide good food.

Just as they were talking, Green Jiao came.

She agreed on behalf of the tribesmen, so this matter had to be arranged immediately.

Currently, the beastmen at the Great Marsh included Lang Bei’s gathering team, ten Black Feather beastmen, Lang Jin’s little wolf hunting team, and all the beastmen from the Green Eye and White Sparrow tribes.

There were still so many beastmen in the tribe to feed, so Lang You had to go back.

Lang Yan asked Lang You to have Lang An send some sub-beastmen over to cook, enough in number to manage the meals for two hundred beastmen.

The White Sparrow and Green Eye beastmen were the main labor force; the weather was hot, so to prevent heatstroke, they could only let them work at night, and they also had to ensure a meal in the middle of the night.

Lang Yan arranged for Lang Bei to continue gathering and Lang Jin’s team to hunt.

Lin Qiu, Lang Yan, and the Black Feather beastmen worked together with the beastmen of the two tribes.

According to the Wolf Tribe’s plan, they would use the silt from the bottom of the water to build raised fields, which were agricultural fields on the water.

When the time came, they could plant in the fields and raise fish in the water, killing two birds with one stone.

Although it was easy to say, when it came to the actual work, they had to dig up the silt from the bottom of the water bit by bit to build the fields; it wasn't a one-day task.

The night was quiet, and the sounds of insects and frogs echoed throughout the Great Marsh.

To scoop up the silt from the river, shallow areas were easy, but in water several meters deep, they couldn't let the beastmen dive down to scoop it, so they needed tools.

It was also hot at night, but it was more bearable than during the day.

At this moment, Lin Qiu asked the White Sparrow Patriarch and Green Jiao to pick ten dexterous beastmen from their own tribes to help make tools. The other beastmen followed Lang Yan to work in the shallow areas first.

On the first night, the beastmen hadn't done these things before, and both the beastmen on the shore and in the water were a bit chaotic.

But the beastmen had extremely strong adaptability and were not bad at hands-on work.

Everyone stumbled as they chopped wood, whittled wood, and searched everywhere for suitable stones and vines, finding all the usable materials nearby.

The beastmen in the water dug and piled up the mud, going from not daring to start to throwing away the wooden sticks and using their hands to scoop it.

A chaotic night passed, and when dawn came, the sky was still gray.

The beastmen had stayed up all night and were dizzy with sleepiness; when they looked at the sky, they thought it was going to rain and excitedly climbed up to cheer.

But halfway through their cheers, seeing the ash falling in the sky, they hurriedly covered their mouths and noses with linen cloth and squatted on the ground like mushrooms.

It wasn't raining; it was the black ash obscuring the sun.

Fortunately, the beastmen who cooked had arrived early last night and had already prepared breakfast; after eating, the beastmen closed their eyes and fell into a deep sleep.

The sky was gloomy, black ash was floating everywhere, and the nearby trees had their leaves curled and plants withered from the continuous scorching sun for several days.

Every beastman was very exhausted.

Everyone didn't even have time to wash themselves and fell asleep covered in mud.

From time to time, uncomfortable coughing sounds came from the forest; the beastmen covered their mouths and noses and curled up to sleep.

The White Sparrow Patriarch lay on a tree, looking at a row of gray-white fur balls squatting on a branch higher than him, blew away the falling black ash, and smiled silently.

He was more open-minded; as long as the beastmen were there, the tribe was there.

Furthermore, with neighbors like the Wolf Tribe, even if they had to borrow some food, they could survive this hardship.

As long as these little ones were fine, it didn't matter if they were tired.

chapters.translated_text:
You have to throw some food into the cage to lure the fish in. Lin Qiu waited until the beastmen returned from their hunt, received his share of the meat, and then set aside a portion to put into the fish trap.

Lang Yan looked at the meat in the cage but said nothing.

Lang Mo gnawed on his own piece of meat, which he had roasted to perfection, while staring longingly at the fish trap.

"Why are you giving it to the fish? If you're not going to eat it, you can give it to me."

Lang Shi sank his fangs into his meat, his wolf eyes full of trust.

"Qiu is doing something important."

Lang Mo: "Isn't it just catching fish?"

Despite what he said, there was a hint of anticipation in his eyes.

Lang Yan watched Lin Qiu grab the fish trap and head toward the river; after a moment of thought, he followed.

The sky was a dark, bruised blue, and the surroundings were becoming blurry.

The water by the riverbank was deep, and there was a fear of missing one's footing and falling straight to the bottom.

Lin Qiu heard footsteps and looked back to see Lang Yan. He suddenly remembered waking up in the other man's nest that morning, and his eyes flickered, his eyelashes trembling rapidly.

"Aren't you going to eat your meat?"

Lang Yan snatched the fish trap from Lin Qiu's hand. "The riverbank is dangerous. How do you set it?"

Lin Qiu saw that he didn't seem to find anything strange, thinking that perhaps he had accidentally rolled into his nest after Lang Yan had left in the morning.

As soon as the thought crossed his mind, he remembered the handful of wolf fur, and Lin Qiu couldn't help but curl his toes tightly.

His face remained calm, though it felt a bit hot.

Seeing Lang Yan walking by his side in his peripheral vision, he felt lucky that it was almost completely dark now.

He would definitely be careful tonight.

Lin Qiu didn't have much experience in setting fish traps either, so he just told Lang Yan to throw it into the deep water, throwing it as far as the length of the animal-hide rope allowed.

Watching the fish trap sink into the water, Lin Qiu signaled for Lang Yan to tie the animal-hide rope to a stone on the bank.

Now, all that was left to do was wait.

After dinner, inside the cave.

The beastmen had no entertainment, so they went to sleep as soon as they finished eating.

Lin Qiu lay in his nest, his back to Lang Yan, his fingers gripping the edge of the animal hide tightly.

His back was tense, and thinking of the fur ball tucked between the two grass nests, he couldn't help but pull the hide up to cover his head as well.

The cave wasn't exactly quiet; some wolf-beastmen were snoring, others were grinding their teeth or talking in their sleep. The firewood in the pit crackled, and the wind whistled from time to time.

Lin Qiu, covered by the hide, felt as if he had cut off everything outside; it took a long time before he finally relaxed his body and slowly drifted into a stupor.

In the middle of the night, Lang Yan opened his eyes.

The cub, Lang Xue, had crawled out of its nest again and spontaneously curled up against Lin Qiu's neck. Lin Qiu seemed used to it, instinctively wrapping his arm around the cub, their heads pressed together in an exceptionally intimate way.

Lang Yan watched the cub for a while, then his gaze swept over the curled-up form of Lin Qiu.

A rare, peaceful night.

Waking up the next day, Lin Qiu first checked where he was sleeping, then looked at his hands. Clean and tidy; he hadn't done anything bad.

His brows relaxed, and he greeted Lang Guo at the entrance calmly before going to check the fish trap, completely failing to notice the slightly flickering look in Lang Guo's eyes.

Seeing Lang An pulling weeds with the other beastmen, Lin Qiu called out to him.

Regardless of whether they had caught anything, he had to let Lang An, who had participated, see it.

As soon as he called out, apart from Lang An and two other older sub-beastmen who came over, the other beastmen remained diligently at work.

Only a few curious ones glanced over before lowering their heads to continue working.

Compared to watching the excitement, their work was more important.

Pulling up the trap took some effort, but fortunately, the animal-hide ropes the beastmen had twisted were strong enough. The fish trap began to move slowly, and murky bubbles rose to the surface.

Lang An pulled the rope along with Lin Qiu, saying, "It's so heavy."

Lin Qiu stared intently into the water.

Not until he felt the vibration on the hide rope did Lin Qiu and Lang An pull with all their might almost simultaneously. The fish trap broke through the water, and Lang An said happily, "We got some, we got some!"

Lin Qiu stared closely into the cage, and seeing the flash of a large fish with silvery-white scales, his brows finally smoothed out.

They brought the cage to the bank and dragged it further away from the river. Now, the contents were clearly visible.

The cage had been made large to begin with, and it seemed the fish inside hadn't eaten anything good, as they were packed tightly together.

Two large fish, about the same size as the ones caught last time, and enough smaller fish to fill a basin.

There were also river shrimp the size of a palm, large crabs...

It was definitely not a wasted effort.

The other two sub-beastmen said excitedly, "Let's check the other one."

As they spoke, they walked over to the other cage together. Several of them pulled with combined effort, and there was a clattering sound from inside; the catch was just as plentiful.

Although there was only one large fish, there were several weighing two or three pounds. Plus the river shrimp and crabs, combined with the first cage, it was enough for the tribe's largest clay pot to cook three times.

Lang An’s smile was bright; watching the fish jumping around on the bank felt like finding a windfall.

The other two beastmen were also happy, though they looked a bit regretful at the ones pinched to death by crabs or suffocated.

Lin Qiu: "Ask the priest about these fish. If they can be eaten, let's prepare them during the hottest part of the day, otherwise, they won't have the strength after pulling weeds."

"Okay, I'll go ask the priest!"

"I'll go tell the little cubs."

The two sub-beastmen were in their thirties or forties, in the prime of their lives, but both were thin due to lack of food. The more expressive one was called Lang Yu, and the steadier one was called Lang Shuang.

Both sub-beastmen had originally been members of the gathering team, but now that their physical strength couldn't keep up, they stayed behind to guard the cave.

When the priest learned that Lin Qiu had really caught fish using the vine-woven cage, he directly excused Lin Qiu from helping him that morning and told the tribe's skilled beastmen to cooperate and make more fish traps immediately.

Members of Lang Bing's squad swarmed over, and seeing the large and small fish laid out on the grass mat, they realized they had been caught by the cage and exclaimed in surprise, grabbing the cages to fiddle with them.

Lang Mo smiled, his tail wagging.

"My efforts weren't in vain." As he spoke, he lay on the ground to stretch his waist and asked loudly, "Qiu! Do you need more vines?"

Qiu: "The priest gave instructions, the more the better."

He had intended to help the tribe, and now it had become a task assigned by the priest. Lin Qiu adapted well, simply gathering the beastmen assigned to make the fish traps and urging them to hurry.

Lang Mo, on the other hand, took two strong beastmen into the forest to find more vines and prepare materials.

For a time, the area in front of Lang Mountain became lively.

The priest said that Lin Qiu should distribute the first batch of fish, so Lin Qiu let everyone prepare and eat them.

So, smoke began to rise in front of Lang Mountain. The beastmen scaled and gutted the fish, and following Lin Qiu's instructions, they also removed the gills.

Perhaps it was because this fish-trap incident made the beastmen realize he was truly changing, their attitudes slowly shifted, and they were no longer subtly ostracizing him.

After a meal of grilled fish, the lingering resentment about him stealing food was punctured, providing an outlet for it to dissipate.

Lin Qiu had spent the whole morning weaving fish traps, and seeing that the tribe's sub-beastmen had also picked up the skill, he planned to go for a walk in the forest in the afternoon.

Based on the beastmen's consumption, eating only fish was not enough.

Apart from being able to change their form and having greater strength, beastmen were actually no different from humans. They grew millet, which meant that food with sufficient starch content could also satisfy them.

The gathering team only looked for wild fruits and leafy vegetables; they rarely looked for plant roots.

In this vast expanse of mountains before him, Lin Qiu didn't believe there was nothing else to eat.

In the morning, Lang Mo and two other beastmen had cleared out almost all the vines in the nearby forest, and now, after lunch and a short rest, they were gathering them to transport back.

Lin Qiu passed by, holding the wooden stick he had prepared for spearing fish last time, stepping over the thick leaves as he walked past them.

Lang Mo: "Qiu? We have enough vines."

Lin Qiu: "I'm just going for a walk."

Lang Mo immediately said, "I'll go with you."

Lin Qiu had never ventured into this primeval forest, so he didn't refuse.

The Wolf Tribe was located in the north of the eastern continent, where the year was long and divided only into the snowy season and the rainy season. The snowy season was bitterly cold, often covered by heavy snow, with streams drying up, the great river freezing over, and snow deep enough to submerge half the cave entrance.

The rainy season was characterized by continuous rain, accompanied by high temperatures, humidity, sweltering heat, and countless snakes, insects, rats, and ants.

Some beastmen who managed to survive the snowy season often died during the rainy season.

The priest said that during the rainy season, tribe members were often bitten by snakes and insects. That was why a large part of the medicine they made now was for detoxification.

The forest in front of Lang Mountain was flat, with only the winding, undulating mountains on the horizon. The forest here was extremely lush, but animal resources were scarce.

Lin Qiu looked around inside and didn't even see many traces of birds.

Seeing him looking around and occasionally digging at the ground with his wooden stick, Lang Mo asked, "Qiu, what are you looking for?"

Lin Qiu: "Food."

"The ground is just dirt, where would there be food?" Lang Mo looked at the treetops. "There are fruits up there, but they're sour enough to make your teeth ache. Do you want to eat them?"

Lin Qiu looked up; he didn't recognize the tree, but the fist-sized green-skinned fruits on the branches were indeed quite tempting.

Even from this distance, he could almost smell the sourness.

Lin Qiu squinted, and before he could see clearly, Lang Mo had already darted up the tree.

He was agile, and having cushioned his stomach with the noon meal, he had some strength now.

Lin Qiu watched him scramble to the tip in a few steps, look around, and directly grab a branch heavy with fruit, snapping it with a surge of arm strength.

The crisp sound of snapping wood drifted through the quiet forest.

"Qiu, move aside."

Lin Qiu stepped back, and Lang Mo threw the branch down, landing on the ground in a few movements.

He leaned against the tree, and seeing Lin Qiu go to pick the fruit, he laughed and said, "We've all eaten the fruits in the forest; these are ripe now, but they're still sour."

Lin Qiu picked one, the fruit coming off the branch with a crisp sound.

He sniffed it; it had a fresh, fragrant scent.

Lin Qiu wiped it off simply, wanting to try the taste, and took a bite.

Before he could do anything, Lang Mo was drooling, his face wrinkled into many folds.

"Slurp." Lang Mo's mouth was secreting saliva uncontrollably, his shoulders shivered, and seeing Lin Qiu only slightly frown, he asked in surprise, "Not sour?"

Lin Qiu: "It's alright."

"Crunch—"

Lin Qiu saw Lang Mo take a big bite.

"Ow!" The sourness made the beastman jump, baring his teeth and spitting it out.

Lin Qiu squeezed the fruit, which felt soft, and broke it open; inside was white pulp with black seeds.

Lin Qiu squatted down, picked the fruits one by one, and put them in his basket.

Lang Mo was sticking his tongue out, drooling clear saliva.

"Do you really like eating this?" He couldn't help but shudder.

Lin Qiu: "I can try cooking with it. I haven't seen this at the priest's place, so I'll take it back to study."

As he spoke, half a basket was filled with the fruits from that branch.

They continued to walk and stop; sunlight filtered through the gaps, casting mottled light and shadows on the two of them.

Lang Mo led the way, learning from Lin Qiu, he found a branch and swung it as he walked, sending broken branches and leaves flying everywhere.

Lin Qiu trailed behind, and a leaf suddenly flew onto his face.

He grabbed it casually, and just as he was about to throw it away, he suddenly paused.

"Wait a minute."

Lang Mo was swinging away with gusto, and upon hearing this, he threw his wooden stick, which flew straight into the bushes.

"Huh?"

Lin Qiu held up the triangular leaf. "This, look for this."

Lang Mo squinted and pointed to the side casually. "Isn't this everywhere?"

Lin Qiu: "Dig it up and let's see."

Lang Mo ran to retrieve his stick, his expression serious. "That's an itchy root, you can't eat it."

笼子得扔些食物才能吸引鱼进去，林楸等到外出捕猎的兽人们回来，得了自己分的那一块肉，再分出去一些，放进鱼笼里。
狼岩看着笼子里的肉，没说什么。
狼莫啃着自己刚刚烤得正合适的肉块，眼巴巴盯着鱼笼。
“怎么还给鱼吃，不吃可以给我。”
狼石犬牙嵌入肉块，狼眼满是信任。
“楸要做大事。”
狼莫：“不就是捞鱼嘛。”
嘴上说着，但眼里也有一丝期待。
狼岩看林楸抓着鱼笼往河边去，想了想，跟了上去。
天色黑青，周围有些模糊了。
河边水深，怕一不小心踩空了，直接坠入河底。
林楸听着脚步声，回头看是狼岩。蓦地想起今早上在人家窝里醒来，林楸眼神一闪，睫羽飞速颤了颤。
“你不去吃肉？”
狼岩抓过林楸手上的鱼笼，“河边危险。怎么放？”
林楸看他一点没有奇怪的表现，想着自己兴许是在他早上走了之后才不小心滚到他窝里的。
念头才一闪，想起那满手的狼毛，林楸脚趾忍不住扣紧。
他面上依旧平静，只有些发烫。
余光看狼岩走在自己身侧，庆幸现在天快彻底黑了。
他今晚一定注意。
下鱼笼林楸也没经验，直接叫狼岩往深水里扔，兽皮绳有多长久扔多远。
看着鱼笼没入水中，林楸示意狼岩将兽皮绳绑在岸边的石头上。
接下来，只需要等着就好。
晚饭后，山洞内。
兽人们没什么娱乐，吃完东西就抓紧时间睡。
林楸躺在自己窝中，背对着狼岩的方向，手指紧紧扣在兽皮边缘。
他背脊绷紧，想起塞在两个草窝中间的毛球，忍不住拉高了兽皮将脑袋一起遮住。
洞内不算安静，有的狼兽人打呼噜，有的磨牙说梦话。火堆里木柴燃烧，风吹着时不时呼呼响。
林楸蒙着兽皮，仿佛隔绝了外面的一切，过了许久才放松身体，慢慢昏睡。
半夜时，狼岩睁眼。
幼崽狼雪又爬出窝，自发地蜷缩在林楸颈侧。林楸也像习惯了，顺手圈着幼崽，两个脑袋贴着脑袋，格外亲近。
狼岩看了会儿幼崽，又划过蜷缩成一团的林楸。
难得安分一晚。
翌日醒来，林楸先看一下自己睡觉的地方，再看手中。干干净净，没做坏事。
他眉头一松，平静地跟洞口的狼果打招呼，然后去起鱼笼，丝毫没注意到狼果略微闪烁的眼神。
见狼安在跟兽人们拔草，林楸唤了他一声。
不管有没有抓到，得让参与了的狼安都看看。
他一喊，除了狼安跟另外两个年长的亚兽人过来，其他兽人依旧勤勤恳恳地忙。
只有些好奇的，抬眼看了看这边，又低头下去干活。
比起看热闹，手上的活儿比较重要。
起笼子费些劲儿，好在兽人们搓的兽皮绳足够结实。鱼笼慢慢动了，水面冒出些浑浊的泡泡来。
狼安跟林楸一同拉着绳子，道：“好重。”
林楸紧盯着水中。
直到感受到兽皮上的震动，林楸跟狼安近乎同时用力，鱼笼破水而出，狼安高兴道：“有了有了！”
林楸紧盯笼子里头，见闪过一尾鳞片银白的大鱼，眉头也跟着舒展开来。
笼子起到岸边，拖得离河远一些。这下里面是看得清清楚楚。
笼子本就做得大，想是里头的鱼没吃过好的，居然挤得严严实实。
两尾大鱼，跟上次抓的差不多大，剩下其他小鱼能装一盆。
还有巴掌长的河虾，大螃蟹……
怎么着都不白干活。
另外两个亚兽人兴奋道：“再看看另一个。”
说着，他们一起往另一个笼子那边走。几人合力一起拉，笼子里噼里啪啦的声响，渔获同样不少。
大鱼虽然只有一尾，但两三斤的鱼有好几条。再有河虾，螃蟹，加上第一笼，够部落里最大的陶锅煮个三次。
狼安笑容明媚，看着岸上的活蹦乱跳的鱼跟白捡似的。
另两个兽人也高兴，不过看着被螃蟹夹死的，还有些憋死的，面上一阵可惜。
林楸：“这鱼问问祭司，要能吃等会儿天最热的时候就弄来吃，不然他们拔完草没力气。”
“好，我去问祭司！”
“我跟那些小崽子们说去。”
两个亚兽人都三四十了，正值壮年，但食物不足两人都瘦弱。情绪外放些的叫狼雨，沉稳点的叫狼霜。
两个亚兽人原本也是采集队的成员，不过现在体力跟不上了，就留守山洞。
祭司知道林楸真的用藤编的笼子捕到了鱼，直接免了林楸今日上午给他帮忙，叫部落手巧的兽人配合着，立马制作鱼笼。
狼冰小队的成员呼啦啦凑来，看着摆在草毯上的大鱼小鱼，知道是笼子抓上来的，纷纷惊呼，抓过笼子就摆弄起来。
狼莫笑嘻嘻，尾巴摇晃。
“不白费我一番力气。”说着趴在地上舒展一下腰，扬声问，“楸！还要不要藤条？”
楸：“祭司交代了，越多越好。”
本就打算帮部落一把，现在成了祭司交代的任务。林楸适应良好，只把分配过来做鱼笼的兽人们凑一堆，快些赶工。
狼莫则先带着两个有力气的兽人去林子里多找些藤条，准备材料。
一时间，狼山前热闹起来。
祭司说，先起来的这一批鱼叫楸分配，楸便让大家做了吃了。
所以这会儿狼山前冒起了烟，兽人们去鳞破肚，又听林楸说的，把鱼鳃也去掉。
许是林楸做鱼笼这一遭叫兽人们意识到他真的在改正，态度便慢慢转变了些，不再若有似无地排斥。
一顿烤鱼下肚，那点对他偷食物的怨气也被戳破，有溢散出去的口子。
林楸忙了一上午编鱼笼，部落的亚兽人们看着也上手了，他打算下午去林子里转一转。
照着兽人们的消耗，仅仅吃鱼是不够的。
兽人除了能变化形态，力气大些，跟人其实没什么两样。他们种植粟，说明淀粉含量足够的食物对他们来说也能饱腹。
采集队寻找的都是野果跟叶菜，鲜少有植物根系那一类。
这眼前茫茫大山，林楸不信没别的吃的。
上午狼莫带着两个兽人几乎把近处林子里的藤蔓全清理出来了，这会儿吃过午饭，休息了会儿，又在归拢运回去。
林楸路过，手上捏着上次准备扎鱼的木棍，踩着厚厚的叶片才他们身旁经过。
狼莫：“楸？藤条够了。”
林楸：“我随便转一转。”
狼莫立即道：“我跟你一起去。”
林楸没钻过这原始森林，没拒绝。
狼部落所在的位置在东边大陆靠北，一年时间漫长，只分雪季跟雨季。雪季严寒，常常暴雪覆盖，溪水断流，大河上冻，雪厚的时候能淹没半个山洞口。
雨季便是连续不断地下雨，伴随着高温，潮湿，闷热，还有数不清的蛇虫鼠蚁。
有些兽人好不容易熬过了雪季，也容易在雨季里死亡。
祭司说，雨季里，部落经常有兽人被蛇虫咬。所以现在做的药很大一部分是解毒的。
狼山前面的林子平坦，只天际线处是蜿蜒起伏的群山。这边林子里，树木极为茂盛，但动物资源却不足。
林楸在里面看了看，甚至连鸟的踪影都少见。
狼莫见他四处张望，时不时用木棍刨一下地面，问：“楸，你找什么？”
林楸：“吃的。”
“地上都是土，哪有什么吃的。”狼莫望着树顶，“那上面有果子，不过酸掉牙，你要吃不？”
林楸仰头，不认识什么树，但树上拳头大小的青皮果子确实挺诱人。
隔着这么远，仿佛都能闻到酸味儿。
林楸虚了虚眼，还没看清，狼莫就蹿上了树。
他身姿矫捷，中午那一顿垫了肚子，这会儿有点力气。
林楸看他几步蹿到尖儿上，四处看了看，直接掰着一片果子多的树枝，手臂用劲儿一折。
咯吱咯吱的脆响，在旷静的林间飘荡。
“楸，你往旁边让让。”
林楸退开些，狼莫见树枝一扔，几下落地。
他背靠着树，见林楸去摘那果子，笑了声道：“林子里果子我们都吃过，这个现在熟了，但还是酸。
林楸摘下来个，果子离枝，清脆一声。
他嗅了嗅，一股清新的香味儿。
林楸简单擦了下，想试试味道，便一口咬下去。
他还没怎么着，狼莫流着哈喇子，脸上皱巴巴的起了好多道褶子。
“吸溜。”狼莫嘴里疯狂分泌唾液，肩膀一抖，看到林楸只微微蹙眉，奇道，“不酸？”
林楸：“还行。”
“咔嚓——”
林楸见狼莫咬了一大口。
“嗷！”酸得兽人跳脚，龇牙往外呸。
林楸捏着果子偏软，直接掰开，里面是带白瓤的，有一颗颗黑色的种子。
林楸蹲下，把果子一个个摘下来，放在篮子里。
狼莫吐着舌头，直流清涎。
“你真喜欢吃啊？”他控制不住地哆嗦一下。
林楸：“可以做菜试试。我没在祭司那里看到过这个，带回去研究一下。”
说着，那一树枝的果子装了半篮子。
又继续走走停停，阳光穿缝而过，两人身上光影斑驳。
狼莫在前面开路，也学着林楸找了一根树枝，边走边回挥舞，打得断枝残叶到处飞。
林楸落在后头，面上忽然飞过来一片叶子。
他随手一抓，正要扔，忽的顿住。
“等一下。”
狼莫打得正起劲儿，闻言手中木棍甩飞出去，直直扎入灌木丛。
“啊？”
林楸举着那三角状的叶片，“这个，找找。”
狼莫一虚眼，随手往侧边一指，“这不到处都是？”
林楸：“挖来看看。”
狼莫跑去捞回木棍，面容肃然，“长痒痒根，不能吃。”

重新修葺过的棚子太小，住不下这么多兽人。
没下雨还好，白雀跟绿眼兽人都能飞树上去睡，但总这样不行。
于是睡过一觉之后，狼岩又安排起小狼修棚子，林楸则跟白雀和绿眼兽人继续做捞淤泥的工具。
这雨不知道什么时候才来，能挖一点是一点。
*
狼山。
时间回到前一天，狼游刚赶回部落，就被自家兽人给围了。
他们往他身后瞧了瞧，后头没兽人。
狼莫胳膊搭在他肩上问：“王呢？楸呢？贝呢？山火都快烧到我们这边来了，他们怎么还不回来？”
“瞎说什么！”狼安给了狼莫一下。
狼游：“他们忙着呢。”
他这边让狼安赶紧安排亚兽人过去做饭，然后才有空坐下来，跟兽人们说南边的事。
“白雀部落和绿眼部落都被烧了，他们现在跑到大泽避难，王让他们帮忙改造大泽。”
“什么？！”
“那岂不是又多了一百多张嘴巴！”
“咱部落有那么多食物吗？”
“吃鱼。”狼安淡淡道。
大泽那边的事也是大事，不敢耽搁。
狼安直接把狼雨狼虹叫过来。
他俩去大泽做饭不是一次两次了，有经验。
两个兽人必定不够，支部落过来的亚兽人们跟他们也干了这么久的活儿了，各方面都熟悉，狼安便又点了八个亚兽人，凑足十个过去。
兽人安排好，狼雨立即把要带的盐、锅碗、陶罐等各种需要用到的东西找齐，随后出发。
狼岩和林楸不在，部落有事，那便祭司做主。
狼山这边也忙。
先前砍倒的树木堆积在空地上，狼起那边需要木材，兽人们得把合适的挑出来，枝丫剔除干净，堆在一边让这些木头风干才能用。
用不上的树枝截断，晒干后，搬进山洞堆放整齐。
部落用的柴火多，要时不时囤一些。
余下这百来个狼兽人，也得吃喝。
狩猎队要捕猎，还要趁着这个机会，多弄些咩咩兽回来养着。
狼贝的采集队不在，但支部落回来的狼潭他们也是采集队的。虽走了几个去大泽，留下来的还有十来个，再加上没跟着狼贝离开的兔兽人们，继续采集。
兽人各自忙各自的事去了，食堂里的兽人一下少了许多。
食堂门口，祭司杵着拐，也不知道在看什么。
“祭司，还有多久才下雨啊？”狼莫扇着风，力道极大，吹得祭司头发凌乱张扬。
目光也随着祭司看来看去。
老祭司：“活儿干完了？”
“还能有什么活儿？这鬼天气，做砖坯，砖坯裂开，烧砖，那窑前又站不了兽人。楸要的水壶也做好了，没事儿了。”
“麻草。”祭司道。
狼莫脸一僵，“哦……”
忘了，兽人们陆陆续续收割那么多麻草回来，还泡在水里呢。
狼莫带上小队的成员走了。
狼阔没跟上去，而是走到老祭司身边，捏着扇子，给年迈的老兽人扇风。
他们从支部落一回到狼山，就跟着狼莫他们烧砖和巡逻，狼山外的事都轮不到他们去忙。
这门口热气浮动，烘得兽人皮都皱了，也只有放了冰的屋里才勉强好受些。
“祭司，回屋里吧。”
老祭司捏紧拐杖，又望了一眼天边，叹口气，慢慢往屋里走。
狼阔搀扶着他手臂，眉目低垂，长腿一步步按照祭司的步伐，走得很慢。
“天被这层灰遮住，什么都看不清。雨水还不下来，南边也不知道烧到什么地方去了。”
“兴许过几天雨就下来了。”
老祭司在凳子上坐下。
狼阔见遍地躺着的同伴陆续醒来，也叹息道：“我记得小的时候，雨季没这么难熬。”
“以往雪季最冷的时候还能出去走走呢。”身边的同伴在草席上打个滚，咕哝一声。
老祭司笑了下，面上愁郁散了些。
他目光带着怀念，道：“你们小时候……那得三十多年前，那会儿在中央大陆，日子也已经过得勉强。”
“要更早的时候，气候适宜，水草丰茂，猎物成群……那会儿，才是兽神大陆最宜居的时候。”
狼阔笑起来，他生得眉眼清正，很是可靠。
三十多的年纪，沉稳睿智，他管着部落年纪正中间的的一批狩猎队成员。要是部落以前没分开，狼莫、狼火他们这一批兽人，得从小栽在他们屁股后头跑。
现在嘛，曾经的小狼已经长成，部落的各项事情他们已然能承担起。
狼阔他们在支部落也累了十几年了，到这边居然也过起了老年兽人的日子，就像狼狡他们一样，成日里守在部落中。
那些个小狼们把他们捧着敬着，觉得他们都是一把老骨头了，轻易动不得。
狼阔有时候都怀疑自己是不是真的老掉牙了，想想着实好笑。
“或许这雨过几天就下了，祭司也别太担心。往前几百年，没准也遇到过这样的情况……”
老祭司想了想，“是这样的……”
可这也不能叫祭司放宽心，这天气热，南边能烧起来，他们这边也有可能。
这雨下不下来，大家都提心吊胆的。
“阔啊！”
一道声音从窗外乍然响起，狼阔寻声望去，狼狡带着一身木屑站在窗外，笑容和蔼地看着他。
曾经在支部落满面愁苦的老兽人，现在神采奕奕，精神抖擞。
狼阔瞧着也跟着扬起嘴角，道：“狡叔有事？”
“你们睡好了？”
“还行。”
“那快点过来帮我们刨木头，我们活儿干不完了。”
狼起现在在搞小船，又听回来的狼游来说，楸那边还在做什么捞泥巴的工具……
哎呀！哎呀！
这事情堆在手里了，光靠他们二十双手，怎么做得完嘛！
狼阔手掌搭在双腿上，笑着站起来。
来了狼山，好像是不用他们总去外面跑，但似乎也同样闲不下来了。
“行，我们去帮忙。”
狼山有祭司盯着，各个小队长又尽职负责，狼岩和林楸不在部落，也不会出乱子。
*
大泽。
天上黑灰愈发的浓重，像一层发霉的铺盖卷儿，厚厚地捂在头顶。
空气中满是熏人的树木燃烧的味道，呛得兽人们咳嗽不已。
兽人们已经多日不见阳光，只有南边透红的火光不散。
虽然如此，天儿却更热了，像有兽人在身边架起一堆柴火，围着他们炙烤。
连续五天，兽人们白日休息，夜里忙活，渐渐已经习惯。
有狼部落管饭，他们不用再操心食物的事，吃得饱了，每天又忙个不停，大家没心思去想以后，渐渐也都从这一场山火中回过神来。
狼部落的活儿说难也不难，只麻烦些。
近两百个兽人每天重复着把水底的淤泥捞起来，垒在一块。
起先会胳膊疼，会腰酸，腿上也会长满痒得不行的疙瘩。
但食物管够，加上狼兽人给了药，待他们适应之后，在饥饿困苦中虚弱下去的身体，反倒渐渐好转。
正是傍晚，干燥的树叶被微风吹得窸窣作响，兽人们感受不到一点凉爽。
大伙儿睡醒过后，等着吃过晚饭。吃完晚饭，又要开始干活了。
白雀兽人心态好，做事积极，日子稳定下来后，也不操心之后的事，一个心思干活。
雀十二白作为白雀兽人当中年轻一辈的队长，已经提前把自己小队的成员召集过来，开始分配今晚上的任务。
堆泥巴也是有技巧的。
基底要实，要宽，挖出来的泥松松垮垮胡乱一摊，一个晚上就能被水冲走一半，那是白做工。
白雀兽人们秉承着吃了狼部落的东西就得好好做事的想法，他们摸索了几天，挖泥巴也挖出一点心得来。
十几个年轻的白雀兽人围坐在一起，旁边或坐或站着些年长的白雀兽人，也跟着一起听着。
白雀族长坐靠在附近的一棵大树树干上。
他揭开腿上已经干掉的草药糊糊，挠了挠腿上的红点点，乐乐呵呵地听着自家小兽人们分配任务。
正听得高兴，边上忽然一声长叹。
白雀族人忍了忍，没忍住白眼一翻。
这是第几百次了！
“我说，给狼部落干活要是委屈你们了，你们不干就是。想走就赶紧走，别委屈自己。”
绿壬闭着眼睛，靠在树干。
他这几天一直坐在这里，除了干点活，就没挪过窝。
树根旁边的草都被他坐死了一片。
绿壬没有说话。
他也没力气说话。
部落一而再再而三受到打击，他这个当族长的，如同陷入泥沼，越挣扎陷得越深。
他想到上一任族长把绿眼部落交到自己手里时的殷切期盼，想到绿眼部落的族人因他的决定伤亡，想到部落的未来彻底在他手里毁了……无数想法压在他身上，他已经快喘不过气了。
“哎——”
“哎哎哎！有什么好哎的！”
“狼部落管吃管喝，你当初想投靠狼部落不就是为了一口食物！那你想想，现在日子跟投靠狼部落有什么区别？！”
绿壬眼皮下的眼珠动了动。
白雀族长已经忍了很久了，今天开了个头，他非得把怨气发泄完不可。
不然憋屈了自己，不利于他长命百岁！
“反正按照狼王说的，这大泽要改造完，没个七八年肯定是不行的，你只要好好干，认真干，这跟投靠狼部落有什么区别？”
“我们只管一心干活，食物他们还会做好了送到手里，还不用你自己做！你有什么不满意的？”
“年纪轻轻，成天哎哎哎！我听着都丧气！”
“你也不看看你那些族人，明明吃饱了挺乐呵，一看到你这要死不活的样子，也跟着你愁眉苦脸的！还有我们……我们两个部落搭伙做事，我家兽人做得好好的，一看你们那脸色，我们自己也做不下去！”
“好歹没死，只要活着，今天是只能啃点鱼干，但没准几年后抱着肉干撑死都行！怎么就这么想不开！”
“咳、咳咳……”绿壬当了族长这么多年还没被这么说过。
他被怼得胸口起伏，忍不住咳嗽。
白雀族长看了一眼其他绿眼兽人，都没往这边凑，他继续嘀嘀咕咕。
“咳！别、别说了。”
白雀族长歪过身子，绕过树看了他一眼。
绿壬睁开眼，与他对上。
白雀族长一下子缩回脑袋，气势骤降，“我可没说错……”
“咳！咳咳咳咳咳……”绿壬一下子咳得撕心裂肺，吓得绿眼兽人们纷纷围拢过来。
白雀兽人们挪了挪屁股，靠近他们族长。
雀二白用手肘别了别白雀族长，小声道：“雀大白，那绿壬看着都没多少气儿了，你可别把他气死了。”
白雀族长：“哼！你当我怕！”
白雀族长瞄了一眼围着绿壬的绿眼兽人，嘴巴动了动，收回目光。
不怕不怕，这还是在狼部落，他们不敢动手。
说了这么一通，白雀族长身心舒畅了。
听见狼兽人喊吃肉汤的声音，大小白雀兽人们积极地站起来，追着小狼们一起去排队。
“十二白，今晚跟我们去抓长虫！”狼金边跑边喊道。
雀十二白盯紧棚子下的队伍猛冲，面上冷酷道：“我们要挖泥巴。”
“那抓半夜，挖半夜。”
“你真看得起我。”
“嘿嘿。”狼金笑得有些傻，“看得起看得起，找长虫还是你们会找，我们又不会飞，光四条腿跑着去找费时间。”
有白雀帮忙，他们部落的速度比以前快一倍，剩下的时间才好完成王交代的任务。
雀十二白的人形比小狼矮一个头，头发齐脖，纯白色的，五官生得也圆润漂亮，尤其一双眼睛，眼头微圆，眼尾微翘，嘴巴一瞥，就是个高冷的小少年。
“你怎么不叫羽涯他们？”
“涯他们那不是听王指挥。”
“我不也得听狼王……”
“嘿嘿，我已经跟王说了。”
雀十二白一听，哼了声，呲溜一下蹿到小狼前面排队，双手抱臂，不开口了。
他们年纪相当，以前白雀怕狼兽人，那是觉得他们一爪子能弄死他们。
但小狼跟成年狼兽人不一样，蠢兮兮的，又跟他们说得上话，相处几天，两边有空就能玩儿在一起了。
白雀兽人跟狼兽人相处得越来越愉快，尤其是有个厚脸皮的雀二白带头，大伙儿渐渐跟狼兽人熟悉了。
绿眼兽人跟狼兽人有仇怨，加上自家族长这样，大家一起生活这么久，空闲时他们也只坐在角落，只跟自己的兽人说话。
他们本以为，这样的日子要持续到离开狼部落的时候。
可当天晚上，他们就发现族长变了。
吃饭时，开始只能吃半碗肉汤的族长一口气吃了一碗。
兽人们跟他说话时，他看了绿皎很久。
绿皎险些以为他回光返照，眼眶都蓄起泪了，绿壬一拍他肩膀，捏紧道：“不能被白雀比下去。”
绿皎有些懵：“族、族长？”
什么跟白雀比？
挖泥巴吗？这有什么好比的？
绿壬收回手，低着头念了一句。
后头围着的绿眼兽人没听见，只有最近的绿皎听到了。
他有些恍惚，慢慢走出了兽人堆，然后被自己伴侣绿月担忧地握住了手。
“皎？”
绿皎掏了掏耳朵。
他刚刚没听错吧？
族长说“就是赖也要赖在狼部落”，这话很像他们族长的做事风格。
果然没变。
但这话听着，他们族长像是想通了。
是想通了。
白雀族长那一番话如同拨开云雾，直接让绿壬念头通达了。
是啊！
他们最开始想的，不就是靠着狼部落吗？
现在这样，那不正好！
这就是他们的机会！
他们用救狼兽人幼崽都换不来的机会，却因为部落被烧毁，得到了这个机会！
此时不抓住，要待何时？
想通之后，绿壬心中的郁气散得一干二净！
族长好了，绿眼兽人精神一振。
可好了是好了，现在又有点奇怪。
也不知道是不是白雀族长惹了他，他跟人家较劲似地干活，忙着忙着，一个没注意，一屁股将白雀族长撞进淤泥里。
绿眼兽人：“……”
白雀族长怒吼：“绿壬！”
绿壬被吼了一声，却和和气气地把兽人搀扶起来，看着他满身泥泞，直接将人家拎起往水里晃了两下。
白雀族长更脏了，看他们族长的眼神也更阴沉，要不是手短了一截，怕是已经直接上手掐住了他们族长脖子。
绿月拽了拽自家伴侣的兽皮裙，小声道：“族长……疯了？”
这是挑衅吗？
可他们两个部落之间有仇吗？
绿皎谨慎地握住自己伴侣的手，目光从两个族长间掠过，落到远处狼王身上，然后是狼王旁边的林楸身上……
看他俩没反应，默默收回目光，垂眼看着自己伴侣。
“应该不是故意的，刚恢复点力气，手脚不听使唤正常。”
“是、是这样的吗？”绿月怀疑地看着自己伴侣，又忍不住掰着他脑袋，仔仔细细看了一遍他的眼睛。
他怀疑他的伴侣有点眼瞎。
绿皎失笑，拉下自己的伴侣的手，狠狠搓了两下。
“没瞎。”
绿月也弯眼笑起来。
绿皎看着他们像猛喝了一罐子草药的族长……
“能振作起来是好事，不管因为什么原因。”
兽人们不解，但此时也想不通他们族长为什么这么积极。
不过等看到打肉汤时，狼雨笑呵呵地多给他们族长打了两块肉，绿眼兽人眼睛一下亮了。
懂了！
多干活能多吃肉！原来如此！
白雀兽人一看，这怎么能行？
他们不能被比下去！
狼岩和林楸隐隐感觉到这种气氛，但好像对狼部落没什么影响，甚至干活的进度都快了不少。
既然如此，他们索性就不管了。
两个部落的兽人较着劲儿，你追我赶，不仅干活速度快，效率也高。
短短五天，眼前这一片辽阔的水面上，已然垒出两块方方正正的土块。
林楸上去走过，确确实实是垒实了的泥，不会一踩就垮。
淤泥颜色黑沉，味道腥臭，不知藏在水底多少年。
但这样的泥极其肥沃，以后在上面种植，直接不用施肥，庄稼就能长得极好。
“就是这样，按照这个样子继续做，等明年，我们兴许就可以在上面种植了。”
白雀和绿眼兽人都是见过狼山那边种植的尾巴草的。
他们虽不明白放着好好的没水的地方他们不去开垦，为什么盯上这片水域，但都暗自觉得，狼部落不会白用功。
又是一个阴沉沉的天。
兽人们忙活一夜，这会儿刚收工，乱七八糟躺在岸上，如同还没下火堆的叫花鸡，浑身泥泞。
这棚子扩大了许多，目前还在扩建。负责这事的小狼们每天忙得团团转，一边打猎，一边还得修棚子。
虽累，但也锻炼了兽人。
如今小狼也能独当一面了。
大伙儿忙了一夜，都有些疲惫。但他们刚从泥里滚了出来，一身泥浆，头发上都沾了不少淤泥，就这么睡，没准明天起来又得浑身痒痒。
臭烘烘的兽人们躺了会儿，艰难爬起来，找地方清洗。
他们拿着狼部落自制的洗澡药粉，人手一包。
药粉还带着香味，这东西往身上搓搓洗洗，能避免淤泥里的肥气弄出的痘疮，洗完身上干干净净，一点泥腥味都没有。
靠东边，原本是一处长满蛮草的干湖。
如今近处的蛮草被收割送回去了狼部落，兽人们往湖里垫了许多石头，又引了水，再往岸边铺了石板，这里成了兽人们专属的洗澡的地方。
兽人们下水洗澡，狼岩拎着帕子，却绕行这边，去林子里藏着的溪涧。
林楸一身泥，跟在他后头。
下水的白雀兽人和绿眼兽人瞄着他俩，等他们走过，才放心跳入水中。
不是林楸他们不在这边洗，是兽人们不习惯。毕竟不是一个部落的，狼岩在这里他们不自在。
他俩这些天来也跟两个部落的兽人一起忙碌，他们也都不懂垒田这事儿，只能跟着兽人们一起摸索。
天天下水，天天熬夜，熬得他俩一看到天亮就想往地下躺。
等走进林子，林楸拉着狼岩的手腕，闭着眼睛，跟着他往前走。
他们王生得健壮挺拔，连腕骨捏着都像捏了一把钢筋，筋骨感十足。
林楸累得抬不起腿，被杂草绊住也只趔趄几下，在王身边，他摔不着。
狼岩手往前伸了下，林楸顺着他的力道往前走了几步，腿上没力，直直往前栽。
狼岩看着笑了声，弯腰将他单手抱起来。
林楸晃了下腿，因为极度疲劳，声音变得黏糊，像吃了一口粘牙的糖：“你也累，放我下来……”
嘴上这么说着，胳膊却诚实地抱住他的脖子，脑袋靠在他肩膀，没力气再动了。
狼岩歪头碰了下他额角，快步往前走。
没一会儿，林间传来叮咚作响的水流声。
再走几步，就见两臂宽的溪流从林间冲出来，溪石密布，水尤清冽。
狼岩走上其中没有一点青苔、干净得突兀的两块石头上，抱着林楸坐下来。
林楸闭着眼睛抬头，声音含糊道：“到了吗？”
狼岩没动，捂着林楸耳朵静坐了会儿，他便又睡熟了。
狼岩笑着抚了下林楸沾了泥点子的脸，随后撩起水，慢慢给他把泥先清洗干净。
随后再抹上草药粉搓一搓，再冲一遍水。
林楸小睡一会儿，迷迷糊糊睁开眼，想要坐起来，狼岩扶着他的后腰，帮他稳住。
林楸低头一看，自己光溜溜的，什么都没穿。
他脚趾蜷缩，红着脸看着狼岩。
“害羞了？”狼岩喉间溢出一声笑，又低又沉，像醇厚的酒酿。
林楸攀着他胳膊倾身，直接扑进他怀里。
狼岩看着他绯红的耳朵，鼻尖蹭了蹭，“这样就看不见了？”
林楸鼻尖哼出一声气音。
他的伴侣迷糊的时候跟平常很不一样，会更黏人些，也更可爱些。
“我身上脏。”
林楸顺手摸一把水，往狼岩胳膊上蹭。
“不困了？”狼岩下巴贴着他额头，双手护着林楸腰间，拢得牢牢的，像巨龙守着他的宝藏，极为霸道。
林楸：“困，但你也累。”
耳畔传来闷声笑，一把窄腰被狼岩手臂掐得紧紧的。
林楸认认真真给狼岩清洗，忽的，耳垂又湿又烫。
林楸手一颤。
他手撩起水往狼岩身上泼，心神乱了，胡乱在他身上搓。
手碰到一处滚烫，林楸仰头看着狼岩。
狼岩灰眸虚虚笼着他，充满着热意。他低头轻轻在林楸唇边咬了下，大手贴着他手背，引着他清洗。
林楸动了动唇，眼红得润透。
“还、还在外面……”
“嗯。”狼岩鼻尖呼出一阵热意，烫得林楸耳侧起了一层鸡皮疙瘩。
后腰处的大掌烫得灼人，粗糙的指腹摩擦着皮肤，有些痒，有些磨人。
林楸额头抵着狼岩额头，眼里蓄水，主动将手紧紧环住他脖子。
“王……”
“嗯。”狼岩忍不住将林楸抱起，亲亲他侧脸，鼻尖拱蹭他耳垂。
他们已经很久没有亲近了。
chapters.title: 第160章
chapters.translated_text:
The renovated shed was too small to accommodate so many orcs.

It was fine when it wasn't raining, as the White Sparrow and Green-Eyed orcs could fly up to the trees to sleep, but that couldn't go on forever.

So, after a night's sleep, Lang Yan arranged for the young wolves to build more sheds, while Lin Qiu continued making tools for dredging silt with the White Sparrow and Green-Eyed orcs.

There was no telling when the rain would come, so they had to dig as much as they could while they had the chance.

*

Lang Mountain.

Going back to the previous day, as soon as Lang You hurried back to the tribe, he was surrounded by his fellow orcs.

They peered behind him, but there were no other orcs.

Lang Mo draped an arm over his shoulder and asked, "Where's the King? Where's Qiu? Where's Bei? The forest fire is almost reaching us; why haven't they returned yet?"

"Stop talking nonsense!" Lang An gave Lang Mo a swat.

Lang You replied, "They're busy."

He then urged Lang An to quickly arrange for the sub-beasts to prepare food, only then finding a moment to sit down and tell the orcs about the situation in the south.

"The White Sparrow and Green-Eyed tribes have both been burned down. They've fled to the Great Marsh for refuge, and the King has them helping to renovate the marsh."

"What?!"

"Doesn't that mean there are over a hundred more mouths to feed!"

"Does our tribe have that much food?"

"We'll eat fish," Lang An said calmly.

Matters at the Great Marsh were also urgent; they couldn't afford to delay.

Lang An immediately called for Lang Yu and Lang Hong.

They had been to the Great Marsh to cook more than once and had experience.

Two orcs definitely wouldn't be enough. The sub-beasts who had come from the branch tribe had been working with them for a long time and were familiar with everything, so Lang An picked eight more sub-beasts to make a group of ten.

Once the orcs were arranged, Lang Yu immediately gathered the salt, pots, bowls, clay jars, and other necessary items, and then they set off.

With Lang Yan and Lin Qiu away, if the tribe had any issues, the Priest would be in charge.

Things were busy at Lang Mountain as well.

The trees that had been felled earlier were piled up in the clearing. Lang Qi needed timber, so the orcs had to pick out the suitable ones, trim off the branches, and stack them aside to let the wood air-dry before it could be used.

The unusable branches were cut into pieces, dried in the sun, and then moved into the caves to be stacked neatly.

The tribe used a lot of firewood and needed to stockpile some from time to time.

The remaining hundred or so wolf orcs also needed to eat and drink.

The hunting team had to hunt, and they also had to take this opportunity to bring back more Baa-Baa beasts to raise.

Lang Bei's gathering team wasn't there, but Lang Tan and the others who had returned from the branch tribe were also part of the gathering team. Although a few had gone to the Great Marsh, there were still a dozen left, and combined with the rabbit orcs who hadn't left with Lang Bei, they continued gathering.

The orcs went about their own tasks, and the number of orcs in the cafeteria dropped significantly.

At the entrance of the cafeteria, the Priest leaned on his cane, not sure what he was looking at.

"Priest, how much longer until it rains?" Lang Mo fanned himself with great force, blowing the Priest's hair into a messy, wild state.

His gaze followed the Priest's, looking back and forth.

The old Priest asked, "Is your work done?"

"What other work is there? In this cursed weather, if we make bricks, they crack; if we try to fire them, no orc can stand in front of the kiln. The water jugs Qiu wanted are finished too, so there's nothing left to do."

"Hemp grass," the Priest said.

Lang Mo's face stiffened, "Oh..."

He had forgotten; the orcs had harvested so much hemp grass one after another, and it was still soaking in the water.

Lang Mo took his squad members and left.

Lang Kuo didn't follow; instead, he walked to the old Priest's side, holding a fan and fanning the elderly orc.

Ever since they returned to Lang Mountain from the branch tribe, they had been following Lang Mo and the others to fire bricks and patrol; they didn't have a turn to handle matters outside of Lang Mountain.

The heat wafting at the entrance was enough to wrinkle an orc's skin; only in the rooms where ice was kept could one feel somewhat comfortable.

"Priest, let's go back inside."

The old Priest gripped his cane tightly, looked at the horizon once more, sighed, and slowly walked inside.

Lang Kuo supported his arm, eyes lowered, his long legs matching the Priest's pace, walking very slowly.

"The sky is covered by this layer of ash; I can't see anything clearly. The rain still won't come, and I don't know how far the fire has spread in the south."

"Perhaps the rain will come in a few days."

The old Priest sat down on a stool.

Seeing his companions who had been lying on the ground waking up one by one, Lang Kuo sighed, "I remember when I was young, the rainy season wasn't this hard to endure."

"In the past, we could even go out during the coldest part of the snow season," a companion beside him rolled over on the straw mat and muttered.

The old Priest smiled, and the gloom on his face dissipated a little.

With a nostalgic look in his eyes, he said, "When you were young... that was over thirty years ago. Back then, on the Central Continent, life was already barely manageable."

"Even earlier, the climate was suitable, the water and grass were lush, and prey was abundant... that was when the Beast God Continent was most habitable."

Lang Kuo laughed; he had a clean, upright appearance and looked very reliable.

At over thirty years old, he was steady and wise, managing a group of hunting team members in the middle age range of the tribe. If the tribe hadn't split up before, orcs like Lang Mo and Lang Huo would have been trailing behind them since they were little.

Now, however, the little wolves had grown up, and they could already shoulder the various tasks of the tribe.

Lang Kuo and the others had been tired for over a decade at the branch tribe, and here they had actually started living the life of elderly orcs, just like Lang Jiao and the others, guarding the tribe all day long.

Those little wolves treated them with such respect, thinking they were all old bones that shouldn't be moved easily.

Sometimes Lang Kuo wondered if he was really getting long in the tooth, which was truly funny to think about.

"Perhaps the rain will fall in a few days, so don't worry too much, Priest. A few hundred years ago, maybe they encountered similar situations..."

The old Priest thought for a moment, "That is true..."

But that couldn't put the Priest's mind at ease; the weather was hot, and if the south could catch fire, it was possible for them too.

With the rain not coming, everyone was on edge.

"Kuo!"

A voice suddenly rang out from outside the window. Lang Kuo looked toward the sound and saw Lang Jiao standing outside with wood shavings all over him, looking at him with a kind smile.

The old orc who used to be full of sorrow at the branch tribe was now radiant and full of energy.

Lang Kuo smiled back and asked, "Is something the matter, Uncle Jiao?"

"Are you done sleeping?"

"It's alright."

"Then hurry over and help us plane the wood; we have too much work to finish."

Lang Qi was currently working on a small boat, and he heard from Lang You, who had just returned, that Qiu was making some kind of mud-dredging tool over there...

Oh my! Oh my!

The work was piling up; how could they finish it with only their twenty hands!

Lang Kuo rested his palms on his legs and stood up with a smile.

Coming to Lang Mountain, it seemed they didn't have to run outside all the time, but it seemed they couldn't stay idle either.

"Alright, we'll come help."

With the Priest watching over Lang Mountain and each squad leader being diligent and responsible, there wouldn't be any chaos even with Lang Yan and Lin Qiu away.

*

The Great Marsh.

The black ash in the sky grew thicker, like a moldy quilt draped heavily over their heads.

The air was filled with the suffocating smell of burning wood, making the orcs cough incessantly.

The orcs hadn't seen sunlight for many days; only the red glow of the fire in the south remained.

Despite this, the weather was even hotter, as if someone had built a pile of firewood around them, roasting them.

For five consecutive days, the orcs rested during the day and worked at night, gradually getting used to it.

The Wolf Tribe provided food, so they didn't have to worry about that anymore. Once they were full and busy all day, they had no time to think about the future, and gradually, they all recovered from the shock of the mountain fire.

The Wolf Tribe's work wasn't hard, just tedious.

Nearly two hundred orcs repeated the task of dredging silt from the bottom of the water and piling it up every day.

At first, their arms would ache, their waists would be sore, and their legs would be covered in itchy bumps.

But with enough food and the medicine provided by the wolf orcs, once they adapted, their bodies, which had been weakened by hunger and hardship, actually began to improve.

It was evening, and the dry leaves rustled in the breeze, but the orcs couldn't feel a hint of coolness.

After waking up, everyone waited for dinner. After dinner, they would have to start working again.

The White Sparrow orcs had a good attitude and were proactive. Once their lives stabilized, they didn't worry about the future and focused entirely on their work.

Que Shi'er Bai, as the captain of the younger generation of White Sparrow orcs, had already gathered his squad members to distribute the tasks for the night.

There was a technique to piling mud.

The base had to be solid and wide; if the mud was just loosely dumped, half of it would be washed away by the water in one night, making it all wasted effort.

The White Sparrow orcs, holding the belief that since they ate the Wolf Tribe's food, they had to work hard, had explored for a few days and gained some insight into digging mud.

A dozen young White Sparrow orcs sat in a circle, with some older ones sitting or standing nearby, listening along.

The White Sparrow Patriarch sat leaning against the trunk of a large tree nearby.

He peeled off the dried herbal paste on his leg, scratched the red spots, and listened happily to his young orcs assigning tasks.

Just as he was enjoying it, a long sigh came from beside him.

The White Sparrow Patriarch resisted, but couldn't help rolling his eyes.

This was the hundredth time!

"I'm telling you, if working for the Wolf Tribe is such a grievance, then just don't do it. If you want to leave, just go; don't make yourself miserable."

Lü Ren closed his eyes, leaning against the tree trunk.

He had been sitting here for days, and apart from doing a little work, he hadn't moved.

The grass by the tree roots had been sat to death by him.

Lü Ren didn't speak.

He didn't have the strength to speak either.

His tribe had been hit again and again, and as the Patriarch, he felt like he was trapped in a quagmire, sinking deeper the more he struggled.

He thought of the earnest expectations of the previous Patriarch when he handed the Green-Eyed tribe to him, thought of the casualties his people suffered because of his decisions, and thought of the tribe's future being completely destroyed in his hands... Countless thoughts weighed on him, and he could barely breathe.

"Sigh—"

"Sigh, sigh, sigh! What is there to sigh about!"

"The Wolf Tribe provides food and drink; didn't you want to rely on the Wolf Tribe for food in the first place! Think about it, how is life now any different from relying on the Wolf Tribe?!"

The eyeballs under Lü Ren's eyelids moved.

The White Sparrow Patriarch had been holding back for a long time; today, since he had started, he had to vent all his resentment.

Otherwise, holding it in would be bad for his health!

"Anyway, according to the Wolf King, it will take seven or eight years to finish renovating this Great Marsh. As long as you work hard and diligently, how is this different from relying on the Wolf Tribe?"

"We just focus on working, and they even deliver the food to our hands, and you don't even have to cook it yourself! What are you dissatisfied with?"

"You're young, and you sigh all day long! It's depressing just to listen to!"

"Look at your own people; they were happy enough when they were full, but as soon as they see your lifeless face, they get all gloomy too! And us... our two tribes are working together; my orcs are doing fine, but when they see your faces, we can't keep working either!"

"At least we aren't dead. As long as we're alive, today we might only be able to chew on some dried fish, but maybe in a few years, we'll be able to eat our fill of dried meat! Why are you so stuck on this!"

"Cough, cough..." Lü Ren hadn't been spoken to like this in all his years as Patriarch.

He was so frustrated that his chest heaved, and he couldn't help but cough.

The White Sparrow Patriarch glanced at the other Green-Eyed orcs, who didn't come over, and continued muttering.

"Cough! Stop, stop talking."

The White Sparrow Patriarch leaned over and looked at him from around the tree.

Lü Ren opened his eyes and met his gaze.

The White Sparrow Patriarch immediately retracted his head, his momentum dropping, "I didn't say anything wrong..."

"Cough! Cough, cough, cough, cough..." Lü Ren suddenly coughed violently, scaring the Green-Eyed orcs into gathering around him.

The White Sparrow orcs shifted their bottoms, moving closer to their Patriarch.

Que Er Bai nudged the White Sparrow Patriarch with his elbow and whispered, "Que Da Bai, Lü Ren doesn't look like he has much breath left; don't go and anger him to death."

The White Sparrow Patriarch replied, "Hmph! You think I'm afraid!"

The White Sparrow Patriarch glanced at the Green-Eyed orcs surrounding Lü Ren, his mouth moved, and he looked away.

Not afraid, not afraid; this was still the Wolf Tribe, and they wouldn't dare to make a move.

After saying all that, the White Sparrow Patriarch felt refreshed.

Hearing the wolf orcs calling for meat soup, the White Sparrow orcs, big and small, stood up eagerly and chased after the little wolves to line up.

"Shi'er Bai, come catch long-worms with us tonight!" Lang Jin shouted while running.

Que Shi'er Bai stared intently at the line under the shed and said coldly, "We have to dig mud."

"Then catch them for half the night and dig for half the night."

"You really think highly of me."

"Hehe." Lang Jin laughed a bit foolishly, "I do, I do. You guys are better at finding long-worms. We can't fly, so running around on four legs is a waste of time."

With the White Sparrows helping, their tribe's speed was twice as fast as before, and only then could they finish the tasks assigned by the King.

Que Shi'er Bai's human form was a head shorter than the little wolves, his hair was shoulder-length and pure white, and his features were round and pretty, especially his eyes—the inner corners slightly round and the outer corners slightly upturned. With a pout of his lips, he looked like a cold, young boy.

"Why don't you ask Yu Ya and the others?"

"Ya and the others are under the King's command."

"Don't I have to listen to the Wolf King..."

"Hehe, I already told the King."

Upon hearing this, Que Shi'er Bai huffed, slid in front of the little wolves to line up, crossed his arms, and stopped talking.

They were of similar age. Before, the White Sparrows were afraid of the wolf orcs because they thought one swipe of their claws could kill them.

But the little wolves were different from the adult wolf orcs; they were silly and could talk to them. After spending a few days together, the two sides played together whenever they had free time.

The White Sparrow orcs got along better and better with the wolf orcs, especially with the thick-skinned Que Er Bai leading the way; everyone gradually became familiar with the wolf orcs.

The Green-Eyed orcs had a grudge against the wolf orcs, and with their Patriarch like that, after living together for so long, they only sat in the corners during their free time, talking only to their own kind.

They originally thought this life would continue until they left the Wolf Tribe.

But that same night, they discovered that their Patriarch had changed.

At dinner, the Patriarch, who could only manage half a bowl of meat soup before, drank a whole bowl in one go.

When the orcs spoke to him, he looked at Lü Jiao for a long time.

Lü Jiao almost thought he was having a final burst of energy and his eyes welled up with tears. Lü Ren patted his shoulder and gripped it tightly, saying, "We cannot be outdone by the White Sparrows."

Lü Jiao was a bit confused, "Pa-Patriarch?"

Outdone by the White Sparrows in what?

Digging mud? What was there to compete about?

Lü Ren withdrew his hand and muttered something with his head down.

The Green-Eyed orcs gathered behind didn't hear it, only Lü Jiao, who was closest, heard.

He was a bit dazed, slowly walked out of the crowd of orcs, and was then held by his partner, Lü Yue, with concern.

"Jiao?"

Lü Jiao picked at his ear.

He hadn't misheard, right?

The Patriarch said, "Even if we have to cling on, we must cling to the Wolf Tribe." This sounded very much like their Patriarch's style.

Sure enough, he hadn't changed.

But hearing this, it seemed their Patriarch had figured things out.

He had indeed figured it out.

The White Sparrow Patriarch's words were like clearing away the clouds, directly clearing Lü Ren's mind.

Yes!

Wasn't relying on the Wolf Tribe what they wanted in the first place?

Now that it was like this, wasn't it perfect!

This was their opportunity!

They had gained an opportunity they couldn't have bought even by saving the Wolf Tribe's cubs, all because their tribe was burned down!

If they didn't seize it now, when would they?

After figuring it out, the gloom in Lü Ren's heart dissipated completely!

With the Patriarch better, the Green-Eyed orcs felt a surge of energy.

But while he was better, he was now a bit strange.

Whether it was because the White Sparrow Patriarch had provoked him, he worked as if he were competing with him. While busy, he didn't pay attention and bumped the White Sparrow Patriarch into the silt with his butt.

The Green-Eyed orcs: "..."

The White Sparrow Patriarch roared, "Lü Ren!"

Lü Ren was roared at, but he kindly helped the orc up, and seeing him covered in mud, he directly picked him up and shook him twice in the water.

The White Sparrow Patriarch was even dirtier, and his look toward their Patriarch was even gloomier. If his arms weren't a bit short, he would have probably reached out and choked their Patriarch's neck.

Lü Yue tugged at his partner's animal skin skirt and whispered, "Patriarch... has he gone crazy?"

Was this a provocation?

But did the two tribes have a grudge?

Lü Jiao cautiously held his partner's hand, his gaze sweeping past the two Patriarchs and landing on the Wolf King in the distance, then on Lin Qiu beside the Wolf King...

Seeing that they didn't react, he silently withdrew his gaze and looked down at his partner.

"It shouldn't be intentional. He just regained some strength, so it's normal for his hands and feet to be uncoordinated."

"Is, is that so?" Lü Yue looked at his partner suspiciously and couldn't help but hold his head and look carefully into his eyes.

He suspected his partner was a bit blind.

Lü Jiao laughed, pulled down his partner's hand, and rubbed it hard twice.

"I'm not blind."

Lü Yue also smiled, his eyes curving.

Lü Jiao looked at their Patriarch, who looked like he had just downed a jar of medicine...

"It's a good thing he's cheered up, no matter the reason."

The orcs were puzzled, but they couldn't figure out why their Patriarch was so proactive.

However, when they saw Lang Yu smiling and giving their Patriarch two extra pieces of meat during the meat soup distribution, the Green-Eyed orcs' eyes lit up.

Understood!

More work meant more meat! So that was it!

When the White Sparrow orcs saw this, how could that be allowed?

They couldn't be outdone!

Lang Yan and Lin Qiu vaguely felt this atmosphere, but it didn't seem to have any negative impact on the Wolf Tribe; in fact, the progress of the work had sped up significantly.

Since that was the case, they simply let it be.

The orcs of the two tribes competed with each other, chasing and catching up, not only increasing the speed of the work but also its efficiency.

In just five days, on the vast expanse of water before them, two square plots of land had already been built.

Lin Qiu walked over them; they were indeed solid mud that wouldn't collapse when stepped on.

The silt was dark and had a fishy, foul smell, having been hidden at the bottom of the water for who knows how many years.

But such mud was extremely fertile; in the future, when planting on it, the crops would grow extremely well without the need for fertilizer.

"That's it. Keep doing it this way, and by next year, we might be able to plant on it."

Both the White Sparrow and Green-Eyed orcs had seen the tail-grass planted at Lang Mountain.

Although they didn't understand why they were targeting this water area instead of reclaiming the good, dry land, they all secretly felt that the Wolf Tribe wouldn't do anything in vain.

It was another gloomy day.
