### Chapter 163

Lin Qiu watched from the side, smiling. As the orcs surged forward, they ended up at the back of the line.

"King, aren't you going?"

Lang Yan gripped his hand tightly. Lin Qiu realized belatedly that Lang Yan must have been worried just now. He leaned in, watching the small, bobbing boat on the river, and said softly, "It's fine, I can swim. And you're here watching from the shore..."

"Mn."

Lang Yan’s voice remained cold and hard, though his expression betrayed nothing. Lin Qiu couldn't help but nuzzle his shoulder, leaning against him and staying still.

Since the boat had just been built, it was a novelty to the tribe’s orcs. They had played with the carts for ages, and even the rain couldn't dampen their enthusiasm for this new toy. Lang Huo, being bold, was the first in line. He leaped onto it lightly, as if weightless, and the boat slid out onto the water. He stood firmly, arching an eyebrow at the other orcs with a smug expression.

The next second, his feet slipped, and *splash*—he fell into the water.

The orcs froze, then erupted into laughter.

"Hahahaha! That's what you get for being smug! You fell in!" Among the crowd, Lang Mo laughed the hardest.

Lang Huo climbed back onto the shore with a dark face. He quickly grabbed a rope, wrapped it around Lang Mo four or five times, and tied a dead knot. Lang Mo’s arms were pinned, and he tilted his head back, shouting, "Small-minded! I only laughed at you a couple of times, you can’t even handle that?"

Lang An looked at the dripping wet Lang Huo and patted Lang Mo’s arm. "Enough, you were the one provoking him." Once the knot was untied, Lang An pushed Lang Huo and Lang Mo forward. "You two get on. Try it together."

"Both of us?" Lang Mo and Lang Huo exchanged glances, then both turned their heads away.

Lang Qi, holding a large leaf over his head, said from the side, "Go on, try it. I want to see if it works."

Lang Mo was reluctant, but Lang Huo huffed and hopped on. Not wanting to let Lang Huo dawdle, Lang Mo jumped on as well. The boat wobbled violently. Unlike Lang Huo, who was trying to act cool, Lang Mo quickly squatted down, and only felt safe when he realized the edge of the boat was at his waist.

The boat drifted on the river, feeling quite peaceful. After the two of them went back and forth, they didn't even want to get off. The orcs behind them urged, "Hurry up! We haven't had a turn yet!"

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan stood there as long as the orcs played. Lin Qiu looked at the large leaf over their heads, then at the King’s profile. Suddenly, he stood on his tiptoes. Lang Yan, as if he had been watching him the whole time, turned his head just in time and bit down on the corner of Lin Qiu’s lip—with a bit of force.

Lin Qiu pursed his lips, his tongue tracing the tooth mark, his eyes filled with a faint smile. *Still angry?*

"Don't want to try it?"

"No rush."

Lin Qiu moved his hand, which had become sweaty from being held. "Shall we go back?"

Lang Guo had already gathered the cubs to leave; the rain was picking up, and if they got soaked, they’d have to change clothes again.

Lang Yan and Lin Qiu walked back, but even after returning to the cafeteria, they stood by the window watching the river. Just then, Lin Qiu’s hem was tugged. The force was light, like a gust of wind. He turned, saw no one, looked around, and felt it again.

He looked down to see a small cub. Lin Qiu chuckled, bent down, and lifted the cub onto the windowsill. "Xue, not busy right now?"

Lang Xue hugged his arm, leaning against him affectionately. He looked at the Wolf King next to him, greedily reached out his other small hand toward Lang Yan, and said obediently, "King."

"Mn." Lang Yan pinched the cub's cheek, and the cub promptly grabbed his arm as well. One on the left, one on the right—they completely filled his arms.

Watching the cub nuzzle one, then the other, Lin Qiu couldn't stop smiling. Before the cub had learned to shift into human form, he had always liked to crawl into Lin Qiu's nest at night. Now that he was older and studying with the Priest, he rarely had time to play. Sometimes it made Lin Qiu's heart ache, but the cub never complained, sitting patiently for half a day just to identify herbs.

The wolf tribe’s cubs were all obedient and precious. Lin Qiu watched him lean against them, looking tired, his thick, curly eyelashes drooping as he went quiet. Lin Qiu smoothed his soft hair. "Don't force yourself if you're tired. Tell the Priest you need a few days of rest. You're still young; you need to grow."

The cub didn't speak, just tilted his head and rubbed against his arm.

"Qiuqiu..."

"Mn."

The cub opened his little fist, which he had been clenching tightly. He looked up with tired, milky eyes and said softly, "I want a necklace like A-Sheng’s."

In his palm was a small tooth. Lin Qiu held the cub's little hand with his larger one, inspected it carefully, and took it. "Alright, I'll make you one. But I'm going to the Great Swamp tomorrow, so Xue might have to wait a little while."

"Mn!" The cub smiled, looking like a green fruit covered in rain dew—clean and exceptionally sweet. He buried his fluffy head into Lin Qiu’s chest.

Lin Qiu looked at his awkward position—he insisted on hugging both of them, making it hard to find a comfortable place to lean. Lang Yan leaned his legs against the windowsill, glanced at the river, and pinched the cub’s cheek. "When did the tooth fall out?"

"Before the rainy season."

"Open your mouth and let me see."

The cub obediently opened his mouth.

"It's grown in quite a bit." Lang Yan stared at the sharp tooth, then pulled his hand back.

Lang Xue nodded. "It grows fast."

Having finished his business, the cub sat up straight, legs swinging gently, and watched the river while leaning on Lin Qiu’s arm. His lessons with the Priest were demanding; he rarely had such leisurely times.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan remained silent. The cubs that Lang Guo had chased back inside also ran over, and Lin Qiu and Lang Yan's legs were immediately claimed. Each leg was hugged by two small bodies.

Lin Qiu looked back and signaled for the cubs to be quiet. They went silent, though they kept climbing onto their legs with grunts and groans. Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan in resignation.

Lang Yan reached back, and the cubs hung off his arm like they were on a swing. Excited, they were hoisted up by Lang Yan and placed on the windowsill. Lang Xue sat in the middle of the two of them. Gradually, his breathing became shallow, and his eyelids drooped bit by bit.

The cubs coming up from behind saw him and covered their mouths. Xue was the first of his batch to turn into a human; he was always busy, and never had time to play with the others.

Lin Qiu felt a weight in his arms and gently gathered Lang Xue’s small body.

Lang Guo walked over, glanced at his arms, and whispered, "He’s asleep?"

Lin Qiu nodded.

"Give him to me." As Lang Guo reached out, Lang Xue’s eyelashes flickered, as if about to wake up.

Lin Qiu patted the cub’s back and said to Lang Guo, "I’ll put him back later. It’s been a while since I held him."

Lang Guo smiled, reached out, grabbed the cubs hanging off Lin Qiu’s legs, and set them on the windowsill.

Lin Qiu handed Lang Xue’s little tooth to Lang Yan. Lang Yan took it, looked at it for a moment, then stood up to find some leaves to wrap it in, tying it together with hemp thread.

Further away, the orcs on the river were having a blast, with cheers breaking out from time to time. They played until noon.

Lang Qi packed up the boat and came to find Lang Yan and Lin Qiu. Lin Qiu cradled the sleeping Lang Xue and moved from the windowsill to the straw mats laid out in the cafeteria. The cub had slept all morning in his arms. When he finally opened his eyes, he rested his head against Lin Qiu’s chest, looking blank and slightly disoriented.

Lin Qiu handed the sketches of other boat styles to Lang Qi, and while he was at it, he touched the back of the cub's neck. He felt warm. He picked up a fan and began to fan him gently. Once the cub had woken up and was sitting properly, Lin Qiu said, "Go find An and get some water. Move around a bit, it'll be time to eat soon."

The cub climbed up, using the floor for support. Small as he was, he was shorter than the adult orcs sitting down. He bypassed the orcs to get water, then walked back to sit beside Lin Qiu, pressing his small body against him.

Lin Qiu glanced at him; the cafeteria was cool enough, so he just swayed the fan. The breeze made the cub’s soft hair flutter. He lowered his eyes, looking lazy, but had recovered some energy. Seeing he was fine, Lin Qiu continued discussing the various boat designs with Lang Qi.

Even though the tribe had limited resources and couldn't build large ships right now, satisfying Uncle Qi's curiosity was doable. Lang Qi listened, still hungry for more information.

When Lang An called out that the meat soup was ready, Lang Qi packed up the blueprints and went to join the queue. He walked behind Lang Yan and Lin Qiu, suddenly remembering something. "King, the materials for bows and arrows are accumulating too slowly. I'm afraid we won't be able to make many before the snow season."

Lang Yan: "I'll think of a way regarding the materials."

Lang Qi nodded. He only concerned himself with the making; whatever materials the tribe had, he would collect. He left the rest to the King.

Lin Qiu walked in front, holding Lang Xue’s hand. He turned and asked, "How about we ask the neighboring tribes?"

Making bows required animal horns, tendons, and hides, plus animal glue. One beast only yielded so much material; the wolf tribe had over two hundred orcs, and they were still far from equipping everyone with bows.

Lang Yan: "We can ask the Black Feather tribe."

The White Sparrow and Green Eye tribes were out of the question for now.

"We can also talk to the branch tribe. Don't they have contact with other tribes? See if they can ask around?"

Lang Yan nodded.

"Then should we ask the Black Feather orcs to make a trip? Since it’ll be half a year before the branch tribe returns, there’s still time to collect quite a bit."

"Good, I'll ask."

They settled the matter in a few words. Lang Qi felt that was the only way. Lang Xue took small steps, following Lin Qiu, listening intently. Lin Qiu looked down and saw his thoughtful expression. He hooked the cub’s soft cheek with his finger. "Has Xue thought of any ideas?"

The cub shook his head, his eyes clear, bangs sticking to his forehead, still a bit damp from his nap.

Lin Qiu: "If you can't think of anything, don't worry about it. Let's go eat."

As the tribe’s use of ice increased, the Priest only gave the herbal paste to the orcs who went out hunting and gathering.

The next day, Lin Qiu and his group left before the rain could start again. They took some herbs with them, and the stockpile that Lang Bing and the others had spent half the rainy season gathering shrank again.

When they arrived at the Great Swamp, they had barely rested when Lang Yan heard from Lang Yu that Yu Ya had come looking for them. Ever since this young orc had traded with Yu Qian, he had been working diligently in the wolf tribe. Aside from the time he stood out while chasing the Grey-Winged orcs with Yu Le when Lang Sheng and Lang Yuan were snatched, he had been quite low-key.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan went out to see him. They had left for the Great Swamp early in the morning, arriving at noon, and by the time they rested, it was nearly evening. The rain was heavy again, and thin streams of water trickled from the hay roofing.

Yu Ya and five other young Black Feather orcs were all there. As soon as Lang Yan appeared, the six of them couldn't help but stand at attention. Lin Qiu stayed at Lang Yan’s side, observing quietly. The young orcs were nervous, their lips pressed tightly, eyes darting everywhere.

"Something up?" Lang Yan asked.

"Uncle Wolf King, we heard you wanted to find Black Feather orcs to send a message to the branch tribe. We want to try."

*Uncle Wolf King?*

Lin Qiu smiled. He didn't know who taught them that, but it was a strange way to address him.

Lang Yan signaled for them to sit and sat cross-legged on a grass cushion opposite them. Lin Qiu didn't linger; seeing Lang Yu and the others busy at the stove, he went to help, though he kept listening to the conversation behind him.

"Can you find the branch tribe?"

"We..." Yu Ya gripped his knees so hard they turned white. "We can definitely find it."

Lang Yan didn't refuse immediately. "It takes our wolf orcs half a month to get from Wolf Mountain to the branch tribe. How long will it take you to fly there?"

Yu Ya’s eyes lit up, thinking he had agreed. He immediately calculated: it took wolf orcs half a day to get from Wolf Mountain to their tribe, but they could fly there in half a morning. They were twice as fast as the wolves.

"Seven or eight days."

Lang Yan: "Does Yu Dan know?"

Yu Dan was the adult sub-orc who stayed behind in the wolf tribe to work. With Yu Qian gone, he was the leader of these orcs.

Yu Ya rubbed his palms against his knees, his voice lowering. "We haven't told him yet."

Lang Yan: "You aren't adults yet. Even though I think highly of you, I can't let you go alone. If your tribe leader asks, I won't know what to say."

The young orcs hung their heads in disappointment.

"However..."

Before he could finish, the six orcs perked up like wheat sprouts soaked in water.

Lang Yan: "Go ask your Uncle Dan if there are any adult orcs willing to lead the team. If there are, I can let you go. Of course, they have to agree too."

"We're going to ask right now!"

The young orcs were impatient, and even though it was raining, they ran out immediately.

The shelters near the Great Swamp were divided into two rows. The first row was built by the wolf orcs, and the back was later expanded in a line to both sides. Now that there were many orcs, the wolf cubs dared not build further forward, fearing floods, so they cleared the bushes in the back and built new shelters.

The wolf orcs lived in the front row, and the remaining space was occupied by the White Sparrows. The back row was for the Green Eye and Black Feather orcs. At that moment, the White Sparrow and Green Eye orcs hadn't returned yet, and Lang Xiao and Lang Bei were out gathering food.

The Black Feather orcs were sitting in their shelter, sewing pants. They had been given some linen by the tribe, but they had to make the clothes themselves. Yu Ya and the others rushed in and sat before their uncles, acting exceptionally obedient.

Yu Dan glanced at them as he worked, his bone needle easily piercing the linen; his eyebrows lifted. This was much easier to sew than animal hide.

"Uncle Dan..."

Yu Dan’s beautiful phoenix eyes swept over them. "If you're hungry, find An. There's no food here."

"We're not hungry."

"Oh." Yu Dan went quiet again. The other four adult Black Feather orcs snickered, staying silent. Whenever the young ones acted like this, they were definitely asking for something.

"Uncle Dan... we want to go to the branch tribe to deliver a message for the wolf orcs."

Yu Dan frowned, slowly putting down his cloth.

"No."

The branch tribe at Wolf Mountain was too far; they were just underage cubs. Plus, it was the rainy season; the road would be hot and stifling. If something happened to them, Yu Zhang would spend days and nights cursing him. Yu Zhang was Yu Ya’s father and the most protective of his cubs.

"We want to go."

* * *

Lin Qiu was helping to break up dry firewood, branches the orcs had gathered outside. On the stove, there were dried fish brought from Wolf Mountain. That would be dinner; if Lang Xiao and Lang Bei brought back food, they would save it for tomorrow.

Lang Yan stood up to help. He had great strength, so Lin Qiu gave him the wood he couldn't break. "Why did you say that, King? Are you really letting them go?"

Lang Yan said: "Cubs can't hide behind adult orcs forever. If there’s an opportunity for training, letting them go won't hurt."

Lang Yu heard him and chopped down with a knife, breaking a fish-length of dried meat into two. He laughed, "What if it were Lang Jin and the others?"

"If there are adult orcs following, it’s fine."

"The King really thinks of the Black Feather tribe." Always considering their training.

Lang Yan: "It's not certain that Yu Dan will agree."

Yu Dan didn't *want* to agree, but the cubs were persistent, and Lang Yan had said an adult orc could lead them... He looked at his own young ones. There were only seven cubs in total. Yu Le, and these six. Compared to the wolf tribe, they had far fewer.

The Black Feather tribe guarded them like the apples of their eyes. In the past, they were so spoiled they didn't know the immensity of heaven and earth—they even dared to steal salt. But they had been in the wolf tribe for a long time, and subconsciously, they couldn't help but compare the two groups.

The wolf tribe had two wolf cub teams—Lang Jin’s hunting team and Lang Bing’s gathering team. And even younger ones like Lang Sheng’s group. Even though they hadn't officially been split into teams yet, as outsiders, they could see that there were leaders among the cubs.

The wolf tribe’s teams were cultivated from a young age. When the cubs were small, they practiced hunting within the tribe, and once they reached a certain age, they were let out to explore.

But the Black Feather orcs? Before the salt-stealing incident, they never let them join in hunting; they kept them leashed for fear of injury. To wait for them to be capable like Lang Jin’s team, they would probably have to be full-grown adults.

Yu Dan couldn't help but wonder if they were too cautious.

* * *

When Yu Ya sought out Lang Yan again, Lang Yan was a bit surprised. He hadn't expected the overprotective Black Feather orcs to agree. This time, Yu Dan came with them, straight to the point: "Wolf King, how many young orcs do you plan to let go?"

Lang Yan: "That depends on how many you allow."

Before coming here, the cubs had already argued about who would go. Now, they followed their elder obediently, watching Lang Yan with expectant eyes. They all wanted to go. This was their first long trip; compared to traveling from Black Feather to the Wolf tribe, going as far as the branch tribe was real training, real exploration.

Yu Dan: "What if they all want to go?"

"If you agree, fine. Of course, you are responsible for their safety."

Yu Ya’s eyes brightened, and he hugged his companions. They were too excited to catch the implication in Lang Yan’s words.

Yu Dan was stunned. "We came here to work." Not to play. For the Feather clans, flying to deliver a message was an easy task; as long as they ate well, it was nothing.

Lang Yan: "This counts as work too."

If the Black Feather orcs didn't go, only their own orcs could. That would take longer and delay other things.

"Fine, we’ll go!" Yu Dan agreed.

Lang Yan said: "We brought enough dried fish. You can take it as rations for the road."

Yu Dan laughed. "It seems the Wolf King calculated everything beforehand." The dried fish had been brought from Wolf Mountain, and there was plenty. With fish plentiful in the Great Swamp, there was no need to bring so much.

Next, Lang Yan told them the markers for the road to prevent them from getting lost. With adult Black Feather orcs leading, he didn't worry about the cubs flying astray.

Once they had their orders, Yu Dan and the others gathered the cubs to go over the precautions.

After they left, Lang Yu asked: "Should we brew some herbal tea and give it to them?"

"Brew it. I'll go grind some medicine powder; the tea won't last a day without going sour," Lin Qiu said. If they were asking for help, they had to be prepared.

Lang Hong helped pack the dried fish while Lin Qiu prepared the herbs, grinding them into powder so they could be mixed with water later. By the time they ate in the evening, everything was ready. The Black Feather orcs slept, waiting for the rain to stop.

Beneath the wolf tribe’s shelter, the oil lamp flickered. Lin Qiu unwrapped the leaves containing Lang Xue’s tooth and frowned at the grain-sized item. It was hard to drill a hole in it. Last time, for Lang Sheng’s, Lang Qi had helped drill the hole.

The other orcs were asleep, and Lin Qiu and Lang Yan were busy studying how to drill a hole into the tiny thing. Without proper tools, they used the tip of a small knife to gently scrape back and forth. It was precision work.

Lin Qiu worked for a while until his eyes grew sore, and then Lang Yan took over. The two took turns, eyes straining, until they managed to carve out a tiny groove.

Lin Qiu rubbed his eyes, tears welling up from the strain. "Let's sleep first, we'll finish tomorrow."

Lang Yan put the tooth away and blew out the lamp.

They had just crawled into their nest when footsteps sounded in the rain. Every wolf orc in the shelter immediately became alert, eyes dark, staring outside.

The White Sparrow and Green Eye orcs, who were trying to approach the sleeping area quietly, hesitated, their feathers fluffing up slightly. They cautiously waved their wings at the wolf orcs.

Lang Yu lay back down.

The shelter echoed with the muffled sounds of orcs falling back into their nests.

Lin Qiu asked softly: "Have you eaten? There's dried fish by the stove."

The orcs from the two tribes smiled sheepishly at him, rubbing their bodies as if to shake off the chill they felt from being stared at by the wolf orcs. They hurried to the stove, divided the fish, and returned to their own shelter.

"Wolf orcs are really vigilant," Que Twelve whispered.

Que Erbai stood at the entrance, shaking his feathers. "They should be. Our tribe needs to learn that."

Que Twelve bit into a piece of fish and said slowly, "If our tribe were approached, Uncle Erbai would be the one sleeping the deepest."

Que Erbai whacked Twelve with his wing. "Is that any way to talk?!"

Que Twelve dodged skillfully, and Que Erbai’s wing ended up hitting Que Thirteen instead.

"Chirp!" Que Thirteen’s fish flew away, and he rushed out to chase it.

The White Sparrow tribe leader flicked his wing, sending the fish back to him. He glared at Que Erbai. "Enough! Eat, and get to sleep!"

Que Thirteen hugged his recovered fish, took a big bite, and mumbled, "Uncle Erbai is old enough to be stealing my fish!"

Que Erbai: "Who would want your fish?!"

*Who do you think you’re looking down on?!* He had eaten Sharp-horn beast, You-you beast, Curved-horn beast, Red bird, grilled fish...

*Gulp!* Que Erbai swallowed hard.

*Forget it, forget it.* He wasn't going to argue with a little fool!
chapters.title: 第163章

chapters.source_text:
翌日，雨小了。
羽单和另外三个成年兽人，带着羽涯他们离开了大泽。
这是羽涯第一次出远门，他背上背着兽皮袋，兴奋地带着队伍往前蹿去。
羽单几个成年兽人跟在后头，静静看着他们。
“单，连飞几天，他们不一定受得住。”
羽单眼睛一眯，巨大的羽翼抖落细密的雨珠，“他们自己选的，再累都要坚持下去。”
大泽。
林楸和狼岩一起送走了黑羽兽人。
只眨眼间，灰黑色的兽人们变成了几个黑点。
林楸道：“这事儿没告诉黑羽部落那边，到时候羽猎过来，没见到兽人……”
“走都走了，他们要担心，自己去追。”狼岩握住林楸手腕，看他头上沾满的细雨，把他往棚子底下带。
狼雨坐在草团上，盯着远处水面。
雨滴落下，水面一个接一个的小圈荡漾开。
“王，楸，咱们是不是得做雨具了？这雨一时半会儿不会停。”
林楸：“做。”
正好，从部落回来的白雀和绿眼兽人也休息够了，听说要干活，慢慢聚集起来。
狼兽人从狼山带了些麻线和晒干的大叶片，还有兔兽人做的蓑衣样品，供兽人们参考。
白雀兽人和绿眼兽人都是手巧的，翻看后，便自己拿来材料，去一旁坐着忙活。
斗笠需要竹篾编织成型，林楸还没在这地方见过竹子，只能用藤条或者柔软的枝条代替。
兽人们一起忙活着，还有一部分兽人继续做捞泥巴的工具，也不算耽搁事儿。
三个部落的兽人，本来分做三堆。
狼金挪了挪屁股，坐到白雀兽人堆里，胳膊肘碰了一下雀十二白道：“你们昨天怎么和绿眼兽人一起回来的？”
雀十二白：“碰巧遇到的。”
“那还真巧。”
“你们部落怎么样？”
“住的石林没事，其他地方都被烧了。”雀十二白声音低了些。
狼金还笑呵呵道：“那没办法了，你们只能给我们干活了。”
不远处，狼雨听着小狼说的话，闷笑两声。
“一点不会说话，也不怕招人家恨。”
林楸手上箍着斗笠，叹息道：“情商堪忧。”
亏得是已经玩在一起的朋友了，换个陌生一点的兽人，小狼说这话得挨打。
“白雀部落还能住，那绿眼部落……”
“烧完了。”绿月过来问林楸做斗笠，闻言轻声道。
林楸抬头，招呼他坐。
几个狼族亚兽人挪了挪位置，绿月就正好坐到林楸对面。
绿眼部落虽说现在做事积极，但与他们来往还是不多。他们只派代表来跟他们说话，比方说绿皎，还有他的伴侣绿月。
亚兽人们跟绿月要更熟悉些。
绿月的性子文静，也有主见，能扛事儿，做事不疾不徐，看着慢但上手快。
绿眼部落当中，也并不是所有兽人对狼兽人亲近。绿月不同，当初要不是狼星抢到他们部落来，他剩下这一个幼崽肯定活不了。
兽人也有私心，他们做不到狼部落这样绝对的团结，但至少面上看着还是齐心的。
下雨天，外面的活儿暂且停了。
直到两天后，手上的雨具做好，兽人们才又下水继续忙活。
今年雨季雨水少了些。
大泽往年这个时候已经涨水，差不多快要淹没到棚子这边，今年却没多少变化。
兽人们不关注这个，没涨水挺好，方便他们干活。
两个部落的兽人已经熟悉这水里的活儿，狼岩和林楸又跟了几天，狼岩便不让林楸下水了。
不用日夜颠倒，林楸有空就打磨幼崽的小牙，顺带跟着狼贝他们出去采集，找一找有没有漂亮的石头。
下了七八天的雨终于停了。
棚顶支出来的干草上，雨珠汇聚，啪嗒一下落在路过的小狼头顶上。
小狼摸摸脑袋，再看看棚顶，愤怒地把手一挥，直接将棚顶上一排的雨珠给拍下来。
然后左看右看，见一滴不剩，这才满意了，龇着个大牙花子继续往里走。
狼贝站在旁边，望了一眼天色。
她长得高大，长发利落地梳成马尾，英气又干练。
小狼正是长高的时候，瘦条条的，才到她下巴高。
小狼撞见她，道：“贝姨，队长问你今晚上还去不去捕猎？”
“不去了。”
“嗷，那我去跟队长说。”
兽人们晚上不适合做采集的活儿，他们一般都是跟小狼出去找猎物，遇到能吃的野菜就挖一些，要采集还是得白天。
狼贝打算早点出去，赶着早上没太阳的那一会儿采集完，立马回来。
第二天一早，林楸跟着他们一起，带着干粮就出发。
走的时候天还黑着，等到了目的地，路边的草丛上还挂着露珠。
他们到了东边的一处河滩。
河水浅，河床被晒得干涸了。下了那么多天的雨，也只汇聚出些水洼。
不过河边的野菜长得好，是下雨后新长出来的，正嫩，一掐就断。
亚兽人们到了地方，立刻分散开来。
能采集的时间就这一会儿，他们还得赶着太阳最烈之前回去，以免晒出问题。
林楸也低头掐野菜，还没掐到一把，狼贝道：“楸，你去河里找找河贝。”
林楸：“要吃吗？”
河贝腥气重，以前他爷奶家都是捡来剁碎了喂鸭子，鸭子长得很肥壮。
“你不是帮雪做项链，里面有珠子。”
林楸笑起来，把背篓放下，甩甩手上的露水。
“那我得看看。”
“河贝里的珠子也少，得海贝。楸可以多捡一点。”狼清补充道。
“好。”
河滩其实挺宽，有二三十米，因着才下过雨，边上的泥也是软的。
林楸捡了根棍子，试探着戳进去，不会陷人，才慢慢往下走。
河滩平，散落着少许乱石，主要还是堆积着些泥。
林楸往泥上看。
兽人们管河蚌叫河贝，这两个应该是一个东西。河贝的颜色是黑褐色，贝上一圈一圈的纹路，个头巨大。
林楸随手捡起泥上裸露出一半的贝壳，那贝壳如同一个瓢，他摆手摊开比了比，发现贝壳还要大些。
岸上有兽人喊道：“楸，露出来的都是空的，要捡藏在泥里的。”
林楸回头，“好！”
“找洞！一般泥上面会有个小洞，贝就藏在下面。”
兽人们一下想到了狼贝，都笑了起来。
狼贝也翘了下嘴角，身上斜挎着藤筐，两手唰唰掐野菜掐得飞快。
像兽人们说的，找准小洞，往下探不过二三厘米，就能触摸到一个硬硬的东西。
林楸渐渐熟练，一找一个准。
林楸抓紧时间，找到就扔在一处，等堆了差不多一筐的量，林楸上岸去拿背篓。
狼贝看了一眼，道：“楸，这个很重，就在这边破开。”
林楸一顿，“我还想着摘点野菜。”
“没事，我们兽人多，不差你一个。”
“行。”
林楸带了小刀来的，河贝里面不是都有珠子，兽人们又不吃这肉，带回去也是浪费体力。
这会儿有些热了，林楸鼻尖冒汗。
他直接找了块石头坐下，在河滩里取珠。
河贝大，每个都沉甸甸的。
林楸把小刀探入贝壳缝隙，还得使劲儿才插得进去，小刀沿着边缘割两下，再一拧就开了。
他开贝壳的动作快，不过找珠不熟练。
狼贝时刻注意着这边，叫狼清去帮忙。
狼清放下藤筐，利落跳下河岸。与狼贝一样的高马尾在空中晃动，随着主人微微摇晃。
“楸，你开贝壳，我来找。”
狼清往林楸旁边一坐，接过林楸手上的贝壳就开始忙活。
林楸笑起来，额间有汗，脸上泛着点红。
狼清看他一眼，道：“也不用这么赶，别伤了手。”
林楸：“没赶，就是太阳快出来了，有点热。”
林楸说着，手上不停。
两个兽人配合着，速度很快。
开了四五个，林楸都怀疑到底里面有没有了，狼清忽然道：“有了。”
狼清捏着珠子往水里一晃，摊开手给林楸看。
林楸一瞧，白色的珍珠并不那么圆，也不大，比黄豆还小些，但胜在珍贵。
林楸眉头舒展，“有就行。”
太阳渐渐出来，二十几个贝壳被林楸开完。得到的珍珠也只三颗，趁着还有点时间，狼清和林楸一起又找了些。
后头兽人们采集完，林楸以为大家要走了，结果他们也跟着跳到河滩上，一半帮忙找，一半帮忙开贝壳。
直到快把这一片河滩翻个底朝天，珍珠凑足了一小把，狼贝才下令回去。
回程路上，狼贝和林楸道：“明天再来。”
林楸：“应该够了。”
“还要挑一挑，有些不圆。”
林楸弯起嘴角，体会到了亚兽人们对幼崽的疼爱。虽然大伙儿嘴上不说，可对于幼崽的事，都用了心思。
他也只好应下。
这边离大泽不算远，若单是采集，兽人们一般不会走太远。
回程也幸亏是在林子里奔跑，不然林楸得中暑。
回到大泽，林楸觉得自己后背的狼毛烫得厉害，变成人形，才觉黑背的皮肤有些刺疼。
昨晚忙了一晚上的兽人在睡觉，大家放轻脚步，先将藤筐卸在林子里。
亚兽人们在棚子里趴下来，热得吐舌头喘气。
狼雨端来解暑的草药汤，一个兽人倒上一点儿，道：“专门给你们留着的，喝吧。”
亚兽人们屏息。
狼雨笑着，学着狼岩道：“要不然我喂。”
狼贝爪子推了他一下，张开嘴道：“来。”
“想得美。”狼雨放下碗道，“自己喝，反正难受的不是我。”
“我睡觉去了，你们要是饿了，陶锅里有鱼汤。”
大泽这边大部分兽人都是晚上干活，所以狼雨他们做饭也是早晚两顿，加上半夜一顿。
采集队今天白天出去的，中午也得吃，早上那一顿狼雨就做得多了些。
亚兽人们休息好了，先去湖边冲洗一下身上的汗，随后去吃饭。
吃得半饱，就回草窝里睡觉。
林楸不着急睡，他先去把带回来的珠子洗干净，把圆润的先选出来。
其他形状不好的暂且留着，要是最后圆的找不到那么多，就把这些打磨一下，一样能用。
洗干净手，林楸压着步子，靠近棚子角落。
草窝里，狼岩睡熟了。
林楸没进去，而是在草窝旁边的草团上坐下来。
林楸手臂搭在草窝边缘，下巴枕在手臂上，静静看着狼岩出神。
草窝大，狼岩侧对着林楸这边睡的。
林楸一来他就察觉到了，只是太困，没睁眼，而是将手探出去。
直到抓到自家伴侣的手，他才放任自己意识沉落。
林楸轻轻打了个哈欠，眼里溢出水雾。
他目光从交握的手上，缓缓移到狼岩脸上。
黑了，好像也瘦了点。
本就流畅的下颌线愈发收紧，骨相更是突出，本就俊气的脸愈发帅气逼人。
林楸勾了勾紧握他的手，摩挲着他手心的厚茧。
不过他还是黏人，和狼王霸气的形象一点不相符。
最近忙，林楸也没了睡午觉的习惯。只趴在草窝边眯了一会儿，便轻轻松开狼岩的手，起身出去。
下次回去前，他得把幼崽的小项链做好。
现在小米牙还没钻出孔，更别说还有那几十颗排队等着的珍珠。
趁着没别的事，他先忙一会儿。
雨季已经过半，最热的时候当属那连续半个多月的晴日。经历了那一阵，林楸都觉得其他时候没那么热了。
大泽广袤，湖水碧绿。
近岸旁的水面上垒起田地，方方正正的，一直往湖心岛那边延伸。
候鸟的幼崽已经养大了，那场山火后，走了一批，如今剩下的不多。
这会儿大泽里没兽人，它们便落在那淤泥上，踩出一串细长的爪印，翻找着泥里的小虫和鱼虾。
林楸坐在灶台那边的棚子里，一边看着，一边打磨手上的小牙，感受着这一时的静谧。
要是天气再好点，不那么热，应该会更舒服。
忙了一会儿，林楸靠着柱子，揉着发酸的手腕。他目光远眺，掠过大泽，一直到那水天相接的尽头。
这场山火熄了，但不知道那边葡萄园怎么样？
那葡萄是好东西，林楸还打算每年都酿些葡萄酒，烧没了可惜。
云朵柔软，飘到阳光下，天一下暗了些。
林楸收回目光，打算继续打磨，就看狼岩从棚子最里面走出来。
林楸弯眼，目光追着他。
狼岩也笑起来，脚步忍不住加快，蹲在林楸面前。
他俩就这么互相看着，林楸歪了歪头，噗嗤笑出声，额头抵着他肩膀。
“像两个傻子。”
狼岩揉了揉他的头发，手掌滑落，贴在林楸后颈。摸着一手湿汗，他拢起那一头长发，轻轻捏住。
“下次羽猎过来，叫他往这边送些硝石。”
“人家部落里有的都被你薅尽了。”
林楸一抬头，脸颊被狼岩轻轻咬住。他笑着偏头，无奈道：“哪有你这样的。”
动不动就咬，牙痒痒吗？
幼崽都不这样了。
狼岩起身，找了把扇子过来，坐在林楸旁边给他扇风。
兽人们都还没醒，林楸低头又认真打磨起来。
狼岩守着他，瞧着那些珠子，明白过来他上午干什么去了。
“海里的更漂亮。”
“你见过？”
“嗯。”
狼部落位置不靠海边，部落里大多兽人甚至从来没有去过海边。
以前集市还开着时，南部的集市就是在海上。
那边居住的兽人就会采集珍珠，用来跟其他兽人交换东西。
亚兽人和雌性兽人爱美，喜欢用珍珠做饰品。有些雄性兽人也会给自己伴侣或者喜欢的兽人交换珍珠。
狼岩还记得，部落以前有些阿叔们还是有珍珠饰品的。
且不只是白色，还有粉色、黑色。颜色越奇特的，越是珍贵。
在兽人们富裕时，一颗好的白色海珠，能换半头咩咩兽。一颗粉色的，能换一头咩咩兽。
林楸听他说着珍珠的事，手酸了，往他身上一靠，两手往他掌心一搭，道：“珍珠在海底，兽人们潜水下去？”
这必然会有伤亡，比起陶罐能换弯角兽，珍珠好像又显得不那么珍贵了。
“有海洋兽人。”狼岩捏着林楸手腕道。
“人鱼！”
林楸下巴抵着他肩，双眼泛着光。
说实话，他很感兴趣。
狼岩下颌慢慢绷紧，林楸嘴角悄悄上扬，伸手挠了挠狼岩下巴。
“王啊，你的醋劲儿真的好大。”
狼岩听不懂什么是醋劲儿，但他还听不出林楸话里的调侃吗？
狼岩低头，咬了一下林楸鼻尖。
“虽然有些海洋种族是很好看，但一股海腥味。”
林楸闷头在他肩膀上闷笑，“你这是歧视。”
狼岩：“我说的事实。”
林楸才不信他现在会说什么事实。
那股酸味儿都呛人了。
笑够了，林楸没了力气，软了骨头趴在狼岩身上。
狼岩再也不提那什么海洋兽人了，而是当个支架，一边给林楸揉手腕，一边给他扇风。
等到林楸缓过来，坐直了，这话题就这么飘了过去。
过了会儿，林楸手上打磨的小牙换到了狼岩手上。他靠着狼岩，看着那新挖出来的淤泥上找食的鸟发呆。
看着看着，天边一个黑点闯入他视线中。
林楸还以为是黑羽兽人回来了，刚一坐直，狼岩看了一眼道：“是羽猎。”
羽猎过来的动静把其他狼兽人惊醒，不过他们也只看了一眼，又倒草窝里去了。
羽猎收拢翅膀，一下就化为人形。他看林楸和狼岩都在棚子底下，三步并作两步，走了过来。
“楸！狼王！你们怎么跑到这边来了？”
狼岩：“过来送猎物？”
“送了，不过不是送弯角兽。我们北边也下来一群咩咩兽，两头咩咩兽抵一头弯角兽行不行？”
“当然可以。”林楸道。
羽猎知道他俩都可以做部落的主，早预料到了他们会同意，这会儿也是笑呵呵的。
林楸看他精神面貌与之前有些不同，笑问：“遇到什么好事了？”
羽猎：“那不就是北边下来的咩咩兽群嘛。”
他们以前捕猎不往北边走，那边什么都没有，只有荒漠和草原。
也是知道狼部落从北边抓了不少咩咩兽，所以这次山火后，不得已翻遍了整个部落领地，连北边也去了。没想到运气不差，让他们找到了猎物。
“楸，我能问问，你们部落的咩咩兽怎么养的吗？”
林楸看了眼狼岩。
狼岩：“可以。”
林楸：“那你得回去找溶，他知道得多。”
“成。”羽猎声音雀跃，高兴得就差一蹦而起，往天空飞两圈。
激动过后，看狼岩和林楸还坐那儿搓搓搓，往前挪了挪，站在大太阳底下扭扭捏捏道：
“还、还有一件事。”
狼岩：“想问原野部落？”
“诶！不愧是狼王，我就知道……”
林楸瞧着他满头大汗，道：“你要不进棚子里面来？”
“不用不用，我问了就走。”
“不吃一顿？”
“可、可以吗？”
狼雨哼笑一声，趴在矮墙上冲他道：“你还吃得少了？”
“嘿……”羽猎往棚子里走，挠挠头道，“我那不是听莫他们说，这边没啥吃的。”
狼雨：“哦……想吃好的。”
“没有没有没有！”羽猎飞快摇着脑袋。
狼雨：“行了，晚上吃长虫，也不差的。”
狼雨这边逗完了兽人，溜溜达达走到灶台这边，差不多要开始准备晚饭了。
羽猎想起正事儿，又急匆匆看向狼岩。
“狼王，原野部落……自从乔帮忙那次之后，再没来过了。”
现在离雨季结束不到两个月，该来的早来了，难不成嫌雨季热，等收获季来？
“他们暂时应该不会来了。”
羽猎精神一振，忙道：“真的？！”
他激动得脸皮都有点抽搐，硬是按耐住，双手抓着自己的兽皮裙，捏得青筋暴起。
要是他们真的不来，黑羽部落的兽人岂不是再也不用担心随时没命了。只要他们跟着狼部落一起发展，总有一天，他们也能吃肉吃饱。
狼岩：“别这么激动，只是猜想。”
“狐弦是个心眼小的，他既然决定了灭了黑羽部落，一次两次没成功，也不会罢休……”
狼岩说着，一边还在打磨小牙。
林楸看着羽猎，兽人眼眶通红，一改前一秒的喜悦，牙齿咬得咯吱响，都快碎了。
“他们雪季都能来，雨季也定然不怕。至于为什么不来……”狼岩看了一眼羽猎，心里有些沉，“他们怕是知道我们狼部落插手了。”
羽猎瞳孔一缩。
“我们……把你们牵连进来了。”
“也不算，前面一次帮你们，是互惠互利。后头一次帮你们，也是碰巧。”
“那还不是一样。”
“笨！王没把你们当陌生兽人才这么说！”灶台边，狼雨的话慢慢飘过来。
羽猎意识到自家部落被狼部落当成亲近部落那一刻，心中狂喜。那喜悦甚至压住了对原野部落的惶恐。
“谢、谢谢狼王。”他干巴巴道。
狼雨：“傻了。”
林楸回头看狼雨一眼，眼中带着无奈的笑。
狼雨摆摆手，“不说了，我不说了。”
他嘀嘀咕咕：“羽族脑子小，不聪明，我不多说点，他懂不起。”
林楸看向面前这个年轻的黑羽兽人，就这么一会儿，经历几次情绪起伏，面皮有些扭曲，似笑非笑，似哭非哭。
林楸看一眼自家王，说不清他刚刚到底是不是在逗弄兽人。
他道：“原野部落把我们当做了同盟，顾忌狼部落，不会轻易再过来。但你们也要警惕起来，趁着有限的时间赶紧发展部落。”
“我们会的！”
狼岩：“羽单那一队黑羽兽人我派出去给支部落送信了。”
“嗯？”
狼岩话题跳得太快，羽猎没反应过来。
狼岩道：“我们部落要做弓箭，缺少材料，你们帮忙收集一些？”
“当然可以！”
“行，你反正要回狼山的，去问问狼起，他告诉你收集哪些。”
“好！”
林楸看他这么听话，跟自家狼兽人面对狼岩一样。
有些奇怪？
但按照目前两个部落的关系，好像又正常。
林楸怕他现在有点懵，没听清楚，道：“羽涯他们去支部落了。”
“去！让他们去，我们族长说了，你们说什么都成。”
他们还欠狼部落一个要求，狼岩还没说呢。现在知道狼部落被他们牵连，兴许也被原野部落惦记上了，欠得就更多了。
羽猎对狼部落的感激不知道怎么回报，但他知道，狼部落做事有分寸，小兽人在这边也是锻炼。
他乐意，他们族长也乐意。
林楸点点头，看来黑羽兽人对他们的信任也有点深啊。

**Chapter 164**

The next day, the rain lightened.

Yu Dan, along with three other adult beastmen, led Yu Ya and his group away from the Great Marsh.

This was Yu Ya’s first time traveling far from home. He had a beast-skin bag strapped to his back, and he bounced forward in excitement, leading the way. The adult beastmen followed behind, watching them quietly.

"Dan, they’ve been flying for days. They might not be able to hold up."

Yu Dan narrowed his eyes, his massive wings shaking off fine droplets of rain. "They chose this themselves. No matter how tired they are, they have to keep going."

***

Back at the Great Marsh, Lin Qiu and Lang Yan watched as the Black Feather beastmen departed. In the blink of an eye, the dark-feathered figures had dwindled into tiny specks.

Lin Qiu remarked, "We didn't tell the Black Feather tribe about this. If Yu Lie comes by later and doesn't see them..."

"They’ve already left. If they're worried, they can go chase after them themselves." Lang Yan took Lin Qiu’s wrist, noticing the fine rain clinging to his hair, and guided him under the shelter.

Lang Yu sat on a grass mat, staring at the distant water. As the raindrops fell, tiny ripples spread out across the surface one after another.

"King, Qiu, do we need to start making rain gear? This rain doesn’t look like it’s going to stop anytime soon."

Lin Qiu: "Let’s make some."

It just so happened that the White Sparrow and Green-Eyed beastmen who had returned from the tribe were well-rested. Hearing that there was work to be done, they slowly gathered together.

The Wolf beastmen brought hemp thread and dried large leaves from Wolf Mountain, as well as the sample straw raincoat made by the Rabbit beastmen, to serve as a reference. The White Sparrow and Green-Eyed beastmen were dexterous; after examining the samples, they picked up materials and sat down to start working.

Conical hats needed bamboo strips to hold their shape. Since Lin Qiu hadn't seen any bamboo in this area, he had to use vines or flexible branches instead. The beastmen worked together, and those not making gear continued working on tools for scooping mud, so nothing was delayed.

The beastmen from the three tribes were originally sitting in three separate groups. Lang Jin shifted his seat to move into the White Sparrow group, nudging Que Shi'erbai with his elbow: "How did you end up coming back with the Green-Eyed beastmen yesterday?"

Que Shi'erbai: "We just happened to bump into each other."

"That’s quite a coincidence."

"How is your tribe?"

"The Stone Forest where we live is fine, but everywhere else was burned," Que Shi'erbai said in a lower voice.

Lang Jin laughed heartily: "Nothing to be done about that. I guess you’ll just have to work for us then."

Not far away, Lang Yu heard what the young wolf said and muffled a laugh. "He has no tact at all. He's not even afraid of making enemies."

Lin Qiu, busy fastening a hat, sighed: "His social intelligence is truly worrying."

It was fortunate that they were already friendly acquaintances. If he had said that to a stranger, the young wolf would have been beaten.

"The White Sparrow tribe is still habitable, but the Green-Eyed tribe..."

"It’s completely burned," Green Moon said, having walked over to ask Lin Qiu about the hat.

Lin Qiu looked up and gestured for him to sit. A few Wolf-tribe demi-beastmen shifted, allowing Green Moon to sit right across from Lin Qiu. Although the Green-Eyed tribe was proactive in their work, they didn't interact much with the others, usually only sending representatives like Green Jiao or his partner, Green Moon.

The demi-beastmen were more familiar with Green Moon. He was quiet by nature but had his own ideas, could shoulder burdens, and worked at a steady pace—slow to the eye, but quick to pick up new skills.

Not all Green-Eyed beastmen were close to the Wolf tribe, but Green Moon was different. If Lang Xing hadn’t snatched him into their tribe back then, his last remaining cub wouldn't have survived. Beastmen could be selfish; they couldn't achieve the absolute unity of the Wolf tribe, but at least on the surface, they were working as one.

Because of the rain, outdoor work was paused. It wasn't until two days later, once the rain gear was finished, that the beastmen returned to the water to continue their work.

The rainfall this rainy season had been lighter. In past years, the water in the Great Marsh would have already risen high enough to flood the area near the shelters, but this year, it hadn't changed much. The beastmen didn't pay it much mind—no rising water was a good thing; it made their work easier.

The beastmen from the two tribes were already familiar with the water work. After Lang Yan and Lin Qiu joined them for a few days, Lang Yan told Lin Qiu not to go into the water anymore.

No longer needing to work day and night, Lin Qiu spent his time polishing the cub's little teeth, or tagging along with Lang Bei and the others to forage, looking for pretty stones.

***

The seven or eight days of rain finally stopped.

Raindrops gathered on the dry grass extending from the roof, *plop*, landing on the head of a passing little wolf. The little wolf touched his head, glared at the roof, and angrily swiped his hand, knocking down the entire row of remaining raindrops. Only after looking left and right to ensure none were left did he walk on, baring his little teeth in satisfaction.

Lang Bei stood nearby, looking at the sky. She was tall, her long hair neatly tied into a ponytail, looking capable and heroic. The little wolf was currently going through a growth spurt, lean and lanky, only reaching her chin.

The little wolf bumped into her: "Aunt Bei, the captain wants to know if you're still going hunting tonight?"

"Not tonight."

"Oh, then I’ll go tell the captain."

Beastmen weren't suited for foraging at night; they usually went out with the little wolves to look for prey and would dig up edible wild vegetables if they found them, but the best time for gathering was during the day. Lang Bei planned to head out early, finish gathering before the sun got too hot, and return immediately.

The next morning, Lin Qiu joined them, setting off with dry rations. It was still dark when they left, and by the time they reached their destination, dew still hung on the grass along the path.

They arrived at a river beach on the east side. The water was shallow, and the riverbed had dried out. Even after so many days of rain, only a few small puddles remained. However, the wild vegetables along the bank grew well—fresh and tender, breaking with a single pinch.

The demi-beastmen scattered as soon as they arrived. They only had a short window to forage before they had to return to avoid the scorching sun.

Lin Qiu also began pinching vegetables. Before he could even fill a handful, Lang Bei said, "Qiu, go to the river and look for river clams."

Lin Qiu: "Are we going to eat them?"

River clams had a strong fishy smell. Back at his grandparents' house, they used to chop them up to feed the ducks, which made the ducks grow very plump.

"You’re helping Xue make a necklace, right? It needs beads."

Lin Qiu laughed, put down his basket, and shook the dew off his hands. "Then I should take a look."

"There aren't many pearls in river clams; you need sea clams for that. Qiu, you should pick a few more," Lang Qing added.

"Alright."

The river beach was quite wide, twenty or thirty meters across. Because it had just rained, the mud along the edge was soft. Lin Qiu picked up a stick and probed it into the mud; since it didn't sink in, he slowly walked down.

The beach was flat, scattered with a few loose rocks, but mostly accumulated mud. Lin Qiu looked at the mud. The beastmen called river mussels "river clams." They were dark brown, with circular rings on their shells, and were quite large.

Lin Qiu picked up a shell half-exposed in the mud. It looked like a scoop. He held his palm out to compare, finding the shell was even larger.

A beastman on the bank shouted: "Qiu! The ones exposed are all empty! You have to look for the ones buried in the mud!"

Lin Qiu turned back: "Okay!"

"Look for holes! Usually, there's a little hole on top of the mud, and the clam is hiding underneath."

The beastmen immediately thought of Lang Bei and laughed. Lang Bei also curled the corner of her mouth, a vine basket slung across her body, her hands moving quickly as she pinched vegetables.

Just as the beastmen said, once he targeted a small hole and poked down just two or three centimeters, he could feel something hard. Lin Qiu gradually became skilled, finding one every time. He worked quickly, piling them up, and when he had about a basket’s worth, he went up to the bank to grab his container.

Lang Bei took a look: "Qiu, these are very heavy. Just break them open here."

Lin Qiu paused: "I was thinking of picking some more vegetables."

"It's fine. We have plenty of beastmen, we don't miss one person."

"Alright."

Lin Qiu had brought a small knife. Not every river clam had a pearl, and since the beastmen didn't eat this meat, carrying it back would be a waste of energy. It was getting hot, and beads of sweat popped up on Lin Qiu's nose. He found a stone and sat down to extract the pearls.

The clams were large and heavy. Lin Qiu inserted his small knife into the gap of the shell—it took some force to wedge it in—sliced along the edge, and gave it a twist to pop it open. He was fast at opening them but not skilled at finding the pearls.

Lang Bei, keeping an eye on him, called for Lang Qing to help. Lang Qing put down her basket and nimbly jumped off the bank. Her ponytail swayed in the air as she moved.

"Qiu, you open the shells, I'll look."

Lang Qing sat down beside him, took a shell from him, and began working. Lin Qiu laughed, his forehead damp with sweat, his face flushed.

Lang Qing glanced at him: "No need to rush. Don't hurt your hands."

Lin Qiu: "I'm not rushing, it's just getting hot now that the sun is coming out."

Lin Qiu continued working without stopping. The two worked in tandem, and their speed was fast. After opening four or five, Lin Qiu began to doubt if there were any inside at all, when Lang Qing suddenly said, "Found one."

Lang Qing dipped the pearl into the water to rinse it and opened her hand to show Lin Qiu. He took a look—the white pearl wasn't perfectly round, nor was it large, smaller even than a soybean, but its value lay in its rarity.

Lin Qiu’s brows relaxed. "As long as there are some, that's enough."

As the sun climbed higher, Lin Qiu finished opening over twenty shells. They had only found three pearls. Taking advantage of the remaining time, Lang Qing and Lin Qiu searched for more. When the other beastmen finished foraging, Lin Qiu thought they were leaving, but instead, they jumped onto the river beach, half of them helping to search and half helping to open shells.

It wasn't until they had practically turned the entire beach upside down and gathered a small handful of pearls that Lang Bei ordered them to return.

On the way back, Lang Bei told Lin Qiu: "Come back tomorrow."

Lin Qiu: "That should be enough."

"We need to pick through them; some aren't round."

Lin Qiu curled the corners of his mouth, feeling the love the demi-beastmen had for the cubs. Even if they didn't say it, they poured their hearts into everything concerning the little ones. He had no choice but to agree.

They weren't far from the Great Marsh; if they were just foraging, the beastmen usually wouldn't travel too far. Luckily, the journey back was through the forest, or Lin Qiu would have suffered from heatstroke.

When they returned to the Great Marsh, Lin Qiu felt the wolf fur on his back burning hot. He shifted back to his human form and felt his skin prickling with pain. The beastmen who had been busy all night were now sleeping, so everyone walked lightly and left their baskets in the woods.

The demi-beastmen collapsed in the shelter, panting with their tongues out from the heat. Lang Yu brought over a cooling herbal soup, pouring a little for each one. "Left this just for you all. Drink."

The demi-beastmen held their breath. Lang Yu smiled and, mimicking Lang Yan, said, "Or I could feed you."

Lang Bei swatted at him and opened her mouth: "Come on."

"In your dreams," Lang Yu said, putting the bowl down. "Drink it yourself. I’m not the one suffering. I'm going to sleep. If you're hungry, there's fish soup in the clay pot."

Most of the beastmen at the Great Marsh worked at night, so they usually cooked three meals: two morning/evening ones and one in the middle of the night. Lang Yu had cooked extra for the foragers who went out during the day.

Once they were rested, the demi-beastmen went to the lake to wash off their sweat before eating. After a half-meal, they returned to their grass nests to sleep.

Lin Qiu wasn't in a hurry to sleep. He washed the pearls he brought back and picked out the round ones. He set aside the ones with irregular shapes for now—if he couldn't find enough round ones later, he would polish those down; they would work just as well.

After washing his hands, Lin Qiu stepped softly toward the corner of the shelter.

In the grass nest, Lang Yan was fast asleep. Lin Qiu didn't go in but sat on a grass mat beside the nest, resting his arms on the edge and pillowing his chin on them, watching Lang Yan in a daze.

The nest was large, and Lang Yan was sleeping on his side, facing Lin Qiu. He sensed Lin Qiu’s arrival the moment he sat down, but he was too tired to open his eyes; instead, he reached a hand out. He didn't relax his consciousness until he caught his partner's hand.

Lin Qiu let out a soft yawn, his eyes brimming with mist. He shifted his gaze from their clasped hands to Lang Yan's face. He had gotten darker, and it seemed he had lost a bit of weight. His already sharp jawline was even tighter, and his features were even more prominent, making his already handsome face look breathtaking.

Lin Qiu tugged at the hand holding his, caressing the thick calluses on his palm. Yet, he remained as clingy as ever, which didn't fit his image as a fearsome Wolf King at all.

Because he’d been busy lately, Lin Qiu had lost the habit of napping. He dozed by the nest for a while, then gently released Lang Yan’s hand and stood up to head outside. Before they left next time, he had to finish that little necklace. The cub's teeth weren't ready yet, let alone the dozens of pearls waiting in line.

Since there was nothing else to do, he would work for a while.

The rainy season was already more than halfway over, and the heat was nowhere near as intense as those two weeks of continuous, burning sunshine. After experiencing that, Lin Qiu felt that other times weren't all that hot anymore.

The Great Marsh was vast, its lake water a deep green. Near the shore, fields were built on the water, square and tidy, stretching toward the island in the center of the lake. The migratory birds' cubs had grown up; after that forest fire, many had left, and few remained. With no beastmen around the marsh for the moment, they landed on the silt, leaving long trails of claw prints as they foraged for bugs and small fish.

Lin Qiu sat in the shed by the stove, watching them while polishing the little teeth, enjoying this moment of quiet. If the weather were just a bit cooler, it would be even better.

After a while, Lin Qiu leaned against a pillar, rubbing his sore wrists. He looked out past the Great Marsh to the horizon where the water met the sky.

The forest fire had been extinguished, but he wondered how the vineyard was doing. Those grapes were good things; Lin Qiu had planned to make wine every year, and it would be a shame if they were burned.

The clouds were soft, drifting under the sun, and the sky dimmed slightly. Lin Qiu withdrew his gaze, planning to continue polishing, when he saw Lang Yan walk out from the back of the shed.

Lin Qiu’s eyes curved, his gaze following him.

Lang Yan also smiled, unable to help but quicken his pace, crouching in front of Lin Qiu. The two just looked at each other like that. Lin Qiu tilted his head and let out a chuckle, pressing his forehead against Lang Yan’s shoulder.

"We look like two idiots."

Lang Yan ruffled his hair, his palm sliding down to rest on the nape of Lin Qiu’s neck. Feeling the damp sweat, he gathered up that long hair and squeezed it gently.

"When Yu Lie comes by next time, I’ll tell him to send some saltpeter this way."

"The stuff they had in their tribe has already been picked clean by you."

Lin Qiu looked up, and his cheek was lightly bitten by Lang Yan. He tilted his head away with a smile, saying helplessly, "Is there anyone else like you?"

He bit him whenever he felt like it—were his teeth itchy? Even the cubs didn't do that anymore.

Lang Yan stood up, found a fan, and sat next to Lin Qiu, fanning him. The other beastmen hadn't woken up yet. Lin Qiu bowed his head and began polishing again with concentration. Lang Yan watched him, looking at the pearls, and realized what he had been doing all morning.

"The ones in the sea are prettier."

"You’ve seen them?"

"Mn."

The Wolf tribe's territory wasn't near the sea; most of the beastmen in the tribe had never even been to the coast. Back when the market was still open, the southern market had been on the sea. Beastmen living there would harvest pearls to trade with others. Demi-beastmen and female beastmen loved beauty and liked using pearls for jewelry, and some male beastmen would trade for pearls for their partners or someone they liked.

Lang Yan still remembered that some of the older uncles in the tribe had pearl jewelry. And they weren't just white; there were pink and black ones too. The more unique the color, the more precious they were. Back when the beastmen were wealthy, a good white sea pearl could be traded for half a Me-Me beast. A pink one could trade for a whole one.

Lin Qiu listened to him talk about the pearls, his hands aching, so he leaned against him and rested his palms in Lang Yan's, saying, "Pearls are at the bottom of the sea; do the beastmen dive down for them?"

There must be casualties. Compared to clay pots that could trade for a Bighorn beast, pearls didn't seem quite as valuable.

"There are Ocean beastmen," Lang Yan said, squeezing Lin Qiu’s wrist.

"Merpeople!"

Lin Qiu rested his chin on Lang Yan’s shoulder, his eyes sparkling. Honestly, he was very interested.

Lang Yan’s jaw slowly tightened. Lin Qiu felt the corners of his mouth rise and reached out to scratch Lang Yan's chin.

"Oh, King, you’re really very jealous."

Lang Yan didn't understand what "jealousy" meant, but he could certainly tell when Lin Qiu was teasing him. He lowered his head and bit the tip of Lin Qiu’s nose. "Although some ocean tribes are very good-looking, they smell like fish."

Lin Qiu laughed into his shoulder, "That’s discrimination."

Lang Yan: "I’m stating facts."

Lin Qiu didn't believe a word of his "facts." That sour, jealous scent was almost choking.

After enough laughing, Lin Qiu lost his strength and went limp, hanging on Lang Yan. Lang Yan never mentioned those Ocean beastmen again, instead acting as a support, rubbing Lin Qiu’s wrists while fanning him. By the time Lin Qiu recovered and sat up straight, the topic had drifted away.

After a while, Lin Qiu traded the little teeth he was polishing for Lang Yan's hands. He leaned against him, staring blankly at the birds foraging in the newly turned mud. While watching, a black dot entered his field of vision.

Lin Qiu thought the Black Feather beastmen had returned, but just as he sat up straight, Lang Yan took a look and said, "It’s Yu Lie."

The commotion of Yu Lie’s arrival woke the other Wolf beastmen, but they only took one look before collapsing back into their grass nests.

Yu Lie folded his wings and immediately shifted into his human form. Seeing Lin Qiu and Lang Yan sitting under the shelter, he walked over in three long strides.

"Qiu! Wolf King! Why did you come over here?"

Lang Yan: "Here to deliver prey?"

"Delivered, but not Bighorn beasts. A herd of Me-Me beasts came down from the north. Would two Me-Me beasts for one Bighorn be okay?"

"Of course," Lin Qiu said.

Yu Lie knew that both of them could make decisions for the tribe, and he had expected them to agree, so he was all smiles. Seeing that his spirit was different than before, Lin Qiu asked with a smile: "What good news did you run into?"

Yu Lie: "It’s just that herd of Me-Me beasts from the north."

They didn't usually hunt north, as there was nothing there but deserts and grasslands. But knowing the Wolf tribe had caught many Me-Me beasts from the north, they had no choice after the forest fire and searched their entire territory, even heading north. Luckily, they weren't unlucky and had found prey.

"Qiu, can I ask, how does your tribe raise Me-Me beasts?"

Lin Qiu glanced at Lang Yan.

Lang Yan: "You can."

Lin Qiu: "Then you have to go back and find Rong; he knows more about it."

"Deal." Yu Lie's voice was bright; he was so happy he could have jumped up and flown two circles in the sky.

After the excitement passed, seeing Lang Yan and Lin Qiu still sitting there polishing, he shuffled forward a bit, standing under the scorching sun, fidgeting: "Also... there is one more thing."

Lang Yan: "Want to ask about the Wilderness tribe?"

"Hey! As expected of the Wolf King, I knew..."

Lin Qiu saw him drenched in sweat and said, "Why don't you come inside the shelter?"

"No, no, I'll just ask and go."

"Not staying for a meal?"

"Can... can I?"

Lang Yu snorted, leaning over the low wall to mock him: "You haven't eaten enough?"

"Heh..." Yu Lie walked into the shelter, scratching his head. "I didn't hear what Mo and the others said, that there was nothing to eat here."

Lang Yu: "Oh... wanting to eat well."

"No, no, no!" Yu Lie shook his head rapidly.

Lang Yu: "Fine. We’re eating long-worms tonight, they’re not bad."

After teasing the beastman, Lang Yu strolled over to the stove; it was almost time to start dinner. Yu Lie remembered his real purpose and hurriedly looked back at Lang Yan.

"Wolf King, the Wilderness tribe... ever since that time Qiao helped, they haven't come back."

There were less than two months left until the end of the rainy season. Anyone who was coming would have already arrived. Was it possible they disliked the heat of the rainy season and would wait for the harvest season?

"They likely won't come for now."

Yu Lie’s spirits lifted, and he quickly asked, "Really?!"

He was so excited his face twitched, but he forced himself to hold back, his hands gripping his beast-skin skirt until his veins stood out. If they really didn't come back, the Black Feather beastmen wouldn't have to worry about losing their lives at any moment. As long as they continued to develop with the Wolf tribe, one day, they would be able to eat their fill of meat.

Lang Yan: "Don't get too excited, it's just a guess."

"Hu Xian is small-minded. Since he decided to destroy the Black Feather tribe, and hasn't succeeded after one or two tries, he won't give up easily..."

As Lang Yan spoke, he continued to polish the little teeth. Lin Qiu looked at Yu Lie; the beastman's eyes were bloodshot, and the joy from a second ago had vanished, replaced by his teeth grinding so hard it sounded like they were about to crack.

"They can come during the snow season, so they certainly won't fear the rainy season. As for why they aren't coming..." Lang Yan glanced at Yu Lie, his heart sinking. "They likely know the Wolf tribe has intervened."

Yu Lie’s pupils shrank.

"We... we’ve dragged you into this."

"Not necessarily. The first time we helped you was for mutual benefit. The second time was just a coincidence."

"That’s the same thing."

"Stupid! The King wouldn't have said that if he thought of you as strangers!" Lang Yu’s voice drifted over from the stove.

The moment Yu Lie realized his tribe was being treated as kin by the Wolf tribe, a surge of wild joy flooded his heart. That joy even suppressed his fear of the Wilderness tribe.

"Th-thank you, Wolf King," he said dryly.

Lang Yu: "He’s gone stupid."

Lin Qiu looked back at Lang Yu, a helpless smile in his eyes. Lang Yu waved his hand: "I’m not saying anything, I’m not saying anything." He muttered to himself: "Feather tribe brains are small and not smart; if I don't say more, he won't understand."

Lin Qiu looked at the young Black Feather beastman in front of him. In such a short time, he had experienced several emotional ups and downs, his face contorted—half-laughing, half-crying. Lin Qiu looked at his King, unable to tell if he had just been teasing the beastman.

He said: "The Wilderness tribe regards us as an alliance; fearing the Wolf tribe, they won't easily come again. But you must stay vigilant and take advantage of the limited time to develop your tribe."

"We will!"

Lang Yan: "I’ve sent Yu Dan’s team of Black Feather beastmen to deliver a message to the branch tribe."

"Huh?"

Lang Yan had changed the subject too quickly; Yu Lie didn't react.

Lang Yan said: "Our tribe wants to make bows and arrows but lacks materials. Can you help us collect some?"

"Of course!"

"Alright. You're going back to Wolf Mountain anyway, go ask Lang Qi, he’ll tell you what to collect."

"Good!"

Lin Qiu watched him listen so obediently, just like their own Wolf beastmen did with Lang Yan. Was it a bit strange? But given the current relationship between the two tribes, it also seemed normal.

Lin Qiu was afraid he might be a bit dazed and hadn't heard clearly, so he added: "Yu Ya and the others have gone to the branch tribe."

"Let them go! Let them go! Our Chief said whatever you say is fine."

They still owed the Wolf tribe a favor that Lang Yan hadn't requested yet. Now that he knew the Wolf tribe had been dragged in by them and might be on the Wilderness tribe’s radar too, they owed them even more.

Yu Lie didn't know how to repay his gratitude to the Wolf tribe, but he knew that the Wolf tribe did things with a sense of proportion, and having the little beastmen here was good training. He was willing, and their Chief was willing.

Lin Qiu nodded; it seemed the Black Feather beastmen’s trust in them ran quite deep.
chapters.title: 第164章

chapters.source_text:
羽涯他们去支部落送消息，一来一回一共八天，比羽涯自己预估的时间足足少了一半。
黑羽兽人刚落在大泽岸边，就被狼雨送了一大碗熬煮得近乎发黑的草药汁。
林楸看兽人们萎靡，但眼神清亮，应该只是累了，没有生病。
“路上没遇到什么事儿吧？”
羽涯两眼迷离地摇头，被同伴给了一肘子。
羽涯一痛，一下灌了一大口草药汤，瘪嘴苦脸道：“有……有个棕熊部落跟我们问路，要找你们。”
“棕熊部落……”林楸喃喃，他好像有那么点印象，“是支部落北部那个？”
“我们不知道，是半路遇到他们的，担心出问题，我们话都没说赶紧跑了。”
林楸点头，“警惕是好事。要找我们多打听打听总会找得过来，你们先去休息。这趟好在是你们去，比我们快多了。”
“嘿嘿……”几个小兽人被林楸一句话哄得傻笑。
羽单他们早躺窝里摊开了。
说实话，他们去的最远的地方是原野部落，要飞几个月，这几天的距离不算什么。
但是热啊……
热得他们胸闷口苦，食欲消减，什么也不想干。
也不知道这雨季什么时候才过去。
*
雨季末了，后头几场雨下来，一天比一天舒服。
直到雨季结束，兽人们猝不及防，还有些没反应过来。
他们跑去找祭司，祭司也正在计算。
“祭司祭司，今年雨季怎么一下就结束了？”
“对啊，我还以为还要再热一个月。”
祭司嫌他们吵，把兽人赶出山洞。
祭司旁边，草团上坐着一个小小的身影，他两个小手抱着石杵，一点一点研磨着药粉。
听到这些阿叔们口中忽然道了一声“楸”，幼崽立马直起身子，往洞口看。
没见到林楸，他鼓鼓腮帮子，又收回目光继续碾磨药粉。
大泽的活儿还没做完，白雀兽人和绿眼兽人还得继续。狼岩确认他们能独自干活后，放下心，和林楸回了狼部落。
黑羽兽人也被狼岩带了回去。
两个兽人刚进山洞，就听到兽人们闹哄哄地说着什么雪季。
林楸听了一耳，看着坐在祭司身边的幼崽，笑着招了招手道：
“雪。”
狼雪抬头，惊喜道：“楸叔！你们回来了！”
他扔下草药就冲着林楸跑去，直直撞进他怀里，双手抱着他的腰，小脑袋一下闷在他身上。
笑着笑着，幼崽嘴巴一瘪，眼泪就下来了。
哭得闷闷的，脑袋紧紧贴着林楸，一副可怜样。
这次走得久，雨季结束了才回来。
林楸摸着他后脑勺。
幼崽的头发软，像绒毛一样，他把狼雪抱起，脸贴着他脸问：“这么想我？”
“嗯。”狼雪不好意思，抹了下眼睛，乖乖趴在他肩头。
林楸抱着他找地方坐下来，把项链拿出来，给他戴上。
一整圈的小珍珠，中间是小小的狼牙。
狼雪脖子一凉，他低头看看，又小心翼翼地伸手摸一摸。
“喜欢吗？”
“嗯！”幼崽破涕为笑，又黏糊抱着他脖子。
另一边，兽人们把狼岩围了。
一口一声王，殷切不已，听得林楸牙酸。
“祭司刚刚说什么？”狼岩坐下来，问道。
兽人们也不出去了，在狼岩身边蹲了一圈。
林楸一看，似曾相识。
待到外面追着咩咩兽放牧的幼崽回来，又蹲了一圈，林楸了然。
他说幼崽怎么这么喜欢守着人，原来是一脉相承，小的跟大的学的。
“王，我们可想你了。”狼莫坐在狼岩腿边道。
“王不在，我们吃肉都吃不香。”狼西道。
其他兽人点着脑袋认同着。
狼岩不理他们，而是看着祭司。
老祭司好不容易算完，再把从前雨季的天数拉出来一比较，“王，你看。”
狼岩接过，兽人们纷纷坐起来，往他身边凑。
“今年少了八天嘞！”
“不是，你们看十五年前，雨季比今年多了十六天！”
老祭司捋了下胡子，点头道：“总体上来看，雨季时间短了。”
“那雪季呢？”狼莫问。
“没怎么变。”
“哦……所以这个正常吗？”
“不知道。”
“祭司，你别什么都不知道……嗷！”
老祭司收回拐杖，因着年老下垂的眼皮挡住半扇眸子，静静看着兽人时，显得阴恻恻的。
狼莫揉一揉自己手背，不敢说话了。
林楸放下狼雪过来，兽人们自动让开。
狼岩把兽皮递给他看，林楸手一滞。在兽皮上看到熟悉的文字，还是有点不习惯。
祭司记录的有关雨季雪季的数据很多，只缺少了狼部落迁徙那几年的，前头在中央大陆的数据，还有后期定居狼山这边的数据都是齐全的。
总体来看，雨季天数是在减少，雪季变化倒是不大。
“雨季天数减少，是好事还是坏事？”
“不确定。”祭司道。
气候的变化影响太大，短时间内又看不出来。
但祭司知道，从前的兽神大陆不会几个大陆都这么热，有些大陆不同区域不同气候，但总体来说，以前兽神大陆大部分地方是宜居的。
现在他年纪大了，也没有像年轻时候那样到处走，所以他下不了结论。
“走一步算一步吧。”狼莫悄悄道。
狼岩：“说的是。”
至少他们活着这几十年，影响不大。
回到部落，林楸和狼岩狠狠洗刷了一番，睡过一觉，便又开始忙碌。
雨季一过，就意味着雪季近了。
他们要开始储存食物。
部落兽人如此之多，去年存的那点食物可不够。狼岩忙着带领狩猎队捕猎，林楸则忙部落里的事。
地里第三批麻草得全部收了，咩咩兽吃的三叶草也得收割。尾巴草叶片已经泛黄，他们种得又多，收割尾巴草也是个大工程。
天高云淡，暑热散去大半。
雨季之后这段时间的气候格外舒服。
风拂过身体，带着衣服鼓起，触感是柔软温和的。
风中带着成熟的果子香味，还有淡淡的干草香，这是独属于丰收的味道。
赶着尾巴草收割之前，林楸与兔葵、羽单一起，领着兽人们开始收割麻草和三叶草。
重新被狼起他们打磨过的石镰稍稍锋利一些，兽人有劲儿，抓着一把麻草割掉放倒，便继续往前。
林楸和兔兽人只管割，后头黑羽兽人把麻草打捆，放上板车，再运去河边。
雨季过后，狼起又做出来两台织机，部落织布的效率高了一点。但麻布一出来，就被兽人们分完了。
麻线紧缺，兽人们不仅割了地里的，在外面遇到了麻草也会割回来，可还是不够。
今年种子收得多，想必明年还要多种些。
暑热还没彻底散尽，晃着那一丝尾巴犹豫不决。
太阳一出来，弯腰割麻草的兽人们头晕眼花。
林楸撑着后腰站起来，眼前一黑，抓着一把麻草缓了一会儿，眼前才清晰。
兔葵抹了一把额头的汗，嘴上干得起皮。他声音又慢又沉道：“休息吧，这会儿热起来了。”
林楸咽了下发干的喉咙，道：“行，休息。”
后头兔艾吆喝一声，兽人们从麻草地里钻出来。他们也一身草屑，垂头佝背，疲惫地拎着重重的石镰回去。
林楸揉着手腕，骨头缝里发酸。
兔葵看他一眼，道：“石镰就是重，用久了要歇一歇。”
林楸这手是给珠子打孔弄的，之前休息几天就好了。就是用石镰久了，又有点酸。
“回去喝点凉茶，解解渴，下午再继续。”
兔葵点头，已经没力气说话了。
天气凉快一点了，狼莫他们也重新忙起来。
垒窑、烧砖、建房，很快，东边狼力他们的小房子旁边，又打了三个房子的地基。
新的一个砖窑也建好了。
林楸看着，忽然想到了大泽那边的两个部落。
雪季水面结冰，外面能冻死兽人，干不了什么活儿。
现在两个部落的兽人也没找地方重新定居，还帮着狼部落做事，雪季的时候怎么办？
难不成他们雪季不仅要顾着自家兽人的食物，那两个部落也得负责？
林楸思索着，打算等晚上狼岩回来的时候问问。
食堂外，窗口边的屋檐下被狼安放了一张长桌。
长桌用料实在，桌板都有五厘米厚。
狼起他们虽然极力往好了做，但木桌上凹凸不平的砸痕、爪印，摸着还是刮手。就这么一张桌子，没半个月还做不出来。
不过桌子重，也格外稳当，兽人们随便往上面靠，一点不会动。
桌后的窗口紧挨着后厨，能从窗口看到灶台上兽人们忙碌的身影。
兽人要是不想进食堂，直接取水喝，来这里就行。
装水的罐子放在窗口里面台子上，兽人站起来就能够得到。
桌上有碗，要喝直接倒。
这一批陶碗烧得小一些，至少不像个小盆，装一碗水刚好够狼兽人一口气喝完。
不过林楸看着兔葵捧着碗，一抬手，碗就把他的脸遮住了。
狼兽人们还是贪大。
林楸弯唇笑了笑，自个儿去倒水喝。
“楸！今天中午还剩点昨天兽人们采集回来的长痒痒根，还有点肉和几根大骨头，怎么吃？”狼安看见林楸，靠过来窗边，手肘撑在上面笑盈盈地问。
他肩膀搭了一缕微卷的长发，笑起来眼尾是岁月添上的褶皱，腰间绑着围裙，一副爽利样子。
林楸就喜欢现在兽人们身上这股活气。
他道：“不怕麻烦的话，弄个山药丸子汤？剩下的野菜过水凉拌就好。”
“不麻烦。”
不就是剁肉，他们兽人多。
不多时，屋里响起切肉的声音。
石刀剁向木墩子，闷闷的响声似有韵律一般。这声音听在耳朵里，就意味着食物饱足，教兽人们忍不住在这声音中痴睡一番。
狼潭过来窗边，看了眼罐子里水，又拎进去加满了抱过来。
“楸。”
林楸道：“潭叔。”
“你阿父他们就快从支部落那边过来了。”
狼潭说了这一句话，就笑着走了。
大碗遮住林楸半张脸，露出的眉眼笑成一牙弯月。他能感觉到亚兽人在高兴，跟他说这话也没什么目的……单纯只是高兴。
兽人们喝完水，刚把碗放下，正打算去洗。窗里面又伸出来一双手，把碗抱走了。
“几个碗而已，我们洗，你们去歇着。”
兽人们去各自的草窝。
兔葵想着支部落那边还有不少兽人要回来，问林楸道：“楸，雪季冷，这边山洞够不够睡？”
不够的话，他们也能趁着还没到雪季，赶紧加工一下其他山洞，能挖多深挖多深。
山洞不够，他们还能挖地洞，地洞睡着还更暖和。
“够，狼莫那边还在建房子，食堂这边也能住，雪季挤着也暖和。”
“大家暂且将就个一年，等明年房子多了，就住得开了。”
*
今年，兽人早早开始囤积猎物。
狩猎队早上出发时，就分了东、南、北三个方向去。
狼游往北，狼岩也跟着他们一起。
狼山北部有草原，也有大河、树林。狼游他们的目标不是领地最北端的草原，雨季过了，草原上的咩咩兽群已经迁徙离开。
北边林子里他们来得少些，狼游想碰碰运气，看有没有猎物。
找来找去，还真让他们遇到一只尖角兽。
兽人们当即开始包围追击。
北边的树丛稍微稀疏一些，灌丛没那么密集。兽人们紧盯那四处逃窜的猎物，被它带着一路往北去。
采集队没跟着他们这一队，抓猎物的兽人够了，狼岩便在林子里走动，遇到了草药就采。
如今有不少草药成熟，他也认识一些。
部落草药告急，等部落安定，他们就得外出一趟。到那时，便不是出去三五天，说不定半年也回不来。
狼岩琢磨着这事儿，忽然听到一声摔倒的闷响。
他警惕抬头，就看见狼游从地上爬起来。
“呸！”狼游吐出嘴里刚刚啃得泥和草，眼看猎物消失不见，心中气闷。
他刚要往地上踢一脚，脚下一顿，惊道：“王！兽人！”
兽人们被他一嗓子分了神，再回头，哪里还有什么猎物。
“狼游！”
“队长，你叫什么啊？！猎物都跑没了。”
狼游不说话，等着狼岩过来。
大伙儿围起来，一看，纷纷抓着武器警惕起来。
狼力抓着长矛，往地上那张棕色皮毛戳了戳。兽人不动，他长矛插地，一挑，把兽人翻过来。
“熊兽人！”
其他兽人拿起武器就要往兽人身上扎。
狼岩：“别动。”
“王，是熊兽人！”大伙儿紧张道。
先前部落才被熊兽人偷袭，狼兽人们有点应激。
狼岩看着那棕褐色兽毛，跟枯草一样，粗糙暗黄。他道：“是棕熊兽人，支部落那边的。”
熊塞快要饿得见兽神之前，迷糊听得一群兽人围着他在说话。这让他想起来部落里去世的兽人就会这样……
呜呜呜……他怎么就死了呢！
他还没完成族长交给他的任务！还没找到狼部落！
该死的……狼部落到底藏在哪儿了，他们为什么找了这么久都没有找到！
绝望之中，他颤颤巍巍睁开眼。
“没死？”
唰的一声，狼兽人们飞快往后退一步，武器全部举起，冲着熊塞身上的致命处。
尤其是脖子那一处，瞄准得最多。
熊塞一看是狼兽人，双目睁大。
“狼、狼……”
“狼什么狼？你们为什么跑到我们部落？有什么目的？说！”狼力长矛抵住兽人脖子，稍稍用力，熊塞疼得呜的一声——
嚎啕大哭。
“呜呜呜我没死……找、找到了！我终于找到你们了呜呜呜……”
就剩一张熊皮子和骨头的兽人，哭得都快碎了。
他边哭边说，狼兽人们听着，脸色变了变，从愤怒转化为同情。
怎么会有这么笨的兽人？
从支部落那边过来也不过半月，他们居然在外面晃荡了近乎两月。
哭了半截，兽人捂着肚子，表情狰狞。
狼兽人还以为他中毒了，谁知道熊塞满眼蓄泪，看着他们细若游丝来了一句：“我好饿……”
没等兽人们回答，他白眼一翻，再次晕了过去。
看来是真饿了。
狼力戳戳他，不醒。
又戳戳附近散落的其他熊兽人，也一动不动。
狼游蹲下，探了下其他兽人的呼吸，皱眉道：“王，好像快不行了。”
狼岩：“带回去。”
*
临近傍晚，狩猎采集队回来了。
雨季结束，他们早早开始囤积食物。猎物还是少，出去一天，三个狩猎队分开的，也仅有一个狩猎队带回来猎物。
今晚只有一头呦呦兽。
不过奇怪的是，林楸听到外面兽人回来的动静，走出山洞口。在模糊的光影中，他看到狼游那一队兽人手上拎着大兽皮袋一样的东西。
难不成半路捡了人家物资？
林楸下山去看。
走到半路，看狼岩蹲在溪边洗手，林楸扬起眉梢，快步跑下山。
狼岩直起身，长臂一捞，把险些停不住脚的林楸带回来。
“跑什么？”狼岩低头，鼻尖碰了下他鼻尖。
林楸把着他手臂，冲着他一笑。
“没刹住。”
“王，咱们抢人家物资了？”
腰上的手圈得紧，林楸只能隔着狼岩肩膀往前面看。
不是兽皮袋，是兽皮。
成捆成捆的兽皮，不知多少张。
“不是。”狼岩瞧着自家伴侣颈侧的细腻肌肤，忍不住低头，挺拔的鼻子压上去，又轻轻咬了咬。
林楸一哆嗦，连忙偏头，“有兽人看着。”
狼岩松开他。
林楸摸摸颈侧，飞快瞄了一眼远处的兽人，然后继续挨着狼岩站着。
狼岩笑了一声，还以为他要跑。
“王，哪里来的兽皮？”
狼岩转身，慢慢往食堂走。
林楸见他不说话，去勾他的手指，被狼岩反手拢住，十指相扣。
“棕熊部落的。”
“棕熊？”林楸想起来自己隐隐在哪里听过，看到小河边洗麻的黑羽兽人，想起来了。
“之前羽涯不是说他们要来找我们？”
“是他们。”
这都雨季结束，离羽涯说那话都过去两个月了，这棕熊兽人才找到他们部落？
从南边支部落过来狼山也不过半月，他们难不成不是找他们这个狼部落，而是找其他？
“他们迷路了。”
林楸看向狼岩。
狼岩低头，看他迷茫的呆样，低头轻轻碰了下林楸额头，“然后饿晕了。”
林楸扑哧一笑，狼岩看着他笑得粉白的脸颊，也弯了下唇角。
“他们是来交换东西的。”
“那兽人呢？”
“后边，黑山洞关着，让安送了点鱼汤过去。”
狼游狩猎队去的北边，也不知道黑熊兽人怎么找的路，明明从南边可以过来，结果都到了北边还没找到。
要不是狼游追击猎物踩了他们一脚，还不知道那里有兽人。
晚风悠然而过，林楸与狼岩牵着手，沿河边慢慢走。
狼石带着兽人在杀猎物，狼莫则把河里的笼子起了。
笼子里的鱼少了，他们抓了这么久，鱼也学聪明了。
林楸看着那笼子里倒出来的一些小鱼小虾，问狼岩：“他们想交换什么？”
“还晕着，没来得及问，大概率也是陶罐和渔网。”
“那多半也是从支部落那里知道这两样东西的？”
“嗯。”
棕熊部落挨着他们支部落北边，两个部落虽然会抢夺猎物，但没到绿眼部落那种直接进部落偷抢的程度。
两个部落虽有摩擦，但不至于成仇。
要是他们给的东西合理，确实可以交换。
晚风拂面，发丝飘扬着，交缠在一起。
林楸想起白雀那边的事，脚步停下来。
“王，雪季大泽那边，兽人们干不了活儿。他们现在正是囤食物的时候，也没走，雪季怎么办？”
“那是他们自己该考虑的事，我又不是他们的族长。”
林楸脑袋转过弯来，笑了笑，“好像是这样。”
“放心，不会忙得太晚。”
囤粮关乎兽人性命，没有哪个部落那么蠢，将自身性命寄托在另一个部落身上。
就算是绿眼部落，也不敢完全信任他们。
晚风吹得太舒服，林楸不想走了。
他侧身倚靠着狼岩，望着狼山的方向。
食堂上炊烟袅袅。
幼崽在广场上玩儿，追着追着，从广场上趴了一地的狩猎采集队的兽人们身上爬过去。
兔兽人们和黑羽兽人瘫坐在地上，含笑看着，虽然疲惫但眼中饱含收获的幸福……
林楸下巴贴着狼岩肩头，双手被他攥在掌中，他笑着懒声道：“王，走不动了。”
狼岩弯腰蹲在他身前。
自家伴侣难得的要求，他哪能不同意。
林楸趴上他背，被他背着，宽厚的背像能托起他一切的情绪。
林楸双手抱着他脖子，身子发懒，半阖眼眸。
忙了一天，他也累了。
狼岩回来他就想靠着，清醒时总是羞，唯有这会儿脑子混沌，他才放肆一点。

Here is the translation of the chapter:

### Chapter 165

Yuya and his party went to the branch tribe to deliver news. The round trip took only eight days—exactly half the time Yuya had estimated.

The Black Feather beastmen had just landed on the banks of the Great Swamp when Lang Yu shoved a large bowl of medicinal herb soup, boiled to an almost pitch-black color, into their hands. Lin Qiu observed that although the beastmen looked exhausted, their eyes were clear and bright; they were merely tired, not sick.

"Did you run into any trouble on the road?"

Yuya shook his head with a hazy expression, only to be elbowed by a companion.

Wincing in pain, Yuya gulped down a mouthful of the herbal soup and grimaced. "There... there was a Brown Bear tribe that asked us for directions; they were looking for you all."

"The Brown Bear tribe..." Lin Qiu murmured. He seemed to have a vague impression of them. "Is that the one north of the branch tribe?"

"We don't know. We met them halfway. We were worried about trouble, so we didn't say a word and just ran."

Lin Qiu nodded. "Vigilance is a good thing. If they really want to find us, they’ll eventually ask around enough to locate us. You lot go get some rest first. It’s a good thing you were the ones to go; you’re much faster than us."

"Heh heh..." The young beastmen giggled, easily appeased by Lin Qiu's praise.

Yu Dan and the others had already flopped down into their nests. Truth be told, the furthest place they had ever traveled to was the Plains tribe, which took months to fly to; this trip was nothing. But the heat... it was stifling, leaving them bitter-mouthed and lacking appetite. They didn't want to do anything at all.

He wondered when this rainy season would finally end.

***

Towards the end of the rainy season, the subsequent rains became lighter, and each day grew more comfortable than the last. By the time the rainy season officially ended, the beastmen were caught off guard, caught in a daze as if they hadn't realized it had actually happened.

They ran to find the Shaman, who was in the middle of his own calculations.

"Shaman, Shaman! Why did the rainy season end so suddenly this year?"

"Yeah! I thought it would stay hot for another month."

Annoyed by their clamor, the Shaman chased the beastmen out of the cave. Beside him, a small figure sat on a cushion of grass, holding a stone pestle with two tiny hands and grinding herbal powder bit by bit. 

When he heard these "uncles" suddenly mention the name "Qiu," the cub immediately straightened his back and looked toward the cave entrance. Seeing that it wasn't Lin Qiu, he puffed out his cheeks and returned to his grinding.

The work at the Great Swamp wasn't finished yet, so the White Sparrow and Green-Eyed beastmen had to keep at it. Once Lang Yan confirmed they could work independently, he felt relieved and returned to the Wolf tribe with Lin Qiu. The Black Feather beastmen were brought back by him as well.

The moment the two entered the cave, they heard the beastmen noisily discussing the Snow Season. Lin Qiu caught a snippet of the conversation, then looked at the cub sitting beside the Shaman and waved with a smile.

"Xue."

Lang Xue looked up, eyes widening in surprise. "Uncle Qiu! You’re back!"

He tossed aside the herbs and dashed toward Lin Qiu, crashing straight into his arms. He wrapped his small hands around Lin Qiu's waist and buried his little head against him. He tried to smile, but his mouth quivered, and tears began to well up. 

He cried muffled sobs, his head pressed tightly against Lin Qiu, looking pitiful. This trip had lasted a long time; they had only returned after the rainy season had ended.

Lin Qiu stroked the back of his head. The cub's hair was soft, like fuzz. He picked Lang Xue up and asked, cheek-to-cheek, "Did you miss me that much?"

"Mm." Embarrassed, Lang Xue wiped his eyes and obediently leaned his head on Lin Qiu's shoulder.

Lin Qiu sat down with him and took out a necklace to put around his neck. It was a string of small pearls with a tiny wolf tooth in the center. Lang Xue felt the coolness against his neck, looked down, and reached up to touch it cautiously.

"Do you like it?"

"Mm!" The cub smiled through his tears, clinging tightly to Lin Qiu's neck once more.

Elsewhere, the beastmen had surrounded Lang Yan. They called him "King" over and over with such fervent devotion that it made Lin Qiu's teeth ache.

"What did the Shaman just say?" Lang Yan asked as he sat down. The beastmen stopped pacing and squatted in a circle around him.

Lin Qiu watched, feeling a sense of déjà vu. When the cubs, who had been out chasing Baa-baa beasts, returned and squatted in another circle, Lin Qiu understood. He had wondered why the cubs loved hovering around the adults so much; it was clearly a learned behavior passed down from the older ones.

"King, we missed you so much," Lang Mo said, sitting by Lang Yan’s knees.

"When you weren't here, even the meat didn't taste good," Lang Xi added. The other beastmen nodded in agreement.

Lang Yan ignored them and looked at the Shaman. The old Shaman had finally finished his calculations and pulled out the records of past rainy seasons for comparison. "King, look."

Lang Yan took the hide, and the beastmen all leaned in close.

"It's eight days shorter this year!"

"No, look at fifteen years ago—the rainy season was sixteen days longer than this year!"

The old Shaman stroked his beard and nodded. "Overall, the rainy season is indeed getting shorter."

"What about the Snow Season?" Lang Mo asked.

"It hasn't changed much."

"Oh... so is this normal?"

"I don't know."

"Shaman, don't just say you don't know... Ouch!"

The old Shaman retracted his cane. His drooping eyelids partially covered his eyes, and when he looked silently at the beastmen, he appeared quite sinister. Lang Mo rubbed his hand, not daring to speak again.

Lin Qiu put Lang Xue down and walked over, the beastmen parting to make way for him. Lang Yan handed him the animal hide, and Lin Qiu paused. He was still not quite used to seeing the familiar characters written on hide.

The Shaman had recorded a significant amount of data regarding the rainy and snow seasons. The only years missing were those when the Wolf tribe had migrated; the data from the Central Continent before that, and the data since settling near Wolf Mountain, were complete. Overall, the number of days in the rainy season was decreasing, while the snow season remained relatively stable.

"Is the decrease in the rainy season days a good thing or a bad thing?"

"It is uncertain," the Shaman replied.

Climate change had too great an impact to be judged in such a short time. However, the Shaman knew that in the past, the Beast God Continent hadn't been this hot everywhere. Different regions had different climates, but generally, most of the continent had been quite livable. Now, he was old and didn't travel like he used to, so he couldn't draw a definitive conclusion.

"We'll just take it one step at a time," Lang Mo whispered.

Lang Yan: "Indeed." At least for the decades they lived, the impact shouldn't be too severe.

***

Back at the tribe, Lin Qiu and Lang Yan scrubbed themselves clean, took a long sleep, and then immediately went back to work. Once the rainy season ended, the Snow Season was close at hand.

They had to start storing food. With so many beastmen in the tribe, what they had stored last year wouldn't be enough. Lang Yan was busy leading the hunting parties, while Lin Qiu managed affairs within the tribe.

The third batch of hemp grass in the fields had to be harvested, and the clover eaten by the Baa-baa beasts also needed to be cut. The leaves of the "tail grass" were turning yellow, and since they had planted so much, harvesting it was a massive project.

The sky was high and the clouds were sparse; the summer heat had largely dissipated. The period following the rainy season was exceptionally pleasant. A breeze swept across their bodies, making their clothes billow; the touch was soft and gentle. The air carried the scent of ripening fruit and a faint smell of dried grass—a fragrance unique to the harvest season.

Before the tail grass harvest, Lin Qiu led the beastmen, alongside Tu Kui and Yu Dan, to start reaping the hemp and clover. The stone sickles, which had been sharpened by Lang Qi and his group, were a bit keener, and the beastmen worked with vigor—grabbing a handful of hemp, slicing it down, and moving on.

Lin Qiu and the Rabbit beastmen focused on cutting, while the Black Feather beastmen behind them bundled the hemp, loaded it onto carts, and transported it to the river. After the rainy season, Lang Qi had made two more looms, increasing the efficiency of the tribe's cloth production. But as soon as the linen came out, it was snatched up by the beastmen. Hemp thread was in short supply; the beastmen not only harvested what was in the fields but also gathered wild hemp whenever they encountered it, yet it still wasn't enough. They had collected many seeds this year, so they would surely plant more next year.

The summer heat hadn't completely vanished; it lingered, reluctant to leave. Whenever the sun came out, the beastmen, bent over harvesting hemp, would feel dizzy.

Lin Qiu straightened up, bracing his lower back. His vision went black for a moment, and he gripped a handful of hemp, waiting until his sight cleared. 

Tu Kui wiped the sweat from his forehead, his lips cracked and dry. He spoke slowly, his voice raspy. "Let's rest; it's getting hot."

Lin Qiu swallowed a dry gulp and said, "Alright, let's rest."

Tu Ai shouted from behind, and the beastmen emerged from the hemp field. They were covered in grass clippings, hunched over, and exhausted as they dragged their heavy stone sickles back. Lin Qiu rubbed his wrists; his joints were aching.

Tu Kui glanced at him. "The stone sickles are heavy; you have to take breaks when using them for a long time."

Lin Qiu’s hands were already sore from drilling holes in beads, and using the stone sickle for so long had only worsened it. 

"Let's go back and drink some herbal tea to quench our thirst, then we'll continue in the afternoon."

Tu Kui nodded, too tired to speak.

As the weather cooled, Lang Mo and the others got busy again. Kilns were built, bricks were fired, and houses were constructed. Soon, three more house foundations were laid next to Lang Li's small house in the east. A new brick kiln was also finished.

Watching them, Lin Qiu suddenly thought of the two tribes near the Great Swamp. During the Snow Season, the water would freeze, and the cold outside was enough to kill a beastman; no work could be done. The beastmen of those two tribes hadn't found a place to settle yet and were still helping the Wolf tribe—what would they do during the Snow Season? Was he expected to feed not only his own tribe but those two as well?

Lin Qiu pondered this, planning to ask Lang Yan when he returned that night.

Outside the canteen, under the eaves near the window, Lang An had placed a long table. It was made of solid materials, with a table surface five centimeters thick. Although Lang Qi and the others had tried their best to make it smooth, there were still uneven dents and claw marks on the wood. It had taken them half a month just to build this one table. However, it was heavy and incredibly sturdy; the beastmen could lean on it as much as they wanted, and it wouldn't budge.

The window behind the table was right next to the kitchen, where one could see the beastmen busy at the stoves. If a beastman didn't want to enter the canteen and just wanted to drink water, they could come here. A large clay jar of water was placed on a ledge inside the window, reachable as soon as a beastman stood up. There were bowls on the table; if they wanted to drink, they could just pour it themselves.

This batch of clay bowls was smaller—at least they didn't look like small basins anymore. One bowl held exactly enough water for a Wolf beastman to drink in one gulp. However, Lin Qiu watched as Tu Kui held the bowl; with one lift of his hand, the bowl covered his entire face. The Wolf beastmen were still greedy for larger portions.

Lin Qiu smiled and went to pour some water himself.

"Qiu! There's some 'Long Itch Root' the beastmen gathered yesterday, plus some meat and big bones. How should we eat them?" Lang An leaned against the window, his elbows resting on the edge, smiling. A strand of slightly curly hair rested on his shoulder; fine lines of age creased the corners of his eyes, and he wore an apron, looking capable and efficient.

Lin Qiu loved this vitality in the beastmen. 

He said, "If it's not too much trouble, how about a Yam Ball Soup? Just blanch the remaining wild vegetables and dress them with sauce."

"It's no trouble at all."

It was just chopping meat; they had plenty of beastmen for that. Before long, the sound of meat being chopped echoed through the room. The stone knives hitting the wooden logs had a rhythmic, muffled sound. To the beastmen, this sound meant a full meal, making them want to drift into a deep, satisfied sleep just listening to it.

Lang Tan came to the window, checked the water jar, and brought it inside to refill it before returning.

"Qiu."

"Uncle Tan."

"Your father and the others will be coming from the branch tribe soon."

After saying this, Lang Tan left with a smile. The large bowl covered half of Lin Qiu's face, but his visible eyes curved into crescents. He could feel the Sub-beastman's happiness, and there was no ulterior motive—just pure joy.

Once the beastmen finished drinking and set their bowls down, intending to wash them, a pair of hands reached out from the window and whisked the bowls away.

"It's just a few bowls, we'll wash them. You go get some rest."

The beastmen retreated to their respective grass nests. Tu Kui, thinking about the many beastmen coming from the branch tribe, asked Lin Qiu, "Qiu, it's cold during the Snow Season. Are there enough caves here for everyone to sleep?"

If not, they could take advantage of the remaining time to expand the other caves—digging them as deep as possible. If caves weren't enough, they could dig underground burrows; those were even warmer to sleep in.

"It's enough. Lang Mo is still building houses over there, and people can stay in the canteen area too. It’s warm when everyone huddles together in the Snow Season. Everyone will just have to make do for one year. By next year, when there are more houses, there will be plenty of room."

***

This year, the beastmen began stockpiling prey early. When the hunting parties set out in the morning, they divided into three directions: East, South, and North.

Lang You went North, and Lang Yan went with them. The north of Wolf Mountain had grasslands, big rivers, and forests. Their goal wasn't the far northern grasslands; the rainy season had passed, and the herds of Baa-baa beasts had already migrated. They rarely came to the northern woods, but Lang You wanted to try his luck to see if there was any prey.

After searching, they actually encountered a Sharp-Horned beast. The beastmen immediately began to surround and chase it. The northern woods were slightly sparser, with less dense brush. The beastmen kept their eyes on the fleeing prey, following it all the way north.

The gathering party hadn't followed this group, and since there were enough beastmen to catch the prey, Lang Yan wandered through the woods, picking herbs when he found them. Many medicinal herbs were now ripe, and he recognized a few. The tribe's herbal supply was running low; once things were stable, they would need to go on a long trip. At that point, it wouldn't be a three-to-five-day affair—it might take half a year before they could return.

Lang Yan was pondering this when he heard a muffled thud of something falling. He looked up, alert, and saw Lang You scrambling up from the ground.

"Ptui!" Lang You spat out the mud and grass he had accidentally bitten into. Watching the prey disappear, he felt frustrated. Just as he was about to kick the ground, he paused and gasped, "King! Beastmen!"

The other beastmen were distracted by his shout, and by the time they looked back, the prey was gone.

"Lang You!"

"Captain, what are you yelling for?! The prey got away!"

Lang You didn't answer, waiting for Lang Yan to come over.

The group gathered around and, upon seeing what it was, reached for their weapons, growing alert. Lang Li grabbed a spear and poked the brown fur on the ground. The beastman didn't move, so he used the spear to flip the body over.

"A Bear beastman!"

The other beastmen raised their weapons, ready to strike.

"Don't move," Lang Yan commanded.

"King, it's a Bear beastman!" the group said nervously. The tribe had just been ambushed by Bear beastmen earlier, and the Wolf beastmen were a bit on edge.

Lang Yan looked at the brown fur; it was coarse, dark yellow, and resembled withered grass. He said, "It's a Brown Bear beastman, from the branch tribe."
