In the past, whenever a beastman was injured, the thin and tiny boy would stand off to the side, completely at a loss.

Unable to save the injured, he would look even more heartbroken than the wounded beastmen themselves.

But now, Yule was squatting by Yuhua’s leg, though slightly nervous, treating Yuhua’s wound with herbs in a surprisingly professional manner.

He used to be such a shy and timid cub, but now he was the calmest among them all.

The beastmen were naturally glad to know he had learned well at the Wolf Tribe, but thinking that this thorough transformation was caused by the late chief’s passing... several sub-beastmen turned around again to wipe away tears.

Yule watched as Yuhua’s lips gradually regained their normal color, and upon hearing a faint sob, he turned back to see that every single adult beastman was standing right where they were, all of them smiling at him the moment they caught his eye.

Only their eyes were fiercely red.

Yule was very strong.

He was the tribe’s priest, and he was supposed to be strong.

Yet after all this time, looking into the uncles' gazes—filled with both relief and heartache—his lips trembled uncontrollably.

He bit down hard, and his vision blurred.

"Oh dear, you've suffered," several uncles stepped forward, gently patting his head.

Yule suddenly threw himself onto Yuqian, without saying a word, just burying his face and tightly hugging the man's waist.

Yuqian gently stroked his hair, lowering his voice: "Our A-le has grown up, grown into a capable little priest. Your Uncle A-hua’s life was only saved thanks to A-le..."

"That kind of long worm can't kill a beastman..." Yule mumbled, his voice muffled.

"Well, if A-le hadn't come back, we wouldn't have had a way either."

Seeing how obedient he was, Yuqian couldn't help but tilt his head back, blinking hard to hold back his tears.

The Snow Eagle beastmen's two attacks, the old chief's death, the loss of most of their clansmen—the tribe had already been through enough hardship.

They, the adult beastmen, could hold on, but how could they let the little beastmen bear it?

Not only had Yuya and the others become sensible, but Yule had also worked hard to learn about herbs in such a short time, his personality shifting completely. Seeing this, their hearts ached terribly.

Only when a tribe wasn't strong enough would the cubs suffer along with them.

It was their own lack of ability; otherwise, like the cubs of the Wolf Tribe, weren't they all carefree day in and day out, doing whatever they pleased, and being raised better than the cubs of any other tribe?

The adult Heiyu beastmen secretly steeled their hearts.

The cubs were working hard, so they had to keep up.

This coming snow season, they had to catch enough prey; they couldn't let the little beastmen go hungry.

*

Lang Chi led the beastmen of the branch tribe all the way north, a massive procession.

After walking for more than ten days, everyone finally caught sight of the Great Marsh.

"We're almost there, almost there," Lang Wan dropped his animal-skin pack and quickened his pace toward the water's edge.

They were all getting on in years, in their forties or fifties, and hadn't walked such a long distance in over a decade.

They carried far too many things, even bringing along their reliable stone tools.

While everyone had some energy when they first started out, during the second half of the journey, the beastmen trudged forward like shelled bugs, huffing and puffing with every step.

Lang Chi signaled for the beastmen to stop and rest.

Everyone unloaded their belongings, dropped flat right where they stood, and hung out their tongues, completely motionless.

"If you're like this just from walking, how are you going to help with work in the future?" Lang Chi asked.

Lang Xing rolled his eyes upward and stared at him, "Why don't you look at how fast you walked? You haven't rested for a single day."

Lang Chi: "Didn't we rest when we ate dried fish?"

Lang Xing flipped over, presenting the back of his head to Lang Chi, not even wanting to speak to him.

These past few days, they traveled by day and mostly gnawed on the dried fish they had saved beforehand. Before the last bite of dried fish was even swallowed, Lang Chi would shout to move and start running ahead by himself.

Rest?

He had the nerve to say that.

The beastmen were sprawled out everywhere, but Lang Chi couldn't settle down.

Their current location happened to be right on the southeasternmost edge of the Wolf Tribe's territory. Lang Chi walked around, and as he walked, he simply gathered some stones and piled them up into short boundary markers.

"Chieftain, what are you doing?" Lang Zang turned his head from the ground, breathing heavily, the thick puffs of air blowing the grass flat right in front of his snout.

"Nothing much."

"Are you setting up tribal boundaries?"

"Just casually."

Lang Zang pressed his head against the grass to think for a second, then pushed up with all four legs and scrambled over to help pile up stones too.

Lang Chi glanced at him.

Lang Zang: "Since we've arrived, it's only right for the tribe's territory to expand a bit. Besides, there aren't any other tribes around here anyway."

Lang Shan's territory wasn't small, and it already included a section of the Great Marsh directly to their south.

The Great Marsh stretched far out to the southeast, boundless and vast. When beastmen visited the branch tribe, they had to detour for several days. Since they had to detour anyway, they might as well mark it as part of their own tribe.

Lang Xing watched from afar and nudged Lang Wan, signaling him to look.

Lang Wan curled his lip, "He's just excited, has nothing to do, and is getting restless and doing something stupid."

The boundaries of Lang Shan's territory were laid out when the old Wolf King was still around; there must have been a good reason why they didn't include this area back then.

There was no prey here, and it was so far from the tribe that patrols took many days just to go back and forth. Incorporating this area was purely asking for trouble.

Once they had rested enough, the beastmen set off again.

At most, in five days, they would arrive.

*

The Great Marsh.

The rainy season had ended, and the beastmen had reverted to working by day and sleeping by night.

The Great Marsh hadn't flooded much this rainy season. So far, a row of earth blocks had already been piled up in front of the wooden houses.

The black silt looked like moldy tofu, sitting in clumps scattered across the water's surface.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan set out from the tribe, heading straight for the Great Marsh, while the other beastmen went hunting.

It was afternoon, and the beastmen were still resting after finishing their meat soup.

As Lin Qiu and Lang Yan emerged from the woods behind the shed, they ran right into a little wolf poking its head out of the shed with a wary expression.

"King? Qiu!" Lang Jin hopped out over the low wall joyfully and scurried over to them.

"Didn't you go hunting?" Lang Yan asked.

Lang Jin lifted his chin proudly, "Yesterday we caught a large curved-horn beast, and a big, big, big long worm."

Lang Yan pinched his shoulder, "Not bad."

"Heh..." The little wolf walked side by side with Lin Qiu, tilting his head and asking, "Qiu, what are you guys here for?"

"Did Bai Que ask you whether we were coming or not?"

The little wolf nodded, "Seems she asked."

"We can't get any work done here during the snow season, so I came to see how they're planning things."

"Oh, can't work... Does that mean we can go back?"

"We still need to dig lotus roots."

"Fine..."

Lang Yan glanced sideways at the little wolf, grabbed Lin Qiu's wrist, and pulled him along at a faster pace.

Lang Jin trotted happily behind them.

The beastmen were still resting, and Lin Qiu and Lang Yan were tired from traveling here.

They made do with the leftover meat soup in the pot to line their stomachs and rested for a while in a grass nest before the two chieftains sought them out.

When Lang Yan and Lin Qiu came out, Chieftain Bai Que smiled warmly and said, "Wolf King, Qiu, you've finally arrived."

"Sit."

Straw mats were placed under the empty shed, and the beastmen sat down directly.

Chieftain Bai Que said, "The snow season is almost here, and we want to temporarily stop our work and return to the tribe to store some food."

"Alright." Lang Yan had come for this exact matter and had no reason to stop the beastmen.

"A-and there's one more thing. As you know, our tribe was burned down, so we were hoping to borrow your fishing nets first..."

Chieftain Bai Que had originally thought about simply catching some fish within the Wolf Tribe's waters, but once he said those words aloud, he really found it hard to continue.

He thought to himself that their tribe also had rivers and lakes.

If there truly weren't many fish, at the worst, they could fly further away to the southeast side of the Great Marsh. The Wolf Tribe didn't manage that area, so they could catch fish there and dry them into preserved fish to take back.

As long as they figured something out, they wouldn't starve during the snow season.

Lang Yan agreed to this as well.

Bai Que breathed a sigh of relief, "Then we'll head back tomorrow."

After Chieftain Bai Que finished speaking, Green Tu looked at Lang Yan.

"We have nowhere else to go. We'll help you with other tasks—can you take us in?"

Lang Yan: "What tasks are there to do during the snow season?"

The Bai Que beastmen's eyelids twitched, and they cast a secret glance at Green Tu.

How craftly!

He actually said it straight out! Judging by the Wolf King's expression, he might even agree! If he had known, he would have said it too.

Green Tu touched the bricks on the wall behind him. This shed had been reinforced by the beastmen with bricks and tiles previously, and those square, stone-like things felt very different to the touch.

Green Tu had also seen the Wolf Tribe's houses.

"Your Great Marsh needs to be remodeled, and the land in the water will definitely need to be farmed. Many beastmen will probably come here in the future... Living in sheds all the time definitely won't do. If you let us stay here, we'll help you build houses."

"Once the houses are built, you let us live through the snow season. We won't need you to provide food; we just want your permission to catch fish in the Great Marsh."

Hearing this, it didn't sound any different from the current way they worked.

They were still working for the Wolf Tribe, but the Wolf Tribe only needed to supply ingredients—which the Green-Eyed beastmen would catch themselves anyway, saving the wolf beastmen the trouble.

However, the roads would be blocked during the snow season, and the wolf beastmen certainly wouldn't come over to the Great Marsh, giving the Green-Eyed beastmen a much higher degree of autonomy here.

This was something the wolf beastmen wouldn't normally allow.

Green Tu also knew that Lang Yan didn't trust them. He lowered his head, looked at the floating dust before his eyes, and sighed: "You can send wolf beastmen over, and we... our cubs can be sent to Lang Shan."

Lin Qiu frowned.

Having been in the beast world for so long, Lin Qiu understood what a tribe's cubs meant to that tribe.

Granted, if the Green-Eyed Tribe sent their cubs to Lang Shan, the wolf beastmen would inevitably have to take care of those cubs' food and drink, which sounded a bit like they were taking advantage of the Wolf Tribe.

But to actually send their cubs out as a form of hostage against themselves—the Green-Eyed beastmen were truly capable of doing it!

Lang Yan: "There's plenty of empty space in the north."

"But our tribe isn't like Bai Que, where we can just find a small lake and catch some fish to survive."

They were a large-bodied feathered tribe; only large rivers and lakes could sustain the tribe.

Even if they went to look now, Green Tu couldn't guarantee that his clansmen wouldn't end up like they did in the south—starving to death halfway through the snow season.

He wanted to take advantage, but at the same time, he didn't dare gamble.

Call him a parasite, call him shameless—without the Wolf Tribe, he didn't have the confidence to sustain the tribe again.

Building houses for the Wolf Tribe would give them a place to settle. Relying on the Great Marsh, even if the snow season froze everything over, with their experience at the branch tribe, they could still fish things out.

"Wolf King, this is no different from us exchanging labor for food right now..."

Lang Yan: "I'll consider it."

The two chieftains left, and Lin Qiu shifted his position, sitting facing Lang Yan.

Seeing Lang Yan frowning deeply in thought, Lin Qiu placed a hand on his thigh and leaned forward to look at his face.

"Hmph!"

Lang Yan suddenly lowered his head and nibbled the tip of Lin Qiu's nose.

Lin Qiu covered his nose and reached out to pinch Lang Yan's ear.

Lang Yan tilted his head to dodge, but Lin Qiu's stubborn streak flared up—he was determined to get a pinch in, reaching out to chase after it.

Lang Yan pulled Lin Qiu's lunging body into his arms, tilting his head slightly and letting him pinch however he liked.

Lin Qiu pressed against his chest, "What are you thinking?"

Lang Yan pinched Lin Qiu's cheek and curved the corners of his lips, "I don't want to raise their cubs for them."

"You agreed?" Not wanting to raise their cubs for them didn't mean he disagreed with the Green-Eyed Tribe staying at Lang Shan to work during the snow season.

"Uncle Chi should be arriving soon."

"Huh?"

"Let him decide."

*

"Achoo!"

"Chi! The prey got away!"

The beastmen of the branch tribe were walking north along the southeastern section of the Great Marsh. Gnawing on dried fish every day, they could barely hold on anymore when, coincidentally, they encountered a呦呦 beast drinking water by the water's edge.

They had set up their ambush perfectly, but Lang Chi's sneeze startled the creature, sending it darting into the woods out of sight.

The beastmen slumped crookedly all over the ground, clutching their oil-starved bellies and sighing incessantly.

Lang Chi rubbed his nose, then touched the back of his neck, feeling as though he was being watched by something.

"Let's keep moving."

"We can't walk anymore..." The beastmen hadn't eaten or rested well along the road. Gnawing on dried fish had left them sallow and thin, and carrying heavy and light packs made them look like refugees fleeing north.

"Should we catch some more fish?"

Lang Wan spat twice, fell backward, and said, "I don't want to eat fish!"

After eating fish for a whole year, he didn't know where this rebellious streak came from at the moment, but anyway, he didn't want to eat that stuff at all right now.

It was fishy and stinking, tasted bland, didn't fill you up for long after eating, and stripped away all your body fat.

"Then boil some tail-grass seeds?"

Lang Wan rolled over and stared at Lang Chi.

"Feeling generous? Didn't you say we couldn't eat them?" Despite his words, he sat up swiftly. Before even building a stove, he scooped several large ladles of shelled tail-grass seeds into an earthen pot and poured water in.

Once it was wet, he couldn't back out.

Lang Chi: "Take it easy."

They had only ground that one animal-skin pouch, about half a clay pot's worth. With Lang Wan's ladle, half of it disappeared instantly.

While washing the grains, Lang Wan instructed the beastmen to build a stove, squeezing in a casual reply to Lang Chi: "I am taking it easy, taking it easy. Look how much is still left."

By the Great Marsh, blue smoke curled leisurely upward.

The first hunting team, which was hunting nearby, was startled and hurriedly scrambled up to the treetops to look into the distance.

"Captain! There's smoke again!" A beastman hugged a tree trunk with all four limbs, slid down quickly, and said anxiously.

Lang You: "You go notify the King. The other beastmen, follow me to take a look."

The fire source was close to them, so Lang You led the team running at top speed, even bumping into a呦呦 beast along the way.

Without Lang You needing to give an order, the beastmen quickly gave chase.

The rest of the beastmen continued running forward with him.

There was rustling in the bushes. The branch tribe's beastmen, rich in hunting experience, raised their heads and, upon seeing the swaying figures in the woods, stood up in surprise.

"Little Wolf?"

Lang You paused. He looked at the large and small bundles scattered by the water's edge, as well as the wolf beastmen with greying temples, and then looked at the smoke rising from their stove. A smile bloomed in his eyes.

"You're back."

Lang Chi nodded and looked at the dozen or so young wolf beastmen around him.

"Did the King send you to pick us up?"

Anticipation showed on the faces of the middle-aged and elderly beastmen.

Lang You: "No, I saw smoke over here and thought something caught fire."

The beastmen's faces fell, and they sat down one after another.

Slow-witted as he was, Lang You could still sense the beastmen's unhappiness. He said, "The King and Qiu have been preparing places for everyone to live for a long time now, and they're also busy storing food. Right now, they're just waiting for you uncles to arrive."

Beastmen were easy to coax; upon hearing those words, the corners of their mouths curled high up.

"Then where are they now?"

"Right here in the Great Marsh."

*

By the Great Marsh, the Bai Que beastmen were rushing to store food and had packed up and left early.

The Green-Eyed beastmen remained here, waiting for Lang Chi's arrival.

Since they weren't leaving, Lang Yan continued to put them to work.

The work of piling up fields was temporarily paused, and it was time to dig lotus roots again.

The lotus roots in the shallow water area had been dug up last year, but no management was done afterward, so this year's lotus roots were clearly not as dense as last year's. At a single glance at this difference, the wolf beastmen understood why Qiu said they needed to farm them themselves.

Fortunately, they hadn't over-harvested. The Great Marsh was full of them everywhere, and digging a few more spots yielded plenty.

The Green-Eyed beastmen had eaten lotus root soup here before and weren't strangers to this thing.

But when their feet sank into the silt, their hands reached down along the lotus leaves, and they touched lotus roots as thick as a forearm, they still couldn't help feeling envious.

Why did the Wolf Tribe have so many good things!

"Splash, splash—"

The Green-Eyed beastmen looked to the side. The Wolf Tribe's little wolves had already fished out a pile.

After being slightly washed clean, the lotus roots were placed neatly on wooden boards, completely devoid of the dirty appearance of growing in silt.

Mimicking the little wolves, they swished the silt-covered lotus roots in the water to wash them clean, revealing nodes of lotus root that were noticeably whiter than their own skin.

"So this part can be eaten too."

"Chieftain, it seems... our tribe used to have these too," Green Jiao said.

Green Tu tightly pinched a half-withered lotus leaf and muttered, "There were plenty of them in the south."

Those lakes, big and small—especially the shallow ones—were completely filled with them. The flowers that bloomed were huge and pretty, and the sub-beastmen liked them very much.

But they didn't know...

They didn't know this thing was edible, nor did they know there was another section hidden underneath.

Had they known earlier...

But how could there be so many "had knowns"?

"Then, are we still staying at the Wolf Tribe?"

He could go catch fish and dry them into fish strips just like the Bai Que beastmen. Not only that, but they could also find a lot of this thing called lotus root, meaning they wouldn't have to worry about the snow season at all.

In an instant, Green Tu reined in all his remorse.

"Stay!"

The past could not be undone, the mistakes had already been made, and they had received their punishment.

Now the male beastmen of the tribe had already been left with lingering illnesses, making it even harder for them to catch prey or feed so many sub-beastmen and cubs.

The Green-Eyed beastmen pulled down lotus leaves to block their sides. Hearing the chieftain's words, they pulled weakly at the corners of their mouths, unable to even muster a smile.

Yes, besides doing these chores, what else could they do?

Go out hunting?

It would be a miracle if they didn't get counter-killed by the prey.

With their current physical ailments, digging mud every day left them crying out in pain at night, unable to sleep—let alone hunt.

*

Harvesting lotus roots was also hard work.

Although the wolf beastmen had diverted the water away from areas with abundant lotus roots beforehand, the silt was too deep to move a single step.

Since the Green-Eyed Tribe wasn't leaving right now, Lang Yan didn't plan to summon more wolf beastmen over.

With everyone working together, they could still dig up plenty in a day.

At noon, a fine drizzle fell like mist, and dark clouds drifted across the sky like black gauze.

The beastmen hauled the lotus roots harvested in the morning up to the bank.

The wild lotus roots hadn't been tended to, but thanks to the fertile silt, they grew quite well.

The tender lotus roots were white, thin-skinned, translucent and tender, snapping apart at the slightest pinch.

The beastmen were thirsty, so they directly washed a few sections of tender lotus roots, snapped them apart, and distributed them among themselves.

Raw lotus root could also be eaten, and its fresh fragrance was even richer.

The Green-Eyed beastmen finished hauling the last batch of roots, sat by the water's edge with drooping shoulders, and crunched on raw lotus roots with great relish.

When the wolf beastmen of the first hunting team hurried over anxiously, Lang Yan was also waiting for them to return from hunting, intending to have them call for beastmen to pull flatbed carts over once they returned to Lang Shan.

"King! Over to the southeast of the Great Marsh, there's a fire! The captain has already taken the beastmen over to check."

"How is there a fire again?!" Lin Qiu and Lang Yan stood up at the same time.

The Green-Eyed beastmen also frowned, straightened up, and looked toward the southeast.

But their line of sight was blocked, and they couldn't see anything.

"We only saw a wisp of smoke rising, no red glow."

Just as Lin Qiu wanted to suggest going to take a look, Green Yue stood up and lowered his voice behind him: "Qiu, I'll go take a look."

Looking back and seeing it was Green Yue, Lin Qiu nodded immediately, "Be careful."

The feathered tribe had wings, making them best suited for reconnaissance.

Lang Yu began arranging the food for the midday meal. With ready-made ingredients, cooking up a batch of lotus root soup was an absolute certainty.

However, as he patted the lotus roots, he couldn't help saying to Lin Qiu: "Qiu, don't worry, it probably won't spread into a big fire."

Lin Qiu: "Mn."

The previous big fire had left lingering fears in their hearts. They couldn't be too careful—better safe than sorry. Only by identifying the fire source could they truly set their minds at ease.

Green Jiao was covered in mud, the mud splatters on his chest already dried.

Only his hands were clean as he held the tip of a tender lotus root, feeding his cub bit by bit.

"A-ba." The cub placed his small hand on the back of Green Jiao's hand and looked in the direction Green Yue had left.

Green Jiao coaxed him softly: "A-ba will be right back."

Green Yue indeed returned very quickly.

The moment he landed, he said: "The smoke has already gone out, and I couldn't find where the fire started."

Lin Qiu's thoughts shifted, and a realization hit him as his gaze met Lang Yan's.

"The branch tribe?"

"Most likely."

Hearing their words, a flash of desolation crossed Green Yue's eyes.

The branch tribe... Were Lang Chi and the others coming back?

If so, there would be no need for them to be here at all.

"A-ba!"

The little cub bumped his small body forward, wrapping both hands tightly around his leg.

Green Yue looked at his exhausted mate. The man was still holding half a section of lotus root with tiny bite marks on it, which his cub had just nibbled.

Green Yue picked up the cub and walked over to Green Jiao's side.

With his back to Lang Yan and Lin Qiu, he looked down at his mate, sorrow etched between his brows.

The cub was turned around by him and went back to nibbling on the lotus root in Green Jiao's hand, unable to see his sorrow, but Green Jiao saw it clearly.

He raised his hand and stroked Green Yue's tightly furrowed brow.

"Don't worry, I'm here."

Even if they couldn't stay at the Wolf Tribe, he wouldn't let his mate and cub go hungry again. Didn't they just learn about another kind of food right now?

Green Yue pressed his lips tight, resting his forehead against the cub's back, feeling utterly lost.

What on earth should their tribe do...

Before the snow season arrived, every tribe felt the urgency of storing food. In past years, they would have been busy by this time too.

But now the Wolf Tribe's attitude was uncertain; the chieftain wanted to stay at the Wolf Tribe, and they could do nothing but wait.

"A-ba?" The cub wanted to turn around. Green Yue tightened his arm and kissed his hair.

He said gently, "Be a good boy, eat slowly."

The cub then hugged his father's hand again, obediently crunching away with his small teeth. With a *crunch, crunch* sound, the cub seemed to have found something fun and ate with gusto.

Green Yue and Green Jiao looked at him, their hearts filled with deep affection, sorrow, and also a trace of relief.

Relieved that he was young and didn't understand matters.

Having followed them through such a turbulent journey, yet being foolishly content—given any food, he would eat it with complete absorption.

His younger brother was gone; after asking a few times and knowing he had gone to another place and wouldn't come back, he stopped asking.

Green Yue stroked his soft hair, a sour ache filling his heart.

They were originally driven out by the branch tribe to begin with; how could those people possibly want the Green-Eyed beastmen to stay at Lang Shan?

Where else could they possibly go?

chapters.title: 第169章
chapters.translated_text:
Hearing that Lang Yan was at the Great Marsh, the beasts of the branch tribe immediately asked Lang You to lead the way.

A dozen wolf beasts helped carry some of their load, and four entire bags of tail grass were piled onto Lang You's back, so heavy that his four legs went soft and he quickly braced himself.

He took a deep breath and said, "I should have known to bring a wooden cart."

Lang Cang walked past Lang You, glanced at him, and said, "Are you useless, kid? Hurry up and lead the way."

Lang You walked into the forest, and the members of the first hunting team who came with him each had things placed on them by the beasts of the branch tribe.

The procession formed a long line, entering the dense jungle.

Fortunately, the beasts of the branch tribe had already been running along the southeast side of the Great Marsh for two days, otherwise Lang You wouldn't have found them so quickly.

In the dim jungle, the remaining beasts, who had just caught a young deer and were waiting for their captain to return, saw the long procession and were so stunned they almost let their prey escape.

"Uncle Chi?"

"Uncle Wan, Uncle Xing... you're all back!"

The wolf beasts eagerly crowded around, and then their backs sank with a heavy load—

They silently carried the tail grass seeds, obediently following behind their captain.

Lang Wan moved his neck, stretched his legs, and easily kept pace among the young wolf group.

To them, captains like Lang You were just young wolves, pups like Lang Jin were just cubs, and little ones like Lang Sheng were ones they hadn't even seen before.

"Ah-You, is your king fishing by the Great Marsh?"

How long had it been since he heard an elder address him like that?

Lang You looked at the white wolf beast with slightly dull fur beside him and said, "Uncle Wan, it's not fishing."

"Then is it hunting?"

"Not that either."

"Then what is it? Hey! Why are you so dawdling, spit it out!"

Lang You was choked up by him.

Was it that he didn't want to talk? It was just that Uncle Wan's mouth was too fast and didn't give him a chance.

He took a deep breath and quickly said, "The King and Qiu are guarding the White Sparrow beasts and Green-Eyed beasts as they dig mud; they are going to reshape the Great Marsh to farm and raise fish in the future."

Lang Wan instantly stopped in his tracks.

Lang You watched him still running forward and almost bumped his head into a tree.

"Green-Eyed beasts?"

"Which Green-Eyed beasts? The Green-Eyed beasts from the south? What are they here for! How could you let them sneak into Wolf Mountain?!"

So your old self only heard those four words.

In an instant, the uncles who had just been sighing and complaining about not being able to walk overtook the first hunting team and headed straight to the front of the procession.

Lang Li walked to Lang You's side, looked at the backs of the branch tribe's beasts, and said in a low voice, "Should we give the King a heads-up beforehand?"

To keep the Green-Eyed beasts and their own elders separated, otherwise, they were afraid of a fight.

Lang You said with a deadpan face, "Can you run ahead of them?"

Lang Li looked at the beasts who were about to disappear from sight and fell silent.

Not carrying these tail grass seeds that were about to crush them to death was fine. But four bags of tail grass seeds on every single beast—he couldn't do it anyway.

"The King will definitely be able to solve it."

Lang Li thought about it and nodded. "The King can solve it."

*

Lang Yan watched the beasts of the branch tribe burst out from the forest. Before he even had time to greet them, he saw them aggressively sweep past the wolf beasts and head straight for the Green-Eyed beasts resting by the shore.

Lang Yan's eyelid twitched.

"I'll teach you to trick the young wolves!"

"I'll teach you to be shameless!"

"Robbing the branch tribe wasn't enough, you still come near the young wolves. We are old, but we aren't dead yet!"

Lang Yan didn't even have time to stop them before the beasts started fighting.

Of course, it was a one-sided beating.

Green Yue fiercely protected his cub, while Green Jiao pulled his mate into his arms to shield him. A fist swung down, striking an old wound on his back, making him grunt in pain and curl up.

But the next moment, Green Yue and the cub in his arms were pulled away.

Green Jiao's eyes turned red, fury surging in his chest, and just as he was about to counterattack, he saw his mate and cub pushed backward by a wolf beast to a safe area.

"We don't hit cubs and sub-beasts."

Green Jiao gritted his teeth, thinking he would just let them beat him.

He knew the branch tribe's hatred toward them.

Lang Yan: "Stop them!"

The young wolves and Lang Yu and the others quickly hugged the waists of their respective elders. If they were in beast form, they hugged their hind legs or pulled their tails, dragging them backward anyway.

Lang Chi's dark gaze landed on Green Ren, and his raised fist was grabbed by two young wolves.

The wolf beasts moved too fast.

Green Ren was the patriarch and took the most beatings, blood spilling from the corner of his mouth.

"Yan, don't tell me you are the one who took them in at the Wolf Tribe."

"Uncle Chi, it was me."

"You—"

"But it's not taking them in."

The wolf beasts grumbled and cursed, while the young wolves hugged them, using sweet words and persuasion until they finally calmed down.

Lang Wan shoved a young wolf away. He squatted in front of this group of Green-Eyed beasts, his eyes fixed tightly on them.

Yes, back then the branch tribe took them in to get through the snow season and then drove them away; it was because they had soft hearts.

But they couldn't come over and trick the young wolves!

The young wolves didn't know what they had done...

"They know," Lang Yan said, looking at his wolf beast elders with some helplessness.

"Knowing, why still keep them!" Lang Cang said angrily.

At this moment, Lang You's team finally crawled out of the forest, panting.

Lin Qiu saw that their waists were bent inward from the heavy load and hurriedly signaled the young wolves to help put the things down first.

A young wolf looked at the wolf leg it was hugging.

Lang Cang jerked his leg away, his dark eyes staring fixedly at the young wolf.

The young wolf smiled sheepishly and let go. "Won't hit, won't hit anymore."

"No more hitting, let go."

The young wolves hurriedly helped the hunting team unload the cargo.

Lang Yan signaled Lang Yu to prepare more food, while he coaxed the beasts on both sides to sit down and explained the situation on the Wolf Tribe's side.

"What? You were robbed by nomad beasts!"

Lin Qiu hurriedly held down Lang Wan, who was so furious he was about to go pick a fight. He hadn't expected this seemingly gentle beast to be so hot-tempered.

He blew up at the slightest touch, like a cannon.

"It's already fine."

Lang Wan looked at him, suddenly raised his hand, and pinched Lin Qiu's cheek hard.

"Little wolf pup! Don't tell me you spoke well of them!" His eyes searched through the pile of Green-Eyed beasts, and catching sight of the single white-furred beast, his eyes narrowed.

Bai Song immediately shrank behind his companions.

Lang Chi scolded, "Stop talking nonsense, Qiu is on great terms with the King."

Lang Wan stared at Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu: "My face hurts, Uncle Wan." As memories flashed back, Lin Qiu remembered when he was young, Lang Chi was always away from the tribe, and he would be chased around by Lang Wan holding a stick.

It was actually quite nostalgic.

Lang Wan snorted, let go of his hand, and seeing that his skin had turned red from just a pinch, he frowned and roughly rubbed it for him instead.

Lang Yan pulled Lin Qiu to his side.

He continued, "There was a wildfire here earlier, and their two tribes fled to the Great Marsh. Exactly as we need to renovate the Great Marsh, we provide food and they do the work, consider it an exchange."

The beasts of the branch tribe stopped talking upon hearing that the Green-Eyed beasts had saved two cubs.

Hearing about the wildfire just now, and thinking of the forest blackened by fire they saw all the way up here, lingering fear gripped their hearts.

They looked at the neatly squared plots of land above the water surface; they didn't understand what Lang Yan and the others were trying to do, but it would certainly be useful.

"An exchange is an exchange then," Lang Wan said in a low voice. "Then when are they leaving?"

It was almost the snow season, and since they were back now, whatever work needed doing they could do themselves.

Even if the Green-Eyed beasts saved the cubs, the Wolf Tribe had repaid them and didn't owe them anything.

The wolf beasts of the branch tribe still held resentment and hostility toward the Green-Eyed Tribe.

They had killed quite a few beasts from the Green-Eyed Tribe and didn't believe the Green-Eyed beasts could let go of the enmity of dozens of clansmen's lives to live in peace and harmony with them.

"About this, I was just going to ask you."

"Ask us for what? Isn't it fine for the King to decide?" Lang Xing said lazily.

Lang Yan looked at Green Ren.

Green Ren repeated what he had previously said to Lang Yan.

Lang Wan stared at the group of cowering Green-Eyed beasts in silence.

Lang Xing pushed the back of his own cub, signaling him to go play with Lang Jin and the others.

He looked at the cub held in Green Yue's arms; this cub was the one he had fished out of the treehouse back then.

Tears welled up in Green Yue's eyes as he stroked the cub's head. He only looked at him gratefully and said nothing.

Lang Xing's head turned away, and the sarcastic words didn't come out.

The sub-beasts and cubs among these Green-Eyed beasts were all pulled out of the Green-Eyed Tribe by them. Their survival relied on fish from their tribe and the fishing nets they provided.

Yet these sub-beasts and cubs were not entirely innocent either.

The male beasts came to steal and rob food, and when they brought it back, wouldn't these ones eat it just the same?

Everyone's gaze fell on Lang Chi.

Lang Chi said in a deep voice, "No."

"We can build our own houses, and we can handle the matters of the Great Marsh ourselves, we don't need you."

Lin Qiu snapped a blade of grass in his hand with a click and let out a soft breath.

The Green-Eyed beasts slumped in despair, and the sounds of low sobbing drifted out.

Lang Yan clapped his hands, stood up, looked at Green Ren, and said, "Thank you for your hard work during this time."

Unable to bear looking at those ignorantly blinking cubs, Lang Chi walked away quickly.

Food was scarce in the snow season; who knew if keeping them in the Wolf Tribe would lead them to rob the tribe a second time due to hunger?

This hidden danger could not be left behind!

Lang Yan was also decisive; since he said to let Lang Chi decide, he let Lang Chi make the call.

The wolf beasts left one after another, and after finding sheds to put their luggage away, the beasts quickly sat down to rest.

This trip back had worn them out thoroughly.

Lang Xing lagged behind, and hearing the fast-approaching footsteps, he stopped.

"Xing."

Lang Xing turned around and looked at the sub-beast who used to sit blankly in a grass nest, guarding a dead cub.

His spirit had recovered, and his complexion looked a bit better.

"Looking for me?"

Green Yue shook his head. "I hadn't said thank you to you yet."

Lang Xing waved a hand. "I didn't do anything."

"No matter what, thank you."

The Wolf Tribe had no reason to take in their tribe, and they should indeed leave.

The Green-Eyed beasts were used to robbing and had eaten too much food obtained for free, always thinking about getting something for nothing.

The patriarch said even if they had to sponge off them, they must stay here.

But Lang Chi and the others had come, shattering their hopes.

Holding the cub, Green Yue watched the sub-beast stride away. He walked with the wind, so dashing and confident.

Only after coming here did he realize that sub-beasts could also work.

The sub-beasts of the Wolf Tribe could work in the water, cook, forage, and even hunt. But they... the sub-beasts of the Green-Eyed Tribe only needed to raise their cubs, guard the tribe, and wait for the male beasts to bring back food.

They relied too heavily on the male beasts.

Now, although the male beasts in their own tribe were injured, all of their sub-beasts were uninjured, healthy, and sound.

If they could stand on their own feet and obtain food like the Wolf Tribe did—without relying on robbery or handouts—that would probably be wonderful too.

The Green Yue of the past might have been afraid, just like the Green Yue who could only stay and hug his dead cub blankly, guarding the treehouse, not daring to ask for help, not daring to look for the male beasts who went out, not daring to do anything.

But now...

Green Yue looked at the cub in his arms.

The hardest times had passed, what could they not do?

Lang Xing was a sub-beast, and he could do it.

He wanted to try it too.

"Let's go," Green Yue returned to his mate's side and said in a low voice.

Green Jiao hugged him, but motioned for him to look at their patriarch.

Green Ren's expectations had fallen through, as if his soul had been sucked out. His gaze grew vacant once more, reverting to the state he was in when he first arrived at the Wolf Tribe.

He seemed to have experienced the sky falling and the earth shattering, with no hopes left, and a dead aura blanketed his face.

"Patriarch..." Green Yue was startled.

"The patriarch is broken." Green Jiao gripped his mate's hand, feeling panic-stricken in his heart.

His fighting spirit was completely gone.

Green Yue squeezed his mate's hand and looked at his companions one by one. They all noticed Green Ren's change; like a body without a spine, sitting limply on the ground, they looked identical to Green Ren.

Green Yue: "Let's go."

They could not afford to delay any longer.

If the others didn't want to survive, he did.

Green Jiao was also at a loss, but suddenly noticing the firmness in his mate's eyes, he snapped back to his senses.

He gripped Green Yue's hand tightly and said, "Alright, let's go."

The patriarch could no longer shoulder responsibilities. Green Jiao looked at his clansmen and said, "Pack your things now, we're leaving immediately."

Beside the stove, Lang Yu saw them moving one after another and raised his voice, "Eat your last meal before leaving, those who worked today."

The Green-Eyed beasts instinctively looked toward their patriarch.

But Green Ren remained sitting in place, his gaze fixed, his mouth seemingly muttering something.

A beast leaned closer to listen.

"Stay, stay..."

The beast's lips trembled as he looked pale-faced at Green Jiao.

Green Jiao said, "Pack your things, we'll set off as soon as we finish eating."

The beasts began to move, sluggishly at first, but now they had a purpose.

They actually didn't have many things left, and whatever they did have had been burned in the wildfire. The more they packed, looking at those scattered bits of animal skins, bones, and fur that were completely useless, the more grief welled up from within.

Bai Song knelt by the grass nest, burying his face in his hands and weeping.

They didn't even have a single animal skin; how were they going to survive the snow season!

"Have some backbone!" Green Jiao slapped him across the back.

Bai Song whimpered, "Jiao, how is the patriarch right now any different from the old, muddle-headed beasts of the tribe in the past? Where can we go now? What about the snow season?"

Green Yue stood at the entrance of the shed, quietly watching him.

"Then try with all your might. Don't always conclude you can't do it before even trying anything."

They had all been like that in the past.

But that wouldn't do!

While the Green-Eyed beasts were busy packing, the beasts of the branch tribe gathered around the stove, watching Lang Yu and the others cook while chatting.

Smelling the fragrance of the meat bones, Lang Wan felt the greedy worm in his stomach being hooked out.

He poked his head out to look at the oily and rich lotus root and bone soup, swallowed his saliva, and said with certainty, "Better than what I make."

Lang Yu laughed until his shoulders shook. "I heard you're in charge of making meat soup in the branch tribe?"

"Who else if not me?"

"You used to burn the roasted meat the worst, why is it you making it, instead of Xing?"

"Who are you looking down on? Could any bad taste be worse than starving?"

Lang Yu gave a light click of his tongue and stopped laughing.

This beast—if you joked with him, he could choke you until you had nothing to say.

"Where's An? Didn't see him come," Lang Wan asked casually.

"An is in charge of the meat soup on Wolf Mountain's side."

"That's good, he's got blessings in the future."

The branch tribe's beasts had no oily nourishment in their stomachs and were craving it badly. But there were still many matters at hand, so they didn't rush to satisfy their stomachs first.

"How many of these lotus roots have been dug?" Lang Chi asked.

When he came to Wolf Mountain last year, he did eat some lotus roots. Stewed in soup they were soft and waxy, stir-fried they were crisp and sweet, though they ran out after just a few days of eating.

Lin Qiu: "We've only just started digging."

Lang Wan: "Then once the Green-Eyed beasts leave... there won't be any beasts digging here?"

"We'll do it," Lang Xing said straightforwardly.

"That works too. Since we're already here, Yan, don't call the young wolves over, just tell them to do whatever they're supposed to do."

With all the beasts of their branch tribe back, anyone could guess the pressure on Wolf Mountain was heavy. If they didn't stockpile more food, they feared it truly wouldn't be enough to eat.

Lang Yan looked at Lin Qiu.

"Why are you looking at Qiu? Could it be you still can't make the call?" Lang Xing said.

Lin Qiu said, "You guys just came back, go up to Wolf Mountain to rest first..."

"We'll rest right here."

"All right then," Lin Qiu agreed.

Taking advantage of the fact that the weather wasn't too cold yet, letting them dig a bit was fine. Once the weather turned cold, they wouldn't be allowed into the water.

Although wolf beasts had strong bodies, the beasts of the branch tribe weren't very young anymore, and having toiled for so long over there, their physical foundations were probably somewhat depleted.

Lin Qiu didn't want them to develop rheumatism issues.

"I heard Lang You talking about White Sparrow earlier, where is White Sparrow?"

"They went back; they also need to busy themselves preparing food for the snow season."

Hearing this, Lang Chi let out a hum.

"Look at White Sparrow, and look at them..." Tribes weaker than them knew how to provide for themselves, yet these ones only knew how to take advantage.

"Alright, stop talking about it," Lang Wan said.

All right and wrong were between the branch tribe and the Green-Eyed Tribe; there was no need to cause further annoyance to the beasts of Wolf Mountain.

"Besides digging lotus roots, we can also take care of that mud along the way. Qiu... Yan, you can teach us when the time comes."

Lang Yan nodded.

Lin Qiu's gaze swept across Lang Xing's face and then turned back to Lang Yan.

Wasn't he the one addressed first just now?

Lang Xing: "What are you looking at? Help me take care of the cub."

Lin Qiu looked at the cub hiding behind Lang Xing all this time; its beast form was similar to Lang Xue's, a small black wolf.

Lin Qiu: "Should we send it back to the tribe?"

"No need, let him adapt here first."

"Fine."

Lin Qiu still felt something was off.

"Let him follow Yu, I'm going down to dig lotus roots."

Lang Xing frowned. "Dig what dig, it's so dirty, you're not allowed in the water!"

Lin Qiu understood.

The uncles of the branch tribe were so indulgent toward him...

Combined with his memories, he had reason to suspect that the original Lang Qiu's personality was, to a certain extent, spoiled by the beasts.

"Then you guys aren't going back to Wolf Mountain first?"

"Go back for what? There's so much to do, let's do it first." They hadn't come back to eat free meals; the Green-Eyed beasts had been driven away by them, so the remaining work had to be taken over by someone.

Old fogies like them couldn't run fast enough to hunt, and their eyes were blind for foraging, so digging lotus roots and mud in the murky water fit them just right.

And so the matter was settled.

The soup was almost done simmering, and Lang Yu stir-fried another dish of sliced meat with wild vegetables. For the beasts of the branch tribe, this meal could be considered very sumptuous.

Lang Yu called everyone to eat and also shouted toward that row of sheds in the back.

Green Yue and Green Jiao brought the cubs out first, with the clansmen following behind them. Bai Song mingled right in the middle supporting Green Ren, his head lowered as far as it could go.

"Hmph." Seeing him, Lang Chi wished he could strangle him to death.

If not for him tricking the cubs, how could Qiu have made such a mistake!

The Green-Eyed Tribe even claimed they banished him.

Look, had their words ever counted for anything?

Out of sight, out of mind, the branch tribe's beasts stood up one after another to find their eating bowls and chopsticks from their luggage.

Lang Yu sighed and waved at the hesitant Green-Eyed beasts.

"Come quickly."

A few sub-beasts quickly dished up meat soup for them and scooped stir-fried dishes, and the Green-Eyed beasts immediately retreated back to that row of sheds in the back.

In this front row, only Green Yue and his cub remained.

Lang Chi and the others had also returned and were now lining up to ladle soup.

After taking a sip of that lotus root and bone soup, Lang Wan pursed his lips and cast an admiring look at Lang Yu.

"Good taste."

Lang Yu chuckled with a hum. "Of course."

Lang Wan: "Don't get cocky just because I praised you, or else I won't praise you anymore."

"Tsk! As if I care."

Where had the branch tribe's beasts ever eaten such good food? Whenever they boiled soup, they threw all ingredients into a pot together. Sometimes the fish meat fell apart, mixing with the boiled-to-mush wild vegetables, and they only added a little salt—the taste was truly bitter and fishy.

They couldn't even stew soup well, let alone stir-fry.

At this, everyone stopped grumbling and simply buried their heads in fierce eating.

Lin Qiu lagged behind to ladle soup. Turning back to find a spot, he noticed Green Yue looking over at him with a plea in his eyes.

Lin Qiu walked closer and said in a low voice, "Is there anything you need help with?"

Putting aside the complex relationship between the two tribes, Lin Qiu actually quite liked the sub-beast Green Yue.

He had a gentle temper and was methodical in what he did. Perhaps because he had relied more on his mate in the past, he appeared somewhat fragile at times.

This was different from the sub-beasts he understood.

Or rather, the sub-beasts of the Green-Eyed Tribe were different from those of other tribes; they were better protected by their male beasts and only needed to raise cubs, yet they lacked much survival capability.

Upon hearing Lin Qiu's words, a hint of bitterness crept into Green Yue's smile.

"I haven't even said it yet... and you already know I have something."

"Then spit it out."

Immediately, the branch tribe's beasts slowed down their wolfing-down motions and perked up their ears to listen.

Green Yue: "I want to borrow a fishing net."

Lang Xing looked at Lang Wan.

Lang Wan was biting down on a piece of lotus root, chewing fiercely.

Why was he looking at him? The sub-beast wasn't asking him.

But the next moment, Lang Wan felt the gaze falling on him, raised his head, and locked eyes directly with Lin Qiu.

"Uncle Wan."

"Tsk, Lang Chi." Lang Wan shot a glare like a knife toward Lang Chi.

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Chi again.

Lang Chi wanted to click his tongue too.

"Borrow it," he said in a depressed tone.

The youngster always sided with outsiders.

Lin Qiu smiled at Green Yue. "Borrow it. But our tribe has exchanged some fishing nets away, the ones left are all old and torn nets—do you know how to mend them?"

"Yes! We do," Green Yue said immediately, so excited he almost poked the cub's mouth.

"Just take ours directly," Lang Wan said.

Lang Chi stared at him.

Lang Wan turned slightly sideways, acting as if he didn't see it.

Lang Chi: The little ones learn from the big ones, they're all the same!

Having asked this question, Green Yue stopped asking further.

Lin Qiu thought he might also want to ask about ways to keep warm during the snow season, but he only ate the meat soup in his bowl quickly and didn't speak again.

So Lin Qiu stopped bringing it up either.

They were all adult beasts, unlike young wolves or little ones like Lang Sheng who only knew how to laugh foolishly all day long.

In view of the fact that they had saved the cubs, he would help where he could.

After finishing that midday meal, the Green-Eyed Tribe, led by Green Jiao, prepared to leave.

"Which way are you heading?" Lin Qiu went to see them off and spoke with Green Yue.

"South."

"The south is a bit easier to get through the snow season, that's good."

Green Yue's eyes were red as he smiled. He said softly, "Thank you for taking care of us during this time."

If not for the Wolf Tribe, they wouldn't have known how to survive after the wildfire.

Lin Qiu shook his head instead. "You helped us work, it was only right."

Green Yue stopped by the edge of the Great Marsh. "Then we're leaving."

"Safe journey."

Green Yue savored those words and raised a smile. "Thank you."

His smile was very gentle and also very firm.

It was very different from when he first arrived at the Wolf Tribe—like something had propped up his spine, and he was no longer fragile and helpless.

As per custom, the wolf beasts still had to escort them until they left the Wolf Tribe's territory.

Calling it an escort was also surveillance.

Lang You followed them, heading west first, and then they left the Wolf Tribe from the southwest direction, traveling south.

Lin Qiu didn't know if they would ever run into the Green-Eyed Tribe again in the future, but he hoped that what the Wolf Tribe had displayed would be useful for their future survival.

The beast world was harsh, and life was not easy.

Hopefully, they could find their own way to live.
