支部落的兽人听说狼岩在大泽，当即让狼游带路。
十几头狼兽人帮着分担一点东西，狼游背上压下来整整四袋尾巴草，重得他四条腿一软，连忙撑起来。
他深吸一口气，道：“早知道应该带板车来。”
狼藏路过狼游，瞥他一眼道：“你小子是不是不行？赶紧带路。”
狼游往林子里走，跟他来的狩猎一队的成员们，每个身上都被支部落的兽人们放了东西。
队伍如长龙，进入茂密的丛林。
好在支部落的兽人已经沿着大泽东南边跑了两天，不然狼游还没这么快找到他们。
丛林阴暗，抓到一头呦呦兽，等着自家队长回来的其余兽人们看到那长长的队伍，愣得差点放跑手里的猎物。
“赤叔？”
“晚叔，星叔……你们都回来了！”
狼兽人们高兴得凑上去，然后背上一重——
他们默默扛着尾巴草籽，乖乖跟在他们队长后头。
狼晚动了动脖子，抻了抻腿儿，轻轻松松跟在小狼队伍中。
对他们来说，狼游这些个队长就是小狼，狼金那些小狼就是幼崽，而狼生这些小的，他们甚至都没见过。
“阿游啊，你们王在大泽边捞鱼吗？”
多久没听到长辈这么叫他了。
狼游看着身侧毛色略暗淡的白狼兽人，道：“晚叔，不是捕鱼。”
“那是捕猎？”
“也不是。”
“那是什么？哎呀！你怎么磨磨唧唧的，你倒是说啊！”
狼游被他噎了一下。
他是不想说吗？是晚叔的嘴巴太快了，不给他机会。
他深吸一口气，快速道：“王和楸在守着白雀兽人和绿眼兽人挖泥巴，他们要改造大泽，以后用来种地和养鱼。”
狼晚顿时停下脚步。
狼游看着他还在往前跑，差点一头撞树。
“绿眼兽人？”
“哪个绿眼兽人，我们南边过去的绿眼兽人？他们来干什么！怎么能让他们混进狼山来？！”
敢情您老就听到这四个字。
霎时，刚刚还唉声叹气嚷嚷着走不动的阿叔们越过狩猎一队，直奔到队伍前头去。
狼力走到狼游身边，看着支部落兽人们的背影，低声道：“要不要提前跟王说一声？”
把绿眼兽人和自家长辈们隔开，不然怕打架。
狼游木着脸道：“你能跑到他们前头去吗？”
狼力看着快不见身影的兽人们，不吭声了。
他们不背这些快把他们压死的尾巴草籽，可以。但每个兽人身上四袋尾巴草籽，他反正不行。
“王肯定能解决。”
狼力想想，点头，“王能解决。”
*
狼岩看着从林子里蹿出来的支部落的兽人，还没来得及迎接，就看他们气势冲冲掠过狼兽人们，直奔坐在岸边休息的绿眼兽人去。
狼岩眼皮一跳。
“我让你们哄骗小狼！”
“让你们不要脸！”
“抢了支部落还不够，又接近小狼，我们是老了不是死了！”
狼岩甚至没来得及阻止，兽人们就打起来了。
当然，是单方面殴打。
绿月猛地护住自己幼崽，绿皎又拉着自己伴侣护在怀里。拳头抡下来，打在背上旧伤处，疼得他闷哼着蜷缩起来。
可下一瞬，怀里的绿月和幼崽被拉了出去。
绿皎眼一红，胸腔怒意翻滚，正要反击，就看到自家伴侣和幼崽被狼兽人往后一推，推到安全地带。
“我们不打幼崽和亚兽人。”
绿皎咬着牙，想着就任由他们打了。
他知道支部落对他们的恨。
狼岩：“阻止他们！”
小狼们和狼雨他们赶紧抱住自家长辈的腰，是兽形的就抱他们后腿儿，扯尾巴，反正要把他们往后拉。
狼赤黑沉沉的目光落在在绿壬身上，举起的拳头被两个小狼抱住。
狼兽人动手太快。
绿壬是族长，挨打最多，嘴角都溢出血来。
“岩，你别跟我说，是你收留他们在狼部落的。”
“赤叔，是我。”
“你——”
“但不是收留。”
狼兽人们骂骂咧咧，小狼们抱着他们，好说歹说，才让他们消停。
狼晚一把推开小狼，他蹲坐在这群绿眼兽人面前，眼睛紧紧盯着他们。
是，当初支部落收留他们熬过了雪季，又驱赶走他们，是他们心软了。
但他们不能过来骗小狼！
小狼不知道他们做的事……
“知道。”狼岩道，他看着自家这些狼兽人长辈们，有些无奈。
“知道为什么还要留他们！”狼藏气道。
这时候，狼游小队才气喘吁吁从林子里挪出来。
林楸看他们腰都压得塌下去一截，赶紧示意小狼们一起把东西先放下来。
小狼看着自己抱住的狼腿儿。
狼藏抽了抽腿，眼睛黑漆漆地盯着小狼。
小狼嘿嘿笑着松开，“不打，不打了啊。”
“不打了，松开。”
小狼们赶紧帮着狩猎队卸货。
狼岩示意狼雨多准备点食物，他则安抚两边兽人坐下来，也把狼部落这边的情况说了说。
“什么？你们被流浪兽人抢了！”
林楸忙按住愤怒得就要去干架的狼晚，他没想到这个看起来温和的兽人这么暴躁。
一点就炸，火炮似的。
“已经没事了。”
狼晚看看他，忽然抬手，紧紧捏住林楸的脸颊。
“小狼崽子！别是你给他们说了好话！”他眼睛在绿眼兽人堆里寻找，瞧见那唯有一个的白毛兽人，眼睛一眯。
白松立刻缩在同伴后头。
狼赤斥道：“别胡说八道，楸跟王好着呢。”
狼晚盯着林楸。
林楸：“脸疼，晚叔。”记忆乍现，林楸想起幼时狼赤总不在部落，他被狼晚抓着棍子追着跑的情形。
还挺亲切。
狼晚哼声，松开手，见他脸皮被这么一捏就红了，皱了皱眉，又胡乱给他揉了揉。
狼岩将林楸拉到自己身边来。
他继续道：“之前这边出现山火，他们两个部落逃到大泽。正好我们需要把大泽修整一下，我们给食物，他们干活，算是交换。”
支部落的兽人在听到绿眼兽人救了两个幼崽后就没说话了。
这会儿又听到山火，想到一路上来，看到那被火烧得发黑的林子，心中后怕。
他们又瞧着水面上方方正正的地块，不明白狼岩他们要干什么，但总归有用。
“交换就交换吧。”狼晚低声道，“那他们什么时候走？”
这都快雪季了，他们又回来了，有什么活儿他们自己干。
绿眼兽人就算救了幼崽，狼部落也回报了，不欠他们。
支部落的狼兽人对绿眼部落还是有怨，有敌意。
他们弄死了不少绿眼部落的兽人，也不觉得绿眼兽人能放下几十条族人性命的仇，跟他们友好相处。
“这事，正要问问你们。”
“问我们干什么？王决定不就好了。”狼星慢悠悠道。
狼岩看向绿壬。
绿壬把之前跟狼岩说过的话再说了一遍。
狼晚盯着一群畏畏缩缩的绿眼兽人不语。
狼星推推自己幼崽后背，示意他找狼金他们玩儿去。
他看向绿月怀中抱着的幼崽，这个幼崽还是当初他从树屋中捞下来的。
绿月眼里蓄泪，摸摸幼崽脑袋，只感激地看了看他，什么也没说。
狼星脑袋一转，讽刺的话没说出来。
这些绿眼兽人里的亚兽人和幼崽都是他们从绿眼部落拎出来的。他们活下来，靠着他们部落的鱼，还有他们给的渔网。
可这些亚兽人和幼崽也并不无辜。
雄兽人来偷抢食物，带回去他们还不是一样会吃。
大家的目光落在狼赤身上。
狼赤沉声道：“不行。”
“房子我们自己会建，大泽的事我们自己会做，用不着你们。”
林楸啪嗒一下扯断了手里一根草，他轻轻呼出一口气。
绿眼兽人们颓然，还有低泣声传出来。
狼岩拍了拍手，起身，看着绿壬道：“这段时间辛苦你们。”
狼赤不忍看那些眼神懵懂的幼崽，快步离开了这里。
雪季食物稀缺，谁知道留他们在狼部落，他们会不会因为饥饿第二次抢劫部落。
这个隐患不能留！
狼岩也干脆，说让狼赤决定，就让狼赤决定。
狼兽人陆续离去，兽人们找棚子放好行李，赶紧坐下来歇一歇。
这一趟回来，可把他们累得够呛。
狼星落在后头，听到快步跟来的脚步声，停了下来。
“星。”
狼星回头，看着这个之前枯坐草窝中，守着死去幼崽的亚兽人。
他的精神恢复了，气色也好了些。
“找我有事？”
绿月摇摇头，“还没跟你说一声谢谢。”
狼星摆手，“我没做什么。”
“不管怎么样，还是谢谢。”
狼部落没有收留他们部落的必要，他们是该走。
绿眼兽人抢习惯了，也吃多了白来的食物，总想着不劳而获。
族长说赖也要赖在这里。
可狼赤他们来了，他们的希望破灭。
绿月抱着幼崽，看着亚兽人大步离去，他走路带风，那么潇洒自信。
他来了这里，才意识到亚兽人也可以干活的。
狼部落的亚兽人可以下水劳作，可以做饭，可以采集，甚至可以捕猎。可他们……绿眼部落的亚兽人只需要养好幼崽，守好部落，只等雄兽人带回食物就好了。
他们太依赖雄兽人了。
如今自家部落里雄兽人虽伤了，但他们亚兽人都无病无伤，身体健康。
要是他们能立起来，能像狼部落一样不靠抢，不靠施舍，获得食物，那应该也很好。
以前的绿月或许会怕，就像那个幼崽死了，却只能呆呆抱着他，守在树屋里，不敢去求救，不敢去找外出的雄兽人，什么都不敢的绿月。
可是现在……
绿月看着怀中幼崽。
最难的时候都过去了，还有什么不能的。
狼星是亚兽人，他可以。
自己也想试试。
“走吧。”绿月回到自己伴侣身边，低声道。
绿皎抱了抱他，却示意他看向他们的族长。
绿壬的期待落空，如同被抽走了神，目光又变得空洞，成了刚开始来狼部落的模样。
他仿佛经历了天塌地陷，再没了期望，脸上弥漫着一股死气。
“族长……”绿月心惊。
“族长废了。”绿皎握紧伴侣的手，心中惶惶。
他的心气彻底没了。
绿月攥紧伴侣的手，又一一看向同伴们。他们都注意到了绿壬的变化，如同没了主心骨，跌坐在地上的样子与绿壬一般无二。
绿月：“走吧。”
由不得他们再耽搁了。
他们不想活命，他想。
绿皎也六神无主，可骤然注意到伴侣眼底的坚定，猛地回了神。
他紧紧握住绿月的手，道：“好，我们走。”
族长担不起事了，绿皎看向族人们，道：“现在去收拾东西，我们马上离开。”
灶旁，狼雨看他们陆陆续续动了，扬声道：“吃完最后一顿再走，今天干了活儿的。”
绿眼兽人们下意识看向他们族长。
可绿壬依旧坐在原地，目光发直，口中似念着什么。
有兽人凑近了听。
“留、留下……”
兽人唇一哆嗦，脸色苍白地看向绿皎。
绿皎道：“收拾东西，吃完就出发。”
兽人们动了起来，虽迟缓，但有了目的。
他们其实没多少东西，有的也在山火中被烧了。越是收拾，看着那些根本不顶用的零零散散的兽皮、骨头和绒毛，越发悲从中来。
白松跪在草窝边捂脸哭。
他们连一张兽皮都没有，雪季怎么能熬得过去！
“出息！”绿皎一巴掌拍在他背上。
白松呜咽：“皎，族长现在这个样子跟部落以前傻了的老兽人有什么区别。我们现在能去哪里？雪季怎么办？”
绿月站在棚子入口，静静看着他。
“那就拼尽全力一试，别总什么都没做，就笃定自己不行。”
他们以前都是这样的。
但这样不行！
绿眼兽人忙着收拾东西的时候，支部落的兽人们围在灶台这边，一边看着狼雨他们做饭，一边说话。
狼晚闻着那肉骨头香，肚里馋虫被勾了出来。
他探头看，瞧着那汤色油润的莲藕骨头汤，咽了咽口水，肯定道：“比我做得好。”
狼雨笑得抖肩，“听说你在支部落负责做肉汤？”
“除了我还有谁？”
“你以前烤肉烤得最糊，怎么就你做，不是星去做？”
“看不起谁？再难吃能有饿肚子难受？”
狼雨轻啧一声，不笑了。
这兽人，跟他说笑，他能堵得你开不了口。
“安呢？没见着他来？”狼晚随口问。
“安负责狼山那边的肉汤。”
“挺好，以后有福了。”
支部落兽人肚里没油水，馋得厉害。但眼前还有不少事，让他们没急着顾肚子。
“这些藕挖了多少了？”狼赤问。
他去年来狼山，可是吃了些藕。炖汤软糯，清炒脆甜，不过没吃几天就没了。
林楸：“才开始挖。”
狼晚：“那绿眼兽人们一走……这边没兽人挖了？”
“我们来吧。”狼星直截了当道。
“也行，反正都到这儿了，岩你也别叫小狼们过来了，叫他们该干什么干什么。”
他们支部落的兽人都回来了，想想都知道狼山的压力大。不多囤点食物，怕真不够吃。
狼岩看向林楸。
“你看楸干什么？难不成你还做不了主？”狼星道。
林楸道：“你们才回来，先去狼山休息休息……”
“就在这休息。”
“那行吧。”林楸应下。
趁着现在天气还不算冷，让他们挖一挖也可以。等天凉了，就不能让他们下水了。
虽说狼兽人身体强健，但支部落的兽人们年纪都不小了，在那边又操劳那么久，身体底子怕是有些亏空。
林楸不想让他们又落下个风湿的毛病。
“之前还听到狼游说白雀，白雀呢？”
“回去了，他们也要忙着准备雪季的食物。”
狼赤闻言哼了一声。
“看看白雀，再看看他们……”比他们弱小的部落都知道自食其力，偏他们只知道占便宜。
“行了，别说了。”狼晚道。
各中是非，都是支部落跟绿眼部落的，不必再让狼山的兽人们心烦。
“除了挖藕，那泥巴我们也顺带弄一弄，楸……岩，你到时候教一教我们。”
狼岩点头。
林楸目光从狼星面上划过，又看向狼岩。
刚刚不是先叫的他？
狼星：“看什么看，帮我带幼崽。”
林楸看向那个一直藏在狼星身后的幼崽，兽形跟狼雪差不多，是一只小黑狼。
林楸：“要不要送回部落去？”
“不用，让他先在这边适应适应。”
“行吧。”
林楸还是觉得哪里不对劲。
“让他跟着雨，我还要下去挖藕。”
狼星眉头一皱，“挖什么挖，那么脏，不许下水！”
林楸懂了。
支部落的阿叔们对他好纵容啊……
结合记忆，他有理由怀疑，原来的狼楸那性格，有几分也是兽人们纵出来的。
“那你们不先回一趟狼山？”
“回什么回，事这么多，先做。”他们回来不是吃白饭的，绿眼兽人被他们赶走了，剩下的活儿总得有兽人接手。
他们这群老家伙捕猎跑不动，采集眼睛瞎，正好浑水里挖藕和挖泥巴。
事儿就这么定下了。
汤炖煮得差不多了，狼雨又炒了个肉片炒野菜。这顿对支部落的兽人来说，可以算得上很丰盛了。
狼雨招呼吃饭，也冲着后头那一排棚子喊了一声。
绿月和绿皎先带着幼崽出来，族人跟在他们身后，白松混在最中间搀扶着绿壬，脑袋低得不能再低。
“哼。”狼赤看见他，恨不得把他掐死。
要不是他拐骗幼崽，楸怎会做下那样的错事！
绿眼部落还说驱逐他。
看看，他们说话算过数吗？
支部落的兽人眼不见心不烦，纷纷起身，去自己的行李里找吃饭的碗筷。
狼雨叹气，冲着踟蹰的绿眼兽人招手。
“快来。”
几个亚兽人快速给他们盛了肉汤，又夹了炒菜，绿眼兽人立刻回到了后头那排棚子里。
前面这一排，只留下绿月和他的幼崽。
狼赤他们也回来了，这会儿各自排队，打汤。
待喝上那一口莲藕骨头汤，狼晚抿了抿唇，佩服地看了一眼狼雨。
“好滋味。”
狼雨哼笑，“那是。”
狼晚：“夸你别翘尾巴，不然我不想夸。”
“嘁！当我稀罕。”
支部落的兽人哪里吃过这样的好东西，他们煮汤都是一锅食材全部一起放。有时候鱼肉散了，混着煮得烂了的野菜，里面就放了点盐，那滋味真是又苦又腥。
炖汤都炖不好，更别说炒了。
这下大家也不哼哼了，一味地埋头苦吃。
林楸落在后头盛汤，他回头找位置，瞧着绿月看来，眼里带着请求。
林楸走近，低声说：“有什么需要帮忙的吗？”
抛开两个部落之间复杂的关系，林楸其实挺喜欢绿月这个亚兽人。
他脾气温和，做事也有条理。或许是以前更多依赖自己的伴侣，所以有时候柔弱了些。
这跟他理解的亚兽人不一样。
或者说，绿眼部落的亚兽人跟其他部落的亚兽人都不一样，他们被雄兽人保护得更好，只需要养育幼崽就行，却也没多少生存的能力。
绿月一听林楸的话，笑容多了几分苦涩。
“我还没说呢……你就知道我有事。”
“那就说说。”
顿时，支部落的兽人放慢刨食的动作，竖着耳朵听着。
绿月：“我想，借一下渔网。”
狼星看向狼晚。
狼晚叼着一块莲藕，狠狠咬了一口。
看他干什么，亚兽人又不是问他。
可紧接着，狼晚感觉到落到身上的视线，抬头一瞧，正对上林楸。
“晚叔。”
“啧，狼赤。”狼晚眼刀子甩向狼赤。
林楸又看向狼赤。
狼赤也想啧一下。
“借。”他气闷道。
幼崽总是胳膊肘往外拐。
林楸笑看着绿月，“借。不过我们部落交换出去一些渔网，剩的都是旧网和破网，你们会补吗？”
“会！我们会。”绿月立刻道，他激动得险些戳到幼崽嘴巴。
“直接拿我们的去。”狼晚道。
狼赤盯着他。
狼晚微微侧身，当没看见。
狼赤：小的就是跟大的学的，都一个样！
绿月问过这话，就不再继续问了。
林楸以为他还想问问雪季保暖的方式，可他却只快速吃着碗里的肉汤，没有继续开口。
林楸便也不再提。
他们都是成年兽人，总不是小狼或者狼生那些幼崽那样，一天只知道傻乐呵。
看在他们救了幼崽的份儿上，能帮的他也会帮。
吃过中午那顿饭，绿眼部落在绿皎的带领下，就要走了。
“你们往哪边去？”林楸去送，跟绿月说话。
“往南。”
“南边雪季好过一点，也好。”
绿月红着眼，笑了起来。他轻声道：“这段日子，谢谢你们照顾。”
要没有狼部落，山火过后，他们都不知道怎么活。
林楸却摇头，道：“你们帮我们干活，都是应该的。”
绿月停在大泽边，“那我们走了。”
“一路顺风。”
绿月品了品这话，扬起笑来，“谢谢。”
他笑得很温柔，也很坚定。
与他刚来狼部落时很不一样，像有东西撑起了脊梁，不再柔弱无依。
照例，还是得狼兽人们送他们，直到他们离开狼部落领地。
话说是送，也是监视。
狼游跟着他们，先往西，然后他们从西南方向离开狼部落，往南而行。
林楸不知道以后还会不会再遇见绿眼部落，但他希望，狼部落这边展露出来的东西，会对他们以后的生存有用。
兽世艰难，生命不易。
但愿他们能找到自己的活法。

chapters.translated_text:
Lin Qiu followed the nearest vine.

"Leaves opposite or in whorls of three, triangular-ovate shape, seven to nine veins branching out from the leaf base..."

Lin Qiu matched the characteristics of the yam with the plant in front of him one by one.

"Dig."

Lang Mo immediately blocked Lin Qiu, shaking his head vigorously, "You really can't eat that. The Priest doesn't allow us to touch the 'itchy root'."

Lin Qiu: "Why?"

"You forgot..." As he spoke, he remembered that Lin Qiu had damaged his brain and really had forgotten, so he had to explain it to him.

"A long, long time ago, the first ones we discovered were the round itchy roots. Eating them raw makes your mouth numb, but the cubs and sub-beasts really liked them roasted... At first, there were no problems, but later everyone brought back more itchy roots, including the long ones. As a result, that time, many sub-beasts died directly, and the cubs also..."

"Anyway, after that, the Priest decreed that no one is allowed to touch this again."

Lin Qiu: "Are you sure it was eating this that caused the accident?"

Lang Mo: "These are all things the gathering team collects often."

Lin Qiu: "Is it possible that they collected the wrong thing?"

Lang Mo didn't know; this happened many years ago, before he was even born.

"No, you have to ask the Priest before you can dig it up." His attitude was firm.

Lin Qiu: "Then can I dig it up and ask the Priest if it's okay?"

Lang Mo hesitated, poking the ground with a wooden stick.

The soil layer was loose and almost entirely humus, extremely fertile. This yam had been growing for who knows how many years; the vine was as thick as a finger.

Lin Qiu: "It's settled then."

He bypassed Lang Mo, first using a wooden stick to scrape away the layer of loose soil covering the vine, and after clearing it, he began to dig with the stick.

Lang Mo paced around Lin Qiu, constantly looking toward Lang Shan (Wolf Mountain).

Lin Qiu: "Help me."

Lang Mo: "Let's get this straight first: you are not allowed to eat it without asking the Priest!"

Lin Qiu: "I know."

Yams are not easy to dig out. Following the vine down, it wasn't until nearly a meter deep that they saw the top of the yam. Both of their wooden sticks had split, and finally, fearing that it would be dark before they left the forest, Lang Mo transformed into his wolf form and dug with his claws.

Those sharp claws hooked out chunks as long as Lin Qiu's finger. The paw pads were larger than his palms, and the pile of dirt behind the wolf's butt grew at a visible rate.

Lin Qiu moved the soil behind him, while Lang Mo buried his head and dug away with a grunt.

After digging down another meter or so, Lang Mo sat on the ground and shook the mud from his claws, "That's enough."

Lin Qiu took a look, "Not yet, there's at least half left underneath."

"How do you know? Have you dug it before?" The wolf head turned over, tongue lolling out like a big dog.

Lin Qiu: "No, I can tell just by looking."

Lang Mo: "Why is it so deep?"

He shifted his butt, spat out the mud in his mouth with a few 'pfft' sounds, and started digging again with a grunt.

Lin Qiu reminded him while moving the soil, "Try not to break it."

...

Lang Shan.

The grass in the fields had already been cleared, and in the wide black soil, the delicate seedlings looked very fragile.

The beastmen were worried, so they could only continue to guard them.

The vines from the forest had all been transported back to Lang Shan. Lang An led the tribe's sub-beasts to use up the batch of vines Lin Qiu had brought back, and adding the original two, there were a total of eight fish traps.

Lang Shi lay on the ground, and seeing that Lang Mo was not in the team transporting the vines, and Lin Qiu was also missing, he asked about it.

Lang Xi: "Mo is following Qiu in the forest, digging up dirt."

He had gone to look; the dirt was piled so high that Lang Mo's entire wolf body could be hidden in the pit.

"What's the point of digging dirt? It's almost dark, and it's not safe in the forest."

Lang Shi stood up, intending to go take a look, when two dirty beastmen returned.

Lin Qiu was fine, only his hands and animal skin clothes were dirty.

Lang Mo looked like he had rolled in the mud; his entire coat was covered in it, changing his color. He wasn't a black wolf anymore, but a brown one.

Both beastmen looked a bit exhausted, carrying wooden sticks.

When they reached Lang Shan, Lang Mo flopped onto the ground, and Lin Qiu, carrying his basket of fruit and the yam, moved over and sat down to catch his breath.

"What did you two go do?" Lang Shi and Lang Xi approached, their eyes falling on the wooden sticks.

"What is this?"

A wolf claw hooked it, and white sap immediately seeped out.

Lang Xi shook his claw and quickly wiped it on the ground.

"Itchy root?"

"Why did you dig this up? If the Priest finds out, you're going to get in trouble."

Lang Shi poked at it, intending to throw it away.

Lin Qiu immediately said: "Wait! It was hard to dig up."

Lang Shi: "Qiu, do you want to eat this?"

Lin Qiu: "I have a use for it; I'll ask the Priest before doing anything."

Lang Shi then relaxed his claws, and disgusted by the dirt all over Lang Mo, he turned and went to lie down further away.

The bonfire was lit, the night sky was clear, and the stars spread across the entire firmament above their heads.

Lang Mo was so tired he lay on the ground, and before long, he was snoring softly. His front paws twitched from time to time, the mud-caked claws hooking into the green grass.

Lin Qiu watched from afar as Lang Yan led the returning team, a huge curved-horn beast in the middle of the group.

The beastmen in the tribe clearly saw it too and were cheering, when suddenly two beastmen ran out of the group, carrying an unconscious beastman toward the Priest's cave.

The cheering of the beastmen suddenly fell silent, and they all stood up. Like a school of fish under attack, they were somewhat panicked.

"King, what happened to Lang You?"

Lang Yan swept his gaze over his tribesmen, and seeing Lin Qiu sitting behind a beastman, covered in mud, his eyes paused for a moment before looking away.

"He was gored while capturing the curved-horn beast."

"Clean up the prey first, I'm going to take a look."

The beastmen looked toward the cave with worry, but Lang Yan's words were immediately carried out by the others.

The beastmen skillfully slaughtered the prey. The curved-horn beast looked even bigger than the last one, but no one in the tribe had a smile on their face.

By the bonfire, everyone was quiet.

Lang An continued to lead a group of beastmen to peel the vines, Lang Shi oversaw the slaughtering, and the hunters and gatherers who had returned handed over the food and lay on the ground to rest.

Everyone's heads were turned toward Lang Shan, looking worriedly at the cave lit by firelight.

Seeing this, Lin Qiu picked up the yam and the fruit in the basket and quietly headed toward the Priest's cave.

The fire in the cave was burning brighter than ever.

On the Priest's wooden board, the beastman was laid flat. Lang Yan stood beside him, watching the Priest examine him.

Lang Bing was there too.

Lin Qiu softened his footsteps as he approached. Lang Yan tilted his head slightly, and seeing Lin Qiu enter, he noticed the yam in his hand was a bit of a hindrance, so he took it and set it aside.

The whole process was silent; no one spoke.

Lin Qiu looked at the beastman lying on the board.

There was a large bruise on his chest, which had already swollen up. The Priest looked serious and first told Lang Bing to feed the beastman a bowl of soup mixed with medicinal powder.

Then he felt carefully along the beastman's bones, and after a long while, he let out a sigh of relief.

"It's okay, nothing is broken."

Beastmen have excellent recovery abilities; as long as the injury isn't life-threatening, it can slowly heal with medicine.

Fortunately, the Wolf Tribe was one of the largest on the Beast God Continent, and the line of Priests had never been broken. Over the years, medical knowledge had accumulated through generations, and they could treat most major and minor injuries.

The beastman had fainted, so the injury was not light.

It could not be ruled out that his internal organs might have suffered an impact.

But current medical skills had not reached the point of being able to open up the body, so the Priest could only use medicine and wait, observing the beastman's subsequent reactions.

After checking, the Priest had Lang Bing pick some herbs for external injuries from the wooden rack, mash them into a paste, and apply it to the beastman's chest.

Then he picked and chose among the herbs himself, mixed a new batch, and put them in an earthenware pot to boil.

After finishing, the Priest wiped his hands and looked over.

Seeing that Lin Qiu had arrived at some point, he was about to ask when he saw the yam, which was as tall as a beastman, placed to the side.

"You went to dig up itchy roots?"

Lin Qiu: "It's good stuff."

"You dare to dig up anything! You'll be sorry when your whole body is itching later." The Priest said, walking over to the yam.

Remembering a past event, a hidden pain flashed in his heart, and he sighed: "You forgot about this, and I don't blame you, but itchy roots cannot be eaten."

Lin Qiu had already learned the situation from Lang Mo, so he naturally knew what the old Priest was talking about.

He said: "They can be eaten, they are delicious."

"You ate them?!" The old Priest's drooping eyes widened, and he hurried over with his wooden staff, as if to inspect Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu: "No, I've eaten them before."

Lang Yan looked at Lin Qiu's profile, his voice low: "Don't eat just anything."

Lin Qiu: "I heard about that incident from Lang Mo. I am certain this one is edible and delicious. But the round itchy root is more dangerous."

This incident happened when the old Priest was still young. At that time, the previous Priest had just passed away, and he hadn't learned many of the things left behind. The beastmen were hungry, and when they couldn't find prey, they looked everywhere for plants to eat.

The itchy root was a food discovered when the previous Priest was still alive.

But before eating it every time, it had to be inspected by the previous Priest.

And after the current old Priest became the Priest, the beastmen also brought back many itchy roots and gave them to him to look at.

He hadn't even identified them clearly before the beastmen impatiently roasted them and ate them.

That time, more than a dozen beastmen died, and almost all the cubs who had just transformed into human form perished.

That was the thing the old Priest regretted most in his life.

Since then, he simply forbade all beastmen from digging up itchy roots. He himself didn't dare to touch the thing again.

He closed his eyes, suppressing the pain in his heart.

"You are not allowed to eat it."

Lin Qiu: "It can be eaten."

The Priest opened his eyes, which were bloodshot. He said firmly: "Lang Qiu, I said, you are not allowed to eat it."

Lin Qiu's gaze was calm, "Priest, have you ever thought that the problem wasn't this plant? At that time, so many types of itchy roots were mixed together; who knows if one of them was the problem?"

"All the beastmen ate them at that time; why did some die while others lived? Are you sure they all ate the same thing?"

The old Priest: "Then no one should eat any of them."

Lin Qiu's heart sank.

"This thing is everywhere in the forest. If it can be eaten, we could at least store enough food to feed the beastmen for several months."

The lack of food had reached this point; they couldn't give up eating because of a past choking incident.

Lang Yan grabbed Lin Qiu's wrist and said to the Priest: "I'll talk to him."

He took Lin Qiu away and took the yam with him.
chapters.source_text:
林楸寻着最近的一根藤蔓过去。
“叶对生或三片轮生，三角状卵形叶片，叶脉七到九条自叶脉发出……”
林楸将山药的特征与眼前的植物一一对应。
“挖。”
狼莫一下挡在林楸面前，脑袋直甩，“真的吃不得，痒痒根祭司不让碰。”
林楸：“为什么？”
“你忘了……”说着想起林楸坏了脑袋，是真的忘了，只好跟他解释一通。
“很久很久以前，我们最先发现的是圆痒痒根，那个直接吃麻嘴，但是烤着吃幼崽跟亚兽人都很喜欢……起初没什么问题，但后来大家找了更多的痒痒根回来，也包括长痒痒根，结果那一次直接死了好多个亚兽人，幼崽也……”
“反正之后祭司就规定，不许再碰这个。”
林楸：“确定是吃了这个出事的？”
狼莫：“都是采集队经常采集的。”
林楸：“有没有可能，采集错了？”
狼莫不知道，这是好多年前的事情了，那时候都还没有他呢。
“不行，你要问了祭司才能挖。”他态度强硬。
林楸：“那我挖了问祭司能不能行？”
狼莫犹豫，拿着木棍在地上戳戳戳。
地面土层松软，几乎都是腐殖土，极其肥沃。这山药不知长了多少年，藤蔓有指粗。
林楸：“就这么定了。”
他绕过狼莫，先用木棍刨了刨藤蔓下覆盖的一层松软土层，刨开后开始用木棍挖。
狼莫绕着点林楸走动，不停地往狼山的方向看。
林楸：“帮忙。”
狼莫：“先说好，不问祭司你不许吃！”
狼楸：“知道。”
山药可不好刨，沿着藤蔓往下，快一米的地方才看到山药顶端。两人木棍都劈叉了，最后狼莫怕天黑还没出林子，直接变了狼形用爪子刨。
那利爪勾出来，有林楸一指长。爪垫比他手掌还大，狼屁股后头刨出来的土堆以肉眼可见的速度增多。
林楸在后头转移土壤，狼楸埋头吭哧吭哧挖。
往下又刨了一米多，狼莫一屁股坐在地上，抖了抖爪子里的泥，“可以了。”
林楸瞧了眼，“还不行，底下起码还有一半。”
“你怎么知道？你挖过？”狼脑袋转过来，吐着舌头，像条大狗。
林楸：“没有，看一眼就知道。”
狼莫：“怎么这么深。”
他挪着屁股起，呸呸两三吐出嘴巴里的泥，又吭哧吭哧开始挖。
林楸一边转移土壤一边提醒，“尽量别挖断了。”
……
狼山。
地里的草已经拔完了，宽阔的黑土中，细嫩的苗子看着很脆弱。
兽人们担心，便只能继续守着。
这边林子里的藤条已经尽数运送回狼山，狼安带领着部落的亚兽人们把林楸弄回来的那批藤条用完了，加上原来的两个，总共八个鱼笼。
狼石趴在地上，见运送藤条回来的队伍中没有狼莫，林楸也不在，便问了句。
狼西：“莫跟着楸在林子里挖土。”
他去看了的，土都堆了好高，狼莫整个狼身都能藏在土坑里了。
“土有什么好挖的，天快黑了，林子里不安全。”
狼石起身，正打算去看看，两个脏兮兮的兽人回来了。
林楸还好，只手跟兽皮衣脏。
狼莫那简直像在泥巴里打了滚，浑身毛发裹着泥巴，变了颜色。不是黑狼，成了棕狼。
两个兽人看着都有些疲惫，身上似挑着木棍。
等走到狼山近前，狼莫往地上一趴，林楸拎着自己装果子的篮子跟山药，挪了挪，也先坐下来缓一缓。
“你们干什么去了？”狼石跟狼西靠近，目光落在那木棍上。
“这是什么？”
狼爪勾了勾，立马渗出白色的汁液。
狼西一抖爪，飞快在地上擦了擦。
“痒痒根？”
“你们挖这个干什么？要是祭司知道了，要挨收拾的。”
狼石扒拉着，打算给扔了。
林楸立即道：“等会儿！好不容易挖来的。”
狼石：“楸，你想吃这个？”
林楸：“我有用，会问过祭司再说。”
狼石这才松了爪，又嫌弃狼莫浑身的土，调头去远一点的地方趴着。
篝火升起来了，夜空清朗，群星从头顶铺开整个苍穹。
狼莫累得趴在地上，没一会儿就扯着细长的呼噜睡过去。前爪还时不时抖两下，带泥巴的爪子勾着青草。
林楸远远看着狼岩带领着外出的队伍回来，队伍中间一头硕大的弯角兽。
部落里的兽人显然也看到了，正欢呼着，忽然有两个兽人跑出队伍，扛着个昏迷的兽人往祭司山洞跑。
兽人们的欢呼声一下沉寂，纷纷起身。像被袭击的鱼群，有些慌乱。
“王，狼游怎么了？”
狼岩一眼扫过自己部落的族人，见林楸坐在兽人后头，一身泥，目光一顿，收了回来。
“抓捕弯角兽的时候被顶了一下。”
“先收拾猎物，我去看看。”
兽人们担忧地看向山洞，不过狼岩的话立即有兽人执行下去。
兽人们熟练地宰杀猎物，那弯角兽看着比上次的那一头都大，但部落里没有一人脸上有笑容。
篝火旁，大家静悄悄的。
狼安依旧带领着一部分兽人给藤蔓剥皮，狼石主持着宰杀猎物，而狩猎回来的捕猎队、采集队的队员们，则交托了食物，趴在地上休息。
大家脑袋全部对着狼山，担忧地望着亮着火光的山洞。
林楸见状，拿起山药跟篮子里的果子，静悄悄地往祭司的山洞去。
洞中火堆烧得从未有过的明亮。
祭司那张木板上，兽人被放平躺在上面。狼岩立在兽人旁侧，看着祭司检查。
狼冰也在。
林楸放轻脚步声靠近，狼岩微侧头，见林楸进来，手上山药有些碍事儿，便顺手拎走放在一旁。
全程无声无息，没人说话。
林楸看了眼木板上躺着的兽人。
他的胸口出一大块青紫，已经肿起来了。祭司正一脸严肃，先叫狼冰往兽人嘴里灌了一碗药粉兑的汤。
然后手寻着兽人的骨头细细地摸去，半晌，松了一口气。
“还好，没断。”
兽人恢复能力很好，只要不是危及性命的伤，配着药物，慢慢能治愈。
幸得狼部落本来就属于兽神大陆上数一数二的大部落，祭司也从未断代过，经年累月，医术世代累积，大病小伤都能看一看。
兽人晕过去，这伤并不轻。
不排除里面脏器可能受到冲击。
但现在的医术还没到能开膛破肚的程度，祭司也只能用药，只能等时间，看看兽人之后的反应。
检查完，祭司让狼冰从木架子上捡了些治疗外伤的草药，打做糊糊，贴在兽人胸口上。
随后自个儿又在药材当中挑挑拣拣，重新配了些草药，放在陶罐里熬煮。
忙完了，祭司擦着手看来。
见林楸不知什么时候也来了，正要问，看见放在一旁有兽人那么高的山药。
“你们去挖痒痒根了？”
林楸：“好东西。”
“什么都敢挖！到时候浑身发痒有你好看的。”祭司说着，走到山药旁边。
想起从前的一桩事，心中闪过隐痛，叹道：“这事儿你忘了，也不怪你，痒痒根不能吃。”
林楸早从狼莫那里了解了情况，自然知道老祭司说的是什么。
他道：“能吃，好吃。”
“你吃了？！”老祭司眼皮耷拉的眼睛一下睁大，几下杵着木杖来，像要检查林楸。
林楸：“没，以前吃过。”
狼岩看着林楸侧脸，声音略低：“别什么都吃。”
林楸：“那事儿我听狼莫说了，这个我敢肯定能吃，还好吃。但是圆痒痒根这个就危险些。”
这件事情发生在老祭司还年轻的时候，那时候上一任祭司刚刚去世不久，他留下的很多东西他都还没学完。兽人们又饿，猎物找不到就四处找植物来吃。
痒痒根是上一任祭司在的时候大家寻找到的食物。
但是每一次吃之前，都必须经过上一任祭司过目。
而在现在的老祭司成为祭司之后，兽人们同样找了许多痒痒根回来，也给了他看。
他甚至还没辨别清楚，兽人们就迫不及待烤了下嘴。
那一次，死了十几个兽人，刚变化成人形的幼崽几乎全部死亡。
那是老祭司这辈子最后悔的事情。
从那以后，他干脆禁止所有的兽人挖掘痒痒根。他自己也不敢再碰一下这个东西。
他闭眼，压下心中的沉痛。
“不许吃。”
林楸：“能吃。”
祭司睁眼，眼中猩红一片。他强硬道：“狼楸，我说了，不许吃。”
林楸目光沉静，“祭司，你有没有想过，出问题的不是这个，当时那么多种类的痒痒根混在一起，谁知道是不是其中一种出了问题。”
“当时所有兽人都吃了，为什么有的兽人没了，有的兽人还好好活着。他们吃的是不是一样的，您都确定吗？”
老祭司：“那就都别吃。”
林楸心沉了沉。
“这个东西，林子里处处都有，如果能吃，那我们起码能储存够兽人足够吃几个月的食物。”
缺乏食物已经到了这个地步，不能因噎废食。
狼岩抓住林楸手腕，对祭司道：“我跟他说。”
他带着林楸离开，顺手拿走了山药。
chapters.title: 第17章

chapters.translated_text:
Not a cloud in the sky, which was a brilliant blue, and migratory birds flying high heading south.

After seeing off the green-eyed orcs, Lang You headed straight for Wolf Mountain, preparing to bring back the flatbed carts and the small boats made by Lang Qi.

The only youyou beast they had caught was left behind at the Great Marsh, and he ran back empty-handed.

"You, how is it you're only back this late?"

The orcs sleeping in the cafeteria heard the commotion, yawning and squinting as they looked at the orcs of the first hunting team.

Then they looked outside the cafeteria, where it was pitch black—it was the middle of the night.

Lang You touched the clay pot and felt it was still somewhat warm; hungry, he quickly ladled himself some meat soup. Sitting down on the floor, he said, "Uncle Chi and the others are back."

"All of them are back?" Lang An also sat up from his straw nest, bleary-eyed.

Lang You nodded. "All back, and they've brought all their belongings."

"How come I don't see any other orcs?"

Lang An said as he prepared to get up. Returning at this hour meant they must have traveled hard, so he needed to make some food for everyone. There was only the meat soup left for Lang You and the others in the clay pot.

"They're gathering lotus roots at the Great Marsh and won't be coming back just yet. I'll take the flatbed carts over to them tomorrow."

Lang An paused, then lay back flat into his straw nest.

After thinking for a moment, with a trace of sleepiness in his voice, he said, "I'll go with you guys tomorrow too."

It had been so many years since they last saw each other, he wanted to go take a look.

Lang You's squad had returned late, so on Wolf Mountain, not many orcs knew that Lang Chi and the others were back.

Early the next morning, after finishing breakfast, Lang You led his team, pulling the flatbed carts and two small boats, and prepared to leave in a hurry.

Lang An went to the cave to inform the priest, then quickly hurried to catch up.

"What is An going to the Great Marsh for?" Lang Mo asked.

He had slept in the cave last night and knew nothing about what happened in the cafeteria. Lang Xi hung over his shoulder, balancing on one leg, and said, "Uncle Chi and the others are back."

"Uncle Chi is back... Huh? When did Uncle Chi get back? Where are they?"

Lang Mo turned his head.

Seeing their noses about to touch, Lang Xi pushed his face away in disgust and said, "They're working at the Great Marsh."

Lang Mo's face was squeezed out of shape, and he muttered indistinctly, "They're not even coming back to Wolf Mountain for a trip?"

"Bai Que and the green-eyed orcs have all left; there are no orcs over there."

Hearing this, the orcs who had wanted to tag along for the excitement gave up the idea.

They were busy too. All one hundred and twenty-seven orcs of the branch tribe were now finally back, and adding the orcs of Wolf Mountain, that made over two hundred mouths to feed. If they didn't desperately hunt and forage for food, they really would go hungry.

Lang Mo nudged Lang Xi with his elbow. "Let's go. You take Uncle Kuo's orcs to make bricks, and I'll build houses, otherwise there'll be nowhere to live."

"Uncle Kuo isn't hunting?"

The two of them looked at Lang Kuo, who was sitting to one side drinking meat soup.

Truth be told, since Uncle Kuo's physique had recovered, his cheeks had flesh, he was tall with long legs, and he was more handsome than both of them. Uncle Kuo was quite the flower of the older generation in the Wolf tribe.

"I'm old," Lang Kuo waved a hand.

Lang Mo and Lang Xi kept deadpan faces. "It's not that bad."

"You're only in your thirties."

"Thirty-nine," Lang Kuo corrected. "I'm eating the meat soup of a forty-year-old. In another year, I'll be heading toward fifty."

"Really don't want to go out and run around?"

Lang Kuo and the others had also been part of the hunting team in the branch tribe, but coming back to Wolf Mountain, they just followed along to play with mud. Lang Mo and Lang Xi enjoyed it, but Uncle Kuo had been assigned his job by their own automatic delegation.

Lang Kuo: "Not going."

Run around for what? Having run around for so many years, he was tired.

He thought playing with mud and building houses was quite a lot of fun.

"Then what about the other uncles?"

The orcs following Lang Kuo all waved their hands. "Not going, not going."

No matter how big the Wolf tribe was, the prey was only this much, and four hunting teams were plenty. Any more would just be running along in vain, wasting physical strength and consuming extra food, which wasn't worth it.

"Fine then... off to play with mud it is." Lang Mo took the lead and left.

Lang Kuo finished his meat soup in one breath and slowly followed behind.

During his days here on Wolf Mountain, he finally understood what it meant to actually live life... rather than just endure it day by day.

Seeing the orcs spontaneously put away their playful mindset, the priest didn't say much more, took a walk outside, and returned to the cave.

He was getting old, and Bing hadn't completely finished learning all his skills yet. The snow was still light, and Bing was currently too busy gathering herbs to handle everything; some things needed to be taught in careful detail, so he was busy too...

*

The sunlight was warm, and two small boats drifted on the Great Marsh.

The small boats were piled full of lotus roots. Little Wolf sat in a small boat, paddling and ferrying the lotus roots to the shore trip after trip.

Without the orcs of the Feathered tribe to help, it was somewhat more troublesome for the orcs to enter the water and transport things, but the small boats had arrived just in time, and the little wolves treated it like a game, scrambling to use them.

In the drained depressions, footprints of varying depths were everywhere.

Half of the branch tribe's orcs were in these depressions, bent over toward the mud, one hand slightly braced against the mud's surface while the other searched underneath.

Lang Wan's entire arm was plunged into the mud. Feeling something hard, just as he was about to fish it out, Lang Star next to him shrank his feet back and turned to look at him with a blank expression.

The two orcs were in identical bending postures as they searched for lotus roots, and as their eyes met, both couldn't help laughing.

"This thing grows really deep."

Lang Wan withdrew his claws.

Lang Star shrank his feet back and raised his chin to avoid swallowing a mouthful of muddy water.

"Searching for them one by one like this, who knows when we'll finish."

"It's not easy just for a bite to eat... If it were easy to find, it would have been in our bellies long ago."

Although they said this, the movements of the two demi-orcs were also quite deft.

They fished up a complete section of lotus root, treating it like a treasured find, and carefully washed away the mud on the surface in the water. Looking at the white and tender appearance of the lotus root, they smiled from the bottom of their hearts.

"It's really good. Qiu, that little cub, has finally figured things out; he can find any kind of food."

"He is different, but even before falling into the water, he was a crafty little sprite."

"Heh..." Lang Wan was very tall, the corners of his eyes curling up. "I think his soul came back."

"Maybe he saw the Beast God."

"That's true too."

The lotus leaves rustled as more than thirty orcs all bent their waists, plunging both hands into the mud to search for that hidden treasure.

The little wolves mingled among them. With the elders having arrived and orcs doing the work, their playful urges flared up again.

A few little wolves gathered in a bunch, holding basins in their hands, searching for loaches in the footprints left behind by the orcs.

"Wow! I found one!"

"I found one too!"

"Mine is big!"

"I got two!"

"Awooo! This pit is full of them!"

The noisy, bustling voices came over from time to time, sounding like someone had put a loudspeaker right by their ears, making the orcs' ears ache.

Yet it hadn't been this lively around them for a long time, and Lang Wan and the others couldn't bear to drive them away.

They could only endure it, listening to the little wolves competitively hunting those mud-worms.

After the rainy season, the water in the Great Marsh gradually dried up, and the remaining thirty-odd orcs were busy continuing to scoop out mud and prepare the fields.

The plots of land extended toward the scattered grassy islands in the middle of the lake, and the deep ditches between the plots became increasingly deep, connecting into a web-like expanse.

Lang Chi stepped barefoot in the mud, standing on the field, and couldn't help asking Lang Yan beside him, "This land is in the water; it's used to grow lotus roots?"

"The lotus root field is just where wild lotus roots currently grow; we can use it after clearing and leveling it. The dry land on top will be used to grow vegetables."

"Just grow vegetables?"

"Not only that. Seeds are limited right now, and we still need to search for more suitable ones."

The small boats shuttled across the water. The little wolves felt the paddles weren't thrilling enough and spontaneously learned how to use punting poles. Thrusting those long poles into the water and pushing off hard, the small boats shot straight forward.

The orcs of the branch tribe looked on with novelty.

With a thump, the bow of a boat collided with the edge of the piled-up mud.

"Load the lotus roots!" A little wolf shouted. The little wolves who were digging loaches all straightened up, smiling as they each took charge of moving the piled-up lotus roots beside them onto the small boat.

Along with them, the freshly caught loaches filled half a basin as well, densely packed and jumping about actively.

The bottom of the basin banged against the side of the boat with a clatter, and the loaches nearly leaped out.

Lang Jin and Bao Xiu immediately blocked the top with their hands, startled, "Mud-worms... there are so many loaches!"

Qiu called this thing a loach.

"There's more!" Seeing the small boat was full, the little wolves rushed back to catch more.

Lang Jin and Bao Xiu paddled the boat, which was loaded with lotus roots, intending to leave, but the bow was stuck in the mud pile, a bit too deep, and it wouldn't move.

Lang Cang casually lent a hand, pushing the small boat free.

Such a small thing, drifting and bobbing on the surface of the water, looking like it could flip at any moment.

"Is this another good thing Qiu came up with?" Lang Cang asked.

"Most likely," Lang Wan said.

As he said this, there was even a hint of pride.

Lang Star looked at him and smiled. "You didn't use to look kindly upon that little cub, changed your tune?"

Lang Wan: "Am I going to hold a grudge against him?"

Who knew who used to be so angry every time they saw Qiu that their stomach hurt and they couldn't sleep.

The lotus leaves rustled as Lang Wan bent his waist.

Looking at the turbid water surface, the corners of the lips on that blurry reflected face were curved upward.

After seeing the current Qiu, everything about Qiu back in the Wolf tribe seemed to have blurred away.

The Qiu who made him gnash his teeth in hatred, wishing he could lock him up and break his legs, the Qiu who made him so angry he cried—vanished in an instant.

As an orc who was familiar with Qiu, he should have felt unaccustomed to it, but without realizing it, he had very easily accepted Qiu's changes.

Qiu should be like this.

He was supposed to be like this!

Qiu had been raised by him when he was little.

Before there were clay pots, he was responsible for roasting meat, so he often stayed behind in the tribe.

There were very few cubs who went with them to the branch tribe; Lang Ye's group were all mischievous male wolf cubs, and only Qiu was the most obedient.

He had treated Qiu like his own biological cub as he raised him.

He had watched as Qiu changed from obedient and soft to surly and prickly, covered all over in thorns as if they were going to harm him, growing further and further away from them the older he got.

But the one in front of him right now...

Lang Wan couldn't help gazing into the distance toward the riverbank, looking at Lin Qiu.

He was squatting by the water's edge, washing the lotus roots, talking with Lang Yu beside him. Laughing as they spoke, his expression was soft, faintly bearing the shadow of that childhood appearance.

Lang Wan was left in a daze just watching.

"What are you daydreaming about?" Lang Star gave him a shove, getting some mud smeared on his arm.

Lang Wan snapped back to his senses and suddenly smiled.

"Pretty good."

"What's pretty good?" Lang Star smeared another handful of mud onto his arm.

Lang Wan glanced at his arm. "Star, do you think you're still a little cub?"

Lang Star smiled triumphantly. "I'm happy."

Actually, the branch tribe's orcs were all very happy at this moment. Happiness had reached its peak, leaving them unsure of how to express it.

Encountering the green-eyed orcs right as they returned and going through all that chaos—only now did that aching, swollen emotion continuously surge forth.

They were back.

Having wished for it for so many years, getting their wish fulfilled, it would have been a miracle if they hadn't gone mad with joy.

Therefore, the orcs right now channeled all that energy into their work.

It was as if they were brimming with strength; pile after pile of lotus roots were packed full and transported to the shore, moving even faster than the young orcs dug them.

This speed startled the little wolves.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan didn't dare let them get too tired.

When it was nearly time, Lang Yu called out from the shore for them to eat.

But the elders weren't like the young wolf orcs; they lingered and didn't move. When shouted at from the shore again, they called back loudly, "You guys eat first, we'll finish digging this bit."

Lang Yu glanced at Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu shook his hands, stood up, and said, "Then I'm sending it over! If it spills later..."

"We're coming, we're coming!"

Lang Yu smiled. "Still Qiu who has a way with them."

The orcs successively came ashore, fearing Lin Qiu would march over to deliver it himself.

The small patch of marshland near the shore had been dug through by Bai Que and the green-eyed orcs earlier, and many stone slabs had been laid down, allowing the orcs to cross quickly.

Passing by Lin Qiu, Lang Wan said, "Don't urge us next time, we'll come up ourselves when we're hungry."

Lin Qiu: "That won't do. Eating on time is the rule."

Lang Wan stared at him.

Lin Qiu didn't back down at all.

But suddenly his cheek smarted. Lin Qiu: "Uncle Wan!"

Lang Wan withdrew his hand, looked at Qiu who looked like a little smeared kitten, let out a laugh, and happily went off to eat.

Lang Star slowly walked at the back, glanced at Lin Qiu, and also raised his hand.

"Hiss—" Lin Qiu winced. "Uncle Star!"

The corners of Lang Star's mouth curled up as he withdrew his hand and walked away.

"Why does everyone like pinching my face so much!"

Watching the mud on Lin Qiu's face become symmetrical, a chuckle escaped the orcs' throats, though no one reminded him.

Lin Qiu rubbed both of his cheeks, then looked at his hands and gritted his teeth.

"Treating me like a cub to tease!"

"Qiu was originally raised by them from a cub." Lang Yan came ashore, looked at his mate's face, and wanted to wipe it for him.

But looking at his own hands, he could only lead him to the water's edge.

Lin Qiu squatted beside him, his arm brushing against his.

Seeing him staring blankly at the water's surface, Lang Yan asked in a low voice, "Unhappy?"

Lin Qiu: "No."

He looked at that face identical to his own, plunged his hand into the water, and scattered the image.

Lin Qiu didn't know why he had appeared here, nor did he know if the original wolf Qiu had become Lin Qiu.

But at this moment, he completely did not want to go back anymore.

He had a mate, and he was greedy for the elders' kindness; even if they were old folks... they were good old folks.

It was just a pity that the Abba they spoke of—the one he looked so much like—wasn't here.

But how could everything in life be complete? Lin Qiu was already very content. He only hoped he wouldn't suddenly be sent back because of some circumstance again.

He was afraid of going back.

"Qiu! Come eat quickly! An made roasted meat!"

Lang An had also come over with Lang You and the others, bringing quite a bit of sweet herb.

As soon as he arrived, he didn't reminisce with Lang Wan and the others, but instead took charge of the cooking, making delicious food for the orcs.

Seeing Lin Qiu and Lang Yan enter, Lang An served them their food.

Steamed tail-grass seed rice, paired with roasted meat that was charred and fragrant all over, a little side dish, and a bowl of bone soup—they had never eaten anything like this back on Wolf Mountain.

The roasted meat was sliced thin, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, carrying a strong spicy aroma with a slight numbing sensation on the lips.

Yet that flavor was incomparable to burnt meat chunks.

Not only did Lang Wan and the others eat ravenously, but even the little wolves buried their heads in shoveling rice, whining aggrievedly as they ate: "Why haven't we eaten anything like this before?"

Lang An replied coldly, "No time to make it."

Lang Jin nudged Bao Xiu beside him. "Do you believe that?"

Bao Xiu puffed out both cheeks, making "aowu aowu" sounds as he buried his head and shoveled hard.

An would only whip up something good to eat if he was in a good mood. It wasn't that he couldn't make it, it was that he didn't feel like doing it.

With too many orcs, making any casual variety was troublesome.

Lang An carried his bowl and plopped down right next to Lang Wan. Lang Star was right on the other side; these were all companions he had grown up with.

"Delicious, right?"

"Not bad, better than Lang Yu's cooking."

Lang Yu swallowed a piece of roasted meat and said, "Then don't eat it."

Lang Wan: "That won't do."

Lang Star chuckled, comfortably stretching out his legs, and swaggeringly tilted his head back to down a mouthful of soup.

Looking on, Lang An said, "Feels like it's a good time for wine now."

"What's this other good thing we haven't seen before?"

"Qiu made it."

The demi-orc uncles chatted back and forth, exchanging small talk about daily life as if they had never been separated at all.

Yet inadvertently, noticing the silver-white strands mixed in each other's hair, the deep wrinkles at the corners of their eyes when they smiled, as they spoke, their voices somehow trailed off into silence.

Lin Qiu looked over and saw that every single uncle had his head lowered, looking as if they were intensely focused on eating.

But upon closer inspection, the corners of their eyes shimmered with crystal tears, and the hands holding the clay bowls were trembling slightly—silent and heart-wrenching.

It wasn't that they didn't miss each other, nor that they weren't emotional, but having been separated for far, far too long, none of them dared to dig too deeply into each other's past experiences. They could only carefully discuss these ordinary matters, slowly releasing the emotions of years apart.

No one went up to disturb them.

Even the little wolves quieted down, cautiously glancing over there and eating in silence.

*

The days grew shorter, and after a few rounds of rain, the weather turned completely chilly.

Batch after batch of lotus roots were transported back to Wolf Mountain. The branch tribe's orcs were active workers, and all the lotus roots that could be easily reached were dug out, while the lotus fields were also made much flatter in the process.

It wouldn't do to let them keep digging now.

After discussing it, Lang Yan and Lin Qiu called the orcs back.

With so many orcs in the tribe, the lotus roots dug up right now couldn't be stored long-term.

Fresh lotus roots didn't keep well and wouldn't last until the snow season. Taking advantage of the lotus root supplement, the orcs turned all the daily-foraged wild vegetables and fruits into dried vegetables and dried fruits wherever possible, and ate whatever couldn't be processed.

Day by day, the several caves on Wolf Mountain gradually filled up.

Still, it wasn't enough.

The lotus roots in the Great Marsh could continue to be dug, but Lang Chi and the others couldn't be the ones doing it.

By evening, they arrived at Wolf Mountain.

As soon as they arrived, they had dinner, and after eating, they returned to their respective caves.

Down on the mountain, it was rowdy; the orcs were busy reminiscing.

In the small cave, Lin Qiu and Lang Yan had just finished bathing and were sitting by the fire drying their hair.

Bringing up the matter of the lotus roots, Lang Yan said, "Uncle Chi and the others won't go next time, we'll let the hunting team go instead."

With plenty of orcs in the tribe now, the older orcs could just follow the young orcs out for a stroll and refamiliarize themselves with the territory.

Lin Qiu sat on his lap, leaning face-to-face against his shoulder as Lang Yan combed through his hair, feeling somewhat drowsy.

"Not saving them to eat during the snow season?"

"They don't keep long. If we dig them when it gets any colder, the young orcs will freeze."

They had all stepped in that mud; even in the blazing sun, the mud underneath chilled your legs. If the weather got any colder, the mud would feel bone-chillingly cold.

He had to look out for the health of the older generation of orcs, but the young ones too.

"Then we need to rush the digging. If there's an excess, no worries, we can make lotus root starch. That stores well."

Sleepy, Lin Qiu spoke rather vaguely.

Lang Yan didn't rush to question him further, just gathering and tossing his long hair, thinking of getting it dried quickly so they could go to sleep.

Don't let the branch tribe's orcs look spirited; everyone was actually exhausted.

By the end, they just plopped down wherever they stood, words still lingering in their mouths as their eyes slowly closed.

The branch tribe's orcs and Wolf Mountain's orcs lay together. Separated for over ten years, the Wolf tribe was gathered together once more.

*

Early the next morning, a light rain began to fall from the sky.

The rain threads were fine and dense, and a mist shrouded the mountain forest.

The moment the door opened, a fresh and pleasant breeze hit his face, instantly waking Lin Qiu up.

He stretched lazily and gazed out into the distance.

Over on the mountain ridge where the Black Feather tribe lived to the west, mountain mists rose like blue smoke, winding among the peaks.

A layer of rain mist also draped over the large river, faint and drifting slowly away.

Nearby, smoke billowed from the chimneys of the Wolf tribe's cafeteria.

In the gloomy weather, the mountain forests, vegetation, stream stones, and long river seemed to have their vibrant colors polished away, blending into a traditional landscape ink painting.

With more orcs around, the ten stoves built in the cafeteria were all put to use.

The orcs cooked with clay pots; the pots were small, and getting all the meals out at once was always somewhat troublesome. If they were replaced with large iron pots, two or three stoves would be plenty to handle it.

It was still early, but Lang Yan and the hunting and gathering team had already set out.

Lin Qiu went down the mountain alone. The misty drizzle couldn't wet his clothes, and he walked slowly.

Just as he stepped onto the last stair, he saw Lang Stone carrying Bao Zhi back from patrol, while Lang Wan, Lang Star, and Lang Cang were sitting under the cafeteria eaves, staring right at him.

Lang Wan: "Stone? When did you have a cub?"

Looking at the cub strapped to his chest in a beast-skin pouch, Lang Stone rubbed its head and chuckled.

"I didn't give birth to it."

"Then your mate gave birth to it?"

"No..." Seeing Bao Zhi tilt its head to look at him, Lang Stone touched its ears and didn't continue.

This Cloud Leopard cub was attached to him, so Lang Stone mostly carried it with him wherever he went, and specifically had Lang An sew a beast-skin pouch of a suitable size for it.

After raising it for so long, an affection had grown; it wasn't right to say things that would hurt the cub's feelings.

Lang Stone walked away.

Treading through the curtain of rain, Lin Qiu walked slowly toward the eaves.

Lang Wan frowned and said, "Little wolf cub! Not even afraid of getting worms in your hair in the rain."

The exact same words as in his memories.

Lin Qiu walked quickly. Reaching the eaves, he was pulled by Lang Wan to sit down beside him, feeling somewhat helpless.

When the branch tribe's orcs came over last time, Lin Qiu wasn't very familiar with them, and everyone was busy on ordinary days, so they didn't get to exchange many words.

But the ones sitting right in front of him were influential figures in the tribe, and also the ones who used to discipline him when he was little.

Unaccustomed to chatting idly with elders, and with Lang Yan absent, Lin Qiu could only bite the bullet and sit there.

"Dumbed down? You used to give ten replies for every one of my sentences."

"No way..."

"Still not admitting it."

Lang Star bumped Lang Wan with his elbow, and Lang Wan then remembered the main business. He said, "When did Lang Stone get a Cloud Leopard cub?"

"Did he find a Cloud Leopard orc for a mate?" Lang Star also turned his head to ask.

"No... that cub is just one we rescued from that wandering tribe. Lang Stone helped him once, and he just clung on."

"Is that so..."

That tone sounded somewhat disappointed.

Without saying more to Lin Qiu, Lang Wan stood straight up and stepped into the rain and mist.

Lin Qiu said, "Uncle Wan, where are you going?"

Lang Star and Lang Cang followed, casually telling him, "We're just taking a stroll. We came back late yesterday and haven't gone out to look around yet."

The red birds, bleating beasts, brick kiln, and small houses the little wolves talked about—they were curious about every single one of them.

Lin Qiu muttered, "Why aren't they talking about worms growing in hair now..."

Getting up, Lin Qiu found a few straw hats and went straight to deliver them.

The three elders took the straw hats, looked at them, clapped them onto their heads, and waved their hands. "Hurry back, aren't you afraid of your hair..."

"I know!"

Lin Qiu immediately took a step back and turned to run back to the cafeteria.

At the entrance, Lang Guo stood at the front with a bunch of little cubs behind him, looking at him with smiles.

A cub squeezed to the front, tugged on Lin Qiu's trouser leg, and asked, "Qiu, who are they?"

The orcs had returned late yesterday, spending half the night reminiscing with family and friends.

Led by Lang Guo, the cubs had finished their meat soup early and gone back to their straw nests to sleep, so they hadn't had a chance to speak with the later-arriving orcs.

Lin Qiu: "You guys call them Grandpa."

"Grandpa who?"

"Grandpa Priest."

"That's not Grandpa Priest..."

The cubs chattered among themselves, curiously looking outside again.

"They're also orcs who came back from the branch tribe. When they left, you guys weren't born yet, and Guo was only as big as you guys back then."

The cubs raised their little heads, looking at Lang Guo, then looking outside.

There was still unfamiliarity in their eyes.

Lin Qiu rubbed a little cub's head and said, "It's fine, you'll get used to them after a while."

On the other side, Lang Wan and the others strolled around until they reached the red bird enclosure.

On a rainy day, the red birds hid under the shed.

The heated kang room was occupied by Lang Rong for hatching eggs; a fire was burning inside, making it somewhat warm, so the red birds didn't like going in right now.

In the rain and mist, the three orcs pressed against the fence, stretching their necks to look inside.

"One, two, three... fifteen, sixteen... Hey yoyoyo, how many are there actually?" Lang Cang pressed his entire body against the fence, making it creak.

Disdainfully, Lang Wan said, "Didn't An say over a hundred?"

Lang Star gazed at the fiery red feathers of the red birds, his focus lingering on their legs, and after a moment he said, "It's just that there's a bit too little meat on them."

Lang Cang: "An said they taste good."

Seeing a little wolf emerge from inside, Lang Wan immediately stood straight up, and the three orcs nodded benevolently at the little wolf.

"What's your name?"

"Lang Chuan."

Another head poked out from the shed, and Lang Wan was startled. "Eh? Identical."

Lang Star thought about it. "Could it be those two older ones of Lang Bei's?"

Lang Tao also stood up, standing shoulder-to-shoulder with his brother.

Seeing the three elders muttering among themselves—what they were saying seemed to be about things from when their mother and father were young—they quietly pricked up their ears to listen.

Lang Cang: "Bei is strong and gathers the most wild vegetables; I don't know how she ever took a fancy to thin-armed, thin-legged Hu."

Lang Wan: "Who says his arms and legs are thin, he's just a bit whiter."

Lang Star: "True, no other male orc is whiter than him, and he looks pretty good too. Back then, when Bei took a fancy to him, she dragged him into her nest. And that year they had these two."

Lang Wan: "No kidding, proves he wasn't useless."

With that, the three orcs walked away and went around to the bleating beasts' enclosure.

The two little wolves exchanged a glance and quickly followed.

Yet they stopped talking; arriving at the bleating beast enclosure, they stood rigidly outside the fence, gazing at the bleating beasts inside.

"They're alive... so many of them," Lang Wan said in a low, floating voice like mist.

Lang Star: "Now I understand why we were able to come back."

Whether it was the fish in the large river or the lotus roots in the Great Marsh, no matter how abundant these foods were, they couldn't sustain over two hundred wolf orcs.

The important thing was meat.

Red meat that could sustain their energy.

They had eaten fish for half a year; at first they could fill their stomachs, but eating only fish would make them increasingly lacking in strength. Mixing it with vegetables and occasionally caught prey, they slowly managed to scrape by.

But with many orcs, it meant that catching a single piece of prey wasn't enough to divide among everyone, leading to everyone starving together.

Before returning, they had been apprehensive, afraid of increasing the burden on these little wolves.

As for now, not anymore...

If you could say the red birds were just for tasting flavor, the bleating beasts could give them the strength to run, work, and fight.

Meat mixed with all sorts of wild vegetables and tail-grass seeds meant they could eat their fill.

To be more substantial, every single meal would be meat.

But back when they were in the Central Continent, this was something they wouldn't even dare to imagine.

The three orcs just leaned against this railing, watching continuously.

Lang Rong was inside taking care of the newborn baby bleating beasts. Hearing the noise and coming out, he spotted the elders who had just returned from the Great Marsh yesterday.

"Little wolf cub, come over," Lang Wan said in a low voice.

Lang Rong stepped forward a few steps, and two more little wolves poked their heads out from the shed.

They were two young orcs Lang Rong had asked Bing for when he couldn't keep up after listening to Lin Qiu's advice earlier.

One was named Lang Mi, and the other was named Lang Dou.

Both demi-orcs were very meticulous, frequently following Lang Bing to gather herbs and knowing some herbal knowledge, making them suitable for taking care of the baby bleating beasts.

The three little wolves stepped forward, standing in front of them across the fence.

Thinking they were going to ask about the bleating beasts, Lang Rong rehearsed mentally, intending to start telling them about Qiu helping a dystocic bleating beast give birth.

But the three elders didn't ask anything at all; instead, they simply took off the straw hats from their heads, placed them onto the cubs' heads, and patted them down.

"Good cubs, go inside, don't get rained on."

Lang Rong froze, the words he wanted to say stuck in his throat.

"Let's go, it's almost time to eat, remember to come back soon."

The rain threads fell like needles at a slant, chilling Lang Rong's arms slightly.

Lang Rong bit his lip, watching them depart.

Lang Chuan and Lang Tao outside also came up, looking perplexedly at the dazed Lang Rong.

Lang Rong murmured, "Just now, they seemed to be crying..."

"No, their eye rims were just red," Lang Mi said softly.

Lang Dou touched the hat on top of his head and broke into a smile. "Maybe it was just rain hanging from the corners of their eyes?"

Lang Rong smiled too.

"Yeah, it was the rain."

万里无云，天空一片澄蓝，南下的候鸟高飞而过。
狼游送走了绿眼兽人之后，径直赶往狼山，准备把板车还有狼起做的小船都带过去。
他们唯一抓的那头呦呦兽放在了大泽，空手跑回来。
“游，你们怎么这么晚才回来？”
睡在食堂里的兽人听到动静，打着哈欠，眯着眼看着狩猎一队的兽人们。
再看看食堂外，乌漆嘛黑，都半夜了。
狼游摸着陶罐上还有余温，饿得忙盛了点肉汤喝。他往地上一坐，道：“赤叔他们回来了。”
“都回来了？”狼安也从草窝里坐起来，睡眼惺忪。
狼游点点头：“都回来了，家当都带完了。”
“怎么没看见兽人？”
狼安说着要起，这个时候回来，肯定赶了路，得给大伙儿做点食物。陶锅里只有给狼游他们留的肉汤。
“他们在大泽采藕，暂时不回来，我明天把板车给他们送过去。”
狼安一顿，又平躺回草窝。
他想了想，声音里带着些困意，道：“我明天也跟你们去一趟。”
多少年没见了，他去看看。
狼游小队回来得晚，狼山这边，知道狼赤他们回来的兽人不多。
第二天一早，狼游吃完早饭，带队拉着板车和两艘小船急匆匆要走。
狼安去山洞跟祭司说了一声，也赶紧跟了上去。
“安跟着去大泽干什么？”狼莫道。
他昨晚睡在山洞，不知道食堂里的事情。狼西挂在他肩膀上，单腿支棱着，道：“赤叔他们回来了。”
“赤叔回来……嗯？赤叔什么时候回来的？在哪儿？”
狼莫转过头来。
狼西看他俩快碰在一起的鼻子，嫌弃地推开他的脸，道：“在大泽干活儿。”
狼莫脸被他挤得变形，囫囵道：“都唔回狼山一趟？”
“白雀和绿眼兽人都走了，那边没兽人。”
一听这话，想跟过去凑凑热闹的兽人歇了心思。
他们也忙呢，支部落一百二十七个兽人如今回来齐了，加上狼山的兽人，两百多张嘴巴，不拼了命地抓猎物，找食物，还真会饿肚子。
狼莫手肘别了一下狼西，“走，你带阔叔兽人烧砖，我建房子，不然没地儿住了。”
“阔叔不捕猎？”
他俩看向坐在一旁喝肉汤的狼阔。
别说，阔叔这身板养起来，两颊有肉，身高腿长，比他们都俊气。阔叔也是狼部落老一辈中的一枝花了。
“我老了。”狼阔摆摆手。
狼莫狼西木着脸，“也不至于。”
“你才三十多岁。”
“三十九。”狼阔纠正，“吃四十岁的肉汤了，再过一年，那就奔五十了。”
“真不想出去跑跑？”
狼阔他们在支部落也是狩猎队的，回来狼山就跟着他们玩儿泥巴，狼莫狼西那是喜欢，阔叔可是被他们自动分配工作的。
狼阔：“不去。”
跑什么跑，跑那么多年了，累了。
他觉得玩儿泥巴、砌房子挺好玩儿的。
“那其他阿叔们呢？”
跟着狼阔的兽人都摆手，“不去不去。”
狼部落再大，猎物就这么点儿，四个狩猎队妥妥够了。多了也是跟着空跑，浪费体力，还得多消耗食物，不值当。
“行吧……那就玩泥巴去了。”狼莫带头离开。
狼阔一口气刨完肉汤，慢吞吞跟上。
在狼山这段日子，他才体会到，什么叫过日子……而不是熬日子。
祭司看兽人们自发收起了玩闹的心思，就没多言，在外面走走就回山洞去了。
他年纪大了，冰还没彻底学完他一身本事。雪也还小，冰现在忙着采集草药顾及不过来，有的东西得细细教，也忙呐……
*
阳光和煦，大泽上飘着两只小船。
小舟上放着满满当当的莲藕，小狼坐在小船中，划着桨，一趟一趟把莲藕往岸上送。
没有羽族的兽人帮忙，兽人下水和运送东西要麻烦一些，但小舟送来得正是时候，小狼当玩儿似的，抢着用。
放了水的洼地中，到处是深浅不一的脚印。
支部落的兽人们一半在这水洼中，躬身对着淤泥，一手微微撑着泥面，一手往泥下寻摸。
狼晚整个手臂陷入淤泥，摸到个硬硬的东西，刚要捞，旁边狼星缩了缩脚，面无表情转头看着他。
两个兽人是一模一样的弯腰摸藕的姿势，四目相对，都忍不住笑。
“这玩意儿长得真深。”
狼晚收回爪子。
狼星缩了缩脚，扬起下巴，免得喝上一口淤泥水。
“这么一根一根摸，要摸到什么时候去。”
“为了一口吃的，可不容易……它要好找，早入了我们肚子。”
虽这样说着，但两个亚兽人动作也麻利。
他们捞起一截完整的莲藕，如获至宝，小心翼翼地放在水中抹去表面的泥，瞧着藕身白白嫩嫩的样子，打心底一笑。
“真好。楸那小崽子开了窍了，什么食物都能找到。”
“是不一样，但是没落水之前也鬼机灵。”
“嘿……”狼晚是极高的，眼尾都翘了起来，“我看是回魂了。”
“见兽神了也说不定。”
“也对。”
莲叶晃动，三十多个兽人都弯着腰，双手扎入淤泥中，寻找着那藏起来的宝贝。
小狼们混在其中，长辈们到了，有兽人干活，他们玩儿心又起。
几个小狼一堆，手上抓着盆子，在兽人们走过的脚印中摸泥鳅。
“哇！我摸到了！”
“我也摸到了！”
“我的大！”
“我两条！”
“嗷嗷嗷！这个坑里全是！”
咋咋呼呼的声音时不时传来，像在耳边放了个喇叭，扰得兽人们耳朵疼。
可身边好久都没这么热闹了，狼晚他们又不忍心驱赶。
只能忍受着，听着小狼较着劲儿地摸那泥虫。
过了雨季，大泽里的水慢慢干涸，剩下的三十多个兽人忙着继续捞淤泥整田。
田块朝着湖中间散落的草岛延伸，田块与田块之间的深沟愈发的深，网似的连成一片。
狼赤脚踩淤泥，站在田上，忍不住问旁边的狼岩：“这地在水里，用来种藕？”
“藕田就是现在长野藕的地方，修整过就能用。面上的地干，用来种菜。”
“就种菜？”
“不止，现在种子有限，还要多寻一些合适的。”
小船在水上穿行，小狼嫌船桨不够过瘾，自发学会了撑杆。那长杆扎入水中，用劲儿一撑，小船直接蹿了出去。
支部落的兽人们看得新奇。
咚的一声，船头撞在围起来的淤泥边。
“装藕！”小狼一声吆喝，挖泥鳅的小狼都直起身，笑嘻嘻各自负责把身边堆起的藕往小船上搬。
连带着刚刚抓的泥鳅也装了半盆，密密麻麻，活蹦乱跳。
盆底砰的一下磕在船边，泥鳅险些蹦出来。
狼金和豹休立马用手挡在上面，惊道：“泥虫……泥鳅这么多！”
楸喊这个叫泥鳅。
“还有呢！”小狼们看小船上放满了，又赶紧回去抓。
狼金和豹休划着载满莲藕的船打算离开，船头扎在淤泥堆，有些深，走不动。
狼藏顺手帮了一把，把小船推走。
那么小个东西，就在水面飘飘荡荡，看起来要翻不翻。
“这又是楸弄出来的好东西？”狼藏问。
“多半。”狼晚道。
这话说着，还有点自豪。
狼星看着他笑，“以前不嫌弃那小崽子，现在转性了？”
狼晚：“我还能跟他记仇？”
也不知道谁以前每天看见楸都气得肚子疼，睡不着觉。
荷叶窸窣，狼晚弯下腰来。
他看着浑浊水面，模糊倒影的那张脸上，唇角弯着。
在见了现在的楸后，之前在狼部落有关楸的一切好像都模糊了。
那个让他恨得牙痒痒，恨不能关起来打断腿的楸，气得他哭的楸一下就消失了。
作为熟悉楸的兽人，他本该觉得不习惯，可他在自己没发觉的情况下，极轻易的就接受了楸的变化。
楸应该是这样的。
他本该是这样！
小时候的楸是他带的。
没陶锅之前，他负责烤肉，所以常留在部落中。
跟他们去支部落的幼崽没几个，狼夜那一群都是调皮的雄兽人崽子，独独楸最乖。
他把楸当亲生崽子带着。
他是看着楸从乖软变得乖戾，浑身长满了刺，仿佛他们要害他一般，年纪越大与他们离得越远。
可眼前这个……
狼晚忍不住远眺河岸，看着林楸。
他蹲在水边搓洗着莲藕，与旁边狼雨说话，说得笑了，神态柔和，隐隐有那小时候的影子。
狼晚看得都恍惚了。
“发什么呆？”狼星推了他一把，弄了点淤泥沾在他胳膊上。
狼晚回神，忽然笑了。
“挺好。”
“好什么好？”狼星又往他胳膊上抹了一把泥。
狼晚瞥了手臂一眼，“星，你当自己还小？”
狼星得意地笑，“我高兴。”
其实支部落的兽人此刻都很高兴，高兴到了极致，便不知怎么表露。
刚回来就遇到绿眼兽人，折腾一通，这会儿那股酸胀的情绪才源源不断地涌出来。
他们回来了。
盼了那么多年，得偿所愿，没高兴疯了都是好的。
所以兽人们此刻，大家把那股劲儿用在了干活上。
好像浑身都是劲儿，那莲藕一堆一堆装满了往岸上运，比年轻兽人们挖得都快。
这速度，看得小狼们都诧异。
林楸和狼岩不敢让他们太累。
忙到差不多，岸上狼雨就喊着吃饭。
可长辈们不像年轻狼兽人，迟迟不动，岸上再喊，他们就扬声回道：“你们先吃，我们把这点挖完。”
狼雨看了眼林楸。
林楸甩甩手，站起来道：“那我送过来了啊！等会儿要是洒了……”
“回来了回来了！”
狼雨一笑，“还是楸有办法。”
兽人们陆续上岸，生怕林楸给他们送过去。
近岸边的小块沼泽地被之前白雀和绿眼兽人挖过，又搭了不少石头板子下去，兽人们飞快通过。
狼晚路过林楸身边，道：“以后别催，我们饿了自己上来。”
林楸：“那不行，按时按点吃饭，这是规定。”
狼晚盯着他。
林楸毫不退让。
但是他脸颊忽然一疼，林楸：“晚叔！”
狼晚收回手，看着小花猫一样的楸，笑了一声，高高兴兴去吃饭。
狼星慢慢走在后头，看了一眼林楸，也抬手。
“嘶——”林楸吃疼，“星叔！”
狼星翘起嘴角，收了手就走。
“怎么这么喜欢捏我的脸！”
兽人们看着林楸脸上的泥对称了，喉咙间溢出一声笑，谁都没提醒。
林楸揉了揉两边腮帮子，再看手，磨了磨牙。
“把我当幼崽逗！”
“楸本来是他们从幼崽带大的。”狼岩上岸，看着自己伴侣的脸，想给他擦一擦。
可看了看自己的手，只能带他去水边。
林楸蹲在他旁边，手臂与他挨着。
狼岩见他对着水面发呆，低声问：“不高兴了？”
林楸：“没有。”
他看着那张与他一模一样的脸，手没入水中，打散了画面。
林楸不知道自己为什么会出现在这里，也不知道原来的狼楸是不是成了林楸。
但这一刻，他是彻底不想再回去了。
他有伴侣，也贪恋长辈们的好，就算是老登……也是个好老登。
只是可惜，他们说的，他很像的阿爸不在。
可哪能事事都圆满，林楸已经很知足。他只希望，他不要又突然因为什么情况再回去。
他害怕回去了。
“楸！赶紧来吃饭了！安做了烤肉！”
狼安也跟着狼游他们过来了，带了不少香草。
他来了也不跟狼晚他们叙旧，直接掌勺，给兽人们做好吃的。
狼安看林楸和狼岩进来，给他俩打饭。
蒸熟的尾巴草籽饭，加上烤得焦香四溢的烤肉，还有一点配菜，一碗骨头汤，他们以前在狼山都没吃过这样的。
烤肉是片下来的，外酥里嫩，带着浓烈的辛香，有一点点麻嘴。
可那味儿是糊肉块不能比的。
不止狼晚他们吃得狼吞虎咽，连小狼们都埋头刨饭，边吃边委屈哼唧：“为什么我们以前没吃过这样的？”
狼安冷漠，“没空做。”
狼金撞了下旁边豹休：“你信吗？”
豹休鼓着两腮帮子，嗷呜嗷呜埋头使劲儿刨。
安要心情好才会捣鼓些好吃的，他不是做不出来，他是不乐意做。
兽人太多，随便弄个花样都麻烦。
狼安端了碗，一屁股坐到狼晚旁边。边上还挨着狼星，都是他以前一起长大的同伴。
“好吃吧？”
“不错，比狼雨手艺好。”
狼雨叼着一块烤肉咽下，道：“那你别吃。”
狼晚：“那不行。”
狼星笑了一声，惬意地伸直了双腿，潇洒仰头灌了一口汤。
狼安看着，道：“感觉现在适合喝酒。”
“又是什么我们没见过的好东西？”
“楸做的。”
几个亚兽人阿叔们说着话，你来我往，话着家常，仿佛他们之间从没有分开过。
可不经意间，瞧着对方发丝中夹了银白，笑起来眼角皱纹深刻，说着说着，不知怎么就没了声音。
林楸看过去，阿叔们各个低着头，像很专注地在吃饭。
可若是细看，他们眼角闪着晶莹，扶着陶碗的手在轻颤，无声无息的，教人心酸。
不是不想念，也不是不激动，可分开太久太久，都不敢问深了各自的事。只能小心说着这平常事，缓缓释放那多年不见的情绪。
谁也没有凑上去打扰。
就连小狼也安分下来，小心翼翼往那边看一眼，默默吃饭。
*
白日渐短，几场雨后，天气彻底转凉。
一批一批的莲藕被运回了狼山，支部落的兽人干活积极，能轻易下脚的莲藕都被挖了出来，顺带把藕田也整得更加平整。
现在不好再叫他们继续挖了。
狼岩和林楸一商量，叫上兽人们回去了。
部落兽人多，现在挖回去的莲藕是存不下来的。
新鲜莲藕不禁放，存不到雪季去。兽人们趁着有莲藕的补充，把每日采集回来的野菜瓜果能做成菜干果干的都做了，做不了的再吃掉。
日积月累，狼山的几个山洞渐渐装满。
不过依旧不够。
大泽里的莲藕还可以继续挖，但不能让狼赤他们挖。
晚间，他们到了狼山。
一到就吃晚饭，吃过后各回各的山洞。
这会儿山下闹哄哄的，是兽人们在叙旧。
小山洞中，林楸和狼岩刚洗完澡，坐在火堆边烘头发。
说起莲藕的事，狼岩道：“赤叔他们下次就不去了，让狩猎队去。”
部落如今兽人充足，老兽人们正好跟着年轻兽人出去转转，再熟悉熟悉领地。
林楸坐在他腿上，面对面靠着他肩，被狼岩梳着头发，有些昏昏欲睡。
“不留着雪季吃了？”
“放不久，再冷一点挖的话，年轻兽人也要冻坏。”
那泥里他们都是踩过的，就是烈日炎炎，那淤泥底下也凉腿。天气再冷一点，泥里就是刺骨的寒。
他不仅要顾及老一辈兽人们的身体，也要顾及年轻兽人。
“那要赶着挖了。要是有多的，也不怕，可以做藕粉。这个耐放。”
林楸犯困，说得含糊。
狼岩没急着追问，只拢着他的长发拨弄着，想着快点烘干了去睡。
别看支部落的兽人看起来精神，大家其实都累了。
说到最后，就地一趴，话还裹在嘴里，慢慢就闭上了眼睛。
支部落的兽人和狼山的兽人躺在一起，相隔十多年，狼部落再一次聚齐了。
*
第二天一早，天上下起了小雨。
雨丝细密，雾气笼罩山林。
一打开门，清新怡人的气息扑在脸上，林楸一下清醒过来。
他伸了个懒腰，往远处眺望。
西边黑羽部落那群山上，山岚如青烟袅袅而起，盘绕山间。
大河上也笼着一层雨雾，淡淡的，慢慢飘着走。
近处，狼部落的食堂烟囱上，也是炊烟弥漫。
阴暗天气中，山林草木，溪石长河如同被磨掉一层艳色，入了这一副山水墨画中。
兽人多了，食堂修的那十个灶也用上了。
兽人们用陶锅做饭，锅小，要一口气出餐，总麻烦些。要换成大铁锅，两三口灶就忙得过来。
天还早，但狼岩和狩猎采集队已经出发了。
林楸独自下山，濛濛细雨沾不湿衣裳，他走得也慢。
他才踩在最后一截台阶上，就看见狼石抱着豹枝巡逻回来，狼晚、狼星、狼藏三个就坐在那食堂屋檐下，盯着他看。
狼晚：“石？啥时候生的崽子？”
狼石看着胸口前用兽皮兜装着的幼崽，揉了一把他脑袋，笑呵呵的。
“不是我生的。”
“那是你伴侣生的？”
“不是……”狼石见豹枝仰着脑袋瞧他，摸了摸他耳朵，没继续说下去。
这云豹幼崽就黏他，狼石大多时候就随身带着，为此还专门找狼安给缝了个大小合适的兽皮兜。
养这么久，也养出感情了，不好说这话让幼崽伤心。
狼石走了。
林楸踏着雨幕，慢慢往屋檐下走。
狼晚皱眉道：“小狼崽子！淋雨也不怕脑袋上长虫子。”
与记忆中一模一样的话。
林楸快步走，到了屋檐下，被狼晚拉着往身边一坐，有些无奈。
上次支部落那边兽人过来，林楸跟他们不算熟悉，平日里都忙，说不上几句话。
可眼前坐着这几个，是部落里说话有用的，也是他小时候管他的。
林楸不习惯跟长辈闲聊，狼岩又不在，他只能硬着头皮坐着。
“傻了？以前我说一句你回十句。”
“哪有……”
“还不认账。”
旁边狼星撞了狼晚一下，狼晚这才想起正事，他道：“狼石什么时候有个云豹崽子了？”
“他找了云豹兽人当伴侣？”狼星也偏过头来问。
“没有……那幼崽，就是我们从那个流浪部落里救回来的，狼石帮了他一次，他就赖上了。”
“这样啊……”
这语气，听着好像很失落啊。
狼晚没跟林楸多说，直接起身，踏入雨雾中。
林楸道：“晚叔，你去哪儿？”
狼星、狼藏随后，顺便跟他道：“我们随便逛逛，昨天回来得晚，还没出去看看。”
小狼们说的红鸟、咩咩兽、砖窑、小房子……他们哪个都好奇。
林楸咕哝：“现在怎么不说头发里长虫子……”
林楸起身，找了几个草帽，直接给他们送过去。
三个长辈拿着草帽看看，往脑袋上一扣，摆手道：“快回去，也不怕头发……”
“我知道！”
林楸立刻后撤一步，转身跑回食堂。
门口，狼果立在前头，后头一堆小崽子，笑眯眯地看着他。
幼崽凑到前头来，拉着林楸裤腿道：“楸，他们是谁啊？”
昨天兽人们回来得晚，半宿都在跟亲朋好友叙旧。
幼崽被狼果带着早早吃完肉汤，回草窝里睡觉，也没跟后来的兽人们说上话。
林楸：“你们喊阿爷。”
“阿爷是谁？”
“祭司阿爷。”
“不是祭司阿爷……”
幼崽七嘴八舌说着话，又好奇看着外面。
“他们也是支部落回来的兽人，他们走的时候，你们还没出生，果那个时候才你们这么大。”
幼崽仰起小脑袋瓜，看看狼果，又看看外面。
他们眼里还是陌生。
林楸揉了下幼崽的脑瓜子，道：“没事，熟悉了就好了。”
另一边，狼晚几个转悠着，就到了红鸟圈那边。
下雨天，红鸟躲在棚子底下。
火炕屋被狼溶占用着孵蛋，里头烧着火，有些热，现在红鸟不喜欢进去。
雨雾中，三个兽人趴在围栏，扯着脖子往里看。
“一、二、三……十五、十六……哎哟哟，该多少了？”狼藏整个身体压得围栏咯吱响。
狼晚嫌弃道：“安不是说了，一百多只。”
狼星瞧着红鸟火红的羽毛，重点在那腿上逡巡，半晌，他道：“就是肉少了点。”
狼藏：“安说味道好。”
狼晚看着里面有小狼出来，立马站直，三个兽人冲着小狼和蔼地点点头。
“叫什么？”
“狼川。”
屋里又探个头出来，狼晚一惊，“诶？一模一样。”
狼星想了想，“怕不是狼贝那两个大的。”
狼滔也站出来，与他兄弟并排。
他俩看着三个长辈叽里咕噜，说的好像是他阿母和阿父年轻时候的事，悄悄竖起耳朵听。
狼藏：“贝力气大，采集的野菜最多，不晓得她怎么看上细胳膊细腿儿的呼。”
狼晚：“人家哪里细胳膊细腿儿，就是白了点。”
狼星：“是，雄兽人没谁比他白的，长得也不错，贝当时看上了就拉他进了窝。当年就有了他两个。”
狼晚：“可不，说明不废。”
说着，三个兽人远离，又绕去咩咩兽那边。
两小狼对视一眼，赶紧跟上。
可他们却不说了，到了咩咩兽圈，直直地站在圈外头，看着里面的咩咩兽。
“活的呢……好多头。”狼晚声音放低，轻飘飘的，像雾。
狼星：“我算知道我们为什么能回来了。”
不论是大河里的鱼，还是大泽里的藕，这些食物再多，也不能养活两百多个狼兽人。
重要的是肉。
是能维持他们能量的红肉。
鱼他们吃了半年，起先能吃饱，但只吃鱼，会越来越没力气。他们混着菜，混着时不时捕到的猎物，慢慢能熬过去。
可兽人多了，意味着只抓一头猎物不够分，那大家全部一起挨饿。
回来之前他们忐忑过，害怕加重这群小狼的负担。
现在嘛，不会了……
要说红鸟只是沾沾味的，咩咩兽就能让他们有力气奔跑，干活，打架。
肉混着杂七杂八的野菜，尾巴草籽，便能吃得饱了。
要再扎实些，那便顿顿是肉。
不过放在以前在中央大陆的时候，这也是不敢想的。
三个兽人就趴在这栏杆边，一直看着。
狼溶在里面照顾新生的小咩咩兽，听到声音，出来就见昨天才从大泽回来的长辈们。
“小狼崽，过来。”狼晚低声道。
狼溶往前，走了几步，屋里又钻出两个小狼。
他们是狼溶后来听了林楸的话，忙不过来时，又向冰要的两个小兽人。
一个叫狼迷，一个叫狼逗。
两个亚兽人，心很细，经常跟着狼冰采集草药，也知道些草药知识，适合照顾咩咩兽幼崽。
三个小狼往前，隔着围栏，站在他们前头。
狼溶以为他要问咩咩兽的事情，心里打着腹稿，正打算从楸开始给难产的咩咩兽接生开始说起。
但三个长辈却什么都没问，只是把头上草帽摘下来，扣在他们脑袋上，按了按。
“好崽崽，进去吧，别淋到雨。”
狼溶愣住，要说的话堵在喉咙中。
“走了，等会儿要吃饭了，记得赶紧回来。”
雨丝如针，斜着飘落，刺得狼溶手臂微凉。
狼溶抿唇，目送他们离去。
外面的狼川狼滔也凑上来，疑惑看着愣神的狼溶。
狼溶喃喃道：“他们刚刚，好像哭了……”
“没有，只是眼眶红了。”狼迷轻轻道。
狼逗摸了摸头顶的帽子，扬起一抹笑，“兴许是眼角挂着雨呢？”
狼溶也笑起来。
“是，是雨。”
chapters.title: 第170章

chapters.translated_text:
Lang Wan, Lang Xing, and Lang Cang, three beastmen, were walking back along Wolf Mountain. Catching a scent different from that of the wolf beastmen, they peered into a cave with an open door—

Straw mats covered the floor, and round, plump straw nests were arranged in a circle against the cave walls. The nests were neat and uniform in size, without a single stray piece of hay or twig sticking out.

"This must be where the rabbit beastmen live," Lang Cang said.

Lang Wan: "So clean."

Lang Xing: "Why do I feel like the wolf cubs' nests look filthy after seeing this?"

Lang Wan chuckled.

The wolf cubs didn't have the patience to keep their nests like this.

"Let's go."

They didn't linger and headed slowly toward the cafeteria.

Halfway there, all three beastmen stopped simultaneously. Their gazes swept to the side, meeting a pair of eyes looking out from a crack in a door.

The eyes were calm and filled with curiosity.

The moment they locked eyes with them, the gaze became extremely timid, as if they had seen a plague god.

The next moment, the sound of messy footsteps and a thud came from inside the cave.

Lang Wan noticed the door was only slightly ajar, not closed tightly.

"Not a beastman who committed a mistake?"

Lang Xing: "And not a wolf beastman either."

Lang Wan had his hand on the door, about to open it, when someone from the cafeteria urged, "Uncle Wan! Uncle Xing! Uncle Cang! Meat soup is ready!"

Separated by the door, the three sub-beastmen inside tensed their bodies, burying their heads tightly into their legs.

Lang Wan let go of the door and walked quickly toward the cafeteria.

"Don't rush!"

They cooked mushrooms for lunch today; mushrooms were scarce at this time and were all brought back by the gathering team. Out of twenty vegetable baskets, only two contained them.

Lang An had made a stir-fried mushroom dish.

The mushrooms were fresh and tender, perfect for eating with the dry tail-grass seed rice. It turned out Lang An and the others had actually made it today.

Besides these two, there was the lotus root and bone soup they had been eating every day recently, plus an extra dish of tender lotus root stir-fried with meat slices.

The beastmen held their bowls, which were filled with solid tail-grass seed rice topped with mushrooms and lotus root stir-fry, with a side of lotus root and bone soup.

"Tsk tsk tsk, what kind of life is this," Lang Huo said.

Most of the tables in the cafeteria were finished, and the beastmen sat together in small groups to eat. Lang Yun pulled out the stool next to Lang Huo, sat down with a thud, and said, "An said it's to celebrate the tribe's reunion."

"So, there won't be any more after this?"

"Our tribe isn't that wealthy yet; how could we eat this well every meal?"

A table away, Lin Qiu calculated the food the tribe had stored; by next year, it should be enough.

This year, they couldn't eat dry tail-grass seed rice for every meal, but they could manage porridge once a day.

Dried vegetables and dried fish were definitely enough, but meat was still scarce.

However, they could definitely ensure the beastmen ate fresh meat every few days this snow season. They could slowly eat the hundred-plus red birds, and they could also slaughter seven or eight male bleat-beasts.

It was much better than the first snow season.

The cafeteria was filled with beastmen, and the rabbit beastmen were also mixed in, sharing tables with the wolf beastmen instead of sitting in the corner to eat like before.

The Wolf Tribe didn't have a rule about not talking while eating, but everyone was either immersed in the delicious food or afraid of being robbed by their companions if they ate too slowly. In a cafeteria of over a hundred beastmen, there was only the sound of beastmen shoveling food.

It was raining, so the little wolves didn't go out.

Lang Bing put down his bowl and sat opposite Lin Qiu. Lang Xue followed him, the cub holding her own bowl steadily.

Lang Bing helped the cub climb onto the stool and sit down.

Lin Qiu looked at the two and felt something was missing.

"Yu Le hasn't come back yet?"

"Don't know."

"Did he say how long he was going back for?"

Lang Xue: "Doesn't seem like he did..."

The little beastmen hadn't finished their training yet; if the time away was too long, they would easily get rusty.

"When Yu Lie comes next time, tell him..."

"Hahahaha, eating already?"

A familiar voice rang out. Yu Lie was carrying a large bag, vaulting over the low wall onto the corridor.

Lin Qiu looked at Yu Le, who was following him and also carrying a beast-skin bag.

"Speak of the devil."

Lang Xue: "Uncle Lie is here to mooch off our food again."

Lin Qiu had finished eating early, and there wasn't much left in his bowl. He stood up to greet them. Yu Lie looked toward him—it was unclear if he was looking at Lin Qiu or the dishes in the beastmen's bowls, but his eyes seemed to be glowing.

"Qiu! The beast tendons and horns the Wolf King told us to save, I've brought them for you."

"And two bleat-beasts," Yu Le added.

Lin Qiu met Yu Lie's expectant gaze and asked, "Have you eaten?"

Yu Lie grinned, "No."

"Go eat yourself. Leave the things here; I'll get someone to pack them up."

"Alright, we're going then."

Including Yu Le, five beastmen had come. The other three put down the tightly bound bleat-beasts and happily followed Yu Lie to mooch some food.

Inside, Lang Huo stared at him.

Yu Lie: "Eh? Huo, didn't you go hunting?"

Lang Huo: "Didn't go."

Their second hunting team was now responsible for digging lotus roots, along with the little wolf team. However, the King had told them to wait until the rain stopped, so they had this day of leisure.

Yu Lie naturally blended in with the wolf beastmen.

Lang Wan and the others watched him, knowing the relationship between the Black Feather Tribe and the Wolf Tribe was good now, so they withdrew their gazes after observing for a while.

Outside the corridor, Lin Qiu called over Lang Mo's team, who had finished eating.

"Mo, take the two bleat-beasts to the pen and keep them separate for a few days."

"And this?" Lang Mo patted the bulging beast-skin bag.

Lin Qiu opened it to look; a fishy, foul smell wafted out.

He turned his head away, choked, and said, "Send it to Uncle Qi; it's all material for making bows and arrows."

"Got it."

Lang Mo signaled two beastmen to take the bleat-beasts, then slung the beast-skin bag over his shoulder and walked away.

Lin Qiu washed his hands, went around to the windowsill, grabbed the food for the three sub-beastmen, and headed toward the cave.

Those three sub-beastmen had been living in the tribe for a long time now.

Now, the cloud leopard cub, Bao Zhi, hung around Lang Shi all day, slowly interacting with the beastmen and barely managing to say a few words.

But the three of them remained silent, hiding in that cave as if self-isolated.

They were adult beastmen; the hardships they had suffered were carved into their bones and were difficult to resolve. They couldn't help with this, and over time, the beastmen of the Wolf Tribe stopped expecting them to speak.

They were just being taken care of like this until now.

Lin Qiu walked to the cave door, knocked, and then opened it to place the bowls and chopsticks inside.

The sky was dark, and the deepest part of the cave was pitch black.

The half-closed door blocked most of the light, and only three dark shadows could be seen.

Lin Qiu hadn't come to deliver food for a long time, and the atmosphere was a bit oppressive as soon as he arrived.

"Time to eat."

There was no movement in the cave.

Lin Qiu closed the door and walked a few steps away before the sound of very light footsteps echoed from inside.

He left the area, waiting for the beastmen to finish so he could collect the bowls later.

Lang Bing and Lang Xue were sitting by the window. Seeing him return, they finished their meal quickly, took their bowls to wash, and tidied up Lin Qiu's as well.

"Qiu, it's almost snow season."

Lin Qiu took his bowl and walked alongside them.

"Yes, it's almost snow season."

"The cave those three beastmen live in is shallow; should we move them to another one?"

Lang Bing asked, and Lang Xue also looked up.

Lin Qiu supported the cub's head to make her watch her step, thought for a moment, and said, "See if they are willing to move."

"The deeper caves should only be the two that Yu Shan and the others lived in when they were sick last snow season."

"That won't work, the uncles are already living there."

"Then there's only the Black Cave behind the mountain."

Lang Bing nodded, planning to go ask later.

"Have they never come out?"

"They come out at night," Lang Bing said. "Just for a moment, then they go right back in."

"Did you find out which tribe they are from?"

"No, they won't open their mouths."

*

A while later, Lang Bing went to collect the bowls.

Lin Qiu followed him. When they opened the door, they saw the bowls were returned exactly as he had placed them, with the angle of placement not off by a hair.

The food inside had been eaten clean, as if washed.

Lang Bing picked them up and asked toward the dim cave, "It's almost snow season, this cave isn't warm enough. Do you want to change to another one?"

The response was the rustling of hay.

Lang Bing turned, and the door creaked shut.

After walking away, Lang Bing said to Lin Qiu, "They don't want to."

"Huh?" The beastmen hadn't spoken, so how did the little wolf know?

"They just don't want to." Lang Bing delivered their food the most often, and he was also responsible for treating the sub-beastmen's bodies, so he had the most contact with them and understood a little.

"Fine, if they don't want to, they don't want to."

The sub-beastmen were no kin to them; taking them in was already the Wolf Tribe's kindness.

They wouldn't treat these three sub-beastmen like they did the cubs, thinking of everything for them. They had provided a choice, and if the sub-beastmen didn't want it, they wouldn't force them.

After Lin Qiu and the other left, the sound of hay in the cave grew louder.

But there was still no sound of beastmen speaking, as if their throats were blocked.

After lunch, the beastmen who wanted to rest went to rest.

The beastmen from the branch tribe had just returned and were still curious about Wolf Mountain, so they asked the companions who had returned earlier to lead the way and continued wandering around.

Walking and walking, they somehow circled back to the cave where the three sub-beastmen lived.

Through the crack in the door, there was another pair of eyes peeking out.

Lang Wan frowned, suddenly grabbed the door and pulled it open, and before the beastman inside could run away, he grabbed him by the neck.

"Wan!"

"Umm... wuu wuu..." The sub-beastman in his hand was full of fear, trembling violently.

"Who are you? Why are you in the Wolf Tribe?"

The beastmen in the cafeteria noticed the commotion and ran over.

"Wan, let go of the beastman," Lang An said hurriedly.

Lang Wan refused to let go and pulled the sub-beastman out.

"Who are they?" he asked Lang An.

"Sub-beastmen saved from a wandering tribe, just like the cub Lang Shi brought."

"Have you figured out their background?"

"N-no."

"You dare to keep them in the tribe without knowing!" Lang Wan's voice rose.

"No, we asked, but they can't speak. We also interrogated the beastmen from the wandering tribe, and they said they didn't remember..."

"Since you don't know, why didn't you lock them up!" Lang Xing also had a dark face, looking at the beastmen of Wolf Mountain.

"You guys are too bold."

After being attacked by a wandering tribe once, they still dared to put strange beastmen at the front of Wolf Mountain, with the door left ajar and no beastmen guarding them. If they really ran away with the secrets of Wolf Mountain and attracted covetous eyes...

It was no wonder Lang Xing thought this way; their branch tribe had encountered all kinds of beastmen seeking help, and it turned out those beastmen were all trying to steal their food.

Not a single beastman was an exception.

Even if this sub-beastman was a victim of a wandering tribe, what did that have to do with the Wolf Tribe! Who knew if he would target the Wolf Tribe for his own tribe...

The elders' faces were livid, and none of them showed sympathy for this sub-beastman.

Lang Wan stared at him, remembering the eyes hidden behind the crack in the door.

He couldn't help but exert force with his hand.

"Umm..."

"Wan, Uncle Wan."

Lang Wan swept a glance over, and Lang Mo was also silenced as if his neck had been pinched.

"I don't care if you are a victim of a wandering tribe. The Wolf Tribe saved you and provided food and drink. If you develop any improper thoughts, then don't live."

"Umm..."

"Speak!"

"Umm, no, I don't dare."

The beastman's voice was hoarse, and the other beastmen who had wanted to stop Lang Wan stopped instantly.

He spoke...

Lang Wan narrowed his eyes.

Wasn't he able to speak?

"What's your name, which tribe are you from?"

"Wuu..." The tears on the sub-beastman's face fell drop by drop, looking extremely pitiful. The young wolf beastmen watching grabbed their paws, looking at the elders and then at the sub-beastman, wanting to help but not daring to move.

"Speak!" Lang Wan's eyes sharpened!

"Lu, Lu Ye, White River, White River Tribe."

Lang Wan looked at the other two sub-beastmen in the cave.

"Come out!"

Lin Qiu heard about the matter and hurried over. He saw all three sub-beastmen curled up in the daylight, their voices hoarse, intermittently explaining their origins.

Lin Qiu slowed his pace and looked at Lang Bing, who had run over with him.

"Didn't you say they wouldn't speak?" Lin Qiu said softly.

In the back row, Lang Mo, hearing his words, rubbed his tight heart, remembering Lang Wan's fierce look just now. A chill rose from the soles of his feet, and he couldn't help but shiver.

"If they didn't speak, they would have lost their lives."

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Bing, "Will there be a problem?"

When the sub-beastmen first came to the tribe, their mental state was abnormal. Now, how could they look like they could speak and cry, with clear eyes, leaving only a little fear?

Lang Bing: "Their bodies were fine long ago. The three sub-beastmen could communicate, but they never spoke to us."

Actually, he was getting impatient too.

If it hadn't been for Lang Wan's pressure, they didn't know how long they would have hidden.

Just as he thought of this, he heard Lang Wan ask: "Since your bodies are fine, why are you still clinging to the Wolf Tribe?"

"No..."

"I only listen to the truth."

The three sub-beastmen trembled slightly.

"W-we were afraid you would send us away. The tribe, the tribe is already gone, I have nowhere to go..." Lu Ye was a deer-tribe beastman, and those deer eyes were filled with tears, watery, making the beastmen's hearts soften.

"Is that so?" Lang Xing glared at his own beastmen, hating that they were so soft-hearted.

What kind of look was that!

The young beastmen jumped and buried their heads tightly.

Lu Ye buried his head, "Y-yes..."

Lang Xing said coldly, "Fine, drive him out."

The young beastmen didn't move, and Lang Cang was about to take action.

Lu Ye was terrified, retreating backward, trembling and saying, "No... I will die! I will die in the snow season, wuu wuu..."

Not a single beastman pleaded for him.

The young beastmen weren't stupid; they were just generous. Sympathy was sympathy, but they didn't allow themselves to be played for fools.

Seeing that they really wouldn't help, Lu Ye cried out in fear, saying, "I'll tell you, I-I wanted to see how you get food. I still have cubs in the tribe, I can't let them starve..."

Lin Qiu watched and felt something was wrong.

He tugged at Lang Bing, "Were they fine a long time ago?"

"Pretty much."

"I mean their brains were fine too."

Lang Bing shook his head, "I can't see their brains, and the priest can't either."

So not speaking wasn't because they were still sick, but because they were afraid of being exposed, or didn't dare to tell the wolf beastmen.

If it hadn't been for Uncle Wan's pressure, he wouldn't have known.

After finding out the situation, the three beastmen were locked in the Black Cave, with more beastmen guarding them.

In the cafeteria, the beastmen of the branch tribe sat upright, staring at the young ones from Wolf Mountain in front of them. Their faces were dark, as if a storm were coming.

Everyone was like newly hatched red bird chicks, quietly huddling together, heads lowered, not daring to speak.

"You guys are too bold!" Lang Chi spoke up, "You dare to put strange beastmen in the front mountain without finding out their background, and you don't even send beastmen to guard them!"
