Lin Qiu said, "Let’s see how much medicine you need first, and then we can see how much salt we can trade for with the remaining supplies?"

"That works."

Yang Juan had brought all the injured beastmen from the tribe, eleven in total.

Lin Qiu looked at the burn sites on the beastmen, his brows furrowing tightly.

The wounds already had a smell.

Fortunately, only one beastman had a large area of infection that needed cleaning. According to the beastmen, the wound had originally healed, but then it got wet, repeatedly worsening until it rotted.

"You should only need one pack of the external wound powder."

Lin Qiu checked the ones with blinded eyes, raspy throats, twisted hands, and broken feet one by one...

"For the beastmen with damaged eyes and throats, I can only give some medicine to make them feel better, but I can't cure them completely. I can fix the twisted hands. I can't do anything about the broken legs."

There were eleven patients in total, not all injured in the forest fire.

One patient needed debridement and anti-inflammatory treatment. Three patients only needed a little external powder.

Among the remaining seven, one had a sprain, one had a fracture, and five mostly had lingering illnesses from smoke inhalation.

The symptoms ranged from severe to mild; the severe ones were blind, mute, and coughed day and night, while the mild ones had eyes that watered easily and couldn't stand the light.

Lin Qiu estimated the value of the herbs they needed and swapped them directly for the herbs the beastmen brought.

Once he had a rough estimate, he said to Yang Juan, "Most of these herbs are common, only two are precious. For the wound powder, one basket per pack."

Yang Juan nodded.

They had brought two baskets of herbs.

Being able to trade for two packs was enough.

Seeing him agree, Lin Qiu caught a glimpse of the wolf beastmen unfolding the animal skins they had brought and asked directly, "How are the skins?"

"Pretty good." Inspecting the goods was a necessary part of the trading process.

The wolf beastmen checked the skins one by one, looking carefully.

It seemed these skins were meant for trading; they were tanned carefully, thick, and very soft.

They were just a bit small.

Facing the expectant gazes of the Black Sheep beastmen, Lin Qiu pointed to the beastman with the twisted hand and said, "I can only fix his hand; for the others, I can only give some medicine to make them feel better. To be completely cured, especially him..."

Lin Qiu pointed to the beastman with the broken leg.

"His leg is broken, but the bone has already healed. Because the bone is crooked, he will still be in pain. To get better, you’d have to find our priest to break the bone and reset it, so his leg won't hurt in the future."

The wolf beastmen listened, remembering when the priest saved Yu Hua by amputating his leg, and couldn't help but bare their teeth.

The Black Sheep beastmen heard this, their legs going weak, unable to even stand steady.

Especially the beastman with the broken leg; looking at the wolf beastmen’s sharp teeth, he felt it was all very sinister.

He trembled, and in the end, he was so scared his eyes turned red.

"I, I... I won't get it treated."

"No!" Yang Juan said sternly. "The patriarch said if it can be treated, it must be treated."

The other beastmen, who had been blocked by the Black Sheep beastmen, saw that the Wolf tribe was truly there to trade and stopped hesitating.

Fearing the Black Sheep beastmen would trade away everything, they hurried to squat on both sides.

Seeing they had all decided, Lin Qiu looked at the group of dark-skinned beastmen and said, "I can't cure you completely, only alleviate your pain. So if you want treatment, it’s two skins per beastman. See if you want to do it?"

"Treat it!"

Seven beastmen, fourteen skins.

Fortunately, they had brought enough skins; between their own tribe’s and the ones they borrowed, they had twenty-five in total.

Lin Qiu nodded upon hearing this.

He stopped guarding the stall and took out his herb-carrying pouch. Lang Huo helped by having the sick beastmen move to an empty space to expose their wounds.

Lin Qiu: "Huo, get some boiled water."

Lang Huo brought their water bottle.

Lin Qiu: "Start a fire directly and boil it in a clean pottery pot."

Lang Huo nodded and set down the bottle.

Lang Yan let Tu Ai guard the stall and went to Lin Qiu’s side.

While Lin Qiu treated the patients, Tu Ai continued to greet customers.

After setting aside fourteen skins, there were eleven skins and a basket of dried meat left.

"Are you using all of these to trade for salt?" Tu Ai asked.

Yang Juan squatted down, looking at the white salt with longing eyes.

He had never seen such clean salt.

It wasn't salt particles mixed with dirt and stone; it was as white as snow and as fine as quicksand.

Seeing him stare down for a long time without answering, Tu Ai thought he hadn't seen it before and hesitated.

He scraped a bit out with a leaf and held it out to him.

"Taste it first, our salt is definitely better than what you’ve traded for..."

Before he could finish, Yang Juan took the leaf.

He tilted his head back and poured all the salt on the leaf into his mouth.

Tu Ai’s face wrinkled, and he stuck out his tongue in empathy.

Their salt was very salty.

But Yang Juan’s expression didn't change; he savored it carefully and swallowed it all.

Tu Ai: "You..."

Yang Juan coughed from the saltiness. When a beastman offered him water, he waved it away. He licked his lips, as if trying to scrape up every bit of saltiness and swallow it into his stomach.

He looked at the salt on the stall with near-fanatical eyes, the corners of his mouth curled high, his dry, cracked lips bleeding.

"Trade! Trade it all!"

Hearing him agree, Tu Ai felt a surge of joy, but catching a glimpse of the moisture in the beastman’s eyes, he was shocked.

He suddenly remembered the Rabbit tribe back at Green Lake, also trading hard-grown plants everywhere for a bit of salt... Tu Ai lowered his head, his eyes stinging.

Both his shoulders felt heavy, and his head was pressed down.

Tu Ai turned back and saw several hands pulling away from him.

Lang Yun said, "Our tribe doesn't lack salt, don't cry."

Tu Ai: "I’m not crying."

Tu Ai’s eyes were red; he turned back, once again grateful that they had joined the Wolf tribe.

Tu Ai took a deep breath, smiled, and pointed to the candles and matches, resuming his role as a host.

"Don't you want to look at other things? This can start a fire, and you can see at night."

As he spoke, he demonstrated striking a match in front of a group of beastmen.

The beastmen recoiled in shock.

One beastman retreated too quickly and fell on his butt.

They watched Tu Ai light the candle; the flame was weak but didn't go out, and they gasped in surprise.

"Want it?" Tu Ai pitched.

"No, no, just salt." Yang Juan coveted everything. He stared at the pottery jars on display for a long time, forcing himself to tear his gaze away from such good things.

He wanted everything, but he didn't have enough to trade.

Tu Ai said, "Alright, one basket of dried meat for one scoop of salt."

Tu Ai patted their rattan basket.

This basket was smaller than the one Yang Juan brought, finely made, holding about ten pounds of meat, and was specifically used by the beastmen as a measuring tool.

The large scoop for the salt was also specially made by Lang Mo at Lin Qiu’s request; it was the size of an adult beastman’s palm, and one scoop definitely held two pounds of salt.

Now that dried meat was precious and salt was precious, the meat could trade for more salt than before.

But only a few tribes were as fair as the Wolf tribe; most still kept to the old ways.

When beastmen went to the large tribes in the west to trade for earth salt, that salt was scraped off the ground, mixed with mud and sand, and one basket of meat only got a handful of salt.

The basket used to hold that meat was as big as Yang Juan’s.

Dried meat was more valuable than animal skins; the eleven skins the Black Sheep tribe had left—ten skins for one basket of meat—could trade for one scoop of salt plus a little extra.

The Black Sheep beastmen hadn't expected to be able to trade for salt and hadn't brought containers for it.

The wolf beastmen, seeing they were the first customers, kindly gifted them a worn-out animal skin pouch.

Once the two large scoops of salt were poured in, the pouch was half full and heavy in the hand.

"Our salt is saltier and cleaner; you only need a little bit per meal. It’s much more cost-effective than other tribes' salt," Tu Ai said.

"That’s right, that’s right," Yang Jin, who had tasted it, nodded repeatedly.

He knew the quality of the Wolf tribe’s salt.

Yang Juan asked, "Can we trade again in the future?"

Tu Ai: "Of course."

A smile appeared on the Black Sheep beastman’s weathered face.

This trip wasn't a loss; both sides felt it was good.

Having obtained the goods, Yang Juan moved aside to guard his sick tribesmen.

Once the Black Sheep beastmen left, the other beastmen squatting on both sides gathered around.

They looked at the wolf beastmen’s stall and then at the group of wolf beastmen around Tu Ai. They crossed their hands, watching them nervously.

Lang Yun curled his lips, revealing his two sharp canine teeth, and smiled. "Want to trade?"

The beastmen nodded eagerly.

Lang Yun: "Where are the things to trade?"

The beastmen were stunned.

Mao Li looked anxiously toward the market entrance and said, "I told my beastmen to go back and prepare, you guys wait a bit longer."

The other beastmen were all shocked, staring blankly at him.

What did he mean he told his beastmen to go back and prepare?

When did that happen?

Mao Li calmed down and said, "What are you looking at me for?"

"Cunning!"

This market was small, and beastmen came often, never expecting to trade for salt, so the goods they brought were limited.

Now, seeing they didn't have enough to trade, they had to immediately tell their tribesmen to go back and get more.

The blue-tailed beastman had seen the cat beastman’s actions earlier and had also told his beastmen to go back and prepare early.

They just needed to wait.

Tu Ai, having nothing to do, continued to introduce the Wolf tribe’s good things to them.

Lan Jing was interested in everything. When Tu Ai introduced the pottery jars, he looked up and saw the White Sparrow beastman squatting on one.

"White Sparrow?"

Que Shi’er Bai looked at him with an unfamiliar expression.

Lan Jing: "Little White Sparrow, why didn't your patriarch come?"

The blue-tailed beastmen were very beautiful, with fair skin, especially that light blue hair draped over their shoulders like natural decoration.

But Que Shi’er Bai looked at the beastman talking to him, thought carefully, and confirmed he didn't know him.

"You know our patriarch?"

"Que Dabai, right?"

"What’s your relationship?"

Lan Jing played with his long blue hair, hummed lightly, and said, "Has he found a partner yet?"

Que Shi’er Bai shook his head.

Lan Jing stopped asking.

Tu Ai looked at the White Sparrow with a gossiping expression.

Que Shi’er Bai jumped off the pottery jar, turned his head to look around, saw his uncle, and fluttered over, landing lightly beside Que Erbai.

Que Erbai was watching Lin Qiu treat the patients.

His wing was nudged, and he looked at the little white sparrow.

Que Shi’er Bai raised his wing and pointed at Lan Jing. "Uncle Erbai, that blue-tailed beastman asked if the patriarch has found a partner. Does the patriarch know him?"

The wolf beastmen present pricked up their ears to listen.

Even Lin Qiu couldn't help but glance at Lan Jing.

Que Erbai: "Oh, they used to be together."

Lin Qiu’s hand shook.

The wolf beastmen all raised their heads, looking at Que Erbai in surprise.

Que Erbai didn't care at all about spilling his brother’s secrets. He laughed and said, "What of it? We Feather tribe members aren't like you wolf beastmen who only find one partner for life."

That made some sense.

But wasn't it a coincidence to run into the White Sparrow patriarch’s old flame here?

Lin Qiu coughed lightly, remembered he still had patients, and suppressed the urge to ask more, focusing on the treatment.

The beastman’s wound must have healed and then broken open repeatedly; there was already necrotic tissue.

Lin Qiu burned his knife in the fire, turned back, and asked, "Who’s coming? Help remove the necrotic tissue."

"Cut meat?" Lang Huo said, reaching out with interest.

Lin Qiu: "...It’s about the same as cutting meat."

The pinned-down Black Sheep beastman had a look of terror.

Lin Qiu said, "Your wound already has pus and blood; we must cut away the necrotic tissue and squeeze out the pus, otherwise no matter how much medicine we apply, it will never heal."

"No, no... don't..."

The beastman kicked his legs and retreated.

Yang Juan signaled for more beastmen to come forward and hold him down.

The beastman couldn't escape, feeling desperate, and could only look at Lin Qiu with teary eyes.

Yang Juan asked for him, "Does, does it hurt?"

His own teeth felt a bit sour, let alone the beastman about to have his flesh cut.

Lin Qiu: "Don't worry, there’s medicine to make it not... not that painful."

Yang Juan grabbed the beastman’s shoulders firmly and said, "Did you hear that? It won't hurt."

"Ahhh!!!" The beastman was in so much pain he bit the stick in his mouth to pieces. He was teary-eyed, his cries of pain muffled.

Who said it wouldn't hurt!

Who said that!

Lin Qiu’s forehead was covered in sweat. Seeing the Black Sheep beastmen couldn't hold him down, the wolf beastmen stepped in to help. Their large hands were like iron hoops, grabbing the beastman’s leg and making him unable to move.

Lin Qiu kept pouring medicinal water onto the wound and said to Lang Huo, "The pus and blood must also be squeezed out, it must be squeezed clean."

Lang Huo threw down the knife, which was stained with bits of flesh.

The flesh had changed color and had a foul smell.

Lang Huo didn't change his expression. Lin Qiu rinsed his hands with medicinal water, and then Lang Huo grabbed the beastman’s wound and started squeezing.

"Wuwu ahhh..." The beastman whimpered, his body trembling in pain.

Lin Qiu watched the pus and blood flow out bit by bit, his brows furrowed.

There was too much; he thought the wound was still okay, but looking at it now, the flesh inside had rotted for the most part.

It was a good thing this beastman was tough, otherwise he would have been like the other burned beastmen in their tribe and long gone.

The Black Sheep beastmen also looked at his leg, watching the thick yellow liquid flow down.

"It didn't look like that much on the surface..."

"That’s why his wound wouldn't heal; that’s the reason."

Lin Qiu could see that medicine had been applied to the wound, but since it wasn't cleaned properly, the effect of the herbs was greatly diminished.

After finally cleaning it, Lin Qiu looked at the hole in the beastman’s leg and handed the medicinal water to Lang Huo.

"Irrigate the inside of the wound."

The Black Sheep beastman had already fainted.

Even in his unconscious state, he still let out soft groans of pain.

The other beastmen who needed treatment looked at their companion’s miserable state, feeling a bit chilled, and even retreated slightly.

Lin Qiu watched Lang Huo debride the wound. After finishing, he said to the beastmen whose thoughts were written all over their faces, "You don't have to be like that."

Everyone breathed a sigh of relief.

But the beastman with the broken leg touched his twisted leg, thinking that he could live just by making do.

On this side, the beastman’s wound was cleaned, and Lin Qiu sprinkled the powder made by the priest onto the wound and wrapped it with cloth.

Lang Huo stood up, shook his hands, his forehead covered in sweat.

"I’m going to wash my hands."

He said, striding away with his long legs.

Lin Qiu signaled Yang Juan to move the beastman to the side to let him rest.

Yang Juan looked at his miserable companion and said, "Didn't you say it wouldn't hurt?"

Lin Qiu: "I said it wouldn't be *that* painful, I didn't say it wouldn't hurt at all."

Yang Juan: "..."

Lin Qiu went to wash his hands, and Lang Yan followed him.

They asked the Black Sheep beastmen where there was water nearby and were just about to head over when, as they reached the edge of the bushes, Lang Yan paused.

Several large lions suddenly jumped out of the woods.

Lin Qiu was startled and dodged.

Before he could run, he heard a large lion say, "You’re done trading? You’re leaving? We agreed you’d wait for us!"

Lin Qiu’s heart pounded, and his face turned pale.

Lang Yan stared at them with a dark face, cold air radiating from him.

"No..." we’re done trading.

Lin Qiu’s hands were dirty, so without thinking, he stood on tiptoe and pressed his cheek against Lang Yan’s mouth.

Lang Yan took a deep breath, his nose brushing against Lin Qiu’s face, rubbing it once, before grabbing him and walking away.

The lion beastmen, carrying large bags and small bundles, looked at each other.

Shi Ye also looked up, seeing the wolf beastmen all huddled together, looking at them defensively, and slowly began to understand.

Shi Ye laughed heartily and said, "Misunderstanding, misunderstanding, we..."

He slapped a large lion nearby on the head.

"Roar!"

"What are you roaring for! You just scared the beastman."

The large lion stared at Shi Ye with a resentful look.

Who scared whom?

It was clearly Shi Ye who did it himself!

林子里，水边。
狼火先一步洗完手回去。
林楸蹲在狼岩身侧，双手浸入水中。山泉水凉，林楸洗干净手，刚拿出来就被狼岩抓过去。
他看着狼岩用帕子包裹住他的手，往前挪了挪，脑袋拱了下狼岩肩膀。
“吓到了？”
“有点。”
那么大个狮子忽然从树丛里蹦出来，是个人都要被吓到。
狼岩：“你还没习惯。”
林楸蹭了蹭他，“几十年养成的认知，哪能这么容易改变。”
狼岩抓着他的手起来。
“所以要学会感受，要是刚刚敏锐一点，你就能知道林子后头有兽人来，他们并没有隐藏。”
林楸点头，“我可能得练习练习。”
他没这个习惯。
“好，这一路上多感受。”
林楸应下。
回去后，七头大狮子已经把他们的摊位围住了。
狮兽人兽形庞大，比狼兽人还大。
鬃毛凌乱，又没打理过，加上正是换毛的时候，毛发一块一块团在一起，像流浪了十几年，自带一股沧桑感。
人形的狮兽人也魁梧。
不过没了毛皮遮掩，瘦削的身体就露了出来，只骨架还大。
哎！都瘦。
“来了来了。”狮也看着林楸和狼岩道。
以他的眼力，自然看得出狼兽人队伍里做主的就是这两个。一个狼王，一个狼王伴侣。
林楸还要继续给黑羊兽人配草药，没在摊位前守着，径直去了黑羊兽人那边。
狼岩看兔艾已经缩到狼兽人后头。
狼云蹲在前面，冲着他招手。
“王，他们要用兽皮换盐。”
狼岩上前，狼云指着那一堆兽皮道：“这么多兽皮，全部换盐。”
狼云不担心盐不够，因为他们带了很多。
他担心兽皮太多，他们不好带走。
狮也见狼岩的目光落到他们带过来的兽皮上，赶紧拿起一张，举起来拍了拍。
那爪子跟蒲扇似的，又大又有劲儿，拍得兽皮上的灰四溅，发出沉闷的响声。
“我们的兽皮又大又厚。你摸一摸，我们可没拿差的兽皮来。”
确实，狮兽人的兽皮一张顶黑羊部落两张，甚至三张。
狼岩看着这些兽皮好多都是中央大陆的野兽皮，道：“几年前的？”
“新的，新的！”狮也声音雄浑，都瘦得没多少肉了，说话还中气十足。
“这是我们离开中央大陆前准备的猎物，肉我们吃了，兽皮也留下来了。”
狼岩：“鞣制得不算好。”
“这还不好？”
狼岩没废话，看了眼狼云。
狼云立马把黑羊部落带来的兽皮拎起来一张，递到狮也跟前。
狮也一摸，“诶？”
他双手拍上去，搓揉两下，兽皮也软得卷起来。是比他们稍微有那么一点点硬的兽皮鞣制得好一点。
狼岩：“你们的兽皮大，但拿回去我们还要重新弄一遍，六张兽皮一勺盐。”
他们的兽皮是黑羊部落的两三倍大，本来可以五张一勺盐，但狼兽人还得费点力气重新鞣制，多一张算工费。
狮算了算他们带来的兽皮。
一共七十张……
“七十张……能换多少盐来着？”狮也掰了半天手指也没算清。
狼岩：“十一勺，还四张。”
能装满满一背篓的盐了。
“那四张也换了。我们换这么多，你再多给我们一点盐。”
“差两张兽皮，给你们十二勺。”
“行！行。”
猫栗就蹲在旁边守着，看着狼兽人一勺一勺盐往狮兽人的兽皮袋里装。
兽皮袋渐渐鼓起，狮兽人又换了一个兽皮袋。
猫栗看得焦急，他盯着狼兽人装盐的兽皮袋，忍不住道：“你们别换完了。”
“放心，还有。”狼云一边吭哧吭哧挖盐，一边道。
他们一行三十六个兽人，有十个都背着盐，分量足足的。
狮兽人带着两个兽皮袋的盐，心满意足地离开了。
狼兽人没等多久，另外几个小部落也都陆续过来。无一例外，他们都要盐。
交换完的兽人离开，林楸也配完草药回来。
摊位前现在只剩下六个猫兽人。
为首的猫栗蹲在前面，身后五个猫猫保持兽形，缩在他后面，直直地蹲了一溜。
林楸看到那四个爪子黢黑，身上分布着黑色条纹的棕色小猫，瞳孔缩了缩。
狼岩指腹刮过他的脸，眼神询问。
林楸将手塞入他掌中，十指相扣，狠狠抓捏两下。
他第一次看到这么小的猫猫兽人！
虎头虎脑，毛一看就很柔软。眼睛还是蓝色的，像雨后的天空一样透蓝。
狼岩看看那群猫族，再看看自己伴侣，似乎明白了什么。
他脸有点黑，抬手挡住林楸视线。
林楸仰头，狼岩手掌跟着挪动。
“我就看一看。”林楸小声道。
猫栗他们已经交换完盐了，但他们没走。
兔艾问：“还有没有想交换的？”
猫栗指了指他们的陶罐。
“这个……怎么换？”
兔艾赶紧道：“不同大小的陶罐不一样，你等着。”
兔艾和狼兽人们把大大小小的罐子都抱出来。
猫栗身后的其他猫兽人轻轻用爪子勾了勾猫栗的兽皮裙。
“我们没东西了。”
带来的兽皮全部交换了。
猫栗手往后，指了指他们的摊位。
几个猫兽人曲着爪爪，兴奋地往猫栗背上一拍，立即转身去把那些鱼干肉干收拾好。
兔艾拎起个陶碗，拳头那么大，给他介绍：“这种小的陶碗，一块兽皮一个。”
“这个陶罐我们一般用来装盐和油，两块兽皮一个。”狼云举起个小陶罐，那罐子放在他手中，刚好巴掌大。
“再大一点的，可以放在火上烧，五张兽皮一个。”
“最大的……十张兽皮一个。”
猫栗目光定在那个中等大小的陶罐上
他双手搭在膝上，有心想摸一摸。
狼云看出他的意图，直接把陶罐塞他手里。猫栗一个激动，头顶两个毛毛耳朵扑哧一下冒出来，微微一颤。
林楸刚抓下狼岩的手，看到这一幕，目光一呆。
狼岩舌尖抵了抵腮帮子，气笑了。
兽人欣赏另一个兽人的兽形，那就意味着对兽人有好感，下一步就该继续考察适不适合成为伴侣了。
他抓着林楸肩膀，脑袋一低，两个大大的狼耳朵从头顶冒出来，杵在林楸面前。
林楸呼吸一滞。
狼耳弹动，林楸的目光彻底被狼岩吸引。
另一边，兔艾和狼兽人们还在做买卖。
猫栗捧着那大肚罐子，爱不释手，不想还了。
他小声道：“鱼干，你们收吗？”
“鱼干？”
兔艾回头。
狼兽人也回头。
他们吃了太多的鱼干了，不知道还要不要。大伙儿拿不定主意，下意识找林楸和狼岩。
然后一眼看见他们王被楸扑过去，头顶两个毛耳朵被林楸紧紧抓住。
兽人们赶紧回头。
狼岩脖子绯红，青筋一跳一跳的。
他双手把住自家伴侣的腰，咬着牙道：“换。”
林楸一心被那一双尖尖耳吸引，笑弯了眼。他撑着狼岩胸口，直起身，鼻尖蹭了蹭那毛耳朵。
为什么以前都没看见过？
他还以为人形的时候不能把毛耳朵放出来。
最终，猫栗用一藤筐的鱼干跟他们换了一个小陶罐。
那陶罐像寻常药罐子那么大，小猫兽人个头小，抱着正好合适。
他们欢欢喜喜抱着交换来的东西打算离开，走前，飞快看了一眼狼王和他的伴侣。
咦……这么多兽人面前，人形还露出兽形特征让伴侣摸……
这跟调情有什么区别。
“咳，咱们现在干什么？”
来交换的兽人都走光了，狼兽人们和兔艾还蹲在摊位前，不敢转身。
兔艾竖起耳朵，慢慢撇向后。
林楸牙根痒痒，趴在狼岩头顶，已经将毛耳朵咬得湿湿的。他疑惑地看向兽人们。
他们怎么不动？
狼岩无奈，麦色的皮肤都看得出绯红一片。
他把伴侣抱下来，耳朵收起来，拉着他钻进林子。
兽人们嘿嘿直笑。
兔艾轻咳一声，“咱们清点一下东西。”
“嘿嘿……”狼兽人继续笑。
带出来的草药少了一点，盐少了两个兽皮袋，陶罐交换出去一个，剩下蜡烛、火柴一个也没卖掉。
“咕咕——”
狼云捂肚子。
兽人们看向他，他无辜道：“饿了。”
兔艾看看林子，“谁去？”
狼兽人们摇头。
万一他们在交配呢？
过去撞上了岂不是要被王按在地上狠狠摩擦。
“那做饭？”
“做饭做饭！”雀二白不把自己当外人，一听做饭，一下睁开眼，从树上飞扑而下。
狼兽人们看看林子，“反正现在不走，做饭！”
林子里。
林楸被狼岩直接抱起来。
他双腿自然地圈在狼岩腰上，双手环抱他脖子，眼神询问。
狼岩没说话，又把耳朵露出来。
林楸眼睛一亮，双手抓上去，捏在手里揉搓。
狼岩闷哼，低下头，脑袋深深埋在林楸肩窝，把他抱得紧紧的。
等林楸揉了好一通，他双手依旧搭在狼岩耳朵上，脸颊红扑扑的。
手指从狠揉变成轻捻，一下一下，弄得狼岩心口犹如虫子在啃，痒得厉害。
“摸够了？”
林楸轻捏。
狼岩没忍住，张口咬住林楸颈侧的软肉。
“那再摸一摸。”
好一会儿，外面都飘着饭菜的味道了，林楸才和狼岩出去。
兽人们蹲在陶锅边，悄悄瞥一眼过来。
林楸这次敏锐，捕捉到视线就直直地看回去，一连看了几个，兽人们都慌忙收回目光。
他奇怪道：“你们看我干什么？”
“咳。”
“咳咳咳咳……”
咳得最厉害的狼火被林楸盯着。
他抬起头，又大咳几声，然后镇定道：“口水呛到了。”
林楸蹙眉。
他觉得哪里有点不对劲儿。
林楸回头看向狼岩。
狼岩静静地站在他身后，神色淡然，灰眸温和，微微抬眉似询问他什么事。
林楸摇了摇头。
算了，他就当兽人们真的被口水呛到了。
他不就摸了伴侣的耳朵，又没干什么坏事。
饱餐一顿，大家闭眼小憩一会儿，继续收拾东西赶路。
这一趟交换的东西兽人们也带着，不然没地方放。有兽人提议放在这附近的部落那里，但狼兽人对他们还没这么信任。
长长的队伍往南行。
一路上没吭声的鹿叶跟在队伍中，期待着到达白河部落的那一刻。
*
白雀部落西部。
白雀族长在空旷的山坡上飞了一圈。
去年才被山火烧过的葡萄园，如今又被绿意覆盖。葡萄抽出嫩枝，成串的花绽放开来。
狼果扛着刚在林子里砍的木头，往地上一放。
小狼站在坡下道：“果，绳子不够了！”
“等会儿！”
狼果没放弃葡萄园，现在幼崽大了，出了窝一般就不用狼果管了。他手里没事儿，便把清理葡萄园这事儿接过来。
他们来得晚了些，去年山火过后活下来的葡萄也不少，早已经牵藤。
兽人们搭架子还得小心些，免得把嫩藤折断。
雪季时，楸分的酒他们早就喝完了。王和楸不在，狼果可不忍心放任这葡萄乱长。
好在楸跟白雀兽人说过怎么管理，狼果把白雀族长叫来，再带了几个小狼过来搭把手。
他们还得赶紧做完，大泽那边的活儿还多着。
正忙着，白雀族长站在枝条上，看着几道绿色的身影从头顶掠过。
“绿眼兽人？”
狼果从藤筐里掏绳子的手一顿，抬头看了一眼，“他们不会在外面没找到定居的地方，又回来给我们帮忙了？”
白雀族长：“没几个兽人。”
大泽。
绿月带着两个兽人落下。
狼雨正在切肉，视线中一抹绿光闪过，定睛一看，才发现是绿眼兽人。
见是绿月，他笑着迎出来。
“你们怎么回来了？”
支部落回来的兽人则皱眉看着他们。
绿月将东西放下，对狼雨温声道：“我们来还渔网。”
“楸呢？”
“楸不在。”
绿月点点头，像是随口一问。
“谢谢你们的渔网，这是我们部落做的鱼干，是之前说好的交换。”
后头两个绿眼兽人把兽皮袋放下。
兽皮袋很大，鱼干装得快要撑出来。
狼雨看了眼，邀请他坐，又给他们倒了一碗水。
绿月捧着陶碗，坐在棚子边缘，静静看着眼前又变了模样的大泽。
“当初遇到山火的时候，还要谢谢你们收留。”
狼雨摇头，“是你们帮我们干活换的。”
他看着眼前这个绿眼兽人。
绿月好似又变了些，目光沉静，愈发有种楸身上那种胸有成竹、镇定自若的感觉。
看来才一个雪季，绿眼部落就发生了不少事。
“你们现在还好吗？”
绿月嘴角的肌肉微微提起，笑得牵强。
“族长死了。”
狼雨眼皮一跳。
绿月轻叹，把他们离开大泽后的事情徐徐道来。
“我们一路往南边走，终于在雪季前找到一个合适的定居位置。那里有很大一片湖，就算湖面上了冻，有你们借的渔网，我们应该也能熬雪季……”
绿眼兽人决定在那里定居，并且连住的山洞都找好了，也收拾干净了。
那边猎物不算多，但湖中鱼多。
他们用渔网捞了很多的鱼起来，做了鱼干，也学着狼兽人做烤鱼、煎鱼……他们想尽办法，让兽人们吃饱，绿眼部落也慢慢恢复元气。
可就在雪季到来的前一天晚上，他们还在说着湖里的鱼足够他们度过雪季的话，可第二天早上起来，就发现族长不见了。
“那他去哪你……”说到一半，狼雨哑然。
他已经知道了结果。
绿月苦笑，嘴角是弯的，可眼里溢满悲伤。
“我们在湖里发现了他。”
绿月想不明白，他们明明都找到合适的定居地方了，而且以那地方的条件，他们也不至于饿死。
只要好好经营，他相信，他们也能吃饱穿暖，如同狼部落一样。
他有这个自信。
可族长就在这时，投了湖。
这对绿眼兽人们来说，是一个巨大的打击。
兽人们好不容易有了希望，却因为族长主动寻死，打击得差点追随他而去。
狼雨沉默，他看着大泽上忙碌的兽人们，听着叮叮当当敲砖铺路的声音，良久，才道：“他当时在大泽，就有点奇怪了。”
绿月：“是，皎当时就说族长废了。”
他那会儿只当族长没了期望，不想再经营部落了，哪知道他是想死。
绿月把这件事说出来，心中总算没那么压抑了。
这些话他又不能跟族人去说，只能跟狼兽人说。
他调整了下心情，扬起笑，对着狼雨道：“我们打算离开那里，重新找合适的地方定居。”
狼雨看着兽皮袋里那堆渔网，目光一顿。
“去哪儿？”
“他们说南边没有雪季，我们打算再走远一点，去没有雪季的地方。”
他的族人们因为袭击狼部落，落下了病根，天一冷，伤处就是彻骨的疼。
这是他们自己造成的，怪不了狼部落。
相反，绿月却感激他们。
没有狼部落，他就不会成为绿眼部落的族长，不会明白，亚兽人不是只能待在窝里生蛋带崽，他们也可以养活部落。
狼雨慢慢将装渔网的兽皮袋拿过来，他打开，看到了那张渔网。
是新的。
他们给绿眼部落的渔网本来就很旧了，用了这么久，不可能还变成一张新的网。
绿月见他察觉，笑容变得有些骄傲，也有些不好意思。
“你们介不介意……我们学你们织渔网？”
狼雨看着眼前这个脱胎换骨般的亚兽人，他眉眼的自信惊人。
他道：“能学过去，那是你们的本事。”
绿月弯唇，“谢谢。”
“留下吃一顿肉汤再走？”
绿月起身，静静地看着狼雨，看着四处忙碌的亚兽人们。他道：“不了，部落还需要我，我得赶回去。”
“以后要是有机会……”绿月笑起来，很文静，也很坚定，“再见。”
他们匆匆来，匆匆离开。
狼雨追了几步，站在已经可以行走的大泽边缘，目送他们飞远。
绿眼兽人的羽毛炫目，阳光下灼眼。
狼雨想，他们部落的雄兽人虽然撑不起来了，但那么多没有受伤的亚兽人和雌性兽人，还有那么多慢慢长成的幼崽，也会重新支撑起绿眼部落。
狼雨高兴他们能重新振作起来，但也有些怅然。
部落迁徙是常态，这句再见，不知道还能不能兑现。
他还挺欣赏绿月这个朋友。
*
半个月后。
兔兽人曾经的部落——
绿湖。
兔艾站在湖边，捡起一片绿色的羽毛。
风拂过，羽毛从他手中飞落，掉在湖面，越飘越远。
林楸看着，道：“绿眼部落来过。”
一路走来，林楸可谓是忙个不停。
林子里有一只鸟狼岩都得停下来，看着他，让他判断那是个大鸟还是小鸟。
练习多了，林楸慢慢习惯调动五感，去观察身处的环境。
绿湖不愧被称为绿湖，名字很贴切。
这里是河流的下游，地势平坦，岸旁都是青草。水在这里汇聚成湖泊，阳光下碧绿澄澈。
这是一片极大的湖。
狼兽人是昨天晚上到的，到了之后，先打探周围的情况，然后便发现这里有不少部落曾经在这里停歇过。
其中一个，就是他们熟悉的绿眼部落。
狼兽人闻着味道，观察附近的生活痕迹，断定绿眼部落应该是前脚走，后脚他们就到了。
在兔艾的带领下，兽人们也赶了一个多月的路。
此时停下来，大家都迫不及待地修整。
现在已经是第二天中午，还有不少兽人睡得四仰八叉，呼噜声震天。
湖边平整，兔兽人们以前都是挖洞住在地下。
附近倒是有山洞，不过不在湖边，所以他们照旧是搭棚子睡觉。
一路走来，干粮已经吃完了。
林楸也一觉睡过了早晨，现在饿得肚子直叫，但也只能起来找食。
兔艾对这边熟悉，知道湖边有不少能吃的植物。
林楸带着醒了的兽人和他一起，身上斜着挎个藤筐，在四处采集。
哗啦一声——
狼岩在一旁抛下渔网，慢慢往回拉。
林楸采着野菜走到他旁边，手上拿着地上摘的浆果，凑到他嘴边。
狼岩低头轻轻咬过来。
手臂同时绷紧，拎着渔网一抬，被渔网抓住的鱼摔在岸上。
林楸蹲下，戳了戳那鱼，叹了口气。
狼岩一脚将要跳到湖里的鱼踢远一点，问兔艾：“这边一般能打到什么猎物？”
兔艾指了指湖水，“宽嘴兽。”
“长什么样？”林楸问。
“跟弯角兽一样大，四个蹄子，嘴巴又大又宽，尾巴是扁的。宽嘴兽喜欢吃水里的草，也能在林子里跑。我们以前只能靠碰运气，抓到几头小的，成年水兽都在深水处。”
林楸听这话，觉得应该不是他认识的那些动物。
林楸、兔艾和白雀们继续采集，狼岩抛了几网后，兽人们也差不多起来了。
他让狼兽人杀鱼，随后招来雀十二白。
“狼王。”雀十二白跑过来。
白雀兽人们矮小，雀十二白也才到狼岩肩膀高。
他头发白，眉毛也白，身条细长，像个少年人，但他其实成年了。
雀十二白小脸板着，不爱笑。
狼岩：“去水面上看看，有没有艾说的宽嘴兽。”
“好。”
兽皮一掉，一只胖白雀落在地上。他抖了下翅膀，振翅一飞，冲着宽阔的湖面去。
兔艾在一边喊道：“离湖面远一点！他们会跳起来……”
“哗啦——”
林楸震惊，看着那如水牛一样从平静水面扑腾起来的宽嘴兽，湖水被他搅动得如烟花炸开，砰的一声响。
好大！
“王！绳子！”
兽人们迅速把绳子打成圈送来。
狼云兴奋地喊道：“小白雀，把它往这边引！”
雀十二白绷着小脸，侧转身体，往岸边来。
狼火抱起兽人们的弓箭过来，“用这个！”
嗖嗖嗖几声——
湖水剧烈晃动了一会儿，没了声响。
林楸看着兽人们把绳子甩出去，绷直，然后往岸边拉。
有弓箭就跟开了挂一样。
还没近身，猎物就被拿下。
chapters.title: 第184章
chapters.translated_text:
**Chapter 184**

By the woods, by the water’s edge.

Lang Huo had finished washing his hands and returned first. Lin Qiu crouched beside Lang Yan, submerging his hands into the water. The mountain spring was icy; as soon as he pulled his hands out, Lang Yan grabbed them.

He watched as Lang Yan wrapped his hands in a cloth, then moved closer, nudging his head against Lang Yan’s shoulder.

“Frightened?”

“A little.”

Anyone would be startled if a lion that massive suddenly leaped out of the bushes.

Lang Yan said, “You still aren’t used to it.”

Lin Qiu rubbed against him. “My perception was formed over decades; it’s not that easy to change.”

Lang Yan pulled him up by the hands.

“That’s why you need to learn to sense your surroundings. If you had been more perceptive just now, you would have known there were beastmen behind the woods—they weren’t hiding.”

Lin Qiu nodded. “I probably need to practice.” He didn't have that habit yet.

“Good, spend this journey practicing your awareness.”

Lin Qiu agreed.

When they returned, seven large lions had already surrounded their stall. Lion beastmen had massive beast forms, even larger than wolf beastmen. Their manes were disheveled and unkempt, and since it was molting season, the fur was matted in clumps, giving them the look of wanderers who had spent a decade in the wild.

In their human forms, they were equally burly. However, without the thick fur to hide them, their lean, muscular frames were exposed, showing just how large their skeletons were. *Sigh, they’re all so thin.*

“We’re here, we’re here,” the lion, Shi Ye, said, looking at Lin Qiu and Lang Yan. With his experience, he could naturally tell that these two were the ones in charge of the wolf beastman group: the Wolf King and the Wolf King’s partner.

Lin Qiu still had to finish preparing medicinal herbs for the Black Sheep beastmen, so he didn't stay at the stall and headed straight to the sheep tribe.

Lang Yan saw Tu Ai shrinking behind a wolf beastman. Lang Yun was crouching in front, beckoning to him.

“King, they want to trade beast skins for salt.”

Lang Yan stepped forward. Lang Yun pointed to a pile of skins and said, “So many skins, all for salt.”

Lang Yun wasn’t worried about running out of salt—they had brought plenty. He was worried that there were too many skins to carry.

Seeing Lang Yan’s gaze fall on their skins, Shi Ye hurriedly grabbed one and gave it a solid slap. His paws were like large fans—big and powerful—sending dust flying from the hide with a dull thud.

“Our skins are big and thick. Touch them yourself; we didn’t bring any crappy ones.”

It was true; one lion skin was worth two or three of the Black Sheep tribe’s skins.

Lang Yan looked at the pile, noticing many were from beasts of the Central Continent. “From a few years ago?”

“New, they’re new!” Shi Ye’s voice was booming, and despite being thin, he still had a full, resonant tone. “These were prey we prepared before leaving the Central Continent. We ate the meat and kept the skins.”

Lang Yan commented, “The tanning isn’t very good.”

“This isn’t good enough?”

Lang Yan didn’t waste words; he glanced at Lang Yun. Lang Yun immediately picked up a skin from the Black Sheep tribe and handed it to Shi Ye.

Shi Ye touched it. “Eh?” He rubbed it between his hands, and the skin folded softly. It was indeed better tanned than their slightly stiff hides.

Lang Yan: “Your skins are large, but we have to re-process them when we take them back. Six skins for one scoop of salt.”

Since their skins were two or three times larger than the Black Sheep tribe's, normally it would be five skins for a scoop, but because the wolves had to put in the effort to re-tan them, the extra skin was for labor costs.

Shi Ye calculated the skins they brought. Seventy in total… “Seventy… how much salt is that?” Shi Ye counted his fingers for a long time but couldn’t figure it out.

Lang Yan: “Eleven scoops, with four skins left over.”

That was enough to fill a full basket of salt.

“Exchange those last four, too. We’re trading so much, give us a little extra salt.”

“Two more skins, and I’ll give you twelve scoops.”

“Deal! Deal.”

Mao Li crouched nearby, watching the wolf beastmen scoop salt into the lions' bags. As the bags bulged, the lions swapped for new ones. Mao Li watched anxiously, staring at the salt bags, and couldn't help but say, “Don’t trade it all away.”

“Don’t worry, there’s plenty,” Lang Yun said, digging out the salt with a grunt.

Their party of thirty-six beastmen had ten people carrying salt—the quantity was more than sufficient.

The lion beastmen left, satisfied, carrying two bags of salt.

They didn’t have to wait long before other small tribes arrived. Without exception, they all wanted salt.

After the traders left, Lin Qiu returned from finishing the medicinal herbs.

Only six cat beastmen remained at the stall. The leader, Mao Li, crouched in front, while five cats behind him remained in their beast forms, huddled in a straight line.

Seeing the brown kittens with ink-black paws and black striped markings, Lin Qiu’s pupils constricted.

Lang Yan traced his face with his thumb, his eyes questioning. Lin Qiu stuffed his hand into Lang Yan’s palm, fingers interlocking, and squeezed hard.

He had never seen such tiny cat beastmen! Their faces were round, their fur looked incredibly soft, and their eyes were as blue as the sky after a rainstorm.

Lang Yan looked at the cat tribe, then back at his partner, and seemed to understand something. His face darkened slightly, and he reached out to block Lin Qiu’s view.

Lin Qiu looked up; Lang Yan’s palm moved with him.

“I’m just looking,” Lin Qiu whispered.

Mao Li and his group had already exchanged their salt, but they didn’t leave.

Tu Ai asked, “Is there anything else you want to trade?”

Mao Li pointed to their clay pots. “These… how do you trade them?”

Tu Ai quickly said, “The price depends on the size. Wait a moment.”

Tu Ai and the wolf beastmen brought out all the pots, big and small.

The other cat beastmen behind Mao Li gently tugged at his beast-hide skirt with their paws. “We don’t have anything left.” All the skins they brought had been traded.

Mao Li pointed backward at their stall. Several cat beastmen curled their paws, tapped Mao Li’s back excitedly, and immediately turned to pack up their dried fish and jerky.

Tu Ai picked up a clay bowl, fist-sized, and introduced it: “This small bowl is one skin each.”

“We usually use these for salt and oil, two skins each,” Lang Yun said, holding up a palm-sized pot.

“The larger ones can be placed over a fire, five skins each.”

“The largest ones… ten skins each.”

Mao Li’s gaze settled on a medium-sized clay pot. He rested his hands on his knees, wanting to touch it. Seeing his intention, Lang Yun handed the pot directly to him. Mao Li was so excited that two fuzzy ears suddenly popped out from the top of his head, trembling slightly.

Lin Qiu had just pulled down Lang Yan’s hand when he saw this, his gaze going blank.

Lang Yan pressed his tongue against his cheek, feeling both annoyed and amused.

If a beastman admired another’s beast form, it meant they had a favorable impression of them, and the next step would be to assess whether they were suitable as a partner.

He grabbed Lin Qiu’s shoulders, lowered his head, and two large wolf ears popped out from his own head, nudging Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu’s breath hitched.

The wolf ears flicked, and Lin Qiu’s attention was completely captivated by Lang Yan.

On the other side, Tu Ai and the wolf beastmen were still busy trading.

Mao Li hugged the pot, unable to put it down. He whispered, “Do you accept dried fish?”

“Dried fish?” Tu Ai turned around. The wolf beastmen looked over too. They had eaten so much dried fish that they weren’t sure if they wanted more. They looked instinctively to Lin Qiu and Lang Yan, only to see their King being pounced on by Qiu, his ears held tightly by Lin Qiu’s hands.

The beastmen immediately looked away.

Lang Yan’s neck was flushed, his veins pulsing. He held his partner’s waist, gritting his teeth, and said, “Trade.”

Lin Qiu was focused entirely on those pointed ears, his eyes curved into crescents. He braced his hands on Lang Yan’s chest, straightened up, and rubbed his nose against the fur.

*Why haven’t I seen these before?* He thought human form couldn't reveal beast features.

In the end, Mao Li traded a basket of dried fish for a small pot. The pot was about the size of an ordinary medicine jar; for the small kitten beastmen, it was just the right size to hold.

They left happily, but before heading out, they took one last swift look at the Wolf King and his partner.

*Geez… in front of so many beastmen, showing beast features while in human form to let a partner touch them… what is this, if not flirting?*

“Ahem, what do we do now?”

The trading beastmen were all gone, but the wolf beastmen and Tu Ai were still crouching by the stall, not daring to turn around.

Tu Ai tilted his ears, glancing backward. Lin Qiu, teeth itching, was still leaning over Lang Yan’s head, having bitten the furry ear until it was damp. He looked at the beastmen with confusion. *Why aren’t they moving?*

Lang Yan felt helpless, his wheat-colored skin visibly flushed. He brought his partner down, retracted his ears, and dragged him into the woods.

The beastmen chuckled.

Tu Ai coughed lightly. “Let’s count up our stock.”

“Hehe…” the wolf beastmen continued to laugh.

They had less medicine, two bags fewer of salt, and one less pot, but the candles and matches hadn't sold.

“Grrrrrumble—”

Lang Yun covered his stomach. The beastmen looked at him, and he said innocently, “I’m hungry.”

Tu Ai looked toward the woods. “Who’s going?”

The wolf beastmen shook their heads. *What if they’re mating?* If they went over and ran into them, they’d be ground into the dirt by the King.

“Then… let’s cook?”

“Cook! Cook!” Que Erbai didn’t consider himself an outsider; as soon as he heard “cooking,” he opened his eyes and dove down from the tree.

The wolf beastmen glanced at the woods. “They aren’t leaving yet anyway—let’s cook!”

In the woods.

Lin Qiu was scooped up by Lang Yan. He wrapped his legs around Lang Yan’s waist, arms around his neck, eyes questioning.

Lang Yan didn’t speak, just revealed his ears again.

Lin Qiu’s eyes lit up. He grabbed them and kneaded them. Lang Yan grunted, lowering his head to bury it into Lin Qiu’s neck, hugging him tight.

By the time Lin Qiu had kneaded them enough, his hands were still resting on Lang Yan’s ears, his cheeks flushed bright red. His fingers changed from a firm rub to a light flick, over and over, making Lang Yan feel as if bugs were crawling in his heart—an unbearable itch.

“Had enough?”

Lin Qiu gave a light pinch.

Lang Yan couldn't hold back; he leaned in and bit the soft skin on Lin Qiu’s neck.

“Then let’s touch some more.”

A while later, with the smell of food drifting through the air, Lin Qiu and Lang Yan finally came out.

The beastmen were crouching by the clay pot, stealing glances. Lin Qiu, now perceptive, caught their gaze and stared straight back. One by one, the beastmen hurriedly looked away.

He asked strangely, “Why are you looking at me?”

“Ahem.”

“Cough, cough, cough…”

Lang Huo, the one who coughed the hardest, was stared down by Lin Qiu. He looked up, let out a few more loud coughs, and said calmly, “Choked on my own spit.”

Lin Qiu frowned. He felt like something wasn’t right.

He looked back at Lang Yan. Lang Yan stood silently behind him, his expression indifferent, his grey eyes gentle, one eyebrow slightly raised as if asking what was wrong.

Lin Qiu shook his head. *Forget it.* He’d just assume the beastmen had actually choked. It’s not like he did anything bad—he just touched his partner’s ears.

After a hearty meal and a short nap, they packed up to continue their journey. They were carrying the goods they’d traded, as there was nowhere else to put them. Some suggested leaving them at a nearby tribe, but the wolf beastmen didn’t trust them enough yet.

The long procession marched south.

Lu Ye, who had been silent the whole time, followed the group, looking forward to reaching the White River Tribe.

***

Western White Sparrow Tribe.

The White Sparrow chief flew a circle over the open hillside. The vineyard, burned by a forest fire last year, was now covered in green again. The grapevines were putting out tender branches, and clusters of flowers were in full bloom.

Lang Guo hoisted the wood he’d just chopped in the woods and dropped it. Little Wolf stood at the bottom of the slope. “Guo, we’re out of rope!”

“Hold on!”

Lang Guo hadn’t given up on the vineyard. Now that the pups were older and out of the nest, they didn't need much care, so he took over cleaning the vineyard. They had come a bit late, but many vines had survived the fire and were already growing.

The beastmen had to be careful setting up the trellises so they wouldn't snap the tender vines.

During the snowy season, they had long finished the wine Qiu had shared. With the King and Qiu away, Lang Guo couldn’t bear to let the grapes grow wild. Fortunately, Qiu had told the White Sparrow beastmen how to manage it, so Lang Guo called the White Sparrow chief to help, bringing along a few little wolves to lend a hand.

They had to finish quickly; there was still plenty of work to do back at Daze.

While busy, the White Sparrow chief stood on a branch, watching several green shadows streak overhead.

“Green-eyed beastmen?”

Lang Guo paused while reaching for rope in a basket and looked up. “They couldn't have failed to find a place to settle and came back to help us, right?”

White Sparrow chief: “There aren’t many of them.”

Daze.

Green Moon landed with two beastmen. Lang Yu was cutting meat when a flash of green crossed his vision. Looking closely, he realized it was the Green-eyed beastmen.

Seeing it was Green Moon, he smiled and went to greet them. “Why are you back?”

The beastmen who had returned from the branch tribe frowned at them.

Green Moon put the goods down and said gently to Lang Yu, “We came to return the fishing nets.”

“Where’s Qiu?”

“Qiu isn’t here.”

Green Moon nodded, as if it were a casual question. “Thanks for the nets. This is dried fish from our tribe, as we agreed.”

The two Green-eyed beastmen behind him set down the hide bags. The bags were large, and the dried fish was ready to burst out.

Lang Yu looked them over, invited them to sit, and poured them a bowl of water. Green Moon held the bowl, sitting at the edge of the shelter, quietly watching Daze, which had changed so much.

“We have to thank you for taking us in when we encountered the forest fire.”

Lang Yu shook his head. “You worked for it. It was a trade.”

He looked at the Green-eyed beastman. Green Moon seemed to have changed; his gaze was calm, and he had an air of confidence, much like Qiu. It seemed that in just one snowy season, a lot had happened in the Green-eyed tribe.

“Are you all doing okay now?”

The corners of Green Moon’s mouth lifted slightly, a forced smile. “The chief is dead.”

Lang Yu’s eyelids twitched.

Green Moon sighed softly, slowly recounting what happened after they left Daze.

“We walked south and finally found a suitable place before the snowy season. There was a large lake. Even if the surface froze, with the nets you lent us, we figured we could survive…”

The Green-eyed beastmen decided to settle there. They found a cave and cleaned it up. There wasn’t much game, but the lake was full of fish. They used the nets to catch plenty, made dried fish, and learned to roast and fry it, just like the wolves. They tried everything to keep everyone fed, and the Green-eyed tribe slowly recovered.

But the night before the snowy season arrived, while they were talking about how the fish would last them the winter, they woke up the next morning to find the chief missing.

“Then where did he…” Lang Yu trailed off. He already knew the outcome.

Green Moon gave a bitter laugh, the corners of his mouth turned up, but his eyes overflowed with sorrow. “We found him in the lake.”

Green Moon couldn't understand it. They had found a suitable place; they wouldn’t have starved. As long as they managed it well, he believed they could be fed and clothed just like the Wolf Tribe. He had that confidence. But the chief just threw himself into the lake.

It was a huge blow to the Green-eyed tribe. The beastmen had finally found hope, and the chief’s suicide almost made them want to follow him.

Lang Yu was silent. He looked at the busy beastmen at Daze, heard the clanging of bricks being laid for roads, and after a long time, said, “He was acting a bit strange when he was at Daze.”

Green Moon: “Yes, Jiao said back then that the chief was a lost cause.” He thought the chief had just lost his drive, never realizing he wanted to die.

Having said this out loud, Green Moon felt a little less oppressed. He couldn’t tell his tribesmen, so he could only tell the wolf beastmen.

He adjusted his mood, raised a smile, and said to Lang Yu, “We plan to leave that place and find another suitable spot to settle.”

Lang Yu looked at the stack of fishing nets in the hide bag. “Where to?”

“They say there’s no snowy season in the south. We’re planning to walk further, to a place without winter.”

His tribesmen had fallen ill because of the attack on the Wolf Tribe; whenever it got cold, their old wounds ached to the bone. This was their own doing; they couldn’t blame the Wolf Tribe. On the contrary, Green Moon was grateful to them. Without the Wolf Tribe, he wouldn’t have become the chief of the Green-eyed tribe, and he wouldn’t have realized that non-beastmen (sub-beastmen) weren't just meant to stay in the nest and raise pups—they could also support the tribe.

Lang Yu took the bag and opened it, looking at the fishing nets inside. They were new. The nets they had originally lent were old—after so much use, it was impossible for them to be returned as new.

Seeing him notice, Green Moon’s smile became a little proud, and a little embarrassed. “Do you mind… us learning how to weave fishing nets?”

Lang Yu looked at the reborn sub-beastman, his confidence striking. “If you can learn it, that’s your skill.”

Green Moon curled his lips. “Thank you.”

“Stay for a bowl of meat soup before you go?”

Green Moon stood up, looking at Lang Yu and the busy sub-beastmen nearby. “No, the tribe needs me. I have to get back.”

“If there’s a chance…” Green Moon smiled, quiet and firm, “we’ll meet again.”

They came in a rush, and they left in a rush.

Lang Yu chased after them for a few steps, standing at the edge of the road-building site, watching them fly away. The Green-eyed beastmen’s feathers were dazzling, scorching in the sunlight.

Lang Yu thought that while the male beastmen of their tribe might not be able to hold things up anymore, the many uninjured sub-beastmen and females, along with the pups slowly growing up, would rebuild the Green-eyed tribe.

Lang Yu was happy they had regained their spirit, but he felt a sense of loss. Tribal migration was the norm; he didn’t know if this "see you again" could ever be fulfilled. He really did admire his friend, Green Moon.

***

Half a month later.

The former tribe of the Rabbit beastmen—Green Lake.

Tu Ai stood by the lake, picking up a green feather. The wind blew, and the feather flew from his hand, landing on the water and drifting further and further away.

Lin Qiu watched and said, “The Green-eyed tribe was here.”

Along the way, Lin Qiu had been kept busy. Even if there was a bird in the woods, Lang Yan would stop and make him guess whether it was a large bird or a small one. After much practice, Lin Qiu slowly got used to mobilizing his senses to observe his surroundings.

Green Lake was aptly named. It was the downstream of a river, with flat terrain and grassy banks. Water gathered here to form a lake, clear and emerald-green under the sunlight. It was a vast lake.

The wolf beastmen arrived last night. After scouting the area, they found that many tribes had stopped here before, and one of them was the familiar Green-eyed tribe. Based on the traces, they had likely left just before the wolves arrived.

Under Tu Ai’s guidance, they had walked for over a month. Now that they were stopped, everyone was eager to rest. It was the second day, and many were still sprawled out, snoring like thunder.

The lakeshore was flat. The rabbit beastmen used to dig tunnels underground. There were caves nearby, but they weren’t by the lake, so they continued to set up shelters to sleep.

They had finished their rations on the road. Lin Qiu had also overslept, and now his stomach was grumbling, but he had to get up to find food. Tu Ai knew this area well and knew many edible plants grew by the lake.

Lin Qiu brought the awakened beastmen with him, a basket slung over his shoulder, to forage.

*Splash!*

Lang Yan cast a net nearby and slowly pulled it back. Lin Qiu, holding berries he’d picked, walked over and held one to Lang Yan’s mouth.

Lang Yan lowered his head and gently took it. At the same time, his arm tensed, he lifted the net, and the fish caught inside landed on the bank.

Lin Qiu crouched down, poked the fish, and sighed.

Lang Yan kicked a fish that was trying to jump back into the lake further away and asked Tu Ai, “What kind of prey can usually be caught around here?”

Tu Ai pointed to the lake. “Wide-mouthed beasts.”

“What do they look like?” Lin Qiu asked.

“As big as a horned beast, four hooves, wide mouth, flat tail. They like to eat water plants and can run in the woods. We used to rely on luck to catch small ones; the adults are in deep water.”

Listening to this, Lin Qiu felt they weren't animals he recognized.

Lin Qiu, Tu Ai, and the White Sparrows continued foraging. Once Lang Yan cast a few more nets, the other beastmen began to wake up. He had the wolf beastmen gut the fish and called for Que Erbai.

“Wolf King.” Que Erbai ran over. The White Sparrow beastmen were small; Que Erbai only reached Lang Yan’s shoulder. He had white hair, white eyebrows, and a slender frame, like a teenager, even though he was an adult. He kept a straight face, rarely smiling.

Lang Yan: “Go look over the water and see if there are any of the wide-mouthed beasts Tu Ai mentioned.”

“Okay.”

His hide dropped, and a plump white sparrow landed on the ground. He shook his wings, took off, and headed for the vast lake.

Tu Ai shouted, “Stay away from the lake surface! They’ll jump up…”

*Splash—!*

Lin Qiu was shocked, watching the wide-mouthed beast—as big as a water buffalo—burst up from the calm surface. The water exploded like fireworks. *So big!*

“King! Rope!”

The beastmen quickly threw a looped rope over.

Lang Yun shouted excitedly, “Little White Sparrow, lead it this way!”

Que Erbai kept his face stiff, turning his body to head for the shore.

Lang Huo brought over their bows and arrows. “Use these!”

*Swish, swish, swish—*

The lake churned violently for a moment, then went quiet. Lin Qiu watched as the beastmen threw the rope, pulled it taut, and dragged it to the bank.

With bows and arrows, it was like a cheat code. Before they even got close, the prey was taken down.

chapters.title: 第185章
chapters.translated_text:
Tu Ai was still a bit dazed.

They were also beastmen, and although they were herbivorous beastmen, this was a classification based on their ancestors' dietary choices.

They couldn't survive on grass alone; they needed to eat meat as well.

Think back to how they used to squat by the riverbank for two or three days—sometimes seven or eight—just for a single bite of meat, and only if they were lucky enough to encounter a wide-mouthed beast.

They couldn't handle the large ones; they couldn't kill them, and if they provoked one, they might end up losing their own lives, so they could only target the small ones.

But why was it that as soon as the wolf beastmen arrived, they encountered a wide-mouthed beast? And encountering it was one thing, but with just a few quick bangs, that massive beast was dragged onto the shore.

Tu Ai felt a bit trance-like.

He looked at the wild vegetables that barely covered the bottom of his rattan basket, and then at the wide-mouthed beast that was taller than him even while lying down.

Is this the strength of the wolf beastmen?

So, hunting is this easy for them!

"Eh? Are you stunned?" Lang Yun waved his hand in front of Tu Ai.

Tu Ai blinked, looking at the wide-mouthed beast with its neck bristling with arrowheads.

Even if the beast had thick skin, it couldn't withstand so many arrows from the beastmen.

Tu Ai said from the bottom of his heart, "Truly amazing."

Lang Yun curled his lips, smug, "Well, don't look at who caught it."

Lang Huo: "Lang Yun!"

"Yeah!"

"Bring a clay pot! The blood is about to drain out!"

"Coming, coming!"

It seems there will be no shortage of meat for the next few days.

"How about we set off for the Chishan Tribe as soon as we finish eating?" Lin Qiu asked Lang Yan, who was following him.

They were lucky this time to have encountered prey.

One could tell along the way that prey was truly scarce; they had only caught some two or three times. Now that they had such a large piece of prey, and if they caught a few more fish later, they at least wouldn't go hungry on the way to the Chishan Tribe.

Lang Yan considered it and agreed.

"Alright."

Lin Qiu pinched off some fresh wild vegetables and said to Que Ershi nearby: "Ershi, go tell Lang Huo and the others to hurry up and divide the prey, and catch some more fish. We'll continue our journey after lunch."

"Okay!" Que Ershi dropped his rattan basket and ran to find Lang Huo.

From afar, Lin Qiu heard a chorus of wails.

Lin Qiu took a handful of wild vegetables handed to him by Lang Yan, then hesitated and said, "Will it be too rushed?"

Lang Yan looked at Lu Ye, who was also gathering in the group.

They still had to go to the Baihe Tribe, and it had already been over a month since they left Langshan.

This exceeded their estimated time.

Lang Yan said, "Not rushed, it would be best to be even faster."

They didn't know if anything else would delay their journey later, so it was best to return to Langshan as soon as possible.

A fire was set up on the open ground by the lake, and the beastmen built a simple stove with stones.

Meat was boiling in the clay pot, seasoned only with salt and ginger slices; nothing else was added.

The wolf beastmen had been lacking fat and oil along the way, and today's prey was large enough for everyone to have a good meal of meat.

No need to settle for thin soup—just meat!

The meat of the wide-mouthed beast tasted different from any other meat Lin Qiu had eaten.

The texture was finer, oilier, and not stringy at all.

Moreover, the wide-mouthed beast had the most fat among the prey the beastmen had caught, and the oil jars that had been empty were now filled to the brim.

"This is delicious." The wolf beastmen gnawed on the bones without even lifting their heads, their teeth scraping against the bones, making a teeth-gritting sound.

The meat was solid, and the feeling of fullness was stronger than the meat soups they usually ate.

Lin Qiu's appetite had also increased; before, he could eat at most one rib, but now he could finish three and still have room for more.

The meat on the ribs wasn't trimmed at all; holding the bone, the meat on it felt heavy in his hand.

After eating, Lin Qiu burped, tilted his head, and leaned against Lang Yan, feeling lazy.

Lang Yan grabbed his hand, wiped it with a leaf, and then said, "Do you want to eat a little more?"

Lin Qiu: "I can't."

Lang Yan rubbed his chin against Lin Qiu's forehead, his eyes softening.

This trip hadn't been in vain; Qiu's body was much better than before, able to eat and sleep, and his muscles felt much firmer to the touch. His waist was still slender, but there were thin muscles on his abdomen, white and segmented—very beautiful.

The meat in the two pots was scraped clean by the thirty-plus beastmen.

Even the water used to boil the bones was drunk by the beastmen.

Everyone lay on the ground, bellies bulging, squinting their eyes and feeling dizzy, sighing, "This place isn't bad either."

"Then why did those Green-Eyed beastmen leave?"

Que Erbai scratched Lang Yun's hair, squatted down, and said, "There's a mound by the river."

The beastmen saw it while gathering; the mound wasn't high, and a stone was pressed on top of it.

This was a common burial method used after beastmen passed away.

Lang Yun turned over, plucked Que Erbai off his hair, placed him on his chest, and pressed his palm onto his head.

"Is the Green-Eyed patriarch gone?"

"Most likely," a companion nearby said. "When they left, the Green-Eyed patriarch looked sickly."

Que Erbai was pressed flat like a pancake.

He nudged his head against Lang Yun's palm, unable to squeeze out, so he tucked himself into the crook of his thumb, resting his chin on it.

"Then they probably won't come back."

"Probably not."

Most wolf beastmen didn't have deep feelings for the beastmen of the Green-Eyed Tribe; migration was a very normal thing for beastmen, and they were all just passing through.

After resting for a while, everyone packed up their things, taking the meat and the remaining wild vegetables with them.

The beastmen were ready to go, and one after another, they looked back at Lu Ye in the group.

The sub-beastman consciously covered his eyes.

They were already very far from Langshan, so there was no need to cover Lu Ye's eyes. But considering they were also going to a wolf tribe, it was better to keep them covered for the safety of their own kind.

Tu Ai had never been to the Chishan Tribe and didn't know the specific route.

According to Tu Kui's description, they needed to head west into the western mountain range.

A certain type of tree grew where the Chishan beastmen lived, and after the rainy season, the entire mountain would turn red because of these trees.

But it wasn't after the rainy season now, so the wolf beastmen couldn't rely on this feature to find them.

They could only take it one step at a time.

Tu Kui said it took several days to walk from Green Lake to the Chishan Tribe; the original Rabbit Tribe and the Chishan Tribe should have been neighbors.

Standing by Green Lake, the beastmen could vaguely see the vast mountain range to the west, mountains lush and winding. They weren't as precipitous as the mountains where the Black Feather beastmen lived, but they were more majestic and grand.

The Chishan Tribe should be in these mountains.

In three days, the wolf beastmen reached the foot of the mountains.

The mountains stood like a screen before them, and the beastmen could no longer see their full extent.

The beastmen stood at the foot of the mountain, heard Lang Yan say "rest," threw their things down, and lay down directly.

These mountains were layer upon layer, and the Chishan Tribe was inside.

"How long are we going to have to search?" Lang Yun said.

Lin Qiu also sat down to rest, kneading his legs: "We don't know each other, won't it be bad to just go in and look?"

Lang Yan held his legs and placed them on his own, his large hands kneading them.

Lin Qiu freed his hands, propped them behind him, felt the breeze on his face, and subconsciously caught the scent in the wind.

"They should know we're approaching these mountains."

"Then we wait for them to come?"

"Yes."

Lin Qiu sat up straight, propped himself on Lang Yan's arm, and tilted his head to look into his eyes.

"King, are you sure?"

Lang Yan looked at the face leaning in close and lowered his head to touch his nose against it.

"Sure."

Tu Kui said the Red Wolves chased prey all the way to the edge of their tribe, which meant this entire mountain range was where the Chishan Tribe beastmen were active.

If they had to find them themselves, they wouldn't know how long it would take to climb up and down the mountains.

Let's wait for one night; if they are sharp, they should know beastmen have arrived. If they don't know, we'll give a shout tomorrow, and they'll know.

Lin Qiu was stunned after hearing their King's plan.

Lang Yan kneaded his tight calf, "Does it hurt?"

Lin Qiu's smile bloomed, "So it's that simple."

"Then... what if they aren't friendly to us?"

"How could they..." Lang Yun heard Lin Qiu's words from afar, rolled over, scratched behind his ear with his hind paw, and said, "When we wolf beastmen look for mates, we often don't see eye-to-eye with the beastmen in our own tribe, so we like to go to the market to find them; we just like those from other wolf tribes."

Even if the market isn't open now, every tribe basically has wolves of every color. If you trace it back, you might even find your grandmother's sister or grandfather's brother.

Wolf beastmen are more united than other species, regardless of fur color, so the danger of facing a strange wolf tribe isn't that high.

Of course, this is an ideal situation; it doesn't exclude the possibility of ill-intentioned wolf tribes.

*

Chishan is the mountain range where Lang Yan and the others were.

The Chishan Tribe beastmen lived in the mountains year-round. Now that prey was scarce in the mountains, they would chase prey whenever they encountered it, and a few times they had even chased it down the mountain.

The mountains were continuous, lush with trees.

The Chishan Tribe beastmen were familiar with every mountain peak and every gully, running through them as if on flat ground.

The beastmen from Langshan didn't hide their tracks when they came; thirty-plus beastmen, catching fish, gathering, and building fires—the smoke rising made it hard not to notice.

In the middle of the mountain range, the mountain peak with the fewest trees.

The entire mountain was hollowed out, hiding a huge cave inside.

In this cave, the beastmen had dug winding passages and caves within caves.

A Red Wolf with fiery red fur was buried in digging a hole, the mud clawed out scattering everywhere, and the Red Wolf's fur was also covered in mud spots.

"Patriarch."

Bang! The Red Wolf paused.

The sub-beastman squatting outside the small cave entrance shrank his claws, his ears pressed against his forehead.

Lang Ying slowly backed out, his butt wiggling, moving half his body out of the small cave.

He shook the mud off his body, felt the pain on his forehead, and coldly glanced at the half-grown sub-beastman beside him.

"Lang Gu, what is it?"

Lang Gu was also a Red Wolf, his fur not as black-red as the patriarch Lang Ying's. His father and papa were both Red Wolves, so his fur color was brighter, but because of a lack of nutrition, it lacked luster.

"Patriarch, twenty-four wolf beastmen, one rabbit beastman, one deer beastman, and ten white sparrow beastmen have arrived at the foot of the mountain."

Lang Ying lowered his head and walked toward the passage.

The small cave he dug was inside the large cave, and the entrance to the small cave was narrow, only wide enough for one beastman to pass through.

He walked in front, and Lang Gu followed behind him.

"From one tribe?"

"It looks like it, but also not."

Lang Ying swept his tail, slapping it against the little wolf's forehead with a bang.

"What do you mean 'looks like it but also not'!"

Lang Gu drooped his tail, looking at their King with grievance.

"What are they here for?" Lang Ying crawled out of the passage, bent his legs forward, and stretched his body.

Lang Gu: "They brought a lot of things; I don't know if they're here to find us."

"What kind of wolves?"

"Black wolves, gray wolves, white wolves, and a red-black wolf."

A red-black wolf?

Then this wolf tribe must also have Red Wolves.

Lang Ying: "Go, call all the tribesmen back."

*

Night fell, Lin Qiu set up a shelter and nestled into Lang Yan's fur.

The light from the fire outside shone into the shelter, and Lin Qiu buried his face into Lang Yan's body.

"King, are we not arranging for beastmen to keep watch tonight?"

"Lang Huo and I will."

Lin Qiu felt at ease hearing that.

He saw that all the beastmen had gone to sleep and thought nothing had been arranged.

"Sleep." Lang Yan pressed his head against Lin Qiu's, circled him onto his belly, and covered Lin Qiu tightly with his deep, long wolf fur.

Lin Qiu closed his eyes and fell asleep shortly after.

In the middle of the night, the fire went out.

Light footsteps came from outside the shelter; Lang Yan opened his eyes and exchanged a look with Lang Huo.

"Chishan Tribe?"

Lang Yan looked at the feet of the beastmen outside and said in a low voice.

The footsteps paused, and the wolf beastmen climbed up vigilantly, muscles tensed, facing the surroundings of the shelter.

Instantly, a cloud of smoke poured into the shelter.

The visitors were not friendly!

The wolf beastmen held their breath and rushed out of the shelter, immediately colliding with the Chishan Tribe beastmen waiting outside. They opened their mouths to bite, and the Chishan Tribe beastmen collided with them in return.

Lang Huo was the squad leader; he found the Chishan Tribe's wolf king and rushed in front of him.

Lang Ying turned his head, dodging his pounce and bite.

Lang Huo turned over and slammed into him; Lang Ying was slightly annoyed and bit his ear. Seeing his neck exposed, Lang Huo opened his mouth to bite.

But his ear was gently nibbled.

It wasn't a fatal bite, but an extremely light one, like flirting.

Instantly, Lang Huo's entire back went numb, his tail stiffened, and his whole body lost control, pressing down on the sub-beastman.

Like a frozen fish, stiff as a board.

Lang Ying lowered his head, face-to-face with Lang Huo.

The black-red wolf was sturdy; one look and you could tell he was a good hunter.

The Red Wolf was beautiful, though a bit thin. But his body was long and well-proportioned, and he smelled very good.

Lang Huo didn't know why, but being watched by him, his eyes slowly drifted, and his head turned away.

Lang Ying brought his nose close.

Lang Huo's ears twitched; he looked at him, then dodged.

He looked again.

Lang Ying used his claws to hold his head straight.

Lang Huo couldn't help but look at him again, and finally, his eyes fixed; he lowered his head, and their noses touched.

Both beastmen shivered and simultaneously turned their heads away.

Why did the atmosphere suddenly become so sticky?

Lin Qiu was next to Lang Yan, not knowing what was going on.

Lang Ying glanced at Lang Yan, then saw Lin Qiu beside him, and clicked his tongue in regret.

He lifted his chin.

Lang Yan nodded.

Instantly, only wolf beastmen with mates, along with the White Sparrows, Tu Ai, and Lu Ye, remained at the shelter.

"King?" Lin Qiu scratched the giant black wolf lying in front of him.

Lang Yan: "It's fine, they must have encountered the same problem as us."

But judging by the situation just now, for some reason, there were more sub-beastmen and females in this tribe than male beastmen.

Dry cave.

Lang Huo was pushed by the red-haired beastman and fell onto the dry grass.

His Adam's apple rolled, and he looked up at the sub-beastman.

"Lang Huo," Lang Huo said proactively.

"Lang Ying." The sub-beastman lifted his long legs and sat on him, his long hair brushing against Lang Huo's nose, his fingers pinching his ears.

Lang Huo's face turned red; he didn't know where to put his hands.

"I am the patriarch of the Chishan Tribe, twenty-eight, no mate. Are you willing to have cubs with me?"

Lang Huo: "...How about we get to know each other a bit more?"

Lang Ying was slightly annoyed, glaring at the beastman.

He had already followed him into the cave, and he was still saying this.

He lowered his head and bit Lang Huo's lip, using some force; a tooth mark immediately appeared on Lang Huo's mouth.

Lang Huo's heart stirred, his hand resting on the sub-beastman's back, gently stroking it.

Lang Ying hummed softly, slightly less angry.

He said: "We know enough."

The beastmen of Langshan might not know, but the Chishan Tribe beastmen had been observing them for most of the day.

Wolf beastmen are more cautious than most when looking for mates, but once they see eye-to-eye... it's like thunder striking fire, vigorous and intense.

Lang Ying had already been irritable from digging the cave.

He had taken a liking to Lang Huo at first sight.

And Lang Huo... he gripped the waist of the sub-beastman sitting on his lap tightly; the deeper he dug, the more determined he became.

He kissed the sub-beastman's lips deeply, capturing the sweet scent, feeling that he liked him so much.

He had found him.

His mate.

*

In the shelter, Lin Qiu leaned against Lang Yan and fell asleep again.

However, he tossed and turned, unable to sleep well.

The White Sparrows were squatting to one side, Tu Ai was also rolling around, and finally, one by one, the beastmen sat up, looking at each other.

The fire had long gone out, and there was no light around.

Lin Qiu rubbed his face, still not understanding.

Is this a robbery?

The beastmen from the mountain ran down and snatched away the wolf beastmen of their tribe. And they only wanted beastmen, not wealth.

"Qiu, is it really okay?" Tu Ai asked in a low voice.

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan; the King was already asleep.

"It should be fine," he said, though he wasn't sure himself.

Tu Ai lay back down.

If Qiu said it was fine, it must be fine.

Lin Qiu also lay back down, carefully resting his head on Lang Yan's chest, frowning in thought.

The King said the Chishan Tribe encountered the same situation as them.

Was it a lack of food?

But they didn't take their food...

Could it be that the beastmen didn't have mates?

But that didn't make sense either; if they didn't have mates, why take their beastmen away?

Their group consisted entirely of male beastmen.

It was dark just now, and it was a sudden chaotic fight; Lin Qiu hadn't seen clearly whether those beastmen were sub-beastmen or male beastmen, only knowing that the one Lang Huo faced should be a sub-beastman.

It couldn't be that male beastmen and male beastmen...

Lin Qiu shook his head rapidly.

Lang Yan chuckled helplessly, his chest feeling itchy from Lin Qiu rubbing against it.

He pressed his mate's head down, his voice tinged with sleepiness, and said: "It's a good thing, don't overthink it."

"A good thing..." Lin Qiu repeated.

Since the King said so, he wouldn't worry.

"Sleep, you'll know tomorrow." Lang Yan pulled him into his arms, their foreheads touching, and fell back asleep.

*

The next day, at the first light of dawn.

Lin Qiu felt himself being poked, and then heard a crisp sound.

Lin Qiu remembered what happened last night, opened his eyes wide, and sat up, only to see Lang Huo holding his own hand, squatting at the shelter entrance with a slightly aggrieved look.

And their King was staring at Lang Huo with a dark face.

Lin Qiu propped himself up on Lang Yan's arm, yawned, leaned softly against his back, and looked at Lang Huo in confusion.

"You're back, nothing happened, right?"

Lang Huo couldn't help but curl his lips, but remembering the important matter, he quickly held it back and shook his head.

"Qiu, help me out."

Lang Yan's face grew even darker.

Lin Qiu reached out and covered his eyes.

"Tell me."

Lang Huo was a bit coy.

Lang Yan grabbed Lin Qiu's wrist to pull it down, and Lang Huo quickly said in one breath: "Qiu, please prepare more food; I'll bring my mate down to eat later. Is that okay?"

Lin Qiu was stunned.

Your what?

Wasn't he a bachelor last night?

"Can... can you?"

Lin Qiu understood.

He saw the bite marks on Lang Huo's neck and the scratch marks on his chest, and immediately knew what had happened last night.

A bit wild, huh...

"Don't worry, leave it to me." Lin Qiu patted his chest, suddenly energized.

His hand was taken down.

Lang Huo faced the wolf king's disdain and majesty, and zoomed into the mountain forest.

Not long after, quite a few wolves came down the mountain, and almost every one of them had the same request.

Lin Qiu didn't dare to delay, quickly directing the White Sparrows and Tu Ai to help, and even calling on the wolf beastmen who had mates and stayed in the shelter.

"Ai, take five White Sparrows and find some fresh wild vegetables."

"Ershi, take the remaining White Sparrows and help me fetch some water."

"King, cut the meat. Cut all the meat we have left!"

"Other beastmen, help me build a few more stoves."

Lang Yan didn't move.

Lin Qiu grabbed his hand, "Hurry, don't delay. Isn't this a happy occasion? We need to celebrate."

Lang Yan: "You haven't slept enough."

Lin Qiu laughed, his head bumping into Lang Yan's chest.

Seeing that the beastmen weren't paying attention, he stood on tiptoe and quickly bit Lang Yan's corner of the mouth.

Lightly, like a soothing gesture.

"You're the Wolf King, and I'm the Wolf King's mate. Shouldn't we help out when our own beastmen ask?"

Lang Yan slowly turned his face, looking at Lin Qiu.

The look was very obvious.

Lin Qiu hugged his neck and quickly bit his cheek.

Lang Yan's lips curled, and he slowly walked to the cutting board and began to cut the meat.

Fortunately, the wide-mouthed beast was big enough, and the beastmen had been frugal along the way, with plenty of salted meat left over.

Lin Qiu stood in front of their two clay pots.

He paused, looked back at Lang Yan, and said: "King, are two pots not enough?"

Lang Yan: "Add two more pots."

Lin Qiu watched the wolf beastmen build the stoves; his original intention was to have them build four more. Adding the original two, six would be plenty.

"Four pots? Is that enough? How many beastmen are in their tribe?"

Lang Yan's face turned cold again.

"Don't tell me you want to prepare food for their entire tribe?"

Lin Qiu quickly said: "Enough, enough, just four."

If he added any more, the King would be angry!

He knew Lang Yan wasn't stingy; he was just afraid he would be tired.

Lin Qiu thought about it, four pots were not bad; if other beastmen wanted to eat, they could borrow the clay pots.

By mid-morning, Lin Qiu and Tu Ai were squatting behind these four pots, watching the fire while looking up at the mountain.

The sunlight, like gold paper, fell into the lush green leaves, a bit dazzling.

Something moved in the forest, and Lin Qiu immediately turned his head to look.

A tall sub-beastman walked out calmly, his red hair tied high, his features bright and beautiful—a kind of scorching beauty.

He was wearing Lang Huo's clothes, long sleeves made of linen, light and simple, but on him, they looked like they were custom-made.

The sub-beastman descended to the foot of the mountain, covered his stomach with his hand, and pressed it gently.

He didn't come over but stood to the side to wait.

Lang Huo crawled out of the forest, took his hand proactively, and walked to the beastmen.

Lin Qiu stood up hurriedly, patting the dust off his body.

"Huo, introduce us."

"Lang Ying," the red-haired beastman said proactively.

He looked at Lin Qiu, then at the meat soup in the four pots, and suddenly lowered his head, touching his nose against Lin Qiu's.

Lin Qiu blinked.

"Hello."

Lang Ying curled his lips, "Hello to you too."

Lang Ying sat down and nodded to Lang Yan, "Long time no see."

Lang Yan: "Hmm."

Lin Qiu moved aside, and seeing Lang Huo still standing by the pot, he waved his hand: "It's ready to eat, get your own bowl and serve it."

"Yeah!" Lang Huo immediately went to get the clay bowl.

He was eager, looking very attentive.

Lin Qiu sat down beside Lang Yan, looking at this sub-beastman who was as bright as a red rose.

He was beautiful, flamboyant, and his red hair was extremely eye-catching.

Lin Qiu was very curious.

Lang Ying yawned lightly, resting his chin on his hand, looking lazy and satisfied. He looked at Lin Qiu and said slowly: "We met at the market when we were very young."

But at that time, neither knew which tribe the other was from; they only had a fleeting encounter.

Wolf beastmen identify beastmen by scent, which is sometimes more accurate than looking at faces.

Since both beastmen were outstanding among the wolf beastmen, it wasn't hard to remember a little something from their childhood.

Lin Qiu: "No wonder the King was so at ease."

Lang Ying's eyes curved.

"Our Chishan Tribe is different from your tribe; we have always had more sub-beastmen and female beastmen, and even the cubs born are like this."

Lin Qiu was surprised; that was strange.

This was the exact opposite of most tribes.

Lang Huo brought over a full bowl of meat soup, with more meat than soup.

The meat soup was still hot, so Lang Huo placed leaves on the ground and set the bowl on them. Then he sat down beside Lang Ying.

As soon as he sat down, Lin Qiu saw Lang Ying leaning lazily against him.

Lang Huo lowered his eyes to protect him, his arm blocking his lower back in a protective posture. His ears were very red, but he was very intimate with Lang Ying.

This was different from what he had imagined.

He looked at Lang Yan.

Lang Yan said in a low voice: "Once a wolf beastman determines the other is their mate, no matter how long they have been together, they will protect them with all their heart."

Once determined, it's truly set in stone; they don't think about separating, but treat the other with extreme caution and seriousness, maintaining them.

This is different from humans who need long-term interaction to confirm the other's character, Lin Qiu thought.

They are purer and simpler.
