The meat soup was ready, and the wolf beastman in charge of cooking shouted toward the window, causing beastmen to swarm in from all directions.

The scene was like chickens raised in the mountain forests of a farm; as soon as they heard it was feeding time, they scrambled down the mountain, afraid they would miss out on a bite if they were late.

It was lunchtime now.

Although the hunting and gathering team was away, there were still many beastmen left on Wolf Mountain. Each beastman got a bowl of meat soup, and in no time, the clay pot was empty.

It was raining today, but it was a light drizzle, and Lang Wan and Lang Xing were still leading the beastmen in building houses while wearing straw rain capes.

After taking a sip of the hot soup and feeling the chill in their bodies dissipate, the two older beastmen sighed with satisfaction.

The next moment, an even louder sigh of contentment came from nearby.

The two beastmen glanced over, then looked away.

This Black Feather beastman had run to the Wolf Tribe many times; they had been a bit wary at first, but now they didn't even feel anything.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan carried their bowls and sat down at Yu Lie's table.

The table was by the window, which was wide open.

The drizzle was misty, and the window frame acted like a picture frame, framing the withered yellow grass outside, the clear, deep river, and the colorful mountain forest in the distance.

Outside was the sound of fine rain, and inside was the slurping sound of beastmen drinking hot soup.

"Rest here for the night after you finish eating? It's still raining, so it's not easy to go back," Lin Qiu said casually.

Yu Lie finished a piece of lotus root in a few bites and said, "I have to go back; the tribe is busy too."

"Then will you let Yu Le come back before the Snow Season?"

"It depends on him."

The beastmen of the two tribes were already very familiar with each other, so there was no need for polite small talk, and the beastmen didn't really know how to make it anyway.

"I'll bring Yu Le's rations before the Snow Season."

"No need."

"Then I'll bring medicinal herbs."

"That works."

Yu Lie chuckled, took another big slurp of soup from his bowl, and after swallowing it, felt heat radiating through his whole body.

He set down his bowl, wiped his mouth, and asked, "Qiu, can the tail grass be harvested yet?"

Lin Qiu looked out the window, thought about the condition of his own tail grass, and said, "After this rain stops, we can start harvesting."

"Got it, I'll tell our tribe leader when I get back."

Last year, the Wolf Tribe gave the Black Feather Tribe some tail grass seeds.

This year, in order to grow the tail grass well, the Black Feather beastmen ran to Wolf Mountain frequently, and they had managed to grow it successfully.

This Snow Season might be the first one where the beastmen of the Black Feather Tribe could eat their fill.

After finishing his bowl of meat soup, Yu Lie washed his bowl, chatted with Lin Qiu and Lang Yan for a while, and then called his companions who had come with him to leave.

Before leaving, Yu Le went to see them off.

Yu Lie looked at the young beastman who had grown to his shoulder height, smiled, and ruffled Yu Le's hair with enough force that the young beastman leaned backward.

Yu Lie hurriedly steadied him.

Yu Le just smiled helplessly.

He looked at his uncle with clear eyes; the immaturity was gone from his face, and he had become steady and reserved.

Yu Lie paused, patted his shoulder, and sighed, "You've grown up."

Yu Le: "Uncle, hurry up and go, otherwise it will be dark by the time you get back."

Yu Lie: "I know, I'm leaving now."

The black-gray feathered beastmen flapped their wings and flew off, disappearing into the horizon in an instant.

Yu Le withdrew his gaze, returned to the cafeteria, took Lang Xue's hand—who had just finished his meat soup—and the two, one big and one small, went into the large cave.

Lang Bing was not there; he had taken the young beastman gathering team out to collect medicinal herbs.

The only ones left to learn about medicinal herbs were Yu Le and Lang Xue.

The two little ones were very self-motivated and would take the initiative to study without anyone urging them. They were so diligent that they actually needed someone to persuade them not to study too hard.

After lunch, the beastmen washed the pots and bowls, and those who wanted to nap took a nap.

When they woke up, the rain had gotten heavier.

Now the work outside couldn't continue. Lang Wan, Lang Xing, and the other beastmen of the construction team dispersed; those interested in ironware headed to Lang Qi's cave, and the sub-beastmen who wanted to look after the cubs went into the large cave to stay with them.

The beastmen gathered in groups of two or three, and with the rare free time, they had endless things to talk about.

By evening, the hunting and gathering teams returned.

The rain had let up, so the beastmen got up to go outside and move around.

The cubs excitedly ran out and darted among the hunting team's beastmen. Because they were short, they treated the tall adult beastmen like pillars, circling around them.

Lang Yun was exhausted and was about to take a detour when he suddenly smelled a scent drifting from the cubs.

He grabbed Lang Hua on a whim.

The cub looked at him blankly.

Lang Yun pinched the cub's cheeks with his fingers, making them puff out.

He frowned and leaned down to sniff.

The cub leaned back as hard as he could, raised his little hand, and slapped Lang Yun on the face with a "pop."

Lang Yun winced in pain, loosened his grip on the little cub, and asked, "What did you eat at noon?"

"Meat soup."

"That's not right."

The cub's eyes rolled, and he stared at him with a grin.

"What was it?"

"I won't tell you!" Lang Hua ducked under his arm, and as Lang Yun lost his grip, the cub ran away quickly.

Lang Yun saw Lang He staring at him with a strange expression.

He grabbed his partner's hand and marched aggressively toward the cafeteria, shouting as he walked: "Qiu! What delicious food did you give the little cubs?!"

The cubs whose companion had just been held hostage swarmed over, using their heads as weapons to ram into him.

Lang He stepped aside, looked at Lang Hua, who was quietly directing the cub team, raised an eyebrow, and stood by with a smile.

They were all cubs who wouldn't let themselves be taken advantage of; that was good.

"Qiu! The cubs are ramming me!"

When Lang Yun returned, the tribe became lively. He was as loud as dozens of beastmen, and his voice carried all the way outside Wolf Mountain.

Lin Qiu heard the complaint but didn't leave the cafeteria.

He was busy.

"Qiu! The hunting team brought back a large curved-horn beast and two sharp-horn beasts." Lang Shuang went out to check and came back to ask Lin Qiu, "Which one should we kill?"

"Why so many today?"

"They said Ying put in the effort."

Lin Qiu curled his lips, a flash of appreciation in his eyes.

As expected of the Wolf King.

"Kill the curved-horn beast, let the beastmen eat more meat."

"Alright."

Lang Yu went out to pass the word, and Lang Shi took the beastmen to slaughter the prey.

The evening meal hadn't been prepared yet, as they were waiting for the meat to be brought back.

Lin Qiu made the cubs' food first.

Several bleating beasts in the tribe were still nursing their young, so Lin Qiu had Lang Rong help him milk a bucket of milk.

The bleating beast's milk was plentiful but had a slightly fishy taste.

Since he couldn't make steamed eggs in the evening, he used the milk to make some milk cakes for the cubs. They were currently steaming in the iron pot, smelling fragrant and milky.

Lang Yun, who had been shouting, followed the scent inside. When he heard it was the cubs' food, he stopped howling and just followed behind Lin Qiu.

Even Lang He couldn't bear to watch and walked out, covering his eyes.

Lang Yun had truly lost all shame for the sake of a bite to eat.

Lin Qiu stopped helplessly and said, "I'm making something else for the adult beastmen."

"Can't I taste what's in the pot?"

As soon as Lang Yun finished speaking, Lin Qiu looked at the heads popping up behind the stove and said firmly: "There are so many adult beastmen; if everyone tastes a little, will the cubs eat air?"

"Just me, I'll be quiet. And add Lang He."

Lin Qiu met the gaze of the sub-beastmen behind the stove.

Lang Yu smiled slightly.

Lin Qiu: "No."

Behind the stove, the sub-beastmen retracted their heads.

Lang Yun: "Hmph!"

"Hmphing won't help."

Lang Yun followed Lin Qiu for a while, and seeing that the cubs had also come in, he simply sat down in the pile of cubs and continued to probe what they had eaten at noon.

Lang Sheng tucked his little hands in and looked at this uncle who was even more childish than them, saying nothing.

Lang Yuan tugged on his sleeve and said softly, "Lang Sheng, let's tell him."

Lang Sheng turned his head and looked at Lang Hua.

They hadn't told him because they were standing up for Ah Hua.

Lang Hua turned his head away, chin held high, silent.

Lang Yun leaned his whole body down, resting his big head on the cubs' small shoulders; he was heavy, making the cubs' shoulders slump.

He even nudged and rubbed against them, acting more like a cub than the cubs themselves.

Lang Hua was pushed around by his rubbing, and finally, out of impatience, he let out an "Aiya," pushed Lang Yun's shoulder with his little hand, shifted his bottom back, and with a head full of messy hair, said, "I'll tell you!"

"What did you eat?"

"Eggs!"

"Do you think I haven't eaten eggs?"

"It wasn't a round boiled egg, it was opening the eggshell, then stir, stir, stir..."

"Then pour in water."

"Then stir, stir, stir."

"Put it in the pot to boil."

"And there was meat too."

Lang Yun thought carefully about what the cub said, then lay down on the ground, spreading his arms and legs, "I'm so pitiful, I was hungry at noon and didn't eat anything."

"There will be food in a while."

"In a while it'll be stewed soup again, the cubs have special delicious food, but the big beastmen don't..." Lang Yun said, sneaking a glance at Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu saw Lang Yan coming over and signaled for him to look at Lang Yun.

"Noisy." Lang Yan frowned.

"The King is also biased..."

A vein throbbed on Lang Yan's temple.

"If you don't want to eat, get out."

Lang Yun climbed up nimbly, looked at the cubs, sighed deeply, and left, dejected.

The cubs watched blankly, then scrambled up and rushed to Lang Yan.

Lang Yan ruffled the cubs' hair, "Stay a bit further away from here."

"King, Uncle Lang Yun..."

"He's faking it."

"But... he's so pitiful..."

Lin Qiu laughed when he heard this and said, "Then what should we do?"

"Qiuqiu..." The cub leaned his small body over, grabbing his pants.

Lin Qiu hurriedly grabbed his waistband and looked at Lang Yan helplessly.

Lang Yan shooed the cubs away to his side.

When several pairs of little hands grabbed his pants again, Lang Yan looked calm. Lin Qiu knew at a glance that he had gained experience from being grabbed by the cubs.

He must have tightened his belt secretly.

Lang Yan: "There are many adult beastmen; we have to wait for the curved-horn beast to be slaughtered before we can make them delicious food. It's not safe here, go play on the side."

When the cubs heard this, they weren't worried anymore.

They rushed out, eager to tell Lang Yun this good news.

That way, Uncle Lang Yun wouldn't cry anymore.

*

Lin Qiu's gaze swept over the other two empty iron pots, and he made up his mind to clean the pots tonight.

He tapped his fingers on the empty iron pot and looked at Lang Yan.

Lang Yan nodded.

The meat wasn't ready yet, so Lin Qiu went to check the wild vegetables the gathering team brought back today.

Two or three dozen rattan baskets of various sizes were placed in the square, and the wild vegetables, dampened by the rain, were still fresh.

At this time of year, there were fewer vegetable leaves.

The beastmen had gone to the east and brought back a lot of wild chives and wild onions. Lin Qiu saw the chive flowers mixed in and said, "You can collect more of these next time."

Lang Qing followed him and asked, "Can the flowers be eaten?"

"They can be made into a sauce, it's excellent for dipping meat."

"Good."

Lang Qing planned to collect a few baskets tomorrow.

The wild vegetables were mixed, and as long as they were edible, the beastmen collected them.

Some vegetable leaves had thorns on the back, but since the beastmen collected the tender leaves, the thorns were soft and not too prickly.

There were too many vegetables to eat, so half of them had to be dried and stored.

Lin Qiu looked again; he found several baskets of slightly older chives, and there were many root vegetables as well.

Most had a lot of fiber and contained plenty of starch, which was filling, but they didn't taste good.

Lin Qiu's hands passed over those tough roots, looking specifically for the ones that tasted good.

Finally, five baskets of wild vegetables were pulled out, and the sub-beastmen went to the river to wash them clean before bringing them back to the cafeteria.

"Qiu, don't you want the purple flower roots?"

The purple flower roots were the ones with the most fiber; chewing them was like chewing on wood.

This plant bloomed in clusters of purple flowers, the flowers were the size of beans, the leaves were slender, but the roots were very fat.

The beastmen didn't have much food before, and in the late Snow Season, they relied on chewing these roots to survive.

The purple flower roots got sweeter the more you chewed them, and eating a lot of them made your stomach feel full.

Lin Qiu: "Hard to chew."

"Then we won't collect them anymore?"

"Collect them." Lin Qiu thought of another use for these purple flower roots.

Making starch.

Lang Qing didn't ask why they should collect them if they were hard to chew, and said, "Do you want a lot or a little?"

If they wanted a lot, they would collect more. If they wanted a little, they would spend their energy collecting other plants, trying to bring back as many other delicious wild vegetables as possible.

"I'll try to see if I can make starch out of these first; if I can, we'll collect more."

Lang Qing heard it was another thing he didn't know about, but anything Qiu made was definitely good, so they should collect more.

"Qiu! The meat is ready!" Lang Shuang shouted to Lin Qiu from the cafeteria window.

Lin Qiu waved his hand, "Coming."

The freshly slaughtered meat was still steaming, and next to a pile of fatty and lean meat was a basin of curved-horn beast blood.

Lin Qiu took a look and signaled to the sub-beastmen waiting for his instructions: "Uncles, take five clay pots, add water, and bring it to a boil."

"Then I'll cut the meat," Lang Shuang said.

Lin Qiu pointed to the fatty and lean meat and said, "Cut it into chunks, half a finger wide."

"Got it."

The stove became busy, and the hunting and gathering team washed their claws and slowly entered the cafeteria.

The light beside Lin Qiu dimmed, and seeing Lang Ying leaning against the windowsill with his arms crossed, he momentarily thought he saw Lang Huo.

Both of them liked to lean around in this position.

"Tired?"

Lang Ying's gaze fell on the increasingly sticky minced meat in Lin Qiu's hands and said, "Hungry."

"Wait a little longer. Go sit on the side and rest, eat some fruit."

One-third of what the gathering team brought back were fruits, red, yellow, green, and black—all sorts of colors. They were washed and placed on the table, ready to be eaten.

"Want to eat meat," Lang Ying said slowly.

Next to him, Lang Shuang heard this and started cutting the meat even faster.

The knives used in the cafeteria now were all iron knives that Lin Qiu had brought back from the Chishan Tribe; the blades were thin and extremely sharp.

If you weren't careful and cut your hand, you would bleed.

In these past few days, not one of the beastmen in charge of cooking hadn't been injured.

Fortunately, they adapted quickly; they could use heavy stone knives, so a thin iron knife was nothing.

Lin Qiu finished chopping the meat and signaled for the sub-beastmen to light the fire on the iron pot side as well.

"Qiu, the meat is cut."

"What about the wild vegetables?"

"Here!" The guard team beastmen carried the vegetable baskets in.

Lin Qiu: "Shuang, cut the chives into sections."

"Do you need our help?" The other sub-beastmen uncles were afraid they wouldn't be able to keep up, so they stopped weaving and came over.

The manpower was suddenly sufficient.

Lin Qiu immediately assigned tasks: some to chop vegetable leaves, some to cut herbs, and some to tend the fire.

As soon as the iron pot was hot, Lin Qiu put oil in it.

In a moment, the white, greasy fat melted, emitting wisps of smoke.

Large chunks of meat were poured in, stir-fried until golden brown on all sides, and then various herbs were added.

"Qiu! The water in the clay pots is boiled."

"Good."

Lin Qiu poured the water from the clay pots into the iron pot.

Immediately, bubbles began to bubble up in the pot.

One clay pot of water wasn't enough, so Lin Qiu poured in two and a half pots.

He covered it with a lid and simmered it over high heat.

"Qiu, the water here is ready too."

"Coming."

The empty clay pot continued to be heated, and Lin Qiu put oil in it, added herbs, and stir-fried them. He stir-fried until the herb scent came out, then added the water from the clay pot.

Gurgle, gurgle—

There was no need to wait; the water boiled.

"Uncle Shuang! Come over and put the blood curd into the pot. Cut it into pieces, like I did just now, and put it into three pots."

Lang Shuang immediately took over Lin Qiu's work.

"What about that pile of minced meat?" Lang Ying asked.

"It's for the cubs."

"I want to eat it."

"I can't make much in a short time, how about I make it for you tomorrow morning?"

Lang Ying lazily raised his eyelids.

"Hmm."

A large iron pot full of braised pork, three pots of chive and blood curd soup, two clay pots of stir-fried wild vegetables, and the cubs' wild vegetable meatball soup and milk cakes—all done!

"Dinner is served!"

It was already dark, and a few candles were lit in the cafeteria, making it bright enough for the beastmen to see the food in their bowls clearly.

The fatty and lean meat was bright red and glistening with oil.

"Why is it this color?" The beastmen poked it with their chopsticks, their throats bobbing; they really wanted to eat it, but were afraid to.

Lin Qiu: "I added a coloring plant, it's edible."

It wasn't that they hadn't made braised pork before, but never this red. Everyone was so tempted by the fragrance that they drooled as soon as they opened their mouths; they couldn't hold back anymore and buried their heads to take a big bite.

With one bite, the meat softened and melted away.

The taste of meat filled their tongues, not fatty or greasy, and their stomachs clamored for more.

The solid meat made the beastmen so happy their toes curled, and after a sip of the flavorful chive and blood curd soup, it was refreshing!

The stir-fried wild vegetables were also delicious, with just a hint of bitterness. But mixed with the pork cracklings, there was no unpleasant grassy taste left, only crispness and freshness.

"Delicious!"

In the heat of the meal, a beastman asked: "Qiu! Is there any tail grass seed rice?"

"No."

Lin Qiu also felt it was a pity; there was no rice.

"When can we harvest the tail grass?"

"When the rain stops."

"Harvest! After we harvest, I want to eat tail grass rice! And this meat too!"

Lin Qiu thought of that taste, pursed his lips, and nodded.

"Okay."

He wanted to eat it too.

The firelight flickered, and the cubs sat in the corner, quietly eating their own food.

Each of them only got two pieces of milk cake, and the rest were for the very small cubs. The milk cake was sweet, and when you bit into it, it felt like eating ice, but it was even better than ice.

The cubs originally wanted to save it, but the uncles nearby were eyeing them covetously.

After finishing the milk cake in a few bites, they looked at the wild vegetable meatball soup in their bowls, and the cubs' eyes curved with joy.

With a poke of the chopsticks, the round meatballs were picked up.

They brought them to their mouths, took a big bite—the meatballs were bouncy, the wild vegetables were refreshing, and the cubs could eat ten in one go.

The uncles wouldn't give them any more than that.

Lin Qiu saw the cubs finish what was in their bowls, hiccup, and still look at him expectantly.

Lin Qiu was thinking there should be a little bit left in the pot.

Lang Yan, who was sitting next to him, reached out and touched the cubs' stomachs.

They were bulging high; they couldn't eat anymore.

"If you eat any more, you'll get indigestion. Do you want to go find the priest to drink herbal soup?"

The cubs shrank back, immediately shaking their heads, not daring to ask for more.

After dinner, the beastmen held their stomachs and hiccuped, their faces flushed, looking tipsy as if they had eaten some rare delicacies.

Everyone went to the stream to wash their bowls, and when they saw Lin Qiu, they surrounded him to ask about tomorrow's food.

Hearing that they would have meatball soup tomorrow morning, they were happy again.

"Since Qiu came back, life has more to look forward to." The beastmen beamed, and their hands scrubbing the clay bowls were even more energetic, the bottoms of the bowls squeaking.

A companion nearby said: "I heard the cubs even had minced meat steamed eggs today, and that milk cake, I want to eat that too."

The beastman spoke loudly, and Lin Qiu sighed, bumping his head against Lang Yan's shoulder.

"Why are your beastmen so gluttonous?"

"Don't spoil them."

"There aren't enough ingredients, it's hard to spoil them even if I wanted to."

The beastmen seemed to be washing the bowls seriously, but they were actually listening with their ears pricked. When they heard Lin Qiu couldn't make it, they rubbed their bulging stomachs and smacked their lips, which were still drooling.

Sigh—

It wasn't that they were gluttonous, their own mouths just wanted to try it.

It seemed they wouldn't be able to eat it for a short time.

The hunting and gathering team's beastmen were already very tired, so after cleaning up, they went back to their straw nests to sleep.

The cubs were herded into the cave by Lang An, along with the other eight cubs, and they shared a nest to sleep together.

The number of beastmen moving outside gradually decreased.

Lin Qiu didn't rush to leave and continued to sit in the cafeteria with Lang Yan.

More houses had been built, but sleeping space was still limited. At night, some beastmen would bring straw mats to the cafeteria and lay down animal skins to sleep.

The sub-beastmen weren't in a hurry to sleep either; they wove fishing nets while discussing cleaning the down feathers exchanged from the brown bear beastmen tomorrow.

Lin Qiu saw they were still full of energy and glanced at Lang Yan.

What should he do?

He was still waiting to open the pot.

Lang Yan stood up directly, walked to the stove, took out both pots, stacked them together, and carried them out.

The sub-beastmen moved aside and continued talking.

Lin Qiu: That's it?

Lin Qiu hurriedly followed, watching Lang Yan place the iron pot in the square, then stand straight, waiting for him to come over.

Lin Qiu: "Are we opening the pot now?"

"Wait a little longer."

Lang Yan washed his hands and pulled Lin Qiu up the mountain first.

After a while, the sub-beastmen blew out the candles and lay down. Lang Shuang turned over and suddenly said: "Eh? Did the King move the pots out just now?"

"Did he move them?"

"I didn't notice."

"I didn't see it either."

"Sleep, sleep, we have to get up early tomorrow to make meatball soup for the beastmen."

The lights in the cafeteria and the cave went out for a while, and on the mountain, Lin Qiu pushed open the door of the small cave.

"Hurry, hurry."

He was sleepy and wanted to finish his work quickly so he could go to sleep.

Lang Yan followed behind him, not understanding why his partner had to be so secretive just to open a pot. However, he respected his partner's ideas, and if there was something to do, he would just do it with him.

The rain had stopped now.

The path down the mountain was slippery, and the two beastmen walked cautiously.

The beastmen were all asleep, and Wolf Mountain was silent.

It was pitch black all around, and Lin Qiu slipped, nearly rolling down the mountain.

Lang Yan was quick-witted, pulled him back, and directly picked him up to sit on his arm.

Lin Qiu hugged his neck, burying his head tightly against him, his heart still beating rapidly.

He was scared to death!

Lang Yan had a cold face, also feeling lingering fear.

"We should lay some charcoal ash on the road."

"Hmm."

After getting down the mountain, the two beastmen secretly moved the iron pot to the west side, although Lang Yan didn't think it was secretive.

They stopped only when they were out of sight of the Wolf Mountain side.

The wolf beastman in charge of the night patrol stood on Wolf Mountain, looking at this scene, and scratched his head in confusion.

"The King and Qiu... what are they doing?"

"They have the pots, could it be they're eating alone?"

Lang Mu slapped his companion on the forehead, "Are the King and Qiu that kind of beastmen?"

As he spoke, he turned his feet and followed them toward the west.

The beastman who was hit rolled his eyes.

If you don't believe it, why are you running over there?

"King..." Lang Mu said secretly.

Lin Qiu paused and looked at the guard team that had followed.

"You... aren't you going to patrol?"

"You... what are you doing?"

Lin Qiu sighed, "Opening the pot."

If it weren't for the uncles feeling bad about that bit of meat, they wouldn't have to act like thieves...

Lang Yan quietly watched this group of people who were here to join in the fun.

Lang Mu jumped, touched his nose, and ran away with a stiff smile on his face.

"Hey!"

"Hey!"

On the patrol route, the beastmen all felt regretful.

They also wanted to have a private meal like the cubs.

肉汤好了，负责做饭的狼兽人对着窗外吆喝一嗓子，接着，兽人从四面八方涌过来。
那架势像养殖场里放养在山林里的鸡，一听到放粮，争先恐后往山下飞蹿，生怕晚了少吃上一口。
这会儿吃的是午饭。
虽说狩猎采集队不在，但留在狼山的兽人也不少，一个兽人一碗肉汤，没一会儿，一个陶锅就空了。
今天下雨，但雨小，狼晚和狼星带着兽人穿着蓑衣都还在建房子。
等喝上一口热汤，身上冷意被驱散，两个也算上了年纪的兽人喟叹一声。
下一瞬，旁边传出更大的含着满足的叹气声。
两个兽人一瞧，又收回视线。
这黑羽兽人往狼部落跑了许多次了，他们开始还有点防备，现在看着都没感觉了。
林楸和狼岩端着碗，在羽猎那一桌坐下。
桌子靠窗，窗户大开。
细雨蒙蒙，窗框像一幅画框，把外面枯黄的青草、碧透的长河以及更远处的五彩山林框在一处。
外面是细密的雨声，屋里是兽人们喝着热汤的呼噜声。
“吃完在这边休息一晚？还在下雨，不好回去。”林楸随口道。
羽猎三两口吃完一块莲藕，道：“要回去，部落也忙。”
“那雪季之前让羽乐回吗？”
“看他自己吧。”
两个部落的兽人已经很熟了，不用说什么场面话，兽人也不怎么会说。
“羽乐的口粮，我雪季前给送来。”
“用不着。”
“那就送草药。”
“也行。”
羽猎嘿嘿笑了声，又端起碗吸溜一大口汤，咽下去后，感觉浑身都在冒热气儿。
他搁下碗，一抹嘴，道：“楸，尾巴草能收了吗？”
林楸看了眼窗外，想着自家尾巴草的情况，道：“这场雨下完就可以赶着收了。”
“成，我回去就跟我们族长说。”
去年狼部落给了黑羽部落一些尾巴草的种子。
今年为了种好这尾巴草，黑羽兽人频繁往狼山跑，也算把尾巴草种出来了。
今年雪季，或许是黑羽部落的兽人们第一次能吃饱的雪季。
一碗肉汤吃完，羽猎把碗洗了，又跟林楸和狼岩说了会儿话，就招呼跟来的同伴一起离开了。
走之前，羽乐去送。
羽猎看着已经长到自己肩膀高的小兽人，笑着揉了一把羽乐的脑袋，力道不轻，小兽人被他带得后仰。
羽猎赶忙拉住他。
羽乐却是无奈地笑。
他清澈的眼睛望着自家阿叔，脸上不见青涩，稳重了，也内敛了。
羽猎一顿，拍了拍他肩膀，感慨：“长大了。”
羽乐：“阿叔，快走吧，不然回去都天黑了。”
羽猎：“知道了，这就走。”
黑灰色的羽族兽人振翅一飞，顷刻消失在天边。
羽乐收回目光，回食堂，牵起刚刚吃完肉汤的狼雪，一大一小又进了大山洞中。
狼冰不在，他带着小兽人采集队出去采集草药了。
学习草药的兽人就剩羽乐和狼雪。
两个小家伙自觉得很，不用任何兽人催促就主动去学，太刻苦了，反倒需要兽人劝一劝，叫他们不要学得太狠了。
吃完午饭，兽人们刷锅洗碗，该睡午觉的睡午觉。
睡醒起来，雨势又大了。
这下外面的活儿都不好继续再做了，狼晚、狼星还有建筑队其他兽人分散开来，对铁器感兴趣的就往狼起的山洞里钻，想带幼崽的亚兽人们就进大山洞守着自己幼崽。
兽人们三三两两聚集在一起，难得空闲，一时间也是说不完的话。
躺到傍晚，狩猎队和采集队回来。
雨势也小了，兽人们才起身出去活动活动。
幼崽兴奋地跟着跑出去，在狩猎队的兽人们中乱窜。他们个子矮，把长条的成年兽人当柱子一样绕来绕去。
狼云累得不行，正想绕远一些，忽然闻到一股从幼崽身上飘上来的味儿。
他随手一逮，拎着狼花。
幼崽懵懵地看着他。
狼云手指捏着幼崽的脸一掐，掐得腮帮子鼓起。
他皱眉，低头嗅了嗅。
幼崽极力往后仰，小手抬起，啪的一声打在狼云脸上。
狼云疼得龇牙，松了松小崽子，问：“你们中午吃了什么？”
“肉汤。”
“不对。”
幼崽眼珠一转，盯着他嘿嘿一笑。
“什么？”
“就不告诉你！”狼花脑袋往他手臂下一绕，狼云脱手，幼崽飞快跑开。
狼云看狼禾一脸奇怪地盯着他。
他抓上自己伴侣的手，气势汹汹往食堂里走，边走边喊：“楸！你给小崽子们吃什么好吃的了？！”
刚刚被挟持了同伴的幼崽蜂拥而来，拿脑袋当武器，直接往他身上撞。
狼禾让开一步，看着幼崽队伍里悄悄指挥的狼花，一挑眉，笑眯眯地站在一旁。
都是不吃亏的崽崽，这样挺好。
“楸！幼崽撞我！”
狼云回来，部落就热闹了。他一个顶部落几十个兽人，叽里呱啦的，声音都传到狼山外去了。
林楸听到告状的声音，也不出食堂。
他正忙着呢。
“楸！狩猎队带回来一头大弯角兽，两头尖角兽。”狼霜出去看了看，又回来问林楸，“杀哪头？”
“今天怎么这么多？”
“说是影出了力。”
林楸翘起嘴角，眼里闪过欣赏。
不愧是狼王。
“杀弯角兽吧，让兽人们多吃点肉。”
“行。”
狼雨出去一趟，说了一声，狼石就带着兽人宰杀猎物去了。
晚上的食物还没做，就等兽人们带肉回来。
林楸先把幼崽的食物做了。
部落里好几头咩咩兽还在哺育幼崽，林楸直接让狼溶帮忙挤了一桶奶回来。
咩咩兽的奶水多，味道有点腥。
晚上做不成蒸蛋，便用这点咩咩兽奶给幼崽们做了点奶糕出来。这会儿还在铁锅上蒸，味道香甜，奶味十足。
狼云嚷嚷着，闻着味儿进来，一听是幼崽的食物，也不嚎了，就跟在林楸后面走。
连狼禾都看不过眼，捂着眼睛出去了。
为了一口吃的，狼云也是不要脸了。
林楸无奈停下，道：“我给成年兽人做其他的。”
“锅里的我不能尝吗？”
狼云一说完，林楸看着灶台后一下竖起的脑袋，态度坚定：“成年兽人这么多，一个尝一点，幼崽吃空气吗？”
“就我尝，悄悄的。再加一个狼禾。”
林楸对上灶台后亚兽人们的视线。
狼雨微微一笑。
林楸：“不行。”
灶台后，亚兽人们脑袋缩了回去。
狼云：“哼！”
“哼也没用。”
狼云跟了林楸一会儿，看幼崽也进来了，干脆往幼崽堆里一坐，继续打探他们中午吃了什么。
狼生小手一揣，看着面前这个比他们还幼稚的阿叔，不说话。
狼圆扯了扯他的衣袖，软软糯糯道：“阿生，我们告诉他吧。”
狼生脑袋一转，看向狼花。
他们可是给阿花出气才不说的。
狼花脑袋一偏，抬着下巴不语。
狼云整个身体压下来，大脑袋靠在幼崽小肩膀上，沉沉的，压得幼崽肩膀一塌。
他偏还一拱一蹭的，比幼崽都还会哼唧。
狼花被他蹭得东倒西歪，最后不耐烦，“哎呀”一声，小手推着狼云肩膀，屁股往后挪了挪，顶着一头乱糟糟的头发才道：“告诉你！”
“吃的什么？”
“蛋！”
“你当我没吃过蛋？”
“不是圆滚滚的煮蛋，是蛋壳打开，然后搅搅搅……”
“然后倒水。”
“再搅搅搅。”
“放锅里煮。”
“还有肉喔。”
狼云顺着幼崽的话仔细想了想，往地上一躺，双手双脚摊开，“我好可怜啊，我中午饿着肚子，什么都没吃。”
“等会就有吃的了。”
“等会儿又吃炖汤，幼崽都有专门做的好吃的，大兽人都没有……”狼云说一句，悄悄瞥一眼林楸。
林楸看着狼岩过来，示意他看看狼云。
“吵。”狼岩皱眉。
“王也偏心……”
狼岩额角青筋跳了跳。
“不想吃就滚。”
狼云利落地爬起来，看看幼崽，长叹一声，垂头丧气地离开。
幼崽们呆呆看着，然后一下爬起来，冲到狼岩面前。
狼岩揉了把幼崽脑袋，“离这边远一点。”
“王，阿云叔……”
“装的。”
“可是……好可怜……”
林楸听着笑了声，道：“那要怎么办？”
“楸楸……”幼崽小身子靠过来，手拽着他裤子。
林楸忙拎着裤腰，无奈看向狼岩。
狼岩把幼崽一拨，赶到自己身边。
几双小手再抓上他的裤子，狼岩一脸镇定。林楸一看就知道，他被幼崽抓出经验了。
肯定悄悄紧了裤腰带。
狼岩：“成年兽人多，要等弯角兽杀好才能给他们做好吃的。这边不安全，边上玩儿去。”
幼崽一听，不担心了。
他们着急跑出去，要把这个好消息告诉狼云。
这样阿云叔就不会哭鼻子了。
*
林楸目光扫过那另外两口空着的铁锅，打定主意今晚上得把锅收拾好。
他手指在那空着的铁锅上敲了敲，看向狼岩。
狼岩点头。
肉还没好，林楸先去看看今天采集队带回来的野菜。
大大小小二三十个藤筐就在广场上摆着，野菜沾了雨水，这会儿还水灵灵的。
这个时节，菜叶就少了。
兽人们往东边去的，带回来不少野韭、野葱，林楸看到混杂在其中的韭菜花，道：“下次可以多采点这个回来。”
狼清跟着他，闻言道：“花也能吃？”
“可以做酱，蘸肉一绝。”
“好。”
狼清打算明天采几筐回来。
野菜杂，只要能吃的，兽人们都采集回来了。
有些野菜叶片背面还带刺，不过兽人们采的是嫩叶，刺软，稍稍不那么扎嘴。
这么多菜吃不完，一半要晒干存放起来。
林楸又找了找，有点老了的韭菜能找出来好几筐，还有不少是块根类的植物。
大多纤维很多，有不少淀粉，管饱，但吃起来不适口。
林楸的手掠过那些口感不好的块根，专找味道好的。
最后拖出来五个藤筐的野菜，就由亚兽人们去河边洗干净，再拿回食堂。
“楸，紫花草根不要吗？”
紫花草根就是那纤维最多的根，啃它像在干嚼木头。
这种草开一簇一簇的紫色花朵，花才豆大，叶片纤长，但根很胖。
兽人们以前没多少食物，雪季后期，就靠嚼这个根度日。
紫花草根越嚼越甜，多吃点，肚子还有饱腹感。
林楸：“难啃。”
“那以后不采了？”
“采。”林楸想到了这紫花草根的另一个归处。
做淀粉。
狼清也不问为什么难啃还要采，道：“要得多还是少？”
要得多，他们就多采。要得少，他们就把精力花在其他植物采集上，尽可能多地带回来其他好吃的野菜。
“这些我先试试能不能做出淀粉来，能做就多采。”
狼清听着又是个不知道的东西，楸做出来的肯定是好东西，那还是要多采。
“楸！肉好了！”食堂窗边，狼霜冲着林楸喊。
林楸一挥手，“来了。”
新杀的肉还热气腾腾的，一堆肥瘦相间的肉旁，还放着一盆弯角兽血。
林楸看了眼，示意等着他安排的亚兽人们道：“阿叔们，拿五口陶锅加水烧开。”
“那我来切肉。”狼霜道。
林楸指着那肥瘦相间的肉道：“切成一坨一坨的，半指宽。”
“成。”
灶上忙起来，狩猎采集队洗干净爪子，也慢悠悠进了食堂。
林楸身边的光线一暗，见灶台边，狼影抱臂靠在窗台，恍惚间还以为看到了狼火。
他两口子都喜欢这个姿势靠来靠去。
“累了？”
狼影目光落在林楸手上愈发黏糊的碎肉上，道：“饿了。”
“再等会儿。先坐旁边去休息休息，吃点果子。”
采集队带回来的果子占了三分之一，红的、黄的、青的、黑的五颜六色。这会儿洗干净了，摆在桌上，要吃就拿。
“想吃肉。”狼影慢吞吞道。
旁边狼霜一听，切肉都快了。
现在食堂用的刀具都是林楸从赤山部落带回来的铁刀，刀刃薄，极锋利。
稍不注意切到手，就会流血。
这些天，负责做饭的兽人们没一个没有受过伤。
好在适应得也快，石刀那么重他们都使得，何况薄薄一片的铁刀呢。
林楸把碎肉剁好，然后示意亚兽人把铁锅这边的灶也生好火。
“楸，肉切完了。”
“野菜呢？”
“来了！”护卫队的兽人拎着菜筐进来。
林楸：“霜，韭菜切段。”
“要我们帮忙吗？”其他亚兽人阿叔怕这边忙不过来，停了织布的事，也过来了。
人手一下充足了。
林楸顿时安排下去，有剁野菜叶的，有切香草的，有烧火的。
铁锅一热，林楸往锅里放油。
片刻，白腻的油脂融化，冒出丝缕烟气。
大块大块的肉往里一倒，翻炒得四面焦黄，再下入各种香草。
“楸！陶锅里的水烧好了。”
“好。”
林楸把陶锅里的水倒进铁锅。
顿时，锅里嘟噜嘟噜也冒气泡泡。
一口陶锅的水还不够，林楸足足倒了两锅半。
盖子一盖，大火焖煮。
“楸，这边的水也好了。”
“来了。”
空出来的陶锅继续烧火，林楸往里放油，加香草翻炒。炒出那香草的味道，然后加入陶锅里的水。
咕嘟咕嘟——
不用等，水就开了。
“霜叔！你过来往锅里下血旺。切块，像我刚刚那样，下三口锅。”
狼霜立即接手林楸的活儿。
“那堆碎肉呢？”狼影出声。
“幼崽的。”
“我要吃。”
“一时半会做不了多少，明早上给你们做？”
狼影懒懒抬了下眼皮。
“嗯。”
满满一个大铁锅的红烧肉，三个锅的韭菜血旺汤，再炒两个陶锅的炒野菜，然后是幼崽的野菜肉丸子汤和奶糕，齐活！
“开饭了！”
天已经黑了，食堂里点了几根蜡烛，亮晃晃的，兽人们把碗里的食物看得清清楚楚。
那肥瘦相间的肉红亮亮，油汪汪的。
“怎么会是这个颜色？”兽人们用筷子戳一戳，喉咙一滚，很想吃，但怕吃。
林楸：“放了染色的植物，能吃。”
以前不是没做过红烧肉，但没这次这么红。大伙儿被那香味儿熏得一张嘴就流口水，实在忍不住了，埋头咬了一大口。
一抿，肉软烂化开。
荤肉的味道充斥舌尖，不肥不腻，肚子叫嚣着要更多。
实打实的肉吃得兽人们幸福得脚趾都张开了，再喝上一口鲜味十足的韭菜血旺汤，爽快！
炒野菜也好吃，就带着一点点的苦味。但混着油渣，一点难闻的草味都没有了，只剩脆爽鲜嫩。
“好吃！”
吃到兴头上，兽人问：“楸！有尾巴草籽饭没有？”
“没。”
林楸也可惜，没干饭啊。
“什么时候才能收尾巴草啊？”
“雨停。”
“收！收完我要吃尾巴草饭！还要这个肉！”
林楸想到那滋味，抿了抿唇，点头。
“可以。”
他也想吃。
火光晃动，幼崽们坐在角落，安安静静吃自己的食物。
奶糕他们一个只分了两块，其余的都是小小幼崽的。那奶糕甜甜的，一抿像吃冰，可比冰更好吃。
幼崽本来想留着的，可旁边的阿叔们虎视眈眈。
三两口吃完奶糕，再看碗里的野菜肉丸子汤，幼崽乐得眼睛都弯起来了。
筷子一戳，圆滚滚的肉丸子就被戳了起来。
送到嘴边，嗷呜咬下一大口，丸子弹牙，野菜清爽，幼崽一口气能吃十个。
再多的，阿叔们就不给了。
林楸见幼崽吃完碗里的，打个嗝，还眼巴巴地看来。
林楸正想着锅里应该还有一点。
坐在他旁边的狼岩就伸出手，摸了摸幼崽的肚子。
鼓得高高的，已经不能再吃了。
“再吃积食，想去找祭司喝草药汤了？”
幼崽一怂，立马甩脑袋，不敢再要。
晚饭毕，兽人们捧着肚子直打嗝，面皮透着红，一脸微醺，活像吃了什么山珍海味。
大伙儿去溪边洗碗，见了林楸，还围着他问一问明天的伙食。
知道明早上吃丸子汤，又是一喜。
“楸回来，日子越过越有盼头。”兽人喜笑颜开，搓陶碗的手都更有劲儿，碗底被他搓得咯吱咯吱响。
旁边同伴道：“听说今天幼崽还吃了肉沫蒸蛋的，还有那个奶糕，我也想吃。”
兽人话说得大声，林楸无奈，脑袋往旁边狼岩肩膀上磕了一下。
“你的兽人怎么这么馋？”
“别惯着他们。”
“材料都不够，想惯着也难。”
兽人们看似在认真洗碗，实则竖着耳朵听，真听到林楸做不了，摸一摸鼓起的肚子，再咂吧一下还在流口水的嘴巴。
哎——
不是他们馋，是他们自己的嘴巴想试一试而已。
看来短时间内是吃不上了。
狩猎采集队的兽人们已经很累了，收拾完，自个儿回草窝睡觉。
幼崽被狼安一并赶进山洞，连带那八个幼崽，分了窝，一起睡觉。
外面活动的兽人渐渐少了。
林楸没急着走，和狼岩在食堂里继续坐着。
房子建得多了，但睡觉的地方还是有限。食堂这边晚上也会有兽人拿上草垫，再铺上一层兽皮睡觉。
亚兽人们也不急着睡，一边织渔网，一边商量着明天把棕熊兽人交换过来的羽绒清理了。
林楸看他们精神得不行，眼神瞥向狼岩。
怎么办？
他还等着开锅呢。
狼岩直接起身，走向灶台，把两口锅都弄出来，叠在一起往外搬。
亚兽人们往旁边让了让，然后继续说话。
林楸：就这？
林楸赶紧跟出去，看着狼岩把铁锅往广场上一放，然后站直了，等着他过来。
林楸：“现在开锅吗？”
“再等等。”
狼岩洗干净手，拉着林楸先上山。
过了会儿，亚兽人们熄了蜡烛躺下。狼霜翻个身，忽然道：“诶？刚刚王是不是把锅搬出去了？”
“搬了吗？”
“我没注意。”
“我也没瞧见。”
“睡了，睡了，明天还要早起给兽人们做丸子汤呢。”
食堂和山洞里的灯熄了一会儿，山上，林楸推开小山洞的门。
“快走快走。”
他困了，赶紧干完活赶紧睡觉。
狼岩跟在他身后，不明白开个锅而已，他的伴侣为什么要偷偷摸摸。不过他很尊重伴侣的想法，有事陪他一起做就是了。
雨这会儿停了。
下山路湿滑，两个兽人走得小心翼翼。
兽人们都睡觉了，狼山一片寂静。
四周漆黑，林楸脚一滑，险些滚下山去。
狼岩眼疾手快，将他拽回来，直接将他抱坐在手臂上。
林楸抱着他脖子，埋头紧紧靠着他，心跳还在急促跳动。
吓死他了！
狼岩冷着脸，也是后怕。
“路上该铺点木炭渣。”
“嗯。”
下了山，两个兽人偷偷摸摸把铁锅移到西边去，虽然狼岩不觉得是偷偷摸摸。
狼山这边看不见了，才停下。
负责晚上巡逻的狼兽人站在狼山上，看着这一幕，有些不解地抠了抠脑袋。
“王和楸……做什么呢？”
“带着锅呢，难不成吃独食？”
狼木一巴掌拍在同伴脑门上，“王和楸是那样的兽人们？”
说着，他脚步一转，直接跟着往西边跑。
挨打的兽人翻个白眼。
你不信，还往那边跑什么？
“王……”狼木悄咪咪道。
林楸一顿，看了眼跟来的护卫队。
“你们……不去巡逻？”
“你们……干什么呢？”
林楸叹气，“开锅。”
要不是阿叔们心疼那点肉，他们也不至于做贼一样……
狼岩静静看着这群凑热闹的家伙。
狼木一个激灵，摸摸鼻子，僵着个脸笑着撒腿就跑。
“哎！”
“哎！”
巡落路上，兽人们无不遗憾。
他们也想像幼崽一样开小灶。
chapters.title: 第200章

chapters.source_text:
细雨未歇，绵绵密密像牵丝儿的糖浆一样一直不断。
天还没亮，林楸就钻出兽皮毯，闭着眼睛穿好衣服，翻过狼岩。
一只脚还没过去，狼岩就抓住了他的小腿。林楸一个不察，跌坐下来，手忙脚乱撑着狼岩胸口怕坐坏了他。
“天没亮。”
“我知道，但是昨天答应了兽人们的肉丸子必须得做。”
林楸看着狼岩也要坐起来，按住他肩膀，道：“你睡。”
狼岩：“我……”
吧唧一声，脸颊一软。
狼岩睁眼，手托着林楸后颈，压他在怀里放肆地亲。
伴侣要亲亲，怎么能不满足呢？
等到林楸出了山洞，舌尖舔一舔唇角，轻轻嘶了一声。
欲求不满的兽人还是少招惹，差点就出事了。
林楸看着路下山，到了食堂，亚兽人们已经开始在切肉了。
“楸！你下来干什么？还早呢，快回去睡着。”狼霜道。
“我来帮忙。”
“那丸子我们知道怎么做。”
“没事，那我做其他的。”
狼生他们能吃丸子汤，那八个丁点儿大的幼崽可啃不了。他们还小，主要得喝奶。
林楸也不弄复杂了，干脆拎着桶去西边挤奶。
天还黑着，隐隐约约只看得见西边几个小房子。
隔壁的红鸟还在睡觉，时不时听见几声低低的叫声，像梦呓。
林楸打开咩咩兽圈的围栏，见小狼们也已经醒了。
狼溶和狼川狼滔两兄弟这会儿在准备咩咩兽和红鸟的食物，狼逗和狼迷两个小狼在清扫棚子。
下着雨，小狼们不会放咩咩兽出去，它们吃的是之前收割回来的三叶草。
红鸟吃的则是剁碎的野菜，还有兽人们的厨余。这些东西都混在一起，放上些尾巴草籽壳，搅拌搅拌就可以给红鸟吃了。
“楸。”
林楸点头笑起来，看小狼有点肿的眼睛。
“怎么这么早起来？”
瞧着都没睡够，迷迷瞪瞪的。
狼溶打个哈欠，“它们饿了直叫，先喂了我们再去睡一会儿。”
林楸瞧着他们做得差不多了，看起来起得比他还早。
“我来挤点咩咩兽奶。”
“我们来。”狼逗放下扫帚，赶紧去水缸边洗干净手过来。
林楸跟咩咩兽不亲，也不敢凑近。
把桶交给小狼，他便帮着喂红鸟和咩咩兽。
忙活一阵，咩咩兽奶挤好了。
今天没昨天多，只有半桶。小狼面露难色道：“楸楸，没多的了，小咩咩兽要吃。”
林楸道：“够了。”
差不多半桶，只是给那批最小的幼崽吃，用不着那么多。
“那你们弄完休息，我走了。”
“好。”小狼垂着脑袋，又是一个哈欠。
林楸止步，提醒道：“你们还在长身体，必须保证睡眠，要是忙不过来，狡叔们觉少……”
小狼立刻站得笔直。
“楸！我们可以的。”
“别逞强，你们的身体最重要。”
“没有没有，我们睡够了的。睡不够我们也会补觉。”
“好。”林楸见小狼听进去了，这才离去。
提着咩咩兽奶离了西边，回到食堂，兽人们已经在剁肉了。
林楸单独找了一口灶，把咩咩兽奶倒进陶罐里煮开。
兽人们闻着那奶香味儿，忍不住感慨：“我们以前就没想到抓野兽挤奶喂幼崽。”
“带崽的野兽我们都不抓，谁能想得到？”
其他亚兽人们也跟着点头。
以前捕猎时，带崽的母兽他们都直接掠过，哪能想到自家幼崽还能吃野兽的奶？
鲜奶放温，林楸抱着罐子，拿上八个小碗进了山洞。
兽人们听到剁肉的声音也陆陆续续起了，大伙儿顶着乱糟糟的头发，迷迷瞪瞪地往外走。
忽然闻到一股奶香味儿，一下盯住林楸抱着那罐子，停了下来。
“楸……”
林楸匆匆走过，边道：“幼崽的。你们早上吃丸子汤。”
“我也想当幼崽了……”
兽人们叹气，继续往外走。
以前他们当崽子的时候，吃的都是糊糊，哪来这么多花样？这群小崽子真让兽人羡慕！
山洞拐角，幼崽都已经醒来。
地上铺着兽皮，他们四处乱爬。爬到拐角处，狼安直接用围栏挡住，幼崽出不去。
林楸抱着罐子一出现，幼崽立马抬起头，四条腿软软趴在兽皮上，奶奶地嗷了一声。
又脆又响亮。
看着是饿急了。
狼安：“我现在像要生崽子似的，见天儿的这么把他们守着。每天就盼着个兽人过来跟我说说话，带崽子不是个什么轻松活儿啊！”
林楸：“怪不得以前狼果暴躁。”
“对啊，我之前还嫌他脾气大了。”
幼崽还很小，这会儿还不能放出去见风。天气冷了，他们窝在山洞里，也不能让他们受凉。
到了雪季，更是连窝都不能让他们出。
“楸，雪季要不然让幼崽住火炕屋去？”
山洞里没有火炕，只能生个火堆。
幼崽还太小，扛不住，除非他像红鸟孵蛋那样变成兽形趴在窝里让他们靠着。
以前狼果是这样做的，狼安觉得自己一把老骨头了，这样下去得废。
林楸：“是，得去。”
雪季太冷了，成年兽人在山洞里都熬不住，莫说幼崽。
“正好新房子又要建好了，到时候先不分了，让幼崽们住着。”
“那就好。”
“吃的什么？”狼安一下把话转到吃食上去。
林楸：“咩咩兽奶。”
狼安把这群小崽子抓到草窝里去，然后往地面铺着的兽皮上再铺上两层大叶片。
然后把陶碗一一放上去。
林楸往里面倒咩咩兽奶。
“闻着没那么腥？”狼安道。
“我煮过，稍稍好一点。”
狼兽人现在才开始给幼崽喝咩咩兽奶。林楸怕幼崽拉肚子，不敢给太多。
奶一倒出来，幼崽急得往外爬。那小爪子格外有劲儿，压在草窝上，啪嗒啪嗒的响。
狼安一个个抓出来，放在碗前，一个幼崽一个碗，幼崽埋头就喝，这下看起来好多了。
罐子里剩下的，林楸递给狼安。
狼安抱住，道：“你忙去吧，我守着。”
林楸点头，随后离开。
狼安瞧了眼罐子里就剩一个底儿的咩咩兽奶，也没动。
虽说这一批幼崽出生时间相差不远，但也有身体壮的和身体稍弱一点的，饭量也有区别。
狼安瞧着哪个幼崽不够，就给添点儿。
*
肉剁好，煮丸子汤就快。
林楸回到食堂，已经有兽人捧着碗在吃了。
丸子做得大，有幼崽的拳头大小，狼兽人们也是一口一口，吃得腮帮子鼓起。见林楸进来，还眯着眼睛冲林楸笑。
“楸，快来吃。”
“马上。”
汤里还放了不少菜，为了管饱。
早饭过后，狩猎采集队就出去忙。
最近也有不少草药成熟，狼冰也得带着小狼们出去。
狼山没什么外来兽人了，狼岩也跟着狩猎队寻找猎物。
林楸想着做淀粉，要把食堂里清理出一块空地。
角落里，昨天幼崽挖出来的藕粉还湿湿的。这么放下去得坏，林楸让亚兽人们把灶台上的陶锅拿了，然后把藕粉放到灶台上去。
借着灶里的余烬，慢慢烘着。
藕粉弄好，林楸留下狼霜和另外两个亚兽人给他帮忙，其他亚兽人该做什么做什么。
兽人们提着藤筐出去，把紫花草根洗干净。
这草根长得跟树根一样，手搓还不好洗，得用摩擦力大的瓜瓤。
搓洗干净，再抬回食堂，然后再搬来之前用过的石碾，像擦藕那样摩擦。
这紫花草根更硬，得费一番力气。
幼崽们看得起劲儿，也跑过来帮忙。
林楸磨得手酸，看着石碾上流淌下去的白浆，就知道里面的淀粉足，不白忙活。
三筐紫花草根，兽人们磨了一个上午。
最后磨得幼崽都没耐性，跑连廊上去练习打架去了。
狼霜瞧着收集起来的三盆水，道：“这跟藕粉有什么区别？”
林楸：“藕粉能泡了水就吃，这个可以用在菜里。”
亚兽人们理解的能放菜里的东西都是香草那些，味道都很独特，眼前这个……
味道寡淡，生啃只有一点甜味。
兽人们不知道到底怎么用，还是要看楸做出来才知道。
三个大盆的水端去角落里放着，照旧盖上筛子，免得落了灰尘。
时候不早，亚兽人们又得准备做午饭了。
林楸想着弯角兽那点内脏还没处理。
也是现在天冷了，放个一晚上不会坏。
他起身去收拾内脏。
下着雨，兔葵他们也干不了地里的活儿。想着也无事，便跟着林楸走。
走到河边，看到那满满一大盆的内脏，兔兽人们捏着鼻子，蹲在林楸身边。
“楸，我们帮忙。”
林楸看着他们的样子，笑道：“你们受得住吗？”
兔兽人松开手，呼吸到一点气味，立马别开头。
“别逞强，现在地里还没开始收尾巴草，趁着有空，赶紧歇一歇。”
“这个也不累，就是臭了点。”
赤山部落的兽人今天也没跟着狩猎队出去，而是窝在狼山四处溜达。
狼影在狼山找了一圈，看林楸在河边，迈着两条长腿，散步一样悠闲地走了过来。
瞧着一群兔兽人围着那盆打哕，狼影走近，蹲下，道：“你们边儿上去。”
兔兽人立刻往旁边挪了挪。
他们还是有点怂狼影的。
林楸瞧着他熟练地拎起肠子，找到头，开始往外倒粪便。亚兽人面不改色。
“不嫌弃？”
“嫌弃什么？里面不都是草。”
“说得也对。”
但即便是草，也得反反复复搓洗干净。
大肠小肠洗了七八遍，最后一遍兽人才舍得裹上一点盐，继续搓洗。
兔兽人们离了有一臂远，洗不了肠子，那就洗其他内脏。
林楸看着他们手里的一副肝脏，道：“葵，你们等会儿把手里那些拿到食堂去，让阿叔们切片用点香草腌一下。”
“好。”
兔兽人走了，狼影和林楸手里的大肠小肠也洗得差不多了。
两兽人合力往水里一捞，把肠子捞起来，啪的一下，扔进盆里。
林楸端着盆往食堂走，问：“赤山部落怎么吃这些？”
狼影懒懒道：“洗干净，切一切，能烤就烤，不能烤就煮。反正味道不怎么好。”
狼影是不爱吃这些的。
但一头猎物去掉骨头本就没有多少肉，食物紧张，狼兽人不会放过一点肉。
林楸：“好吃的。”
狼影：“我就等着你做。”
部落里腌着些酸菜，林楸之前做时，亚兽人们看会了怎么做，便自己摸索着腌了不少。
林楸抓了些起来，还是用他的这口铁锅，准备炒个酸辣弯角兽肝。
“楸，兽肝切好了。”
“好。”林楸守着一个案板，几下剁碎了酸菜，道，“阿叔，铁锅这边烧火。”
说着，林楸又往另外两口铁锅里加水。
“另外两口锅加什么水，不是没有……”说着，兽人们察觉到不对，站起来看了看那两口铁锅。
油汪汪的，哪里还没开锅。
狼霜一脸心疼，刀都切歪了。
“我就说昨晚王把锅拿出去了。”
“这得费多少肥肉啊！”
林楸看着阿叔们拍大腿，心虚地转开视线。又瞧见狼影看来，兽人一双眸子仿佛洞察一切。
林楸冲他一笑，狼影撇开眼。
林楸不吭声，阿叔们心痛了一会儿，还是得继续烧火。
“别唉声叹气了，楸好不容易拿回来的锅，怎么能一直放着不用，那才是浪费。”狼霜说着，心口又痛，干脆一转眼，不去看那两口锅。
不是他们吝啬，两块掌心大小的肉，放在两三年前，他们想吃都还吃不到。
何况那全是肥肉，再不济就是肥油，饿得狠了的时候能保命的。
他们吃饱的时间太短了，这些想法一时半会转变不过来。
林楸也明白，所以才昨晚上喊了狼岩偷偷做。
不过三口大铁锅都好了，不用烧多余的灶，三口锅一口炒菜，一口炖汤，一口还能蒸米饭。
前些时候兔兽人收的那点尾巴草虽说被吃得差不多了，但其余的也已经等着收割。
锅不用那么多，烧火的兽人都轻松了。
加上铁锅热得快，又大，往常要做两三个小时的食物，现下一个多小时就好了。
亚兽人们瞧着那圆嘟嘟的锅底，脸颊被火光映得通红，眼里也带着一簇小火苗。
“是好东西！又大又结实。”
“可不，汤滚得好快！”
“哎呀，早知道该一起开锅，浪费了不少柴。”
亚兽人们说着自己都笑出声来。
先前心疼的是他们，现在后悔晚开锅的也是他们。
铁锅好用，尤其是炒菜。
林楸守着最边上那一口锅。
锅里放了热油，再怎么烧，它不会像陶锅那样，生怕烧久了就啪嗒一声裂开。
兽人们用陶锅炒菜时都心惊胆战的。
这锅好，烧得油温高高的，肉一下去，顷刻就变了颜色。
再稍稍一翻炒，立马盛出来，都怕炒久了肉老了。
林楸再往里一放酸菜，锅底烧大火，热油激得酸菜比肉还香。这会儿再把刚刚炒过的弯角兽肝放进去，稍稍一搅和，就可以捞起来了。
“影，来尝尝。”
狼影就一直守着林楸，看他怎么做。
赤山部落的兽人也跑来灶前烧火，顺带偷师。
厨子不偷吃，那说明这菜真难吃。每个兽人都尝了尝，狼山的兽人还习惯，赤山部落的兽人愣是话都说不出来。
各种猎物的内脏他们不是没吃过，可不是苦就是臭，腥味都是其次的了。
楸刚刚炒菜，他们可是眼睁睁看着他放下去的肝脏，绝对不是用鲜肉替代的。
可这东西一入口，半点腥臭的味道都没有不说，还带着一股浓浓的酸辣味道，臭味成了香味。
那弯角兽肝又嫩又滑，简直比肉还好吃。
“怎么会这样……”
就因为那几个才坛子里捞出来的蔫巴巴的菜？
林楸：“好吃吧？”
兽人们愣愣点头。
狼影：“多看多学，回部落咱们也做。”
几个要回赤山部落的亚兽人马上打起精神，抓着林楸问诀窍。
他们问什么林楸答什么。
狼山的亚兽人们笑眯眯的，让他们去边上说话，然后把另外两口铁锅里滚开的水舀出来，开始煮鱼汤。
部落再富裕，也达不到一天三顿能吃野兽肉的条件。
鱼还是要吃的。
灶台上的藕粉做饭时被移到了角落，林楸用筷子翻了翻，大块的藕粉已经能弄碎了。
幼崽在外打架打出一身汗，呼啦啦跑进来。
林楸闻到幼崽身上的闷汗味儿，一指戳在张开手臂往自己腿上抱的幼崽额头，道：“去找阿叔要热水，把身上的汗擦一擦。”
幼崽傻乐呵着，冲他露出一口小白牙，然后拐弯，找亚兽人们要水。
鱼汤好得快，成年兽人吃的酸汤鱼，幼崽就吃鱼茸混着奶白色的鱼汤。
鱼肉现在不怎么受欢迎，大家盛了一份，目光直盯着那炒肝。
林楸尝了尝味，觉得放点淀粉应该还要更滑嫩一些。
林楸吃着，见狼溶那五个小狼匆匆来了食堂，囫囵吃完，抓着碗就离开。
林楸皱眉，“溶！吃饱了没有？”
“吃饱了！”
狼霜可看得真切，这几个小狼就盛了半碗鱼汤。
“肯定没吃饱。”
林楸站起来，跟了几步，小狼才急急道：“楸，红鸟蛋孵出来了。”
林楸快步往前，拦住小狼。
“你们再吃点，我去看。”
“要把布拉开，把小红鸟捡出来。”
“好。”
林楸继续往前走，赤山部落的兽人一听，连忙跟了上来。
小狼孵出来不少次红鸟了，狼山的兽人都看习惯了，也不去凑这个热闹。
火炕屋。
林楸还没进去，就听到细弱的红鸟叫声。
他推开门，里面叫声一静。
狼影和赤山部落的兽人跟在后头，往里看了眼，跟着林楸进去。
火炕屋打扫得很干净，窗户也开着，室内还算明亮。
这个时节不冷，小狼进出都会关上火炕屋的门，让大红鸟待在外面棚子，火炕屋则用来孵蛋。
红鸟这边的火炕屋有两个，林楸进来的这个是今年新修的。
走到火炕边，刚刚还叫着的小家伙此刻一动不动，保持安静。像外面有天敌似的，自动触发了自我保护机制。
林楸把布掀开，下面全是蛋。
大部分蛋壳已经破成两半，小红鸟钻了出来，歪斜地挤在蛋壳中间，身上的绒毛被火炕烘得蓬松。
“影，帮忙拿一下你腿边的筐。”
狼影随手提起，眼睛还盯着那些小红鸟。
刚刚破壳的红鸟他们见都没见过，以前看到的要么就是蛋，要么就是已经会跑的小红鸟了。
小狼孵的红鸟也不是一个两个，而是上百个。
一大批红鸟蛋摆放在火炕上，没有大红鸟，就这么靠小狼孵化出来了。
兽人们虽然刚来那一天就听说过，但亲眼看到这么多红鸟一起出来，心中依旧震撼。
林楸看兽人们柱子一样杵在一旁，无奈道：“来了就帮忙，小心点，把毛干了的红鸟捡出来放筐里。”
兽人立马动手。
小红鸟他们见过。
在林子里，偶尔能看见跟着大红鸟找食的小红鸟。不过一窝一般只有几个，兽人们遇到了也不会抓。
可眼前这个火炕上，一个、两个……五个、十个……
兽人们越捡越小心。
刚破壳的红鸟太小，浑身都是软乎乎的毛，连小爪子都是软乎的。
透过绒毛能感觉到它们的体温，暖暖的。
就那么一点儿，还不及他们巴掌大。力道稍重，就能掰折了他们的爪子。
一连捡完半个火炕的红鸟，亚兽人们热出了一身汗。
火炕屋里虽然收拾得干净，脚底下也没红鸟粪，但炕上孵化的小红鸟破壳后，又被烘干，炕面上都散发着一股闷臭味。
可捡完红鸟，没哪一个兽人出去。
林楸看他们继续杵着，道：“怎么了？”
“你们怎么想到孵红鸟蛋的？”狼影声音发紧，看来捡个小红鸟还受到了冲击。
林楸：“不就是为了多一口肉。”
狼影喉头滚了滚，“那……你们怎么知道自己可以孵蛋？”
林楸：“你想想红鸟怎么孵蛋的？不就是需要把蛋藏在肚子下，靠自身的体温把它们孵化出来。”
“用火炕也一样，只要摸索出接近红鸟肚子上的温度，多来几次，总有点经验。”
兽人们若有所思。
虽然有几个词听不懂，但结合一下实际，还是能明白过来。
“不过这事儿我没怎么参与，都是小狼们去试。试了一年，勉强摸出点门道来。”
狼影听完不语，他弯腰，掌心贴在那炕表面。
面上还是温温的。
狼禾他们见状，也伸手试探。
“真会想……底下烧火，上面发热，就是雪季最冷的时候睡在上面也不会冷。”
难怪，他们能孵出红鸟。
林楸笑道：“狼莫在你们那边，要是有空，你们可以叫他试试。”
狼影瞧着蛋壳里藏着的浑身湿漉漉的小红鸟，道：“我觉得我们很快就要搬过来。”
这么多年都过来了，火炕做了也用不了多久。
何况铁器制作的不易，狼影回去之后也不打算抽调兽人做其他的。
他们只需要赶紧把狼山要的铁器做完，然后搬家。
林楸听出他意思，一边捡蛋壳，一边道：“随便你们。”
“那要不要带点红鸟回去养养？”
“麻烦。”狼影道。
小红鸟脆弱，回去路上要一个多月，还没到地方恐怕就死了。
“你要是有这个心思，不如把小红鸟也拿去交换。我想应该有部落想试着养一养。”
林楸一顿，看向狼影。
狼影唇角一勾：“像你说的，红鸟再小也是肉。”
狼部落可以从其他部落换肉干来，也可以换没长大的红鸟给其他部落养。
要是他们有能耐，养成狼部落这个样子，还愁什么食物。
如果狼影之前没决定来狼部落，他肯定是要带上些小红鸟和小咩咩兽回去试试的。
现在嘛，只一心想着把事办完，早早过来。
林楸被狼影这聪明劲儿惊了一下。
他之前可一点没想到还能这么办。
“……是可以考虑考虑。”
chapters.title: 第201章
chapters.translated_text:
The drizzle had not ceased, falling in a dense, continuous stream like thin, trailing syrup.

Before dawn had even broken, Lin Qiu crawled out from under the animal-hide blanket, eyes closed as he dressed and climbed over Lang Yan.

Before he could even get one leg over, Lang Yan grabbed his calf. Caught off guard, Lin Qiu tumbled back down, frantically bracing his hands against Lang Yan’s chest to avoid crushing him.

"It's not dawn yet."

"I know, but the meatballs I promised the beastmen yesterday have to be made."

Seeing Lang Yan trying to sit up too, Lin Qiu pressed down on his shoulder and said, "You sleep."

Lang Yan: "I..."

*Smack.* A soft sensation pressed against his cheek.

Lang Yan opened his eyes, his hand cupping the back of Lin Qiu’s neck, pulling him into his embrace to kiss him wantonly.

When one's partner wants a kiss, how could one not oblige?

By the time Lin Qiu left the cave, he licked the corner of his lip and let out a soft hiss.

It’s best not to provoke a beastman who isn't satisfied; things almost got out of hand.

Lin Qiu watched the path down the mountain. When he reached the canteen, the sub-beastmen had already started chopping meat.

"Qiu! Why are you down here? It's still early, go back and get some sleep," said Lang Shuang.

"I'm here to help."

"We know how to make those meatballs."

"It's fine, I'll do something else then."

Lang Sheng and the others could eat meatball soup, but the eight tiny cubs couldn't chew that. They were still too young and needed to drink milk primarily.

Lin Qiu didn't want to make things complicated, so he simply grabbed a bucket and headed west to milk the bleat-beasts.

It was still dark, and only the faint outlines of a few small houses were visible to the west.

The red birds next door were still sleeping, and from time to time, he could hear low chirps, like sleep-talking.

Lin Qiu opened the fence of the bleat-beast pen and saw that the wolf cubs were already awake.

Lang Rong and the brothers Lang Chuan and Lang Tao were preparing food for the bleat-beasts and red birds, while the two little cubs, Lang Dou and Lang Mi, were cleaning the shed.

Because of the rain, the cubs wouldn't let the bleat-beasts out, so they were eating the clover harvested earlier.

The red birds were fed chopped wild vegetables mixed with the beastmen's kitchen scraps. These were all mixed together with some tail-grass seed husks, stirred up, and ready to be fed to the birds.

"Qiu."

Lin Qiu nodded and smiled, noticing the cubs' slightly swollen eyes.

"Why are you up so early?"

They looked like they hadn't slept enough, still dazed and groggy.

Lang Rong yawned, "They were hungry and kept calling out, so we fed them first before going back to sleep for a bit."

Lin Qiu saw they had almost finished; it seemed they had woken up even earlier than he had.

"I'll come to milk the bleat-beasts."

"We'll do it." Lang Dou put down his broom and hurried to the water vat to wash his hands before coming over.

Lin Qiu wasn't close with the bleat-beasts and didn't dare get too near them.

He handed the bucket to the cubs and helped feed the red birds and bleat-beasts instead.

After a while, the bleat-beast milk was ready.

There wasn't as much as yesterday, only half a bucket. The cub looked troubled and said, "Qiuqiu, there isn't any more; the baby bleat-beasts need to eat."

Lin Qiu said, "That's enough."

Half a bucket was plenty; it was only for the smallest batch of cubs, so they didn't need that much.

"Alright, you guys go rest after you're done. I'm leaving."

"Okay." The cub hung his head and let out another yawn.

Lin Qiu stopped and reminded them, "You are still growing, you must ensure you get enough sleep. If you can't keep up, Uncle Jiao and the others don't need much sleep..."

The cubs immediately stood up straight.

"Qiu! We can do it."

"Don't push yourselves; your health is the most important thing."

"No, no, we've slept enough. If we don't get enough, we'll make up for it later."

"Good." Seeing that the cubs had taken his words to heart, Lin Qiu left.

Carrying the bleat-beast milk away from the west side, he returned to the canteen, where the beastmen were already chopping meat.

Lin Qiu found a separate stove and poured the milk into an earthenware pot to boil.

The beastmen smelled the milky aroma and couldn't help but sigh, "We never thought of catching wild beasts to milk them for the cubs before."

"We never catch beasts with cubs, so who would have thought of it?"

The other sub-beastmen nodded in agreement.

In the past, when hunting, they would always pass over mothers with cubs; how could they have imagined that their own cubs could drink the milk of wild beasts?

Once the fresh milk had cooled to a warm temperature, Lin Qiu held the pot and took eight small bowls into the cave.

Hearing the sound of meat being chopped, the beastmen had also started waking up one by one, walking outside with messy hair and dazed expressions.

Suddenly smelling the milky scent, they stopped and stared at the pot Lin Qiu was holding.

"Qiu..."

Lin Qiu hurried past, saying, "It's for the cubs. You guys are having meatball soup for breakfast."

"I wish I were a cub too..."

The beastmen sighed and continued walking outside.

Back when they were cubs, they only ate mush; where would they have had so many fancy things? These little cubs were truly the envy of the beastmen!

Around the corner of the cave, the cubs were all awake.

Animal hides were spread on the ground, and they were crawling around everywhere. When they reached the corner, Lang An used a fence to block them so they couldn't get out.

As soon as Lin Qiu appeared with the pot, the cubs immediately lifted their heads, their four legs sprawled softly on the hides, and they let out a milky "ao."

It was crisp and loud.

They looked starving.

Lang An: "I feel like I'm raising cubs myself, guarding them like this all day long. Every day I just hope a beastman comes by to talk to me; raising cubs is no easy task!"

Lin Qiu: "No wonder Lang Guo used to be so irritable."

"Exactly, and I used to complain about his temper."

The cubs were still very small and couldn't be let out into the wind yet. The weather was getting cold, and they were huddled in the cave; they couldn't be allowed to catch a chill.

When the snow season arrived, they wouldn't even be able to leave their nest.

"Qiu, should we let the cubs live in the heated-brick room during the snow season?"

There were no heated bricks in the cave, only a fire pit.

The cubs were too small to handle the cold unless he turned into his beast form and lay in the nest like a red bird incubating eggs, letting them lean against him.

Lang Guo used to do that, but Lang An felt that his old bones wouldn't be able to take it for long.

Lin Qiu: "Yes, they must go."

The snow season was too cold; even adult beastmen could barely endure it in the cave, let alone the cubs.

"It just so happens that the new houses will be finished soon; we won't divide them up yet, let the cubs live there."

"That's good."

"What are they eating?" Lang An immediately shifted the topic to food.

Lin Qiu: "Bleat-beast milk."

Lang An grabbed the little cubs and put them into the grass nest, then laid two layers of large leaves over the animal hides on the floor.

Then he placed the earthenware bowls on top one by one.

Lin Qiu poured the bleat-beast milk into them.

"It doesn't smell that gamey?" Lang An said.

"I boiled it, so it's a little better."

The wolf beastmen had only just started giving the cubs bleat-beast milk. Lin Qiu was afraid of them getting diarrhea, so he didn't dare give them too much.

As soon as the milk was poured, the cubs scrambled to crawl out. Their little claws were surprisingly strong, pattering against the grass nest.

Lang An grabbed them one by one and placed them in front of the bowls—one cub per bowl. The cubs buried their heads and drank, looking much better now.

Lin Qiu handed the remainder in the pot to Lang An.

Lang An held it and said, "You go ahead and get busy, I'll watch them."

Lin Qiu nodded and then left.

Lang An glanced at the small amount of milk left at the bottom of the pot but didn't touch it.

Although these cubs were born around the same time, there were differences in their physical strength and appetites.

Lang An watched to see which cub didn't have enough and added a little more.

*

Once the meat was chopped, the meatball soup was quick to cook.

When Lin Qiu returned to the canteen, some beastmen were already holding bowls and eating.

The meatballs were large, the size of a cub's fist, and the wolf beastmen were eating them bite by bite, their cheeks bulging. Seeing Lin Qiu enter, they squinted and smiled at him.

"Qiu, come and eat."

"Right away."

There were plenty of vegetables in the soup to make sure everyone was full.

After breakfast, the hunting and gathering teams went out to work.

Many medicinal herbs were maturing recently, so Lang Bing also had to take the cubs out.

There were no more foreign beastmen on Wolf Mountain, so Lang Yan also followed the hunting team to look for prey.

Lin Qiu was thinking about making starch and needed to clear an empty space in the canteen.

In the corner, the lotus root starch the cubs had dug up yesterday was still damp. It would spoil if left like this, so Lin Qiu asked the sub-beastmen to remove the earthenware pots from the stove and place the starch on the stove top instead.

Using the residual heat from the stove, it dried slowly.

Once the lotus root starch was handled, Lin Qiu kept Lang Shuang and two other sub-beastmen to help him, while the others went about their tasks.

The beastmen went out with vine baskets to wash the purple-flower grass roots.

These roots grew like tree roots and were hard to wash by hand; they had to use the abrasive flesh of gourds.

After scrubbing them clean, they brought them back to the canteen and moved the stone mill used previously to grind them, just like they did with the lotus roots.

These purple-flower grass roots were harder and took quite a bit of effort.

The cubs, watching with interest, also ran over to help.

Lin Qiu’s hands were sore from grinding, but seeing the white slurry flowing down from the mill, he knew it was full of starch and that the work wasn't in vain.

The beastmen spent the whole morning grinding three baskets of purple-flower grass roots.

By the end, the cubs lost interest and ran to the corridor to practice fighting.

Lang Shuang looked at the three basins of water collected and asked, "How is this different from lotus root starch?"

Lin Qiu: "Lotus root starch can be eaten just by adding water, but this can be used in dishes."

The sub-beastmen understood things that could be put in dishes as herbs, which had unique flavors, but this...

It was bland, with only a hint of sweetness when eaten raw.

The beastmen didn't know how to use it and would have to wait until Qiu made something with it.

The three large basins of water were placed in the corner and covered with a sieve to keep the dust out.

It was getting late, and the sub-beastmen had to prepare lunch again.

Lin Qiu remembered that the viscera of the curved-horn beast hadn't been processed yet.

It was cold now, so it wouldn't spoil if left for a night.

He got up to clean the viscera.

It was raining, and Tu Kui and the others couldn't do field work. Thinking there was nothing to do, they followed Lin Qiu.

When they reached the river and saw the large basin full of viscera, the rabbit beastmen pinched their noses and squatted beside Lin Qiu.

"Qiu, we'll help."

Lin Qiu looked at them and smiled, "Can you handle it?"

The rabbit beastmen let go of their noses, took a breath of the air, and immediately turned their heads away.

"Don't push yourselves. The tail-grass harvest hasn't started yet, so take a break while you have the time."

"This isn't tiring, it's just a bit smelly."

The beastmen of the Chishan tribe didn't follow the hunting team out today but were wandering around Wolf Mountain.

Lang Ying had searched Wolf Mountain and, seeing Lin Qiu by the river, walked over with his long legs, as leisurely as if he were taking a stroll.

Seeing a group of rabbit beastmen retching around the basin, Lang Ying walked over, squatted down, and said, "You guys move aside."

The rabbit beastmen immediately moved to the side.

They were still a bit intimidated by Lang Ying.

Lin Qiu watched as he skillfully picked up the intestines, found the end, and began to empty the feces. The sub-beastman didn't change his expression.

"You don't mind?"

"Mind what? Isn't it all just grass inside?"

"That's true."

But even if it was just grass, it had to be scrubbed clean repeatedly.

The large and small intestines were washed seven or eight times; only on the last time did the beastman deign to rub them with a bit of salt to continue scrubbing.

The rabbit beastmen stayed an arm's length away; since they couldn't wash the intestines, they washed the other viscera.

Lin Qiu looked at the liver in their hands and said, "Kui, take those to the canteen later and let the uncles slice them and marinate them with some herbs."

"Okay."

The rabbit beastmen left, and the large and small intestines in the hands of Lang Ying and Lin Qiu were almost clean.

The two beastmen worked together to scoop them out of the water and *thwack*, threw them into the basin.

Lin Qiu carried the basin toward the canteen and asked, "How does the Chishan tribe eat these?"

Lang Ying said lazily, "Wash them, chop them, roast them if you can, boil them if you can't. Anyway, the taste isn't very good."

Lang Ying didn't like eating these things.

But once the bones were removed, there wasn't much meat on a prey animal, and with food being scarce, the wolf beastmen wouldn't waste a single bit of meat.

Lin Qiu: "They're delicious."

Lang Ying: "I'm just waiting for you to make them."

There was some pickled cabbage in the tribe. When Lin Qiu made it before, the sub-beastmen learned how to do it and had pickled quite a lot themselves.

Lin Qiu grabbed some and used his iron pot to prepare a stir-fried spicy curved-horn beast liver.

"Qiu, the beast liver is sliced."

"Good." Lin Qiu stood by a cutting board, chopped the pickled cabbage in a few strokes, and said, "Uncle, start the fire under the iron pot."

As he spoke, Lin Qiu added water to the other two iron pots.

"Why add water to the other two pots? Isn't there no..." The beastmen realized something was wrong and stood up to look at the two iron pots.

They were glistening with oil; they had clearly been used.

Lang Shuang looked heartbroken, his knife even slipping.

"I knew the King took the pots out last night."

"Think of how much fat that must have wasted!"

Lin Qiu saw the uncles slapping their thighs and guiltily looked away. He noticed Lang Ying looking at him, his eyes seeming to see through everything.

Lin Qiu smiled at him, and Lang Ying looked away.

Lin Qiu didn't say anything, and although the uncles were heartbroken for a while, they still had to continue the fire.

"Don't sigh and moan. Qiu finally brought back the pots; how can we just leave them unused? That would be the real waste," Lang Shuang said, though his heart still ached, so he turned his head away to avoid looking at the pots.

It wasn't that they were stingy; two pieces of meat the size of a palm were something they couldn't even get two or three years ago.

Especially since it was all fat, or at the very least, lard, which could save their lives when they were starving.

They had only been full for a short time, and these thoughts couldn't be changed overnight.

Lin Qiu understood, which was why he had asked Lang Yan to do it secretly last night.

But now that all three large iron pots were ready, there was no need to burn extra stoves; one pot for stir-frying, one for stewing soup, and one for steaming rice.

Although the tail-grass the rabbit beastmen harvested earlier was almost gone, the rest was already waiting to be harvested.

With fewer pots needed, the beastmen tending the fire had an easier time.

Plus, the iron pots heated up quickly and were large, so food that usually took two or three hours now took just over an hour.

The sub-beastmen looked at the round pot bottoms, their cheeks flushed red by the firelight, and a spark of excitement in their eyes.

"They are good things! Big and sturdy."

"Indeed, the soup boils so fast!"

"Oh, if we had known, we should have opened all the pots together; we wasted a lot of firewood."

The sub-beastmen laughed at themselves as they spoke.

They were the ones who felt heartbroken earlier, and now they were the ones regretting not using the pots sooner.

The iron pots were great, especially for stir-frying.

Lin Qiu stood by the pot on the end.

He put hot oil in the pot; no matter how long he cooked, it wouldn't crack like the earthenware pots, which they were always afraid would *snap* if cooked too long.

The beastmen were always terrified when stir-frying in earthenware pots.

This pot was great; the oil temperature got very high, and as soon as the meat went in, it changed color instantly.

After a quick stir-fry, he took it out immediately, afraid the meat would get tough if cooked too long.

Lin Qiu added the pickled cabbage, turned the fire up high, and the hot oil made the cabbage smell even better than the meat. He then added the stir-fried liver back in, gave it a quick toss, and it was ready to be taken out.

"Ying, come and taste."

Lang Ying had been watching Lin Qiu the whole time, seeing how he did it.

The Chishan tribe beastmen also ran to the stove to tend the fire and steal a few techniques.

If a cook doesn't steal a bite, it means the food is truly bad. Every beastman tasted it; the Wolf Mountain beastmen were used to it, but the Chishan tribe beastmen were so stunned they couldn't speak.

It wasn't that they hadn't eaten the viscera of various prey before, but it was either bitter or smelly, and the gamey odor was secondary.

They had watched Lin Qiu add the liver with their own eyes; it definitely wasn't replaced with fresh meat.

Yet, as soon as it hit their tongues, there was no trace of the gamey smell; instead, it was filled with a rich, sour, and spicy flavor, and the stench had become an aroma.

The curved-horn beast liver was tender and smooth, tasting even better than meat.

"How can this be..."

Just because of those wilted vegetables fished out of a jar?

Lin Qiu: "Is it good?"

The beastmen nodded blankly.

Lang Ying: "Watch more and learn more; we'll do this when we get back to the tribe."

The few sub-beastmen who were returning to the Chishan tribe immediately perked up and grabbed Lin Qiu to ask for the secret.

Lin Qiu answered whatever they asked.

The Wolf Mountain sub-beastmen smiled and told them to go talk to the side, then scooped out the boiling water from the other two iron pots to start making fish soup.

No matter how wealthy the tribe was, they couldn't afford to eat wild beast meat three times a day.

They still had to eat fish.

The lotus root starch on the stove had been moved to the corner during cooking. Lin Qiu stirred it with chopsticks, and the large chunks of starch were already easy to break up.

The cubs, having worked up a sweat fighting outside, came running in.

Lin Qiu smelled the stuffy sweat on the cubs and poked the forehead of a cub who was reaching out to hug his leg, saying, "Go ask the uncles for hot water and wipe the sweat off."

The cub giggled, showing his little white teeth, and then turned to ask the sub-beastmen for water.

The fish soup was ready quickly; the adult beastmen ate sour fish soup, while the cubs ate fish paste mixed with the milky-white fish broth.

Fish meat wasn't very popular now; everyone took a portion but kept their eyes fixed on the stir-fried liver.

Lin Qiu tasted it and thought that adding a little starch would make it even smoother and more tender.

As Lin Qiu ate, he saw Lang Rong and the five little cubs hurry into the canteen, finish their food in a rush, and leave with their bowls.

Lin Qiu frowned, "Rong! Are you full?"

"Full!"

Lang Shuang saw clearly that these little cubs had only had half a bowl of fish soup.

"They definitely aren't full."

Lin Qiu stood up and followed a few steps, but the little cub said urgently, "Qiu, the red bird eggs have hatched."

Lin Qiu quickened his pace and stopped the little cub.

"You guys eat some more, I'll go check."

"You have to pull the cloth back and pick out the little red birds."

"Okay."

Lin Qiu continued forward, and the Chishan tribe beastmen, hearing this, hurriedly followed.

The cubs had hatched red birds many times, and the Wolf Mountain beastmen were used to it and didn't bother joining in the fun.

The heated-brick room.

Before Lin Qiu even entered, he heard the faint chirping of red birds.

He pushed the door open, and the chirping inside went silent.

Lang Ying and the Chishan tribe beastmen followed behind, took a look inside, and went in after Lin Qiu.

The heated-brick room was kept very clean, and the windows were open, making the interior quite bright.

It wasn't cold this season, so the cubs would close the door when they went in and out, keeping the adult red birds in the shed outside, while the heated-brick room was used for incubating eggs.

There were two heated-brick rooms for the red birds, and the one Lin Qiu entered was newly built this year.

Walking to the heated brick, the little ones that were chirping just a moment ago were now motionless, keeping quiet. It was as if they had triggered a self-protection mechanism, sensing predators outside.

Lin Qiu lifted the cloth, and underneath were eggs.

Most of the eggshells had broken into two halves, and the little red birds had crawled out, squeezed crookedly in the middle of the shells, their downy feathers fluffed up by the heat of the brick.

"Ying, help me grab the basket by your leg."

Lang Ying picked it up casually, his eyes still fixed on the little red birds.

They had never seen red birds that had just hatched; what they had seen before were either eggs or little red birds that could already run.

The cubs didn't just hatch one or two red birds, but hundreds.

A large batch of red bird eggs was laid out on the heated brick, and without an adult red bird, they had been hatched by the cubs.

Although the beastmen had heard about it on their first day, seeing so many red birds hatch at once was still shocking.

Lin Qiu saw the beastmen standing there like pillars and said helplessly, "Since you're here, help out. Be careful, pick out the red birds whose feathers are dry and put them in the basket."

The beastmen immediately started working.

They had seen little red birds before.

In the forest, they could occasionally see little red birds following their mothers to find food. But a nest usually only had a few, and the beastmen wouldn't catch them if they encountered them.

But on this heated brick, one, two... five, ten...

The beastmen became more and more careful as they picked them up.

The newly hatched red birds were too small, covered in soft down, and even their little claws were soft.

Through the down, they could feel their body temperature—warm.

They were so tiny, not even the size of their palms. A little too much force, and they could break their claws.

After picking up half the red birds on the heated brick, the sub-beastmen were sweating.

Although the room was kept clean and there were no droppings on the floor, the little red birds that had hatched and dried on the brick gave off a stuffy, musty smell.

But after picking them up, not a single beastman left.

Lin Qiu saw them still standing there and asked, "What's wrong?"

"How did you think of hatching red bird eggs?" Lang Ying’s voice was tight; it seemed that picking up the little red birds had been quite a shock.

Lin Qiu: "Isn't it just to have more meat?"

Lang Ying swallowed hard, "Then... how did you know you could hatch eggs?"

Lin Qiu: "Think about how red birds hatch eggs. They just need to hide the eggs under their bellies and use their own body heat to hatch them."

"It's the same with the heated brick; as long as you figure out the temperature close to a red bird's belly, and try a few times, you'll eventually gain some experience."

The beastmen were thoughtful.

Although they didn't understand a few of the words, they could understand the meaning when combined with reality.

"But I didn't really participate in this; the cubs tried it themselves. They tried for a year and barely figured out a way."

Lang Ying didn't speak after listening; he bent down and pressed his palm against the surface of the brick.

It was still warm.

Seeing this, Lang He and the others also reached out to test it.

"They really know how to think... fire underneath, heat on top; even in the coldest part of the snow season, you wouldn't be cold sleeping on this."

No wonder they could hatch red birds.

Lin Qiu smiled, "Lang Mo is on your side; if you have time, you can ask him to try."

Lang Ying looked at the wet little red birds hiding in the eggshells and said, "I think we will be moving over here soon."

They had survived for so many years, and it wouldn't take long to build a heated brick.

Besides, ironware wasn't easy to make, and Lang Ying didn't intend to pull beastmen away to do other things after returning.

They just needed to finish the ironware Wolf Mountain needed as soon as possible and then move.

Lin Qiu understood his meaning and, while picking up eggshells, said, "Suit yourselves."

"Do you want to take some red birds back to raise?"

"Too much trouble," Lang Ying said.

The little red birds were fragile, and the journey back would take more than a month; they would probably be dead before they even arrived.

"If you have the mind for it, you might as well take the little red birds to trade. I think there are tribes that would want to try raising them."

Lin Qiu paused and looked at Lang Ying.

Lang Ying’s lips curled: "As you said, no matter how small a red bird is, it's still meat."

The wolf tribe could trade for dried meat from other tribes, or they could trade the young red birds for other tribes to raise.

If they had the ability to raise them like the wolf tribe did, they wouldn't have to worry about food.

If Lang Ying hadn't decided to come to the wolf tribe earlier, he would definitely have taken some little red birds and little bleat-beasts back to try.

Now, he was only focused on finishing the task and moving over early.

Lin Qiu was surprised by Lang Ying’s cleverness.

He hadn't thought of that at all.

"...It is something to consider."

"Qiu! We're back!"

The little wolves, returning from the Daze with lotus roots, ran excitedly through the rain. They wore straw rain capes on their backs and pulled handcarts behind them. The lotus roots on the carts were long, whole, and intact; having been washed clean by the rain along the way back, the top layers were spotless.

Hearing the commotion, Lin Qiu stepped out of the heated-bed room.

Lang Rong and the others had finished their meat soup and returned; the task of feeding the little red birds was left to them.

Lang Ying followed Lin Qiu outside, while Lang He and a few other sub-beasts, interested in the egg hatching and feeding, stayed behind to watch.

"Qiu—"

"Stop howling, I'm right here."

Lin Qiu walked over from the west side. The little wolves parked in the plaza grinned and tilted their heads up to look at him.

"Qiu, we're hungry."

Lin Qiu looked at the fluffy ears on the little wolves' foreheads, flattened by their straw rain hats; only a tiny tip of their large wolf ears poked out.

He reached out and tugged at a hat, asking, "Are you wet?"

"Just a little bit."

Lin Qiu didn't believe it was "just a little bit"; he had seen them stepping in puddles just moments ago.

"Go dry off. I'm going to check the cafeteria."

"Awoo!" The little wolves let out an excited howl that made Lin Qiu’s ears buzz, leaving him unable to hear anything for a moment.

He let go, and the hat flopped back down onto the little wolf's forehead.

The little wolf’s head was bumped, and he looked at Lin Qiu innocently with eyes like black beans.

Lin Qiu rubbed his ears and quickly moved away from them.

Lang Ying stood still, watching the little wolves unload the lotus roots.

There were six full carts, each stacked high. The lotus roots were a pale, pinkish-white; the older sections were mostly half an arm's length and slightly darker in color.

This stuff was hidden deep in the silt. Perhaps some beasts had discovered it and dug it up to eat before, but as far as he knew, none of the tribes in the middle of the Eastern Continent knew that this existed beneath those round leaves.

Just a dozen roots, boiled briefly with bones, could fill the bellies of dozens of beasts.

And the taste wasn't bad at all.

Lang Shan really had so many good things...

The little wolves were eager to eat and unloaded the cargo efficiently. Seeing Lang Ying still standing there watching, they felt a pang of nervousness.

Lang Jin gave him a silent look and casually snapped off the tenderest tip of a lotus root.

It sounded crisp just from the snap.

"Wolf King, d-do you want some?"

Lang Ying looked at the little wolf who was baring his teeth in a flattering way and took it.

Seeing how clean the lotus root was, he took a bite; it had a fresh fragrance and was quite sweet.

Only then did he raise an eyebrow, turn around, and head into the cafeteria.

The little wolves shook the water off their fur and, with a howl, immediately ran toward the large cave.

They hurriedly dried each other off and then rushed into the cafeteria in a swarm.

Lang Shuang and the others were used to making food for the beasts, so the portions were just right. By the time the little wolves returned, there wasn't much food left in the pots.

Lin Qiu thought for a moment and simply stir-fried some wild vegetables with cracklings, sautéed the remaining organs with various pickled vegetables, and added an egg drop soup—that should be enough.

The little wolves were boisterous; entering the room felt like dozens of flamingos running past, clattering and making their presence known.

Lang Ying stepped aside, and the little wolves lightened their steps as they passed him.

When they reached Lin Qiu, they opened their mouths, ready to howl again.

Lin Qiu: "Grab your bowls and serve yourselves."

"Awoo!"

Lin Qiu rubbed his ears, feeling quite helpless.

They were truly noisy.

Two dishes and a soup—it would be great if there were a bowl of white rice to go with it.

Sigh!

Thinking about how they only had tail-grass seed rice, and he didn't know where to find real rice.

"Rice?" Lang Ying repeated.

Lin Qiu was startled.

It turned out he had muttered his inner thoughts aloud.

"Rice... it's similar to tail-grass. It's a plant called paddy that grows ears when it matures. After the ears ripen, they are dried and husked. The inside is usually white, and the grains are a bit larger than tail-grass seeds. The leaves are long and thin, and it usually grows in water..."

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Ying, explaining in detail, just to see if he knew anything about it.

After he finished, Lang Ying shook his head.

"Never seen it."

"Then where do you think I could find it?"

"Based on what you said, maybe you'd find it if you head south." Things that grow in water are most abundant in the south. It's hotter there, and there are more plants.

Lin Qiu's hope faded, and he said, "I guess I'll just have to look later."

"Qiu, Qiu, Qiu..."

Lin Qiu looked at the little wolves helplessly, "Coming."

He couldn't let the little wolves serve themselves, or they would fight over the food, turning the cafeteria into a battlefield.

As soon as Lin Qiu finished serving, the sound of the little wolves eating voraciously filled the room.

Against this background noise, Lang Ying broke off another piece of tender lotus root, took a bite, and looked at Lin Qiu: "Anything else to do?"

"No, take a break."

But there was no resting. Not long after Lin Qiu sat down, he saw the uncles bringing the undried lotus root powder to the stove.

Besides the lotus powder, the dried fish, dried vegetables, and dried fruits in the cave also needed to be roasted.

Lin Qiu got up to help, and Lang Shuang said to him, "The rain has lasted too long. The dried fish and vegetables aren't fully dried; they're going to spoil."

"We don't have to move them all here. Why not try lighting fires in the caves?"

"We are, but there's just too much; we can't dry it all at once, so we're bringing some to the cafeteria."

Once these things were placed near the stove, the residual heat wasn't enough. The beasts simply lit the fire in the stove and roasted them over a low flame.

Afterward, they left a few beasts to watch over them, while others went to wash more lotus roots and brought them in to start making lotus powder.

Lang Ying took a look and followed them.

Lin Qiu noticed that whenever he saw something new, he had to go check it out.

"Uncle, the previous batch of lotus powder isn't even dry yet," Lin Qiu said.

"It's fine, just roasting it will work," the sub-beast said. "We need to make as much as we can while we have time. Isn't it time to harvest the tail-grass? All the beasts remaining at Lang Shan will have to go; we won't have enough hands."

The beasts valued grain extremely highly.

They would rather be tired than let the harvestable tail-grass get wet, moldy, and ruined.

Not even a handful.

They were rushing the work now, fearing they wouldn't be able to handle other tasks later if they were too exhausted.

Hearing this, Lin Qiu, who had planned to take a nap in the cave, decided to sit down and help instead.

Lang He and the other beasts returned after watching the little wolves feed the red birds.

As soon as they entered, they saw the Lang Shan little wolves lying on the ground in a mess, taking up most of the space.

In the other half of the room, their King and other beasts sat among the lotus roots, rubbing the joints against stones or iron plates.

"King."

Lang Ying glanced over and said, "Help."

Lang He immediately went to wash his hands with his companions.

Lin Qiu had thought about making a grater when he was making kitchen tools, but Lang Mo and the others didn't have that skill yet. However, since the tribe needed to crush many lotus roots, they had simply made some uneven iron plates when forging iron tools.

Lin Qiu hadn't thought of it when processing purple flower roots earlier, but now he had taken the iron plates out to use.

As for the effect, it actually required one hand to hold it steady, which took more effort.

It seemed it still needed improvement.

Lin Qiu discussed how to improve it with Lang Ying, telling him to go back and inform Lang Mo. He also wanted to see if they could make a grater.

The tribe had many beasts with huge appetites; in the future, if they wanted to eat shredded meat, they would be cutting until their hands went numb.

Lang Ying listened while rubbing the lotus roots against the iron plate placed in a basin.

He listened to Lin Qiu talk about making small raised holes on a piece of iron, with the edges of the holes thin and sharp, so that it would shred the root with one pass.

Lang Ying: "Difficult."

"It has to be done, but let's prioritize the main farm tools and weapons first. This can wait; if you have time later, you can try it."

Lin Qiu was also thinking about the beasts being able to make more refined things in the future, like cart wheels.

There was still plenty of time; let the beasts get proficient slowly.

There were many beasts making lotus powder; the uncles were there, the rabbit beasts came to help, the cubs were joining in the fun, and finally, Lang He and the others joined in too.

There wasn't enough room by the stone mill, and there were few iron plates, so they had to find some stone slabs and ask Lang Qi to help use chisels and hammers to make some indentations.

It worked; it was essentially a simplified stone mill.

Speaking of stone mills, Lin Qiu also casually asked Lang Qi and the others to make a few.

Lang Qi, who had just been given another task by Lin Qiu's casual remark: "..."

"See? I told you, Qiu will always have new things for us to make."

Lang Jiao, who was already marinated in the scent of wood, silently blew on the sickle handle in front of him, then looked at the other tools piled to the side that still needed handles, and sighed softly.

He used to think that being old meant being useless, but now he felt that being old wasn't used like this.

This group of old guys stayed in this cave every day; it wasn't a prison, but it felt like one.

Their butts were sore from sitting, and they had to go to the priest for medicine.

He was too embarrassed to show his old face.

The youngest in the group, Lang Pi, leaned on the wooden stump in front of him and slowly stood up, his bones cracking.

The beasts were used to it.

Lang Pi stretched and immediately held his waist.

"Can't do it anymore, I'm going out for a walk."

How could he have a bad waist at such a young age?

Lang Qi waved his hand, "Take the old guys with numb feet out too."

The beasts were in pain and happy at the same time.

Sigh! Although they were old, what would the tribe do without them?! Which young beast could sit like this and tinker with these tools?

*

It rained for two more days before it finally cleared up.

The ground was still wet and needed to be dried before harvesting.

However, Lang Qi and the old beasts hurried and finally finished installing the sickle handles.

With the handles extended, the beasts could save some effort.

Now that the sun was out, the sub-beasts quickly swept the water off the plaza, took the chairs out of the cafeteria, and moved all the dried fish, meat, vegetables, fruits, lotus powder, and starch that needed drying out onto the chairs.

In no time, most of the plaza was occupied.

The starch had been scooped out of the water for two days and kept in the room roasting; it had now turned into fine, finger-sized particles.

Three baskets of purple flower roots yielded three basins of water, and the starch settled at the bottom of each basin was a full finger thick.

It was even more than Lin Qiu had imagined.

When the gathering team saw the drying starch, they didn't need Lin Qiu to tell them; the next day, they dug up more than twice the amount of purple flower roots.

Now the beasts were grinding both lotus powder and starch; they hadn't rested for days.

The rain stopped, and after the sun had been out for half a day, the rabbit beasts, who had been idle for days, went down to the fields.

They stepped into the fields to check how the soil was drying.

They touched the tail-grass stalks; they were still a bit wet.

It wasn't good to harvest them while wet; if it rained again, they wouldn't have time to dry thoroughly, and they would spoil in the cave in just a few days.

There was too much tail-grass, and it was hard to dry, so it was better to let it dry in the field until there was no moisture before cutting.

Rabbit Kui returned and said to harvest tomorrow.

In the evening, when Lang Yan returned, Lin Qiu asked him to arrange the tail-grass harvest.

Harvesting tail-grass was a big deal; the sooner it was brought in, the better.

The next morning, except for the little wolves going to the Daze, Lang Tan's gathering team, and the second hunting team, all other beasts stayed at Lang Shan to harvest the tail-grass.
