He sat on the grass mat like a jade Buddha, watching the Feather Clan members in the distance.

"Gone?"

"Gone."

"Send them off."

Hu Xiaowei's eyelids twitched; he lowered his head and said with reluctance, "Patriarch, they are heading south."

Hu Xian: "Whether they go south or east, didn't they choose to betray us when the tribe was in difficulty?"

Hu Xiaowei lowered his head even further.

"The High Priest said, the Beast God..."

Hu Xian raised his hand, "...that Feather Clan beastman who was disrespectful to the Beast God just now, have him go along to send them off too."

Hu Xiaowei's scalp went numb.

He didn't dare to say another word, lowered his head respectfully, and left quickly.

*

Northern District of the Yuanye Tribe.

Among the dense stone houses, in the area where the Small Cat tribe lived, there was quite a commotion at the moment.

After Mao Ci returned, the tribesmen who had been waiting in the stone houses for his news all came out.

They were all well-proportioned and slender, slightly thinner than the Lion or Bear tribes, with light steps and quick speed.

Mao Ci looked at the tribesmen who had approached, signaling them not to speak. He looked around at the houses of the neighboring tribes, and seeing no movement, he let the beastmen follow him into the house.

"Ci... how did it go?"

Since coming to the Yuanye Tribe, they had changed to calling Hu Xian "Patriarch," and the original leader Mao Ci was now just called by his name.

Mao Ci's house was larger, almost twice the size of the small stone house in the plaza.

The beastmen followed him in, and seeing Mao Ci nod, their eyes went dull, and they sat slowly on the ground, hands supporting themselves.

"Everyone go pack your things; let's leave early," Mao Ci said.

"But Ci... isn't it good to stay in the Yuanye Tribe?"

"Yeah, even if there's less food now than before, it's still better than being outside where we can't find any food at all."

Hearing this, Mao Ci said in a deep voice, "I've already told you the reason, and you all agreed. Now that I've told the Patriarch, you want to go back on your word?"

The beastmen fell silent.

Mao Ci: "We leave tonight. Go pack your things."

The beastmen were confused; yes, they had agreed before.

But that was because Mao Ci said that if they didn't leave, the food they got later would be even less, and the Yuanye Tribe would surely fall into chaos.

But that was just his speculation. Now that they had calmed down, the thought of the wandering life after leaving the Yuanye Tribe made them afraid.

Mao Ci saw what the beastmen were thinking and said, "Fine, for those who want to stay, I won't force you. Those who want to come with me, go pack your things."

After he finished speaking, nearly half the beastmen stood up.

Compared to Hu Xian, the Patriarch of the Yuanye Tribe, they actually identified more with Mao Ci.

Although they had joined the Yuanye Tribe for so many years, they could count the number of times they had seen Hu Xian on one hand.

They trusted Mao Ci's judgment, just as they had when he decided to join the Yuanye Tribe. Since they were leaving this time, they would follow him.

The Yuanye Tribe allocated houses based on who arrived first; in the Small Cat tribe area, Mao Ci's tribe had been the first to arrive.

Among them, the Short-Tailed Cat tribe on the left had left as early as last year after the snow season. The house was left empty, and later, many beastmen who had joined were housed there.

The Small Cat tribe's packing couldn't be very quiet, no matter how hard they tried.

In the stone houses on the left, a Black Panther beastman sat at the door, tossing a stone in his hand, his gaze looking over here without any attempt to hide it.

He wore a wide animal hide around his waist, and his exposed skin was covered in many scars; a long scar ran directly across his face from his left temple to his right jaw.

The scar clung to his face like a centipede, distorting the shape of his eyes, nose, and mouth.

The nearby beastmen were all afraid of him.

"Ba, there's a mission."

The Black Panther beastman looked at the Grey-Winged beastman, Hui Xun, who had landed silently beside him. His gaze was cold, his eyes filled with indifference.

Hui Xun: "Tonight, take the food and send the Small Cat tribe off."

The Black Panther beastman nodded.

Hui Xun flew away silently.

*

Night fell.

The Yuanye Tribe was afraid that departing beastmen would cause panic among others, so they usually had them leave at night.

After dinner, the Black Panther beastman took his team of beastmen in advance and collected the food to be given to Mao Ci's tribe outside the Priest Plaza gate.

Afterward, the beastmen moved in the dark to wait for them in the south.

The Yuanye Tribe was built on the plains in the center of the Central Continent, surrounded by walls made of stone and mud; the walls weren't high, and beastmen could climb over them in a few moves.

To the south, the sky was pitch black, and the trees within a hundred meters of the wall had been cleared away.

The Black Panther beastman folded his arms, leaning quietly against the wall, gazing at the blurred moon in the sky.

He was tall, but his appearance was terrifying; anyone who saw him at night would be startled.

The beastmen in his team had been with him the longest and knew his personality wasn't as scary as he looked; other than being quiet and ugly, he had no flaws.

Most of them were scattered beastmen who had come to join the Yuanye Tribe; they had been arranged to live with the Black Panther beastman, worked together, hunted together, and gradually became familiar with each other.

Everyone recognized the Black Panther beastman's strength and accepted him as their captain.

Over the past two years, they had accomplished many things under him, gained the tribe's trust, and received a good share of food, so they were even more loyal to him.

At this time, the Small Cat tribe beastmen hadn't come out yet.

The Yuanye Tribe did not allow beastmen to be outside the walls after dark, so there were no other beastmen around.

Bao Dong, also a Black Panther beastman, walked over and leaned against the wall, whispering, "Captain, are we really sending them off or faking it?"

The Black Panther beastman swept his gaze over, and Bao Dong immediately shut up.

Movement came from the other side of the wall.

Mao Ci came out with his tribesmen.

The two sides met and headed south.

Hui Xun landed on the wall, with Hu Xiaowei, representing Hu Xian, beside him to send the beastmen off.

Hu Xiaowei watched the beastmen disappear into the bushes and whispered, "Aren't you going with them?"

Hui Xun: "Ba is trustworthy."

Hu Xiaowei: "What an ugly name."

Hui Xun: "He was picked up from the forest by the Priest; even after being saved, he was covered in scars and was like a mute. Don't you think this name is very fitting?"

"He has a name."

"You mean Bao Wen?" Hui Xun took off, leaving a sentence behind, "That's even uglier."

Hu Xiaowei watched him follow and, knowing he was cautious, left with peace of mind.

*

Sending beastmen off with food meant first getting them out of the area where Yuanye Tribe beastmen usually roamed.

Entering the forest, Mao Ci said, "Ba, give us the supplies."

The Black Panther beastman didn't speak, just kept running forward.

Mao Ci could only lead his tribesmen to follow.

They watched the beastmen who were sending them off carrying large bags of things on their backs; without checking, they could smell the scent of dried meat inside.

The food carried by more than thirty beastmen was enough, even if it took them two or three months to find a place to settle down.

The cat beastmen were moved.

Even Mao Ci felt immense admiration for Hu Xian.

For a Patriarch to do this much, it was no wonder the tribe's beastmen were so loyal to Hu Xian.

He even thought that if they could really find a place to settle down this time, he would bring his beastmen back to visit and offer more to the Beast God.

The other beastmen of the Small Cat tribe followed the beastmen who were sending them off, slowly gathering around Mao Ci.

Leaving the place they had lived for over ten years, and because of something that might not even happen, the beastmen were extremely reluctant.

Seeing the Yuanye Tribe send them off with so much food and even specifically sending beastmen to accompany them, the beastmen who weren't firm in their decision began to hesitate on the spot.

"Ci... maybe we should go back..."

Mao Ci's heart wavered too.

But as long as he thought about the day he and his tribesmen might become slaves or food for other strong beastmen, his heart hardened again.

He said, "Those who don't want to leave can stay."

There had been such a scene during the day, so the beastmen didn't dare to say more. The main group hurried forward, and the few who didn't want to leave didn't dare to stop directly, so they had to follow the team forward reluctantly.

The team traveled for half the night, and finally, the Black Panther beastman stopped.

The other beastmen also put down their things one after another and sat down to rest.

Mao Ci led the beastmen to find water and brought it back for the beastmen who had sent them off to drink.

He said to the leading Black Panther beastman, "Let's stop here. You should head back once you've rested."

In the dense forest, the moon was hidden so that not a trace could be seen.

Everything around was pitch black and eerie.

The cat beastmen, who were used to staying in stone houses after dark, felt a bit terrified.

The Black Panther beastman put down the leaf filled with water, looked at the Small Cat leader in front of him, and said, "Count the beastmen, see if anyone is missing."

"No one."

"Are you sure, not even one?" The Black Panther beastman looked steadily at Mao Ci.

Mao Ci didn't know why, but he felt a chill down his spine under that gaze.

He took a step back and said, "Not one."

As soon as he finished, the thirty-plus beastmen who had come to send them off leaped up, their claws aiming directly for their throats.

"Ah!" Screams echoed in the forest.

Hui Chi went toward the sound, only to see cat beastmen lying on the ground everywhere, and the beastmen who had come to send them off wiping blood from their bodies with animal hides.

The smell of blood was heavy.

Hui Chi hid in the woods, watching Bao Ba take the lead, skillfully digging a pit to dispose of the beastmen's bodies.

He hid in the shadows, counting them one by one, and only after confirming the number was correct did he fly away.

The Black Panther beastman seemed to sense something and glanced in the direction he had flown.

In the large pit half-filled with mud, the cat beastmen lay face up.

"Captain," Bao Dong whispered.

"Continue."

The large pit was gradually filled, and the beastmen took the food they had brought, along with the cat beastmen's luggage, and retreated quickly.

The Black Panther beastman was at the very back.

Once they were far away, he looked back and heard a gust of wind pass by from behind.

His gaze turned cold.

They really checked thoroughly.

A long time later, the moonlight was completely hidden, and everything in the forest was covered by the night.

Beside the filled and packed pit, there was a dull thud, and the surface mud collapsed.

A claw reached out.

The night was pitch black, and the cat beastmen breathed heavily, their pupils reflecting the terrified faces of their companions.

"Le-Leader... he, he wants to kill us!"

"Keep your voice down!" Mao Ci said.

He searched around while stumbling out of the mud.

His body was twitching abnormally, his pupils were still trembling, and the excessive blood loss made his face pale.

No one would believe that the tribe they had followed for so many years would actually do such a thing to them.

But the situation just now made them have to believe it.

"Run, if you don't want to die, keep sitting there like a fool!" Mao Ci covered the wound on his arm, grabbed his animal hide skirt, tore it, and tied it tightly.

He pushed the mud back step by step, with great difficulty.

"Leader..." the beastman was terrified, clutching the bleeding area, both in pain and fear, "Where are we going?"

"East."

chapters.title: 第21章
chapters.translated_text:
Dawn broke, and Lin Qiu looked at the cold, desolate Wolf Mountain, slowly following the orcs as they headed toward the back of the mountain.

Lang Gu had passed away last night.

He had gotten his wish and fallen into an eternal sleep.

Behind Wolf Mountain, one could look out over the northern ranges and the grasslands to the east. The grave on the mountain was small, covered with a pile of stones. They had been carefully selected and placed there one by one by the orcs.

The passing of an orc was something everyone had expected.

Yet, the deep-seated pain suppressed in their hearts surged up once more, leaving them numb, dazed, and desperate. They walked like walking corpses along this familiar path of the funeral procession.

There was no grand ceremony for the orcs' burial; it was simply quiet—a deathly silence.

The orcs had dug a deep pit. They lowered Lang Gu, who had been wrapped tightly in the tribe's best animal skin, gently, fearing to disturb the long sleep he had craved for so long.

Soil covered the old orc, who no longer made a sound.

Just as they had done dozens of times before, they repeated the process. The soil was leveled, and then the orcs brought stones to weigh it down.

The orc was asleep now, and they did this to keep animals from disturbing him, ensuring he could rest in peace.

Lin Qiu watched quietly from the side, feeling that he should be calm at this moment.

But then he felt a softness against his cheek. He looked up to see Lang An stroking his face, smiling at him gently.

Lang An’s eyes were bloodshot and somewhat swollen.

"Don't cry, Qiu. He got what he wanted."

Lin Qiu’s eyelashes trembled. "I'm not crying."

Lang An said nothing more, just watched him quietly.

Few orcs came to the back of Wolf Mountain. Under those stacked stones lay the orcs who had passed away one after another in the fifteen years since they had migrated here.

There were old orcs, cubs, and his own mates and brothers...

They rarely came to disturb them.

Lang Yan stood by the grave, watching as the stones were stacked firmly. His gaze swept over the one at the very top, and he lowered his eyes.

With his father there, the departed orcs would not lose their way.

They had come silently and now departed in silence.

Lang Yan lagged behind, watching Lin Qiu, whom the other orcs had passed, and slowly approached him.

Lin Qiu glanced at him, then continued to press down the wild grass as he walked forward.

He appeared somewhat silent, his eyelashes damp, his fair face devoid of color.

Lin Qiu: "He was Lang Gu."

Lang Yan: "Yes."

Lin Qiu: "I only met him once."

He hadn't even had the chance to thank the old orc who had shown him kindness when he first arrived at the tribe.

Lang Yan: "It was his own choice; I didn't do enough."

Lin Qiu heard the weight and the self-reproach in his words. He took a light breath and slowly let it out. The scent of the morning wind in his nose no longer carried the smell of freedom or relief.

Lin Qiu made up his mind.

"Yam... the 'itchy root,' I’m certain it can be eaten."

Lang Yan was not surprised and responded smoothly, "The prey has been caught, and the itchy roots are being collected. If we test them a few more times in front of everyone, they will accept it. The priest will, too."

Lin Qiu turned his head, and Lang Yan looked at him as well.

Their eyes met, and Lin Qiu did not look away.

He looked into those gray eyes, wanting to say, "You don't doubt me?" but Lang Yan’s expression was calm, as if he had already placed his trust in him.

"Lang Qiu?" Lang Yan said softly.

"Lin Qiu."

Lin Qiu tugged at the corner of his mouth, attempting to show friendliness, but his cheeks were so pale that he looked somewhat transparent and fragile.

"Hmm." Lang Yan watched him for a moment, then looked away.

"Stay in the tribe and try not to go to the river. Both gathering teams have gone out to look for itchy roots; we can test them tomorrow. The priest has agreed, too. You can go learn about the different types of itchy roots from him first."

"Okay."

Lang Yan walked alongside him past the back mountain, then left with the hunting party.

Lin Qiu watched the orcs’ figures quickly disappear into the distance.

He hadn't hidden anything, and Lang Yan had known all along.

Since he had offered this trust, Lin Qiu would not let him down.

...

The departure of the old orc left the remaining members of the tribe in low spirits, but they all performed their duties, continuing with their work.

They all had to live on.

Lin Qiu entered the old priest’s cave; the air inside was filled with the smell of medicinal brews.

The injured orc placed in the priest’s cave had already woken up, but the priest wouldn't let him move, so he had to keep lying down.

Seeing Lin Qiu arrive, the old priest said, "Brew your own medicine."

As he spoke, he handed the medicine in his hand to the lying orc.

The orc pinched his nose, gulped a few times, and drank it clean.

If Lin Qiu hadn't heard a retching sound, he would have thought that medicine tasted better than his own.

Being familiar with the priest’s cave, Lin Qiu moved the clay pot to wash it, then added water to brew his own.

As the water temperature rose, fine bubbles formed in the clay pot.

Lin Qiu sat on the grass mat by the pot, his gaze seemingly fixed on the flames, though he was actually lost in thought.

The orc lay quietly after drinking his medicine.

The old priest sat behind his wooden board, motionless, like a stone statue.

After a long while, the water in the pot boiled.

Lin Qiu looked at a fine crack on the clay pot and said, "Priest, the pot is going to break."

The priest moved his stiff fingers like a rusted machine and turned to look. Even his voice was rusted, hoarse and halting: "Broken... it was bound to break sooner or later."

The tribe had once been prosperous; they had traded for so many clay pots from the Qiushan tribe, but they had all broken during one migration after another.

Just like the orcs of the tribe.

Lin Qiu: "We can make new ones."

The old priest: "It’s not that easy."

Lin Qiu: "It isn't easy, but if we try more often, we might succeed."

The old priest was very tired now; he felt he couldn't catch his breath and didn't even want to respond to Lin Qiu.

This orc usually didn't speak unless necessary, but now he was talking a lot.

"Try it yourself then, no one is stopping you," the priest said impatiently.

"I need orcs."

The old priest: "The itchy root matter isn't even settled, and now you're fussing over clay pots! You’re doing this on purpose to torment the orcs!"

Lin Qiu: "Didn't you tell me to try?"

The old priest was angry and struck his wooden staff toward him.

Lin Qiu dodged to the side and said slowly, "You’re not young anymore; be careful of getting dementia if you keep staying here."

The old priest glared at him. Although he didn't know what dementia was, it certainly wasn't a kind word.

"Don't curse an old orc like me." After saying this, he wiped his face and stood up shakily.

"Take down that animal skin bag from the top of the wooden rack."

Hearing this, Lin Qiu stood up to get it.

The old priest told Lin Qiu to pour it out, and Lin Qiu immediately saw dried yam slices, taro slices, and slices of some Araceae plants.

Besides those, dried leaves and vines were also kept inside.

The old priest said, "Since you brought it up, you need to be able to recognize all the itchy roots."

Lin Qiu: "You can’t just be a hands-off master, old man."

The old priest: "Stop saying things I don't understand."

"Although I’ve been teaching Lang Bing to be the next priest, I see you aren't stupid either. It’s good for the tribe if more orcs know what these plants are."

With that, he decided what Lin Qiu would be doing in the cave for the rest of the morning.

Starting with the itchy roots, under the priest’s guidance, Lin Qiu systematically learned about the plants and animals of the Beast God Continent... Except for things like divination, which Lin Qiu didn't learn, he had to learn everything a future priest should know.

Learning was Lin Qiu’s strength; whether he liked it or not, he couldn't escape it.

Because he was still in his probationary period.

After a busy morning and another bowl of bitter medicine, Lin Qiu descended the mountain, feeling dizzy.

Seeing that Lang Guo had brought the cubs out again, Lin Qiu paused and walked toward them.

The cubs were near the orcs who stayed behind to guard the Wolf tribe, and as Lin Qiu approached, he clearly felt the atmosphere was wrong.

He remained calm and observed silently.

He saw some orcs avoiding him, and the simple smiles they had when fishing had turned into hatred.

Lin Qiu watched from afar, then turned and left the area where the orcs were gathered.

"Awoo!" the cubs called out behind him.

Lang Guo glared at a few orcs in the group who had bad attitudes, then picked up the cubs and chased after Lin Qiu.

"Qiu, where are you going?"

Lin Qiu stopped, and Lang Guo shoved the cubs into his arms.

Lin Qiu held Lang Xue and Lang An’s cub and said, "I’m going to the cave to sleep for a while."

"Aren't you angry?"

Lin Qiu: "I'm fine."

Lang Guo: "They are just... sigh! Their brains are slow, they can't turn the corner."

They blamed Lang Gu’s death on the lack of food, and Lang Qiu had been sent here precisely because he had stolen food.

They didn't know how to vent, so they transferred their hatred.

Lin Qiu: "It's okay, the cubs followed."

He looked past Lang Guo at the cubs behind them; they were like sesame balls scattered on the ground, each pulling at their delicate voices, shouting angrily at Lang Guo.

Why did she only bring those two cubs and not them!

Lang Mo and Lang Shi saw everything clearly from the group of orcs.

Seeing Lin Qiu leave, Lang Mo turned to the few orcs who had shown obvious hostility and said, "What were you doing just now?"

Lang Xi pressed down on Lang Mo’s back, biting his ear to restrain the impulsive orc.

"They are just sad about Lang Gu; they’ll be fine in a few days."

The few black wolves and gray wolves were all members of the tribe’s guard team. The leader was named Lang Mu, and he had a long, healed scar on his left shoulder blade with no fur.

They were all under Lang Shi’s command.

Hearing Lang Xi’s words, they couldn't hold back anymore and said bitterly, "The tribe is already in this state, and he’s still helping other orcs. Why should he be released after being locked up for only a few days?"

"Why should we not pursue this and have to forgive him?"

"Isn't it just catching some fish and weaving a few cages! You’re just going to let it go like that?!"

Lang Mu rushed to the front, and seeing Lang Mo baring his teeth, he wasn't afraid at all.

"You must think that Lang Gu dying is just that—he’s nothing to you! But Qiu was from a branch tribe to begin with. It’s one thing for you to side with him, but why should I? I just don't like him, so what?"

Lang Shi stood up, but before he could get close, Lang Mo was so angry that he lunged at the orc, and they started fighting.

Orcs were naturally combative, and this quickly turned into a brawl.

The other orcs rushed to pull them apart, inevitably getting hurt in the process. Watching the chaos, Lang Shi felt a surge of anger, stepped forward, grabbed two wolves, and pulled them apart.

"Enough! What are you doing!"

"Did I say something wrong? Why should Lang Qiu, who committed such a huge mistake, have been bitten to death long ago, and why was he sent to our tribe to be an eyesore!" Lang Mu spat out the wolf fur in his mouth, his eyes red.

Lang Shi’s face turned livid with anger.

"Do you know what you’re saying?!"

Lang An saw him preparing to strike, pressed him down, and said, "Let them fight. Now that they’ve eaten a little more and have some strength, it’s better if they fight it out."

His voice was gentle, but his gaze was cold.

The Wolf tribe had finally found a glimmer of hope for survival; if the orcs messed it up, they would deserve to die.

Lang Mu and his group thought of the fish they had just eaten, their faces twisted slightly, and they shook off Lang Shi’s hand and crawled to another spot.

Lang Mo shouted with his neck stiff, "I don't know who was gnawing on fish so happily yesterday!"

Lang Xi tugged at Lang Mo’s ear. "Say less."

Lang Mo: "Hmph! I just can't stand it."

Lang Shi slapped Lang Mo’s forehead heavily. "If you’ve got nothing better to do, go get more vines. What are you arguing about?"

Lang Shi was about to hit back, but Lang Xi bit his scruff and pulled him to the side.
chapters.source_text:
天明了，林楸看着冷寂的狼山，慢慢跟着兽人们往山后走。
狼古昨晚没了。
他如愿地永远睡着了。
狼山后头，能远眺北边群山，跟东侧的草原。那山上的坟茔小小一个，上面重叠着许多石头。都是兽人们精挑细选，一个个放下的。
兽人逝去，大家意料之中。
可强压在心底的阵痛再次袭上来，整个人木然，呆滞，绝望。他们如行尸走肉，走在这条熟悉的送葬的路上。
兽人们的埋葬没有多么盛大的仪式，只是安静，静得死寂。
兽人挖了坑，很深。将用部落最好的兽皮裹得严严实实的狼古放了下去，轻轻的，怕惊扰了他奢求已久的长眠。
泥土覆盖，压在再无声息的老兽人身上。
像以往重复几十次那样，继续重复着。土壤填平，再由兽人们搬来石块儿压住。
兽人已经睡着了，怕有动物再惊扰他，这样能让他安稳。
林楸静静地在一旁看着，他觉得自己此刻应该是冷静的。
但颊边一软，抬眼，狼安抚摸过他侧脸，温柔地对着他笑。
他眼中通红，已经有些肿。
“不哭，楸。他得到了他的所求。”
林楸颤睫，“我没哭。”
狼安不再说话，只静静瞧着。
狼山山后少有兽人过来，那些叠高的石块儿下，是搬迁过来十五年后陆陆续续逝去的兽人。
有老兽人，有幼崽，也有他的伴侣、兄弟……
他们很少过来打扰。
狼岩站在坟茔旁边，看着石块儿垒得严实了，目光往最顶上的那一座一扫，敛了目光。
他阿父在，逝去的兽人们不会迷路。
他们悄无声息来，又静静离开。
狼岩落在后头，看着被兽人们越过的林楸，缓慢靠近。
林楸看了他一眼，继续压住荒草，往前走。
他显得有些沉默，睫毛湿着，白皙的脸上没有血色。
林楸：“他是狼古。”
狼岩：“嗯。”
林楸：“我只见过一面。”
他还没来得及谢谢这个当他刚来部落时，对他释放出善意的老兽人。
狼岩：“他自己的选择，是我没做好。”
林楸听出他话里的沉重与安慰，轻轻吸了一口气，又慢慢吐出来。鼻腔里的晨风里的味道，早已经不是自由与释然的味道。
林楸下了决心。
“山药……就是长痒痒根，我能确定，能吃。”
狼岩并未诧异，流畅地接下他的话，“猎物抓回来了，痒痒根也在收集，当着大家的面多试几次，他们会接受的。祭司也会。”
林楸侧头，狼岩也看来。
目光一触，林楸并未移开。
他看着那双灰色的眸子，想说“你不怀疑”，可狼岩神色平静，似早已经交托了信任。
“狼楸？”狼岩轻声说。
“林楸。”
林楸扯了扯嘴角，试图表示友好。但脸颊太白，显得有些透明和脆弱。
“嗯。”狼岩看了他一会儿，移开目光。
“好好呆在部落，尽量别去河边。两个采集队都出去找痒痒根了，明天就可以试。祭司也同意了，你可以先跟他了解一下各类痒痒根。”
“好。”
狼岩一直与他并排走过后山，随后带着捕猎队的兽人们出发。
林楸看着兽人很快消失在远处的身影。
他没隐瞒，狼岩也早已经知晓。
他交出这一份信任，林楸便不会辜负。
……
老兽人的离开让留在部落的兽人们情绪低落，但也都各司其职，继续手中的活儿。
他们都要好好活着。
林楸进了老祭司山洞，洞内弥漫着药水的味道。
那个安置在祭司山洞里受伤的兽人已经醒了，只不过祭司不让他挪动，他便只能一直躺着。
见林楸来，老祭司道：“自己的药，自己熬。”
说着，将手上的药递给躺着的兽人。
兽人一捏鼻子，咕噜几下，喝了个干干净净。
如果林楸没听到一声呕吐，还当那药比自己的好点儿。
来祭司的山洞已经熟门熟路，林楸将陶锅搬去清洗干净，随后再加水熬自己的。
水温升高，陶锅里鼓出细密的泡泡。
林楸坐在锅边的草团上，目光似专注地看着火苗，实则发了会儿呆。
兽人喝完药，安静躺着。
老祭司坐在他那木板后头的位置上，一动不动，也如石人一般。
许久，锅里水沸腾。
林楸看着陶锅上的一道细缝，道：“祭司，锅要坏了。”
祭司动了动僵硬的手指，像生锈的机器，转头看来。连声音也生锈了，嘶哑卡顿：“坏了，早该坏了。”
部落富裕过，曾今从丘山部落换来那么多陶锅，也在一次又一次的迁徙中坏掉。
就像部落的兽人一样。
林楸：“可以做新的。”
老祭司：“哪有那么容易。”
林楸：“是不容易，但多试试没准就成了。”
老祭司现在很累，只感觉一口气喘不上来，连林楸的话都不想回。
这兽人平时能不说就不说，现在话倒多了。
“你自个儿试去，又没谁拦着你。”祭司不耐烦。
“我要兽人。”
老祭司：“痒痒根的事情还没弄好，又折腾陶锅，你存心折腾兽人！”
林楸：“不是你叫我试？”
老祭司气，抓着木杖往他那边敲。
林楸往旁边一躲，慢吞吞道：“年纪不小了，再呆下去小心老年痴呆。”
老祭司瞪人，虽然不知道什么是老年痴呆，但是准不是什么好话。
“别诅咒我一个老兽人。”说完，抹了把脸，颤颤巍巍起来。
“木架子最上面的那个兽皮袋拿下来。”
林楸闻言，起身去拿。
老祭司让林楸倒出来，林楸一眼看到了晒干的山药片，还有芋头片，已经一些天南星科植物的切片。
除此之外，还有晒干的叶片及藤蔓也保存在其中。
老祭司道：“既然是你提出来的，痒痒根你得认全了。”
林楸：“您老也不能当甩手掌柜。”
老祭司：“别说那些我听不懂的。”
“狼冰虽然被我当做下一任祭司教导，但我看你也不笨，多些兽人知道这些草是什么对部落好。”
说着，就决定了林楸之后在山洞的一上午该干什么。
林楸从痒痒根开始，在祭司的教导下，系统地了解兽神大陆的植物、动物……除了占卜之类的林楸没学，下一任祭司该学的，林楸都得学。
学习是林楸的长处，不管他乐不乐意，反正逃不掉。
因为他还在考核期。
忙了一上午，又灌了一碗苦药，林楸昏昏沉沉下了山。
瞧见狼果又把幼崽带出来了，林楸脚下一顿，冲着幼崽靠近。
幼崽挨着留守狼部落的兽人们近，林楸过去，明显感到了气氛不对。
他不动声色，默默观察。
见有些兽人避开他，捞鱼时那朴素的笑意成了憎恨。
林楸远远看着，脚步一转，离开了这处兽人聚集的地方。
“嗷呜！”幼崽在后面喊。
狼果瞪了一眼兽人堆里的几个态度不好的，抱着幼崽追上林楸。
“楸，你去哪儿？”
林楸停下，狼果将幼崽往他怀里一塞。
林楸抱着狼雪跟狼安的幼崽，道：“我去山洞睡会儿。”
“你不生气？”
林楸：“还好。”
狼果：“他们就是……哎！脑子笨，转不过弯来。”
他们把狼古的死归咎于缺乏食物，而狼楸当初就是因为偷食物才被送来。
他们不知道怎么发泄，转移了仇恨。
林楸：“没事，幼崽跟来了。”
他越过狼果看向偷身后，幼崽像散落地面的芝麻球，一个个扯着稚嫩的嗓音，万分生气地对着狼果叫。
为什么只带那两个幼崽，不带他们！
狼莫跟狼石在兽人堆里看得清清楚楚。
见林楸走了，一转头，狼莫对着刚刚几个态度明显不对的兽人道：“你们刚刚干什么？”
狼西压在狼莫背上，叼着他耳朵将冲动的兽人压制住。
“他们就是伤心狼古，过几天就好了。”
几个黑狼、灰狼同是部落护卫队的，为首的叫狼木，左侧肩胛处一刀极长的已经愈合的疤痕，没有毛。
他们都受狼石管。
这会儿听了狼西的话，再憋不住，恨恨道：“部落都已经这样了，他还帮着别的兽人，凭什么他就关了几天就能放出来了。”
“凭什么我们就要不追究，还要原谅他。”
“不就是抓到点鱼，编几个笼子！你们就这样算了？！”
狼木冲到前面来，见狼莫龇牙，半点不怕。
“你肯定觉得狼古死了就死了，他又跟你没关系！可楸本来就是支部落的，你向着也就算了，凭什么要我也向着。我就是看不惯他，怎么着？”
狼石起身，还没来得及靠近，狼莫气得直接扑上去跟兽人打做一团。
兽人本就好斗，这一下成了混战。
兽人们赶紧上来拉，免不了被误伤几下。狼石看着闹成这样，一股气冲上头，上前逮住两只狼就扯开。
“行了！你们在干什么！”
“我说错了吗？凭什么他狼楸做了那么大的错事，早该被一口咬死，为什么还要送到我们部落来碍眼！”狼木吐出嘴里的狼毛，红着眼道。
狼石气得脸铁青。
“你知道你在说什么吗？！”
狼安看他蓄力，一把按住，道：“让他们打，现在稍微多吃一点，有力气了，打死才好。”
他声音温柔，目光却冷。
狼部落好不容易能看到点活下去的希望，要是叫兽人搅和了，那才该死。
狼木一伙想到自己才吃过的鱼，脸上扭曲几分，抖开狼石的手，往另一处趴着。
狼莫哼梗着脖子嚷嚷：“也不知道谁昨天啃鱼啃得那么香！”
狼西揪了把狼莫的耳朵，“你少说两句。”
狼莫：“哼！我就看不惯。”
狼石一巴掌沉甸甸地拍在狼石的脑门上，“闲着没事多弄点藤条回来，吵吵什么。”
狼石要打回去，叫狼西叼住他后颈，往旁边拉。

清晨，雾气笼罩山林时，兔葵就已经和种植队的兽人们吃过尾巴草籽熬的青菜瘦肉粥，拎上藤筐农具，下地干活。
今年狼影带着赤山部落的兽人回来以后，部落一下又多了百来号兽人。
狼岩给各个小队分了些。
猎物有限，狩猎队的兽人没怎么变化，采集队多了一个队伍。
大泽那边分了一半兽人过去种地、养鱼和建房子，剩下那一半，大部分匀到种植队来了。
地里这时候正忙，兽人们早出晚归，只要不是下大雨，几乎每天不歇。
就这么从化雪后一直忙到现在，也才刚刚把大河两岸的地翻耕完，播种了不到一半的尾巴草种子。
地里的活儿兽人们已经做熟练了，兔葵守着，出不了岔子。
林楸腾出手来，在广场上和狼果一起守着幼崽。
部落发展得快，兽人们吃饱穿暖，这两年迎来了第一个幼崽数量爆发期。
部落如今幼崽总共有七十六个，五岁以上幼崽，也就是狼生那一批崽子，算上兔芫和豹枝，一共十八个；两岁以上的幼崽九个。
余下的四十九个，都是这两年出生的，狼兽人幼崽、兔兽人幼崽以及黑羽兽人幼崽都有。
狼果一个兽人根本守不过来。
为了看好这群幼崽，狼影把狼菇分了过来，羽山也让羽江过来帮忙看着。
这会儿，幼崽被带出来在广场上晒太阳。
广场上铺平了一层草席，又堆放了几个尾巴草秆编织的大草窝。
幼崽不安分，争先恐后地从兽人小腿高的草窝里翻出来，落在草席上。
软软弹弹的，一点事儿没有。
爪子沾了地面，就兴奋地在广场上到处乱爬。
阳光洒在幼崽身上，他们绒毛成了一道虚影。幼崽那大爪垫梆梆压在地面，虎虎生风地扑腾着往前。
狼菇忙来忙去，跑一个捡一个，这边刚放回草窝，那边草窝里又爬出来几个。
他全程笑盈盈的，脚步轻快，也不见累。
狼果、林楸和羽江坐在边上，看着他忙活。
狼果：“还是年轻好，有劲儿。”
林楸：“说得你多大似的。”
狼果肩膀往他肩膀一撞，“我都当阿爸了，你觉得我还小？”
两年前连带狼果幼崽一起，那九个幼崽早能离开山洞到处跑了。
狼生他们天天带着这九个小的玩儿，这会儿也不知道跑哪个草垛里躲着去了。
小崽子能变人形，说明身体健康，只要不出意外，后面能好好长大。
兽人也不用时时刻刻把他们放在眼皮子底下，只需要时不时看上一眼，确认他们安全就行。
最麻烦的还是眼前这一批幼崽。
他们虽然小，但数量多，各个精力十足。
闹起来时，他们几个加在一起都忙不过来。
“嗷！”
广场上，忽然响起极响亮的一声幼崽嚎叫。
林楸几个慌忙看去，就见狼菇掐着那个带头往外爬的幼崽的咯吱窝，将他往广场中心带。
幼崽不乐意，身体绷直，坦露出圆鼓鼓的小肚皮，仰头冲着狼菇大声地叫。
他一叫，其他幼崽停下，也跟着叫。
“嗷！”
“嗷嗷嗷！”
狼崽子这么叫也就算了，兔兽人幼崽和黑羽兽人幼崽也被带得从小这么叫唤。
一时间，广场上白的、红的、灰的小毛团嚷个不停，林楸感觉此刻宛如置身在夏日里的水田里，处处是蛙叫，聒噪得很。
林楸揉了揉耳朵。
“狼影不喜欢说话，狼火话也不多，他俩的幼崽怎么这么暴躁？”
这一堆幼崽里，就属狼影幼崽主意最大，最执着，嗓门最大。
狼菇听了还笑。
他把幼崽放在臂弯，拍了拍他屁股道：“他不乐意嘛，还不会说话，只能这么叫了。”
“嗷！”幼崽一口咬在他胳膊上。
可惜牙没长好，咬着也不疼。
林楸：“性子倒是一样。”
都记仇，听不得坏话。
天空一暗，吱哇乱叫的幼崽们被满空的黑羽兽人惊住，总算停了下来。
他们蹲坐下来，脑袋仰得高高的，看着黑羽兽人看得一动不动，像缩小版的石狮子。
羽山一扇翅膀，风吹得幼崽身上的毛毛摇晃。
“嗷！”幼崽激动。
羽山一笑，几乎飞到广场另一头才把抓着的兽皮袋放下。
他慈爱地看着这一群幼崽，尤其是其中几个秃毛黑羽兽人幼崽。
看够了，才道：“楸！岩说安排兽人煮盐。”
林楸纳闷：“不是王他们拉车去挖盐了，怎么是你们带回来的？”
“西边来了个新部落，狼岩在那边盯着。”
“又来一个？”
“嗷！”
林楸听到幼崽叫，看了看脚边，捡起地上的毛球往广场上扔。
幼崽立马追过去，四条腿跑得乱七八糟的，仿佛各有各的路。
羽山道：“看着还是个中等部落，不过是个食草兽人部落，应该没什么问题。”
林楸：“好，你们先忙，煮盐的事我会安排。”
羽山颔首，刚走几步就被幼崽围住。
幼崽抱住他的腿，期待地看着天空。
狼果捞起身边放着的长杆，挡在幼崽身前。
幼崽爪子抵着长杆，巴巴地望着。
狼果无情道：“想也别想。”
羽山看了看已经爬到自己腰上的小狼崽，笑呵呵的。他粗糙的手顺了顺幼崽的毛，下一瞬，拎着幼崽后颈放了下来。
幼崽太小，就算被狼兽人养得胖墩墩的，那也不能随便跟他们上天。
“楸，我们继续巡逻去了。”羽山说完赶紧走，就怕被幼崽缠上，待会儿跑不掉。
林楸应了声，也起身，打算先安排煮盐的事。
旁边食堂窗口，狼安探头出来，道：“楸，食堂的灶不够，得重新搭灶。”
“好。”
部落现在大半的灶都用上了。
两三个亚兽人负责一口锅，一般保证一餐能让兽人们有三种以上选择。
最小的幼崽也单开一口锅做食物。
做饭的兽人还是那么多，只每一餐用的食材种类多了些，消耗的食物量没怎么变。
也是选择多了，兽人们挑着自己喜欢的食物大吃特吃，这两年幼崽身体健康，小狼身高猛蹿，连一直忙个不停的成年兽人们身体也一个赛一个结实。
加上训练，如今成年狼兽人身体已经算恢复到巅峰时期。
部落煮的盐多，这事儿又费时，单用食堂那几口锅不知道要煮到什么时候去。
垒灶对兽人们来说就是个简单活儿。
煮盐能快就快。
垒灶得找建筑队的兽人。
部落里房子建得差不多了，广场除了靠大河那一边，东、西和北边都建了房子。
地方不够，兽人又绕着狼山继续往北建。
现在从狼山前到狼山后，有一条平整宽阔的路连接，路两边都整齐排布着红砖平房。
房子建得差不多了，兽人们够住，建筑队目前就主要忙着建城墙和炼铁的事。
狼莫他们从赤山部落回来后又带了不少矿石。
他除了去建墙那边，就是在西边建炼铁炉。
林楸去西边喊兽人。
为了隐蔽，狼莫打算把这炼铁炉建在西边山里。
兽人们进出都小心翼翼，生怕哪天被那些偷偷进入原野部落的兽人看见。
林楸沿着宽阔的路往北走，路过狼山，往山上看一眼。
这两年，山上也有变化。
兽人们在山顶建了个哨塔，狼石安排了兽人日夜轮守。时时刻刻，部落都有一双眼睛看着狼山四周。
林楸与哨塔上的兽人目光对上，兽人颔首，林楸笑了笑，继续往前。
狼山的路都修得笔直。
路面被压实了，很平整，兽人闭着眼睛走在上面都不怕摔。
路两旁房屋高低一致，兽人们都住进去了。这会儿各家大门紧闭，兽人们都出去干活了。
狼山安稳，兽人们也越来越会过日子。
各家小屋前用破烂的陶罐装了土，种着漂亮的野花野草。
也有爱吃果子的，专门问了兔葵要培育出来的果树苗，种在自己院子里。
林楸看着这欣欣向荣的景象，慢慢呼出一口气。
狼山这些改变，不白费这两年来大家累死累活地搞发展，搞建设。
走过狼山，林楸便见黑山洞里走出一个兽人。
“莫，忙吗？”
狼莫灰头土脸的，眼睛却亮，他道：“有好吃的？”
林楸：“有活儿。”
狼莫拍了拍身上的灰，叹一声，道：“要的兽人多吗？”
“搭几个灶，煮盐。”
“等着。”
说完，狼莫又钻进黑山洞。
林楸跟了上去。
黑山洞被他们挖通了，里面七拐八绕的，像兔兽人在地底的巢穴。
林楸跟着狼莫走，拐了好一会儿，才找到一条路，继续前行。
林楸看着前面狼莫的背影，道：“挖这个山洞的意义是什么？”
“藏路啊。”
“你们那炉子一建，到时候烧起来，那黑烟你藏得住吗？”
狼莫一下停住。
林楸早有预料，先一步停下脚。
“所以你没想过这个问题？”
“……到时候我们用兽皮把炉子堵上。”
林楸笑出了声。
跟兽人们相处其实很轻松。
几乎没有勾心斗角的事，有什么就说什么，兽人们自己还经常做些令人发笑的事。
林楸都觉得这几年笑的次数比他上辈子加起来还多。
狼莫哀嚎，声音在弯弯绕绕的山洞中回荡——
“那不是白让兔艾他们挖这么久了！”
林楸示意他继续走，一边安慰道：“仔细想想，也有好处，至少可以遮掩你们出入那边的痕迹。以后部落要是有个什么事，这个山洞也可以当兽人们转移的地方。”
狼莫是被兽人夸两句就能飘天上去的，当即尾巴翘起来，道：
“我就说我这个决定很不错！”
狼岩把炼铁的事全权交给了狼莫。
现在狼莫带着小队的成员直接脱离了护卫队，专注做铁器相关的事，包括但不限于修补铁器，研究钢铁，寻找铁矿。
狼莫脑子有时候不太聪明，但正事上没出过岔子，还算靠谱。
*
走了好一会儿，林楸才见到光亮。
从另一个洞口出去，面前就豁然开朗。
这里是一处山谷，群山包围，可惜兽神大陆有羽族的存在，不然这个位置确实很难让兽人发现。
狼莫从赤山部落带回来的兽人小队已经是搭炉子的熟手，只获取材料跟加工材料麻烦一些，他们回来也一个月了，这会儿才开始建炼铁炉。
大家在各忙各的，分外认真。
这边的兽人主要是狼莫小队原来那七个狼兽人和狼影分来帮忙的二十个兽人。
这二十多个兽人是炼铁的核心。
另外帮忙打下手的一堆兽人，则都是从建墙那边轮流过来学习的兽人。
狼莫手一挥，万分豪气道：“楸，要几个？”
近处的狼西抓起一团泥冲他甩去。
林楸笑：“六个差不多。”
狼莫吆喝：“来十个兽人！垒灶台。”
话落，就近的狼西拍拍手，带起一阵灰尘，慢慢走了过来。
随后，队伍里又主动走出来九个兽人。
行吧，多四个不多。
林楸：“走吧，赶紧弄完你们做自己的。”
*
广场上，放风完的幼崽被带回屋内。
部落建了个大房子专门给狼果带崽子，房子里头带一个大火炕，雪季的时候，空地上会铺上兽皮，让幼崽们待在屋里玩儿。
天气热了，兽皮就换成了草席。
屋内还放了不少林楸让狼起做的玩具，还有兽人们揣着一片慈心为幼崽做的狼毛球。
出了黑山洞，狼西边走边问：“楸，用铁锅还是用陶锅？”
“铁锅。”
兽人们点头，立马开始干活。
日头渐高，几只飞鸟越过狼山，落在了地里，啄食刚撒进地里的尾巴草种子。
兽人摆动双手，大声吆喝。
飞鸟往兽人这边看上一眼，细长的鸟头往后一撇，像是轻蔑，又继续吃。
“嘿！年年来，年年喊，现在还喊不动了！”
羽猎振翅，直直冲着鸟抓去。
“嘎！！！”
一时间，鸟儿慌张散去。
羽猎凌空越过林楸他们头顶，还有闲心问：“楸，吃鸟肉吗？”
林楸仰头，只看见漫天飞舞的鸟毛。
“吃！”狼莫大喊。
林楸脚步一顿，扭头，“你什么时候跟来的？”
“一直在啊。”狼莫嘿嘿笑。
*
羽山又带着黑羽兽人们往两个部落领地间巡逻去了。
林楸看了眼西边，没见到狼岩回来的身影，又往屋里去。
“安，有没有空闲的亚兽人，让他们明天煮盐。”
“好，我安排。”
隔着窗口，狼安又往外看了一眼。
那些盐用兽皮袋装着堆在外面，大兽皮袋和藤筐一共装了有三十几个。一个板车能装个五六袋，这点差不多五个板车的量。
“这点够吗？”狼安道。
“自己吃肯定够。”
“周边几个部落差不多又要来换盐了，部落剩的没多少，盐能放，要不今年多煮一点？”
林楸想想也是，便道：“王回来我跟他说。”
狼安拿着大铁勺，倚在窗边却没急着走。
他刚刚也听到了羽山的话，叹道：“这两年也不知道那边出什么事，都好几个部落从中央大陆过来了。”
林楸点头，心里也有些压力。
“是，听影说，都是无力再给原野部落供奉的部落，还有部落是从原野部落脱离出来的……”
原野部落越难，只会越盯紧了他们。
“那原野部落也没食物了？”
“多半吧。”
“该！叫他们什么都不做，就等着兽人们白送食物。”
“他们那样，还不知道要生什么事。”
狼安心中一凛，道：“咱这边部落都多了好几个，还是要多注意一点。”
林楸：“狼石他们都盯着的，放哨的兽人日夜守着，羽山和狼影他们都在巡逻，应该出不来岔子。”
狼安望了望窗外，幼崽不在广场了。
狼山上那哨塔上南边北边各站着一个兽人。
狼部落是用大量兽人警戒，才让部落这两年没出什么事。
狼安：“就是不知道什么时候是个头……”
是啊，也不知道什么时候是个头。
林楸往河边走，一边走一边想这事儿。
这两年，狼部落北边、西南边、东南边、东边多了些小部落。他们和黑羽部落、白雀部落一起，直接将狼部落包围在中央。
那些兽人部落离他们很近。
但又不在狼部落领地，他们管不了。
中央大陆过来的兽人越多，说明那边越不安定。
照着这两年来原野部落派兽人侵扰他们部落的情况来看，那边情况肯定不乐观。
那边越不乐观，他们这边越不敢掉以轻心。
还有周边这些个新来的兽人部落……林楸其实也奇怪，这些兽人分明怕他们，却使劲儿往这边扎堆。
王还专门让亲和力比较强的兔兽人去问过，结果都是从中央大陆来的。
再问，便是想要和兔部落一样，要加入狼部落。
“我们部落的好名声从东部大陆传到中央大陆了？”狼莫听到又一个新部落过来，如此问道。
林楸一边帮忙挖河泥，一边道：“咱们以前在中央大陆名声不好？”
“好啊，但不至于兽人都往我们附近涌啊。”
“那兴许有兽人帮我们宣传。”
“谁？”
“豹休也说不定呢。”
狼莫嗤笑一声，“那小崽子都两三年没消息了，怕是早把我们忘了，亏得我们还养了他两年，养出个白眼豹。”
林楸玩笑的心思歇下。
豹休当初走，是摆明了不找到他们祭司不罢休，就算没命，他想必也要找。
狼莫一铲子将泥扔筐里，又哼哼道：“……也不知道他现在是好是坏，找到他们祭司了没有。”
林楸弯眼。
嘴硬心软。
旁边狼西道：“放心吧，他掉河里、被嗡嗡虫咬都能活，命大着呢。”
林楸喃喃：“是啊，他命大着呢……”
说着闲话，兽人们找了广场南边一块空地，用板车拉了一车砖来，又从河岸抠了些湿泥，开始垒灶。
狼兽人做什么都喜欢按多了做。
吃到好吃的，也得连续几天顿顿吃，吃够了才歇。
部落大铁锅量足，足足二十多口。
除此之外，还有不少样式不同、兽人们自创的圆的扁的大的小的铁锅，不过放在山洞里，一直没用就是了。
林楸帮忙把铁锅搬出来，路过广场，就得往西边看一下。
狼莫啪的一下把一桶泥砸在地上，跟着他踮脚往西边眺望。
林楸冷眼看来。
他嘿嘿笑说：“你要担心王，让羽涯他们带你去呗，正好他们刚回来取草药种子，这会儿还没走。”
如今狼冰的草药也扩大了种植范围。
他不像以前那样只随意几株往林子里种，而是专门划分了位置，找到合适药物生长的地方，批量种植。
西边那些山脉，就是种草药的好去处。
羽涯他们反正要过去，飞的比跑的更快些。
林楸：“我倒是不担心王，我担心那个中等部落。”
过了中午，兽人们建好的灶被太阳晒干，锅放上去，嵌得刚刚好。
狼莫拍拍手，叉腰道：“成了！煮盐要我们帮忙不？”
林楸：“不用，你做你自己……”
“楸！”
林楸猛地抬头，就看南边掠来一道黑影。
“祭司在不在？！”
羽千神色慌张，速度奇快，灰黑色的翅膀的羽毛上往下滴着水。
林楸闻着味儿不对，一瞧，哪里是什么水，分明是血！
林楸呼吸一滞，细看，才见羽千背后驮着一个兽人。
他忙道：“祭司往北边看墙去了，你先把他放屋里。”
“猎！”林楸冲着东边喊了一声。
“诶！”
“快去北边把祭司带回来，有兽人受伤。”
林楸话没说完，一阵风从天空掠过，几下不见了羽猎的身影。
林楸跟着羽千进小屋。
他帮着把兽人从羽千背上扶下来，一看，发现兽人是好久不见的雀溪。
羽千小心翼翼蹲在炕边，声音发哑，道：“他跟狼潭他们采集的时候摔了，脑袋正好撞在石头上，一直冒血。我们用布给他按着，现在看着血流得慢了一点。”
林楸瞧着兽人发白的唇，是失血过多。
“好，我知道了。你先去休息一会儿，收拾一下，我在这里看着。”
羽千点头，瞧着自己一身的血，赶紧去了澡堂。
血腥味有些浓，部落其他兽人闻到，匆匆赶了过来，堵住了门口。
林楸一边准备止血的草药，一边赶兽人。
“别堵着，自己做自己的事去。”
兽人们瞧了眼炕上，见躺着的是之前他们从流浪部落手中救下的雀溪，问了情况，就离开了。
“楸！”
林楸在准备缝伤口的工具，外面羽猎一喊，他险些被自己扎上一针。
林楸头也不抬，问：“祭司呢？”
“哎……我叫你慢点！”老祭司搀扶着自己老腰，吹胡子瞪眼的。
他嘴上说着，脚下不慢，杵着拐杖就往屋里走。
老祭司一眼看到兽人被麻布裹得严严实实的脑袋，道：“打架了？”
“没有，自己摔的。”
林楸抓了凳子放在老祭司身后让他坐，又把工具、草药都给他准备齐全了，一一摆放在祭司手边。
祭司把拐杖往林楸手里一塞，没好气道：“你又不是不会！”
林楸：“他这个伤在后脑。”
老祭司一顿，也不跟林楸吵嘴了。
他用林楸递过来的湿帕子擦了手，看着林楸把兽人脑袋上的麻布慢慢揭开。
瞧着那后脑一个血糊糊的洞，整张老脸都皱紧了。
“把他头发剪了。”
林楸照做，全程小心翼翼。
祭司接着立马清理伤口，上药，包扎。
“楸，抓药。红鱼草半把、乌丝藤三片……”
林楸听着祭司口述草药，拎上个筐子去那靠墙的一排药柜里抓药。
药柜是狼起按照林楸的图纸打的，药材归类方便，抓药也方便。
祭司一连说了几个，林楸头一个拉开装红鱼草的药柜，手便顿住。
“祭司，红鱼草没了。”
“红鱼草去上面山洞找，抓其他的。”
林楸一连开了四五个药柜，里面的草药大多都见底了。
“祭司，咱们部落草药又用完了？”
老祭司没好气道：“早就用得差不多了。”
“我去山洞看看。”
祭司放草药的地方，除了这个屋子，就是以前他住的那个山洞。
老祭司很少上山洞去了。
一般都是狼冰上去拿药、收拾。
林楸进去，里面没什么霉味儿。狼冰有点洁癖，把里面收拾得干干净净。
他环顾一圈，山洞里处处堆放着装草药的兽皮袋、陶罐……老祭司的山洞已经变成储存草药的地方了。
看这草药的量，后头两三年应该不用愁。
可等他按照药材的归类把祭司说的药材找了一圈，最后只拎起半个兽皮袋的红鱼草，旁的要么剩一点药渣，要么连个影儿都没见到。
林楸心提起来，默念了几声那几种草药的名字，才想起来这其中的几味药都不是东部大陆产的。
林楸又立马去看了看他们之前从东部大陆南边交换回来的草药。
一瞧，兽皮袋里满满当当。
药味很浓，是一个月前狼影他们从赤山部落带回来的，连带着还有不少红糖。
他们肯定是去了一趟南边。
可这些都不是祭司要的。
林楸匆忙下山，进了屋，老祭司看了一眼他的脸色，道：“没了？”
林楸摇摇头。
“我早就说过，部落没草药了。集市不开，其他大陆的草药又交换不来……”
空了的那些还不算最紧要的，有些救命的草药，老祭司直接藏起来了，一点都不敢动。
“好在这两年你们用不着，不然我还不知道上哪里找去。”
林楸：“这样不行。”
“我还知道不行！能怎么办？”
“东部大陆南边我们都去了，其他大陆又不是不能去。”
老祭司抄起拐杖就想给林楸一下。
“别想！”
东部大陆南边兽人们过去就走了好几个月，要是去其他大陆，少不得半年。
这跟他们从中央大陆迁徙到东部大陆有什么区别？
林楸拿着空荡荡的篮子，“可兽人要用啊。”
“呸！用什么用！净乱说话！”
林楸无奈，“这个先不说，雀溪还躺着，祭司换个方子。”
老祭司想到那点家底，气得吹胡子。
换换换！
药效大打折扣，喝了作用微乎其微。
“祭司……”
“换换换！烦死了。”
*
忙完，林楸身上也沾了血。
他出去匆匆换了一身衣服回来，刚进屋，就看到兽人半阖着眼睛看着门口。
这么快就醒了？
老祭司坐在一旁，身边蹲着狼雪，正借着现成的案例教导幼崽怎么治伤。
林楸进去，兽人眼睛随着他转动。
“他醒了？”
“你走了就这样，就这么半睁眼看着兽人，一直没动过。”祭司道。
“脑子没大问题吧？”
“你自己看。”
“我要是能看得出来，还用叫祭司？”
老祭司抓着拐杖佯装打来，林楸躲开，笑了一下。
老祭司没好气道：“死不了！”
狼雪等祭司凶完，欢欣扑过来，抱着林楸的腰。
林楸一笑，摸了摸幼崽已经到他腰高的小脑袋。
“不是在外面跟狼生他们玩儿？”
“猎叔说有病人，我就回来了。”
林楸找地方坐下。
狼雪挪了挪凳子，与他并排。
他对林楸道：“祭司说，他要好好养一养才能把流的那么多的血补回来。”
“放心，不会苛待他的。”
狼雪笑得欢欣，一转头，面对着祭司，又立马绷着雪白的小脸认真起来。
一老一小继续上课。
老祭司声音又慢又轻，很催人入眠。
林楸打了个哈欠，干脆起身，走到兽人身边。
兽人眼珠跟着转动。
林楸帮他理着身上盖着的兽皮毯，轻声问：“还记得自己是谁吗？”
雀溪注视着他。
许久，眼角缓缓落下一道湿痕。
“谢……谢。”
林楸的手一顿，眼中闪过诧异，不过几息，又如常地将他肩膀盖好。
他声音轻缓道：“不用谢。”
*
雀溪不傻了。
这件事如风暴一般，立马席卷整个狼部落。
晚间，兽人们坐在食堂里吭哧吭哧刨食时，还抽出空说：“他怎么撞了个脑袋就清醒了？楸以前也这样。咱们是不是撞一下脑袋，也会见到兽神？”
“幸运的话，会。不幸的话，你会傻。”狼安没好气道。
老祭司：“去撞吧，我反正没那么多草药来救。”
“万一我也能变得跟楸一样知道很多事呢？部落多一个能沟通兽神的兽人，不是好事？”
“呵。”
直接没兽人理他了。
林楸听到祭司的话，才是真的明白那不是玩笑。
部落真缺少草药了。
狼云：“……呵！”
谁不会呵啊！
“呵、呵！！！”
同桌的兽人们龇牙嫌弃，纷纷端着碗往旁边挪了挪。
狼禾也默默转到后桌，当做不认识狼云。
有时傻过头了也不好。
丢脸。
chapters.title: 第210章
chapters.translated_text:
Early in the morning, while mist still shrouded the mountains and forests, Tu Kui had already finished a meal of vegetable and lean meat porridge made from tail-grass seeds with the beastmen of the planting team, then picked up his rattan baskets and farm tools to head out to the fields.

This year, after Lang Ying returned with the beastmen from the Chishan Tribe, the tribe suddenly grew by over a hundred members.

Lang Yan had distributed them among the various squads.

Prey was limited, so the hunting team hadn't changed much, but an extra team was added to the gathering squad.

Half of the beastmen from Daze were sent over to farm, raise fish, and build houses, and most of the remaining half were allocated to the planting team.

The fields were busy at this time; the beastmen left early and returned late, working almost every day unless there was a heavy downpour.

Having been busy like this since the snow melted, they had only just finished tilling the fields on both sides of the big river and had sown less than half of the tail-grass seeds.

The beastmen were already skilled at the field work, and with Tu Kui watching over them, nothing could go wrong.

Lin Qiu was freed up to watch over the cubs in the plaza along with Lang Guo.

The tribe was developing rapidly, and with the beastmen well-fed and clothed, these past two years had seen the first population boom of cubs.

The tribe now had a total of seventy-six cubs. Those over five years old—the batch including Lang Sheng, Tu Yuan, and Bao Zhi—totaled eighteen; there were nine cubs over two years old.

The remaining forty-nine were all born in the last two years, including wolf-beastman cubs, rabbit-beastman cubs, and black-feathered beastman cubs.

Lang Guo couldn't possibly watch them all by himself.

To keep an eye on this group of cubs, Lang Ying had assigned Lang Gu to help, and Yu Shan had also sent Yu Jiang over to assist.

At this moment, the cubs were being brought out to the plaza to bask in the sun.

A layer of straw mats had been spread flat on the plaza, and several large grass nests woven from tail-grass stalks were piled up.

The cubs were restless, scrambling to climb out of the nests—which were as high as a beastman's calf—and tumbling onto the straw mats.

They were soft and bouncy, and none of them were hurt.

Once their paws touched the ground, they excitedly crawled all over the plaza.

Sunlight spilled onto the cubs, turning their downy fur into a blur. Their large paw pads pressed firmly against the ground as they pounced forward with great vigor.

Lang Gu was busy running back and forth, picking them up one by one; he would just put one back in the nest, and several more would crawl out from the other side.

He remained all smiles throughout, his steps light, showing no signs of fatigue.

Lang Guo, Lin Qiu, and Yu Jiang sat on the sidelines, watching him work.

Lang Guo remarked, "It's good to be young; you have so much energy."

Lin Qiu replied, "As if you're that old yourself."

Lang Guo bumped his shoulder against his, saying, "I'm already a father; do you think I'm still young?"

Two years ago, including Lang Guo's own, those nine cubs had long been able to leave the cave and run around everywhere.

Lang Sheng and the others spent their days playing with those nine little ones, and by now, who knew which haystacks they were hiding in.

The fact that the little cubs could transform into human form meant they were healthy, and as long as no accidents happened, they would grow up well.

The beastmen didn't need to keep them under their noses every second; they only needed to check on them occasionally to ensure they were safe.

The most troublesome ones were this current batch of cubs.

Although they were small, there were many of them, and each was full of energy.

When they started making a fuss, even all of them combined couldn't keep up.

"Awoo!"

A very loud howl from a cub suddenly rang out in the plaza.

Lin Qiu and the others looked over in a panic, only to see Lang Gu pinching the armpits of the cub that had led the charge to climb out, carrying him toward the center of the plaza.

The cub was unhappy, his body stiffening, exposing his round little belly as he tilted his head back and yelled loudly at Lang Gu.

As soon as he yelled, the other cubs stopped and followed suit.

"Awoo!"

"Awoo-awoo-awoo!"

It was one thing for the wolf cubs to howl like that, but the rabbit-beastman cubs and black-feathered beastman cubs had also been influenced to howl like this from a young age.

For a moment, the white, red, and gray little fur balls in the plaza kept clamoring; Lin Qiu felt as if he were in a summer paddy field, with frog croaks everywhere—it was incredibly noisy.

Lin Qiu rubbed his ears.

"Lang Ying doesn't like to talk, and Lang Huo doesn't say much either; how come their cubs are so irritable?"

Among this pile of cubs, Lang Ying's cub was the most opinionated, the most persistent, and had the loudest voice.

Lang Gu just laughed when he heard this.

He held the cub in the crook of his arm, patted his bottom, and said, "He's unhappy, and he doesn't know how to talk yet, so he can only howl like this."

"Awoo!" The cub bit down on his arm.

Unfortunately, his teeth hadn't grown in properly, so it didn't hurt at all.

Lin Qiu remarked, "Their personalities are the same."

Both held grudges and couldn't stand hearing bad things about themselves.

The sky darkened, and the cubs, who had been screeching, were startled by the sky full of black-feathered beastmen, finally quieting down.

They sat down, heads tilted high, watching the black-feathered beastmen without moving, like miniature stone lions.

Yu Shan flapped his wings, the wind causing the fur on the cubs to sway.

"Awoo!" The cubs were excited.

Yu Shan smiled, flying almost to the other side of the plaza before setting down the animal-skin bag he was clutching.

He looked at the group of cubs with affection, especially the few bald black-feathered beastman cubs among them.

After watching enough, he said, "Qiu! Yan said to arrange for the beastmen to boil salt."

Lin Qiu was puzzled: "Didn't the King and the others take the carts to dig for salt? Why are you the ones bringing it back?"

"A new tribe arrived in the west, and Lang Yan is keeping an eye on them over there."

"Another one?"

"Awoo!"

Hearing the cub howl, Lin Qiu looked at his feet, picked up a fur ball from the ground, and threw it into the plaza.

The cub immediately chased after it, his four legs running in a chaotic mess, as if each had a mind of its own.

Yu Shan said, "It looks like a medium-sized tribe, but it's a herbivorous beastman tribe, so there shouldn't be any problems."

Lin Qiu replied, "Alright, you all go ahead and get busy; I'll arrange the salt boiling."

Yu Shan nodded, but was immediately surrounded by cubs after taking only a few steps.

The cubs hugged his legs, looking up at the sky expectantly.

Lang Guo picked up a long pole he had placed nearby, blocking the cubs in front of them.

The cubs pressed their paws against the pole, looking on longingly.

Lang Guo said heartlessly, "Don't even think about it."

Yu Shan looked at the little wolf cub that had already climbed onto his waist and chuckled. His rough hand smoothed the cub's fur, and the next moment, he picked the cub up by the scruff of his neck and set him down.

The cubs were too small; even if they were raised to be chubby by the wolf beastmen, they couldn't just be taken into the sky.

"Qiu, we're going back to patrol." Yu Shan finished speaking and left in a hurry, fearing he'd be pestered by the cubs and wouldn't be able to get away later.

Lin Qiu acknowledged him and also stood up, intending to arrange the salt boiling first.

At the canteen window nearby, Lang An poked his head out and said, "Qiu, the canteen's stoves aren't enough; we need to build more."

"Alright."

Most of the tribe's stoves were already in use.

Two or three sub-beastmen were responsible for one pot, generally ensuring that the beastmen had more than three choices for each meal.

The smallest cubs also had a separate pot for their food.

The number of beastmen cooking remained the same, but each meal had a wider variety of ingredients, and the amount of food consumed hadn't changed much.

It was also because there were more choices that the beastmen ate their fill of the food they liked; in these two years, the cubs had been healthy, the little wolves had grown rapidly in height, and even the adult beastmen, who were busy all the time, had become stronger than ever.

Coupled with the training, the adult wolf beastmen had now returned to their peak physical condition.

The tribe boiled a lot of salt, and it was a time-consuming task; using just those few pots in the canteen, who knew how long it would take.

Building stoves was a simple job for the beastmen.

The faster they could boil the salt, the better.

To build stoves, they had to find the beastmen from the construction team.

The houses in the tribe were mostly built; besides the side near the big river, houses had been built on the east, west, and north sides of the plaza.

Since there wasn't enough space, the beastmen continued to build north around Wolf Mountain.

Now, from the front of Wolf Mountain to the back, there was a smooth, wide road connecting them, with red-brick bungalows arranged neatly on both sides.

The houses were mostly finished and the beastmen had enough to live in, so the construction team was currently mainly busy building the city wall and smelting iron.

Lang Mo and the others had brought back quite a lot of ore after returning from the Chishan Tribe.

Besides going to the wall construction site, he spent his time building iron smelting furnaces in the west.

Lin Qiu went to the west to call for the beastmen.

For the sake of secrecy, Lang Mo intended to build the iron smelting furnace in the mountains to the west.

The beastmen were cautious when entering and leaving, fearing that one day they would be spotted by those beastmen who secretly entered the wilderness tribe's territory.

Lin Qiu walked north along the wide road, passed Wolf Mountain, and glanced up at it.

In the last two years, there had been changes on the mountain as well.

The beastmen had built a watchtower on the summit, and Lang Shi had arranged for beastmen to stand guard day and night. At every moment, the tribe had eyes watching the surroundings of Wolf Mountain.

Lin Qiu met the gaze of the beastman on the watchtower; the beastman nodded, Lin Qiu smiled, and continued forward.

The roads on Wolf Mountain were all built straight.

The road surface was compacted and very smooth; the beastmen could walk on it with their eyes closed without fear of falling.

The houses on both sides of the road were of uniform height, and the beastmen had all moved in. At this moment, the doors of each house were tightly closed, as the beastmen had all gone out to work.

Wolf Mountain was stable, and the beastmen were becoming increasingly adept at living their lives.

In front of each small house, broken pottery jars were filled with soil, growing beautiful wild flowers and grasses.

There were also those who loved fruit and specifically asked Tu Kui for fruit tree saplings to plant in their own yards.

Lin Qiu looked at this flourishing scene and let out a slow breath.

These changes on Wolf Mountain made all the hard work everyone had put into development and construction over the past two years worth it.

After passing Wolf Mountain, Lin Qiu saw a beastman walking out of the Black Mountain Cave.

"Mo, are you busy?"

Lang Mo was covered in dust, but his eyes were bright. He asked, "Is there something good to eat?"

Lin Qiu replied, "There's work to do."

Lang Mo patted the dust off his body, sighed, and asked, "Do you need many beastmen?"

"Build a few stoves to boil salt."

"Wait for me."

After saying this, Lang Mo dived back into the Black Mountain Cave.

Lin Qiu followed him.

They had dug through the Black Mountain Cave, and it was winding inside, like the underground burrows of rabbit beastmen.

Lin Qiu followed Lang Mo, turning for quite a while before finding a path to continue forward.

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Mo's back in front of him and asked, "What's the point of digging this cave?"

"To hide the path."

"Once your furnace is built and you start burning it, can you hide that black smoke?"

Lang Mo stopped abruptly.

Lin Qiu had anticipated this and stopped his feet in advance.

"So you didn't think about this problem?"

"...We'll just use animal skins to plug the furnace when the time comes."

Lin Qiu laughed out loud.

Getting along with the beastmen was actually very easy.

There was almost no backstabbing; they said what was on their minds, and the beastmen themselves often did things that made people laugh.

Lin Qiu felt he had laughed more in these few years than in all his previous life combined.

Lang Mo wailed, his voice echoing in the winding cave—

"Then all the effort Tu Ai and the others spent digging for so long was for nothing!"

Lin Qiu gestured for him to keep walking, comforting him, "Think about it carefully; there are benefits too. At least it can conceal the traces of your coming and going. If something happens to the tribe in the future, this cave can also serve as a place for the beastmen to relocate."

Lang Mo was the type who could float to the sky with just a little praise from the beastmen, and his tail immediately perked up as he said:

"I knew my decision was excellent!"

Lang Yan had handed the iron smelting matter entirely to Lang Mo.

Now, Lang Mo and his squad members had directly left the guard team to focus on iron-related tasks, including but not limited to repairing ironware, researching steel, and searching for iron ore.

Lang Mo's brain wasn't always very sharp, but he never made mistakes on important matters and was quite reliable.

*

After walking for a while, Lin Qiu finally saw light.

Emerging from another cave entrance, the view before him suddenly opened up.

This was a valley surrounded by mountains; it was a pity that the Feather Tribe existed on the Beast God Continent, otherwise this location would indeed be hard for beastmen to discover.

The beastman squad that Lang Mo brought back from the Chishan Tribe were already skilled at building furnaces; it was just that obtaining and processing materials was troublesome. They had been back for a month, and only now were they starting to build the iron smelting furnace.

Everyone was busy with their own tasks, being exceptionally serious.

The beastmen here were mainly the seven wolf beastmen from Lang Mo's original squad and the twenty beastmen Lang Ying had sent to help.

These twenty-plus beastmen were the core of the iron smelting.

The other group of beastmen helping out were all those who came over in turns from the wall construction site to learn.

Lang Mo waved his hand, looking extremely heroic: "Qiu, how many do you need?"

Lang Xi, who was nearby, grabbed a lump of mud and threw it at him.

Lin Qiu laughed: "Six is about enough."

Lang Mo shouted: "Ten beastmen! Come build the stove."

As soon as he finished speaking, Lang Xi, who was nearby, clapped his hands, kicking up a cloud of dust, and walked over slowly.

Subsequently, nine more beastmen from the team voluntarily stepped out.

Fine, four extra wouldn't hurt.

Lin Qiu: "Let's go, finish it quickly so you can get back to your own work."

*

In the plaza, the cubs who had finished their playtime were brought back indoors.

The tribe had built a large house specifically for Lang Guo to look after the cubs; the house contained a large heated brick bed, and during the snowy season, animal skins would be spread on the open floor for the cubs to play in the room.

When the weather got hot, the animal skins were replaced with straw mats.

Inside the room were also many toys that Lin Qiu had asked Lang Qi to make, as well as wolf-fur balls that the beastmen had made for the cubs with loving hearts.

After exiting the Black Mountain Cave, Lang Xi asked while walking: "Qiu, should we use iron pots or pottery pots?"

"Iron pots."

The beastmen nodded and immediately started working.

As the sun rose higher, a few birds flew over Wolf Mountain and landed in the fields, pecking at the tail-grass seeds that had just been sown.

The beastmen waved their hands and shouted loudly.

The birds glanced at the beastmen, tilted their slender heads back as if in contempt, and continued eating.

"Hey! They come every year, we shout every year, and now they don't even listen!"

Yu Lie flapped his wings and dived straight at the birds.

"Caw!!!"

In an instant, the birds scattered in a panic.

Yu Lie flew over the heads of Lin Qiu and the others, still having the leisure to ask: "Qiu, do you want to eat bird meat?"

Lin Qiu looked up, seeing only bird feathers flying all over the sky.

"Yes!" Lang Mo shouted.

Lin Qiu paused his steps and turned his head: "When did you follow us?"

"I've been here the whole time." Lang Mo laughed.

*

Yu Shan had taken the black-feathered beastmen to patrol between the two tribal territories again.

Lin Qiu glanced to the west, didn't see Lang Yan returning, and headed back to the house.

"An, are there any free sub-beastmen? Have them boil salt tomorrow."

"Alright, I'll arrange it."

Through the window, Lang An looked outside again.

Those salts were packed in animal-skin bags and piled outside; there were over thirty large animal-skin bags and rattan baskets in total. One flatbed cart could hold five or six bags, so this was about five carts' worth.

"Is this enough?" Lang An asked.

"It's definitely enough for our own consumption."

"The surrounding tribes are about to come to trade for salt again, and the tribe doesn't have much left. Salt can be stored, so why don't we boil a bit more this year?"

Lin Qiu thought that made sense, so he said: "I'll tell him when the King returns."

Lang An held a large iron spoon, leaning against the window but not in a hurry to leave.

He had just heard Yu Shan's words and sighed: "I don't know what happened over there in the last two years; several tribes have come over from the Central Continent."

Lin Qiu nodded, feeling some pressure in his heart as well.

"Yes, I heard from Ying that they are all tribes that could no longer afford to pay tribute to the Wilderness Tribe, and some tribes even broke away from the Wilderness Tribe..."

The more difficult things were for the Wilderness Tribe, the more they would keep an eye on them.

"So the Wilderness Tribe has no food either?"

"Most likely."

"Serves them right! Telling them to do nothing but wait for the beastmen to give them food for free."

"With them like that, who knows what kind of trouble will arise."

Lang An felt a chill in his heart and said: "Our tribe has grown by several members, so we still need to be more careful."

Lin Qiu replied: "Lang Shi and the others are watching; the sentry beastmen are guarding day and night, and Yu Shan and Lang Ying are patrolling, so there shouldn't be any mishaps."

Lang An looked out the window; the cubs were no longer in the plaza.

On the watchtower on Wolf Mountain, a beastman stood on both the south and north sides.

The Wolf Tribe used a large number of beastmen for vigilance, which was why the tribe hadn't had any trouble in the last two years.

Lang An: "I just don't know when it will end..."

Yes, who knew when it would end.

Lin Qiu walked toward the river, thinking about this matter as he went.

In the last two years, more small tribes had appeared to the north, southwest, southeast, and east of the Wolf Tribe. Together with the Black Feather Tribe and the White Sparrow Tribe, they directly surrounded the Wolf Tribe in the center.

Those beastman tribes were very close to them.

But they weren't in the Wolf Tribe's territory, so they couldn't manage them.

The more beastmen coming from the Central Continent, the more unstable it was over there.

Judging by the situation over the past two years where the Wilderness Tribe sent beastmen to harass their tribe, the situation over there was definitely not optimistic.

The less optimistic it was over there, the less they dared to let their guard down.

And then there were these new beastman tribes in the surrounding area... Lin Qiu was actually also curious; these beastmen were clearly afraid of them, yet they were crowding toward this side.

The King had even specifically asked the rabbit beastmen, who had better affinity, to go and ask, and the result was that they all came from the Central Continent.

When asked further, they said they wanted to join the Wolf Tribe, just like the Rabbit Tribe.

"Has our tribe's good reputation spread from the Eastern Continent to the Central Continent?" Lang Mo asked this when he heard another new tribe had arrived.

Lin Qiu, while helping to dig river mud, said: "Was our reputation in the Central Continent bad before?"

"It was good, but not to the point where beastmen would all flock to our vicinity."

"Then perhaps someone helped us advertise."

"Who?"

"Maybe Bao Xiu."

Lang Mo sneered: "That little cub hasn't had any news for two or three years; he's probably forgotten us long ago. It was a waste of us raising him for two years, raising a white-eyed leopard."

Lin Qiu's playful mood faded.

When Bao Xiu left, it was clear he wouldn't stop until he found their priest; even if it cost him his life, he would likely still search.

Lang Mo threw a shovel of mud into the basket and hummed: "...I don't know if he's good or bad now, or if he's found their priest."

Lin Qiu's eyes curved.

Hard mouth, soft heart.

Lang Xi, who was nearby, said: "Don't worry, he can survive falling into a river or being bitten by buzzing insects; he has a tough life."

Lin Qiu murmured: "Yes, he has a tough life..."

While chatting, the beastmen found an empty space on the south side of the plaza, brought a cart of bricks, scooped some wet mud from the riverbank, and started building the stove.

Wolf beastmen liked to do everything in excess.

If they ate something delicious, they had to eat it for every meal for several days until they were satisfied before stopping.

The tribe had plenty of large iron pots, a full twenty or more.

Besides those, there were many iron pots of different styles, round, flat, big, and small, that the beastmen had created themselves, but they were kept in the cave and hadn't been used yet.

Lin Qiu helped move the iron pots out; passing through the plaza, he had to look toward the west.

Lang Mo slapped a bucket of mud on the ground and followed him, standing on tiptoe to look toward the west.

Lin Qiu looked at him coldly.

He laughed and said: "If you're worried about the King, ask Yu Ya and the others to take you; they just came back to get herb seeds and haven't left yet."

Now, Lang Bing's herb planting had also expanded in scope.

He didn't just plant a few stalks in the forest as before, but specifically designated locations, finding places suitable for the growth of medicinal plants to plant them in batches.

Those mountains to the west were a good place to grow herbs.

Yu Ya and the others were going over there anyway, and they flew faster than they ran.

Lin Qiu: "I'm not worried about the King; I'm worried about that medium-sized tribe."

After noon, the stoves built by the beastmen were dried by the sun, and the pots were placed on top, fitting perfectly.

Lang Mo clapped his hands and put his hands on his hips: "Done! Do you need our help to boil the salt?"

Lin Qiu: "No, you go do your own..."

"Qiu!"

Lin Qiu looked up abruptly and saw a black shadow sweeping in from the south.

"Is the Priest here?!"

Yu Qian's expression was panicked, his speed was extremely fast, and water was dripping from the feathers of his gray-black wings.

Lin Qiu smelled something wrong; upon closer inspection, it wasn't water at all, but blood!

Lin Qiu's breath hitched, and looking closer, he saw Yu Qian carrying a beastman on his back.

He hurriedly said: "The Priest went to look at the wall in the north; put him in the house first."

"Lie!" Lin Qiu shouted toward the east.

"Yeah!"

"Hurry to the north and bring the Priest back; a beastman is injured."

Before Lin Qiu finished speaking, a gust of wind swept across the sky, and Yu Lie's figure disappeared in a few moments.

Lin Qiu followed Yu Qian into the small house.

He helped lift the beastman off Yu Qian's back and, upon looking, discovered it was Que Xi, whom he hadn't seen in a long time.

Yu Qian squatted carefully by the heated bed, his voice hoarse: "He fell while gathering with Lang Tan and the others, his head hit a rock, and it's been bleeding ever since. We used cloth to press it, and now it looks like the bleeding has slowed down a bit."

Lin Qiu looked at the beastman's pale lips; it was excessive blood loss.

"Alright, I know. You go rest for a while and clean up; I'll watch here."

Yu Qian nodded, looked at his own blood-stained body, and hurried to the bathhouse.

The smell of blood was quite strong, and other beastmen in the tribe smelled it and rushed over, blocking the doorway.

Lin Qiu prepared the herbs to stop the bleeding while driving the beastmen away.

"Don't block the way, go do your own work."

The beastmen glanced at the bed, saw that it was Que Xi, whom they had previously rescued from the wandering tribe, asked about the situation, and left.

"Qiu!"

Lin Qiu was preparing the tools to stitch the wound when Yu Lie shouted outside, and he almost pricked himself with a needle.

Lin Qiu didn't look up and asked: "Where is the Priest?"

"Hey... I told you to slow down!" The old Priest supported his old waist, blowing his beard and staring.

While he was talking, his feet didn't slow down, and he walked into the house leaning on his cane.

The old Priest took one look at the beastman's head, which was wrapped tightly in linen, and asked: "Did you fight?"

"No, he fell."

Lin Qiu grabbed a stool and placed it behind the old Priest for him to sit, then prepared the tools and herbs for him, placing them one by one by the Priest's side.

The Priest shoved his cane into Lin Qiu's hand and said irritably: "It's not like you don't know how!"

Lin Qiu: "His injury is on the back of his head."

The old Priest paused and stopped arguing with Lin Qiu.

He wiped his hands with the wet towel Lin Qiu handed him and watched as Lin Qiu slowly uncovered the linen on the beastman's head.

Seeing the bloody hole on the back of his head, his entire old face wrinkled tightly.

"Cut his hair."

Lin Qiu followed instructions, being careful throughout.

The Priest then immediately cleaned the wound, applied medicine, and bandaged it.

"Qiu, get the medicine. Half a handful of red fish grass, three pieces of black silk vine..."

Lin Qiu listened to the Priest's dictation of the herbs, picked up a basket, and went to the row of medicine cabinets against the wall to get the medicine.

The medicine cabinet was built by Lang Qi according to Lin Qiu's drawings; the herbs were categorized conveniently, and it was easy to get them.

The Priest listed several, and as Lin Qiu pulled open the first cabinet containing red fish grass, his hand paused.

"Priest, the red fish grass is gone."

"Find the red fish grass in the mountain cave, get the others."

Lin Qiu opened four or five medicine cabinets in a row, and most of the herbs inside were bottoming out.

"Priest, has our tribe's herb supply run out again?"

The old Priest said irritably: "It was already almost gone a long time ago."

"I'll go check the mountain cave."

Besides this room, the place where the Priest kept herbs was the cave he used to live in.

The old Priest rarely went up to the mountain cave anymore.

Usually, it was Lang Bing who went up to get medicine and tidy up.

Lin Qiu went in; there was no musty smell inside. Lang Bing had a bit of a clean-freak habit and kept it spotless.

He looked around; the cave was piled everywhere with animal-skin bags and pottery jars containing herbs... The old Priest's cave had become a place to store herbs.

Looking at the amount of herbs, they shouldn't have to worry for the next two or three years.

But when he finished searching for the herbs the Priest mentioned according to their categories, he only picked up half an animal-skin bag of red fish grass; the others either had a little bit of dregs left or couldn't be found at all.

Lin Qiu's heart rose, and he recited the names of those herbs several times before remembering that several of these medicines were not produced in the Eastern Continent.

Lin Qiu immediately went to check the herbs they had exchanged from the south of the Eastern Continent.

Upon looking, the animal-skin bag was full.

The medicinal smell was very strong; it was brought back by Lang Ying and the others from the Chishan Tribe a month ago, along with quite a lot of brown sugar.

They must have made a trip to the south.

But these were not what the Priest wanted.

Lin Qiu hurried down the mountain and entered the house; the old Priest took one look at his face and said: "Gone?"

Lin Qiu shook his head.

"I said long ago that the tribe has no herbs. The market isn't open, and herbs from other continents can't be exchanged..."

The ones that were empty weren't the most critical; the old Priest had hidden some life-saving herbs directly, not daring to touch them at all.

"Fortunately, you haven't needed them in the last two years, otherwise I wouldn't know where to find them."

Lin Qiu: "This won't do."

"I know it won't do! What can we do?"

"We've been to the south of the Eastern Continent; it's not like we can't go to other continents."

The old Priest picked up his cane and wanted to hit Lin Qiu.

"Don't even think about it!"

It took the beastmen several months to go to the south of the Eastern Continent; if they went to other continents, it would take at least half a year.

How was this any different from their migration from the Central Continent to the Eastern Continent?

Lin Qiu held the empty basket: "But the beastmen need to use them."

"Pah! Use what! Stop talking nonsense!"

Lin Qiu was helpless: "Let's not talk about this for now; Que Xi is still lying there, Priest, change the prescription."

The old Priest thought of those few family assets and was so angry he blew his beard.

Change, change, change!

The medicinal effect would be greatly reduced, and drinking it would have minimal effect.

"Priest..."

"Change, change, change! So annoying."

*

After finishing, Lin Qiu was also covered in blood.

He went out to quickly change his clothes and came back; just as he entered the house, he saw the beastman looking at the doorway with half-closed eyes.

Woke up so soon?

The old Priest sat to one side, with Lang Xue squatting beside him, teaching the cub how to treat injuries using the current case.

Lin Qiu entered, and the beastman's eyes moved with him.

"He woke up?"

"He was like this when you left, just looking at the beastmen with his eyes half-open, not moving at all," the Priest said.

"Is there no major problem with his brain?"

"See for yourself."

"If I could tell, would I still need to call the Priest?"

The old Priest grabbed his cane and pretended to hit him; Lin Qiu dodged and smiled.

The old Priest said irritably: "He won't die!"

Lang Xue waited for the Priest to finish being fierce, then happily pounced over, hugging Lin Qiu's waist.

Lin Qiu smiled and touched the little head of the cub, who was already as tall as his waist.

"Weren't you playing with Lang Sheng and the others outside?"

"Uncle Lie said there was a patient, so I came back."

Lin Qiu found a place to sit down.

Lang Xue moved the stool and sat side by side with him.

He said to Lin Qiu: "The Priest said he needs to rest well to replenish the blood he lost."

"Don't worry, he won't be mistreated."

Lang Xue smiled happily, but when he turned to face the Priest, he immediately tightened his snowy little face and became serious again.

The old one and the young one continued their lesson.

The old Priest's voice was slow and light, very sleep-inducing.

Lin Qiu yawned and simply stood up, walking to the beastman's side.

The beastman's eyeballs followed him.

Lin Qiu helped him tidy the animal-skin blanket covering him and asked softly: "Do you remember who you are?"

Que Xi stared at him.

After a long time, a wet trail slowly fell from the corner of his eye.

"Tha... thank you."

Lin Qiu's hand paused, a flash of surprise in his eyes, but after a few breaths, he covered his shoulders as usual.

He said in a soft, slow voice: "You're welcome."

*

Que Xi was no longer silly.

This news swept through the entire Wolf Tribe like a storm.

In the evening, while the beastmen were sitting in the canteen digging into their food, they still found time to say: "How did he wake up just by bumping his head? Qiu was like that before too. If we bump our heads, will we see the Beast God?"

"If you're lucky, yes. If you're unlucky, you'll be silly," Lang An said irritably.

The old Priest: "Go ahead and bump it; I don't have that many herbs to save you anyway."

"What if I can become like Qiu and know many things? Wouldn't it be a good thing for the tribe to have one more beastman who can communicate with the Beast God?"

"Heh."

No beastman paid any attention to him.

When Lin Qiu heard the Priest's words, he truly understood that it wasn't a joke.

The tribe really was lacking herbs.

Lang Yun: "...Heh!"

Who couldn't "heh"?

"Heh, heh!!!"

The beastmen at the same table bared their teeth in disgust and moved their bowls to the side one after another.

Lang He also silently moved to the back table, pretending not to know Lang Yun.

Sometimes being too silly wasn't good either.

It was embarrassing.

After the meal, Lin Qiu carried the medicine to Que Xi.

Lang Bing only learned that there was a new patient in the tribe after returning, and seeing Lin Qiu delivering medicine, he followed along.

Que Xi was still lying in the large house, which was the place specifically designated by the Priest for treating beastmen; the Priest had his own separate living quarters.

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Bing, who had followed him, and said, "You've been busy all day, go get some rest. I'll watch over things here."

Lang Bing: "I'll take a look."

His face showed undisguised exhaustion, and his voice was low.

Lang Bing had been leaving early and returning late these days, busy planting and gathering herbs, and hadn't really rested.

Lin Qiu: "We have enough herbs here for now, don't push yourself too hard."

"I have to..." Lang Bing's eyelids drooped as he murmured, "Qiu, there aren't many medicinal herbs left in the tribe."

Lin Qiu paused, the medicinal soup in the bowl swaying gently, the bitter scent reaching his nose.

He said softly, "I know."

Lang Bing looked at him, "I want to go out and trade for herbs."

"No," Lin Qiu refused without hesitation.

"Qiu..."

"Even if the King came, it wouldn't be allowed."

Lang Bing was the next priest that the Priest had spent great effort to cultivate; the previous few had already passed away, and if anything happened to him, Lin Qiu didn't even dare to imagine the consequences.

"But we can't go on without herbs."

Lang Bing hadn't expected that he would tell this idea to Lin Qiu first, only to be refused without a second thought.

Lang Bing felt stifled; he had been sleepy just a moment ago, but now he was suddenly wide awake.

Seeing Lang Bing glaring at him, Lin Qiu said, "Didn't we get through the past ten-plus years just fine?"

Lang Bing: "That was because the Priest made preparations before the migration. We traded away half our belongings just to get that many herbs."

When they migrated, half of what they brought were herbs, as the Priest was afraid the beastmen might encounter emergencies on the road.

By that time, several major markets had already closed. Among those herbs, some were what the Wolf Tribe had saved previously, and some were traded from other tribes in the Central Continent.

Although Lang Bing hadn't experienced that event personally, he knew about it.

But so many years had passed, and the herbs were long since mostly used up.

"You all went last time, I can go too."

"Don't be stubborn."

"Qiu!" Lang Bing stomped his foot in annoyance.

He wasn't a little wolf anymore; he was an adult, and finding herbs for the tribe was also his responsibility.

Watching his restless state, Lin Qiu raised his hand to ruffle his hair just as he used to, "Don't be anxious, this matter can't be rushed. When your King returns, I will discuss it with him."

It had been two years; they did indeed need to go out once.

But given the tribe's current situation, there were many things that needed to be arranged.

Only after hearing him say this did Lang Bing let out a soft huff and continue walking with him.

As Lin Qiu reached the door with the medicine, he saw Yu Qian walking out.

He had just delivered food to the beastman.

Que Xi was severely injured and could only eat thin porridge made from tail-grass seeds; it was only a small bowl, and the beastman had only eaten half of it.

"Is he awake?" Lin Qiu asked.

Yu Qian looked at the remaining food in the bowl with regret and whispered, "He's awake, but he won't speak, he just keeps shedding tears."

Yu Qian was responsible for patrols in the south and east, occasionally leading beastmen to hunt, but mostly stationed at the Great Marsh. Yu Qian knew Que Xi's situation and took extra care of him.

This sub-beastman was beautiful, an extremely prominent presence even among a group of good-looking beastmen.

Yu Qian often saw him working by Yang Zhi's side.

He wouldn't speak, just acting wooden and dull.

When not working, he would usually squat beside Yang Zhi. But once a strange beastman approached him, he would react violently, crying and hiding, his strength also terrifyingly great.

The wolf beastmen all said he had gone foolish.

But Yu Qian didn't think so.

He thought Que Xi must have suffered a blow and was self-isolating. Just like when Yu Shan was injured back then, his entire temperament changed, and it took years for him to recover.

For Que Xi to wake up, it would take time and an opportunity.

This fall was that turning point.

He had just delivered the food inside and saw the look in Que Xi's eyes, so he knew he was awake.

However, he had been crying the whole time.

He cried quietly, large teardrops rolling down the corners of his eyes, as if he wanted to cry out all his grievances.

Yu Qian felt a tightness in his chest just watching.

Waking up was a good thing, but also a bad thing.

Those hardships would be remembered one by one, winding around him like hemp rope; it was too torturous.

When Lin Qiu and Lang Bing entered, Que Xi was still lying on his side, his gaze hollowly fixed on one spot, oblivious to everything.

"Drink the medicine."

Que Xi's body trembled, a reaction etched into his bones.

He looked as if he had just been fished out of water, his body soaked in sweat mixed with tears.

Lang Bing tentatively reached out his hand in front of him.

Seeing that he didn't dodge, he slowly helped him sit up.

Lin Qiu handed over the bowl, and Que Xi took it with trembling hands, lowering his eyes to pour it into his mouth bit by bit.

The medicinal soup tasted very bitter; Lin Qiu had drunk plenty of it in the past, and now just smelling it made him feel slightly nauseous.

Yet he showed no reaction, crying while drinking, his tears like a trickling stream, seemingly endless.

Lang Bing checked his wounds.

Lin Qiu sat to the side, looking at his swollen eyes, and said softly, "Stop crying, your wounds haven't healed yet."

After Que Xi finished the medicine, he was helped back to sleep by Lang Bing.

As the two beastmen packed up to leave, Que Xi suddenly grabbed Lin Qiu's hand, then pulled it back abruptly.

Lin Qiu turned back, "What do you want to say?"

"I, I... cough, cough..."

He hadn't spoken for years, his throat was hoarse, and his words were incoherent. But he was very urgent; he had to say it.

Lin Qiu gave the bowl to Lang Bing and patted his back.

Upon being touched, Que Xi curled back into the kang.

Lin Qiu had to withdraw his hand and said, "Take your time."

"I..." Que Xi looked at Lin Qiu apologetically, gripping the animal skin blanket tightly, restraining his body's trembling.

He gathered his breath and said, "I want to return to the tribe."

Lin Qiu: "You can go back once you're better."

Que Xi braced his body, staring intently at Lin Qiu.

Seeing this, Lang Bing stepped over, wanting to press him down and tuck him into the animal skin blanket. He said with a cold face, "Rest properly if you're injured, don't waste our herbs!"

Que Xi: "Re-return to the tribe..."

Lang Bing really disliked disobedient sick beastmen.

"Fine, you can go back whenever you want, we won't stop you."

Que Xi's head stung, his face turning pale.

He endured the wave of dizziness, and just as Lang Bing was about to move, he said weakly, "Our tribe... rice, trade."

Lin Qiu's pupils constricted.

"You have rice?!"

Que Xi cried and laughed, repeating hoarsely, "Yes, rice. Tha-thank you."

*

Lin Qiu and Lang Bing were still in a daze when they left.

Rice.

The rice he had been thinking about for four or five years.

How could this not make Lin Qiu excited?

When walking out, if Lang Bing hadn't been supporting him, he would have almost tripped.

Lang Bing said coldly, "You're such a big beastman, and you still can't watch where you're walking? Is that thing better than our tail-grass?"

"Both are good." Lin Qiu couldn't help but curl his lips.

Lang Bing saw him regain his composure and huffed, but his hand kept gripping Lin Qiu's tightly.

"We sent Lu Ye to the White River Tribe, and now we have to send him back to his tribe too? Are we wolf beastmen specifically for sending beastmen to other tribes?"

Lin Qiu laughed, "He didn't ask us to send him."

"Then... are you going?" Lang Bing had a cold face, but Lin Qiu could see the anticipation in his raised eyebrows.

"Wait for the King to return, and we'll discuss it."

"Tsk, discuss again."

Lin Qiu stood firm, stomped his weak feet, and couldn't help but laugh at Lang Bing.

"Don't be anxious."

"I am anxious! I'm so anxious I can't stand it!"

"Then should I go find your King now?"

"You are not allowed to go!"

Look, he's the one who's anxious, and he's also the one who won't let him go find Lang Yan.

Lin Qiu smoothed Lang Bing's beautiful white hair and said warmly, "Go get some rest first. When you wake up tomorrow morning, maybe the King will be back."

"Hmph!"

Lin Qiu's smile grew brighter.

Still the same little wolf temper.

Lang Bing: "Que Xi, do you need a beastman to watch him?"

Lin Qiu: "I'll watch."
