Although the beastman hadn't been awake long, judging by his performance during this time, his personality should be quite good, matching what Lu Ye said.

Que Xi wasn't used to speaking yet, but the first thing he did upon waking up was to trade rice with them.

Lin Qiu and Lang Bing could both tell that he was doing it to show gratitude to the Wolf Tribe.

Rice, peanuts, potatoes... these crops were related to the survival of the tribe; no one would easily bring them out, yet he offered to trade them just like that.

Lin Qiu wasn't afraid of him deceiving the Wolf Tribe.

He was thinking more about how, after changing worlds, these crops hadn't even changed their names; perhaps there was some connection between this world and his previous one.

This was a good thing for him.

With crops, there was hope to feed the beastmen.

And now that there was rice, could wheat, soybeans, corn, and sweet potatoes be far behind?

Lin Qiu sent Lang Bing off to rest, while he took the bowl back to the cafeteria.

The cafeteria had piped in stream water using wooden tubes, so the beastmen didn't need to carry jars to the stream to fetch water, which was much more convenient.

Lin Qiu washed the bowl and turned around to see the Priest, Lang An, Lang Ying, Tu Kui, Yu Qian, Lang Chi, as well as Lang Wan and Lang Xing sitting on stools waiting for him.

And Lang Bing, whom he had told to rest, was sitting with them now.

It looked like a three-court trial.

Lin Qiu wiped his hands and said calmly, "Waiting for me?"

"Qiu, come here," Lang An said.

Lin Qiu glanced at Lang Bing.

Lang Bing didn't feel guilty at all and looked back.

As soon as Lin Qiu sat down, the Priest asked, "Are you planning to send that beastman back to his tribe?"

"I never said that."

Lang An: "It's better not to go."

Several beastmen nodded.

Lang Bing looked anxious and said stiffly, "He wants to trade rice with us."

Lang Wan: "He can fly. Can't he just go back himself once he recovers? If he has the sincerity, he can just send the rice over, right?"

Lang Bing: "But we need to trade for herbs!"

Lang An flicked Lang Bing's forehead.

"It's you who wants to go."

Lang Bing lowered his head, "Uncle An..."

The old Priest sighed, "The tribe is short on herbs, and things aren't stable now, so it's understandable that he's anxious."

Lang Chi: "Those herbs, I'm afraid we'd have to go to the Western Continent and Southern Continent to trade for them; it's too far and not safe."

Lang Xing: "Didn't we often travel far when we went to the markets before?"

Lang Wan: "Is it the same? What's the situation now? What was the situation before? Besides, we have to carry goods for trade; can we just leave whenever we want?"

"Then can't we leave after preparing?" Lang Bing said.

Lang Ying rested his face on his hand, lifting his eyelids to look at them.

He had been dragged here by Lang An.

The beastman said this counted as a small meeting, and he had to be a representative.

"We can go."

All the beastmen turned their heads, staring at Lang Ying.

Lang Ying felt no pressure, his posture unchanged, his eyelids lifting as he scanned the beastmen one by one and said, "Don't you all think so?"

The beastmen's tense faces twitched.

They did think so, but there had to be a process before agreeing...

Lang Ying yawned, clapped his hands, stood up and said, "Wait until Lang Yan returns. If you keep arguing back and forth now, it'll all be for nothing if he doesn't agree."

The old Priest shot a glare at Lang Ying.

Lang Ying: "Did I say something wrong?"

"Nothing wrong, nothing wrong, go to sleep quickly." Lang An stood up, pulling Lang Bing along with him.

Lin Qiu: "Is that it?"

Lang An stopped after a few steps and gave a summary of this short meeting: "We definitely need to trade for herbs. And the rice that Qiu keeps talking about, he has it too. Either we make a trip, or they come here; we'll see what the King says when he returns."

Lin Qiu curled his lips, watching the beastmen leave somewhat unnaturally.

It was good that Lang Ying was there; otherwise, everyone would have kept rambling.

"Qiu, are you coming?" Lang Ying stopped and turned to ask him.

Lin Qiu: "I'll watch over the beastman, you all go to sleep."

Que Xi had a head injury, so it was best to have a beastman who knew medicine watch at night. The Priest was too old, that wouldn't work; Lang Bing and Yu Le had to work tomorrow, that wouldn't work either; Lang Xue was too young, definitely not.

Only he was the most suitable.

Now that the beastmen all had houses, they didn't crowd into the cafeteria to sleep anymore. Once the beastmen left, there wasn't a single beastman in the room; it was very empty.

After washing up, Lin Qiu carried a pot of boiled water and slowly walked to Que Xi's room.

There was a moon tonight, hanging round and full in the sky, like a golden-brown wheat cake.

Looking at it, Lin Qiu thought of the moon in the other world.

He was living quite well now, and the resentment toward those parents had slowly faded—not that he didn't resent them, but they were too far apart, and it was meaningless.

Also, he felt this place was very good.

Very, very good.

"Awoo?"

In the watchtower on Wolf Mountain, Lang Shi, who was on duty tonight, saw Lin Qiu standing in the square without moving and thought something had happened.

Hearing the small inquiry, Lin Qiu found it amusing and waved at him with a smile.

"Nothing."

Lang Shi's ears twitched, he withdrew his gaze, and continued to stare around vigilantly.

Lin Qiu brought the hot water into the room, deliberately lightening his footsteps.

A candle was lit in the room, half-burned, the fire-tree oil dripping onto the clay candle holder below, piling up and then solidifying again.

By the dim light, Lin Qiu saw Que Xi curled up on the kang, eyes closed, fast asleep.

He stood in the room for a while, then left quietly.

The snow had only melted for two months, the small insects in the ground were just waking up, and the chirping outside was low and intermittent.

Lin Qiu crossed the square, which was white under the moonlight, and walked slowly toward the south.

When the ground beneath his feet became soft, he bent his legs and sat down, slowly lying back.

For two years, Lin Qiu had been like a farmer with a whip, driving the beastmen to work hard like old oxen.

Now, houses had been built on Wolf Mountain and the Great Marsh, roads had been repaired, and the food grown in the fields and the livestock raised by the beastmen could almost cover their daily meals.

The food brought back by the hunting and gathering teams was all extra.

Lin Qiu could basically be a hands-off manager.

It was indeed time to go out.

But the trouble was that while the Wolf Tribe was stable, the outside was dangerous.

This trip out required full preparation, and once they left, there was no telling how long it would take to return.

Lin Qiu gazed at the starry sky, his thoughts drifting.

There was movement in the forest in the distance, and the beastmen on duty on Wolf Mountain immediately sensed it.

Seeing it was their own beastmen, they relaxed their vigilance and looked elsewhere.

Lang Yan had returned with the salt-gathering team.

The wheels rolled, and the beastmen were pulling the carts forward.

Hearing the sound, Lin Qiu sat up, patted the grass clippings off his body, smiled, and walked a few steps forward, watching the team of beastmen approaching.

"Qiu! You were waiting for us!" Lang Qiao smiled, his voice full of energy.

An impatient low growl came from a nearby house; most likely, a beastman who was about to fall asleep had been woken up by Lang Qiao's shout.

Lang Qiao immediately shut his mouth and raised his claws at Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu smiled brightly, "Yes, waiting for you. Do you want to eat?"

"Eat!"

"I'll go check the cafeteria."

Lang Yan signaled for the beastmen to leave the carts in the square, then took Lin Qiu's hand and walked side by side with him.

"It's cold outside, don't lie out here in the wind."

Lin Qiu said, "How did you know I was lying outside?"

"Your hands are cold." Lang Yan rubbed the back of Lin Qiu's hand, then completely enclosed it in his palm.

Lin Qiu looked at the items on the cart, "Is it salt?"

"Yes."

"Perfect, I was just thinking of asking you to dig up more."

Some beastmen hadn't returned, and Lang An had asked them to prepare some food before sleeping, so it could be heated and eaten right away.

Lin Qiu lit the fire and sat a bit to the side.

Lang Yan sat down beside him.

"Que Xi is awake."

"A beastman tribe came from the west."

They spoke at the same time, then paused and laughed.

Lang Yan was a bit tired, leaning his head on Lin Qiu's shoulder, and said, "You go first."

Lin Qiu added firewood to the stove and whispered, "Today, when Que Xi was working with the beastmen at the Great Marsh, he fell and hit his head. Yu Qian carried him back for treatment. The beastman has regained consciousness and remembers his past."

"He told me their tribe has rice."

Lang Yan wrapped his arms around Lin Qiu's waist, rubbing deeper into his neck.

He relaxed his body, his voice low and slow: "They still have beastmen in their tribe?"

"Lu Ye didn't know his situation before, but if he can say that, they must have it. It's just far away, over in the Western Continent."

"Finding new food is a good thing."

"I think so too. He really wants to return to his tribe, and rice is important. I was thinking we should make a trip, and our tribe is also short on herbs, so we can trade for more along the way."

"Hmm."

"You agree just like that?" Lin Qiu was surprised.

Lang Yan's nose brushed against his neck, his breathing making Lin Qiu itch.

"Speak." Lin Qiu tapped his knee.

Lang Yan: "It's time to go out and see. Trade for herbs, find food, and see if there are any other Wolf Tribes."

When the markets were still open, there was communication between the Wolf Tribes of the various continents. After so many years, who knew what their situation was now.

The broken connections had to be re-established.

It was both to trade resources and to let the wolf beastmen flourish again. Compared to other tribes guarding their own little plots of land, the wolf beastmen preferred communication between Wolf Tribes.

"Lang Bing wants to go too."

"If the Priest allows it, he can."

"Then let Lang Bing tell the Priest. Alright, I'm done, now tell me yours."

Lang Yan chuckled, his voice sounding lazy.

He was lazy too, having held Lin Qiu for quite a while without letting go.

The beastmen who were rushing to eat poured in, and seeing this scene, they all covered their eyes and grinned.

The gaps between their fingers were wide enough to fit another finger.

Lang Yan let go and straightened up; before his gaze even swept over them, the beastmen scurried off to get their bowls.

Lang Yan looked at the firelight, remembering the scene he saw at the Black Feather Tribe today, his eyes devoid of warmth.

"A beastman tribe came from the west today, with nearly two hundred beastmen."

"They are composed of the remnants of a dozen tribes."

"These tribes were originally those that paid tribute to the Wild Tribe in the Central Continent, but because they stopped the tribute, they were hunted down by the beastmen of the Wild Tribe, just like Yu Shan and the others."

"These beastmen gathered together slowly on the road, forming a temporary tribe."

"Then why did they come toward us?"

Lang Yan had originally gone to dig salt.

That area was the border between the Wolf Tribe and the Black Feather Tribe; being able to find them there meant these beastmen had run directly to the Black Feather Tribe.

Were they not afraid?

Lang Yan: "Someone pointed the way for them."

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan's gray eyes, suddenly gripping Lang Yan's arm, and said, "Bao Xiu?"

"It wasn't the same beastman pointing the way, and it wasn't Bao Xiu," Lang Yan hooked Lin Qiu's slender fingers, squeezed them gently, and said, "One of them was a beastman from the Wild Tribe itself, called Bao Ba; his original name was Bao Wen."

"What does he look like? Is he a black panther beastman?"

"He has many scars on his body, a scar running across his face, and he is a black panther."

Lin Qiu gripped Lang Yan's hand tightly.

"King, do you think it could be Bao Xiu?"

Their tribe didn't associate with any panther beastman tribes; the only panther beastman they knew and who knew their tribe's location was Bao Xiu.

Lang Yan: "It's not impossible."

Lin Qiu thought about this possibility and fell silent for a moment.

If it really was Bao Xiu, then he would have needed to travel alone from the Eastern Continent to the Central Continent; perhaps he met his own companions on the road, but at such a distance, anything was possible.

If he successfully reached the Central Continent and wanted to become an "executioner" for the Wild Tribe, he would have to gain their trust.

In just a year or two, could he do that?

Lin Qiu thought about it and felt the possibility was small.

"Then who else pointed the way?" he asked again.

"They said it was a clouded leopard beastman."

Lin Qiu was still thinking if they knew any clouded leopard beastmen when Lang Qiao and the team of beastmen ran over.

They looked at the edge of the steaming pot, anxious and constantly standing on tiptoe.

"Qiu, is it ready to eat?"

Lin Qiu came back to his senses, looked into the pot, and quickly said, "Stir it, it should be ready."

...

This place was too far from the Wild Tribe, and neither Lin Qiu nor Lang Yan could be sure who that panther beastman was.

Maybe it wasn't Bao Xiu, but a panther beastman who could calculate and determine their location.

Such capable people weren't unheard of in the Beast God Continent.

Lin Qiu stopped worrying and let Lang Yan go eat first.

He took two candles, lit them, and placed them on the table.

The beastmen were also starving, holding their bowls and just stuffing food into their mouths.

They were eating the food that the sub-beastmen had set aside from the big pot in the evening, both stir-fried and stewed dishes.

The tribe could now use peanuts to press oil, so they were generous with oil in their cooking.

With plenty of oil and salt, these dishes were very appetizing.

As the beastmen ate, Lin Qiu took the opportunity to go to Que Xi's place.

He entered quietly, only to find a small figure curled up beside Que Xi.

The cub was lying by the edge of the kang, his head resting against Que Xi's arm. He wasn't asleep either; when Lin Qiu entered, he opened a pair of pitch-black eyes to look at him.

"Bao Zhi? Why aren't you sleeping, why did you run here?"
chapters.source_text:
饭后，林楸端了药给雀溪送去。
狼冰回来后才知道部落多了一个病患，见林楸送药，也跟了上去。
雀溪还躺在那大房子内，那是祭司专门给兽人看病的地方，祭司另有住处。
林楸看跟上来的狼冰，道：“忙了一天了，去休息，这边我看着。”
狼冰：“我看看。”
他脸上是难以掩饰的疲惫，说话声音也低。
狼冰这些天都早出晚归，忙着种药采药，也没怎么休息过。
林楸：“咱们这边的草药够用，别逼自己太紧。”
“不紧不行……”狼冰眼皮耷拉，低喃，“楸，部落其他药材都没剩多少了。”
林楸停下，碗里的药汤轻轻晃动，苦涩的味道传至鼻尖。
他轻声道：“我知道。”
狼冰看着他，“我想出去，去交换草药。”
“不行。”林楸毫不犹豫地拒绝道。
“楸……”
“王来了都不行。”
狼冰是祭司费尽力气培养出来的下一任祭司，前面几个已经没了，他再出点事，林楸都不敢想会有什么后果。
“可我们没草药也不行。”
狼冰没想到，他第一个把这个想法告诉林楸，可他想都没想就拒绝了。
狼冰气闷，刚刚还困倦，现在一下就精神了。
林楸见狼冰瞪着他，道：“前头十几年不也过来了？”
狼冰：“那是迁徙之前祭司做了准备，我们把半身家当换了，才得来那么多草药。”
当初迁徙，带的东西半数都是草药，祭司就怕兽人在路上有个万一。
那时候几个大集市就已经关了，那些草药当中，一部分是狼部落以前攒的，一部分还是从中央大陆其他部落交换来的草药。
狼冰虽没亲历这件事，但也是知道的。
可这么多年过去了，草药早就用得差不多了。
“你们上次都去了，我也能去。”
“别犟。”
“楸！”狼冰恼得跺脚。
他不是小狼了，他已经成年了，为部落寻找草药也是他的责任。
林楸瞧着他这焦躁样子，抬手还像以前那样揉了揉他脑袋，“别急，这事不能冲动。等你们王回来，我和他商量。”
两年了，他们确实需要出去一趟。
但现在部落这个情况，需要安排的事不少。
狼冰听他这样说，才轻哼一声，继续跟他走。
林楸端着药走到门口，就看羽千从里面走出来。
他刚给兽人送了饭。
雀溪伤重，只能吃尾巴草籽做的稀粥，就那么一小碗，兽人吃了还剩一半。
“醒着吗？”林楸问。
羽千可惜地看了一眼碗里剩下的食物，低声道：“醒着的，就是不说话，一直掉眼泪。”
羽千负责南部和东部的巡逻，偶尔带兽人们捕猎，大多时候驻守在大泽那边。羽千知道雀溪的情况，对他也多加照顾。
这个亚兽人漂亮，在一堆容貌不差的兽人里都是极其突出的存在。
羽千经常看到他跟在羊止身边做事。
他也不说话，木木呆呆的。
寻常不干活的时候，他就蹲在羊止身边。可一旦陌生兽人靠近他，他反应极大，又哭又躲，力气也大得吓人。
狼兽人们都说他傻了。
羽千却觉得不是。
他想，雀溪应该就是受了打击，自我封闭。就像当初羽山受了伤一样，整个兽人性情大变，几年才恢复过来。
雀溪要清醒过来，需要时间，也需要契机。
这次摔倒，便是转变。
他刚刚送饭进去，看到雀溪的眼神，便知道他醒了。
不过他一直在哭。
哭得安静，泪珠大滴大滴沿着眼角往下滚，像要把委屈哭尽似的。
羽千看着心里都闷得慌。
醒了，是好事，也是坏事。
那些难处会被一一记起，像麻绳一样把他缠紧，太折磨了。
林楸和狼冰进去时，雀溪依旧侧躺着，目光空洞地看着一处，无知无觉。
“把药喝了。”
雀溪身体一颤，像刻入骨子里的反应。
他像刚被从水里捞出来似的，浑身汗水混着泪水，都湿透了。
狼冰试探着把手伸到他眼前。
见他不躲，才慢慢搀扶他坐起来。
林楸把碗递过去，雀溪颤着手接过，垂眸一点一点往嘴里灌。
药汤味道很苦，林楸以前喝过许多，现在光是闻着就隐隐作呕。
可他却一点反应都没有，边喝边哭，泪水如涓涓细流，不断绝似的。
狼冰检查他伤口。
林楸坐在一旁，瞧着他肿起来的双眼，轻声道：“别哭了，伤还没好。”
雀溪喝完药，又被狼冰扶着睡下。
两个兽人收拾了东西要走，雀溪却突然抓住林楸的手，又倏地收回。
林楸回头，“想说什么？”
“我、我……咳咳……”
他几年没说话了，嗓子嘶哑，语不成句。可又很急，不说还不行。
林楸把碗给了狼冰，抚着他后背。
雀溪被触碰，又往炕里蜷缩。
林楸只好收回手，道：“你慢慢说。”
“我……”雀溪歉意地看着林楸，紧紧抓住兽皮毯，克制住浑身的颤抖。
他鼓足一口气道：“我想回部落。”
林楸：“好了你就能回了。”
雀溪撑着身体，紧紧看着林楸。
狼冰见状，几步过来，想把他按下去塞进兽皮毯里。他冷着脸道：“受伤了就好好休息，别白费了我们的草药！”
雀溪：“回、回部落……”
狼冰很不喜欢不听话的病兽人。
“好了，随便你什么时候回去，我们不拦着。”
雀溪脑袋刺疼，脸色发白。
他忍过那一阵眩晕，在狼冰快要动手时，才虚弱道：“我们部落……水稻，交换。”
林楸瞳孔一缩。
“你们有水稻？！”
雀溪又哭又笑，哑声重复：“有，水稻。谢、谢谢你们。”
*
林楸和狼冰离开时还有些恍惚。
水稻。
他心心念念四五年的水稻。
这怎么能叫林楸激动？
出门时，要不是狼冰扶着他，他险些还摔一跤。
狼冰冷飕飕道：“这么大个兽人了，还不会看路？那东西能比我们尾巴草还好？”
“都好。”林楸忍不住翘起唇角。
狼冰看他缓过神，哼了一声，手却抓着林楸不放。
“咱们把鹿叶送到白河部落，还要把他也送回部落，我们狼兽人是专门给其他部落送兽人的吗？”
林楸失笑，“他也没叫我们送啊。”
“那……你要去吗？”狼冰冷着个脸，但林楸还是从他上扬的眉梢看出了他的期待。
“等王回来，商量商量。”
“啧，又商量。”
林楸站稳，跺了跺发软的脚，又忍不住笑狼冰。
“你别急。”
“我急！急得不行了！”
“那我现在去找你们王？”
“不许去！”
看看，急也是他，不让他去找狼岩也是他。
林楸顺了顺狼冰漂亮的白发，温声道：“先去休息吧，明早上起来，说不定王就回来了。”
“哼！”
林楸笑容愈发灿烂。
还是小狼脾气。
狼冰：“雀溪，要不要兽人盯着？”
林楸：“我守。”
兽人虽醒来没多久，但从这期间的表现来看，他性格应该挺好，跟鹿叶说的话匹配得上。
雀溪现在话都还说不习惯，可清醒过来的头一件事就是要跟他们交换水稻。
林楸和狼冰都看得出来，他是为了感激狼部落。
水稻、花生、土豆……这些作物，关乎部落生死，谁都不会轻易拿出来，可他张口就要用这个交换。
林楸倒不怕他骗狼部落。
他更多是在想，换了一个世界，这些作物连名字都没变过，这个世界与他从前那个世界或许有什么关联。
这对他而言是好事。
有作物，那就有养活兽人们的希望。
而现在水稻有了，小麦、大豆、玉米、红薯还会远吗？
林楸把狼冰赶去休息，他则带着碗回了食堂。
食堂这边用木管引了溪水来，兽人们吃喝用水也不用提着罐子去溪里打水，方便许多。
林楸洗干净碗，回身就看祭司、狼安、狼影、兔葵、羽千、狼赤还有狼晚、狼星坐在凳子上等着他。
而被他叫去休息的狼冰，此刻也跟他们坐在一起。
跟三堂会审似的。
林楸擦干手，淡声道：“等我呢？”
“楸，你过来。”狼安道。
林楸扫了眼狼冰。
狼冰一点不心虚，看了回来。
林楸方一坐下，祭司就开口问：“你打算送那个兽人回部落？”
“我可没这么说。”
狼安：“不去才好。”
几个兽人点点头。
狼冰看着急了，硬邦邦道：“他要跟我们交换水稻。”
狼晚：“他能飞，等他养好身体自己先回去，要有那个诚意，再把水稻送过来不就行了？”
狼冰：“可我们要交换草药！”
狼安弹了一下狼冰额头。
“是你想去吧。”
狼冰低下头，“安叔……”
老祭司叹道：“部落是缺草药，现在又不安稳，他急也是应该。”
狼赤：“那些草药，怕是要去西部大陆和南部大陆才能换到，太远了，不安全。”
狼星：“以前去集市，不也经常走很远。”
狼晚：“能一样吗？现在什么情况？以前什么情况？更何况还要带交换的物资，能说走就走吗？”
“那准备准备总能走？”狼冰道。
狼影手撑着脸，虚抬着眼皮看着他们。
他是被狼安拉过来的。
兽人说这算开小会，他也得当个代表。
“能走。”
兽人们全部转头，盯着狼影。
狼影一点不吃压力，姿势没变，眼皮一掀，反倒是一一扫过兽人们，道：“你们难道不这样想的？”
兽人们绷着的脸抽动。
想是这么想的，那不得有个过程才能答应……
狼影打了个哈欠，拍拍手，起身道：“等狼岩回来再说。你们现在扯来扯去，他不同意都白瞎。”
老祭司横了狼影一眼。
狼影：“我说错了？”
“没错没错，赶紧去睡觉。”狼安站起来，顺带拉着狼冰。
林楸：“就这么结束了？”
狼安走了几步停下来，给这个短暂的会议来了个总结：“交换草药肯定是要交换的。还有楸一直念叨的水稻，他那边也有，不是我们去一趟，就是那边来一趟，具体怎么样，王回来说。”
林楸唇角一翘，看着兽人们略微不自然地离开。
也是狼影在，大伙儿想啰嗦都啰嗦不起来了。
“楸，走不走？”狼影停步，回身问他。
林楸：“我守着兽人，你们去睡。”
雀溪伤到头，晚上有个懂医的兽人守夜最好。祭司年迈，不行；狼冰和羽乐明天要干活，也不行；狼雪太小，更不行了。
只他最合适了。
现在兽人们都有有房子，也不在食堂扎堆睡觉了。兽人们一走，屋里一个兽人也没有，空旷得很。
林楸洗漱完，拎上一壶白开水慢慢去雀溪那屋。
今晚上有月亮，圆滚滚地挂在半空中，像煎得焦黄的麦饼子。
林楸看着，想到了另一个世界的月亮。
他现在过得挺好，对那对父母的怨意也慢慢放下，不是不怨，是相隔太远，也没意义了。
还有，他觉得这里很好。
很好很好。
“嗷呜？”
狼山上的哨塔中，今晚负责放哨的狼石看林楸站在广场上不动，还以为出什么事了。
林楸听着那小小声的询问，觉得好玩儿，笑着冲他挥了挥手。
“没事。”
狼石耳朵动一动，收回目光，又紧盯着四处。
林楸把热水送进屋中，刻意放轻了脚步。
屋内点着一只蜡烛，燃了一半，火树油落在下方陶制烛台上，堆成一团又重新凝固。
林楸借着微光，见雀溪趴在炕上，闭着眼睛睡熟了过去。
他在屋里站了一会儿，又悄声离开。
雪才化两月，地里的小虫刚刚苏醒，外面虫鸣声低浅，断断续续的。
林楸穿过月光下泛着白的广场，慢慢往南边走。
待脚下的触感变得柔软，他才曲腿坐下，慢慢往后躺倒。
两年时间，林楸像拿着鞭子的农人，驱赶着兽人们像老牛一样努力干活。
现在狼山和大泽房屋都建起来了，路也修好了，地里种的粮食和兽人们养的牲畜差不多已经能覆盖兽人们的一日三餐。
狩猎采集队带回来的食物，都是多出来的。
林楸基本上已经可以当个甩手掌柜。
现在确实可以出去了。
但麻烦就麻烦在狼部落这边还算安稳，外面却危险。
这一趟出去，必须做足了准备，而且一旦出去，还不知道多久能回来。
林楸望着星空，思绪飘逸。
远处林子里有动静，狼山上放哨的兽人立马察觉。
见是自家兽人，又放松警惕，目光看向别处。
狼岩带着采盐的队伍回来了。
车轮滚滚，兽人们正拉着板车向前。
林楸闻声坐起来，拍了拍身上的草屑，笑着往前走了几步，看着渐渐靠拢过来的兽人队伍。
“楸！你等我们呢！”狼乔笑着，说话中气十足。
附近房子里传出一声不耐的低吼，多半是快睡熟的兽人被狼乔这一声吵醒了。
狼乔立马闭上嘴，冲着林楸抬了抬爪子。
林楸粲然一笑，“是，等你们呢。要不要吃饭？”
“吃！”
“我去食堂看看。”
狼岩示意兽人们把板车放广场，随后握住林楸的手，与他并肩前行。
“外面冷，别躺在外面吹风。”
林楸说：“你怎么就知道我躺没躺在外面？”
“手是凉的。”狼岩摩挲林楸手背，随后完全拢在掌心。
林楸看了眼板车上的东西，“是盐？”
“嗯。”
“正好，本来还想叫你们多挖一些回来。”
有兽人没回来，狼安睡前让兽人们备着一些食物，这会儿直接热了就能吃。
林楸把火点燃，往旁边坐了点。
狼岩挨着他坐下来。
“雀溪醒了。”
“西边来了个兽人部落。”
他俩同时开口，又一顿，笑了起来。
狼岩有些累，低头靠在林楸肩上，道：“你先说。”
林楸往灶里添柴，低声道：“今天雀溪在大泽那边跟着兽人们做事的时候摔了脑袋，羽千把他背回来治疗。兽人清醒了，记得以前的事了。”
“他跟我说，他们部落有水稻。”
狼岩圈住林楸的腰，更深地往他颈窝蹭了蹭。
他放松身体，声音低缓：“他们部落还有兽人？”
“之前鹿叶都不清楚他的情况，他能这么说，肯定是有的。不过就是远，在西部大陆那边了。”
“能找到新食物，这是好事。”
“我也觉得。他很想回部落，水稻也重要。我想着还是得走一趟，而且咱们部落也缺草药，沿路可以再多换一些回来。”
“嗯。”
“你这就同意了？”林楸讶异。
狼岩鼻尖贴着他颈侧，呼吸扫得林楸发痒。
“说话。”林楸点点他膝头。
狼岩：“该出去看看了。交换草药，寻找食物，再看看还有没有狼部落。”
曾经集市还开着时，几个大陆的狼部落之间都有交流，时隔这么多年，也不知道他们现在是什么情况。
断了的联系，得重新建立起来。
既是为了交换资源，也是让狼族兽人重新繁盛起来。比起其他部落守着自家那一亩三分地过日子，狼兽人更喜欢狼部落之间互相交流。
“狼冰也想去。”
“祭司允许的话可以。”
“那就让狼冰跟祭司说吧。好了，我说完了，再说你的。”
狼岩低笑出声，声音有些懒。
他人也懒，抱了林楸好一会儿了还不松开。
门口急着吃饭的兽人们涌进来，见到这一幕，纷纷捂着眼睛咧嘴笑。
那手指岔开的缝隙能再塞一根手指了。
狼岩松开手，直起身，眼神还没扫过去，兽人们就一溜烟跑去拿碗。
狼岩看着火光，想起今天在黑羽部落看到的那一幕，眼底不见暖色。
“今天西边来了个兽人部落，有近两百个兽人。”
“他们是十几个部落残存的兽人组成的。”
“这些部落原本都是中央大陆那边给原野部落上供的那些部落，但因为结束了供奉，就和羽山他们一样，被原野部落的兽人追杀。”
“这些兽人是路上慢慢汇聚在一起的，算是个临时部落。”
“那他们怎么会往我们这边来？”
狼岩原本是去挖盐的。
那边是狼部落和黑羽部落的交界处，能在那里发现他们，说明这些兽人都直接跑到黑羽部落去了。
他们竟然不怕？
狼岩：“有兽人给他们指路。”
林楸看着狼岩那双灰色的眸子，猛地捏住狼岩手臂，道：“豹休？”
“不是同一个兽人给他们指路，也不是豹休。”狼岩勾住林楸细长的手指，轻轻捏了捏说，“其中一个是原野部落自己的兽人，叫豹疤，他本来的名字叫豹文。”
“长什么样？是黑豹兽人吗？”
“身上很多疤痕，脸上贯穿一道伤疤，是黑豹。”
林楸握紧狼岩的手。
“王，你说会不会是豹休？”
他们部落没跟什么豹兽人部落来往，唯一认识且知道他们部落方位的豹兽人，就只有豹休。
狼岩：“也不是不可能。”
林楸细想这个可能性，一时间沉默。
如果真是豹休，那么他需要独自一个兽人从东部大陆走到中央大陆，或许路上他会遇到自己的同伴，但这么远的距离，什么可能性都有。
如果他成功到了中央大陆，要成为原野部落的“刽子手”，还必须得到那边的信任。
这么一两年的时间内，他做得到吗？
林楸细想，便觉得这可能性小了。
“那还有谁指路？”他又问。
“说是云豹兽人。”
林楸还在想他们有没有认识的云豹兽人，狼乔和小队的兽人们就跑过来。
他们瞧着冒烟的锅边缘，急得一直踮脚。
“楸，可以吃了吗？”
林楸回神，看了看锅里，赶紧道：“搅一下，应该可以了。”
……
这边距离原野部落太远，林楸和狼岩都不能确定那豹兽人是谁。
说不定不是豹休，而是个能掐会算的豹兽人确定了他们的方位。
这样的能人，兽神大陆也不是没有。
林楸不纠结了，让狼岩先去吃饭。
他拿了两支蜡烛点燃，放在桌面。
兽人们也饿狠了，抱着碗只顾着往肚里塞。
他们吃的都是晚上亚兽人们从大锅里匀出来的饭菜，炒菜炖菜都有。
部落现在能用花生榨油，饭菜也舍得放油。
油大、盐重，这些菜很下饭。
兽人们吃着，林楸抽空去了一趟雀溪那边。
他悄声进去，却发现雀溪身边蜷缩着一个小小的身影。
幼崽趴在炕边，脑袋挨着雀溪手臂。他也没睡，林楸进来时，他还睁着一双乌黑的眼看来。
“豹枝？你不去睡觉，怎么跑这里来了？”
chapters.title: 第211章

chapters.source_text:
林楸把幼崽抱起来，看了眼雀溪的情况，确认没事，才带着幼崽离开屋内。
广场上昏黑，豹枝抱着林楸脖子，乖乖靠在他肩上。
当初幼崽受惊吓时年纪还小，生了一场病，那些事情就忘了。他现在跟狼生他们玩儿得好，看起来也跟寻常幼崽已经没什么两样。
林楸掌心托着他后背，轻声问他：“是睡不着吗？”
“看他。”
“看雀溪？”
“嗯，看雀溪。”
“他摔到石头上，撞了脑袋。不过他吃了药汤，也包扎好了，多养几天就没事了。”
豹枝直起身，两个小手揣在身前。
他低着头，小脸的软肉挤在一起，鼓鼓的。
原本细胳膊细腿儿的，现在也被狼部落养好了。
“不开心？”
“雀溪要走了。”
“他清醒了，知道自己从哪里来，所以想回自己部落。”
豹枝抬头看着林楸，“那我的部落呢？”
兽人幼崽早熟，林楸并没把他当个什么都不知道的小崽。
“你也想回去？”
“想。”
林楸一怔，握住幼崽搅缠在一起的手道：“好，等雀溪醒了，我们问问他，兴许他知道你的部落在哪儿。”
豹枝呆呆看着林楸，然后又抱住他的脖子，依恋地靠过来。
“我记不起来了……”他失落道。
“没关系，或许有一天会记起来的。”
“那我走了，还能回来吗？”
“狼部落随时欢迎。”
幼崽展颜，软嫩的脸颊贴过来，狠狠蹭了一下林楸。
“我肯定会回来看你们的。”
“好。那现在可以去睡觉了？”
狼岩半晌等不来林楸，出来找他。走过食堂拐角，就看见自家伴侣抱着那云豹幼崽轻声哄。
月光朦胧，他的伴侣也像这月色一样，看着微冷，实际也似月色温柔。
把幼崽送去睡觉后，狼岩牵着林楸想回屋。
他们的屋子也是抽签来的，位置就在广场北边。房子在山脚，走几步路就可以上山。
回了屋，林楸脱了衣服刚一躺下，就被狼岩捞进了怀里。
林楸感觉到后颈贴来的脑袋，拍了拍身前横着的手臂，道：“快睡吧。”
狼岩面颊贴在自家伴侣的发上，闻着淡淡的植物清香，懒懒应声。
他累了一天了，没多久就没了动静。
林楸陪着他躺了一会儿，随后轻轻拿开腰上横着的手臂。他拿了衣服，放轻动作，在一旁穿上。
狼岩怀里一空，便醒了过来。
林楸穿好衣服，转身就看见他睁大的眼睛，笑了声，他坐在床边，双手捂在狼岩的眼睛上。
“我今晚要看着点儿雀溪，你继续睡。”
狼岩双手拢着林楸的腰。
绷紧的肌肉跟铁箍似的，压在后腰上，还在缓缓收紧，林楸呼吸都有些不畅。
“王？”
林楸松开贴在他眼上的手。
见他闭着眼睛，睫都不颤一下。
装睡？
“狼岩？”
狼岩一下侧身，仗着力气大，勾着林楸嵌入怀中，脑袋埋在他颈侧。
林楸无奈，干脆又陪他躺了一会儿。
夜深了。
外面传来细微的动静，放哨的兽人们在换班。
林楸好不容易把腰上的手拿开，出了屋子，走到雀溪那边。
屋里蜡烛燃尽了。
林楸重新拿了一根点燃，刚一放下，便见雀溪是睁着眼睛的。
他吓了一跳，小声问：“我把你吵醒了？”
雀溪张了张嘴，第一下没出声。
林楸给他倒了一杯水，扶着他喝过，雀溪才哑着嗓子道：“自己醒了。”
林楸这会儿离他近，才看清他一头的汗，神色惊惶，眼里还残留着深深的恐惧。
想起他经历的那些，他一时顿住。待感觉到手里的轻轻拉扯，才想起来松开手，看着雀溪往远处挪了挪。
他应该是不习惯别人碰他。
“……我给你端盆热水来，你擦擦身。”
灶里有余烬，灶上温着水，兽人们早上起来的时候直接能用水洗脸。
林楸兑了一盆热水过来，又给他找了一身衣服。
兽人不方便弯腰，他就帮他拧帕子。
林楸坐在凳上，手放在膝上，手指泛红。
他垂眸看着盆中。
炕上窸窸窣窣的，兽人正在慢吞吞擦身。
烛火暗淡，兽人的动作也慢吞吞的，有些费劲儿。
林楸看着水中涟漪，道：“你知道你的部落具体在什么地方吗？从我们这边过去，要多久？”
雀溪捏紧帕子，水珠顺着手指流到手臂上。
他顺着林楸的话，回忆起部落，眼中的惊惧慢慢褪去，换上了怀念和期待。
“我们部落……部落……叫红雀部落。”
“它在西部……大陆南端，部落有一条河……我们经常把食物搬到木筏上，顺着河一直运到海边……我、我知道怎么回去。”
他一直没有忘记部落。
被熊沉抓了那么多年，走了那么远的路，每一次停下来，他就会认认真真地把路线记下来。
每一天，每一夜，每个被关押的时刻，他都要去回忆，只有这样，他才能在灰暗的日子里坚持下去。
这两年虽然痴了，不去想了，会有些遗忘，但路上重要的标志他都记得。
他一下沉浸在记忆中，话也多了起来。
“我们部落专门种水稻，附近的部落都会、都会跟我们交换。大家的兽人吃得饱，长得也好……周围的部落因为我们会种水稻经常跟我们往来，大家都很好。”
“部落很漂亮，很少下雪。那里一年都很暖和，山上什么时候都有瓜果吃……”
林楸静静看着他。
亚兽人思念着故土，原本磕磕绊绊的话说得越来越顺畅。烛光映照着他的一双眸子，清澈温柔。
他满心期待着回去，甚至忘记了这一程的伤痛。
林楸听着，也被他带入那群山下的小部落……他们会在树上建树屋，雨大风大的时候就躲进山洞里。
他们勤劳，会种水稻，会采集山上数不尽的瓜果嫩叶做食物。
兽人每天吃得饱饱的，幼崽安稳长大，年迈的兽人也能承欢膝下。
听着很美好……
这是林楸见过这么多部落后，唯一一个日子过得这么好的部落。
雀溪一口气说了很久，说到自己都忘了头疼，忘了手上已经冷却的帕子，忘了林楸刚刚问过的问题。
他像是要把这些年没开口说出的话全部吐露出来，声音不疾不徐，林楸却能体会他的雀跃，以及对部落的怀念和温柔。
很久之后，说话间，雀溪不经意看着林楸的一双眼睛，注意到其中的笑意，他忽然一怔。
仿佛被这笑意温柔托起，被触碰到心底，声音缓缓停了下来。
雀溪眼眶红了，又是笑，却又想哭。
“对不起……”
“为什么要说对不起？”
“对不起。”
这两年，他是傻了。但有关这两年的记忆并没有丢失。
他知道眼前的兽人是狼部落的领头兽人之一，知道狼部落这么大的变化，都因为他的主意。
他们的到来，给狼部落造成了困扰。
此时此刻，林楸还坐在这里听他说这些没用的话，非但不恼，还静静陪着他。
外面漆黑，这会儿应该不早了吧。
林楸冲着他伸了伸手，示意他把帕子给他，道：“不用说对不起，你又没做错什么。”
盆中水波晃动，雀溪也被泪水模糊了视线。
此刻再想，那些血腥的、恶心的东西被部落的美好压了下去。雀溪再看着眼前这个脸色平静的兽人，仿佛他刚刚那一句话，只是随口一问而已。
可雀溪心思细腻，知道他是故意提起。
“谢谢。”
林楸把帕子递给他，道：“你今天已经说了好多个谢了。”
“该谢的。”
雀溪含泪笑起来，看着却很哀伤。
他想，要不是狼兽人，此刻的他恐怕早没有命在这里想念部落了。
他赶紧接了帕子把自己擦干净，换上衣服。
林楸倒了水回来，他道：“刚刚忘了说……我被熊沉他们从西部大陆带过来，走走停停，走了好几年。从这边过去，我……我确实不知道要走多久。”
“不知道就不知道。”林楸听他的声音更哑了，他道，“天晚了，赶紧躺下睡觉。”
林楸给雀溪换了一张兽皮毯。
亚兽人看着他，慢慢皱起眉头。
“伤口疼了？”
雀溪落在兽皮毯下的手紧紧掐住衣摆，露出个浅笑来。
“你去睡觉吧，不用守着我。”
“没事，快睡吧。”
雀溪闭上眼，脑中这几年的今日与在部落时候的情景反复出现，他有些作呕，身体开始不受控制地颤抖，他极力抓着衣摆，克制着。
他控制自己去想着部落，去想着自己的同伴。
可那一幕幕血色，总会抢先一步，出现在脑海中。
还是睡不着。
头晕，恶心，他胃里翻滚，很想吐。
雀溪紧咬牙，在忍不住之前，忙道：“楸，我可以叫你楸吗？”
“当然。”
“去红雀部落很远……”
他又犹豫了。
他想他的病应该是还没有好，他肯定走不回去了。
他已经麻烦狼部落许多，不能再让他们帮忙。
林楸：“我们会好好考虑的。”
他看着雀溪眼皮下转动的眼珠，问：“你在红雀部落还有亲兽人吗？”
“有……我阿爸阿父都在，阿爷阿奶也在。我还有一窝的两个哥哥，一个妹妹。两个哥哥都有伴侣了，他们也有幼崽。”
“那你们部落真好。”
三代同堂，在兽神大陆上多难得。
“对，我们部落很好。”
“你们那边离海边近？”
“近，很近。沿着河漂流一天就到了。海很大，很漂亮，过了海就是南大陆了。那边有很多南大陆的兽人，他们还有很多海兽人……”
林楸低声引导着亚兽人说话。
慢慢的，雀溪的声音越来越小，直至睡着。
林楸看见了他的颤抖，看见了他强行忍耐着。不出意外，雀溪虽然清醒了，但依旧还有心理问题，但这个林楸和狼部落都帮不上忙。
只能靠他自己。
林楸起身，轻手轻脚挪开凳子，往外走。
门口投来一道影子，兽人就那么无声无息地站在外面。
林楸不用想就知道是谁。
他走到兽人近前，将门带上。
门口略高，林楸站在上面，视线正好与狼岩齐平。
他低声问：“怎么又醒了？”
狼岩双臂展开，正好圈在他腰上。手臂收紧，一提，便将他抱起往他们自己的房子走。
林楸摸了摸他耳朵，轻轻打个哈欠，枕在他肩上。
他其实也困了。
“以后让别的兽人守。”
“谁守？祭司、冰、乐还是雪？”
“我守。”
林楸低声一笑，额头往他肩上蹭了蹭，“你守我放心，兽人多半不敢放心。”
“你放心就可以。”
目前，部落里能治病的兽人也没几个。
狼冰已经把该学的都学了。祭司年迈，精力不足，他也担起下一任祭司的责任，部落兽人们有什么小伤小病都在狼冰这里看。
狼冰不行的，或是他不在部落，兽人们才会找祭司。
狼冰现在也不轻松，祭司的各种事情都落在他身上，他还要牵头培育种植草药，忙起来都不见人。
羽乐留在狼部落学治病，开始得晚，还没出师。现在也跟在狼冰后头到处跑，两个兽人天天去山里打转，忙得不行。
除开他俩，部落就只有一个小不点狼雪在学治病。
“还是少了。”林楸道。
“再让祭司选几个幼崽教。”
林楸见狼岩一句话就懂了他的意思，笑着蹭了下他肩膀。
狼岩的体温比他高些，刚从床上起来，上衣也没穿。他的肩膀很宽，皮肤摸着发紧，靠上去跟靠在藤枕上似的，很紧实的感觉。
“祭司教狼雪一个都说累了。”
“他现在有空就去钓鱼，一坐就是一天，没看见他累。”
“祭司头发都白完了……忙了一辈子了，该让他歇一歇。”
“嗯，别愁他了。”狼岩把林楸按在兽皮毯上，捏着兽皮毯两个角将他一裹，直接卷了两圈，再搂进怀里。
林楸手脚动弹不得，只能用眼睛瞪他。
“我还要出去。”
狼岩手脚缠上来，林楸扬起脖子，感觉呼吸都不畅了。
“王……唔！”
狼岩叼着那修长的颈，“别想。”
*
林楸昨晚熬到很晚，早上狼岩起身他都没感觉。
睡到日上三竿，林楸直接被饿醒了。
阳光透过窗棂，有些刺眼，林楸虚着眼睛往窗外瞧了一眼，立马把手臂横在脸上。
门被推开，听到熟悉的脚步声，林楸唇角翘了起来。
手臂被拉开，目之所及是自家伴侣的俊脸。
林楸抬手摸了摸，道：“雀溪怎么样？”
狼岩握住他手腕，往小臂内侧的软肉上咬了一口。
“牙痒？要换牙？”
狼岩搂着他腰将他抱起来，闭口不言。
林楸一笑，靠在他胸口，身上没什么力气。
“王，我好饿啊……”
狼岩摸了摸他的脸，声音隔着胸腔传来，震得林楸耳朵发麻，“留了饭菜的。”
“雀溪呢？”
狼岩把他从兽皮卷里拨出来，又不说话了。
“雀溪？”林楸仰头追问。
狼岩盯着他，又往他鼻尖咬了一口。
“没问题。”
林楸弯眼笑。
是吃醋吧？
小心眼，这都醋。
这会儿食堂里兽人们正忙。
大家都在准备午饭了，林楸却刚刚起来。
早上吃的简单，一个鸡蛋韭菜饼，一碗尾巴草籽粥，还有亚兽人们腌制的下饭小菜。
整个食堂就林楸坐在桌旁吃，狼安瞧着他眼下发青，道：“昨晚守了多久？”
“守到狼石他们换班的时候。”
“也不早了。”
“吃完饭我再去他那边看看。”
“我们刚刚才去看完回来……”狼安看了一眼窗外，声音低了下去，“他清醒是清醒了，可瞧着比以前傻的时候更难过，吃也吃不了多少，睡也没见他睡得多好。”
林楸：“他脑袋受了伤，头疼，睡也睡不好。”
再多的原因，兽人们心照不宣，也不去戳人家伤疤。
“他这样怕是要养很久，楸，你和王打算什么时候让兽人们出发？你们两个还跟着去？”
“这事儿还没商量呢。”林楸笑说，“你们不阻止了？”
狼安又想起狼影，忍不住抓紧了刀柄，往菜板上剁了两下。
“又叫影来笑我们？”他没好气道。
“狼影是那脾气。”
*
食堂的烟囱上往外冒白烟，林楸就着炖肉的香味，吃过了这不早不晚的一餐。
他洗了碗筷，刚走到碗柜前，就看到几辆板车驶入广场前。板车的木头车轱辘换成了铁轱辘，好用得很，跑在兽人们修的路上，轻若无物似的，兽人们带东西往来大泽和狼山，也轻松不少。
这会儿兽人们正忙着煮盐。
那十几口大锅一字排开，兽人站在漆黑的大铁锅前，搅动盐水，热气腾腾，场面很是壮观。
板车一停，高高堆积的兽皮袋后头，走出来一个兽人。
他神色慌张，看来看去，踟蹰着没动。
“是来看雀溪的吧？”铁锅边忙活的兽人问。
兽人是羊止。
他之前一直跟雀溪形影不离的，雀溪受伤，他心里发慌，今早就央求着狼兽人带他回来看看雀溪。
羊止被兽人突然出声吓得一哆嗦。
他双手捏在身前衣摆，肩背佝偻，格外小心谨慎，道：“是看雀溪。”
兽人给他指了指屋子。
他立马埋头快速穿过广场，走到了那边屋子。全程低着头，不敢乱看。
林楸看完，走了出去。
狼金见了林楸，咧着个嘴巴就道：“楸！我们回来了。”
“板车拉的是什么？”
“狮也跟我们交换的草药和兽皮。他们还要换小红鸟。”
“那你找狼溶去。”
这几年，自从白雀部落和他们换了红鸟之后，南边几个部落也慢慢开始跟他们交换起红鸟苗。
小红鸟脆弱，原本还不好带回去。
不过现在有黑羽兽人帮忙，去哪里就是飞一趟的事情。
就靠着他们，狼部落这交换红鸟的生意目前已经覆盖了白雀部落、大狮部落、小猫部落、黑羊部落在内的十几个部落。
连近两年新搬来的周边部落也开始和他们交换小红鸟。
“等会儿去找狼溶。楸，有饭吗？我们好饿！”
“要等一会儿。”狼安在窗边道。
“安！要吃肉！！！”狼兽人们扯着嗓子就喊，活像狼安上了年纪耳朵不行了，听得站在近处的林楸脑子都嗡嗡响。
好吵。
林楸忙走开了些，听着屋里传来的笑骂声，也跟着舒展眉头，面上带了笑。
“楸！你别走啊。”
“没走。”就是嫌他们吵。
狼金指挥着同伴把东西卸下来，林楸打开看了看，草药品质还是和以前一样。
他把草药分了类，指挥着小狼们放祭司山洞里去。
又看了看兽皮，也叫他们先存山洞，以后有用。
事情做完，狼金带着自己的小狼队进食堂里守食去了。
林楸原本打算去看看雀溪，现在羊止在，两个兽人想必要说说话，他等会儿再去。
他目光转了一圈，看狼溶在红鸟圈前跟狼岩说话，走了过去。
他走得慢，目光划过熟悉的伴侣，落在狼溶身上。
小狼这两年变化挺大，身高一下子拔高了，以前他是那几个伙伴中个子最小的，现在都赶得上狼金了。
以前小脸还白白净净的，现在皮肤完全晒成了小麦色。
“……北边草原的草还没长多少，再等等。”
林楸听了一耳，看着狼岩伸过来的手，顺势将手放在他掌中。
“要去北边放咩咩兽？”林楸问。
“今年该过去了。”
部落现在有两百多头咩咩兽，原本关咩咩兽的围栏都有些小了。
他们现在一般是雪季让咩咩兽在这边过冬，喂的是储存的牧草。
雪季过后，草长出来了，就把咩咩兽往北赶。
兽人会跟着，一直放牧到北部草原，雨季的时候就直接驻扎在北部草原。
前头两年也差不多是这个时间前后，狼溶就赶咩咩兽过去了。
“狼金回来要带小红鸟走。溶，小红鸟现在有多少？”
“两百三十一只，够。”
林楸点点头。
他过来只简单说了几句话，便靠着狼岩，听着他们继续商量。
狼部落北边，原野部落的兽人已经被他们清理了一遍，目前来说应该还算安全。
但这么多咩咩兽，肯定不能只让狼溶他们跟着去。
狼岩跟狼溶说着安排哪些兽人跟过去，林楸就静静听着，也不说话，浑身懒懒地靠着狼岩。
现在用他操心的事不多，每天就是在狼山转转，看看这个小队建墙，瞧瞧那个小队种地，有时候顺手帮一帮忙。
不过做不了多久，兽人们就赶他去休息。
无非是去年忙得太狠，兽人们被他指挥得团团转都没倒下，他却倒了。
狼部落就没出过这样的事情。
林楸那一躺，当场给兽人吓得够呛，现在都有心理阴影了。
林楸也很抱歉，那段时间正是收尾巴草最忙的时候，狼岩偏还拘着他在屋里躺了七八天，他也不敢再消耗自己。
站得累了，他又往东边走。
瞧见老祭司在钓鱼，走过去直接坐在草地上。
方一坐好，老祭司就道：“我是不会同意狼冰跟你们一起去的。”
林楸一想就明白过来，狼冰肯定跟他说了要去西边的事。
“祭司，我又没撺掇狼冰。”
“哼！就是你们天天往外跑，把他心也带野了。”
林楸白眼一翻，很不雅。
也就他敢在祭司面前这样。
祭司看得直吹胡子，手里一抖，刚刚咬钩的鱼也跑掉了。
瞧着拉起来的鱼钩空荡荡的，他拍下鱼竿，硬声硬气道：“你跟他说，让他别去。”
林楸正想玩笑着回，一抬头，看着祭司浑浊的眼里闪过的隐痛，玩笑的心思顿时歇了。
“我……”
“你说的话他听。”
“别为难楸。”狼岩过来，直接驳了老祭司的话。
“那你说！”老祭司没好气道。
“你把他带大的，你比我们更了解他。”
祭司鱼竿一抛，抓起拐杖，气冲冲地就离开了。
林楸：“看看……生气了。”
狼岩：“走得这么快，说明身体挺好，再让他教几个幼崽也可以。”
“你想都不要想！”
狼岩唇角一勾。
“说话也中气十足，再多教几个没问题。”
祭司顿时走得更快了。
林楸曲指点了点狼岩膝头，“你悠着点。”
狼岩看着老祭司的背影，想到曾经那一场让狼部落损失大半兽人的惨烈大战，他握紧林楸的手压在膝上，眼神微微失焦。
“不这样，他永远走不出来。”

Lin Qiu picked up the cub, glanced at Que Xi’s condition, and after confirming he was fine, left the room with the cub.

The plaza was dim, and Bao Zhi hugged Lin Qiu’s neck, leaning obediently against his shoulder.

When the cub was first frightened, he was still young and fell ill, causing him to forget those events. Now that he played well with Lang Sheng and the others, he looked no different from any ordinary cub.

Lin Qiu supported the cub’s back with his palm and asked softly, "Can't you sleep?"

"Looking at him."

"Looking at Que Xi?"

"Mm, looking at Que Xi."

"He fell onto a rock and hit his head. But he has taken the medicinal soup and has been bandaged up; he’ll be fine after resting for a few more days."

Bao Zhi straightened up, tucking his two little hands in front of him.

He lowered his head, the soft flesh of his little face bunched together, looking puffy.

He had originally been thin and scrawny, but now he had been well-nourished by the Wolf Tribe.

"Are you unhappy?"

"Que Xi is leaving."

"He has regained his senses and knows where he came from, so he wants to return to his own tribe."

Bao Zhi looked up at Lin Qiu, "Then what about my tribe?"

Beastman cubs matured early; Lin Qiu didn't treat him like a child who knew nothing.

"Do you want to go back too?"

"I do."

Lin Qiu was startled. He held the cub’s intertwined hands and said, "Alright, when Que Xi wakes up, we’ll ask him. Perhaps he knows where your tribe is."

Bao Zhi stared blankly at Lin Qiu, then hugged his neck again, leaning in with attachment.

"I can't remember..." he said, feeling lost.

"It’s okay, perhaps one day you will remember."

"Then if I leave, can I come back?"

"The Wolf Tribe welcomes you anytime."

The cub beamed, pressing his soft, tender cheek against Lin Qiu and rubbing hard.

"I will definitely come back to see you all."

"Good. Can you go to sleep now?"

Lang Yan had waited for a while but didn't see Lin Qiu, so he came out to look for him. Walking past the corner of the cafeteria, he saw his partner holding the clouded leopard cub and coaxing him softly.

The moonlight was hazy, and his partner looked just like the moonlight—seemingly cold, but actually as gentle as the lunar glow.

After sending the cub to sleep, Lang Yan took Lin Qiu’s hand, wanting to return to their room.

Their house had also been obtained through a lottery, located on the north side of the plaza. The house was at the foot of the mountain, just a few steps away from the mountain path.

Back in the room, as soon as Lin Qiu took off his clothes and lay down, he was scooped into Lang Yan’s arms.

Feeling the head resting against his nape, Lin Qiu patted the arm draped across his chest and said, "Go to sleep."

Lang Yan pressed his cheek against his partner’s hair, smelling the faint, fresh scent of plants, and responded lazily.

He had been tired all day, and before long, he fell silent.

Lin Qiu lay with him for a while, then gently moved the arm across his waist. He picked up his clothes and, moving quietly, put them on.

Feeling the emptiness in his arms, Lang Yan woke up.

Once Lin Qiu was dressed, he turned around to see Lang Yan’s wide-open eyes. He chuckled, sat on the edge of the bed, and covered Lang Yan’s eyes with his hands.

"I need to keep an eye on Que Xi tonight, you keep sleeping."

Lang Yan wrapped his arms around Lin Qiu’s waist.

His tensed muscles felt like iron hoops pressing against his lower back, slowly tightening, making it hard for Lin Qiu to breathe.

"King?"

Lin Qiu released the hands covering his eyes.

Seeing him keep his eyes closed without even a flicker of his lashes.

Pretending to be asleep?

"Lang Yan?"

Lang Yan suddenly turned on his side, relying on his superior strength to hook Lin Qiu into his embrace, burying his head in the crook of his neck.

Lin Qiu sighed helplessly and simply lay with him for a while longer.

The night deepened.

Faint movements came from outside; the sentry beastmen were changing shifts.

Lin Qiu finally managed to remove the hand from his waist, left the room, and walked over to where Que Xi was.

The candle in the room had burned out.

Lin Qiu lit a new one, and as soon as he set it down, he saw that Que Xi’s eyes were open.

He was startled and asked in a low voice, "Did I wake you up?"

Que Xi opened his mouth, but no sound came out at first.

Lin Qiu poured him a cup of water and helped him drink it. Only then did Que Xi say in a hoarse voice, "I woke up on my own."

Only now, being close to him, did Lin Qiu see the sweat on his forehead, his panicked expression, and the lingering, deep fear in his eyes.

Remembering what he had been through, he paused. When he felt a gentle tug on his hand, he remembered to let go, watching as Que Xi shifted further away.

He must not be used to being touched by others.

"...I'll bring you a basin of hot water so you can wipe yourself down."

There were embers in the stove, and water was kept warm on it so the beastmen could wash their faces directly when they woke up in the morning.

Lin Qiu brought over a basin of hot water and found him a set of clothes.

Since the beastman couldn't easily bend over, he helped him wring out the towel.

Lin Qiu sat on a stool, his hands resting on his knees, his fingers turning red.

He lowered his eyes to look into the basin.

There was a rustling sound from the kang; the beastman was slowly wiping his body.

The candlelight was dim, and the beastman’s movements were slow and laborious.

Watching the ripples in the water, Lin Qiu asked, "Do you know exactly where your tribe is? How long would it take to get there from here?"

Que Xi gripped the towel tightly, water droplets running down his fingers onto his arm.

Following Lin Qiu’s lead, he recalled his tribe, the terror in his eyes slowly fading, replaced by nostalgia and anticipation.

"Our tribe... the tribe... is called the Red Sparrow Tribe."

"It’s in the west... at the southern end of the continent. There is a river in the tribe... we often load food onto rafts and transport it down the river to the seaside... I, I know how to go back."

He had never forgotten his tribe.

Captured by Xiong Chen for so many years, having traveled such a long way, every time they stopped, he would carefully memorize the route.

Every day, every night, every moment he was imprisoned, he would recall it; only in this way could he persevere through the dark days.

Although he had been mentally muddled for the past two years and stopped thinking about it, leading to some forgetfulness, he still remembered the important landmarks along the way.

Immersed in his memories, he became more talkative.

"Our tribe specializes in growing rice, and nearby tribes would always... always trade with us. Everyone’s beastmen were well-fed and grew up strong... because we grow rice, the surrounding tribes often interacted with us, and everyone was very kind."

"The tribe is very beautiful, and it rarely snows. It’s warm there all year round, and there are always melons and fruits to eat on the mountains..."

Lin Qiu watched him quietly.

The sub-beastman missed his homeland, and his once-stumbling speech became increasingly fluent. The candlelight reflected in his eyes, which were clear and gentle.

He was filled with anticipation about returning, even forgetting the pain of this journey.

Listening, Lin Qiu was also drawn into that small tribe beneath the mountains... they would build treehouses, and when the rain and wind were heavy, they would hide in caves.

They were hardworking, growing rice and gathering the endless melons, fruits, and tender leaves from the mountains for food.

The beastmen were well-fed every day, the cubs grew up safely, and the elderly beastmen could enjoy their twilight years surrounded by family.

It sounded wonderful...

This was the only tribe Lin Qiu had seen, out of so many, that lived such a good life.

Que Xi spoke in one breath for a long time, until he forgot his headache, forgot the towel that had already cooled in his hand, and forgot the question Lin Qiu had just asked.

It was as if he wanted to pour out all the words he hadn't been able to say over these years. His voice was steady and unhurried, yet Lin Qiu could feel his excitement, as well as his nostalgia and tenderness for his tribe.

A long time later, while speaking, Que Xi inadvertently looked into Lin Qiu’s eyes and noticed the smile within them; he suddenly froze.

As if gently lifted by this smile and touched deep in his heart, his voice slowly trailed off.

Que Xi’s eyes reddened; he was smiling, yet he also wanted to cry.

"I'm sorry..."

"Why are you saying sorry?"

"I'm sorry."

For the past two years, he had been foolish. But the memories of those two years were not lost.

He knew the beastman before him was one of the leaders of the Wolf Tribe, and he knew that the Wolf Tribe’s massive changes were all due to his ideas.

Their arrival had caused trouble for the Wolf Tribe.

At this very moment, Lin Qiu was still sitting here listening to him talk about these useless things, not only not annoyed but quietly keeping him company.

It was pitch black outside; it must be quite late now.

Lin Qiu reached out to him, signaling for him to give him the towel, and said, "No need to say sorry, you haven't done anything wrong."

The water in the basin rippled, and Que Xi’s vision blurred with tears.

Thinking about it now, the bloody, disgusting things were suppressed by the beauty of his tribe. Que Xi looked at this calm-faced beastman again, as if that previous question had just been a casual inquiry.

But Que Xi was sensitive and knew he had brought it up on purpose.

"Thank you."

Lin Qiu handed him the towel and said, "You’ve already said thank you many times today."

"It’s worth thanking."

Que Xi smiled through his tears, looking very sorrowful.

He thought, if it weren't for the wolf beastmen, he probably wouldn't be alive right now to miss his tribe.

He hurriedly took the towel, wiped himself clean, and changed his clothes.

After Lin Qiu poured out the water and returned, he said, "I forgot to mention just now... I was brought over from the Western Continent by Xiong Chen and his group, traveling and stopping for several years. From here, I... I really don't know how long it will take."

"If you don't know, you don't know." Lin Qiu heard his voice become even hoarser and said, "It's late, lie down and go to sleep."

Lin Qiu changed the animal skin blanket for Que Xi.

The sub-beastman looked at him, his brows slowly furrowing.

"Is the wound hurting?"

Que Xi’s hand under the blanket gripped his hem tightly, revealing a faint smile.

"You go to sleep, no need to watch over me."

"It's fine, go to sleep."

Que Xi closed his eyes. The scenes of the past few years and the scenes from his tribe appeared repeatedly in his mind. He felt nauseous, and his body began to tremble uncontrollably. He tried his best to grip his hem, restraining himself.

He forced himself to think about his tribe, to think about his companions.

But those bloody scenes would always appear in his mind first.

He still couldn't sleep.

Dizzy and nauseous, his stomach churned, and he felt like vomiting.

Que Xi bit his lip tightly, and before he couldn't hold it back anymore, he hurriedly said, "Qiu, can I call you Qiu?"

"Of course."

"Going to the Red Sparrow Tribe is very far..."

He hesitated again.

He thought his illness probably hadn't healed yet; he definitely couldn't walk back.

He had already troubled the Wolf Tribe enough and couldn't let them help anymore.

Lin Qiu: "We will consider it carefully."

He watched the eyeballs moving beneath Que Xi’s eyelids and asked, "Do you still have family in the Red Sparrow Tribe?"

"Yes... my father and papa are both there, and my grandpa and grandma are too. I also have two older brothers and a younger sister. Both brothers have partners, and they have cubs too."

"Then your tribe is truly wonderful."

Three generations living under one roof—how rare that was on the Beast God Continent.

"Yes, our tribe is very good."

"Is your side close to the seaside?"

"Close, very close. Drifting along the river for a day and you arrive. The sea is huge and very beautiful. Across the sea is the Southern Continent. There are many beastmen from the Southern Continent there, and they have many sea beastmen..."

Lin Qiu whispered, guiding the sub-beastman to speak.

Slowly, Que Xi’s voice became smaller and smaller until he fell asleep.

Lin Qiu saw his trembling and saw him forcing himself to endure. Not surprisingly, although Que Xi had regained his senses, he still had psychological issues, but this was something neither Lin Qiu nor the Wolf Tribe could help with.

He could only rely on himself.

Lin Qiu stood up, moved the stool away on tiptoe, and walked outside.

A shadow was cast at the doorway; the beastman was standing outside silently.

Lin Qiu didn't need to think to know who it was.

He walked up to the beastman and closed the door.

The threshold was slightly raised; Lin Qiu stood on it, his line of sight perfectly level with Lang Yan’s.

He asked in a low voice, "Why are you awake again?"

Lang Yan spread his arms, circling his waist. He tightened his grip, lifted him up, and walked toward their own house.

Lin Qiu touched his ear, gave a light yawn, and rested his head on his shoulder.

He was actually sleepy too.

"Let other beastmen keep watch from now on."

"Who should watch? Priest, Bing, Le, or Xue?"

"I will watch."

Lin Qiu chuckled softly, rubbing his forehead against his shoulder, "I’m at ease if you watch, but most beastmen probably wouldn't be."

"As long as you are at ease, that’s enough."

Currently, there were few beastmen in the tribe who could treat illnesses.

Lang Bing had already learned everything he should. The priest was elderly and lacked energy, so he had also taken on the responsibilities of the next priest. The tribe’s beastmen went to Lang Bing for any minor injuries or illnesses.

Only if Lang Bing couldn't handle it, or if he wasn't in the tribe, would the beastmen go to the priest.

Lang Bing wasn't having an easy time either; all the priest’s various tasks fell on him, and he also had to lead the cultivation of medicinal herbs, so he was never seen when he was busy.

Yu Le stayed in the Wolf Tribe to learn medicine, but he started late and hadn't finished his apprenticeship. Now he followed Lang Bing everywhere, and the two beastmen spent their days running around in the mountains, extremely busy.

Aside from them, the tribe only had little Lang Xue learning medicine.

"It's still too few," Lin Qiu said.

"Let the priest choose a few more cubs to teach."

Seeing that Lang Yan understood his meaning with just one sentence, Lin Qiu smiled and rubbed his shoulder.

Lang Yan’s body temperature was higher than his, and having just gotten out of bed, he wasn't wearing a top. His shoulders were broad, his skin felt taut to the touch, and leaning against him felt like leaning on a rattan pillow—very firm and solid.

"The priest says he's tired just teaching Lang Xue alone."

"He goes fishing whenever he has free time, sitting there for a whole day; I don't see him being tired."

"The priest’s hair has all turned white... he’s been busy his whole life, it’s time to let him rest."

"Mm, don't worry about him." Lang Yan pressed Lin Qiu onto an animal skin blanket, pinched the two corners to wrap him up, rolled him twice, and pulled him into his arms.

Lin Qiu couldn't move his hands or feet and could only glare at him.

"I still need to go out."

Lang Yan wrapped his limbs around him; Lin Qiu lifted his neck, feeling like he couldn't breathe.

"King... Mmph!"

Lang Yan nibbled on that slender neck, "Don't even think about it."

*

Lin Qiu had stayed up very late last night, and he didn't even feel Lang Yan get up in the morning.

Sleeping until the sun was high, Lin Qiu was woken up directly by hunger.

The sunlight through the window lattice was a bit blinding; Lin Qiu squinted at the window and immediately threw his arm across his face.

The door was pushed open, and hearing the familiar footsteps, the corners of Lin Qiu’s lips curled up.

His arm was pulled away, and what met his eyes was his partner’s handsome face.

Lin Qiu reached out to touch it and asked, "How is Que Xi?"

Lang Yan gripped his wrist and took a bite of the soft flesh on the inside of his forearm.

"Teeth itchy? Need to change teeth?"

Lang Yan hugged his waist and lifted him up, remaining silent.

Lin Qiu smiled, leaning against his chest, feeling weak.

"King, I'm so hungry..."

Lang Yan touched his face, his voice coming through his chest, making Lin Qiu’s ears tingle, "I left food for you."

"What about Que Xi?"

Lang Yan pulled him out of the animal skin roll and didn't speak again.

"Que Xi?" Lin Qiu looked up and pressed.

Lang Yan stared at him and took another bite of his nose.

"No problem."

Lin Qiu’s eyes curved into a smile.

Is he jealous?

Small-minded, jealous even over this.

At this moment, the beastmen in the cafeteria were busy.

Everyone was preparing lunch, but Lin Qiu had just gotten up.

Breakfast was simple: an egg and chive pancake, a bowl of tail-grass seed porridge, and some side dishes pickled by the sub-beastmen.

In the whole cafeteria, only Lin Qiu sat at the table eating. Lang An noticed the dark circles under his eyes and asked, "How long did you watch last night?"

"Until Lang Shi and the others changed shifts."

"That's not early."

"I'll go check on him again after I finish eating."

"We just came back from checking on him..." Lang An looked out the window, his voice dropping, "He is awake, but he looks even sadder than when he was foolish. He can't eat much, and he doesn't seem to be sleeping well either."

Lin Qiu: "He suffered a head injury, has headaches, and can't sleep well."

As for other reasons, the beastmen knew without saying, and they didn't poke at others' scars.

"He’s going to need a long time to recover like this. Qiu, when do you and the King plan to let the beastmen set off? Are you two going to follow?"

"We haven't discussed that yet," Lin Qiu said with a smile, "Are you not going to stop us?"

Lang An thought of Lang Ying again, couldn't help but tighten his grip on the knife handle, and chopped twice on the cutting board.

"Calling Ying to laugh at us again?" he said irritably.

"That’s just Lang Ying’s temperament."

*

White smoke rose from the cafeteria’s chimney, and Lin Qiu ate this neither-early-nor-late meal accompanied by the scent of stewed meat.

He washed his bowl and chopsticks, and just as he walked to the cupboard, he saw several flatbed carts entering the plaza. The wooden wheels of the carts had been replaced with iron ones, which were very useful. Running on the roads built by the beastmen, they felt as light as nothing, making it much easier for the beastmen to transport goods between Daze and Wolf Mountain.

At this moment, the beastmen were busy boiling salt.

The dozen or so large pots were lined up, with beastmen standing in front of the pitch-black iron pots, stirring the brine. It was steaming, and the scene was quite spectacular.

As the cart stopped, a beastman emerged from behind the high-piled animal skin bags.

He looked flustered, glancing around, hesitating and not moving.

"Are you here to see Que Xi?" the beastman busy by the iron pot asked.

The beastman was Yang Zhi.

He had been inseparable from Que Xi before; with Que Xi injured, he felt panicked and had begged the wolf beastmen to bring him back to see Que Xi this morning.

Yang Zhi was startled by the beastman’s sudden voice and shivered.

He held his hands in front of his chest, his back hunched, being extra cautious, and said, "I'm here to see Que Xi."

The beastman pointed him toward the house.

He immediately buried his head and quickly crossed the plaza, walking to that house. He kept his head down the whole time, not daring to look around.

After watching, Lin Qiu walked out.

Seeing Lin Qiu, Lang Jin grinned and said, "Qiu! We’re back."

"What’s on the flatbed carts?"

"Medicinal herbs and animal skins traded with the Lion Tribe. They also want to trade for little red birds."

"Then go find Lang Rong."

In the past few years, ever since the White Sparrow Tribe traded red birds with them, several tribes in the south had slowly started trading for red bird seedlings with them as well.

Little red birds were fragile and originally hard to bring back.

But now with the help of the Black Feather beastmen, going anywhere was just a matter of a flight.

Relying on them, the Wolf Tribe’s red bird trading business now covered more than a dozen tribes, including the White Sparrow Tribe, Great Lion Tribe, Little Cat Tribe, and Black Sheep Tribe.

Even the surrounding tribes that had moved in over the last two years had started trading for little red birds with them.

"I’ll go find Lang Rong in a bit. Qiu, is there food? We’re so hungry!"

"You have to wait a while," Lang An said from the window.

"An! We want to eat meat!!!" the wolf beastmen shouted at the top of their lungs, as if Lang An were old and hard of hearing, making Lin Qiu’s head buzz as he stood nearby.

So noisy.

Lin Qiu hurriedly walked away, listening to the laughter and scolding coming from the room, and his brows relaxed, a smile appearing on his face.

"Qiu! Don't go."

"I'm not going." Just annoyed by their noise.

Lang Jin directed his companions to unload the goods. Lin Qiu opened them to take a look; the quality of the medicinal herbs was the same as before.

He sorted the herbs and directed the little wolves to put them in the priest’s cave.

He looked at the animal skins and told them to store them in the cave for future use.

Once the work was done, Lang Jin led his little wolf team into the cafeteria to guard their food.

Lin Qiu had originally planned to see Que Xi, but now that Yang Zhi was there, the two beastmen would surely want to talk, so he would go later.

His gaze swept around, and seeing Lang Rong talking to Lang Yan in front of the red bird enclosure, he walked over.

He walked slowly, his gaze passing over his familiar partner and landing on Lang Rong.

The little wolf had changed quite a bit in the last two years; his height had shot up. He used to be the smallest among his companions, but now he was catching up to Lang Jin.

His face used to be fair and clean, but now his skin was completely tanned to a wheat color.

"...The grass in the northern grasslands hasn't grown much yet, wait a bit longer."

Lin Qiu listened for a moment, and seeing Lang Yan’s hand reaching out, he placed his hand in his palm.

"Going to the north to graze the sheep-beasts?" Lin Qiu asked.

"It's time to go this year."

The tribe now had over two hundred sheep-beasts, and the original enclosure was a bit small.

They usually let the sheep-beasts spend the winter here during the snowy season, feeding them stored forage.

After the snowy season, when the grass grew, they would drive the sheep-beasts north.

The beastmen would follow, grazing them all the way to the northern grasslands, and during the rainy season, they would station themselves directly in the northern grasslands.

It was around this time in the previous two years that Lang Rong had driven the sheep-beasts over.

"Lang Jin is coming back to take the little red birds. Rong, how many little red birds are there now?"

"Two hundred and thirty-one, enough."

Lin Qiu nodded.

He had only said a few simple words when he came over, then leaned against Lang Yan, listening to them continue their discussion.

To the north of the Wolf Tribe, the beastmen of the Wilderness Tribe had already been cleared out by them, so it should be safe for now.

But with so many sheep-beasts, they definitely couldn't just let Lang Rong and his team go alone.

Lang Yan was discussing with Lang Rong which beastmen to send along, and Lin Qiu listened quietly without speaking, leaning lazily against Lang Yan.

There wasn't much for him to worry about now; he spent his days wandering around Wolf Mountain, watching one team build walls, another team farm, and sometimes helping out.

But he couldn't do it for long before the beastmen would chase him off to rest.

It was nothing more than the fact that he had been too busy last year, and the beastmen had been run ragged by his orders while he collapsed.

Such a thing had never happened in the Wolf Tribe before.

Lin Qiu’s collapse had scared the beastmen half to death, and they now had psychological shadows.

Lin Qiu felt very sorry; that period was the busiest time for harvesting tail-grass, and Lang Yan had kept him lying in the room for seven or eight days, so he didn't dare to overexert himself again.

Tired of standing, he walked toward the east.

Seeing the old priest fishing, he walked over and sat directly on the grass.

As soon as he sat down, the old priest said, "I will not agree to let Lang Bing go with you."

Lin Qiu understood immediately; Lang Bing must have told him about going to the west.

"Priest, I didn't incite Lang Bing."

"Hmph! It's because you all run outside every day, making his heart wild too."

Lin Qiu rolled his eyes, which was very unrefined.

Only he dared to do that in front of the priest.

The priest was so angry his beard blew, and his hand shook, causing the fish that had just taken the bait to escape.

Looking at the empty hook, he slapped his fishing rod down and said stiffly, "You tell him not to go."

Lin Qiu was about to reply jokingly, but when he looked up and saw the hidden pain flashing in the priest’s cloudy eyes, his playful mood vanished.

"I..."

"He listens to what you say."

"Don't make things difficult for Qiu." Lang Yan came over and directly refuted the old priest’s words.

"Then you say it!" the old priest said irritably.

"You raised him; you know him better than we do."

The priest threw his fishing rod, grabbed his cane, and stormed off angrily.

Lin Qiu: "Look... he's angry."

Lang Yan: "Walking so fast shows his body is quite healthy; letting him teach a few more cubs is fine."

"Don't even think about it!"

Lang Yan’s lips curled.

"His voice is full of energy; teaching a few more is no problem."

The priest immediately walked even faster.

Lin Qiu tapped Lang Yan’s knee with his finger, "Take it easy."

Lang Yan looked at the old priest’s back, thinking of the fierce battle that had caused the Wolf Tribe to lose most of its beastmen. He gripped Lin Qiu’s hand tightly on his knee, his eyes slightly unfocused.

"If he doesn't do this, he will never be able to move on."
