chapters.source_text:
广场上，狼果又把幼崽带出来晒太阳了。
他拿了几个大藤筐，筐里缝了一层兽皮，坐着很柔软。
幼崽数量多，狼果、狼菇、羽江各自抱着一个藤筐才装得下。
幼崽不安分，互相挤着，一些踩着同伴的身体往外爬，还有些直起身，前爪搭在藤筐边缘，爬不出来就哼哼唧唧。
狼果一边稳住藤筐，一边等他们爬到一半就往筐里一拨。
幼崽倒进筐里，嗷地大叫一声，不服气似地。
狼果捏住幼崽嘴筒子，笑眯眯道：“小狼崽子，你吵到我耳朵了。”
“呜呜呜……”
“呜……”
幼崽挣扎的呜呜声与屋里压低的哭声交叠，刚刚还闹腾的幼崽一下安静下来，警惕地竖着小耳朵听。
狼果看了一眼身侧的房子，是祭司治病的地方。
“里面怎么了？”狼菇轻声问。
羽江：“是个陌生兽人的声音。”
狼果示意他两个离开，等走到广场上，离那屋子远了，他才道：“是那个跟雀溪一起被救回来的羊兽人。”
屋子里。
哭声一静。
羊止捂着嘴，坐在雀溪旁边，单薄的肩膀轻颤，脊背愈发弯了下去。
“你别哭了……”雀溪温声安抚，他声音也虚弱，脸上不见颜色。
羊止却止不住地流泪。
“你走了，我怎么办……”
羊止一来，看到雀溪的伤口被狼兽人包扎好了就忍不住为他高兴。
可还没说上几句话，就听雀溪说他自己打算回部落去。
鹿叶走了，羊止在这里唯一能说得上话的就是雀溪。他胆子小，始终惧怕着狼兽人，这两年又和雀溪形影不离，在狼部落根本没交到什么朋友。
他本以为这里只有他和雀溪相依为命，哪知道一来就听到他要抛下自己离开。
羊止一下觉得天都塌了。
他反反复复说道：“你走了我怎么办……你走了我怎么办……”
雀溪忍住一抽一抽的头疼，伸出手，握住他的手腕。
“狼部落很好，你在这边都几年了，也没少吃少穿的，我走了你依旧能跟着他们，不用怕。”
“我怕，我就是怕。”羊止扑倒在炕边，紧紧抓住雀溪的手，“……你不走，不走好不好……”
他泪流不止，惊恐又期冀地看着雀溪，如同洪水中的人抓住了浮木，力气极大，捏得雀溪手泛白。
“溪，我们不走好不好。在狼部落能吃饱，也没有危险，不走行不行……”
“止。”雀溪眼皮低垂，有些无力地被他扯着手，拉得身体都倾斜了。
可无论羊止怎么哭，怎么哀求，他都没松口。
“止，我想回部落。”
“可我呢？！我没有部落了。”羊止崩溃道。
“所以你就在狼部落好好的，这里不会再发生以前的那些事了，这两年我们不也安稳地过来了，不用怕。”
“我怕，怕啊……所以你留下……”
雀溪累了。
他手被兽人拉扯得酸疼，脑袋也被哭声扰得嗡鸣声阵阵。
可无论他怎么劝，羊止仿佛听不见他说的话一般。
他闭上眼，最后一次道：“我要回部落。我的族人还在等着我。”
“你怎么就知道你的族人还在？他们比我的部落都还弱小，万一也没了呢？！”
雀溪一怔。
他被羊止眼里的怨意惊到，一把甩开手，遍体生寒。
“你知道你在说什么吗？”他声音轻颤。
“难道没有这个可能吗？”
羊止维持不住镇定，一想到雀溪要走，要留他一个在这里，他就快要癫狂。
“羊止！”
雀溪用看陌生兽人的眼神看着他，声音虚弱，却裹挟着冷意：“我不喜欢听到这种话。”
“那你留下。”
雀溪头一回觉得跟他说话这么累。
算了，说不通。
他闭口不言。
羊止又蹑手蹑脚往前，啜泣着，试图拉住他的手。
雀溪躲开，羊止跌坐在地上，无声流泪。
他低声道：“这几年你傻了，我那么照顾你，你就这样抛下我……”
雀溪心中冷意蔓延，对羊止彻底失望。
难道在他们被狼部落救之前，他在那些兽人中周旋，极力护下更多的兽人的命是假的？
这一刻，雀溪看清了羊止的性子。
他属实懦弱。
在他看来，羊止留在狼部落是最好的选择。
如果他的部落……出事，他几乎不用思考，求也要求着留下来。
狼部落很好，非常好。
这是他这几年，用自己这一双眼睛看到的，最适合投靠的部落。
在被狼部落的兽人带来这里之前，雀溪对外一直被熊沉当做伴侣。不是熊沉多喜欢他，而是有伴侣的族长对外能获得兽人更多的信任。
熊沉看得上他的样貌和性子，所以偶尔他说的话也有用处。靠着这点微不足道的用处，他能护一个兽人是一个。
虽然可能最后他们会在他睡一觉之后消失不见，但他真的用尽他的全力去阻拦。
没曾想，原来他之前做的那些事，兽人却当看不见。
“雀溪，你留下来好不好……”
雀溪声音平静，“那你和我一起走，我带你回红雀部落。”
羊止抓着他的手，一味地流泪，却不回应他。
雀溪眼神变得冷漠。
看看，羊止想留下的，却不想他离开。就算用这两年照顾他的情分要挟，也要让自己也一并留下。
雀溪不想闹得太难看，他抽回手，道：“你出去吧，我累了。”
羊止坐在地上一动不动。
大门是关上的，羊止进来时害怕，从里面把门拴上了。
他不想出去，他还没说通雀溪。
*
羊止的哭声瞒不过路过屋前的兽人。
大家也有分寸，不会偷听人家的讲话。
狼莫和狼西经过，狼西手臂搭在狼莫肩膀上，忍不住道：“他俩关系挺好。”
“我俩关系也好，我要是受伤了，你会不会像这么哭？”
狼西立马把胳膊收回来，狠狠搓了搓，然后嫌弃地看了狼莫一眼，立刻往广场上走。
狼莫：“狼西！亏我对你这么好！你有没有良心？！”
狼西快步往前走。
狼莫在后头追，叽里咕噜控诉着，满脸不高兴的样子。
当着狼果几个兽人的面儿，他追上狼西，一把勾住狼西脖子，“我问你，你有没有良心？！”
“你听听你问的东西肉不肉麻？”
“怎么就肉麻了？”
“怎么不肉麻了？！”
狼西往回看了一眼，发现狼果几个都盯着他俩，还看得津津有味。
他给了狼莫一肘子道：“就是你这样，我们才找不到伴侣！”
“我怎么样了？你倒是说清楚！”
狼果一边把爬到自己脑袋上的幼崽摘下来，一边对旁边的羽江和狼菇说：“他俩看着就像一起过日子的对吧？”
“你听！”狼西指着他三个，急得跳脚。
狼莫：“你们胡说八道什么？！”
狼果无辜，“我说什么了？”
“你……”狼莫收回目光，再看看自己此刻跟狼西的距离，脸一皱，两个兽人同时嫌弃地转头避开。
他俩一前一后走远了。
狼果笑了一声，收回目光。
他看了一眼雀溪躺着那屋，敛了笑容，幽幽道：“那屋里有些不对劲儿啊。”
“哪儿不对劲儿？”
狼菇两个胳膊间搂了一排小崽子，他疑惑看来，幼崽们也好奇，抬了一排小脑袋。
“我们刚刚过来，那屋里兽人就在哭，现在都坐在这里多久了，狼莫他们经过，还听见里面兽人在哭。就是撞了个脑袋，至于哭得跟雀溪没了一样？”羽江给他解惑道。
狼果点头，就是这个意思。
狼菇年纪小点，之前一直在赤山部落，没经历过多少事。
他一边把怀里的幼崽白的和白的放在一起，黑的和黑的放在一起，一边不忘道：“肯定感情很好。”
“能有多好？又不是一个部落的。”狼果道。
三个兽人当中，羽江年纪最大，可以当他俩的阿叔了。
他像教幼崽一样，给狼菇掰开揉碎了说。
“要是关系真的好，他们就该相互体谅。雀溪受了伤，还伤的脑袋，可羊止守着他哭了那么久，换做是你，你舒服？”
“不舒服。”
“那不就对了。”
“那……要不要去提醒一下？”
狼果跟羽江对视一眼，两个兽人同时摇头。
“他们的事我们不掺和。”
那两个是部落收留的兽人，又不是他们自己的兽人。他两个之间的事，狼兽人不好插手。
雀溪那屋的门关了许久。
狼果抱着晒过太阳的幼崽吸了吸毛毛，闻着那暖融融的味道，是晒透了，再往藤筐里一放。
他们都打算收幼崽了，那边门还紧闭着。
有什么话要说这么久？
三个兽人带着幼崽经过，特意放轻脚步，竖着耳朵听了听。
里面的哭声低低切切，像雨季的虫鸣一样一直没断过。
居然还在哭！
要不是哭声夹杂着说话声，他们还以为里面的雀溪出事了。
三个兽人面面相觑。
狼菇：这下得管一管了吧？
雀溪还是祭司治的病兽人，用的是他们部落的草药。要是在里面出了问题，岂不白救？
狼果犹豫了下，打算敲门。
没等动作，藤筐里的幼崽感觉到藤筐不摇晃了，有些不乐意，幼崽们趴在藤筐边缘，“嗷”的一声——
中气十足。
顷刻，屋里传来凳子打翻的声音。
狼果一手捏幼崽的嘴，一手推门，却发现门从里面栓上了。
……
部落午饭好了。
林楸估摸着时间差不多，过来看看雀溪，顺带给他送饭。
远远见狼果几个站在门口，疑惑道：“怎么守在这儿？”
“这屋……”
砰的一声，门被打开。
羊止看外面这么多狼兽人，且林楸还在，慌忙地低下头，藏住哭肿的眼睛。
狼果话说到一半，见兽人这模样，唇角一勾，眼神有些冷。
原来他在作怪。
“刚刚怎么……”林楸在问狼果。
羊止立即打断，小声道：“雀溪刚刚说他头晕。”
狼果翻了个白眼，示意狼菇两个先带幼崽离开。
林楸觉得兽人之间气氛不对，他没急着追问，而是对身体藏在门背后的羊止道：“午饭好了，你也过去吃吧。”
说着，林楸端了碗进去。
羊止见狼果他们离开，手指蜷了蜷，犹豫地站在门口。
他看一眼里面的雀溪，又看看外面往食堂涌的兽人们，后退一步，悄声回到炕边。
林楸在检查雀溪的情况。
他满头大汗，脸色煞白，头上包扎好的伤口已经在渗血。
“溪？”
雀溪艰难睁开眼，难受得想呕。
瞧见站在林楸身后，满脸担忧的羊止，他疲惫地闭上眼。
林楸看出来，道：“羊止，你先去吃饭，雀溪需要休息。”
羊止嗫嚅道：“我……”
“去吧。”林楸声音平静，却不容推拒。
狼果放下幼崽去食堂，路过门口，还往里看了眼。
他笑眯眯瞧着还没走的羊止，道：“哟，还在？”
羊止埋下头，如芒在背。
他快步往外面走。
兽人离开，林楸放下东西，赶紧给雀溪检查伤口。
“我以为你们关系应该很好。”
“说不上好，也说不上差。”不过是身处困境时，互相照料了一下。
羊止不欠他什么，他也不欠羊止。
林楸给雀溪重新换了药包扎好，看他脸色还难看，轻声道：“你现在最重要的是养好身体，一切以自己为先。”
雀溪：“我明白。羊止……”
“我们会把他送去大泽那边。他要想走，我们不拦着。但狼部落也不白养他，依旧像以前一样，做事换食物。”
雀溪点头，头又一阵眩晕。
他安静吃完林楸送来的食物，喝了汤药，又重新躺了下去。
林楸拿上空碗出门。
雀溪看着，在他踏出门那一刻，道：“我不想再见他。”
林楸一顿，“小狼去大泽会把他带上的。”
“谢谢。”
林楸半掩上门，一眼看见外面站着的狼果。
林楸：“不是去吃饭了？”
狼果哼声，“等你。”
“那走吧。”
两个兽人慢慢往食堂走，狼果道：“两年没见那羊兽人，怎么感觉变了个性子？”
“嗯？”
林楸对羊止了解不多，怎么就变了？
“他一直在这边屋里哭，雀溪状态不好吧。”
“确实。”
“你说他哭什么？”
“他性子怯弱，就像那缠绕在树上的藤。现在这个能让他缠绕的树挪开了，他支撑不起来，害怕了。”
狼果想想，唇角一勾。
“听着像是这么一回事。但楸，我不喜欢他。”
“好恶不要表露得这么明显。”
狼果撇嘴，用肩膀撞林楸一下，不服气道：“我在自己部落我还要忍？”
林楸一笑，“别小狼性子。”
“哼！”
“阿爸！！！”
狼果的幼崽从北边跑回来，一身泥泞，举着双手冲着狼果来。
狼果往旁边一撤，幼崽摔在草地上，打了个滚，又急吼吼地爬起来，闷头往狼果腿上撞。
狼果把幼崽拎起来，嫌弃地看看他身上，抖了抖，一把甩给林楸，顺带把林楸手里的空碗抢了过来。
“嗷！”
林楸接住小崽子，立刻感觉到一股臭烘烘的味道钻入鼻腔。
林楸屏息，看向狼果。
“你自己的幼崽。”
“送你了。”
“楸楸叔。”
林楸看着怀里胖墩墩的幼崽，一头软乎的白发，刚好到耳。皮肤白白的，脸颊两坨红，眼睛也是狼果一样的冰蓝色。
这小家伙几乎是狼果的翻版。
“狼久久，你跑泥里打滚去了？”
“嗷！”
“你还嗷，不怕你阿爸追着你打屁股？”
幼崽傻兮兮一笑，小手捂住屁股。
“不打。”
林楸想到之前狼果追着幼崽到处跑都忍不住笑。
“其他幼崽呢？”
“吃饭。”
“那你怎么不去吃？”
幼崽味儿实在大，林楸抱了一会儿，带他回食堂，交到狼果手上。
狼果毫不掩饰自己的嫌弃，目光转了一圈，见狼夜在，直接把幼崽扔他怀里。
“你的臭崽子。”
“嗷！”幼崽不服气。
狼果扬起下巴挑衅：“你要咬我啊？”
“嗷呜！”
“来咬啊。”狼果冲他勾勾手指。
狼夜按住乱动的幼崽，又看看他幼稚的阿爸，无奈道：“不送饭回去？”
“哦，差点忘了。”
幼崽那边离不开成年兽人，狼果是兽人派出来拿食物的。他一溜烟就跑了，留下父子俩面面相觑。
“嗷！”
狼夜捏捏幼崽脸，“嗷什么嗷，多大了，说话都不会？”
幼崽推开狼夜的手，两只黑漆漆的小爪子抵在他脸上，推得远远的。
他撅着屁股往桌下滑动。
狼夜一松手，小崽子就跑到幼崽堆里去了。
“夜，吃完饭就走吗？”同伴问。
“走。”
他们没出去捕猎，王让他们留下来，等会儿还要去一趟西边。
羽山他们要到处巡逻，没空时时刻刻守着那边新来的部落。刚好狼夜他们要过去熬硝，顺带守着他们。
食堂窗明几净，长桌擦得锃亮。
脏兮兮的幼崽围了三张桌子，吃得头也不抬。
隔壁桌，狼金和同伴们几下填饱肚子，打个嗝，端着空碗起身，顺手揉了一把幼崽脑袋。
狼金摸到一手湿汗，甩了甩手，道：“掉水里了？”
幼崽忙着吃饭，低低应了一声，头都没抬一下。
狼金笑了两声，往洗碗池走。
小狼成年了，加上这几年吃得饱了，身体拔高，肩膀也变得宽厚起来。
他们褪去了少年气，比以前成熟不少。
如今小狼队彻底能独当一面。
一群高大的、满是朝气的兽人从旁走过，上了年纪的阿叔们看着就很欣慰。部落的幼崽好好长大了，部落才会有更好的未来。
林楸放了筷子，看他们路过，问：“金，你们什么时候去大泽？”
“等会儿睡一觉就走。楸，我让羽涯送红鸟去那边。”
“羽涯他们不是出去了？”
羽涯那几个黑羽兽人现在跟着羽乐和狼冰他们到处跑。
十几个小狼加上五个黑羽兽人，都是成年兽人了，出门在外大家也不用太担心。
“那……羽猎叔？”狼金看向食堂里坐着吃饭的羽猎。
羽猎：“我不行，得帮兔葵搬种子。”
羽猎旁边坐着的另几个黑羽兽人也点点头。
林楸身边，狼岩放下筷子道：“狮也他们在大泽那边待多久？”
“说是不急。”
“那就等羽涯他们回来。”
狼部落往外交换小红鸟，不只是交换完就行了，他们还要负责把小红鸟送到对方部落去。
兽人们四条腿在地上跑，对小红鸟来说太颠簸，怕是没到部落，小红鸟就没了，所以需要黑羽兽人负责送。
当然，运费另算。
黑羽兽人经过那几场和雪鹰兽人的战斗，数量本就少了。
现在一大半壮劳力跟着羽山和羽千在两个部落间巡逻、捕猎，一部分在地里帮忙，剩下的就是老的、小的和身体不行的，有这个精力飞远路的，就那群刚刚长成的小黑羽兽人最合适。
他们去送红鸟，兽人也不会亏待他们。
狼部落这边会给他们准备干粮，对方部落准备的“运费”也全归他们自己。
“那我们留一晚。楸！我们后面几顿都要吃好吃的。”
“雨在大泽那边亏待你们了？”
两边伙食标准都一样，为了让他们满意，狼雨还经常回来学习。
就这，他们每次回来依旧会馋嘴。
“大泽是大泽，这边是这边，不一样。”
兽人们热热闹闹说着话，角落里，羊止降低存在感吃饭。
他看着碗里的尾巴草籽干饭，还有各式各样的菜，埋下头，又默默吃了一大口。
雀溪说得不错，他留在狼部落是最好的安排。
羊止从始至终都没想过离开，但是他不明白，为什么雀溪就不能同他一样，也留下来。
“看什么？”
林楸听到狼岩在耳边说话。
他收回目光，轻声道：“没看什么，我吃完了。”
狼岩：“等我一会儿。”
林楸便坐着不急着走。
狼影高大，几乎能把他挡完。林楸下巴虚虚贴在狼岩肩侧，静静观察着角落里的羊止。
羊止在狼部落也好几年了，似乎始终不能适应。
狼兽人经过他身边，他都会紧绷一些。
兴许他跟雀溪一样，始终没从那段日子里走出来。
但这样风声鹤唳的样子，并不适合过日子。长此以往，兽人精神会崩溃。
“王。”
“嗯。”
“西边那个中等部落有羊兽人吗？”林楸收回目光，声音放得很轻。
或许在同族身边，他才会更自在。
“有。”狼岩道，“想把他送过去？”
林楸：“先问问他的想法吧，要是不愿意留在狼部落……”
*
“我愿意的！我会好好干活！求求你们，不要让我走！”
广场角落，羊止哭得上气不接下气。
林楸和狼岩站在一处，被他这激烈的反应弄得有些无奈。
林楸：“我就只是问问。你确认你的部落……覆灭了吗？还有没有同伴在？”
羊止捂着眼睛蹲下来，哭得耳朵都红了。
“我、我不知道……好多同伴都被抓了，我跑了，但也被抓住了。”
林楸尽量平和道：“好，如果以后你遇到你还幸存的族人，想走我们也不拦着你。”
“我呜……”他一味地流泪。
狼岩：“狼部落不养闲兽人，你用劳动换食物，不能歪心思。”
“不会，我不会！”
林楸：“那好，明天就跟狼金他们回去吧。”
哭声一止，只断了一息又重新接上。
“我、我想守着溪，他这样需要兽人照顾，你们太忙，我可以帮忙照顾他。”
林楸脸色有点怪异。
狼岩握住他的手，看向羊止道：“雀溪愿意的话，可以。”
兽人呜呜地哭，听得久了，根本没有心思跟他说话。
狼岩拉着林楸离开，走远了，才问：“不想他留下来？”
“嗯。”羊止看着怯弱，但心思多，相处间不止狼果觉得不舒服，他也一样。
狼岩：“用示弱让兽人妥协，跟武力威胁没什么两样，不舒服也是应该。”
“你看出来了？”
“不难看出来。但雀溪一走，需要提醒狼雨多盯着他一点，最好送走。”
“嗯？”
林楸没想到他是这个打算。
“他现在没有其他心思，但雀溪走了，他又融入不了狼部落，时间久了，歪心思就起来了。”
别看他现在似乎一直在哭，一直显示出他的无害和弱势，但当利益摆在他面前，他会毫不犹豫地出卖狼部落。
他对他们没有归属感。
他现在还畏惧他们，却不得不依靠他们。
狼部落发展得越来越好，他的部落却没了，要是心里极端些，还容易成仇。
狼部落现在面对着原野部落的侵扰，内部不能再乱，哪怕是一点可能性，也要掐断。
林楸心里沉了沉：“好，让那边多留意。”
chapters.translated_text:
In the plaza, Lang Guo had brought the cubs out to sunbathe again.

He had taken several large wicker baskets, lined with animal hides, making them very soft to sit in.

There were many cubs, and it took Lang Guo, Lang Gu, and Yu Jiang each holding a basket to accommodate them all.

The cubs were restless, squirming against each other; some climbed over their companions to get out, while others stood up, resting their front paws on the edges of the baskets, whimpering when they couldn't climb out.

Lang Guo steadied the baskets with one hand while pushing the cubs back in whenever they climbed halfway out.

The cubs tumbled back into the baskets, letting out loud, indignant "Aos."

Lang Guo pinched a cub’s snout and smiled, saying, "Little wolf pup, you're hurting my ears with all that noise."

"Wuwuwu..."

"Wu..."

The cubs' struggling whimpers overlapped with the muffled crying coming from inside the house. The previously rowdy cubs suddenly quieted down, their little ears pricking up in vigilance.

Lang Guo glanced at the house beside him; it was where the priest treated the sick.

"What's going on in there?" Lang Gu asked softly.

Yu Jiang replied, "It's the voice of that stranger beastman."

Lang Guo signaled for the two of them to leave. Once they reached the plaza and were far enough from the house, he said, "It's that sheep beastman who was rescued along with Que Xi."

Inside the house.

The crying stopped.

Yang Zhi covered his mouth, sitting beside Que Xi, his thin shoulders trembling, his back hunching further.

"Stop crying..." Que Xi comforted him gently, though his own voice was weak and his face was drained of color.

But Yang Zhi couldn't stop the tears.

"If you leave, what will I do..."

When Yang Zhi first arrived and saw that Que Xi's wounds had been bandaged by the wolf beastmen, he couldn't help but be happy for him.

But before they had spoken many words, he heard Que Xi say he intended to return to his own tribe.

Lu Ye was gone, and the only person Yang Zhi could talk to here was Que Xi. He was timid, always fearful of the wolf beastmen, and having been inseparable from Que Xi for the past two years, he hadn't made any friends in the Wolf Tribe.

He had assumed they would rely on each other here, never expecting that as soon as he arrived, he would hear that Que Xi was going to abandon him and leave.

Yang Zhi felt as if the sky had collapsed.

He repeated over and over, "What will I do if you leave... what will I do if you leave..."

Que Xi endured the throbbing headache, reached out, and gripped his wrist.

"The Wolf Tribe is very good. You've been here for years, and you haven't lacked food or clothing. Even if I leave, you can still stay with them; there's no need to be afraid."

"I'm afraid, I'm just afraid." Yang Zhi threw himself against the edge of the kang, clutching Que Xi's hand tightly. "...Don't go, please don't go..."

He wept uncontrollably, looking at Que Xi with a mix of terror and hope, like a drowning person clinging to driftwood, gripping so hard that Que Xi’s hand turned white.

"Xi, let's not leave, okay? We can eat our fill in the Wolf Tribe, and there's no danger. Can't we just stay..."

"Zhi." Que Xi lowered his eyelids, his body tilting as he was pulled by his hand, feeling powerless.

But no matter how Yang Zhi cried or begged, he wouldn't budge.

"Zhi, I want to go back to my tribe."

"But what about me?! I don't have a tribe anymore," Yang Zhi cried out in despair.

"That's why you should stay here in the Wolf Tribe. The things that happened before won't happen again. We’ve lived peacefully for the past two years, there’s no need to be afraid."

"I'm afraid, I'm so afraid... so please stay..."

Que Xi was tired.

His hand ached from being pulled, and his head was buzzing from the sound of the crying.

But no matter how he tried to persuade him, Yang Zhi seemed unable to hear a word he said.

He closed his eyes and said for the last time, "I am going back to my tribe. My tribespeople are still waiting for me."

"How do you know your tribespeople are still there? They were even weaker than my tribe; what if they're gone too?!"

Que Xi was startled.

He was shocked by the resentment in Yang Zhi's eyes, and he jerked his hand away, feeling a chill run through his entire body.

"Do you know what you're saying?" his voice trembled.

"Isn't it possible?"

Yang Zhi couldn't maintain his composure; the thought of Que Xi leaving and abandoning him here made him feel like he was going insane.

"Yang Zhi!"

Que Xi looked at him as if he were a stranger, his voice weak but laced with coldness: "I don't like hearing things like that."

"Then stay."

For the first time, Que Xi felt it was so exhausting to talk to him.

Forget it, it was pointless.

He stopped speaking.

Yang Zhi crept forward again, sobbing, trying to grab his hand.

Que Xi dodged, and Yang Zhi fell to the floor, crying silently.

He whispered, "You've gone soft these past few years. I took such good care of you, and this is how you abandon me..."

A coldness spread in Que Xi's heart, and he felt completely disappointed in Yang Zhi.

Was it a lie that before they were rescued by the Wolf Tribe, he had maneuvered among those beastmen, doing his utmost to protect the lives of as many beastmen as possible?

At this moment, Que Xi saw Yang Zhi's true nature clearly.

He was truly cowardly.

In his view, Yang Zhi staying in the Wolf Tribe was the best choice.

If his own tribe... had met with disaster, he wouldn't even need to think; he would beg to stay.

The Wolf Tribe was good, very good.

This was the tribe he had seen with his own eyes over the past few years that was most worth joining.

Before being brought here by the wolf beastmen, Que Xi had always been treated as a mate by Xiong Chen to the outside world. It wasn't that Xiong Chen liked him much, but a chieftain with a mate could gain more trust from other beastmen.

Xiong Chen appreciated his appearance and temperament, so occasionally what he said had some weight. Relying on this insignificant usefulness, he was able to protect one beastman after another.

Although they might disappear after he woke up from a sleep, he had truly tried his best to stop it.

Never did he expect that the beastmen would turn a blind eye to everything he had done.

"Que Xi, please stay..."

Que Xi’s voice was calm, "Then come with me, I will take you back to the Red Sparrow Tribe."

Yang Zhi clutched his hand, weeping blindly, but did not respond to him.

Que Xi's eyes turned indifferent.

Look, Yang Zhi wanted to stay, but didn't want him to leave. Even using the sentiment of having taken care of him for two years as leverage, he wanted to force him to stay as well.

Que Xi didn't want to make a scene, so he pulled his hand back and said, "Go out, I'm tired."

Yang Zhi sat on the floor, motionless.

The door was closed; Yang Zhi had been afraid when he came in and had bolted the door from the inside.

He didn't want to leave; he hadn't convinced Que Xi yet.

*

Yang Zhi's crying could not be hidden from the beastmen passing by the house.

Everyone had their own sense of propriety and wouldn't eavesdrop on others' conversations.

Lang Mo and Lang Xi passed by, Lang Xi’s arm draped over Lang Mo’s shoulder, and he couldn't help but say, "They have a pretty good relationship."

"Our relationship is good too. If I were injured, would you cry like that?"

Lang Xi immediately pulled his arm back, rubbed it vigorously, gave Lang Mo a look of disgust, and walked toward the plaza.

Lang Mo: "Lang Xi! I treat you so well! Do you have any conscience at all?!"

Lang Xi walked faster.

Lang Mo chased after him, grumbling and complaining, his face full of displeasure.

In front of Lang Guo and the others, he caught up to Lang Xi and hooked his arm around his neck, "I'm asking you, do you have a conscience?!"

"Listen to how mushy the things you ask are!"

"How is it mushy?"

"How is it not mushy?!"

Lang Xi looked back and saw that Lang Guo and the others were staring at them, watching with great interest.

He elbowed Lang Mo and said, "It's because of you that we can't find mates!"

"What's wrong with me? You better explain yourself!"

Lang Guo, while picking a cub off his head, said to Yu Jiang and Lang Gu beside him, "They look like they're living together, don't they?"

"Listen!" Lang Xi pointed at the three of them, jumping in frustration.

Lang Mo: "What nonsense are you talking about?!"

Lang Guo looked innocent, "What did I say?"

"You..." Lang Mo withdrew his gaze, looked at the distance between himself and Lang Xi, his face wrinkled, and both beastmen turned away in mutual disgust.

They walked away one after the other.

Lang Guo chuckled and looked away.

He glanced at the house where Que Xi was lying, his smile fading, and he said gloomily, "Something isn't right in that room."

"What's not right?"

Lang Gu, holding a row of cubs in his arms, looked over in confusion, and the cubs also looked curious, lifting a row of little heads.

"We just came over, and the beastman in there was crying. We've been sitting here for so long, and when Lang Mo and the others passed by, they still heard the beastman crying. It's just a bump on the head, is it worth crying as if Que Xi were dead?" Yu Jiang explained to him.

Lang Guo nodded; that was exactly what he meant.

Lang Gu was younger and had been in the Chishan Tribe before, so he hadn't experienced much.

While putting the white cubs together and the black cubs together in his arms, he didn't forget to say, "They must have a very good relationship."

"How good can it be? They aren't even from the same tribe," Lang Guo said.

Among the three beastmen, Yu Jiang was the oldest and could be their uncle.

He explained it to Lang Gu as if he were teaching a cub.

"If the relationship were really good, they should be considerate of each other. Que Xi is injured, and it's a head injury, but Yang Zhi has been sitting there crying for so long. If it were you, would you feel comfortable?"

"Not comfortable."

"Exactly."

"Then... should we go and remind them?"

Lang Guo and Yu Jiang looked at each other, and both shook their heads.

"We won't interfere in their business."

Those two were beastmen taken in by the tribe, not their own. It wasn't easy for the wolf beastmen to intervene in their affairs.

The door to Que Xi's room had been closed for a long time.

Lang Guo hugged the sun-warmed cubs, sniffing their fur, smelling the warmth of the sun, and then placed them back into the wicker basket.

They were all planning to put the cubs away, but the door over there was still tightly shut.

What could they have to talk about for so long?

The three beastmen passed by with the cubs, deliberately softening their footsteps, pricking up their ears to listen.

The crying inside was low and persistent, like the chirping of insects in the rainy season, never stopping.

They were still crying!

If not for the sound of talking mixed in with the crying, they would have thought something had happened to Que Xi inside.

The three beastmen looked at each other.

Lang Gu: Should we do something now?

Que Xi was a patient treated by the priest, using their tribe's medicinal herbs. If something went wrong inside, wouldn't the rescue be in vain?

Lang Guo hesitated, intending to knock on the door.

Before he could move, the cubs in the basket felt the basket stop shaking and were unhappy, leaning over the edge of the basket and letting out an "Ao"—

Full of energy.

Instantly, the sound of a stool being overturned came from the room.

Lang Guo pinched a cub's mouth with one hand and pushed the door with the other, only to find it bolted from the inside.

...

Lunch for the tribe was ready.

Lin Qiu estimated the time and came over to check on Que Xi, bringing him food as well.

Seeing Lang Guo and the others standing at the door from afar, he asked in confusion, "Why are you guarding here?"

"This room..."

With a bang, the door was opened.

Seeing so many wolf beastmen outside, and with Lin Qiu there, Yang Zhi hurriedly lowered his head, hiding his swollen, teary eyes.

Lang Guo, who had been speaking, saw the beastman's appearance, curled his lips, and his eyes turned cold.

So he was the one causing trouble.

"What just..." Lin Qiu asked Lang Guo.

Yang Zhi immediately interrupted, whispering, "Que Xi just said he felt dizzy."

Lang Guo rolled his eyes, signaling for Lang Gu and the other to take the cubs away first.

Lin Qiu felt the atmosphere between the beastmen was off. He didn't rush to ask, but said to Yang Zhi, who was hiding behind the door, "Lunch is ready, you should go eat too."

As he spoke, Lin Qiu carried the bowl inside.

Seeing Lang Guo and the others leave, Yang Zhi curled his fingers and stood hesitantly at the door.

He glanced at Que Xi inside, then at the beastmen streaming toward the cafeteria, took a step back, and returned to the side of the kang in silence.

Lin Qiu was checking on Que Xi's condition.

He was sweating profusely, his face pale, and the bandage on his head was already seeping blood.

"Xi?"

Que Xi opened his eyes with difficulty, feeling nauseous.

Seeing Yang Zhi standing behind Lin Qiu with a face full of worry, he closed his eyes in exhaustion.

Lin Qiu noticed and said, "Yang Zhi, you go eat first, Que Xi needs to rest."

Yang Zhi stammered, "I..."

"Go." Lin Qiu's voice was calm but left no room for refusal.

Lang Guo put down the cubs and headed to the cafeteria, glancing inside as he passed the door.

He looked at Yang Zhi, who hadn't left yet, with a smile, and said, "Oh, still here?"

Yang Zhi lowered his head, feeling like needles were pricking his back.

He walked quickly outside.

Once the beastman left, Lin Qiu put down his things and hurriedly checked Que Xi's wound.

"I thought you two had a very good relationship."

"Not good, not bad." Just taking care of each other while in a difficult situation.

Yang Zhi didn't owe him anything, and he didn't owe Yang Zhi anything.

Lin Qiu re-bandaged the wound with fresh medicine, and seeing his face still looked bad, said softly, "The most important thing for you now is to recover your health; put yourself first."

Que Xi: "I understand. Yang Zhi..."

"We will send him to Daze. If he wants to leave, we won't stop him. But the Wolf Tribe won't support him for nothing; he will still work for food as before."

Que Xi nodded, his head spinning again.

He finished the food Lin Qiu brought, drank the medicinal soup, and lay back down.

Lin Qiu took the empty bowl and went out.

Que Xi watched him, and the moment he stepped out, said, "I don't want to see him again."

Lin Qiu paused, "Little Wolf will take him along when they go to Daze."

"Thank you."

Lin Qiu half-closed the door and immediately saw Lang Guo standing outside.

Lin Qiu: "Aren't you going to eat?"

Lang Guo snorted, "Waiting for you."

"Let's go then."

The two beastmen walked slowly toward the cafeteria, and Lang Guo said, "I haven't seen that sheep beastman in two years; why does it feel like his personality has changed?"

"Hmm?"

Lin Qiu didn't know much about Yang Zhi, so how had he changed?

"He's been crying in that room the whole time, Que Xi's state isn't good, is it?"

"Indeed."

"What do you think he's crying for?"

"He's timid by nature, like a vine wrapped around a tree. Now that the tree he relied on has been moved, he can't support himself and is afraid."

Lang Guo thought about it and curled his lips.

"Sounds like that's the case. But Qiu, I don't like him."

"Don't show your likes and dislikes so obviously."

Lang Guo pouted, bumped his shoulder against Lin Qiu's, and said defiantly, "I have to endure it even in my own tribe?"

Lin Qiu smiled, "Don't be like a little wolf."

"Hmph!"

"Papa!!!"

Lang Guo's cub ran back from the north, covered in mud, charging toward Lang Guo with both hands raised.

Lang Guo stepped aside, and the cub fell onto the grass, rolled over, scrambled up anxiously, and bumped headfirst into Lang Guo's leg.

Lang Guo picked up the cub, looked at him with disgust, shook him, and tossed him to Lin Qiu, taking the empty bowl from Lin Qiu's hand in the process.

"Ao!"

Lin Qiu caught the little cub and immediately felt a stinky smell enter his nose.

Lin Qiu held his breath and looked at Lang Guo.

"Your own cub."

"He's yours now."

"Qiuqiu Uncle."

Lin Qiu looked at the chubby cub in his arms, with a head of soft white hair that reached his ears. His skin was fair, his cheeks were rosy, and his eyes were the same ice blue as Lang Guo's.

This little guy was almost a carbon copy of Lang Guo.

"Lang Jiujiu, did you go rolling in the mud?"

"Ao!"

"You're still 'Ao'-ing, aren't you afraid your papa will chase you and spank your butt?"

The cub smiled foolishly and covered his butt with his small hands.

"Won't hit."

Lin Qiu couldn't help but laugh, remembering how Lang Guo used to chase the cub everywhere.

"Where are the other cubs?"

"Eating."

"Then why aren't you eating?"

The cub smelled really bad, so Lin Qiu held him for a while, brought him back to the cafeteria, and handed him to Lang Guo.

Lang Guo didn't hide his disgust, glanced around, saw Lang Ye, and threw the cub directly into his arms.

"Your stinky cub."

"Ao!" the cub protested.

Lang Guo raised his chin provocatively: "Are you going to bite me?"

"Aowu!"

"Come on, bite me." Lang Guo hooked his finger at him.

Lang Ye held down the squirming cub, looked at his childish papa, and sighed helplessly: "Not sending food back?"

"Oh, almost forgot."

The cubs needed adult beastmen to look after them, and Lang Guo had been sent to get food. He ran off in a flash, leaving the father and son staring at each other.

"Ao!"

Lang Ye pinched the cub's face, "What are you 'Ao'-ing about? How old are you, and you still can't talk?"

The cub pushed Lang Ye's hand away, his two little black paws pressing against his face, pushing him far away.

He slid under the table with his butt sticking out.

As soon as Lang Ye let go, the little cub ran into the pile of other cubs.

"Ye, are you leaving after you finish eating?" a companion asked.

"Yes."

They weren't going out to hunt; the King had asked them to stay, and they had to go to the west later.

Yu Shan and the others were patrolling everywhere and didn't have time to guard the newly arrived tribe. It just so happened that Lang Ye and the others were going over to boil saltpeter, so they could guard them at the same time.

The cafeteria was bright and clean, the long tables wiped until they shone.

The dirty cubs surrounded three tables, eating without even lifting their heads.

At the next table, Lang Jin and his companions finished their meal in a few bites, burped, stood up with their empty bowls, and casually ruffled a cub's head.

Lang Jin felt wet sweat on his hand, shook it, and said, "Did you fall into the water?"

The cub was busy eating, gave a low response, and didn't even lift his head.

Lang Jin chuckled twice and walked toward the washbasin.

The little wolves had grown up, and with plenty of food over the past few years, they had grown taller, and their shoulders had become broad and thick.

They had shed their youthful air and were much more mature than before.

Now, the Little Wolf Team could completely stand on their own.

A group of tall, energetic beastmen walked by, and the older uncles looked on with satisfaction. Only when the tribe's cubs grew up well would the tribe have a better future.

Lin Qiu put down his chopsticks, watched them pass, and asked, "Jin, when are you going to Daze?"

"We'll leave after a sleep. Qiu, I'll have Yu Ya send the little red birds over there."

"Aren't Yu Ya and the others out?"

Yu Ya and those black-feathered beastmen were now following Yu Le and Lang Bing everywhere.

A dozen little wolves plus five black-feathered beastmen, all adult beastmen, so there was no need to worry too much when they were out.

"Then... Uncle Yu Lie?" Lang Jin looked at Yu Lie, who was sitting in the cafeteria eating.

Yu Lie: "I can't, I have to help Tu Kui move seeds."

The other black-feathered beastmen sitting next to Yu Lie also nodded.

Beside Lin Qiu, Lang Yan put down his chopsticks and said, "How long will Shi Ye and the others stay in Daze?"

"They said they're not in a hurry."

"Then we'll wait for Yu Ya and the others to come back."

The Wolf Tribe exchanged little red birds, but it wasn't just a matter of finishing the exchange; they were also responsible for delivering the little red birds to the other tribe.

Beastmen running on four legs on the ground was too bumpy for the little red birds; they feared the birds wouldn't survive the trip, so they needed the black-feathered beastmen to deliver them.

Of course, the shipping fee was calculated separately.

The number of black-feathered beastmen had already dwindled after those few battles with the Snow Eagle beastmen.

Now, more than half of the strong laborers were following Yu Shan and Yu Qian to patrol and hunt between the two tribes, some were helping in the fields, and the rest were the old, the young, and those who were not physically fit. The most suitable ones for this long-distance flight were that group of young black-feathered beastmen who had just grown up.

If they went to deliver the red birds, the beastmen wouldn't treat them badly.

The Wolf Tribe would prepare dry rations for them, and the "shipping fee" prepared by the other tribe would all belong to them.

"Then we'll stay for one night. Qiu! We want to eat delicious food for the next few meals."

"Did Yu treat you badly in Daze?"

The food standards were the same on both sides, and to keep them satisfied, Lang Yu often came back to learn.

Even so, they would still crave food every time they came back.

"Daze is Daze, this side is this side, it's different."

The beastmen talked noisily, while in the corner, Yang Zhi kept a low profile and ate.

He looked at the tail-grass seed meal in his bowl, along with various dishes, lowered his head, and silently took another big bite.

Que Xi was right; staying in the Wolf Tribe was the best arrangement.

Yang Zhi had never thought of leaving from the beginning, but he didn't understand why Que Xi couldn't stay like him.

"What are you looking at?"

Lin Qiu heard Lang Yan speaking in his ear.

He withdrew his gaze and said softly, "Nothing, I'm done eating."

Lang Yan: "Wait for me a moment."

Lin Qiu sat there, not in a hurry to leave.

Lang Yan's shadow was tall, almost blocking him completely. Lin Qiu rested his chin lightly on Lang Yan's shoulder, quietly observing Yang Zhi in the corner.

Yang Zhi had been in the Wolf Tribe for several years, but he seemed unable to adapt.

Whenever a wolf beastman passed by him, he would tense up.

Perhaps he, like Que Xi, had never walked out of that period of time.

But such a fearful and suspicious appearance was not suitable for living. In the long run, a beastman's spirit would collapse.

"King."

"Hmm."

"Are there any sheep beastmen in that medium-sized tribe to the west?" Lin Qiu withdrew his gaze, his voice very light.

Perhaps he would feel more at ease among his own kind.

"Yes," Lang Yan said. "Want to send him over?"

Lin Qiu: "Let's ask his thoughts first; if he doesn't want to stay in the Wolf Tribe..."

*

"I'm willing! I'll work hard! Please, don't make me leave!"

In the corner of the plaza, Yang Zhi was crying until he was out of breath.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan stood together, feeling somewhat helpless at his intense reaction.

Lin Qiu: "I was just asking. Are you sure your tribe... has been wiped out? Are there any companions left?"

Yang Zhi covered his eyes and squatted down, crying until his ears turned red.

"I, I don't know... many companions were captured, I ran away, but I was also captured."

Lin Qiu tried to be as peaceful as possible: "Okay, if you encounter any surviving tribespeople in the future, we won't stop you if you want to leave."

"I, wu..." he just wept blindly.

Lang Yan: "The Wolf Tribe doesn't support idle beastmen. You exchange labor for food; don't have any crooked thoughts."

"I won't, I won't!"

Lin Qiu: "Alright then, go back with Lang Jin and the others tomorrow."

The crying stopped, only to resume after a breath.

"I, I want to watch over Xi. He needs a beastman to take care of him, and you are all too busy. I can help take care of him."

Lin Qiu's expression was a bit strange.

Lang Yan held his hand and looked at Yang Zhi: "If Que Xi is willing, that's fine."

The beastman kept crying, and after listening for a long time, there was no heart left to talk to him.

Lang Yan pulled Lin Qiu away, and when they were far away, he asked: "Don't want him to stay?"

"Hmm." Yang Zhi looked timid, but he had many thoughts. Not only did Lang Guo feel uncomfortable during their interactions, but he did too.

Lang Yan: "Using weakness to make beastmen compromise is no different from threats of force; it's normal to feel uncomfortable."

"You saw it too?"

"It's not hard to see. But once Que Xi leaves, we need to remind Lang Yu to keep an eye on him, it's best to send him away."

"Hmm?"

Lin Qiu hadn't expected this to be his plan.

"He doesn't have other thoughts now, but once Que Xi leaves, he won't be able to integrate into the Wolf Tribe. As time goes by, crooked thoughts will arise."

Don't look at how he seems to be crying all the time, showing his harmlessness and weakness; when interests are placed in front of him, he will betray the Wolf Tribe without hesitation.

He had no sense of belonging to them.

He still feared them now, but had to rely on them.

The Wolf Tribe was developing better and better, but his tribe was gone; if his heart became extreme, it would easily turn into hatred.

The Wolf Tribe was currently facing harassment from the Wilderness Tribe, and the interior could not be in chaos. Even if there was only a slight possibility, it had to be nipped in the bud.

Lin Qiu's heart sank: "Okay, let them keep a close eye on that side."

After Lin Qiu and Lang Yan finished questioning Yang Zhi, they walked together toward the mountain.

Halfway up, Lin Qiu stopped and looked at Yang Zhi, who was once again sneaking into Que Xi’s room.

"Que Xi probably won't agree."

"Maybe."

Lang Yan took Lin Qiu’s hand, interlacing their fingers, and pulled him along toward the mountain peak.

As they climbed the steps to the top, the beastman standing on the high watchtower greeted them.

Lang Yan nodded, and the beastman turned his gaze away, returning to his diligent watch.

Lang Yan gripped Lin Qiu’s waist and lifted him, placing him onto the large boulder at the summit.

Lin Qiu’s long hair fluttered, brushing against Lang Yan’s cheek; it felt slightly cool and carried a faint, fresh scent of grass and trees.

Once he was seated, Lang Yan braced his hands against the stone and hopped up, sitting beside Lin Qiu.

The view of Lang Mountain was now unobstructed.

Lin Qiu looked at the rows of houses below, the expansive farmland, the red bird pens and mie-mie beast pens where livestock were raised...

"Our tribe has changed so quickly."

"Counting from when you first came to Lang Mountain, it’s been five or six years."

"It’s been that long already..."

Lin Qiu gazed at the winding river in front of Lang Mountain; the river had never changed. He had been so busy burying himself in work that he had forgotten so much time had passed.

"Do you want to go back?" Lang Yan asked, looking at his slightly dazed profile.

"No."

Lang Yan smoothed out his wind-tangled hair, the corners of his lips curving slightly.

They both knew what Lang Yan meant by "going back." Lang Yan asked because he was certain Lin Qiu wouldn't leave, and Lin Qiu’s unhesitating answer confirmed it.

Lin Qiu laughed, sat cross-legged on the boulder, and patted Lang Yan’s leg.

"King, let’s discuss the trip to the Que Xi tribe."

"Alright."

This trip to the Red Sparrow tribe would certainly not be as easy as the last one to the Eastern Continent.

They were heading to the southern tip of the Western Continent, which required passing through the Central Continent. The Central Continent was a place where beastmen gathered, though it was unclear how many tribes remained there now.

"King, have you ever been to the southern part of the Central Continent?"

"No." Lang Yan sat cross-legged facing Lin Qiu, grabbing one of his hands to fiddle with. He pinched from the base of the palm to the fingertips, then rubbed the soft flesh between the fingers, like a cub finding a favorite toy—it was hard to say what was so fun about a hand.

Lin Qiu looked at him with a smile, shifted over to sit side-by-side, and leaned lazily against his shoulder.

"If we go from here, we have to cross the entire southern part of the Central Continent. About how long will the trip take?"

"Half a year or a year, it’s possible."

Back then, when the Wolf tribe left the middle of the Central Continent and reached the edge of the Eastern Continent, it took about half a year.

They had been migrating as an entire tribe, so they moved slowly. Furthermore, they weren't familiar with the route; which way to go depended entirely on the Priest and the Wolf King, with no target destination, only a general direction calculated by the Priest.

They stopped and started along the way and even tried to settle in other places, so the time added up.

Going to the southern part of the Western Continent would be different.

With Que Xi to show the way, the party would certainly not be as large as a migration group, and there would be no cubs or elderly beastmen, so the speed should be much faster.

"So a round trip would take one or two years?"

Lang Yan rubbed his cheek against Lin Qiu’s hair and said, "Or, would you rather stay in the tribe?"

"Don't even think about it!" Lin Qiu said.

Since this trip was so far, Lang Yan would definitely have to go.

If this route could be established, they could have beastmen who had been there lead future trade parties, just like they currently did with the Black Bear tribe.

Even though the journey was long, the rice and the herbs from the Western Continent made it worth the trip.

Seeing him furrow his brows in worry, Lang Yan smiled, held his wrist, and said, "I can't say for sure. Whether it’s a year or two, we’ll only know once we go."

Back when the Great Market existed, traveling far was a common thing for beastmen. But after the Great Market disappeared and life became difficult, and more wandering beastmen appeared outside, going on a trip had indeed become more dangerous than before.

The more Lang Yan thought about it, the more he circled Lin Qiu’s wrist with his hand to measure the size, unable to help saying, "Qiu, don't go, okay?"

"No."

"It’s dangerous."

"Don't treat me like a cub. I haven't been training for nothing these past few years."

Lang Yan chuckled, rubbing his chin against his partner’s hair, feeling how exceptionally smooth it was.

Very well, he would protect him.

"Then this time, which beastmen should go?"

As Lin Qiu spoke, he glanced at Que Xi’s room; Yang Zhi hadn't come out yet.

Lang Yan: "This trip is too far, so it depends on the beastmen’s willingness. However, I plan to have the Black Feather beastmen and the Rabbit beastmen go along. As for exactly who, we’ll discuss and decide tonight."

"Good."

The round trip was too long; some beastmen were timid, while others were homebodies and didn't want to travel so far. They would see tonight.

The large stoves in front of the plaza were still burning, steam rising.

Bags of rock salt dug up from the mines were poured in to be boiled, and the resulting salt was snow-white and translucent.

Lin Qiu watched the beastmen pack the finished salt into bags and carry them to the warehouse, saying, "And what do you plan to take for trade?"

"The same things as last time will do."

"What about cloth? Wine? The pickled vegetables that An and the others made? Or the animal skins we traded from other tribes?"

After Lin Qiu finished, he saw Lang Yan looking at him, his gray eyes carrying a faint smile, teasingly: "Is Qiu trying to empty out the Wolf tribe?"

Lin Qiu made a fist and tapped his palm.

Lang Yan caught his hand, pried his fingers open, and pressed his calloused fingertips into his palm.

Once, twice, his hand turned red.

Lin Qiu: "The tribe has plenty of things to trade now, but since this trip is long, we should try to bring things of high value."

"Alright, I’ll listen to you."

"I’ll go to the warehouse to take inventory later. Our tribe has saved up some good things over the years, and it would be a pity if they spoiled from sitting in the cave too long."

"That’s fine."

The warm breeze was gentle, mixed with the fragrance of grass and flowers.

Lin Qiu subconsciously caught the scent in the wind, smelled pollen, and was choked into a sneeze.

Seeing Lang Yan laughing, he rubbed his nose and said, "I’m so used to identifying scents that I can’t even properly enjoy the scenery."

"Then stay further away from the woods."

"Let’s go down the mountain and check on Que Xi."

They were still waiting for him to recover so he could take them to the Red Sparrow tribe. Yang Zhi had been in there for so long; he shouldn't delay his recovery.

Stairs had been built on the mountain, making the descent much easier than before.

However, the path was narrow, so Lang Yan walked in front and Lin Qiu followed behind.

They were only one step apart.

Lin Qiu placed his hand on Lang Yan’s shoulder, and just as he was about to speak, Lang Yan reached back with both hands and hoisted him onto his back.

"Eh?"

Lang Yan: "What’s wrong?"

Lin Qiu: "No, let me down."

"Didn't you want me to carry you?"

Lin Qiu quickly glanced at the beastmen boiling salt down the mountain.

The salt-making beastmen were busy with their work and hadn't noticed. Just as Lin Qiu breathed a sigh of relief, he remembered there was a watchtower on the mountain. He looked up and met the gaze of the beastman on duty.

The beastman on the watchtower calmly looked away, continuing to stare into the distance with a serious expression.

Lin Qiu clung to Lang Yan’s shoulders, a blush spreading from his neck to his face.

"Put me down quickly!"

Lang Yan stopped and loosened his grip slightly. Only after ensuring Lin Qiu was standing steadily did he turn to look at him.

Seeing his flushed cheeks, he chuckled and pinched Lin Qiu’s face.

Lin Qiu quickly swatted his hand away, secretly gritting his teeth: "Don't laugh."

Lang Yan: "I’m not laughing."

"If you aren't laughing, why are your eyes and the corners of your mouth curved?"

He couldn't tease him anymore; if he teased him any more, he’d explode.

"Do you want to go see the beastman tribes in the west?"

"Go where?"

"The west."

The topic changed too quickly. Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan’s deadpan expression, not knowing whether to be annoyed or not.

He let go, walked to the front, and ran down the mountain in a few strides.

Lang Yan: "Slow down."

Lin Qiu ignored him, his long hair flying as he took two steps at a time, running even faster.

Lin Qiu went down the mountain and headed straight for the cafeteria.

He grabbed a pot of hot water and carried it to Que Xi’s room.

Pushing the door open, Que Xi was lying on the kang, appearing to be asleep.

Yang Zhi was sitting beside him, whispering something. Lin Qiu’s entrance startled him, and the beastman fell right off the stool.

Lin Qiu: "Is he asleep?"

Yang Zhi looked at Que Xi, his back hunched and shoulders shrunken, his hands clasped together, nervously picking at them.

"N-no, not asleep."

As if to confirm his words, as soon as Yang Zhi finished, Que Xi opened his eyes.

Lin Qiu: "Have you discussed it? Do you need Yang Zhi’s care during this time?"

Yang Zhi’s mouth opened slightly, his voice stuck in his throat.

Que Xi didn't want to embarrass Yang Zhi in front of Lin Qiu. His voice was hoarse as he said, "I just took a fall; there’s no need to trouble Zhi to take care of me. I’m already much better now. Zhi, you should go back to Daze."

"No, no... I’ll stay with you, I’ll watch over you." Yang Zhi stood up in a panic, lunged onto the kang, and grabbed Que Xi’s hand.

Que Xi didn't move, but looked straight into his teary eyes and said, "If you watch over me... what about the work you owe? If you want to help me, help me do my share as well."

Yang Zhi’s hand loosened, holding Que Xi’s hand weakly, not daring to look at Lin Qiu behind him.

He didn't speak either, as if waiting for Lin Qiu to start.

Lin Qiu’s lips lifted, but there was no smile in his eyes. "You can owe it for now."

Yang Zhi’s hand tightened.

Que Xi felt the pain, his hand trembling, but he couldn't pull it away.

Lin Qiu: "But later, you might have to do two shares of work to trade for it."

Yang Zhi lowered his head, motionless.

Que Xi looked at Yang Zhi and said, "Hurry to Daze, or you’ll owe more and more. My share..."

"You can owe that too, and when you’re better, we’ll do it together," Yang Zhi said, cutting him off.

His voice was very soft and thin, damp, like the hissing of a snake in the woods on a gloomy, rainy day.

Lin Qiu pinched the bridge of his nose.

He was truly stubborn.

He set the water down and said, "Que Xi needs to rest."

"I’ll just stay here and keep him company; I won't disturb him."

Not disturbing him?

Look at how pale Que Xi’s face was.

Que Xi: "I don't need it."

Yang Zhi: "Your injuries aren't healed yet; you need a beastman to watch over you."

"I said, I don't need it."

"You don't know how badly you fell. You were bleeding so much. If I hadn't begged Yu Qian to bring you here to find the Wolf Priest, you..."

"You’re so noisy." Lang Guo didn't know when he had entered. He draped his arm over Lin Qiu’s shoulder, and seeing the beastmen in the room looking at them, he clicked his tongue in disgust.

It was unclear who he was disgusted with.

Yang Zhi was eventually dragged out by Lang Guo.

"With this kind of beastman, does he listen when you talk?"

Lin Qiu pulled up a stool and sat down, saying, "I’ve never encountered a beastman like this."

"That’s why I say you’re slow. Just using your hands would solve it."

Lin Qiu laughed at his words, "In that regard, I’m not as good as you."

Lang Guo was pleased by his flattery and hummed, "You’re too soft-hearted; you don't seem like a wolf beastman at all."

"Like what kind of beastman, then?"

"None of them. Even Tu Kui and the others aren't made of mud. You were probably foolish for too long; this is something that needs practice."

Lin Qiu had indeed dealt more with civilized people in the past, where a cold face could avoid a lot of trouble, so this was his first time seeing someone like this.

"Thanks for the advice."

"Don't mention it. When are you sending him away?" He was talking about that Yang Zhi from earlier.

Lin Qiu: "Tomorrow, when Lang Jin and the others go back to Daze, have him go with them."

Lin Qiu gave Que Xi some water, told him to rest, and then left with Lang Guo, closing the door behind them.

Seeing Yang Zhi squatting by the river, Lin Qiu said, "I didn't know he had this kind of personality before."

"How many in the Wolf tribe knew?"

When Lu Ye was around, he hadn't stood out among the three rescued sub-beastmen.

Later, when Lu Ye left, the two of them were sent to Daze, where there was food and drink. Yang Zhi took care of the foolish Que Xi and didn't really hang out with the wolf beastmen, only talking to Que Xi. Who could have discovered he was like this?

"Forget it, let’s not talk about him. It’s too annoying. What about the trip to the Red Sparrow tribe? Any arrangements?"

"We’ll discuss it tonight. Do you want to go?"

"Can I get away? I’m just curious."

"Not taking the cubs this time?"

"They’re all asleep; I came out to get some air."

"Alright then, come with me to take inventory of the tribe’s assets."

Over the past few years, the beastmen had planted more and more land, and the tribes they had traded with had also come to them one after another to continue trading.

The tribe had saved up quite a lot of goods, all properly stored in caves and the new warehouses built by the beastmen.

Among them were animal skins, herbs, cane sugar, honey, cloth, wine, ironware, pottery... there was plenty of everything, all of which could be taken out for trade.

Lin Qiu had to take inventory of the quantities one by one to see how much could be taken out, and then evaluate what to bring.

While Lin Qiu was busy, Lang Jin and the others woke up from a good sleep and headed west.

Lang Jin leaned his arms on the fence of the red bird pen, watching Lang Rong feed the birds inside, and said: "Rong, the Lion tribe wants to trade for red birds. Help me catch some."

"How many?"

"Seventy."

Lang Rong straightened up, "They want that many this year?"

"I said it was a lot too."

"Do they have that much to trade? Not trading for salt anymore?"

"They are. They brought a lot of animal skins and herbs."

"Prey is so scarce now, where did they get so much..."

"That’s what you don't know. They’ve already taken the business of trading small red birds to the south, and those smaller tribes get their small red birds from them."

Small tribes didn't have abundant resources and only traded for five or ten red birds at a time; the Wolf tribe wouldn't let the Black Feather beastmen go out to deliver them individually.

Not only would such a trip delay the work in the tribe, but they wouldn't get much in return.

The journey was long, and the small tribes didn't dare travel so far; getting them from the Lion tribe, which was closer, was indeed a good method.

"When are you leaving?"

"Tomorrow morning."

"Alright, I’ll have them ready for you tomorrow morning. Are you delivering them or..."

"Let Yu Ya and the others deliver them."

Lang Rong felt relieved. That group of wolf beastmen were reckless; although they had built roads now, they only cared about speed and not stability. If they shook his red birds into trouble, all his hard work hatching the red bird eggs would be for nothing.

*

Tonight, the hunting and gathering team returned early, so they ate dinner early.

The sun had just set, and the sky over the Black Feather tribe was still a pale orange, like the color of a just-ripened orange—light, clean, and not as intense as the evening glow in the rainy season.

After the beastmen finished eating, some found their cubs to play with; some carried basins with towels over their shoulders to the bathhouse; others scattered in front of Lang Mountain, talking, playing, and chasing each other, the sounds of laughter echoing across Lang Mountain.

Lin Qiu was also getting ready to bathe.

The tribe’s bathhouse had been built for two or three years now. Beastmen used to be accustomed to just finding a creek or a pool to wash in, and they didn't wash very often.

Once the bathhouse had water piped in, the water would flow with a turn of a valve, and it even rained down from above, so they didn't have to carry water in anymore. The beastmen gradually started going to the bathhouse to wash.

There was one bathhouse on the north side and one on the south. Each bathhouse had fifty cubicles, which were slightly larger, enough to accommodate an adult wolf beastman in his beast form to wash inside.

The bathhouse was stocked with scented powder and balm for washing fur, all made by Lin Qiu with the help of Lang Bing and Yu Le.

The beastmen were very active, rolling around in the dirt and mud every day, and after a long time, the smell on their bodies would become heavy.

Once they mixed in with the beastmen who washed themselves until they smelled good, without Lin Qiu having to say anything, those sloppier beastmen would sheepishly go to wash, and the utilization rate of the bathhouse became even higher.

It wasn't built in vain.

Lin Qiu went inside, finished washing his body and hair, and took the opportunity to scrub his clothes, hanging them on the clothesline he had strung up in front of his house.

He left his hair loose, water dripping from the ends.

The linen towel didn't absorb water very well, and Lin Qiu’s hair was long and thick now; just wiping it to this point made his arms ache.

He decided to just leave it loose and go outside to let it air dry; it would dry faster that way.

Walking out the door, he saw that Lang Yan had returned as well.

"King, about the matter tonight?"

"We’ll talk when it gets dark."

"What about the Daze side?"

"Let the little wolves tell them when they go back tomorrow. If anyone wants to go, they can go."

Lin Qiu: "Alright. I’m going for a walk, and I’ll check on Que Xi on the way."

Lang Yan hooked his arm around Lin Qiu’s waist and pulled him back.

Lin Qiu took a few steps back, his back pressed against his chest, and turned around helplessly.

Suddenly, it got dark in front of him, and Lin Qiu felt a bite on his lips.

Before he could react, he was released, and Lang Yan walked into the house with his long legs.

Lin Qiu pursed his aching lips; there was a tooth mark on them.

It seemed he couldn't mention Que Xi right now.

*

Over at Que Xi’s, Lang Bing had returned and was checking his wounds again.

Yu Le and Lang Xue were guarding his side, listening to him talk, and they seemed to be listening quite intently.

Lin Qiu stood at the door and watched. Que Xi’s spirits were better now, and he even greeted him with a smile when he saw him.

Lin Qiu decided not to go in; seeing that he was fine, he walked toward the plaza.

Lang Sheng and his group of cubs popped out from somewhere and hugged his legs with giggles.

Lin Qiu smelled the sour, sweaty odor of the cubs and wrinkled his nose: "Where did you go today? I haven't seen you all day."

"We went to the wall."

The city wall was long now, and it was quite wide on top with a broad view, so the cubs liked to run on it.

Lin Qiu pressed his finger against the stinky cub’s head and slowly pushed it away.

"Did you wash?"

"Awoo!" The cub’s fur stood on end, "Qiu, you’re disgusted with us again!"

Lin Qiu curled his lips and pinched the cub’s pouting face, "You’re stinky, and you won't let me be disgusted?"

"Not disgusted!"

"Disgusted."

They were all six, seven, or eight years old—big cubs now—yet they were still like they were when they were little.

Lin Qiu lowered his eyes and met the gaze of Lang Guo’s cub, Lang Jiu.

The cub’s soft hair was soaked through.

"Ah Sheng, take them to wash."

"After we wash, Qiu, you have to play with us."

"What do you want to play?"

"Kickball!"

"Then you’ll just get stinky again."

"Then..."

"Don't 'this' or 'that' me. Go wash quickly. After you wash, your King has something to say. By the time the other beastmen arrive, it’ll just be you little ones missing."

"Awoo! Little ones, let’s go!" Lang Sheng waved his arm, and the cubs ran off with him.

Lin Qiu heard this form of address and tapped Lang Sheng’s head with his finger.

"Don't learn bad habits."

Lin Qiu had only used the term "little ones" once, and this cub had remembered it.

"Awoo, awoo, awoo, awoo, awoo, awoo!" Lang Sheng shouted.

The other cubs followed closely, responding with "Awoo, awoo" as well.

Lin Qiu rubbed his ears and walked toward the cafeteria with a headache.

So noisy.

*

When the time came, the beastmen of Lang Mountain gathered.

The cafeteria was suddenly packed with beastmen, almost to the point of overflowing.

Que Xi and Yang Zhi were not there. Que Xi was not in a condition to move, as he would get dizzy, and Yang Zhi didn't dare come; there were too many beastmen here, he was timid, and besides, he wasn't suited to be here.

"Is everyone here?" Lang Yan asked.

"All the beastmen on Lang Mountain except for the cubs are here."

Lang Sheng sat in the middle with his companions, counting them in a serious manner, then said: "The big cubs are all here, and the little cubs..."

"They are too small, so they won't participate for now," Lang Guo said, pinching his cub’s mouth shut.

"This time, we are discussing the trip to the Western Continent. Going to the Western Continent will take at least a year to return. This time, I won't directly point out which beastmen to go. Those who want to go, stand up; those who don't want to go, stay seated."

As soon as he finished, Lang Bing stood up without hesitation.

The Priest saw him and angrily tapped his cane.

Lang Bing turned his head away, stubbornly refusing to look at the old Priest.

Not many beastmen stood up; many stayed seated, and some were neither standing nor sitting properly, half-squatting...

Lin Qiu sighed helplessly, "What’s the meaning of this?"

Lang Mo was the one half-squatting, and he asked: "King, why not designate us? We can go, or we can not go."

The beastmen nodded. What did it matter if the road was long? They listened to the King anyway. If the King told them to go, they would go; if the King didn't tell them to go, they wouldn't go.

Lang Yan: "I’m considering that some beastmen don't want to leave Lang Mountain for so long, and I want to give those who want to go out and see the world a chance. Whether you stay on Lang Mountain or come along, you are all working for the Wolf tribe; there is no good or bad. So, those who want to go, stand up properly."

The beastmen looked at each other.

Lang Qiao raised his hand and said: "King, can we discuss it among ourselves first?"

"You may."

As soon as he finished, the entire cafeteria was filled with the sound of talking, a buzzing noise like hundreds of mosquitoes flying in the room.

The beastmen found their partners and companions, huddled together, and chattered non-stop.

Lin Qiu rubbed his ears and met the gaze of the cubs sitting in a row in front of him.

They had all turned into their beast forms, all in colors of black, white, and gray; only the cubs still in the den were red wolf beastmen.

They looked much bigger than two- or three-month-old puppies, with pointed wolf ears and tails like feather dusters trailing behind them.

The cubs were attending the meeting seriously, their hind legs squatting, front legs straight, and large paws resting in front of them.

"Qiu, can we go?"

"No."

Lang Sheng’s ears drooped, "When can we go out?"

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan beside him, signaling them to ask their own King.

"King..." The cubs rested their front paws on the table, revealing half their heads, their eyes wet and pleading as they looked at their King.

Lang Yan remained unmoved, instead saying: "You’re still small, and don't go to the wall as much."

The cubs’ bodies went limp, their heads resting on their front legs as they listened to the discussions of the uncles around them, their eyes full of envy.

Lin Qiu saw this, tapped Lang Yan’s knee with his finger under the table, and whispered: "Can they at least go to Daze?"

The cubs’ ears twitched, looking over expectantly.

Lang Yan: "Staying on Lang Mountain is the safest."

The cubs buried their heads in their paws, their whole bodies radiating unhappiness.

Awoo, awoo, awoo, awoo, awoo!

So angry!
