chapters.translated_text:
The boiled soy milk was rich and fragrant, completely different from the soup made by boiling whole black beans.

Lang Bing carried his bowl back to the group of young wolves, sat cross-legged on his animal skin, and sipped it slowly.

The beastmen sniffed the air, unable to stay lying down any longer. They climbed up and surrounded Lang Bing, their eyes fixed intently on his bowl.

"What is this?"

"Soy milk."

Lang Bing took another sip. You couldn't taste the black beans at all in this soy milk; the texture was soft, smooth, and silky without a trace of bean dregs. The bit of white sugar elevated the flavor of the soy milk to a whole new level.

Delicious!

Lang Bing narrowed his eyes slightly, feeling that even if he felt terrible after drinking it, he had to drink his fill.

Lang Jin smelled that unique aroma, his Adam's apple bobbing. He stretched his neck out so far that his eyeballs were almost falling into Lang Bing's bowl.

Lang Bing slapped his hand over Lang Jin's face, pushed him away, and looked at Lang Rong on the other side, saying, "If you want some, go find Qiu. I don't have any extra."

Lang Rong pursed his lips. "Is it good?"

"It's good."

Yu Ya: "It's sweet, right?"

"It's sour."

Lang Jin: "Give me a taste."

Lang Bing glanced at him, held his bowl, and silently turned his back.

What a stingy guy!

Lang Jin was so angry his belly puffed up. He clutched his head, rolled once on the animal skin, and quickly scrambled back up.

Lang Bing took a slow sip of soy milk and added fuel to the fire: "Hmm... it's not good, really not good."

Lang Jin grabbed his own bowl and rushed toward Lin Qiu.

Seeing this, the other beastmen followed a step behind, clutching their bowls as they trailed after him.

A group of beastmen ran through the darkness, making enough noise that the beastmen boiling meat soup noticed them.

Lang Huo: "What are they going to do?"

"Drinking soup?" Lang Yun said.

Black bean soup—isn't that just grinding beans, squeezing out the juice, and boiling it? It shouldn't be any different from boiling the beans directly.

Lang Ying shifted his gaze from Lang Bing, who was sitting quietly on his animal skin, to the group of beastmen rushing toward Lin Qiu.

"It probably doesn't taste bad."

Lang Huo: "Then should I go ask for some for you?"

Thinking of the situation over the past few days, Lang Ying tugged on his sleeve.

"No."

Lin Qiu was currently curdling the tofu.

While gently stirring the black soy milk, he slowly poured the gypsum water into it, one circle, two circles, three circles... controlling the flow to be extremely thin.

There was a technique to stirring the soy milk; it needed to be stirred from the bottom of the pot, and the movements had to be light and slow.

Gradually, flocculent matter appeared in the soy milk.

Lin Qiu was just debating whether to add more gypsum water when Lang Jin rushed over and shouted loudly: "Qiu! I want to drink some!"

Lin Qiu's hand shook, and the remaining gypsum water in the pottery bowl poured right in.

Lin Qiu took a deep breath and glanced at Lang Jin, cold air radiating from him.

He gritted his teeth in restraint and continued stirring.

Lang Jin froze under his gaze, standing stiffly to the side, not daring to move. The other beastmen who had followed also stood silently, holding their bowls, not daring to leave or move forward.

Lang Yan shot Lang Jin a sidelong glance.

"King..." Lang Jin whispered.

Qiu is so scary right now...

The flocculent matter in the pot increased, and the soy milk became clear. Lin Qiu stopped.

He snatched the fire poker from Lang Yan's hand, tapped it straight onto the beastman's head, and gritted his teeth: "Can you change your habit of howling at every little thing!"

"Ow..." Lang Jin lowered his head, letting him hit him, and responded in a tiny voice.

Lin Qiu said irritably: "What are you here for?"

"To drink soy milk."

"It's gone."

Lang Yan took the fire poker from Lin Qiu's hand and shifted his gaze to his side.

Lin Qiu: "There's only a little bit, just taste it and be done!"

"Ow... woo." Lang Jin started to howl, but remembering Lin Qiu's words, he restrained himself and whimpered softly.

Lang Yan gestured to the pottery bowl sitting on a rock to the side. "Pour it yourself."

"Awoo."

The beastmen automatically lined up, stepped forward obediently, and restrained themselves to pour just a tiny bit into their bowls.

Lang Jin took a sip, his eyes lit up, and then he accidentally drank it all.

He licked his lips and looked at the empty soy milk, a flash of disappointment in his eyes.

Seeing this, Lin Qiu said: "Leave once you've finished. Don't block the way here."

The group of beastmen shook their heads, their eyes fixed on the pottery pot.

"There's still some in the pot..."

It's gone?!

When they arrived, they clearly saw white soy milk inside. How did it change in just this short time?

The fire at the bottom of the pot had gone out. Lin Qiu looked into the pot and smelled a hint of gypsum.

He glared at Lang Jin, who silently shuffled behind the others.

Too much gypsum was added to this pot of tofu pudding; it was definitely over-set and had a strong gypsum taste. Lin Qiu had been extremely careful, but it was ruined by Lang Jin's shout.

Lang Jin: "I'm sorry."

"Don't hang around here." Lin Qiu didn't like the look of him right now.

"Qiu, why..." Lang Rong pointed into the pot.

"Because of the gypsum water."

Lin Qiu wanted to explain in detail, but he realized the beastmen wouldn't understand.

He looked at the clear-eyed Lang Rong, thinking that his lesson plan for teaching characters was almost ready. Just learning characters might not be enough; maybe he should prepare math, chemistry, and physics as well?

Otherwise, it was just making tofu pudding, and he was afraid these silly beastmen would think it was some kind of beast god manifestation.

For some reason, Lang Rong felt a chill down his back, the exact same feeling as when he was squatting by the water pool that day.

He slowly turned his head, avoided Lin Qiu's gaze, and moved further back, hiding in the crowd of beastmen, only then feeling more comfortable.

Lin Qiu withdrew his gaze, thinking that this couldn't be rushed.

"Eat the tofu pudding later. You guys go see if the meat on Lang Qiao's side is ready."

"Ow." The beastmen walked away obediently to avoid being annoying.

After walking a few steps, they looked at their empty bowls, remembered the taste of the soy milk, and couldn't help but lift their heads, pouring out the last few drops from the bottom of the bowl and licking the edges.

"Didn't drink enough," a Black Feather beastman whispered.

"N-next time, let's ask Qiu to make more." Yu Ya didn't sound very confident. They were the ones who were picky before, and now they were the ones who wanted to eat it.

"We'll help," Lang Jin whispered in agreement.

A group of the youngest beastmen slowly walked out of the darkness toward the large iron pot.

The sub-beastmen had finished their work and were resting on the rocks. Several male beastmen were watching the fire; besides the meat in the two large iron pots, there was also a pot of tail-grass seed porridge that had just started simmering.

Braised pork should be eaten with dry rice, but unfortunately, they didn't bring much tail-grass seed and didn't dare to eat too much.

As soon as they arrived, the beastmen who had been watching Lin Qiu for a while grabbed their shoulders or patted their heads, asking: "What was Qiu doing over there?"

"Soy milk," Yu Ya said, looking up at his uncle.

Yu Lie ruffled his young beastman's hair messily and asked: "Was it good?"

As soon as he finished speaking, he saw these young beastmen licking their lips.

Was it really that good?

Yu Lie glanced toward Lin Qiu's side.

The cooking areas were about ten meters apart, and Yu Lie had been helping with butchering the prey, so he hadn't gone over to look.

"It's gone."

"What?"

Yu Ya's eyes were clear, and he said with great regret: "It's all gone."

"Then what's in that pot?"

"That's not soy milk."

"It's tofu pudding," Lin Qiu said.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan had also come over. The tofu pudding over there had slowly set, and they were just waiting for the food on this side to be ready.

"What is tofu pudding?" asked Lang Chou, who was sitting in front of the stove.

Before Lin Qiu could answer, several beastmen who had just watched Lin Qiu make the tofu pudding began explaining all at once.

Lin Qiu smelled the meaty aroma and looked at this group of gluttonous beastmen, humming softly.

Who was the one being picky at the start?

Lang Yan squeezed his wrist and said: "Next time they want to eat, make them do it themselves."

"Okay."

Lin Qiu had soaked very few black beans and originally intended to make tofu, but after pressing the tofu pudding, a lot of water was squeezed out, and he was afraid he would only get one piece of tofu, not enough to share.

"Do you want sweet, salty, or spicy?"

"C-can we have all of them?" a group of young beastmen whispered.

Lin Qiu looked at them.

The beastmen buried their heads lower and lower.

Lin Qiu: "That's fine."

It was just a matter of making some seasoning.

The beastmen had made braised pork, and the herb bits were ready-made. He took a small bowl and seasoned it simply, and the fragrant dipping sauce was ready.

The tofu pudding made with gypsum was tender, and whether you ate it sweet or salty depended on your own taste.

However, there was only a little bit of tofu pudding, so they could only get a taste.

The meaty aroma here was heavy, and the beastmen were immersed in it, all attracted by the two pots of braised pork. The things Lin Qiu made with black beans would have to wait behind the meat for now.

The crescent moon moved toward the center of the valley, the sky was clear, and the moonlight gradually illuminated the valley.

The lid on the large iron pot was lifted, and steam billowed up. The beastmen leaned back to avoid the heat.

As the steam cleared, a large pot full of bright red, oily braised pork came into the beastmen's view.

Lin Qiu heard the sound of continuous swallowing.

He pursed his lips, lifted his chin slightly, and looked at Lang Yan standing behind him: "I'm a little hungry too."

Lang Yan lowered his head and pressed his face against Lin Qiu's. "Then eat a bit more later."

There was definitely enough meat tonight. The meat of an entire Youyou beast had been butchered and braised, and the remaining organs and bones had been cleaned and salted, enough for another meal tomorrow morning.

The other Youyou beast would be saved to eat slowly.

Not to mention anything else, the braised pork was ready, and the tail-grass seed porridge cooked quickly; it was golden in color, and after boiling on high heat until now, the rice soup was silky.

Accompanied by a sharp knock on the pot, the cook Lang He said: "Dinner time!"

The beastmen had everything ready when they came out.

Everyone carried their usual pottery bowls, plus a wooden bowl and a water bottle. They were all packed in mesh bags and hung on their bodies, making them very convenient to take out at any time.

The riverbank was full of rocks, so the beastmen used their pottery bowls to scoop a large bowl of braised pork, then used their wooden bowls to fill up with tail-grass seed porridge, and carried them to the flat ground where the animal skins were spread out to eat.

There was a fire burning here too, so they weren't afraid of not being able to see.

"Qiu, tofu pudding," Lang Jin said.

Lin Qiu: "Wait."

The tofu pudding had set, smooth and tender. Lin Qiu brought over three large bowls; each bowl was filled with a little bit, and it was gone.

Lang Jin smelled the meat, resisted his hunger, and helped Lin Qiu carry the bowls over.

The tofu pudding wobbled as they walked, just like the milk cakes Qiu made.

Lin Qiu arranged the three bowls along the campfire and placed the dipping sauces in the middle.

"If you want sweet, add sugar yourself; there are seasonings for salty and spicy."

After speaking, Lin Qiu took a spoonful for himself with the spoon in the bowl. He tasted it; the tofu pudding wasn't as tender as expected, but it still melted in his mouth.

After tasting all three flavors, they were all okay, and only then did Lin Qiu start eating the meat.

Seeing this, the beastmen looked at the meat in their bowls, then at the tofu pudding, which was only one bowl per group, and without further ado, they dug into their bowls first.

In an instant, the tofu pudding on Lin Qiu's side was gone.

Lin Qiu took a bite of the braised pork, his eyes narrowing slightly.

The meat had been stewed long enough, it was soft, tender, and flavorful, and the seasoning was sufficient, so the gamey smell was almost undetectable.

It had been a long time since he had tasted this flavor.

"Qiu, how is it?" Lang He asked with a smile.

Lin Qiu: "Delicious!"

Lang Yun said proudly, "My partner made... mm?"

Lang He pinched his lips together and said gently with a smile: "Eat your food quietly."

Lang Yun nodded silently.

The braised pork had already been divided into their respective bowls, so there was no grabbing it. Lang He looked at the bowl of tofu pudding in front of him, curious.

He remembered the consequences of eating black beans, but he couldn't resist and scooped a little with his spoon.

He added a little bit of sugar, and as soon as it entered his mouth, it slipped down his throat before he even noticed.

Lang He's pupils shrank. He stared blankly at the tofu pudding, and his hand couldn't help but scoop another spoonful.

This time he added the salty seasoning, and tasting it again, the flavor was different from the sweet one.

Lin Qiu: "How is it?"

Lang Yun smiled and quickly scooped another spoonful. Now the beastmen understood: this tofu pudding was delicious too!

With only those three bowls of tofu pudding, the beastmen snatched it clean in a flash.

"Mm!"

"This is made of black beans?!" The beastmen were so shocked they almost wanted to dig out what they had already eaten to take a look.

Lin Qiu: "You guys watched me make it."

Lang Ying pursed his lips at the little bit of tofu pudding he had. He was disgusted by the idea of flatulence, but under Lang Huo's repeated recommendations, he had taken a small bite.

The texture was indeed like the milk cakes Lin Qiu made, but it wasn't greasy at all. It could also be paired with various seasonings, and the flavor changed with the seasoning.

He was staring at Lin Qiu's head right now, his eyes filled with curiosity.

He really wanted to go inside and see what was different about that brain compared to theirs.

How exactly did he think?

"Qiu! Didn't eat enough..." The beastmen regretted it. They were shoveling braised pork into their mouths while staring at Lin Qiu, whining, lacking confidence but wanting to eat more.

Lin Qiu ignored them and said: "Hurry up and eat. Sleep after you're done; we have to hit the road tomorrow."

Beastmen: "..."

If only they hadn't acted so disgusted earlier.

The meat in the bowl was delicious, and the thing Qiu made was also delicious; they wanted both!

"I saw you soaked more black beans just now. Can we eat them tomorrow?" The beastmen were clearly not giving up.

Lin Qiu grinned, and the beastmen followed suit, grinning until their mouths reached their ears.

Lin Qiu: "No."

"Ow! Woo..." Just as the beastmen were about to howl, they faced Lang Yan's cold glare and scrambled to cover each other's mouths.

Lin Qiu curled his lips, very amused.

*

The mountain forest was full of snakes and insects. Countless bugs flew toward the burning campfire and disappeared into the flames.

After finishing a bowl full of braised pork and tail-grass seed porridge, the beastmen clutched their bellies in satisfaction, burped, and then slowly took their empty bowls to the river to wash them clean.

Lin Qiu took his toothbrush and tooth powder, followed in Lang Yan's footsteps, and went to the river to wash up.

Just as he arrived, he watched helplessly as Lang Rong slipped and fell half into the water.

Lin Qiu was so scared his sleepiness vanished.

Fortunately, Lang Jin and Lang Bing, who were beside him, reacted quickly. Both beastmen grabbed his arms at the same time and pulled him back onto the shore.

The two beastmen looked at the soaking wet Lang Rong, still shaken.

All three beastmen stood stiffly, unable to recover for a long time.

Lin Qiu walked over quickly and asked: "Are you okay?"

Lang Rong was so scared his face turned pale, and the pottery bowl in his hand fell into the water. He shook his head foolishly. Lin Qiu watched and pulled him further back.

"Go to the rocky area; the water is deep here."

Lang Bing and Lang Jin supported Lang Rong, whose legs were still weak, and quickly went elsewhere.

Lin Qiu listened to the sound of the rushing river. It was invisible at night, but the sound was like muffled thunder, enveloping them from all directions.

"This water is flowing so fast."

Que Xi sat on a rock on the riverbank, washing his face with a handful of water, and said: "It's always like this here. If you follow this river further south, you'll reach the Blue Lake of the Feather Tribe. This river flows all the way into the Blue Lake, and the fish and shrimp inside support many beastmen."

Lin Qiu: "Does the water rise here?"

Que Xi shook the water off his hands, tucked his wet hair behind his ears, and shook his head lightly: "I haven't encountered it when I came here."

Lin Qiu looked at the river surface, then at the high mountains on both sides of the riverbank.

This valley was narrow, and the river must be very deep.

"If the water rises, we can only climb over the mountain," Lin Qiu whispered, planning to mark an extra path on his map.

If they encountered the rainy season and the valley flooded, that would be no small matter.

After washing up and returning to the flat area, Lin Qiu looked at Lang Rong, who had recovered, felt slightly relieved, and lay down beside Lang Yan.

The river was too fast; if a beastman rolled in, they wouldn't know where to look.

The river valley was also dangerous; they couldn't stay too long. They would rest for the night and leave tomorrow.

They didn't soak many beans tonight. It would be fine to drink some soy milk tomorrow morning, but not enough to make tofu pudding. Making it was time-consuming... better to wait until they left the river valley to find time to make it.

Lin Qiu's mind wandered, and he slowly fell into a deep sleep.

A few clouds slowly drifted in front of the moon, and the valley became pitch black.

The mountains were high and the valley deep. The high mountains on both sides were covered with all kinds of trees and intertwined vines, like a curtain covering everything inside.

The beastmen quieted down.

The beastmen responsible for the night watch hid in the shadows, motionless.

Yu Lie watched the high mountains quietly, while Lang Yun beside him looked up, watching the same spot.

"Is there a tribe nearby?" Lang Yun's gaze was cool, the silliness faded, and his whole body was filled with vigilance against being spied on.

Yu Lie: "Yes."

"Is it that one?"

"Not sure."

When the beastmen stopped here today, Yu Lie had taken the Black Feather beastmen to patrol around as usual. There were indeed tribes nearby, quite a few, just behind the two high mountains on either side.

They were all small tribes and hadn't marked their territory on these two mountain peaks, so when Lang Huo and Lang Ying led the team to hunt this evening, they went straight in.

However, based on the traces of activity nearby, these beastmen would come to the valley to find food, and most of the wolf beastmen knew of their existence.

Their team wouldn't stay long, and those tribes were really too small. They wouldn't take the initiative to disturb them and hoped the other side would be friendly.

It was normal for these tribes to arrange for beastmen to watch them.

As long as they didn't do anything bad, the wolf beastmen and Black Feather beastmen wouldn't take the initiative to cause trouble.

The beastmen's night watch was in pairs, rotating between the first and second half of the night. Yu Lie and Lang Yun watched the first half, and there was no movement on the mountain.

When changing shifts, they reminded Tu Ai and Lang Shun, who were responsible for the second half of the night, and then went to sleep.

The fire had almost gone out by now. Tu Ai added some firewood, hugged his knees, and squatted by the fire, seemingly dazed, but in reality, his ears were pricked up, quietly listening to the movement in all directions.

Lang Shun hid at the back of the team, motionless.

The sky grew darker, and the fire burned and went out.

Tu Ai's ears moved, and he suddenly turned his head to see a hole at the foot of the mountain not far away.

To be precise, this hole should have been there all along.

Tu Ai looked at the small hole. The beastman hiding inside was pitch black and, startled, retracted his claws and hid back into the hole.

Lang Shun was about to come over, but Tu Ai raised his hand behind him to stop him.

The beastman had no malice.

After waiting for a while, the thing blocking the small hole was pushed away. The beastman seemed to have been bumped by something and suddenly rolled out of the hole.

He met Tu Ai's gaze, was so scared his fur stood on end, curled into a ball, and finally rolled down the slope to a few steps away from Tu Ai, motionless, as if playing dead.

Tu Ai watched quietly and recognized it: it was a Black Monkey beastman.

And a cub at that.

The wolf beastmen were awakened by the movement, glanced at it, saw no threat, turned over, smacked their lips, reminiscing about the taste of braised pork in their dreams, and continued to sleep.

Tu Ai saw a few more pairs of small eyes in the cave, timid and hiding inside, not daring to come out.

Just listening to the messy footsteps coming from the cave, he knew how anxious they were right now.

Tu Ai thought for a moment, took out his dried fish from the evening, placed it beside him, and continued to observe.

After a long time, the little black ball finally slowly retracted its tail and claws, revealing its little head.

Tu Ai tore off a bit of fish meat and reached out.

The Black Monkey cub's fur stood on end again, and it immediately curled itself up.

Tu Ai paused and continued to wait.

Lang Shun recalled what Yu Lie had said, paying attention to the surroundings while watching Tu Ai lure the cub.

Yu Lie said there were at least three tribes nearby.

Following the direction of the river, the mountain on the left was the Black Monkey tribe. They were small in size; an adult Black Monkey beastman was only the size of a medium pottery jar, and the small ones... like the one in front of him, were only the size of his palm when curled up.

There were also two Feather Tribe tribes on the mountain on the right.

The beastmen on this mountain seemed to be more timid; no beastmen were lying on the mountain top watching them. Only this group of Black Monkey beastmen on the left...

Lang Shun had a thought, remembered something, and silently counted the number of cubs by the fire and hidden in the cave.

Looking at the mountain top again, there were no more prying eyes.

Could it be that these cubs were the ones watching them all night?

"Squeak." The cub made a very light sound, looking at the fish meat Tu Ai was holding out again. Its claws gripped, eager to try.

Tu Ai: "Eat it."

The cub quickly looked up at him and tentatively reached out.

The tiny black claw had just touched the dried fish and was quickly retracting when Tu Ai immediately tightened his fingers. The cub was scared into a ball and was lifted by Tu Ai to his front.

"Squeak!!!"

In the small hole, the movement of the three cubs became even more chaotic.

Tu Ai patted the furry ball in his hand and whispered: "Eat."

The black ball shivered, wrapping its claws and tail even tighter around itself.

Tu Ai whispered: "I'll ask a few questions. Once I'm done, that big piece of dried fish is yours, and I'll let you go back."

After a while, the little black ball finally looked up. Under the firelight, its round, bright eyes were watery.

Tu Ai smiled embarrassedly.

It seemed he had scared the little guy to tears.

Lang Shun silently handed over his own dried fish.

The little black ball shrank again, and Tu Ai said: "Two pieces of dried fish."

"Y-you ask."

Tu Ai looked at the small hole. "Your companion went back to report, right? Did you sneak out? Do you want to..."

"Squeak!!!"

The cub darted out, its speed incredibly fast, disappearing into the small hole in an instant.

Tu Ai listened to the clanging sounds coming from inside. After a while, the little black ball finally walked out again.

It hesitated, not daring to move forward, but was still thinking about the dried fish Tu Ai mentioned.

Tu Ai took the initiative: "Did you discuss it?"

The little black ball nodded, carefully looked at the sleeping wolf beastmen, and slowly approached Tu Ai.

"Come on, here's the deposit first." Tu Ai took a piece of dried fish and stuffed it into its arms.

The little black ball held the large piece of dried fish foolishly. The dried fish was longer than it was; one piece of dried fish could completely cover it.

It stumbled and sat on the ground.

It looked at the dried fish in its arms, then at Tu Ai, and the tip of its tail curled and landed gently on Tu Ai's palm.

Deal.

煮熟的豆浆香味浓郁，跟那完完整整的黑豆煮出来的汤完全不一样。
狼冰端着碗，回到小狼堆里，盘腿坐在自己的兽皮上，慢悠悠地喝着。
兽人们吸了吸鼻子，渐渐趴不住，爬起来围着狼冰，一双眼睛直勾勾落在他碗中。
“这是什么？”
“豆浆。”
狼冰又抿了一口，这豆浆喝着完全尝不出来是黑豆的味道，口感柔润丝滑，没有一点豆渣，那点白糖更是将豆浆的风味提升了一大截。
好喝！
狼冰微微眯眼，觉得就算喝完之后会很糟糕，他也要喝个够。
狼金闻到那独特的味道，喉结滚动，脖子伸得长长的，眼珠子都快掉狼冰碗里了。
狼冰一巴掌盖在他脸上，将他推开，又看另一侧的狼溶，道：“要喝去找楸，我可没多的。”
狼溶抿了抿唇，“好喝吗？”
“好喝。”
羽涯：“是甜的对不对？”
“酸的。”
狼金：“你给我尝一口。”
狼冰看他一眼，捧着碗默默背过身去。
这护食样！
狼金气得肚子鼓了鼓，捂着脑袋又往兽皮上一滚，滚了一圈快速爬起来。
狼冰慢慢来上一口豆浆，加了一把火，“嗯……不好喝，很不好喝。”
狼金抓上自己的碗就往林楸身边冲。
其他兽人见状，落后他一步，也捧着碗跟上去。
一群兽人在黑暗中奔跑，动静大得煮肉汤的兽人们也注意到这边。
狼火：“他们去干什么？”
“喝汤？”狼云道。
黑豆汤，不就是把豆子磨了挤出汁水煮，跟直接煮豆子应该没什么两样。
狼影目光一转，从静坐在兽皮上的狼冰身上移到奔向林楸那边的兽人队伍上。
“应该味道不差。”
狼火：“那我去给你要点？”
狼影一想到这几天的情况，拽住他衣角。
“不要。”
林楸正在点豆腐。
他一边轻柔地搅拌着黑豆豆浆，一边把石膏水缓缓倒入其中，一圈两圈三圈……水流控制得极细。
搅拌豆浆也有讲究，需要从锅底搅上来，动作要轻，要慢。
渐渐的，豆浆里出现絮状物。
林楸正琢磨着要不要再加点石膏水进去，狼金急匆匆跑来就大声吆喝一句：“楸！我要喝！”
林楸手一抖，陶碗里剩下的一点石膏水全倒了进去。
林楸深吸一口气，看了一眼狼金，冷气嗖嗖往外冒。
他磨了磨牙忍耐，又继续搅拌。
狼金被他看得一僵，杵在一旁不敢动弹。其他跟上来的兽人也默默站好，捧着碗，不敢走也不敢往前。
狼岩斜睨了狼金一眼。
“王……”狼金小小声道。
楸现在好吓兽人……
锅里絮状物增多，豆浆变得清亮，林楸停了下来。
他抄起狼岩手里的烧火棍，直直往兽人脑袋上一敲，咬牙切齿道：“你能不能改一改你那动不动就嗷嗷叫的习惯！”
“嗷……”狼金低头任由他打，小小声地应道。
林楸没好气道：“来干什么？”
“喝豆浆。”
“没了。”
狼岩拿过林楸手上的烧火棍，目光往身侧移了一下。
林楸：“只有一点，尝尝味儿得了！”
“嗷……呜。”狼金刚想叫，想起林楸刚刚的话，极力克制自己，叫得小小声。
狼岩示意身侧石头上放着陶碗，“自己倒。”
“嗷呜。”
兽人们自动排队，乖乖巧巧地上前，克制地往碗里倒上那么一点点。
狼金端着碗抿了一口，眼睛一亮，然后一不小心就喝完了。
他舔了舔嘴唇，再看已经没剩了的豆浆，眼里闪过失落。
林楸见了，道：“喝完就走，别在这里挡着。”
一群兽人摇头，目光落在陶锅里。
“锅里还……”
没了？！
他们过来时分明看见里面还是白白的豆浆，就这么一会儿，怎么就变了？
锅底的火灭了，林楸看了看锅里，闻到了一股石膏味儿。
他瞪了狼金一眼，狼金默默往他们身后挪了挪。
这一锅豆花石膏倒多了，肯定老了，石膏味儿也重，林楸千小心万小心，还是被狼金一嗓子搞坏了。
狼金：“对不起。”
“别守在这边。”林楸现在看他不顺眼。
“楸，为什么……”狼溶指了指锅里。
“加了石膏水的原因。”
林楸想细致解释，可他发现兽人肯定听不懂。
他看着眸子清澈的狼溶，想着，他那教习字的教案准备得差不多了，光习字好像也不行，要不然数学、化学、物理一起准备得了？
不然点个豆花而已，他怕这些傻兽人还当什么兽神显灵了。
不知怎么，狼溶觉得有点后背发凉，就跟那天蹲在水潭边一模一样的感觉。
他缓慢侧头，避开林楸的视线，又往后挪了挪，藏在兽人堆里，这才舒服了些。
林楸收回目光，想着，这事急不来。
“豆花等会儿吃，你们去看看狼乔那边的肉好了没有。”
“嗷。”兽人们乖乖走开，免得讨嫌。
走了几步，又看看空荡荡的碗，想起那豆浆的味道，忍不住捧着碗仰起头，把碗底剩下那最后几滴倒出来，再嘬了嘬碗边。
“没喝够。”一个黑羽兽人小声道。
“下、下次叫楸多做一点。”羽涯这话说得没什么底气。嫌弃的是他们，现在想吃的也是他们。
“我们帮忙。”狼金小声附和道。
一群年纪最小的兽人慢慢从黑夜里走出来，到了大铁锅这边。
亚兽人们已经忙完了，他们坐在石头上正在休息。几个雄兽人看着火，除了两口大铁锅的肉，还有一锅刚刚开始熬的尾巴草籽粥。
红烧肉本该配干饭的，可惜他们没带多少尾巴草籽，不敢多吃。
他们一过来，关注了林楸那边好一会儿的兽人抱住他们肩膀，或者拍了拍他们脑袋，问：“楸那边在做什么？”
“豆浆。”羽涯仰头看着自家阿叔道。
羽猎胡乱捋了一把自家小兽人的脑袋毛，道：“好吃？”
话落，就看到这些小兽人舔嘴巴。
真有这么好吃？
羽猎往林楸那边看了一眼。
两边做饭的位置大概隔了十几米，羽猎一直帮着这边分割猎物，也没过去看过。
“没了。”
“什么？”
羽涯双眼清澈，万分可惜道：“都喝没了。”
“那那个锅里的是什么？”
“不是豆浆。”
“是豆花。”林楸道。
林楸和狼岩也过来了，那边豆花慢慢凝固好了，就等着他们这边好了开饭。
“豆花是什么？”坐灶前的狼丑问。
他问完，不等林楸开口，几个刚刚围观了林楸点豆花的兽人就七嘴八舌地解释起来。
林楸闻着肉香味，瞧着这群馋嘴的兽人，轻轻哼了一声。
开始嫌弃的是谁？
狼岩捏捏他手腕，道：“下次他们要吃让他们自己做。”
“好啊。”
林楸泡的黑豆少，本来打算做豆腐，但把那点豆花一压，挤出不少水分来，恐怕就只能得一块豆腐，不够分。
“吃甜的还是咸的、辣的？”
“能、能都要吗？”一群年轻兽人小声道。
林楸看着他们。
兽人们把脑袋越埋越低。
林楸：“都可以。”
也就调个料的事。
兽人们做了红烧肉，香草碎末都是现成的，他拿了个小碗简单调味，香喷喷的蘸料就好了。
石膏做的豆花嫩，吃甜的咸的看各自口味。
不过豆花就那么一点，也就能尝个味儿。
这边肉香味浓重，兽人们徜徉在肉香里，全被这两锅红烧肉吸引。林楸用黑豆做的东西，暂时要排在肉后面。
弯月往山谷中间移动，天空洁净，月辉渐渐将山谷中照得微明。
大铁锅上的锅盖被揭开，水汽滚滚而腾起，兽人们后仰着身子避开那热气。
遮眼的蒸汽一散，满满一大锅红亮的泛着油光的红烧肉映入兽人眼帘。
林楸听到了接连不断的咽口水的声音。
他抿了抿唇，微扬起下巴，看着身后站立的狼岩道：“我也有点馋了。”
狼岩低头，脸贴了贴他的脸，“那等会儿多吃点。”
今晚的肉肯定是够的，整整一头呦呦兽的肉被兽人全弄下来做了红烧肉，剩下的那些内脏跟骨头也洗干净了，用盐腌着，明早上还能吃一顿。
剩下那头呦呦兽则要留着慢慢吃了。
不说其他，红烧肉好了，那尾巴草籽粥也熟得快，色泽金黄，大火烧煮到这会儿米汤能拉出丝来。
伴随着一声利落的敲锅声，掌勺的狼禾道：“开饭！”
兽人们出来时东西都准备得齐全。
大家常用来吃饭的陶碗都随身带着，还有一个木碗，一个水壶。都用网兜装好，挂在身上随时都可以拿出来，很方便。
河滩石头多，兽人们用自己的陶碗盛了一大碗的红烧肉，再用木碗装了一碗尾巴草籽粥，端着去铺兽皮那边的平地吃饭。
这边也烧着火堆，不怕看不见。
“楸，豆花。”狼金道。
林楸：“等着。”
豆花都凝固好了，滑滑嫩嫩的。林楸拿了三个大碗过去，一个碗装上一点就没了。
狼金闻着肉香，忍着馋，帮着林楸把碗端过来。
那豆花随着走动一晃一晃的，像楸做的奶糕一样。
林楸沿着火堆把三个碗摆开，蘸料也放在中间。
“吃甜的自己加糖，咸的、辣的都各有调料。”
说完，林楸先用碗里的勺子给自己来了一勺。他尝了尝味道，豆花没预期的嫩，但还是一抿就化开。
一一尝过三种味道，都还可以，林楸才开始吃肉。
兽人们见状，看看碗里的肉，再看看眼前仅仅只有一碗的豆花，不管三七二十一，先往碗里刨了一点再说。
霎时，林楸这一方的豆花没了。
林楸咬了一口红烧肉，眼睛微眯。
这肉炖的时间足够久，软烂入味，调料也下得足，肉腥味几乎吃不出来。
这一口味道也是好久没吃了。
“楸，怎么样？”狼禾笑问。
林楸：“好吃！”
狼云得意，“我伴侣做的……唔？”
狼禾捏着他两片唇瓣，温柔笑道：“安安静静吃你的。”
狼云默默点头。
红烧肉已经分了，就在各自碗里，抢不着。狼禾看着面前那一碗豆花，倒是好奇。
他想起吃了黑豆的后果，但还是没忍住，用勺子舀了一点。
他放了一点点糖，一抿入口，几乎没有察觉，豆花就滑入喉咙。
狼禾瞳孔一缩，呆看着那豆花，手没忍住，又盛了一勺。
这次放的咸味的调料，再一尝，风味跟甜的又不一样。
林楸：“怎么样？”
狼云微笑，飞快又舀了一勺，这下兽人明白了，这豆花也好吃！
就那么三个碗的豆花，兽人们三下五除二抢了个干净。
“唔！”
“这是黑豆做的？！”兽人惊得恨不能把吃进嘴里的掏出来看看。
林楸：“你们不是看着我做的。”
狼影抿着嘴里那一点点豆花，他嫌弃放屁，在狼火的连声推荐下，才咬了那么一小口。
口感确实像林楸做的奶糕，但吃着一点不腻味。还能放各式各样的调味料，味道随着调味的变化而变化。
他此刻盯着林楸的脑袋，眼里带着探究。
他很想进去看看，那脑袋里到底跟他们有什么不一样。
到底是怎么想的？
“楸！没吃够……”兽人们后悔了，他们一边往嘴里刨着红烧肉，一边盯着林楸，哼哼唧唧，没底气，但想吃。
林楸无视，道：“赶紧吃吧，吃完睡觉，明天还要赶路呢。”
兽人：“……”
早知道不表现得那么嫌弃了。
碗里的肉好吃，楸做的那个也好吃，都想吃！
“我看到你刚刚还泡了黑豆，明天能吃不？”兽人显然不死心。
林楸嘴巴一咧，兽人跟着傻乐呵，嘴角咧到耳根了。
林楸：“不能。”
“嗷！呜呜……”兽人们在快要叫出来时，顶着狼岩的冷眼，手忙脚乱地互相捂住同伴的嘴。
林楸嘴角一翘，乐得很。
*
山林多蛇虫，那架起的火堆上，数不尽的虫子飞来，没入火焰。
一碗满满当当的红烧肉就着尾巴草籽粥吃尽，兽人们餍足地捂着肚子，打着饱嗝，再慢吞吞地拿着空了的碗去河边洗干净。
林楸拿上牙刷牙粉，踩着狼岩的步子，跟去河边洗漱。
才刚到，就眼睁睁看着狼溶一脚踩滑，半个身体栽进水中。
林楸吓得瞌睡都醒了。
好在他身边狼金和狼冰反应快，两个兽人同时抓住他的手臂，往岸边一提，把他带了上来。
两个兽人看着湿漉漉的狼溶，心有余悸。
三个兽人都僵立着，半晌没回神。
林楸快步走上前，问：“没事吧？”
狼溶吓得脸都白了，手里的陶碗也落进水里。他傻傻摇头，林楸看着，又把他往后拉了拉。
“去乱石那边，这边水深。”
狼冰跟狼金架着腿还发软的狼溶，赶紧去了别处。
林楸听着河水翻滚的声音，夜里看不见，声如闷雷似的，从四面八方笼罩过来。
“这水流得好急。”
雀溪坐在河滩的石头上，就着一汪水搓洗脸颊，闻言道：“这里是这样的，沿着这条河再往南边走，就到羽族的蓝湖了。这河一直流到蓝湖里，里头的鱼虾养活了不少兽人。”
林楸：“这边会涨水吗？”
雀溪甩甩手上的水，把湿了的头发撩到耳后，轻摇头道：“我过来这边的时候，没有遇到过。”
林楸看看河面，再看向河岸两边的高山。
这处山谷狭窄，河水应当很深。
“要是涨水了，只能翻山。”林楸小声说着，打算给自己的地图上多标注一条路。
要是遇到雨季，山谷涨水，那可不是小事。
洗漱完，回到平坦的地方，林楸看着已经恢复过来的狼溶，心里稍稍放下些，跟着躺在狼岩身边。
那河水太急，要是兽人滚下去，他们都不知道去哪里找。
河谷也危险，他们不能停留太久，休息一晚，明天就得离开。
今晚泡的豆子不多，明早喝点豆浆还行，做豆花不够。做这个也费时间……还是等离开了河谷再找时间做吧。
林楸胡思乱想着，慢慢也睡熟了。
几朵云慢慢行至月前，山谷间黑得伸手不见五指。
山高谷深，两岸高山上长满了各式各样的树木，藤蔓交错，如幕布一样遮掩着里面的一切。
兽人们安静下来了。
负责守夜的兽人隐在暗处，一动不动。
羽猎静静看着那高山上，身旁狼云仰着头，与他看着同一处。
“这附近有部落？”狼云目光微凉，褪去了傻气，浑身是对窥探着的警惕。
羽猎：“有。”
“是那个？”
“不确定。”
今天兽人们停留在这一处时，羽猎照旧带着黑羽兽人先四处巡逻过。这附近确实有部落，还不少，就在这左右两座高山后头。
他们都是小部落，也没把领地划定到这两边山头，所以今天傍晚的时候狼火和狼影带队才会直接进去捕猎。
不过根据附近活动的痕迹，这群兽人们会到山谷来找食，狼兽人也大多都知道他们的存在。
自家队伍不会停留多久，那几个部落也实在太小，他们不会主动打扰，也希望对方友善一些。
这些部落安排兽人来盯着他们也很正常。
只要他们不做坏事，狼兽人和黑羽兽人也不会主动挑事。
兽人守夜是两两一组，上半夜和下半夜轮换。羽猎和狼云盯了前半夜，山上没有动静。
交班时，他们提醒了下负责下半夜的兔艾和狼顺，随后便睡下了。
火堆烧到这会儿已经快熄了，兔艾又往里添了些木柴，抱着膝头蹲在火堆边，看似在发呆，实际耳朵竖起，静静听着四方动静。
狼顺隐在队伍最后面，没动。
天色愈沉，火堆烧了又熄。
兔艾耳朵动了动，忽的转头，便看见不远处山脚多了一个洞。
确切的说，这洞应该一直都有。
兔艾看着小洞，那里面藏着的兽人黑漆漆的，被吓得一下缩回爪子，藏进小洞。
狼顺要过来，兔艾往后抬起手，制止了他。
兽人没恶意。
就这么又等了一会儿，那小洞前挡着的东西又被推开。兽人像被什么撞了一下，忽然骨碌碌地从洞里滚出来。
他一下对上兔艾的视线，吓得毛都炸了，直接蜷缩成一个球，最后沿着斜坡滚到离兔艾几步远处，一动不动，像在装死。
兔艾静静看着，这下认出来，是个黑猴兽人。
还是个幼崽。
狼兽人们被动静惊醒，瞥了一眼，见没什么威胁，又翻个身，咂巴着嘴，回味着梦里红烧肉的味道，继续睡觉。
兔艾看着那山洞里还有几双小眼睛，怯生生的，躲在里面不敢出来。
光是听着洞里隐隐传来的凌乱的脚步声，就知道他们此刻有多着急。
兔艾想了想，掏出自己晚上的鱼干，就放在身侧，然后继续观察。
许久，那小黑球终于缓缓收了尾巴和爪子，露出小脑袋来。
兔艾撕了点鱼肉下来，伸手。
黑猴幼崽又一炸毛，立刻把自己团了起来。
兔艾一顿，又继续等着。
狼顺回想羽猎说的话，一边注意着四周的动静，一边看兔艾诱引小崽子。
羽猎说，这附近起码有三个部落。
顺着河流的方向，左边的山头就是这黑猴一族的兽人，他们个头小，成年黑猴兽人也就中等陶罐大小，小的……就跟前这个，团起来只有他一个巴掌大。
右边山头也有，是两个羽族部落。
这边山头的兽人胆子好像要小一些，没兽人趴在山头看他们。只有左边这群黑猴兽人们……
狼顺心念一动，想起什么，默默数了数火堆边和藏在洞里的幼崽数量。
再看山头，已经没有窥探的视线了。
难不成盯了他们半夜的就是这群幼崽？
“吱。”幼崽很轻地一声，看着兔艾又递过来的鱼肉。爪子抓握，跃跃欲试。
兔艾：“吃吧。”
幼崽飞快抬起头看他一眼，试探着伸手。
那黑漆漆的小爪才才摸到鱼干快速往回收，兔艾立刻收紧手指，幼崽吓得团成球，被兔艾拎到跟前来。
“吱！！！”
小洞里，那三个幼崽的动静更加凌乱。
兔艾拍了拍手里炸毛的球，低声道：“吃。”
黑球瑟瑟发抖，爪子和尾巴把自己包裹得更紧。
兔艾低声道：“我问点事，问完那一大条鱼干归你，再放你回去。”
半晌，小黑球终于抬头，火光下，他那一双圆亮的眼睛水汪汪的。
兔艾不好意思地笑笑。
好像把人家吓哭了。
狼顺默默把自己的鱼干递过来。
小黑球又一缩，兔艾道：“两条鱼干。”
“你、你问。”
兔艾看看那小洞，“你同伴回去报信了，你们偷跑出来的？要不要……”
“吱！！！”
幼崽一下蹿了出去，速度奇快，一瞬间消失在小洞中。
兔艾听着里头传出叮铃哐当的声音，好一会儿，小黑球终于又走出来。
他踟蹰着不敢往前，又惦记着兔艾说的鱼干。
兔艾主动道：“商量好了？”
小黑球头一点，小心翼翼看了看睡着的狼兽人们，缓缓靠近兔艾。
“来，先给定金。”兔艾拿着一条鱼干往他怀里一塞。
小黑球傻呆呆地抱着一大条鱼干，那鱼干比他还长，一个鱼干能把他完全遮住。
他踉跄了下，一屁股坐在地上。
他看看怀里鱼干，再看看兔艾，尾巴尖一弯，轻轻落在兔艾掌心。
成交。

chapters.title: 第222章
chapters.translated_text:
The fire burned a bit brighter. Tu Ai poked at the center of the pile, sending scarlet sparks drifting everywhere.

Lang Shun sat a short distance from Tu Ai, while between them, the four black monkey cubs were hugging their share of dried fish, gnawing on them quickly and eagerly.

Tu Ai turned the piece of dried fish he was still roasting and whispered to the cubs, who were only as tall as his calves, "Eat slowly, there are bones."

"Zhi zhi zhi!"

"You're saying you haven't eaten for two days?"

"Zhi!"

Lang Shun silently sped up the pace at which he broke the dried fish, taking the opportunity to remove the large bones inside.

He spread his large hand out in front of the smallest cub beside him. The cub grabbed it, its paws nimbly tearing the fish into four portions. It kept only its own share and passed the rest in a bundle to the other side.

The other cubs cooperated tacitly; one hand stuffed fish into their mouths while the other reached out to take new pieces from their companions.

"What happened to the adult beastmen of your tribe?"

"Zhi..."

"Expelled?"

The cubs slowed their eating. All four sniffed at the same time, heads bowed, looking pitiful.

Seeing this, Tu Ai took the roasted fish off the fire and placed it horizontally in front of the cubs.

"Zhi!!!" The four little black balls pounced on it and started gnawing.

They weren't sad anymore.

Tu Ai and Lang Shun exchanged a look, both feeling sympathetic.

They had learned what they needed to know: in short, the nearby Black Monkey tribe had recently undergone a change in leadership. The new chief had defeated the old one and expelled his four cubs from the tribe.

The previous chief had been severely injured in the fight and had died. The cubs' father was young, beautiful, and fertile, so he had become the new chief's mate and no longer wanted these four cubs.

They were only a year old and couldn't transform into human form yet. The new chief must have thrown them out with the intention of letting them die.

Fortunately, there were still kind-hearted beastmen in the Black Monkey tribe who would secretly help them. Combined with their own ability to climb trees to pick fruit and raid bird nests, they had managed to survive this long.

"Hiccup—" The four little cubs were full.

They had only gnawed one side of the last whole dried fish Tu Ai gave them, picking the meat clean until only the skeleton remained. The other half was left perfectly intact, seemingly saved for tomorrow.

Full and sleepy, the cubs flicked their long tails, hooking them tightly together. Their round, full bellies rose and fell as they drifted off to sleep.

*

Dawn broke.

The first thing the beastmen did upon waking was roll up their animal skin blankets and hay, tying them with thin hemp ropes, ready to be carried away.

Lin Qiu let his long hair hang loose, leaned on Lang Yan’s arm, and put on his animal skin boots.

He swept his gaze toward the fire pit, which now only had embers left, and asked, "Where are those little cubs from last night?"

"They left," Lang Yan said.

Lin Qiu looked toward the foot of the mountain and spotted a small hole blocked by leaves and hay. The opening was about the size of an adult beastman's pottery bowl, plugged so tightly it was hard to notice at first glance.

"Qiu! Bean curd!" A few young beastmen saw him wake up and ran over, smiling at him ingratiatingly.

Lin Qiu: "No."

"Qiu, we were wrong, we won't say we don't want to eat black beans anymore..."

Lin Qiu raised a hand to interrupt them, saying, "There aren't enough beans, and it takes time. It can only be made for the evening meal."

"Then soak more black beans now!"

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan.

Lang Yan glanced at the young beastmen, wrapped an arm around Lin Qiu, and walked away.

Lang Jin and the others didn't dare to follow.

"Qiu..."

"Soak them yourselves."

"Ao!!!"

By the riverbank, at a clear water pool.

Just as Lin Qiu and Lang Yan stopped, Tu Ai and Que Xi arrived.

"King, Qiu! Some Black Monkey beastman cubs came by last night."

Lin Qiu said, "We know."

Beastmen were never anything less than vigilant when out in the wild; how could they not have known about the movement last night?

Que Xi said softly, "I went to take a look at the Black Monkey tribe this morning. Their tribe is at the bottom of the valley on the other side of the mountain. It's a small tribe with seventy or eighty beastmen."

Lin Qiu: "We'll leave after breakfast; no need to disturb them."

Que Xi nodded.

Tu Ai looked at Lang Yan and Lin Qiu, swallowing the words he wanted to say.

There were countless suffering cubs on the Beast God Continent; at least these few still had elders from their own tribe to feed them, so they could survive.

The days were getting longer, and while there was still some mist covering the mountain peaks when they first woke, the sun came out shortly after, and the mist dispersed.

The beastmen hurried to finish breakfast, shouldered their belongings, and continued on their journey.

The terrain along the big river was steep, and the beastmen had to walk south along the cliffside. Fortunately, they had the Black Feather beastmen scouting the path, so they wouldn't end up on any dead ends.

As usual, Lang Huo and Lang Ying led the way, with Lin Qiu and Lang Yan at the very back.

The mountain road was difficult, especially with the beastmen carrying so many supplies.

The Black Feather beastmen flew in mid-air to find the direction, while Lang Ying and Lang Huo identified the most suitable footing. The beastmen followed closely, eyes fixed on their feet, moving with extreme caution.

With the roaring sound of the turbulent river in their ears and the steep mountain path, no one dared to lose focus.

They walked along the mountain by the riverbank for two days before finally emerging from the rugged mountains, and the view suddenly opened up.

Outside the mountains was a vast grassland that stretched all the way to a massive lake as blue as a gemstone.

This was Blue Lake.

Looking out, the lake seemed boundless to the south, with only a straight cliff wall on the west side. It looked as if the mountain had been cleaved by a blade, standing as a straight barrier on the west side of the great lake.

It was already afternoon, and the setting sun was hanging low. The evening glow was magnificent, spreading across the great lake like colorful silk.

Suddenly, the sound of flapping wings filled the air. The beastmen looked up to see thousands of birds with snow-white feathers and pink flight feathers soaring over their heads.

They moved with graceful, dancing postures, as if chasing the sunset into the depths of the colorful clouds.

Grassland, blue lake, birds, evening glow... Lin Qiu's eyes widened slightly as he took in the vast and magnificent scenery.

He murmured, "This view..."

"So many birds, so much meat... Ao!"

Lin Qiu looked at the fresh poop on Lang Yun's forehead, speechless, and leaned against Lang Yan, nudging him to move aside.

Lang Yan chuckled, his neck brushing against Lin Qiu, and said, "We've reached the edge of their territory."

"Were those beastmen just now?"

"Yes."

Lang He looked at his mate and immediately moved far away.

Lang Yun looked pitiful: "He!"

Lang He turned his head away, saying, "Go wash up! You're filthy!"

Lang He didn't plan on getting within a step of Lang Yun for the next few days.

After the commotion, Lang Huo and Lang Ying walked over.

The lake breeze was gentle, and orange and smoky-purple flowers bloomed on the grass. The flowers and grass reflected the fading sunset, swaying gently, making everyone feel relaxed.

"Achoo! Achoo!!! Why are there so many flowers?"

Lin Qiu: "..."

He helplessly rested his head against Lang Yan's neck, his claws digging into the ground. Can't we just enjoy the scenery in peace!

Lang Yan tilted his head to rub against him, a faint smile on his face.

"King, this is someone else's territory ahead. Are we sleeping here tonight?" Lang Qiao looked around and asked loudly.

"Put the things down."

The lake was extremely vast; calling it a lake was more like an inland sea.

There were many Feather tribes here, each dividing the territory along the lake, and even the parts of the lake surface belonged to specific tribes clearly.

"Their territory includes Blue Lake and a large area of small mountains west of the cliff," Que Xi said to Lang Qiao, who had started digging a fire pit.

"Are they all big tribes?" Lang Qiao asked while digging, looking at the western cliff, which was covered in dense holes.

One hole per family; how many beastmen must live there?

"The main ones are the White Feather tribe and the Red Feather tribe. Each tribe has thousands of beastmen. Others like the Blue Sparrow tribe and the Black Beak tribe only have a few hundred combined."

Before Xiong Chen chose to attack a tribe, he would learn everything about them, and Que Xi had learned quite a bit as well.

These Feather tribes were also targets of Xiong Chen, who had stolen many of their eggs and cubs when he led the rogue beastmen.

Que Xi still remembered how these Feather tribes were filled with uncontrollable rage, their eyes splitting with fury.

It was miserable and pitiful, but he had been powerless to help.

Que Xi's gaze fell on the clear blue lake. In his memory, the blood in the lake spread like the evening glow in the sky, eventually dyeing the entire shore red.

His head throbbed. Que Xi covered his head, the veins on his forehead bulging slightly.

"What's wrong?" Lang Qiao asked.

"Nothing, I'm fine." Que Xi's voice was extremely soft, scenes of blood-red flashing through his eyes before being forcibly suppressed.

He had to return to his tribe.

He had to return to his tribe safely and in one piece!

*

It was rare to encounter big tribes, and they had brought so many things, surely wanting to trade.

Lang Yan called Yu Lie over and told him to take a few beastmen to ask the Feather beastmen across the way about trading.

Yu Lie agreed and took Yu Ya and the others with him.

Around Blue Lake, except for the east, all sides were raised high mountains. Because the lake was so large, like a sea, the beastmen could only see the cliff on the west side.

This cliff was near the river's mouth, where food in the water was abundant, making it the best place to build nests.

The cliff stretched for miles, divided between the White Feather and Red Feather tribes, each occupying half. Other tribes could only huddle in the cliffs in other directions.

At this moment, dozens of wolf beastmen and Black Feather beastmen approached Blue Lake from the river. The Feather beastmen who were out were called back, standing in strict formation.

Within the White Feather tribe, at the top of the cliff.

White Feather Chief Bai Qi stood on the highest tree on the cliff top. She held onto the trunk, her white hair tied high, her posture upright and imposing.

She watched the group of wolf beastmen, who seemed as relaxed as if they had arrived at their own tribe, her eyes cold.

Below, several White Feather beastmen perched on the branches; their beast forms were slender and delicate, full of ethereal grace.

These were the influential beastmen of the White Feather tribe.

The other tribesmen were currently back in their nests, on guard, protecting their eggs and cubs.

"Chief, should we drive them away?" the beastmen below asked, looking up at their chief, Bai Qi.

"We don't know the situation, don't clash head-on." Several red shadows flew through the air and landed on a tree opposite them.

"Hong Jiao, what are you here for?" Bai Qi said coldly.

Their two tribes fought tooth and nail over food here daily; they had no pleasant looks for each other.

Red Feather Chief Hong Jiao smiled slightly, "Just came to look."

"Get lost!"

Hong Jiao: "No."

Bai Qi's chest heaved. She leaped from the treetop, swinging her fist toward Hong Jiao's face.

Hong Jiao dodged, avoiding his face, and reached out to grab Bai Qi's fist, helplessly pulling her down from the treetop.

"Alright, put aside old grudges for now. I'm here to discuss something."

Bai Qi shook off his hand and looked at the Black Feather beastmen who had flown to the side of Blue Lake.

They didn't advance, but looked toward this side, seemingly waiting for them to send someone over.

"I'll go see." As soon as Hong Jiao flew up, Bai Qi grabbed his tail and pulled him back with force.

Hong Jiao felt the pain, "What are you doing!"

Bai Qi said coldly: "Do you want to die?"

The biggest advantage of the White Feather and Red Feather beastmen was that they were good-looking, but they had little combat power; they only showed off among the Sparrow tribes. The Black Feather beastmen opposite had wingspans larger than their entire bodies, and their size was two or three times theirs.

Not to mention there were so many wolf beastmen behind them!

Bai Qi hadn't dealt with wolf beastmen before, but she had heard of their capabilities. When they flew over just now, she heard a wolf beastman say how good their meat tasted; who knew if they were like the Black Bear tribe from before...

Thinking of the attack on the tribe, Bai Qi trembled all over.

Her cubs!

Her three cubs!

Bai Qi felt a weight on her shoulder. She looked up sharply, her eyes bloodshot, and pushed Hong Jiao away.

"Bai Yuan!"

"Chief." The White Feather beastman who had spoken on the tree flew down.

"Looking at them, they won't stay here long. Have half the beastmen keep watch tonight. Order every beastman not to approach them. If anything happens, take the cubs and fly away immediately."

"Yes!"

*

Yu Lie took Yu Ya and the other young ones, politely staying at the edge of the tribe for a long time. They clearly saw them, but not a single beastman came over.

Yu Ya had traveled all day and was tired. He sat down, hugged his Uncle Yu Lie's leg, and said, "Uncle Yu Lie, are they coming or not?"

Yu Lie looked at the wolf beastmen behind him, who were busy setting up pots and had already netted several fish from the river.

"Uncle Yu Lie, it's almost time to eat..." Another young Black Feather beastman hugged Yu Lie's other leg.

Yu Lie: "Not waiting anymore, I'll go see."

"Then we..."

"You stay here."

This group of Feather tribes looked very cautious; if too many beastmen went, they would treat it as an attack. He would just go pass a message and come back.

Thinking this, Yu Lie shook off Yu Ya and the others, swooping across the lake. His wings stirred up a gale that stung his face.

He flew straight toward the west.

Almost the moment he moved, the western cliff seemed to be covered in a layer of white snow. All the beastmen hidden in their nests came out, spreading their wings and hissing in warning.

Yu Lie stopped, looking at the cliff that had instantly turned from black to white, and said loudly, "We are the Wolf tribe from the Eastern Continent, passing through. We wanted to ask if you want to trade! We have salt, pottery, herbs..."

"No trade!"

"You have entered our territory, please leave immediately, or we will attack!"

Yu Lie was stunned. He looked at the bristling beastmen all over the cliff and flapped his huge gray-black wings, slowly retreating.

"Uncle Yu Lie."

Yu Lie retracted his wings and placed his large hands on the heads of Yu Ya and the other young beastmen.

"No luck."

"Why?" Yu Ya squinted into the distance, watching the white color slowly dissipate.

"What do you mean why? Let's go!"

After Yu Lie returned, he went to find Lang Yan first.

Lin Qiu and Lang Yan were leaning together, drawing a map. Yu Lie walked over, and Lang Yan looked up and said, "No?"

Yu Lie nodded, "They are very guarded against us, they didn't even give us time to talk."

Que Xi helped add wood to the fire and said softly, "That's how it is."

Seeing Lin Qiu and the Black Feather beastmen looking at him, Que Xi sighed, his fingers avoiding the thorns on the firewood, and he lowered his eyes, as if recalling: "When Xiong Chen brought beastmen over, he used cubs to trick them into relaxing their guard. Their casualties were very heavy..."

Not just heavy, it could almost be described as tragic.

Those parents watched helplessly as their cubs were stuffed into the mouths of those rogue beastmen, and they almost completely collapsed.

They attacked madly, but the rogue beastmen led by Xiong Chen only needed one palm to slap these Feather beastmen to the ground, blood flowing from their mouths...

Que Xi remembered clearly that none of the beastmen led by Xiong Chen had disappeared during those days. But during those days, Xiong Chen and his group had eaten very well.

His palms unconsciously gripped the firewood, the thorns stinging his skin. Que Xi slowly pulled himself out of the memory.

He gently placed his bleeding fingers on his knees and said softly, "It's only right that they are guarded against strange beastmen now."

Yu Lie cursed under his breath.

Lin Qiu looked toward the west and tapped the back of Lang Yan's hand, "Forget it, the road ahead is still long, we'll eventually meet a tribe that wants to trade."

Lang Yan: "Okay."

Que Xi bit his lip and whispered, "Should I go ask the other Sparrow tribes?"

"No need," Lang Yan said.

Lin Qiu gripped one of Lang Yan's fingers and shook it gently, unable to help but sigh.

He had originally planned to trade some supplies here, but it seemed that wouldn't work.

These Feather tribes weren't friendly, and it wasn't suitable for them to stay here too long.

After dinner, Lang Yan and Lin Qiu took turns on guard, letting the other beastmen get some sleep.

Once tonight passed, they would leave tomorrow morning.

Night fell, the full moon rose from the lake, and stars filled the sky. In this place without industrial pollution, the night was a beautiful sight.

Lin Qiu sat on the grass covered with hay and animal skins, looking at the moonlight reflected in the deep blue lake, smelling the faint floral fragrance, feeling deeply that this was a good place.

The fire burned brightly, with a few small fish the beastmen caught in the evening roasting on top—this was Lin Qiu and Lang Yan's midnight snack.

Lin Qiu waited for the fish skin to curl and turn golden-brown, slowly flipping the fish and sprinkling a handful of crushed herbs on top.

Lang Yan leaned against him, gently waving a fan to shoo away the insects swarming toward the fire from all directions.

The night was quiet, and the western cliff merged into the darkness, no longer visible. But Lin Qiu could still feel that they were being watched, and the number of beastmen staring at them was not small.

Lin Qiu: "They are near the sea, and since these beastmen are Feather tribes, it should be much easier for them to get salt than the Gray Rabbit beastmen."

"Yes."

"I wonder if they have a priest. Such a big tribe, if we could trade for herbs..."

"Zhi."

A very small, milky sound came from behind. Lin Qiu rested his elbows on Lang Yan's knees and leaned back to look.

"Heh..."

He knew it!

The four little black balls were squatting in the corner, their large, round eyes looking this way—or more accurately, looking at the fragrant roasted fish in Lin Qiu's hand.

"Come here." Lin Qiu curled his finger and beckoned.

The four black monkey cubs carefully walked to the fire, their mouths wet from the temptation of the roasted fish. Their eyes were fixed solely on the fish, no longer vigilant or afraid; their bodies and minds were occupied by the roasted fish.

Lin Qiu picked up the roasted fish and shook it gently; the cubs' big eyes followed the movement.

"Want to eat?"

"Gulp—" A very loud sound of swallowing.

Lin Qiu: "Tell me, what is their tribe's priest called? How old are they? Is their medical skill good?"

He moved the fish forward, and the four little coal balls followed step by step, as if soul-lost, completely ignoring Lin Qiu's words.

Lin Qiu shoved the fish into Lang Yan's hand. The cubs stopped, looked up, and saw it was the Wolf King; their fur stood on end, like steel needles.

Lin Qiu: "Answer the questions first, then eat the fish. This is a trade."

"Gulp!"

The leading cub finally came to its senses, quickly grabbed the cubs behind it, and moved away from Lang Yan. They grabbed onto each other, running in a line to Lin Qiu's side.

"Zhi?" The cub squatted down, its long tail wrapped around its waist, small feet together, curling its whole body up, looking at him with those large, round eyes.

Lin Qiu: "Do both tribes have priests?"

"Zhi!"

"One? Which tribe's?"

"Zhi."

"Both tribes? Were the two biggest tribes one family before?"

"Zhi!"

"Not one family?"

The cubs could only say "zhi." Lin Qiu didn't understand their language that well; half-understanding and half-confused, he ended up confusing himself by asking back and forth.

"It's a priest supported by both tribes together; they probably weren't originally their tribesmen."

This touched on Lin Qiu's knowledge blind spot. He looked at Lang Yan, signaling him to continue explaining.

The sub-beastman's black hair was loosely tied up, falling to one side of his shoulder, his cold, clear brows as elegant as the moonlight.

Lang Yan couldn't help but scratch his chin. His palm felt heavy as his mate let go of his strength, resting his head in his palm.

Lang Yan said: "On the Beast God Continent, some tribes don't have priests, so they hire them from outside. The tribe provides enough reward to support the priest, and the priest works for the tribe."

"Zhi!"

Right!

"Then is he easy to talk to? Can we trade with him separately?"

Since it was a hired priest, what he did wasn't entirely controlled by these two tribes, so there was a good chance of trading.

"Zhi..." The leading black monkey cub scratched its belly, its tone uncertain. The cub behind it stretched out a paw, grabbed the face of the one in front, and leaned forward, saying to Lin Qiu, "Zhi zhi zhi, zhi zhi zhi."

This sentence was too long. Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan.

Lang Yan's eyes lost their smile. He held Lin Qiu's wrist and said softly, "They are gone."

"Huh?"

"Zhi zhi zhi..."

"Their priest left suddenly half a year ago, and the things these beastmen provided to support the priest also disappeared. They don't have a priest now."

Lin Qiu hooked his finger around Lang Yan's and tightened it slowly.

Sigh! It seems this trade really won't work.

"Forget it."

Lin Qiu looked at the four little heads tilted up and handed them the roasted fish. The leading cub divided the fish, and they buried their heads to eat.

Lin Qiu leaned against Lang Yan.

He listened to the happy "zhi zhi zhi" sounds of the cubs eating, his chin against Lang Yan's shoulder, and asked softly: "Where did they hire their priest from? So unreliable?"

"Some priests are raised by the tribe using all its resources, but they look down on their own tribe. They choose to defect and leave, seeking support elsewhere to live a life without worrying about food. There are many such priests."

"Zhi zhi zhi!"

Lin Qiu heard the sound and looked to the side. The cubs were nodding as they ate, not knowing if they were approving of his roasted fish or agreeing with what Lang Yan just said.

Lang Yan put his arm around Lin Qiu's waist, pulling him into his arms, his chin against his hair.

There was a faint floral fragrance, and it was very smooth.

He couldn't help but rub against it again, his nose pressed against the long hair, sniffing.

"Actually, there are also a few priests who, in order to support their own tribe, go to work for some big tribes, and the support they receive is fed back to their own tribe."

Lin Qiu: "Then if a tribe raises a few more priests, wouldn't they be worry-free about food and clothing?"

"Zhi." Four round heads nodded at the same time.

That's possible...

Lang Yan chuckled softly, his lips brushing Lin Qiu's ear, "If a tribe had the ability to raise several priests, it wouldn't be a weak tribe."

"Whatever, our priest is old but still strong, and those little cubs have grown up, let him keep picking and teaching."

"The priest would be so angry if he heard that."

"How old is he, and he doesn't have that much capacity?"

"Zhi."

Exactly, stingy, stingy!

火堆又烧得旺了些，兔艾掏了掏火堆中间，猩红的火星子四处乱飘。
狼顺和兔艾隔了一段距离，中间四个黑猴幼崽抱着分到的鱼干啃得又快又急。
兔艾翻动着手上还在烤的另一条鱼干，低声对着这几个才自己小腿高的幼崽道：“慢点吃，有刺。”
“吱吱吱！”
“你说你们两天没吃东西了？”
“吱！”
狼顺默默加快了掰鱼干的速度，顺带把里面的大刺去掉。
他大手摊开在身侧最小的幼崽面前，幼崽顺手抓过，爪子灵巧地扯了扯，分成四份，只留自己那一份，其他抓成一把，往另一边传。
其他幼崽配合默契，一手往嘴里塞鱼干，一手伸向旁边的同伴手里拿新的鱼干。
“你们部落的成年兽人干什么去了？”
“吱……”
“驱逐？”
幼崽吃鱼干的速度慢了下来，四个幼崽同时吸了吸鼻子，低着头，一副可怜兮兮的样子。
兔艾见状，把烤好的鱼干取下来，直接横放在幼崽面前。
“吱！！！”四个小黑球直接趴上去就啃。
这下不伤心了。
兔艾跟狼顺对视一眼，皆是同情。
该打听的也打听完了，简单来说，这附近的黑猴部落前不久才进行了一次族长变更，新任族长打败了老族长，连带他的四个崽子也驱逐出了部落。
上一任族长在打斗中伤得严重，已经死了，四个崽子的阿爸年轻貌美，又能生，现在已经成了新任族长的伴侣，也不要这四个崽子。
他们才出生一年多，还不会变人形。新任族长把他们扔出来肯定是抱着让他们死的想法。
好在黑猴部落还有心善的兽人，会悄悄接济他们几个，加上他们自己会爬树摘果子，掏鸟蛋，所以也挨过了这么久。
“嗝——”四个小崽子吃饱了。
兔艾最后给他们的那条完整的鱼干，他们只啃了一面，鱼肉啃得干干净净的，只剩下骨头架子。另一半完完整整，看着是打算留着明天吃。
幼崽吃饱犯困，长尾巴一甩，四条尾巴紧紧勾在一起，吃得鼓鼓的肚子就这么一起一伏，睡着了。
*
天亮了。
兽人们爬起来的第一件事就是把兽皮毯和干草一卷，用细麻绳捆好，只等走的时候带上就行。
林楸披散着长发，撑着狼岩的手臂，把兽皮靴穿上。
他视线往只剩余烬的火堆旁一扫，问道：“昨晚那几个小崽呢？”
“走了。”狼岩道。
林楸往山脚看了看，瞧见个用叶片和干草堵住的小洞，那洞口有成年兽人的陶碗碗口大，堵得严严实实的，乍一眼还看不出来。
“楸！豆花！”几个年轻兽人看他醒了，噔噔噔跑过来，讨好地冲着他笑。
林楸：“不行。”
“楸，我们错了，我们再也不说不想吃黑豆了……”
林楸抬手打断兽人的话，道：“豆子不够，而且费时间，只能晚上那一顿做。”
“那现在多泡点黑豆！”
林楸看向狼岩。
狼岩扫了一眼年轻兽人们，手臂一揽，带着林楸就离开了。
狼金他们想跟上来都不敢。
“楸……”
“你们自己泡吧。”
“嗷！！！”
河滩边，一处清澈的水洼地。
林楸和狼岩刚停下，兔艾和雀溪就过来了。
“王，楸！昨晚有几个黑猴兽人幼崽来过。”
林楸道：“我们知道。”
兽人们出门在外都不是一般的警惕，怎么会不知道昨晚的动静。
雀溪轻声道：“我早上悄悄去黑猴部落看了眼，他们部落在山另一头的谷底，是个有七八十个兽人的小部落。”
林楸：“我们吃过早饭就走了，不用去打扰他们。”
雀溪点头。
兔艾看了看狼岩和林楸，想说的话也咽了下去。
兽神大陆上受苦受难的幼崽不知凡几，这几个幼崽好歹还有自家部落的长辈投喂，能活下去。
现在天亮得早些，刚醒这会儿山巅还有些雾气笼罩，没多久，太阳出来，雾气也就散了。
兽人们赶着吃过早饭，背上东西，又继续出发。
大河这边地势陡峭，兽人们要沿着山崖边顺着大河往南走，好在有黑羽兽人探路，不至于让他们走到什么绝路上。
照旧是狼火和狼影在前面带路，林楸和狼岩落在最后头。
山路艰难，何况兽人们还驮着这么多东西。
黑羽兽人们飞在半空中，寻找方向，狼影和狼火找准最合适的地方落脚，兽人们紧紧跟着，都盯着脚下，小心翼翼。
耳边是湍急的河流传出的轰隆声，山路又陡峭，大家不敢分神。
就这么沿着河岸边的山一直走，走了两天之后，兽人们才出了这崇山峻岭，眼前也豁然开朗。
山外是一处广袤的草地，草地一路延伸，直达蓝如宝石的巨大湖旁。
这便是蓝湖。
放眼望去，湖面往南似无边无际，只西侧有一处笔直的崖壁。那山崖如同被一刀破开，笔直地阻隔在大湖西边。
此时已经是下午，夕阳垂落。晚霞绮丽，彩绸似的在那大湖上铺陈开来。
忽的，一阵展翅声袭来，兽人们抬头看去，成千上万只羽毛洁白，只飞羽带粉的鸟群从兽人们头顶飞跃。
它们姿态翩跹，身姿优美，像追逐着落日，往那彩霞深处飞去。
草地、蓝湖、飞鸟、晚霞……林楸双目微睁，将这辽阔壮丽的景色收入眼中。
他喃喃：“这景色……”
“好多鸟，好多肉……嗷！”
林楸看着狼云脑门上正热乎的粑粑，一脸无语地靠着狼岩，抵着他往旁边让了让。
狼岩低笑出声，脖颈蹭过林楸，道：“到他们领地边缘了。”
“刚刚那是兽人？”
“嗯。”
狼禾再看自己的伴侣，顿时离得远远的。
狼云可怜兮兮：“禾！”
狼禾偏过脑袋不看他，道：“洗干净去！脏死了！”
狼禾最近几天都不打算再靠近狼云一步。
闹完，前面的狼火和狼影走过来。
湖风悠然，草地上开着橘红和烟紫色的小花，花草映着快要消失的晚霞，轻摇着，看得人都放松了下来。
“阿嚏！阿嚏！！！怎么这么多花。”
林楸：“……”
他无奈地把脑袋往狼岩颈侧一放，爪子狠狠抓了抓地，能不能好好欣赏一下风景了！
狼岩偏头蹭了蹭他，脸上隐隐带着笑。
“王，前面就是人家的领地了，我们今晚在这里睡吗？”狼乔四处看了看，扬起声问。
“放东西吧。”
湖面极其广阔，说是湖，更像一处内海。
这边羽族部落多，各自沿湖划分地界，就连湖面哪一处属于哪一个部落都分得清清楚楚。
“他们的领地范围包括蓝湖以及山崖那边往西的一大片小山。”雀溪蹲在已经开始挖灶的狼乔身边道。
“都是大部落？”狼乔一边刨坑，一边看着西边山崖，那崖壁上有密密麻麻的洞。
一个洞口一家兽人，这得住多少兽人。
“最主要的是白羽部落和红羽部落，他们一个部落就是上千个兽人，其他的像蓝雀部落、黑嘴部落的兽人加起来也只有几百个。”
熊沉选择袭击一个部落前，会把这个部落了解得很清楚，雀溪也跟着知道不少事。
这边几个羽族也是熊沉的目标，当初他带着流浪兽人抢了不少这几个羽族的蛋和幼崽。
雀溪现在都记得这群羽族怒不可遏，目眦尽裂的样子。
很凄惨，很可怜，但他也无能为力。
雀溪目光落在那澄澈的蓝湖上，记忆中湖里的鲜血就像天上的晚霞一样蔓延开来，最后染红了整个湖岸。
头隐隐作痛，雀溪捂住自己的脑袋，额角青筋隐隐凸显。
“你怎么了？”狼乔问。
“没事，我没事。”雀溪声音极轻，眼中一幕幕血红闪过，最后被强压下来。
他要回部落。
他要平平安安、完完整整地回到部落！
*
难得遇到大部落，他们带出来这么多东西肯定是想要交换的。
狼岩把羽猎叫来，让他带几个兽人去跟对面那些羽族兽人问一问交换的事。
羽猎应下，把羽涯几个带上就走。
蓝湖四周，除了东部，其他地方都是隆起的高山。只湖太大，似海一般辽阔，所以兽人们一眼望去只能看得见西边那处山崖。
这处山崖靠近大河入湖口，水中食物充足，也是最好的筑巢位置。
山崖绵延数里，被白羽部落和红羽部落瓜分，一个部落占据一半的位置。其他部落只能蜗居在其他几个方向的山崖间。
此刻，几十个狼兽人和黑羽兽人从大河那边靠近蓝湖，外出的羽族兽人都被叫回，严阵以待。
白羽部落当中，山崖顶端。
白羽族长白栖站在崖顶的最高一棵树上，她手把着树干，一头白发高高束起，身姿挺拔，英气逼人。
她静静看着那一群闲适得仿佛到了自家部落的狼兽人，眼中尽是冷意。
往下，树枝上停落的几个白羽兽人，他们兽形修长纤细，仙气十足。
这几个兽人都是白羽部落说得上话的兽人。
而其他的族人，此刻都归巢戒备，护住自己的蛋和幼崽。
“族长，要不要把他们赶走？”底下的兽人仰头看着他们族长白栖。
“不知道情况，不要硬碰硬。”几抹红影从空中飞过，最后停在对面的一棵树上。
“红角，你来干什么？”白栖冷声道。
他们两个部落平日里在这边争抢食物抢得你死我活，对对方可没什么好脸色。
红羽部落族长红角微微一笑，“过来看看。”
“滚！”
红角：“就不。”
白栖胸口起伏，直接从树梢飞跃过去，抡起拳头冲着红角脸上打去。
红角躲闪，避开自己的脸，抬手握住白栖的拳头，无奈地抓着她落下树梢。
“好了，旧怨先放下，我是来商量事情的。”
白栖甩开他的手，看着已经飞到蓝湖旁的黑羽兽人。
他们没有往前进，而是看着这边，似乎等着他们派兽人过去。
“我去看看。”红角刚一飞，白栖一把抓住他尾巴，大力扯回来。
红角吃疼，“你干什么！”
白栖冷声道：“你想死？”
白羽红羽兽人最大的优点就是长得好看，但都没什么战斗力，他们也就在几个雀部落中间逞逞能。对面那几个黑羽兽人一个翅膀张开就比他们整个长，体型更是他们两三倍大。
更何况他们后面还有那么多狼兽人！
白栖没跟狼兽人打过交道，但也听过他们的能耐。刚刚飞过来时他还听到有狼兽人在说吃他们的肉多，谁知道是不是和之前的黑熊部落一样……
想起部落被袭击的事，白栖浑身都在颤抖。
她的崽子！
她整整三个崽子！
白栖肩膀一重，她猛地抬头，双目血红，一把将红角推开。
“白鸢！”
“族长。”树上刚刚说话的那个白羽兽人飞身落下。
“看他们的样子不会在这里停留多久，让一半兽人今晚守夜，命令任何一个兽人都不许靠近他们，一旦有事，立刻带幼崽飞离。”
“是！”
*
羽猎带着羽涯几个小的，礼貌地停留在人家部落边缘许久，他们分明看到这边了，却没有一个兽人过来。
羽涯赶了一天的路，早累了，他一屁股坐下，抱着他羽猎叔的大腿道：“阿猎叔，他们到底来不来啊？”
羽猎看看身后忙得热火朝天的狼兽人，他们都搭起锅，往河里捞上来几网鱼了。
“阿猎叔，都快吃完饭了……”羽猎另一条腿一重，又一个年轻黑羽兽人抱过来。
羽猎：“不等了，我去看看。”
“那我们……”
“你们原地等着。”
这群羽族看着非常谨慎，去多了兽人他们会当做是袭击。他过去传个话就过来。
想着，羽猎挣脱羽涯两个，一下飞掠过湖面，翅膀待起罡风，有些刮脸。
他直直冲着西边而去。
几乎他行动的瞬间，西边山崖上如同被覆盖了一层白雪。藏在巢里的兽人全部出来，张开翅膀，嘶声警告。
羽猎停下，看着那瞬间由黑变白的山崖，高声道：“我们是东部大陆的狼部落，路过你们这边，想问问你们要不要交换东西！我们有盐、陶器、草药……”
“不换！”
“你已经进入我们领地，请你立刻离开，否则我们将立马发动攻击！”
羽猎一呆，他看着整片山崖上的炸毛兽人，挥动灰黑的巨大翅膀慢慢往后退。
“阿猎叔。”
羽猎收回翅膀，大手一左一右扣在羽涯几个年轻兽人头上。
“没戏。”
“为什么？”羽涯眯着眼盯着远处，看着那缓缓消散的雪色。
“哪有什么为什么，走了！”
羽猎回来后，先去找狼岩。
林楸和狼岩正靠在一起画地图，羽猎过来，狼岩抬头看了一眼道：“不行？”
羽猎点头，“他们对我们很防备，说句话的时间都不给。”
雀溪帮着往灶里添柴，闻言轻声道：“是这样的。”
见林楸和几个黑羽兽人看来，雀溪叹了口气，手指避开干柴上的刺，垂下眼，似回忆道：“当初熊沉带着兽人过来，用幼崽骗得他们放松警惕，他们伤亡很重……”
岂止重，几乎可以用惨烈来形容。
那些当父母的兽人眼睁睁地看着自己的幼崽一个一个被塞入那些流浪兽人口中，几乎是直接崩溃。
他们发狂地攻击，可熊沉带领的流浪兽人只需要一掌，这些羽族就被拍在地上，嘴角流出鲜血……
雀溪记得很清楚，那几天他们这些被熊沉带着的兽人一个也没有消失。而那几天，熊沉他们却吃得很饱。
掌心无意识攥紧木柴，手心刺疼，雀溪慢慢从回忆中抽离。
他轻轻将渗血的手指放在膝上，轻声说：“他们现在防备陌生兽人也是应该的。”
羽猎低骂了一声。
林楸看向西边，手指点了点狼岩手背，“要不算了吧，后头路还很长，总能遇到想要交换的部落。”
狼岩：“好。”
雀溪咬唇，低声道：“要不然我再去问问另外几个雀部落？”
“不用。”狼岩道。
林楸攥住狼岩一根手指，轻轻地摇了摇，还是忍不住一叹。
原本设想好的在这里交换出去一部分物资，现在看来是不行了。
这些羽族态度不算友好，他们也不适合在这里停留太久。
晚饭过后，狼岩和林楸轮守，让其他兽人赶紧去睡觉。
今晚一过，明天早上他们就走。
夜幕降临，圆月从湖面升起，群星布满天际。在这个没有工业污染的地方，夜色也是一场美景。
林楸坐在铺了干草和兽皮的草地上，望着幽蓝的湖中投下的月影，闻着淡淡花香，深觉这是个好地方。
火堆烧得旺，上面架着几条今天傍晚时兽人们捞起来的小鱼，这是林楸和狼岩的夜宵。
林楸等着鱼皮卷曲，表面成了焦黄，慢悠悠地给鱼翻个面，又往上撒上一把香草碎末。
狼岩挨着他，轻摇扇子，赶着四面八方涌向火堆的虫子。
夜色沉静，西边山崖融入黑夜中，早已经看不清。但林楸还是能感觉到，他们依旧被监视着，盯着他们的兽人数量还不少。
林楸：“他们这边近海，这些兽人又是羽族，要获取盐应该比灰兔兽人要方便很多。”
“嗯。”
“也不知道他们有没有祭司，这么大个部落，要是能交换草药的话……”
“吱。”
身后传出很小很小的一声，奶声奶气。林楸手肘撑着狼岩膝头，偏着身体往后瞧。
“呵……”
他就知道！
四个小黑球蹲在角落，又大又圆的眼睛看着这边，更准确的说，是看着林楸手上那香气十足的烤鱼。
“过来。”林楸曲指勾了勾。
四个黑猴幼崽小心地走到火堆边，被烤鱼馋得嘴边的毛毛都湿了。一双眼睛只顾盯着烤鱼，也不警惕害怕了，身心都被那烤鱼占据。
林楸拎起烤鱼，轻轻晃动，幼崽的大眼睛也跟着转动。
“想吃？”
“咕咚——”好大一声咽口水的声音。
林楸：“说说，他们部落的祭司叫什么？多大了？医术好吗？”
他抓着烤鱼往前挪，四个小煤球一步一步跟上去，失了魂一样，完全忽略了林楸的话。
林楸把烤鱼往狼岩手里一塞，幼崽停下，抬头一看是狼王，毛发一根一根竖起来，钢针似的。
林楸：“先回答问题，再吃鱼。这是交换。”
“咕咚！”
领头的那小崽子终于回过神来，快速抓着身后的幼崽离开狼岩，他们一个抓着一个，一整串跑到林楸这边。
“吱？”幼崽蹲坐下来，长尾巴圈在自己腰上，小脚并拢，整个身子团起来，用那双又大又圆的眼睛看着他。
林楸：“他们两个部落都有祭司？”
“吱！”
“一个？哪个部落的？”
“吱。”
“两个部落的？这最大的两个部落以前是一家的？”
“吱！”
“不是一家的？”
幼崽只会吱，林楸跟他们语言没那么通，半懂半不懂，问来问去反倒把自己搞晕了。
“是两个部落一起供养的祭司，原本应该不是他们的族人。”
这涉及到林楸知识盲区，他看向狼岩，示意他继续解惑。
亚兽人黑发松散地挽起，落在肩膀一侧，清冷的眉眼似月色一般淡雅。
狼岩忍不住挠挠他下巴。掌心一重，自家伴侣直接卸了力道，把脑袋放在他掌心。
狼岩道：“在兽神大陆，有的部落没有祭司，他们会从外面聘请祭司。部落给足报酬供养祭司，祭司也为部落做事。”
“吱！”
对！
“那他好说话不？我们能单独和他交换东西吗？”
既然是被聘请来的祭司，那他做的事也不完全受制于这两个部落，还是很有交换的可能的。
“吱……”为首的黑猴幼崽挠了挠肚皮，语气有些不确定，后头的幼崽爪子一伸，抓着前面那个兽人的脸，自己探起身子，冲着林楸道，“吱吱吱，吱吱吱。”
这句话太长了，林楸看向狼岩。
狼岩眼里没了笑意，捏着林楸手腕，轻声道：“不在了。”
“嗯？”
“吱吱吱……”
“他们的祭司半年前就突然离开了，这些兽人给祭司供养的东西也消失了，他们现在没有祭司。”
林楸勾住狼岩手指，缓缓收紧。
哎！看来这交换真的行不通了。
“算了。”
林楸瞧着仰起的四个小脑袋，把烤鱼递给他们。领头的崽子把烤鱼一分，他们就埋头吃起来。
林楸倚靠在狼岩身上。
他听着这几个小崽子吃得“吱吱吱”的快活声，下巴贴着狼岩肩膀，低声问：“他们的祭司是从哪儿请来的，这么不靠谱？”
“有些祭司被部落举全部落的力量培养出来，却看不起自家部落。他们会选择叛逃离开，去其他地方寻求供养，然后过上不愁食物的生活。这样的祭司不少。”
“吱吱吱！”
林楸听到声音往旁边一看，几个小崽边吃边点头，也不知道是认可他做的烤鱼还是赞同狼岩刚刚说的话。
狼岩手臂搭在林楸腰上，将他往怀里拢了拢，下巴挨着他头发。
有淡淡的花香，还很顺滑。
他忍不住又蹭了蹭，鼻尖紧贴着那长发嗅闻。
“其实也有少数祭司为了供养自家部落，会去一些大部落做事，得到的供养会回馈给自己部落。”
林楸：“那一个部落多培养几个祭司，岂不是衣食无忧？”
“吱。”四个圆圆的脑袋同时点了点。
可以哦……
狼岩低声一笑，唇瓣擦过林楸耳朵，“要是一个部落能有培养几个祭司的能力，那它就不会是一个弱小的部落。”
“管他呢，咱们祭司老当益壮，那群小崽子也长大了，让他继续挑挑，继续教着。”
“祭司听了怕得好一阵气。”
“多大岁数了，还没那个肚量？”
“吱。”
就是，小气小气！

chapters.translated_text:
The wind picked up, ripples spread across the lake, and the reflection of the moon was shattered.

Lin Qiu covered his mouth and yawned slowly, tears welling up in his eyes.

He rested his cheek against Lang Yan’s chest, curling up in a comfortable position.

The four little black balls were already asleep.

They were huddled tightly together by the campfire, tails hooked, curled into a ball, snuggling against each other while letting out little snores.

Lin Qiu scratched Lang Yan’s palm with his finger and asked, "King, are we still letting them follow us?"

He could see that this group of cubs had latched onto them; they had followed from the valley, trekking through such difficult terrain for two days. He didn't know whether to call them persistent or brainless.

Lang Yan replied, "If the beastmen from the Black Monkey tribe who look after them notice, they should be coming for them soon."

Lin Qiu scanned the surroundings, listened for any movement, and said, "But they haven't."

Lang Yan: "Tomorrow morning, have Yu Lie send them back."

It would be better for them to stay where they were than to follow them.

The wolf beastmen still had a very, very long way to go, and the cubs were fragile; they had no energy to spare to help others look after their young.

It was almost midnight, and Lin Qiu would fall asleep if he kept sitting there.

He pushed off Lang Yan’s rock-hard shoulders to stand up, stomped his feet, stretched, and looked around with clear eyes, listening intently to the sounds in the wind.

Lang Yan looked up, his gaze following Lin Qiu, his sharp brows relaxing.

"Are you sleepy?"

Lin Qiu glared, then covered his mouth to yawn, his eyes becoming even more watery.

Lang Yan’s lips curled slightly as he opened his arms and said, "It’s time to switch shifts, come back and sleep."

Lin Qiu: "It's not time yet, what's the rush?"

*

The west bank of the Blue Lake, on the cliff.

The Feather tribe beastmen built their nests high up; crouching in their nests, they could see the burning campfire in the distance.

Bai Cang was the strongest warrior of the White Feather tribe, and his nest was positioned high with plenty of space.

They hadn't started a fire on their side. Bai Cang and his partner sat on the edge of the nest made of branches and dried grass, staring at the opposite side for half the night.

Bai Cang’s partner licked his lips, as if he could smell the scent of the roasted fish.

But compared to roasted fish, what he wanted more was salt.

"A-Cang, does the Chief really not agree to trade?" the frail sub-beastman leaned into Bai Cang’s arms, his lips pale, speaking in a very low voice.

Their tribe lacked salt, severely. The priest they had invited had disappeared for some unknown reason, taking a large amount of the tribe's supplies with him, including most of their salt.

They suspected the Red Feather beastmen were involved, and the Red Feather beastmen suspected them of the same thing.

Since the two tribes gathered in this area, their relationship had been hit-or-miss, with constant cooperation and conflict.

But they couldn't figure those things out for now, and they didn't know where that priest had run off to. The beastmen only knew that they needed salt right now.

Desperately!

The supplies for this year's salt trade weren't ready yet, and the salt saved from last year was gone; the beastmen could only go to the cliff walls to find salt frost seeping out of the rocks.

But that was far from enough.

They really were running out of strength.

"The Chief is wary of all strange beastmen right now." Bai Cang held his partner close, his large hands massaging his weak arms and legs bit by bit. He spoke in a whisper, his lips almost touching his partner's ear.

"But we have to live..."

"They are of unknown origin; we dare not trust them easily."

"They are wolf beastmen. Who else could they be from the Eastern Continent? Look at how strong they are; they must be the wolf tribe that left the Central Continent. Only they have the ability to sustain a tribe."

Bai Cang listened to his partner getting more and more agitated, gently covered his mouth, and whispered in his ear, "Don't be anxious."

"We could secretly..."

The sub-beastman’s long, slender fingers rested weakly on Bai Cang’s arm, wanting to exert force but unable to muster the strength.

There were many beastmen in the White Feather tribe. One nest could hatch four or five cubs, and even if only half survived, there would still be two.

They relied on this boundless Blue Lake; just by eating fish and foraging, they could raise their cubs, which was why their numbers were growing.

The beastmen had lived for most of their lives and had experienced things like Xiong Chen’s incident a few times. Although their hearts ached, faced with food and things they craved, they still had their own agendas.

The Chief was young and, due to the loss of her cubs, was somewhat reactive to all strange beastmen; they understood that. Most beastmen shared the Chief's attitude, but a small number of them had their own ideas for their own benefit.

Therefore, when Lang Yan saw the dark shadow appearing from behind the mountain, he wasn't surprised at all.

Lin Qiu followed Lang Yan’s gaze to look back, and seeing the figure standing straight in the night, his hair stood on end.

He clearly hadn't been asleep and had been paying attention to the surroundings, yet he still wasn't as sharp as Lang Yan.

"King!" The other beastmen jumped up.

Lang Yan: "Lie down."

The beastmen didn't understand why, but they did as they were told, only changing direction to face inward.

"Can you trade salt here?" The beastman was hidden in the shadows, his back pressed tightly against the steep slope, his voice kept low, as if he didn't want to be discovered by certain beastmen.

They were all smart beastmen; their minds turned, and they immediately understood.

Lang Yan: "Trade."

His eyes swept toward Lang Chou, who was near the salt bag, and the beastman immediately crawled up, carrying the remaining half-bag of salt and placing it in front of the stranger.

The beastman crouched down, stuck his hand into the salt, and then touched it to his lips.

"One basket of dried meat for one spoonful of salt." Lang Chou gestured for him to look at the spoon in the bag.

The beastman’s breathing became erratic. Lin Qiu noticed this and looked at Lang Yan, who pulled his wrist and brought him to his side.

"No dried meat, is there anything else that can..."

Lang Chou quickly said, "Herbs, animal skins, dried fish will also do."

When mentioning dried fish, Lang Chou’s features wrinkled in obvious disgust.

The beastman’s breathing deepened for a moment, and the muscles of the wolf beastmen and Black Feather beastmen lying on the ground had already quietly tightened.

"Pearls, will they do?"

"What do we want those for... Mmph!" Lang He covered Lang Yun’s mouth tightly, smiling and signaling the beastman to continue.

Lang Yun hummed; he was almost used to having his mouth covered by his partner.

Lang Yan: "Let me see."

The beastman reached out, and Lang Qiao nearby took the pearls. He rolled them with his fingers; the handful of pearls was exceptionally round and large.

He passed them back, and the pearls landed in Lang Yan’s hand.

Lin Qiu leaned in with Lang Yan to look at the campfire, instantly attracted by the pearls.

They were very beautiful, round pearls, looking like sea pearls, and the color actually had a hint of pink. There were five in total, very uniform in size, and he didn't know where the beastman had gotten them.

Such things had a good market in the past when food was plentiful, but now...

"Trading all five?"

"Yes, trade them all for salt."

Lang Yan thought for a moment and said, "One and a half spoonfuls."

"These are sea pearls, they are the same size, and the color is beautiful..."

This was something the beastman had personally searched for to coax his partner into being happy. It took him several years to collect that string, but unfortunately, he had to break it up now to trade for salt.

The beastman remembered his partner’s surprised smile and flushed face when he first gave him the pearls, and compared it to now, holding a body that was nothing but bones and softness, with a face white as a sheet...

Their cubs were gone too.

But he and his partner still had to live.

"One and a half spoonfuls."

The beastman still didn't respond. He abruptly asked, "Are you the wolf tribe from the Central Continent?"

Lang Yan: "Yes."

"Where do you live now?"

"North of the Eastern Continent, you are welcome to come and trade at any time."

"Deal."

One and a half spoonfuls of salt was only enough for him and his partner to last until the rainy season. If Bai Qi couldn't walk out of the shadow of losing her cubs, he thought he might have to take his partner and leave to try his luck elsewhere.

The White Feather tribe was already in a mess.

The beastman came silently and left just as quietly.

In the second half of the night, the campfire went out completely. The beastmen sat up, silently watching the beastmen who came one after another to trade.

Among them were White Feather beastmen, Red Feather beastmen, and small tribes that had flown for half a day just to trade, carrying goods openly from the south of the Blue Lake.

They were far away and had prepared their goods to rush over as soon as they received the news.

When Xiong Chen led the rogue beastmen to attack these Feather tribes, the few Sparrow tribes hadn't been targeted and had escaped the attack.

They didn't have so many twists and turns in their minds; hearing that the Wolf tribe had brought salt to trade and would only stay for one night, they rushed over, afraid of missing out.

The beastmen were so proactive because they understood that they didn't have anything the Wolf tribe would want to plot against.

Although the trading was a bit secretive and the beastmen were acting sneaky, they had managed to trade away two bags of salt and exchange them for several bags of herbs unique to this area.

The herbs were all common ones.

The small tribes didn't have priests; if they got sick, they had to find herbs themselves, so they only knew about three or five kinds. They would collect them when they encountered them, and over time, they had accumulated quite a lot.

Herbs were popular everywhere; even if they took them to the seaside to trade, it would be fine.

However, the tribes by the sea were greedy; a little bit of salt would cost them a whole skin bag of herbs, and even if they stripped their tribe of all its herbs, they couldn't trade for much salt.

When they saw the prices asked by the wolf beastmen, the chiefs of the small tribes grinned from ear to ear.

"Will you come again in the future?" the Blue Sparrow Chief asked in a small voice, curled into a ball.

He was still afraid of the wolf beastmen and Black Feather beastmen, but for the sake of salt, he had to summon the courage to ask.

Lang Yan: "Not necessarily, but you can go to the Wolf tribe to trade."

"Where is that?"

The two sides exchanged information about their tribes, and the chiefs waved their wings in satisfaction, calling their tribesmen to leave quietly.

By the time dawn was approaching, the trading had ended.

No one had slept well tonight; everyone lay on the ground, tilting their heads to look at Lang Yan and Lin Qiu.

"King, can we delay our departure?"

"Hmm."

The beastmen closed their eyes in relief, and before long, the snoring began.

Lin Qiu was also too sleepy to keep his eyes open. He turned on his side, resting his head on Lang Yan’s arm, and slowly fell asleep nestled against his side.

Lang Yan scanned the area, and the four little black balls were gone again.

"Lie."

Yu Lie looked up; he had been on guard all night and was yawning with sleepiness.

"Forget it." Lang Yan looked at Yu Ya and the others who had slept soundly. "Ya, go catch those four little cubs hiding in the tree and send them back to the valley."

"Awoo!" The beastmen stood up straight and responded with full spirit.

Lin Qiu’s eyelashes trembled.

Lang Yan covered his partner’s ears, watching the group of Black Feather beastmen who had learned bad habits from his wolf cubs, and sighed softly.

Learning the bad instead of the good.

"Zhi zhi zhi!" The little black balls were hugging a branch and gnawing on tender leaves when they were suddenly picked up. The other three cubs scattered in the trees bared their teeth in threat, only to be caught by the remaining Black Feather beastmen.

Yu Ya said, "Behave, we're sending you back."

"Zhi!"

"We have to go back, we're leaving."

"Zhi zhi zhi!"

"No, we can't take you, you're too small."

The cubs lowered their heads, watching the beastmen team get further and further away, their lips pouting, their limbs hanging limp, their eyes red.

"Zhi..." the cubs made a small sound, filled with pleading.

Yu Ya flapped his wings, looking at the dense forest below, and repeated, "You are too small."

*

Dawn had broken, and the group of beastmen staying by the river entrance hadn't gotten up yet.

Bai Qi took a look, returned to the cliff, and had breakfast with the wild vegetables and fruits gathered yesterday.

After eating, she clapped her hands and, seeing the Red Feather beastmen flying down to the cliff top, looked away indifferently.

"They haven't left yet."

"I'm not blind."

Bai Qi looked at the meadow where the wolf beastmen were staying, seeing only a few beastmen up, wandering around the grass, occasionally glancing over here.

They hadn't given up yet.

"Chief, are we arranging foraging and hunting today?" Bai Yuan asked after finishing breakfast in the nest and flying up.

Bai Qi: "Have the hunting and foraging beastmen go to the back mountain, and keep half the beastmen in the tribe on guard."

"Yes."

Bai Yuan arranged it efficiently.

Bai Qi looked at the eyesore of a beastman beside her and said, "If you have something to say, say it; if not, you can get lost."

Hong Jiao’s lips curled, and he said with a smile, "Don't tell me you didn't notice beastmen sneaking out last night."

Bai Qi’s pupils shrank, and she grabbed the beastman by the neck, her eyes cold and sharp. "What did you say?"

"Oh, so you didn't know."

Bai Qi threw him aside and landed directly in the nest below.

She had felt beastmen going out last night, but she hadn't expected them to be so bold as to contact the Wolf tribe after she had given the order.

Hong Jiao gave a mocking laugh. "You are still as arrogant as ever."

"Hong Jiao! Get out!" Bai Qi’s eyes were bloodshot, looking at him as if he were an enemy.

Hong Jiao felt a dull pain in his heart. He turned his head away and said in a deep voice, "I came to tell you that last night, several small tribes in the south had already traded for salt with the wolf beastmen. Their salt is better than the tribes by the sea, and they didn't ask for much. If you were smarter, you would..."

"I don't need you to teach me!"

Hong Jiao sneered, "Fine, I'm leaving."

Hong Jiao left in a flash, the wind from his wings lifting Bai Qi’s long hair, and the beastman trembled with anger.

"Which beastmen went out last night, all of you come up here!"

In the cave below, Bai Cang gently supported his partner’s back, feeding him water with salt added, bit by bit. The sub-beastman saw his unhurried appearance and worriedly placed his cold hand on his arm.

"A-Cang."

Bai Cang: "Drink slowly, no rush."

A large hand stroked his partner’s somewhat coarse long hair, sliding down to support his chin, which was pointed from weight loss. He watched him finish the water sip by sip before putting down the fruit shell bowl and gently smoothing his back.

"Do you feel better?" Bai Cang asked, pressing his face against his partner’s.

The sub-beastman pointed upward.

Bai Cang held his hand and whispered in his ear, "Don't be afraid."

He slowly coaxed his partner to sleep, looking out of the nest; only a few beastmen were flying up.

Last night, nearly a hundred beastmen had gone.

Bai Qi’s prestige was declining.

Bai Cang waited a while longer, confirming his partner was fast asleep and there was no more sound from above, before gently laying his partner down, covering him with a fur blanket, and slowly flying to the cliff top.

As he moved, gradually, the beastmen who had traded with the Wolf tribe also flew up one after another.
