Bai Qi looked at Bai Cang, who was leading them, and laughed in anger.

"Do you not put me, the Chief, in your eyes at all?" She began with a question.

Bai Cang watched her quietly, and while other beastmen lowered their heads in guilt, Bai Cang said, "Qi, do you still remember your responsibility as Chief?"

Bai Qi’s pupils shrank; for a moment, her eyes were filled with pain and struggle.

"Cang, who knows if they are the next Black Bear tribe!"

"That is why, as Chief, you should judge, not deny everything as soon as you encounter strange beastmen. If you miss this opportunity, do you know how many beastmen in the tribe will..." Bai Cang stopped his words in time.

This was a beastman he had watched grow up, and one he had taught step by step to become a qualified Chief; he couldn't bear to say harsh words.

"But my cubs, my cubs..." Bai Qi bit her lip until it split and bled. Her eyes were bloodshot, her voice drifting as if in a dream, rising and falling. "I want to judge well, but I can't. When I see strange beastmen, I see them..."

"Chief..." The other beastmen, provoked by her appearance, stepped forward with red eyes to support her.

Bai Qi was a good Chief, there was no doubt about that.

To choose a Chief, the tribe had to pick a beastman with high combat power and a brain. Bai Qi had been smart and healthy since she was young; Bai Cang had valued her as a good seedling and focused on training her.

She had lived up to expectations, growing into a reliable beastman, defeating other competitors to become the Chief of the White Feather tribe.

Three years ago, the beastmen of the White Feather tribe were still living their lives in an orderly manner. But after that attack...

The blow to Bai Qi was too great; she still hadn't recovered.

Bai Qi leaned on the beastman’s arm and sat down slowly.

She lowered her head, eyes wide open, but couldn't stop the tears from falling drop by drop.

Hong Jiao said she was arrogant, and he was right.

She had trusted her own judgment too much, trusted that she could protect the tribe, which allowed those beastmen to step into their tribe under the guise of treating their cubs.

She watched in despair as her cubs disappeared one by one, along with her tribesmen, his tribesmen, and their cubs...

This was all her fault as Chief.

Bai Cang: "Have you figured it out?"

"Uncle Cang..." Bai Qi’s voice was hoarse as she slowly raised her head to look at this beastman who was like her father. "I don't want to be this..."

"Bai Qi!"

"Being Chief isn't something you can just decide to do or not do. Think carefully before you speak; is your decision worthy of the effort you put in before?"

"I, I hate it..." Bai Qi broke down, crying, her hands pressed tightly against her chest, her voice sharp, the veins on her neck bulging. After three years of suppression, it was as if she wanted to vent all her pain.

"I hate it!"

She hated those culprits who had hurt so many of their tribesmen and cubs, only to escape without a trace, and who knows where they were enjoying themselves right now!

She wanted to chase after them every moment, find them, and tear them to pieces!

But she was the Chief, she couldn't!

*

The beastmen sleeping on the grass were startled, their scalps tingling from that shrill cry. They scrambled up on all fours, heads poking out like groundhogs, staring at the cliff to the west.

"Were they discovered?" Lang Chou whispered.

Lang Jin sat limp on the fur blanket, bowing like a worshiper, his upper body slumped, and said sleepily, "What does it have to do with us..."

Lin Qiu: "It sounds a bit wrong."

"How about I go take a look?" Que Xi walked over slowly.

He might be able to guess a little of what Bai Qi was thinking. Xiong Chen was dead, and he felt this news should be told to them.

"Don't go," Lin Qiu said.

The two sides weren't familiar; if they suddenly launched an attack, they were so far across the lake that they wouldn't be able to save him in time.

Que Xi thought for a moment, then looked back at Lin Qiu and Lang Yan, and still said, "I'll go."

Lin Qiu didn't know why he was so persistent, but the sub-beastman didn't belong to the Wolf tribe, and they had no right to make decisions for him.

Lin Qiu: "Then be careful."

Que Xi’s beast form was small, but his feathers were bright red. Flying over the blue lake, he could be seen at a glance.

Lin Qiu watched him slowly become a small dot, withdrew his gaze, and slowly climbed up.

"Alright, hurry up and get breakfast ready; we'll leave once we've eaten."

The beastmen were diverted by the commotion and couldn't sleep anymore.

Everyone got up, first filling the water bottles with boiled water, then tilted their heads and asked, "Qiu, what are we eating this morning?"

Lin Qiu: "Something quick."

Lang Qiao: "Roasted dried fish?"

"Awoo! We don't want dried fish!" the beastmen protested in unison, their voices muffled and loud, somewhat deafening.

Lin Qiu said, "Then let's have tail-grass seed porridge, with some dried meat and wild vegetables."

"Yay!" The beastmen raised their hands and cheered, some even jumping up and rolling in mid-air.

Lin Qiu’s eyes held a smile.

Okay, their likes and dislikes were very obvious.

Lang Jin supported the ground with both hands, quickly straightening his upper body. He spat out the fur that had gotten into his mouth from the animal skin and asked, "What about Ya and the others? Will they catch up to us when we leave?"

Yu Lie: "It's fine, you guys go first, I'll go over and take a look, then bring them over."

The iron pot boiled water quickly, and soon steam rose from the surface.

Lang Qiao had finished washing two large scoops of tail-grass seeds, and Lang Yun followed behind, holding two arm-length pieces of dried meat, smiling with a look of pure delight.

Dried meat, oh dried meat! They had been out for so long and had only eaten dried meat once!

How could any beastman not be tempted by that?

"Did you wash the vegetables? So smug," Lin Qiu said.

He could be lazy now; the beastmen did the cooking, and he didn't need to hunt or forage, so he just drew maps. He could be considered the most relaxed among the beastmen.

Tu Ai: "I'll go!"

"Come back."

Tu Ai ran back.

Tu Lin and Tu Cao looked at each other, took the rattan basket, and went to wash the wild vegetables.

Taking advantage of the time, Lang Ying hooked his arm around Lang Huo’s neck and shouted to Lin Qiu, "Qiu, we're going to find some mushrooms."

"Okay, don't go too far."

"Just on the mountain behind us."

Lin Qiu buried his head in sorting through the things traded by the beastmen last night. The herbs had already been classified by Lang Bing, and there were some tubers and fruits that the beastmen hadn't distinguished yet.

Lin Qiu poured everything out and signaled for Tu Ai to come and identify them.

"The ones that don't last long, wash them later for the beastmen to eat. Keep the ones that can be stored, and check carefully to see if there's anything poisonous."

"Do the ones that make your mouth numb count?"

"Yes."

As soon as he finished speaking, Tu Ai took out something that looked like a withered vine.

"This is hoof-leaf vine; the leaves look like animal hooves, and the fruit is delicious. The vine can also be eaten, but it makes your mouth numb, though the juice is sweet. Do you want to try it?"

"Yes!"

"Try your ass!" Lin Qiu slapped away the claws of Lang Jin and the other young beastmen and put the thing aside.

Fortunately, there were only two or three, mixed in with the miscellaneous wild fruits and tubers.

The small tribes had limited abilities, and this was all they could bring to trade. It was dark last night, so they hadn't checked carefully, but they trusted that those beastmen wouldn't dare to lie to the wolf beastmen.

Tu Ai sorted through the rest and nodded, "These can all be eaten."

Lin Qiu brought over the skin bag, and Tu Ai shoveled the food into it.

"We definitely have to detour around the Feather tribe's territory these next two days, so we won't waste time foraging or hunting on the road. This food is just enough to fill our bellies."

Just as he was busy, he suddenly felt that there was no sound around him.

Lin Qiu looked up and saw a dense mass of Feather tribe beastmen flying over the Blue Lake. The sight made Lin Qiu’s heart tighten, and he stood up instantly.

Lang Yan grabbed his wrist, pulled him behind him, and comforted him, "It's okay."

"What are they doing?"

"Who cares what they're doing, just fight... Awoo!" Lang Yun covered his head.

Lang Yan and Lin Qiu, while on guard, looked at Lang He with a hint of relief.

Finally, there was a beastman who could keep this idiot in check.
chapters.title: 第223章
chapters.source_text:
起风了，湖面涟漪四起，月影被打碎。
林楸捂着嘴，慢慢打个哈欠，眼里蓄了泪水。
他脸颊靠在狼岩胸膛，给自己选了一个舒服的姿势窝着。
四个小黑球已经睡着了。
他们蹲在火堆旁紧紧挨着，尾巴勾在一起，团成球，互相依偎着，睡得小呼噜一阵一阵的。
林楸手指挠了挠狼岩掌心道：“王，还让他们跟着我们？”
他看这群小崽子是赖上他们了，从山谷那边跟过来，那么难走的路跟了两天，也不知道该说这群小崽子有毅力，还是没脑子。
狼岩：“如果黑猴部落那边照料他们的兽人发现，该找过来了。”
林楸目光扫过四处，听了听动静，道：“可是没有。”
狼岩：“明天一早，让羽猎把他们送回去。”
与其跟着他们，不如留在原来那地方。
狼兽人还要走很远很远的路，幼崽脆弱，他们也没心思帮人家照料小崽子。
快半夜了，林楸再坐下去要睡着了。
他撑着狼岩硬邦邦的肩膀站起来，跺了跺脚，再伸个懒腰，目光清亮地看向四处，细听那风声里的动静。
狼岩仰头瞧着，目光随着林楸而动，锋利的眉眼舒展着。
“困不困？”
林楸一瞪，然后捂嘴打个哈欠，眸子又多了点水润。
狼岩唇角微扬，摊开手臂道：“该换班了，回来睡觉。”
林楸：“没到时间，急什么。”
*
蓝湖西岸，山崖。
羽族兽人的巢做得高，他们蹲在巢中，就能看见远方燃烧着的火堆。
白苍是白羽部落最厉害的勇士，他的巢位置高，空间也大。
他们这边没生火，白苍跟自己的伴侣坐在树枝和干草搭建的巢穴边缘，望着对面望了半夜。
白苍的伴侣舔一舔唇，仿佛也闻到了那烤鱼的味道。
但比起烤鱼，他更想吃的是盐。
“阿苍，族长真的不同意交换吗？”脆弱的亚兽人靠在白苍怀里，唇色泛白，极小声地道。
他们部落缺盐，很缺。他们请来的祭司不知道为什么突然消失，带走了他们部落大量物资，包括极大部分的盐。
他们怀疑背后有红羽兽人的参与，而红羽兽人同样怀疑这事是他们干的。
两个部落从聚集在这一块地方时，关系时好时坏，合作与争斗不断。
但那些事他们暂且理不清楚，现在也不知道那个祭司跑到了哪里去，兽人只知道，他们现在很需要盐。
非常需要！
今年交换盐的物资还没准备齐全，去年特意省下来的盐没有了，兽人们只能去崖壁上找石头里渗出来的盐霜。
可那远远不够。
他们真的快没力气了。
“族长现在对一切陌生兽人都排斥。”白苍拢着自己的伴侣，大手一下一下帮他按捏着无力的手和腿。他嘴唇几乎贴在伴侣耳边，发出的是气音。
“可我们得活啊……”
“他们来历不明，不敢随便信任。”
“他们是狼兽人，东部大陆的狼兽人还能有谁？看他们那强壮样子，肯定也是原来中央大陆出去的那个狼部落，也就只有他们才有养活部落的能力。”
白苍听着自己伴侣越说越激动，轻轻捂住他的嘴，在他耳边低声道：“别急。”
“我们可以悄悄……”
亚兽人修长的五指虚软地搭在白苍的手臂上，想用力，却使不上劲儿。
白羽部落的兽人很多，他们一窝可以孵出来四五个幼崽，就算活下来一半，也能有两个。
他们面前就靠着这无边无际的蓝湖，只靠吃鱼和采集也能养活幼崽，所以他们部落的兽人数量越来越多。
兽人们活了大半辈子，熊沉那样的事情也经历过几次，他们虽然心痛，但面对食物和渴求的东西，依旧各有心思。
族长年轻，因为失去幼崽对一切陌生兽人都有些应激，他们理解。大部分兽人与族长态度一致，但也有少部分兽人为了自身利益，有自己的想法。
所以，当狼岩看到那从山后出现的黑影时，没有任何意外。
林楸顺着狼岩的视线往后看，见那夜色中笔直站立的一道影子，汗毛都立起来了。
他分明没睡，也注意着四处，可还是没有狼岩的敏锐。
“王！”其他兽人一跃而起。
狼岩：“躺下。”
兽人们不明所以，但还是照做，只是换了个方向，面向里侧。
“你们这里可以交换盐？”兽人隐在暗处，后背紧紧贴着陡坡，声音也压得低低的，似乎不想被某些兽人发现。
大伙儿都是聪明兽人，脑子一转，立马就明白过来。
狼岩：“换。”
他眼神往靠近盐袋的狼丑身上一扫，兽人立刻爬起来，提着剩余那半袋子盐，放在兽人面前。
兽人蹲下，手插入盐中，然后沾了沾唇。
“一筐肉干一勺盐。”狼丑示意他看袋子里那勺子。
兽人呼吸一乱，林楸这下注意到了，他看了看狼岩，被他拉住手腕，往身侧带了带。
“没有肉干，还有其他能……”
狼丑迅速道：“草药、兽皮、鱼干也成。”
说到鱼干，狼丑五官皱紧，嫌弃得很明显。
兽人呼吸沉了一瞬，躺地上的狼兽人和黑羽兽人肌肉已经悄悄绷紧。
“珠子，行吗？”
“要那个干……唔！”狼禾捂紧了狼云的嘴，笑着示意兽人继续。
狼云哼哼，都快习惯被他伴侣捂嘴了。
狼岩：“看看。”
兽人伸出手，附近的狼乔把珠子接了过去，他用手指盘了盘，那一把珠子格外圆润，个头也大。
他向后递去，珠子落到了狼岩手里。
林楸跟着狼岩凑近火堆看，瞬间被那珍珠吸引了注意。
是很漂亮圆润的珍珠，看着是海珠，颜色居然带点粉色。一共五颗，个头很均匀，也不知道兽人从哪里得来的。
这样的东西在以前食物充足的时候很有市场，但现在……
“五颗都换？”
“换，全换盐。”
狼岩思考了下，道：“一勺盐。”
“这是海珠，个头一样，颜色也好看……”
这是兽人曾经为了哄伴侣开心，亲自去找的，他找了好几年才凑足了那么一串，可惜，如今要为了交换盐把那一串打散。
兽人想起当初送珍珠的时候伴侣惊喜的笑和红扑扑的脸，再对比现在他抱着只剩骨头和绵软的身体，还有白得没有血色的脸……
他们的幼崽也没了。
但他和他的伴侣还要活着。
“一勺半。”
兽人还是没应，他突兀道：“你们是中央大陆的那个狼部落？”
狼岩：“是。”
“现在住在哪里？”
“东部大陆北边，随时欢迎来交换。”
“成交。”
一勺半的盐，只够他和他的伴侣吃到雨季去。要是白栖始终走不出失去幼崽的阴影，他想，他或许要带伴侣离开，去其他地方碰碰运气。
如今的白羽部落，已经一团乱了。
兽人悄无声息地来，又悄悄离开。
后半夜，火堆直接熄灭了，兽人们坐起来，静默无声地看着一个接一个过来交换的兽人。
这其中有白羽兽人、红羽兽人，还有光明正大驮着东西飞了大半天才从蓝湖南边专程过来交换的小部落。
他们离这边远，才收到消息就准备东西往这边赶了。
熊沉带领流浪兽人攻击这些羽族的时候，几个雀族根本没被看上，躲过了这次袭击。
他们心里可没那么多弯弯绕绕，只听到有兽人说狼部落带了盐交换，最多停留一晚上，他们便慌慌张张过来了，生怕晚了一步错过。
兽人们这么积极，也是明白，他们身上没狼部落可图的东西。
交易虽然有些偷偷摸摸，兽人们也鬼鬼祟祟，但好歹慢慢换出去两袋子盐，换回来几袋子这边特有的草药。
草药都是寻常草药。
几个小部落没有祭司，生病了只能自己找草药医治，也就知道那么三五种药材。寻常遇到了就采集回去，积少成多，渐渐攒了不少。
草药在哪里都受欢迎，就算拿到海边去交换草药也是可以的。
不过海边那些部落心黑，一点点盐就要他们一个兽皮袋的草药，就算兽人们把部落里的草药都薅尽了也换不回来多少盐。
等看了狼兽人这边的要价，几个小部落的族长笑得牙花子都出来了。
“以后还来吗？”蓝雀族长缩成一团，小声问。
他还是怕狼兽人和黑羽兽人的，但为了盐，不得不鼓起勇气问。
狼岩：“不一定，但你们可以去狼部交换。”
“在哪儿？”
双方又交换了一下部落信息，几个族长心满意足地一挥翅膀，招呼族人悄悄摸摸离开。
天快亮时，交换也结束了。
今晚谁都没睡好，大家往地上一躺，歪着头看向狼岩和林楸。
“王，我们能晚点赶路不？”
“嗯。”
兽人安心闭眼，没过多久，这呼噜声就起了。
林楸也困得睁不开眼，他侧身，脑袋枕着狼岩手臂，窝在他身侧也慢慢睡去。
狼岩目光一扫，那四个小黑球又不见了。
“猎。”
羽猎抬头，他戒备了一晚上，这会儿也困得打哈欠。
“算了。”狼岩看向睡了一个整觉的羽涯几个，“涯，你们去把树上藏的那四个小崽子抓了，送回山谷那边。”
“嗷！”兽人直挺挺站起来，中气十足应道。
林楸眼睫颤了颤。
狼岩捂住自家伴侣的耳朵，看着那群跟自家狼崽子学坏了的黑羽兽人，轻轻叹气。
好的不学坏的学。
“吱吱吱！”小黑球正抱着树枝啃嫩叶呢，忽然被拎了起来。另外三个分散在树上的小崽子龇牙威胁，又被剩下几个黑羽兽人顺手抓起来。
羽涯道：“乖一点，送你们回去。”
“吱！”
“不回去不行，我们要走了。”
“吱吱吱！”
“不行，我们不能带你们，你们太小了。”
幼崽低下头，看着越来越远的兽人队伍，瘪了瘪嘴，四肢垂软下来，眼眶红红的。
“吱……”幼崽声音小小，含着恳求。
羽涯振翅，目光看着底下密林，还是那句话：“你们太小了。”
*
天亮了，大河入口边停留的那群兽人还没有起来。
白栖看了一眼，回到山崖上，就着昨天采集的野菜野果吃了一顿早饭。
吃完，他拍拍手，看到飞落到崖顶的红羽兽人，淡然移开眼。
“他们还没走。”
“我没瞎。”
白栖看向远处狼兽人停留的草地，只见那边只起来了几个兽人，零零散散地在草地上活动，时不时往这边看一眼。
他们还没死心。
“族长，今天安排采集和捕猎吗？”白鸢在巢中吃完早饭，飞上来询问。
白栖：“让捕猎和采集的兽人去后山，部落留一半的兽人守着。”
“是。”
白鸢利落地安排下去。
白栖看向身边这个碍眼的兽人，道：“有事说事，没事可以滚了。”
红角唇角勾着，笑说：“你别告诉我，你昨晚上没有发现有兽人悄悄出去了。”
白栖瞳孔一缩，一把攥住兽人脖子，眼神冷厉，“你说什么？”
“哦，原来你不知道啊。”
白栖一把将他甩开，直接落到下方巢穴。
她感觉到昨晚有兽人出去，但没想到他们有这么大的胆子，在她下了命令之后依旧去和狼部落接触。
红角讥讽一笑，“你还是这么自大。”
“红角！你给我滚！”白栖双目赤红，看他如同看仇人。
红角心中隐隐作痛，他别开头，沉声道：“我来是告诉你，昨晚上南边几个小部落都已经和狼兽人们交换到了盐，他们的盐比海边的部落更好，要的东西也没那么多，你要是聪明一点，就……”
“我还用不到你来教！”
红角嗤笑，“行，我滚。”
红角噌的一下离去，翅膀带起的风掀起白栖的长发，兽人气得哆嗦。
“昨晚都有哪些兽人出去过，都给我上来！”
下方山洞，白苍轻轻托着自己伴侣的后背，一点一点喂他加了盐的水。亚兽人看他不慌不忙的样子，担忧地把冰凉的手搭在他手臂上。
“阿苍。”
白苍：“慢点喝，不急。”
大掌抚摸了下亚兽人有些粗糙的长发，顺着滑下，托住他瘦得下巴尖尖的脸颊。看着他一口一口将水喝完，才放下果壳碗，手落在他后背轻轻地顺了顺。
“好受了吗？”白苍脸贴着自己伴侣的脸，又问。
亚兽人指了指上面。
白苍握住他的手，在他耳边低声道：“别怕。”
他慢慢哄着亚兽人睡熟了，目光看着巢外，飞上去的兽人简直零星。
昨晚上，可是有接近百个兽人去了的。
白栖威望下降了。
白苍又等了一会儿，确认自己的伴侣睡熟了，而上头也没有再传出声音来，他才轻轻将亚兽人放下，给他盖好兽皮毯，慢慢飞上了崖顶。
他一动，渐渐的，出去跟狼部落交换过的兽人也陆陆续续飞了上去。
白栖看着领头的白苍，直接气笑了。
“你们是不是根本不把我这个族长放在眼里。”她开口便是质问。
白苍静看着她，在其他兽人愧疚地低下头的时候，白苍却道：“栖，你还记得你身为族长的责任吗？”
白栖瞳孔一缩，一瞬间，她眼里满是痛苦和挣扎。
“苍，谁知道他们是不是下一个黑熊部落！”
“所以你身为族长，该去判断，而不是遇到陌生兽人就先否认。如果错失了这次机会，你知道部落多少兽人会因为你这个决定而……”白苍的话及时止住。
这是他看着长大的兽人，也是他教导着一步一步成为一个合格族长的兽人，他到底是不忍心说下重话。
“可我的幼崽，我的幼崽啊……”白栖紧咬住唇，咬得唇瓣撕裂，沁出鲜血。她眼里遍布血丝，声音飘荡，犹在梦中，忽上忽下，“我想好好判断，可我不能，我看到陌生兽人就像看到了他们……”
“族长……”其他兽人被她的样子一激，红着眼，上前扶着她。
白栖是个好族长，这是毫无疑问的事。
部落选族长，要选武力高且有脑子的兽人。白栖从小就聪明，身体也健康，白苍就是看重她是个好苗子，着力培养。
她也不负众望，长成了一个可靠的兽人，打败其他竞争者，成为白羽部落的族长。
在三年前，白羽部落的兽人们还在有条不紊地过着自己的日子。可经历那一次袭击之后……
白栖受到的打击太大了，她到现在都还没缓过来。
白栖撑着兽人的手臂，缓缓坐下来。
她低垂着头，睁大了眼睛，也阻止不了那泪水一滴一滴地掉落。
红角说她自大，说得没错。
她就是太信任自己的判断，信任自己能护住部落，才让那群兽人借着治疗幼崽的名头踏入了他们部落。
她绝望地看着自己的幼崽一个一个没了，还有族人、他的族人和他们的幼崽……
这都是她这个族长的错。
白苍：“想明白了？”
“苍叔……”白栖声音嘶哑，缓缓抬起头看着这个如同她阿父一般的兽人，“我不想当这个……”
“白栖！”
“族长不是你相当就当，想不当就不当的，你说话之前好好想想，你的决定对得起你之前做的努力吗？”
“我、我恨啊……”白栖崩溃大哭，手紧紧压在自己胸口，声音尖利，脖子上的青筋暴起。压抑三年，仿佛要将一切痛苦宣泄出来。
“我恨啊！”
她恨那群罪魁祸首伤了他们那么多族人和幼崽，如今却逃得无影无踪，此刻不知道还在哪一处逍遥！
她无时无刻不想追过去，找到他们，把他们碎尸万段！
可她是族长，她不能！
*
草地上睡觉的兽人们一惊，被那声凄厉的叫声吓得头皮发麻，四肢并用地爬起来，跟土拨鼠一样支着个脑袋盯着西边山崖。
“他们被发现了？”狼丑小声道。
狼金软趴趴地一屁股往兽皮毯上一坐，叩拜似的，上半身趴下来，困顿道：“关我们什么事……”
林楸：“听着有点不对劲。”
“要不，我去看看？”雀溪慢慢走上前来。
白栖的想法，他或许能猜到一点。熊沉死了，他觉得这个消息应该要告诉他们一下。
“别去。”林楸道。
两边不熟，万一那边突然发动攻击，隔着湖这么远，他们想救都来不及。
雀溪低眉思考了下，再回头看着林楸和狼岩，还是道：“我去一趟。”
林楸不知道他为什么这么坚持，但亚兽人并不是狼部落的，他们也无权做主。
林楸：“那你注意安全。”
雀溪的兽形很小，但羽毛又红又亮。飞在蓝汪汪的湖面，一眼就可以看到。
林楸看着他慢慢变成一个小点，收回目光，慢慢爬起来。
“好了，赶紧忙活早饭吧，吃完了咱们就走。”
兽人们被那么一打岔，也睡不着了。
大家爬起来，先把凉白开灌水壶里，然后仰起脖子问：“楸，早上吃什么？”
林楸：“来个快的。”
狼乔：“烤鱼干？”
“嗷！我们不吃鱼干！”兽人们声音齐齐抗议，声音闷响，有些震耳。
林楸道：“那就尾巴草籽粥吧，加点肉干和野菜。”
“好诶！”兽人举手欢呼，更有甚者直接蹦起来在半空中打了个滚。
林楸眼眸含笑。
可以，喜恶很明显。
狼金两手撑着地面，很快将自己上半身直起来，他呸了两口钻进嘴里的兽皮上的毛，问：“涯他们呢？我们走了他们来追我们？”
羽猎：“没事，到时候你们先走，我过去看看，再带他们过来。”
铁锅烧水很快，不多时，水面就冒出了烟。
狼乔淘洗好两大瓢尾巴草籽，后头跟着的狼云手上拿着两个手臂长的肉干，笑得一脸没出息。
肉干啊肉干，他们出来这么久，也才只吃了一次的肉干！
这让哪个兽人不心动呢？
“菜洗没有？这么得意。”林楸道。
他现在也能偷懒了，做饭有兽人做，捕猎采集用不到他，就画画地图，可以说兽人当中他算最轻松的。
兔艾：“我去！”
“回来。”
兔艾又跑回来。
兔林和兔草两个对视一眼，接过藤筐，去洗野菜。
趁着还有点时间，狼影手臂往狼火脖子上一勾，扬声冲着林楸道：“楸，我们去找点蘑菇。”
“行，别走远了。”
“就在后头山上。”
林楸埋头翻了翻昨晚上兽人交换过来的东西，里面的草药狼冰已经分好类了，还有些块根和果子之类的，兽人们还没区分。
林楸把东西倒出来，示意兔艾过来认一认。
“放不久的等会儿洗了给兽人们吃了，能放的先放着，仔细看看有没有什么带毒的。”
“吃了麻嘴巴的算吗？”
“算。”
话落，兔艾就从里面拿出来一根枯树藤一样的东西。
“这个是蹄叶藤，叶子长得像兽蹄，结的果子好吃。这藤也可以吃，就是吃了嘴麻，但汁水甜甜的。要不要尝尝？”
“要！”
“要个屁！”林楸一巴掌拍开狼金几个年轻兽人伸过来的爪子，将东西放一边。
好在只有两三根，跟杂七杂八的野果块根混在一堆。
小部落的兽人能力有限，能拿出来交换的也就这些东西，昨晚黑灯瞎火的，他们没检查那么细，但也谅那些兽人不敢骗狼兽人。
兔艾划拉了一下剩下的东西，点点头，“都可以吃。”
林楸把兽皮袋拎过来，兔艾往里刨食物。
“我们这两天肯定要先赶着绕开羽族的领地，路上就不耽搁时间去采集捕猎了，这些食物刚好能填填肚子。”
正忙着，忽然感觉到周围没什么声音了。
林楸一抬头，就看见蓝湖上空，乌压压的羽族兽人飞过来，那阵仗，看得林楸心中一凛，瞬间站了起来。
狼岩握住他手腕，将他拉到身后，安抚道：“没事。”
“他们要干嘛？”
“管他们要干嘛，打就是……嗷！”狼云捂脑壳。
狼岩和林楸戒备之余，略显欣慰地看了一眼狼禾。
总算有兽人能制得住这蠢蛋了。

chapters.title: 第224章
chapters.translated_text:
A large flock of White-Feathered orcs swooped over Blue Lake, hovering above the water; the sound of their beating wings was a low hum, like a torrential downpour drumming against the lake surface.

Sounds erupted urgently from the forest behind the mountain as Lang Ying and Lang Huo led the orcs in a leap down from the hillside. There were only thirty-some orcs, yet they charged with the momentum of a thousand troops.

Each of them was tall in their beast form, their paw pads landing silently. In an instant, they returned to the formation, watching the flock of Feathered orcs with guarded expressions.

Bai Qi: "Wolf King. We have come to trade."

The orcs all noticed the flash of red in the flock. Que Xi let out a crisp cry, flew down, and landed on Tu Ai's shoulder.

He stretched his wings, chirped a few times, and Tu Ai nodded.

"Que Xi says they are here to trade," Tu Ai said.

Lang Yan raised his hand to signal the orcs to bring out the goods; there was no need to remain on guard.

The White-Feathered orcs landed and placed the items they had brought on the lakeshore. A moment later, another humming sound arrived as the Red-Feathered orcs from the west bank swarmed over as well.

Lin Qiu glanced at the orcs preening their feathers not far away, feeling as if they had arrived at some natural tourist attraction. So many Feathered orcs!

The items brought by the White-Feathered tribe included medicinal herbs, animal hides, and various beautiful pearl shells they had collected. They didn't just want salt; they also wanted to trade for the Wolf tribe's herbs, pottery, and fishing nets.

Lang Qiao, who was in charge of the trade, tallied the supplies while arranging for the orcs to pack items for the White-Feathered orcs.

However, while herbs and hides were easy to trade, those decorative items...

"King?"

Lang Yan scanned the area and said, "The tribe won't trade for them collectively. If any orc likes them, they can trade for them individually."

"But they don't have anything," Lin Qiu said.

"One scoop of salt per orc's share. Once they use it, they can go back and work to make it up."

Upon hearing this, the orcs still hesitated.

Lang Yun noticed his mate glancing at the beautiful pearls in the hands of a White-Feathered orc before quickly looking away. He stepped forward, about to speak, when Lang He suddenly grabbed his hand.

"Don't you want them?"

Lang He shook his head gently and whispered, "It's not worth it. Save the salt to trade for food."

Many orcs felt the same as Lang He. They had been struggling with hunger just a few years ago and still carried a sense of crisis. They felt that while things like pearls were beautiful, if they had to trade salt or food for them, it was better not to trade at all.

"As long as you like them..." Lang Yun tilted his chin toward the White-Feathered orc. "I'll trade for them."

Lin Qiu stood to the side with his arms crossed, nudging Lang Yan with his shoulder. "Look, they have their good points too."

"Hmm, just a bit stupid."

"Their mate is right there, protecting them. You'd better keep your voice down."

Hong Jiao led his clansmen forward, first nodding to Lang Yan. "Hong Jiao, Chief of the Red-Feathered tribe, and also... Bai Qi's mate."

Lang Yan: "What are you trading for?"

Hong Jiao hadn't expected him to be so direct; he was startled for a moment, then his smile became a bit more sincere.

"Trading for salt."

As soon as he finished speaking, Lang Yun handed the string of beautiful pearls he had just traded for to his mate, then brought over a bag of goods to pitch. "We have more good things than just salt. Look, clay pots, clay pans, herbs, fishing nets, matches, candles—all things you don't have here. Want some?"

Hong Jiao glanced at Bai Qi, who looked indifferent and stood far away from him, and said, "Still just salt."

"Fine then."

Lang Yun waved his hand behind him, and Lang Jin and the others stepped forward with salt bags.

The two sides agreed on the amount of salt to trade based on the items the Red-Feathered tribe had brought. Once the trade was done, they checked each other's bags.

Lang Yan and Lin Qiu just watched from the side to ensure the orcs didn't make mistakes or miss anything. The two Feathered tribe chiefs finished checking their traded goods and walked over toward them.

"Wolf King." Hong Jiao looked at Lin Qiu. "Wolf King's mate?"

"Just call me Qiu."

"Qiu." Hong Jiao looked at Bai Qi nearby and reached out to pull her over. "This is Bai Qi."

Bai Qi glanced at Hong Jiao, pulled her hand away, and walked forward slowly.

"Your salt is very good. It's not sea salt?"

"No, it's our own salt," Lin Qiu smiled.

"Can we trade again in the future?"

"Yes."

That salt cave of theirs was a salt mine; the orcs kept digging, and the more they dug, the more there was.

"About what happened before... I'm sorry." Bai Qi lowered her eyes, her fingers trembling as if in a spasm. Suddenly, Hong Jiao grasped her hand, and this time, Bai Qi did not shake it off.

Bai Qi looked at Lin Qiu and Lang Yan, her eyes slightly red.

She said sincerely, "And thank you, for destroying the Black Bear tribe."

Lin Qiu: "We did it to save our own cubs, but he did die quite miserably."

Tears welled up in Bai Qi's eyes, but she was smiling.

She said, "Let's be friends. White-Feathered tribe, Bai Qi."

Lin Qiu: "Wolf tribe, Lin Qiu."

Hong Jiao kept his peripheral vision on his mate. Seeing her like this, his lips trembled slightly, but he began to smile bit by bit.

Noticing Lang Yan's gaze, he looked back, suppressed his smile, and asked, "Where is the Wolf tribe located?"

"To the northeast, behind the highest mountain. It should take you seven or eight days to get there."

Hong Jiao nodded and said no more, only gripping Bai Qi's hand tightly.

The trade ended quickly, and the orcs departed.

The two groups of Feathered orcs that had arrived one after another were now mixed together, white and red; many were pairs of one red and one white, clearly mates.

It seems the chief's attitude really influences tribal relations!

Lin Qiu clapped his hands. "Alright, let's eat, then set off once we're done."

They had traded quite a bit this time. They had brought eighty bags of salt in total, and had only traded thirteen scoops—about one bag—with the Gray Rabbit tribe earlier.

This time, the two large Feathered tribes had traded for ten bags, plus the two bags traded sporadically last night, totaling thirteen bags traded so far.

They had brought fewer fishing nets and pottery, so only one or two of those were traded, along with some herbs.

As for the things they had traded for, there were even more.

They had traded for twenty-six bags of black beans from the Gray Rabbit orcs, and now twenty-one bags remained after eating.

Last night, they had traded for ten bags of fruit and tubers, ten bags of herbs, and eighty small animal hides and about twenty large ones.

Just now, they had traded for another sixty bags of herbs, forty baskets of dried meat, thirty baskets of dried fish, and some beautiful ornaments the orcs had traded for themselves...

The things the orcs had to carry had not decreased; in fact, they had increased significantly.

Fortunately, they were all light; if each orc carried a little, they could manage.

They had stayed by the lake long enough today. After breakfast, the orcs extinguished the fire, grabbed a handful of grass to scrub the large iron pot clean, hung it securely on the cargo, and continued their journey.

Yu Lie called out and went back to find Yu Ya and the others.

Coming out of the valley, because the slopes were steep and there were no paths, and the orcs were carrying heavy loads, it had taken them two days. Yu Ya and the others could fly over and should be able to arrive in half a day.

Lang Huo and Lang Ying, who were leading the team, continued walking, and the group slowly followed.

Lin Qiu carried his belongings and walked slowly along the large lake to the west with Lang Yan.

They had just asked the White-Feathered orcs about this, and the other party had indicated they could pass through their territory.

If they had gone south, the orc team would have had to make a huge detour before continuing southwest.

Suddenly, a crisp cry sounded in the sky. Lin Qiu looked up and saw a White-Feathered orc circling above.

"He's the guide. Follow him," Lang Yan said.

Lang Huo in the front responded, following the direction of the White-Feathered orc along the north shore of the lake to the west, climbing gentle slopes, crossing high cliffs, and entering low, scattered mountains.

The White-Feathered orc in the sky led them for two days. Yu Lie also returned with Yu Ya and the others. Once they left the edge of the White-Feathered tribe's territory, the orc in the sky let out one more cry and left.

Lin Qiu unfolded the map in his hand, discussed the route ahead with Que Xi, and filled in the places they had just passed on the map bit by bit.

Through wind and rain, the journey was long. As they covered more ground, the corners of the map were slowly filled in.

In the blink of an eye, they had been out for three months.

The rainy season in the south seemed harder to endure than at Wolf Mountain. It rained for a while every single day. When it cleared up, the sunlight hit their bodies like a glowing hot iron, so scorching that the orcs found it unbearable.

Stones scattered on the ground, baked by the sun for half a day—if an orc accidentally stepped on one, they would yelp and jump up, cargo and all.

By this time, the orcs had reached the very edge of the Eastern Continent; further ahead was the territory of the Central Continent.

But the advancing team stopped here. The orcs found a large cave, cleaned it up, and moved right in.

This group of orcs, who had never been to the southernmost part of the continent, mostly had rashes, and a few of the weaker ones had fallen ill and collapsed.

Insects chirped in the dense forest, and the humidity was so thick it felt like it was clogging the orcs' nostrils, making it hard for everyone to breathe.

It had just rained, but a moment later, sunlight pierced through the gaps in the trees, reflecting off the rain-drenched leaves in the forest, making it very dazzling.

Trees swayed. Near the cave entrance, two thin, narrow trees were pushed aside by a pair of hands.

Lin Qiu and Lang Bing emerged carrying rattan baskets and walked quickly back to the front of the cave.

The trees outside the cave had been cut down by the orcs, and a shed had been built at the entrance, with a stove underneath, holding the iron pot and the clay pot for boiling medicine.

Lin Qiu and Lang Bing were the orcs in the team who knew how to treat illnesses. They had just gone out for a search and had indeed found quite a few medicinal herbs in the forest that matched their symptoms.

Lin Qiu put down the rattan basket and sat down, bracing his knees.

His clothes were soaked through, and his long hair, tied up high, had become a mess from pushing through the forest. Strands of hair were stuck to his face and neck with sweat. His body felt itchy and sticky, and Lin Qiu frowned tightly.

Lang Bing, beside him, was in the same sorry state—covered in red spots, drenched in sweat, with dead twigs in his hair, rotten leaves hanging on his clothes, and tree sap that had turned brown smeared on his legs...

Lin Qiu grabbed the rattan basket and rummaged through the herbs he had just washed.

A cool breeze hit his neck, and Lin Qiu sighed in relief.

He looked at Tu Ai, who was fanning them, and asked, "Where are the other orcs?"

Out of the tribe's sixty-some orcs, four were ill, and over thirty others had rashes.

It wasn't just the heat; it was also because they had been traveling for so long without proper rest, and they were exhausted.

Before Lin Qiu and Lang Bing went to find herbs, these orcs were still staying in the cave.

Tu Ai was also dizzy from the heat. He had cut his hair short—it was uneven and not very pretty, but it was cool.

"The King took some orcs out to hunt. Ying and the Black-Feathered orcs went to see if there are any tribes nearby."

Different environments nurture different orcs. Everyone was sick; if Qiu and Bing couldn't handle it, the local orcs should have a way.

Lin Qiu was irritable from the heat. He waved his hand. "Fan yourself. Let's get the medicine ready quickly."

The four most severely ill orcs were Lang He, Lang Rong, Que Xi, and Lang Yun.

Of the four, three were sub-orcs. The only male orc, Lang Yun, had been bitten by a snake—though this time it wasn't because he was being an idiot and stepped on a snake's tail, but because he had shielded his mate, Lang He.

The snake was very venomous, and the situation was extremely critical at the time. If it hadn't been for Lin Qiu and Lang Bing's quick reactions, he would have lost his life.

Lang He might have been frightened by Lang Yun, and after the shock, he fell ill the next day.

The other two orcs... Lin Qiu and Lang Bing determined both had heatstroke. Que Xi had a weak constitution and had been sick several times on this journey, and Lang Rong was exhausted combined with the high temperature, so it wasn't surprising he fell ill.

They were the four most serious cases. The other orcs, while not bedridden, were also sickly and looked pale.

Lang Bing prepared medicine for the heatstroke, while Lin Qiu pounded the herbs for the rashes into a paste and had Tu Ai take it inside for the orcs to smear on their bodies.

The herbs were effective; they felt cool and soothing on the skin.

Lin Qiu applied some to himself and then smeared some on Lang Bing.

Lang Bing didn't stop picking through the herbs, slightly lifting his chin to make it easier for Lin Qiu, and said, "I found a few types of herbs here that the tribe is lacking. When the sun goes down, I'll tell the orcs to go find more."

"Okay."

Stopping here meant consuming resources every day, whether it was food or herbs; they had to replenish them.

Lin Qiu helped Lang Bing finish applying the herbs, washed his hands, and rested for a while before going into the cave to check on the sick orcs.

There was a large clay pot in the cave; it was originally something they had brought to trade, but now they were using it.

The pot was filled with boiled water infused with heat-relieving herbs, left to cool to a lukewarm temperature for the orcs to drink whenever they needed.

It was fortunate they hadn't drunk raw water along the way, otherwise, who knew what other problems would have arisen.

The cave was large, likely once inhabited by some tribe, and there was enough room for their entire team of orcs to lie down.

Now, more than ten orcs were lying inside.

Some had stood guard at night and were now catching up on sleep, while others were delirious from illness.

Lin Qiu headed to the corner.

Lang Yun's lips were pale as he sat beside Lang He, waving a fan to keep him cool.

Lin Qiu asked in a low voice, "Are you alright?"

Lang Yun shook his head, sweat dripping from his face.

He had lost too much blood, which was why his complexion was so poor.

The situation had been urgent, and they had to drain the blood while searching for an antidote. Fortunately, the poison was neutralized, and he just needed to recover.

Lin Qiu crouched down and felt Lang He's forehead; it was still hot.

He checked Lang Zhao and Que Xi one by one; they were the same as Lang He.

Inside the cave, Tu Cao and Tu Lin were watching over them, using water to wipe their bodies to lower their temperature, but the effect was minimal.

When the orcs first collapsed, Lang Bing had fed them heat-relieving medicine, which helped for a while, but after one night, their temperatures had risen again.

Lin Qiu sighed inwardly.

He only hoped this batch of herbs would be useful.

In truth, orcs shouldn't get this sick, but not only were they uncomfortable, they had also been delayed.

Outside, Lang Bing had already started boiling the medicine.

Lin Qiu saw that the other orcs had applied the rash-treating herbs and were now covered in green. He smiled for the first time in a while and signaled for Tu Lin and the others to apply some to Que Xi and the others as well.

The rainy season was hard to travel in; he didn't know how long they would be delayed.

It wasn't early anymore; it was almost afternoon.

The other orcs were away, and they hadn't had lunch yet. Lin Qiu simply took out some tail-grass seeds, intending to make porridge, and blanched the wild vegetables the orcs had gathered to make a cold salad.

It was hot, and no one had an appetite; they had been eating like this for the past few days.

However, this meant the tail-grass seeds were being consumed faster, and only three bags remained.

A mile east of the cave, there was a river, and the water the orcs used was taken from there.

The stones by the river were arranged neatly, clearly moved there by orcs from elsewhere. This was proof enough that a tribe had once lived here. It was just unclear if they had migrated or perished.

The clay pot for water outside was empty. Lin Qiu took a rattan basket and two empty clay pots to the river to fetch water.

A path had already been worn from the cave to the river by the orcs.

Lin Qiu filled the two pots, carried one on his back, held the other, and stood up slowly.

The moment he looked up, he felt a gaze from directly ahead, and his hair stood on end.

Lin Qiu looked toward the forest opposite and only saw a black shadow quickly flash by.

Without a second thought, he left the riverbank quickly, almost running back to the cave.

Lang Bing was guarding the clay pots, watching the medicine.

Seeing Lin Qiu return in a hurry with a vigilant expression, he frowned, stood up, and took the pots from him. "What's wrong?"

"There are orcs on the other side of the river."

Lin Qiu put down the rattan basket; half the water had spilled out, and his entire back was soaked.

"Did you see clearly what kind of orcs they were?"

"No."

"There are no tribes nearby," Lang Bing said, his eyes cold.

They carried a lot of goods, and they hadn't hidden the fact that they were trading along the way, so it wasn't surprising they were being targeted.

Lin Qiu: "Don't go out alone for now. Let's wait until the King and the others return."

"Alright," Lang Bing said.

Lang Yan and the others wouldn't hunt too far away. If something happened, a shout from here should be audible over there. Lin Qiu wasn't that afraid, but he was worried about encountering ill-intentioned orcs. The orcs in their cave were in poor condition, and if a fight broke out, injuries would be inevitable...

Lin Qiu looked toward the river and suppressed the worry in his heart.

He quickly washed the pot, poured the water from the clay pots into it, and started boiling it.

Cooking in front of the stove during the rainy season was torture; the heat from the fire beat down on him, and the sweat was unstoppable.

Lin Qiu's cheeks were flushed red from the heat, and his throat was dry. Once the fire was lit and the dead branches inside caught, he stepped back two paces and wiped the sweat from his face.

"Is the medicine ready?"

Lang Bing looked at the clay pot, his face also flushed red from the heat, and said, "Almost."

Lin Qiu sat further away, staring at the stove fire, holding a fan and occasionally fanning Lang Bing's back.

The orcs were now used to wearing shorts and short-sleeved shirts, all made of linen; it was breathable and could also block some insects.

It was hot, so Lang Bing didn't even braid his hair anymore. He just rolled his long hair up on his head and pinned it casually with a polished twig; as long as he didn't run or jump, his hair wouldn't fall down.

His back was never dry, and his neck was covered in rashes and sweat, making him itch so badly that he couldn't help but scratch whenever he lost control. After scratching, there were red marks, and it looked terrible now.

The herbal paste Lin Qiu had applied was also mixed with sweat and falling off.

"I don't know how long this rainy season in the south lasts... there are at least four more months of this to endure."

Lang Bing: "Then tell Tu Ai and the others to dig a hole underground. We'll stay here and wait until the weather cools down before we move on."

Lin Qiu laughed, wiped the sweat from his head, and fanned Lang Bing vigorously.

"You think quite beautifully."

"Then what else can we do..."

They usually didn't move around much during the rainy season; even hunting was done at night.

"Otherwise, we might as well just travel at night."

Lin Qiu waved the fan, considering the possibility.

"That might not work. It's dark at night, and it's not safe."

"How safe is it during the day?"

"At least you don't have to step on a snake just because you can't see it."

"But if you see one, you're still in trouble."

He was talking about Lang He and Lang Yun; it seemed they were destined to have trouble with snakes.

"Let's wait for the King to come back and discuss it..." Lin Qiu laughed weakly. He was being baked so hard his brain couldn't function, and there was a fire in his chest, burning him with anxiety.

Once the medicine was boiled, Lang Guo poured it into cold water to cool it down. When it wasn't so hot, he poured it into three bowls and sent them into the cave.

A moment later, he came back out with the empty bowls, added water to the clay pot, and kept watching the pot to continue boiling.

"You go rest for a while, I'll watch it."

"It's hot, I can't sleep."

"It's even hotter outside."

"I'm not going."

Lin Qiu gritted his teeth. This little wolf cub was as stubborn as an ox when he wanted to be!

By the time Lin Qiu's two pots of tail-grass seed porridge were ready, half the afternoon had passed.

He quickly switched to another clay pot, added water, and once it boiled, blanched a large basket of wild vegetables, rinsed them in cold water, and started mixing the salad.

Just as he finished and called the orcs to eat, he heard the sound of wings flapping in the sky.

Lang Ying, Yu Lie, and Lang Yan, who had gone out hunting, had all returned.

In places with fewer tribes, wild beasts had room to grow, so the number of prey here was slightly higher than in areas with tribes.

They brought back two pieces of prey, beasts unique to the south, which had already been processed, so they could be boiled and eaten immediately that night.

The orcs returned to the cave and collapsed directly.

They didn't even mind the water in the pot infused with heat-relieving herbs anymore and drank it all up.

Seeing that Lang Yan had returned, Lin Qiu took some porridge and sat down beside him.

As soon as he sat down, he felt a wave of heat rush over him. Before they even touched, Lin Qiu felt hot.

Looking at Lang Yan, his bare upper body was covered in sweat, large drops of sweat rolling down his undulating muscles, and his whole body was scorching.

Lin Qiu handed him the bowl and brought in the cloth he had been drying outside for him to wipe his sweat.

"Where did you go?"

"South. We're almost at the seaside here."

"Did you encounter any tribes?"

Lang Yan shook his head.

Lang Ying and the others had gone out specifically to look for tribes. Hearing this, they looked toward Lin Qiu, their voices weary. "There are no tribes here."

He and the Black-Feathered orcs had finished circling the area and hadn't seen any tribes.

Lin Qiu glanced at the orcs who had fallen asleep after drinking the medicine and lowered his voice. "It's fine if we didn't encounter any. Bing's herbs are effective."

"Hmm, eat quickly." Lang Yan looked down at Lin Qiu's cheeks, which had thinned quite a bit, feeling a pang of heartache.

Lin Qiu: "This bowl is for you, I'll go get some..."

"No need." Lang Yan held Lin Qiu's hand. "You eat, I have no appetite right now."

Lin Qiu ate slowly, thinking of the black shadow he had seen by the river earlier, and mentioned it to Lang Yan.

Lang Yan took the cloth he had used to wipe his sweat, washed it, hung it on a branch to dry, then brought a fan inside, sat beside Lin Qiu, and fanned him while asking, "Did you see clearly what kind of orcs they were?"

"No."

"Don't worry, I'll go take a look later."

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

With Lang Yan fanning him, Lin Qiu felt a bit better. He finished his porridge in a few bites, then took the fan and let Lang Yan eat.

After the two large pots of tail-grass seed porridge and the large basin of cold salad were consumed, the orcs finally lay down on the ground, feeling a bit more comfortable.

Lin Qiu and Lang Bing went to check on the sick orcs again; they had also eaten a little and regained some color.

Lin Qiu asked them one by one, and the orcs all nodded, saying they felt a bit better. Only then did he return to Lang Yan's side, lie down on the animal hide, and feel completely exhausted.

As he drifted off to sleep, Lin Qiu was still thinking about gathering herbs later, and how to arrange things afterward—whether they should travel at night and rest during the day...

He thought about it, and muttered about it under his breath.

Lang Yan's eyes softened. He touched Lin Qiu's flushed earlobe with his finger, fanned him gently, and said, "Sleep, we'll talk when you wake up."

With the orcs sick, Qiu and Lang Bing had been busier than anyone else these past two days.
chapters.source_text:
一大群白羽兽人飞掠蓝湖，悬停在湖面，振翅的声音低鸣，如滂沱大雨敲击湖面。
后山林子里声音急响，狼影和狼火带着兽人从山上一跃而下，仅有三十几个兽人，却如千军万马奔来。
他们个个兽形高大，爪垫落地收声，顷刻回到队伍中，防备地看着这群羽族。
白栖：“狼王。我们来交换。”
兽人们都注意到队伍里的那抹红，雀溪清脆叫了声，飞落下来，停在兔艾肩头。
他抻了抻翅膀，叽叽喳喳说了几句，兔艾点点头。
“雀溪说是来交换的。”兔艾道。
狼岩抬手示意兽人们把东西拿出来，不用再戒备。
白羽兽人们降落，把带来的东西放在湖岸，片刻，又有嗡鸣声传来，西岸的红羽兽人也涌了过来。
林楸看了眼在不远处梳理羽毛的兽人，仿佛到了某个自然景区。好多羽族！
白羽部落带来的东西有草药、兽皮还有他们收集起来的各种漂亮的珍珠贝壳，他们不仅要盐，也要交换狼部落的草药、陶器以及渔网。
负责交换的狼乔一边清点物资，一边安排兽人们给白羽兽人装东西。
不过草药和兽皮好换，那些装饰的东西……
“王？”
狼岩扫了一眼，道：“部落不统一交换，要是有兽人喜欢，可以自己单独换。”
“可他们没东西。”林楸道。
“一个兽人一勺盐的份额，用了就回去干活补上。”
兽人们一听，还是犹豫。
狼云见自己伴侣看了一眼白羽兽人手里的漂亮珍珠，又迅速收回目光，他往前一步正要开口，狼禾忽然拉住他的手。
“不是想要吗？”
狼禾轻轻摇头，低声道：“划不来，盐留着换食物。”
很多兽人跟狼禾想的一样，他们几年前还在饥饿中挣扎，现在依然有一股危机感，他们觉得珍珠这些东西，漂亮是漂亮，但如果用盐或者食物来换，那不如不换。
“只要你喜欢……”狼云对白羽兽人扬了扬下巴，“我换。”
林楸抱臂站在一旁，肩膀碰了碰狼岩，道：“瞧瞧，人家也是有优点的。”
“嗯，就是蠢了点。”
“人家伴侣在，护着呢，你可小点声吧。”
红角领着族人上前，先跟狼岩颔首示意，“红角，红羽部落族长，也是……白栖的伴侣。”
狼岩：“换什么？”
红角没想到他这么干脆，惊了一瞬，笑容真诚了几分。
“换盐。”
他刚一说完，狼云把换好的漂亮珍珠串交给自己伴侣，拉上一兜子东西过来推销，“我们的好东西不只盐，你瞧瞧，陶罐、陶锅、草药、渔网、火柴、蜡烛，都是你们这边没有的，要不？”
红角看了一眼面上冷淡、离他远远的白栖，道：“还是只要盐。”
“行吧。”
狼云往后一挥手，狼金几个拎着盐袋子上前。
两边根据红羽部落拿来的东西商定好交换盐的数量，换完，再互相开袋检查检查。
狼岩和林楸只在一旁盯着，免得兽人们弄错或者遗漏，边上两个羽族的族长看完交换过来的东西，往他俩这边过来。
“狼王。”红角又看向林楸，“狼王伴侣？”
“叫我楸就行。”
“楸。”红角看向一旁的白栖，伸手将他拉过来，“这是白栖。”
白栖看了红角一眼，抽出手来，缓缓走上前。
“你们的盐很好，不是海盐？”
“不是，我们自己的盐。”林楸笑道。
“以后还能交换？”
“可以。”
他们那盐洞就是个盐矿，兽人们往下挖，越挖越多。
“之前的事情……抱歉。”白栖垂眸，手指痉挛似地颤了颤，忽的，红角握住了她的手，白栖这次没有甩开。
白栖看向林楸和狼岩，只眼眶有一点红。
她诚恳道：“也谢谢你们，灭了黑熊部落。”
林楸：“我们也是为了救自己的幼崽，不过他确实死得挺惨的。”
白栖眼眸溢出泪水，却是笑着的。
她道：“交个朋友。白羽部落，白栖。”
林楸：“狼部落，林楸。”
红角余光时刻注意着自己伴侣，见她这副模样，唇轻颤着，却是一点一点笑了起来。
注意到狼岩的视线，他抬头看了回去，敛了笑，问道：“不知道狼部落在什么位置？”
“东北方向，最高的一座山后头。你们过去应该七八天就能到。”
红角点头，不再说话，只是手紧紧攥住白栖。
交换很快结束，兽人离开。
刚刚那先后两群过来的羽族兽人，此刻白的红的混在一起，不少都是一红一白，显然是一对。
看来族长态度影响部落关系啊！
林楸拍拍手，“行了，吃饭，吃完出发。”
这次交换的东西不少，他们一共带了八十袋的盐，前头只跟灰兔部落换了十三勺，差不多一袋出去。
这次两个大的羽族部落一共换出去十袋，还有昨晚零零散散换出去的两袋，一共换出去十三袋了。
渔网、陶这些带得少，就换出去那么一个两个，草药也换出去了一些。
至于换回来的东西，那就更多了。
他们从灰兔兽人那里换了二十六袋的黑豆，现在吃得还剩下二十一袋；
昨晚换了十袋果子和块根，十袋草药，还有八十张小兽皮二十来张大兽皮；
刚刚从两个羽族手里又换了六十袋的草药，四十筐肉干，三十筐的鱼干，还有些兽人们自己换的一些漂亮的饰品……
兽人们要背的东西非但没少，还多了许多。
好在都是些轻的，一个兽人匀一点，也能带。
今天在湖旁已经停留得够久，早饭过后，兽人们把火灭了，抓了一把草，把大铁锅搓洗得干干净净，然后挂在货物上绑好，便驮着继续赶路了。
羽猎招呼一声，就回去找羽涯他们几个。
从山谷出来，因为坡陡又没路，兽人们还带着重物，所以他们走了两天。羽涯他们飞过去，大半天时间就应该能到。
领队的狼火和狼影继续走了，队伍慢慢跟上。
林楸背着东西，跟狼岩一起缓缓沿着大湖往西边走。
这也是他们刚刚问过白羽兽人，对方表示可以从其领地内借道过去。
要是往南边走，兽人队伍还得绕上一大圈，才能继续往西南边走。
天上忽然一声清脆的啼叫，林楸仰头，便看见个白羽兽人在上空盘旋。
“他是领路的，跟着他走。”狼岩道。
前头狼火应声，寻着白羽兽人的方向沿着湖边北岸一直往西，爬上缓坡，翻过高崖，又步入低矮错落的群山。
天上的白羽兽人给他们领了两天的路，羽猎也和羽涯他们回来了，等离开白羽部落的边缘，天上的兽人又是一声鸣叫，便离开了。
林楸展开手中的地图，和雀溪一起商讨后面的路程，又将刚刚走过的地方一点一点在地图上补足。
风雨潇潇，路途漫漫，随着走过的地方越多，地图一角慢慢被填满。
转眼，已经出来三个月。
南边的雨季似乎要比狼山那边更难熬一些，一天之中总有一会儿在下雨。雨后又放晴，那阳光照在身上，如同烤红的烙铁贴来，烫得兽人们很是难熬。
随处落在地面的石块，被阳光晒过半天，兽人一不小心踩上去，烫得嗷呜一声，连带着背上的货物一起蹦起来。
到此时，兽人们才算走到了东部大陆的最边缘处，再往前，就是中央大陆的范围了。
但前行的队伍此刻停了下来，兽人们找了一个大山洞，收拾干净后，直接住在了里面。
他们这群从来没来过大陆最南端的兽人，此刻大部分身上起了疹子，还有几个体弱的，直接生病倒下了。
密林中虫鸣声声，湿气浓稠得仿佛堵住了兽人们的鼻孔，让大家难以呼吸。
方才下过雨，没片刻，阳光又穿过树缝投下来，照得林子里沾了雨水的叶片反光，很是晃眼。
树木摇曳，近山洞口，两株细窄的小树被一双手一把扒开。
林楸和狼冰背着藤筐钻出来，快步回到了山洞前。
山洞外的几棵树被兽人们砍了，洞口也搭了棚子，底下建了灶，放着铁锅和熬药的陶锅。
林楸和狼冰是队伍里会治病的兽人，刚刚他们出去找了一圈，倒是在林子里找到不少对症的草药。
林楸放下藤筐，撑着膝盖坐下。
他身上的衣服湿透了，高高扎起来的长发因为钻了林子，也变得凌乱不堪。碎发被汗水沾湿，贴在脸和脖子上，身上发痒又黏腻不堪，林楸眉头拧得死紧。
他旁边的狼冰也同样狼狈，身上起了红点子，也一身湿汗，头发上沾着枯树枝，衣服上挂着烂树叶，腿上蹭着已经变成褐色的树浆……
林楸抓过藤筐，翻找里面刚刚洗净的草药。
颈边微凉，一阵风袭来，林楸喟叹一声。
他看了眼旁边给他们扇风的兔艾，问道：“其他兽人呢？”
部落一行六十多个兽人，病了四个，另有三十多个兽人身上长疹子。
不仅是热的，也是因为他们在外行走这么久，没怎么好好休息，累出来的。
林楸和狼冰去找草药前，这些兽人还在山洞待着呢。
兔艾也热得晕眩，他把自己头发剪成了短发，坑坑洼洼的，不好看，但凉快。
“王带了一部分兽人出去捕猎了，影和黑羽兽人去看看周围有没有部落。”
一方水土养一方兽人，大伙儿病了，要是楸和冰不行，那当地的兽人应该有办法。
林楸热得心浮气躁的，他摆了摆手，“你自己扇风，我们赶紧把药弄出来。”
病得最重的兽人有四个，狼禾、狼溶、雀溪、狼云。
四个兽人里，三个是亚兽人。唯一一个雄兽人狼云又是被蛇咬了，不过这次不是他犯贱踩蛇尾巴，而是给自己伴侣狼禾挡了一下。
那蛇很毒，当时极其凶险，要不是林楸和狼冰反应快，他现在小命都没了。
狼禾可能也是被狼云吓到了，受了惊，第二天就病倒了。
剩下两个兽人……林楸和狼冰判断都是中暑，雀溪身体底子差，这一路上生了好几次病，狼溶也是疲劳加上高温，病倒也不奇怪。
最严重的就是他们四个，其他兽人虽没躺着起不来，但也病歪歪的，脸色不怎么好看。
狼冰给中暑的兽人配药，林楸便把给兽人治疗疹子的草药锤烂，再让兔艾端进去，让兽人们往身上抹。
这草药还是有作用的，抹在身上一股冰凉感，很舒服。
林楸给自己涂了点，又往狼冰身上抹。
狼冰捡药的动作不停，稍稍扬起下巴方便林楸动作，边道：“我发现这边有几种草药正是部落缺的，等会儿太阳落山，叫兽人去多找些回来。”
“可以。”
停在这儿每天都在消耗，不论是食物还是草药，他们得做一点补充。
林楸帮狼冰把草药抹完，洗干净手，又休息了会儿，才进山洞去看生病的兽人。
洞里放着个大陶罐，本来是他们带出来交换的，现在被他们用了。
罐子里装满了煮开的水，浸了解暑的草药，又放得温凉，兽人们要喝就取。
也幸亏这一路走来没喝生水，不然这会儿不知道还会出现什么样的问题。
山洞大，应该是曾经某个部落住的地方，他们整个队伍的兽人躺进来地方也够。
现在里面躺了十多个兽人。
一部分是晚上守了夜，现在在补觉，一部分就是病得迷迷糊糊的。
林楸往角落去。
狼云唇色发白，坐在狼禾身边，摇着扇子给他扇风。
林楸低声问：“你身上没什么问题吧？”
狼云摇摇头，汗珠从脸上掉落。
他是放血放多了，脸色才难看。
当时情况紧急，只能一边放血一边找解毒的。好在毒已经解了，养一养就行了。
林楸蹲下，探了探狼禾的额头，还是烫。
他又一一摸了狼照和雀溪，也跟狼禾一样。
山洞里，兔草和兔林守着他们，用水帮他们擦拭着身体降温，但效果一般。
先前兽人们晕倒的第一时间，狼冰就给他们喂了解暑的草药，也就好了一阵，不过一晚，这体温又升高了。
林楸在心里叹气。
只希望这次的草药有用。
其实兽人的病根本不会这么严重的，但这群兽人难受了不说，就这么耽搁了。
外面狼冰已经开始熬药了。
林楸看其他兽人已经把治疗疹子的草药涂抹上，整个成了绿色，他难得笑了下，示意兔林他们也给雀溪几个涂上一些。
雨季不好走，也不知道这一阵会耽搁到哪去。
这会儿时间不算早，快下午了。
其他兽人都不在，他们也还没吃午饭，林楸干脆弄了些尾巴草籽出来，打算做个粥，再把兽人们采集回来的野菜烫一烫，弄个凉拌菜。
天热，大伙儿都没胃口，他们这几天都这样吃的。
不过这样一来，尾巴草籽也消耗得快了些，如今还剩三袋。
山洞往东边走一里地，有一条河，兽人们用的水都是从这里取的。
河边的石头排列得整齐，明显是兽人从其他地方搬过来的。这足以证明，这地方曾经有个部落。只是不知道是迁徙了，还是灭亡了。
外面装水的陶罐没水了，林楸拿上个藤筐，拎上两个空陶罐去河边装水。
从山洞到河边，这里已经被兽人们踩出来一条路。
林楸装好两罐水，背一罐，抱一罐，缓缓站起。
方一抬头，他感受到正前方一道视线，汗根根竖起。
林楸往对面林子里一看，只瞧见一道黑影迅速掠过。
他想也不想，快速离开河边，几乎是跑回了山洞旁。
狼冰守在陶罐边，看着药。
看林楸急匆匆回来，神色警惕，他皱起眉头，站起来接过他手上的罐子道：“怎么了？”
“河对岸有兽人。”
林楸将背着的藤筐放下，里面水已经洒出来一半，他整个后背也打湿了。
“看清楚是什么兽人了吗？”
“没有。”
“这附近没有部落。”狼冰眼神有些冷。
他们带的东西多，这一路遇到部落也没遮掩可以交换东西的事，被盯上了也不奇怪。
林楸：“现在先别单独出去了，等王他们回来再说。”
“好。”狼冰道。
狼岩他们捕猎不会走太远，出事了这边嚎一声，那边应该能听见。林楸倒没那么怕，只是担心遇到了不怀好意的兽人，他们山洞里这些兽人状态不好，要是打起来，免不了受伤……
林楸看了看小河那边，压下心中的担忧。
他快速洗了锅，把陶罐里的水倒进去，开始烧水。
雨季在灶前做饭简直是折磨，火烘在身上，汗水根本止不住。
林楸被烤得面颊泛红，喉咙发干。等生好火，放进去的枯树枝也引燃了，他才退开两步，擦了擦脸上的汗。
“药好了吗？”
狼冰看了眼陶罐，同样顶着一张热红的脸道：“快了。”
林楸坐远了些，盯着灶火，拿着扇子时不时给狼冰扇一扇后背。
兽人们现在也习惯了下半身短裤，上半身短袖，都是麻布做的，透气，也能挡一些虫子。
天气热，狼冰麻花辫都不编了，就把长发在头上卷一卷，用一根打磨过的树枝随意一别，不跑不跳，头发就不会掉下来。
他那后背也没干过，后颈又是疹子又是汗，痒得他难受，一会儿没控制好就忍不住挠一挠，挠完就是几道红痕，现在看着惨不忍睹。
林楸给他抹的草药糊糊也混着汗掉了。
“也不知道南边这雨季持续多久……之后起码有四个月的日子，还是这样难熬。”
狼冰：“那叫兔艾他们往地下挖个洞，咱们就住在这里，等着天气凉快了，我们再走。”
林楸笑了声，擦了擦头上的汗，用力给狼冰扇了一下风。
“你想得倒挺美。”
“那不然怎么办……”
他们以往雨季都不怎么出来活动，就是捕猎也是晚上行动。
“不然，干脆也晚上赶路算了。”
林楸摇着扇子，思考这个可能性。
“不一定行，晚上看不见，不安全。”
“白天能安全到哪里去？”
“至少不用看见长虫就一脚踩上去吧。”
“那看见了不还是遭了。”
说的就是狼禾狼云两口子，他们看着是跟长虫过不去了。
“等王回来商量商量吧……”林楸无力笑了两声。他现在被烤得脑子转不动，心口有一团火似的，烧得他焦躁。
草药熬好，狼果倒出来放冷水里晾一晾，等没那么烫了，再倒出来分到三个碗里，送进山洞。
没一会儿，他再端着喝空了的碗出来，又往陶锅里加水，守着锅继续熬。
“你去休息会儿，我看着就行。”
“热，睡不着。”
“外面更热。”
“不去。”
林楸咬了咬牙，这小狼崽子，倔的时候跟头牛似的！
等到林楸那两锅尾巴草籽粥好了，下午已经过去一半。
他快速换了一口陶锅，加水，煮开后把一大筐野菜烫熟了，再捞起来放水里过一下，然后开始拌菜。
全部弄好，刚叫兽人们吃饭，便听到天上有拍动翅膀的声音。
狼影、羽猎还有出去捕猎的狼岩他们都回来了。
部落少的地方野兽有成长空间，这里的猎物数量比有部落的地方稍稍多一些。
他们带回来两头猎物，是南边才有的兽类，已经处理过了，晚上可以直接煮了就吃。
兽人们回到山洞，直接瘫软下来。
罐子里放了解暑草药的水大伙儿也不嫌弃了，喝得一干二净。
林楸见狼岩也回来了，端了粥去他身边坐着。
刚一坐下，就感觉一股热气冲过来，他俩还没挨着，林楸就觉得热了。
再一看狼岩，他裸露的上半身全是汗，大滴大滴的汗水顺着起伏的肌肉往下掉，整个兽人身上发烫。
林楸把碗给他，把外面晾着的帕子拿进来，让他擦汗。
“跑哪儿去了？”
“南边。这边快到海边了。”
“遇到部落了吗？”
狼岩摇了摇头。
狼影他们是专门出去找部落的，闻言看向林楸这边，声音疲惫道：“这边没有部落。”
他和黑羽兽人们把附近这一圈转完了，都没看到部落。
林楸看了一眼喝完草药睡熟的兽人，放低了声音，道：“没遇到没事，冰的草药有效果。”
“嗯，快吃吧。”狼岩垂眸望着林楸瘦了不少的脸颊，有些心疼。
林楸：“这碗给你，我去盛……”
“不用。”狼岩握住林楸的手，“你吃，我现在没胃口。”
林楸慢慢吃着，想起刚刚在河边看到的黑影，又给狼岩提了一句。
狼岩把擦完汗的帕子拿出去洗了，挂在树枝上晾好，又拿了扇子进来，坐在林楸身边一边扇风一边问：“看清楚是什么兽人了吗？”
“没有。”
“别担心，我等会儿去看看。”
林楸：“好。”
有狼岩扇着风，林楸好受了些，他几下吃完粥，然后接过扇子，换狼岩去吃。
等到两大锅的尾巴草籽粥和一大盆的凉拌野菜消耗完，兽人们才安安稳稳躺在地上，舒坦了一些。
林楸和狼冰又去检查了一下生病的兽人，他们刚刚也跟着吃了点东西，恢复了几分气色。
林楸挨个问了问，兽人都点头说好受了些，他才放心地回到狼岩身边，往兽皮上一躺，浑身疲惫。
迷迷糊糊闭上眼睛时，林楸还惦记着等会儿采集草药的事，还有之后怎么安排，要不要晚上赶路白天休息……
他想着，嘴上也嘀嘀咕咕说着。
狼岩眸色放软，手指碰了碰林楸的泛红的耳垂，轻轻摇着扇子，道：“睡吧，睡醒了再说。”
兽人生病，这两天楸和狼冰比他们还忙。

“楸、楸！你快醒醒……楸！”
林楸倏地睁眼，直挺挺坐起来。他眼神刚聚焦，就看到狼冰满脸焦急的样子。
“怎么了？”
“溶他们又热起来了！”
林楸立马爬起来，便听到一声呕吐声。兽人们急得团团转，围着狼溶几个，又不知道该做什么。
看到林楸醒了，眼睛绯红地看过来，可怜又无助。
林楸唇角绷紧，快速道：“先前那草药不是起作用了？”
“是起了，可他们身上的热刚压下去没多久，又起来了。我刚刚还打算喂第二次，他们就吐了。”
林楸看到那群围着病患的兽人，忙道：“你们离远一点，别靠近他们。”
“楸……”狼云抱着自己伴侣，快哭出来了。
林楸：“再熬一次，试着灌进去。”
兔艾走上前来，“楸，我们去熬药。”
“行，快些。”
草药降温不行，只能物理降温。
林楸让兔林和兔草继续给兽人擦身体，又直接拉开狼云，跪坐到狼禾身边，道：“冰，看着。”
他用水沾湿兽人后颈，手臂，直接给兽人刮痧。
情况紧急，各种方法都试一下，先看看有没有用。
狼冰虽然不解，但仔细盯着，看了一会儿他就蹲到狼溶身边，也跟着弄起来。
此刻，狼岩站在一旁，把其他兽人挡在身后。他目光沉冷，思索着让黑羽兽人带上他们返程的可能性。
他们到这里之前，往前面五天的路程大概有一个小部落，但那个部落没有祭司，他不确定去这一趟有没有用。
再往前……
“猎，你往前看看，有没有能治病的部落。”
“行。”羽猎立马行动。
同时，林楸一边刮痧一边想，兽人身体滚烫，这高热反反复复，这情况已经不太像他所了解的中暑了。
可他们一路走来，又没出现过其他问题。
他们带来的草药没用，上午出去找的草药效果不大，林楸咬咬牙，听着狼禾迷迷糊糊地呼疼，想要抽手躲避，手攥得他紧紧的。
狼云在一旁绷着下颌不敢出声，眼睁睁看着狼禾身上颈侧和手肘内侧被林楸刮出来大片大片的淤血。
等到出了痧，兽人危急的症状好像缓了一点。
但这样还是不行。
“冰，你守着，我出去找找还有没有其他草药。”
狼部落缺了不少南边的草药，他们在林子里见到了些，但没找全，林楸心里默念着几味药材，拎起藤筐就往外走。
狼岩道：“影，你看着点。乔，你带十个兽人跟我们一起出去找。”
狼影曲腿靠墙坐着，闻言点了下头。
他目光看着狼禾，忍不住捏紧了手。
狼冰是老祭司培养了多年的兽人，已经可以担起祭司的职责了，要是他都没办法，那这几个兽人……
狼影敛下睫，不敢继续往下想。
洞外，林楸疾步走出去，一边走一边想，他学艺不算精，只能给狼冰打下手。但好歹也学了点，关于中暑的常识也是知道的。
按理说，第一次喂了药兽人温度降下来就该好了，可后头两次反复，他越想越觉得不对劲。
“王，这几天狼溶他们有没有什么遇到什么特殊的事，或者有什么特殊的表现？”
狼岩细想了下，道：“我没有发现，跟他们离得近的兽人也没发现什么。”
西边他们去过了，得去东边找。林楸走到小河边，忽然停下来。
他直直看着小河对面，那边林子更深，昏暗的树丛间仿佛有视线往这边看来。
不待林楸细看，瞬间，狼岩追了上去。
狼乔让十个兽人分两队，分别包抄。
林楸跟着钻入林子，跑了一段，想起来他还有要紧的事。
“王，你们追，我找草药。”
山洞里还有兽人等着，不能耽搁。
“仔细点，遇到危险就躲。”
“好。”
几乎是狼岩消失在林间的下一瞬，林楸转头就看到了一个兽人。
他藏在林子深处，从始至终没有动过，仿佛与树木融为了一体，连气息都隐藏了。
“楸？”
林楸瞳孔一缩，拔腿就跑。
兽人一笑，林楸跑没两步，衣服被拉住，嘴巴也顺带被堵住。
“小狼崽子，跑什么，不是想救兽人吗？”
林楸反手脱了藤筐砸过去，兽人侧头，捏着林楸手腕，“救不救？不救我走了。”
林楸被他捏住两只手，嘴巴也被堵住。
离得近，林楸看清了他的模样。
居然是个……狼兽人。
林楸呼吸慢慢缓和下来，紧盯着面前这个兽人。
不知道为什么，这个兽人给他的感觉就像狼晚他们给他的感觉一样。
“这才乖。”兽人松手，像不怕他喊似的，顺手还搓了一把林楸脑袋。
他把身后的兽皮兜取下来，塞进林楸背篓，“你跟另一个小狼崽子摘的那草药不对症，他们是被这边特有的一种虫咬了，就这个。”
兽人抬起手掌，示意他看。
林楸见那团成一团的软体虫子，忙往后退了退，也顺势躲开兽人的攻击范围。
“呵……”兽人唇角微勾，“你们是要迁徙？”
林楸抿唇不语。
“别往中央大陆去，那边很乱，要是迁徙的话，往东部大陆北边走，去狼部落。”
几乎是他话落的一瞬，林楸脑子里闪过那些此刻定居在狼部落周围的小部落。
他死死盯着兽人的脸，“你……”
“走了，记住了，别往西边走，危险。”
兽人转身就消失在了林子里。
林楸想起还生病的兽人，顾不得追，他迅速打开兽人给的兽皮兜，里面躺着正新鲜的草药。
看那根上的泥，也就是今天采的。
兽人多半是看到他们采了草药后，再去找的这个。
林楸把草药记下来，又迅速找了一些，等到狼岩回来，他闻到浓重的血腥味，还没开口，狼岩道：“没事，找草药吧。”
“找到了。”
“那就回去。”
快步回去的路上，林楸发现了自己想的那几味草药，他顺带摘了，一边跑一边跟狼岩道：“我刚刚看到了一个狼兽人。”
“嗯。”
“你不意外？”
“我们遇到了一队原野部落的兽人。”
林楸紧紧抓住狼岩的手，“你们没事吧。”
“没事。应该是原野部落的兽人追捕另一个兽人部落，恰好被我们遇上了。”
这里靠近中央大陆，原野部落做这样的事已经很熟练了，遇到了也不奇怪。
“他们会跟来吗？”
“杀完了。”
狼岩追过去的时候，那一窝原野兽人看见他们就动手，他们也只好还手。
不过引他们过去的兽人却是跑得快，要不是树上有血腥味，他们都还没发现他从哪里跑的。
林楸：“那刚刚那个兽人给的草药能用吗？他说兽人是被虫子咬的。”
“试试，他们引我们去解决那群原野部落的兽人，给我们治疗兽人的草药，算是交换。”
情况紧急，确认手中的草药吃了也毒不死，狼冰就给兽人们煮了喂了。
以防万一，狼冰又把林楸采集回来的另外几味能退热的草药也熬了。
草药起作用的速度很快，只半个小时，兽人们发红的脸就恢复了原来的颜色。
林楸和狼冰反复检查了他们的身体，询问之后，确认他们被兽人所说的那种虫子咬过，林楸和狼冰才软了身体，一下坐在地上。
果然是因为这个。
谢天谢地，总算好了。
“呜……”
林楸眼皮一跳，还以为又出什么事了。他抬头一看，狼云正抱着他伴侣，脑袋埋在人家肩上，那哭哭啼啼的样子，看得林楸脑仁疼。
“什么出息！”狼冰道。
“你懂个屁！”狼云轻轻护着狼禾，细细用打湿的帕子擦了擦他的脖子和脸颊，现在手都还在哆嗦。
刚刚那一出可把他吓得不轻。
林楸脑子涨涨的，又一身的汗。
他揉了揉脑袋，呆坐了半晌，才有心思去想刚刚遇到的事。
“王。”林楸看向从洞外拎着陶罐进来的狼岩，“刚刚那个兽人是狼兽人。”
“我知道。”
他的伴侣说过，但好像忙得头昏脑涨，已经忘记了。
狼岩倒了一碗水过来，递给林楸。
“我不渴。”林楸道。
“喝点。”狼岩端着碗凑到他唇边。
干燥的唇沾到水，渴意瞬间涌上来，林楸双手托着碗边，一口气喝了半碗。
哪里是不渴，是根本还没回过神来。
狼岩把剩下的水喝完，放了碗，曲腿坐在他身边。
林楸继续说：“他以为我们也是正在迁徙的部落，还让我们往狼山走。”
“去我们自己部落？”狼乔坐过来，好奇道。
他们当时被兽人故意引到北边去，没跑多远就跟一群原野部落的羽族对上，直接打了起来。
打完了，才发现引他们过去兽人早已经不见。但那个兽人多半也受伤了，他走过的树枝上残留着血痕。
他们担心楸，打完了又赶着回去，也没看到他说的什么狼兽人。但狼乔清楚的是，引诱他们过去的那个兽人，不是狼兽人。
据此推断，那应该是一个各种族兽人混杂的部落，不是纯粹的狼部落。
“他有没有说他叫什么？”
“他长什么样？”狼火和狼影也坐过来，满眼探究。
林楸：“不知道叫什么，是个中年雄兽人。白发，黑瞳，比我高上半个头，气质很温和。他身上有草药的味道，可能是个祭司。”
狼兽人们脑子里过了一遍，纷纷摇头。
“以前跟我们打过交道的狼祭司，没有一个是白发黑瞳的。”
要不就是白发蓝瞳，要不就是黑发黑瞳，还有红发红瞳的，反正就是没有楸说的这种。
除了兽人年老，头发会变白，一般来说发色就是毛色。
那兽人只是中年兽人，这个年纪的白狼祭司……多半是北部大陆的。
可又一想，不对、不对……
北部大陆的祭司怎么会跑东部大陆南边来？这迁徙迁得也太远了吧，横跨大陆南北，比他们还能跑。
狼火：“他对这边很熟悉？”
林楸：“看着是很熟悉。救狼溶他们的草药就是他给的。”
狼金挪了挪，也凑过来，围了一圈。
“他就没说他是哪个部落的？”
“没有。”林楸倒是想问，可他跑得飞快。林楸当时顾忌着部落的兽人，也没追。
“肯定在附近，要不我们现在去找找？”狼金一拍大腿，提议道。他兴致勃勃，看起来不热了，也不累了。
狼火抬手给了他一个脑瓜崩。
狼金龇牙，“那你们说，怎么着？”
一个清楚他们部落位置，却不认识他们的狼兽人，一个四处在南边散布谣言，说他们部落能养活兽人的狼兽人……
狼金只要一想想，就爪子痒痒。
“羽猎呢？”狼岩问。
“还没回来。”狼火道。
“羽涯。”
“嗷！”
“你带几个黑羽兽人去找羽猎，先让他不找部落了，悄悄搜一下这附近，看看还有没有原野部落的兽人，发现其他兽人踪迹也立马回来告知。”
“是！”
兽人应该藏得很深。
他们之前留在这山洞时，羽猎他们检查过附近都没看到什么兽人，现在却钻出来一个原野部落的队伍，还可能存在一个陌生的兽人部落，得细细搜查一遍。
他们应该还要在这里停留两天，等狼溶几个彻底好了，他们才会继续走，安全为重。
狼岩把事情安排下去，兽人们也能安心准备晚饭了。
天热，肉不能久放。
林楸把两副内脏直接煮成了一锅兽杂汤，再和着兽人们找回来的块根清炖一锅肉，弄个凉拌野菜就齐全了。
菜做好，兽人们端着自己的碗来分。
林楸站到离灶远一点的地方去，身体靠着树干，狼岩站在他旁边，给他扇扇子。
吹在脸上的风是热的，林楸脑门上的汗一刻不歇地顺着脸颊和脖子流下来。好在稍稍没了憋闷感，林楸发胀的脑子也好受些。
林子里小虫一闪一闪地亮灯了，羽猎他们还没回来。
林楸休息了会儿，缓和过来，他看向狼岩道：“接下来就进入中央大陆了……那个兽人让我们不要去，说那边危险。”
“听他那意思，那边应该有不少原野部落的兽人活跃着。”
“嗯，只能小心一点。”
最好是把说这话的兽人找出来，问问那边的情况，也好做个准备。
但显然，这要让狼岩失望了。
羽猎回来的时候是半夜，林楸和狼岩根本没睡。
看到他那瞬间，林楸先清点了下黑羽兽人的数量，发现一个没少，才放下心来。
“岩，我们没看见其他兽人。”几个黑羽兽人抱着碗，一边吃一边道。
“一点踪迹都没发现？”
“只在东边发现了你们弄死原野部落兽人的地方，另一个部落兽人的踪迹很浅，我们顺着痕迹找了找，最后直接找不见了。”
“他们确实很会隐藏。”
连狼岩都没注意到那个藏起来等着林楸落单的狼兽人。更别说那个在高树上如履平地的兽人。
“辛苦了，这几天麻烦你们多注意一点。吃完赶紧去休息吧，也累了。”
羽猎点头，带着一串黑羽兽人蹲角落里吃晚饭去了。
部落里的兽人好了，这是好事。但那虫子太毒，按照那狼兽人的说法，在这边被那虫子咬是常事儿，所以这草药还得多备些。
加上狼冰想多采集一些这边的草药，兽人们养病的这两天，其他兽人便分出来一些，跟着林楸和狼冰出去采集。
羽猎带着羽涯他们负责这几天的巡逻，确保兽人安全。狼乔负责带队捕猎采集，狼岩则和狼影几个，继续寻找那个狼兽人的踪迹。
好不容易遇到一个清楚这边情况的兽人，狼岩还真不想错过。
两天后。
山洞外，棚子边。
林楸站在垒砌的石头上，一手扶着棚子的柱子，一手牵拉着兽皮一角，指挥着棚顶上忙活的兔艾。
棚顶上被林楸铺上了兽皮，上面顺带晒着他们这两天采集回来的各种草药。
暑气重，草药两天就能晒得一捏就碎。
今早上才采集回来的草药，晒到这会儿天快黑了，也干得差不多了。
林楸这会儿在收草药和兽皮了，草药摊晒在棚顶的兽皮上，他把兔艾放上去，让他帮忙取一下。
林楸正忙着，外出的兽人也回来了。
狼冰又和年轻狼兽人们带回来不少草药，回来之后，他也顾不得休息，让大家赶紧拉了几张兽皮出来，把草药倒在上面摊开。
今晚就得走了，草药能摊一会儿是一会儿，免得太湿，到时候堆在一起容易捂着了。
打猎采集回来的兽人们去休息了，留在山洞里的狼溶几个出来，开始做饭。
他们休息了两天，草药也吃了两天，现在看着活蹦乱跳的，林楸也不怎么担心了。
他走了会儿神，兔艾已经把兽皮草药卷推到他手边了。
林楸抓着兽皮草药卷，往后注意着脚下，哪知道一低头就碰到狼岩额头，撞出一声闷响。
他还没叫疼，堵在他身后的狼岩先嘶了一声。
林楸没好气地抱着兽皮卷往他手上一塞，回过身去，再让兔艾把其他兽皮卷拖过来。
狼岩把裹着草药的兽皮放下，两手落在林楸腰侧。那宽松又轻薄的衣服被他收拢，一下显出了林楸的身形，腰窄而韧，往下是漂亮的弧度，腿……
腿上一疼——
狼岩无奈松开一只手，看了眼腿上的脚印。
“石头不稳，我护着你，别摔了。”
林楸裹着兽皮卷又往他怀里一放，抖了抖衣服道：“不知道热？”
狼岩额头抵着林楸后颈，“火气好大。”
“别捣乱。”林楸手指戳着他肩膀，把他弄远一点。天气热，狼岩体温又高，他不喜欢靠得太近。
等到棚子上的草药全被收下来，林楸拎着大灰兔子，把兔艾放了下来。
兔艾搓了搓长耳朵，然后叼上他的短裤，蹦蹦跳跳钻入林子，换成了人形出来。
林楸见狼岩还杵在自己身后，抓起一旁放着的扇子，重重扇了两下，扇得头发胡乱飞舞。
狼岩瞧着林楸脸颊泛红，手背贴了贴，林楸用扇子抵着他的手，手掌往他胸口上一摸，一手的汗。
林楸：“去洗澡，等会儿吃过晚饭休息一会儿我们就出发了。”
今晚上走也是兽人们商量出来的。
白天着实热，兽人们背着重物，稍稍走几步就是汗。喝的水还没流的汗多，时间长了容易脱水中暑。
大伙儿思虑再三，还是决定晚上走。
“一起？”
林楸一扇子扇在狼岩面前，转身往山洞走。
狼岩停在原地，垂下眼，叹息一声。
谁能想到，以前怎么靠近都不会拒绝的伴侣，现在都开始嫌弃他了。
“愣着干什么，走啊。”
狼岩抬眼，便见林楸拿了帕子和他俩的衣服出来。狼岩唇角一勾，亦步亦趋跟在林楸身后。
晚上要出发了，兽人们都在忙着收拾东西，收拾自己。
刚刚回来的兽人还在休息，还没有兽人往河边去。林楸到了地方，下意识先往林子里看了看，耳边传来狼岩踩水的声音，林楸收回目光，就看他站在水中，对自己伸手。
林楸把衣服帕子放在岸边，抓着他手慢慢下去。
小河水不算浅，踩着底下铺了石板的地方，水深能到腰间。
河水沁凉，林楸往里一坐，舒坦得喟叹一声。
狼岩靠过去，圈着伴侣腰肢，心满意足地将他搂抱在怀里。
楸好久都不让他抱着睡觉了。
“你们还是没找到那个狼兽人？”
“没有。不过发现他们踪迹了。”
“在哪儿？”
“往西边去了。”狼岩解了林楸绑头发的布条，看着长发散落下来，铺了满背，常年藏在衣服底下的肌肤在黑发的映衬下，更是莹润白皙。
狼岩看着看着，鼻尖顺着林楸颈侧，一点一点蹭到他肩上。
林楸揪了一把他的脸，手藏在水下，“不许乱来。”
狼岩一颤，肌肉一瞬间绷紧，显出流畅而健硕的轮廓。他张嘴咬住林楸的肩，下口轻轻的，又忍不住继续咬，想要用力将他吞入口中。
林楸手抵着他下巴，沾了水的修长手指压在他唇上，眼尾有些红。
“别磨蹭，事情多着呢。”
狼岩低声一笑，大掌托着林楸后颈，深深地吻了上去。
不磨蹭，他快一点就是了。
chapters.translated_text:
"Qiu, Qiu! Wake up... Qiu!"

Lin Qiu opened his eyes abruptly and sat bolt upright. As his vision focused, he saw Lang Bing’s face filled with anxiety.

"What’s wrong?"

"Rong and the others are running hot again!"

Lin Qiu scrambled up immediately, just in time to hear a retching sound. The beastmen were pacing back and forth in a panic, surrounding Lang Rong and the others, not knowing what to do.

Seeing Lin Qiu wake up, they looked over with crimson eyes, appearing pitiful and helpless.

Lin Qiu’s lips tightened, and he asked quickly, "Didn't the herbal medicine work earlier?"

"It did, but their fever only stayed down for a little while before spiking again. I was just about to feed them a second dose when they threw it up."

Lin Qiu looked at the group of beastmen surrounding the patients and hurriedly said, "Move back, don't get too close to them."

"Qiu..." Lang Yun was holding his mate, on the verge of tears.

Lin Qiu: "Brew another batch, try to force it down."

Tu Ai stepped forward, "Qiu, we’ll go brew the medicine."

"Okay, hurry."

Herbal medicine wasn't enough; they needed physical cooling as well.

Lin Qiu told Tu Lin and Tu Cao to continue wiping down the beastmen, then pulled Lang Yun aside, knelt beside Lang He, and said, "Bing, watch closely."

He dampened the beastman’s neck and arms with water and began to perform gua sha directly on him.

The situation was critical; they had to try every method to see if anything worked.

Although Lang Bing didn't understand, he watched carefully. After a while, he crouched down beside Lang Rong and started doing the same.

Meanwhile, Lang Yan stood to the side, blocking the other beastmen behind him. His gaze was cold and grim as he considered the possibility of having the Black Feather beastmen escort them back.

Before they arrived here, there was a small tribe about five days' journey back, but that tribe had no priest, and he wasn't sure if going there would be of any use.

Further ahead...

"Lie, go ahead and see if there are any tribes that can treat illnesses."

"Understood." Yu Lie immediately took action.

At the same time, as Lin Qiu performed the gua sha, he thought that the beastmen’s bodies were burning hot, and this recurring high fever didn't look like the heatstroke he was familiar with.

Yet, they hadn't encountered any other issues along their journey.

The herbs they brought were useless, and the ones they found this morning had little effect. Lin Qiu gritted his teeth, listening to Lang He mumble in pain, trying to pull his hand away, but the beastman gripped him tightly.

Lang Yun stood by with a clenched jaw, not daring to make a sound, watching as Lin Qiu scraped large patches of dark blood out from the sides of Lang He’s neck and the insides of his elbows.

Once the "sha" (bruising) appeared, the beastman’s critical symptoms seemed to ease slightly.

But this still wasn't enough.

"Bing, you keep watch. I’m going out to see if I can find other herbs."

The Wolf Tribe was missing many herbs from the south. They had seen some in the forest but hadn't found them all. Lin Qiu silently recited the names of a few medicinal plants, picked up his rattan basket, and headed out.

Lang Yan said, "Ying, keep an eye on things. Qiao, take ten beastmen and go with us to search."

Lang Ying sat leaning against the wall with his legs bent and nodded at the words.

He looked at Lang He, unable to stop himself from clenching his hands.

Lang Bing was a beastman trained by the old priest for many years and was already capable of taking on the duties of a priest. If even he couldn't handle this, then these beastmen...

Lang Ying lowered his lashes, not daring to think any further.

Outside the cave, Lin Qiu walked briskly, thinking that his skills weren't refined enough and he could only assist Lang Bing. But he had learned a little, and he knew the basics of heatstroke.

Logically, the fever should have subsided after the first dose of medicine, but the two recurrences made him feel that something was wrong.

"King, have Lang Rong and the others encountered anything unusual these past few days, or shown any strange symptoms?"

Lang Yan thought carefully and said, "I haven't noticed anything, and the beastmen close to them haven't either."

They had already been to the west, so they had to search to the east. Lin Qiu walked to the small river and suddenly stopped.

He stared straight across the river. The forest there was deeper, and it felt as if eyes were watching from the dim thickets.

Before Lin Qiu could look closely, Lang Yan caught up in an instant.

Lang Qiao signaled the ten beastmen to split into two teams and flank the area.

Lin Qiu followed them into the forest, ran for a bit, and remembered he had urgent business.

"King, you go ahead and chase, I’ll look for herbs."

There were still beastmen waiting in the cave; they couldn't delay.

"Be careful. If you encounter danger, hide."

"Okay."

Almost the moment Lang Yan disappeared into the woods, Lin Qiu turned his head and saw a beastman.

He was hiding deep in the forest, having not moved from the start, as if he had merged with the trees, hiding even his scent.

"Qiu?"

Lin Qiu’s pupils shrank, and he turned to run.

The beastman chuckled. Before Lin Qiu could take two steps, his clothes were grabbed, and his mouth was covered.

"Little wolf cub, why are you running? Don't you want to save your beastmen?"

Lin Qiu backhanded his rattan basket at him. The beastman tilted his head and grabbed Lin Qiu’s wrist, "Are you saving them or not? If not, I’m leaving."

Lin Qiu was held by both hands, his mouth still covered.

Being this close, Lin Qiu could see his appearance clearly.

He was actually a... wolf beastman.

Lin Qiu’s breathing slowly calmed down as he stared intently at the beastman in front of him.

For some reason, this beastman gave him the same feeling that Lang Wan and the others did.

"That’s better." The beastman let go, as if not afraid that he would shout, and even ruffled Lin Qiu’s hair.

He took off the animal skin pouch from his back and stuffed it into Lin Qiu’s basket, "The herbs you and the other little wolf cub picked are not the right cure. They were bitten by a bug unique to this area. It’s this one."

The beastman raised his palm to show him.

Seeing the ball of soft insects, Lin Qiu hurriedly stepped back, taking the opportunity to move out of the beastman’s attack range.

"Heh..." The beastman’s lips curled, "Are you planning to migrate?"

Lin Qiu pursed his lips and said nothing.

"Don't go toward the Central Continent; it’s very chaotic there. If you’re migrating, go to the north of the Eastern Continent, to the Wolf Tribe."

Almost the moment he finished speaking, images of the small tribes currently settled around the Wolf Tribe flashed through Lin Qiu’s mind.

He stared fixedly at the beastman’s face, "You..."

"I’m off. Remember, don't go west; it’s dangerous."

The beastman turned and disappeared into the forest.

Lin Qiu remembered the sick beastmen and couldn't afford to chase him. He quickly opened the pouch the beastman had given him, which contained fresh herbs.

Looking at the mud on the roots, they had clearly been picked today.

The beastman must have seen them picking herbs and then went to find these.

Lin Qiu memorized the herbs and quickly found a few more. When Lang Yan returned, he smelled a heavy scent of blood. Before he could speak, Lang Yan said, "It’s fine, let’s find the herbs."

"I found them."

"Then let’s go back."

On the way back, Lin Qiu found the herbs he had been thinking of. He picked them along the way and said to Lang Yan while running, "I just saw a wolf beastman."

"Hmm."

"You’re not surprised?"

"We ran into a group of Wild Tribe beastmen."

Lin Qiu grabbed Lang Yan’s hand tightly, "Are you all okay?"

"We’re fine. It seems the Wild Tribe beastmen were hunting another tribe of beastmen, and we just happened to run into them."

This area was close to the Central Continent, and the Wild Tribe was skilled at such things, so it wasn't strange to encounter them.

"Will they follow us?"

"They’ve been killed."

When Lang Yan chased after them, that group of Wild Tribe beastmen attacked as soon as they saw them, so they had no choice but to fight back.

However, the beastman who lured them there ran fast. If it weren't for the scent of blood on the trees, they wouldn't have even known where he had run off to.

Lin Qiu: "Then can the herbs that beastman gave us be used? He said the beastmen were bitten by bugs."

"Try it. They led us to deal with those Wild Tribe beastmen, and they gave us herbs to treat our beastmen; it counts as an exchange."

The situation was urgent, and after confirming that the herbs wouldn't be poisonous if eaten, Lang Bing boiled them and fed them to the beastmen.

Just in case, Lang Bing also brewed the other fever-reducing herbs Lin Qiu had collected.

The herbs worked quickly. In just half an hour, the flushed faces of the beastmen returned to their original color.

Lin Qiu and Lang Bing checked their bodies repeatedly. After asking, they confirmed they had been bitten by the type of bug the beastman mentioned. Only then did Lin Qiu and Lang Bing’s bodies go limp, and they sat down on the ground.

It really was because of that.

Thank heavens, they were finally better.

"Wuu..."

Lin Qiu’s eyelid twitched, thinking something else had happened. He looked up and saw Lang Yun holding his mate, his head buried in the other’s shoulder. The sobbing sight made Lin Qiu’s head ache.

"What a disgrace!" Lang Bing said.

"What do you know!" Lang Yun gently protected Lang He, carefully wiping his neck and cheeks with a damp cloth, his hands still trembling.

What just happened had scared him out of his wits.

Lin Qiu’s head felt heavy, and he was covered in sweat.

He rubbed his head and sat blankly for a long time before he had the energy to think about what had just happened.

"King." Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan, who was carrying a clay pot in from outside the cave, "The beastman from earlier was a wolf beastman."

"I know."

His mate had said so, but he seemed so dizzy and exhausted that he had already forgotten.

Lang Yan poured a bowl of water and handed it to Lin Qiu.

"I’m not thirsty," Lin Qiu said.

"Drink some." Lang Yan held the bowl to his lips.

As his dry lips touched the water, thirst surged up instantly. Lin Qiu held the bowl with both hands and drank half of it in one breath.

He wasn't "not thirsty"; he just hadn't regained his senses yet.

Lang Yan drank the rest of the water, put the bowl down, and sat beside him with his legs bent.

Lin Qiu continued, "He thought we were also a tribe in the middle of migrating and even told us to go to Wolf Mountain."

"To our own tribe?" Lang Qiao sat over, curious.

They had been intentionally lured to the north by that beastman, and not long after, they ran into a group of Feather Tribe beastmen from the Wild Tribe and started fighting.

After the fight, they realized the beastman who lured them there was already gone. But that beastman was likely injured; there were bloodstains on the branches he had passed.

They were worried about Qiu and rushed back after the fight, so they didn't see the wolf beastman he spoke of. But Lang Qiao was certain that the beastman who lured them there was not a wolf beastman.

Based on this, it must have been a tribe with mixed beastmen, not a pure Wolf Tribe.

"Did he say what his name was?"

"What did he look like?" Lang Huo and Lang Ying also sat over, their eyes full of inquiry.

Lin Qiu: "I don't know his name. He was a middle-aged male beastman. White hair, black eyes, half a head taller than me, and his temperament was very gentle. He smelled of herbs; he might be a priest."

The wolf beastmen went through their memories and shook their heads one after another.

"None of the wolf priests we’ve dealt with before had white hair and black eyes."

They were either white-haired with blue eyes, black-haired with black eyes, or red-haired with red eyes; there was just no one like what Qiu described.

Except for when a beastman grew old and their hair turned white, generally, hair color matched fur color.

That beastman was only middle-aged. A white-wolf priest of that age... was likely from the Northern Continent.

But then, thinking about it, no, no...

How could a priest from the Northern Continent come to the south of the Eastern Continent? This migration was too far, spanning the north and south of the continent; they could run further than even they could.

Lang Huo: "Is he very familiar with this area?"

Lin Qiu: "He seemed very familiar. The herbs that saved Lang Rong and the others were given by him."

Lang Jin shifted over, and they formed a circle.

"Did he say which tribe he was from?"

"No." Lin Qiu had wanted to ask, but he ran away too fast. Lin Qiu was worried about the beastmen in the tribe at the time, so he didn't chase him.

"He must be nearby. Should we go look for him now?" Lang Jin slapped his thigh and suggested. He was full of excitement, looking neither hot nor tired anymore.

Lang Huo raised his hand and flicked him on the forehead.

Lang Jin winced, "Then what do you suggest?"

A wolf beastman who knew their tribe’s location but didn't recognize them, a wolf beastman who was spreading rumors in the south that their tribe could provide for beastmen...

Just thinking about it made Lang Jin’s claws itch.

"Where is Yu Lie?" Lang Yan asked.

"Not back yet," Lang Huo said.

"Yu Ya."

"Awooo!"

"Take a few Black Feather beastmen and go find Yu Lie. Tell him to stop looking for tribes for now and quietly search the area to see if there are any more Wild Tribe beastmen. If you find traces of other beastmen, come back and tell us immediately."

"Yes!"

The beastmen must be hiding very deeply.

When they first stayed in this cave, Yu Lie and the others had checked the surroundings and hadn't seen any beastmen, but now a Wild Tribe team had popped up, and there might be a mysterious beastman tribe, so they had to search carefully.

They were likely to stay here for another two days. They wouldn't continue their journey until Lang Rong and the others were completely better; safety was the priority.

Lang Yan arranged the tasks, and the beastmen could finally prepare dinner with peace of mind.

It was hot, and meat couldn't be kept for long.

Lin Qiu boiled the two sets of offal into a soup, stewed some meat with the tubers the beastmen had brought back, and made a cold-dressed wild vegetable dish to complete the meal.

Once the food was ready, the beastmen brought their own bowls to be served.

Lin Qiu stood further away from the stove, leaning against a tree trunk, while Lang Yan stood beside him, fanning him.

The wind blowing on his face was hot, and the sweat on Lin Qiu’s forehead flowed down his cheeks and neck without stopping. Fortunately, the feeling of suffocation had eased slightly, and his throbbing head felt a bit better.

Small bugs in the forest were blinking like little lights, and Yu Lie and the others still hadn't returned.

After resting for a while and feeling better, Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan and said, "We’re entering the Central Continent next... that beastman told us not to go, saying it’s dangerous there."

"From what he said, there should be many Wild Tribe beastmen active there."

"Hmm, we just have to be careful."

It would be best to find the beastman who said that and ask about the situation there so they could be prepared.

But clearly, this would disappoint Lang Yan.

Yu Lie returned in the middle of the night, and Lin Qiu and Lang Yan hadn't slept at all.

The moment he saw him, Lin Qiu first counted the number of Black Feather beastmen and, finding none missing, finally felt relieved.

"Yan, we didn't see any other beastmen," several Black Feather beastmen said while holding their bowls and eating.

"No traces at all?"

"We only found the place in the east where you killed the Wild Tribe beastmen. The traces of the other tribe’s beastmen were very faint. We followed the tracks for a while, but eventually, they just disappeared."

"They are indeed very good at hiding."

Even Lang Yan hadn't noticed the wolf beastman who was hiding and waiting for Lin Qiu to be alone, let alone the beastman who moved on the high trees as if on flat ground.

"Thank you for your hard work. Please be more vigilant these next few days. Eat and go get some rest; you must be tired."

Yu Lie nodded and took the Black Feather beastmen to a corner to eat dinner.

The beastmen in the tribe were better, which was a good thing. But the bugs were very toxic, and according to that wolf beastman, being bitten by them was common here, so they needed to stock up on more of these herbs.

Plus, Lang Bing wanted to collect more local herbs. During the two days the beastmen were recovering, others split up to go out and collect herbs with Lin Qiu and Lang Bing.

Yu Lie and Yu Ya were responsible for patrols to ensure safety. Lang Qiao led the hunting and gathering teams, while Lang Yan and Lang Ying continued to search for traces of that wolf beastman.

Having finally encountered a beastman who understood the situation here, Lang Yan really didn't want to miss the chance.

Two days later.

Outside the cave, by the shed.

Lin Qiu stood on a pile of stones, holding a pillar of the shed with one hand and pulling a corner of an animal skin with the other, directing Tu Ai, who was busy on the roof.

Lin Qiu had covered the roof with animal skins, and they were using the space to dry the various herbs they had collected over the past two days.

The heat was intense, and the herbs would be dry enough to crumble with a pinch in just two days.

The herbs collected this morning were almost dry now that it was nearly dark.

Lin Qiu was busy collecting the herbs and skins. He put Tu Ai up there to help him retrieve them.

Just as Lin Qiu was busy, the beastmen who had gone out returned.

Lang Bing and the young wolf beastmen brought back a lot more herbs. Upon returning, he didn't even rest, telling everyone to quickly pull out a few animal skins and spread the herbs out on them.

They had to leave tonight, so they had to spread the herbs out as much as possible to prevent them from getting too damp and rotting if piled together.

The beastmen who had been hunting and gathering went to rest, and Lang Rong and the others, who had been staying in the cave, came out to start cooking.

They had rested for two days and taken the medicine for two days, and now they looked lively, so Lin Qiu wasn't worried anymore.

He was distracted for a moment, and Tu Ai had already pushed the rolled-up animal skins and herbs to his hand.

Lin Qiu grabbed the roll, watching his feet as he moved backward, but he didn't expect to bump into Lang Yan’s forehead, causing a dull thud.

Before he could complain of pain, Lang Yan, who was behind him, hissed first.

Lin Qiu huffed and shoved the roll into his hands, turned around, and asked Tu Ai to drag the other rolls over.

Lang Yan put down the animal skin wrapped around the herbs and placed both hands on Lin Qiu’s waist. His loose, thin clothes were pulled tight by him, instantly revealing Lin Qiu’s figure—a narrow, supple waist, followed by beautiful curves, and his legs...

A pain in his leg—

Lang Yan helplessly let go with one hand and looked at the footprint on his leg.

"The stones aren't stable. I’m protecting you so you don't fall."

Lin Qiu wrapped the animal skin roll and put it in his arms again, shaking his clothes, "Don't you know it’s hot?"

Lang Yan pressed his forehead against the back of Lin Qiu’s neck, "You’re so hot-tempered."

"Don't mess around." Lin Qiu poked his shoulder with his finger, pushing him a bit further away. The weather was hot, and Lang Yan’s body temperature was high; he didn't like being too close.

Once all the herbs on the shed were collected, Lin Qiu picked up the big gray rabbit and put Tu Ai down.

Tu Ai rubbed his long ears, then bit his shorts, hopped into the forest, and came out in human form.

Seeing Lang Yan still standing behind him, Lin Qiu grabbed a fan from the side and fanned it heavily, making his hair fly everywhere.

Lang Yan saw Lin Qiu’s flushed cheeks and touched them with the back of his hand. Lin Qiu blocked his hand with the fan, and Lang Yan touched his chest—it was covered in sweat.

Lin Qiu: "Go take a bath. We’ll leave after we eat dinner and rest for a while."

Leaving tonight was something the beastmen had discussed.

It was truly hot during the day, and the beastmen were carrying heavy loads; they would be covered in sweat after walking just a few steps. They lost more water through sweat than they drank, making it easy to get dehydrated and suffer heatstroke.

After much deliberation, everyone decided to travel at night.

"Together?"

Lin Qiu fanned him once and turned to walk toward the cave.

Lang Yan stood where he was, lowered his eyes, and sighed.

Who would have thought that a mate who would never refuse him before would now start avoiding him?

"What are you standing there for? Let’s go."

Lang Yan looked up and saw Lin Qiu holding a cloth and their clothes. Lang Yan’s lips curled, and he followed closely behind Lin Qiu.

They were leaving tonight, so the beastmen were busy packing and getting themselves ready.

The beastmen who had just returned were still resting, and no one had gone to the river yet. When Lin Qiu arrived, he subconsciously looked into the forest first. Hearing the sound of Lang Yan stepping into the water, Lin Qiu withdrew his gaze and saw him standing in the water, reaching out to him.

Lin Qiu put the clothes and cloth on the bank and grabbed his hand to slowly go down.

The river wasn't shallow; stepping on the stone-paved bottom, the water reached his waist.

The river water was cool, and Lin Qiu sat down in it, sighing with relief.

Lang Yan leaned over, encircling his mate’s waist, and pulled him into his arms with satisfaction.

Qiu hadn't let him hold him while sleeping for a long time.

"You still didn't find that wolf beastman?"

"No. But we found their tracks."

"Where?"

"They went west." Lang Yan untied the cloth strip binding Lin Qiu’s hair, watching his long hair fall down and cover his back. The skin, usually hidden under clothes, looked even more radiant and fair against the black hair.

As Lang Yan watched, his nose brushed against the side of Lin Qiu’s neck, rubbing against his shoulder bit by bit.

Lin Qiu pinched his face, his hand hidden under the water, "Don't mess around."

Lang Yan shivered, his muscles tensing for a moment, revealing smooth and muscular contours. He opened his mouth and bit Lin Qiu’s shoulder, gently at first, but then he couldn't help but continue, wanting to swallow him whole.

Lin Qiu pressed his chin with his hand, his long, water-dampened fingers pressing against his lips, the corners of his eyes slightly red.

"Don't dawdle, there’s a lot to do."

Lang Yan chuckled lowly, his large palm supporting the back of Lin Qiu’s neck, and kissed him deeply.

No dawdling; he would just be faster.
