chapters.source_text:
到了洞外，见狼岩端着碗筷过来。
林楸往旁边让开，狼岩：“醒了？”
林楸：“嗯。”
狼岩把碗递过来。
“给你留的，慢慢吃，我们走了。”
狼岩注意到林楸脸上薄红，还以为是生病，他道：“哪里不舒服？”
林楸呆呆捧着碗，身上的冰壳子似乎一戳就破。
瞧着清清冷冷一个人，但脸皮薄得不像话。故作镇定的样子格外的讨人喜欢。
狼岩其实是故意没将楸挪回窝里。
他们并不是伴侣，楸总这样，其他兽人难免误会，对他也不好。
可要是直接提，楸脸皮薄，肯定以后躲得他远远的。狼岩并不希望看到这样的局面，所以将主动权交给林楸，让他衡量。
“对不起。”
狼岩：“嗯？”
“我……睡到你的草窝里了。”林楸轻声，“我不是故意的。”
等会儿他吃完了就回去把边缘加高。
狼岩闷笑，“嗯，没事。我走了。”
“哦。”林楸眼尾都有些红了。说话却绷着嗓子，面上一派镇定，再逗准要跑了。
很反差，但在狼岩看来，是乖的。
跟小时候哭唧唧要抱，到了他跟前又背过身去，等到抱到怀里了，才软乎乎地趴在肩头，小爪子抓得紧紧的。
还是一样的。
兽人大部队一走，林楸也已经将自己哄好了。
那些都是意外。
谁睡觉的时候还保留意识，时刻警惕。以前生活得够累了，现在自己舒服才好。
林楸安抚好了自己。
上午在祭司那边忙完，下午跟狼莫他们继续调配黏土。
而先前剩下的那一批，等今天攒一攒柴，又可以开始进窑。
林楸忙着烧陶这边的事情，另一边的地里，狼安他们也没闲着。
祭司把除了狼楸跟护卫队第一小队之外的兽人都叫去那边。
他们地开得宽，移栽要快。
亚兽人们心细，他们就做疏苗移栽的活儿。狼石跟狼木领着第二护卫队的，就在地里按照提前画好的线条，刨沟。
狼身巨大，有时候一爪子踩下去就是一片苗子。
狼木一队兽人叫狼安几个好一通骂。
声音传得远，连西边山洞里的林楸几个都听到了。
狼莫幸灾乐祸，“叫他不识好赖，听听狼安骂的。”
林楸踩着泥，没吭声。
泥土配好，接着继续盘泥条做锅。昨晚吃了一顿汤，叫兽人们意识到陶碗的好处，现在都嚷嚷着自己也要一个。
狼兽人饭量大，一个碗差不多一个小型的陶盆大小。有得他们做。
玩儿了一下午泥巴，空了一半的山洞慢慢被填满。
休息一晚，第二天清理窑膛之后，等地里那边不缺人手了，这边木柴也齐了，林楸又开始烧陶。
第二次比第一次心态稳些，知道要熬许久，兽人们先睡足了觉。
依旧是中午过后开始烧，还是狼莫他们看火。
这边烧起来就离不得兽人，狼石以及狼莫小队的兽人们都留在这边看火，林楸依旧两边走。
忙着忙着，就把山洞里那一遭事甩在脑后，面对着狼岩也自在了。
依旧是到第二天下午，窑火熄灭。
地里那边疏苗跟移栽完成，排水沟也开好了。兽人们把草木灰撒下去，那边黑得跟一块臭豆腐似的。
等了两天，终于又迎来再一次开窑。
这次练手的陶陶罐罐没了，每一个泥坯兽人们都做得大小差不多。
其中大型陶碗最多，一个得林楸手捧着，好几斤重。
托在狼岩蒲扇似的大掌里，看着就刚刚好。
陶碗这一批做了五十个，大的陶锅、陶罐各五个。林楸其实还打算做水缸或者储粮的缸子，但那个太大，现在来说还有点难度。
林楸看着全部搬出来的陶器，完好的碗有二十一个，碎的倒是只有几个，但带裂纹的近乎一半。
陶锅陶罐更是，不是破的就是有裂缝的，能用来装东西，但不能用来装水。
还是不成。
狼莫一招手，第一护卫小队的兽人们拉上狼石，头碰头，头发乱糟糟全是窑里带出的灰，七嘴八舌又开始讨论起来。
“为什么会有这么多带裂缝的？”
“是不是黏土这次弄得干了一点？”
“也有可能陶块末碾得不够碎，加得不够。”
林楸只能跟着兽人们探讨，改进，继续做。
看兽人们抓得头发乱飞，林楸：“……”
“不用那么大压力，我们慢慢改。”
兽人们猛地抬头。
他们看着林楸的眼下，已经发青了。
不是他们给自己的压力太大，是楸自己比他们还能熬！
有他激着，他们不得不更努力。就怕林楸身体那么脆，一不小心比他们先熬死了！
兽人们静静盯了他一会儿，安静一瞬，又继续头碰头，说得更起劲儿。
林楸觉得自己在西边山洞待得有点久，脑袋晕乎。看着外面又渐渐黑下来的天空，缓缓起身。
骨头嘎嘣一声响，兽人们齐刷刷看来。
林楸：“坐久了。”
兽人们：“呵……”
一样坐的，怎么没听他们骨头响！
不行不行，不能让楸再跟着熬。
又是一天。
狩猎队跟采集队回来了。
今日没打到什么猎物，采集队倒是带回来不少植物，尤其是山药，直接成捆成捆地用藤蔓绑着，像山里进货回来。
有这么好挖？
林楸看狼岩在安排兽人起鱼笼，他脚步一顿，也慢悠悠去了河边。
狼岩落在兽人们后头，看着林楸来，等了会儿，随着他一起过去。
林楸：“捕猎队跟采集队都是去一个地方？”
狼岩：“大致上一个路线。”
这是以往养成的习惯。
陆地上不只他们一个部落，亚兽人跟着他们一起走，虽然是在部落领地内，但万一遇到危险，他们也能及时增援。
林楸明了。
说着，已经到了河边。
部落里几十个笼子全下了水的，早上兽人们已经起了一遍，狩猎队跟采集队都是吃过鱼肉才出去的。
这会儿兽人们两两负责一个鱼笼。
林楸往近了看，兽人们一身蛮力，拽着笼子一扯。
啪的一声——
拉藤蔓的兽人往后仰去，林楸看着刚刚起来的笼子断开了藤蔓缓缓沉水，还没来得及反应，边上守着的兽人就跳了下去。
看样子，他们已经很熟练了。
林楸胳膊一重，叫狼岩给轻轻拉到离岸边远一点的位置。
林楸：“鱼笼经常掉？”
旁边狼石绷着手臂慢慢扯，不像其他兽人那么着急，回道：“十个里面掉一个。”
林楸看着鱼笼陆陆续续被拉上来，大部分都有鱼，不过相较最开始放鱼笼的时候，还是少了些。
也就是笼子够，凑足了量，才勉强够部落的兽人们吃。
而且藤蔓再怎么软，都会拉得鱼笼变形，好多鱼笼还得修补修补才能用。
林楸见跳水的兽人拉着笼子上来了，对狼岩道：“藤条好像不行。”
狼岩：“将就着能用。”
鱼捞起来，兽人们直接在岸边杀鱼。那些鱼肠鱼腮抠出来，又扔回去空的鱼笼里，循环利用。
林楸看了一会儿，叫狼岩带离了河边。
虽说现在有鱼笼了，但是亚兽人跟未成年的兽人不许靠近河边的规矩，依旧没松。
回到狼山，林楸去找狼贝。
雌性兽人正躺在篝火边，双手枕在脑后，闭着眼，嘴里嚼着那种带着甜味儿的草。
林楸的脚步声惊动了兽人，她睁眼，立马坐起来，眼里带笑。
“楸，今晚咱们吃什么？我们挖了很多山药。”
那边狼安已经带着兽人们削山药皮去了，今天就是只啃山药，也能啃个够。
狼贝甩了甩爪子。
就是挖得多了，手指骨头缝有点酸。
林楸在她身边停下。
他跟狼贝不怎么熟，一时间想着怎么开口。
狼岩：“坐下说。”
他不知从哪儿拿了个黄皮的果子，一边递给林楸，边在他旁边坐下来。
林楸接着，有他在，这下不陌生了。
狼贝看着是有正事，嚼吧嚼吧嘴里的甜草，咽下，随后两双黑白分明的眼睛注视过来。
她眼睛格外大，炯炯有神。
林楸：“你们采集队见过一些……皮很难折断的植物吗？很有韧性，能直接像藤条一样捆着东西……”
狼贝：“有，挺多。”
“要那个干什么？”
“做绳子。”
“兽皮绳不行吗？”
狼岩：“部落里的兽皮绳用完了，要重新做。”但是现在猎物都没多少，兽皮紧缺，做不出多少。
狼贝点点头。
“那我们明天割回来……”说着一顿，看了眼狼岩，直接道，“楸想不想跟我们一起出去采集？”
狼岩目光微动，看向林楸。
林楸偏头，与狼岩对视。
“可以吗？”
狼岩：“可以。”
狼岩忽然想到，应该给林楸“解禁”了。就靠着他为部落做出的陶器，就可以告知兽人们，林楸经过了考核期。
林楸目光微亮，“那我去。”
他其实一直想出去看看，无奈被原身的过错束缚着。
“那明天你得早点起来。”狼贝一本正经道。
他们都看见了，楸经常早上的时候滚到王的窝里，藏在王的毛毛里，睡得可舒服了。
部落所有兽人当中，也就他睡得最久。
林楸：“好。”
狼莫几个一回来，就听到采集队薅人，立马围住林楸道：“楸，你要加入采集队吗？”
林楸迷茫，“没有啊。”
“那你跟采集队出去干什么？”
林楸：“找些材料。”
“哦……”找材料好，楸再继续烧陶他们压力大。
兽人们也不继续追问，捂着酸酸涨涨的脑子往地上一滚，变做原型，双目呆滞，一动不动的像个巨型毛绒玩偶。
现在捏泥巴已经不是一个单纯的好玩儿的事。
他们要思考配比，关注火候，一天天手都没干净过。
“嗷！”狼莫一拍脑袋。
为什么还要想！
他好累，比捕猎一天都累！
狼贝看着有些古怪的几个做陶的兽人，默默远离。
怕不是做陶做疯了。
chapters.translated_text:
Arriving outside the cave, he saw Lang Yan approaching with a bowl and chopsticks.

Lin Qiu stepped aside to make room, and Lang Yan asked, "Awake?"

Lin Qiu: "Mm."

Lang Yan handed over the bowl.

"Left this for you. Eat slowly; we're leaving."

Lang Yan noticed the faint flush on Lin Qiu’s face and, thinking he might be ill, asked, "Is something bothering you?"

Lin Qiu held the bowl blankly, the icy shell around him looking as if it could shatter with a single poke.

He was a cold and aloof person, yet his skin was impossibly thin. His attempt to feign composure was exceptionally endearing.

In truth, Lang Yan had intentionally not moved Qiu back to his own nest.

They were not mates, and if Qiu kept doing this, other beastmen would inevitably misunderstand, which wouldn't be good for him.

But if he brought it up directly, Qiu, being thin-skinned, would surely avoid him in the future. Lang Yan didn't want to see that happen, so he left the initiative to Lin Qiu to weigh for himself.

"I'm sorry."

Lang Yan: "Hmm?"

"I... slept in your grass nest," Lin Qiu said softly. "I didn't mean to."

He would go back and build up the edges once he finished eating.

Lang Yan chuckled under his breath, "Mm, it's fine. I'm leaving."

"Oh." The corners of Lin Qiu’s eyes were slightly red. He kept his voice steady and his expression calm, but he was on the verge of running away if teased any further.

It was a stark contrast, but in Lang Yan's eyes, it was adorable.

It was just like when he was little—crying and wanting to be held, only to turn his back once he reached him, and then, once finally in his arms, clinging softly to his shoulder with his little claws gripped tight.

It was still the same.

Once the main group of beastmen left, Lin Qiu had already coaxed himself into a better mood.

Those were all accidents.

Who stays conscious and alert while sleeping? Life had been exhausting enough before; now, he should just prioritize his own comfort.

Lin Qiu settled his mind.

After finishing his work with the priest in the morning, he spent the afternoon continuing to mix clay with Lang Mo and the others.

As for the previous batch, once they gathered enough firewood today, they could start loading the kiln again.

While Lin Qiu was busy with the pottery, Lang An and the others weren't idle in the fields.

The priest had called all the beastmen except for Lang Qiu and the first guard squad to work there.

They had opened up a large area, so the transplanting needed to be fast.

The sub-beastmen were meticulous, so they handled the thinning and transplanting. Lang Shi and Lang Mu led the second guard squad, digging furrows in the field according to pre-marked lines.

The wolves were massive, and sometimes a single paw step would crush a whole patch of seedlings.

Lang Mu’s squad of beastmen received a thorough scolding from Lang An and the others.

The sound carried far, reaching even Lin Qiu and his group in the western cave.

Lang Mo gloated, "Serves him right for not knowing better. Listen to how Lang An is yelling."

Lin Qiu stepped through the mud without a word.

Once the clay was mixed, he continued coiling the clay strips to make pots. After having soup last night, the beastmen realized the benefits of pottery bowls and were now clamoring for one of their own.

The wolf beastmen had huge appetites; one bowl was roughly the size of a small pottery basin. They had their work cut out for them.

After playing with mud all afternoon, the half-empty cave was slowly filling up.

After a night's rest and cleaning the kiln the next day, once the fields no longer lacked manpower and the firewood was ready, Lin Qiu began firing the pottery again.

His mindset was steadier for the second attempt than the first. Knowing it would be a long process, the beastmen made sure to get enough sleep beforehand.

They started firing after noon as before, with Lang Mo and his group watching the fire.

Once the fire was lit, it couldn't be left unattended, so Lang Shi and Lang Mo’s squad stayed to watch it, while Lin Qiu moved back and forth between the two areas.

As he got busy, he pushed the incident in the cave to the back of his mind and felt at ease facing Lang Yan again.

It wasn't until the following afternoon that the kiln fire died out.

In the fields, the thinning and transplanting were finished, and the drainage ditches were dug. The beastmen scattered wood ash, making the ground look as dark as stinky tofu.

After waiting two days, they finally welcomed another kiln opening.

This time, there were no practice pots; every clay piece the beastmen made was roughly the same size.

Large pottery bowls were the most numerous, each weighing several pounds and requiring Lin Qiu to hold them with both hands.

Resting in Lang Yan’s fan-like palm, they looked just right.

They had made fifty of these pottery bowls, along with five large pots and five jars. Lin Qiu had actually intended to make water vats or grain storage jars, but those were too large and still a bit difficult for now.

Looking at all the pottery moved out, twenty-one bowls were intact. Only a few were shattered, but nearly half had cracks.

The pots and jars were even worse—either broken or cracked, usable for holding things but not for water.

Still not good enough.

Lang Mo waved his hand, and the first guard squad pulled Lang Shi over. Head to head, their hair messy and covered in the ash from the kiln, they began discussing things in a flurry of voices.

"Why are there so many with cracks?"

"Was the clay a bit too dry this time?"

"It's also possible the crushed pottery bits weren't ground fine enough or weren't added in enough quantity."

Lin Qiu could only join the beastmen in discussing, improving, and continuing to work.

Seeing the beastmen pulling at their hair in frustration, Lin Qiu: "..."

"No need for so much pressure. We'll improve slowly."

The beastmen looked up abruptly.

They looked at the dark circles under Lin Qiu’s eyes.

It wasn't that they were putting too much pressure on themselves; it was that Qiu could endure even more than they could!

With him pushing them, they had to work harder. They were afraid that Lin Qiu, with his fragile body, would accidentally die from exhaustion before they did!

The beastmen stared at him quietly for a moment, then, after a brief silence, put their heads together again and continued their discussion even more vigorously.

Lin Qiu felt he had been in the western cave for too long and felt dizzy. Seeing the sky outside darkening again, he slowly stood up.

His bones cracked with a pop, and the beastmen all looked over in unison.

Lin Qiu: "Sat for too long."

The beastmen: "Heh..."

They had been sitting just as long, so why didn't they hear their bones crack!

No, no, they couldn't let Qiu keep pushing himself like this.

Another day passed.

The hunting and gathering teams returned.

They hadn't caught much game today, but the gathering team brought back plenty of plants, especially yams, tied in bundles with vines as if they had gone on a shopping spree in the mountains.

Were they that easy to dig?

Lin Qiu saw Lang Yan arranging for the beastmen to check the fish traps. He paused, then strolled toward the river as well.

Lang Yan trailed behind the beastmen. Seeing Lin Qiu coming, he waited a moment and then walked over with him.

Lin Qiu: "Do the hunting and gathering teams go to the same place?"

Lang Yan: "Generally the same route."

It was a habit formed in the past.

They weren't the only tribe on the land. The sub-beastmen traveled with them; even though they were within tribal territory, they could provide timely reinforcements if they encountered danger.

Lin Qiu understood.

As they spoke, they arrived at the riverbank.

Dozens of traps had been set in the water. The beastmen had already checked them once in the morning, and both the hunting and gathering teams had eaten fish before heading out.

Now, the beastmen were working in pairs, each responsible for one fish trap.

Lin Qiu watched closely as the beastmen, with their brute strength, pulled on the traps.

With a snap—

The beastman pulling the vine fell backward. Lin Qiu watched as the trap that had just been raised broke its vine and slowly sank back into the water. Before he could react, the beastman guarding the side jumped in.

It seemed they were already very experienced.

Lin Qiu felt a weight on his arm as Lang Yan gently pulled him further away from the bank.

Lin Qiu: "Do the fish traps break often?"

Lang Shi, standing nearby, tensed his arms and pulled slowly, not as anxious as the other beastmen, and replied: "One out of ten breaks."

Lin Qiu watched as the fish traps were pulled up one after another. Most had fish, though fewer than when they first started using the traps.

It was only because they had enough traps to make up the quantity that the tribe’s beastmen could barely get enough to eat.

Moreover, no matter how soft the vines were, they would eventually deform the traps, and many had to be repaired before they could be used again.

Seeing the beastman who jumped in pull the trap up, Lin Qiu said to Lang Yan, "Vines don't seem to work well."

Lang Yan: "They'll do for now."

Once the fish were caught, the beastmen cleaned them right on the bank. The fish guts and gills were scooped out and thrown back into the empty traps for recycling.

Lin Qiu watched for a while before Lang Yan led him away from the river.

Even though they had fish traps now, the rule that sub-beastmen and underage beastmen were not allowed near the river remained strictly enforced.

Returning to Wolf Mountain, Lin Qiu went to find Lang Bei.

The female beastman was lying by the campfire, hands behind her head, eyes closed, chewing on that sweet-tasting grass.

The sound of Lin Qiu’s footsteps startled her. She opened her eyes, sat up immediately, and smiled.

"Qiu, what are we eating tonight? We dug up a lot of yams."

Over there, Lang An was already leading the beastmen to peel the yams. Even if they only gnawed on yams today, they would have plenty.

Lang Bei shook her claws.

She had dug so much that her finger joints were a bit sore.

Lin Qiu stopped beside her.

He wasn't very close to Lang Bei and was wondering how to start the conversation.

Lang Yan: "Sit down and talk."

He produced a yellow-skinned fruit from somewhere, handed it to Lin Qiu, and sat down beside him.

Lin Qiu took it; with him there, it didn't feel awkward anymore.

Lang Bei looked like she had serious business. She chewed the sweet grass in her mouth, swallowed, and then fixed her black-and-white eyes on him.

Her eyes were exceptionally large and bright.

Lin Qiu: "Have you ever seen any plants in the gathering team... whose skin is hard to break? Very tough, and can be used to tie things up just like vines..."

Lang Bei: "Yes, quite a few."

"What do you need that for?"

"To make rope."

"Can't you use animal hide rope?"

Lang Yan: "The tribe's animal hide rope is used up and needs to be remade." But there wasn't much game now, so hides were scarce, and they couldn't make much.

Lang Bei nodded.

"Then we'll cut some back tomorrow..." She paused, looked at Lang Yan, and said directly, "Qiu, do you want to come gathering with us?"

Lang Yan’s gaze flickered as he looked at Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu turned his head to meet Lang Yan’s eyes.

"Can I?"

Lang Yan: "You can."

Lang Yan suddenly thought it was time to "lift the ban" on Lin Qiu. Based on the pottery he had made for the tribe, he could inform the beastmen that Lin Qiu had passed his probation period.

Lin Qiu’s eyes brightened, "Then I'll go."

He had actually always wanted to go out and see, but was held back by the mistakes of the original body.

"Then you have to get up early tomorrow," Lang Bei said seriously.

They had all seen it—Qiu often rolled into the King’s nest in the morning, hiding in the King’s fur, sleeping so comfortably.

Out of all the beastmen in the tribe, he was the one who slept the longest.

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

As soon as Lang Mo and the others returned, they heard the gathering team poaching him and immediately surrounded Lin Qiu: "Qiu, are you joining the gathering team?"

Lin Qiu was confused, "No."

"Then why are you going out with the gathering team?"

Lin Qiu: "To find some materials."

"Oh..." Finding materials is good; if Qiu kept making pottery, they would be under too much pressure.

The beastmen didn't ask further. Clutching their sore, throbbing heads, they rolled onto the ground, transformed into their original forms, and lay there blankly, looking like giant plush toys.

Making mud was no longer just a fun activity.

They had to think about ratios, watch the heat, and their hands were never clean for a single day.

"Awooo!" Lang Mo slapped his head.

Why did he still have to think!

He was so tired, more tired than after a full day of hunting!

Lang Bei watched the strangely acting pottery-making beastmen and silently moved away.

They must have gone crazy from making pottery.

Lang Yan went to the shaman’s cave to discuss things with him. Both sides agreed on the matter regarding Lin Qiu, so they gathered the tribe’s beastmen.

Usually, a tribe only calls all its beastmen together for major events.

The last time was to discuss splitting off a branch tribe.

The beastmen were a bit nervous. "Could it be that we're migrating again?"

"Where else could we move to?"

The hunting team hadn't caught any prey today, but they had fish to eat, which could barely tide them over. If they migrated, they wouldn't even have enough food saved up for the journey.

The beastmen were a mix of anxious and curious.

Lang Yan and the shaman stood on the platform in front of the cave. With a wave of his hand, the beastmen’s murmurs died down. Everyone looked up, gazing ahead.

Lang Yan: "We are not migrating. The tribe has seen some good changes recently, and none of these would have been possible without Qiu’s suggestions. So, regarding whether Qiu will continue to stay in the tribe..."

"Let him stay!"

The beastmen shouted in unison.

They were all a bit nervous, their eyes scanning the crowd of beastmen before landing on Lin Qiu, who was standing at the back.

"Qiu, don't be afraid."

"Qiu, the King can't chase you away."

Lang Yan stared at Lang Mo and the others surrounding Lin Qiu, his eyes darkening. Did they think he couldn't hear them?

"King! Qiu has already finished his punishment, and he’s been very well-behaved lately..."

Lang Yan swept a glance over them, and Lang Mo and the other beastmen shut their mouths.

"Did I say I was going to kick Qiu out?"

"But you—didn't you say Qiu had changed for the better? That usually means sending someone back to the branch tribe."

Lang Yan stared at Lang Mo, whose voice grew smaller and smaller until he finally fell silent and hid behind Lin Qiu.

The shaman tapped his wooden staff and said slowly, "The two tribes are one family. Based on Qiu’s recent performance in the tribe, the King and I have discussed it: from now on, Qiu can move freely within the Wolf Tribe just like the rest of you."

"Awoo!"

"Awoo, awoo!"

The shaman’s words were like water poured into a hot oil pan; the crowd erupted, and the beastmen cheered, happily lifting Lin Qiu into the air.

Lin Qiu had expected a simple formality, but now, being tossed up and down like a chick in the beastmen's hands, the sudden sensation of weightlessness turned his face pale.

Lang Yan frowned and moved quickly toward them.

The beastmen scattered in fright, and as Lin Qiu fell, Lang Yan caught him steadily.

"Ugh!" Startled, Lin Qiu grabbed Lang Yan’s arm, his eyes squeezed shut and his lips pressed into a thin line, clearly terrified.

Lang Yan glared at the group of beastmen who had tossed the person and run off; he really wanted to kick them into the river one by one.

The beastmen flopped onto the ground, shifted into their beast forms, and covered their eyes with their paws.

*You can't see me, you can't see me...*

Lang Yan set Lin Qiu down. "Are you alright?"

Lin Qiu’s legs felt weak, and he gripped Lang Yan’s arm tightly; Lang Yan held his elbows firmly to steady him.

"They can be reckless sometimes. If you don't like it, just tell them directly."

Lin Qiu: "I was just startled, I'm fine."

In truth, it was more that he wasn't used to it.

"Can I go gathering with Lang Bei and the others tomorrow?"

Lang Yan: "It's a long way."

Lin Qiu: "I can turn into a wolf, too."

Lang Yan let go of his arms, his frown softening, amused by his rare playful remark.

"Eat your fish first. Go to sleep early tonight; we're leaving very early tomorrow."

Lin Qiu glanced at his own arm, lightly touched the finger marks Lang Yan had left, and whispered, "Okay."

The shaman watched them leave, and Lang Bing helped him into the cave.

"Shaman, does the King want to become mates with Qiu?"

The old shaman: "How would I know what your King is thinking?"

Lang Bing: "They’re already sharing the same grass nest."

The old shaman tapped Lang Bing on the forehead, not too hard, but the young beastman still rubbed his head while staring at him.

Stubborn as a curved-horn beast.

"Focus on learning your herbs; Qiu is almost catching up to you."

"I won't let him catch up to me!"

*

The next day.

As the first line of white appeared on the horizon, the sound of fish traps splashing out of the water echoed along the big river.

The hunting and gathering teams were already up, with beastmen helping to pull up the traps and prepare breakfast. By the time the beastmen were holding their steaming bowls of fish soup, it was only just dawn.

Lin Qiu sat up the moment he heard movement in the cave. Having not woken up this early in a long time, he was still a bit dazed.

Lang Yan put on his animal skins and looked at the blank-faced Lin Qiu, the corners of his lips curling up.

"Get up."

Lin Qiu nodded, pushed aside the animal skin, and climbed out. He was wearing his mended animal skin clothes, his shoulder-length hair loose and slightly messy.

Lang Yan waited nearby, watching him fold his bedding, and then reached over to pick up the cub that had been sleeping with its little belly rising and falling beside the grass nest, moving it back to Lang Guo’s side.

With his long legs, he reached Lin Qiu in a few strides. "Let's go."

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

One didn't ask if he should wait, and the other didn't ask if he shouldn't; a single look and a single sentence carried a familiar, tacit understanding.

Other beastmen were already up; the first batch was already clutching their pottery bowls and strange wooden spoons, gulping down fish soup.

The beastmen responsible for cooking in the tribe had gradually become fixed, led by Lang An, along with Lang Yu, Lang Shuang, and six other sub-beastmen.

They worked in groups of three, taking turns, which made it easier for everyone.

This morning's meal was fish and wild vegetable soup.

Wolf beastmen had big mouths and were used to being hungry, so they ate quickly. Even though every beastman’s bowl was the same size and the portion was fixed, they liked to hold the bowl and pour the soup into their mouths after scooping a few times with their spoons.

That was why beastmen often choked on fish bones—it wasn't entirely the bones' fault, but their own impatience.

This morning, the fish was boiled until soft and tender, mixed with the leftover wild greens and yams from yesterday’s gathering, like a big hodgepodge.

Lin Qiu held his bowl and poked at it with his chopsticks.

The bowl was packed tight with meat and vegetables, with very little soup.

Lang Yan explained to him: "Hunting and gathering take a lot of energy, and you'll be going out too."

Lin Qiu glanced at Lang Yan’s bowl, which also had more meat and vegetables.

He nodded and began to eat this exceptionally hearty breakfast.

The beastmen hadn't been using pottery pots for long, and other than the few cooking methods they’d learned from Lin Qiu, they hadn't done much extra research.

Fish balls and meat balls were hard to make, and they hadn't tried them yet.

Stir-fried meat with wild greens, meat and vegetable soup, bone and yam soup, bone and wild vegetable soup, fish and vegetable soup—that was about it.

The beastmen weren't picky as long as there was food; their only goal was to fill their stomachs.

After breakfast, the beastmen washed their own bowls.

Lang Mo’s group had been researching constantly and had made many pottery jars and bowls. Now, every beastman had one, marked with their own claw prints, and they used their own bowls for every meal.

Once washed, the bowls were put away.

Most were kept by their grass nests, while a few were left casually by the pottery pots or in places they liked to lie down, so they could hold them while napping. Or, they would turn them upside down and use them as pillows, as the height was just right.

Just as Lin Qiu finished washing his, Lang Yan reached out.

He handed his bowl over, and Lang Yan placed it inside his own, setting them both by the pottery pot outside.

"There’s too much fur in the cave," Lang Yan said.

It was almost time for shedding season. When the beastmen shook their heads, their long fur flew like needles, covering everything in the cave. If you walked around the cave during the day and looked at the grass nests, you’d see wolf fur hanging off all the hay and wooden sticks.

Once finished eating, the beastmen began to assemble.

By now, the morning sun was peeking over the horizon, casting brilliant rays. The dew on the grass in front of Wolf Mountain had already been brushed off by the passing beastmen, while the forests and meadows beyond the mountain were thick with mist.

The hunting team stood on one side, the gathering team on the other.

The younger gathering and hunting teams, led by Lang Bing and Lang Jin respectively, followed behind.

This gathered most of the beastmen of Wolf Mountain. Once everyone was present, they set off in a grand procession toward the east.

Leaving Wolf Mountain, following a command from the hunting team in the lead, the beastmen began to run through the morning light, shifting fluidly from human form to beast form.

Lin Qiu carried his basket on his back. Seeing dozens of massive wolves appear ahead, he quickly took off his basket, focused his mind, and transformed into a black wolf.

He stayed by Lang Bei’s side.

The wolf forms of the gathering team were generally smaller than those of the hunting team members running ahead.

But Lang Bei was different; she was almost as large as the wolves in front.

Majestic and awe-inspiring, her wolf eyes sharp.

"Qiu, once we pass the forest, we’ll need to pick up the pace."

Lin Qiu held his basket in his mouth and glanced at the rattan baskets hanging on the beastmen’s backs. Only then did he realize why they made them single-shouldered; they fit perfectly on their backs when in beast form, and the length of the straps was just right.

Lin Qiu: "Mm."

The sunlight chased after them rapidly, its dazzling golden rays dispersing the morning mist, making the surrounding forests and trees distinct.

Lin Qiu adjusted to running, staying silent and sticking close to Lang Bei.

Although it was his first time running on four legs, it felt like an innate ability; the more Lin Qiu ran, the more accustomed he became.

The east was a flat forest, while the northeast was a mix of endless grasslands and long rivers.

A path had been worn through the forest by the beastmen, who sprinted silently and in perfect order.

They were like fish in water, moving with ease.

Even the golden light spots peering through the gaps in the trees couldn't catch them, save for the occasional flash of gold on their fur, which only highlighted their incredible speed.

Dozens of giant wolves wove through the dense trees, with only a rustling sound as light as the forest's own breathing.

Lin Qiu stared intently at the scene, his heart racing, his eyes sharp and bright.

This life experience, so completely different from his past, made his heart surge, and his exhausted spirit felt thoroughly released in this moment.

The Wolf Tribe’s territory was vast, and the beastmen usually hunted in the east, northeast, or south.

From Wolf Mountain, it took half a morning just to run there.

As they were about to leave the forest that blocked out the sky, a clear wolf howl came from behind.

"Awoo!" Lang Bei replied.

Beastmen in the wolf pack ahead also responded.

Lin Qiu looked back, but before he could see clearly, Lang Bei said to him: "The little wolves need to gather herbs nearby; we’ll meet up again on the way back."

"What about Lang Jin and the others?" Lin Qiu asked.

"They... the King didn't arrange for them to follow the hunting team today, so they should be with Bing and the others."

"They always like to be together," Lang Bei said.

After running for a while longer, the light suddenly brightened, and the view opened up.

It was a vast grassland, endless and boundless. Knee-high green grass spread out like a velvet carpet along the rolling land. The wind made the grass sway, and the fresh scent was completely different from the heavy woody fragrance of the forest—it was open and free.

Out of the forest, the silhouettes of the wolf pack became even clearer.
chapters.title: 第35章
chapters.source_text:
狼岩去了一趟祭司山洞，跟祭司商量了下。两边都同意林楸的事，便将部落的兽人召集起来。
一般部落有大事，才需要全部兽人到场。
上一次还是商量分出支部落的事情。
兽人们有些紧张，“难不成又要迁徙？”
“还能迁到哪里去？”
今天狩猎队又没捕捉到猎物，但他们现在有鱼吃，能勉强撑一撑。要是迁徙，他们路途上吃的食物都攒不够。
兽人们有忐忑的，也有好奇的。
狼岩跟祭司站在山洞前的平台上，手一抬，兽人们议论的声音沉寂。大家都抬起头，看着前方。
狼岩：“不迁徙。最近部落有些好的改变，这些都离不开楸的建议。所以关于楸是否继续留在部落的事……”
“留！”
兽人们齐喊。
他们都有些紧张，目光在兽人中寻找，随后一下落在兽人后头的林楸身上。
“楸，你别怕。”
“楸，王赶不走你的。”
狼岩盯着围绕在林楸身边的狼莫那几个，眸色深了深，当他听不见？
“王！楸已经接受完惩罚了，最近也乖乖的……”
狼岩一个眼神扫过去，狼莫几个兽人闭嘴。
“我说了要把楸赶出去？”
“可你、你不是说楸改好了嘛，那肯定要送人家回支部落的。”
狼岩盯着狼莫，兽人声音越来越小，最后闭嘴，躲在林楸身后。
祭司敲了敲木杖，慢慢道：“两个部落本就是一家，按照楸最近在部落的表现，我跟王商量，之后楸就跟你们一样可以随意在狼部落活动。”
“嗷呜！”
“嗷呜嗷呜！”
祭司这话像油锅里倒水，一下炸开了锅，兽人们哄闹，喜笑颜开地将林楸举起来。
林楸本来以为就简单走个过场，这下在兽人们手头跟小鸡仔一样，抛高落下，陡然失重让他脸色发白。
狼岩眉一皱，迅速靠近。
兽人们吓得一哄而散，林楸落下，叫狼岩稳稳接住。
“唔！”林楸吓得抓住狼岩胳膊，眼睛闭得紧紧的，唇绷直，显然是怕。
狼岩盯着那群扔了人就跑的兽人，很想一个个踹河里去。
兽人们趴地，变兽形，爪子捂住眼睛。
看不见我，看不见我……
狼岩将林楸放下，“没事吧？”
林楸腿一软，紧紧抓着狼岩手臂，狼岩也稳稳托着他手肘。
“他们有时候莽撞，不喜欢就直说出来。”
林楸：“就是吓了一跳，没事。”
其实更多的是不习惯。
“我明天能跟狼贝他们去采集了？”
狼岩：“要走很远。”
林楸：“我也会变狼。”
狼岩松开手，被他难得一句顽皮话逗得眉头松开。
“先吃鱼吧。今晚早点睡，明天起来很早。”
林楸瞥了眼自己手臂，轻轻摸了摸狼岩捏出来的五指印，低声道：“好。”
祭司看着他俩离开，狼冰搀扶着他进山洞。
“祭司，王是不是想跟楸结成伴侣？”
老祭司：“你们王的想法，我哪里知道。”
狼冰：“他们都一个草窝了。”
老祭司拍了下狼冰额头，力道不轻不重，少年兽人却捂着脑袋盯着他。
倔得跟弯角兽一样。
“好好学你的草药，楸都快赶上你了。”
“我才不会让他赶上我！”
*
翌日。
天边刚吐出一线白，大河边就响起鱼笼哗啦出水的声音。
狩猎队跟采集队已经起来了，兽人们帮着捞鱼笼，做早饭。待兽人捧着热气腾腾的鱼汤时，也不过天微明。
林楸听到山洞里的动静就坐起来，许久没这么早起来，人还有些懵。
狼岩穿好兽皮，看着目光呆滞的林楸，唇角翘了下。
“起了。”
林楸脑袋一点，掀开兽皮爬起来。他身上穿着补好的兽皮衣，半长的头发散在肩膀，有些凌乱。
狼岩在一旁等着，看着他叠好兽皮，顺手也拎着草窝边睡得小肚子起伏的幼崽放回狼果那边去。
他腿长，几步就走到林楸身边，道：“走吧。”
林楸：“好。”
两个一个没说要等，一个没说不等，一个眼神一句话，就有种熟悉的默契。
其他兽人早起了，最早的一批已经抱着自己的陶碗，抓着千奇百怪的木头勺子往嘴里灌鱼汤。
部落里现在做饭的兽人渐渐固定下来，狼安为首，带着狼雨、狼霜还有另外六个亚兽人。
他们三个人一组，轮流做，也能轻松一些。
今早的是鱼肉野菜汤。
狼兽人嘴巴大，饿成习惯了，吃东西急。就算每个兽人的陶碗大小一样，也都是固定份额的一碗，但用勺子舀着舀着后头就喜欢抱着碗往嘴里灌。
所以常常有兽人吃鱼卡住，也不能全怪鱼刺多，还得是他们自己心急。
今早鱼肉煮得软烂了，昨天采集队剩下的叶菜还有山药都混了些煮在一起，像个大杂烩。
林楸端着自己的碗，用筷子挑了挑。
碗里的肉跟菜都装得实，汤少。
狼岩跟他解释：“狩猎跟采集耗费力气，你也要跟着出去。”
林楸看了眼狼岩的碗里，也是肉跟菜比较多。
他点点头，开始吃这格外扎实的一顿早餐。
兽人们现在用陶锅烹饪还没多长时间，只除了从林楸哪里学到的几样做菜的法子，也没什么额外的研究。
鱼丸、肉丸难做，还没做过。
肉片炒野菜、肉片野菜汤、骨头山药汤、骨头野菜汤、鱼肉野菜汤，就这几种。
兽人们有吃的不挑，一切以灌饱肚子为主。
早饭吃过，兽人们自己洗碗。
狼莫那边成天研究，弄出来不少陶罐、陶碗，兽人们现在人手一个，都用自己爪子在上面标记了，吃饭也用自己的碗。
碗刚洗完，各自放好。
大多放在自己草窝边，少部分随意放在陶锅边，以及自己喜欢趴着的地方，打盹的时候得抱着。又或者扣过来，脑袋枕着，高度也合适。
林楸这边刚洗完，狼岩伸手。
他将碗递过去，被狼岩放在他的碗里，一起放在了外面陶锅边。
“洞里毛多。”狼岩道。
快到换毛的时候了，兽人们一甩脑袋，长毛跟飞针似的，洞里到处都是。要是白天去山洞里转一转，看看兽人的草窝，那些干草、木棍上到处都挂着狼毛。
吃完了，兽人们开始集结。
此时天边吐出朝阳，霞光万丈，狼山山前的草叶上露珠已经被来往的兽人们碰掉，而狼山外的林野草地，雾气正浓。
狩猎队一边，采集队一边。
狼冰跟狼金分别带领的年轻的采集跟狩猎队，则跟在后头。
这一下汇聚了狼山大半的兽人，人数齐了，便浩浩荡荡向着东部出发。
离开狼山，随着前头狩猎队里发出的一声令，兽人们开始在晨曦中奔跑，从人形自如地转化为兽形。
林楸背着他的背篓，看着前方一下出现几十头体型巨大的狼，一时间脱下背篓赶紧凝神，也变做一只黑狼。
他跟在狼贝的身边。
采集队的兽人们狼形相较于前头奔跑的狩猎队的成员们，都普遍小了一些。
但狼贝不一样，她几乎跟前面的狼一样大。
威风凛凛，狼眼锐利。
“楸，过了林子，我们就要加快速度了。”
林楸叼着背篓，看了眼挂在兽人们背上的藤筐，这才发现兽人们为什么要做单肩的了。因为变成兽形刚好能固定在背上，绳子的长短且是刚刚好的。
林楸：“嗯。”
阳光迅速追赶而来，耀眼的金色光芒驱散晨雾，四周的山林树木都变得分明起来。
林楸适应着奔跑，一声不吭，紧紧跟在狼贝的身边。
虽说四条腿奔跑是头一次，但仿佛与生俱来的能力，林楸跑着跑着就越是习惯。
东部是平坦的森林，东北部交错着一望无际的草地、长河。
林子里被兽人们踏出来一条路，兽人无声无息地飞奔而过，井然有序。
他们如鱼儿入水，游刃有余。
林间缝隙里窥探过来的金色光斑都难以捕捉他们，只偶尔狼毛上一闪而过的碎金，彰显着他们速度之快。
几十头巨狼穿梭在茂密的林木中，只有轻得仿佛森林呼吸的沙沙声。
林楸紧紧盯着这一幕，心绪起伏，眸光明锐。
这全然与从前不同的人生体验，叫他心潮澎湃，疲惫的精神在这一刻得到彻底释放。
狼部落的领地非常大，兽人们捕捉猎物的地方一般在东部、东北部或者南部。
从狼山过去，跑都要跑半个上午。
待快要离开遮天蔽日的林子，身后传来一声清亮的狼嚎。
“嗷！”狼贝应了。
前方的狼群也有兽人应了。
林楸回头，还没看得清楚，狼贝跟他道：“小狼们要在附近采集草药，回去的时候再一起。”
“狼金他们呢？”林楸问。
“他们……王今天没安排他们跟着狩猎队，应该就跟冰他们一起了。”
“他们总喜欢一起。”狼贝说。
又跑了一阵，忽然天光骤明，豁然开朗。
这是一大片草原，无边无际。腿高的青草如绒毯一般沿着土地的起伏铺陈开来。风吹得青草晃动，那清新的味道是与森林中厚重的木香截然不同，空旷而自由。
出了林子，狼群的身影更清晰了。

chapters.translated_text:
Lin Qiu chased after them in silence, gradually hearing his own rapid panting, knowing that his stamina was starting to lag behind.

The members of both the hunting team and the gathering team were selected from the strongest and healthiest orcs in the tribe; even the sub-orcs among them had good endurance.

Lang Bei, as the captain of the gathering team, was the first to notice Lin Qiu's situation.

They still had a long way to run, and there was no prey to be caught in this area.

Things won't go well for Qiu if this continues.

Lang Bei slowed down, signaling the other orcs to keep up with the hunting team ahead.

"Qiu, sit on my back."

Lin Qiu looked up at the black wolf that had stopped beside the pack, who was also looking at him.

Lang Bei: "Hey, the King will carry you."

Lang Bei ran off to catch up with the team.

Lang Yan stood in front of Lin Qiu; even though both were in wolf form, Lang Yan was half a head taller than Lin Qiu.

He lowered his head, his nose tip brushing against Lin Qiu's ear.

Lin Qiu's ear twitched, and he watched as the wolf turned sideways and crouched down.

Lin Qiu hurriedly shifted into human form and put on the animal skin clothes from his basket. Without the fur to cover him, his earlobes were completely red.

Lang Yan: "They are going to run far away."

Lin Qiu didn't dare to hesitate, climbing onto Lang Yan's back, not knowing where to put his hands.

Lang Yan stood up, "Lie down, clamp your legs tight, and wrap your arms around my neck."

Lin Qiu didn't say a word, doing exactly as he was told.

"Let's go," Lang Yan said.

"Mm."

The black wolf began to run slowly; the pack had already gone far ahead, looking like black mushrooms growing in the grass, in clusters.

Lang Yan was slowly accelerating, the wind rushing past his sides so quickly that Lin Qiu could barely open his eyes.

He lowered his body, lying completely flat on Lang Yan's back.

His fair, slender fingers sank into the long black fur, almost completely hidden. His cheeks pressed against the wolf fur, which was a bit prickly, but the fur his fingers were tightly gripping felt soft and fluffy.

In a few moments, Lang Yan caught up with the team.

The lead orcs judged the direction of the prey and adjusted accordingly; Lang Yan knew Lin Qiu was thin-skinned, so he just followed at the back.

Lin Qiu's body felt a bit tired from the tension.

His arms were sore, and his legs couldn't hold on tightly anymore.

Lang Yan: "It should be soon."

Lin Qiu silently turned his face, his nose brushing against the wolf fur, breathing shallowly.

"Mm."

Finally, when Lin Qiu felt the stinging heat of the sun on his back, the orcs slowly slowed down and eventually lay down in front of a grassy slope.

Lin Qiu had no strength left.

Lang Yan walked slowly, approaching the other orcs.

Lin Qiu's face was buried in the wolf fur, his limbs relaxed, hanging limply on Lang Yan.

The orcs were long used to this.

Qiu had already rolled into the King's nest several times; whenever they wanted to tease him, the King would give them a warning look.

Later, even when Qiu woke up in the Wolf King's nest and realized what he had done while asleep, he still didn't move his nest.

Hmm... no orc could resist the charm of their King.

Lang Yan stopped behind the orcs. After he lay down, Lin Qiu rolled off to the side, his body touching the slightly cool grass. He lay there for a few seconds before silently sitting up.

A trace of a smile flashed in Lang Yan's eyes, which he didn't dare let Lin Qiu see.

He was thin-skinned.

He stared at the herd of prey the orcs had discovered in the distance and whispered to Lin Qiu: "Follow Lang Bei to gather, and rest if you're tired."

Lin Qiu looked at the big black wolf's erect, fluffy ears. He lowered his eyes, quietly hiding the black wolf fur he had accidentally plucked out in his hand.

"I know."

"Mm."

The gathering team parted ways with the hunting team here.

After Lin Qiu recovered from his weakness, he watched the sub-orcs shift back into human form and tighten their animal skin skirt belts; they were all slender-waisted and long-legged, light and lean.

They carried rattan baskets on their backs and were ready to go.

Lang Bei was in front giving instructions to the orcs about what to gather today. Turning back, he saw Lin Qiu looking around and didn't assign him any tasks.

As the orcs in front moved, Lin Qiu followed along.

"Qiu, we are gathering on the grassland today and will also go to the riverside over there. See if there are any plants you want," Lang Bei said as he walked over.

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

The gathering team usually followed the hunting team; if they went to the forest, they gathered in the forest, and if they came to the grassland, they gathered on the grassland.

Lin Qiu watched the orcs scatter and immediately began to search.

The wild vegetables the orcs gathered were varied and numerous; except for wild chives, he didn't recognize most of them.

The plants on the grassland were in full view, tall and short.

Lin Qiu didn't know where to start for a moment, but a quick glance suggested there probably wasn't anything suitable.

He looked at the plants the orcs were gathering and decided to just gather along with them while searching.

Wild chives had a strong smell, and the orcs used to eat them raw, so they didn't like the taste. They had their own types of plants to gather, digging up anything edible.

Lin Qiu observed that the orcs almost habitually ignored the wild chives. Only when there was nothing else nearby would they perfunctorily grab a handful.

Lin Qiu then lagged behind, plucking everything the orcs had left behind.

Pulling wild chives made a crisp sound as the leaves snapped—a "pop"—which was very stress-relieving. Lin Qiu got a bit addicted to pulling them, and since there were many wild chives on the grassland, he soon had half a basket full.

"Qiu."

Lin Qiu was squatting in the grass, pulling happily, occasionally grabbing a nearby weed to examine.

Looking up, he saw a young female orc carrying some grass stems over.

She placed the grass stems in front of Lin Qiu, glanced at the wild chives in his basket, and whispered: "Qiu, these don't taste good."

Lin Qiu didn't know how to explain that he had become addicted to pulling them, so he simply said: "I actually quite like them."

Lang Qing nodded, pointing to the grass stems on the ground: "The captain asked me to find these; they are the kind of grass you mentioned that is hard to pull apart on the grassland."

"Okay, thank you."

Lang Qing smiled at him, bright and beautiful, before running off to gather more.

Lang Qing was a female gray wolf orc, about the same age as the original owner of his body. She was always steady and very good at studying things.

Of all the plants the gathering team collected, besides Lang Bei, she was the only one who could remember them all. So, even though she was young in the gathering team, everyone trusted her.

Lang Bei was also focusing on training her.

There were many insects in the grass. Lin Qiu flicked away one that had crawled onto his ankle and applied some of the insect-repellent powder distributed by the tribe onto himself.

He set his basket down, sat on it, and examined the grass stems Lang Qing had brought.

They were all dwarf weeds, the tallest being no more than an arm's length. Spring grass stems were at their tenderest; they hadn't fully grown yet and were so soft they would break at a touch.

Lin Qiu tried to bend them for a while but couldn't find any that could be used.

The timing was wrong; even if he could find hemp-like plants now, they weren't mature and couldn't be harvested.

In the distance, the orcs of the gathering team had already scattered.

Lin Qiu walked around a bit more; it was no longer early.

The wind slowly picked up on the grassland; it was very strong, blowing his animal skin clothes until they puffed up.

Lin Qiu was submerged in the grass from the knees down, his long hair fluttering in the wind, so he casually picked a blade of grass to tie it up.

Lin Qiu looked out toward the edge of the huge lake that was embedded in the grassland like green jade; the orcs were moving with the grass waves, already chasing the prey.

The wolf pack surrounded the herd of prey, closing in step by step.

The main body of the prey was quietly let out of the encirclement, and the three trapped prey animals were driven to run by the orcs once again.

The encirclement closed, and the three teams had clear divisions of labor.

From afar, it looked like three small circles surrounding a white dot.

The horns of the sharp-horned beasts were extremely dangerous, so the orcs avoided the front and chose to attack from the sides and back.

Lin Qiu looked out and spotted Lang Yan at a glance.

He aimed for the prey's neck, and with a single strike, he tore open the sharp-horned beast's throat.

The surrounding orcs swarmed in at the opening, leaving the fallen sharp-horned beast no chance to get back up.

The wind howled, making it hard for Lin Qiu to keep his eyes open.

The long hair he had casually tied up with a blade of grass came undone again, whipping against his face in the wind, and for a moment, he couldn't see what was happening in the distance.

The orcs were actually very fast at catching prey; the reason it took time was because prey was scarce and needed to be searched for.

Otherwise, with the hunting ability of these wolf orcs, in an era of abundant food, developing into a large tribe would be an easy task.

By the same token, the lack of prey was the biggest blow to them.

Catching the sharp-horned beasts wasn't difficult; in a short while, three of them were carried up.

Only then did Lin Qiu realize why Lang Bei and the others had started gathering in such a rush after arriving—because the hunting team gave them very little time.

However, catching prey also consumed a huge amount of energy for the hunting team's orcs.

At this moment, they threw the prey onto the ground and lay down one after another, unwilling to move.

What they ate in the morning wasn't enough to cover the energy spent running on the road, and after the exertion just now, their stomachs were completely empty.

The gathering team took advantage of their rest period to search around, and their rattan baskets were almost full.

It must be afternoon now; the wind blew clouds to cover the sun.

Staying on the grassland, Lin Qiu felt a bit cold.

He picked up his basket, ready to return with the orcs.

Before long, the gathering team returned, their rattan baskets overflowing. The orcs resting on the ground turned green at the sight.

Seeing that most of what was picked was the long, flat-leafed pungent grass, they all turned their heads and sneezed as if they could smell it.

"Bei, why pick so much pungent grass?! I don't want to eat it!"

Lang Bei: "Qiu likes it."

The wolf orcs who were about to howl a few more times immediately changed their tune: "If Qiu likes it, then pick more."

Lin Qiu heard their conversation and looked at the gathering team's rattan baskets, which were almost entirely filled with large bundles of wild chives.

This made him feel a bit embarrassed.

When Lang Qing asked him earlier, he had just said it casually because it was the only one he recognized.

Lang Yan walked to Lin Qiu's side and whispered: "It's fine. For wolf orcs, green leafy grass is either 'don't like' or 'really don't like'; there isn't any they love to eat."

Lin Qiu's gaze fell on Lang Yan's pointed ears.

"I'll... try to make it taste good."

Lang Yan lay down: "Let's go back; it's going to rain."

As soon as Lang Yan said this, the orcs shook their fur and stood up.

Getting back early meant they could go lie on Wolf Mountain, and even if they were hungry and had a short dream, they could still smell the scent of Lang An and the others cooking meat—that would be a sweet dream.

The gathering team turned around and left first.

The hunting team carried the prey and followed in sequence.

Lin Qiu took two steps, looked at Lang Yan who was still lying on the ground looking at him, and said: "I'll run for a while first."

Lang Yan: "Not hungry yet? You have the strength?"

He shouldn't have said that; as soon as he did, his stomach cramped.

In the end, Lin Qiu sat on Lang Yan's back, holding his neck tightly. The wind was getting stronger now, and Lin Qiu had to bury his face in Lang Yan's fur just to barely keep his eyes open.
chapters.source_text:
林楸沉默地追逐着，渐渐听得自己急促的喘息，知道他的体力有些跟不上了。
狩猎队跟采集队的队员都挑选的是部落里身强体健的兽人，即便是亚兽人，也是耐力好的。
狼贝作为采集队队长，第一个发现林楸的情况。
他们还要跑很一段路，这边没有猎物可以捕捉。
楸这样下去不行。
狼贝跟着慢下来，示意其他兽人先跟上前面的狩猎队。
“楸，坐我身上。”
林楸抬头，看着停在狼群旁侧的黑狼，他也看着这边。
狼贝：“嘿，那王背你。”
狼贝跑开，跟上队伍。
狼岩站在林楸前，即便都是狼形，狼岩也比林楸高上半个脑袋。
他低头，鼻尖碰了碰林楸的耳朵。
林楸耳朵一抖，就看他侧过身，半趴下来。
林楸匆匆忙忙变了人形，穿好背篓里的兽皮衣。没有皮毛遮挡，耳垂已经红了个透。
狼岩：“他们要跑远了。”
林楸哪里敢犹豫，爬上狼岩的背，双手不知道哪里放。
狼岩起身，“趴下，腿夹紧，手抱着我的脖子。”
林楸一声不吭，他说什么就照着做。
“走了。”狼岩道。
“嗯。”
黑狼慢慢跑起来，狼群已经远去，像长在草地里的黑蘑菇。一丛一丛的。
狼岩在慢慢加速，风迅速擦过身侧，林楸几乎睁不开眼睛。
他伏低身子，彻底趴在狼岩的背上。
白皙修长的手指陷入黑色长毛中，几乎被全部藏了起来。脸颊贴着狼毛，有些扎脸，但手指紧紧抓着的狼毛里面却软乎乎的。
几下，狼岩跟上了队伍。
领头的兽人判断着猎物的方向，随时调整着，狼岩知道林楸脸皮薄，只跟在后头。
林楸身子绷得有些累了。
胳膊发酸，腿也夹不紧。
狼岩：“应该快了。”
林楸默默侧脸，鼻尖擦过狼毛，浅浅地呼吸。
“嗯。”
终于，在林楸感觉到后背晒得有些刺疼的时候，兽人们慢慢放缓速度，最后在一个草坡前趴了下来。
林楸已经没劲儿了。
狼岩慢慢走着，靠近兽人们。
林楸脸闷在狼毛里，四肢放松，软趴趴地挂在狼岩身上。
兽人们早见怪不怪。
楸都滚了好几次王的窝里了，他们想提醒，王还警告地看他们。
后头楸都在狼王窝里醒了，知道自己睡着的时候干的事儿，还是没有搬窝。
嗯……他们王的魅力没有兽人可以抵挡。
狼岩在兽人后头停下，趴下来后，林楸侧身往下一滚，身体接触微凉的草丛，躺了几秒，默默坐了起来。
狼岩眼里闪过一丝笑，不敢叫林楸看见。
他脸皮薄。
他盯着远方兽人们发现的猎物群，跟林楸低声说：“跟着狼贝采集，累了就休息。”
林楸看着大黑狼竖起来的大耳朵，毛绒绒的。他垂眸，悄然藏起来手里不小心薅下来的黑色狼毛。
“我知道。”
“嗯。”
采集队就在这里跟狩猎队分开。
林楸缓过了手软脚软之后，看着亚兽人们变回人形，勒紧兽皮裙腰带，一个个腰细腿长，轻盈瘦削。
他们身上挎着藤筐，已经准备就绪。
狼贝在前面跟兽人们交代今天采集的东西，回头见林楸四处张望着，也没给他安排事情。
前面兽人们移动，林楸就跟着走。
“楸，我们今天在草原上采集，也会去那边的河边，你看看有没有你想要的植物。”狼贝走过来道。
林楸：“好。”
采集队一般跟着狩猎队走，去森林，就在森林里采集，来草原，就在草原上采集。
林楸看着兽人们散开，立马开始寻找起来。
兽人们采集的野菜杂且多，除了野韭，其他的他大都不认识。
草原上的植物一览无余，高高低低。
林楸一时间无从下手，不过大致看一眼，应当也没有合适的。
他看了眼兽人们采集的植物，干脆也跟着边采集，边寻找。
野韭味道重，兽人们以前都是生吃，所以不太喜欢这个味道。他们有自己的采集种类，只要能吃就挖。
林楸观察着，兽人们几乎习惯性地忽略野韭。实在附近没其他的了，敷衍性地抓两把。
林楸便落在后面，将兽人们遗落的全掐在手中。
扯野韭有叶片崩断的脆响，啵的一下，很解压。林楸扯得有些上瘾，加上草原上野韭多，不一会儿就积攒了半背篓。
“楸。”
林楸蹲在草丛扯得欢，时不时抓一把附近的野草过来看看。
一抬头，一个年轻雌性兽人抱着些草茎过来。
她将手里的草茎放在林楸身前，看了眼他背篓里的野韭，低声道：“楸，这个不好吃。”
林楸不知怎么解释自己掐上瘾了，索性道：“我还挺喜欢。”
狼清点头，指着地上的草茎道：“队长让我找的，都是草原上你说的那种不好扯断的草。”
“好，谢谢。”
狼清冲着他笑了下，明媚妍丽，又继续跑远采集去了。
狼清是雌性灰狼兽人，跟原身差不多的年纪。素来稳重，很会钻研。
采集队采集的所有植物除了狼贝能记全，就属她能行。所以在采集队中她年纪虽然小，但大家都很信服她。
狼贝也重点在培养她。
草丛里虫子多，林楸看着爬到脚踝上的，随手弹走，又把部落分配的驱虫药粉往身上抹了些。
他将背篓放倒，坐在上面，把狼清拿来的草茎细看。
都是矮生的杂草，最高的不过手臂长。春日的草茎都是最嫩的时候，还没长成，嫩得一折就断。
林楸掰了半晌，挑不出能用的。
时机不对，这会儿就算能找到麻类植物，也并没成熟，还不能采收。
远处，采集队的兽人们已经四散开。
林楸又四处走了走，时间已经不算早了。
草原慢慢起了风，风很大，吹得兽皮衣鼓起来。
林楸膝盖以下淹没在草丛中，长发随风飘逸，叫他随手摘了根草叶扎起来。
林楸远眺着草坡下，那一汪如碧玉嵌入草原的巨大湖泊边缘，兽人们随着草浪移动，已经追逐起来猎物来。
狼群围困住猎物群，步步逼近。
猎物大部队被悄然放跑出包围圈内，被围困的三只猎物再一次被兽人驱逐着跑起来。
包围圈合拢，三队分工明确。
远远看着像三个小圆球围着一个白点。
尖角兽的角极其锋利，兽人们都避开正面，选择侧边与背后攻击。
林楸远眺着，一眼看到狼岩。
他瞄准了猎物的脖子，只一下出击，便勾破了尖角兽的脖子。
围困的兽人们趁空一拥而上，叫倒下的尖角兽没有一丝再爬起来的机会。
风声烈烈，吹得林楸有些睁不开眼睛。
随意用草叶扎起来的长发又散开了，被胡乱吹得打在脸上，一时间再也看不清远方是个什么情景。
兽人们抓捕猎物的速度其实是很快的，之所以耗时，还是猎物稀少需要寻找。
否则照着狼兽人们这捕猎能力，在食物充足的时代，发展成一个大部落是轻而易举的事情。
同样的，猎物缺少，他们受到的打击也是最大的。
抓尖角兽不难，不一会儿，三头尖角兽被扛了上来。
林楸这才知道狼贝他们到了地方之后就匆匆忙忙开始采集，因为狩猎队留给他们的时间太短。
不过抓捕猎物对狩猎队的兽人来说，消耗也巨大。
这会儿把猎物抬上来，往地上一扔，纷纷趴在地上不愿意动了。
早上吃的那点，还不够路上奔跑消耗的，刚刚再一发力，这会儿胃里已经耗得干干净净。
采集队再趁着他们休息这一阵，四处找一找，藤筐里差不多都齐了。
这会儿应该是下午了，风吹得云雾遮住了太阳。
草原上呆着，林楸觉得有些泛冷。
他背起背篓，准备跟兽人们回了。
没一会儿，采集队回来，一个个藤筐里都冒了尖儿。趴地上休息的兽人们看着脸都绿了。
见摘得最多的还是那长扁叶呛草，一个个仿佛闻到味儿似的，偏头冲着一边打喷嚏。
“贝，怎么采这么多呛草？！不想吃！”
狼贝：“楸喜欢。”
还打算嚎两句的狼兽人立马变脸，“楸喜欢，那就多摘。”
林楸听到他们对话，才去看采集队的藤筐，几乎面上都是大捆大捆的野韭。
这一下弄得他有些不好意思。
刚刚狼清问他，他也是随口一说，因为就认识这一种。
狼岩走到林楸身边，低声道：“没事。绿叶草对狼兽人们来说，无非是不喜欢和非常不喜欢，就没有爱吃的。”
林楸目光落到狼岩的尖耳朵上。
“我、试着弄好吃。”
狼岩趴下，“回去吧，要下雨了。”
狼岩这话一出，兽人们也甩一甩毛，站了起来。
早点回去早点去狼山趴着，还能闻着狼安他们煮肉的味儿，就算饿着肚子做个短梦，那也是个美梦。
采集队掉头，先走。
狩猎队扛着猎物，依次跟上。
林楸走了两步，看着还趴在地上冲他望过来的狼岩，他道：“我先跑一会儿。”
狼岩：“还没饿？有力气？”
不说还好，一说胃里抽搐了下。
最后林楸还是坐在了狼岩的背上，他紧紧抱着狼岩脖子。这会儿风越发大，林楸只能将脸藏在狼岩的毛毛里，才能勉强睁眼睛。
chapters.title: 第36章

chapters.translated_text:
They rushed along the way, passing through the grasslands and entering the forest.

The sky outside was gradually turning overcast, and the woods were somewhat dim.

The orc team ran a bit further, and after the orcs let out a few howls, there were responses from the distance.

After merging with the two young orc teams, they picked up speed again and headed toward Wolf Mountain.

Lin Qiu buried his chin into Lang Yan’s fur and asked in a low voice, "What is the name of the orc who always calls out in the hunting team?"

Lang Yan replied, "Lang Huo, the captain of the first hunting squad."

"The hunting team is divided into squads?"

"Yes."

Lang Yan, carrying Lin Qiu, lagged behind, and hearing that Lin Qiu didn't know this, he explained it to him.

The Wolf Tribe’s hunting team had the most members, totaling over sixty orcs. The hunting team was divided into three squads, each with over twenty orcs, led by the strongest orc among them as the captain.

"Lang You, who was injured earlier, is the captain of the first squad. Lang Huo is the captain of the second squad, and there is also Lang Qiao, a gray wolf, who is the captain of the third squad."

"In the past, when we went out, the three squads would separate to look for prey, but now, this group of sharp-horned beasts is the most numerous in the territory. So, everyone came here today to finish the battle quickly."

The division wasn't just for the convenience of catching prey; sometimes when they went out, they needed one or two squads to patrol the territory and drive away orcs from other tribes.

Don't look at how there aren't many prey in their tribal territory; there were still other tribes eyeing it.

The gathering team also had over twenty orcs, all led by Lang Bei. She had been leading them for over twenty years; since they had fewer orcs, they didn't divide into squads.

Lin Qiu’s head rested lightly against the side of Lang Yan’s neck, the two talking in low voices. Because the wolf fur was so long, it looked like they were snuggling intimately.

The orcs in front started to get bored as they ran, looking around.

They wouldn't go hungry tonight, so they felt more relaxed now than when they arrived.

The orcs gathered in small groups, whispering to each other.

"What secret words are the King and Qiu whispering about?"

As the orcs ran, their pace slowed, and those behind rushed up, kicking the buttocks of the black wolves in front.

"Are you moving or not?"

"Awoo! Don't be noisy, let's listen to what the King and Qiu are saying!"

"Saying what?"

The orcs pricked up their ears one by one, slowing down as they ran. Lin Qiu looked over, feeling a bit strange.

The orcs' eyes lit up, and they whispered, "Qiu’s face is so small, the King’s fur covers more than half of it."

"With only his eyes showing, he looks just like a cub."

Lang Yan’s ears twitched, drawing Lin Qiu’s attention, who retracted his gaze to stare at those ears.

The black wolf’s ears were large, covered with a layer of fine, dense fluff.

They should... feel very good to touch.

Lang Yan shot a sharp glance over, causing the fur on the orcs' backs to bristle. They quickly turned their heads and scrambled forward at full speed.

They rushed ahead of the gathering team, startling the orcs in the gathering team who hurriedly asked, "What’s behind us?"

"Awoo? It’s the King," a wolf said, tilting his head.

Lang Bei gave the wolf a swat.

"Why are you tilting your head? You're old enough, do you think you look cute like that?"

The wolf asked, "Am I not cute?"

The young orcs mixed in the crowd giggled and tilted their heads, "Cute, cuter than the cubs."

Adult wolf orcs had thick skin; if they couldn't tell which was a cub, they would just give them a lecture.

The closer they got to Wolf Mountain, the more relaxed the orcs became, though their stamina had reached its limit.

Passing through the woods, they could already see the orcs active in front of Wolf Mountain.

Lang Yan changed from a jog to a walk, and noticing the gaze still lingering on his ears, he turned his head to meet Lin Qiu’s eyes.

"What’s wrong with my ears?"

Lin Qiu’s legs tightened instantly.

"Nothing."

Lang Yan: "...Hmm."

His ears twitched again.

Lin Qiu watched as the orcs in front emerged from the woods, gripping Lang Yan’s fur tighter, "I can get down now."

Lang Yan stopped, "Alright."

"Eh, where’s the King?" the orcs in front looked back.

After a while, Lang Yan walked slowly out of the woods, carrying the basket in one hand and supporting Lin Qiu with the other.

"What happened to Qiu?"

The orcs looked on with concern and all stopped.

Lin Qiu felt embarrassed and subconsciously tightened his grip on Lang Yan, "My legs are numb."

The orcs grinned and were about to say something, but with one sweep of Lang Yan’s gaze, they quickly covered their mouths and ran off.

Upon reaching the front of Wolf Mountain, they flopped onto the ground, closing their eyes and playing dead.

"Shi! An! Hungry..."

Lang Shi had already led his team to welcome them; they were responsible for butchering the prey, while Lang An on the other side led the orcs to start cleaning the pottery pots and making a fire to cook.

It wasn't dark yet outside the forest, but a light rain began to fall.

The orcs had thick fur, so they didn't care and just lay on the ground shouting about being hungry. The raindrops clung to their fur like frosting, and with a slight shake, they were clean again.

The rain remained light, but Lin Qiu wasn't used to sitting outside.

The small amount of fish and greens he’d eaten in the morning had been completely consumed. Lin Qiu went to the stream to wash the medicinal powder off his body and returned to the grass nest in the cave, wrapping himself in animal skins to wait.

Hearing movement, Lang Guo poked his head out from the corner, and seeing Lin Qiu had returned, he came out on tiptoe.

"Qiu," he crouched by Lin Qiu’s grass nest, "did you find the plants you wanted?"

Lin Qiu’s hair was slightly damp on the surface, hanging limply over his shoulders, making him look even more listless.

The afternoon had been overcast, and the prairie wind was quite strong. Lin Qiu had been blown by the wind the whole way back, and now he had a bit of a headache.

Added to his hunger, he felt even worse.

When Lang Guo asked, he only shook his head.

"Where are the cubs?"

Lang Guo replied, "They’re all asleep."

Now that the tribe used large pottery pots to cook food, he saved the time of cooking separately for the cubs, which made things much easier.

"You must have gone to the prairie today; there really aren't many suitable plants there," Lang Guo thought for a moment, "There should be more in the south."

Lin Qiu said, "I'll go take a look next time."

After a while, Lang Yan came in. Seeing Lin Qiu wrapped in animal skins, talking softly to Lang Guo, and looking a bit wilted, he felt concerned.

Lang Yan asked, "Guo, where are the cubs?"

Lang Guo pointed inside the cave, "They’re asleep."

Lang Yan placed the burning wood he was holding into the fire pit in the cave, turning his back to Lin Qiu and Lang Guo, slowly adding firewood to make the fire burn brighter.

He stood up, "The meat soup will be ready soon."

Lang Guo jumped up, "King, please watch the cubs, I’ll be back as soon as I bring the meat soup."

That group of animals was starving; eating meat was a matter of snatching.

Lang Guo ran out like a gust of wind. The fire illuminated the cave walls, and Lang Yan moved aside, letting the firelight fall on Lin Qiu.

He said, "Let's eat in the cave today."

Lin Qiu clutched the edge of the animal skin, his hair loose, his smooth chin buried in the fur of the skin. His cheeks were pale from the wind, and he hadn't recovered yet.

Lang Yan said, "I'll bring it over."

Lin Qiu looked into his eyes, "That's a bother."

The top of his head felt slightly heavy, being rubbed gently twice.

Lang Yan said, "It's no bother."

Outside the cave, the orcs lined up in a long queue.

Lang An and the others were making meat and green vegetable soup tonight; the meat slices were palm-sized, and the greens were added one by one.

Except for the pot for the cubs, which was chopped finer, everything else consisted of large, hearty slices of meat.

It was raining at night, and not making a stew was also to save time.

However, they kept the meat bones; they could wake up a bit earlier tomorrow morning to boil them.

When Lang Yan came out, Lang Mo and the others, who had returned from the western cave, were holding their bowls and looked up to ask, "King, why didn't Qiu come out?"

Lang Yan replied, "He’s not used to going out for the first time, so I let him eat in the cave."

He took his and Lin Qiu’s bowls and lined up behind the other orcs. Four pottery pots were being used to serve the meat and vegetable soup, and it was soon Lang Yan’s turn.

With both pottery bowls in hand, Lang Yan walked with steady steps into the large cave.

Lang Mo stared at him, not forgetting to stuff meat slices into his mouth.

"Qiu is too fragile."

"Wasn't he like that when he was little?"

Lang Mo thought carefully, and in his memory, there seemed to be such a weak little cub. But they weren't in the same batch as Qiu; by the time they could run, Qiu was still... still...

"Eh? Who was Qiu always clinging to when he was little?"

Beside him, Lang Xi tilted his chin toward the figure approaching the cave in the distance, "The King."

"Oh, no wonder."

Lang Mo felt that Qiu’s attitude toward Lang Yan was different from his attitude toward them; so it had been like that since he was small.

Inside the large cave, Lin Qiu sat by the fire, holding his bowl and eating slowly.

The freshly cooked meat and vegetable soup was very hot. Lin Qiu took a sip of the soup, his lips turning a bit red from the heat, looking better than when he was just sitting in the grass nest.

Lang Yan glanced at him, walked further into the cave, and took two pieces of light-furred animal skin from where the skins were kept.

Seeing Lin Qiu looking over, he said, "To make you an animal skin garment."

Lin Qiu retracted his gaze, picked up a piece of green vegetable, bit it gently, his eyebrows carrying a hint of ease and pleasure.

"I haven't found a plant that can be used to make rope yet."

Lang Yan said, "It doesn't matter if you can't find one; you can use vines."

Lin Qiu’s stomach felt warm, the throbbing pain in his head had faded, and his energy had recovered somewhat.

"I still need to find it," he said.

Lang Yan replied, "Hmm."

Lang Yan picked up his own bowl and sat in the cave with Lin Qiu, slowly eating their dinner.

After eating their fill, Lin Qiu went out with Lang Yan to wash the bowls.

The orcs were rubbing their bellies with satisfaction, burping, and stumbling into the caves.

Although they were eating meat and soup together, the amount of meat was the same as before, but being able to fill up on liquid was enough to make the orcs happy.

They put their bowls down like treasures, flopped comfortably into their grass nests, closed their eyes, and went to sleep.

It was still drizzling outside, and as they walked through the grass, their feet were wet.

Lin Qiu hurried to finish washing up and returned to the cave.

He was a bit tired, but since he had been carried by Lang Yan for almost the entire trip there and back, he was doing fine. It was still early, so Lin Qiu cut the animal skin Lang Yan had given him to make a garment.

The skin Lang Yan gave him was a bit thick and rather stiff; Lin Qiu had to put in some effort to poke through it with a stone knife.

A large claw suddenly reached over the edge of the slightly raised grass nest.

It was larger than Lin Qiu’s open palm, and the claws moved. Lin Qiu tentatively handed the animal skin over.

Lang Yan lazily hooked his claw, and a hole was made.

He lifted his claw, his gray eyes still looking over.

Lin Qiu placed the spot where he needed a hole next to the wolf claw, and it was done in a few seconds.

Lin Qiu stared at those exceptionally large claws for a while, his eyes shining, and said softly, "Thank you."

"Hmm," Lang Yan retracted his claw and tucked it against his chest, "Don't stay up too late."

"Okay."

Lin Qiu’s gaze followed him, his fingertips unconsciously stroking the hole made in the animal skin.

Lang Yan said, "It should still be raining tomorrow, don't follow us."

Lin Qiu inadvertently met Lang Yan’s eyes and calmly looked away.

He lowered his head, guiding the strip of animal skin through the holes. The dim, yellowish firelight seemed to melt the ice covering him, making him seem much gentler.

He said in a low voice, "I know."

Lang Yan’s tail swept lightly across the dry grass, and he looked down at the claw tucked against his chest.

He hooked the claw out, then pulled it back in.

A flash of confusion crossed his gray eyes.

What was Qiu looking at just now?
chapters.source_text:
一路奔袭，穿过草地，进入林间。
外面天色渐阴，林子里也有些昏暗。
兽人队伍再往前继续跑了一段，兽人嚎了几句，远处就有回应。
跟两个少年兽人队伍汇合，便又加快速度冲着狼山去。
林楸下巴陷入狼岩的毛毛里，低声问：“狩猎队里总是叫的那个兽人叫什么？”
狼岩：“狼火，狩猎队一队的队长。”
“狩猎队也分小队？”
“嗯。”
狼岩背着林楸落在后头，听林楸不明这些，便跟他讲了下。
狼部落的狩猎队人数最多，一共六十多个兽人。狩猎队分三个小队，一个小队二十多个兽人，由兽人当中最厉害的一个担当队长。
“之前受伤的狼游是一队的队长，狼火是二队队长，还有狼乔，是头灰狼，是三队的队长。”
“以往出来，都是三个队伍分开寻找猎物，但现在领地内只有这边这一群尖角兽最多。所以今天都过来的这边，速战速决。”
分队不只是为了方便抓捕猎物，有时候出来，还需要一队或者两队巡逻领地，驱逐其他部落的兽人。
别看他们部落领地里猎物不多，但也有部落盯着的。
采集队的兽人也有二十多个，都是狼贝带着。她都带了二十几年了，他们兽人少，就没有分什么队。
林楸脑袋虚贴在狼岩颈侧，两个低低说着话。因为狼毛太长，像亲昵地挨在一起。
前头的兽人跑着跑着开始无聊，东张西望的。
今天晚上又不会饿肚子了，这会儿就比来的时候轻松。
兽人们几个一团，交头接耳。
“王跟楸说什么悄悄话呢？”
兽人们跑着跑着步子放慢，后头的冲上来，一脚丫子蹬在前面黑狼的屁股上。
“走不走？”
“嗷！不要吵，听听王跟楸说什么？”
“说什么？”
兽人一个个向后竖起耳朵，跑着跑着就慢了下来。林楸看去，有些奇怪。
兽人们眼睛一亮，悄悄道：“楸的脸好小，王的毛毛都挡了一半多。”
“只露一双眼睛，像幼崽一样。”
狼岩耳朵弹动，叫林楸注意到，收回目光盯着那双耳朵看。
黑狼耳朵很大，覆盖着一层浅而密的绒毛。
应该……摸着很好。
狼岩一道锐利的眼光甩过去，兽人们脊背上的毛毛一炸，飞快转过头，撒开脚丫子往前跑。
一下冲到采集队前面去，吓得采集队里的兽人忙问：“后面有什么？”
“嗷？王啊。”狼歪着脑袋道。
狼贝给了狼一爪子。
“歪什么歪，一把年纪了，以为你这样很乖吗？”
狼：“不乖吗？”
少年兽人们混在一堆里，嘻嘻哈哈歪脑袋，“乖，比幼崽都乖。”
成年狼兽人脸皮可厚，幼崽分不清哪个是幼崽，教训一顿就是了。
越接近狼山，兽人们越轻松，不过体力也已经到了底。
穿过林子，已经能看见狼山前活动的兽人。
狼岩从慢跑变为走，察觉到还落在耳朵上的视线，侧过头，与林楸对视。
“我耳朵怎么了？”
林楸一瞬间双腿夹紧了。
“没什么。”
狼岩：“……嗯。”
他耳朵又动了动。
林楸看着前面的兽人已经钻出林子，抓得狼岩的毛毛紧了紧，“我可以下来了。”
狼岩停下，“好。”
“诶，王呢？”前面的兽人回头看。
没一会儿，狼岩一手拎着背篓，另一只手撑着林楸，慢慢从林子里走出来。
“楸怎么了？”
兽人们目光关切，也都停了下来。
林楸不好意思，下意识紧了紧抓着狼岩的手，“腿麻了。”
兽人们咧嘴，刚要说两句，叫狼岩目光一扫，赶紧捂着嘴巴跑了。
到了狼山前，往地上一趴，闭目装死。
“石！安！饿……”
狼石已经带着队伍迎接了，他们负责杀猎物，另一边的狼安则带着兽人们开始洗干净陶锅，生火做饭。
林子外天还没黑，但下起了小雨。
兽人皮毛厚，也不管不顾地趴在地上喊饿。雨点像糖霜一样沾在毛毛上，稍微一抖，又干净了。
雨势一直很小，但林楸不习惯坐在外面。
只早上吃的那点鱼跟青菜已经消耗一空，林楸去溪边洗干净身上的药粉，回到山洞的草窝里，拥着兽皮等着。
狼果听到动静，从拐角探出个脑袋，见林楸回来了，轻手轻脚出来。
“楸。”他蹲在林楸草窝边，“你找到要的植物了吗？”
林楸表面的头发有些湿，顺毛搭在肩上，显得更没精神。
下午天阴，草原风有些大，林楸回来也吹了一路的风，现在有点头疼。
加上肚子饿，更难受了。
狼果问，他只摇了摇头。
“幼崽呢？”
狼果：“都睡着呢。”
现在部落里用大陶锅做食物，他都省了单独给幼崽做饭的时间，轻松了不少。
“你们今天应该去的草原，那边确实没多少合适的植物。”狼果想了想，“南边应该更多些。”
林楸：“我下次去看看。”
过了会儿，狼岩进来。看林楸披着兽皮，轻声跟狼果说着话，有些蔫。
狼岩：“果，幼崽呢？”
狼果指了指洞内，“睡着了。”
狼岩将手里燃烧的木头往洞中烧火的地方放好，背对着林楸两人，慢慢添柴，将火堆烧得旺些。
他起身，“肉汤要好了。”
狼果噌的一下站起来，“王，你看一下幼崽，我端了肉汤就回来。”
那群牲口饿狠了，吃肉要靠抢。
狼果一阵风似的跑了出去，火堆映亮了洞壁，狼岩往旁边让了让，火光落在林楸身上。
他道：“今天就在山洞里吃吧。”
林楸捏着兽皮边缘，散着发，莹润的下巴陷在兽皮的毛毛里，脸颊被风吹得发白，还没缓过来。
狼岩：“我端过来。”
林楸看着他的眼睛，“麻烦。”
头顶微重，被轻轻揉了两下。
狼岩：“不麻烦。”
山洞外，兽人们排起长队。
狼安他们今天晚上做肉片青菜汤，肉片是巴掌大的，青菜是一颗一颗的。
只除了幼崽吃的那一锅剁得细一些，其他的都是分量十足的大肉片。
晚上下雨，不做炖汤也是为了省时间。
不过肉骨头他们留下来了，等明天早上可以早一点起来熬。
狼岩出来，已经从西边山洞回来的狼莫几个端着自己的碗，抬头问：“王，楸怎么没出来？”
狼岩：“第一次出去不适应，让他在山洞吃。”
他拿着自己跟林楸的碗一起，排在兽人们后头。四口陶锅一起打肉片青菜汤，很快就到了狼岩。
两个陶碗端好，狼岩迈着稳稳的步子进了大山洞。
狼莫盯着看，不忘往嘴里塞肉片。
“楸太脆弱了。”
“他小时候不就是这样。”
狼莫仔细想了想，印象中，似乎有那么一个弱唧唧的幼崽。不过他们都跟楸不是一批的，他们会跑那会儿，楸还在、还在……
“诶？楸小时候总缠着谁来着？”
边上狼西冲着远处往山洞靠近的身影，一抬下巴，“王啊。”
“哦，怪不得。”
狼莫觉得楸对狼岩跟对他们的态度不一样，原来从小就这样。
大山洞中，林楸坐在火堆旁，捧着碗慢慢吃着。
刚出锅的肉片青菜汤很烫，林楸抿了一口汤，唇色被烫得有点红，看起来比刚刚待在草窝里时好了些。
狼岩看了眼，先往山洞里面走，从放兽皮的地方拿了两块浅毛的兽皮出来。
见林楸看来，他道：“给你做兽皮衣。”
林楸收回目光，夹了一根青菜，轻轻咬住，眉梢带着一丝轻松愉悦。
“我还没找到能做绳子的植物。”
狼岩：“找不到也没事，可以用藤条。”
林楸胃里暖和了，头没有抽疼的感觉，精神也恢复了些。
“还是要找到。”他道。
狼岩：“嗯。”
狼岩端起自己的碗，与林楸坐在山洞里慢慢吃着这一顿晚饭。
吃饱了，林楸随着狼岩一起出去洗碗。
兽人们满足地摸着肚子，打着饱嗝，晕乎乎地进山洞里来。
虽说连肉带汤一起吃，肉的分量还是原来那样，但能混个水饱，也足够兽人们欢喜。
宝贝似的将碗一放，舒舒服服地趴进草窝里，闭目，睡觉。
外面依旧下着小雨，草鞋荡过，脚下湿漉漉的。
林楸赶着洗漱完，回到山洞。
他有些累，但一来一回几乎都靠狼岩背着，倒也还好。这会儿还有些早，林楸就把狼岩给的兽皮裁剪好，做兽皮衣。
狼岩给的兽皮有点厚，偏硬，林楸用石刀戳也得费点劲儿。
微微加高的草窝边，忽然伸过来一个大爪子。
比林楸张开手掌还要大些，爪子动了动，林楸试探着将兽皮递过去。
狼岩懒懒地一勾爪，就是一个洞。
爪子抬起，灰眸依旧看过来。
林楸把要打洞的地方放在狼爪边，几下就弄好了。
林楸盯着那格外大的爪爪看了会儿，眼里透着光亮，轻声道：“谢谢。”
“嗯。”狼岩收回爪子，揣在胸口，“别弄太晚。”
“好。”
林楸目光追逐着，指腹无意识摩挲着兽皮上弄出来的洞口。
狼岩：“明天应该还下雨，别跟着去了。”
林楸不经意与狼岩对视上，淡淡收回目光。
他低头，牵引着穿过兽皮的兽皮条。昏黄的火光似融化了罩在他身上的坚冰，好似温和许多。
他低声道：“知道了。”
狼岩尾巴轻轻扫过干草，低头看了眼自己胸口揣着的爪子。
爪子勾出，又收了回去。
灰眸闪过一丝不解。
楸刚刚在看什么？
