Lin Qiu’s basket also contained some hemp. He had intended to show it to the gathering team to let them keep an eye out, but since they weren't there, he had to leave it for now.

From afar came the sound of little wolves fighting. Lin Qiu looked at the excited little wolves huddled together, then at the cubs crawling hard at his feet.

He tightened his pant legs.

Lang An: "The little wolves are still growing and need rest, so they didn't go today."

Compared to the adult beastmen, these little wolves seemed exceptionally energetic.

They couldn't even stay still while lying down, insisting on reaching out their paws to provoke other little wolves. When they fought, they’d end up with a mouthful of fur, and if they couldn't win, they’d just run away with an "awoo" of misery.

Lin Qiu gently pushed aside the cubs at his feet, took a few small Codonopsis roots, and walked into the forest.

The cubs wanted to follow, but Lang Guo blocked them with a long wooden stick.

When the fur ball was thrown again, the cubs chased after it. If they couldn't outrun their companions, they’d use their mouths to bite; big or small, the wolves were all the same.

Once inside the forest, there were quite a few little wolves.

They looked up with dirty faces, then immediately continued digging holes.

Lin Qiu watched them digging for the yams they had dug before and reminded them, "Those are for seeds."

Lang Jin: "..."

He looked up, stiffened his neck, and said very loudly, "We know!"

With a wave of his hand, the little wolves followed him away to find another spot.

Lin Qiu looked over and saw Lang Bing had come too.

The three little wolves were walking with their arms around each other’s shoulders when Lang Rong lost his footing and fell, dragging the other two down with him, landing right in the hole they had just dug.

Lin Qiu raised an eyebrow, looking at the silent pit.

Feeling embarrassed?

He finished planting the herbs and, to save the little wolves some face, returned to Wolf Mountain first.

Lang Jin immediately climbed out, dragging the sullen Lang Bing and the sheepishly smiling Lang Rong.

The three beastmen ran to the spot where Lin Qiu had just been and looked closely.

Lang Jin squatted down and tugged at the vine that had just been planted, "Why is he planting grass?"

Lang Bing looked at the purple fruit vine, lost in thought.

Lang Jin stood up, stared at Lin Qiu’s retreating back, and concluded, "He was definitely laughing at us just now!"

Lang Bing: "You’re overthinking it."

Lang Rong pulled at Lang Jin, who looked like he wanted to fight, "Are we still digging or not?"

Lang Jin: "Of course we’re digging!"

chapters.source_text:
西边。
狼莫带着兽人开窑，林楸在一旁看着，忽然听到一声狼嚎。
声音清脆，有些急促，林楸皱眉看向狼山方向。
狼莫：“小狼在召集同伴，没事。”
窑盖打开，兽人们纷纷往后避开。
热气烘着脸，窑里余温依旧挺高。
这次狼莫做的几乎都是大型陶器，有陶锅、陶罐，还有林楸说的水缸。
狼莫见破碎的少，心里稍稍安定。
他跟林楸道：“你说的砖我们也烧了的，不过窑里装不下，做得不多。”
林楸：“现在用不上，以后可以试试建专门的砖窑。”
“砖窑？怎么建。”
“莫！别说了，快点下去。”狼西道。
陶罐重，得他们自己来搬。
两边窑也是一起烧的，兽人跳下去往上搬，都是大肚罐子，一个十几斤重。
林楸在一旁帮忙，兽人们将罐子往山坡下面递。
“这次烧得挺好。”
经手的五六个罐子都漂亮。
一个窑里不过十个，余下的是林楸说的砖。巴掌大的红砖，一个两三斤重，大小均匀。
兽人们看着新奇，不过捏起来敲了敲，砖就碎了。
狼莫：“这看着就不成。”
“楸，你说说砖窑怎么建？”狼莫还在追问。
兽人这是一头扎烧窑的事上了。
林楸：“我先想想，你们先把部落用的陶制齐吧。”
“这不，齐了。”狼莫靠着身边的大陶缸，笑得看不见眼。
另一边狼石也把窑里的东西全弄出来了，那边都是一样的大缸，陶罐陶锅就少。
林楸：“这么快就好了？”
“那是，也不看看谁……”话没说完，狼西推了他一把。兽人眼下青黑，皮都要垮到嘴角了。
“裂的。”
“嗯？”狼莫立马站直，绷着神经绕着大缸看了好几圈。
狼西一想到还要继续烧，眼神呆滞，“底下。”
狼莫一翻水缸，瞧着下面好大个裂纹，“嗷呜！”一声悲鸣，抓狂地揪住头发。
“啪——”
狼石那边几个缸也碎了。
刚刚一切都是假象。
林楸只能安慰：“其他是好的。”
说实话，比最开始他烧的那两次好了不知多少。不仅陶罐做得匀称，厚薄均匀，大小也如同复制粘贴，非常标准。
对比之前的那几批，这一批算是精品。
林楸好心建议：“要不然休息一阵？”
兽人们烧陶完全是自己给自己加强度，几乎前一批刚烧完，后头一批的泥坯就阴干好了，接着又进窑，继续烧。
狼莫八个兽人，加上狼石，天天待在西边。
算起来其实距离第一次烧窑都过去一个多月了，兽人们雷打不动地忙。中间还时常再轮个夜班，仔细一想，这能不疯吗？
知道这边开窑，狼安带着亚兽人过来。
瞧见地上摆的陶锅陶罐，两眼放光，一个兽人抱两个，又乐乐呵呵地离开。
地上躺尸的护卫队一队的成员们被忽略了彻底。
狼安走了几步，回头笑得十分灿烂，“莫，反正你们有空，再多做些，部落里还想多攒一些以后拿去交换。”
狼莫长啸：“嗷！！！！”
林楸：“……”
现在狼莫他们烧窑已经比林楸厉害，林楸已经帮不上什么忙。
看躺了一地的狼兽人，林楸暂时先不打算琢磨砖窑，给他们增加工作量。
就这么九个兽人，技术骨干，不能在部落起步阶段就搞废了。
凡事慢慢来。
狼莫忽然感觉后背一阵寒。
他慌忙爬起来，手按在地面。
狼西挂他背上，有气无力，“你找什么……”
狼莫：“有水。”
“又没下雨，哪里来的水。”
狼莫：就是啊，又没下雨，躺着为什么后背一凉呢。
中午，狼木一小队的兽人被狼安叫着去河边捞鱼。
鱼笼用得久了，偶尔会坏，但胜在数量多，狼安他们闲来无事又会编着补充，倒也不少。
不过鱼现在好像变聪明了，往笼子里钻的慢慢变少。
两个队伍的小狼脏兮兮地一人扛着根极长的山药从林子里钻出来，大摇大摆，仰着下巴往成年兽人跟前转。
都是这个时候过来的，哪个不知道他们心里想的什么。
狼安惊道：“哎哟，哪里挖的山药，这么大？”
“林子里挖的啊。”
“怎么找的，比狼莫他们之前挖的都好！”
小狼整个人都抻得笔直笔直的，“就随意看见了啊。”
林楸看着一堆小泥人各个跟斗胜的雄鸡似的，脖子都扯得不能再长了。
“好小狼，我给你们做好吃的。”
小狼眼睛一亮，排着队，欢欢喜喜地将山药放一堆。
狼安同样笑眯眯的。
中午有吃的了。
河边，狼金三个看着狼木捞鱼。
笼子拉起来，大鱼少了很多，螃蟹跟河虾倒还是不少。
那大虾不知养了多久，手掌那么长，肉质透明。
三个小狼帮着把笼子里的渔获倒进大陶罐里，脑袋扎在罐口，往里一看，幽幽叹气。
“阿木叔，鱼越来越少了。”
这都起了五个笼子了，才一条大鱼。
狼木：“早上才放下去的笼子，有就不错了。”
狼金直起身，走到河边，“咱不会把河里的鱼捞完了吧。”
正说着呢，几尾半臂长的鱼游荡在河边。
妥妥的挑衅！
狼金眼睛睁大，狼冰屏息，狼溶呆呆看着。
鱼耶……
三个小狼瞬间动起来，你拉我，我挤着你，狼金想伸爪，拼命用屁股抵着后头的两个，狼溶惦记着部落里的规矩，不让靠近河……
“别弄，别弄，要跑了！”
鱼就像逗他们，一甩尾，潇洒地离开岸边。
还慢悠悠的，简直挑衅！
非得抓它不可！
狼金蹦起来就要往里跳，狼冰预料般，霎时抓住他。
狼溶：“跑了跑了！”
“啪——”
水花四溅。
小狼们湿漉漉转头，林楸提起木棍，三条鱼慢慢浮上来，翻了肚子。
“嗷！”小狼捂住头倒吸一口凉气。
林楸：“学会借用工具。”
小狼：“嗷。”
三个傻呆呆的，看着不聪明。
林楸：“捡鱼。”
狼金跟狼溶乖乖蹲下去，捞起鱼。
“给。”两个往前递。
林楸扔了棍子，道：“别靠近河边，杀了，见者有份。”
“嗯？”狼听不懂。
林楸：“还是放罐子里吧。”
两个小狼乐颠颠地跑去放鱼。
林楸侧头看小白狼，狼冰眼睫一抖，“你刚刚在林子里种的……”
“紫果藤。”
“为什么要种？”
林楸往狼山走，狼冰跟着他，没得到答案不罢休。
林楸：“想种就种了。”
狼冰蹙眉，“我们能找到很多。”
狼冰不觉得林楸这个行为只会有一次，林楸做什么都跟狼部落的兽人不一样。
林楸停下，看着他。
他对狼冰的印象，是个不喜欢说话，专注做自己事情的小白狼。
这会儿看，还有点较真。
“你知道狼部落为什么要迁徙吗？”
狼冰：“没食物。”
林楸平静问：“照着现在狼山的情况，你觉得这附近几十年后还会有现在充足的物产吗？”
“是不是又要迁徙？”
狼冰瞳孔一缩。
“你想，定下来。”
林楸诧异，“难不成你们喜欢迁徙？”
狼冰绷着个脸，盯着他。
又不说话了。
林楸不管他，继续往狼山走。狼冰又跟着，跟山洞里那些跟脚的幼崽一个样。
“光靠种植草药……”狼冰有些急切，好像明白林楸的意思了，但又不知道他要具体怎么做。
偏偏以前看不惯他，又不好意思问。
林楸：“部落不是已经在做了？尾巴草。”
狼冰气闷，偏就不明白跟他说！
他抓心挠肺的，长长的白发辫子甩开在身后，追赶到林楸身边，气鼓鼓道：“哪有那么简单！”
林楸：“……”
不喜欢跟小孩交流，累得慌。
非得刨根问底，他们又不熟。
林楸不愿意说话了。
*
“楸，你跟冰说什么呢？站那儿半晌不动了。”狼安几个兽人围在一块儿，手上削着山药皮。
林楸在一旁帮忙，道：“就说了些种草药的事儿。”
“草药还能种？”
“能，尾巴草都能种。”
亚兽人们点点头，“有道理。”
然后就不再问了。
看看，多简单的沟通，一点不费心力和情绪。
兽人们不关心种不种药草，也不习惯去想那些对他们来说很遥远的未来，兽人们的眼里只有眼下。
今天吃什么？
明天能抓到猎物吗？
仅此而已。
环境影响人，兽人每天都需要花费大量的精力为食物奔波，吃饱就是此刻最大的事儿。
而狼冰很聪明，也是个会思考的小狼。
他是下一任祭司人选，性子拗，想得多，但对于林楸来说，不想交流。
跟别扭又聪明的小狼说话，很累……
“冰，你要抓鸟吗？”
狼冰看着肩膀上搭来的脏兮兮的手臂，往边上一侧，“什么抓鸟？”
狼金嘿嘿笑，“你在这儿当树啊，一直不动。”
“想什么呢？”
狼冰看着两个小伙伴，道：“你们说，我们要是在附近种很多很多草药，很多很多尾巴草，以后就能吃饱？”
狼金两条粗粗的眉毛一竖，“你闲着没事儿做？”
狼溶倒是思考了下，“不行，要打猎呢，种不了那么多。”
“一点一点种呢？”
“诶？”狼金的黑爪子往狼冰头上招呼，被一巴掌打开。
“你是不是生病了，种草药干什么，那么难吃。你要喜欢，我现在叫祭司给你熬几碗。”
他说着真要去。
狼溶把他拉住，三个小狼围着坐在一起。
狼金鼓着眼睛，像个青蛙，双手抱胸。
他搞不懂小伙伴脑子抽什么筋，他总跟不上他的想法。
还有，明明为他好，还打他！
他生气了！
chapters.title: 第42章
chapters.translated_text:
The west side.

Lang Mo was leading the orcs in opening the kiln when Lin Qiu, who was watching from the side, suddenly heard a wolf howl.

The sound was sharp and somewhat urgent; Lin Qiu frowned and looked toward the direction of Wolf Mountain.

Lang Mo: "The little wolves are calling their companions, it's nothing."

The kiln cover was opened, and the orcs stepped back one after another.

Hot air brushed against their faces; the residual heat inside the kiln was still quite high.

This time, Lang Mo had made mostly large pottery, including clay pots, jars, and the water vats Lin Qiu had mentioned.

Seeing that there were few broken pieces, Lang Mo felt slightly relieved.

He said to Lin Qiu, "We also fired those bricks you mentioned, but the kiln couldn't hold much, so we didn't make many."

Lin Qiu: "We don't need them right now, but we can try building a dedicated brick kiln in the future."

"A brick kiln? How do you build one?"

"Mo! Stop talking and get down here quickly," Lang Xi said.

The pottery jars were heavy, and they had to move them themselves.

The kilns on both sides had been fired together. The orcs jumped down to move the items up; they were all big-bellied jars, each weighing over ten jin.

Lin Qiu helped from the side as the orcs passed the jars down the hillside.

"They fired quite well this time."

The five or six jars he handled were all beautiful.

There were no more than ten in a kiln, and the rest were the bricks Lin Qiu had mentioned. They were palm-sized red bricks, each weighing two or three jin, and uniform in size.

The orcs found them novel, but when they squeezed and tapped them, the bricks crumbled.

Lang Mo: "This doesn't look like it will work."

"Qiu, tell me, how do you build a brick kiln?" Lang Mo was still pestering him.

These orcs had really thrown themselves into the business of firing kilns.

Lin Qiu: "Let me think about it first. You guys should finish making the pottery the tribe needs."

"But we're done," Lang Mo said, leaning against a large pottery vat nearby, grinning so hard his eyes disappeared.

On the other side, Lang Shi had also cleared everything out of his kiln; that side was full of the same large vats, with fewer pottery jars and pots.

Lin Qiu: "It's done so quickly?"

"That's right, don't look at who..." Before he could finish, Lang Xi pushed him. The orc had dark circles under his eyes, and his skin seemed to sag toward the corners of his mouth.

"It's cracked."

"Hmm?" Lang Mo stood up straight immediately, tensing his nerves as he circled the large vat several times.

Thinking about having to fire them again, Lang Xi’s eyes went dull, "The bottom."

Lang Mo flipped the water vat over and saw a huge crack on the bottom. "Awoo!" he wailed in misery, frantically pulling at his hair.

"Snap—"

Several vats on Lang Shi's side also shattered.

Everything just now had been an illusion.

Lin Qiu could only offer comfort: "The others are fine."

To be honest, it was much better than the first two times he had fired them. Not only were the jars symmetrical and uniform in thickness, but their sizes were also as consistent as if they had been copy-pasted—very standard.

Compared to the previous batches, this one could be considered high quality.

Lin Qiu kindly suggested: "Why not take a break for a while?"

The orcs were completely overworking themselves with the pottery firing. Almost as soon as one batch was finished, the mud blanks for the next were already air-dried, and they would immediately go into the kiln to be fired again.

Lang Mo's eight orcs, plus Lang Shi, stayed on the west side every single day.

Counting it up, it had actually been over a month since the first kiln firing, and the orcs had been working tirelessly without fail. They even frequently rotated night shifts; when you thought about it, how could they not be going crazy?

Knowing that the kiln was being opened, Lang An brought the sub-orcs over.

Seeing the pottery pots and jars laid out on the ground, their eyes lit up; each orc grabbed two and left happily.

The members of the first guard squad lying like corpses on the ground were completely ignored.

Lang An walked a few steps, then turned back with a brilliant smile, "Mo, since you have time, make some more. The tribe wants to save up more to use for trade later."

Lang Mo let out a long howl: "AWOOO!!!!"

Lin Qiu: "..."

By now, Lang Mo and the others were better at firing kilns than Lin Qiu, and he couldn't really help much anymore.

Looking at the wolf-orcs lying all over the ground, Lin Qiu decided not to think about the brick kiln for now and add to their workload.

With only these nine orcs—the technical backbone—they couldn't be burned out during the tribe's early development phase.

Everything should be done slowly.

Lang Mo suddenly felt a chill on his back.

He scrambled up in a panic, pressing his hands to the ground.

Lang Xi hung on his back, listless, "What are you looking for..."

Lang Mo: "There's water."

"It hasn't rained, where would there be water?"

Lang Mo: That's right, it hasn't rained, so why did his back feel cold while lying down?

At noon, Lang Mu's squad of orcs was called by Lang An to go to the river to catch fish.

The fish cages had been used for a long time and occasionally broke, but they were good because there were so many of them. Lang An and the others would weave more to replenish them when they had free time, so there were quite a few.

However, the fish seemed to have become smarter, and fewer and fewer were swimming into the cages.

The little wolves from both teams emerged from the forest, each carrying an extremely long yam, looking dirty and swaggering, chins held high as they circled the adult orcs.

Everyone came over at this time; who didn't know what they were thinking?

Lang An exclaimed: "Oh my, where did you dig up these yams? They're so big!"

"Dug them in the forest."

"How did you find them? They're even better than the ones Lang Mo and the others dug before!"

The little wolf stretched himself straight, "Just saw them by chance."

Lin Qiu looked at the pile of little mud-covered figures, each like a victorious rooster, their necks stretched as far as they could go.

"Good little wolves, I'll make you something delicious."

The little wolves' eyes lit up, and they lined up, happily placing the yams in a pile.

Lang An was also smiling.

There was food for lunch.

By the river, Lang Jin and the other two watched Lang Mu catch fish.

When the cages were pulled up, there were far fewer big fish, but there were still plenty of crabs and river shrimp.

The big shrimp had been growing for who knows how long; they were as long as a palm, and their flesh was translucent.

The three little wolves helped pour the catch from the cages into a large pottery jar, sticking their heads into the opening, and sighed gloomily after one look.

"Uncle Mu, there are fewer and fewer fish."

They had pulled up five cages, and there was only one big fish.

Lang Mu: "These cages were only put in this morning; it's good enough that there's anything at all."

Lang Jin straightened up and walked to the riverbank, "We aren't going to fish the river dry, are we?"

Just as he was speaking, several fish half an arm's length long swam by the riverbank.

It was a blatant provocation!

Lang Jin's eyes widened, Lang Bing held his breath, and Lang Rong stared blankly.

Fish...

The three little wolves moved instantly, pulling and shoving each other. Lang Jin wanted to reach out his claws, desperately pushing his backside against the two behind him, while Lang Rong worried about the tribe's rules against getting too close to the river...

"Don't move, don't move, they're going to run away!"

The fish seemed to be teasing them, flicking their tails and swimming away from the bank with grace.

They were even moving slowly—it was practically a provocation!

They had to catch them!

Lang Jin jumped up, ready to dive in, but Lang Bing, as if anticipating it, grabbed him instantly.

Lang Rong: "They're gone, they're gone!"

"Splash—"

Water sprayed everywhere.

The little wolves turned their heads, dripping wet, to see Lin Qiu lift a wooden stick. Three fish slowly floated to the surface, bellies up.

"Awoo!" The little wolves gasped, covering their heads.

Lin Qiu: "Learn to use tools."

Little wolves: "Awoo."

The three of them looked silly and not very bright.

Lin Qiu: "Pick up the fish."

Lang Jin and Lang Rong obediently squatted down and scooped up the fish.

"Here." The two handed them forward.

Lin Qiu threw the stick and said, "Don't get close to the riverbank. Kill them; everyone who sees them gets a share."

"Hmm?" The wolves didn't understand.

Lin Qiu: "Better put them in the jar."

The two little wolves ran off happily to put the fish away.

Lin Qiu turned his head to look at the little white wolf. Lang Bing's eyelashes flickered, "What you planted in the forest just now..."

"Purple fruit vines."

"Why plant them?"

Lin Qiu walked toward Wolf Mountain, and Lang Bing followed him, refusing to give up until he got an answer.

Lin Qiu: "I planted them because I wanted to."

Lang Bing frowned, "We can find plenty."

Lang Bing didn't think this behavior of Lin Qiu's would only happen once; everything Lin Qiu did was different from the orcs of the Wolf Tribe.

Lin Qiu stopped and looked at him.

His impression of Lang Bing was that of a little white wolf who didn't like to talk and focused on doing his own thing.

Looking at him now, he seemed a bit serious.

"Do you know why the Wolf Tribe migrates?"

Lang Bing: "No food."

Lin Qiu asked calmly: "Given the current situation of Wolf Mountain, do you think there will still be as much abundant produce nearby in a few decades?"

"Will you have to migrate again?"

Lang Bing's pupils shrank.

"You want to settle down."

Lin Qiu was surprised, "Don't tell me you guys like migrating?"

Lang Bing kept a straight face, staring at him.

He stopped talking again.

Lin Qiu ignored him and continued walking toward Wolf Mountain. Lang Bing followed him, just like the cubs in the cave who would follow at his heels.

"Just relying on planting herbs..." Lang Bing was a bit anxious, as if he understood what Lin Qiu meant, but didn't know exactly how he intended to do it.

Yet, having looked down on him before, he felt embarrassed to ask.

Lin Qiu: "Isn't the tribe already doing it? Tail grass."

Lang Bing felt stifled; he just didn't understand why he wouldn't explain it to him!

He felt frustrated, his long white braided hair swinging behind him as he caught up to Lin Qiu and said indignantly, "It's not that simple!"

Lin Qiu: "..."

He didn't like communicating with children; it was exhausting.

They had to get to the bottom of everything, and they weren't even close.

Lin Qiu didn't want to talk anymore.

*

"Qiu, what are you and Bing talking about? You've been standing there for a long time without moving." Lang An and a few other orcs were gathered together, peeling yams.

Lin Qiu helped from the side, saying, "Just talked about planting some herbs."

"Herbs can be planted?"

"Yes, even tail grass can be planted."

The sub-orcs nodded, "That makes sense."

And then they stopped asking.

See, what simple communication; it didn't take any effort or emotion at all.

The orcs didn't care about planting herbs, nor were they used to thinking about a future that seemed very distant to them; the orcs only had the present in their eyes.

What to eat today?

Can we catch prey tomorrow?

That was all.

The environment influenced people; the orcs had to spend a great deal of energy every day struggling for food, so being full was the most important thing at the moment.

But Lang Bing was very smart and also a little wolf who knew how to think.

He was the candidate for the next priest, stubborn in nature and prone to overthinking, but for Lin Qiu, he didn't want to communicate.

Talking to a stubborn and smart little wolf was very tiring...

"Bing, do you want to catch birds?"

Lang Bing looked at the dirty arm draped over his shoulder and shifted to the side, "Catch what birds?"

Lang Jin laughed, "You're acting like a tree here, not moving at all."

"What are you thinking about?"

Lang Bing looked at his two companions and said, "Do you think if we planted lots and lots of herbs and lots and lots of tail grass nearby, we could be full in the future?"

Lang Jin's two thick eyebrows stood up, "Do you have nothing better to do?"

Lang Rong thought about it for a moment, "No, we have to hunt; we can't plant that much."

"What if we plant a little bit at a time?"

"Eh?" Lang Jin's black claws reached for Lang Bing's head but were slapped away.

"Are you sick? Why plant herbs? They taste so bad. If you like them, I'll tell the priest to boil a few bowls for you right now."

He said it as if he were really going to do it.

Lang Rong pulled him back, and the three little wolves sat together in a circle.

Lang Jin's eyes bulged like a frog's, his arms crossed over his chest.

He couldn't understand what was wrong with his friend's brain; he could never keep up with his thoughts.

Also, he was clearly trying to be nice to him, and yet he hit him!

He was angry!

chapters.title: 第43章
chapters.translated_text:
Lang Rong asked, "Bing, what are you thinking about?"

Lang Bing looked toward the pile of orcs at Lin Qiu, who was quietly peeling skins, looking completely harmless.

He was so gentle to them, yet ignored him.

Lang Bing slowly tightened his face, unhappy.

In his head, he kept replaying the scene Lin Qiu had described: countless foxtail grasses, endless medicinal herbs.

If they could settle on Wolf Mountain for generations, they wouldn't need to forage, only hunt for prey...

What if, what if the prey could also be raised by them? Then maybe the separated branch tribes could return.

Lang Bing's breathing became shallow.

But they had already planted as large a patch of foxtail grass as possible, and it was only enough to last half the snow season.

There were so many orcs, how could that be possible?

"Bing..."

Two faces leaned in, both filled with worry.

Lang Bing took a deep breath and clenched his fists, "I think Lang Qiu is amazing."

Lang Rong: "Hmm?"

He didn't understand.

Lang Jin: "He needs the King to carry him whenever he goes out hunting, how is he amazing..." He accidentally shouted too loudly, and Lang Rong quickly covered his mouth.

Lin Qiu’s knife paused, cutting a notch into the yam.

To the other orcs, it seemed as if he hadn't heard, and he continued to meticulously peel the yam.

However, to Lang An, the peel seemed a bit thick; there wasn't much of the yam core left.

But it didn't matter, the little wolves dug up plenty of yams.

Lang An looked toward the little wolves and frowned, saying, "I'll go take a look."

Lang Jin: "Mmph mmph mmph!"

Lang Rong watched Lang An approach, pulled back his hand, and warned, "Don't talk nonsense."

He let go, and Lang Jin sat properly.

"I wasn't talking nonsense, everyone saw it, it's a fact that Qiu is weak... Ouch!"

"A fact?" Lang An withdrew his palm, "I think you're the one who looks like a fact."

Lang Jin sought help from his companions.

But one pretended to be obedient, the other was lost in thought, so he got hit twice more.

And Uncle Lang An was supposed to be the gentlest!

Now he was protecting Lang Qiu!

"You're full now, do you want to be grounded like your Uncle Lang Mu?"

Lang Rong raised his slightly pale face, looking refined and like a likable, well-behaved child. "Uncle An, it was all Lang Jin's words. He also said Qiu always keeps a cold face and doesn't look like a good wolf at all."

"You!"

A gust of wind struck, and Lang Jin quickly covered his forehead.

"Ouch!"

Lang An pinched the little wolf's face, "You think covering it stops me from hitting you? I'm warning you, watch your mouth. If your King hears you, hmph hmph..."

Lang Jin wilted, "I didn't say anything..."

Lang Rong nodded, "I'll testify."

"You were the one stoking the fire just now!"

The two started fighting, and Lang An glanced suspiciously at Lang Bing, who was still lost in thought, before walking away slowly.

Returning to the stream, Lang An said, "The little wolves are ignorant, they're just full and bored."

Qiu went out to help the tribe find things, so what if the King carried him? If they talked him into quitting, they’d only be eating these few types of stewed soup from now on.

"Qiu, how should we eat this later?" Lang An asked with a kindly smile.

Lin Qiu: "How about grilled fish?"

*

All the small clay pots in the tribe were brought out.

The grilled fish Lin Qiu spoke of was different from what they had imagined.

Originally, they would just grill the fish over the fire and place it on top of various wild vegetables.

In the large clay pot, hot oil was heated, and on top of the already charred and fragrant fish, various seasonings were added: green onions, ginger, garlic, Sichuan peppercorns, and a type of yellow fruit.

As the oil sizzled, the overpowering aroma made the wolf orcs sneeze repeatedly.

All the little wolves were attracted, and even if their noses felt uncomfortable, they refused to leave.

Lang Jin’s chopsticks clattered as he tried to pick up food, swallowing hard and leaning over to look into the clay pot.

"Achoo! Is it ready yet, is it ready?"

Lang An was also tempted, but he had to maintain the appearance of an adult wolf in front of the little ones.

He blocked the little wolves and checked the fire under each clay pot, nearly falling in from the fragrance wafting from the pots.

He swallowed his saliva, "Not yet, the fire was just lit."

It wasn't easy to put clay pots on the stove, so they used stones to build simple small hearths. At this moment, the fire under the pots was roaring, and the oil inside was bubbling.

Green onions, ginger, wild garlic, peppercorns, and some chopped wild vegetables used for seasoning—the longer they boiled, the more intense and pungent the aroma became.

"Lang An, An! Hungry!!!" The orcs were rolling around in impatience.

"Stop shouting!"

The few who were cooking, including Lang An, weren't doing much better. They guarded the two small clay pots, frequently turning their heads away for fear that they would reach in if they lost focus for a second.

"Qiu, can we eat it now?" Lang An asked with restraint.

"Qiu! Uncle Qiu! Can we eat it now?"

Lang Jin ran to Lin Qiu’s side holding his bowl, calling him "Uncle Qiu" more affectionately than he would his own father.

Lang Rong pursed his lips, swallowed his saliva, and looked at his companion in astonishment.

No way, he didn't like the guy just a moment ago, and now he’s changed his tune?

Lang Bing commented coldly: "Shameless."

Lang Rong continued to swallow and nodded vigorously.

"But, it really smells so good..."

Lin Qiu glanced at the little wolves, who were acting like they were standing on hot coals, and said, "Want to eat?"

"Yeah, yeah!" It wasn't just Lang Jin; all the little wolves, who knew they could only eat the grilled fish if Lin Qiu nodded, surrounded him, so hungry they were nearly crying.

Lin Qiu: "I let your King carry me, and you're not convinced?"

"Convinced! Convinced!"

"That was Lang Jin, it has nothing to do with us!"

"We're happy to have the King carry you for as long as you want!"

"If the King doesn't want to, we'll tie him up! Uncle Qiu, hungry..."

Lin Qiu looked cold and aloof, appearing to be a serious person, but sometimes he had a bit of a mischievous streak.

Seeing the little wolves were truly about to cry, Lin Qiu coughed lightly. Seeing Lang An and the others looking at him with the same longing, he couldn't tease them anymore.

He said: "Five orcs per small clay pot."

As soon as he finished speaking, even Lang Mo and the others sat down properly.

"One bowl of mashed yam per person to eat with it." No rice, so this had to do for now.

Everyone was well-behaved, but in reality, they quickly scooped up their yam with their bowls and stared intently at Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu: "Eat slowly, let the clay pot cook it so the flavors soak in; it tastes better."

Lin Qiu looked at the clay pot in front of him, the oily soup soaking into the fish meat, and the vegetables were about done. He said, "Eat."

Clatter, clatter—the chopsticks clashed.

The little wolves quickly reached into the clay pot with their chopsticks, their bowls piled high, yet they continued to dig into the pot.

Lin Qiu watched silently, thinking: It seems unrealistic to expect everyone to eat grilled fish quietly at a time like this.

Not until the grilled fish in the pot was finished did the little wolves grunt at each other, turn their backs, and shovel food into their mouths.

They were fighting over the vegetables as if they were sworn enemies.

The grilled fish was already crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, and with the hot oil, the aroma of the spices soaked into the meat. Even though it hadn't been cooked for long, it had flavor.

After the first bite, the orcs froze.

They looked at their bowls, then at the clay pot that had been picked clean except for the soup. They grabbed it and poured the last bit into their bowls.

"Awoo awoo!" They didn't let go even though it burned their hands.

Lin Qiu: "..."

"Maybe I shouldn't make this next time."

"Awoo awoo awoo!!!" They were burying their heads in their food, unable to speak clearly.

Fearing Lin Qiu wouldn't make it again, they quickly swallowed what was in their mouths and said urgently:

"You have to make it!"

"Make it!"

What does it feel like to be hungry to the point of tears?

It was exactly how everyone looked right now.

It was clearly fish they were already tired of eating, but how did it suddenly taste so good after being grilled, topped with various herbs, and drizzled with oil? Wow!

It was delicious enough to meet the Beast God!

The complex aromas of various seasonings mixed together, fighting on their tongues, making them want to swallow their own tongues along with the food.

Crunch, crunch—

The little wolves were chewing the fish bones dry.

"So good... awoo awoo..." It was hard to describe with words; everything turned into unconscious "awoo" exclamations.

Lin Qiu bit into a piece of fish and savored the taste.

There weren't many seasonings, but the freshness of the fish made up for it.

The herbs used were all fresh ones found directly in the fields, and their flavors were already extremely rich. It was normal for the little wolves to be shocked by their first meal with such complex seasonings.

Lang An swallowed the fish in his mouth, leaned toward Lin Qiu, and couldn't help but ask: "Qiu, which other spices are you looking for? I'll tell Lang Bei and the others to help find them."

It was too delicious; Lang An couldn't help but snatch another piece.

He couldn't keep his mouth idle; the moment he did, he started drooling.

Qiu even said the seasonings were insufficient and might not taste good, but this was delicious enough to meet the Beast God, okay?

Look at the little wolves; their heads were buried in their bowls.

Hearing the conversation, the little wolves’ ears perked up, and they quickly said affectionately: "Uncle Qiu, we can help you find them."

"Yeah, mmph!"

"We'll find them!"

As the little wolves spoke, they quickly winked at their captain.

Lang Bing silently ate more than half, mashed yam in his mouth, licked his lips, and said with slight reserve: "We'll find them."

Lin Qiu: "Alright."

...

The Priest's cave.

The old priest had his own clay pot, slowly enjoying his lunch. Hearing the little wolves fawning over Lin Qiu below, he snorted, peeled a large shrimp shell, and ate it with satisfaction.

The little wolves were never convinced by anything, yet a single meal of grilled fish bought them off.

Truly pathetic!

After a while, hearing footsteps coming up the mountain, the old priest immediately scraped what was left in his clay pot into his bowl and ate it quickly.

"Priest." Lang Bing entered.

Seeing the old orc with his own clay pot, a flash of light appeared in his eyes, but after getting closer and seeing the pot was clean, he pursed his lips and stayed away from him.

"It’s hard to get a day off, what are you doing running up here?"

Lang Bing: "I want to take the little wolves to plant medicinal herbs."

The priest put down his bowl, "The tribe doesn't lack medicinal herbs; just foraging is enough."

He sighed and said: "If the market were still open like before, then we could plant some."

Not all tribes had priests.

Some tribes had lost their heritage and had no priest to treat illnesses, so they always had to pay a huge price to get help from another tribe's priest.

In the past, when the market was still open, he could sell prepared medicinal powders and trade them for food. But now, that wasn't possible...

Lang Bing listened to the priest’s words, thought for a moment, and shook his head.

"I want to plant some that we use often, just to try. If it works, we won't have to spend energy foraging in the future."

The freed-up manpower could do other things for the tribe. Like making pottery, building sheds, and perhaps other things...

Qiu still needed to find seasonings and grass for making rope; Lang Bing felt he could do many, many more things.

Their tribe wouldn't stay in the status quo forever.

Under Qiu’s influence, the tribe had come alive.

The old priest: "If you want to plant, then plant."

He was old and couldn't do much, but he was happy to see the lifeless tribe flowing again.

"Where's Qiu?"

"Sleeping."

Lang Bing thought of the orc who had gone into the large cave and laid down in the grass nest after eating the fish...

"Qiu is still very weak, should we give him some more medicinal herbs?"

The old priest glared, "Are medicinal herbs things you can just eat whenever?"

Lang Bing pursed his lips. He was just worried; Qiu was really, really weak. His physical strength couldn't even compare to their group of little wolves.

The tribe still needed him.

Lang Bing looked at the leftover grilled fish in the old priest's bowl and licked his lips again.

He wasn't greedy.

He was just concerned about his fellow tribesman.
chapters.source_text:
狼溶道：“冰，你在想什么？”
狼冰看向兽人堆里，安静削皮，没有一点攻击性的林楸。
对他们那么温和，对自己爱答不理。
狼冰慢慢绷着脸，不高兴。
他现在脑袋里不停地跟着林楸描绘的情景发展，数不清的尾巴草，无数的草药。
世世代代狼山定居，不用采集，只需要抓猎物……
要是，要是猎物也能靠他们自己养呢？那分开的支部落是不是就能回来。
狼冰呼吸都轻了。
可他们已经尽最大可能种那么大一块地的尾巴草，不也只够吃半个雪季。
兽人就这么多，哪里可能呢？
“冰……”
眼前凑过来两张脸，都是担忧。
狼冰深吸一口气，握紧拳头，“我觉得，狼楸很厉害。”
狼溶：“嗯？”
没明白。
狼金：“他出去捕猎都要王背，哪里厉害……”一不小心嚷嚷大声了，狼溶忙堵住他嘴巴。
林楸刀一顿，将山药切下一道口子。
其他兽人看来，他仿佛没听见，依旧细致地给山药削皮。
不过那皮在狼安看来有些厚了，山药芯都没多少了。
但也没事，小狼挖的山药多。
狼安看向小狼那边，压着眉头道：“我去看看。”
狼金：“唔唔唔！”
狼溶看着狼安过来，收回手，警告：“不许乱说。”
他松开，乖乖坐好。
“我才没乱说，大家都看见了，本来楸很弱就是事实……嗷！”
“事实？”狼安收回巴掌，“我看你才像事实。”
狼金求助小伙伴。
结果一个装乖，一个出神，就他又挨了两下。
明明狼安叔最温柔的！
现在都护着狼楸！
“现在吃饱了，还想跟你们狼木叔一样关禁闭？”
狼溶扬起略白的脸，斯斯文文，是讨人喜欢的乖孩子样。“阿安叔，都是狼金一个人说的。他还说楸总冷着脸，一看就不是好狼。”
“你！”
手风袭来，狼金飞快捂着脑门。
“嗷！”
狼安捏住小狼的脸，“捂着我就打不到了？我可警告你，嘴巴别乱说，要是叫你们王听见了，哼哼……”
狼金蔫巴，“我没说什么……”
狼溶点头，“我作证。”
“那你刚刚拱火！”
两人打起来，狼安疑惑看了眼旁边还在出神的狼冰，慢悠悠走了。
回到溪边，狼安道：“小狼不懂事，吃饱了撑的。”
楸那是出去帮部落找东西，王背一背怎么了，要是说得楸不干了，他们以后就只吃这几样炖汤去。
“楸，等会儿怎么吃？”狼安笑得和蔼可亲。
林楸：“烤鱼怎么样？”
*
部落里的小陶锅都拿了出来。
林楸说的烤鱼与他们料想的不一样。
原本照旧是将鱼在火上烤一烤，然后就放在了铺满了各种野菜上面。
那大陶锅里热油一烧，本就焦香的鱼肉上又铺了各式各样的调料，葱姜蒜花椒，还有一种黄色的果子。
那油一激，霸道的香味刺激得狼兽人们直打喷嚏。
小狼全被吸引了过来，就是鼻子不舒服，也赖着不走。
狼金筷子夹得哒哒响，拼命咽口水，探头往陶锅里看。
“阿嚏！好了没，好了没？”
狼安也馋，但在小狼面前得有成年狼的样子。
他挡开小狼，看了看各个小陶锅底下的火，被锅里的香味扑得快栽进去。
他咽了咽口水，“没好，火才点燃。”
灶上不好放小陶锅，所以直接用石头简易搭了的小灶来。此时锅底下火烧起来，锅里油汪汪的，鼓着泡泡。
葱姜野蒜花椒，还有些断成截的有调味作用的野菜，煮得越久，味道愈发的浓烈扑鼻。
“狼安，安！饿！！！”兽人急得打滚。
“别喊了！”
狼安几个做饭的也没好到哪里去，守着面前两口小陶锅，频频别开头，就怕一个走神就伸了手进去。
“楸，能吃了吗？”狼安克制着问。
“楸！阿楸叔！能吃了吗？”
狼金捧着碗跑到林楸身边，阿楸叔的喊得比亲爹都亲热。
狼溶抿唇，咽了咽口水，错愕地看着自己的小伙伴。
不是，刚刚还看不上人家，现在就变脸了？
狼冰冷声点评：“不要脸。”
狼溶继续咽口水，狠狠点头。
“可是，真的好香啊……”
林楸扫了眼边上跟烫脚似的小狼，道：“想吃？”
“嗯嗯！”不止狼金一个，都知道只有林楸点头才能吃烤鱼的小狼全围在他身边，馋得快哭了。
林楸：“我让你们王背，你们不服？”
“服！服！”
“狼金说的，不管我们的事！”
“让王背你多久，我们都乐意！”
“王不愿意我们把他绑过来！阿楸叔，饿……”
林楸脸上清清冷冷，看着是个正经人，但有时候也有点恶趣味。
见小狼真快哭了，林楸轻咳一声，在狼安几个用同样的渴求目光看来时，不好再逗了。
他道：“一口小陶锅五个兽人。”
话落，连带狼莫几个都坐好了。
“一人一碗山药泥，就着吃。”没米饭，只能先这样了。
大家规规矩矩，实则飞快地捧着自己的碗盛了山药，然后紧盯林楸。
林楸：“慢慢吃，得让陶锅煮得入味儿，更好吃。”
林楸看了眼面前的陶锅，油汤浸入鱼肉，菜也差不多，道：“吃吧。”
噼里啪啦，筷子打架。
小狼飞快往陶锅里伸筷子，碗里堆得高高的，还继续往锅里捞。
林楸默默看着，想：这个时候让大家安安静静吃个烤鱼好像不现实。
直到锅里烤鱼分完了，小狼才互相哼一声，背对着，猛地往嘴里刨。
抢个菜抢得跟结了仇似的。
烤过的鱼本就外焦里嫩，热油一激，香料的味道浸入鱼肉。虽说没煮多久，但味儿也有了。
第一口下去，兽人定住。
看了看碗里，再看了看被抢得只剩下汤的陶锅。抓着就往锅里倒最后那点儿。
“嗷呜嗷呜！”烫手了还不松。
林楸：“……”
“要不下次不做了。”
“嗷呜嗷呜嗷！！！”一个埋头苦吃，话都说不好。
生怕林楸不做了，又飞快咽下嘴里的，急切道：
“要做！”
“做！”
馋哭了是什么感觉？
就是现在大家这个模样。
分明是已经快要吃腻味了的鱼，怎么忽然烤了一下，再放上各种草，再倒油，哇！
好吃到见兽神！
各种复杂的调料香味混合在一起，在舌尖打架，连舌头都想一起吞了下去。
咔嚓咔嚓——
小狼干咀嚼鱼刺。
“好吃嗷……嗷呜嗷呜……”已经难以用话来形容，全成了无意识的嗷呜感叹。
林楸咬着一块鱼肉，品了品味道。
调料不多，胜在鱼鲜。
配的香草也都是直接地里找的新鲜的，味道本就极其浓郁。小狼们头一顿吃这种复合调料的，被冲击一下正常。
狼安咽了咽嘴里的鱼肉，挨着林楸忍不住问：“楸，你要找的其他香料是哪些，我叫狼贝他们帮着找。”
太好吃了，狼安忍不住又叼了块。
嘴里不能闲着，一闲着，就直流清涎。
楸还说调料不足，不一定好吃，这都好吃到见兽神好吗？
看看小狼，脑袋钻碗里了。
听到这边说话，小狼耳朵一竖，忙亲亲热热道：“阿楸叔，我们可以帮你找啊。”
“对唔！”
“我们找！”
小狼说着，飞快给他们队长使眼色。
狼冰默默一口气吃了大半，嘴里抿着山药泥，舔了舔唇，稍稍矜持道：“我们找。”
林楸：“好啊。”
……
祭司山洞。
老祭司一人一口陶锅，慢悠悠地享受着属于自己的午饭。听到底下小狼献殷勤，哼了声，剥开大虾壳，一口吃了个满足。
小狼天不服地不服的，一顿烤鱼就收买了。
真没出息！
过了会儿，听到往上山来的脚步声，老祭司立马将陶锅里剩下的扒拉到碗里，吃得飞快。
“祭司。”狼冰进来。
看老兽人单独一口陶锅，眼睛里亮光一闪，可靠近之后看锅里干干净净，抿唇离他远一点。
“好不容易休息一天，跑上来干什么？”
狼冰：“我想带着小狼们种草药。”
祭司放下碗，“部落不缺草药，只采集已经够用。”
他叹了口气，道：“要是像以前那样集市还开着，倒是可以种。”
不是所有部落都有祭司。
有的部落断了传承，没有祭司看病，总得花极大的代价才能找到其他部落的祭司帮忙。
以往集市还开着，他还能卖一卖制作好的药粉，也能换回些食物来。但现在不行了……
狼冰听着祭司的话，想了想，摇头。
“我想种些我们常能用到的，先试试，要是能行，以后不就可以不用花精力采集。”
空下的人手，可以为部落做其他的事。像烧陶，像建棚子，或许还有其他……
楸还要找调料，找做绳子的草，狼冰觉得他还会做很多很多事。
他们部落不会一直维持现状。
在楸的影响下，部落活起来了。
老祭司：“你想种就种吧。”
他老了，折腾不了。但也乐意看着死气沉沉的部落重新流动起来。
“楸呢？”
“睡觉。”
狼冰想到吃完鱼就进了大山洞，躺进草窝的兽人……
“楸还是很弱，要不要再给他吃点草药？”
老祭司一瞪，“草药是随便能吃的吗？”
狼冰抿唇，他就是担心，楸真的很很弱。体力连他们这群小狼都比不过。
部落还需要他。
狼冰看着老祭司碗里没吃完的烤鱼，又舔了下唇。
他才不是馋。
他是关心同族。

太阳晒得人犯懒，吃了一顿香喷喷烤鱼的兽人们躺在棚子底下，鼾声四起。
梦中还忍不住馋，嘴筒子搁的那一处全是口水。
鱼少，没吃够。
下午，狩猎队的兽人们回来时，刚将猎物一扔，立马耸着鼻子四处嗅闻。
闻着闻着，眼睛一眯，把留守在狼山的兽人抓来问。
“你们吃了什么？”
“鱼啊。”狼无辜。
鱼有那么香吗？
兽人将同伴扔开，趴在地上，闷闷不语。
安肯定背着他们做好吃的了！
狼鼻子灵，甚至有些找到了中午用过的小陶锅。
明明都洗干净了，还叫兽人抱着，就认准了狼山的兽人一定开过小灶。
大伙儿也不躺了，气势汹汹，要找狼岩撑腰。
“王，他们背着我们吃好吃的！”
“王，我们也要吃。”
“王！他们偏心！”
“王……”
狼岩脑子被吵得嗡嗡的。
他把狼安叫来，小狼嘿嘿笑着凑过来看热闹。偏看着成年兽人吃不着，还在一旁拱火，七嘴八舌地说着多好吃，最后被抓住揍了一通。
狼山前小狼“嗷呜嗷呜”惨叫，听得瘆人。
林楸出来，幽幽泛光的狼目盯住他。
狼眼里哀怨、悲愤，活像刚刚经历过渣男的背叛。
林楸默默止步，靠近狼岩。
“他们怎么了？”
狼岩：“他们……”
“鱼！！！楸，我们也要吃烤鱼！！！”
杀猪时的叫唤都没他们响亮。
烤鱼今晚肯定是吃不成了。
中午起了一次鱼笼，这才放下去半天，捞起来的鱼也不够百来个兽人吃。
为了安抚兽人，林楸跟狼安他们商量，定下明天晚上吃。
这会儿有空闲的兽人去起一次鱼，先养在陶罐里。
昨天只吃了狩猎二队捕捉回来的呦呦兽，狼岩他们抓的那一头还养着，明早上也不吃鱼，吃呦呦兽。
这样鱼攒到明天晚上，差不多够了。
勉强算安抚好了兽人，等狼木那边杀了猎物，狼安这边立马开始烧火炖汤。
小狼今天中午挖的山药吃完了，狼安就先炖肉，炖到差不多，再烫菜。
瞧见木架子上林楸送来的草药，狼安利落地抓了一把，分别扔几个陶锅里。
趴得近的兽人动了动鼻子，抬起脑袋，圆圆的两眼发懵，显得有几分憨，“安，你刚刚放什么了？”
狼安：“草药。”
“不吃草药！我们没病！”狼挪到他身边，飞快扒拉他的腿。
狼安被抓得踉跄，眉头渐渐皱起来。
“祭司给的。”
“也不吃！不吃！”狼爪抱着安的腿撒泼。
“补身体的！”
狼眼里怀疑。
“楸说好吃。”
狼翻个身，看着狼安抓起灶台上的木棍，默默滚远了去。
他们看着跟狼贝说话的林楸，还是怀疑。
草药能好吃？
*
“楸，你说这个草能做成跟兽皮绳一样耐用的绳子？”
采集队的兽人也都坐在棚子底下，围着林楸。他们手里拿着林楸说的麻草，翻来覆去地看。
又折断了，学着林楸扯下来一层皮。
指甲一划，稍稍用力就断了。
这跟楸之前说的也不一样啊。
林楸：“就是这个。现在它还没长成，要再等等。”
林楸将麻皮撕开，叫兽人们看看什么是纤维，以后遇到了差不多的植物都可以留意。
做麻绳是一回事，林楸更想做的是衣服。
只要是麻，不管是亚麻、苎麻、葛麻……又或者是本土的纤维植物，都可以用。
兽人们拿着手上的麻草还在回忆什么地方有这个，狼清看着林楸手上完整一块麻皮被勾着那一缕一缕的麻纤维……
脑中灵光一闪，忽然道：“大泽那边，有种蛮草，那个可以吗？”
林楸没见过这个草，看向狼贝。
“蛮草……”狼贝目光定在林楸手上被他撕成一缕一缕的麻草上。
楸说的这个纤维什么的兽人听得雨里雾里的，但如果能像他之前说的，能扯成一丝一丝的，这个蛮草也能。
“这个应该符合楸的要求。我们明天还去南边，给你带回来看。”
“要不然我跟着去？”
要能用，直接割几捆回来，免得再跑一次。
“那祭司那边呢？”
“我请个假。”
“请个假是什么？”兽人们抬起头，两眼迷茫，十分真诚问道。
林楸：“就是跟祭司说明天去不了，有事。”
“哦哦。”兽人们点点头。
楸总说这些他们听不懂的话。
趁着现在有空，林楸跑了一趟祭司的山洞。说了明天不来的事，结果老兽人还不答应。
还叫他学学狼冰，大概意思就是他不够认真，小狼可不像他这么三天打鱼两天晒网的。
林楸：“我又不是下一任祭司人选。”
老祭司扬起木杖想给他一下，气道：“还真把你阿父他们忘了！”
林楸一下想起来还有个支部落的存在。
“您不会想让我当支部落的……”林楸蹙眉，“我不当。”
“小狼崽子！你以为没有祭司的部落能延续多久！支部落那边治病还得那么远过来找我，要我死了呢？”
“狼冰啊。”
老祭司拿起木杖拍了他一下。
“你再说一遍？”
林楸揉了揉胳膊，看着再度扬起的花里胡哨的木杖，那叮叮当当的脆响，像警告。
他往后撤，“我又没说不学了。明天出去，下次休息日那天补上总行了。”
老祭司：“哼！”
哼就是答应了。
林楸立马跑下山。
想让他当支部落的祭司，坚决不行。
现在跟着祭司学这些东西是为了更好地利用兽神大陆的动植物，他当增加些常识。
祭司还要占卜，沟通兽神，跳什么祭舞……
比起本土兽人，林楸身体脆，活儿多了立马能萎靡。
这辈子他只想创造一个稍微好一点的能休息的环境，然后平淡安稳度过。
*
“什么味儿？”
趴在棚子下的狼兽人直起脑袋，在空中嗅闻。
陶锅这边棚子的狼兽人捂住鼻子，再度怀疑地爬起来，直冲冲地杵在灶台边，往陶锅里看。
“这个真的能吃吗？”
狼安有一点点忐忑，但心里对林楸的信任占据了上风。
他一把推开兽人，“能吃。”
楸叫他少放一点，狼安当然放得极少极少，一锅一小把。
“吃饭了！”
这边一声吼，兽人们爬起来，先找自己碗。
棚子下，兽人排成几队，幼崽也叼着自己的碗，站在队伍中央。
狼果走在他们后头，前面的狼兽人挪动，就小心戳一下幼崽屁屁。小狼就乖乖往前走。
这些日子小狼养得好，长得快，一天三顿，肉眼可见的结实。
现在爬林楸的草窝都不用踩木梯了，勾着爪子就能翻上去。
前面的狼挪着小步子，时不时回头看一眼，脚趾扣紧了地面。
“果，你让幼崽们一边儿去，我怕踩到他们。”
狼果阴恻恻，“你敢踩到你就死定了。”
狼缩了缩脖子。
“哪有这么小的幼崽自己打饭。”狼嘀咕，索性直接转身，退着走。
为首的小狼眼睛一亮，也学着转头，叫狼果用木棍轻轻戳了戳肚子。
软绵绵的，陷下去一个小窝窝。
“好好走。”
狼崽爪子搭在木棍上，推了推，推不动。
见狼果慢慢沉着脸，狼崽一激灵，立马对着狼果龇出两粒小小的犬牙笑，很乖巧地转回去。
狼果扫了眼后头试图跟着转过来，又回头乖乖排队的一溜小团子，叼不动碗的就用脑袋拱，爪子扒拉，尾巴都绷直了在使劲儿。
他们其实不小了。
最小的都是去年雪季过后才出生的，要是食物充足地养着，早能跑能跳跳。
可惜现在一年期可以变化人形的幼崽极少，像狼雪，快三岁了还没变。
好在今年万事顺利，幼崽不仅一个没死，还长大了。幼崽四条小腿儿不像从前软绵，有了力气，平日里放出来就四处跑，还能打架。
狼果欣慰不已。
狼兽人的幼崽，就该这样。
排在前头的兽人已经打到肉汤了，照旧是两个最馋嘴的狼莫跟狼金。
狼金捧着碗跟狼莫走到一边，碗放在矮墙上，两眼盯着那碗里冒出来的草药根。
狼金戳了下，闻了闻，皱着鼻子。
“阿莫叔，王是不是觉得我们一顿吃多了，放这个让我们少吃一点……嗷！”
狼金回头，怒目而视。
谁打他？！
对上狼岩目光，嘴巴一咧，傻笑。
“王……”
狼岩：“少吃一顿饿不死。”
“吃！我要吃！”狼金赶紧护着碗，视死如归般，吸溜一大口。
旁边，狼莫咂摸着嘴里的肉汤。
再看看狼金烫得吐舌头，抬起他那挂着两坨黑眼圈的脸笑问：“怎么样？”
狼金：“烫烫烫！”
狼莫胳膊撑着矮墙，全身重量倚靠在上头，胡子拉碴，头发凌乱，气质颓废。
他又咂嘴两下，觉得味道是有点怪，但吃着吃着，好像还可以。
不理会旁边烫得流眼泪的小狼，又吃了口肉。
除了有点草药的味道，一点不苦不酸不涩不腥，味道很独特，他能接受。
狼莫吃着吃着，眼皮耷拉，然后悲愤地将碗里所有的食物一口闷了。
陶缸怎么会裂来着……
是火不够均匀，还是材料配比……
狼莫一头砸在矮墙上，呜呜咽咽，叫旁边吐着烫红的舌尖的狼金好奇看来。
“阿莫叔，你怎么了？”
狼莫抬起头，看着他碗里还满满当当的肉。
“你叔饿，分我一点儿？”
他把碗推过去。
chapters.translated_text:
The sun was lazy, and the orcs, having eaten a fragrant meal of grilled fish, lay under the shed, snoring loudly.

Even in their dreams, they couldn't help but crave more, their mouths drooling where they rested.

There were few fish, and they hadn't had enough.

In the afternoon, when the hunting team returned, they threw down their prey and immediately twitched their noses, sniffing around.

As they sniffed, their eyes narrowed, and they grabbed the orcs who had stayed behind at Wolf Mountain to interrogate them.

"What did you eat?"

"Fish," the wolf replied innocently.

Could fish really be that fragrant?

The orc threw his companion aside, lay on the ground, and remained sullenly silent.

An must have been cooking something delicious behind their backs!

Wolf noses are sharp; some even found the small clay pot used at noon.

Even though it had been washed clean, they still made the orcs hold it, convinced that the Wolf Mountain orcs must have cooked a private meal.

Everyone stopped lying down, looking aggressive, and went to find Lang Yan to back them up.

"King, they ate delicious food behind our backs!"

"King, we want to eat too."

"King! They are biased!"

"King..."

Lang Yan’s head was buzzing from the noise.

He called Lang An over, and the little wolf came over grinning to watch the fun. Seeing the adult orcs unable to eat, he fanned the flames from the side, chattering about how delicious it was, until he was finally caught and given a beating.

In front of Wolf Mountain, the little wolf let out "Awoo, awoo" cries, which sounded chilling.

Lin Qiu came out, his faintly glowing wolf eyes fixed on him.

The wolf eyes were filled with grievance and indignation, looking just like someone who had just experienced the betrayal of a scumbag.

Lin Qiu silently stopped and approached Lang Yan.

"What's wrong with them?"

Lang Yan: "They..."

"FISH!!! Qiu, we want to eat grilled fish too!!!"

Even the squeals of a slaughtered pig weren't as loud as them.

Grilled fish was definitely off the menu for tonight.

The fish traps had been checked at noon, and having been in the water for only half a day, the catch wasn't enough for nearly a hundred orcs.

To appease the orcs, Lin Qiu discussed it with Lang An and the others, setting the meal for tomorrow night.

The orcs who were free now went to check the traps once more, keeping the catch in clay pots.

Yesterday they only ate the Youyou beasts caught by the second hunting team; the one Lang Yan and his group caught was still being kept, so they wouldn't eat fish tomorrow morning, but the Youyou beast instead.

This way, the fish would accumulate until tomorrow night, which should be just about enough.

Having barely appeased the orcs, as soon as Lang Mu finished butchering the prey, Lang An immediately started a fire to stew the soup.

The yam the little wolf dug up at noon was gone, so Lang An stewed the meat first, and once it was almost done, he blanched the greens.

Seeing the herbs Lin Qiu had sent on the wooden rack, Lang An deftly grabbed a handful and threw them into several clay pots.

An orc lying nearby twitched his nose, lifted his head, his round eyes dazed and looking a bit foolish, "An, what did you just put in?"

Lang An: "Herbs."

"We don't eat herbs! We aren't sick!" The wolf crawled to his side and quickly pawed at his leg.

Lang An staggered from being grabbed, his brows gradually furrowing.

"The priest gave them."

"Still don't eat! Don't eat!" The wolf claws hugged An's leg and threw a tantrum.

"It's to nourish the body!"

There was suspicion in the wolf's eyes.

"Qiu said it's delicious."

The wolf rolled over, watched Lang An pick up a wooden stick from the stove, and silently rolled away.

They looked at Lin Qiu, who was talking to Lang Bei, still suspicious.

Can herbs be delicious?

*

"Qiu, you said this grass can be made into rope as durable as animal hide rope?"

The orcs of the gathering team were also sitting under the shed, surrounding Lin Qiu. They held the hemp grass Lin Qiu had mentioned, looking at it over and over.

They broke it again, learning from Lin Qiu how to peel off a layer of skin.

A scratch with a fingernail, and with a little force, it snapped.

This was different from what Qiu had said before.

Lin Qiu: "This is it. It hasn't fully grown yet; we have to wait a bit longer."

Lin Qiu tore open the hemp skin, showing the orcs what fibers were, so they could keep an eye out for similar plants in the future.

Making hemp rope was one thing, but what Lin Qiu really wanted to make was clothing.

As long as it's hemp, whether it's flax, ramie, kudzu... or even local fibrous plants, they could all be used.

The orcs were still holding the hemp grass, trying to recall where they had seen it, while Lang Qing watched the complete piece of hemp skin in Lin Qiu's hand being pulled into strands of hemp fiber...

A flash of inspiration hit his mind, and he suddenly said: "Over by the Great Marsh, there's a kind of 'savage grass,' would that work?"

Lin Qiu hadn't seen this grass and looked at Lang Bei.

"Savage grass..." Lang Bei's gaze fixed on the hemp grass in Lin Qiu's hand that he had torn into strands.

The orcs were confused by what Qiu said about fibers, but if it could be pulled into strands as he described, this savage grass could do it too.

"This should meet Qiu's requirements. We're going to the south again tomorrow; we'll bring some back for you to see."

"How about I go along?"

If it could be used, he could cut a few bundles and bring them back, saving another trip.

"What about the priest's side then?"

"I'll ask for leave."

"What is asking for leave?" The orcs raised their heads, eyes dazed, asking very sincerely.

Lin Qiu: "It means telling the priest I can't go tomorrow because I have something to do."

"Oh, oh." The orcs nodded.

Qiu always said these things they didn't understand.

Taking advantage of his free time, Lin Qiu ran to the priest's cave. He mentioned not coming tomorrow, but the old orc wouldn't agree.

He even told him to learn from Lang Bing, implying he wasn't serious enough, and that the little wolf wasn't as "fishing for three days and drying nets for two" as he was.

Lin Qiu: "I'm not the next candidate for priest."

The old priest raised his wooden staff, wanting to hit him, and said angrily: "You've really forgotten about your father and the others!"

Lin Qiu suddenly remembered the existence of a branch tribe.

"You don't want me to be the... of the branch tribe," Lin Qiu frowned, "I won't do it."

"Little wolf cub! How long do you think a tribe without a priest can last! The branch tribe has to come so far to find me for healing; what if I die?"

"Lang Bing is there."

The old priest picked up his wooden staff and smacked him.

"Say that again?"

Lin Qiu rubbed his arm, looking at the gaudy wooden staff raised again, its tinkling sound like a warning.

He retreated, "I didn't say I wouldn't learn. I'm going out tomorrow; I'll make it up on the next rest day, is that okay?"

The old priest: "Hmph!"

A hmph meant he agreed.

Lin Qiu immediately ran down the mountain.

He absolutely would not be the priest of the branch tribe.

Learning these things from the priest now was just to better utilize the flora and fauna of the Beast God Continent, and to increase his general knowledge.

The priest also had to divine, communicate with the Beast God, and perform some kind of sacrificial dance...

Compared to the local orcs, Lin Qiu's body was fragile; if he had too much work, he would wither immediately.

In this life, he only wanted to create a slightly better environment where he could rest, and then live a plain and stable life.

*

"What's that smell?"

The wolf orcs lying under the shed lifted their heads and sniffed the air.

The wolf orcs near the clay pots covered their noses, got up again suspiciously, and stood straight by the stove, looking into the clay pots.

"Can this really be eaten?"

Lang An was a little nervous, but his trust in Lin Qiu prevailed.

He pushed the orc away, "It can be eaten."

Qiu told him to use only a little, and Lang An naturally used very, very little—a small pinch per pot.

"Time to eat!"

At this shout, the orcs scrambled up, first looking for their own bowls.

Under the shed, the orcs lined up in several rows, and the cubs also held their own bowls in their mouths, standing in the middle of the line.

Lang Guo walked behind them; when the wolf orcs in front moved, he would carefully poke the cubs' butts. The little wolves would obediently walk forward.

These days, the little wolves were well-fed and growing fast; eating three meals a day, they were visibly sturdy.

Now they didn't even need a wooden ladder to climb into Lin Qiu's grass nest; they could just hook their claws and flip up.

The wolf in front took small steps, looking back from time to time, his toes gripping the ground tightly.

"Guo, move the cubs to the side; I'm afraid of stepping on them."

Lang Guo said sinisterly, "If you dare to step on them, you're dead."

The wolf shrank his neck.

"Who has cubs this small getting their own food," the wolf muttered, simply turning around and walking backward.

The leading little wolf's eyes lit up, and he tried to turn around too, only to be gently poked in the belly by Lang Guo with a wooden stick.

It was soft and squishy, creating a little dimple.

"Walk properly."

The wolf cub put his paws on the wooden stick and pushed, but it wouldn't budge.

Seeing Lang Guo's face slowly darkening, the wolf cub gave a start, immediately baring his two tiny canine teeth at Lang Guo with a smile, and obediently turned back.

Lang Guo scanned the line of little fluffballs behind him who were trying to turn around and then obediently went back to queuing; those who couldn't hold their bowls used their heads to nudge them, their claws to scrape, their tails stiff with effort.

They weren't actually that small.

The youngest were born after the snow season last year; if they had been raised with enough food, they would have been running and jumping long ago.

Unfortunately, there were very few cubs who could transform into human form within a year; like Lang Xue, who was almost three and still hadn't transformed.

Fortunately, everything went smoothly this year; not a single cub died, and they had grown up. The cubs' four little legs weren't as soft as before; they had strength, and when let out, they would run around and even fight.

Lang Guo was very gratified.

Wolf orc cubs should be like this.

The orcs at the front of the line had already gotten their meat soup, as usual, the two gluttons, Lang Mo and Lang Jin.

Lang Jin held his bowl and walked to the side with Lang Mo, placing the bowl on a low wall, his eyes fixed on the herb roots floating in the bowl.

Lang Jin poked it, smelled it, and wrinkled his nose.

"Uncle Mo, does the King think we ate too much in one meal, so he put this in to make us eat less... Ouch!"

Lang Jin turned back, glaring.

Who hit him?!

Meeting Lang Yan's gaze, he grinned and smiled foolishly.

"King..."

Lang Yan: "Skipping one meal won't starve you."

"Eat! I want to eat!" Lang Jin hurriedly protected his bowl and, with a look of "death before dishonor," took a big gulp.

Beside him, Lang Mo smacked his lips at the meat soup.

He looked at Lang Jin, who was sticking his tongue out from the heat, and asked with a smile on his face, which was marked by two dark circles: "How is it?"

Lang Jin: "Hot, hot, hot!"

Lang Mo leaned his arms on the low wall, his whole weight resting on it, his beard stubbly, his hair messy, his temperament decadent.

He smacked his lips again, feeling the taste was a bit strange, but as he ate, it seemed okay.

Ignoring the little wolf next to him who was sticking out his tongue from the heat, he took another bite of meat.

Aside from a hint of herbal taste, it wasn't bitter, sour, astringent, or fishy at all; the taste was unique, and he could accept it.

As Lang Mo ate, his eyelids drooped, and then he indignantly downed all the food in his bowl in one go.

How did the clay pot crack again...

Was the fire uneven, or was it the material ratio...

Lang Mo smashed his head against the low wall, whimpering, which made Lang Jin, who was sticking out his scalded red tongue, look over curiously.

"Uncle Mo, what's wrong with you?"

Lang Mo raised his head, looking at the bowl still full of meat.

"Your uncle is hungry, share some with me?"

He pushed his bowl over.
chapters.title: 第44章

chapters.translated_text:
Lang Jin looked at his bloodshot eyes, hesitated, picked and chose in the bowl, and gave him one of the second-smallest chunks of meat.

Lang Mo was afraid he would go back on his word and finished it immediately.

He patted the little wolf on the shoulder and wobbled away again, clutching his bowl.

"That's strange."

"What's strange?" Lang Bing set down his bowl.

Lang Rong lay on the other side of Lang Jin, "It seems to be Uncle Mo."

Lang Jin shook his head, "No, I meant the meat soup is strange." He took a big gulp from his bowl and sighed, "It's delicious!"

Lang Bing: "You think everything is delicious."

Lang Rong nodded silently.

There weren't many herbs in it, but the flavor was strong. The beastmen had mixed opinions, but they still ate with all their might.

Thinking of the grilled fish they could eat tomorrow night, this bowl of strange-tasting meat soup was nothing.

Early the next morning, Lin Qiu left Wolf Mountain with the beastmen.

He ran with Lang Bei and the others for a while, but couldn't keep up later, so he climbed onto Lang Yan's back.

Because they were going to the Great Marsh this time, it would take half a day of running from Wolf Mountain, which was very physically demanding.

Only the beastmen from the first hunting team and the gathering team went there, while the other hunting teams went to hunt separately.

After passing through the forest countless times, crossing a dry lake covered in grass, passing rivers, and weaving through woodlands, they finally arrived at what the beastmen called the Great Marsh.

This was the southernmost tip of the Wolf Tribe's territory.

The river network was dense, and the marshes and lakes were endless. Countless aquatic plants grew within, with clusters of white and purple flowers like brocade floating on the lake surface. Flocks of birds nested and bred here, their noisy cries echoing through the sky.

Lin Qiu looked at the dense flocks of birds in the sky; they seemed to even block out the sun.

"With so many birds, it would be enough to eat if we could hunt them down."

Lang Yan flicked his tail, "Can't catch them, and there's no meat on them. If you go further in, you'll sink."

The ground where Lin Qiu and the others were standing was already soft; further ahead, the mud bubbled with black bubbles when stepped on.

The beastmen dared not continue forward.

The purpose of this trip was to get Man Grass, while also gathering and hunting along the way.

Lang Bei casually pulled a handful of waist-high grass nearby; the grass leaves were squeezed, releasing juice, and the surface broke to reveal the white fibers inside.

"This is Man Grass; it's everywhere around here."

Lin Qiu looked out, and indeed, between the lakes and marshes, wherever there was green, this kind of grass grew in clusters.

The leaves were as high as a person's waist, slender, and grew in clumps like thatch.

Lang Bei said: "This grass loves growing in places with lots of water. You can't dig it all up; as long as there's a bit of root, it will keep growing. At our previous migration site, we moved away because there was too much of this and we couldn't plant Tail Grass."

After the rainy season, the beastmen had to store food for the snowy season. Now that prey was scarce, the seeds of Tail Grass were their important food for surviving the winter, so they had to move.

And Man Grass was only discovered after leaving the Central Continent, and it was named by the Priest.

The beastmen didn't often come to the Great Marsh, and since this grass wasn't edible, they didn't have much contact with it, so when Lin Qiu mentioned it, they had forgotten about it.

Lin Qiu pulled it apart to look closely; the fibers were very thick and cut his hands when pulled tight.

This was suitable for making rope.

He said: "It can be used."

Lang Bei: "Alright, then we'll cut it. There are many plants here that aren't on Wolf Mountain. You should look around more; you might find something useful."

Lin Qiu remembered that not far from here, there was also plenty of hemp grass.

Its fibers were fine, perfect for summer clothes, but it would take a few more months to harvest.

Lang Bei assigned two beastmen to be responsible for cutting the grass, while the others looked for edible plants nearby.

The beastmen of the first hunting team stared at the large area where birds were nesting in the center of the water network, silently drooling.

"Can see it, but can't eat it."

The beastmen weren't thinking about the birds, which were all feathers and bones with little meat, but the eggs in the nests.

They still remembered how delicious the wild chive omelet Lin Qiu made was!

But even if they could swim, just walking here was impossible; they would sink.

In the past, when they chased prey to this area, they saw with their own eyes how the prey was swallowed by the mud, and the beastmen almost sank too, but they managed to save them.

Lin Qiu stood behind the wolf pack, looking out at the shimmering Great Marsh under the sunlight, "Are there no large prey animals here?"

Lang Yan: "Rarely."

Lang You sniffed the place, which was full of the smell of birds, and sneezed. A feather hanging on the grass flew up, and he swatted it down with a claw.

A solid wolf paw print appeared on the ground.

Lang You: "King, it's all the smell of birds."

Lin Qiu sniffed; the air was fresh and had the faint fragrance of blooming aquatic plants. How could he not smell the birds?

Lang Yan: "Let's walk around."

Lang You climbed up and led the way, and the beastmen ran along the Great Marsh toward the west.

The southern part of the Wolf Tribe was bounded by the Great Marsh; to cross it, one would need to take a detour of several days.

Further south of the Great Marsh, many small tribes were distributed.

This was a habitat for birds. As the beastmen ran through the grass, they startled flocks of birds into flight. There were far more than what Lin Qiu had seen in the forest; it seemed all the birds were here.

Running around the marsh and climbing the only low hill nearby, one could faintly see the scenery further south.

Deep grass, forests, or intersecting mountain peaks.

It was vague, like a mirage, an unreal scene in a painting, not clearly visible.

Lang You raised his head on the low hill, sniffed, and turned his head to stare at one spot.

It seemed he smelled something else.

The Great Marsh was a natural defense; except for the aquatic and feathered tribes, other beastmen couldn't cross it. Lang You sniffed again, but there was still only the smell of birds.

Splash—

In the jade-clear lake, a large fish seemed to be thrashing its tail. Lin Qiu looked over, immediately stepped back, his body stiff, and pressed tightly against Lang Yan's front side.

"King?" Lang You was excited.

Lang Yan: "Let's see if we can catch it."

It wasn't a fish at all, but a giant python! It didn't know what it had found at the bottom of the water, and it was rolling in the water with its body coiled, splashing water everywhere like a dragon leaping.

The snake was as thick as a waist and over ten meters long. The brown and black patterns on its scales made Lin Qiu feel terrified.

Lang Yan was slightly stunned, looking down at Lin Qiu's hair standing on end.

He was bristling.

"What's wrong?"

"How could there be... such a big snake." Lin Qiu's voice was weak; he almost couldn't speak.

It simply exceeded Lin Qiu's perception of a python; it was as thick as a water bucket and could swallow a person as big as him in one gulp without even pausing.

Lang Yan watched as the wolf beastmen were already tracking the snake's trail, and half-crouched, saying: "Do you want to come up?"

Lin Qiu buried his head, stiff as a puppet, and just climbed up.

He buried his head in Lang Yan's fur and didn't move.

Lang Yan waited for him to get on, stood up straight, and continued to look down the mountain without following.

The further south one went, the more snakes lived in the marsh area.

Originally, there were some near Wolf Mountain, but none this big. For the safety of the cubs, they cleaned them out every year.

There were many fish in the marsh, and no beastmen came here, so the snakes had no natural enemies and rarely grew to this size.

For the wolf beastmen, this kind of large snake didn't pose much of a threat; they weren't poisonous, but they often moved in places with a lot of water, making them hard to catch.

Like the small, brightly colored ones that occasionally ran out of the forest, those were the ones to watch out for.

The snakes hid in the water and were vigilant.

The beastmen observed for a while, and seeing it give up on its prey and head toward the scattered grass islands in the Great Marsh, they were helpless.

However, this made the hunting team know what to catch. Afterward, Lang You directed the beastmen to search along the grass. They really found a few, although not as big as that one, they were as thick as a beastman's arm.

Lin Qiu sat cross-legged on Lang Yan's back, his body numb; he didn't dare to get down at all now.

Lang Yan: "Afraid of this?"

Lang Yan didn't follow the hunting team anymore and carried Lin Qiu back to the gathering team.

Lin Qiu's teeth felt sour, and he had goosebumps all over.

"Afraid."

Lang Yan: "Actually, it's quite delicious."

The image of the giant python thrashing in the water in Lin Qiu's mind wouldn't go away.

Seeing it through a screen before was one thing, but seeing it with his own eyes was another. Lin Qiu felt he might have nightmares tonight.

He didn't want to discuss whether it was delicious with Lang Yan. Returning to the gathering team, he immediately blended in with the beastmen, which gave him a little sense of security.

...

Man Grass grew extremely aggressively; where it took root, it didn't leave any room for other plants.

Both beastmen were efficient workers and had already cut a large area.

Lin Qiu needed a lot, and didn't dare to go to the hunting team to join the fun, so he simply took a small knife and stayed to help.

The tools were still not good enough; he had to make a sickle.

Lang Yan ran around nearby, confirmed there were no snakes in the grass, and then patrolled eastward along the Great Marsh.

Birds liked to nest in the grass, and the vast stretches of Man Grass in the east occupied the dried-up water land. The wind blew, and the waves surged; it was so dense that nothing else could be seen beyond the Man Grass.

Lang Yan plunged in, and the grass waves opened a path at a speed visible to the naked eye. The grass roots were intertwined underfoot, and even if he stepped into a small puddle, he wouldn't sink.

Lang Yan searched around and picked up some bird eggs along the way.

It wasn't until he saw the thousands of lakes and marshes reflecting the golden red that he turned back.

The grass waves swayed, and the figure of the giant black wolf disappeared quickly.

On the other side of the grass sea, a few gray shadows flashed by, and large, long ears poked out a tip before suddenly retracting.

Lang Yan was alert, suddenly turned his head, and his gaze fixed on one spot.

The sunset glow reflected in the sky, and the deep grass swayed with the wind, rustling.

Lang Yan looked at the sun, bit the grass basket woven from Man Grass, and flew back.

It was getting late.

Lang You brought the hunting team back.

Lin Qiu and the others were bundling the cut Man Grass.

Grab two handfuls of suitable grass leaves, tie a knot by crossing them, and pull tight with some force.

Place the aligned grass on top, pull from both sides, press it tightly, then combine the two strands, twist, and press into the grass gap.

The fibers of this Man Grass were extremely strong. The beastmen said that this grass was available at any time; even if you came in winter, you could still find it by digging through the snow.

Lin Qiu had originally thought that there wouldn't be enough hemp grass and that he would have to plant hemp specifically.

Now that this endless sea of grass by the Great Marsh could be used, most of the effort was saved.

Two beastmen plus Lin Qiu worked for about three hours and bundled forty or fifty bundles of grass. Divided among the beastmen, each only needed to carry one bundle.

The grass wasn't as heavy as prey, but it was hard to secure.

There was no other way now, so they could only tie some more grass ropes and cut some vines to tie them directly onto the wolf beastmen.

The black wolves, gray wolves, and white wolves were all lying on the ground, huge in size. Now that they were eating a little better every day, their fur was fluffy, and their wolf eyes were round and bright, looking exceptionally beautiful.

The beastmen of the gathering team tied them onto the wolves first. Two bundles each, one on the left and one on the right, to prevent them from flipping off while running.
chapters.title: 第45章
chapters.source_text:
狼金看着他满是红血丝的眼眶，犹犹豫豫，往碗里挑挑选选，分了他一坨倒数第二小的肉块。
狼莫怕他反悔，立刻吃完。
他拍了拍小狼肩膀，抱着碗又摇摇晃晃离开。
“奇了怪了。”
“奇怪什么？”狼冰搁下碗。
狼溶趴在狼金另一边，“好像是阿莫叔。”
狼金摇头，“不是，我说肉汤奇怪。”他抱着碗喝了一大口，感叹：“好喝诶！”
狼冰：“你什么都觉得好喝。”
狼溶默默点头。
草药放得不多，但耐不住味儿大。兽人们褒贬不一，但还是铆足了劲儿吃。
想到明天晚上能吃到的烤鱼，这一顿味道奇怪的肉汤就不算什么了。
第二天一早，林楸早早跟着兽人们离开狼山。
他先跟着狼贝他们跑了一阵，后头撑不住，又趴在了狼岩背上。
因着这次要去大泽，从狼山过去，一直跑都要跑半天，很费体力。
只狩猎一队的兽人跟采集队的兽人往那边去，其他狩猎队则分开打猎。
不知穿过几次树林，又过长满草的干涸湖，经河流，又穿梭林地，最后终于到了兽人们口中的大泽。
这是狼部落领地的最南端。
河网密布，沼泽湖泊一望无际。数不清的水生植物生长在其中，一簇簇白花紫花如锦，飘在湖面。成群的鸟在此地筑巢，繁衍，嘈杂叫声响彻云霄。
林楸看天上密密麻麻的鸟群，连太阳都似乎遮掩了去。
“这么多鸟，打下来也够吃。”
狼岩甩了下尾，“抓不到，也没肉。再往里面去，会陷进去。”
林楸他们这会儿站着的位置泥土就已经软趴趴的了，再往前，泥土踩着都往外冒黑色泡泡。
兽人们不敢再继续往前。
此行是为了蛮草，也顺带采集捕猎。
狼贝随手扯了一把身边腰高的草，草叶被挤压出汁，表面破碎，露出里面的白色纤维。
“这个就是蛮草，这边到处都是。”
林楸放眼望去，确实，湖泊沼泽交连间，只要有绿色的地方，都丛生着这样的草。
叶片有人腰高，细长，如茅草一簇簇生长。
狼贝道：“这种草最喜欢生长在水多的地方，挖都挖不干净，只要有一点根就能继续长。在我们上一个迁徙地时，就是这个太多种植不了尾巴草，我们才搬走的。”
雨季过后，兽人们就要为雪季储存食物。现在猎物不多，尾巴草的果实就是他们重要的过雪季的食物，所以不得不搬。
而蛮草也是离开中央大陆才发现的，才由祭司命名。
兽人们不常往大泽过来，这种草不能吃，兽人们接触不多，所以当时林楸说起，他们都忘了还有这个。
林楸扯开细看，纤维很粗，拉得紧了都割手。
这种适合做绳子。
他道：“能用。”
狼贝：“行，那我们割。这边有很多狼山没有的植物，你多看看，没准还能找到有用的。”
林楸想起离这边不远，麻草也处处都是。
那个纤维细，做夏天的衣服最好，只不过还需要等几个月来收。
狼贝分出两个兽人负责割草，其余的则在附近寻找能吃的植物。
狩猎一队的兽人们则盯着水网中心那一大片鸟筑巢的地方，默默发馋。
“看得见，吃不着。”
兽人们不惦记那全身是毛跟骨头，没几两肉的鸟，而是那窝里的鸟蛋。
他们还记得林楸做的野韭煎蛋多好吃呢！
可就算他们会水，光是走这边的就行不通，会陷下去。
以前他们追猎物追到这边，亲眼看见那么猎物被泥地吞没，兽人也差点陷下去，好歹他们救上来了。
林楸站在狼群后头，远眺这阳光下波光粼粼的大泽，“这边没什么大型猎物？”
狼岩：“少见。”
狼游嗅着处处是鸟味儿的地方，打了个喷嚏，草上挂着的羽毛飞起来，叫狼一爪子拍下。
地面上出现了结结实实的一个狼爪印。
狼游：“王，全是鸟味儿。”
林楸嗅了嗅，空气清新，还有水生植物开花的淡淡香味。他怎么没闻出来有鸟味儿？
狼岩：“到处走走。”
狼游爬起来，在前带路，兽人们顺着大泽，往西边奔跑。
狼部落南部以大泽为界，要越过大泽，需要绕几天的路程才能过去。
大泽再往南，就分布着许多小型部落。
这里是鸟类的栖息地，兽人奔跑过草丛，惊飞一阵阵鸟群。比林楸在林子里见的多得多，鸟儿怕是都在这儿了。
绕着水泽跑，登上这附近唯一一座矮山，能隐隐看到更南边的景象。
深草、树林，或者山峰交错。
隐隐约约，像海市蜃楼，画中虚景，看不真切。
狼游在矮山上仰起头，嗅了嗅，转着脑袋盯着一处。
好像闻到了其他味道。
大泽是天然的防御，除了水族跟羽族，其他兽人越不过来。狼游又嗅了嗅，还是只有鸟味儿。
噗通——
碧透如玉的湖中似有大鱼甩尾，林楸看去，顿时后撤一步，身体僵硬，紧紧贴在狼岩前侧。
“王？”狼游则是兴奋。
狼岩：“试试抓不抓得到。”
哪里是鱼，分明是一条巨蟒！不知在水底找到了什么食物，卷曲着身体在水中翻滚，水花四溅，如蛟龙腾跃。
那蛇身腰粗，十几米长。鳞片上的斑纹棕黑色交错，看得林楸胆寒不已。
狼岩微怔，低头看林楸炸起来的头发。
炸毛了。
“怎么了？”
“怎么会……有那么大一条蛇。”林楸声音发虚，差点没说出声来。
简直超过了林楸对于蟒蛇的认知，水桶粗，一口将自己这么大人吞了都不待缓一缓的。
狼岩看着狼兽人已经在追踪长虫的踪迹，半趴下道：“要上来吗？”
林楸闷着头，僵得跟木偶似的，一味往上爬。
他脑袋往狼岩毛里扎，一动不动。
狼岩等他上来，站直了，依旧看着山下，没有跟过去。
越往南，水泽这边就生活着越多的长虫。
原本狼山附近也有，但没这么大的，为了幼崽的安全他们每年都要清理一遍。
水泽里鱼多，又没兽人来这边，长虫没天敌，难得长到这么大。
对狼兽人来说，这种大的长虫并没多大威胁，没毒，只是常在水多的地方活动，不好抓。
像林子里偶尔跑出一条小的，颜色艳丽，那才要注意。
长虫藏在水里，又警惕。
兽人们观察了一会儿，看它放弃猎物往大泽里散落的草岛去了，也束手无策。
不过这一下叫狩猎队知道该抓什么了，之后狼游指挥着，叫兽人们沿着草丛搜寻。真叫找出来几条，虽不及那个大，但也有兽人胳膊粗。
林楸盘腿坐在狼岩背上，身体发麻，这下是一点不敢下去。
狼岩：“怕这个？”
狼岩没跟着狩猎队了，背着林楸回采集队那边。
林楸牙根发酸，身上起了一层鸡皮疙瘩。
“怕。”
狼岩：“其实还挺好吃。”
林楸脑海里那巨蟒在水中翻腾的样子挥之不去。
以前隔着屏幕看见是一回事，亲眼见到又是另一回事，林楸觉得自己今晚可能要做噩梦。
不想跟狼岩讨论好不好吃，回到采集队那边，他立刻融入兽人中，让他稍稍有一点安全感。
……
蛮草生长极其霸道，扎根之处，没跟其他植物留下一点余地。
两个兽人都是干活利落的，已经割出来一大片。
林楸要得多，不敢去狩猎队那边凑热闹，干脆拿了小刀，留在这边帮忙。
工具还是不行，得做镰刀。
狼岩在附近跑了跑，确认没看见草丛里有长虫，然后再沿着大泽往东边巡逻。
鸟喜欢在草丛里做窝，东边成片的蛮草占据了干涸的水地，风吹浪涌，密密匝匝看不清蛮草以外任何东西。
狼岩一头扎进去，草浪重以肉眼可见的速度开出一条路。脚下草根茎交织，即便踩到小水坑，也陷不下去。
狼岩四处搜寻，顺带捡了些鸟蛋。
直到看到万千湖沼映着金红，才反身回去。
草浪摇动，黑色巨狼的身影迅速消失。
草海的另一头，几抹灰影闪过，大大的长耳探出个尖，又倏地收回去。
狼岩警觉，忽然回头，目光定在一处。
晚霞映空，深草随风摇曳，沙沙作响。
狼岩看了眼太阳，叼着蛮草编织的草篮，飞快回去。
天不早了。
狼游带着狩猎队回来。
林楸他们正在给割好的蛮草打捆。
抓两把合适的草叶，交错着打个结，用点力扯紧。
把对齐的草放上去，两边一拉，压得结结实实的再两股一合，一搅，压入草缝中。
这蛮草纤维极其结实，听兽人说，这草什么时候都有，就是冬季过来，刨开雪地照样能找到。
林楸原本还想着麻草不够，到时候还得专门种麻。
现在这大泽边一望无际的草海能用，便省下大部分功夫。
两个兽人外加林楸，忙了差不多三个小时，草捆了四五十捆。分担到兽人身上，一个只用背一捆就够了。
草不及猎物重，就是不好固定。
现在没法子，只能再绑些草绳，又割些藤条来，直接往狼兽人身上绑。
黑狼灰狼白狼都趴在地上，硕大一只，现在每天稍稍吃得好一点，毛毛蓬松，狼眼睛圆亮，看着格外漂亮。
采集队的兽人先往他们身上绑。一个两捆，一左一右压着，免得跑着跑着翻了下来。

狼游不用负重，这会儿压在盖了草叶的大虫身上，下巴枕着人家尾巴。
下面的大虫死得不能再死了。
“王呢？”他问。
林楸一边绑着草绳，抖了下胳膊，离他远一点，道：“刚刚是往东边去了。”
说着，没多久，东边出现个黑点。
“嗷！”趴着的兽人忽然站起来。
林楸吓了一跳。
狼贝压着狼脑袋给强按下去，“动什么，掉了！”
“王！哪找的这么多蛋？！”早绑好草捆的兽人们凑着狼岩拿回来的草篮看。
有大半个篮子，怕是端了人家好几窝！
狼岩放下，道：“草里找的。”
“我们也要去找！”说着还没走，叫采集队的兽人抓住尾巴。
狼贝：“我们该回了。”
狼岩：“没有了。”
有倒是有，狼岩不可能将人家的蛋拿完了。凡事留一线，日后还能继续捡。
天不早了，今天回去只会更晚，怕是要跑到半夜。
草捆好，林楸将自己的背篓拿过来，一层草一层蛋这么垫着，面上再塞得严严实实的。
大泽水域上碎金般的波光愈长，兽人们掉头，往狼山跑。
*
傍晚，狼山山前依稀能看见些光亮。
狼冰小队的兽人们从林子里钻出来，纷纷蹲在溪边去洗手。
刚栽了些草药幼苗，手上都是泥。
狼冰正剔着指甲缝里的泥，叫忽然冲过来的狼金一撞，差点栽水里去。
他被狼金一手臂捞回来，顺带甩了他一巴掌。
“嗷！”狼金可怜兮兮地捂住胳膊。
狼溶坐在狼冰另一边，道：“冰，楸说今晚上烤鱼的，他怎么还没回来啊……”
狼金：“对啊对啊。”
狼冰：“他们去大泽了。”
“那要等到什么时候……”狼金往地上一坐，蔫巴了。
“安应该会。”
“可是安做的没有楸做的好吃。”
狼溶默默点头。
想起昨天那一顿烤鱼，咽了咽口水。
……
不管好不好吃，今晚的烤鱼反正是一个兽人做不完的。
从太阳还没落山起，狼安就已经把狼木那一小队的兽人叫过来杀鱼。
八个兽人从天亮杀到天黑，已经从一个兽人杀一条变成了流水线的刮鳞、去腮、破肚挖肠……两个兽人负责一项。
兽人的眼睛也从期待变为焦躁，进而麻木，手中机械又熟练，甚至形成了精炼的几个杀鱼步骤。
狼木：这辈子没这么木过……
从昨晚积攒到今天，几十个笼子捞起来的大大小小三百多条鱼，螃蟹跟虾就不算了，按照一个兽人分两条，怎么都够吃了。
狼木这边杀鱼，狼安那边也得忙着做。
部落里能用的陶锅、陶罐全被他拿出来了，狼石跟狼莫小队的兽人也给他叫了过来，帮忙洗配菜跟调料。
就这一下，部落里能用的香料得用得干干净净。
为了保证味道，狼安打算小锅小锅做。
别以为他刚刚没听到小狼们说什么。
他狼安虽平日里没做过什么好吃的，不代表他不会，只是嫌麻烦。
烤鱼他打算分三批。
狼木那边杀完的鱼一送来，立马上火烤。
“安，楸还没回来。”狼兽人看安已经忙起来，纷纷围过来，守了他一圈。
狼安：“楸教了我的，我会。”
狼兽人们不说话，一双双眼睛只盯着他。
他们很不想怀疑安，但是参考之前的食物，安做得虽然不差，但还是比不上楸做的。
分明楸都答应他们了……
狼安：“等楸回来，你们半夜都吃不到。”
兽人们趴地，尾巴恹恹搭在地上。
楸说话不算话。
狼安：很不想做了！
狼火眼尖，见狼安脸色，赶紧将兽人们驱离。吃不到好吃的是一回事，吃不饱又是另一回事。
……
天黑了，篝火烧得极盛。
兽人们捧着碗吃得狼吞虎咽，那边吃着时不时嚎着感叹一句，因为嚎得多了，都不显得稀奇了。
“安！你做得也好吃！”兽人叼着个完整的鱼骨头，意犹未尽地嗦着汁水。双眼灿亮，就差摇尾巴。
狼安：不是看不上他做的。
对兽人们来说，大锅菜是温饱，小锅菜是享受。那用各种香料做出来的烤鱼，连汤水都想叫人舔干净了。
怎么会那么好吃！
好吃到想起有些兽人多吃了一次，一下就不满足了。
狼兽人暗戳戳地打着吃第二次的主意，撺掇着当队长的狼火、狼乔几个兽人去狼安跟前说。
狼安看一眼就知道他们要放什么屁，毫不理会，赶紧收拾收拾睡觉去了。
累死他了！
果然不能弄小锅菜。
*
林楸他们回部落时，差不多正好半夜。
夜格外的静，兽人们饥饿难耐，全靠惦记着部落的一口美味撑着回来。
一钻出林子，张嘴就开始嚎。
山洞里睡得正熟的兽人一下支棱耳朵，美梦被打断，知道是兽人回来了，幽怨地翻个身，扣紧耳朵接着睡。
这两队兽人也有四十多个，烤鱼都给他们留着，全装在陶锅里，加热一下就能吃。
林楸算是队伍里最轻松的兽人。
到了部落，他迷迷糊糊地滑下狼岩的背，先去灶台那边生火。
狼兽人想是闻到了味儿，一步步挪过来，巴巴地看着。
加热过的烤鱼味道更加香浓，肉浸足了汤汁，味道更醇厚。
睡在草窝里的兽人们眼睛一睁，倏地坐起来，眼睛放光地盯着外面。
狼安提醒：“王在，你们敢抢？”
兽人耷拉耳朵，盘成一坨，尾巴盖在鼻尖。
陶锅里余烬刚熄，加热不用多久，林楸叫兽人们拿碗来分。
估摸着数量，一个兽人两条，小盆似的套碗占得满满当当，再夹点青菜，盛一些汤，只闻一下兽人就忍不住了。
兽人喝汤汁当稀粥一样吸溜。
有些累的，就趴在矮墙上，只顾着往嘴里塞。
林楸也撑在墙面，慢慢吃着。
这矮墙做得太合适，利用率可太高了。
外面兽人疯狂往肚里填食，洞内兽人馋得直舔嘴巴，各个草窝里都是咽口水的声音。
狼安爪垫捂住耳朵，也忍不住。
反正他都会，大不了明天再做。
兽人吃完，往地上一躺，闭眼就不想起来。碗筷四处放着，舔得锃光瓦亮的，一点不像刚刚用过。
林楸吃得晚，也吃得慢。
吃到后头几乎是闭着眼睛往嘴里塞。
狼岩看了眼地上的兽人们，道：“碗洗了，草窝里去睡。”
狼群动了动，想耍赖，“王，困……”
狼岩：“我给你们洗。”
话一落，狼兽人猛地睁眼，连滚带爬抱着碗去溪边。赶紧洗完，往草窝里一滚，呼呼大睡。
林楸：……
瞌睡都没了。
他侧目看着倚在矮墙的兽人，见他还看着自己，林楸道：“我还没吃完。”
林楸就给自己盛了一条小鱼，配菜放得多。
狼岩：“没催你。”
林楸沉沉点头，还是困。
吃完后，他慢悠悠地去溪边洗碗，再洗漱。
狼岩再一次见到他咬树枝，问：“牙不舒服？”
林楸眼皮睁不开，合着眼睛道：“刷牙，剔除牙缝里残留的食物碎屑，免得以后烂牙。”
狼岩：“会疼吗？”
林楸看了看咬碎的枝条，摇头。
狼岩：“部落里有些上了年纪的兽人会喊牙疼，小狼也会。”
林楸想想，道：“等我抽个空，做些牙刷。”
林楸其实也不想咬枝条，只是没遇到合适的毛。
部落之前抓的那些弯角兽、尖角兽还有呦呦兽的毛都不行。
狼岩听名字大概知道牙刷是个什么东西，点了点头，收拾了两人的碗筷拿去放着。
林楸再洗了把脸，迷迷瞪瞪回山洞。
*
林楸一觉睡过上午，中午才爬起来，正好吃饭。
今天狩猎队一队跟采集队没出去。昨天回来太晚，需要补觉。
林楸吃过午饭，狼贝就过来问那些蛮草怎么处理。
林楸：“还是泡水，沤烂了皮才行。”
狼贝应下，就叫兽人干活，林楸则赶紧去祭司山洞。
学了一个下午，林楸打着哈欠从祭司山洞里出来，看狼山棚子顶上的烟囱里炊烟袅袅，已经开始做晚饭了。
更远处，林子里有些动静。
小狼们在里头吵吵闹闹的，不知道是不是又在刨山药。
狼山前不见带回来的那些草，林楸找了兽人问，才知道放狼山西边的小河里泡着了。
林楸踩着草鞋，往西边去。
正巧看着狼岩从西边山洞里出来，林楸加快脚步，走着走着忽然一顿。
他眼睁睁地看着脚下的草鞋甩了出去。
林楸脚趾蜷缩。
西边碎石多，林楸踮着脚埋头往前走。
狼岩捡起，看了眼，“坏了。”
林楸耳尖一点薄红，唇微抿，有些不好意思地拿过来，“没事，我再做。”
狼岩看着林楸脚，脚底粉白，有草鞋压出来的印记。没有大部分兽人脚下都有的茧子。
“来这边做什么？”
“看看蛮草，顺便找你。”
“嗯？”
林楸趿拉着草鞋，靠近河边，边问：“有没有什么动物的毛偏硬一点的？”
“做牙刷？”
林楸点头。
狼岩：“圆鼻兽。”
林楸：“好抓吗？”
狼岩点头，“林子里就有，我叫小狼去看看。”
圆鼻兽喜欢打洞，体型小，一般夜间出来。它们的皮毛粗硬，不过肉是酸的，吃了闹肚子。
掏洞的事儿，适合小狼。
chapters.translated_text:
Lang You didn't have to carry any weight, so he was currently lying on top of the large beast covered in grass leaves, resting his chin on its tail.

The large beast underneath was dead as a doornail.

"Where's the King?" he asked.

Lin Qiu, while tying up the grass rope, shook his arm and moved a bit further away from him, saying, "He went towards the east just now."

As he spoke, not long after, a black speck appeared in the east.

"Awoo!" The lying beastman suddenly stood up.

Lin Qiu was startled.

Lang Bei pressed the wolf's head down by force, "What are you moving for? It'll fall off!"

"King! Where did you find so many eggs?!" The beastmen who had already finished tying their grass bundles gathered around to look at the grass basket Lang Yan had brought back.

It was more than half a basket full; he must have raided several nests!

Lang Yan put it down and said, "Found them in the grass."

"We want to go find some too!" Before they could even leave, they were grabbed by the tail by the beastmen of the gathering team.

Lang Bei: "We should head back."

Lang Yan: "There are no more."

There were some, but it was impossible for Lang Yan to take all of someone's eggs. Leave a little room for everything so you can continue to forage in the future.

It wasn't early anymore; going back today would only be later, and they would probably have to run until midnight.

Once the grass was bundled, Lin Qiu brought over his own basket, padding it with a layer of grass and a layer of eggs, then stuffing the top tightly.

The golden, shimmering ripples on the Daze waters grew longer, and the beastmen turned around and ran toward Wolf Mountain.

*

In the evening, some faint lights could be seen in front of Wolf Mountain.

The beastmen of Lang Bing's squad emerged from the forest and squatted by the stream to wash their hands.

They had just planted some medicinal herb seedlings, and their hands were covered in mud.

Lang Bing was just picking the mud out from under his fingernails when he was bumped by Lang Jin, who had rushed over, and almost fell into the water.

He was fished back by Lang Jin's arm, and he gave him a slap in passing.

"Awoo!" Lang Jin covered his arm pitifully.

Lang Rong sat on the other side of Lang Bing and said, "Bing, Qiu said he was making grilled fish tonight, why hasn't he come back yet..."

Lang Jin: "Yeah, yeah."

Lang Bing: "They went to the Daze."

"Then how long do we have to wait..." Lang Jin sat on the ground, wilting.

"An probably knows how."

"But what An makes isn't as delicious as what Qiu makes."

Lang Rong nodded silently.

Thinking of the grilled fish from yesterday, he swallowed his saliva.

...

Regardless of whether it was delicious or not, one beastman couldn't finish making the grilled fish tonight.

Since before the sun went down, Lang An had already called the beastmen from Lang Mu's squad over to kill the fish.

Eight beastmen killed from dawn until dark, moving from one beastman killing one fish to an assembly line of scaling, removing gills, gutting, and removing intestines... two beastmen were responsible for each task.

The beastmen's eyes also changed from anticipation to restlessness, and then to numbness; their hands were mechanical and skilled, even forming a refined set of fish-killing steps.

Lang Mu: I've never been this wooden in my life...

Accumulating from last night to today, there were over three hundred fish of various sizes caught in dozens of cages, not counting the crabs and shrimp. According to two fish per beastman, it was plenty to eat.

While Lang Mu's side was killing fish, Lang An had to be busy cooking on his side.

All the pottery pots and jars that could be used in the tribe were brought out by him, and he also called over the beastmen from Lang Shi and Lang Mo's squads to help wash the side dishes and seasonings.

Just like that, all the spices that could be used in the tribe were used up completely.

To ensure the flavor, Lang An planned to cook in small pots.

Don't think he didn't hear what the little wolves were saying just now.

Although he, Lang An, hadn't made anything delicious on weekdays, it didn't mean he couldn't; he just found it troublesome.

He planned to grill the fish in three batches.

As soon as the fish killed by Lang Mu's side were delivered, they were immediately put on the fire to grill.

"An, Qiu hasn't returned yet." The wolf beastmen saw that An was already busy, so they gathered around him, guarding him in a circle.

Lang An: "Qiu taught me, I know how."

The wolf beastmen didn't speak, their eyes just staring at him.

They really didn't want to doubt An, but referring to the previous food, although what An made wasn't bad, it still couldn't compare to what Qiu made.

Clearly, Qiu had promised them...

Lang An: "If you wait for Qiu to come back, you won't even get to eat by midnight."

The beastmen lay on the ground, their tails drooping listlessly on the floor.

Qiu didn't keep his word.

Lang An: I really don't want to do it anymore!

Lang Huo had sharp eyes; seeing Lang An's expression, he quickly drove the beastmen away. Not being able to eat something delicious was one thing, but not being full was another.

...

It was dark, and the bonfire was burning intensely.

The beastmen held their bowls and ate ravenously, howling and sighing from time to time as they ate. Because they howled so much, it didn't seem strange anymore.

"An! What you made is also delicious!" The beastman gnawed on a whole fish bone, sucking on the juices with lingering desire. His eyes were bright, and he was just short of wagging his tail.

Lang An: It's not that they look down on what he makes.

For the beastmen, big-pot food was for filling their stomachs, while small-pot food was for enjoyment. That grilled fish made with various spices made people want to lick the bowl clean of even the soup.

How could it be so delicious!

It was so delicious that when they remembered some beastmen had eaten an extra portion, they were immediately unsatisfied.

The wolf beastmen secretly plotted to eat a second time, instigating the team leaders like Lang Huo and Lang Qiao to go and talk to Lang An.

Lang An knew what they were up to with one look, ignored them completely, and quickly packed up to go to sleep.

He was exhausted!

As expected, he shouldn't make small-pot dishes.

*

When Lin Qiu and the others returned to the tribe, it was almost exactly midnight.

The night was exceptionally quiet, and the beastmen were famished, relying entirely on the thought of the tribe's delicious food to make it back.

As soon as they emerged from the forest, they opened their mouths and started howling.

The beastmen sleeping soundly in the caves pricked up their ears, their dreams interrupted. Knowing the beastmen had returned, they turned over resentfully, covered their ears, and continued sleeping.

These two squads of beastmen also had over forty people; the grilled fish had all been saved for them, all packed in pottery pots, and could be eaten after being heated up.

Lin Qiu was considered the most relaxed beastman in the team.

Upon arriving at the tribe, he slid off Lang Yan's back in a daze and went to the stove to start a fire first.

The wolf beastmen seemed to have smelled the scent, moving over step by step, looking on eagerly.

The heated grilled fish tasted even more fragrant and rich, the meat soaked with the soup, making the flavor even more mellow.

The beastmen sleeping in the grass nests opened their eyes, sat up abruptly, and stared outside with glowing eyes.

Lang An reminded them: "The King is here, do you dare to snatch it?"

The beastmen drooped their ears, curled into a ball, and covered their noses with their tails.

The embers in the pottery pots had just gone out, and heating them didn't take long. Lin Qiu told the beastmen to bring their bowls to divide it.

Estimating the quantity, two fish per beastman, the bowl-like pots were filled to the brim. Adding some greens and ladling in some soup, the beastmen couldn't help themselves just by smelling it.

The beastmen slurped the soup like thin porridge.

Some who were tired just lay on the low wall, only caring about stuffing their mouths.

Lin Qiu also leaned on the wall, eating slowly.

This low wall was made just right; its utilization rate was too high.

The beastmen outside were frantically stuffing food into their stomachs, while the beastmen inside the cave were so tempted they kept licking their lips; the sound of swallowing saliva could be heard in every grass nest.

Lang An covered his ears with his paw pads, unable to help himself either.

Anyway, he knew how to make it, so he could just make it again tomorrow.

After the beastmen finished eating, they lay on the ground and didn't want to get up when they closed their eyes. The bowls and chopsticks were left everywhere, licked so clean and shiny that they didn't look like they had just been used.

Lin Qiu ate late and slowly.

By the end, he was almost stuffing food into his mouth with his eyes closed.
