Lang Yan looked at the beastmen on the ground and said, "Wash the bowls and go sleep in the grass nests."

The wolf pack moved, wanting to be lazy, "King, sleepy..."

Lang Yan: "I'll wash them for you."

As soon as the words fell, the wolf beastmen opened their eyes wide, scrambling to grab their bowls and heading to the stream. They finished washing quickly, rolled into their grass nests, and fell into a deep sleep.

Lin Qiu: ...

His sleepiness was gone.

He glanced at the beastman leaning against the low wall, and seeing that he was still looking at him, Lin Qiu said, "I haven't finished eating yet."

Lin Qiu had only served himself one small fish, with plenty of side dishes.

Lang Yan: "I'm not rushing you."

Lin Qiu nodded heavily, still sleepy.

After eating, he slowly went to the stream to wash his bowl and then freshened up.

Lang Yan saw him biting a branch again and asked, "Is your tooth uncomfortable?"

Lin Qiu couldn't keep his eyelids open and said with his eyes closed, "Brushing my teeth, removing the food residue from between my teeth to avoid rotten teeth later."

Lang Yan: "Will it hurt?"

Lin Qiu looked at the bitten branch and shook his head.

Lang Yan: "Some older beastmen in the tribe will cry out about toothaches, and the little wolves do too."

Lin Qiu thought about it and said, "When I have time, I'll make some toothbrushes."

Lin Qiu actually didn't want to bite branches, but he hadn't found suitable bristles.

The fur of the curved-horn beasts, sharp-horn beasts, and you-you beasts that the tribe had caught before wouldn't work.

Lang Yan roughly knew what a toothbrush was from the name, nodded, and tidied up the two's bowls and chopsticks to put them away.

Lin Qiu washed his face again and returned to the cave in a daze.

*

Lin Qiu slept through the morning and didn't crawl up until noon, just in time for lunch.

Today, the first hunting squad and the gathering squad didn't go out. They returned too late yesterday and needed to catch up on sleep.

After Lin Qiu finished lunch, Lang Bei came over to ask how to handle those wild grasses.

Lin Qiu: "Still need to soak them in water until the skin rots."

Lang Bei agreed and told the beastmen to get to work, while Lin Qiu hurried to the priest's cave.

After studying for an afternoon, Lin Qiu walked out of the priest's cave yawning, seeing smoke curling from the chimney on the roof of the Wolf Mountain shed, and dinner had already begun.

Further away, there was some movement in the forest.

The little wolves were making a racket inside, not knowing if they were digging for yams again.

The grass brought back wasn't in front of Wolf Mountain. Lin Qiu asked a beastman and found out it was soaking in the small river on the west side of Wolf Mountain.

Lin Qiu stepped in his grass sandals and headed west.

He happened to see Lang Yan coming out of the west cave. Lin Qiu quickened his pace, but stopped suddenly while walking.

He watched helplessly as the grass sandal on his foot flew off.

Lin Qiu curled his toes.

There was a lot of gravel on the west side, so Lin Qiu walked on tiptoe, head down.

Lang Yan picked it up and took a look, "It's broken."

The tips of Lin Qiu's ears turned a faint red, his lips pursed slightly, and he took it over with some embarrassment, "It's okay, I'll make another one."

Lang Yan looked at Lin Qiu's feet; the soles were pink and white, with marks from the grass sandals. There were no calluses that most beastmen had on their feet.

"What are you doing here?"

"Checking the wild grass, and looking for you by the way."

"Hmm?"

Lin Qiu shuffled in his grass sandals, approached the riverbank, and asked, "Is there any animal fur that's a bit stiffer?"

"To make a toothbrush?"

Lin Qiu nodded.

Lang Yan: "Round-nose beast."

Lin Qiu: "Is it easy to catch?"

Lang Yan nodded, "There are some in the forest, I'll tell the little wolves to go take a look."

Round-nose beasts like to dig holes, are small in size, and usually come out at night. Their fur is coarse and hard, but their meat is sour and causes stomach upset if eaten.

Digging holes is a job suitable for the little wolves.

第47章
chapters.source_text:
西边山洞的前的小河不宽，蛮草全散开了泡在水中。
河下游不远，兽人们直接将岸边的树木砍倒，横亘在河床，阻挡蛮草随水流飘走。
林楸估摸着要泡个四五天。
狼岩站在他后头，目光落在林楸的脚踝。
他踝骨细，草鞋磨久了，有个深色的印记。
草鞋容易破，用兽皮做应该会好一点。
狼山山前，狼嚎声响起，缓慢悠长。像雪季后天上悠然飘过的云，透着一股安然闲适的味道。
兽人在叫吃晚饭了。
狼嚎声还未落，西边山洞猛地蹿出几个兽人，以狼莫为首，往狼山前狂奔而去。
狼岩：“……走吧。”
河岸是个斜坡，林楸草鞋踩在上面，脚慢慢往下滑。他正打算换个位置上去，狼岩拉住他胳膊。
“别用干草做了，一次穿不了多久，回去我给你拿兽皮。”
林楸：“你还有兽皮吗？”
狼岩松开他，“给你做几双兽皮鞋是够的。”
两人并不着急，散步一样回到狼山山前，兽人们都已经大半吃到了肉汤。
今日做的是蛇羹，部落里没什么别的香料了，只有盐。
长虫抓得不多，狼安混了点其他肉煮着。兽人们吃这个的次数少，不放别的，也吃得津津有味。
等林楸捧着一碗蛇羹，瞧着肉跟其他的没什么两样，肉质甚至更加细腻。
但一想到那还没剥皮的样子……
林楸唇角绷直了，挪开一些。
“不行。”
狼岩在他旁边，“吃不了？”
林楸摇头。
有心理障碍。
“不吃我吃！”边上狼莫凑过来，将自己的空碗往前伸了伸，眼睛如宝石般闪亮，“我能吃。”
狼岩：“……莫。”
狼莫默默缩头，看着林楸，手指又往林楸跟前戳了戳自己的空碗。
林楸：“你吃吧。”
“嘿！”狼莫立马抱着林楸的碗往自己碗里一倒，汤汁儿都刮得干干净净，顶着狼岩的视线，他小声道，“王，是楸让给我的，是他主动的。”
刮完，他抱着碗就吃。
旁边比他落后一步的兽人虎视眈眈呢，他保证，他一走立马就会被抢。
兽人们遗憾，后头叹气声都打了几个旋儿。
林楸见狼岩皱眉，一派轻松道：“背回来那些蛋是不是还没动？”
狼岩低头，林楸脸上带着点笑，面庞洁净，目色清澈。没有一点勉强。
看来是真不喜欢。
他道：“没动。”
“那我能吃吗？”
“吃多少都行。”
两人同时开口，视线相触，林楸眼里漾起清浅的笑，竖着两根纤长手指晃了晃，“我就拿两个。”
狼岩：“就是给你跟幼崽找的。”
他目光直白，坦坦荡荡。灰眸像圆月明辉映照的夜空，静谧深邃。旁边围着一圈兽人，听着也没什么异议。
林楸：“好。”
有他的份额，那他就用。
蛇羹其实挺补人，味道也应该不错，但林楸就是接受不了。他以前被勉强太多，现在做什么自己舒服就好。
晚饭他做得简单些，直接做了个蒸蛋。
再吃个青菜沙拉，一顿也就够了。
狼莫、狼西早早吃完，又来林楸跟前守着。他们眼睁睁看着分明是加了水的蛋，都打散了，放锅里咕噜咕噜一下，打开就成了凝在一块的。
兽人睁大眼睛，傻兮兮看着。
林楸：“要尝尝吗？”
“要！”
三个兽人齐点头，狼果洗完幼崽的碗，见状，脚下一拐，靠了过来。
“尝什么？”
林楸：“蒸蛋。”
狼莫几个也知道分寸，刚刚吃饱了，还没那么那么馋嘴。一人分了一点，刚抿进嘴，呲溜一下就滑进肚子里去了！
“诶！”像是要把没尝出味儿的蒸蛋给叫住，还没尝出味儿呢！
狼果抿着蛋羹，点点头，“适合给幼崽吃。”
林楸：“背篓里的蛋都是给幼崽的。”
狼果：“那我明天给他们做，你待会儿教教我。”
“好。”林楸应下，看面前三个一脸失望的狼兽人，眼里略有思索。
林楸上辈子从小到大每天被要求吃一个蛋，乃至工作后都被监督着，衣食住行全被管制，压得他喘不过气。
他其实不怎么爱吃。
且不说这个，那会儿的蛋确实极好获取。
可现在的兽人们吃个蛋都难。
几个兽人就围着一碗蛋羹发馋，苦哈哈的，看着有点可怜……
远远的，狼岩倚在矮墙，长腿微屈，任由吃饱了的幼崽往自己身上爬。
他看着狼莫几个馋嘴的。
就那么两个蛋，分了他们，自己还能剩多少。
“王。”坐在肩上的幼崽打个嗝，狼岩垂眸，脸颊擦过幼崽小身子，“再叫一声。”
“王呜！”奶呼呼的，叫狼岩下巴往幼崽身上抵了抵。
“会说话了。”
狼雪爪子往前挥了挥，“啾！”
狼岩：“蛋有多的，叫狼果给你们做。楸没空。”
狼雪歪了歪脑袋，看着他们的王。脑袋吧唧一下贴在他脸上，爪子抱着他脖子，“困。”
狼岩托着他后背，将幼崽抱在怀里。
看脚下其他爬了半晌没爬上来的幼崽，也一并捞起来，托在手臂。
幼崽有一个能开口了，是好事儿。
他指腹压了压狼雪耳朵，这个幼崽出生前先没了阿父，出生后不久，阿爸也没了。
狼岩掌心托住幼崽小脑瓜，就这么抱了会儿，听到幼崽睡熟的呼噜声，才将他们送回草窝。
*
蛋是稀缺品，兽人们偶尔在林子里也会碰到红鸟的蛋，全凭运气。
狼莫躺在草窝里，狼腿儿翘起，人模人样地晃啊晃。
草窝边，狼西挤过来，嘴筒子抵在他脖子边，小声道：“我们明天去找蛋，我还想吃。”
狼莫爪子撸了一把狼西脑门，“谁不想。”
“红鸟都没几个，红鸟蛋哪里好找。王他们还是从大泽那边带过来的，那么远……”
“我们也去大泽。”
狼莫静静看着他。
狼西：“……你看着我我也还是想吃。”
狼莫：“我明天去问问楸，他总有很多办法。”
“嘿，好！”
狼西往自个儿窝里一滚，安然如睡。
狼莫翻个身，下巴搭在草窝边缘，盯着山洞最里面的林楸。
他想来想去，要吃蛋只能再去大泽，那边很多很多。
可蛋不好捡。
楸应该有怎么捡蛋的办法吧……
狼莫拿不准，眼皮太重，啪的一下盖上就打起了呼噜。
林楸睡到半夜，幼崽又爬窝了。
他听到“啾啾”的声音，只当幼崽乱叫，掌心往幼崽脑袋上一盖，揣入兽皮中，抱着睡去。
狼雪拱了拱他的手心，湿润的圆眼静静瞧着他，又凑近了舔了舔林楸的脸，脑袋才贴着他颈侧团成一个圆。
“啾……”
林楸无意识地拍拍幼崽的背，继续安眠。
狼岩看着这一幕，想到山洞的其他幼崽。
像狼雪这样的，其实还有，但他们小一些，懵懵懂懂。
今年雪季后都没有新的幼崽出生，部落里有伴侣的兽人屈指可数，兽人繁衍也是个大问题。
狩猎队都是青壮年的雄性兽人，中年兽人还要多些，一共六十多个。还有狼石的护卫队，也是十几个雄兽人。
小狼们没长成，暂且都不算。
而亚兽人、雌性兽人就只有成年采集队的那二十多个，还有部落留守的狼安几个。
采集队的亚兽人大部分都有伴侣，而留守狼山的几个亚兽人也已经步入中年，少几个有伴侣，其他的伴侣也都没了。
狼兽人一辈子就认一个伴侣，让他们再找也不现实。
狼岩甩了下尾巴，有些焦躁。
这五六十个雄兽人光棍儿，上哪儿找那么多雌性兽人跟亚兽人。
*
林楸醒来时，发现隔壁草窝边缘挂着的毛毛又多了。
他挪了挪盖在自己脸上的幼崽，捡起一撮，狼毛随着呼吸轻轻晃动。
狼岩掉毛掉得好像越来越多了。
他抓着狼毛搓成一团儿，下意识掰开两个草窝中间的缝隙。当看到那快堆满了底部的狼毛球，有些纳闷。
他什么时候薅了这么多？
“楸。”幼崽也趴在草窝边缘看。
林楸清清楚楚听到他叫自己名字，托着幼崽，“会说话了？”
“楸。”幼崽欢喜，叫得更加响亮。
林楸捏了捏幼崽小耳朵，“只会说这个？”
幼崽亲亲热热地仰头舔他的手，叫林楸捏住嘴筒子，往兽皮衣里一揣。
“不要乱舔，脏。”
草窝缝里狼毛球太多，也看着邋遢。他拿来个藤筐过来，将缝隙里的狼毛球全捡起来放筐里。
藤筐搁在草窝旁边。
林楸站在原地看了会儿，幼崽也从兽皮衣里探出个头，盯着那一筐毛球。
“楸！”
林楸捏住他小爪子，纠正：“不是楸，是球。”
“楸。”
“球。”
“楸！”
林楸想到自己从狼岩身上薅下来这么多狼毛，听着耳根子发痒。他又找来些干草给盖上，也没谁掀开来看。
林楸将缝隙打扫干净，看狼果跟其他幼崽不在山洞，将狼雪带出去。
幼崽跟同伴汇合，滚一团玩儿去。
他们肚子都鼓鼓的，瞧着刚刚吃过了。
成年兽人们趴在矮墙，面前放着个大碗。鱼汤肉是肉，汤是汤，还有一点腥。
兽人们不情不愿地吃着，比喝草药糊糊都艰难。
分明以前吃过更难吃的。
“楸，快来。”狼安道。
林楸走到灶台边，看锅里还剩下不少。
“都不吃？”
狼安叹气，“什么都没了，做出来的味道不好。”
不过再叫兽人们吃一次烤鱼，用尽调料也还是乐意。
“祭司那也没了？”
狼安：“我没敢去问。”
林楸：“我待会儿去问问。”
chapters.translated_text:
The small river in front of the western cave was not wide, and the wild grass was fully spread out, soaking in the water.

Not far downstream, the beastmen had directly chopped down trees along the bank and laid them across the riverbed to prevent the wild grass from drifting away with the current.

Lin Qiu estimated it would need to soak for four or five days.

Lang Yan stood behind him, his gaze falling on Lin Qiu’s ankles.

His ankle bones were thin, and after wearing the straw sandals for so long, there was a dark mark.

Straw sandals broke easily; using animal hide would probably be better.

In front of Wolf Mountain, the sound of wolf howls rang out, slow and long. Like clouds drifting leisurely across the sky after the snow season, it carried a sense of peace and comfort.

The beastmen were calling that dinner was ready.

Before the howling had even faded, several beastmen darted out of the western cave, led by Lang Mo, and sprinted toward the front of Wolf Mountain.

Lang Yan: "...Let’s go."

The riverbank was a slope, and as Lin Qiu’s straw sandals stepped on it, his feet slowly slid downward. Just as he was planning to move to a different spot to climb up, Lang Yan grabbed his arm.

"Don't use dried grass anymore; they don't last long. When we get back, I'll get you some animal hide."

Lin Qiu: "Do you still have animal hide?"

Lang Yan let go of him, "There’s enough to make you a few pairs of hide shoes."

The two were in no rush and walked back to the front of Wolf Mountain as if taking a stroll; most of the beastmen had already received their bowls of meat soup.

Today’s meal was snake stew; there were no other spices in the tribe, only salt.

Not many snakes had been caught, so Lang An had mixed in some other meat to boil. The beastmen rarely ate this, but even without other seasonings, they ate it with great relish.

When Lin Qiu held a bowl of snake stew, he noticed the meat didn't look any different from others; the texture was even more delicate.

But the moment he thought about what it looked like before being skinned...

Lin Qiu’s lips tightened, and he moved the bowl away slightly.

"I can't."

Lang Yan was beside him, "Can't eat it?"

Lin Qiu shook his head.

He had a mental block.

"If you don't eat it, I will!" Lang Mo, who was nearby, leaned over and stretched his empty bowl forward, his eyes shining like gemstones, "I can eat it."

Lang Yan: "...Mo."

Lang Mo silently shrank back, looked at Lin Qiu, and poked his empty bowl toward Lin Qiu again.

Lin Qiu: "You eat it."

"Hey!" Lang Mo immediately grabbed Lin Qiu’s bowl and poured it into his own, scraping out every bit of broth. Under Lang Yan’s gaze, he whispered, "King, Qiu gave it to me; it was his own idea."

After scraping it clean, he held the bowl and started eating.

The beastmen beside him, who were a step behind, were eyeing it covetously; he was certain that if he walked away, it would be snatched immediately.

The beastmen felt regretful, and sighs swirled around behind them.

Seeing Lang Yan frown, Lin Qiu said in a relaxed tone: "The eggs we brought back haven't been touched yet, right?"

Lang Yan looked down. Lin Qiu’s face held a faint smile; his features were clean, and his eyes were clear. There was no sign of reluctance.

It seemed he really didn't like it.

He said: "They haven't been touched."

"Then can I eat them?"

"Eat as many as you want."

The two spoke at the same time. Their eyes met, and a light smile rippled in Lin Qiu’s eyes as he held up two slender fingers and shook them, "I'll just take two."

Lang Yan: "They were meant for you and the cubs anyway."

His gaze was direct and open. His gray eyes were like the night sky illuminated by the full moon, quiet and deep. The circle of beastmen nearby heard this and had no objections.

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

If there was a share for him, then he would use it.

Snake stew was actually quite nourishing, and the taste should have been good, but Lin Qiu just couldn't accept it. He had been forced to do too many things in his past life; now, he just did whatever made him feel comfortable.

He made his dinner simpler, opting for steamed eggs.

With a side of vegetable salad, it was enough for a meal.

Lang Mo and Lang Xi finished eating early and came to wait by Lin Qiu again. They watched with their own eyes as he added water to the eggs, whisked them, put them in the pot, and after a quick boil, they turned into a solid mass.

The beastmen opened their eyes wide, watching foolishly.

Lin Qiu: "Want to taste it?"

"Yes!"

The three beastmen nodded in unison. Lang Guo, having finished washing the cubs' bowls, saw this and veered over.

"Taste what?"

Lin Qiu: "Steamed eggs."

Lang Mo and the others knew their limits; they had just eaten their fill, so they weren't that greedy yet. Each was given a small portion, and as soon as it touched their tongues, it slid down their throats!

"Hey!" It was as if they wanted to call back the steamed egg they hadn't even tasted properly; they hadn't even gotten the flavor yet!

Lang Guo savored the egg custard and nodded, "It’s suitable for the cubs to eat."

Lin Qiu: "The eggs in the basket are all for the cubs."

Lang Guo: "Then I'll make it for them tomorrow; you teach me later."

"Okay." Lin Qiu agreed, looking at the three disappointed wolf-beastmen in front of him, his eyes thoughtful.

In his past life, Lin Qiu had been required to eat an egg every day from childhood, and even after he started working, he was monitored; his life, food, clothing, and travel were all controlled, which made him feel like he couldn't breathe.

He actually didn't like eating them much.

Not to mention that, eggs were indeed very easy to get back then.

But for the beastmen now, even getting an egg was difficult.

Several beastmen were drooling over a bowl of egg custard, looking miserable and a bit pitiful...

In the distance, Lang Yan leaned against the low wall, his long legs slightly bent, letting the cubs who had finished eating climb all over him.

He watched Lang Mo and the others, who were craving food.

With only those two eggs, if they were shared, how much would be left for himself?

"King." The cub sitting on his shoulder burped. Lang Yan lowered his eyes, his cheek brushing against the cub’s small body, "Say it again."

"Wang wu!" It sounded milky, making Lang Yan press his chin against the cub.

"It can talk now."

Lang Xue waved his paws, "Qiu!"

Lang Yan: "There are more eggs; tell Lang Guo to make them for you. Qiu is busy."

Lang Xue tilted his head, looking at their King. He pressed his head against his face and wrapped his paws around his neck, "Sleepy."

Lang Yan supported his back and held the cub in his arms.

Seeing other cubs at his feet who had been trying to climb up for a while, he scooped them up as well and held them in his arms.

It was a good thing that one of the cubs could speak.

He pressed his fingertips against Lang Xue’s ears. This cub had lost his father before he was born, and not long after he was born, his mother had passed away too.

Lang Yan cradled the cub’s little head in his palm, holding them for a while, and only after hearing the cubs' snoring did he send them back to the grass nest.

*

Eggs were a scarce commodity; beastmen would occasionally come across red bird eggs in the forest, but it was all down to luck.

Lang Mo lay in the grass nest, his wolf legs propped up, shaking them in a human-like manner.

Beside the grass nest, Lang Xi squeezed over, his snout resting near his neck, and whispered: "Let’s go find eggs tomorrow; I still want to eat some."

Lang Mo stroked Lang Xi’s forehead with his paw, "Who doesn't?"

"There aren't many red birds, and red bird eggs aren't easy to find. The King and the others brought those from the Great Marsh, which is so far away..."

"We’ll go to the Great Marsh too."

Lang Mo looked at him quietly.

Lang Xi: "...Even if you look at me like that, I still want to eat them."

Lang Mo: "I’ll ask Qiu tomorrow; he always has many ways of doing things."

"Hey, good!"

Lang Xi rolled into his own nest, falling peacefully asleep.

Lang Mo turned over, resting his chin on the edge of the grass nest, staring at Lin Qiu in the deepest part of the cave.

He thought and thought; to eat eggs, they could only go to the Great Marsh, where there were many, many of them.

But eggs were hard to collect.

Qiu should have a way to collect eggs...

Lang Mo wasn't sure, but his eyelids were too heavy; they snapped shut, and he began to snore.

Lin Qiu slept until the middle of the night, when a cub climbed into his nest again.

He heard a "chiu-chiu" sound, but thinking it was just the cub making noise, he covered the cub’s head with his palm, tucked it into his animal hide, and hugged it to sleep.

Lang Xue nudged his palm, his moist, round eyes watching him quietly, then leaned in to lick Lin Qiu’s face before resting his head against his neck, curling into a ball.

"Chiu..."

Lin Qiu patted the cub’s back unconsciously and continued to sleep.

Lang Yan watched this scene, thinking of the other cubs in the cave.

There were others like Lang Xue, but they were smaller and still ignorant.

No new cubs had been born since the snow season this year; the number of beastmen in the tribe with partners could be counted on one hand, and beastman reproduction was a major problem.

The hunting team consisted of young, strong male beastmen, with more middle-aged beastmen, totaling over sixty. There was also Lang Shi’s guard team, which had over a dozen male beastmen.

The wolf pups hadn't grown up yet, so they didn't count for now.

As for the sub-beastmen and female beastmen, there were only the twenty or so in the adult gathering team, plus Lang An and a few others left behind in the tribe.

Most of the sub-beastmen in the gathering team had partners, while the few sub-beastmen left behind at Wolf Mountain were already middle-aged; few had partners, and the others had lost theirs.

Wolf-beastmen only recognized one partner in their lifetime, so it wasn't realistic to ask them to find others.

Lang Yan flicked his tail, feeling somewhat restless.

With fifty or sixty single male beastmen, where were they going to find so many female beastmen and sub-beastmen?

*

When Lin Qiu woke up, he found that there was more fur hanging on the edge of the adjacent grass nest.

He moved the cub that was covering his face, picked up a tuft, and the wolf fur swayed gently with his breathing.

It seemed Lang Yan was shedding more and more fur.

He rolled the wolf fur into a ball and subconsciously pried open the gap between the two grass nests. He was puzzled when he saw that the bottom was almost filled with balls of wolf fur.

When did he pluck so much?

"Qiu." The cub was also lying on the edge of the grass nest, watching.

Lin Qiu clearly heard him call his name, and he supported the cub, "You can talk now?"

"Qiu." The cub was happy and called out even louder.

Lin Qiu pinched the cub’s little ears, "Is that all you can say?"

The cub affectionately tilted his head to lick his hand, so Lin Qiu pinched his snout and tucked him into his animal hide clothes.

"Don't lick randomly, it’s dirty."

There was too much wolf fur in the gaps of the grass nest, and it looked messy. He brought over a rattan basket and picked up all the wolf fur balls from the gaps, putting them into the basket.

The rattan basket was placed next to the grass nest.

Lin Qiu stood there watching for a while, and the cub also poked his head out from the animal hide clothes, staring at the basket of fur balls.

"Qiu!"

Lin Qiu pinched his little paw and corrected him: "Not Qiu, it’s ball."

"Qiu."

"Ball."

"Qiu!"

Lin Qiu thought about how he had plucked so much wolf fur from Lang Yan, and his ears felt itchy just hearing it. He found some dried grass to cover it up, and no one would lift it to look anyway.

Lin Qiu cleaned the gap, and seeing that Lang Guo and the other cubs weren't in the cave, he took Lang Xue out.

The cub joined his companions and rolled into a ball to play.

Their bellies were all round, looking like they had just eaten.

The adult beastmen were lying on the low wall with large bowls in front of them. The fish soup had meat, and the soup was just soup, with a bit of a fishy smell.

The beastmen ate reluctantly, finding it even harder than drinking herbal paste.

Clearly, they had eaten worse things before.

"Qiu, come quickly," said Lang An.

Lin Qiu walked to the stove and saw that there was still quite a bit left in the pot.

"No one is eating?"

Lang An sighed, "Everything is gone, and the taste isn't good."

However, if they were asked to eat grilled fish again, they would still be happy to use up all the seasonings.

"Is it gone at the Priest’s place too?"

Lang An: "I didn't dare to ask."

Lin Qiu: "I’ll go ask later."

chapters.title: 第48章
chapters.source_text:
“没了没了！哪有什么调料，那都是草药！你给我翻完了治病怎么办？！”祭司瞪着一来山洞就讨要药材的兽人，横眉冷眼，气得吹胡子。
为一口吃的这么尽心尽力，叫他当个祭司还推三阻四。
林楸：“真没了？今早的鱼汤您也喝了，好吃不？”
老祭司：“有食物就不错了，管他好不好吃。”
以前没食物都要饿死了，现在还敢挑！
林楸：“哎！”
老祭司：“哎什么哎！赶紧学，除虫的草药粉你会做了吗？狼冰都学到跳祭舞了。”
林楸：“学。”
但是他坚决不学什么祭舞。
在老祭司山洞待了半天，中午又得做饭。祭司这里保管还有存货，林楸目光往木架上飘去，叫祭司斥道：“什么都往我这里拿！”
林楸：“您这是现成的，最多。”
“小狼都给着你种草药了，你不知道叫他们种去！”
林楸一顿，“有道理。”
“那您这儿有没有种子？”
祭司骂骂咧咧，整个部落没兽人敢这么来他这儿这么要东西，就这个最气人！
果然失忆了还是脾性不改，专跟人对着干！
林楸满意地抱着一兽皮兜的种子出去，他翻开看了看，生姜、野蒜、花椒……但凡之前用过的调料，种子应有尽有。
祭司这里不仅收集草药，还收集种子。
小狼们今天不在，林楸打算待会儿跟狼安他们规划一下土地，找地方种了。
昨儿小狼抓到些圆鼻兽割了些毛下来，林楸趁着空，得把牙刷做出来。
狼安看着他下来，笑着过去接。
“这么多，够吃一段时间了。”
林楸：“吃不了，都是用来种的。”
狼安看向那块种尾巴草的土地，“还种啊？”
林楸：“总外面找不是办法。”
狼安其实叫采集队留意了，有没有看他们今天回来就知道。
“那就种吧。”
午饭依旧不好吃，兽人们默默吐着鱼刺，忍不住道：“安今天做的好难吃。”
“安说没调料了。”
“油都没了。”
“那我们要吃这个吃到什么时候？”
“不知道啊……”
美好的生活，怎么就这么短暂呢！
下午，狼安抓了部落壮丁，叫狼木几个挨着种植尾巴草那一块儿翻地。
依旧要翻得四四方方的，草根碎石都得捡出来。
尾巴草那块地每年都要种，只稍微捡捡石头除除草就种了，新翻一块地就麻烦多了。
草根错节，小树到处都是，刨着刨着底下还可能藏着几十斤的大石头。
这是个大工程，没几天弄不完。
种地的事儿急不来，有狼安盯着。
林楸则把做牙刷的材料跟工具找齐，盘腿坐在棚下的矮墙上，开始做牙刷。
圆鼻兽的毛制粗硬，也不像象毛那样跟钢针似的。
毛毛用加草木灰的水煮过脱脂，然后把细木削成扁头。对齐打孔，用细线套着一撮毛的一头穿过孔洞，如此反复，再剪平毛毛，这就行了。
林楸做的时候，狼果跟狼安几个过来凑热闹。
一个个虽然不知道这个用来做什么，但也跟着帮忙，不是削木头，就是捻毛毛。
林楸又做了几把骨柄的，骨柄打磨圆润，看着差不到哪里去。
一堆的材料用完，做出来十多个。
狼果拿着看了又看，“楸，这个用来洗什么？”
林楸：“刷牙。”
“刷牙？”
林楸点头，一人送了一把。
“我们吃东西会把食物残留在牙齿缝隙中，时间久了，牙齿会黑，会坏，还会疼。”
狼果本来还说自己不需要的，一听，立马收好。
狼安：“怪不得部落里好多兽人总喊牙疼，就是去祭司那里吃了草叶止住疼，没多久又会疼。”
他们还以为刺儿扎进去了。
林楸：“我教教你们怎么刷，先试试好不好用。”
说着，一群兽人往溪边去。
幼崽争先恐后地跟着，狼果回头，问：“楸，幼崽需要刷吗？”
林楸：“还小，用兽皮沾水擦擦就好，主要是养成早晚清洁的习惯。”
牙刷挺好用，比林楸咬树枝方便多了。
没有清洁牙齿的牙粉，便用木炭清洁。
刷完牙，狼果舌尖抵着牙齿，感受到干干净净带点涩意的清爽感，一时间还有些不适应。
“好奇怪……”狼果又忍不住舔了舔牙齿。
狼安看着手中的牙刷，“楸，我们能多做些吗？”
狼兽人没有刷牙的习惯，也不是不爱干净，是没这个意识。
论起爱干净，他们已经比那些邋里邋遢的部落好多了，有些部落的兽人一点不讲究，排泄都在自己山洞附近呢。
雨季一闷热，到处都臭烘烘的，能将兽人熏晕过去。
狼安想想脸都有些绿。
想起部落有些兽人张口滂臭，他立马决定部落人手一个，必须强制早晚清洁。
林楸：“可以，最好多做，这个要勤换。”
长期用木炭清洁牙齿也不行，林楸还打算做点牙粉出来。
牙粉的材料多种多样，丁香、薄荷、白芷、茯苓、冰片……端看要什么功效，用什么材料。
只做清新口气，清洁牙齿，最简单的丁香薄荷之类的就够了。
东边大陆不一定有这些植物，但相同功效的，他却能找得出来七八种。这就体现出他跟着祭司学草药的用处了。
祭司那里草药种类多，不常用的草药数量却少，林楸先去要了些出来配置一点。
研究一下午，林楸做牙粉，兽人们做牙刷，弄出来七八种各种香味儿的、效用的，最后叫来兽人们挑选。
狼安：“味道太重的不适合我们，阿嚏！就像这样，阿嚏！一闻到就打喷嚏。”
他捏着鼻子，呛得流眼泪。
林楸拿起他看过的那一款牙粉，里面放了花椒，还有其他带有消炎作用的草药。
“这个我再改进改进。”
这是祭司指定要的，里面消炎的两三味草药都是他挑的。听说他做牙粉，叫他给那些喊牙疼的兽人专门做的一款。
狼雨几个捂着鼻子，飞快点头。
林楸：“再看看其他？”
一共做了八款牙粉，镇静止痛的，消炎除菌的，清新口气的，都有。
除了最开始叫林楸收起来的那一款，兽人们挑挑拣拣，一脸为难。
林楸看着太阳都往西边坠了，兽人们还没选出来。
“楸，哪个都想要……”兽人们不好意思。
他就知道。
林楸：“做牙粉简单，你们挑两种合适大部分兽人的，我大量做。其他的我教你们怎么样？”
“好！”
牙刷牙粉还得给老祭司跟狼岩看，林楸便收到架子上，等狼岩回来再说。
到做饭的时候了，狼安几个忙去了，林楸则教狼果给幼崽蒸蛋。
另一边，狼木刨地刨得两腿抽筋，一个趔趄栽在地里，并排的几个兽人见状，齐齐往他身上歪倒过来。
爪子抽搐，脏兮兮的灰狼道：“木，我不行了。”
狼木抖了抖爪子，泥都嵌爪垫里去了。
他被兽人们压在底下，前头是刚刚翻耕出来的土地，蓬松柔软，旁边是已经小腿高的尾巴草。
经过兽人们精心照料，密密丛丛，比往年的茎秆似乎要粗壮一点点。
狼木：“下去，我要喘不过气了。”
背上的狼往旁边一滚，躺在土中。
狼木坐起来，走到旁边的尾巴草地，小心翼翼勾着爪子，将边缘几株冒出来的草给刨掉。
边上狼挪动着，勾着草叶玩儿，叫狼木一爪子拍开。
“木，是不是又该撒草木灰了？”
狼木：“不知道，问楸去。”
他慢悠悠起身，往棚子方向走。
今年尾巴草长得好，冬季能少挨一点饿。
狩猎队跟采集队回来了，兽人在准备晚饭。狼莫背上趴着狼西，也从西边回来。
狼西掏了下狼莫耳朵，“你问了楸没有？”
狼莫打了个哈欠，“这不现在去问。”
狩猎采集队的兽人回来就往棚子底下趴了一地，幼崽蹦蹦跳跳，把他们当小山爬。
狼岩就坐在矮墙上靠着木柱，垂眸听林楸给他说牙刷跟牙粉。
“狼安说每个兽人配两把。”
狼岩：“怕不行。”
狼兽人牙口好，有些牙根痒痒，一口下去就破了。得多准备着。
“叫安……叫小狼负责吧，能做多少做多少。”
林楸：“小狼有时间？”
狼岩：“少玩儿点就有了。”
狼岩将狼溶招来，给小狼安排。
林楸感觉到袖口被扯了扯，回头见狼莫跟狼木眼里闪着火花，针锋相对。
狼西悄悄道：“楸，一边说话。”
林楸不明所以，跟着狼西往一边去。
“怎么了？”
“楸，你知道怎么靠近大泽中间的那些草岛吗？”
林楸摇摇头，这个他还真没办法。
“你们想吃蛋？”
狼西耷拉个眼皮，脑袋上全是泥灰，“没吃够。”
林楸倒是能做船，但是那里边还处处是沼泽，再想到那湖水中翻滚的蟒蛇，林楸打了个寒颤。
他道：“我想想办法。”
“嗷！”狼西精神了。
只要能吃到，不管早晚，狼都等得下去。
“楸！”狼木终于突破狼莫的封锁。
可到了林楸身边，他又有些惭愧。
狼莫哼声。
林楸对他们的态度一样，只是问：“有什么事？”
狼木：“我只是问问，尾巴草需不需要再撒点草木灰……我刚刚看着，这一次的尾巴草比以往的好一点。”
狼莫也不哼了，眺望东边的地。
狼木不说还没怎么注意，往年他们种的尾巴草长得应该也算茂密，就是混在草丛里，东一块西一块的。
可今年的，放眼望去那一片全是尾巴草，一样的叶片，差不多的高度，长势喜人。
狼莫：“多撒点草木灰是不是长得更好？”
林楸：“也要适度，就像你吃饱了还往肚子里塞。”
狼莫：“那我也塞得下。”
林楸：“……”
chapters.translated_text:
"It's gone, it's all gone! There are no seasonings, those are medicinal herbs! What will you do if you use them all up and someone gets sick?!" The priest glared at the beastman who came to the cave demanding herbs, his eyes narrowed and his beard bristling with anger.

He was so dedicated when it came to food, yet he dragged his feet whenever he was asked to serve as a priest.

Lin Qiu: "Are they really gone? You drank the fish soup this morning, too. Was it good?"

Old Priest: "Having food is good enough; who cares if it tastes good or not."

In the past, they were starving without food, and now they were being picky!

Lin Qiu: "Hey!"

Old Priest: "Hey what hey! Hurry up and learn. Have you learned how to make the insect-repellent herbal powder yet? Lang Bing has already learned to perform the sacrificial dance."

Lin Qiu: "I'll learn."

But he was determined not to learn any sacrificial dance.

After spending half the day in the old priest's cave, he had to cook lunch again. The priest still had supplies stored here. Lin Qiu's gaze drifted toward the wooden shelves, prompting the priest to scold him: "You always take everything from me!"

Lin Qiu: "Yours are ready-to-use, and you have the most."

"The little wolves are already planting herbs for you; why don't you tell them to plant these too!"

Lin Qiu paused, "That makes sense."

"Then do you have any seeds here?"

The priest grumbled and cursed. In the entire tribe, no other beastman dared to come and demand things from him like this; this one was the most infuriating!

As expected, even after losing his memory, his personality hadn't changed—he was always going against people!

Lin Qiu left, satisfied, carrying a pouch made of animal skin filled with seeds. He opened it to take a look: ginger, wild garlic, Sichuan peppercorns... every seasoning he had used before was there in seed form.

The priest didn't just collect medicinal herbs; he collected seeds as well.

The little wolves weren't around today, so Lin Qiu planned to map out the land with Lang An and the others later and find a place to plant them.

Yesterday, the little wolves caught some round-nosed beasts and sheared off some fur. Lin Qiu decided to take advantage of the free time to make toothbrushes.

Lang An saw him coming down and walked over with a smile to take the load.

"There's so much, this will last for a while."

Lin Qiu: "We can't eat this; it's all for planting."

Lang An looked at the plot of land where the tail-grass was planted, "We're planting more?"

Lin Qiu: "Constantly searching outside isn't a long-term solution."

Lang An had actually asked the gathering team to keep an eye out, and they would know if they had found anything when they returned today.

"Then let's plant."

Lunch was still not very good. The beastmen silently spat out fish bones and couldn't help but say: "An's cooking is so bad today."

"An said there are no seasonings left."

"Even the oil is gone."

"Then how long do we have to eat this?"

"I don't know..."

How could such a wonderful life be so short!

In the afternoon, Lang An rounded up the able-bodied men of the tribe and told Lang Mu and the others to turn the soil next to the tail-grass patch.

It still had to be turned into a neat square, and all grass roots and gravel had to be picked out.

The tail-grass plot was planted every year, so they usually just picked out a few stones and pulled some weeds, but breaking new ground was much more troublesome.

The grass roots were tangled, small trees were everywhere, and as they dug, they might even find large stones weighing dozens of pounds hidden underneath.

This was a major project that wouldn't be finished in a few days.

Farming couldn't be rushed, and Lang An was there to supervise.

Lin Qiu gathered the materials and tools for the toothbrushes, sat cross-legged on the low wall under the shed, and began his work.

The round-nosed beast's fur was coarse and stiff, but not like elephant hair, which was as sharp as steel needles.

The fur was boiled in water with wood ash to degrease it, then thin pieces of wood were whittled into flat heads. He aligned them, drilled holes, used thin thread to loop one end of a tuft of fur through the hole, repeated the process, and then trimmed the fur flat. That was it.

While Lin Qiu was working, Lang Guo and Lang An came over to join the fun.

Although they didn't know what these were for, they helped out—either whittling wood or twisting the fur.

Lin Qiu also made a few with bone handles; the bone handles were polished until smooth, and they didn't look half bad.

Once the pile of materials was used up, he had made over a dozen.

Lang Guo picked one up and looked at it repeatedly, "Qiu, what is this used to wash?"

Lin Qiu: "Brushing teeth."

"Brushing teeth?"

Lin Qiu nodded and gave one to everyone.

"When we eat, food gets left in the gaps between our teeth. Over time, teeth turn black, rot, and start to ache."

Lang Guo had originally said he didn't need one, but as soon as he heard this, he immediately put it away.

Lang An: "No wonder so many beastmen in the tribe always complain of toothaches. Even after going to the priest and eating herbal leaves to stop the pain, it starts hurting again before long."

They had thought it was just a thorn stuck in their gums.

Lin Qiu: "I'll teach you how to brush. Let's try it out and see if it works well."

With that, the group of beastmen headed toward the creek.

The cubs followed eagerly. Lang Guo turned back and asked: "Qiu, do the cubs need to brush?"

Lin Qiu: "They're still small; just use animal skin dipped in water to wipe them. The main thing is to build the habit of cleaning morning and night."

The toothbrush worked quite well, much more convenient than the tree branches Lin Qiu had been biting on.

Since there was no toothpaste to clean their teeth, they used charcoal instead.

After brushing, Lang Guo pressed his tongue against his teeth, feeling a clean, slightly astringent freshness, and felt a bit unaccustomed to it for a moment.

"So strange..." Lang Guo couldn't help but lick his teeth again.

Lang An looked at the toothbrush in his hand, "Qiu, can we make more?"

Wolf beastmen didn't have the habit of brushing their teeth. It wasn't that they didn't like being clean; they just lacked the awareness.

When it came to cleanliness, they were already much better than those sloppy tribes. Some tribes were completely unrefined and would even defecate near their own caves.

When the rainy season became humid, it would stink everywhere, enough to make a beastman faint.

Lang An's face turned a bit green at the thought.

Remembering that some beastmen in the tribe had foul breath when they opened their mouths, he immediately decided that everyone in the tribe should have one, and they must be forced to clean their teeth morning and night.

Lin Qiu: "Sure, it's best to make more; these need to be replaced frequently."

Cleaning teeth with charcoal long-term wasn't ideal, so Lin Qiu also planned to make some tooth powder.

The ingredients for tooth powder were diverse: cloves, mint, dahurian angelica, poria, borneol... it all depended on what effect was desired and what materials were used.

For just freshening breath and cleaning teeth, the simplest things like cloves and mint were enough.

The Eastern Continent might not have all these plants, but he could find seven or eight with the same effects. This showed the value of him learning herbs from the priest.

The priest had a wide variety of herbs, though the less commonly used ones were in short supply. Lin Qiu went to ask for some to formulate a small batch.

After researching all afternoon, Lin Qiu made the tooth powder while the beastmen made toothbrushes. They ended up with seven or eight types with various scents and effects, and finally called the beastmen over to choose.

Lang An: "The ones with strong scents aren't for us. Achoo! Just like this one, achoo! I sneeze as soon as I smell it."

He pinched his nose, his eyes watering from the irritation.

Lin Qiu picked up the tooth powder he had been looking at; it contained Sichuan peppercorns and other herbs with anti-inflammatory properties.

"I'll improve this one."

This was one the priest had specifically requested. The two or three anti-inflammatory herbs in it were chosen by him. Hearing that he was making tooth powder, the priest had asked him to make a special version for the beastmen who complained of toothaches.

Lang Yu and the others covered their noses and nodded rapidly.

Lin Qiu: "Want to look at the others?"

They had made eight types of tooth powder in total: calming and pain-relieving, anti-inflammatory and antibacterial, and breath-freshening—they had them all.

Except for the one Lin Qiu had put away at the start, the beastmen picked and chose, looking troubled.

Lin Qiu saw the sun sinking toward the west, and the beastmen still hadn't made a choice.

"Qiu, we want all of them..." the beastmen said, feeling embarrassed.

He knew it.

Lin Qiu: "Making tooth powder is simple. You pick two that are suitable for most beastmen, and I'll make them in bulk. How about I teach you how to make the others?"

"Okay!"

The toothbrushes and tooth powder still needed to be shown to the old priest and Lang Yan, so Lin Qiu put them on the shelf to wait until Lang Yan returned.

It was time to cook. Lang An and the others went to get busy, while Lin Qiu taught Lang Guo how to steam eggs for the cubs.

On the other side, Lang Mu's legs were cramping from digging, and he stumbled into the field. The few beastmen standing next to him saw this and all tipped over onto him.

With twitching claws, the dirty gray wolf said: "Mu, I can't do it anymore."

Lang Mu shook his claws, mud embedded in his paw pads.

He was pinned under the beastmen; in front of him was the newly turned, soft, fluffy soil, and beside him was the tail-grass that had already grown to calf-height.

Thanks to the beastmen's careful care, the stalks were dense and seemed a bit thicker than in previous years.

Lang Mu: "Get off, I can't breathe."

The wolf on his back rolled to the side and lay in the dirt.

Lang Mu sat up, walked to the adjacent tail-grass patch, and carefully used his claws to dig out the few weeds that had sprouted at the edge.

The wolf on the side was moving around, playing with the grass leaves, and Lang Mu swatted him away with a paw.

"Mu, is it time to spread wood ash again?"

Lang Mu: "I don't know, go ask Qiu."

He stood up slowly and walked toward the shed.

The tail-grass was growing well this year, so they might suffer a little less hunger in the winter.

The hunting and gathering teams returned, and the beastmen were preparing dinner. Lang Mo, with Lang Xi on his back, also returned from the west.

Lang Xi poked Lang Mo's ear, "Did you ask Qiu?"

Lang Mo yawned, "I'm going to ask now."

The beastmen from the hunting and gathering teams collapsed under the shed as soon as they returned, while the cubs jumped around, climbing on them like they were little hills.

Lang Yan sat on the low wall, leaning against a wooden pillar, lowering his eyes to listen to Lin Qiu tell him about the toothbrushes and tooth powder.

"Lang An said every beastman should have two."

Lang Yan: "That might not be enough."

Wolf beastmen had strong teeth, and sometimes their gums itched, so one bite could break them. They needed to prepare more.

"Tell An... tell the little wolves to be responsible for it. Let them make as many as they can."

Lin Qiu: "Do the little wolves have time?"

Lang Yan: "They will if they play a little less."

Lang Yan summoned Lang Rong to make arrangements for the little wolves.

Lin Qiu felt his sleeve being tugged. He turned to see Lang Mo and Lang Mu with sparks in their eyes, facing off against each other.

Lang Xi whispered: "Qiu, let's talk over there."

Lin Qiu didn't understand, but followed Lang Xi to the side.

"What's wrong?"

"Qiu, do you know how to get close to those grass islands in the middle of the Great Marsh?"

Lin Qiu shook his head; he really had no way to do that.

"Do you want to eat eggs?"

Lang Xi drooped his eyelids, his head covered in mud and dust, "We didn't get enough."

Lin Qiu could build a boat, but the place was full of swamps, and when he thought of the pythons rolling in the lake water, Lin Qiu shivered.

He said: "I'll think of a way."

"Awoo!" Lang Xi perked up.

As long as they could eat them, the wolves could wait, no matter how long it took.

"Qiu!" Lang Mu finally broke through Lang Mo's blockade.

But once he reached Lin Qiu, he felt a bit ashamed.

Lang Mo snorted.

Lin Qiu treated them the same, only asking: "What's the matter?"

Lang Mu: "I was just asking if the tail-grass needs more wood ash... I was looking just now, and this batch of tail-grass is better than before."

Lang Mo stopped snorting and looked toward the field in the east.

He hadn't noticed until Lang Mu mentioned it. In previous years, the tail-grass they planted was supposed to be dense, but it was mixed in with other weeds, scattered here and there.

But this year, as far as the eye could see, it was all tail-grass—same leaves, similar height, growing impressively.

Lang Mo: "Would it grow even better if we spread more wood ash?"

Lin Qiu: "It needs to be in moderation, just like how you shouldn't keep stuffing your stomach after you're full."

Lang Mo: "But I can still stuff more in."

Lin Qiu: "..."

“其实粪肥最好。”
狼木点头。
他知道楸起先说过，要那发酵过的粪肥，但是动物都少，哪里来那么多粪……
狼西抬头，“鸟粪行吗？”
狼莫：“哪有什么鸟粪？”
狼木几个兽人一激灵，对视一眼，道：“大泽那边全是鸟粪。”
而那周围的树长得一棵比一棵好。
原来粪这么有用！
林楸：“之前不是说没有？”
林楸只到了大泽外围，他们根本进不去。也没看到哪里有那么多的鸟粪。
狼木道：“不是我们部落的。”
狼西：“在大泽最南边，鸟粪堆得厚厚一层，草都不长了。”
兽人们都嫌弃埋汰，没将那一部分纳入领地中。南部那些小部落也离那块地方远远的。
狼木：“那些粪堆了好多年了，是不是就算发酵过了？”
林楸：“那可是好东西。”
狼木跟狼莫面上肃然，立马找狼岩去了。
狼西目光追着他们去，又回头看林楸，“那蛋呢？”
粪肥都有解决法子了，蛋还没有。
林楸看着这个懒懒散散趴在矮墙上的兽人，“我得想想。”
暂不说大泽的鸟蛋不好捡，那么远的路途，狼兽人是跑回来的，运输途中怕都得碎一半。
捡又能捡个几次，鸟飞走了就没了。
不如，自己养些产蛋的。
林楸觉得，比起会迁徙的候鸟，生活在林子里的红鸟就很合适。
它们食谱杂，不像大泽那些鸟，大多数只吃鱼。
天黑了，狼山前两根烟囱冒出滚滚浓烟。
连廊尽头的棚底下，四口灶炖汤，两口灶炒菜。
早上采集队见识到那白水煮鱼多难吃，今天是铆足了劲儿找能增香的调料，没有调料，那就找味道冲的呛草。
趴在连廊上的兽人们脑袋就朝着灶台这边棚子，眼巴巴地等食。
狼岩刚交代完小狼负责做牙刷以及牙粉的事。
正好狼冰的采集小队专门负责采集草药，顺带也可以把牙粉用到的材料找齐。
这边狼溶刚走，狼莫跟狼木就来了。
狼岩远远看了眼林楸。
他蹙着眉，不知道兽人们跟他说了什么，现在绞尽脑汁在思考。
狼岩收回目光，落在眼前两个兽人身上，问：“陶器那边，怎么样了？”
狼莫正色道：“现在可以保证做陶锅十个里面有五个是完好的。做泥坯大家都熟练了，只是烧陶缸还不行。我们明天打算再烧一次，这次又稍微调整了比例，只等烧出来看看。”
狼岩：“能多烧尽量多烧，别忘了还有支部落。”
狼莫：“知道了王。”
狼岩又看向狼木，“你们刚刚问楸什么事？”
狼木立即道：“王，楸说尾巴草需要粪肥，大泽南边堆积的鸟粪就可以。虽然那不是我们领地内，但也是无主的地方……”
其实那边相当于狼部落跟其他小部落之间的隔离带，两边的兽人从不踏足。
他们过去，会引起小部落的恐慌。
兽神大陆各个部落也有约定俗成的规矩，部落领地间间隔的地方，一旦踏足，立即驱离。
要是徘徊不走，视同宣战。
其他部落虽弱小，但狼部落不是不讲道理的，相反，他们在兽神大陆上的风评是极好的。
他们反正确定领地范围后，就从来没去过那边。
可部落为了尽可能有足够多的食物吃，兽人们种植尾巴草的规模是能种植的极限，地块儿翻得格外大。
尾巴草要粪肥，现在翻地种的其他植物肯定也需要粪肥，这需要大量的鸟粪。
狼岩：“可以。”
狼木惊讶，这么干脆？
他还以为要再劝一劝。
狼岩：“提前告知那边一声就行。”
狼木立马道：“那我们去！”
绕地到大泽南边就要好几天，一来一回运输，更是费事儿。这个需要提前安排。
狼岩：“部落商量一下。”
尾巴草的事是大事，饭还没好，狼岩叫上林楸，以及狩猎队、采集队、护卫队的队长，立马去了祭司山洞。
一说事关尾巴草的事，祭司当即同意。
但怎么挖，用什么运，是个问题。
路途遥远，食物不够。
要靠兽人们扛回来，怕没走到大泽就饿死了。
狼岩：“先攒肉干。”
兽人们尽管可以在路上打猎，但一来一回六七天，要是哪天没打到，拉鸟粪都没力气。
攒肉干，行远路，是兽人们的习惯。
林楸：“河里鱼多，可以烘些鱼干。至于怎么抓到更多的鱼，这个我可以想办法。”
听林楸这话，又是要弄新东西。
狼岩：“能行？”
林楸：“我试试，应该可以。”
“好。”
食物的事能解决，然后就是怎么运送。
在曾经确定部落领地范围的时候，兽人们去南边走过一遭，那鸟粪堆得跟土壤一样，一层接着一层。
那些候鸟年年回来，年年栖息在大泽，就往那地儿拉。
狼兽人鼻子灵，挖粪遭罪，运粪遭罪……
大伙儿想想，有些可怜自家兽人。
狼游：“要不就用兽皮袋，这个能收口，绑在身上就回来了。”
狼火：“兽皮袋就那么几个。”
狼火趴地上，黑色狼毛隐隐泛红，似玄色的。还没吃饭呢，王就叫他们过来，原来是挖鸟粪的事儿。
兽皮袋算部落的重要物资，以前都是用来存放尾巴草种子以及部落重要物品。
他们迁徙，也靠着这些兽皮袋。
用来装粪……
不行。
现在兽皮珍贵，装了鸟粪以后还怎么用！
洗干净了也不行！
林楸倒是可以用蛮草做麻袋，但工程量有点大，他还打算赶制几张渔网出来捞鱼。
狼贝身量不比几个兽人矮，杵在几个领队中，气势依旧不弱。
她抱臂站立，思索下，干脆道：“用藤车拉。”
藤车是用藤条做的简易运输工具，底部放平滑的木板，靠着兽人蛮力拉。
林楸听狼岩跟他描绘了下，道：“可以改造一下。”
几个兽人看来。
楸好多的主意！
林楸道：“加两个轮子。”
林楸之前就打算做板车，但受限于工具与人力，他当时不得部落兽人信任，一个人做不出来。
现在就没这个顾虑了。
林楸用祭司山洞里两个小陶罐演示了下，陶罐放在木板底下，推动陶罐滚动。
兽人们眼睛一亮。
狼贝：“像滚木运送。”
“比那个轻松些。”林楸道。
狼岩拍板道：“可以。”
林楸抿唇，看着狼岩有些拿不准，“我担心这个不好穿林子。”
林子里那么多树枝杂草，跑几下就得绊住。
狼岩：“也比藤车好用。”
兽人们很少用藤车，部落里原来的藤车都坏了，所以林楸没看见他们用过。
用藤车时，两头狼并排在前拉着，时不时要停下来搬一下，特别麻烦。
好处就是一次性运送的东西多。
一直往南的话，领地内几乎都是平坦的地方，只要避开过于茂密的林子……稍稍清理一下路障，就好很多。
如果路上再干净平坦一些，就像狼山山前，兽人们拉着这个跑得只会更快。
只要有力，轮子就自己会往前滚动，那对狼兽人来说简直是玩具。
几乎瞬间，狼岩就想到了这双轮车的好处以及铺平路的必要。
他当即下令：“从明天开始，一队二队狩猎，三队立马开始清理路上的障碍物。”
狼兽人东南西北四个方向走，都走的一条路，草几乎都踩没了。
只路上横亘的树木他们都是跳过去，正好，赶紧把该挖的挖掉，该搬的搬走。
狼岩想到了，其他几个队长也立马想到了。
幽暗的山洞里，狼眼放光，林楸被几个大汉跟巨狼盯得不自在，挪到狼岩背后站着。
狼岩警告：“收敛点。”
他又问：“楸，两轮车怎么做？”
林楸看着狼岩垂下来的墨黑长发，背脊覆盖的肌肉漂亮，腰收窄……昏黄的光晕下，阴影分明。
林楸平静看着，只眼睫抖得有些快。
他道：“需要粗壮的原木，切割成掌宽，中间打洞，连接轴木……”
不是个轻松的活儿。
部落里有石斧、石刀一类的工具，但没有铁器，切割木头就是个难事。
狼岩想了想，道：“安、石，你们听楸的安排。”
两兽人点头。
狩猎一队二队跟狼贝的采集队负责食物，狩猎三队清理路障。
小狼负责制作牙刷牙粉。
护卫队一队明天烧陶。
剩下的狼安的队伍跟护卫队二队，都被安排给了林楸。
这样看来，没哪个队伍空闲。
狼冰后头听到这安排，心道，果然这么快兽人不够用了。
山下叫着吃饭，兽人们散去。
林楸跟狼岩走在后头，看着他发尾轻轻晃啊晃。
“王？”林楸轻声道。
他很少唤他，不喊他名字，学着其他兽人这样叫。
“嗯。”狼岩停下，灰眸看来。
“我还有个打算。”
狼岩：“什么打算？”
林楸：“养红鸟，产蛋。”
“是哪个馋嘴的又跟你说了什么？狼西？还是狼莫？”狼岩真想收拾那些贪嘴的。
林楸摇头，眼里泛起涟漪，带了些淡淡的暖意。
“早晚得养，还能补充营养。”
“小狼喜欢在林子里蹿，叫他们遇到了就抓到回来给你养。”那话音像哄狼崽，但一本正经的。
林楸：“最好抓带崽的。”
狼岩：“好，我跟他们说。”
下了山，棚子底下人影绰绰，兽人们排起长队，翘首以盼。
狼岩感觉身旁的林楸学着他步调，目光追在他腰侧，身子微微一摇一晃，是个闲适样。
他寻着视线瞥一眼。
还像个幼崽样，对他动来动去的头发感兴趣。
他问：“忙不忙得过来？不行的话，狩猎二队也可以留下来。”
林楸：“可以，只是需要时间。”
chapters.title: 第49章
chapters.translated_text:
"Actually, manure is the best."

Lang Mu nodded.

He knew that Qiu had mentioned earlier that he wanted fermented manure, but they had so few animals, where would they get so much manure...

Lang Xi looked up, "Does bird droppings work?"

Lang Mo: "Where would we get bird droppings?"

Lang Mu and the other beastmen jolted, exchanged glances, and said: "There are bird droppings everywhere over by the Great Marsh."

And the trees around that area grew better than the last.

So manure was this useful!

Lin Qiu: "Didn't you say there wasn't any before?"

Lin Qiu had only reached the outskirts of the Great Marsh; they couldn't get inside at all. He hadn't seen where there was so much bird dropping.

Lang Mu said: "It's not in our tribe's territory."

Lang Xi: "At the southernmost part of the Great Marsh, the bird droppings are piled up in a thick layer, not even grass grows there."

The beastmen all found it disgusting and didn't include that part in their territory. The small tribes in the south also stayed far away from that place.

Lang Mu: "Those droppings have been piled up for many years, does that count as fermented?"

Lin Qiu: "That's good stuff."

Lang Mu and Lang Mo looked solemn and immediately went to find Lang Yan.

Lang Xi followed them with his eyes, then turned back to look at Lin Qiu, "What about the eggs?"

They had a solution for the manure, but not for the eggs.

Lin Qiu looked at this lazy beastman sprawled on the low wall, "I have to think about it."

Not to mention that the bird eggs in the Great Marsh were hard to collect, the journey was so long that the wolf beastmen would have to run back, and half would likely break during transport.

You could only collect them a few times before the birds flew away and they were gone.

It would be better to raise some egg-laying ones himself.

Lin Qiu felt that compared to migratory birds, the red birds living in the forest were very suitable.

They had a varied diet, unlike those birds in the Great Marsh, most of which only ate fish.

It was dark, and thick smoke billowed from the two chimneys in front of Wolf Mountain.

Under the shed at the end of the corridor, four stoves were stewing soup, and two were stir-frying dishes.

In the morning, the gathering team had seen how terrible the boiled fish was, so today they were determined to find seasonings that could enhance the flavor; if there were no seasonings, they would find pungent herbs.

The beastmen sprawled on the corridor had their heads turned toward the shed by the stove, waiting eagerly for food.

Lang Yan had just finished instructing Xiao Lang to be responsible for making toothbrushes and tooth powder.

It just so happened that Lang Bing's gathering team was specifically responsible for collecting medicinal herbs, so they could also gather the materials needed for the tooth powder.

Just as Lang Rong left, Lang Mo and Lang Mu arrived.

Lang Yan looked at Lin Qiu from afar.

He frowned, not knowing what the beastmen had said to him, but he was now racking his brains in thought.

Lang Yan withdrew his gaze, landed on the two beastmen in front of him, and asked: "How is it going with the pottery?"

Lang Mo said solemnly: "Now we can guarantee that five out of ten pottery pots are intact. Everyone is skilled at making clay blanks, but firing pottery vats still doesn't work. We plan to fire again tomorrow, and this time we have slightly adjusted the ratio, just waiting to see the results."

Lang Yan: "Fire as many as possible, don't forget there are also the branch tribes."

Lang Mo: "Understood, King."

Lang Yan looked at Lang Mu again, "What did you just ask Qiu about?"

Lang Mu immediately said: "King, Qiu said that the tail grass needs manure, and the bird droppings piled up in the south of the Great Marsh will do. Although that is not in our territory, it is also unclaimed land..."

Actually, that area was equivalent to a buffer zone between the Wolf Tribe and other small tribes, and beastmen from both sides never set foot there.

If they went over, it would cause panic among the small tribes.

The various tribes on the Beast God Continent also had customary rules; once someone stepped into the space between tribal territories, they were immediately driven away.

If they lingered, it was treated as a declaration of war.

Although other tribes were weak, the Wolf Tribe was not unreasonable; on the contrary, their reputation on the Beast God Continent was excellent.

Anyway, after they determined their territory, they had never gone there.

But in order to have as much food as possible, the scale of the tail grass planted by the beastmen was at the limit of what could be planted, and the plots of land were turned over exceptionally large.

Tail grass needs manure, and the other plants they turned the land to grow definitely need manure too, which requires a large amount of bird droppings.

Lang Yan: "It's fine."

Lang Mu was surprised, so straightforward?

He thought he would have to persuade him more.

Lang Yan: "Just notify them over there in advance."

Lang Mu immediately said: "Then we'll go!"

It would take several days to go around to the south of the Great Marsh, and the transport back and forth would be even more troublesome. This needed to be arranged in advance.

Lang Yan: "Let the tribe discuss it."

The matter of the tail grass was a big deal. Before the food was ready, Lang Yan called Lin Qiu, as well as the captains of the hunting team, gathering team, and guard team, and immediately went to the priest's cave.

As soon as the matter of the tail grass was mentioned, the priest agreed immediately.

But how to dig it and what to use to transport it was a problem.

The journey was long, and there wasn't enough food.

If they had to rely on the beastmen to carry it back, they were afraid they would starve to death before reaching the Great Marsh.

Lang Yan: "Save up dried meat first."

Although the beastmen could hunt on the road, it would take six or seven days to go back and forth. If they didn't catch anything one day, they wouldn't have the strength to haul bird droppings.

Saving dried meat for long journeys was a habit of the beastmen.

Lin Qiu: "There are many fish in the river, we can dry some fish. As for how to catch more fish, I can think of a way."

Hearing Lin Qiu say this, it was another new thing to be made.

Lang Yan: "Can it be done?"

Lin Qiu: "I'll try, it should work."

"Good."

Food could be solved, then it was how to transport it.

When they were determining the tribe's territory, the beastmen had gone to the south once, and the bird droppings were piled up like soil, layer upon layer.

Those migratory birds returned every year, nested in the Great Marsh every year, and just pooped in that spot.

Wolf beastmen had keen noses; digging manure was miserable, transporting manure was miserable...

Everyone thought about it and felt a bit sorry for their own beastmen.

Lang You: "How about using animal skin bags? They can be closed, tied to the body, and brought back."

Lang Huo: "There are only a few animal skin bags."

Lang Huo lay on the ground, his black wolf fur faintly tinged with red, like dark iron. He hadn't eaten yet, and the King had called them over; it turned out to be about digging bird droppings.

Animal skin bags were important supplies for the tribe, previously used to store tail grass seeds and important tribal items.

When they migrated, they also relied on these animal skin bags.

To use them to hold manure...

No way.

Animal skins were precious now; how could they be used after being filled with bird droppings!

Even if washed clean, it wouldn't work!

Lin Qiu could use wild grass to make sacks, but the workload was a bit large, and he also planned to rush to make some fishing nets to catch fish.

Lang Bei was no shorter than the beastmen, standing among the leaders, her aura still strong.

She stood with her arms crossed, thought for a moment, and said simply: "Use a vine cart to pull it."

A vine cart was a simple transport tool made of vines, with smooth wooden boards at the bottom, relying on the beastmen's brute force to pull.

Lin Qiu heard Lang Yan describe it to him and said: "It can be modified."

Several beastmen looked over.

Qiu had so many ideas!

Lin Qiu said: "Add two wheels."

Lin Qiu had planned to make a cart before, but limited by tools and manpower, he wasn't trusted by the tribe's beastmen at the time, and he couldn't make it alone.

Now there was no such concern.

Lin Qiu used two small pottery jars in the priest's cave to demonstrate, placing the jars under a wooden board and pushing them to make the jars roll.

The beastmen's eyes lit up.

Lang Bei: "Like using rollers to transport."

"It's easier than that," Lin Qiu said.

Lang Yan made the final decision: "It can be done."

Lin Qiu pursed his lips, looking at Lang Yan, a little unsure, "I'm worried this won't be easy to get through the forest."

There were so many branches and weeds in the forest; it would get tripped up after running a few times.

Lang Yan: "It's still better than a vine cart."

The beastmen rarely used vine carts; the original vine carts in the tribe were all broken, so Lin Qiu hadn't seen them used.

When using a vine cart, two wolves had to pull side by side in front, and they had to stop and move it from time to time, which was especially troublesome.

The advantage was that it could transport a lot of things at once.

If they kept heading south, the territory was almost all flat, as long as they avoided overly dense forests... and cleared the road obstacles a little, it would be much better.

If the road was cleaner and flatter, like in front of Wolf Mountain, the beastmen would only run faster pulling this.

As long as there was force, the wheels would roll forward on their own; that was simply a toy for wolf beastmen.

Almost instantly, Lang Yan thought of the benefits of this two-wheeled cart and the necessity of paving the road.

He immediately ordered: "Starting tomorrow, the first and second hunting teams will hunt, and the third team will immediately start clearing obstacles on the road."

The wolf beastmen walked in all four directions, and they all walked on the same path, the grass almost trampled away.

They just jumped over the trees lying across the road; it was just right, hurry up and dig out what should be dug, and move away what should be moved.

Lang Yan thought of it, and the other captains immediately thought of it too.

In the dim cave, wolf eyes glowed. Lin Qiu felt uncomfortable being stared at by several big men and giant wolves, so he moved behind Lang Yan to stand.

Lang Yan warned: "Restrain yourselves."

He asked again: "Qiu, how do you make the two-wheeled cart?"

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan's long, ink-black hair hanging down, the beautiful muscles covering his back, his waist narrowing... under the dim halo, the shadows were distinct.

Lin Qiu watched calmly, only his eyelashes fluttering a little fast.

He said: "Need thick logs, cut into palm-width, drill holes in the middle, connect the axle wood..."

It wasn't an easy job.

The tribe had tools like stone axes and stone knives, but no ironware, so cutting wood was a difficult task.

Lang Yan thought for a moment and said: "An, Shi, you follow Qiu's arrangements."

The two beastmen nodded.

The first and second hunting teams and Lang Bei's gathering team were responsible for food, and the third hunting team cleared road obstacles.

Xiao Lang was responsible for making toothbrushes and tooth powder.

The first guard team would fire pottery tomorrow.

The remaining team of Lang An and the second guard team were all assigned to Lin Qiu.

Looking at it this way, no team was idle.

Lang Bing heard this arrangement from behind and thought to himself, sure enough, beastmen were not enough so quickly.

Down the mountain, they called for dinner, and the beastmen dispersed.

Lin Qiu walked behind with Lang Yan, watching his hair ends swaying gently.

"King?" Lin Qiu said softly.

He rarely called him, didn't call his name, learning to call him like other beastmen.

"Hmm." Lang Yan stopped, his gray eyes looking over.

"I have another plan."

Lang Yan: "What plan?"

Lin Qiu: "Raise red birds, for eggs."

"Which glutton said something to you again? Lang Xi? Or Lang Mo?" Lang Yan really wanted to deal with those greedy ones.

Lin Qiu shook his head, ripples appearing in his eyes, bringing a faint warmth.

"Sooner or later we have to raise them, and it can supplement nutrition."

"Xiao Lang likes to run around in the forest, tell them to catch them and bring them back for you to raise if they encounter them." The tone was like coaxing a wolf cub, but very serious.

Lin Qiu: "It's best to catch those with cubs."

Lang Yan: "Okay, I'll tell them."

Down the mountain, there were shadows under the shed, and the beastmen lined up in a long queue, looking forward to it.

Lang Yan felt Lin Qiu beside him following his pace, his eyes chasing his waist, his body swaying slightly, a leisurely look.

He glanced at him following his gaze.

Still like a cub, interested in his hair that moved around.

He asked: "Are you too busy? If not, the second hunting team can also stay."

Lin Qiu: "It's okay, it just takes time."

chapters.title: 第5章
chapters.source_text:
地耳雨后常见，味道似木耳，有一点土腥味。
林楸幼时在爷奶家吃过地耳炒鸡蛋，现在想起来还有些惦记。不过这个极不好清洗，很容易有泥沙。
现在这种情况，有吃的就行，不挑。
他把野葱放下，地耳全部给捡了。
兽人裹肉块的大叶子随处可见，林楸就用那叶子包着，一起带了回去。
他没遮掩，狼山前的兽人们本不耐他走来走去，可当看到他捧着的黑皮草，心里多了点同情。
这东西他们不吃。
兽人为了填饱肚子，动植物能进嘴的不能进嘴的都尝了个遍。
其他的多半吃了肚子疼才不碰，这个黑皮草吃完虽没事，他们这儿也多，但这东西口感怪异，一吃一嘴的沙子，大伙儿都将其排除在能吃的食物范围内。
林楸抱着自己找来的食材越过草地上趴着的几头狼，狼脑袋也如同指向标一样，跟着他转了个方向。
都盯着他呢。
溪边，林楸先把食材放下，不急着清洗。
他现在手边缺少装东西的工具，还有做饭的器具。
这些天出来之后除了用祭司的陶罐做了一次肉汤，其余时候都是做的烤肉。
他现在需要搭个土灶出来，既能做石板煎肉，也能炖汤。再编些篮子，方便带着出去找食材。
扁平的石板好找，但能做锅的却难。
林楸先在自己那火堆旁用石块混着泥垒起土灶，等着土灶干燥，又从溪水上游走到下游，翻了几十块石头，才找出块石板跟一块大小合适，中部稍微凹陷的石头出来。
石板清洗干净放在一旁，林楸拿起稍硬的鹅卵石，开始对着另一块石头凹槽处敲击。
不远处的兽人竖着耳朵，被刺得脑仁疼。
看清林楸像饿昏了头在用石头敲石头，爪子往耳朵上一扣，嘴筒子往毛尾巴下揣了揣。
往常还算安静的狼山前叮叮当当响了一下午，功夫不负有心人，篮球大小的石锅总算做成了。
往已经干了的灶上一放，大小也合适。
林楸看了眼起了血泡的手，不急着挑破，又捧着石锅去溪边，抓着石头在里头研磨，去掉表面砂砾。
打击石锅坏了几块石头，崩裂出一些石头碎片，林楸捡了几片趁手的当石刀用。
再割了些有韧性的草藤，林楸快速编了个简易的篮子。
万事俱备，林楸开始清洗野蒜跟地耳。
山洞旁侧的小溪水尤清冽，平日里兽人们用水都是从这条小溪中来。溪水甘甜，大家也都是直接捧着就喝。
地耳倒进篮子里放流水中泡着，让流水过滤一段时间，林楸先把手头的野蒜洗干净。
今晚要是有肉，便做个野蒜地耳炒肉。
林楸埋头做自己的，等地耳清洗到第三遍的时候，外出狩猎的兽人们也都回来了。
今日的猎物不大，皮毛不似之前那头弯角兽一样浅，兽人们直接剥皮处理，皮毛鞣制过后用来御寒。
猎物虽然有两头，但个头小，一人分到的肉也少。
部落的兽人往那边涌去，篝火烧起来，微微昏黑的环境中，满是兽人带着愁郁的脸。
许多兽人都捂着肚子，步履蹒跚，像极了末世片里的丧尸。
林楸在兽人中胃口已经算小还饿肚子，这些狼兽人一天只吃那么一块肉，想也知道只是维持不死。
林楸眼眸垂低，看着流水清洗过的地耳，提起篮子。
水流沿着缝隙溅落，来溪水边清洗的兽人看到他篮子里的地耳略一皱眉，又匆匆走了。
林楸避开他们，走到自己单独的火堆边坐下。
夜风吹得火焰晃动，林楸捡了几根带火的木柴放在灶口。他先用石锅烧了一次开水倒掉，又重新盛了溪水继续烧。
不多时，篝火旁的热闹沉寂。
狼莫走了过来，将今日份的肉给他。
是一块瘦肉，比之前的少了一半。
狼莫目光在他跟前的灶上流连，没说什么，憋了一口气赶紧离这边远远的。
今天肉少，他怕闻了林楸做的肉，更饿。
肉少，兽人们大多囫囵尝个味儿就没了。狼山又陷入沉默的氛围里，没有兽人玩闹，也没兽人说笑。
兽人很快散去，狼山山脚只剩下林楸和零星几个兽人。
瘦肉煎不出油，今日的野蒜地耳炒肉味道大打折扣。但菜多，他难得能吃饱。
就在林楸往石板上放地耳时，一个兽人气势汹汹走来。
仿佛是来寻仇。
林楸停下翻炒的动作，一抬头，认出是白日里常趴在山脚下的那个兽人。
他黑着脸，像要来踹翻他的锅灶。
林楸眼神冷淡，静静瞧着。
兽人步子大，几下停在他不远处，忽的扔了个东西砸在林楸怀里。
扔完，他警告道：“再叫我们发现你帮其他兽人偷食物，就不允许你待在部落。”
林楸没来得及说话，兽人就进了大山洞。
林楸皱眉，慢慢垂下睫。
火焰声烈烈，待在外面即便有火堆也有些冷了。
林楸不去想兽人刚刚的动作，正要继续煎肉，瞥见身前兽人刚刚砸来的东西。
他捡起一看，黑漆漆的，是一块硬邦邦的肉干。
眼波轻轻一晃，意识到刚刚兽人那气势汹汹的样子不是来警告他的，是来送温暖的。
还真是跟老祭司一个部落的。
林楸将肉干放下，没动。
肉也只切了一半，按照计划做了个炒肉。
只不过原本只打算用一半的地耳叫他全用了。
他先填饱肚子，喝完石锅里已经温凉的水，随后去溪边洗漱。接着再将石板上剩下的一半用大叶片裹起来，拎着进了山洞。
原野沉寂，虫鸣四面八方响起来。
风吹得林间沙沙响动，林楸感受着胃里的饱腹感，轻轻打了个哈欠。
进了山洞，他在一群狼中辨别出刚刚送他肉干的兽人。
是一头灰狼，听兽人们好像唤他狼石。
林楸不像往常那样直奔草窝，而是抓着手里的东西停在狼石的草窝边。
这异状，叫还没睡着的兽人们纷纷抬头看来。
被几十双狼眼盯着，林楸依旧坦然。
狼石不知道他要干什么，那张狼脸上慢慢变得凶巴巴的。
林楸：“不会了。”
狼石锐利的眼一懵，没明白过来。
林楸看着灰狼略微傻气的表情，道：“以后不会再偷食物。”
狼石恶声恶气：“知道就好。”
林楸将手上的食物放在他窝边，“做得多了，谢谢你的肉干。”
“我不要，你自己……”
话没说完，就见林楸已经离开草窝。
狼石盯着窝边包裹得鼓鼓囊囊的叶片，鼻尖闻到丝丝缕缕的香味。
与单纯的煎肉香味很不一样，混着些奇怪的，但又诱人的味道。
食物珍贵，他一个雄兽人怎好吃亚兽人的食物。
说了不吃……
狼石闭上眼，试图让自己沉睡。
看到林楸找地耳吃的兽人没几个，看那大叶片里包裹的东西，只闻得到一点点的肉香。
狼兽人才不占弱小的亚兽人的便宜。
大家咽了咽口水，又将脑袋藏在毛毛底下，爪子贴着空荡荡的肚子，强迫自己睡觉。
林楸不管他吃不吃，放轻脚步经过闭着眼睛的大黑狼，爬进自己窝里。
他吃得饱，又忙了一天，手上的血泡都忘了挑破，陷入草窝里没一会儿就睡去。
食物少，吃不饱对狼部落的兽人来说是常事，只要再忍一忍，没准儿第二天或者第三天就能吃到更多的肉了。
但不知为什么，这一晚格外难熬。
狼兽人鼻子灵，山洞里那丝丝缕缕的香味分明只有一点点，可偏偏被他们捕捉到。
离得最近的狼石更加难熬。
他做了个躺在肉堆里的梦，梦里那些肉格外的香。他张口去咬，分明咬住了，可吃了下去肚里更饿。
狼石翻个身，烦躁地蹬腿，脑袋耷在草窝外。
鼻尖触及那大叶片，他下意识地嗅闻。
也不知怎么，嘴筒子戳着戳着，弄开了叶片，香味直接传入梦境。
他又张口咬下，这下是实打实的叼住了肉。
好香，好吃……
窸窸窣窣，狼石好不容易做了个饱梦，发了狠地往肚里填。
不过，这肉里面怎么还有草？
狼石惊醒，动了动狼脑袋，瞧着面前被自己舔得干干净净，满是口水的大叶片，一阵心虚。
他下意识地看了看四处。
边上，狼莫幽幽盯着他，眼冒绿光，口水都拉成线了。
狼石脸上僵硬。
狼莫低低哼声，翻个身，闷闷地继续饿肚子。
狼石看着被牙齿戳了几个洞的叶片，尴尬地用爪子刨了刨，藏在草窝底下。
悄悄躺回草窝，又有些意犹未尽地舔了舔嘴巴。
肉很少，但原来把肉跟草混着能这么好吃。还有那黏糊糊的地耳，居然也能有肉味儿。
虽然先前拒绝了现在又给人家食物吃完不好意思，但那么好吃……
狼石又舔了舔嘴巴。
狼莫听得清清楚楚，狠狠地压住自己咕咕叫的肚子。
他才不羡慕！
他一点都不饿！
狼莫忍不住仰起头嗅着山洞里残留的香味，发觉自己这样太过没出息，又用爪子强压着嘴筒子藏起来。
黑皮菜，明天他就去找黑皮菜！
chapters.translated_text:
"Earth ears" (wood ear fungus) are common after rain; they taste like wood ear mushrooms but have a slight earthy, fishy smell.

Lin Qiu used to eat stir-fried earth ears with eggs at his grandparents' house when he was young, and he still craved them now. However, they are extremely difficult to clean and easily trap mud and sand.

Given the current situation, as long as there is food, he isn't picky.

He put down the wild onions and gathered all the earth ears.

The large leaves that the orcs use to wrap meat chunks are everywhere, so Lin Qiu used those leaves to wrap them up and brought them back.

He didn't try to hide them. The orcs in front of Wolf Mountain were originally impatient with him walking back and forth, but when they saw the black-skinned fungus he was holding, they felt a bit of sympathy.

They don't eat this stuff.

In order to fill their stomachs, the orcs have tasted everything, plant or animal, that could possibly be put into their mouths.

Most others only stopped touching it after getting a stomachache. While this black-skinned fungus didn't make them sick and was abundant here, it had a strange texture—every bite was full of sand—so everyone excluded it from the category of edible food.

Lin Qiu held the ingredients he had found and walked past the few wolves lying on the grass; the wolves' heads followed him like compass needles, turning in his direction.

They were all staring at him.

By the creek, Lin Qiu first put down the ingredients, not rushing to clean them.

He currently lacks tools to hold things and utensils for cooking.

Since coming out these past few days, other than making meat soup once with the priest's clay pot, he had only been eating roasted meat.

He needs to build an earthen stove now, which would allow him to pan-fry meat on a stone slab and stew soup. He also needs to weave some baskets to make it easier to carry ingredients when he goes out.

Flat stone slabs are easy to find, but something that can serve as a pot is difficult.

Lin Qiu first built an earthen stove using stones and mud next to his campfire. While waiting for the stove to dry, he walked from the upper reaches of the creek to the lower reaches, flipping over dozens of stones before finding a flat slab and a stone of suitable size with a slightly concave center.

After cleaning the stone slab and setting it aside, Lin Qiu picked up a harder pebble and began tapping at the concave part of the other stone.

The orcs not far away pricked up their ears, the sound giving them a headache.

Seeing Lin Qiu tapping stone against stone as if he were delirious with hunger, they clapped their paws over their ears and tucked their muzzles under their furry tails.

The usually quiet area in front of Wolf Mountain rang with clinking sounds all afternoon. Hard work pays off, and a basketball-sized stone pot was finally finished.

Placing it on the now-dried stove, the size was just right.

Lin Qiu glanced at the blood blisters on his hands, not rushing to pop them, and took the stone pot to the creek, using a stone to grind the inside to remove the surface grit.

He broke a few stones while hitting the pot, creating some stone shards; Lin Qiu picked up a few that were easy to hold to use as stone knives.

After cutting some flexible grass vines, Lin Qiu quickly wove a simple basket.

With everything ready, Lin Qiu began to clean the wild garlic and earth ears.

The water in the small creek beside the cave was particularly clear and cold. The orcs usually got their water from this creek. The water was sweet, and everyone would just cup it in their hands and drink.

He poured the earth ears into the basket and soaked them in the running water, letting the flow filter them for a while, while Lin Qiu first washed the wild garlic.

If there is meat tonight, he will make stir-fried meat with wild garlic and earth ears.

Lin Qiu buried himself in his work. By the time he cleaned the earth ears for the third time, the orcs who had gone out hunting had returned.

Today's prey wasn't large, and the fur wasn't as light-colored as the curved-horn beast from before. The orcs skinned and processed it directly, using the tanned fur to keep warm.

Although there were two pieces of prey, they were small, so the amount of meat each person got was minimal.

The tribe's orcs swarmed over, and as the campfire was lit, the dimly lit environment was filled with the orcs' sorrowful faces.

Many orcs were clutching their stomachs, walking unsteadily, looking exactly like zombies in a doomsday movie.

Lin Qiu already had a small appetite among the orcs and was still hungry. Knowing these wolf-orcs only ate that one piece of meat a day, it was clear they were just barely staying alive.

Lin Qiu lowered his eyes, looked at the earth ears cleaned by the running water, and picked up the basket.

Water splashed along the gaps. The orcs who came to the creek to wash frowned slightly when they saw the earth ears in his basket, then hurried away.

Lin Qiu avoided them and walked to his separate campfire to sit down.

The night wind made the flames flicker. Lin Qiu picked up a few burning logs and placed them at the stove opening. He first boiled a pot of water and poured it out, then refilled it with creek water to continue boiling.

Before long, the bustle by the campfire died down.

Lang Mo walked over and gave him today's portion of meat.

It was a piece of lean meat, half the size of the previous ones.

Lang Mo's gaze lingered on the stove in front of him, but he didn't say anything, held his breath, and quickly moved far away.

There was little meat today, and he was afraid that if he smelled the meat Lin Qiu was cooking, he would be even hungrier.

With so little meat, most orcs just swallowed it to get a taste, and it was gone. Wolf Mountain fell into a silent atmosphere again; no orcs were playing or laughing.

The orcs soon dispersed, leaving only Lin Qiu and a few scattered orcs at the foot of Wolf Mountain.

Lean meat doesn't render much oil, so today's stir-fried meat with wild garlic and earth ears wasn't as flavorful. But with plenty of vegetables, he was able to eat his fill for once.

Just as Lin Qiu was putting the earth ears onto the stone slab, an orc walked over aggressively.

It looked like he was coming for revenge.

Lin Qiu stopped stirring and looked up, recognizing him as the orc who often lay at the foot of the mountain during the day.

He had a dark face, as if he were going to kick over his stove.

Lin Qiu's expression was cold as he watched quietly.

The orc had a long stride and stopped not far from him, suddenly throwing something into Lin Qiu's arms.

After throwing it, he warned, "If we catch you helping other orcs steal food again, you won't be allowed to stay in the tribe."

Lin Qiu didn't have time to speak before the orc entered the large cave.

Lin Qiu frowned and slowly lowered his eyelashes.

The flames crackled; it was getting cold outside even with the campfire.

Lin Qiu didn't dwell on the orc's previous actions and was about to continue frying the meat when he caught sight of the thing the orc had just thrown.

He picked it up and saw it was pitch black—a piece of hard, dried meat.

His eyes flickered slightly, realizing that the orc's aggressive demeanor just now wasn't to warn him, but to show kindness.

He really is from the same tribe as the old priest.

Lin Qiu put the dried meat down and didn't touch it.

He only cut half the meat and made the stir-fry as planned.

However, he ended up using all the earth ears he had originally intended to use only half of.

He filled his stomach first, drank the water in the stone pot that had become lukewarm, and then went to the creek to wash up. Afterward, he wrapped the remaining half on the stone slab in a large leaf and carried it into the cave.

The wilderness was silent, and the chirping of insects could be heard from all directions.

The wind rustled through the forest, and Lin Qiu, feeling full, yawned softly.

Entering the cave, he identified the orc who had just given him the dried meat among the group of wolves.

It was a gray wolf; he heard the orcs call him Lang Shi.

Unlike his usual routine of heading straight to his grass nest, Lin Qiu stopped by Lang Shi's nest with the things in his hand.

This strange behavior caused the orcs who hadn't fallen asleep yet to look up one after another.

Stared at by dozens of wolf eyes, Lin Qiu remained calm.

Lang Shi didn't know what he wanted to do, and his wolf face slowly turned fierce.

Lin Qiu: "It won't happen again."

Lang Shi's sharp eyes were stunned; he didn't understand.

Lin Qiu looked at the gray wolf's slightly silly expression and said, "I won't steal food in the future."

Lang Shi said fiercely, "Good to know."

Lin Qiu placed the food in his hand by the nest, "I made too much, thank you for the dried meat."

"I don't want it, you..."

Before he could finish, he saw Lin Qiu had already left the nest.

Lang Shi stared at the bulging leaf packet by his nest, his nose catching wisps of fragrance.

It was very different from the simple smell of fried meat, mixed with some strange but tempting scents.

Food is precious; how could he, a male orc, eat a sub-orc's food?

He said he wouldn't eat it...

Lang Shi closed his eyes, trying to force himself to sleep.

Not many orcs saw Lin Qiu gathering earth ears to eat, and looking at the things wrapped in the large leaves, they could only smell a tiny bit of meat.

Wolf orcs don't take advantage of weak sub-orcs.

Everyone swallowed their saliva, hid their heads under their fur, pressed their paws against their empty stomachs, and forced themselves to sleep.

Lin Qiu didn't care whether he ate it or not; he walked lightly past the big black wolf with closed eyes and climbed into his own nest.

He was full and had been busy all day; he even forgot to pop the blood blisters on his hands, and he fell asleep in his grass nest shortly after.

Food was scarce, and being hungry was a common occurrence for the orcs of the Wolf Tribe. As long as they endured a little longer, maybe they would have more meat to eat by the second or third day.

But for some reason, this night was particularly hard to endure.

Wolf orcs have keen noses; the wisps of fragrance in the cave were clearly only a tiny amount, yet they were captured by them.

Lang Shi, who was closest, had an even harder time.

He had a dream that he was lying in a pile of meat, and the meat in his dream was exceptionally fragrant. He opened his mouth to bite, and he clearly caught it, but after eating it, his stomach felt even hungrier.

Lang Shi tossed and turned, kicking his legs in frustration, his head hanging out of the grass nest.

His nose touched the large leaf, and he subconsciously sniffed.

Somehow, as his muzzle poked at it, the leaves opened, and the fragrance went straight into his dream.

He opened his mouth and bit down again; this time, he really caught the meat.

So fragrant, so delicious...

Rustle, rustle. Lang Shi finally had a dream where he was full, and he stuffed himself fiercely.

However, why is there grass in this meat?

Lang Shi woke up with a start, moved his wolf head, and looked at the large leaf in front of him that he had licked clean and covered in saliva, feeling a sense of guilt.

He subconsciously looked around.

Beside him, Lang Mo was staring at him gloomily, his eyes glowing green, his saliva hanging in a line.

Lang Shi's face stiffened.

Lang Mo hummed lowly, turned over, and continued to endure his hunger in silence.

Lang Shi looked at the leaf with a few holes poked by his teeth, awkwardly scratched it with his paw, and hid it under the grass nest.

He quietly lay back in the nest, still licking his lips with a lingering sense of satisfaction.

There was very little meat, but who knew that mixing meat with grass could be so delicious? And that slimy earth ear actually had a meaty flavor too.

Although he felt embarrassed for eating the food after refusing it earlier, it was just so delicious...

Lang Shi licked his lips again.

Lang Mo heard it clearly and fiercely pressed down on his growling stomach.

He wasn't jealous at all!

He wasn't hungry at all!

Lang Mo couldn't help but lift his head to sniff the lingering fragrance in the cave, realized he was being too pathetic, and used his paw to force his muzzle to hide away.

Black-skinned vegetable, he's going to find black-skinned vegetable tomorrow!

After dinner, Lin Qiu didn't rush to sleep, but instead pondered the work for tomorrow.

Lang Yan glanced at the gaps in the grass, his gaze pausing for a moment before shifting to the rattan basket placed beside Lin Qiu's grass nest.

Maoqiu had picked it up.

Lang Yan hadn't played enough with Maoqiu when he was a cub, and now that it had become a habit, he didn't say much.

The next day, Lin Qiu got up early.

After breakfast, the various teams went off to attend to their own tasks, with Lang An and Lang Shi leading the beastmen over.

"Qiu, how are we going to catch fish?" Lang An asked.

Lin Qiu had checked the Man grass soaking in the water that morning and found it was retting faster than he had imagined. Lin Qiu said, "An, you all go ahead and fish out the Man grass, clean it thoroughly, and keep only the fibers."

"Got it." Lang An immediately called the beastmen to get to work.

As for Lang Shi's group, they had brought back the logs.

The logs, which were as thick as a person's embrace, needed to be cut into palm-width planks.

Lin Qiu used charcoal to draw lines on them and told the beastmen to split the wood according to the lines.

The only tools available were wolf claws, stone axes, serrated stone sickles, and clam sickles; sawing off a piece completely without damaging it was quite strenuous.

Once the task was assigned, the beastmen immediately set to work.

There was no need for Lin Qiu to supervise this side, so he went to the west.

The beastmen stood directly in the river to wash the Man grass, and the rotting leaf pulp crumbled as soon as it was rubbed. One only needed to cup their hands tightly and pull gently, and the fibers would come right off.

"Qiu, is this okay?"

Without the green leaf pulp, the thing in their hands was completely different from the leaves—it was made of thin, individual strands, like hair.

Lin Qiu: "That's fine."

Lin Qiu watched for a while, then went to find some vines and tied them around the trees outside the forest.

As soon as Lang An's group finished washing, they brought them over to hang and dry.

The fibers couldn't be exposed to direct sunlight for fear of becoming brittle.

The wind was strong under the forest canopy, so it didn't take long to dry.

Washing in running water didn't require many repetitions, and once the sub-beastmen got the hang of it, they were very fast.

While the beastmen were cleaning the Man grass, Lin Qiu began making spindles, as well as shuttles and weights for weaving the fishing nets.

In the small grove in front of Lang Mountain, there was more and more white Man grass fiber on the vines, drying until it fluttered like tassels.

Layer upon layer, wrapped under the shade of the trees, it looked quite fresh.

The beastmen had never seen anything as fine as silk like this before.

At noon, Lang An asked Lang Yu to bring two other sub-beastmen back to cook, but they discovered there were no ingredients, only then remembering to tell Lang Mu and the others to hurry and pull up the fish cages from the water.

Lang Mu and the others winced, shaking their paws that had been tortured by the wood, and ran to the riverside.

The beastmen from the third hunting team who were clearing road obstacles also had to run back for lunch; with so many people, they were busy and overwhelmed.

They just made do by stewing everything in one pot, muddling through to fill their stomachs.

After a hasty lunch, one team of beastmen went back to washing Man grass, and one team went back to cutting wood.

The third hunting team went back out under the sun to clear the road.

It didn't need to be perfectly clean; as long as there were no dead trees or branches blocking the way, it didn't matter if the grass was a bit deep.

Once they got busy, their efficiency was the highest.

In the afternoon, the two little wolf teams were the first to return.

Lang Jin's team brought back the round-nosed beasts they had caught, threw them all into a rattan basket to pen them in, and started shearing the fur.

They could have scalded them in water to pluck the fur, but they weren't eating them, so why kill them?

Lang Bing had the youths from the gathering team shave the wood.

The part for holding the fur had to be flat, and the handle could be whatever; Lang Bing thought about it and decided not to bother, telling the beastmen to handle it themselves when the time came.

It inadvertently improved efficiency.

There was too much to do; Lang Rong ran to the west side once, and after returning, he discussed it with Lang Jin and Lang Bing, splitting off half of the little wolves to help Lang An's side wash the Man grass.

With a dozen more little wolves added, the speed immediately picked up.

The obsidian flakes were very sharp, and one had to be careful not to cut their hands.

Lang Jin let out an "Ow," blood splattered, and the round-nosed beast in the basket shivered in fear.

Lang Bing looked over, a flash of disdain in his blue wolf eyes.

Clumsy.

"We'll swap!"

...

After a few days of busyness, the toothbrushes were ready, the dozen logs for wheels had been cut, and the first fishing net had entered the weaving stage.

Without Lang Yan needing to call them, the beastmen who had seen Lin Qiu brushing his teeth obediently came to collect theirs.

The toothbrushes were packed in rattan baskets, and the tooth powder was kept in small jars.

Lang Bing was in charge of distribution; as the beastmen took them from his hands, he had to remind them: "If it breaks, it's gone."

It wasn't that they couldn't make more, it was just that Lang Bing intended to take the little wolves to help Lin Qiu.

Toothbrushes were a small matter; other things were more important right now.

The wolf beastman: "If it's gone, I just won't brush my teeth."

Lang Bing: "Don't come crying to me when your teeth rot. And don't even think about eating the delicious food Qiu makes later."

The wolf beastman immediately abandoned the idea of being lazy.

Telling them they weren't allowed to eat food made by Qiu? Impossible!

Lang Rong stood especially seriously, his voice mild: "I'll supervise. Brush morning and night; for every time you skip, you'll eat one less meal of Qiu's cooking."

Lang Jin: Not happy.

That night, the beastmen gathered by the creek, holding their large pottery bowls somewhat clumsily, taking a sip of water, swishing it around, and spitting it out. Then they looked at the little wolf leading them in brushing their teeth, learning to dab the tooth powder step-by-step, ensuring every tooth was brushed.

"Snap—"

"Ow! My toothbrush broke!"

Lang Bing: He knew it!

Lang Rong: "Lang Shun, you bit and broke your toothbrush while brushing; I've noted it down."

"No—"

Lang Bing: "Take another one. This time, I'll count it as an accidental bite, but there won't be a next time."

The little wolf was cold and stern; the big guys grabbed the toothbrushes, which were thinner than a finger, and bared their teeth, carefully brushing up and down.

Lin Qiu sat on the low wall, glancing at the big men circling the creek.

Actually, they all looked decent; none were ugly. The little white wolf stood in the middle, straight as a small pine tree, serious and calm.

The sub-beastmen who had finished eating didn't rest, sitting in their grass nests spinning thread.

Lang An was dexterous and learned to weave the fishing net first, immediately taking the idle sub-beastmen from the gathering team to help.

Many hands make light work, and the Man grass fiber was coarse and sturdy, perfect for weaving fishing nets.

As they busied themselves, the weather warmed up completely.

Half a month passed, and one fishing net was woven, though the mesh sizes varied.

Almost every night, the male beastmen of the tribe spun thread, while the sub-beastmen and female beastmen wove nets. Under high-intensity practice, the subsequent two nets were made better and faster.

After the first fishing net was finished, the beastmen began to catch fish.

When the fishing net spread out like a flower and submerged into the water, the beastmen held their breath in anticipation.

Lin Qiu stood to the side watching and said, "Pull."

Lang Shi stirred his arms to close the net and slowly dragged it upward. It was extremely heavy, even more strenuous than pulling a fish cage.

Lang Shi had thought it would be heavy in the water like a fish cage, but when he saw the large fish being pulled up with the net, he was so shocked he shouted, "Faster, faster!"

No one knew exactly what he wanted to be faster at.

"Stop rushing, I'll help you!" Lang Mo chimed in.

Everyone knew they were testing the fishing net today, so the beastmen remaining at Lang Mountain all ran over to watch. Seeing this, they were anxious and joined in one after another.

Lin Qiu, however, was watching the net; it was stretched tight, but it didn't break.

The fish in the river were large, so catching them this way actually made it easy for them to escape.

For now, this was the only method; he wanted to make those huge fishing nets, but he couldn't do it in a short time.

Watching four or five fish being pulled up entangled in the net, the beastmen stomped their feet in excitement.

Once the fish were on the shore, they quickly dug them further inland, only then letting out a sigh of relief.

"If we just hang them like this, they'll fall off and run away."

The big fish were very energetic, their tails slapping loudly.

Lin Qiu almost got hit by a tail.

He looked at the large fish he could see moving in the water and could imagine how dense the fish in the river were.

"From now on, have a few beastmen cast the net every day, and the fish caught in the net will be made into dried fish."

Lang An and Lang Shi exchanged a look and each picked a beastman from their teams.

The male beastmen were responsible for casting the net, and the sub-beastmen were responsible for making the dried fish.

The weaving of fishing nets continued, and seeing the success here, the beastmen on Lang Shi's side who were making the two-wheeled carts were even more motivated.

The wood was cut, polished, and hollowed out, with wood embedded inside to reduce the cart's own weight and distribute the stress. Then, according to the lines Lin Qiu had drawn, they made the cart body.
