Behind them, the branches were thick and intertwined, and every gap was filled with plants, making it impossible for the carts to pass easily.

But the beastmen had no intention of stopping.

Because of the time spent clearing obstacles, even though it was theoretically closer to the west than the Great Marsh—a journey that should have taken half a day at full speed—the beastmen took a full day.

By nightfall, they finally set down the carts and made their final approach in silence.

Lin Qiu couldn't run anymore and slumped onto Lang Yan’s back.

The forest was pitch black, so dark you couldn't see your own hand; the shadows of the trees seemed like clamoring ghosts. The wolf-beastmen found their direction, carrying vine baskets and animal skins, running with the sound of a whistling wind.

Before long, they stopped to wait for news from the front.

The wolves in front seemed to exchange a few words, and then the team set off again.

After a while, they ducked into a cave.

A fire was lit inside.

Lin Qiu sat on Lang Yan’s back, the view gradually brightening. The grease-coated wooden torches burned with an orange glow, crackling softly, and the smell of grease soon filled the cave.

There wasn't a single weed in the cave; the walls, ceiling, and even the floor were all made of rock that shimmered crystal-clear under the firelight.

It was like an ice cave.

It was all rock salt!

Millions of years ago, this place must have been the sea.

The beastmen were silent; with one look from Lang Yan, they immediately began to mine.

Lin Qiu got down from Lang Yan’s back, and just as he was about to speak, Lang Yan said in a low voice, "We are close to the Feather Tribe here; we need to finish moving it and leave quickly."

"But how do we dig this?"

As he spoke, a wolf-beastman swung a stone axe against the rock wall.

At the same time, the wolf-beastman received a slap on the back of the head from a companion.

The beastmen didn't actually like using stone tools; they preferred their claws.

Powdery rock salt fell into the animal-skin bags as the beastmen dug away.

Huge black and gray wolves crouched before the stone wall, their curved, sharp claws popping out with a *swish*, digging into the wall until they were just a blur.

The rock salt fell in a flurry and soon piled up.

The white salt particles looked very pure.

However, Lin Qiu looked at the wolf-beastmen, their fluffy ears flattened, faces tense as they exerted themselves... how was this any different from kittens sharpening their claws?

Seeing Lin Qiu looking around, Lang Yan didn't demand he work.

He hadn't been here before, so it was natural for him to be curious.

Rock salt softened when it absorbed water, making the surface layer easy to remove. The wolf claws were sharp, and with their full-bellied strength, they dug up a pile in no time.

Lin Qiu crouched beside Lang Yan, scraping with a stone axe and chopping when necessary.

The rock salt was transparent, and the fine powder scraped off was white, somewhat like what they ate in the tribe.

Just as Lin Qiu was about to touch some to his mouth, Lang Yan pressed his hand down.

"Don't eat it; it's bitter."

Lin Qiu: "So the stuff in the tribe is processed?"

"Yes."

The large black paw moved away from his wrist, and Lin Qiu brushed off the salt powder.

As long as it was processed, it was fine.

Natural rock salt couldn't be eaten directly after being crushed; it contained many impurities and needed to be filtered, evaporated, and refined before it was edible.

"Why are we being so sneaky?"

Lang Yan’s claw scraped the rock wall, leaving a deep mark.

"Taking this mountain as the boundary, the east is ours, and the west is theirs. Not all tribes have open spaces like the southern part of the Great Marsh."

Territory was a resource, and both were powerful tribes; who would want to occupy less?

"Then do they know there is salt here?"

Lang Yan: "They probably don't."

"Then we..."

"We migrated from this side and discovered it when we were drinking water."

Salt was the most important resource for beastmen. In the past, when they could trade, salt was more expensive than pottery; some tribes even had to use their entire tribe’s resources to barely exchange for a jar.

Now that the market was closed, most beastmen had nowhere to find salt, and life was hard.

Lin Qiu: "Is it very close to them?"

Lang Yan looked at him and whispered, "They live right nearby."

The beastmen of the Feather Tribe can fly, unlike other tribes that mostly live in the center of their territories. They dwell along high mountains and steep cliffs, possessing a natural defensive advantage.

If a real fight were to break out, the Wolf beastmen wouldn't fear them, but they would be at a slight disadvantage without wings.

Although the salt mine is hidden, the Feather Tribe is right here.

If they were to find out and haul away the salt inside, it would take the Wolf beastmen half a day just to run over.

All beastmen need to eat salt; for thousands of years, they have discovered and processed lake salt, sea salt, and rock salt for consumption.

Without it, they have no strength; they cannot live without it.

Because of salt, some tribes have fought to the death, and many have been wiped out.

Lin Qiu dared not speak again.

He shifted into his beast form, tried extending his claws to scrape at the rock wall, and then buried his head to dig as well.

Once they had dug enough, the beastmen shoveled it up from the ground, packed it into animal-hide bags, and transported it out.

Lin Qiu was tired, but he didn't want to sit directly on the ground.

The ground was a bit damp; beastmen coming in from outside had tracked mud mixed with salt, packing it down tightly. It looked like the dirty ice trampled into the ground after a snowfall.

He stood leaning against the base of the wall, his claws idly flicking at the salt piled up in the crevices of the rock wall.

When the beastmen came over to pack what they had just dug into the hide bags, the layer of salt that had been covered earlier was kicked up by Lin Qiu.

Suddenly, his gaze paused.

A feather.

Its color was blue-black like steel, shimmering with a cold gray. It had been pressed under the salt dust, and the feather was soaked into several strands.

Lin Qiu scratched the big black wolf beside him.

Lang Yan looked over.

"Look." Lin Qiu pointed his claw at the ground.

Lang Yan stared at that shiny black feather, flicked it away with a claw, his expression cold and sharp.

"Lang Huo."

"King!" Lang Huo ran over, his black fur tinged with red looking fluffy and dusted with salt particles.

Lang Yan: "Who scouted this cave?"

Lang Huo pointed out a beastman.

Lang Yan hooked the feather and said, "Didn't you smell the scent of the Feather Tribe?"

The Wolf beastman's heart skipped a beat; he twitched his nose, but by now, the cave had long been covered by the scent of the Wolf beastmen.

"King, I thought some wild beast had come in, so I didn't think much of it..."

The cold in Lang Yan's eyes was enough to freeze.

The beastman shut his mouth in fear.

The other beastmen also stopped what they were doing, their expressions solemn and cold, quickly searching the cave for traces of the Feather Tribe.

Lang Yan looked closer at the mine; the traces at the bottom had already been covered by the claws of the Wolf beastmen. When they first arrived, the light was dim and he hadn't paid much attention; he didn't know how much those beastmen had dug.

"Was it Lang You who led the beastmen to dig last time?"

Lang Huo lowered his head, "Yes."

The beastman responsible for scouting had trembling legs; he had made a grave mistake.

It was a shame that everyone thought they were being secretive, but the others had been here long ago, and who knew where they were hiding now, laughing at them.

Lang Yan's face was grim, and the two beastmen in front of him didn't dare to breathe loudly.

"Lang Shun, go to the back mountain and stay there for a few days after we return."

The wolf tucked his tail, his ears pressed tight, "Yes."

Lin Qiu waited for them to finish speaking and walked to Lang Yan's side. He couldn't control his tail, which swished around wildly until it landed on Lang Yan's tail.

As if it had found a place to rest, it became calm.

The Wolf King, who was suppressing his anger, paused and looked over.

Lin Qiu hadn't noticed yet, his eyes full of worry, "They've been here?"

Lang Yan stiffened his tail.

"Mm."

Beastmen have a strong sense of territory; although this is the very edge of their territory, it is still within it.

The Feather Tribe not only came, they stole their salt—this was a blatant provocation.

Lang Yan ordered: "Dig faster."

Once they finished digging, they would settle the score.

Lin Qiu walked away, and Lang Yan's stiff tail dropped, swishing randomly. He watched Lin Qiu carry his clothes out, thinking he was going to change back into human form.

Lang Yan flicked his tail, slamming it against the rock wall with a 'thwack', and the rock salt collapsed into a small hill with a rumble.

The beastmen in the cave tensed up.

They gripped their tools and hammered violently at the stone wall. With the suppressed anger of being provoked, they worked with extreme force.

Rock salt fell to the ground in piles.

The sound traveled out, echoing through the distant mountains, startling the creatures sleeping in the night, and making the beastmen on the high mountains tremble.

The Black Feather beastmen, who knew the Wolf beastmen had come, dared not close their eyes.

More beastmen flew toward the chieftain's cave, their expressions vigilant and slightly panicked.

"They've discovered it."

On the towering mountain, not far from the peak, there was a natural rock cave.

The cave was hidden in the greenery surrounded by trees; standing at the foot of the mountain, the entrance was almost invisible.

Inside the cave, a huge nest had been built with branches and dead wood, shaped like a bowl, with a simple design.

In the nest, the Black Feather beastmen had used downy feathers shed from their bodies to make a cushion—gray-black in color, fluffy and warm. Even with the cold wind howling at the peak, they wouldn't be cold.

Sitting in the nest was an elderly beastman.

He had short black hair, not the black-gray of younger beastmen, but tinged with gray and white. His eyes were weary, his skin loose, and he was wrapped tightly in animal-hide clothes, his aged hands resting on his knees.

The old beastman listened to the violent hammering sounds and looked calmly out of the cave.

Sitting beside him was a young, underage beastman, who also wore a solemn expression.

"Chieftain, they must have discovered it." The young beastman who had flown in first landed, his wings turning into hands, and he walked anxiously to the old beastman.

The Feather Tribe beastmen were no different from the Wolf beastmen, only their builds were more slender.

The old beastman looked at him, his eyes clouded with a gray-white film.

"I told you, you couldn't go."

The young Black Feather beastman lowered his head, as if admitting his mistake, but there was still some stubbornness. He gripped his animal-hide skirt tightly and gritted his teeth:

"If we don't go, are we supposed to let some of our tribesmen starve to death and trade food with the Wilderness Tribe?"

"I led the way; if they come looking, just hand me over!"

"Ya!" the old beastman scolded, clearly angered.

Yu Ya hung his head, as if his neck bone had snapped, letting his head dangle.

The tribe's beastmen arrived one after another, and the cave was soon filled with the Black Feather tribe.

Some remained in human form; most were slender with gray-black hair and dark brown or brown eyes, their arm spans slightly longer than those of the Wolf beastmen.

Those who didn't want to change into human form stayed in their beast forms.

Their sharp claws hooked the edge of the nest, and with a bit too much force, the wooden sticks making the nest snapped.

Their beaks were black and slightly curved, and when their wings were folded, they were half the size of a Wolf beastman.

The young beastman counted the beastmen in the nest one by one and whispered: "Grandpa, everyone is here."

The Black Feather chieftain's voice was weary; as he breathed, his thin chest heaved, seemingly with some difficulty.

"The Wolf beastmen already know; this is them telling us to wait for them."

"Chieftain... that place is half ours, why can't we dig there?" said a sub-beastman protecting a cub beside Yu Ya.

The Black Feather chieftain laughed, his voice a bit hoarse, "What do you think?"

"The salt is in their territory; the deposit was discovered by them, and they dug it out. If you had talked about trading, that would be one thing, but those few youngsters ran off to steal and dig—if we were the Wolf beastmen, would you be happy?"

His breathing became more rapid, and the young beastman immediately patted his back, saying anxiously: "Grandpa, Grandpa..."

The sub-beastman shut his mouth in fear.

Yu Ya grabbed his father's hand, listening to the urgent, rain-like hammering sounds, feeling a trace of unease in his heart.

"Chieftain." The beastmen were worried and couldn't help but lean forward.

The Black Feather chieftain's hands trembled, unable to maintain his posture, and he leaned against the edge of the nest to regulate his breathing.

Nowadays, prey is scarce on the Beast God Continent, and life is hard.

They had also migrated here, just a bit earlier than the Wolf tribe.

Their tribe had eighty-three beastmen, and the youngest batch was the seven including Yu Ya, fifteen or sixteen years old, not yet adults.

Without food, it was hard to raise even the cubs they had.

Many cubs born in previous years had died, leaving only Yu Ya and the others, and the beastmen were unwilling to have more.

Never mind the cubs; it was hard for them to even feed themselves now.

The cave was left with only the old beastman's rapid breathing; the beastmen quieted down, feeling anxious and full of misery.

The tribe was currently in a transition period, and the successor the old chieftain had been training had been injured during a hunt and was now crippled.

Before the previous priest passed away, the next priest hadn't been fully taught yet. The beastmen looked at the old chieftain, then at the young beastman beside him.

Not every beastman could be a priest; a priest needed talent. The previous priest had chosen the chieftain's grandson, Yu Le, and taught him carefully, but before he could finish teaching...

Sigh!

The Black Feather tribe had no more hopes for the future.

Some who were already desperate had jumped straight from the mountain peak, restraining their instincts and not spreading their wings even until death.

Those who remained were numb in body and soul.

They only prayed to live a little longer and for the tribe not to be wiped out so quickly.

To think that they, too, were once a great tribe that dominated the sky...

"Chieftain, the cubs didn't know any better; they were doing it for the good of the tribe... Although what they did was wrong, we tacitly agreed. We will apologize and offer compensation."

The adult beastmen knew about the cubs' actions.

They had even covered for the cubs.

Having done this, they were terrified, but if you asked if they regretted it, they actually didn't.

Compared to the hides and dried meat painstakingly saved by the tribe's beastmen, only to fly for half a month to the Central Continent to trade for salt, why not dig it right at their doorstep?

It was just greed; they hadn't tried to excavate from their side of the mountain but had entered the Wolf tribe's side and dug the salt they had already unearthed.

At a time like this when it was hard to survive, what was there to be picky about?

"But we have no food to compensate them with." Yu Ya said softly, his eyes red.

The adult beastmen sighed, "You don't need to worry about that."

"Chieftain?" They needed the old beastman's consent.

The Black Feather chieftain's voice was aged: "Since the cubs did it, we must apologize, and be sincere."

The fault was theirs, and they should have the right attitude.

*

Without any more hesitation, thirty beastmen hammered and chiseled, while a dozen transported the salt. Before long, the four carts they brought were full.

In the past, this would have required a whole squad of beastmen to carry.

Boiling salt was exhausting work, so the beastmen dug as much as they could, only stopping in the middle of the night.

They weren't in a hurry to return; it was still drizzling outside, so Lang Yan told the beastmen to cover the carts with animal hides and rest in the cave for the rest of the night.

At dawn the next day, Lin Qiu cooked all the remaining fish, and after the beastmen ate, they began to cross the mountain.

After a night, the Wolf beastmen had already calmed down.

The noise they made last night—as long as the beastmen of the Black Feather tribe weren't deaf, they should have heard it long ago.

Whether to run or to fight, they should have an idea by now.
chapters.title: 第61章
chapters.source_text:
羽族的兽人能飞，不像其他部落大多住在领地的中心位置。他们依傍高山险崖而居，有天然的防御优势。
要真打起来，狼兽人虽不怕他们，但没有翅膀也会吃点亏。
盐矿虽隐秘，但羽族就在这儿。
要叫他们知道了，将这里面的盐一搬，狼兽人跑过来都得半天。
兽人们都需要吃盐，千百年来，湖盐、海盐、岩盐都叫他们发现并处理来食用。
不吃没力气，他们离不开这个。
因为盐，有些部落斗得你死我活，覆灭的也不少。
林楸不敢再说话。
他变做兽形，试着伸爪子在岩壁上刮了一下，随后也闷头刨。
刨得差不多了，兽人们将地上的铲起来装进兽皮袋里，往外运送。
林楸累了，又不想直接坐地上。
地面有些湿，兽人从外面进来，脚下踩着泥跟盐混在一起，压得紧实。像下雪后地面被踩出来的冰，脏兮兮的。
他靠墙根站着，爪子随意拨弄着岩壁缝隙堆积起来的盐。
待到兽人过来将刚刚刨的装进了兽皮袋，早先覆盖下来的一层盐叫林楸一踢。
突然，他目光一顿。
一片羽毛。
颜色青黑如钢，泛着冷灰，被一直压在盐沫子下面，羽毛洇湿了成几缕。
林楸挠了挠身边的大黑狼。
狼岩看过来。
“你看。”林楸爪子点地。
狼岩盯着那片黑得发亮的羽毛，一爪弹开，目光冷冽。
“狼火。”
“王！”狼火跑来，黑得泛红的毛毛蓬松，沾了些盐粒子。
狼岩：“谁探查的山洞？”
狼火点了个兽人出来。
狼岩勾着那羽毛，道：“没闻到羽族的味儿？”
狼兽人心一凛，动了动鼻子，这会儿山洞早被狼兽人的味道覆盖。
“王，我以为是野兽进来过，没多想……”
狼岩眼里冷得快结冰。
兽人吓得闭上嘴。
其他兽人也停下手中动作，面色肃然冷沉，迅速在洞内寻找羽族的痕迹。
狼岩再细看这矿洞，底部的痕迹已经被狼兽人的爪子覆盖。刚来时光线昏暗也没多注意，不知道那些兽人挖了多少。
“上次是狼游带领兽人来挖的？”
狼火低头，“是。”
负责探查的兽人腿都哆嗦，这下是犯了大错。
亏得大家自以为隐蔽，结果人家早来了，现在指不定躲在哪里看他们的笑话。
狼岩面色沉凝，跟前两个兽人大气不敢喘。
“狼顺，回去之后自己去后山待几天。”
狼夹着尾巴，耳朵紧压着，“是。”
林楸等着他们说完，走到狼岩身边。他管不住尾巴，胡乱扫动着，一下搭在狼岩尾巴上。
像有了放置的地方，安分了。
压着怒气的狼王一顿，看了过来。
林楸还没注意到，眼里担忧，“他们来过了？”
狼岩僵着尾巴。
“嗯。”
兽人的领地意识很强，这里虽然是领地的最边缘，但也在领地内。
羽族不仅来了，还偷了他们的盐，这是赤.裸.裸的挑衅。
狼岩下令：“赶紧挖。”
挖了，该算账的算账。
林楸走开，狼岩僵着的尾巴垂下来，胡乱扫了下。他看着林楸叼着衣服出去，想是又要换回人形。
狼岩尾巴一甩，啪的砸在岩壁上，岩盐垮塌似的轰隆一下堆成小山。
洞内的兽人们皮一紧。
他们抓着工具对着石壁就是一通暴力捶打。心里又憋着被挑衅的怒气，极其用力。
岩盐成堆成堆地往地下掉。
那声音传出去，一下一下，响彻远山，惊动夜晚沉睡的生灵，震得那高山上的兽人心里发麻。
早知道狼兽人过来的黑羽兽人不敢闭眼。
更多的兽人往族长的山洞飞来，神情警惕，略显慌张。
“他们发现了。”
拔地而起的高山上，离山顶不远处有一处天然岩洞。
山洞隐蔽在树木围绕的绿荫之中，站在山下几乎看不见洞口。
而山洞中，用树枝枯木搭建了一个巨大的巢穴，如钵盂一般，造型朴素。
巢穴之中，黑羽兽人用身上褪下来的绒羽做了垫子，灰黑的色泽，蓬松温暖。即便山顶寒风瑟瑟，也冷不着。
巢中，端坐着一个年迈的兽人。
他一头黑色短发，不似年轻兽人羽毛的黑灰色，而是泛着灰白。他目光沧桑，脸皮松弛，身上裹着严严实实的兽皮衣，一双苍老的手搭在膝上。
老兽人听着那暴力敲砸的声音，平静地看向洞外。
他身边坐着个面容稚嫩，还没成年的兽人，同样的一脸凝重。
“族长，他们肯定发现了。”率先飞进来的年轻兽人落地，翅膀变做双手，焦急地走到老兽人面前。
羽族的兽人跟狼兽人没什么两样，只身形修长些。
老兽人看着他，眼睛漫着一层灰白。
“我说过，不能去。”
年轻黑羽兽人垂着头，像认错，但又有些倔强。他紧紧抓着腰间的兽皮裙，咬牙道：
“不去，我们难道还要饿死一部分族人，拿食物跟原野部落换吗？”
“我带的头，要是他们找来，把我交出去就是！”
“涯！”老兽人呵斥，显然动了怒。
羽涯垂下头，似折断颈骨，吊着脑袋。
部落的兽人陆陆续续都来了，山洞内坐满了黑羽部落的兽人。
他们有的保持人形，大多身姿修长，灰黑色头发，暗褐色或褐色眼睛，臂展比狼兽人稍长。
不乐意变人形的，就用兽形。
锋利的爪子扣住巢穴边缘，力气稍大，做窝的木棍便断裂开来。
他们鸟喙呈黑色，略弯，翅膀收拢体型有狼兽人一半大小。
小兽人一一数过到了巢中的兽人，低声道：“阿爷，来齐了。”
黑羽族长声音疲惫，呼吸间，单薄的胸口起伏几下，似有些困难。
“狼兽人已经知道了，这是在告诉我们等着呢。”
“族长……那地方我们一个部落一半，凭什么不能挖。”羽涯身侧，护崽的亚兽人道。
黑羽族长笑了声，声音有些嘶哑，“你说呢？”
“盐在他们的领地，东西是他们发现，他们挖出来的。你要说交换也就算了，他几个小的跑去直接偷挖，换做我们是狼兽人，你乐意？”
他呼吸急促了些，小兽人立马拍着他后背，急道：“阿爷，阿爷……”
亚兽人吓得闭嘴。
羽涯抓住他阿爸的手，听着那急切如雨的敲击声，心中有一丝忐忑。
“族长。”兽人们担忧，忍不住往前凑。
黑羽族长颤抖着手，维持不了端着的姿势，靠坐在巢穴边缘，调整呼吸。
现在兽神大陆猎物少，日子不好过。
他们也是迁徙过来的，只不过比狼部落早一些而已。
他们部落兽人八十三个，年纪最小的一批就是羽涯这七个，十五六岁，并没成年。
没有食物，有了幼崽也难养活。
前些年生出来的幼崽死了不少，就剩羽涯几个了，兽人们也不愿意再生。
别说幼崽，他们自己现在吃饱都难。
山洞只剩下老兽人的急促呼吸，兽人们安静下来，心中焦躁，满脸困苦。
部落现在青黄不接，老族长培养的接班人在一场捕猎中受伤，废了。
上一任祭司离世前，下一任的祭司也还没教会。兽人们看着老族长，又看看他旁边稚嫩的小兽人。
不是所有兽人都能当祭司，祭司需要天赋者。上一任祭司挑选了族长的孙子羽乐，悉心教导，可还没教完……
哎！
黑羽部落的兽人对未来已经没有奢望。
有些早已绝望的，更是直接从山顶跳了下去，到死都克制着本能没展开翅膀。
留下的这些，身心麻木。
他们只求能活久一点，部落不要那么快覆灭。
想想他们曾经，也是个称霸天空的大部落啊……
“族长，幼崽不懂事，他们也是为部落好……这事他们虽然做得不对，但我们也默许了。我们道歉，赔偿。”
幼崽的行为，成年兽人都知道。
他们甚至还为幼崽扫尾。
做了这事儿，他们提心吊胆的，但要说后悔，其实并不。
比起靠着部落兽人挨饿才积攒出的皮子、肉干，再飞半个月去中央大陆换回来的盐，家门口的为什么不挖。
只是贪了便宜，没试着从自己这边山体开凿，而是进了狼部落那边，挖了人家挖出来的盐。
这个时候都难活命了，还讲究什么。
“可我们没食物赔了。”羽涯红着眼眶，小声道。
成年兽人们一叹，“这个你们就不用管了。”
“族长？”他们要老兽人同意。
黑羽族长声音苍苍：“幼崽干的，也得道个歉，诚心一点。”
错在他们，态度该有。
*
没了顾忌，三十个兽人敲敲打打，十几个兽人运送，没多久，带来的四辆车装满了。
换做以往，这些得用一个小队的兽人来驮。
煮一次盐费劲儿，兽人们尽量多挖，弄到半夜才堪堪收手。
他们不急着回，外面还下着小雨，狼岩叫兽人把车上的用兽皮盖着，回山洞休息半夜。
第二天天一亮，林楸将剩下的鱼全给做了，兽人们吃完，开始翻山。
过了一晚上，狼兽人已经冷静下来。
他们昨晚发出的动静，只要黑羽部落的兽人不是个聋的，早该听到了。
到底是跑，还是打，他们也该有个想法。

兽人们停在这盐矿山顶，仰头看着远处高耸入云的山峰。
“王，咱们冲上去吗？”
狼岩：“等着。”
这里已经是双方领地边缘，黑羽部落就住在那山上，看得见。
狼岩等着他们给个交代。
话落，那山岚缭绕的高峰上，飞下来一群乌压压的黑色鸟人。
翼展四五米，身子还是人形。
顷刻间，兽人落在山头，翅膀变做手臂。
狼兽人警惕起来，目光锐利，紧盯着对面。
黑羽兽人们垂着眼，他们理亏。
为首的黑羽兽人羽山示意兽人将一个一个兽皮袋放在前面，那是剩下的盐。
他道：“动你们的盐是我们不对，我们道歉。”
他往后看一眼，以羽涯为首的五个少年兽人走出来。其他年长的兽人依旧呈半包围状，将他们围在中间。
羽涯抬头，被狼岩看得一个瑟缩。
狼岩皱眉。
是没成年的幼崽。
狼兽人们也有些怒气，做了就做了，推幼崽出来什么本事！
狼兽人里有些躁动，黑羽兽人们忍不住往中心靠了靠，紧张地看着对面。
羽涯鼓起勇气，忐忑了一晚上，早已经害怕了。
“对不起！是我带着同伴进入了你们的领地，挖了你们盐！族长说了不让我去的，但我们不想让部落饿着肚子攒食物，去中央大陆换盐！对不起，你们要怪就怪我们，阿叔他们什么都没做。”
小兽人说着说着，眼泪串成珠子似的往下掉。
狼兽人们脸色更不好。
无论哪个部落，都看中幼崽，对幼崽的行为稍稍宽待一些。
但要是黑羽兽人为了逃脱责任，专门把幼崽推出来认错，那这样的部落就没必要还挨着他们。
幼崽说完，羽山叫他们去后头。
可羽涯看到面前那四十多个巨狼，兽形都比他们大那么多，不想族人被牵连。
他挣扎着拉开羽山的手，其他几个少年也跟着做。
“我们做错的事我们自己承担后果。”
“对！我们做的，跟阿叔他们无关！”
羽山抬手，后头成年兽人上前，抓着幼崽往后拖。
羽山看着眼前以战斗模式排列的狼兽人，道：“幼崽不懂事，但也是我们心存侥幸。扫尾的事是我们做的，我们愿意承担后果。”
狼岩看了眼狼火。
狼火：“既然你们知道，那就明白这是挑衅。”
羽山坚毅的脸上微苦，“是，我们知道。错在我们，但我们拿不出食物来赔偿，我跟我身后这些成年兽人，愿意给狼部落干活，期限你们定。”
这就是要给他们狼部落当奴隶。
羽涯连带几个小兽人全被惊住，怎么也想不到他们想的办法是这个办法。
他立即道：“不、不行！阿山叔，不行……”
他们以为成年兽人有其他的赔偿方式，没想到是当奴隶！他们不是只会傻乐的幼崽了，他们听得明白这背后的意思。
羽山：“带他们回。”
“不要，阿山叔！我们错了！”
“是我们的错！不关他们的事呜呜……”小兽人哭着喊着，眼里全是恐惧跟后悔。
“不是他们，是我……”
小兽人被捂住嘴，消失在了山林里。
羽山以防备的姿态看着狼兽人，害怕他们真冲上去找小兽人的麻烦。
他沉声道：“吃掉的盐……我们没有足够的东西再交换，只有这个。”
狼火毫不犹豫道：“我们对这个没兴趣。”
林楸忽的抬眼，打量着这一群二十多个成年兽人。有手有脚，是干活的好料子。
部落里正缺兽人呢。
他悄摸伸手，轻轻挠了挠狼岩。
狼岩垂眸，看林楸双眼泛着光，抬手挡在他眼前。
“狼兽人不做这种事。”
奴隶，是以往西部大陆那些大部落兴起的东西。
他们仗着自身实力高，部落强大，抢掠那些小部落的食物、领地，甚至是能繁衍的雌性跟亚兽人。
他们驱使那些战败的兽人给他们干活，包括但不限于捕猎、采集、制作食物、建造部落，甚至被虐杀取乐。
几乎绝大部分沦为奴隶的兽人，最后都是个死，区别只是惨死还是更惨地死。
更有甚者，有些兽性未退的兽人，会吃掉战败的兽人。
而这个行为从西部大陆传开，一直延伸到整个兽神大陆。包括最远的南大陆跟北大陆。
不过这样的行为，为大多数有良知的部落所不耻，但凡遇到了，不是远离，就是覆灭了对方部落。
争斗、死亡，部落覆灭，是兽神大陆这些年最常见不过的事。
狼岩知道林楸不知道羽山这话背后的意思，所以不叫他表露出来。
林楸只觉得有些奇怪。
狼岩：“回去跟你说。”
局面僵持着。
狼兽人也看得出来，对面兽人没说假话。
歉也道了，赔偿的诚心也有，但要给他们当奴隶，狼兽人不乐意。
他们部落现在好东西不少，万一这群兽人起了歹念，到时候来个里应外合，倒霉的还是他们。
而且他们不是那样会养奴隶的恶心部落。
狼火跟狼乔也拿不定主意，纷纷看向狼岩。
要是对面部落真是个不认的，他们冲上去打一架反倒简单。
可这个样子，一口气上不来也下不去，憋屈！
羽山也看来。
他知道狼岩才是领头的，道：“我们绝对不说假话，给你们干几年的活儿都可以，但到了期限后，你们得放我们回来。”
狼岩：“我们考虑考虑。”
“王？！”兽人一惊，毛都炸了。
狼岩：“回去再说。”
羽山嘴唇翕动，沉默着。
……
事情暂没有结果，狼兽人撤去得很快。成年兽人们颓丧地跌坐，看着那个没被带走的兽皮袋，眼中迷茫。
“他们要是同意了，我们还能回得来吗？”
羽山：“不知道。”
这个结果，羽部落的兽人们考虑过。
他们兽人住得高，不怕其他部落打来。他们走一部分捕猎能力差的兽人，留下的那些也能守好部落。
部落兽人少一点，留下的兽人还能多吃一点，对部落也是消减一些压力。
而他们这些离开的在狼部落干活，狼兽人给的食物肯定不会多，但只要能不饿死就好，旁的不奢求。
只要坚持坚持，没准等他们回去，兽人们吃饱一点，体质也能更强一点。
至少，部落有一批兽人能活得更久。
兽人们静坐山头，躺下，看着那绵延群山。
曾经他们靠着翅膀飞跃大山轻而易举，获取食物更是简单。可现在，连飞过山的力气都没有了。
当奴隶跟他们现在比起来，差不到哪里去。
死了就死了。
不是所有的部落都能像狼兽人一样，坚信还能好起来。见识了不少同伴从山顶一跃而下，至今，那山脚下从来没有兽人敢过去。
黑羽部落剩下的兽人不是不想跳，是部落还有几个幼崽没长成，他们还有他们的使命。
“回去吧。”
羽山说着，飞往山巅。
挖盐的事过了明路，之后部落的兽人从他们这边开采，狼兽人应该也说不了什么。
起码这次之后，部落不用换盐了。
*
“王，我们真要答应他们？”兽人们追着狼岩问，一个个急切不已，坡没下完就将狼岩围住了。
狼岩瞧着这一个个大狼，冷声道：“我说了要答应？”
“那、那没有。”
狼岩：“先回去。”
部落没盐了，这耽搁了一天，兽人们吃肉都得吃白味儿的。
狼火吆喝一声，兽人散开，排成两两一队，快速往停放盐的地方掠去。
林楸小跑跟在狼岩身边。
他跑得有些喘，狼岩停下，变做狼身叫他爬到背上去。
林楸：“你还没说，刚刚为什么不应？”
狼岩跟他解释了下黑羽部落的意思，林楸抱着他脖子，疑惑：“奴隶？”
“嗯。”
“狼部落没这个规矩。”
林楸：“那要是我们提供食物，他们付出劳力，不压榨他们干活，这样行不行？”
狼岩：“所以我说考虑。”
林楸懂了。
正常来说，请人干活，管饭正常，一般还要再给点钱或者东西出去。
而这是兽世，兽人们领地意识很强，几乎没哪个部落愿意其他兽人踏足。
黑羽部落如果来的话，他们管饭，两顿。
部落现在虽然抓猎物依旧一会儿能抓到，一会儿空手而归，但至少鱼够吃。
但给东西，那就不必了。
黑羽部落的兽人是来赔偿的，给东西就说不过去了。
林楸将这个想法跟狼岩一说，狼岩道：“其实还有个问题。”
“什么问题？”
狼岩停下，看着前方兽人把装满盐的藤筐找出来，放在背上。
每个兽人背得不多，两个半筐的样子。
虽说板车拉着的也够了，但兽人们回去空着背不习惯，顺带带上一点。
狼岩感觉到脖子前的毛毛被轻轻扯了下，尾巴甩动，拍掉后头一株矮树上的叶子。
“别扯毛。”
林楸看着手上一撮，手指捻了捻，一点不心虚了。
兽人在换毛，不扯也得掉。
队伍走起来，狼岩慢慢跟上，灰眸深沉。
“部落现在好东西多，难保他们来了不生歹心。”
兽人们需要外出采集捕猎，部落留守的兽人能有多少。两边部落这么多年几乎没往来，都互相警惕着，谁敢放他们过来。
林楸趴下，吹了下狼岩后颈的毛毛。
“那如果不让他们来狼山呢？”
狼岩一哆嗦，转头，声音略严肃，“楸。”
林楸无辜，“我什么都没干。”
狼岩绷直尾巴。
chapters.title: 第62章
chapters.translated_text:
The orcs stopped at the top of the salt mine mountain, looking up at the peaks in the distance that towered into the clouds.

"King, shall we charge up there?"

Lang Yan: "Wait."

This was already the edge of both territories; the Black Feather tribe lived on that mountain, and it was visible.

Lang Yan was waiting for them to provide an explanation.

As he spoke, a dense swarm of black bird-men flew down from the mist-shrouded peak.

Their wingspans were four or five meters wide, but their bodies were still in human form.

In an instant, the orcs landed on the mountain top, their wings transforming back into arms.

The wolf orcs grew alert, their gazes sharp, staring intently at the opposite side.

The Black Feather orcs lowered their eyes; they were in the wrong.

The leading Black Feather orc, Yu Shan, signaled for the orcs to place several animal skin bags in front—that was the remaining salt.

He said: "It was wrong of us to take your salt. We apologize."

He looked back, and five young orcs led by Yu Ya stepped forward. The other older orcs remained in a semi-circle, surrounding them.

Yu Ya looked up, then flinched under Lang Yan's gaze.

Lang Yan frowned.

They were underage cubs.

The wolf orcs were also feeling some anger; if they did it, they did it, what kind of skill was it to push cubs out to take the blame!

There was some restlessness among the wolf orcs, and the Black Feather orcs couldn't help but huddle toward the center, watching the opposite side nervously.

Yu Ya gathered his courage; having been anxious all night, he was already terrified.

"I'm sorry! It was me who led my companions into your territory to dig your salt! The patriarch told me not to go, but we didn't want the tribe to go hungry while saving food to trade for salt in the Central Continent! I'm sorry, if you want to blame someone, blame us. Uncle and the others did nothing."

As the little orc spoke, tears began to fall like beads.

The wolf orcs' expressions grew even worse.

No matter the tribe, they all valued their cubs and were usually a bit lenient toward their behavior.

But if the Black Feather tribe specifically pushed cubs out to admit fault just to escape responsibility, then there was no need for such a tribe to remain their neighbors.

After the cub finished speaking, Yu Shan told them to go to the back.

But Yu Ya saw the forty-plus giant wolves in front of him, all much larger than them in their beast forms, and he didn't want his tribesmen to be implicated.

He struggled to pull away from Yu Shan's hand, and the other youths did the same.

"We will bear the consequences for the wrong things we did."

"That's right! We did it, it has nothing to do with Uncle and the others!"

Yu Shan raised his hand, and the adult orcs behind him stepped forward, grabbing the youths and dragging them back.

Yu Shan looked at the wolf orcs arranged in a combat formation and said: "The cubs are ignorant, but we also harbored wishful thinking. We were the ones who cleaned up the mess, and we are willing to bear the consequences."

Lang Yan glanced at Lang Huo.

Lang Huo: "Since you know, then you understand this is a provocation."

A bitter look crossed Yu Shan's resolute face. "Yes, we know. The fault is ours, but we don't have the food to compensate. I, along with these adult orcs behind me, are willing to work for the Wolf tribe. You set the duration."

This meant becoming slaves for their Wolf tribe.

Yu Ya and the other young orcs were all stunned; they never imagined this was the solution they had come up with.

He immediately said: "No, you can't! Uncle A-Shan, you can't..."

They had thought the adult orcs had other ways to compensate, not slavery! They were no longer cubs who only knew how to be happy; they understood the meaning behind this.

Yu Shan: "Take them back."

"No, Uncle A-Shan! We were wrong!"

"It was our fault! It has nothing to do with them, wuwu..." The little orcs cried and shouted, their eyes full of fear and regret.

"It wasn't them, it was me..."

The little orcs had their mouths covered and disappeared into the mountain forest.

Yu Shan watched the wolf orcs in a defensive posture, afraid they would actually charge up to cause trouble for the little ones.

He said in a deep voice: "The salt that was eaten... we don't have enough things to exchange, we only have this."

Lang Huo said without hesitation: "We have no interest in that."

Lin Qiu suddenly looked up, sizing up the group of twenty-plus adult orcs. They had hands and feet; they were good material for labor.

The tribe was currently short on orcs.

He quietly reached out and gently scratched Lang Yan.

Lang Yan lowered his eyes, saw Lin Qiu's eyes shining, and raised his hand to block his view.

"Wolf orcs don't do that kind of thing."

Slavery was something that had emerged from those large tribes in the Western Continent in the past.

Relying on their own high strength and powerful tribes, they would plunder the food, territories, and even the fertile females and sub-orcs of smaller tribes.

They drove the defeated orcs to work for them, including but not limited to hunting, gathering, preparing food, building the tribe, and even being tortured to death for amusement.

Almost all orcs who became slaves ended up dead; the only difference was whether they died miserably or even more miserably.

Some even worse ones, orcs who hadn't fully shed their beast nature, would eat the defeated orcs.

This behavior spread from the Western Continent throughout the entire Beast God Continent, including the furthest Southern and Northern Continents.

However, such behavior was despised by most tribes with a conscience; whenever they encountered it, they would either stay away or destroy the other tribe.

Strife, death, and the destruction of tribes had been the most common occurrences on the Beast God Continent in recent years.

Lang Yan knew Lin Qiu didn't understand the meaning behind Yu Shan's words, which was why he didn't let him express it.

Lin Qiu just felt a bit strange.

Lang Yan: "I'll tell you when we get back."

The situation remained deadlocked.

The wolf orcs could also tell that the orcs on the other side weren't lying.

The apology had been made, and the sincerity for compensation was there, but the wolf orcs weren't interested in having them as slaves.

Their tribe had many good things now; if these orcs developed evil intentions and conspired from the inside, they would be the ones to suffer.

Besides, they weren't that kind of disgusting tribe that kept slaves.

Lang Huo and Lang Qiao couldn't make up their minds either, and they both looked at Lang Yan.

If the opposite tribe had really been unreasonable, it would have been simpler to just charge up and have a fight.

But in this situation, they couldn't get it out of their systems—it was frustrating!

Yu Shan also looked over.

He knew Lang Yan was the leader and said: "We are definitely not lying. We can work for you for several years, but when the time is up, you must let us return."

Lang Yan: "We will consider it."

"King?!" The orcs were shocked, their fur standing on end.

Lang Yan: "We'll talk about it when we get back."

Yu Shan's lips moved, and he remained silent.

...

With no result for the time being, the wolf orcs withdrew quickly. The adult orcs slumped down, looking at the animal skin bag that hadn't been taken, their eyes filled with confusion.

"If they agree, will we ever be able to come back?"

Yu Shan: "I don't know."

The orcs of the Yu tribe had considered this outcome.

Their orcs lived high up and weren't afraid of other tribes attacking. If a portion of the orcs with poor hunting skills left, those who remained could still guard the tribe well.

With fewer orcs in the tribe, those remaining could eat a bit more, which would also reduce the pressure on the tribe.

And those of them who left to work for the Wolf tribe—the food the wolf orcs gave surely wouldn't be much, but as long as they didn't starve to death, they wouldn't ask for anything else.

As long as they persisted, perhaps by the time they returned, the orcs would be better fed and their physiques would be stronger.

At the very least, a batch of orcs in the tribe would be able to live longer.

The orcs sat quietly on the mountain top, lying down and looking at the rolling mountains.

Once, they could easily fly over the mountains with their wings, and obtaining food was even simpler. But now, they didn't even have the strength to fly over the mountain.

Being a slave was no different from their current situation.

If they died, they died.

Not all tribes could be like the wolf orcs, firmly believing that things could get better. They had witnessed many companions jump from the top of the mountain, and to this day, no orc dared to go to the foot of that mountain.

The remaining orcs of the Black Feather tribe didn't want to jump; it was just that there were still a few cubs in the tribe who hadn't grown up, and they still had their mission.

"Let's go back."

Yu Shan said, flying toward the peak.

The matter of digging salt had been brought into the open; afterward, if the tribe's orcs mined from their side, the wolf orcs shouldn't be able to say anything.

At the very least, after this time, the tribe wouldn't need to trade for salt.

*

"King, are we really going to agree to them?" The orcs chased after Lang Yan, asking, each of them anxious, surrounding Lang Yan before they had even finished descending the slope.

Lang Yan looked at these big wolves and said coldly: "Did I say I would agree?"

"W-well, no."

Lang Yan: "Let's go back first."

The tribe was out of salt, and with this day's delay, the orcs would have to eat their meat plain.

Lang Huo gave a shout, and the orcs dispersed, lining up in pairs and quickly darting toward where the salt was stored.

Lin Qiu jogged along beside Lang Yan.

He was running a bit out of breath, so Lang Yan stopped, transformed into his wolf form, and told him to climb onto his back.

Lin Qiu: "You still haven't said why you didn't agree just now."

Lang Yan explained the meaning behind the Black Feather tribe's offer, and Lin Qiu hugged his neck, puzzled: "Slaves?"

"Mm."

"The Wolf tribe doesn't have that rule."

Lin Qiu: "Then what if we provide food and they provide labor, without exploiting them—would that work?"

Lang Yan: "That's why I said I'd consider it."

Lin Qiu understood.

Normally, when hiring someone to work, providing meals is standard, and usually, you would give some money or goods as well.

But this was the beast world; orcs had a strong sense of territory, and almost no tribe was willing to let other orcs set foot on their land.

If the Black Feather tribe came, they would provide meals—two meals.

Although the tribe's hunting success varied—sometimes catching prey, sometimes returning empty-handed—at least there was enough fish to eat.

But giving extra goods was unnecessary.

The Black Feather tribe orcs were coming to compensate; giving them extra things wouldn't make sense.

Lin Qiu shared this thought with Lang Yan, and Lang Yan said: "Actually, there is another problem."

"What problem?"

Lang Yan stopped, watching the orcs in front find the rattan baskets filled with salt and place them on their backs.

Each orc wasn't carrying much, about two and a half baskets each.

Although what was on the carts was enough, the orcs weren't used to returning with empty backs, so they took a little extra.

Lang Yan felt the fur in front of his neck being gently tugged, and his tail flicked, knocking the leaves off a small tree behind him.

"Don't pull the fur."

Lin Qiu looked at the tuft in his hand, rubbed his fingers, and felt no guilt at all.

The orcs were molting; it would fall out even if he didn't pull it.

The team started moving, and Lang Yan followed slowly, his gray eyes deep.

"The tribe has many good things now; there's no guarantee they won't develop evil intentions once they come."

The orcs needed to go out to gather and hunt; how many orcs could be left to guard the tribe? The two tribes had almost no contact for so many years and were wary of each other; who would dare let them in?

Lin Qiu lay down and blew on the fur on the back of Lang Yan's neck.

"Then what if we don't let them come to Wolf Mountain?"

Lang Yan shivered, turned his head, and said in a slightly serious tone, "Qiu."

Lin Qiu was innocent, "I didn't do anything."

Lang Yan stiffened his tail.

chapters.source_text:
“把黑羽部落的兽人安排在大泽那边，正好方便采收蛮草跟麻草。等蛮草处理好了，我们的兽人再运送回来，怎么样？”
“还有鸟粪，他们有翅膀，能运重物飞吗？”
“能。”
“那岂不是更好办了，让他们挖鸟粪，运过大泽，我们的兽人直接去那边接收，一来一回省事儿多了。”
林楸细细数来，部落其实就这两个事目前最费兽人，黑羽部落的兽人能帮忙的话，他们会轻松很多。
至于食物，大泽属于狼部落的领地。
那边那么多鱼，怎么都够吃了。
狼岩静静听着，觉得可以。
“回去我跟祭司商量。”
狼岩前头，狼兽人压着步子也静静听着，也觉得不错。
他们管饭，让兽人吃饱，哪个部落还有这样的好事儿。
用食物跟他们交换劳动，这样的话就不算圈养奴隶。
“王！那需要我们守着吗？”狼兽人退着跑，与狼岩并排。
狼岩：“回去商量。”
“嗷。”狼兽人冲着他背上的林楸一笑，咧着嘴巴露出白森森的一口牙，又欢快往前冲去。
他要跟前面没听到的兽人交流交流。
回到部落已经中午，还没到地方，狼就开始嚎着饿。
狼山这边迅速开火做饭。
到了部落，兽人将东西一放，往棚子底下蹿。
进了棚子，狼安一边把木勺使得虎虎生风，一边问：“还以为你们今天早上就该回来了。”
林楸看着他胳膊上好像最近才出现的肌肉曲线，道：“出了点意外。”
“西边那群兽人发现了？”
林楸点头。
他坐上矮墙，依着木柱，浑身放松地靠着。
“狼贝他们昨天割了多少麻草？”
狼安：“不多，十几捆。那个长得分散，没蛮草好割。”
林楸点头。
“黑羽部落的兽人可能会来，到时候他们帮忙。”
“他们来干什么？”狼安立即警惕起来。
林楸：“他们的小兽人跑我们这边挖了盐，他们赔罪呢。”
狼安：“我们可不收奴隶！”
林楸：“不是奴隶，咱们管饭，食物交换劳动。多的就没有了。”
狼安勺子往陶锅边缘一磕，“……好像也可以。”
狼岩回来就跟祭司商量去了。
部落采集狩猎的兽人还没回，运盐的兽人趴地上躺着，饿得肚子叫。
那些搬运回来的岩盐就摆在空地上。
狼安也看了看，道：“又是个麻烦事儿。”
中午的肉汤没盐，兽人们吃得没滋没味。下午，空闲的兽人被狼安叫过来，打算制盐了。
岩盐需要粉碎，部落罐子多，有的兽人直接用木棍舂，有的装兽皮里用石头砸。
在弄坏了一个陶罐之后，狼安追着那兽人打，再勒令不许再用罐子，兽人们只好回山洞拿皮子。
上下两层大皮子一压，兽人围着捶打。
棚子外坐着已经有些晒了，兽人们都在棚子底下干活。林楸也在其中，帮忙研磨。
狼安手上细致，熟练地将兽皮里的岩盐倒进旁边的罐子。
他道：“以前制盐，部落里陶锅不够，幼崽跟祭司的两口陶锅从早上煮到晚上，连续半个月才煮得完。现在好了，山洞里那些陶锅全拿出来一起煮，几天就能做完。”
这边捶打着，狼雨领着兽人已经把陶缸陶锅搬出来。
陶缸加水，把先捶好的细粉扔进去，搅拌溶化后，再过滤。
兽人们没纱布，林楸正想怎么过滤时，就看见有兽人拿着几张棕树皮一样的东西出来。
树皮垫个几层，便跟纱布一样。
狼安见林楸盯着树皮看，道：“那个叫丝皮，我们这边没有，是以前从集市上交换来的。”
林楸：“南边的东西？”
狼安：“南大陆的东西，离我们这里很远很远。”
头一批的过滤出来，兽人们将水倒入陶罐，在灶上烧。边煮边搅，搅到有冰晶似的盐晶析出，慢慢撤掉木柴。
这个过程需要很久，兽人们都不离开陶锅边，盯得很紧。
“这个要煮完就行？”
狼安：“哪能这么容易，要煮好多次。”
狼安只一想到后面不停地围着灶台转，脸都垮了些，露出深深的疲惫感。
他想到以前，就那么两口陶锅，还得小心翼翼不能烧破了。
要重复着忙活连续半个月，那简直是折磨。
林楸看着，忽然道：“要不然加点草木灰试试。”
兽人齐刷刷看来。
“楸，为什么加这个？”
都没一个兽人反驳，只问原因。
他们眼中热切，宛如看到了新鲜出炉的烤鱼。
林楸：“……”
他已经能在兽人们热切的目光中好好坐着，只一时间想不清该怎么解释。
总不能跟兽人们讲什么岩盐里面可能含有氯化镁、氯化钙这些杂质，还可能出现的砷、铅等有毒物质，再跟草木灰里的碳酸钙一反应……
“大概就是，里面有些东西，见了草木灰就……现了原形。”
兽人们懵，林楸也想不出什么好的说辞。
“不如你们拿一锅先试试？”
狼安：“试！”
草木灰而已，多的是。
*
狼岩从山洞出来时，见兽人们都围在灶台边，时不时哇的一声。
“好多脏东西！”
“原来这个叫现原形！”
“楸！你怎么知道的？”
这还是头一次兽人们问林楸这方面的问题，以往都直接做就完了。
林楸道：“我也不知道。”
他还想着兽人们再问怎么解释，狼安就道：“问什么，楸都忘记了。”
“对哦……”
兽人们觉得戳了林楸伤疤，立马闭了嘴。
制盐的效率因为加了草木灰显著提升，兽人们以前需要煮五次才行，现在两次之后好像就不苦了。
但以前出现过兽人吃了盐死掉的事儿，保险起见，他们煮了三次。
狼岩进了棚子，没吭声，看着那陶缸里的奇怪东西，就知道是林楸又做了好事。
由着兽人们忙，狼岩寻了个空地坐下。
林楸挨过来，也不问，就在旁边坐着。
阳光晒得人晕晃晃的，兽人们只睡了半夜，这会儿趴在棚子底下，呼噜声一阵一阵。
林楸听着，也打了个哈欠。
他背靠着矮墙，闭上眼睛。
日头西斜，林楸不知睡了多久，翻个身，就见那残阳红彤彤的坠在山头，像个喜饼。
不远处雾气腾腾的，兽人们围着几口陶锅，还没弄完。
林楸觉得身下垫子舒服，调整了下姿势，瞧见指缝里的一戳毛。
再看自己，半身躺在狼岩身上。
他慢慢坐起来。
跟前好几双眼睛立马收回去。
外出的兽人都回来了。
狼岩懒懒地依旧趴着不动，见兽人都回来了，道：“狼金，把小队队长都叫来。”
对面还不停往林楸身上瞥的小狼立马站起来，跑了。
林楸稳着面色，往旁边挪了挪。
狼岩试图动一下爪子，微不可见地一僵。
压麻了。
他闭目，等着兽人们过来。
林楸瞧着半空飘着的浮毛，抿了下唇，面上有些怪异。
狼岩听着旁边窸窸窣窣的动静，一瞧，眼睁睁看见林楸从嘴里拉出一根黑色的狼毛。
林楸怀疑地往旁边一瞥，目光恰好与狼岩对上。
林楸：“你掉毛太严重了。”
狼岩曲爪，狼尾僵在地上都不晃了。
“不一定是我的。”
林楸：“就是你的。”
……
狼金回来时，兽人们在互相扯毛。
为了度过雪季长出来厚实毛毛现在正在掉，一扯就是一大撮。
狼金往狼溶跟狼冰中间一凑，“干嘛呢？”
狼溶怕爪子上，呆呆道：“王说的。”
狼金看过去，他们王趴在地上，旁边放着个藤筐，楸两只手在他毛毛上抓。
抓几下就是好大一把。
林楸：“叫狼石他们做些木梳出来，梳得快。”
狼岩感觉到皮肤上的拉扯，闷声道：“好。”
“王，扯毛毛干什么？”狼金道。
林楸：“冬季冷，换下来的毛处理过后可以用来捻线，做成毛衣。”
一个狼兽人身上的狼毛很可观，一次换毛能做一件。
“毛衣？”
“狼毛肯定暖和，就是可能有些扎。”
自己穿自己的毛毛，好奇怪。
狼冰琢磨着，出声：“兽皮不好吗？”
“没说不用兽皮，不过兽皮重，裹得不严实里面就空荡荡的，加一件毛衣更舒服。”
“羽绒效果也不错，更轻便，以后再想办法弄一些。”
雪季那么冷，保暖非常重要。
狼冰揪了一把狼溶身上的毛毛，往手背上戳了戳，若有所思。
狼岩看兽人过来了，他坐起来，尽量维持狼王的威严。
忽略对着他身上招呼的林楸，还是很有狼王的样子。
几个小队的兽人绷着脸，想笑又不敢笑。
狼岩：“黑羽部落的事我跟祭司商量过了。”
狼兽人大多都在这儿，大家一起听。
“王，黑羽部落什么事儿？”
狼岩示意狼火讲。
狼火手臂往狼金肩膀上重重一搭，压得这话多的少年往下塌了塌腰。
“火叔，你快讲。”
狼火：“就是黑羽部落趁着我们不在，挖洞里的盐了。”
“什么？！他们敢挖我们的盐！火叔，收拾他们了吗？！”快成年的兽人就是一点就炸，狼火差点按不住他。
“没打。”
“怎么不打？！”
狼火一巴掌拍在小狼脑袋上，“嚷嚷什么，你以为我们不想打。”
回来前还憋屈呢。
凭什么他们进了自家领地，偷了东西，道个歉就过去了？还想来他们部落当奴隶，也看他们乐不乐意收。
但后头听兽人说，王跟楸商量出个主意，狼火也没仔细听。
不想打就是没打，狼金：“我找他们去！”
说着一吆喝，手撑着矮墙一跃而过，气势汹汹带上自己小队跑了。
狼岩：“冰，把他叫回来。”
狼冰起来，抓上狼溶一起跟了过去。
chapters.title: 第63章
chapters.translated_text:
"Let's arrange for the Black Feather tribe's beastmen to stay over at the Great Marsh; it’ll be convenient for harvesting wild grass and hemp. Once the wild grass is processed, our beastmen can transport it back. How does that sound?"

"What about the bird droppings? They have wings—can they fly with heavy loads?"

"They can."

"Then that’s even better. Let them dig up the bird droppings and transport them across the Great Marsh, and our beastmen can just receive them on this side. It’ll save a lot of trouble going back and forth."

Lin Qiu counted them off carefully. These were the two tasks currently consuming the most labor in the tribe. If the Black Feather beastmen could help, their own people would have a much easier time.

As for food, the Great Marsh belonged to the Wolf tribe's territory.

With so many fish there, it would be more than enough to feed everyone.

Lang Yan listened quietly and felt it was feasible.

"I'll discuss it with the priest when we get back."

In front of Lang Yan, the wolf beastman also listened quietly, pacing his steps, and thought it sounded good too.

They would provide meals and keep the beastmen fed—what other tribe offered such a good deal?

Exchanging food for labor meant they wouldn't be considered keeping slaves.

"King! Do we need to keep watch over them?" The wolf beastman ran backward, moving alongside Lang Yan.

Lang Yan: "We'll discuss it when we get back."

"Awoo." The wolf beastman grinned at Lin Qiu on his back, baring a mouthful of white teeth, before happily charging forward again.

He wanted to share the news with the beastmen ahead who hadn't heard it yet.

It was already noon by the time they returned to the tribe. Before they even arrived, the wolves began howling about being hungry.

The Wolf Mountain side quickly started fires to cook.

Upon reaching the tribe, the beastmen dropped their loads and scurried under the sheds.

Once inside the shed, Lang An asked while wielding a wooden spoon with impressive vigor, "I thought you guys would be back this morning."

Lin Qiu looked at the muscle definition on his arms that seemed to have appeared recently and said, "We ran into a bit of an accident."

"Did that group of beastmen in the west find you?"

Lin Qiu nodded.

He sat on the low wall, leaning against a wooden pillar, his whole body relaxing.

"How much hemp grass did Lang Bei and the others cut yesterday?"

Lang An: "Not much, a dozen bundles or so. It grows scattered; it's not as easy to cut as the wild grass."

Lin Qiu nodded.

"The Black Feather tribe's beastmen might come; they'll help out when they do."

"Why are they coming?" Lang An immediately grew wary.

Lin Qiu: "Their young beastmen ran over here to dig up salt, so they're coming to apologize."

Lang An: "We aren't taking in slaves!"

Lin Qiu: "They aren't slaves. We provide food, and they exchange labor for it. Nothing more than that."

Lang An tapped his spoon against the edge of the clay pot, "...That actually sounds okay."

As soon as Lang Yan returned, he went to discuss it with the priest.

The gathering and hunting beastmen hadn't returned yet, and the salt-transporting beastmen were lying on the ground, their stomachs growling with hunger.

The rock salt they had brought back was laid out in the open space.

Lang An took a look and said, "That’s another troublesome task."

The noon meat soup had no salt, so the beastmen ate it without much enjoyment. In the afternoon, Lang An called over the idle beastmen, intending to start processing the salt.

The rock salt needed to be crushed. Since the tribe had many pots, some beastmen used wooden sticks to pound it directly, while others put it in animal skins and smashed it with stones.

After one clay pot was broken, Lang An chased the beastman responsible and forbade anyone from using the pots again, forcing them to go back to the caves to get hides.

With two large hides pressed together, the beastmen surrounded them and pounded away.

It was already quite sunny outside the shed, so the beastmen were working underneath it. Lin Qiu was among them, helping with the grinding.

Lang An was meticulous, skillfully pouring the rock salt from the animal skin into a nearby pot.

He said, "In the past, when we processed salt, we didn't have enough clay pots. The pots belonging to the cubs and the priest had to be boiled from morning until night, and it took half a month to finish. It's better now; we can take all the pots from the caves and boil them together. We can finish in a few days."

While they were pounding, Lang Yu led the beastmen to bring out the clay vats and pots.

They added water to the vats, threw in the finely pounded powder, stirred it until dissolved, and then filtered it.

The beastmen didn't have gauze. Just as Lin Qiu was wondering how to filter it, he saw a beastman bring out something that looked like palm tree bark.

A few layers of tree bark worked just like gauze.

Seeing Lin Qiu staring at the bark, Lang An said, "That’s called silk-bark. We don't have it here; it was exchanged from the market a long time ago."

Lin Qiu: "Something from the south?"

Lang An: "From the Southern Continent, very, very far from here."

The first batch was filtered, and the beastmen poured the water into clay pots to boil over the fire. They stirred as they boiled, and once salt crystals resembling ice began to precipitate, they slowly removed the firewood.

This process took a long time, and the beastmen didn't leave the side of the pots, watching them very closely.

"Is it done once this is boiled?"

Lang An: "It’s not that easy. It has to be boiled many times."

Just thinking about having to keep circling the stove later made Lang An’s face sag, revealing a deep sense of exhaustion.

He thought about the past, when they only had those two clay pots and had to be extremely careful not to crack them.

Having to repeat that busy work for half a month straight was simply torture.

Watching them, Lin Qiu suddenly said, "Why don't you try adding some wood ash?"

The beastmen looked over in unison.

"Qiu, why add that?"

Not a single beastman argued; they only asked for the reason.

Their eyes were eager, as if they were looking at freshly roasted fish.

Lin Qiu: "..."

He was already able to sit comfortably under the beastmen's eager gazes, but he couldn't immediately think of how to explain it.

He couldn't exactly tell them about magnesium chloride, calcium chloride, or potential toxic substances like arsenic and lead in the rock salt, and how they would react with the calcium carbonate in the wood ash...

"It's just that there are some things inside that, once they meet the wood ash, they... reveal their true form."

The beastmen were confused, and Lin Qiu couldn't come up with a better explanation.

"Why don't you try it with one pot first?"

Lang An: "Let's try it!"

It was just wood ash, after all; there was plenty of it.

*

When Lang Yan came out of the cave, he saw the beastmen gathered around the stove, letting out "wow" sounds from time to time.

"So much dirty stuff!"

"So this is what 'revealing their true form' means!"

"Qiu! How did you know that?"

This was the first time the beastmen had asked Lin Qiu a question like this; in the past, they would just do it and be done with it.

Lin Qiu said, "I don't know either."

He was still bracing for them to ask for an explanation, but Lang An said, "Why ask? Qiu has forgotten."

"Oh, that's right..."

The beastmen felt they had poked at a sore spot for Lin Qiu and immediately shut their mouths.

The efficiency of salt production improved significantly because of the added wood ash. The beastmen used to need to boil it five times, but now it didn't seem bitter after just two.

However, since there had been cases in the past where beastmen died after eating salt, they boiled it three times just to be safe.

Lang Yan entered the shed without a word. Seeing the strange stuff in the clay vat, he knew Lin Qiu had done another good deed.

Leaving the beastmen to their work, Lang Yan found an empty spot and sat down.

Lin Qiu moved closer and, without asking, sat down beside him.

The sun was dizzyingly bright. The beastmen had only slept for half the night, and now they were lying under the shed, snoring in waves.

Hearing them, Lin Qiu also let out a yawn.

He leaned his back against the low wall and closed his eyes.

As the sun slanted westward, Lin Qiu didn't know how long he had slept. He turned over and saw the setting sun hanging red and round on the mountaintop, like a festive cake.

Not far away, steam was rising; the beastmen were still gathered around a few clay pots, not yet finished.

Lin Qiu felt the cushion beneath him was comfortable. He adjusted his posture and noticed a tuft of fur between his fingers.

Looking at himself, he realized he was lying half-on Lang Yan.

He slowly sat up.

Several pairs of eyes in front of him immediately looked away.

The beastmen who had gone out had all returned.

Lang Yan remained lazily lying down. Seeing that everyone was back, he said, "Lang Jin, call all the squad leaders over."

The little wolf opposite, who was still stealing glances at Lin Qiu, immediately stood up and ran off.

Lin Qiu kept his expression steady and moved to the side.

Lang Yan tried to move his paw, but it stiffened imperceptibly.

It had fallen asleep.

He closed his eyes, waiting for the beastmen to arrive.

Lin Qiu looked at the floating fur in the air, pursed his lips, and looked a bit strange.

Lang Yan heard the rustling beside him and, looking over, watched as Lin Qiu pulled a black wolf hair from his mouth.

Lin Qiu glanced to the side suspiciously, his gaze meeting Lang Yan's.

Lin Qiu: "You're shedding way too much."

Lang Yan curled his claws, his wolf tail stiffening on the ground, not even swaying.

"It might not be mine."

Lin Qiu: "It is yours."

...

When Lang Jin returned, the beastmen were pulling fur off each other.

The thick fur that had grown for the snow season was now falling out; one pull would bring out a huge clump.

Lang Jin squeezed between Lang Rong and Lang Bing, "What are you doing?"

Lang Rong was busy with his claws and said blankly, "The King said so."

Lang Jin looked over. Their King was lying on the ground with a rattan basket beside him, and Qiu was grabbing at his fur with both hands.

A few grabs yielded a large handful.

Lin Qiu: "Tell Lang Shi and the others to make some wooden combs; it'll be faster to comb it out."

Lang Yan felt the tugging on his skin and muttered, "Okay."

"King, why are you pulling out the fur?" Lang Jin asked.

Lin Qiu: "It's cold in the winter. The shed fur can be processed and spun into thread to make sweaters."

The amount of fur on a single wolf beastman was quite impressive; one shedding season could make one sweater.

"Sweaters?"

"Wolf fur must be warm, though it might be a bit itchy."

Wearing your own fur—how strange.

Lang Bing pondered and spoke up: "Aren't animal skins good enough?"

"I'm not saying we shouldn't use animal skins, but skins are heavy, and if you don't wrap them tightly, there's empty space inside. Adding a sweater makes it more comfortable."

"Down feathers also work well and are lighter; we'll find a way to get some later."

The snow season was so cold that staying warm was crucial.

Lang Bing plucked a handful of fur from Lang Rong and poked it against the back of his hand, lost in thought.

Seeing the beastmen approaching, Lang Yan sat up, trying his best to maintain the dignity of a Wolf King.

Ignoring Lin Qiu, who was still busy with his fur, he still looked very much like a Wolf King.

The beastmen of the several squads kept straight faces, wanting to laugh but not daring to.

Lang Yan: "I’ve discussed the Black Feather tribe matter with the priest."

Most of the wolf beastmen were here, and everyone listened together.

"King, what about the Black Feather tribe?"

Lang Yan signaled for Lang Huo to speak.

Lang Huo draped his arm heavily over Lang Jin's shoulder, pressing the talkative youth down.

"Uncle Huo, tell us quickly."

Lang Huo: "The Black Feather tribe took advantage of us being away and dug up the salt in the cave."

"What?! They dared to dig up our salt! Uncle Huo, did you punish them?!" Beastmen nearing adulthood were easily provoked; Lang Huo could barely hold him down.

"We didn't fight."

"Why didn't you fight?!"

Lang Huo slapped the little wolf on the head, "What are you shouting for? Do you think we didn't want to?"

They had been feeling frustrated even before they got back.

Why should they just apologize and get away with it after entering their territory and stealing things? They even wanted to come to their tribe as slaves—as if they’d be happy to take them.

But later, hearing the beastmen say that the King and Qiu had come up with an idea, Lang Huo hadn't listened carefully.

If they didn't want to fight, then they didn't fight. Lang Jin said, "I'm going to find them!"

With a shout, he vaulted over the low wall and ran off aggressively with his squad.

Lang Yan: "Bing, call him back."

Lang Bing stood up, grabbed Lang Rong, and followed them.

chapters.title: 第64章
chapters.translated_text:
The orcs flicked their tails lazily, lifted their heads, then rested them back down on their paws.

The young wolves were always like this—impatient and unable to suffer the slightest loss.

Back in their day... they were actually no better than Lang Jin. They could even, under the leadership of Lang Yan—who wasn't yet the King at the time—sneak into someone else's nest without a sound.

The tribe basically took a hands-off approach to the young wolves who had already shifted into human form; as long as it wasn't life-threatening, they turned a blind eye to anything slightly dangerous.

To let them grow, the young wolves couldn't be protected like cubs that hadn't left the den yet.

"I've discussed the matter of the Black Feather tribe with the Priest."

Upon hearing this, the orcs’ wolf ears perked up, and they sat up straight.

Lang Yan: "We will provide food, once in the morning and once in the evening, enough to keep them full. They will go near the Great Marsh to harvest and process wild grass and hemp, and transport bird droppings from the south of the Great Marsh to the north, where our orcs will go to collect them."

"Lang Huo, tomorrow you take the orcs from the second team to the west to talk to them. If they agree, go straight to the Great Marsh and teach them."

"Yes!"

Lang Yan looked at Lang An again: "An, you arrange a few orcs to go over and be responsible for the food situation there."

Lang An nodded, "King, how many orcs are they?"

Lang Yan: "Twenty at most."

Lang An: "Then two sub-beasts going over should be enough."

"King, should we arrange for some orcs to go and keep watch? What if they have ill intentions..." Lang Guo said, pulling the cub in front of him closer.

The cub was now raised to be round and chubby; Lang Guo held him steady, and the cub lifted his little head, listening along with the adult orcs.

Although he couldn't understand, he was earnest.

The adult orcs looked over, all of them baring their teeth in mischievous grins. One by one, they reached out their paws, rubbing the cub until he swayed back and forth.

Lang Guo quickly swatted those paws away, but the cub was still quickly divided among the adult orcs.

After a while of commotion, each big wolf had a cub sitting just as straight in front of them.

Pudgy and round.

The big and small ones had similar expressions, looking just like the clay wolf figurines the orcs made.

The tall black wolf shed his cold sternness, and Lang Yan’s gaze was gentle. The cub let out a low, affectionate cry and gently wagged his tail.

But the next moment, it was pressed down by the claw tips of an adult orc.

"Wolves shouldn't wag their tails."

The cub whimpered, unable to break free.

The more Lang Guo watched, the more irritable he became. He knocked on the head of the mischievous big wolf a few times and took the cub back.

Lang Yan: "Alright."

The orcs straightened up.

Lang Yan: "Lang Huo, you all watch over there for a few days, and the task of transporting the bird droppings is also left to you. Be careful when coming and going, you don't need to stare at them constantly."

"Lang Shi, they will be here at most until the rainy season begins. During this time, the orcs under your command should be cautious."

Lang Shi: "Understood, King."

Lang Yan made the arrangements one by one, and the orcs went to their respective duties.

Lin Qiu listened for a while, and after they finished talking, he followed Lang Shi to the cave where the woodworking was done.

His hands were tired from pulling fur, and he wanted to make some combs.

"Qiu, we haven't made the spinning wheel and loom yet." As soon as Lang Shi mentioned this, his face looked as bitter as if he had chugged a pound of bitter melon juice.

Lin Qiu: "I'm not looking at that; I want to make a few combs."

Lang Shi’s heart skipped a beat.

Lin Qiu: "This is simple, I can do it myself."

Lang Shi quietly let out a breath, "There is plenty of wood in the cave, use whatever you want."

After Lin Qiu left, the orcs dispersed as they should.

As it neared evening, there was no need to boil salt for now. Lang An and the others took down the clay pots used for boiling salt, replaced them with ones for soup, and started getting busy.

The other orcs looked at the rattan baskets beside them, their fur standing on end.

"King, are we still pulling fur?"

Lang Yan: "We're boiling soup, put it away."

The wolf orcs packed up the wolf fur and took the opportunity to sweep the corridor with a broom made of tree branches.

By the time it was almost dark, Lang An called for dinner.

Lang Mo ran to the front of the line first. He happily received his portion and said to the back: "It's meat slice soup today."

As he walked to the side, Lang An lifted another full ladle and had just poured it into an orc's bowl. Both of them suddenly looked up, stunned, and then looked at Lang Mo, who had frozen in place.

"Where are the young wolves?!"

"The young wolves didn't come back!!!"

The orcs were restless, not even daring to eat their food.

Lang Yan’s eyes darkened, and he understood immediately. He said coldly: "The west side—it's too late."

*

Time returns to the moment Lang Huo ran off.

Lang Bing and Lang Rong chased after him, but before they could persuade him to go back, Lang Jin draped his arms over their shoulders, one on each side.

"The Black Feather tribe dares to do that because they rely on living high up and think we can't catch them! The King can tolerate it, but I can't. Can you two?"

Lang Bing stared at him with light blue eyes, "Can't you just say you want to fight?"

Lang Jin chuckled, then straightened his expression: "Nonsense! They’ve already done this, and if we still endure it, who knows if they’ll come back again. Just tell me, are you going or not!"

Lang Rong tried to pull the hand off his shoulder, but his strength was no match for Lang Jin's.

He said softly: "The King will be angry, we can't do this."

Lang Jin narrowed his eyes, his face pushing right up to Lang Rong's, his nose almost touching Lang Rong's.

The devil-may-care, unreliable look was gone from his face as he said: "Lang Rongrong, can you not be so cowardly? They were the ones who provoked us."

Lang Rong tilted his head to avoid him and tried to look at Lang Bing on the other side.

Lang Bing deliberately glanced behind them, "Maybe we shouldn't go, they'll definitely come after us."

"Then hurry up and go!"

Lang Jin grabbed them both and charged forward, and the other young wolves let out excited cries, following eagerly.

They ran at full speed. Lang Rong was dragged along, stumbling, and kept pulling up his fur skirt that was riding up.

"Bing! Persuade him, will you."

Lang Bing fanned the flames: "Jin, we really can't go, we can't beat them."

Lang Jin: "They're just a bunch of feather-folk, who says we can't beat them!"

Provoked by this, they ran even faster.

The two of them were tossed onto Lang Jin's back by the young wolves. Lang Rong looked at the smirk on Lang Bing's face and suddenly realized.

"Bing, you..."

Lang Bing: "I heard from Qiu that down feathers make better clothes, I wonder if that's true."

He was very serious, and also very scary to wolves.

Lang Rong’s mouth hung open, which Lang Bing casually closed for him.

The little white wolf looked clean and innocent, but he had enough hidden mischief to dye a river black.

Lang Rong: "Then, how do we explain this to the King?"

Lang Bing: "You think of something."

Lang Rong took a deep breath, "Tell the truth. We couldn't stop Lang Jin and were coerced by him. Poor us, we didn't even get to eat the meat soup, and were dragged away by him on an empty stomach."

"Ao! You two are framing me!"

Lang Rong calmly smoothed his fur skirt, "It's the truth!"

No wonder they could play together; they were cut from the same cloth.

When the orcs of Wolf Mountain realized the young wolves were missing, Lang Yan only let the orcs eat their meat soup first, then told Lang Huo to take a squad and go look for them.

In case they were really being bullied, they could still be rescued.

As for the other orcs, those with tasks tomorrow should hurry back to their dens to sleep, and those who were worried could wait.

This wait lasted until the middle of the night.

There were voices outside, and Lang Yan opened his eyes and walked out of the cave.

Lin Qiu woke up at the slightest movement, yawning, and followed him out.

The young wolves were excited. Seeing Lin Qiu come, they crowded around him, holding something bundled into a ball.

"Qiu! Look, is it this!"

Lin Qiu touched it; it was wrapped in large leaves with vines, but a lot of fluffy, light things were leaking out of the gaps.

"Down feathers?"

"Yes, yes, that's it!"

Lang Yan: "Where are Lang Huo and the others?"

Lang Jin’s smile froze.

Forgot, the King is here too.

He looked at his companions; Lang Bing and Lang Rong were standing there like poor little things, just hanging their heads and not speaking.

"Lang Jin, where are Lang Huo and the others?" Lang Yan asked again.

Lang Jin tightened his grip on the ball wrapped in large leaves, fidgeting, and even sounded slightly proud: "We met them on the way back, but we shook them off."

"Heh."

It was dark, there were no clouds, and the wind felt chilly.

Lang Jin tested the waters, grinning: "King, we just went to the west side to look around, we didn't do anything bad."

"Is that so?"

"Yes, yes, yes!" The young wolves behind Lang Jin tucked their tails between their legs, their ear fur standing on end.

The King is angry!

But weren't they just doing what those Black Feather tribe orcs did? They weren't in the wrong, it should, it should be fine.

Lang Yan: "Wait."

The young wolves were quiet.

Lang Bing lowered his head, grinding the grass under his feet.

Lang Rong: "Lang Jin is too bad, he grabbed us and ran!"

Lang Bing: "Exactly."

The two pretended to whisper, but their "whispers" were loud enough for Lin Qiu to hear.

Lang Yan glanced at the two orcs gloomily. The two young wolves felt their skin tighten, stood up straight, and hung their heads.

Lin Qiu sat on the low wall, blowing in the night wind.

Through the darkness, Lang Yan could clearly see his sleepy face.

"Go back to sleep."

Lin Qiu yawned, "I want to hear what other bad things they did." His tone was languid, with a hint of schadenfreude.

The young wolves, tails tucked, pressed their ears flat against their heads.

They didn't wait long before Lang Huo returned with the orcs. Seeing Lang Yan waiting under the shed, Lang Huo was so angry that when he passed the young wolves, he slapped them with a dull thud.

The young wolves felt a pain in their foreheads and opened their mouths to howl.

"Howl my ass!"

"King, they ran up to someone else's mountain and raided their nest!"

Turning his head, he saw the down feathers still held in the young wolves' hands, and his fur puffed up in anger, making him look like a giant ball.

"Those down feathers are what the Black Feather tribe sheds every year from birth to adulthood! They save them to line their nests for warmth and to incubate eggs! These young wolves plucked it all!"

Lang Huo hadn't even gotten close to the west mountain before he saw a group of feather-folk circling in the sky.

When they arrived, they didn't see the young wolves, but instead were almost attacked.

Lang Yan’s voice was flat: "How did you steal it?"

Lang Jin stammered.

"Lang Bing."

Lang Bing almost ground the grass under his feet into mush, "We don't know, when we went, there were no orcs in their tribe."

Lang Yan: "Last chance."

Lang Rong perked up, curled his toes, and whispered: "When we went, their orcs came down and asked if we had finished discussing, and we said yes. Then they followed us away from the tribe, and the remaining orcs all came to see them off, and then, and then there were no orcs left on the mountain..."

Lang Yan closed his eyes, his temples twitching slightly.

Lin Qiu watched his slowly rising hand and grabbed it, "Don't hit them, what if you make them even dumber."

Lang Yan looked at Lin Qiu.

The young wolves raised their tails, their eyes wet and expectant as they looked over.

Uncle Qiu still cares about them...

Lin Qiu: "I have other ways to teach them a lesson."

The young wolves shivered; Lang Qiu is even worse than the King!
chapters.source_text:
兽人们懒洋洋地甩尾巴，脑袋抬起，换个爪子重新压着。
小狼总这样，性子急，一点吃不得亏。
换他们那会儿……其实也比狼金好不到哪里去。他们甚至能在当时还不是王的狼岩的带领下，悄无声息摸到人家窝里去。
部落对已经变成人形的小狼基本上是放养，只要不危及生命，有点危险的事都睁一只眼闭一只眼。
要让他们成长，小狼必然不可能像还没出窝的幼崽那样护着。
“黑羽部落的事，我跟祭司商量好了。”
兽人们一听，狼耳竖起，端坐起来。
狼岩：“我们提供食物，早晚一次，管饱。他们去大泽附近收割处理蛮草、麻草还有将大泽南部的鸟粪运到北部，我们的兽人再过去搬。”
“狼火，明天你带上二队的兽人去西边，跟他们谈。要是他们答应，就直接去大泽，教会他们。”
“是！”
狼岩又看向狼安道：“安，你安排几个兽人过去，负责那边食物的事。”
狼安点头，“王，他们多少兽人？”
狼岩：“最多二十。”
狼安：“那两个亚兽人过去就差不多。”
“王，要不要安排兽人过去守着？万一他们起了歪心思……”狼果拢着身前幼崽道。
幼崽现在养得圆滚滚的，全被狼果拎着坐好，仰起小脑袋跟着成年兽人一起听。
虽然听不懂，但认真。
成年兽人们看去，个个掀开嘴皮龇牙，笑得贱兮兮。一个个爪子伸过去，将幼崽揉得摇摇晃晃。
狼果飞快拍这些爪子，幼崽还是迅速被成年兽人瓜分。
闹过一阵后，每个大狼跟前，都放着个同样端坐的幼崽。
胖墩墩的。
一大一小神态相似，像兽人们捏的那陶泥小狼。
高大的黑狼褪去了冷肃，狼岩目光温和。幼崽濡慕地低低叫着，轻轻摇晃尾巴。
可下一瞬，叫成年兽人爪尖压住。
“狼不能摇尾巴。”
幼崽哼唧，挣脱不了。
狼果越看越暴躁，梆梆敲了几下作怪的大狼脑袋，将幼崽收回来。
狼岩：“好了。”
兽人们一肃。
狼岩：“狼火，你们在那边看几天，运送鸟粪的事情也交给你们。往来多注意，不用一直盯着。”
“狼石，他们在这边最多到雨季来临之前，这期间你手下的兽人谨慎些。”
狼石：“知道了，王。”
狼岩一一安排下来，兽人们各司其职。
林楸听了会儿，等他们说完，跟着狼石去了做木工活的山洞。
他手扯毛扯累了，要弄梳子。
“楸，纺车和织机我们还没做出来。”狼石一说起这个，脸上苦得像灌了一斤苦瓜汁。
林楸：“我不是看那个，我想弄几把梳子。”
狼石心里一咯噔。
林楸：“这个简单，我自己能做。”
狼石悄悄吐出一口气，“山洞有很多木料，你随便用。”
林楸走后，兽人们该散的也散开。
快到晚间，盐也先不用煮了。狼安几个把煮盐的陶锅端下来，换上做汤的，开始忙活。
其余兽人看着身边藤筐，毛毛都冒尖。
“王，还扯毛吗？”
狼岩：“在煮汤，收起来。”
狼兽人收拾狼毛，顺带用树枝凑成的扫帚把连廊打扫一下。
快天黑时，狼安就叫吃饭了。
狼莫先一步跑去前头排着，他高高兴兴领了自己那份儿，往后道：“今天是肉片汤。”
他往边走，狼安又抬起满满一勺，刚倒进兽人碗中。两人忽的一抬头，愣住，又看旁边定住的狼莫。
“小狼呢？！”
“小狼没回来！！！”
兽人躁动，饭也不敢吃了。
狼岩沉着眸，一下明白过来，他冷声道：“西边，来不及了。”
*
时间回到狼火跑掉的那一会儿。
狼冰跟狼溶追上去，还没劝他回去，狼金两胳膊一左一右搭在他俩身上。
“黑羽部落敢那么做，就是仗着他们住得高，我们逮不住他们！王能忍，我不能忍，你俩能忍吗？”
狼冰淡蓝色眼睛盯着他，“你就说你想打架不就行了。”
狼金嘿嘿一笑，又正色道：“胡说！他们都这样了，我们还忍着，谁知道他们还会不会再来。你们就说，去还是不去！”
狼溶试图拽掉肩膀上的手，奈何力气不如狼金。
他细声道：“王会生气的，我们不能这么做。”
狼金一眯眼，脸怼在狼溶面前，差一根手指贴着狼溶鼻尖。
他脸上不见那吊儿郎当的不靠谱姿态，道：“狼溶溶，你胆子能不能不要这么小，是他们挑衅我们。”
狼溶仰头躲开，又试图看另一边的狼冰。
狼冰故意看一眼后面，“还是不去了吧，他们肯定要追来的。”
“那还不快走！”
狼金抓着他俩往前冲，其他小狼撒欢一叫，兴冲冲跟上。
他们全速往前奔跑，狼溶被拖得踉跄，不停扯住身上往上跑的兽皮裙。
“冰！你劝一劝他啊。”
狼冰拱火：“金，真的不能去，我们打不过。”
狼金：“就是一群羽族，谁说打不过！”
这一激，跑得更快了。
他俩被小狼一甩，坐他后背上。狼溶看着嘴角勾着的狼冰，恍然大悟。
“冰，你……”
狼冰：“听楸说，羽绒做衣服更好，不知道是不是。”
他很认真，也很吓狼。
狼溶张着嘴，叫狼冰顺手一合。
小白狼看着白白净净的，坏水多得能染黑一条河。
狼溶：“那、怎么跟王交代？”
狼冰：“你想。”
狼溶深吸一口气，“实话实说。我们拦不住狼金，还被他胁迫。可怜我们肉汤都没吃，饿着肚子被他抓着走。”
“嗷！你俩害我！”
狼溶镇定地捋了捋兽皮，“这是事实！”
要不说能玩儿到一块儿呢，一个德行。
当狼山的兽人意识到小狼不见了之后，狼岩只让兽人们先吃了肉片汤，随后叫狼火带着小队走一趟。
万一真被欺负了，还能救一救。
其余兽人，明天有事的赶紧回窝里睡觉，不放心的就等着。
这一等，就是半夜。
外面有说话声，狼岩睁眼，走出山洞。
林楸一有动静就醒过来，打着哈欠，也跟了上去。
小狼正兴奋，见到林楸来，往跟前一凑，抱着个团成球一样的东西。
“楸！你看看，是不是这个！”
林楸一摸，大叶片外面缠着藤条，但缝隙里漏出来了好多轻飘飘的东西。
“羽绒？”
“对对对，就是这个！”
狼岩：“狼火他们呢？”
狼金笑容一僵。
忘了，王也在。
他看向同伴，狼冰跟狼溶小可怜似的杵在旁边，就低着头不说话。
“狼金，狼火他们呢？”狼岩再一次问。
狼金抓紧手里大叶片包裹的球，扭扭捏捏，隐隐还有些得意道：“我们回来的时候遇到了，但是甩开了。”
“呵。”
天黑，没有云，风也好像凉飕飕的。
狼金试探着，咧嘴道：“王，我们就是去西边转了转，没做坏事。”
“是吗？”
“是是是！”狼金身后的小狼夹着尾巴，耳朵毛都炸了。
王生气了！
但他们不就是学那些黑羽部落的兽人做的事，他们才不理亏，应该、应该没问题。
狼岩：“等着。”
小狼安安静静。
狼冰低头，碾着脚底下的草。
狼溶：“狼金太坏了，抓着我们就跑！”
狼冰：“就是。”
两人假装说悄悄话，但悄悄话大得林楸都能听得到。
狼岩幽幽看了两个兽人一眼，两个小狼皮子一紧，站得笔直，脑袋耷了下去。
林楸吹着夜风，坐在矮墙上。
狼岩隔着夜色，也能看清他泛着困意的脸。
“回去睡吧。”
林楸打个哈欠，“我想听听他们还干了什么坏事。”他声调轻慢，带了些幸灾乐祸。
夹着尾巴的小狼耳朵吧唧贴在头顶。
也没等多久，狼火带着兽人回来了。见狼岩就在棚子下等着，狼火气得越过小狼时，爪子拍得闷响。
小狼脑门一疼，张嘴嗷呜就嚎。
“嗷呜个屁！”
“王，他们跑人家山上去，把窝给掏了！”
一转头，看到小狼手上还抱着的绒羽，气得毛炸了炸，像个巨形的球。
“那绒羽是黑羽族从小到大每年褪下来的，人家攒着垫窝保暖和孵蛋的！这小狼全给人家薅了！”
狼火还没靠近西山那边，就看到一群羽族在天上盘旋。
他们到了那边没见到小狼，反倒差点被攻击。
狼岩声音淡淡：“怎么偷的？”
狼金支支吾吾。
“狼冰。”
狼冰脚底的草差点被他碾成糊，“我们不知道啊，我们去的时候，他们部落都没兽人。”
狼岩：“最后一次机会。”
狼溶精神一振，脚趾扣紧，小声道：“是我们去的时候，他们的兽人就下来，问我们商量好了吗，我们就说好了。然后他们就跟着我们离开部落，剩下的兽人都来送，然后、然后山上就没兽人了……”
狼岩闭了闭眼，太阳穴隐隐抽动。
林楸看着他缓缓抬起的手，一把握住，“别动手，打更傻了怎么办。”
狼岩看着林楸。
小狼们尾巴一扬，眼睛湿漉漉，期待地看来。
还是楸叔疼他们……
林楸：“我有其他让他们长教训的法子。”
小狼瑟瑟发抖，狼楸比王更坏！

chapters.translated_text:
With so many ideas in his head, he would definitely make them suffer even more.

Little Wolf pondered for a moment and ran up to Lang Yan, but before he could hug his leg and cry, Lang Yan dodged away in disgust.

"I wasn't planning on doing anything," Lang Yan said.

Lin Qiu: "Oh."

He silently let go.

Lang Yan: "Your Uncle Lang Shun is locked up in the back mountain; you go keep him company too. One meal a day—eating too much makes it easy to rot your brain."

"Wooo..." Little Wolf didn't dare to make a loud sound.

Lang Yan, not wanting to see them and get annoyed, signaled for Lang Huo and the others to escort them over.

*

A dozen little wolves, looking wilted and dejected, were driven to the back mountain by Lang Huo, who signaled for the beastmen to move the rocks blocking the cave entrance.

Lang Shun had only eaten one meal that day, in the evening, and had finally fallen asleep; he was just starting to feel hungry in the middle of the night when the cave door was opened.

He woke up groggily, his wolf fur disheveled, and lay there with no energy.

A group of little wolves wailed and clawed at the cave entrance, as if there were man-eating beastmen inside.

Lang Huo and the beastmen pushed them inside one by one.

"No, wooo... don't, Uncle Huo!" Lang Jin opened his mouth and wailed dryly.

The other little wolves were pushed outward by him, and Lang Huo, thinking about how he had chased them to the west and back, felt his temper rising.

He grabbed them one by one and threw them all into the cave.

The little wolves piled on top of each other, and the entrance was sealed—

Lang Shun twitched the paw that was being pressed down.

He said weakly: "What did you guys do?"

Little Wolves: "Awoo, awoo, awoo!"

So noisy!

Lang Shun covered his ears with his paws and shrank into the deepest part of the cave.

Outside, Lang Huo arranged for beastmen to stand guard.

Previously, only Lang Shun was there, and he alone didn't dare run out, but the little wolves were restless and needed beastmen to watch them.

Listening to the howling inside, Lang Huo had never felt that wolf howls were so noisy.

He furrowed his brows and said: "If you keep howling, I'll cut your tongues out."

"Awoooo!!!" They howled even more vigorously.

Inside the cave, Lang Shun faced the howling of a dozen little wolves and painfully covered his ears. He was hungry and sleepy—was this a punishment for the little wolves, or a punishment for him!

Seeing that his threat didn't work, Lang Huo said: "Fine, howl louder, it'd be best if you call the King here."

The cave went silent.

Lang Huo: They just need a good lesson!

If the King hadn't been present at the time, would this group of little wolves still be intact and locked in the cave?

Lang Huo left with the beastmen.

The two beastmen guarding the cave entrance looked at each other and lay down to sleep.

After a while, a light tapping sound came from behind the stone wall; the two wolves twitched their ears but pretended not to hear it.

After tapping a few more times with no response from the beastmen, the little wolf retracted his paw with a whimper.

The little wolf who had been pressing on Lang Jin's back also rolled off, sprawling on the ground with his four paws curled up, not wanting to get up.

Lang Shun was just about to fall into a deep sleep when his nose was poked again.

In this pitch-black cave, with Lang Shun not full and not sleeping well, he said irritably: "Can you let me sleep!"

The little wolf retracted his paw and said aggrievedly: "Uncle Shun, we're hungry."

They had run at full speed to the west in the afternoon and were chased back by Lang Huo at night; they hadn't eaten yet, and their stomachs were growling.

"If you're hungry, go to sleep!"

"Too hungry to sleep."

"Can't sleep... if you can't sleep, can you let me sleep! I only get one meal a day too, if you bother me again, I'll starve to death for you to see!"

The little wolf was sprayed with a face full of saliva.

He arched his butt and silently backed away.

He backed all the way to Lang Jin's side, rubbed his head against Lang Jin's back, and only rolled to the side once he felt he had wiped it clean.

"Jin, we're hungry..." Little Wolf said softly.

Lang Jin rested his chin on Lang Rong's back; Lang Rong was pinned down and couldn't get up, so he kicked his face with his paws, pushing hard against his face.

"Rong Rong, we're hungry..."

Lang Rong ignored him and continued pushing.

"Bing, we're hungry..."

Lang Bing: "Endure it."

Lang Shun listened to the little wolves' low voices, which felt like bugs burrowing into his ears.

Could someone move him to another cave!

Did they care if he lived or died!

*

"King, then what about tomorrow's matter, is it still going to work?"

After such a mess caused by the little wolves, people might be too scared to let their beastmen come over.

They even ran into their nest; how is this any different from stealing meat soup from a beastman's pot? It might even make the Black Feather Tribe hate them.

There were many beastmen awake in the cave; the firelight was dim, and wolf eyes shone like lamps one by one.

Lang Yan: "Huo, did you tell the Black Feather Tribe about what the tribe discussed?"

Lang Huo lay in his grass nest and sighed.

"King, when we went there, the Black Feather Tribe chased us and attacked. I was busy looking for the little wolves and didn't have time to say it."

Lang Yan: "Go again tomorrow."

"And the things the little wolves brought back..."

Lang Yan: "Return them."

Early the next morning, before Lang Huo and the others could leave, a series of urgent wolf howls suddenly rang out on Wolf Mountain.

The beastmen were startled and rushed toward Wolf Mountain, including the hunting and gathering teams that had just set out.

Lang Yan hadn't gone out today, just guarding against this.

Lang Yan stared coldly at this group of winged Feather Tribe members, his tall body standing in front of all the beastmen.

This group of Feather Tribe members relied on their wings to fly around everywhere.

In the back mountain cave, the little wolves who heard the howling were just making a fuss about wanting to eat meat, but they suddenly quieted down and obediently squeezed into the deepest part of the cave.

Lang Shun: "..."

You little wolf cubs!

"You stepped on my face!"

He pricked his ears to listen outside and said: "Are there any beastmen?"

"You are not allowed to come out," someone said outside, "The King is here."

Upon hearing this, Lang Shun bared his teeth, pushed the little wolves off his body, and rolled to the cave entrance to lie down.

In front of Wolf Mountain, the Black Feather Tribe beastmen landed.

They had mobilized almost all their capable beastmen; coming from the west, it was only a matter of a short time at full flight speed.

They were suppressing their anger, and even hunger was nothing compared to it.

The two sides were separated by the width of a small river, swords drawn and bows bent; if one side made a move, they could start fighting in an instant.

Lang Yan: "You dare to step into the Wolf Tribe without even saying hello."

The Black Feather Tribe beastmen stared at the ball-shaped objects on the ground wrapped in large leaves and vines; those were their lost down feathers.

The leading beastman was full of indignation and cursed: "Is it us who came uninvited, or are you the ones who are shameless! We were wrong about the salt, and we even provided a way to compensate. You said you would consider it, but then you ambushed our tribe!"

Lang Yan's brow twitched.

These little wolves!

"This was an accident."

"An accident?! Then I can also say what our little beastmen did was an accident; do you dare to do it but not admit it?" He pointed at the balls on the ground, "The down feathers of our tribe are accumulated by every beastman from birth; they are the most important things to our beastmen! And you actually ran into our nest to steal!"

Lang Yan: "Speak, what do you want?"

The beastman was furious, his hair visibly exploding like a sea urchin.

Lin Qiu pursed his lips, "Will they fight?"

Lang An: "Large tribes don't fight easily."

Because once they start fighting, it's a lose-lose situation. But if they do fight, they aren't afraid either.

"Do you think we are as despicable as you!"

Lang Yan looked at the returning hunting and gathering teams and said: "Lang Huo, tell him our arrangement."

Lang Huo stepped forward.

The beastman opposite still wanted to argue, but Yu Shan came out and grabbed the beastman's shoulder.

Lang Huo didn't dodge or evade, looked at Yu Shan and said: "Our tribe doesn't want slaves, but you can help us with work, and we will provide food—two meals a day, enough to keep you full. Given that your little beastmen did something wrong, besides providing two meals of food, we won't give you anything else."

"Who knows if you..."

Yu Shan glanced to the side, "Yu Zhang, I know you're worried about Yu Ya, but this is not the time for arguing."

Yu Zhang endured it and was pulled into the crowd of beastmen by the ones behind him.

Seeing that there were beastmen on the other side who could listen, Lang Huo explained: "This time it really was an accident. When our King was talking about this matter, the little wolves only heard half of it and ran out. When we were eating meat soup, we remembered the little wolves hadn't returned. I led a team to look for them, which is why you saw us at that time."

The beastmen opposite paused in their expressions after hearing this.

They caught the most obvious word in this sentence: "Full?"

"You are telling a joke."

Lang Yan's gaze was like a black hole, making Yu Shan's spine shiver as he met his eyes.

"Believe it or not, it's up to you."

At this point, it was neither a fight nor not a fight.

Some of the Black Feather beastmen calmed down first and discovered the differences in Wolf Mountain.

Those dozen or so clay pots set out, the large vats big enough to hold two Black Feather beastmen that looked like things built from mud and stone, and that square stone platform with a fire burning on it...

It was very different.

The wolf beastmen were restless.

The beastmen's heads turning back and forth, constantly probing the situation of their tribe, made them furious!

"King..."

Lang Yan raised his hand.

The beastmen fell silent, forcibly enduring it, staring at these beastmen.

Yu Shan also knew that standing here was provoking the wolf beastmen, and said: "Are you... serious?"

Compared to food, everything else didn't matter.

Even if they were being deceived, they were willing to try.

Lang Huo was lukewarm, "Yeah."

He really wanted to say it was fake.

These impolite beastmen!

And that group of troublemaking little wolf cubs in the back mountain!

*

The back mountain cave was opened.

Sunlight shone in, and the little wolves closed their eyes; they couldn't adapt to the light for a moment.

Lang Huo picked up Lang Jin, and the beastmen behind him picked up the rest of the little wolves and walked toward the front mountain.

When the Black Feather Tribe beastmen saw the little wolves who were so hungry they couldn't stand, they finally believed the Wolf Tribe.

All tribes value their cubs; the little wolves were clearly being punished.

"Apologize."

Lang Jin lay on the ground, "Why should I apologize? They stole our salt!"

The other little wolves also pressed their heads under their paws and just wouldn't make a sound.
