The adult beastmen of the Black Feather Tribe felt a bit awkward being talked about like this by the little wolves.

If you trace the cause, it was still because of them.

Lang Huo kicked the little wolf's paw, "Hurry up, we still have things to do."

"I won't! I just won't!"

Lang Yan looked at the pile of little wolves on the ground and said: "Did you finish listening before you ran off to cause trouble?"

Lang An stroked the little wolf's head, "They did apologize..."

"What's the use of apologizing!"

"You! Did I finish speaking?" Lang An slapped the little wolf on the head.

Locked up for a night, and still acting like an annoying brat who only heard half of things and had no patience!

Lang An told them about the Black Feather Tribe coming to be their slaves, and the little wolves stiffened their necks, their faces turning red.

In the end, they were pressed down, unwilling and feeling like they had lost face, and muttered "I'm sorry."

Lang Yan's eyes hurt from looking at them, "Lock them back up."

Lang Huo grabbed the little wolves and dragged them back to the back mountain with a blank expression.

The little wolves, who had no energy just a moment ago, suddenly struggled, "King! Awoooo... we're hungry!"

"King, we were wrong! We know we were wrong, wooo..."
chapters.source_text:
他想法那么多，一定会让他们更痛苦。
小狼一琢磨，跑到狼岩跟前，还没抱腿哭，就叫狼岩嫌弃避开。
“我没想动手。”狼岩道。
林楸：“哦。”
他默默放开。
狼岩：“你们狼顺叔在后山关着，你们也去陪陪他。一天一顿，吃多了容易坏脑子。”
“王呜……”小狼不敢大声。
狼岩眼不见心不烦，示意狼火几个把他们押送过去。
*
十几个小狼蔫头耷脑地被狼火赶到后山，狼火示意兽人把洞门口的石头移开。
狼顺一天就吃了晚上一顿饭，好不容易睡着，半夜正是开始饿的时候，洞门被打开。
他迷迷糊糊醒来，狼毛凌乱，没什么力气地趴着。
一群小狼哀嚎，就扒着洞口，像里面有吃狼的兽人似的。
狼火带着兽人将他们一个个往里推。
“不呜呜……不要啊火叔！”狼金张嘴干嚎。
其他小狼被他带着往外挤，狼火想着追着他们跑了西边又回来，火气也上来了。
他一抓一个准，全往山洞里扔。
小狼一个叠一个，洞口一封——
狼顺抽了抽被压着的爪子。
他有气无力道：“你们干什么了？”
小狼：“嗷呜嗷呜嗷呜！”
吵死了！
狼顺爪子捂着耳朵，往洞口最里面缩了缩。
外面狼火安排兽人值守。
先前只有狼顺在，只他一个不敢往外跑，但小狼不安分，得有兽人守着。
听着里面的嚎叫，狼火从没有一刻觉得狼嚎声这么吵。
他压着眉头道：“再叫，舌头剪了。”
“嗷呜呜！！！”叫得更起劲。
洞内，狼顺直面十几个小狼的嚎叫声，痛苦地捂住耳朵。他又饿又困，这到底是惩罚小狼的，还是惩罚他的！
狼火见威胁不起作用，道：“行，叫大声点，最好把王叫来。”
洞内一静。
狼火：就是欠收拾！
要不是当时王在场，这群小狼还能这么完好无损地直接关洞里？
狼火带兽人走了。
守着洞口的两个兽人对视一眼，趴下睡觉。
过了会儿，石壁后头传来轻轻的敲击声，两狼耳朵一扣，当听不见。
又敲了几下，没兽人应，小狼哼哼唧唧地收回爪子。
压在狼金背上的小狼也滚了下去，瘫在地上，四个爪爪曲起，不想起来。
狼顺将将快要睡熟，鼻尖又被一戳。
在这黑漆漆的山洞里，狼顺吃不饱又睡不好，他暴躁道：“能不能让我睡觉！”
小狼缩回爪子，委屈道：“顺叔，我们饿。”
他们下午飞速跑到西边，晚上又被狼火追着回来，还没吃饭，饿得肚子咕咕叫。
“饿就睡觉！”
“饿得睡不着。”
“睡不着……你们睡不着能不能让我睡！我也才一天一顿，再闹我，我饿死给你们看！”
小狼被喷了一脸口水。
他拱着屁股，默默往后退。
直退到狼金身边，脑袋往狼金背上一蹭，觉得蹭干净了才滚到一边儿去。
“金，我们饿……”狼小小声道。
狼金下巴搭在狼溶背上，狼溶被压得起不来，爪子踹他脸上，使劲儿推他脸。
“溶溶，我们饿……”
狼溶不理会，继续推。
“冰，我们饿……”
狼冰：“忍。”
狼顺听着小狼们那低低的声音，跟有虫子往耳朵里钻一样。
能不能给他换一个山洞啊！
管不管他的死活了！
*
“王，那明天那事，还成吗？”
经过小狼这么一折腾，人家怕都不敢让兽人再来。
都跑到窝里去了，这跟分兽人锅里的肉汤有什么区别，没准还让黑羽部落恨上他们。
洞内没睡的兽人很多，火堆光芒微弱，狼眼一盏盏如灯亮着。
狼岩：“火，部落商量的事跟黑羽部落说没有？”
狼火趴在自己草窝，叹了一口气。
“王，我们去的时候黑羽部落追过来就打。我又忙着找小狼，没来得及说。”
狼岩：“明天你们再去一次。”
“那小狼他们带回来的东西……”
狼岩：“还回去。”
第二天一早，没等狼火他们去，狼山忽然响起一阵急促的狼嚎。
兽人们一惊，飞速往狼山涌，包括才出发不久的狩猎队跟采集队。
狼岩今天没出去，就防着这个。
狼岩冷眼盯着这群长翅膀的羽族，高大的身躯站在所有兽人最前面。
这群羽族仗着有翅膀，到处乱飞。
后山山洞，听到狼嚎的小狼正闹着要吃肉，忽的安静下来，乖乖巧巧往山洞最里面挤。
狼顺：“……”
小狼崽子！
“踩到我脸了！”
他竖耳听着外面，道：“有没有兽人？”
“不许出来。”外面道，“王在。”
狼顺一听，龇牙咧嘴推开身上的小狼，滚到洞口趴着。
狼山前，黑羽部落的兽人落下。
他们几乎出动了所有能打的兽人，从西边过来，全速飞行不过一会儿的事。
他们憋着怒火，连饥饿都算不得什么了。
两方兽人中间隔着一条小河的宽度，剑拔弩张，只需一方动手，瞬间就能打起来。
狼岩：“招呼不打直接踏入狼部落，你们也敢。”
黑羽部落的兽人盯着地上放的，用大叶片跟藤条裹成的球装物，那就是他们丢失的绒羽。
为首的兽人十足愤慨，骂道：“是我们不请自来还是你们自己不要脸！盐的事我们是做错了，也给了赔偿的方法。你们自己说的考虑，结果却偷袭我们部落！”
狼岩眉心跳了跳。
这群小狼！
“这是意外。”
“意外？！那我还说我们小兽人做的事也是意外，敢做就不敢认吗？”他指着地面那些球，“我们部落的绒羽是每个兽人从出生开始积攒，是我们兽人最重要的东西！你们居然跑到我们窝里偷！”
狼岩：“说吧，你们想怎么样？”
兽人暴怒，头发肉眼可见地炸开，像海胆一样。
林楸抿唇，“会打起来吗？”
狼安：“大部落不轻易打架。”
因为一旦打起来，就是两败俱伤。但如果打，他们也不怕。
“你当我们跟你们一样卑鄙！”
狼岩看着回来的狩猎队跟采集队，道：“狼火，跟他说，我们的安排。”
狼火站出来。
对面那兽人还想吵，羽山出来，抓住兽人肩膀。
狼火不闪不避，看着羽山道：“我们部落不要奴隶，但你们可以帮我们干活，我们提供食物，一天两顿，能让你们吃饱。鉴于你们小兽人做错了事，所以除了管两顿食物之外，不会给你们任何其他东西。”
“谁知道你们……”
羽山扫了旁边一眼，“羽长，知道你担心羽涯，但这不是吵架的时候。”
羽长忍了忍，被后头的兽人拉到兽人堆里去。
狼火见对面有兽人听得进去，这才解释：“这次真的是意外，我们王在说这件事的时候，小狼只听了一半就跑出去了。等我们吃肉汤的时候，才想起来小狼没回来。我带队去找，所以你们那会儿才看见我们。”
对面兽人听完，神情一滞。
他们捕捉到这打算话中最明显的一个词，“吃饱？”
“你们在说笑话。”
狼岩目光黑洞洞的，叫对上他视线的羽山后脊战栗。
“信不信由你们。”
说到这儿，打也不是，不打也不是。
黑羽兽人有先冷静下来的，发现了狼山的不同。
那些摆开的十几个陶锅，大得能装下两个黑羽兽人的大缸，像是泥巴跟石头修起来的东西，还有那燃着火的方方正正的石台……
很不一样。
狼兽人躁动。
兽人转来转去的脑袋，不断打探他们部落的情况，看得他们火大！
“王……”
狼岩抬手。
兽人噤声，强行忍耐着，盯着这些兽人。
羽山也知道站在这儿是挑拨狼兽人的神经，道：“你们……说真的？”
比起食物，其他的一切都算不了什么。
就算被骗，也愿意尝试。
狼火不冷不热，“嗯。”
他很想说是假的。
这群不礼貌的兽人！
还有后山那群闯祸的小狼崽子！
*
后山山洞被打开。
阳光照射进去，小狼们闭了闭眼，一下竟适应不了光线。
狼火拎起狼金，后头的兽人拎着剩下的小狼往前山走。
当黑羽部落的兽人看到饿得站不住的小狼，这才信了狼部落。
部落都重视幼崽，小狼明显是在受惩罚。
“道歉。”
狼金趴地上，“凭什么道歉，是他们偷了我们的盐！”
其他小狼也把脑袋压在爪子下，就是不吭声。
黑羽部落的成年兽人被小狼这么说，有些尴尬。
追究缘由，还是因为他们。
狼火踢了踢小狼的爪子，“赶紧的，还有事儿呢。”
“我不！就不！”
狼岩看着地面一堆小狼，道：“你们听完了吗？就跑去作乱。”
狼安摸着小狼脑袋，“他们道了歉的……”
“道歉有什么用！”
“你！我说完了吗？”狼安一巴掌拍在小狼脑袋。
关一晚上，还是个只听半截，耐不住性子的讨嫌样！
狼安把黑羽部落说的给他们当奴隶的事儿一说，小狼梗着脖子，红了脸。
最终还是被按着，不情不愿，又丢了脸似的，哼哼唧唧说对不起。
狼岩看得眼睛疼，“关回去。”
狼火抓着小狼，又面无表情地往后山拉。
刚刚没力气的小狼一下挣扎起来，“王！嗷呜呜……我们饿！”
“王错了！我们知道错了呜……”
chapters.title: 第65章

chapters.source_text:
黑羽部落的兽人见狼兽人这么对小狼，心里的怒气算散了一半。
羽山示意，兽人赶紧把那些球抱起来。
他闷声道：“你们小狼闯一次我们部落，我们闯两次，还是我们欠你们的。要是按照之前那个法子，我们同意。”
狼兽人闻言，心里哼个不停。
还是他们占便宜了。
达成一致后，由狼兽人跟着，看着他们离开领地。
辽阔的天空上，阳光灿金，映得飞行中的黑羽兽人羽毛斑斓，显出隐隐的彩色。
只黑羽兽人也常常是吃不饱，羽毛同样的粗糙，缺少光泽。
“山！为什么同意，他们肯定说的假话！”羽长忿忿道。
猎物那么少，照狼族那饭量怕是自己都吃不饱。
羽山：“要是照小狼长期没吃饱的状态，能有力气跑到我们山上，翻走绒羽？”
并排飞行的兽人冷静道：“那些狼兽人，也不像挨饿很久的样子，他们比大部分部落的兽人都强壮。”
狼兽人吃了几个月的肉汤，鱼汤，一天两三顿，间或吃点补药，就算没怎么长肉，但内里的亏空早在他们没注意的时候慢慢修复。
那精气神，已经不是刚过雪季后的样子。
而且，狼部落出现了很多他们以前没见过的东西。
“食物珍贵，就算他们有，你当他们真能这么好心分给我们。”
羽山：“就算没有，我们还是要去。”
见羽长还要说，羽山沉声道：“错在我们。”
羽长剩下的话一下堵在胸口。
羽山看他慢慢泛红的眼睛，知道他嘴上不讨喜欢，但心向着族人，软下声来道：“放心，去的还是原来那些兽人。”
就算狼兽人说的是假的，那后果也是他们这些身体弱一点的兽人承受。部落不会有影响。
两方经过这一次交集，也都对对方的部落作风有了认知。
兽人，也有兽人的坚持。
羽长低下头，紧咬牙关。
偷盐是他的幼崽带的头，部落兽人都默许着，他也心存侥幸。
但被发现了就是被发现了，当然要付出代价。
他的族人……就是代价。
羽长安静下来，一直到部落，再不说一句，但周身弥漫着浓烈的绝望感。
*
黑羽部落的兽人送走，狼安继续熬盐。
兽人该捕猎的捕猎，该做木工的做木工。
狼火小队也跟着黑羽兽人过去了，等那边选出兽人，直接带领他们去大泽。
板车、渔网、陶锅那些工具，就由去南边捕猎的队伍带过去。
后山。
临近中午，鉴于小狼们昨天晚上没吃，中午就给了一顿饭。狼顺想跟着蹭一顿，叫兽人带出来，关了另一个山洞。
狼部落对兽人们的约束并不紧，但涉及底线的事，该有的惩罚，哪怕是小狼也要受着。
只能这样，他们才会长记性。
若是动手打，狼兽人皮实，别说小狼，成年狼兽人也一样打了就打了，还有下次。
所以小狼的一天一顿饭改在中午那顿，狼顺依旧还是晚上。
这只是保持了以往没食物的时候的寻常，甚至一顿足够他们吃饱。
但试过一天两三顿后，就变得难以忍受。
前山。
狼山恢复平静，林楸先去祭司那里打卡。
下午出来，又去把剩下的木梳做完，随后拿了背篓去河边割草，捞些小鱼小虾，再剁碎了搅拌搅拌，送去西边林子。
红鸟从山洞挪过来也有两天了，有吃有喝，它们适应得很快。
林楸先看了看分开关在笼子里的红鸟，伸手就差点被叨。
林楸倒了些碎草进去，红鸟吃得飞快，开着笼子也不会往外钻。
又看单独放在外面的幼崽，见他来了，全藏了起来。
林楸将食倒在木槽，又换了水，关门出去。
最多再关个三天，可以试着放出来让它们在围栏里走走。
红鸟关在这里，兽人们也会学着他的方式过来喂，一天三次，即便林楸不在也不会出什么问题。
离开西边林子，林楸沿着树林往东走。
日影斑驳，树木在阳光下像泛着翠绿的光点，植物带着蓬勃的生命力。
林楸背着空背篓慢慢穿梭林中，发尾随着步伐轻轻晃动着。
他身量修长，眉间舒展，身上那股疏离消失，一切都那么自然地融入了这片世界。
他是林楸，也是狼楸。
这样的生活，他适应得很好，也很喜欢。
小狼们在南边林子种的草药大部分都活了，地肥，只要环境适宜，草药几乎栽下去就生根。
连之前挖过山药，截断的那一小截藤条上也冒出了新芽。
林楸看在眼里，忽然想到好久没去看的尾巴草。
出了林子，林楸蹲河边洗干净手，往狼山东边走。
一路上，棚下制盐的兽人抬头，笑着叫他。守着狼山的狼莫见他来，挥了下狼爪，又说：“楸，要不再抓些红鸟？不够吃。”
林楸：“不着急。”
往山洞放了背篓，狼果唤他，“楸，晚上咱们吃肉丸吗？”
林楸：“怕是没空，陶锅都占着制盐。”
狼果沮丧，瞧着跑出草窝的幼崽，克制脚步，怕踩着他们。
幼崽追着林楸出山洞，快下棚子，叫搬出山洞做纺车的狼起抬腿挡住，他又说：“楸，那梳子我能做吗？”
林楸：“你有空就行。”
走到狼山东边，林楸停下。
尾巴草长势极好，已经到林楸腿高。施了肥过后，叶片油绿，抽穗的更多了。
林楸拨开尾巴草，蹲下来，看着土壤表面。
施了肥之后，尾巴草长得快，草也长得快。兽人们几天要扯一次，土壤表面还能看见些鸟粪壳子。
狼木刨木头刨得手疼，出来放风，见林楸蹲在尾巴草边，心一凛，跑了过来。
“楸，尾巴草有问题吗？”
林楸：“没有，我就看看施肥效果。”
狼木放眼望去，这数百米长的尾巴草，茂密健壮，就像吃饱了的狼兽人。
但要是细细分辨，还是有区别。
有的抽穗多，有的……叶片发卷！
狼木大惊失色，“怎么会这样？！”
不等林楸开口，狼木飞快跑去狼山。不一会儿，兽人们全放下手里的事儿过来。
狼岩扶着祭司也过来了。
“王，你看。”狼木小心翼翼托着尾巴草的叶片。
狼岩：“那就是施肥多了。”
他们分了田块施肥，看到底用量多少，这块是最多的。
而且不仅叶子出现了问题，植株看着强壮很多，但抽穗的却少了。
施肥时间不算长，只这一片出现了问题。
尾巴草是大家共同管理的，除草、施肥大多时候都是狼木小队以及狼安他们。
狼岩看着眼前细微变化的尾巴草，知道这块地不能就这么放着，得随时观察记录。
“祭司，尾巴草需要有专门的兽人看管。”
老祭司沿着地里慢慢走了一遭回来，听明白狼岩的意思。
这是问他，有没有合适的兽人。
种植的事以前多是祭司看着，但他年迈，走路都慢，何况手上还不止这个事儿。
他细想了下，发现成年兽人中合适的都忙着。
心里想着狼冰可以，但狼冰现在必须跟着他多学多看。他以后是祭司，不止要明白种植，还有很多任务。
要是专门兽人……
“狼溶。”
“虽是小狼，但心细，也空闲。不会的我带在身边教一教就行。”
尾巴草的驯化，种植，都是几代祭司的心血。祭司们摸索过程中，也学会了记录，不然会遗漏。
狼岩想想，那是个大致上做事还算稳当的小狼。
“等小狼结束惩罚后，告诉他。”
“可是王，这块地该怎么办？”
兽人们没施过肥，看到这样子都怕，万一弄死了怎么办。
狼岩：“暂且不动。”
他转头看向一直没说话的林楸，“楸？”
林楸走到那叶片卷曲的地边，将尾巴草拨开看了看。一见上面堆着的肥，跟他开始看的那块地完全不一样。
狼岩显然也看见了。
兽人们不懂，但都学着林楸去扒拉。
连续看完几处地方，立即明白了区别。
兽人们一致道：“肯定是肥太多，地都被盖完了，得清了多余的。”
林楸：“要是下一场大雨，应该会好一点。”
水能稀释一下土壤里的肥气。
祭司看天，有些愁，“快到雨季了，雨水都攒着到那会儿了。”
这些天有雨也是小雨，不管用。
狼岩拿主意道：“先清，清完看看有没有效果。没有的话，河里打水灌。”
林楸想了一下这法子，脑子里想到了大水漫灌。
这样也没错，就像种花一样，施肥施多了一样会多浇水稀释，道理是相通的。
兽人们凑在一块儿研究。
林楸不是专业种地的，有那么一点经验还是小时候来的。
兽人们自己琢磨，慢慢积累出种植经验，兴许更靠谱些。
林楸庆幸自己来看了，不然这块地照着这么施肥，怕是得减产。
他漫无目的地想着，不经意对上狼岩视线。
看了他一会儿，收回目光。
林楸以为他有事，慢悠悠走过去，立在狼岩身侧。
狼岩已经开始安排兽人清理，有条不紊的，听着令兽人安心。
林楸察觉到他又瞥了自己一眼，他奇怪抬头，“看我干什么？”
狼岩一笑，眸中尽是认真，“幸亏你过来。”
chapters.translated_text:
The orcs of the Black Feather tribe felt half their anger dissipate when they saw the wolf orcs treating the wolf pups this way.

At a gesture from Yushan, the orcs hurriedly picked up the balls.

He said in a muffled voice, "Your wolf pups broke into our tribe once, and we broke into yours twice, so we still owe you. If we follow that previous method, we agree."

Hearing this, the wolf orcs snorted inwardly.

They were still the ones getting the better end of the deal.

After reaching an agreement, they were escorted by the wolf orcs until they left the territory.

In the vast sky, the golden sunlight shone down, making the feathers of the flying Black Feather orcs look iridescent and faintly colorful.

The Black Feather orcs were also often underfed, their feathers similarly coarse and lacking luster.

"Shan! Why did you agree? They must have been lying!" Yuzhang said indignantly.

Prey was so scarce; judging by the appetite of the wolf tribe, they probably couldn't even feed themselves.

Yushan replied, "If the wolf pups had been starving for a long time, would they have had the strength to run to our mountain and snatch the down feathers?"

The orc flying beside him said calmly, "Those wolf orcs don't look like they've been starving for long either; they are stronger than the orcs of most tribes."

The wolf orcs had been eating meat soup and fish soup for months, two or three meals a day, with occasional supplements. Even if they hadn't gained much weight, the internal deficiencies had been slowly repaired without them noticing.

Their vitality was no longer what it had been right after the snow season.

Moreover, many things they had never seen before had appeared in the wolf tribe.

"Food is precious. Even if they have it, do you really think they’d be kind enough to share it with us?"

Yushan said, "Even if they don't, we still have to go."

Seeing Yuzhang about to speak again, Yushan said in a deep voice, "The fault is ours."

The rest of Yuzhang's words became stuck in his throat.

Yushan saw his eyes slowly turning red. Knowing that while he was sharp-tongued, he cared for the tribe, he softened his tone: "Don't worry, it will be the same orcs going as before."

Even if what the wolf orcs said was false, the consequences would be borne by those of them who were physically weaker. The tribe would not be affected.

After this interaction, both sides had gained an understanding of the other tribe's style.

Orcs, too, have their own persistence.

Yuzhang lowered his head, clenching his teeth.

It was his cub who had led the theft of the salt, the tribal orcs had tacitly approved, and he himself had harbored a fluke mentality.

But discovered was discovered, and naturally, a price had to be paid.

His tribesmen... were the price.

Yuzhang fell silent, not saying another word until they reached the tribe, but a thick sense of despair permeated him.

*

After the Black Feather tribe orcs were sent off, Lang An continued to boil salt.

The orcs went about their business: hunting, woodworking, and so on.

The Wolf Fire squad also went over with the Black Feather orcs, and once the orcs were selected there, they would lead them directly to the Great Marsh.

Tools like carts, fishing nets, and pottery pots would be brought over by the hunting team heading south.

The back mountain.

Near noon, considering the wolf pups hadn't eaten last night, they were given one meal at noon. Lang Shun wanted to tag along for a meal, but was taken out by the orcs and locked in another cave.

The wolf tribe's constraints on the orcs were not tight, but when it came to bottom-line issues, the necessary punishments had to be endured, even by the wolf pups.

Only then would they learn their lesson.

If they were just beaten, wolf orcs were tough; let alone the pups, even adult wolf orcs would just take a beating and do it again next time.

Therefore, the wolf pups' one meal a day was moved to noon, while Lang Shun's remained in the evening.

This was just maintaining the norm from when there was no food, and one meal was enough for them to be full.

But after trying two or three meals a day, it became unbearable.

The front mountain.

Langshan returned to calm, and Lin Qiu went to check in with the priest first.

Coming out in the afternoon, he finished the remaining wooden combs, then took a basket to the river to cut grass and scoop up small fish and shrimp, which he then chopped up, mixed, and sent to the western woods.

The red birds had been moved from the cave for two days; with food and drink, they adapted very quickly.

Lin Qiu first looked at the red birds kept in separate cages and was almost pecked when he reached in.

Lin Qiu poured some chopped grass in, and the red birds ate quickly; even with the cages open, they didn't try to crawl out.

He looked at the cub kept separately outside, and seeing him arrive, it hid away.

Lin Qiu poured the food into the wooden trough, changed the water, and closed the door as he left.

At most, after three more days of confinement, he could try letting them out to walk around in the enclosure.

With the red birds kept here, the orcs would also learn his method of feeding them three times a day, so there wouldn't be any problems even if Lin Qiu wasn't around.

Leaving the western woods, Lin Qiu walked east along the forest.

The sunlight was dappled, and the trees seemed to shimmer with emerald light spots, the plants full of vigorous vitality.

Lin Qiu walked slowly through the forest with an empty basket on his back, his hair ends swaying gently with his steps.

He was slender, his brow relaxed, and the sense of detachment about him had vanished; everything was so naturally integrated into this world.

He was Lin Qiu, and also Lang Qiu.

He had adapted very well to this life and liked it very much.

Most of the medicinal herbs the wolf pups planted in the southern woods had survived; the soil was fertile, and as long as the environment was suitable, the herbs took root almost as soon as they were planted.

Even the small piece of vine left over from digging yams had sprouted new buds.

Lin Qiu saw this and suddenly remembered the tail grass he hadn't checked in a long time.

Leaving the woods, Lin Qiu squatted by the river to wash his hands and walked toward the east side of Langshan.

Along the way, the orcs making salt under the shed looked up and greeted him with a smile. Lang Mo, who was guarding Langshan, saw him coming, waved a wolf paw, and said, "Qiu, why not catch some more red birds? There isn't enough to eat."

Lin Qiu replied, "No rush."

After putting his basket in the cave, Lang Guo called out to him, "Qiu, are we having meatballs tonight?"

Lin Qiu said, "I'm afraid there's no time; the pottery pots are all occupied with salt-making."

Lang Guo was dejected, watching the cubs running out of the grass nest, restraining his steps for fear of stepping on them.

The cub chased Lin Qiu out of the cave, and just before reaching the shed, Lang Qi, who had been moved out of the cave to make spinning wheels, lifted his leg to block him. He said again, "Qiu, can I make that comb?"

Lin Qiu replied, "As long as you have time."

Walking to the east side of Langshan, Lin Qiu stopped.

The tail grass was growing very well, already reaching Lin Qiu's leg height. After fertilization, the leaves were oily green, and more had sprouted ears.

Lin Qiu pushed aside the tail grass, squatted down, and looked at the soil surface.

After fertilization, the tail grass grew fast, but so did the weeds. The orcs had to pull them every few days, and some bird droppings shells could still be seen on the soil surface.

Lang Mu, whose hands were sore from planing wood, came out for a break and saw Lin Qiu squatting by the tail grass. His heart skipped a beat, and he ran over.

"Qiu, is there a problem with the tail grass?"

Lin Qiu said, "No, I'm just checking the effect of the fertilizer."

Lang Mu looked out; this hundreds-of-meters-long stretch of tail grass was lush and robust, just like well-fed wolf orcs.

But if one looked closely, there was a difference.

Some had many ears, while others... the leaves were curling!

Lang Mu was horrified, "How can this be?!"

Without waiting for Lin Qiu to speak, Lang Mu ran quickly to Langshan. Before long, all the orcs put down what they were doing and came over.

Lang Yan also came over, supporting the priest.

"King, look." Lang Mu carefully held up the leaves of the tail grass.

Lang Yan said, "That's too much fertilizer."

They had divided the fields to fertilize and see how much to use, and this plot had the most.

And it wasn't just the leaves that had problems; the plants looked much stronger, but they had fewer ears.

The fertilization hadn't been going on for long, but only this patch had problems.

The tail grass was managed by everyone, and weeding and fertilizing were mostly done by Lang Mu's squad and Lang An's group.

Lang Yan looked at the subtly changing tail grass, knowing that this plot couldn't just be left alone; it had to be observed and recorded at all times.

"Priest, the tail grass needs to be looked after by a dedicated orc."

The old priest walked slowly along the field and came back, understanding what Lang Yan meant.

He was asking if there was a suitable orc.

Planting matters were mostly overseen by the priest in the past, but he was old, walked slowly, and had more than just this on his hands.

He thought carefully and found that all the suitable adult orcs were busy.

He thought Lang Bing would be fine, but Lang Bing had to follow him to learn and see more now. He would be a priest in the future and needed to understand not just planting, but many other tasks.

If it was a dedicated orc...

"Lang Rong."

"Although he is a wolf pup, he is careful and has free time. If there's something he doesn't know, I'll keep him by my side and teach him."

The domestication and planting of tail grass were the lifeblood of several generations of priests. In the process of exploration, the priests also learned to record, otherwise, things would be missed.

Lang Yan thought about it; he was a wolf pup who generally did things steadily.

"Tell him after the wolf pup finishes his punishment."

"But King, what should we do about this plot?"

The orcs had never fertilized before and were afraid when they saw this; what if they killed it?

Lang Yan said, "Leave it for now."

He turned his head to look at Lin Qiu, who hadn't spoken the whole time, "Qiu?"

Lin Qiu walked to the edge of the plot where the leaves were curling and pushed the tail grass aside to look. Once he saw the fertilizer piled on top, it was completely different from the plot he had looked at earlier.

Lang Yan clearly saw it too.

The orcs didn't understand, but they all learned from Lin Qiu and started digging.

After checking several places in a row, they immediately understood the difference.

The orcs said in unison, "It must be too much fertilizer; the ground is completely covered, we have to clear the excess."

Lin Qiu said, "If there's a heavy rain, it should get a bit better."

Water could dilute the fertilizer gas in the soil.

The priest looked at the sky, a bit worried, "It's almost the rainy season, and all the rain is saved for that time."

Any rain these days was just light drizzle, which wouldn't help.

Lang Yan made the decision, "Clear it first, and see if there's any effect after clearing. If not, we'll fetch water from the river to irrigate."

Lin Qiu thought about this method, and the idea of flood irrigation came to his mind.

That was correct; just like growing flowers, if you fertilize too much, you water it to dilute it. The principle was the same.

The orcs gathered together to study it.

Lin Qiu was not a professional farmer; the little experience he had was from when he was a child.

If the orcs figured it out themselves and slowly accumulated planting experience, it might be more reliable.

Lin Qiu was glad he came to see it, otherwise, if this plot continued to be fertilized like this, it would likely have a reduced yield.

He thought aimlessly, and inadvertently met Lang Yan's gaze.

He looked at him for a moment and then withdrew his gaze.

Lin Qiu thought he had something to do, so he walked over slowly and stood by Lang Yan's side.

Lang Yan had already started arranging for the orcs to clean up, orderly and calm, which made the orcs feel at ease.

Lin Qiu noticed him glancing at himself again, and he looked up strangely, "Why are you looking at me?"

Lang Yan smiled, his eyes full of sincerity, "It's fortunate you came over."
chapters.title: 第66章

chapters.translated_text:
"They're back, Chief! They're back!"

In the Heiyu Tribe, a Heiyu beastman crouched at the peak of the mountain sprinted down into the cave below.

Yule, sitting beside the Heiyu Chief, abruptly sat up straight, a trace of joy lighting up his youthful face. Seeing the old beastman lying in the nest twitch his fingers, he hurried over to help him up.

"Grandpa," Yule whispered.

The Heiyu Chief asked in a hoarse voice, "How many returned? Are any of them injured?"

The bird beastman who brought the news froze, his wings neatly folded in front of his chest. "I-I forgot to look." With that, he anxiously bolted out of the cave headfirst and said, "I'll go check right now!"

"No need, we're back."

Led by Yushan, the beastmen flew down one after another into the cave.

He used his large hand to steady the young boy who had bumped into him, his palm just large enough to cover the top of the boy's head.

Seeing the Heiyu Chief looking over, he withdrew his hand, lowered his head, and walked over in a few strides to sit down before him.

"Chief, everyone is back, and no one is injured. The down feathers have all been brought back as well."

The black wolf beastmen were still waiting outside for their reply. Yushan recounted what had happened at the Wolf Tribe, causing the Heiyu Chief to draw a sharp breath. His breathing sounded heavy and labored.

With drooping eyelids, he nodded and said, "It should have been this way to begin with. Go."

The beastmen who were supposed to go had already been arranged. If not for that commotion caused by the little wolf, they should have been working at the Wolf Tribe long ago.

Yushan took the lead and stood up, the clansmen who were going closely following behind him.

The other beastmen did not dare to see them off this time, fearing their home would be raided, and could only watch desolately.

Some demi-beastmen, watching their mates leave with tears in their eyes, followed a few steps behind without daring to make a sound.

With trembling palms, the Heiyu Chief gripped the down feathers beside him and suddenly spoke up, "Whatever useful things the tribe has, take some with you."

Yushan said in a deep voice, "Chief, leave them all for the tribe."

Having finished these words with his back turned, he plunged down the mountain. His body fell rapidly, breaking through the swirling clouds and mists halfway up the mountainside, the wind cutting against his face like knives, as if trying to tear his body apart.

Yushan's gaze was pitch-black and deadpan.

That patch of lush green drew closer; going any further meant being smashed to pieces.

Yushan experienced the sensation of impending death. At the very last moment, his huge black wings spread out, gliding on the wind, and he landed before Lang Huo.

"Let's go," he said.

Lang Huo nodded, eyeing the eighteen beastmen who landed behind him.

Compared to those who charged into battle at Wolf Mountain, these beastmen were noticeably weaker. Lang Huo felt displeased looking at them, but thinking of the King's intention—labor in exchange for food—if they dared to slack off or play tricks, they needn't expect to take advantage of them.

Among the nineteen beastmen, twelve were males and seven were demi-beastmen. Female beastmen were scarce to begin with, so having none was normal.

Led by the second hunting team, the group of beastmen headed toward the Great Marsh.

The beastmen had run all morning without eating, and then ran all afternoon to reach the Great Marsh. Upon arrival, the wolf beastmen were so hungry they collapsed onto the ground, while the Heiyu beastmen trembled with their wings and foamed at the mouth, scaring the wolf beastmen out of their wits.

Something couldn't possibly go wrong the moment they reached their territory! How was he supposed to report this to the King?

Lang Huo had no choice but to drag himself up and tell his own beastmen to hurry up and catch fish and make a fire.

Pressing against his legs, which ached as if their tendons and bones were being twisted and shredded, Yushan forced himself up in a cold sweat.

His legs were so weak he almost collapsed to his knees after walking only a few steps. Hurriedly bracing himself against a nearby tree, he could only say to the wolf beastman, "Can you... get some water?"

Seeing the Heiyu beastmen looking so fragile and brittle, Lang Huo only found it aggravating.

He called out, "Lang Chou! Go get some water."

A wolf crouching right by the water turned around. He was one of the few wolves in the tribe with an unusual coat pattern—rings of white around both eyes, and pitch-black everywhere else.

The moment he was born, his dad took one look and said the word "ugly," and as people kept calling him that, his name became Lang Chou (Wolf Ugly).

Lang Chou tore off a large, ubiquitous leaf, folded it into a triangular shape, and scooped up some water from nearby.

"Here," he said cheerfully, looking kinder than the other wolf beastmen.

Supporting his clansman, Yushan took it and said, "Thank you."

He bowed his head, pinched open the beastman's jaw, and poured it into his mouth.

Lang Chou watched the Heiyu beastman's rapidly heaving chest. That chest was so emaciated, even more exaggerated than theirs had been at first, that the beating of his heart was clearly visible. His abdomen was sunken, his hip bones protruded, and his two legs looked like a pair of chopsticks.

He hadn't thought much of it before, but looking at it now, he found it terrifyingly skeletal.

Lang Chou lowered his head to look at his own chest, suddenly opened his eyes wide, and reached out to poke the slightly plump flesh on his chest.

His ears twitched, transforming directly into wolf ears that trembled with excitement.

Seeing him showing off in front of the half-dead Heiyu beastmen, Lang Huo roared, "Chou! What are you doing?!"

The mighty and robust black wolf jumped in fright at Lang Huo's roar.

"Team Leader."

He walked up to Lang Huo with a coy and bashful air, a bright gleam still in his eyes. Puffing out his chest, he whispered, "Team Leader, look, we've grown meat."

Lang Huo's gaze swept across his chest, then lowered to look at his own.

"Right, Team Leader!" Lang Chou sidled up to him, his tail seemingly wagging behind him.

Lang Huo paused for a second, raised his head, and scolded, "You're just figuring this out now?! Hurry up! What use is water? If you don't feed them soon, that group of beastmen is going to die!"

Startled by him, Lang Chou's wolf ears abruptly turned back into human ears.

Clutching his buzzing ears and acting as if his tail was on fire, he said hastily, "I know!"

They hadn't brought anything with them, so to eat, they could only catch food from the lake.

The wolf beastmen went around to the side of the low hill one by one before they could jump into the water. Holding their breath underwater, they grabbed fat fish one after another and tossed them onto the bank.

Listening to their conversation, Yushan set his companion down on the ground.

He stood up, but a spasm racked his leg, hurting him so badly that sweat beads the size of beans dripped down his chin.

This was an old injury. When he didn't move much on ordinary days, it only ached faintly. Today, having marched almost without stopping, it had flared up again.

He endured and adjusted for a moment before panting and calling upon the companions who could still walk to help out.

Seeing this, Lang Huo waved a hand dismissively. "Forget it, just go sit down. I'm afraid if you guys go into the water, you won't be able to crawl back out."

The wolf beastmen didn't have a hobby of abusing beastmen; looking at how pale each of their faces was, they could scare someone to death at night.

Thinking of Qiu, Lang Huo let out a lingering sigh.

The King made them stay here for a few days, so they definitely wouldn't get to eat the delicious food Qiu made...

Looking at this group of beastmen still standing motionless, he lost his patience and couldn't be bothered to talk nonsense.

As soon as the fire was lit here, they would immediately start roasting fish.

The Heiyu beastmen squatted off to the side and watched, keeping some distance between themselves and the others.

They ate roasted fish too.

Because they couldn't catch other prey, they ate it frequently.

They weren't very particular about eating roasted fish; they would just grab them and roast them directly. The roasted fish always turned out either burnt or bitter, and had a strong, muddy smell.

Although their beast forms were also birds, beastmen were fundamentally different from animals—at least they wouldn't swallow a whole fish raw.

The Heiyu Tribe ate a lot of fish out of necessity, and most beastmen didn't like eating it.

But whether they liked it or not didn't matter; as long as it filled their stomachs, that was enough.

At this moment, watching the wolf beastmen roast fish, the feeling was completely different.

Why did fish need to be processed like that?

Weren't the scales edible?

Weren't the internal organs also meat?

The stuff right under the fish's head was blood red, pretty much like meat too, and edible.

Watching the fish get whittled down until only a little meat was left, while the water was left bloody, the beastmen felt a pang of heartache at the waste, even though they didn't like eating fish.

Truly, they had food to eat now, so they were this willing to throw things away.

But when the wolf beastmen sliced open the fish meat and applied mashed grass leaves and fruits to it, the Heiyu beastmen couldn't help swallowing their saliva at the strange scent while feeling utterly terrified.

Holding both wings in front of their chests and hunching their necks to conceal themselves, the Heiyu beastmen whispered to Yushan, "A-Shan, are they planning to make a move on us?"

Yushan watched as the beastmen placed the fish meat over the fire, too busy to even bother with them, each staring fixedly at the fish and swallowing saliva.

"Doesn't look like it."

"Don't let your imagination run wild."

"But... Gulp..." The beastman slightly unfurled his wings, lowering his head to look at his rumbling stomach. He sniffed the scent in the air, then suddenly raised his head, looking in astonishment at the source of the fragrance.

"How can this be..."

So fragrant!

The Heiyu beastman lying on the ground twitched his eyelids. Pressing his trembling wings against his clamoring stomach, he turned his head toward the campfire the wolf beastmen had lit.

At a glance, they saw the fish skewered on wooden sticks.

The fish skin was curled, oily and golden-brown. Along the slashes in the fish bodies, the tender white meat was slightly charred, emitting a strange aroma unlike the muddy, fishy smell they used to eat—an exotic fragrance they couldn't quite describe.

It was a bit pungent, but smelling it caused their saliva to secrete so rapidly that they couldn't even swallow it in time.

So hungry, so hungry...

The beastmen pressed hard against their stomachs, feeling dizzy and on the verge of rolling their eyes, when Lang Huo urged, "Is it cooked yet? We're about to die!"

"Right away, right away!" a wolf beastman said. "Don't rush!"

The wolf beastmen were tired too, but their bodies were better nourished, and going hungry for a day was tolerable.

They had a habitual division of labor: six beastmen went down to catch fish, four cleaned the fish, two made the fire, and the rest roasted the fish.

Operating with the efficiency honed by that pack of starving wolves in the tribe, a single batch of roasted fish could yield over a dozen.

The beastmen swallowed their saliva.

With their palates now refined, they couldn't possibly eat anything without seasonings.

But the Heiyu beastmen were watching right beside them; if they gave them unseasoned food on their very first meal, anyone not knowing better would think they were abusing them. Thus, they had no choice but to make them endure for a moment so everyone could eat something flavorful together.

Bustling about, their paws were practically moving at lightning speed.

Carrying over four or five fish, Lang Huo said, "Just consider it done when it's cooked, stop worrying about whether it's charred or not, hurry up!"

"Don't rush!"

The beastman snapped irritably!

Having been roared at, Lang Huo was a bit dazed.

"I..."

"Take it, take it!" The beastman snatched the fish from his hands, shoving a few roasted ones—though not perfectly roasted—back at him. "Hurry, hurry, hurry! Will rushing make it cook faster?"

Lang Huo felt as though he were looking at Lang An when he cooked.

He finally understood why An's personality had changed.

Choosing not to argue with the beastman, Lang Huo took the five roasted fish and handed them to Yushan first. "You hand these out to the ones who are about to starve first."

Staring at the fish, Yushan grasped it.

"Thank you."

"A-Shan," the Heiyu beastman still felt uncertain.

Why were they given food to eat first?

Yushan shook his head and broke off a piece for himself to put in his mouth. Seeing this, Lang Huo snorted inwardly and went back to roasting fish.

"A-Shan?" The beastman clutched Yushan's arm, tension in his eyes.

Pushing his lips together, Yushan swallowed, paused to feel for a moment, and said, "It's fine."

He immediately tore the fish meat apart and distributed it to his companions whose strength was depleted. Though the beastmen lay on the ground unable to move, catching the scent, they scrambled to grab the fish meat and shoved it into their mouths.

Almost the moment it touched their tongues, they froze for a second before devouring it ravenously.

Taking it all in, Yushan touched the tip of his tongue to that tiny bit of fish meat in his mouth that he couldn't bear to swallow.

It really was delicious.

Just what had the wolf beastmen encountered? Why was their tribe so wealthy, and how did they come up with a method of roasting fish like this?

No one provided him with answers.

Nor could Yushan afford to show even a shred of curiosity.

chapters.source_text:
“回来了，族长！他们回来了！”
黑羽部落，蹲在山顶的黑羽兽人飞蹿入底下山洞。
坐在黑羽族长旁边的羽乐骤然坐直，稚嫩的脸上带上些喜意。见躺在窝里的老兽人动了动手，忙过去将他扶起来。
“阿爷。”羽乐小声道。
黑羽族长哑声问：“回来多少，有没有受伤？”
报信的鸟兽人一愣，翅膀端端正正笼在身前，“我、我忘了看。”说罢，又急着闷头冲出山洞道：“我立马去！”
“不用了，我们回来了。”
羽山带头，兽人陆续飞落进山洞中。
他大手抵着撞过来的少年，手掌刚好能盖住少年头顶。
见黑羽族长看来，他收回手，垂头，几步走到他跟前坐下。
“族长，都回来了，没有受伤。羽绒也都拿回来了。”
黑狼兽人还在外面等着他们的答复，羽山将在狼部落的事情说了一遍，黑羽族长吸了一口气，呼吸声很大，有些喘不上来。
他眼皮垂着，点点头道：“本来就该这样，去吧。”
要去的兽人早安排好了，要不是小狼闹那一出，他们现在早应该在狼部落干活儿了。
羽山带头起身，要去的族人紧紧跟着。
旁的兽人这次不敢再送，怕被偷家，只落寞地看着。
有些看着伴侣走的亚兽人眼里含着泪，跟了几步，不敢出声。
黑羽族长手掌哆嗦着，紧紧抓住身旁的绒羽，忽然出声：“部落的东西，用得到的，都带一些走吧。”
羽山沉声：“族长，都留给部落吧。”
他背对着说完这句话，扑向山下。身体极速下坠，破了山腰缭绕的云雾，风如刀割在脸上，似要将身体也四分五裂。
羽山目色一片沉寂。
那片郁郁葱葱的绿意近了，再下去，就要粉身碎骨。
羽山体会着那股死亡欲来的感受，最后一刻，黑色的巨大翅膀张开，乘着风滑翔，落在狼火面前。
“走吧。”他道。
狼火点头，看他身后落下的十八个兽人。
比起在狼山冲锋陷阵的那些，这些兽人明显弱一点。狼火看着心里不爽，但想到王的意思是劳动交换食物，他们要是敢偷奸耍滑，那也别想从他们这里占到便宜。
十九个兽人有十二个雄兽人，七个亚兽人，雌性兽人本来就少，没一个也正常。
一行兽人在狩猎二队的带领下往大泽去。
兽人们跑了一上午没吃饭，又接着跑了一下午到大泽。到了地儿，狼兽人饿得趴地，黑羽兽人更是抖着翅膀口吐白沫，给狼兽人吓得够呛。
总不能才到他们地盘儿就出问题，这让他怎么跟王交代！
狼火不得不爬起来，叫自家兽人赶紧捞鱼生火。
羽山按着自己疼得像被绞烂了筋骨的腿，一头冷汗的撑着起来。
走不了几步腿软得差点跪地上去，他忙撑着一旁的树，只能跟狼兽人道：“能不能……弄点水。”
狼火看黑羽兽人这脆皮样，只觉闹心。
他道：“狼丑！弄点水来。”
就蹲在水边的狼转头，他是部落里少有的毛色分布奇特的狼，两个眼睛一圈是白色，其他地方全是黑色。
一出生，他阿爸看了第一眼就先说了个“丑”字，叫着叫着，名字也就成了狼丑。
狼丑扯下随处可见的大叶片，折成三角状，往附近弄了些水来。
“给。”他乐乐呵呵的，比其他狼兽人看着和善。
羽山扶着自家兽人，接过，“谢谢。”
他闷头捏开兽人下巴，往嘴里灌。
狼丑看着黑羽兽人极速起伏的胸口，那胸口瘦得比他们当初还夸张心脏的跳动都能看得清晰。腹部凹陷，胯骨凸起，两条腿儿跟两筷子似的。
以前不觉，现在再看才发现瘆得慌。
狼丑低头看看自己胸口，忽然睁大眼，伸手戳了戳自己胸口微微鼓起的肉。
耳朵一抖，直接变成狼耳激动地颤了颤。
狼火见他在要死不活的黑羽兽人面前嘚瑟，吼道：“丑！你干什么呢！”
威武健壮的黑狼被狼火吼得一个激灵。
“队长。”
他扭扭捏捏走到狼火身前，眼里还冒着亮光，他挺了挺他胸口，小声道：“队长，你看，我们长肉了。”
狼火目光扫过他胸口，再低头看自己。
“是吧，队长！”狼丑蹭过来，身后似有尾巴在摇。
狼火愣了一秒，抬起头斥道：“你才发现！赶紧的，水管什么用，再不吃东西那群兽人都要死了！”
狼丑被他吓得狼耳倏地变了人耳。
他捂着嗡嗡响的耳朵，火烧屁股似的，急急忙忙道：“我知道了！”
他们什么都没带过来，要吃东西只能去湖里抓。
狼兽人一个个绕到矮山那边才能跳入水，憋足一口气下水，抓着一条条大胖鱼往岸上扔。
羽山听着他们的对话，将同伴放在地上。
他起身，腿上一阵抽搐，疼得他汗如豆大，顺着下巴滴落。
这是旧伤，平日没怎么动弹，也就隐隐作痛。今天几乎没停歇，这才复发。
他忍着适应了会儿，才喘息着，叫上还能走的同伴去帮忙。
狼火看见，手一甩：“得了，坐着去吧。我怕你们下了水就爬不起来。”
狼兽人没虐待兽人的爱好，瞧这一个个脸色白的，夜里能把楸吓死。
狼火想到楸，幽幽叹气。
王让他们在这边待几天，那楸做好吃的，他们肯定吃不到了……
他看着这群还站着不动的兽人，没了耐心，也懒得费话。
等这边火一生好，立即烤鱼。
黑羽兽人蹲在的一旁看着，与他们隔着些距离。
他们也吃烤鱼。
因为抓不到其他猎物，还经常吃。
他们吃烤鱼没那么讲究，都是直接抓起来就烤。鱼烤出来不是糊的就是苦的，味道很大。
虽然他们兽形也是鸟，但兽人跟动物本质上还是有区别，至少不会生吞一整条鱼。
黑羽部落是不得已吃很多鱼，大部分兽人都不爱吃。
可爱吃不爱吃都无所谓，能填饱肚子就行。
此时看到狼兽人烤鱼，那感觉格外不同。
鱼怎么要那么处理？
鳞片不能吃吗？
内脏不也是肉？
鱼脑袋下面的血红血红的，也跟肉差不多，也能吃的。
兽人们看着鱼最后只剩下那点肉，水里血淋淋的。虽然他们不喜欢吃鱼，但见狼兽人浪费也心疼。
果然是有食物吃了，这么舍得扔。
但当狼兽人划破鱼肉，还往上面弄捏碎的草叶、果子，黑羽兽人闻着那奇怪的味道忍不住咽口水的同时，觉得害怕极了。
黑羽兽人两个翅膀拢在身前，缩着脖子遮掩着，对羽山小声道：“阿山，他们是不是想对我们下手？”
羽山看着兽人把鱼肉往火上一架，都没空理会他们，一个个盯着鱼咽口水。
“不像。”
“别乱想。”
“可是……咕噜……”兽人微微摊开翅膀，低头看着自己打鸣的肚子。他嗅了嗅空气中的味道，忽然抬头，惊奇地看向那股香味的来源。
“怎么会……”
这么香！
躺在地上的黑羽兽人眼皮动了动，一直颤抖的翅膀抵着叫嚣的肚子，脑袋转向狼兽人生起来的火堆。
他们一眼看见了木棍上串着的鱼。
鱼皮卷曲，油润金黄。鱼身上的划痕处，那嫩白的肉微焦，泛着一股不同于他们以前吃的土腥味，而是奇异的，他们形容不出来的香味。
有点呛，但是闻着唾液飞快分泌，咽都咽不及。
好饿，好饿……
兽人死死压住肚子，头晕眼花，眼看就要翻白眼，狼火催促：“熟了没？要死了！”
“马上马上！”狼兽人道，“不要催！”
狼兽人也累，但身体养得好些了，饿一天能忍受。
他们习惯性分工忙活，六个兽人下去抓鱼，四个兽人杀鱼，两个生火，剩下的烤鱼。
照着部落那群饿狼练出来的效率，一批烤鱼能出十几条。
兽人们咽口水。
自己嘴巴养叼了，怎么着都不能吃没调料的。
但黑羽兽人就在旁边看着，第一顿就给人家吃没味的，不知道的还以为他们虐待人家。那就只有让他们忍着，大伙儿一起吃味道好的。
忙忙碌碌，爪子都翻出花来了。
狼火又拎着四五条鱼过来，道：“熟了就得了，别什么焦不焦的，快点儿！”
“别催啊！”
兽人暴躁！
狼火被吼了下，有点懵。
“我……”
“拿去拿去！”兽人将他手里的鱼拿走，递给他几条烤熟的，但烤得不完美的，“催催催，催就能好吗？”
狼火仿佛看到了做饭的狼安。
他可算知道了安为什么变了性子。
狼火不跟兽人辩，拿着五条烤好的鱼先递给羽山，“你先给要饿死的分。”
羽山看着那鱼，握住。
“谢谢。”
“阿山。”黑羽兽人还是不确定。
为什么先给他们吃？
羽山摇头，自己掰了一块入口。狼火见了，心里哼了声，又去烤鱼。
“阿山？”兽人抓着羽山胳膊，眼里紧张。
羽山抿着唇，咽下，感受了会儿道：“没事。”
他立即将鱼肉撕碎，分给几个体力耗尽的同伴。兽人们躺在地上动不了，但闻到味儿，挣扎着抓着鱼肉就往嘴里塞。
几乎一入口，愣了下，狼吞虎咽。
羽山看在眼里，舌尖触着嘴里那块舍不得吞下去的一点鱼肉。
真好吃啊。
狼兽人到底遇到了什么，为什么部落里那么富有，还能想出这种烤鱼的办法？
无人给他解答。
羽山也不能漏出一点好奇。

chapters.translated_text:
The grilled fish was ready quickly, and before long, each Black Feather beastman received a piece of fish the size of a palm.

With something finally in their stomachs, they began to recover.

The Wolf beastmen’s hands were sore from grilling. Seeing the Black Feather beastmen finish their first round, one asked, "Captain, can we eat now?"

Wolf Fire: "Eat."

The Wolf beastman grabbed the piece he had just finished grilling and shoved it straight into his mouth.

The beastman responsible for catching and cleaning the fish saw this, rushed back, grabbed the other by the hair, and snatched half of the fish out of his mouth.

They had only eaten once in the morning, ran to the west in the forenoon, and to the south in the afternoon. Now that it was almost evening, who wouldn't be hungry!

The Wolf beastmen scrambled to eat.

The Black Feather beastmen cherished every last bit of fish, licking their lips and only watching secretly.

"A-Shan."

The beastmen gathered around, still wanting more.

Yu Shan said, "This is their territory."

Even though there were plenty of fish in the Great Marsh, they couldn't just catch them.

Everyone could only watch as the Wolf beastmen finished the fish. Fortunately, they ate quickly, and it was only a matter of a few bites, so they didn't have to suffer for long.

Having finally lined their stomachs, the Wolf beastmen regained their senses and noticed the group of hungry beastmen opposite them.

Wolf Fire thought for a moment and said, "Let's make a deal."

"Since we haven't started working yet, how about you catch the fish for this meal, and we do the grilling?"

Yu Shan didn't hesitate at all: "Agreed."

Wolf Fire: "Then hurry, catch as many as you can."

Yu Shan immediately wanted to point out a few beastmen, but apart from those who were exhausted from flying, all who could still fly stood up.

Yu Shan looked at them: "Go."

The sooner they caught them, the sooner they could be full.

A dozen Black Feather beastmen spread their wings and flew in a straight line toward the waters of the Great Marsh.

The fish in the lake had never been fished on a large scale. The Black Feather beastmen had sharp claws and were fast, locking onto their targets and diving down.

Their hook-like claws pierced the fish bodies like iron pincers; not a single fish could escape.

The Wolf beastmen watched the water splashes from the shore and said, "Having wings is still more convenient."

Wolf Fire: "Are our fishing nets not convenient?"

Beastman: "Our fishing nets are the best!"

They could only catch one at a time, so how could it compare to their nets?

The beastmen caught and grilled fish, working like an assembly line until it was completely dark.

In front of the Wolf and Black Feather beastmen, each beastman had two fish.

The Wolf beastmen were fine; after a few bites, they discussed what seasoning the fish lacked today and how it differed from the taste of Lin Qiu's grilling.

Looking a few meters away, the Black Feather beastmen ate without even lifting their heads.

Until the two fish were finished and their stomachs were full, the Black Feather beastmen sprawled on the ground, staring blankly at the star-filled sky.

The beastmen rested their hands on their slightly bulging bellies, lost in thought for a long time.

So comfortable...

So this is what it feels like to be full...

There were many beastmen in their tribe, and they rarely caught enough prey. Even catching fish was time-consuming and laborious, and the grilled fish didn't taste good.

A full meal made the Black Feather beastmen let go of their doubts about the Wolf beastmen's promises.

However, they were still in someone else's tribe and couldn't relax for too long. The beastmen crawled up and huddled closely together again.

Now that they were full, it was time to discuss serious matters.

Tomorrow, beastmen should be coming from Wolf Mountain, and the tools needed for work would be delivered. Wolf Fire began to explain tomorrow's arrangements to the Black Feather beastmen.

The two groups of beastmen sat opposite each other, right next to a large area where wild grass had been cut.

A bonfire burned in the middle, and the beastmen looked sharp and focused, none of them as relaxed as they had been while eating fish.

One side was wary because another tribe had appeared on their territory, and the other was wary because they were living under someone else's roof; both sides were on guard.

Wolf Fire's fur looked even redder in the firelight. He said, "Tomorrow, your beastmen need to be divided into three teams. One team will follow us to the south of the Great Marsh to dig up bird droppings, some will stay here to harvest wild grass, and one team will cut hemp grass. The Wolf beastmen will also be divided into teams to lead you."

Yu Shan nodded, his wings folded in front of him shining in the light.

"It takes us three days to run from here to the Great Marsh, and four days with carts. We will take you there to see it first, and then you will transport it yourselves. The wild grass is this area..." Wolf Fire pointed casually, and the Black Feather beastmen noticed the area that had been harvested.

They hadn't noticed this grass at the Wolf tribe and didn't know what they were cutting it for.

"As for the hemp grass, it grows both further south and north. It grows quite scattered, so you have to walk around to harvest it. After the two types of grass are cut, they need to be soaked in water, and then they need to be..."

As he spoke, Wolf Fire stopped.

"It's still too early; let's just stick with this arrangement for now."

"As for your food, a responsible beastman will come tomorrow."

Yu Shan observed how skillfully they ate fish and knew they usually ate quite a lot. Thinking of the Wolf beastmen catching fish, he asked, "Do you need us to help with hunting?"

Wolf Fire: "No need."

Since he said so, Yu Shan didn't ask further.

"There's not much else. Find a place to sleep for now. You'll be here for a long time, so you can build nests or sleep on the ground, but don't leave this area."

Yu Shan nodded and immediately made arrangements.

The Wolf beastmen, relying on their thick fur, lay on the ground and closed their eyes for a nap.

That night, no one dared to sleep too soundly.

Neither side was familiar with the other, so they couldn't let their guard down.

*

The next day.

The mist was heavy, and a light rain began to fall in the early morning, blurring the scenery around Wolf Mountain.

Wolf An and a few other beastmen were in the field next to the tail grass, wearing straw hats and bending over to collect some herbs that had already grown.

Wolf Fire and the others didn't return last night, so the matter of the Black Feather beastmen helping them with work should be settled.

The beastmen hurried to finish breakfast and then counted the supplies to be taken out: animal skins, pottery jars, pottery pots, salt, stone sickles, and two fishing nets...

They were originally going to bring fish cages, but Wolf Yu stopped them.

"We are only responsible for the beastmen's food over there; we can weave fish cages ourselves. We've already brought two fishing nets, that's enough." The tribe only had one left.

Wolf An helped him pack the herbs: "That works. You and Wolf Hong look after each other. If you're too busy, ask Wolf Fire and the others for beastmen."

Wolf Hong was the sub-beastman going with Wolf Yu this time. He was also a middle-aged beastman who usually worked with Wolf An in the kitchen; both were experienced hands.

After giving clear instructions, the hunting team pulled all the carts the tribe had made—ten in total—and set off to the south with the gathering team and the wolf cubs.

The gathering team and the third hunting team with the wolf cubs would not go near the Great Marsh. Only the first hunting team would go to deliver supplies, and they wouldn't stay long after, as they were responsible for patrolling to the west.

Once the beastmen left, the tribe was empty again.

They couldn't slack off recently, so Wolf Mo's team still didn't rush to fire pottery but was responsible for the safety of Wolf Mountain.

Wolf Mu's team was fully focused on following Wolf Qi to study the spinning wheel and loom.

The field where too much fertilizer had been spread yesterday had been partially cleared. Lin Qiu went for a walk, fed the red birds, and hurried to the Priest's cave.

If he went late, the old priest would nag again.

The Great Marsh.

When the first hunting team arrived, the Black Feather tribe's beastmen were building nests.

It was raining today, and the beastmen had been lying on the ground and were woken up by the rain in the middle of the night.

When they got up in the morning, Wolf Fire thought that there was no shelter from the wind and rain here, so he simply called the Black Feather beastmen to build a few sheds first.

The Black Feather beastmen didn't say much and just buried themselves in the work.

When the first hunting team arrived, the beastmen had just raised the foundation, set up the pillars, and were building the frame.

Wolf Fire heard the movement in the woods, wiped his wet face, and said, "You!" Then, looking back and seeing Wolf Yu coming, his eyes shot out a strong light.

"Yu! We're hungry!"

Wolf Yu: "Wait."

As soon as the two sub-beastmen arrived, they immediately started cooking.

Seeing them building the sheds, they casually said, "Might as well build a stove under the shed like in the tribe, otherwise it won't be easy to cook when it rains later."

Wolf Fire: "Can do."

It was just building a stove; with dozens of beastmen, couldn't they finish it in a day?

The Black Feather beastmen saw another batch of Wolf beastmen arrive and became even more silent and vigilant.

Wolf You didn't stay long, dropped off the supplies and carts, and said, "We're going hunting."

"Good," Wolf Fire replied.

Wolf You led the beastmen to run along the Great Marsh to the east and disappeared in a few moments.

Wolf Yu and Wolf Hong looked around the area, pointed at two beastmen, and went to catch fish first.

The Black Feather beastmen looked at the wooden things parked on the side, then at the things in the two sub-beastmen's hands, and felt a shock in their hearts.

Could it be that the priest of their tribe could also communicate with the Beast God?

Otherwise, how could they come up with these strange and curious things?

The Wolf beastmen didn't care what they thought and were in a hurry to get the sheds built first.

There were three sheds in total: one had a stove built underneath, and the other two were for the Wolf beastmen and the Black Feather beastmen to rest in, respectively.

After the sheds were built, the beastmen had to officially start working.

Harvesting wild grass and hemp grass was fine; the Black Feather beastmen wielded the stone sickles, mastered the strength, and quickly got the hang of it.

But when the ten beastmen led by Yu Shan landed on a vast expanse of white bird droppings, their eyes were full of confusion and a trace of anger.

Wolf Fire's gaze was cold: "Don't look at me with that expression; our Wolf tribe is not a tribe that bullies beastmen on purpose."

He plunged a bone shovel into the bird droppings, wrinkled his nose, pulled up the animal skin wrapped around his neck, and covered his mouth and nose.

This thing was something Qiu had come up with.

It was all because the Wolf beastmen's sense of smell was too sensitive, and standing on this was uncomfortable.

"Dig!"

The Wolf beastmen started working silently, inserting the bone shovel, stepping on it, and pressing down, throwing a full shovel of bird droppings onto the cart.

"You are too weak now. We originally intended to let you fly and transport it to where we are stationed. Now it seems you can only be responsible for digging and using the carts to transport this first part, and we will take it back to Wolf Mountain later. Once you've fattened up, you can use your wings to transport it."

The Black Feather beastmen's faces were colorful.

What they said was so harsh!

What did he mean by "once they've fattened up"?

Was it that easy to get fat now?

What did he mean by "use your wings to transport it"?

Did they think their wings were that easy to use?

Wolf Fire put his hands on his hips: "Alright, how long are you going to stare at me? Get to work."

Yu Shan: "Let's work."

The Black Feather beastmen muttered to themselves: "Really unrefined."

Cutting grass was one thing, but a perfectly good Wolf tribe was actually digging for bird droppings and wanted to transport them back to Wolf Mountain; they weren't even ashamed of how dirty it was.

Not knowing what kind of habits this tribe had, the Black Feather beastmen listened to Yu Shan's words, their hearts sank, and they tensed up, starting to learn how to work like the Wolf beastmen.
chapters.title: 第68章
chapters.source_text:
烤鱼很快，不多时，黑羽兽人一个分得巴掌大一块鱼肉。
肚子里总算有东西，缓了过来。
狼兽人烤得手酸，看黑羽兽人吃过一轮，道：“队长，我们能吃了吗？”
狼火：“吃。”
狼兽人抱着手上恰好烤好的，直接往嘴里塞。
负责捞鱼杀鱼的兽人一看，急忙跑回来，逮住兽人头发，从兽人口中抢下来一半。
一天只早上吃了一顿，上午跑到西边，下午又跑到南边，这会儿都快傍晚了，谁不饿！
狼兽人互相抢着吃。
黑羽兽人珍惜吃完最后一丝鱼肉，舔着舌头，只偷偷看着。
“阿山。”
兽人围过来，还想吃。
羽山道：“这是他们的领地。”
即便大泽里鱼不少，他们也不能抓。
大家只能这样看着，看狼兽人把鱼抢完。好在他们吃得快，也就几口的事儿，他们不用跟着馋。
好歹垫了个肚子，狼兽人理智回归，也注意到对面那群没吃饱的兽人。
狼火想了想，道：“打个商量。”
“现在还没开始干活儿，所以这一顿你们抓鱼，我们烤鱼，怎么样？”
羽山一点不带犹豫的，“可以。”
狼火：“那赶紧，能抓多少是多少。”
羽山当即想点几个兽人出来。但除了几个飞得虚脱的，还能飞的全站了起来。
羽山看着，“去吧。”
早点抓回来，早点吃饱。
只见十来个黑羽兽人翅膀一张，直线飞往大泽的湖水中。
湖中的鱼从没大规模捕捞过，黑羽兽人爪子锋利，速度又快，几乎锁定了目标扑下去。
弯钩似的爪子刺破鱼身，铁钳一般，没一条鱼逃脱得了。
狼兽人们在岸上看着湖中时不时冒出的水花，道：“还是有翅膀方便。”
狼火：“我们的渔网不方便？”
兽人：“我们的渔网最好用！”
他们一次才能抓一条起来，哪有他们的渔网好。
兽人们抓鱼，烤鱼，流水线一样一直忙到天彻底黑下来。
狼兽人跟黑羽兽人面前，一个兽人两条鱼。
狼兽人还好，啃完几口，互相探讨着今日这鱼肉差了什么调料，跟林楸烤的味道又差在什么地方。
再看几米相隔的对面，黑羽兽人吃得头也不抬。
直到两条鱼吃完，肚子饱了，黑羽兽人往地上一摊，双目发直地看着满是星辰的天空。
兽人双手搭在微微鼓起的肚皮上，愣神良久。
好舒服啊……
原来吃饱了是这个感觉……
部落的兽人多，他们抓猎物很少够吃。即便抓鱼，也费时费力，烤出来的鱼还不好吃。
一顿饱饭，让黑羽兽人放下了对狼兽人承诺的怀疑。
不过还是在人家部落，不能放松太久，兽人们爬坐起来，又紧紧挨在一起。
吃饱了，就该商量正事了。
明天应该会有兽人从狼山过来，干活用到的工具都会送来。狼火便开始跟黑羽兽人说明天的安排。
两方兽人对坐，旁边就是割了一大片蛮草的地方。
中间篝火燃烧，兽人们目光炯炯，都打起精神，没一个像刚刚吃鱼那样放松。
一个是领地上出现了别的部落的兽人，一个是寄人篱下的兽人，两方都防备着。
狼火毛发在火光下愈发的红，他道：“明天，你们的兽人需要分三队，一队跟着我们去大泽南边挖鸟粪，一部分留在这边收割蛮草，一队割麻草。狼兽人也会分队带着你们。”
羽山点头，拢在身前的翅膀被映得发亮。
“从这边去大泽，我们要跑三天，带上车跑四天。我们先带你们过去看看，以后就你们自己运送。蛮草就是这一片……”狼火随意一指，黑羽兽人都注意到这一片被收割过的草。
他们在狼部落没注意到这个草，不知道他们割来做什么。
“麻草的话，更南边跟北边都有，长得比较分散，要四处走着收割。两种草割下来后，需要浸泡在水里，之后需要……”
说着，狼火止住。
“还早得很，暂且就这个安排。”
“至于你们的食物，明天会有负责的兽人过来。”
羽山观察他们吃鱼的熟练，知道他们平时定吃得不少。想到狼兽人抓鱼，他问：“需要我们跟着捕猎吗？”
狼火：“不用。”
既然他都这么说了，羽山就不多问。
“没多少事儿，先自己找地方睡觉吧。你们要在这边挺久，搭窝也好，睡地上也好都行，但不要离开这片区域。”
羽山点头，立即安排。
狼兽人仗着毛厚，往地上一趴，闭眼打盹。
这一晚谁都不敢睡太熟。
两边都不熟，不敢放心。

翌日。
雾霭沉沉，凌晨时下起了小雨，狼山周围的景色模糊一片。
狼安几个兽人在尾巴草旁边的地里，戴着草帽，躬身采集些已经长出来的香草。
昨晚狼火他们没回来，黑羽兽人帮他们干活的事儿应该就成了。
兽人们赶着吃完早饭，随后清点要带出去的物资，有兽皮、陶罐、陶锅、盐、石镰，两张渔网……
本来还要带鱼笼的，叫狼雨叫住。
“我们去那边只负责兽人们的食物，鱼笼可以自己编。已经带了两张渔网了，够了。”部落才留下一张呢。
狼安将香草给他装上，“也行，你跟狼虹互相照应着，忙不过来找狼火他们要兽人。”
狼虹是这次跟狼雨一起去的亚兽人，也是中年兽人，平时跟着狼安一起忙活做饭，都是熟手。
交代清楚，由狩猎队拉着部落做好的全部板车，拢共十辆，加上采集队跟小狼们一起，出发往南边去。
采集队跟狩猎三队带着小狼，不会靠近大泽。只狩猎一队过去送物资，送完也不多停留，负责往西边巡逻。
兽人一走，部落又空了。
最近松懈不得，狼莫小队依旧不急着烧陶，而是负责狼山安全。
狼木小队则全力跟着狼起研究纺车跟织机。
昨天那块撒肥撒多了地里，肥已经清理了些，林楸去转了一圈，又喂了红鸟，赶紧去祭司山洞。
去得晚了，老祭司又要啰嗦。
大泽。
狩猎一队到的时候，黑羽部落的兽人正在搭窝。
今天下着雨，兽人们躺在地上，半夜就被雨淋醒了。
早上起来，狼火想着这边没有遮风避雨的地方，干脆先叫上黑羽兽人一起，先搭几个棚子出来。
黑羽兽人们不多说，只埋头做。
狩猎一队一到，兽人们正巧加高了地基，立好柱子，正在搭架子。
狼火听到林子立的动静，擦了把湿润的脸，道：“游！”又往后，看到过来的狼雨，眼睛迸射出强烈的光芒。
“雨！我们饿！”
狼雨：“等着。”
两个亚兽人一到，立马开始做饭。
见他们搭棚子，顺嘴说：“干脆也像部落那样，棚子底下弄个灶台出来，不然之后下雨不好做饭。”
狼火：“可以。”
不就是搭个灶的事儿，几十个兽人，一天还弄不出来？
黑羽兽人看到又一批狼兽人来，更加沉默警惕着。
狼游不多留，放下物资跟板车，就道：“我们捕猎去了。”
“好。”狼火应到。
狼游带领兽人沿着大泽往东边跑，几下消失。
狼雨跟狼虹往附近转了转，点了两个兽人，先去捕鱼。
黑羽兽人看着那停在一旁的木头家伙，再看两亚兽人手上的东西，心中受到了冲击。
难不成，他们部落的祭司也能沟通兽神？
这些稀奇古怪的东西，不然怎么想出来的？
狼兽人不管他们怎么想，急着赶着先将棚子搭好。
一共三个棚子，一个底下搭灶台，另两个分别是狼兽人跟黑羽兽人休息的地方。
棚子搭完，兽人们就该正式干活儿了。
收割蛮草跟麻草还行，黑羽兽人挥舞着石镰，掌握了力道，很快就上手了。
但当以羽山为首的十个兽人落在白茫茫的一片鸟粪上时，目光尽是迷茫，还有一丝丝怒气。
狼火目色冷冽，“别用那个眼神看着我，我们狼部落不是故意欺负兽人的部落。”
他一骨铲扎在鸟粪上，鼻子皱了皱，将脖子上围着的兽皮拉高，捂住口鼻。
这东西是楸弄出来的。
全赖狼兽人嗅觉太敏感，站在这上面难受。
“挖！”
狼兽人闷头开始搞，骨铲往里面一插，脚下一踩，再一压，满满当当一铲子鸟粪甩在板车上。
“你们现在太弱，我们本来打算让你们飞着运送到我们驻扎的那边。现在看来只能你们负责挖跟用板车运送前面这一段，后头我们再弄回狼山。等你们吃胖了，再用翅膀运。”
黑羽兽人面上五颜六色的。
这说的话怎么这么刺耳呢！
什么叫等他们长胖了？
现在有那么容易长胖吗？
什么叫再用翅膀运？
当他们翅膀那么好用？
狼火叉腰，“行了，跟我干瞪眼要等到什么时候，干活儿。”
羽山：“干吧。”
黑羽兽人心里嘀咕：“真是不讲究。”
割草也就算了，好好的一个狼部落还指着鸟粪挖，还要运回狼山去，也不嫌埋汰。
不知道这个部落到底有什么癖好，黑羽兽人们听了羽山的话，心沉了沉，绷着面儿开始学着狼兽人干活儿。

远处的山崖上，一群像雪白似球的白雀兽人全蹲在一个枝头上，远远地看着这边。
他们的爪子抓紧了树枝，黑色的豆豆眼里对远方的黑羽兽人有些忌惮。
“十三白，要不要回去告诉族长啊？”
狼兽人过来也就罢了，他们打了招呼的，现在怎么黑羽兽人也过来了。
他们那么大个羽族，一个翅就能将他们掀翻，要是部落被盯上了，跑都跑不掉。
雀十三白：“看着不像……”
“什么不像？”
雀十三白的小爪子紧了紧树枝，身子往前探，似乎离近这么点距离就能看得更清楚似的。
“黑羽兽人，好像在听狼兽人的话。”
一队雪白的，宛如放了膨大剂的毛绒绒白却立马转头，脑袋向着一个方向，与雀十三白一模一样探身出去。
“怎么可能？黑羽兽人跟狼兽人不是不对付吗？”
“你从哪儿听来的？”
“没有啊，大部落之间不都是这样的。”
“没准儿黑羽兽人被狼兽人抓来的。”
“才不是，哪个部落会这么温柔对待奴隶。”
白雀兽人叽叽喳喳，说个半天，没一个敢再飞得近一些查探。
雀十三白黑豆眼紧盯前方，回正了身体，曲腿一缩，羽毛遮住爪子，活脱脱一个长在树上的猴头菇。
“这样，十九白带二十还有二十五回去跟族长说，其他的都守在这里。”
只要他们不往这边靠近，一切就安全。
他们那点地盘儿，狼兽人还看不进眼里。
蹲在树枝最尖上的雀十九白慢慢往里侧挪了挪，小声道：“为什么是我？”
雀十三白睨他一眼，“你最胖。”
“我不胖。”雀十九白小小声辩驳。
其他白雀兽人掉头，又叽叽喳喳安抚两个就要吵起来的兽人。
“你别攻击他，十九还小，飞不动很正常。”
“就是就是，他也不胖，就是羽毛蓬松，看着大只一点而已。”
另一边，一群长得一样的白雀又对着雀十九白道：“十三是担心你，你飞得慢一点，万一这边真打起来，你落到最后怎么办？”
“对对对，你需要多飞一飞。”
雀十九白悄悄看了一眼雀十三白，立马收回，抻了抻翅膀，小声道：“那好吧。”
“二十，二十五，我们走。”
白雀展翅一扑腾，他们站着的树枝甚至往下弯了弯。
白雀兽人们忍不住抓紧了树枝。
待到雀十九白展翅一扑腾，被压弯的树枝尖尖又回弹几下，晃晃悠悠。
直到他飞远了，其他白雀立刻又叽叽喳喳起来。
“十三白说得没错，十九白真的胖了点。”
“他喜欢吃，又不喜欢动，以后多叫他飞一飞就好了。”
“你说得对。”白雀小小的豆豆眼里，满是认真。
几天时间，大泽这边的事情步入正轨，黑羽兽人们体会到了干活儿干得手软脚软，但食物管够的美好生活。
为了一天两顿的饱饭，黑羽兽人一点怨言都没有。
他们甚至觉得，狼兽人交给他们的事情都太轻松了。不外乎割草，挖粪，要不是他们不允许部落里太多外族，他们甚至都想再推荐兽人。
当再一次看见狼雨准备食物，黑羽兽人聚精会神，悄悄看着。
只见狼雨抓着渔网往湖里一甩，拉起来就是好几条大鱼。
他把大鱼随手扔进那鲜少见到的陶罐里，运回来。再在那石头混合泥搭建的叫灶台的地方，用陶锅烹饪。
驻扎的地方，炊烟升起。
看着那大陶锅里奶白的鱼汤滚滚，兽人熟练加入的鲜嫩水菜。
另一口陶锅，兽人把切片的据说叫呛草的菜也扔进去翻炒，香味儿奇妙不已。
黑羽兽人不停吸气，嗅着味道，手上更是卖力。
狼部落的日子，可真好啊。
黑羽兽人们想着自家部落的日子，心中一刺，像被一盆冰水都头扑来，即将吃到食物的兴奋散了个干干净净。
他们一群兽人倒是在人家部落里好吃好喝，部落也不知道怎么样了……

狼山。
被关了六天的狼顺解禁，出来的第一件事，就是直奔陶锅边，像饿了大半年的流浪兽人，巴巴地看着锅里的肉汤。
狼安见狼顺狼毛凌乱，黯淡无光，好不容易养起来的身体又给饿瘦了。他叹了口气，先给他盛了点肉汤吃。
看他一口闷下去，烫得吐舌头都舍不得吐出来，道：“你慢点吃，嘴巴烫伤了反倒再吃不到其他的。”
狼顺感觉到肚子里的暖意，眼眶一下红了，“安，你不知道，关在山洞里我都饿惨了。”
他吃得毛耳朵不停地动，脑袋都没抬过。
才关了几天，肋骨又清晰可见。
狼安皱了皱眉，忍着没说。看狼岩还没出发，先找了过去。
“王。”
狼岩：“有什么事？”
“小狼们今天是不是也可以放出来了？”
狼岩：“再……”
“王。”狼安忍不住打断他，想起狼顺那样子，有些不忍心道，“王，惩罚兽人的方式是不是换一下比较好了。”
“你看看狼顺，这好不容易养出来的肉，关几天又瘦下来，不说白费了那些吃下去的食物，对兽人身体也不好……”
狼岩看向远处棚子，狼顺正忙着埋头苦吃，见不到他的身影。
“我想想。”
“诶！好好想，做错了事该受惩罚，该让他们长记性，但就怕饿出毛病。”
狼岩点头。
狼安急匆匆又回到灶前，看狼顺吃完了，又爪子推了推碗看来。
狼安顺手想再添点儿，但忽然想起林楸的话，道：“歇会儿再吃，你饿了几天，一下子不能吃太多。”
狼顺耳朵一耷，趴在地上。
狼安看他狼毛打结，又沾了不少灰尘，脏兮兮的，跟流浪兽人似的。
他忍不住道：“你去狼起那里要一把梳子，叫兽人把毛梳一下。”
狼顺抬头，圆溜溜的狼眼中尽迷茫。
他被关在山洞几天没活动过，本该换掉的狼毛一缕一缕打结，整个身体显得分外累赘，一副蠢兮兮的样子。
“梳子是个什么东西？”
他不就被关了几天，怎么部落里又出现新东西了？
＊
“哎！舒服，再用点力。”
林楸下午从祭司山洞出来，就看见狼顺趴在山脚下，旁边狼莫拿着木梳，两手飞动，往他身上刮。
他们边上的藤筐里，梳下来的毛积攒在一起，有些都结成块儿了。
狼莫火都梳出来了，梳子一卡，不管三七二十一，使劲儿往下扒拉。
林楸看着狼顺头皮都给扯平了，圆眼成了吊梢眼，还龇牙咧嘴叫着舒服。
怕不是脑子关出了问题。
狼莫抬头看了眼，见是林楸，道：“楸，你去后山说一声，小狼可以放出来了。”
林楸点头，“好。”
狼顺扬了扬尾巴，叫狼莫一脚踩住，“你不要动！”
狼顺：“不动不动。”
小狼关在一起，十几个兽人一个山洞，洞口一打开，里面顿时传出来一股臭烘烘的味道。
守着洞口的兽人捂住鼻子，撒腿儿就跑。
林楸屏息，对上小狼迷茫的眼神，淡声道：“可以出来了。”
“嗷呜……”小狼声音低低的，充满了委屈。
看见他们挨挨蹭蹭从里面出来，要蹭过来，林楸拔腿就走。
“楸……”
小狼似泣非泣，凄婉哀怨。
林楸脚步一顿，走得更快。
小狼嗷的一声从地上爬起来，两腿打颤，急匆匆地跟上林楸。
“楸！你也不爱我们了吗？”
林楸直接跑了。
狼安几个在棚子底下织渔网，见状还以为出什么事了，警惕站起，一看原来是小狼出来了。
狼安摸了摸陶锅外面，还是温热的。
狼金几个见追不到林楸，看着狼安对他们招手，想起腹中饥饿，饿狼化身，立刻涌入棚子。
狼安正打算将小狼的碗拿过来，忽然闻到一股酸臭味。
就那么停顿的一瞬，小狼扑过来，坐在地上，抱着他腿就开始嚎。
“呜呜呜……安叔，你都不心疼我们，我们被关了这么久，你不给我们送吃的就算了，连看都不来看我们一下呜呜呜……安叔，你好狠的心啊。”
狼安看着小狼身上比狼顺还要脏的狼毛，试图抽了抽腿。
看着小狼鼻涕眼泪往身上糊，可把他恶心的，揪住小狼耳朵立马抽出自己脚，飞快远离。
“臭死了！”
“锅里有食物，洗干净爪子才能碰。”
小狼愣住，意识到遭了嫌弃，憋着嘴，张嘴就嚎。
狼安冷静地继续补刀：“几天没刷牙了，牙都黄了。”
小狼尴尬，小狼住嘴。
哼哼唧唧，扭扭捏捏的，挪着屁股往小溪边狂奔。
他们干干净净的小狼怎么会臭呢？！
一定是狼安叔很久没见他们，一时间不习惯他们的气味。
狼金脑袋往溪水里一扎，飞快搓脸。
狼冰默默拿了牙粉牙刷，仔仔细细给自己嘴巴洗干净。
阳光透过小狼耳朵，红得像碾碎的花汁。
忍着肚子饿，小狼飞快将自己收拾妥当，再回来吃东西。囫囵吃完肉汤，再往棚子底下一倒，互相商量着待会儿去河里洗澡。
要好好搓，狠狠搓，洗得香香白白的。
躺了会儿，小狼不知不觉熟睡过去。
狼安放下渔网，从山洞里出来。先看了看小狼的情况，确认没什么问题，才轻轻绕开他们，去地里看了看。
王说之后负责记录地里作物的情况交给狼溶。
小狼现在在补觉，他这几天先给盯着，等他睡好了起来再交接也不晚。
地里的尾巴草除掉多余的肥料，又灌了两次水，现在也恢复正常了。
大多都抽穗成功，迎风招展着，一片葱郁。
再有一个月，差不多就到雨季，到时候又热又闷。
该准备的，全都得准备起来了。
chapters.translated_text:
On a cliff in the distance, a group of white sparrow beastmen, looking like fluffy white snowballs, were all crouching on a branch, watching this side from afar.

Their claws gripped the branches tightly, and their black, bean-like eyes held a hint of wariness toward the black-feathered beastmen in the distance.

"Thirteen-White, should we go back and tell the tribe leader?"

It would be one thing if it were just the wolf beastmen—they had greeted them, after all—but why were the black-feathered beastmen here now?

They were such a large avian tribe; a single flap of their wings could knock them over. If their tribe were targeted, they wouldn't even be able to run away.

Que Thirteen-White said, "It doesn't look like it..."

"What doesn't look like it?"

Que Thirteen-White's small claws tightened on the branch, and he leaned forward, as if being a little closer would let him see more clearly.

"The black-feathered beastmen seem to be listening to the wolf beastmen."

A row of snow-white, fluffy birds that looked like they had been puffed up with leavening agent immediately turned their heads in the same direction, leaning forward exactly like Que Thirteen-White.

"How is that possible? Aren't the black-feathered beastmen and the wolf beastmen at odds with each other?"

"Where did you hear that?"

"I didn't, but isn't that how it is between large tribes?"

"Maybe the black-feathered beastmen were captured by the wolf beastmen."

"That's not it. Which tribe would treat slaves so gently?"

The white sparrow beastmen chattered away for a long time, but none dared to fly any closer to investigate.

Que Thirteen-White kept his black bean-eyes fixed on the front, straightened his body, tucked his legs in, and covered his claws with his feathers, looking exactly like a monkey head mushroom growing on a tree.

"Like this: Nineteen-White, take Twenty and Twenty-five back to tell the tribe leader. The rest of you stay here and keep watch."

As long as they don't come closer to this side, everything will be safe.

The wolf beastmen wouldn't even bother looking at their tiny patch of territory.

Que Nineteen-White, who was crouching at the very tip of the branch, shifted slowly inward and whispered, "Why me?"

Que Thirteen-White glanced at him, "You're the fattest."

"I'm not fat," Que Nineteen-White whispered in protest.

The other white sparrow beastmen turned their heads and chattered to soothe the two who were about to argue.

"Don't attack him; Nineteen is still young, it's normal that he can't fly well."

"That's right, that's right. He's not fat, his feathers are just fluffy, making him look a bit bigger."

On the other side, a group of identical white sparrows said to Que Nineteen-White, "Thirteen is worried about you. You fly slowly; what if a fight really breaks out here and you're the one left behind?"

"Yes, yes, you need to fly more."

Que Nineteen-White secretly glanced at Que Thirteen-White, immediately looked away, stretched his wings, and whispered, "Alright then."

"Twenty, Twenty-five, let's go."

The white sparrows flapped their wings, and the branch they were standing on even bent downward.

The white sparrow beastmen couldn't help but grip the branches tightly.

When Que Nineteen-White flapped his wings to take off, the bent branch tip bounced back a few times, swaying unsteadily.

Once he had flown far away, the other white sparrows immediately began chattering again.

"Thirteen-White was right, Nineteen-White really has gotten a bit fat."

"He likes to eat and doesn't like to move. We'll just have to make him fly more often in the future."

"You're right." The white sparrows' tiny bean-eyes were full of seriousness.

In a few days, things at Daze had gotten on the right track, and the black-feathered beastmen experienced the wonderful life of having their hands and feet go soft from working, but having enough food to eat.

For the sake of two full meals a day, the black-feathered beastmen had no complaints at all.

They even felt that the tasks the wolf beastmen gave them were too easy. It was nothing more than cutting grass and digging up manure; if it weren't for the fact that they didn't allow too many outsiders in the tribe, they would have even wanted to recommend more beastmen.

When they saw Lang Yu preparing food again, the black-feathered beastmen gathered their focus and watched quietly.

They saw Lang Yu swing a fishing net into the lake and pull up several large fish.

He tossed the large fish into the rarely seen pottery jars and transported them back. Then, at the place built of stone and mud called a stove, he cooked them in a pottery pot.

Smoke rose from the campsite.

Watching the milky white fish soup rolling in the large pottery pot, the beastman skillfully added fresh, tender aquatic greens.

In another pottery pot, the beastman threw in sliced greens—said to be called "pungent grass"—and stir-fried them; the fragrance was wonderfully strange.

The black-feathered beastmen kept inhaling, sniffing the aroma, and worked even harder with their hands.

Life in the Wolf Tribe is truly good.

The black-feathered beastmen thought about life in their own tribe, and a sting in their hearts felt like a basin of ice water poured over their heads, scattering their excitement about eating food completely.

They were living well and eating well in someone else's tribe, but they didn't know how their own tribe was doing...

*

Wolf Mountain.

Lang Shun, who had been locked up for six days, was released. The first thing he did upon coming out was to head straight for the pottery pot, looking at the meat soup like a stray beastman who had been starving for half a year.

Seeing Lang Shun's wolf fur messy and dull, and that he had grown thin again after finally building up his body, Lang An sighed and served him some meat soup first.

Watching him gulp it down, too reluctant to even stick out his tongue despite the heat, Lang An said, "Eat slowly. If you burn your mouth, you won't be able to eat anything else."

Feeling the warmth in his stomach, Lang Shun's eyes turned red, "An, you don't know, I was starving in that cave."

He ate with his furry ears twitching constantly, never once lifting his head.

He had only been locked up for a few days, and his ribs were clearly visible again.

Lang An frowned, holding back his words. Seeing that Lang Yan hadn't left yet, he went to find him first.

"King."

Lang Yan: "What is it?"

"Can the little wolves be let out today?"

Lang Yan: "Wait..."

"King," Lang An couldn't help but interrupt him. Thinking of Lang Shun's state, he said with some reluctance, "King, perhaps we should change the way we punish the beastmen."

"Look at Lang Shun. The weight he finally managed to put on was lost after being locked up for a few days. Not to mention the wasted food, it's not good for the beastmen's health..."

Lang Yan looked toward the shed in the distance, where Lang Shun was busy burying his head in his food, his figure obscured.

"I'll think about it."

"Yes! Please think it over. They should be punished for doing wrong, and they should learn their lesson, but I'm afraid they'll get sick from hunger."

Lang Yan nodded.

Lang An hurried back to the stove, and seeing Lang Shun had finished eating, he saw him pushing the bowl over with his paw.

Lang An reached out to add more, but suddenly remembered Lin Qiu's words and said, "Rest for a while before eating more. You've been hungry for days; you can't eat too much at once."

Lang Shun's ears drooped, and he lay on the ground.

Lang An saw his wolf fur was matted and covered in dust, dirty and looking like a stray beastman.

He couldn't help but say, "Go to Lang Qi and ask for a comb, have a beastman brush your fur."

Lang Shun looked up, his round wolf eyes filled with confusion.

He hadn't moved for days while locked in the cave, and the fur that should have been shed was matted in clumps, making his whole body look cumbersome and foolish.

"What is a comb?"

He had only been locked up for a few days; how did a new thing appear in the tribe?

*

"Ah! That feels good, use a bit more force."

When Lin Qiu came out of the priest's cave in the afternoon, he saw Lang Shun lying at the foot of the mountain, with Lang Mo next to him holding a wooden comb, his hands moving rapidly as he scraped at him.

In the rattan basket beside them, the brushed-off fur was piled up, some of it already matted into clumps.

Lang Mo was brushing so hard he was getting hot; when the comb got stuck, he didn't care about anything and just pulled hard.

Lin Qiu watched as Lang Shun's scalp was pulled taut, his round eyes turning into slanted ones, yet he was still baring his teeth and calling out that it felt good.

He probably had his brain damaged from being locked up.

Lang Mo looked up, and seeing it was Lin Qiu, said, "Qiu, go to the back mountain and say that the little wolves can be let out."

Lin Qiu nodded, "Okay."

Lang Shun flicked his tail, and Lang Mo stepped on it, "Don't move!"

Lang Shun: "Not moving, not moving."

The little wolves were locked together, over a dozen beastmen in one cave. As soon as the cave entrance opened, a foul smell immediately wafted out.

The beastman guarding the entrance covered his nose and ran away.

Lin Qiu held his breath, met the little wolves' confused gazes, and said calmly, "You can come out."

"Awoo..." The little wolves' voices were low, filled with grievance.

Seeing them rubbing against each other as they came out, wanting to rub against him, Lin Qiu turned and walked away.

"Qiu..."

The little wolves sounded as if they were crying, mournful and plaintive.

Lin Qiu paused for a moment, then walked even faster.

The little wolves scrambled up from the ground with a howl, their legs trembling, and hurried to follow Lin Qiu.

"Qiu! Do you not love us anymore?"

Lin Qiu just ran off.

Lang An and the others were weaving fishing nets under the shed. Seeing this, they thought something had happened and stood up vigilantly, only to see it was just the little wolves coming out.

Lang An touched the outside of the pottery pot; it was still warm.

When Lang Jin and the others saw they couldn't catch up to Lin Qiu, they saw Lang An waving at them. Remembering their hunger, they turned into starving wolves and immediately swarmed into the shed.

Lang An was just about to bring over the little wolves' bowls when he suddenly smelled a sour, foul odor.

In that split second of hesitation, the little wolves pounced over, sat on the ground, and started howling while hugging his legs.

"Wuwuwu... Uncle An, you don't care about us. We were locked up for so long, and you didn't send us food, let alone come to see us, wuwuwu... Uncle An, you have such a cruel heart."

Lang An looked at the wolf fur on the little wolves, which was even dirtier than Lang Shun's, and tried to pull his leg away.

Seeing the little wolves smearing snot and tears onto him, he was disgusted. He grabbed a little wolf by the ear, immediately pulled his foot free, and moved away quickly.

"You stink!"

"There's food in the pot; you can only touch it after washing your paws."

The little wolves froze, realizing they were being shunned, and started howling with their mouths pursed.

Lang An calmly delivered the final blow: "How many days has it been since you brushed your teeth? Your teeth are all yellow."

The little wolves were embarrassed and shut their mouths.

Whimpering and fidgeting, they moved their butts and sprinted toward the stream.

How could their clean little wolf bodies stink?!

It must be that Uncle Lang An hadn't seen them for a long time and wasn't used to their scent.

Lang Jin plunged his head into the stream and scrubbed his face rapidly.

Lang Bing silently took the tooth powder and toothbrush and carefully cleaned his mouth.

Sunlight shone through the little wolves' ears, making them as red as crushed flower juice.

Enduring their hunger, the little wolves quickly cleaned themselves up and came back to eat. After gulping down the meat soup, they collapsed under the shed, discussing among themselves about going to the river to bathe later.

They would scrub well, scrub hard, and get themselves smelling good and white.

After lying there for a while, the little wolves fell into a deep sleep without realizing it.

Lang An put down the fishing net and came out of the cave. He checked on the little wolves first, confirmed there were no problems, and then gently bypassed them to check on the fields.

The King said that the responsibility for recording the situation of the crops in the fields would be handed over to Lang Rong.

The little wolves were catching up on sleep now, so he would keep an eye on things for these few days; it wouldn't be too late to hand it over after they woke up.

The tail-grass in the fields had the excess fertilizer removed and had been watered twice, so it had returned to normal.

Most of them had successfully headed, swaying in the wind, a lush expanse of green.

In another month, it would be the rainy season, which would be hot and stuffy.

Everything that needed to be prepared had to be prepared.
chapters.title: 第69章

chapters.translated_text:
Lang Yan was one of the few beastmen in that group who maintained a human form. Beside the roaring bonfire, he stood like a silent stone monument.

Clearly possessing broad shoulders and a straight back, ignoring his somewhat thin chest, his figure could still be considered imposing, yet his soul seemed to have collapsed heavily inward.

He was weighed down by a thousand-jin burden.

Lang Yan was overly acute; Lin Qiu bit his lower lip, then lowered his gaze in silence and continued making his dinner.

"He" was a sinner of the tribe, and no one trusted him.

Even if he was willing to help a little now, he couldn't leave Langshan, leaving him helpless.

He had already revealed enough; it all depended on the attitude of the tribe's decision-makers. If there was suspicion, the day the truth came to light would be the day he either left or died.

Lin Qiu thought that day probably wasn't far off.

He didn't want to think about the future—those two words had been spoken a thousand times by his parents, making him loathe them.

Taking things as they come was his current state.

He felt this was pretty good.

Dinner was eaten late, and the beastmen were exceptionally battered today.

Fortunately, they finally managed to eat a full meal, and when they collapsed into the grass nests, they fell asleep the moment they closed their eyes.

Tonight should be a rare, good night's sleep.

Lin Qiu entered the cave trailing behind the others, and by then, the snoring inside was rising and falling in waves.

The beastmen had no leisure or entertainment time—only endless hunger and a single night of peaceful sleep after rarely being full.

Lin Qiu slowly walked past the grass nests and quietly lay down in his own nest.

Deep in the night, the wind carried moisture. Before long, a light drizzle began to fall outside.

Lin Qiu was a bit cold, and half-asleep, he heard a rustling movement.

It was very close to him.

A soft sensation brushed against his hand, and Lin Qiu suddenly opened his eyes.

The last trace of light from the firepit reflected upon the cub that had crawled to the edge of his grass nest.

Pure white fur, and still those wet, watery eyes.

Lin Qiu instantly pulled back his hand, and the cub's raised paw stepped on empty air, causing it to tumble forward, hit its head first, and roll around in the grass nest.

Lin Qiu scooted backward.

The cub whimpered, stepped unevenly into the soft, springy grass nest, and ran toward Lin Qiu again.

Sensing the gaze from behind, Lin Qiu moved his hands even further away and looked back.

Lang Yan was awake, his gaze fixed on the cub in his nest.

Lin Qiu said in a low voice, "It ran over on its own."

Lang Yan glanced at him. "Mn."

He stood up, his physique extremely tall and large, deep wolf fur covering his whole body in thick, substantial layers.

Sitting sideways in the grass nest and looking up, Lin Qiu couldn't help feeling a start of alarm.

The black wolf's paw pads made no sound on the ground as he approached, trying to pick up the cub by the scruff of its neck.

With his massive head reaching into the nest, Lin Qiu pressed his back tightly against the edge of the nest, which almost felt like he was hugging the wolf's head.

Mischievous as it was, the cub unhappily thrashed around.

Hearing its low, muffled whimper, Lin Qiu then noticed the cub quiet down.

The palm-sized cub was obediently carried in the wolf's jaws, its paws curled up and tail tucked like a ball, and was deposited deep inside the cave.

The wolf beastman guarding the cubs woke up as well, and seeing the cub brought over by Lang Yan, he couldn't help poking it on the forehead.

This wasn't the first time it had run off.

Lang Yan returned to the edge of the grass nest and saw Lin Qiu lying back down, facing the inner side of the cave with his eyes closed.

He was hugging his arms against his chest, likely from the cold.

Lang Yan sighed softly in his heart, turned back into the inner part of the cave, and came out holding an animal skin in his jaws.

Lin Qiu felt a weight on his body, the back of his hand brushing against soft fur.

Lin Qiu opened his eyes, meeting the gaze of Lang Yan who had already walked over to the neighboring grass nest. Under the gaze of those gray eyes, he gently pulled the animal skin up over his shoulders.

"Thank you," he said in a low voice.

Lang Yan closed his eyes and gave a gentle sweep of his tail.

*

The animal skin was of moderate thickness, and wrapped in it, Lin Qiu slept straight until dawn.

Listening to the whimpering of the cubs deep inside the cave, he sat up, clutching the animal skin. His shoulder-length hair brushed against the tip of his nose, tickling him slightly. Lin Qiu smoothed it down a few times, but his palm ended up with a small tuft of black hair.

It was about a finger long, pitch black all over, and somewhat coarse.

Subconsciously, Lin Qiu looked toward the neighboring grass nest.

The cave was too dark to make out whether there was any wolf fur inside.

Today was overcast; lacking sunlight, the wind outside felt cold. Lin Qiu ate breakfast, then ran into the shaman's cave to begin his busy day.

There were always many herbs here, piled up in heaps that weren't limited to the usual dozen or so. There were many that not only Lin Qiu didn't know, but even the shaman had to carefully identify.

Not just plants, but fungi as well.

Lin Qiu watched with his own eyes as the shaman plucked a brightly red mushroom, put it in his mouth, and said, "Poisonous."

The shaman: "Mn."

He still ate it even though it was poisonous.

Discovering that the old shaman had the inclination to taste a hundred herbs, and fearing the old beastman might accidentally kill himself, Lin Qiu said, "Maybe you could raise a Zhizhi beast."

The shaman was slightly annoyed, turning his wrinkled, tree-bark-like face toward him.

Lin Qiu: "Let the wild beasts test it first. If the wild beasts don't die from the poison, then you eat it, lest you go see the Beast God all of a sudden in your old age."

The old shaman looked at the mushroom in his hand, and after a long while, put it down.

The tribe still needed him.

Lin Qiu withdrew his gaze and continued cleaning the plants.

Busy until noon, Lin Qiu began preparing his own lunch.

He didn't like eating purely meat for a meal; mixing meat with vegetables prevented it from feeling greasy.

Of the nearly five catties of meat from last night, more than four catties remained—almost only a corner had been cut off.

Lin Qiu planned to make some meatballs.

Before that, however, he first took a trip down to the stream to haul up the basket he had placed there yesterday.

A sound of splashing water rippled through the calm stream.

Looking closely, Lin Qiu saw only a few small shrimps and fish, smaller than a pinky finger. He hooked a piece of grass and shook it, tilting the basket to reveal barely a small handful.

It was enough for him to make a meatball soup base.

Resources in the stream were limited, so Lin Qiu decided not to target this small stream anymore.

Fortunately, the earth ears and wild garlic given to him by Lang Shi yesterday hadn't been used, and the remaining meat was half-fat and half-lean, which could render out some oil. Today's meal should be delicious.

When Lin Qiu sat down in front of his stove, the beastmen lying on the ground quietly turned their heads, fixing covert gazes on that side.

Seeing Lin Qiu slice the meat very thin and flip it over on a stone slab, the beastmen thought to themselves how such a small bit of meat could ever be enough to eat.

But when Lin Qiu added the wild garlic, a strong fragrance assaulted their nasal cavities, and the beastmen couldn't help swallowing their saliva, their eyes brightening and staring straight ahead.

Lin Qiu first made the pan-fried meat, then used the fat meat to render out a little oil to fry the small fish and shrimps, after which he poured everything into a stone pot to boil.

He stood up, placed half of the pan-fried meat on a leaf, and set it next to Lang Shi.

"As promised."

Putting the things down, Lin Qiu returned to the front of the stove.

To make meatballs, the meat had to be pounded to a paste.

Sounds of clattering started up again from Lin Qiu's side, but the beastmen couldn't maintain their focus; crawling at a very slow pace along the ground, they closed in on Lang Shi.

Lang Shi was still conflicted.

He should return it to Lin Qiu, but the ya-beastman didn't seem to care much about this bit of food.

On his gray-fur-covered wolf face, he frowned one moment and gritted his teeth the next.

Suddenly, his paw was poked.

Lang Shi lowered his head.

Lang Mo: "Are you eating it or not?"

If he wasn't going to eat it...

Lang Mo slowly reached his paw over, but his paw pad stung as Lang Shi bared his sharp claws.

Lang Mo sheepishly pulled it back.

Lang Shi raised his head, looked at the yearning-filled beastmen, and silently placed his two front paws on either side of the large leaf.

Just as he was about to open his mouth—

"Slurp! Slurp slurp..."

"Gulp, gulp gulp!!!"

Lang Shi closed his eyes fiercely and pulled his paws away.

"Eat."

"Awooo!" Over a dozen wolves suppressed their voices and swarmed forward, instantly submerging Lang Shi.
