Langan and the others shook their heads, their hair half-dry, and sat impatiently by the fire to roast.

Langan asked, "King, how long will this rain last?"

In the corridor, the rainwater blown in by the wind gathered into a stream, flowing toward the exit. In the distance, the curtain of rain was being blown sideways. In this weather, nothing could be done outside.

Langyan: "The priest says the first rain will last at least three days."

Three days.

Beastmen couldn't go a day without hunting and still have food, but fortunately, they had dried plenty of fish and vegetables in advance.

Langyan: "From now on, let's keep lunch simple, just enough to fill our stomachs."

The Wolf tribe wasn't a wealthy tribe; hunting was difficult during the rainy season, and since they wouldn't be doing much physically demanding work, two meals a day would actually suffice.

This thought only flashed through Langyan's mind.

The beastmen still needed to nourish their bodies; when winter arrived, that would be the truly difficult time.

Langan: "There was half a sharp-horned beast left from yesterday; we'll boil it with wild vegetables."

Langyan: "Add more water."

Langan smiled: "Alright."

The sub-beastmen returned to the wolf den to first change out of their soaked animal skins. After resting for a while, they came out to prepare lunch.

Lin Qiu watched the beastmen's hair, which was loose and draped over them. Having been caught in the rain together, theirs looked half-dry already.

Lin Qiu tried to learn from them, shaking his head, and his neck made a "crack" sound.

Lin Qiu hissed softly and silently clutched the back of his neck.

Langguo had a cub lying on him, its grape-like eyes watching him intently.

Langguo was laughing. The cub seemed not to understand why he could throw his neck out just by shaking his fur, and one of them walked out and let out an "Awo."

Lin Qiu looked over; the cub had its limbs slightly bent, shaking from its ears to its tail.

Finally, it let out another milky "Awo" and looked at Lin Qiu.

Langguo covered his mouth, laughing even louder: "Hahahaha."

Lin Qiu: "Thanks, no need to teach me."

He had tried it; this method wasn't for him. What just happened was purely a brain fart.

Lin Qiu pinched the side of his neck and gently tilted his head to ease it; fortunately, he hadn't strained a muscle.

The heavy rain slowed down after half an hour, but the intensity was still significant. The beastmen used brooms made of tree branches to sweep the rainwater that had accumulated under the shed.

On the stove, meat soup was boiling in several pots—six pots in total. One pot held the boiled water from the morning, and the other five were boiling meat soup.

There wasn't much meat, so Langan added some wild vegetables to it.

Once this was distributed, the beastmen would basically have consumed it all by the time they woke up from their afternoon nap.

The rain was still falling, and the beastmen were all huddled in the cave with nowhere to go.

Seeing Lin Qiu combing his hair with a wooden comb, they quickly took out their own wooden combs from beside their grass nests and groomed each other's fur.

Opposite Lin Qiu, the cub lay on Langguo and slowly fell into a deep sleep.

Lin Qiu hadn't seen the beastmen all huddled in the cave during the day before. He asked, "What does everyone usually do during the rainy season?"

Langguo: "Hunt, sleep."

Lin Qiu: "That's no different from usual."

Langguo touched the cub, which was getting a bit hot from the fire, and moved them behind him, lining them up from largest to smallest.

Each cub was gray and chubby, with short legs and short tails; only a few had pink paws.

He blocked the front of the cubs and said, "This is just the beginning; it will get hotter later. Everyone will switch to hunting at night, and they rarely return within a day."

The weather was too hot; for a beastman to run under the sun in their beast form was no different from squatting by a fire while wearing a fur coat.

Beastmen couldn't run for half a day at a time like before, so the hunting time would be longer.

Lin Qiu: "Are the herds of prey still the same ones?"

"There will be one more kind."

"At this time, the further south you go, the hotter it gets, so the beastmen will hunt to the north. Deep in the grasslands, there is a kind of 'Miemie' beast with snow-white fur that migrates from the foot of the snow mountains to the grasslands to breed."

"It takes a day or two to run there from Langshan; it's very, very far, and the beastmen only go there to hunt during the rainy season."

In the past, they only went there because the prey in other directions had been hunted out, and they had no choice.

This year, the north actually has less rain and is slightly less hot. Now, even if the beastmen can't return within a day, the tribe has fish as a supplement, so everyone should be very happy to go there.

Lin Qiu wanted to ask more, but someone shouted outside: "Awoooo——"

Time to eat!!!

The beastmen lying in grass nests all over the cave stood up in a flash, ears perked high, and swarmed out.

In the blink of an eye, the beastmen were all gone.

Turning back, Langguo was also rushing out, holding a pottery jar.

"Qiu! Keep an eye on the cubs!"

Lin Qiu: "...Okay."

The cubs woke up. The smaller ones rolled over, their limbs paddling in the air like little turtles, unable to get up. The older cubs had already scrambled up and were charging toward the cave entrance.

Lin Qiu blocked their path.

"Don't rush, Guo will be back soon."

Langxue was charging blindly, and seeing the hand reaching out, he subconsciously opened his claws and rushed over.

Lin Qiu caught him firmly, and when he looked up, he saw Lin Qiu's look of surprise.

Langxue said anxiously: "Qiu! Meat soup!"

Lin Qiu picked up the cub, who was five heads tall. "You turned into a human!"

"Awo?"

Langxue looked at his claws resting on Lin Qiu's shoulder; there were little dimples on the back of his hands, and his fingers were thick and short—not pretty at all.

In an instant, Lin Qiu's arms felt light, and a chubby little white wolf fell out.

He was so startled he hurriedly used both hands to protect it, almost dropping it.

He stopped the other cubs and touched the paws of the stunned Langxue. "Is anything uncomfortable?"

Langxue shook his head, a bit anxious: "Qiu! Drink soup! It'll be gone if we don't."

Lin Qiu: "It won't."

He held the cub and looked for the beastmen. Seeing Langguo come in, he immediately said, "Guo, Xue just turned into a human."

Langguo paused. He carefully avoided the cubs, his voice unable to hide his joy. "Really? I thought you'd never be able to in this lifetime! Quick, eat first, I'm going to tell the priest."

Langguo lined up the cubs' bowls on a large leaf, two spoonfuls of soup per bowl, with small pieces of meat just right for the cubs to gnaw on.

"Qiu, the King saved some food for you, go eat quickly."

Lin Qiu: "Xue turned into a human for a second and then turned back, is he okay?"

"It's fine, it's the first time, it's normal not to be able to control it."

Lin Qiu looked at the cubs on the ground burying their heads in their soup, his fingertips brushing the cub's head, a smile lifting the corners of his lips.

"Guo, call me when you go to the priest's place later."

"Mm, okay!" Langguo smiled brightly; Lin Qiu's attitude toward the cubs was very pleasing to Langguo.

It was wet outside, but the beastmen didn't care; they stood and ate while holding their bowls.

Langyan placed two bowls on the low wall, covering them with large leaves so the rain couldn't get in.

Lin Qiu's steps were light, and seeing Langyan waiting, he couldn't help but quicken his pace.

"King, Xue just turned into a human."

When he said this, the corners of his lips curled up involuntarily, his eyes bright, genuinely happy for the cub.

The ground was made of rammed earth and was slippery from the water, so Langyan reached out.

Seeing Lin Qiu take his hand, smiling brightly, Langyan's tone softened, and he said, "It should have happened long ago."
chapters.title: 第74章

chapters.source_text:
“他变人形的时间有些晚了，等会儿让祭司看看。”
林楸：“果也是这么说的。”
他自然而然靠近狼岩。
腕上的手松开，揭开陶碗上的大叶片，挡在外侧。
林楸：“我去山洞里吃。”
狼岩：“好。”
狼岩帮他拿着大叶片，林楸双手捧着碗，说了声：“等狼起他们有空，得给部落打几张桌椅，不然像这情况都没地方吃饭。”
肉汤又烫，兽人们也是皮糙肉厚，左手倒右手，都不舍得放下来。
狼岩：“先用木桩替着。”
他跟在林楸后头，注意着脚下。
今儿的肉汤清，菜放得多，汤都是绿色。上面漂浮着一点点的油腥，看着略显清淡。
知道部落情况，没兽人抱怨，只管端着碗呼噜噜吃。
这头一场雨大伙儿能休息几天，雨一停，立马得出发。
吃完饭兽人也不睡，有的纺线，有的梳毛，还有织渔网的、学织布的……趴窝里的兽人都少。
他们以前睡得够久，一下闲着，反倒不想睡。
林楸将碗放木桩，自己坐在草垫上。
对面幼崽吃得欢实，整个脑袋快陷进碗里。吧唧吧唧，看着极香，肚子不一会儿就鼓起来了。
也就几个月的时间，幼崽体型一下拉开差距。
狼雪最大，体型像两三个月的阿拉斯加幼犬，最小的幼崽要比他小一半。现在幼崽爬窝，压在他身上都有些喘不过气。
吃过饭，林楸立刻跟狼果一起，带上幼崽去祭司山洞。
狼岩则留下来，看顾其他幼崽。
祭司山洞，老兽人刚坐进窝里打算睡一会儿，两个兽人就来了。
“祭司，你看看雪，他刚刚变人形了。”狼果一手挡住幼崽胸口，一手托着屁股，闷头冲进山洞。
老祭司把要训斥的话咽下，道：“拿过来。”
幼崽被放老兽人手上。
他怕压到老兽人，那兽皮衣里露出来的手太瘦了。
狼雪奶声奶气叫：“祭司爷爷。”
老兽人抚着他脑袋，“没事，祭司爷爷看看。”
老祭司抓着小狼，先看四条腿儿，又碰着幼崽脑袋，问：“疼不疼？”
幼崽摇头，眼里迷茫。
“变人形多久？多大？”
林楸：“就最多十个呼吸，勉强大腿高，胳膊腿儿都是好的。”
老祭司：“……”
幼崽兽形没问题，人形当然也不会缺胳膊少腿儿。
他拍拍幼崽后背，还给狼果。
“耳朵、尾巴有没有变？”
“变了的。”
老祭司道：“亏了底子，三年能变已经不错了。身上不疼就没什么问题，不过他随时可能变人形，其他幼崽多半也快了，给他们分个窝。”
狼果应下。
老祭司想了想，见幼崽被托抱着，干干净净的圆眼还看过来。
他肃着的脸缓和些，起身往架子边走。
“幼崽还小，你们吃的那些口味重的少给他们吃。”他捡了点草药来，都是晒干切了片的，只拳头大一点，“这个隔两天给他们的肉汤里放一点，最多五片。”
“祭司，这是干什么的？”
“雨季闷热，防长疮。”
“知道了，祭司！”
幼崽没问题，不过知道之后肉汤里有草药，有几分不情愿。
狼果跟林楸下了山，冲进大山洞。
狼果将幼崽往林楸怀里一塞，道：“我把这个给安拿过去，楸，你带他进去。”
林楸抱稳，往山洞走。
兽人们忙着，纺车咯吱咯吱轻响，卷好的麻线青白，一股股堆在藤筐。
再往里面一点，那张织了很久的渔网堆在中间，兽人们一边说话，手上不停穿梭。
不用看就能织，已经很熟练了。
“该去北边捕猎了吧。”
“嗯，南边猎物少。鱼最多，在那边天天吃，我都腻了。”
兽人们笑，“能吃饱就不错了，以前你敢说这话？”
“那不都是咱们楸的功劳。”
林楸笑笑，往里面过，又听兽人道：“大泽那边不是有个兔族跑咱们部落来了，你在那边那么久，看到过没有？”
“一根儿毛都没看见，早搬走了。”
“肯定被你们吓跑的。”
林楸脚下一顿，想起自己不小心抓的大灰兔子。
原来兽人们都知道那边有兔族。
要不是他那一抓……
林楸也不知道给人家族群造成了什么影响，但愿他们还能迁移到一个安全的地方。
他走到最里面。
狼岩变做兽形趴在草垫上，幼崽堆在他身上，有的小脑袋叠着他大脑袋，还有好几个压在他背上团成一圈，睡得天昏地暗。
林楸见狼雪挥动爪子，将他放下来。
幼崽往狼岩跟前凑，翻山一样爬到狼岩背上，压住同伴。
狼岩睁眼，入目一双修长的腿，白得过分。
他道：“回来了。”
林楸盘腿坐下来，短裤往上移，腿侧软肉还要嫩些。
狼岩挪了挪脑袋，脑门上的幼崽睡梦中蹬他一下。
狼岩不动了。
林楸笑出声，将幼崽抵着狼岩眼皮的爪子挪开。
狼岩看着倾身过来的林楸，身上带着些香味，淡淡的，狼岩闻着又闭上眼睛。
“下次捕猎要去北边吗？”
“又想去？”
狼岩懒懒的，下巴搭在一个前爪上，眼睛都没睁。
什么叫又？
不过这么处处跟着，是有点奇怪……林楸面颊泛红，表情绷得住，昏暗的山洞中没哪个兽人看得出他不好意思。
林楸看着跟前大黑爪，戳了戳。
狼岩下意识勾爪，可爪垫一下被林楸捏住，他赶紧收回。
“想。”林楸轻声道，“那你同意吗？”
狼岩试图收回爪子，林楸握紧，“东边、南边、西边我都去了，也不差这一次了对不对？”
颇有强买强卖的意味。
狼岩：“雨季跟其他时候不一样。”
路上随时可能下雨，有很多蛇虫，还可能被晒得恶心呕吐，外面跑一阵都会觉得不好呼吸，毛都发沉。
而且光去就是一天，回来又一天，风餐露宿，楸细皮嫩肉的……外面飞虫咬一口都得起个大包。
狼岩这次不打算让林楸跟着。
林楸抿直了唇，却不退让，那双清澈的眸子就盯着狼岩看。他不答应不罢休似的。
狼岩：“看我没用，不许去。”
林楸狠捏了下狼岩爪垫。
大黑狼尾巴一哆嗦，爪子差点露了出来。
“我从来没去过……”
狼岩闭着眼，看不见也听不见。
感觉到林楸又压住他爪子，伸手来勾，他立马抽出爪子塞在胸口。
林楸下意识追着去抓，手一下塞进狼岩胸口，热乎乎的，毛毛裹着很舒服。手背贴着胸口肌肉，毛毛隔着都感觉到紧绷。
林楸眼里闪过一丝慌乱，想要抽手。
狼岩抬起脑袋看来，林楸与他一下只隔着巴掌宽的距离。
鼻尖一湿，狼岩碰了他一下。
林楸瞳孔一缩，顷刻意识到自己刚刚在冲着狼岩耍赖。他面上薄红加深，长睫颤抖个不停，可还倔着半分不退。
狼岩无奈，“不行……”
林楸：“行。”
狼岩牙齿痒痒，很想收拾人。
时隔多年，他再一次体会到了林楸的气人，跟小时候一个样。
“听话。”
林楸扬起下巴，顶着一张红脸，“你听话。”
看看，跟部落这些淘气幼崽没区别。
“阿楸。”
林楸看着他，狼岩不让，他慢慢低下头，失落肉眼可见。
“我又不是幼崽了，我不会添麻烦。”
狼岩被他充满委屈的话弄得心脏刺疼，活像他做了多少对不起他的事似的。
狼岩不知第几次叹气，他松开爪，撸了一把林楸的头发，“下次，我单独带你去。”
“我不。”
林楸知道自己有点得寸进尺了，但怪谁呢，要不是狼岩纵着，林楸会在他头上撒欢儿吗？
狼岩显然也知道这一点，所以不敢太凶。换做其他兽人，一个眼神就乖了。
“偏要去？”
“偏要，我又不是什么都不做，我能给大家做饭。”
“我们是去捕猎的，不是玩儿的。”
林楸在这边缠着狼岩，外面的兽人时不时看一眼，笑呵呵地看热闹。
“他俩还是这么好。”
“小时候就这样，楸连他阿父都不要，就喜欢挂在岩的身上。”
“楸刚来时，我还以为他们真成仇人了。也不知道支部落那边怎么教的，那么乖的一个幼崽，养得那么跋扈。”
“你别说，我都想去看看支部落了。”
“看吧，雪季之前肯定得来往一次。”
部落现在物资还算多，能分一点给那边。
兽人们竖着耳朵听，见狼岩始终不退让，不让楸去，不免嘀咕：“北边而已，去了就去了，王怎么还跟看幼崽似的，楸都成年狼。”
兽人们笑，“成年又怎么样，那不还把他当幼崽，护着呢。”
“楸去看看也好，没准能找到好东西。”
林楸耍赖，狼岩被磨得没脾气。
最后答应，第一次就算了，等他们先去探探路，第二次再跟着一起。
林楸已经歪倒，靠在狼岩身上，笑得眼里都是星星。
很明亮，也很鲜活。
“岩，我要天上的星星。”林楸似玩笑道。他侧脸贴着狼毛，靠在幼崽给他留出的位置上。
清透的眸子里水色一闪，林楸转头，脸埋在狼岩毛毛中。
狼岩尾巴甩动，落在林楸身侧，慢慢道：“有，下次带你找。”
“唔。”林楸悄悄抓紧了狼毛，轻轻在狼岩背上擦了擦眼角，“真有？”
“天上掉下来的石头，有。”
chapters.translated_text:
"He transformed into human form a bit late; let the priest take a look later."

Lin Qiu: "Guo said the same thing."

He naturally moved closer to Lang Yan.

The hand on his wrist loosened, uncovering the large leaf on the pottery bowl and shielding it on the outside.

Lin Qiu: "I'll go inside the cave to eat."

Lang Yan: "Alright."

Lang Yan helped him carry the large leaf, and Lin Qiu held the bowl with both hands, saying: "When Lang Qi and the others are free, we need to make some tables and chairs for the tribe; otherwise, there's nowhere to eat in situations like this."

The meat soup was hot, and the orcs had thick skin, so they tossed it from left hand to right hand, unwilling to put it down.

Lang Yan: "Use wooden stumps for now."

He followed behind Lin Qiu, watching his footing.

Today's meat soup was clear, with plenty of vegetables, making the soup green. A few droplets of oil floated on top, looking somewhat light.

Knowing the tribe's situation, no orc complained, just holding their bowls and slurping it down.

Everyone could rest for a few days during this first rain; as soon as it stopped, they would have to set off immediately.

After eating, the orcs didn't sleep; some spun thread, some combed fur, others wove fishing nets or learned to weave cloth... very few orcs were just lying in their nests.

They had slept enough in the past, so being idle for a moment actually made them not want to sleep.

Lin Qiu placed his bowl on a wooden stump and sat on a straw mat himself.

Opposite him, the cub was eating heartily, his whole head almost buried in the bowl. *Smack, smack*, he looked like he was enjoying it immensely, and his belly soon rounded out.

In just a few months, the size difference among the cubs had become apparent.

Lang Xue was the largest, about the size of a two- or three-month-old Alaskan puppy, while the smallest cub was half his size. Now, when the cubs piled up in the nest, they almost made him breathless when they lay on top of him.

After eating, Lin Qiu immediately went with Lang Guo to take the cubs to the priest's cave.

Lang Yan stayed behind to look after the other cubs.

In the priest's cave, the old orc had just sat down in his nest intending to sleep for a while when the two orcs arrived.

"Priest, take a look at Xue; he just transformed into human form," Lang Guo said, blocking the cub's chest with one hand and supporting his bottom with the other, rushing into the cave headlong.

The old priest swallowed the scolding words he was about to say and said: "Bring him here."

The cub was placed in the old orc's hands.

He was afraid of pressing on the old orc, as the hands exposed from the animal skin garment were too thin.

Lang Xue called out in a milky voice: "Priest Grandpa."

The old orc stroked his head: "It's okay, let Priest Grandpa take a look."

The old priest grabbed the little wolf, first checking the four legs, then touching the cub's head, and asked: "Does it hurt?"

The cub shook his head, his eyes filled with confusion.

"How long did you stay in human form? How big were you?"

Lin Qiu: "At most ten breaths, barely thigh-high; his arms and legs are all fine."

The old priest: "..."

There was nothing wrong with the cub's beast form, so naturally, he wouldn't be missing any limbs in human form.

He patted the cub's back and returned him to Lang Guo.

"Did his ears or tail change?"

"They did."

The old priest said: "Considering his foundation, being able to transform in three years is already quite good. As long as his body doesn't hurt, there's no problem, but he might transform into human form at any time, and most of the other cubs will be soon too; give them a separate nest."

Lang Guo agreed.

The old priest thought for a moment, seeing the cub being held, his clean, round eyes looking over.

His stern face softened a little, and he stood up to walk toward the shelf.

"The cubs are still small; give them less of those strong-flavored things you eat." He picked out some herbs, all dried and sliced, only the size of a fist: "Put a little of this in their meat soup every two days, five pieces at most."

"Priest, what is this for?"

"The rainy season is humid; it prevents sores."

"Understood, Priest!"

There was nothing wrong with the cub, but knowing there were herbs in the meat soup later, he was somewhat reluctant.

Lang Guo and Lin Qiu went down the mountain and rushed into the large cave.

Lang Guo stuffed the cub into Lin Qiu's arms and said: "I'll take this to An; Qiu, you take him inside."

Lin Qiu held him steady and walked toward the cave.

The orcs were busy; the spinning wheel creaked softly, and the rolled hemp thread was green and white, piled in bundles in a rattan basket.

A bit further in, that fishing net which had been woven for a long time was piled in the middle, and the orcs kept their hands moving while talking.

They could weave without looking; they were already very skilled.

"It's time to go north to hunt, right?"

"Yeah, there's less prey in the south. There's plenty of fish, but I'm tired of eating it every day there."

The orcs laughed: "Be glad you can eat your fill; would you have dared to say that in the past?"

"That's all thanks to our Qiu."

Lin Qiu smiled and walked inside, hearing the orcs say again: "Didn't a rabbit tribe from the Great Marsh run to our tribe? You were there for so long, have you seen them?"

"Didn't see a single hair; they moved away long ago."

"They must have been scared away by you guys."

Lin Qiu paused, remembering the big gray rabbit he had accidentally caught.

So the orcs all knew there was a rabbit tribe there.

If it weren't for that catch of his...

Lin Qiu didn't know what impact he had caused on their group, but he hoped they could still migrate to a safe place.

He walked to the very back.

Lang Yan was in his beast form, lying on the straw mat, with the cubs piled on him; some had their little heads resting on his big head, and several others were curled up on his back, sleeping soundly.

Seeing Lang Xue waving his paws, Lin Qiu put him down.

The cub scurried toward Lang Yan, climbing onto his back like climbing a mountain, pressing down on his companions.

Lang Yan opened his eyes, and what met his sight was a pair of slender legs, excessively white.

He said: "You're back."

Lin Qiu sat cross-legged, his shorts shifting upward, the soft skin on the side of his legs even more tender.

Lang Yan shifted his head, and the cub on his forehead kicked him in his sleep.

Lang Yan didn't move.

Lin Qiu laughed out loud and moved the cub's paw, which was pressing against Lang Yan's eyelid, away.

Lang Yan looked at Lin Qiu, who was leaning over; he carried a faint fragrance, and Lang Yan closed his eyes again as he smelled it.

"Are you going north for the next hunt?"

"You want to go again?"

Lang Yan was lazy, resting his chin on a front paw without even opening his eyes.

What did he mean by "again"?

But following him everywhere like this was a bit strange... Lin Qiu's cheeks flushed, but he kept his expression steady; in the dim cave, no orc could tell he was embarrassed.

Lin Qiu looked at the big black paw in front of him and poked it.

Lang Yan subconsciously curled his paw, but when the pad was pinched by Lin Qiu, he quickly withdrew it.

"I want to," Lin Qiu said softly, "Will you agree?"

Lang Yan tried to retract his paw, but Lin Qiu held on tight: "I've been to the east, south, and west; it wouldn't hurt to go this time too, right?"

It was quite a forceful way of bargaining.

Lang Yan: "The rainy season is different from other times."

It could rain at any moment on the road, there were many snakes and insects, and one could get nauseous from the heat; running outside for a while made it hard to breathe, and the fur felt heavy.

Besides, just going there took a day, and coming back took another; sleeping in the open and eating in the wind, and Qiu had such delicate skin... even a bite from a flying insect outside would raise a big bump.

Lang Yan didn't intend to let Lin Qiu follow this time.

Lin Qiu pursed his lips but didn't back down, his clear eyes staring at Lang Yan. It was as if he wouldn't give up until he agreed.

Lang Yan: "Looking at me is useless; you're not allowed to go."

Lin Qiu pinched Lang Yan's paw pad hard.

The big black wolf's tail shivered, and his claws almost popped out.

"I've never been there before..."

Lang Yan kept his eyes closed, neither seeing nor hearing.

Feeling Lin Qiu pressing on his paw again and reaching out to hook it, he immediately pulled his paw away and tucked it into his chest.

Lin Qiu instinctively chased after it, his hand suddenly thrusting into Lang Yan's chest; it was warm, and the fur felt very comfortable. The back of his hand pressed against the chest muscles, and he could feel the tension even through the fur.

A flash of panic crossed Lin Qiu's eyes, and he wanted to pull his hand away.

Lang Yan lifted his head to look, and Lin Qiu was now only a palm's width away from him.

His nose tip felt wet; Lang Yan had touched him.

Lin Qiu's pupils contracted, and he instantly realized he had just been acting spoiled toward Lang Yan. The faint red on his face deepened, and his long eyelashes trembled incessantly, yet he remained stubborn and didn't retreat an inch.

Lang Yan was helpless: "No..."

Lin Qiu: "Yes."

Lang Yan's teeth felt itchy; he really wanted to discipline him.

After many years, he once again experienced Lin Qiu's ability to annoy him; it was just the same as when he was a child.

"Behave."

Lin Qiu lifted his chin, wearing a flushed face: "You behave."

Look at that; he was no different from the naughty cubs in the tribe.

"A-Qiu."

Lin Qiu looked at him; Lang Yan wouldn't let him, and he slowly lowered his head, his disappointment visible to the naked eye.

"I'm not a cub anymore; I won't cause trouble."

Lang Yan's heart ached at his aggrieved words, as if he had done something terrible to him.

Lang Yan sighed for the umpteenth time; he released his paw and ruffled Lin Qiu's hair: "Next time, I'll take you separately."

"I don't want that."

Lin Qiu knew he was pushing his luck, but who was to blame? If it weren't for Lang Yan indulging him, would Lin Qiu dare to run wild on his head?

Lang Yan clearly knew this too, so he didn't dare to be too fierce. If it were any other orc, one look would have made them obedient.

"You insist on going?"

"I insist; it's not like I won't do anything, I can cook for everyone."

"We are going to hunt, not to play."

Lin Qiu was pestering Lang Yan here, and the orcs outside looked over from time to time, laughing and watching the fun.

"They are still as close as ever."

"They were like that when they were kids; Qiu didn't even want his own father, he just liked hanging onto Yan."

"When Qiu first came, I thought they had really become enemies. I don't know how the branch tribe taught him; such an obedient cub, raised to be so overbearing."

"Don't say that; I even want to go see the branch tribe."

"Go see them; we definitely have to visit once before the snow season."

The tribe had plenty of supplies now and could share some with them.

The orcs pricked up their ears to listen, and seeing that Lang Yan still wouldn't back down and let Qiu go, they couldn't help but mutter: "It's just the north; if he goes, he goes. Why is the King still acting like he's looking after a cub? Qiu is already an adult wolf."

The orcs laughed: "So what if he's an adult? He still treats him like a cub, protecting him."

"It would be good for Qiu to go and see; maybe he can find something good."

Lin Qiu acted spoiled, and Lang Yan was worn down until he had no temper left.

Finally, he agreed that the first time would be skipped, and after they went to scout the path, he could follow along the second time.

Lin Qiu had already slumped over, leaning against Lang Yan, his eyes shining like stars.

Very bright, and very vibrant.

"Yan, I want the stars in the sky," Lin Qiu said, as if joking. He pressed his cheek against the wolf fur, leaning into the spot the cubs had left for him.

A watery glint flashed in his clear eyes, and Lin Qiu turned his head, burying his face in Lang Yan's fur.

Lang Yan's tail flicked, landing beside Lin Qiu, and he said slowly: "I have them; I'll take you to find them next time."

"Mm." Lin Qiu quietly gripped the wolf fur and gently wiped the corner of his eye on Lang Yan's back: "Really?"

"The stones that fall from the sky—I have those."
chapters.title: 第75章

chapters.translated_text:
Inside the cave, the orcs were divided into several groups, each busy with their own tasks.

They chatted and laughed, glancing toward the deepest part of the cave from time to time, then lowering their voices again.

Their King was lying on the ground acting as a cushion, covered in a pile of cubs. Qiu was lying on his side, resting on his back, his thin, long limbs curled up. He had been lying there with his eyes closed for a long time, looking as if he had fallen into a deep sleep.

The wind was gradually dying down, but the rain showed no signs of stopping.

Lang Yan wanted to get up and take a look outside, but he couldn't move.

"Fire."

Lang Huo, who was enjoying having his fur groomed in a grass nest, pricked up his ears and turned his snout toward them.

Lang Yan: "Go check if there's any water pooling in the tail-grass field, and see if the bird droppings have gotten wet..."

Lang Huo climbed up, "Understood, King."

Lang Yan's voice was low. Lin Qiu, resting on his back, felt the vibration through his body. He frowned and shifted, his hand tightening on the wolf fur on Lang Yan's chest.

Lang Yan glanced at the hand, which looked even fairer against the black fur. It was thin and long, and he always liked to grab onto something while sleeping.

He didn't even know how many times his wolf fur had been pulled out by him.

Lang Yan lay back down, his chin just covering the hand placed in front of him.

Enduring the ticklish sensation of the cubs biting him like prey or scratching him like a log for sharpening claws in their sleep, he also closed his eyes to doze, taking a rare rest during the day.

Lang Huo went out with a large leaf over his head. The shed for the bird droppings was built sturdily, with the roof reinforced and widened, actually better than the main cave.

Lang Huo simply cut some more reeds and large leaves and covered the top with another layer.

On the other side, the tail-grass swayed in the wind and rain, glistening like jade after being washed by the rain.

The vast expanse of tail-grass created waves, and the roots washed out by the rain were robust. Excess water gathered into small streams, flowing along the drainage ditches to the outside, so there was no water accumulation.

Lang Huo had a large leaf on his head and held a tail-grass spike in his palm; it was as long as his hand.

He grinned, looking a bit silly.

This year's harvest would definitely be good!

Even though his fur was soaked, it couldn't dampen Lang Huo's joy. He returned to the cave entrance, shook his fur twice, and ducked into the cave to report to Lang Yan.

Black Feather Tribe.

The wind high on the mountain was still strong, howling loudly.

In the largest cave near the summit, the entrance was wide open.

The Black Feather orcs were gathered together, all wrapping their bodies with their wings, squatting at the cave entrance without moving.

They hunched their necks, their feathers blown upward.

The rain hit their feathers and then slid smoothly onto the ground; their feathers were not wet at all.

An orc poked his head into the cave.

"The fish caught by the fishing nets are the same as what we used to catch, just with an extra clay pot. Can the food made be any good?"

"I don't know, but that's what Yu Shan and the others are saying."

"Twenty orcs have to go work for them after the rainy season, for three months! The tribe still needs to store food for the snowy season. I don't know if we'll have enough..."

The orcs discussed in low voices, most feeling it was a bit of a loss.

Yu Chang finished listening to his companions' discussion and defended them: "Yu Shan and the others aren't stupid! If you thought it wasn't good, why didn't you say so before? Why are you whispering here now?"

"Yu Chang, why are you in such a rush? Everyone isn't saying anything, just afraid of losing out."

Yu Chang raised an eyebrow, "Hmph! Losing out? Then don't fight for the spots to go to the Wolf Tribe. Stay in the tribe, then you won't lose out."

"Can you not be so harsh? Everyone was just saying it casually..."

"Alright, alright, that's just his personality. I don't know who was the loudest to oppose it at the start, and now they're dying to stick to them."

Seeing that a fight was about to break out, the old patriarch, supported by Yu Le, stood up, glanced at the cave entrance, and walked shakily into the depths of the cave.

Everyone immediately fell silent.

The orcs who cooked the soup were the sub-orcs who had gone to the Wolf Tribe. They had watched a few times and learned how to process fish and what herbs to use for cooking.

When the lid made of dried grass stalks was lifted off the clay pot, all the orcs' gazes were cast over in an instant.

Yu Ya, along with a few young teenagers, had already taken the lead in surrounding the clay pot.

The young teenagers looked at the milky-white fish soup and swallowed their saliva.

"Uncle Jiang, is it ready?"

The sub-orc in charge of making the fish soup was named Yu Jiang. His complexion was pale year-round. When he was young, his abdomen was pierced by a beast's horn while hunting. He was lucky to save his life, but his foundation was damaged.

He had no cubs. At that time, after he recovered, the previous priest couldn't bear to see him so listless, so he arranged for him to take care of the tribe's cubs.

The batch of cubs including Yu Ya had all been raised under his care.

Yu Jiang: "Not yet, wait a little longer."

He put some wild vegetables into the clay pot, blanched them for a while, sprinkled some salt, and then told the orc watching the fire to put it out.

Yu Jiang's face was flushed from the fire, looking a bit healthier.

The soup was so hot, and the tribe didn't have clay bowls like the wolf orcs. Just as Yu Jiang was feeling troubled, he turned his head and saw all the orcs who had been blocking the cave entrance crowding around.

Yu Jiang's gaze fell on the Black Feather patriarch.

"Patriarch, there are no bowls, how should we divide it?"

"We'll make our own!"

The Black Feather orcs flew out in a scramble, afraid of being a step late.

Yu Chang: "Who was doubting it just now?"

No orc paid him any mind; they were all afraid of not having anything to eat if they were late.

By the time the orcs dug out their respective bowls, the fish soup had cooled down enough.

The orcs had eaten plenty of fish in the past. For the Black Feather orcs, fish in the big river were easier to catch than horned prey and carried almost no risk.

But they just didn't taste good.

Yet today's fish soup overturned everyone's thoughts. Not only was there no fishy smell, but the soup even tasted fresh and sweet!

The Black Feather patriarch looked at the soup in his wooden bowl. The fish meat had been boiled for a long time and had softened into fine threads. The greens were added just right, which helped cut the fishy smell for the Black Feather orcs who ate a lot of fish.

His sense of taste had slowly deteriorated, but he could still tell that this fish soup was different.

The old orc looked at the two clay pots, and the jars next to them that were almost identical in size and smooth on the surface...

"Shan."

"Patriarch." Yu Shan shared some of the meat in his bowl with his partner and looked over.

The Black Feather patriarch took a deep breath. He was short of breath, and his voice sounded stifled as he said, "These clay vessels, are you sure they were made by the Wolf Tribe themselves?"

Yu Shan: "Yes, we heard it with our own ears."

The wolf orcs didn't deliberately hide these things.

The fishing nets were the same; when they were at the Great Marsh, if the nets broke, Lang Yu and the others repaired them themselves.

The Black Feather patriarch couldn't eat anymore after drinking half a bowl of soup. His hands were shaking a bit, and the bowl he was holding was taken by Yu Le. The little orc said in a soft, delicate voice: "Grandpa, do you want to eat a little more?"

The Black Feather patriarch's withered palm landed on his shoulder and patted it, "No need, go play. You don't need to stay with Grandpa."

Yu Le didn't leave; he hung his head and sat beside the old orc.

The orcs finished the fish soup, savoring the aftertaste, and flew toward their own caves.

Before long, only the Black Feather patriarch, Yu Le, Yu Shan, and his partner Yu Qian remained in the mountain-top cave.

Once the tribesmen had left, the Black Feather patriarch showed his fatigue.

He was supported and sent into a nest lined with down. His body leaned weakly against the edge of the nest. Just from those few steps, the old orc's breathing was very rapid, and his rib-defined chest heaved violently a few times before he slowly caught his breath.

The Black Feather patriarch was old; he was willing but unable to do many things.

All the big and small matters of the tribe were handled by Yu Shan and his partner Yu Qian. Only when there were things that required the old patriarch to make a decision would the two orcs bring them to ask him.

It wasn't just that the next generation of priests was missing; the Black Feather patriarch also had no heart to cultivate the next patriarch.

Before Yu Shan was injured, he was the most powerful orc in the tribe, and the Black Feather patriarch had originally favored him. But after he was injured, although most orcs still took him as their leader, there were some who were unhappy.

If he were chosen as the patriarch of a tribe, his current physical condition would not allow it.

Orcs were allowed to challenge; if you won, you could be the patriarch.

Once there was no one to suppress the tribesmen, even if Yu Shan were made patriarch, there would be orcs who wouldn't submit, which would be bad for him instead.

So the old patriarch could only hold on; he didn't dare to close his eyes.

Suppressing these chaotic thoughts, the Black Feather patriarch asked: "Shan, Qian, have the orcs to go to the Wolf Tribe been selected yet?"

Yu Shan said: "Patriarch, we discussed it and want to send Yu Ya and the others over."

Yu Qian also said: "The wolf orcs don't like those with complicated minds, but they cherish cubs. Even though Ya and the others have to work when sent over, they can learn something."

It wasn't that they trusted the Wolf Tribe absolutely.

These young orcs like Yu Ya were in the tribe, but the orcs didn't allow them to go out hunting, and they had nothing to do on the mountain. Otherwise, how would they have found the Wolf Tribe's mine?

Going to Wolf Mountain would allow them to eat their fill, and secondly, they wanted to be on good terms with the Wolf Tribe and let the little orcs see the situation of other tribes.

Yu Shan was certain that the Wolf Tribe would get better and better, and they needed to learn more from them.

The Black Feather patriarch: "Don't think about taking advantage of others; they aren't there to look after your cubs."

"We know, Patriarch."

The old patriarch: "Just send two or three young orcs. For the weak orcs, only choose a few who are careful. Those who got along well with the wolf orcs last time, and let the healthy ones go for the rest."

"We took advantage of them last time; don't do that this time."

Yu Shan nodded.

The Black Feather Tribe didn't have as many things to do as the Wolf Tribe. They only needed to fill their stomachs every day. Now with fishing nets and clay pots, they could get twice the result with half the effort, so they could spare some strong orcs.

The old patriarch said: "You two arrange which specific orcs. It's best if you both go along this time."

"Then the tribe..."

"I'm not dead yet."

The two orcs hesitated in their hearts, but they agreed.

Before they left, they would definitely make arrangements.

Especially since they would be gone for three months after the rainy season; that was when they should be preparing food for the snowy season, and they couldn't afford any mistakes.

"Grandpa." Yu Le waited until they left before hurriedly supporting the old patriarch to help him lie down.

The Black Feather patriarch leaned against the edge of the grass nest without moving. Only Yu Le knew that without support, his grandpa couldn't get up at all.

The Black Feather patriarch grasped the little orc's hand, gasped a few times, and said in a hoarse voice: "Le, you go too."

"Grandpa, I won't."

"Listen to Grandpa!" The Black Feather patriarch gripped the little orc's hand tightly, "Only the Wolf Tribe's priest can teach you. You must go, you have to go. Even if you learn a little bit, even if you just know one kind of medicinal herb, it's better than staying by my side all the time."

"Grandpa, I don't want to." Yu Le's little face was pale, tears already hanging at the corners of his eyes, "If I leave, what will you do..."

The Black Feather patriarch: "Don't worry, aren't there so many uncles? Grandpa is fine."

He gripped the little orc's hand tightly, refusing to be refused: "You were personally chosen by the previous priest. You have talent, you were just born a bit late and haven't learned for long... Listen to Grandpa, if the Black Feather Tribe wants to continue to develop, it inevitably, inevitably needs a mature, powerful priest. Le, for the sake of the tribe, and for yourself, you must go."

The little orc choked, lowering his head and not speaking.

Ever since he could turn into human form, he had been by the old orc's side. Yu Ya and the others liked to go out and play, but he had to guard Grandpa. For so many years, he had been playing by himself.

Sometimes he would envy that group of little orcs flying together, but most of the time, he felt that this was also quite good.

"Grandpa, can't Yu Ya and the others go?"

The old orc did not respond.

Yu Le panicked, looked down, and realized that the old orc had already fallen asleep.

Yu Le bit his lower lip hard, his teeth pressing until his lips turned white. Only when it was about to break did he slowly relax.

He looked at the old orc's tightly furrowed brow, moved his hand, and pulled it away.

Yu Le looked at the red marks on it, grasped it with his other hand, and silently shed tears, *plop, plop*.

He shouldn't have let Grandpa worry.

But he was afraid...
