洞内兽人分做几堆，各自忙碌着手上的事情。
他们说说笑笑，时不时看一眼山洞最里头，又压低一点声音。
他们王趴在地上当垫子，幼崽堆了他满身。楸又侧躺着枕在他背上，瘦瘦长长的手脚蜷缩起来，闭着眼睛半晌没动，看着是睡熟了。
风渐小，但雨却没停的意思。
狼岩想起身出去看看，无奈动弹不得。
“火。”
草窝里正享受梳毛的狼火竖起耳朵，嘴筒子冲着这边。
狼岩：“去看看地里尾巴草有没有积水，鸟粪有没有被淋湿……”
狼火爬起来，“知道了，王。”
狼岩声音压得低，靠在他背上的林楸耳朵贴在他身上，感觉到一点震动，拧眉动了动，手攥紧了他胸口的狼毛。
狼岩看了眼黑毛毛衬得更加白皙的手，细细长长的，总喜欢抓点东西睡。
自己狼毛都不知道被他抓下来多少次了。
狼岩重新趴好，下巴刚好捂住放在身前的手。
他忍受着幼崽睡梦中或把他当猎物咬，或把他当磨爪的木头抓挠的刺挠感，也闭眼打盹，难得白日里休息一下。
狼火顶着大叶片出去走了一遭，那放鸟粪的棚子做得结实，棚顶加固加宽，倒比大山洞这边的好一些。
狼火干脆又砍了些芦苇跟大叶片，在面上覆盖了一层。
另一边，尾巴草在风雨中飘摇，雨水洗过，碧玉似的泛着油光。
成片的尾巴草掀起草浪，雨水冲出来的根茎茁壮。多余的水汇聚成细流，沿着排水沟，全部往外面淌，不存在积水的情况。
狼火脑袋上顶着大叶片，掌心托住尾巴草穗，足有他巴掌那么长。
他咧嘴，笑得有些傻气。
今年的收成指定好！
毛毛沾湿了也挡不住狼火心里的愉悦，他回到洞口，抖两下狼毛，钻进山洞给狼岩汇报去了。
黑羽部落。
高山上的风依旧大，烈烈作响。
近山顶那个最大的山洞中，洞口大开。
黑羽兽人聚齐了，全用翅膀裹住身体，蹲在洞口一动不动。
他们缩着脖子，羽毛被吹得扬起来。
雨水拍在羽毛上，又顺滑地掉在地面，羽毛一点没被打湿。
兽人冲着洞里探头。
“渔网抓的鱼跟我们以前抓的不都一样，就多了个陶锅，做出来的食物能好吃吗？”
“不知道，反正羽山他们都这么说。”
“雨季后要去二十个兽人给他们干活，三个月呢，部落还要积攒雪季的食物，也不知道能不能攒够……”
兽人细声讨论着，大多觉得有点亏。
羽长听完同伴议论，维护道：“羽山他们又不蠢！你们要是觉得不好，之前为什么不说，现在在这里说小话。”
“羽长，你急什么，大家又没说什么，只是怕吃亏而已。”
羽长眉梢一吊，“哼！吃亏？那你们别争去狼部落的名额，留在部落才不会吃亏。”
“你说话别这么刺耳行不行，大家这不是随口……”
“行了行了，他就这个性子。也不知道谁开头反对得最大声，现在巴不得贴上去。”
眼看要打起来，老族长扶着羽乐起身，甩了洞口一眼，颤颤巍巍往洞里面去。
大家立马噤声。
煮汤的兽人是去了狼部落的亚兽人，他们看过几次，便也学会了怎么处理鱼，找什么草来烹饪。
待到陶锅上枯草秆做的盖子揭开，一瞬间，所有兽人的目光投射过来。
羽涯带着几个小少年，已经率先将陶锅围了一圈。
小少年看着奶白色的鱼汤，咽了咽口水。
“江叔，好了吗？”
负责做鱼汤的亚兽人叫羽江，面色常年苍白，年轻时捕猎腹部被野兽角戳破，有幸捡回来一条命，但伤了底子。
他没有幼崽，当时病好后了无牵挂的样子前一任祭司看不下去，就安排他照顾部落的幼崽。
羽涯这一批幼崽都是他照顾着长大的。
羽江：“还没好，再等一会儿。”
他往陶锅里又放了些野菜，烫了会儿，撒上点盐，就叫看火的兽人熄火了。
羽江面上被火烤得泛出点红，看着好像健康了一点。
这汤这么烫，部落里没有像狼兽人一样的陶碗。羽江正为难，回过头，后面所有刚刚堵洞口的兽人都围了过来。
羽江目光落到黑羽族长身上。
“族长，没有碗，怎么分？”
“我们自己做！”
黑羽兽人争先恐后飞出去，生怕晚回来一步。
羽长：“刚刚谁怀疑来着？”
没兽人理他，都怕晚了没吃的了。
等兽人们把各自的碗刨出来，鱼汤也凉得差不多了。
兽人们以往没少吃鱼，对黑羽兽人而言，大河里的鱼比那些长角的猎物好抓，几乎没有风险。
但就是不好吃。
可今天的鱼汤却颠覆了大家的想法，没有腥臭味道不说，汤喝着甚至是鲜甜味的！
黑羽族长看着木碗里的汤，鱼肉煮得久了，已经软烂得散成细丝。青菜加得刚刚好，对吃多了鱼的黑羽兽人来说，能压一压鱼腥。
他的味觉已经慢慢退化，但还是能吃出这鱼汤的不一样。
老兽人看着那两口陶锅，还有旁边大小几乎一致，表面光滑的罐子……
“山。”
“族长。”羽山将碗里的肉分了些给伴侣，看了过来。
黑羽族长狠吸一口气，气短，说话有些憋着似的道：“这些陶器，确定是狼部落自己做的？”
羽山：“是，我们亲耳听见的。”
狼兽人并没有刻意隐瞒这些事。
渔网也是，当是在大泽那边，渔网坏了还是狼雨他们自己动手修补的。
黑羽族长喝了半碗汤便吃不下了，他手有些颤，端着的碗被羽乐接住，小兽人细声细气说：“阿爷，还要不要再吃点？”
黑羽族长枯瘦的掌心落在他肩膀，拍了下，“不用，去玩儿吧，不用守着阿爷。”
羽乐不走，垂着脑袋，坐在老兽人旁边。
兽人吃完鱼汤，回味着，飞往自己山洞。
没一会儿，山顶洞中只剩下黑羽族长、羽乐还有羽山跟他的伴侣羽千。
族人走完，黑羽族长露出来疲态。
他被搀扶着送入铺满了羽绒的窝里，身体无力倚靠着窝的边缘。就这么几步，老兽人呼吸很急，肋骨分明的胸口狠狠起伏了几下，才慢慢缓过劲儿来。
黑羽族长老了，很多事有心无力。
部落大事小事都是羽山跟羽千他两口子操持，只有少些需要老族长做决策的，两个兽人才会拿来问他。
不只是下一任祭司断代，下一任族长，黑羽族长也无心再培养。
羽山受伤前是部落最厉害的兽人，黑羽族长本来看好他。可他受伤之后，虽然大多兽人也以他为首，但也也有不乐意的。
如果选他作为一个部落的族长的话，他现在的身体不允许。
兽人允许挑战，打赢了就可以当族长。
一旦没他压着族人，即便让羽山当了族长，也有兽人不服，反倒对他不好。
所以老族长只能撑着，不敢闭眼。
压下这些杂乱的心绪，黑羽族长问：“山、千，去狼部落的兽人选好了没有？”
羽山道：“族长，我们商量了下，想把羽涯他们送过去。”
羽千也道：“狼兽人不喜欢心思多的，但爱护幼崽，涯他们送过去虽然要干活，但能学到些东西。”
不是他们绝对信任狼部落。
羽涯这几个小兽人在部落，兽人们又不允许他们出去捕猎，待在山上也无所事事，不然他们怎么会找到狼兽人那矿洞。
去狼山一来能吃饱，二来，也是想跟狼部落交好，叫小兽人看看其他部落的情况。
羽山肯定，狼部落会越来越好，他们要多学着点。
黑羽族长：“别想着占人家便宜，人家不是给你看幼崽的。”
“我们知道，族长。”
老族长：“小兽人去两三个就行了，体弱的兽人只选几个心细的，上次跟狼兽人相处好的，旁的就让健康的去。”
“上次的事是我们占便宜，这次别这样了。”
羽山点点头。
黑羽部落没狼部落那么多事，他们一天只需要填饱肚子就行了，现在有了渔网跟陶锅，事半功倍，有力气的兽人抽调些走也能行。
老族长道：“具体哪些兽人，你俩安排，最好这次你们都跟着去。”
“那部落……”
“我还没死。”
两个兽人心里犹豫，但还是应下。
他们走之前，务必会安排好。
尤其是雨季过后他们要去三个月，那时候该准备雪季的食物，一点不敢出错。
“阿爷。”羽乐等他们走了，才急忙托着老兽人，帮着他躺下来。
黑羽族长靠在草窝边缘不动。只有羽乐知道，没人搀扶，他阿爷根本起不来了。
黑羽族长握住小兽人的手，急喘几声，声音嘶哑道：“乐，你也跟着去。”
“阿爷，我不。”
“听阿爷的话！”黑羽族长紧紧扣住小兽人的手，“只有狼部落的祭司能教你，你要去，必须去。就算学一点点，哪怕知道一种草药，也比一直守在我身边强。”
“阿爷，我不要。”羽乐小脸苍白，眼泪已经挂在眼角，“我走了，你怎么办……”
黑羽族长：“放心，不是还有那么多阿叔在，阿爷没事。”
他紧紧握住小兽人的手，不容推拒道：“你是上一任祭司亲自选出来的，你有天赋，就是出生晚了些，没学多久……你听阿爷的话，黑羽部落要想继续发展，势必、势必需要一个成熟的，强大的祭司。乐，为了部落，也为了你自己，你必须去。”
小兽人哽咽着，低着头不说话。
他能变成人形后就一直跟在老兽人身边，羽涯他们喜欢出去野，他要守着阿爷，这么多年都是他自己跟自己玩儿。
他有时候会羡慕那一群一起飞行的小兽人，但更多时候，他觉得这样也挺好。
“阿爷，羽涯他们去不行吗？”
老兽人没有回应。
羽乐一慌，低头看着，才发现老兽人已经睡了过去。
羽乐咬紧了下唇，牙齿压得唇瓣发白，快要破皮时，才慢慢放松下来。
他看着老兽人紧皱的眉心，手动了动，抽出来。
羽乐看着上面的红印，另一只手握住，啪嗒啪嗒默默掉下眼泪来。
他不该让阿爷操心的。
可他怕……

chapters.translated_text:
Just as the Black Wolf tribe’s priest had predicted, the rain poured for three whole days.

After three days, the sky finally cleared, turning into a vast, cloudless expanse of azure.

Within just half a morning, the rainwater on the ground evaporated; the area under the previously soggy sheds dried out so quickly that a layer of dust rose with every step.

The beastmen, who had been cooped up in the caves for days, couldn't stand it any longer and all came out.

Lang An directed Lang Mo’s squad to quickly lift the fish traps, while the wolf pups split into two groups: one followed Lang Rong straight to the fields to check on the tail-grass and herbs, and the other followed Lang Bing into the forest to inspect the planted medicinal herbs.

The old priest, leaning on his cane, didn't want to stay in the cave either, so he headed to the fields.

All the beastmen were busy, except for the few squads scheduled to depart for hunting and gathering that evening.

They were currently being forced by Lang Yan to stay in the cave and catch up on sleep.

Even if they couldn't sleep, they had to try, or they wouldn't be able to handle the night of traveling ahead.

Lin Qiu and Lang Guo weren't idle either; one went to help Lang Qi with weaving, while the other brought the pups along to join in the fun, calling it "learning early so it's easier to handle when they grow up."

From the youngest to the oldest, not a single person was idle.

The weather on the Eastern Continent changed drastically. After days of heavy rain, the sun stripped away its final layer of cover, and the heat felt scorching on the skin almost immediately—even the beastmen avoided it.

At noon, on the open ground in front of Wolf Mountain, the grass the beastmen had cut was spread out to dry.

Heat waves shimmered, the grass blades curled and withered, and the beastmen returned drenched in sweat after working for only a short while.

Because of the sweltering heat, fewer beastmen maintained their beast forms; most stayed in human form, wearing only a piece of animal hide around their waists.

Bare-chested and barefoot, they rushed toward the shade of the sheds.

After sitting for only a moment, they found it too hot and all retreated into the caves.

Lin Qiu came out after practicing weaving for a while to find that Lang An and the others had already started a fire to cook.

The beastmen’s foreheads were covered in sweat, their skin flushed red from the heat, and the edges of the animal hides around their waists were soaked and darkened.

Lang Yu and Lang Hong, who were sitting by the stove, were so hot they stayed as far from the fire pit as possible, stretching their arms out to add firewood.

Lin Qiu stood beside them, waving a piece of bark he was using as a fan.

"Hoo—" the beastmen sighed in relief.

"Qiu, faster."

Lin Qiu simply sat down nearby, waving the fan while watching Lang An boil fish soup.

It was so hot that An and the others didn't want to exert themselves; they cooked whatever was easiest to fill their stomachs, avoiding anything troublesome.

Lang An put the ingredients into the pot, covered it, and leaned against a low wall nearby. Sweat beads slid down his body incessantly, and he said listlessly, "I don't even want to use fire anymore."

Lin Qiu: "Would it be better inside the cave?"

Lang An looked at the bark in Lin Qiu's hand—which had been trimmed into shape and fixed with a wooden handle—and was too hot to move, "Except for the big cave, none of the others are any better."

"This is only the beginning."

"Yeah, only the beginning."

Seeing Lang An staring at the fan in his hand, Lin Qiu handed it over, intending to go make a few more.

Lang An took it and fanned his face and neck vigorously. The wind made his hair flutter, and Lang An squinted his eyes, his body softening as he leaned completely against the low wall.

"Qiu..." Lang Yu said with a hint of resentment.

Lin Qiu stood up, "I'll go make some more."

Saying this, he hurried over to where Lang Qi was.

The cave used for woodworking was large and filled with various types of wood. Wood shavings were scattered everywhere, and the beastmen sat on the ground, continuing to struggle with the wood.

They had already started making parts for the second loom, and a pile of broken stone axes and knives lay in the corner while the beastmen sat on the floor.

The cave was slightly better than outside, but the beastmen were still hot.

Lang Mu and the others had just come back from checking the fish traps; their sweat hadn't dried yet, and as they walked into the cave, they were soon covered in wood shavings.

The loom was clacking in the cave, and in order to produce a piece of cloth as quickly as possible, there was almost always a beastman working at it.

However, since it was everyone's first time, the weave of the cloth on the machine was uneven and irregular, showing that they were all novices.

Right now, Lang Guo was the one busy at the loom, while the pups were rolling around in the wood shavings.

Only they didn't seem to mind the heat.

Lang Guo was throwing the shuttle clumsily; seeing Lin Qiu arrive, he stopped his work to look over.

"Qiu, why are you back?"

Lin Qiu: "To make a few more fans."

Fans were easy to make. When he made the first one, the beastmen in the cave had understood immediately. Lang Qi pulled five or six out from behind him and said, "Qiu, you use these first."

Lin Qiu: "When did you make these?"

Lang Guo: "Right when you left."

Lang Qi’s speed was truly fast; he took a piece of bark, sketched a shape with a charcoal pencil, trimmed it with an obsidian knife, and the fan face was done. Then he framed it with wooden strips, attached a wooden handle, and wrapped it with hemp thread for reinforcement—it was finished instantly.

Lang Guo had seen it with his own eyes; it was clearly his first time, yet he worked as if he had done it dozens of times.

In contrast, Lang Mu and the others had only managed to make one in the time it took Lang Qi to make three.

That was the difference!

Lin Qiu: "Uncle Qi... never mind, the loom is urgent, do that first."

As for the wooden tables and stools, they could wait until the beastmen had time.

Lang Qi nodded, burying his head back into his work without asking further.

He had a steady temperament; now that he was in his middle age and had finally found his hobby and talent, among the group of beastmen in the cave, he was the most motivated.

Lin Qiu carried the fans out and distributed one to each beastman who was cooking.

Seeing them look like they had found a savior, fanning their faces vigorously, Lang An said, "This is a good thing; it should have been brought out sooner."

The other beastmen had their hair flying everywhere, tilting their faces to feel the breeze, "It would be even better if it could move by itself."

Lin Qiu: "...That's a nice thought."

But he couldn't make that.

Because of the heat, the beastmen didn't want to eat meat soup anymore.

They were impatient and easily burned their mouths.

Hearing the occasional hiss of pain from the cave, Lin Qiu pondered what else he could make to eat.

In this heat, the beastmen craved cold things.

Without wheat or rice, he couldn't make cold noodles or cold jelly.

He could think about ice jelly and sugar water; the rainy season was hot and many fruits were ripe. If he could just find saltpeter, he could manage a bowl of shaved ice with sugar water.

But that was just a snack; it couldn't fill a beastman's stomach.

"What are you thinking about?" Lang Yan watched the expressions on Lin Qiu's face change—frowning one moment, sighing the next—wondering what difficult problem he had encountered.

Lin Qiu: "I'm thinking of making some food that isn't hot."

Lang Yan: "Don't spoil them."

Seeing his disdain, Lin Qiu bumped his shoulder against Lang Yan's arm; it was solid and burning hot.

He sat up straight, looked at his much sturdier frame, and said, "I'm just thinking about it; I don't even know if I can make it."

That said, after lunch, Lin Qiu went to find the priest.

The beastmen gathered plants according to the season; there were fewer tender leaves now, so they brought back many more fruits. Combined with the sweet grass, making sugar water was relatively easy.

After asking the priest, the materials for making ice jelly did exist.

The knowledge about plants accumulated by generations of priests couldn't be taught in a few months. Lin Qiu waited while the old priest flipped through some animal hides and took out a small bag for him.

"There's only this much."

The priest's cave was large, but it was so cluttered that this small bag was something the priest had dug out from the depths of the cave.

When Lin Qiu looked at it, it was long past its prime and had a musty smell.

"Priest, can this be found nearby?"

"No," the old priest said, "This was traded from the market a long time ago; it doesn't grow here."

Lin Qiu sat down on a pile of grass, "Then when will the market reopen?"

The old priest shook his head, "It's difficult."

Lin Qiu returned to the main cave, feeling dejected.

Because of the heat, the beastmen who had energy in the morning were now sprawled in their grass nests, not wanting to move.

Lin Qiu stepped lightly as he returned to his own grass nest.

Seeing the black wolf in the neighboring nest perk up his ears and turn his head to look, Lin Qiu pursed his lips at him.

A flicker of amusement crossed Lang Yan's eyes; he twitched his ears again and closed them to rest.

...

In the evening, the beastmen ate their final meal, packed some dried fish, and headed north.

Once they left, more than half of the beastmen were gone from Wolf Mountain.

Before it got dark, the beastmen took advantage of the lack of sun to cast a few more nets into the river, catching some fish to process immediately and hang under the sheds to dry.

Lin Qiu stepped on the low wall, responsible for tying the ropes and hanging the fish up.

The beastmen worked until it was completely dark before they finished hanging two rows of dried fish under the sheds.

Every beastman smelled of fish; wolf noses were sensitive, and they didn't like the scent, so they jumped into the small river one by one to bathe.

Lin Qiu sat on a rock in the river, watching the wolf pups roughhousing.

Having been bothered by the sun all day, they were now pushing each other underwater without holding back at all.

Lang Bing and Lang Rong were no match for Lang Jin, who grabbed them with one arm and dunked them into the water.

Before he could gloat, more pups emerged from the water and pounced on him. Lang Bing grabbed his ears, Lang Rong pressed down on his back, and they stirred the water into a muddy mess.

Lin Qiu got out of the river, not bothering to dry off.

The straw sandals on his feet were heavy with water. Lin Qiu walked slowly with his vest draped over his arm, one hand hanging at his side, palm open, letting the night breeze pass through his fingers—it felt somewhat cool.

Lin Qiu's long, wet hair was draped over his back, and the wind slowly dried the moisture from it.

"Qiu." Lang An caught up to him.

"Those little pups, they really need a good bath, the water is all muddy now." He laughed and scolded them, walking to Lin Qiu's side, "We're going into the forest to look for mushrooms tomorrow morning, want to come?"

Lin Qiu: "Yes."

"You have to get up very early."

Lin Qiu nodded, his voice clear and light, like a cool breeze in this hot summer night, which was very pleasant to hear, "If I can't wake up, An, give me a shout."

Lang An: "Alright, we have to leave as soon as the sky brightens, and we'll come back as soon as the sun rises, then we'll eat."

Lin Qiu: "Okay."

They would be picking mushrooms in the nearby forests. With the continuous rain over the past few days and the high temperatures, mushrooms hidden under the leaves had all sprouted.

The rainy season was the season for mushrooms.

The next day, before the sky was even light, Lin Qiu woke up.

Lang Xue was wrapped around his neck like a scarf, and the heat had woken him up.

Lin Qiu tilted his head back, moved the pup down, and placed him to the side.

Lang Xue rolled over, instantly turning into a fair, chubby little toddler. He wrapped his small hands around Lin Qiu's arm, pressed his forehead against it, and continued to sleep soundly.

Lin Qiu felt the dampness on his forehead and thought to himself that the pup didn't seem hot at all.

Outside the cave, the sky was turning a pale blue; dawn was approaching.

The wolf beastmen began to stir one after another, resting their heads on the edges of their grass nests, eyes opening and closing as they shook off their sleepiness.

Lin Qiu didn't go back to sleep either; looking at Lang Xue, who was occupying half of his grass nest, he helped wipe the sweat off the pup.

Even in human form, the pup looked like a two- or three-year-old human child, but with downy white hair, a round, bun-like face, and thick, short arms and legs—he was the cutest pup Lin Qiu had ever seen.

He remembered that Xue’s eyes seemed to be a bluish tint, much like Lang Bing’s.

Lin Qiu, with one arm held by the pup, didn't dare move, so he just took a fan and gently fanned him.

When the beastmen started getting up and Lang Guo came out to pick up the pup, Lin Qiu carefully pulled his arm away and whispered, "He's been in this form for a while."

Lang Guo: "He stayed in it longer this time."

Lin Qiu: "Then you watch him, I'm going."

Lang Guo picked up the pup, and Lang Xue didn't wake up at all. Lin Qiu paused, unable to help but rub his slightly sore arm.

The pup's sleep quality was certainly good.
chapters.source_text:
这场雨真如黑狼部落祭司所说，下了整整三天。
三天之后终于放晴，碧空澄澈，万里无云。
只半个上午，地面的雨水被蒸发，原本湿哒哒的棚子底下，立马干得走路一层灰。
待了几天山洞的兽人们受不了，这会儿也都出来了。
狼安指挥着狼莫小队赶紧起鱼笼，小狼们则分两队，一队跟着狼溶直奔地里查看尾巴草跟香草，一队跟着狼冰去林子里看种下去的草药。
老祭司杵着拐，也不乐意待山洞，便去地里。
兽人都有事忙，除了今天晚上即将出发狩猎采集的几个小队。
他们这会儿被狼岩强制按在山洞里补觉。
睡不着也得睡，不然晚上赶一夜的路，受不住。
林楸跟狼果也没闲着，一个去狼起那边织布，一个带着幼崽凑热闹，美其名曰早点学，等长大一点方便上手。
从小的到老的，没一个闲着。
东部大陆这边天气变化很大，连续下了几天大雨之后，阳光扯去了最后一层遮挡，落在身上不一会儿就觉烧灼，连兽人都避着了。
正午时候，狼山前头一片空地上，兽人们割掉的草被摊开晒着。
热浪浮动，草叶枯卷，兽人们忙了一会儿就大汗淋漓地奔回来。
天气炎热，保持兽形的兽人少了，大多维持人形，腰间围着一块兽皮。
光膀子，光脚丫，风风火火跑到棚子底下。
没坐一会儿，又嫌弃热了，尽数往山洞里钻。
林楸学了一会儿织布出来，狼安几个已经生起火来在做饭。
兽人额角都是汗，皮肤被热气熏得通红，围着腰间的那一圈兽皮边缘被洇湿，颜色都深了些。
坐在灶前烧火的狼雨跟狼虹，更是热得离灶孔远远的，伸长了手臂添柴。
林楸站在他们旁侧，挥了挥手上当扇子的树皮。
“呼——”兽人喟叹。
“楸，再快点儿。”
林楸干脆在一旁坐下来，摇着扇子，看狼安煮鱼汤。
天热，安他们更是不想折腾，什么能吃饱做什么，麻烦的一概不想碰。
狼安把该下锅的下锅，盖上盖子，到一旁矮墙倚着。身上汗珠不停往下滑，他恹恹道：“我都不想用火了。”
林楸：“山洞里会不会好一些？”
狼安看着林楸手中裁剪过形状，又用木柄固定过的树皮，热得无力，“除了大山洞，其他的都不顶用。”
“这才开始。”
“是啊，这才开始。”
见狼安盯着手中扇子，林楸递过去，打算再去做几把来。
狼安接过，对着脸跟颈侧用力地晃。风吹得头发跃动，狼安眯了眯眼，软了些身子彻底靠在矮墙上。
“楸……”狼雨有些怨念。
林楸起身，“我再去做。”
说着，也急急忙忙又去了狼起那边。
做木头活儿的山洞大，被兽人放了许多各式各样的木头。洞内四处散布着木屑，兽人就坐在地上，继续跟木头较劲儿。
第二台织机已经在开始做零部件了，角落里堆积了不少损坏的石斧石刀，兽人们席地而坐。
山洞比外面好一点，但兽人们也热。
狼木几个刚刚还出去捞了鱼笼，这会儿湿汗没干，往山洞里一走，身上裹满了木屑。
山洞里有织机响，为了尽快做出一匹布来，织机前几乎没断过兽人。
不过都是头一次干，那机器上的布紧密不一，也不规整，看得出来大家都是生手。
这会儿织机前忙活的是狼果，幼崽则在木屑堆里打滚。
也就他们不嫌热了。
狼果不怎么熟练地抛梭，看林楸来，目光看过去手上就得停下。
“楸，怎么又回来了？”
林楸：“再做几把扇子。”
扇子好做，他刚刚做第一遍的时候山洞里的兽人就看明白了，狼起直接从身后掏出来五六把，道：“楸，你先用。”
林楸：“你们什么时候做好的？”
狼果：“你刚刚走的时候。”
狼起那手速才叫快，拿了块树皮，用炭笔就那么随手一画，再用黑曜石刀一裁，扇面就做出来了。再用木条一框，夹上木柄，缠绕麻线加固一下，立马就成了。
狼果亲眼看见的，他分明第一次做，却像做了几十次一样。
反观狼木几个，狼起都连做三把，他们才弄出来一把。
这就是差距！
林楸：“起叔……算了，织机急用，先做这个。”
还有木桌、凳子，等兽人们有空再说吧。
狼起点头，闷头忙活手上的，没急问。
他性子稳得住，几十岁了总算找到自己的爱好跟擅长的，山洞一堆兽人里，属他最有干劲儿。
林楸抱着扇子出去，做饭的兽人一人分了一把。
瞧他们像看到救星一样，拿着扇子噗嗤噗嗤猛往脸上扇，狼安道：“这好东西，早该拿出来的。”
另几个兽人头发乱飞，偏着脸感受风，“要是能它自己一直动就更好了。”
林楸：“……想法挺好。”
但他做不出来。
天气热，兽人们都不乐意吃肉汤了。
他们性子急，容易烫嘴。
林楸听到山洞里时不时的轻嘶声，心里琢磨着还有什么能做来吃的。
天气热，兽人们就贪凉。
没有小麦，没有稻米，凉面凉皮也做不出来。
冰粉跟糖水倒是能想一想，雨季炎热，果子成熟得多，只需要找到硝石，他还能凑一碗冰沙糖水出来。
但这是小吃，哪能垫饱兽人的肚子。
“想什么？”狼岩看完了林楸脸上变化的表情，一会儿皱眉一会叹气，不知道遇到什么难事。
林楸：“想弄些不烫的食物。”
狼岩：“别惯着他们。”
林楸见他嫌弃，肩膀碰着狼岩胳膊，结结实实的，滚烫。
他坐直了，看他比自己壮实许多的身板，道：“我就随便想想，做不做得出来还不一定呢。”
话是这么说，午饭过后，林楸就去找了祭司。
兽人们采集植物都是顺应时节，这会儿嫩叶少了，采集回来的就多了不少果子。加上有甜草，吃糖水还算容易。
问过祭司，做冰粉的材料有倒是有。
世代祭司积累的关于植物的知识不是几个月能教完的，林楸等着老祭司翻了翻兽皮，给他拿出一小袋来。
“只有这么多。”
祭司山洞很大，但堆积的东西实在多，这一小袋还是祭司从洞深处翻出来的。
林楸一看，早不能用了，都有一股霉味儿。
“祭司，这附近能找到这个吗？”
“不能。”老祭司道，“这是以前从集市上交换回来的，这里没有。”
林楸往草团上一坐，“那什么时候才能重开集市？”
老祭司摇头，“难。”
林楸沮丧地回到大山洞。
天气热，兽人们上午还有活力，这会儿瘫在草窝里不想动了。
林楸脚步放轻，回到草窝。
目光看着隔壁草窝里黑狼扬起狼耳，转过脑袋看来，林楸冲他瘪了瘪嘴。
狼岩眼里闪过笑意，又颤了下耳朵，闭目养神。
……
傍晚，兽人们吃过最后一顿饭，带上些鱼干，往北而去。
他们一走，狼山少了大半的兽人。
天还没黑，兽人们趁着这会儿没太阳，赶紧又往河里下了几网，捞出些鱼来赶紧处理了，挂在棚子底下晒鱼干。
林楸踩着矮墙，负责套绳子，把鱼往上挂。
兽人忙到天黑尽，才将鱼干沿着棚子底下挂完两排。
兽人们各个身上都是鱼腥味，狼鼻子灵，不喜欢这味道，一个个径直跳进小河里洗澡去。
林楸坐在河里石头上，看小狼们打闹。
白日里太阳晒得烦了，现在一个个互相往水里按，一点不手软。
狼冰跟狼溶弄不过狼金，叫他一个胳膊就拉着往水里灌入。
他还没得意，水里冒出来更多小狼，全扑在他身上去。狼冰抓狼耳，狼溶压狼背，水都给他们搅浑了。
林楸上了岸，身上滴着水也没管。
脚上的草鞋湿了水有些重，林楸臂弯挂着刚刚洗过的背心，慢慢走着，一只手落在身侧，掌心摊开，夜风从指缝中穿过，有些凉意。
林楸湿透的长发散了满背，也被风吹着，慢慢散了水汽。
“楸。”狼安跟了上来。
“那群小狼崽子，好好洗个澡，水都被他们搅浑了。”他笑骂两声，走到了林楸身边，“明天早上我们要去林子里找蘑菇，去不去？”
林楸：“去。”
“要起来很早哦。”
林楸点头，声音清清淡淡，像这暑夜里送来的一阵凉风，听着很舒服，“我要是起不来，安叫我一声。”
狼安：“行，天一亮咱们就得出发，太阳出来立马回来，回来再吃饭。”
林楸：“好。”
采蘑菇就在附近这些林子，这几天连续下雨，温度又高，藏在树叶底下的蘑菇全冒出来了。
雨季是蘑菇的季节。
第二天天没亮，林楸先醒过来。
狼雪裹在他脖子上围了一圈，像戴着围脖，直接给他热醒了。
林楸仰头，将幼崽挪下来，放在侧边。
狼雪打个滚，一下变成个白嫩小娃娃，两个小手抱住他胳膊，额头抵着他手臂继续呼呼大睡。
林楸感受到他额头的湿润，还以为他不热呢。
洞外透着青色，快天亮了。
狼兽人们陆续翻身，脑袋搁在草窝边缘，眼皮一会儿睁一会儿闭，在醒神。
林楸也不睡了，看着占了自己一半草窝的狼雪，帮他擦了擦身上的汗。
幼崽变成人形也跟两三岁大的人类小孩一样，不过绒毛似的头发是白色，圆圆的包子脸，粗粗短短的胳膊腿儿，是林楸见过的最好看的幼崽。
他记得雪的眼睛好像也偏蓝，跟狼冰差不多。
林楸被他抱着一只胳膊，不敢动，只拿了扇子轻轻给他扇风。
等兽人们陆续起来，狼果出来抱幼崽，林楸才小心抽出手，轻声道：“变了有一会儿了。”
狼果：“这次持续时间长点。”
林楸：“那你看着，我走了。”
狼果抄起幼崽，怀里的狼雪一点没醒，林楸一顿，忍不住揉了揉有些酸的手。
幼崽的睡眠质量还是好。
chapters.title: 第77章

chapters.source_text:
早晨凉爽，地上是凝结的露珠，空气清新，四处是淡淡的草木香气。
一天之中，也只有这会儿还算舒服。
兽人们在狼山前集合，除了留下的狼木小队还有狼果、祭司，其他兽人差不多都背着藤筐来了。
狩猎跟采集队要两三天才能回来，这期间兽人们也不会干等着。
森林里蘑菇多，不用走远，大家尽可能多几个兽人过去，早去早回。
狼安一看兽人到齐了，把药粉一撒，清清爽爽的兽人身上立马弥漫着一股刺鼻的味道。
“阿嚏！”
“阿嚏！！！安，够了，别撒了。”
林楸鼻子也有点痒痒，不过忍住了。这药粉里有硫磺的味道，比当初他跟狼安四处撒的药粉味道还要重些。
“出发。”狼安将多余的药粉拍在自己身上，先一步跑出去。
林楸跟在后头，左边是狼莫，右边是狼西。
林楸看了眼狼西的腿，狼西小声道：“很近，我能跑。”
狼莫拍了下林楸胳膊，“放心，有我。”
林楸默默揉了揉，手劲儿忒大，他胳膊上一下起了个红色的巴掌印。
他看向兽人们奔跑的方向，前方林木苍翠，“是上次的黑树林？”
“对咯。”狼莫道。
跑了最多十五分钟，兽人们到了地方。
雨季植物疯长，这边的草木看着又高了一些。
兽人们停下，都在地上寻找趁手的木棍。林楸见状，直接将身边的矮树一压，一脚踩下去，折断了拿起来。
剔除树枝，木棍笔直。
狼莫看得眼馋，举着自己手上的枯木道：“楸，我跟你换。”
林楸瞥了眼，上面还有青苔。
“不换。”
“嗷……”狼莫失落。
前方，狼安交代了几句，叫大家注意虫子，随后分散开来。
狼安回头正想叫上林楸一起，见狼莫跟狼西围着，便专心找蘑菇去。
森林里蘑菇种类千百种，不同的区域，产出的蘑菇不同。
他们来了东部大陆十几年，祭司也挑选出了几种能吃的。
但有些蘑菇长得相似，兽人们分辨不清还容易吃出问题，所以大家很谨慎。
狼莫几个长年累月守着部落，采集次数很少，比不得亚兽人们认识蘑菇的数量。
林楸眼睁睁看着他们找准了一个倒在深草中的巨大枯木，枯木上生长着一种橘黄色的蘑菇，颜色鲜亮，很好看，在深绿色的草丛里惹眼极了。
林楸忙制止：“那个不能吃！”
狼莫抬头，眼神清澈，“不能吗？”
林楸：“应该不能。”
他对兽神大陆植物的了解大半来源于祭司，他还没学到蘑菇这一类，但那颜色那么毒。
不怕一万，就怕万一。
狼莫轻轻一掰，蘑菇掉下来。
“嘿，我还以为我看错了。楸，你放心，能吃。”
林楸：“要不问一问？”
狼莫双手齐上，几下掰了个干净，“不用问，我知道，这个叫金黄菇，能吃的，我们以前吃过。”
林楸看向狼西。
狼西曲着一条腿，正在掏树桩子底下的一丛褐色的蘑菇，有点像茶树菇。
算了，等会儿回去安他们肯定会挑选一遍。
蘑菇没煮，兽人总不能往嘴里塞……
林楸眼睁睁看着远处狼安抓了个白色蘑菇啃了一口。
他心口堵了下，抓着木棍，默默换个地方找去。
雨季正是出蘑菇的盛期，林间露珠刚散，兽人们藤筐就装了一半，待到太阳出来，林子里光斑刺眼时，大多兽人的藤筐已经装不下来。
狼嚎断断续续响起，林楸扯下最后一丛木耳，放入背篓，与兽人们汇合。
木耳厚实，大的赶得上他手掌大。吸饱了水，软弹诱人。
林楸背篓里大多都是这个，他认识的蘑菇不多，怕摘了毒蘑菇，白走一趟。
回去路上，狼莫身上左右两边各搭着一个藤筐。
林楸看了眼，红的、白的、紫的、蓝的，什么漂亮采什么。
林楸盯着藤筐里许久，问：“莫，你确定都能吃？”
狼莫：“能啊，你放心，吃不死的。”
林楸：或许是他真的不了解这里的蘑菇……
汇合途中，兽人从四面八方过来，有的甚至找到西边林子里去了。林楸往前走，眼前黑影一晃，忽然被狼西拉着往后一拽。
与此同时，狼莫抄起木棍一拍，道：“差点，差点……”
林楸看到那挂在树上被拍晕的蛇，鳞片青白，肚腹一节一节白色，他心里发毛，打了个寒战。
“快走。”
狼莫还想用木棍把长虫掏下来，狼西抓着他，示意他看林楸的脸。
煞白！
狼莫立马跟狼西一左一右，拽着林楸离开，嘴上还不停道：“没事，不就一小长虫，虽然很嫩，但肉少。”
狼西绕过林楸拧他胳膊。
狼莫龇牙，嘿嘿一笑，“楸，你为什么怕这个呀？”
林楸：“被咬过。”
“啊？！没事吧！”
林楸：“还行。”
就是小时候在他爷奶家被咬的，爷奶家是老式的砖瓦房，有些年头了。他当是在屋里睡得好好的，不知道怎么钻进来一条。
他至今记得他滑溜溜的鳞片爬过自己脖子，他吓得伸手去抓，然后挨了一口……林楸狠狠闭了闭眼，又一股寒战。
一朝被蛇咬，阴影两辈子。
“怎么了这是？”
林楸被架着出来，脸色不怎么好看，吓得狼安立马抓过他检查。
狼莫：“遇到长虫，楸被吓到了。”
“没被咬吧？”
“没有。”狼西往狼莫身上一挂，腿儿抖了抖。
狼安：“雨季就是多这些，咱们赶紧回。”
有兽人要来扶他，林楸道：“我没事。”就是刚刚狼莫跟狼西招呼都不打一声就抓着他跑，他没反应过来，路还是能走的。
赶着出了林子，回到棚子底下。
这会儿阳光还没照进来，狼安示意兽人们将蘑菇往地上倒。
林楸扫了眼，起码二十多种。
兽人们拿了小刀来，坐在地上开始处理。先刮掉泥脚，再破开看看有没有虫子。
林楸：“这些都能吃？”
狼安笃定：“能。”
林楸还没松口气，狼安：“就是有的吃了会犯困，不过没事，睡一觉就好了。”
林楸汗毛都竖起来了。
不是能吃，是毒不死！
“不行！”
兽人们抬头，迷茫地看着林楸
“楸，什么不行？”狼雨问。
林楸：“犯困是中毒了，这种不能吃的。一次两次吃不死，但谁知道第三次会不会……”
狼安看着一堆颜色鲜艳的蘑菇，说心里话，“长得好看的越好吃。”
林楸：“……”
“咱们要不还是找祭司挑挑吧。”
狼安见林楸紧绷的脸，想着大家都是吃一锅的，楸之前没跟他们一起吃过，万一吃出毛病……
只犹豫了下，狼安去请祭司下来。
老祭司撑着两麻杆似的腿，身上挂着空空荡荡的兽皮，手上拐杖撑着，颤颤巍巍。
“不是说了，别顾着往好看的采。”
狼兽人：“不都一样。”
一样个屁！
祭司气得吹胡子，干脆坐下来，拐杖指一个蘑菇，就叫兽人们找出来全扔了。
拐杖指了七八下，一堆蘑菇一下少了一半。
兽人们耷拉脑袋，肚子里开始咕咕叫了。
“祭司，不够吃了。”狼莫说着，把那橘黄色的蘑菇捡回来，试图悄悄塞进蘑菇堆里。
祭司看见，一拐杖给他打去。
“缺你吃的了？”
“以前是没得选，吃不死也偶尔吃一点，睡一觉不那么难受。”也是怕兽人们饥饿久了，一直绷紧着会崩溃。现在有食物了，谁还那么干？！
“以后这些都不许要。”祭司道。
林楸悄然松了一口气。
剩下的蘑菇不多，兽人们几下就弄完了。祭司也不走，就在这地方守着。
林楸带上还剩下点青草的藤筐，去喂红鸟。
狼莫跟狼西见状，立即跟上。
“楸，红鸟怎么还没生蛋啊？”狼西挂在狼莫背上，问道。
林楸：“不知道。”
兽人才到门口，红鸟像是知道要放饭，嘶叫着跑过来。
“吸溜……”
林楸已经习惯兽人们对着红鸟流口水。
“我进去看看。”
他打开围栏往棚子里走，棚子里还算干净，林楸一眼看见窝里的青色的蛋。他摸了一下，还是温热的。
林楸一喜，又看了眼其他草窝，又发现一个。
原来带崽的红鸟才把小红鸟带出来，应该还不会生，这两个蛋肯定是狼莫后头抓回来的红鸟生的。
林楸没拿走，当引蛋放着，等明天来再看看有没有。
“楸，蛋！你放回去干什么？”门口，两个脑袋支棱着，眼睛像通了电的灯泡，亮得刺眼。
林楸：“看它们还生不生。”
圈里，原来那只没被吃的公红鸟羽毛又长出来了，红得像朝阳，身体也格外健壮。
“不生也可以吃啊。”
林楸：“不够分，再攒攒。”
本来想让红鸟再孵几窝蛋，但答应了狼西的，先吃一点也没什么。而且祭司说红鸟要雨季过后才会再次孵蛋，那就先吃吧。
“要攒几天？”狼西眼巴巴问。
那嘴角口水成丝儿了，叫他一下吸溜回去，是真馋了。
林楸：“大概十个，三五天吧。”
“那我看着。”狼西道。
林楸点头。
看吧看吧，天气热，红鸟蛋也不能多放，攒一攒就吃了。
回到棚子底下，兽人们等林楸回来呢。
狼安见狼莫跟狼西喜气洋洋的，道：“什么事儿这么高兴？”
“红鸟生蛋了。”
“生蛋……蛋？！还真生了！”兽人们放下东西就往西边林子去。
林楸站在灶台边，面对着两个陶盆里洗干净的蘑菇，缓缓抬头。
“蛋……好看？”
狼莫一脸高深莫测，摇头道：“楸，你不懂……”
狼西：“你懂。”
狼莫嘻嘻一笑，嘴角咧开，一副不值钱的样子。
“我们以前养过猎物，红鸟也养过，不说养到它生蛋，养个十天不到就会养死。”红鸟能生蛋了，就代表它在这个环境中愿意繁衍。
那他们就有希望培育出下一代的红鸟，乃至下下一代，下下下一代。
可以想象，未来那西边林子的围栏里，挤满了红鸟。
狼莫露出憨笑来。
狼西翻个白眼，道：“楸，我猜安想问你蘑菇怎么吃？我饿了……”
林楸不纠结这个问题了，看着一堆蘑菇，早饭没吃他现在也饿。
扫了眼棚子底下的鱼，这些鱼干不能动，还得做更多一些，留做兽人们外出捕猎的补给……
“捞点鱼来。”
“嗷！”狼莫吆喝上小队成员，立即去干。
等兽人们欢欢喜喜回来，对着林楸跟看宝贝似的，看得林楸不自在。
狼安道：“好了，干活儿！还饿不饿了？”
“饿了！”
狼安笑着看林楸，目光慈爱得不得了。他道：“楸，蘑菇怎么做？”
林楸：“切片，爆炒。再一部分煮鱼汤，跟之前那些野菜没什么两样。”
“行，我来。”狼安搬过来菜板，招呼来四个兽人赶紧切。
林楸示范了一下，兽人们麻利地干活，然后时不时再看他一眼。
林楸不得不提醒：“注意手。”
狼安：“放心，他们不会。”
林楸见他嘴角就没下去过，无奈道：“安，你别这样看我，红鸟是你们跟我一起养的，跟你们以前养有什么区别？就是运气好。”
狼安：“才不是。”
“我们以前……”狼安都有些想不清楚他们以前是怎么养的了，但他可以肯定的是，没有兽人养个猎物像林楸这么仔细的。
又是修棚子，又是每天送草送小鱼小虾，还会给它们清理住的地方。
像这样天气热了，还问祭司要了草药，给它们煮水。
兽人养幼崽的没这样仔细。
“要是这群红鸟不动，养到雨季过后起码要再孵三窝小红鸟出来，再养到冬季去……”狼安只要一想到冬季还有新鲜的肉吃，就忍不住笑。
chapters.translated_text:
The morning was cool, with dew condensed on the ground, the air was fresh, and a faint scent of grass and trees lingered everywhere.

Of all the times in the day, only this moment could be considered comfortable.

The beastmen gathered in front of Wolf Mountain. Aside from the remaining Langmu squad, Langguo, and the priest, almost all other beastmen came carrying rattan baskets.

The hunting and gathering teams would take two or three days to return, and the beastmen wouldn't just sit around waiting during this time.

There were many mushrooms in the forest, so there was no need to go far. Everyone gathered as many beastmen as possible to go and return early.

As soon as Langan saw that the beastmen had arrived, he sprinkled some medicinal powder, and a pungent odor immediately permeated the fresh-smelling beastmen.

"Achoo!"

"Achoo!!! An, that’s enough, stop sprinkling."

Lin Qiu’s nose was also a bit itchy, but he held it back. This powder had the smell of sulfur, even stronger than the powder he and Langan had sprinkled around before.

"Let's go." Langan patted the excess powder onto himself and ran out first.

Lin Qiu followed behind, with Langmo on his left and Langxi on his right.

Lin Qiu glanced at Langxi’s leg, and Langxi whispered, "It’s very close, I can run."

Langmo patted Lin Qiu’s arm, "Don't worry, I'm here."

Lin Qiu rubbed his arm silently; the man’s grip was too strong, leaving a red handprint on his arm instantly.

He looked in the direction the beastmen were running, where the forest ahead was lush and green, "Is it the black forest from last time?"

"That's right," Langmo said.

After running for at most fifteen minutes, the beastmen arrived at the destination.

Plants grew wildly during the rainy season, and the vegetation here looked even taller.

The beastmen stopped and began searching the ground for suitable wooden sticks. Seeing this, Lin Qiu pressed down on a small tree nearby, stepped on it, snapped it, and picked it up.

After trimming the branches, the wooden stick was straight.

Langmo looked on with envy, holding his own piece of dead wood, and said, "Qiu, let's trade."

Lin Qiu glanced at it; there was still moss on it.

"No trade."

"Awoo..." Langmo felt disappointed.

Ahead, Langan gave a few instructions, telling everyone to watch out for insects, and then they dispersed.

Langan turned back, intending to call Lin Qiu to join him, but seeing Langmo and Langxi surrounding him, he focused on finding mushrooms instead.

There are thousands of types of mushrooms in the forest, and different areas produce different kinds.

They had been in the Eastern Continent for over a dozen years, and the priest had selected a few types that were safe to eat.

However, some mushrooms looked similar, and the beastmen couldn't distinguish them easily, which could lead to problems, so everyone was very cautious.

Langmo and the others had guarded the tribe for years and rarely went gathering, so they didn't know as many mushrooms as the beast-women.

Lin Qiu watched as they spotted a huge dead log lying in the deep grass, on which grew a type of orange mushroom. The color was bright and beautiful, standing out strikingly in the deep green grass.

Lin Qiu quickly stopped them: "That one can't be eaten!"

Langmo looked up, his eyes clear, "It can't?"

Lin Qiu: "It probably can't."

Most of his knowledge about the plants of the Beast God Continent came from the priest, and he hadn't learned about mushrooms yet, but that color looked so poisonous.

Better safe than sorry.

Langmo broke it off gently, and the mushroom fell.

"Hey, I thought I was wrong. Qiu, don't worry, it's edible."

Lin Qiu: "Should we ask someone?"

Langmo used both hands and broke them all off in a few movements, "No need to ask, I know this. It's called a golden mushroom, it's edible, we've eaten it before."

Lin Qiu looked at Langxi.

Langxi was bending one leg, digging out a cluster of brown mushrooms from under a tree stump; they looked a bit like tea tree mushrooms.

Never mind, An and the others would definitely sort through them later.

The mushrooms weren't cooked, so the beastmen couldn't just shove them into their mouths...

Lin Qiu watched helplessly as Langan in the distance grabbed a white mushroom and took a bite.

His chest felt tight; he gripped his wooden stick and silently moved to another spot to search.

The rainy season was the peak period for mushrooms. Just as the dew in the forest dissipated, the beastmen’s rattan baskets were already half full. By the time the sun came out and the light spots in the forest became blinding, most of the beastmen's baskets were already overflowing.

Wolf howls echoed intermittently. Lin Qiu pulled off the last cluster of wood ear mushrooms, put them into his basket, and joined the other beastmen.

The wood ear mushrooms were thick, with the large ones reaching the size of his palm. Soaked with water, they were soft, springy, and tempting.

Lin Qiu’s basket was mostly filled with these. He didn't know many mushrooms and was afraid of picking poisonous ones, which would make the trip a waste.

On the way back, Langmo had a rattan basket slung on each side of his body.

Lin Qiu took a look—red, white, purple, blue; he picked whatever looked pretty.

Lin Qiu stared at the basket for a long time and asked, "Mo, are you sure all of these are edible?"

Langmo: "Yes, don't worry, they won't kill you."

Lin Qiu: Perhaps he really didn't understand the mushrooms here...

On the way to the meeting point, beastmen came from all directions; some had even found their way to the western forest. As Lin Qiu walked forward, a black shadow flashed before his eyes, and he was suddenly pulled backward by Langxi.

At the same time, Langmo swung his wooden stick and struck, saying, "Close, that was close..."

Lin Qiu saw the snake hanging from the tree that had been knocked unconscious. Its scales were greenish-white, and its belly had white segments. He felt his skin crawl and shivered.

"Let's go, quickly."

Langmo still wanted to use his stick to poke the snake down, but Langxi grabbed him and signaled him to look at Lin Qiu’s face.

It was deathly pale!

Langmo immediately went to one side of Lin Qiu, and Langxi to the other, dragging him away while saying, "It's fine, it's just a small snake. Although it's tender, there's not much meat on it."

Langxi reached around Lin Qiu and pinched Langmo's arm.

Langmo bared his teeth and gave a silly grin, "Qiu, why are you afraid of this?"

Lin Qiu: "I've been bitten before."

"Ah?! Are you okay!"

Lin Qiu: "I'm fine."

It happened when he was a child at his grandparents' house. Their house was an old-fashioned brick building that had been around for many years. He was sleeping soundly in the room when, somehow, a snake crawled in.

He still remembered the feeling of its slippery scales crawling over his neck. He reached out to grab it in fear, and then he got bitten... Lin Qiu closed his eyes tightly and shivered again.

Once bitten by a snake, the trauma lasts for two lifetimes.

"What's wrong?"

Lin Qiu was being carried out, his face looking quite poor, which scared Langan into immediately grabbing him to check.

Langmo: "We ran into a snake, and Qiu was scared."

"You weren't bitten, were you?"

"No." Langxi hung onto Langmo, his legs trembling slightly.

Langan: "There are just so many of these in the rainy season, let's head back quickly."

Some beastmen wanted to help him, but Lin Qiu said, "I'm fine." It was just that Langmo and Langxi had grabbed him and run without warning, so he hadn't reacted in time, but he could still walk.

They hurried out of the forest and returned under the shed.

The sun hadn't reached them yet, so Langan signaled the beastmen to dump the mushrooms onto the ground.

Lin Qiu scanned them; there were at least twenty different kinds.

The beastmen took small knives and sat on the ground to start processing them. First, they scraped off the muddy stems, then split them open to check for insects.

Lin Qiu: "Are all of these edible?"

Langan was certain: "Yes."

Before Lin Qiu could breathe a sigh of relief, Langan added: "It's just that some will make you sleepy after eating, but it's fine, you'll be okay after a nap."

Lin Qiu’s hair stood on end.

It wasn't that they were edible; it was that they weren't lethal!

"No way!"

The beastmen looked up, staring at Lin Qiu in confusion.

"Qiu, what's wrong?" Langyu asked.

Lin Qiu: "Feeling sleepy means you've been poisoned; these kinds cannot be eaten. You might not die the first or second time, but who knows about the third..."

Langan looked at the pile of brightly colored mushrooms and spoke his heart, "The ones that look good taste better."

Lin Qiu: "..."

"How about we ask the priest to pick them out?"

Seeing Lin Qiu’s tense face, Langan thought about how everyone ate from the same pot, and Qiu hadn't eaten with them before. If something went wrong...

After only a moment's hesitation, Langan went to invite the priest down.

The old priest leaned on his legs, which looked like hemp stalks, wearing loose animal skins, and supported himself with a cane, trembling as he walked.

"Didn't I tell you not to just pick the ones that look good?"

Beastman: "Aren't they all the same?"

Same my ass!

The priest was so angry his beard puffed out. He simply sat down, pointed his cane at a mushroom, and told the beastmen to find them all and throw them away.

After the cane pointed seven or eight times, the pile of mushrooms was suddenly cut in half.

The beastmen hung their heads, their stomachs starting to growl.

"Priest, there isn't enough to eat." Langmo said, picking up the orange mushroom and trying to sneak it back into the pile.

The priest saw him and hit him with his cane.

"Are you starving?"

"Before, we had no choice. Even if it wouldn't kill us, we'd eat a little occasionally, and it wasn't too bad after a nap." He was also afraid that if the beastmen were hungry for too long, they would break down from the constant tension. Now that there was food, who would still do that?!

"From now on, none of these are allowed." The priest said.

Lin Qiu breathed a quiet sigh of relief.

There weren't many mushrooms left, and the beastmen finished processing them quickly. The priest didn't leave either, staying there to watch.

Lin Qiu took the rattan basket that still had some grass in it and went to feed the red birds.

Seeing this, Langmo and Langxi immediately followed.

"Qiu, why haven't the red birds laid eggs yet?" Langxi asked, hanging on Langmo's back.

Lin Qiu: "I don't know."

As soon as the beastmen reached the entrance, the red birds seemed to know it was feeding time and ran over, screeching.

"Slurp..."

Lin Qiu was already used to the beastmen drooling over the red birds.

"I'm going in to take a look."

He opened the fence and walked into the shed. The shed was still clean, and Lin Qiu spotted a greenish egg in the nest at a glance. He touched it; it was still warm.

Lin Qiu was delighted and checked the other grass nests, finding another one.

It turned out that the red bird with the chicks had only just brought them out and shouldn't be laying yet; these two eggs must have been laid by the red birds Langmo had brought back later.

Lin Qiu didn't take them, leaving them as decoy eggs to see if there would be more tomorrow.

"Qiu, eggs! Why did you put them back?" At the entrance, two heads poked in, their eyes like electrified light bulbs, shining blindingly bright.

Lin Qiu: "To see if they'll lay more."

In the pen, the male red bird that hadn't been eaten had grown its feathers back; it was as red as the morning sun and its body was exceptionally robust.

"We can eat them even if they don't lay more."

Lin Qiu: "Not enough to share, let's save up some more."

He had originally wanted to let the red birds hatch a few more clutches, but he had promised Langxi, so eating a little wouldn't hurt. Besides, the priest said the red birds wouldn't hatch eggs again until after the rainy season, so they might as well eat them.

"How many days do we have to save them?" Langxi asked eagerly.

Drool was forming at the corner of his mouth, and he sucked it back in—he was truly craving them.

Lin Qiu: "About ten, maybe three or five days."

"Then I'll watch them." Langxi said.

Lin Qiu nodded.

Watch them, watch them. The weather was hot, and red bird eggs couldn't be kept for long, so they would eat them once they saved up enough.

Returning under the shed, the beastmen were waiting for Lin Qiu.

Langan saw Langmo and Langxi looking jubilant and asked, "What are you so happy about?"

"The red birds laid eggs."

"Laid eggs... eggs?! They really laid them!" The beastmen put down their things and headed toward the western forest.

Lin Qiu stood by the stove, facing the cleaned mushrooms in two pottery basins, and slowly looked up.

"Eggs... are they that good?"

Langmo had a mysterious expression and shook his head, "Qiu, you don't understand..."

Langxi: "You understand."

Langmo gave a silly grin, his mouth stretching wide, looking quite priceless.

"We've kept prey before, and we've kept red birds too. Not to mention getting them to lay eggs, they would usually die within ten days of being kept." The fact that the red birds could lay eggs meant they were willing to reproduce in this environment.

That meant they had hope of raising the next generation of red birds, and even the next, and the next.

One could imagine that in the future, the fence in the western forest would be crowded with red birds.

Langmo broke into a simple, honest smile.

Langxi rolled his eyes and said, "Qiu, I guess An wants to ask you how to cook the mushrooms? I'm hungry..."

Lin Qiu stopped dwelling on that question. Looking at the pile of mushrooms, he was hungry too, having skipped breakfast.

He glanced at the fish under the shed. These dried fish couldn't be touched; they needed to make more to keep as supplies for the beastmen when they went out hunting...

"Go catch some fish."

"Awoo!" Langmo shouted to his squad members, and they immediately went to do it.

When the beastmen returned happily, they looked at Lin Qiu as if he were a treasure, which made Lin Qiu feel uncomfortable.

Langan said, "Alright, get to work! Are you still hungry?"

"Hungry!"

Langan looked at Lin Qiu with a smile, his gaze incredibly affectionate. He said, "Qiu, how do we cook the mushrooms?"

Lin Qiu: "Slice them and stir-fry them. Use some for fish soup; it's no different from the wild vegetables we had before."

"Alright, I'll do it." Langan moved the cutting board over and called four beastmen to start cutting quickly.

Lin Qiu demonstrated once, and the beastmen worked efficiently, glancing at him from time to time.

Lin Qiu had to remind them: "Watch your hands."

Langan: "Don't worry, they won't."

Seeing that the smile never left Langan's face, Lin Qiu said helplessly, "An, don't look at me like that. You raised the red birds with me; what's the difference from what you did before? It's just good luck."

Langan: "It's not."

"We used to..." Langan couldn't even clearly recall how they used to raise them, but he was certain that no beastman had ever raised prey as carefully as Lin Qiu.

He built the shed, delivered grass and small fish and shrimp every day, and even cleaned their living space.

When the weather got hot like this, he even asked the priest for medicinal herbs to boil water for them.

Even beastmen raising their own cubs weren't this careful.

"If this group of red birds stays, at least three more clutches of chicks will hatch after the rainy season, and then we'll raise them until winter..." Just thinking about having fresh meat to eat in the winter made Langan unable to stop smiling.
chapters.title: 第78章

chapters.translated_text:
The stir-fried mushrooms had nothing added to them. After being flash-fried over high heat, they quickly softened and released their juices. All that was needed was a bowl of rice...

Lin Qiu chewed silently on the slightly chewy mixed mushrooms. Even though nothing had been added, they were full of fresh sweetness.

The beastmen slurped the mushrooms as if they were eating noodles. Even the fish weren't selling as well as before; the mixed mushrooms in the bowls were always the first to be scooped up.

Lang Guo was busy looking after the cubs and hadn't seen how the beastmen prepared the food. He pushed down the raised heads of the cubs, telling them to eat their own meat paste, while opening his own mouth wide and stuffing it full.

The fresh sweetness of the mushrooms danced on his tongue; that dull, earthy taste the beastmen often talked about was completely gone. Lang Guo wondered aloud, "Qiu, did you add sweet grass?"

Lin Qiu: "No."

Lang Guo: "Then why is there a sweet taste, and why does it make me want to eat more the more I have?"

He leaned over to look at the clay pot not far away. The juices had been scraped clean, and some beastmen even wanted to hug the pot and lick it, only to be tapped on the forehead by Lang An with a ladle.

Lin Qiu: "It comes from the mushrooms themselves."

Mushrooms enhance umami, and since they were produced in large quantities during the rainy season, he could select a few suitable varieties, dry them, and grind them into powder to use as a seasoning.

That was another seasoning added to the list.

After eating this meal of mushrooms, the beastmen were clearly more enthusiastic about foraging. After consulting with the priest, Lin Qiu selected two or three completely non-toxic varieties and told the beastmen to gather more.

Because of the high temperature, the sliced mushrooms dried out completely in two or three days. Once ground into powder, whether used in soup or stir-fries, adding just a little bit would impart that fresh, sweet flavor, even if it wasn't mushroom soup.

The beastmen's eyes lit up; they even started adding it to their cold-tossed dishes.

The hunting and gathering team had been gone for three days. When they returned, the clay pots on Lang Mountain were boiling mushrooms, the winnowing baskets on the low walls were drying mushrooms, and the sound of beastmen grinding mushrooms echoed throughout the mountain.

The hunting team felt guilty; if they hadn't returned late, the beastmen wouldn't have had to eat this every day. Look at them, their companions were all... crazy?

Had they eaten too many mushrooms? They had returned with prey, yet not a single wolf came over; everyone was staring at the mushrooms in the pot. Aside from a bit of fish, it was all mushrooms.

And they were all dark and murky. With little fish and so many mushrooms, the beastmen felt uneasy.

Could it be that there wasn't much fish, and they had been made stupid by eating mushrooms?

"King?" The beastmen looked toward Lang Yan.

All beastmen knew that you couldn't eat too many mushrooms or eat them indiscriminately because they were poisonous. In the past, they ate them out of necessity, but now, if there wasn't enough fish, why would they eat so many?

Inside the cave, Lang Mo, who was grinding mushroom powder, heard the commotion and called the other beastmen to go out and welcome them.

Lang Mo wagged his tongue like a puppy and came running on all fours.

The team members followed behind, hurriedly taking the prey the beastmen had brought back before excitedly running back.

The neglected hunting team: "..."

Lang Yan wasn't one of those silly wolves who liked to overthink things. He walked calmly under the shed. When Lang An saw them, he said happily, "King, the mushrooms were all selected by the priest. They are non-toxic and taste very good."

"Hmm."

They had traveled through the night to return, and it just happened to be the tribe's breakfast time. Lang Yan was tired. Seeing Lin Qiu also come out of the cave, his brow relaxed, and he approached with a slow, somewhat lazy gait.

When Lin Qiu saw him, a smile touched his eyes—shallow and cool like morning mist, instantly smoothing out the irritability in the humid, stuffy air.

Lang Yan stopped altogether.

His gray eyes followed Lin Qiu until he stood right in front of him. Lang Yan lowered his gaze to see his delicate features and snow-white face.

"You're back," Lin Qiu said.

Lang Yan: "Caught six bleat-beasts."

He stood in a relaxed posture, rarely appearing so lazy. His long eyelashes were half-lowered, his eyes showing some fatigue, his gaze completely enveloping the person in front of him.

"Caught that many?" Lin Qiu was curious. "I'll go take a look."

Lang Yan moved his long legs, blocking his path.

Lin Qiu's height of 1.8 meters wasn't short, but being this close to Lang Yan, he had to look up to see his face.

Lin Qiu: "?"

Lang Yan: "There is one..."

"King! What should we do about that pregnant bleat-beast?" Lang Mo came running over in a hurry, shouting before he even arrived.

Lang Yan: "Let the priest take a look."

"Awoo!" Lang Mo braked hard, turned around, and ran toward the priest's cave.

Seeing Lin Qiu's confusion, Lang Yan told him, "Beastmen generally don't hunt pregnant females, but that bleat-beast was abandoned by its herd."

"Why?"

Lang Yan: "Because its cub couldn't be born, and the mother was dying."

"I'll go take a look."

Seeing his persistence, Lang Yan stepped aside and followed behind Lin Qiu, who was moving with wind at his heels.

A mother animal giving birth is a tragic sight; amniotic fluid mixed with blood, accompanied by the cub spilling out. Mixed with the stench, it made the wolf-beastmen stay far away.

The old priest was carried down by Lang Mo; the mother animal was already failing.

But as it lay on the ground, it still struggled, moaning incessantly. Its eyes were as clean as a snowfield, filled with a plea toward this group of predators.

The beastmen pressed their wolf ears against their heads, unable to bear watching.

They gradually moved away.

Although their relationship was that of predator and prey, beastmen revered nature and believed they were no different from these animals; it was just the law of the jungle, the law of nature.

Some beastmen left, leaving only a few to stand guard.

The old priest looked into those eyes and told Lang Bing to bring the herbs used for difficult births in beastmen and fed them to it.

Lin Qiu hurried over, with Lang Yan following behind him the whole time.

He asked, "What will happen to that pregnant bleat-beast in the end?"

Lang Yan: "If the priest can save it, it will live, and we will let them go back. If not, we can only eat it."

As they spoke, they arrived at the spot.

A thick, pungent smell floated in the hot, humid air. The remaining beastmen covered their noses, at a loss for what to do.

The herbs had been fed, but how could they take effect so quickly?

"Priest."

The old priest shook his head. "It's been too long."

As soon as Lin Qiu arrived, he saw the two little legs of the bleat-beast cub dragging from the mother's abdomen. Hearing the priest's words, he stepped forward without a second thought.

Lang Yan grabbed his arm. "Don't go."

Lin Qiu grabbed him back. "Let me try, you help me."

Lang Yan: "Okay."

"Qiu!"

Lin Qiu: "It's fine, the King is with me."

Lin Qiu approached, and the bleat-beast lying on the ground moved. Lin Qiu whispered, "I'm helping you, don't kick me."

He grabbed the little bleat-beast's feet; the warm, soft sensation made Lin Qiu stiffen. Watching Lang Yan hold down the mother's front limbs, he mimicked the techniques he remembered from herdsmen delivering lambs and began to exert force.

The bleat-beast's presentation was breech; he needed to straighten the hooves that were wedged against the exit. Lin Qiu gritted his teeth and, holding his breath, reached his hand inside.

The bleat-beast kicked twice, but it didn't even have the strength to struggle.

The onlookers didn't know why Qiu was doing that, but seeing his solemn and serious face, they couldn't help but clench their hands, watching with fear and tension.

He had to be fast; he didn't know how long the little bleat-beast had been suffocating inside.

As the mother bleat-beast raised its head and let out a mournful cry, Lin Qiu slowly applied force, and with a splash—

"It's, it's out! It's out!"

The beastmen didn't have time to be happy before they saw Lin Qiu kneeling on the ground, wiping the little bleat-beast's mouth clean with his palm.

It wasn't moving.

Was it dead?

The old priest looked at the mother animal breathing rapidly on the ground and gripped his staff tightly. "Bing, hurry and get the medicine from the top of the shelf!"

"Lang Mo! Get some grass!"

"Yes!" Lang Mo ran off in a panic.

The little bleat-beast in his arms was steaming hot. As the beastmen approached, Lin Qiu said, "Stay back, don't get anything on you."

"Need animal skin!"

Someone handed over an animal skin. Lin Qiu wiped the little bleat-beast's mouth and nose; it had been too long, and it had inhaled too much amniotic fluid.

He performed CPR while trying to shake the fluid out.

Lin Qiu's hands were shaking, but his mind was extremely calm.

Lang Yan grabbed his trembling hands. "Let me."

He was strong; even though he had stayed up all night, holding a little bleat-beast was effortless for him.

Lin Qiu: "Hot water, animal skin! Priest, the mother bleat-beast..."

The old priest said, "It's fine, don't worry."

Life is fragile, yet tenacious. The little bleat-beast was out, and with the pill given to the mother, it should be fine.

But the little bleat-beast...

It had been so long, and there was still no movement.

The old priest watched Lang Yan's technique and sighed inwardly. If it were that easy to save...

"It's alive! It's alive!"

"It moved!"

Lang Bing had just fed the pill to the mother when he suddenly heard a cheer. He turned his head and saw the little bleat-beast in Lang Yan's hands move its legs and let out a weak cry.

He looked at Lin Qiu in utter astonishment.

The beastmen cheered; the ones who had just dispersed were all gathered around again, though no one knew when they had returned.

Lin Qiu wet an animal skin, wrung it out, and quickly wiped the little bleat-beast clean.

He placed the little bleat-beast beside the mother and watched as she gently licked the cub's head. He let out a sigh of relief, his legs turning to jelly.

Lang Yan caught him. "What do we do next?"

Lin Qiu: "Keep it warm, food..."

Lang Yan lowered his eyes; the arm in his palm was still trembling slightly.

Lang Yan: "I'll arrange it, go wash up."

Lin Qiu: "Okay, be careful, don't let those things get into your eyes or mouth."

"Hmm."

Lin Qiu went to the river to wash his hands clean and used the remaining hot water to take a bath. He changed out of his animal skin clothes, washed them, and hung them up to dry before going to check on the bleat-beasts.

The beastmen had already moved the bleat-beasts into the cave, where they had laid down dry grass and provided green grass and water.

The mother seemed to have regained some strength and was standing on the inner side, letting the wolf-beastmen help the little bleat-beast feed.

The little bleat-beast was still very weak, kneeling and lying down, unable to stand.

The priest said, "You've got guts."

Lin Qiu: "I was too anxious, I didn't think about anything. Priest, what was the pill you fed the bleat-beast?"

The priest: "Nothing special, just ordinary pills."

"Let's go, fewer beastmen should come here; bleat-beasts are timid."

It started raining again. Lin Qiu stepped on the slippery path down the mountain and almost landed on his butt in the mud. Lang Bing caught him. "Can't your claws grip the ground?"

As he spoke, he looked at the straw sandals on Lin Qiu's feet. "How... how did you think of saving the bleat-beast like that?"

The little wolf's hair was messy, but he didn't care about the rain hitting his face. He grabbed Lin Qiu, his eyes full of curiosity.

Lin Qiu: "I didn't think; if the little bleat-beast didn't come out, both of them would have died."

That bloody scene—even the wolf-beastmen didn't dare reach out easily, yet this seemingly weak beastman dared to.

The little wolf was thoroughly impressed.

Lin Qiu: "How much longer are you going to drag me through the rain?"

Lang Bing: "I'm afraid you'll fall."

Regardless, Lang Bing held onto Lin Qiu tightly for the rest of the walk down the mountain.
chapters.title: 第79章
chapters.source_text:
炒蘑菇什么都没加，经大火爆炒，蘑菇快速变软，汤汁渗透出来，只需要一碗大米饭……
林楸默默嚼着有点韧劲儿的炒杂菇，里面什么都没放，却满是鲜甜。
兽人跟吸溜汤面一样吸溜蘑菇，鱼都没以前那么好卖，碗里的杂菇先被捞了个遍。
狼果忙着带幼崽，没看到兽人怎么做食物，他将幼崽仰起的脑袋按下，叫他们吃自己的肉糊糊，一边张开大口，把嘴里塞得满满当当。
蘑菇的鲜甜在舌尖跳跃，兽人们常说得那股闷味一点也没有了，狼果纳闷道：“楸，你们放甜草了吗？”
林楸：“没有。”
狼果：“那为什么会有甜味儿，还越吃越想吃。”
他探头看不远处的陶锅里，汤汁儿都刮得干干净净，还有兽人想抱锅舔，叫狼安一勺子敲在脑门上。
林楸：“蘑菇自带的。”
蘑菇增鲜，正好雨季大量产出，他可以挑选几个合适的品种，晒干磨粉当鲜味剂。
调料这不又多了一样。
吃了这一顿蘑菇，兽人们明显对采蘑菇一事更加积极。林楸询问祭司过后，选了两三种完全没毒的，叫兽人们多采集。
温度高，蘑菇切片晒个三两天就彻底干了。研磨成粉，无论是做汤还是炒菜，放一点进去，就算不是做的蘑菇汤，也能尝到那股鲜甜味道。
兽人们眼睛都亮了，吃点凉拌菜都得往里放。
狩猎采集队走了三天，回来时，狼山的陶锅里煮的是蘑菇，矮墙上的簸箕里晒的是蘑菇，狼山里兽人们磨得咯吱咯吱细响的还是蘑菇。
狩猎队愧疚，要不是他们回来得晚，兽人们怎么会天天吃这个。瞧瞧，同伴一个个都……疯了？
吃蘑菇吃多了吧，他们带着猎物回来了，还没一头狼过来大家全盯着那锅里的蘑菇，除了一点鱼，全是蘑菇。
还都乌漆嘛黑的，鱼少蘑菇多，兽人们心里忐忑不已。
难不成鱼也不多，吃蘑菇吃傻了？
“王？”兽人们看向狼岩。
兽人都知道，蘑菇不能多吃或者乱吃，里面带毒，以前没吃的不得已，现在要不是鱼不够，兽人们怎么会吃这么多。
山洞内，研磨蘑菇粉的狼莫听到动静，叫上兽人出去迎接。
狼莫哈巴狗一样甩着舌头，四条腿儿奔来。
身后小队成员跟着，急急忙忙将兽人们带回来的猎物接过去，又兴奋地往回奔。
被冷落的狩猎队：“……”
狼岩不是这群傻狼，喜欢脑补，他从容地走到棚子下，狼安见了他们，喜道：“王，蘑菇都是祭司挑选过的，都是没毒的，味道很好。”
“嗯。”
他们夜里赶路回，这会儿恰好是部落吃早饭的时间。狼岩困乏，见林楸也从山洞里出来，眉头舒展，步履缓慢，有些懒散地靠近。
林楸见了他，眼里落了笑意，浅浅的，像晨雾一般带着微凉的气息，一下抚平了闷湿气息里的躁意。
狼岩干脆停了下来。
灰眸追着林楸，直到他走到跟前，狼岩垂眸就能看见他精巧的五官，雪似的脸。
“回来了。”林楸道。
狼岩：“抓了六头咩咩兽。”
他放松站着，少有这般懒散样子。长睫半低，眼里有些疲倦，眸光全然罩住跟前的人。
“抓这么多？”林楸好奇，“我去看看。”
狼岩长腿一挪，却挡在他跟前。
林楸一米八的个头不算矮，但与狼岩离得近了，他得仰头才能看见他的脸。
林楸：“？”
狼岩：“有一头……”
“王！那头带崽的咩咩兽怎么办？”狼莫匆匆跑来，人还没到，嘴巴就嚷嚷开。
狼岩：“叫祭司看看。”
“嗷！”狼莫一个急刹，调转方向往祭司山洞跑。
狼岩见林楸疑惑，跟他说：“兽人一般不捕猎怀孕的母兽，但那头咩咩兽是被族群抛弃的。”
“为什么？”
狼岩：“因为它的幼崽生不出来，母兽也快死了。”
“我去看看。”
狼岩看他坚持，也就往旁边让了一步，跟在脚下生风的林楸后头。
母兽产崽是惨烈的，羊水混着血水，伴随着幼崽哗啦啦往外掉落。混合着腥气，叫狼兽人们都离得远远的。
老祭司被狼莫背下来，那头母兽早已经不行了。
但它躺在地上，还依旧挣扎着，不停地哀鸣。它目光似雪原干净，对他们这群捕食者含着祈求。
兽人们听得狼耳贴紧了脑门，不忍心看。
他们陆续远去。
虽然他们的关系是捕食者与猎物的关系，但兽人敬畏自然，认为自己跟这些猎物没什么两样，只不过弱肉强食，是自然法则。
兽人走了些，只零星几个守着。
老祭司看着那双眼睛，叫狼冰把兽人难产用的草药拿来，给它喂下。
林楸匆匆过来，狼岩一直跟在他身后。
他问：“那个有崽的咩咩兽最后会怎么办？”
狼岩：“祭司能救的话，活下来，我们会放它们回去。不能的话，只有吃了。”
说着，就到了地方。
一股浓烈的腥味漂浮在湿热的空气中，还留下的兽人捂着鼻子，手足无措。
草药喂了，可哪里能这么快起作用。
“祭司。”
老祭司摇摇头，“太久了。”
林楸一来，就看到咩咩兽腹下拖着的两条小咩咩兽的腿。又听到祭司的话，想也不想上前。
狼岩一把抓住他胳膊，“别去。”
林楸反手抓住他，“让我试试，你帮我。”
狼岩：“好。”
“楸！”
林楸：“没事，王跟着。”
林楸靠近，躺在地上的咩咩兽动了动。林楸低声道：“我帮你，你别蹬我。”
他抓住小咩咩兽的脚，一股温热柔软的触感击得林楸一僵，他看着狼岩按住咩咩兽的前肢，学着记忆中牧民给羊接生的手法，开始使劲儿。
咩咩兽的胎位不正，需要把藏在里面抵着出口的蹄子摆正，林楸紧咬住牙关，屏息地将手探入。
咩咩兽脚下蹬了两下，挣扎的力气都没有。
围观的兽人不知道楸为什么要那样做，但看着他郑重严肃的脸，也不自觉地捏紧手，害怕又紧张地看着。
动作要快，小咩咩兽不知在里面憋了多久。
随着母咩咩兽仰起脑袋，一声悲鸣，林楸慢慢使劲儿，哗啦一声——
“出、出来了！出来了！”
兽人们来不及高兴，就看林楸跪在地上，手掌抹干净小咩咩兽的嘴巴。
不动弹了。
死了吗？
老祭司看着地上急促喘息的母兽，握紧了拐杖道：“冰，快去把架子最上面的药拿过来！”
“狼莫！弄点草来！”
“诶！”狼莫慌慌张张跑远。
怀里的小咩咩兽热气腾腾的，兽人们靠近，林楸道：“远一点，别沾到了。”
“要兽皮！”
不知谁递过来的兽皮，林楸过来给小咩咩兽擦着嘴巴跟鼻子，太久了，羊水呛入太多。
他一边做心肺复苏，一边试图将羊水甩出来。
林楸手抖着，脑子却十分冷静。
狼岩抓住他颤抖的手，“我来。”
他力气大，虽熬了夜但抱着一只小咩咩兽完全不费事儿。
林楸：“热水，兽皮！祭司，母咩咩兽……”
老祭司道：“没事，放心。”
生命是脆弱的，也是顽强的。小咩咩兽出来了，那药丸给母兽吃下去，它应该没什么问题。
但是小咩咩兽……
这么久了，还没动静。
老祭司看着狼岩的手法，心里叹了口气。要是这么好救……
“活了！活了！”
“动弹了！”
狼冰刚将药丸给母兽喂下，忽然听到一阵欢呼。他转头一看，狼岩手里的小咩咩兽动了两下腿，虚弱地叫出了声。
他十分惊诧地看向林楸。
兽人们欢呼，刚刚散去的兽人，不知道什么时候全围了过来。
林楸把兽皮打湿拧干，迅速给小咩咩兽擦拭干净。
他将小咩咩兽放在母兽身边，看着母兽轻轻舔着小兽的脑袋，松了一口气，腿也软了。
狼岩一把扶着他，“接下来，怎么做？”
林楸：“保暖，食物……”
狼岩垂眸，掌心的胳膊还微微颤抖着。
狼岩：“我来安排，去洗一洗。”
林楸：“好，你注意，别让那些东西沾到眼睛或者嘴巴里。”
“嗯。”
林楸去河边洗干净手，又用剩下的热水洗了个澡，身上的兽皮衣换下来，洗干净了晾着，再去看咩咩兽。
兽人们已经把咩咩兽转移到到山洞里，洞内铺了干草，放了青草跟水。
母兽似乎恢复些力气，正站在里侧，任由狼兽人帮着小咩咩兽喂奶。
小咩咩兽还很虚弱，这会儿跪趴着，站不起来。
祭司道：“胆子挺大。”
林楸：“太着急，什么都没想。祭司，你给咩咩兽喂的药丸是什么？”
祭司：“没什么，寻常药丸。”
“走吧，这里少些兽人来，咩咩兽胆小。”
又下起雨来了，林楸踩着滑溜溜的下山路，差点一屁股坐泥地里。狼冰一把将他捞住，“你爪子不会抓地？”
说着看了眼林楸脚下的草鞋，“你怎么……怎么想到那么救咩咩兽的？”
小狼白发乱了，顾不得雨水打在脸上，手抓着林楸，满眼好奇。
林楸：“没想，小咩咩兽不出来两个都得死。”
那血腥场面，即便狼兽人都不敢轻易伸手，偏偏这个看起来弱唧唧的兽人敢。
小狼心服口服。
林楸：“还要拉我淋雨到什么时候？”
狼冰：“我怕你摔。”
反正下山这一段，狼冰给林楸抓得紧紧的。

chapters.translated_text:
When the hunting and gathering parties returned, it was night once again.

The meat distributed today was still quite a lot. Lin Qiu hadn't finished yesterday's yet, and he intended to save the leftovers.

The beastmen, having filled their bellies for two days in a row, slowly filed into the cave, slumped into their grass nests, smacked their lips in satisfaction, and fell fast asleep a moment later.

Lin Qiu once again lagged behind as he went in.

The beastmen weren't as hostile as they were at the beginning; they just pricked up their ears to listen or glanced at him briefly before looking away, still unwelcoming overall.

Lin Qiu walked straight to his own grass nest and pulled back the animal skin to wrap around himself.

His fair chin was hidden in the soft animal fur, making his face look no bigger than a palm. His bones were also thin, making him look more fragile than most sub-beastmen.

As he turned over, a pulling sensation came from his arm, aching slightly.

Lin Qiu lifted the animal skin and glanced at his arm by the nearby fire; a thin layer of skin had been scraped off the sunburned area, which didn't look very pleasant.

Lin Qiu hooked his fingers into the animal skin on his body, rubbed it for a moment, and turned to look at Lang Yan.

The tribe definitely stored animal skins, and he wanted some to make clothes; he was willing to trade items for them. But now he couldn't leave the perimeter of Lang Mountain and had nothing to offer.

If he tanned raw hides himself... but any beast in the tribe that hadn't been skinned had its fur burned off directly, and the hide was also divided up for the beastmen to eat.

Lin Qiu frowned slightly and lay back down.

He could only think of other ways.

Lin Qiu closed his eyes to brew some sleepiness, while Lang Yan lowered his gaze, looking at the curled-up sub-beastman in the nest.

Even with his eyes closed, his eyeballs were still moving, wondering what scheme he was cooking up again.

In the fire, the wood burned pitch-black, occasionally accompanied by a burst of crackling splitting sounds. Not a single beastman spoke in the cave, only steady, drawn-out breathing could be heard.

It was raining again, and Lin Qiu groggily burrowed deeper into the animal skin.

The animal skin was huge, hiding even his head inside, almost shrinking into a ball.

Lang Yan paid attention to the hand the sub-beastman was using to clutch the animal skin; scratches and cuts were scattered across it, some already scabbed over, others oozing wisps of blood.

Those slender, pale fingers looked like they would snap at the slightest bend.

Not just his behavior, but even his appearance seemed somewhat different from when he was first sent here.

Lang Yan looked at that hand and recalled, finding that his previous memories of the sub-beastman were very vague; all he could remember now were his hysterical angry curses.

The rain aided sleep, and coupled with the spacious animal skin, Lin Qiu wasn't as tense as he had been the first two nights; instead, he slept exceptionally peacefully.

Yet in the middle of the night, a sharp pain suddenly shot through his palm.

Looking once again at the cub that had successfully stepped its little paws onto his palm, Lin Qiu was somewhat speechless.

The cub's paws were small and somewhat sharp, sinking into his palm with a slight ache.

Lin Qiu watched it sniff his palm, then silently lifted its little paw. The paw pads were very tender, differing far too much from those of adult beastmen.

Lin Qiu pulled back his hand and hid it inside the animal skin.

The cub thought he was playing with it, and happily lunged back into the animal skin. Its short tail wagged, looking no different from a puppy.

Lin Qiu didn't dare to move it and immediately looked behind him.

Lang Yan was lying in his nest and abruptly opened his eyes.

Lin Qiu had known all along that he was sharp, but he was still startled by the sharp, edge-filled gray eyes.

He glanced at the cub in his own grass nest, then looked back, and Lang Yan knew what was going on.

Lang Yan stared at the cub.

The cub's tail stiffened, and it burrowed frantically into Lin Qiu's animal skin.

Lang Yan stood up, and Lin Qiu quickly sat up, pulling back the animal skin.

A moment later, Lang Yan closed in.

With a gentle flip by him, the cub's belly faced the sky.

His snout poked against the cub's belly, but unexpectedly, his large ear brushed past his chest.

Lin Qiu abruptly clenched his palms tightly.

Once he carried the cub away by the scruff of its neck, Lin Qiu tensed the corners of his mouth and immediately wrapped himself tightly in the animal skin, closing his eyes.

Lang Yan returned and swept his gaze over Lin Qiu's nest.

The sub-beastman's eyelashes were trembling fiercely, and the hand gripping the edge of the animal skin was clenched tight.

He was quite bold—he dared to make demands of the priest—so he shouldn't be easily frightened.

Lang Yan slowly moved into his grass nest, thinking about the cub's rounded belly.

It wasn't hungry, so why did it keep running over to Lin Qiu's grass nest?

He cast a suspicious glance at Lin Qiu.

During conflicts between tribes, it wasn't unheard of to lure out cubs and kill them. That was a huge blow to a tribe.

But these days he had been quite well-behaved, and hadn't contacted beastmen from other tribes, except for having a faint trace of fragrance on his body...

Whenever he got close, he could always smell it when the sub-beastman passed by, and it was in his nest too.

It wasn't the scent of food, but an indescribable, light fragrance. Somewhat like the flowers growing beneath snowdrifts in the snow season, faint and shallow.

Wolf beastmen had sharp noses, and Lin Qiu set up his nest right beside him, so he could smell it almost every night.

Lang Yan closed his eyes, intending to ask the priest about it.

Since the sub-beastman was right under his nose now, no matter what, he couldn't flip the heavens upside down.

*

For several consecutive days, the harvested prey was still quite a lot, and Lin Qiu had saved up some meat.

However, as the weather grew hotter and hotter, meat would also turn smelly if left too long. Whatever he couldn't finish, Lin Qiu directly turned into jerky.

Staying out in the sunlight was impossible now.

The sunlight here was different from before; it was exceptionally bright and dazzling.

Lin Qiu moved the stove to a spot at the foot of the mountain that could provide a bit of shade, and also covered his body with some large leaves.

It was already afternoon, and the beastmen had long since plucked the nearby ground fungus clean. Before the hunting party returned, having nothing to eat, they simply lay flat on the ground to endure.

Lin Qiu also had only the meat and greens distributed by the tribe left on hand.

Jerky was roasting on the stove, while Lin Qiu sliced off some fresh lean meat distributed last night, cut it into small pieces, and pounded it in a stone pot.

The meat was pounded into paste, rolled into meatballs, and then boiled until cooked.

Lin Qiu didn't eat them all; he left two in a hollowed-out wooden bucket, submerged in the stream.

When night fell, as his palm once again cupped a soft ball of a cub, Lin Qiu opened his eyes and quietly met its gaze.

The cub didn't make a fuss or a noise, happily wagging its tail as it climbed up his arm onto his shoulder, familiarly curling itself into a ball and nesting against the side of his neck.

A damp little tongue licked his cheek, and Lin Qiu turned his face away.

He looked at the cub, and the cub looked at him.

Displeased that Lin Qiu wouldn't budge, the cub frantically rubbed its head against his face. Clingy and sticky.

Lin Qiu watched for a while, until the cub was tired of rubbing and slumped down like a round winter melon. Only then did he gently tap its head, his index finger stroking its seashell-like little ears.

Time and again, it was always this white wolf cub.

Lin Qiu moved and spread open his hand.

The leaves scattered, and the round meatballs were overflowing with aroma.

The cub's eyes lit up, and it plunged its head right onto them, its tiny teeth gnawing on them as it wagged its tail into a blur.

Lin Qiu clearly heard the change in breathing behind him—Lang Yan had woken up.

And he was still watching this scene.

Not stopping it meant he permitted it.

Lin Qiu pressed his lips together, a trace of a smile slowly pulling at the corners of his mouth.

Although Lang Yan couldn't see Lin Qiu's expression clearly, he could sense that the other was in a pretty good mood right now.

Glancing sideways at the cub, Lang Yan withdrew his gaze.

He had asked the priest this morning about the fragrance he smelled, only for the stern old beastman to let out a rare laugh.

Lang Yan didn't get an answer, but that laugh looked fishy.

Lang Yan didn't want to puzzle over it; as long as it didn't affect the tribe, the rest didn't matter.

This white wolf cub in the nest was named Xue, the largest among the cubs, and was already two years old. The tribe's cubs could transform into human shape within one to three years of birth, and could run and jump after taking human form.

The old priest said that in past years cubs could successfully transform in about a year, but nowadays with insufficient food, it often took three years, or even five.

Lang Yan thought of the cub's weak limbs and frail body, and for a moment, all other thoughts vanished.

The herds they had recently hunted had already left the tribe's hunting grounds, and they had no choice but to search for new herds.

Although the meat distributed these past few days wasn't exactly little, the beastmen ate however much there was.

Lang Yan hadn't failed to consider having the beastmen boil meat mixed with greens every meal like the sub-beastman, eating only half.

But upon second thought, it wouldn't work.

The sub-beastman could barely manage to fill his stomach, but the male beastmen consumed a massive amount of meat; even if they swallowed it mixed with greens and water, without enough meat, it still wouldn't cut it.

Moreover, the tribe didn't have that much energy to prepare food the way the sub-beastman did, nor did they have that many pottery pots.

Catching prey and filling their bellies had already exhausted them to the limit.

Lang Yan only felt his heart sink even lower; his wolf tail hung motionless, and his mountain-like body slumped down.

*

Over the next few days, food grew scarce once again.

Lin Qiu was doing all right, but the beastmen were almost too hungry to speak; starting from when they slumped outside the cave in the morning, they wouldn't even budge an inch by the afternoon.

Lin Qiu had no doubt that they weren't sleeping, but rather starving faint.

Lin Qiu sat at the foot of Lang Mountain, watching quietly, his heart sinking along with it.

At the current difficulty of hunting, the wolf beastmen would only grow weaker and weaker, and starving to death was a normal outcome.

Lin Qiu swept his gaze across the cluster of beastmen, frowned, and suddenly remembered the old beastman he met when the ban was first lifted.

He hadn't seen the person in many days.

He looked at the wolves sprawled on the ground; between breaths, their sunken bellies looked somewhat terrifying.

This couldn't go on.

In the afternoon, the beastmen returned.

This time the prey was small, but there were three of them. Leaving one as a guarantee for tomorrow, the remaining two were both slaughtered.

Lin Qiu watched them skin the animals. After a pause, seeing Lang Yan go down to deliver meat to the few isolated caves on Lang Mountain, he stepped over in his straw shoes and hurried closer.

Lang Yan stopped.

This spot was a bit far from the bonfire; the firelight couldn't reach here, and it was dim, with only the outline of Lang Mountain and the faint, glowing embers in the caves behind.

When Lin Qiu was two steps away from him, he stopped.

Being this close for the first time, he realized how tall Lang Yan was in human form.

He was almost a whole head taller than him.

His spine was straight as he stood waiting for him to approach, his gray eyes lowered, waiting for him to speak.

Lin Qiu: "I want animal skins. I can trade things for them."

Lang Yan's gaze swept over the straw shoes at his feet and nodded.

He agreed exceptionally readily, which was beyond Lin Qiu's expectations.

"I can't produce anything right now, but once I leave Lang Mountain I can..."

Lang Yan: "No."

Ordinary animal skins weren't rare things; they had a whole pile piled up in their cave.

"Fresh ones?"

Lin Qiu paused, "Without fur."

Lang Yan: "Mn."

The ones in the cave all had fur; the ones that were kept entirely were the ones with long fur.

Winter was very cold, and their fur could barely guarantee they could stay active outside for a short while. If in human form, they had to wrap themselves up so only their eyes showed before daring to go out.

He was giving him the animal skin just to see what he wanted to do.

Lang Yan walked back to the pile of beastmen.

Over there, the animal skin had just been peeled off and was still warm, and it was immediately delivered over to Lin Qiu's side.

Two skins, about the size of an adult sheep's pelt, were brought over to him by Lang Yan.

He gladly accepted them, intending to start making things tonight after finishing dinner—the sooner the better.

Lang Yan left, the flames burning upward. Lin Qiu reached out, and a wisp of black wolf fur drifted slowly into his hand.

Lin Qiu subconsciously glanced at Lang Yan.

Twirling the wolf fur between his fingers...

If there was enough wolf fur, maybe making a sweater would also be possible.

Lang Yan looked over, their gazes meeting. Lin Qiu felt somewhat guilty under the gaze of those gray eyes and looked away first.
