Not to mention anything else, even cooking something delicious was difficult because they lacked the energy to experiment due to the weather.

The few middle-aged sub-beastmen were so happy that their shuttles moved a bit faster.

As Lang An worked, he suddenly stopped and asked, "Priest, was this year's rainy season shorter than previous ones?"

The old priest replied, "It was shorter, but only by a few days."

Lang Yan watched as Lin Qiu took a few sips of warm water. In the firelight, the young man's cheeks were fair and smooth, his long, slender eyelashes lowered. After finishing the water, his lips looked a bit more rosy.

He took the cup from him and placed it on the low table nearby. Only after the beastmen finished their clamor did he say:

"It's a good thing the rainy season is over. There's a lot to do ahead. Tomorrow, the hunting teams will patrol in the east, west, and south directions, and while they're at it, they should ask the Black Feather Tribe when they plan to come over."

The captains of the three hunting teams nodded.

The night deepened. Lin Qiu lay on his side in the grass nest, his hand tucked under his cheek, with only a bit of animal skin draped over his waist.

Before he knew it, the rainy season had passed.

Listening closely now, even the chirping of insects was less frequent than before.

The wind blowing into the cave didn't feel as stuffy as if it were trapped behind a thin membrane; one could faintly feel a hint of coolness carrying moisture.

It was most noticeable at night. Usually, the beastmen had to add ice once in the middle of the night, but now they only needed to remove the curtain at the cave entrance to let the outside air in, and it wouldn't be that hot.

The next morning, after breakfast, the beastmen set off to patrol in all directions except for the north.

The tribe generally conducted two comprehensive patrols throughout the year.

One was now, and the other was after the snow season.

Beastmen coveted the prey in each other's territories. During the snow and rainy seasons, most tribes lacked the energy to patrol, so some beastmen would take the opportunity to sneak into other tribes' territories to hunt.

The wolf beastmen spent most of the rainy season in the north, so they didn't need to go there, but the other directions were a different story.

Although the Black Feather Tribe and the White Sparrow Tribe were trustworthy, one couldn't guarantee that wandering beastmen like Bao Xiu wouldn't break in.

These beastmen had no fixed residence and were restless; sometimes they would gather in groups specifically to harass other tribes.

Those who could wander for a long time must have some ability. If such beastmen were to infiltrate the tribe, it would easily lead to trouble.

The three hunting teams set off with dried fish, and the gathering team and the two small wolf teams also followed along. Once they left, the tribe suddenly felt much emptier.

After the light rain last night, the morning air was filled with a refreshing coolness.

Lin Qiu wore a loose top made of linen and long trousers, followed by four cubs who looked like chubby radishes.

The cubs were gradually learning to transform into human form, so it wasn't suitable for them to stay with the other cubs who hadn't left the nest yet.

The oldest, Lang Xue, was learning things from the priest, so these few followed the sturdiest little gray wolf, Lang Sheng—the one who had transformed into human form in the washbasin and almost crushed the other cubs.

Now that the cubs were well-fed and healthy, their excessive energy began to show.

They spent their days darting around the cave and in front of the wolf mountain. As soon as they opened their eyes in the morning, they would jump on the adult wolves, chase red birds, touch the sheep-beasts, and when they got tired, they would collapse and fall asleep instantly, requiring the beastmen to pick them up one by one.

Once they were well-rested, they would continue to cause trouble, running around the caves, getting snacks from Lang An, wooden puppets from Lang Qi, and sweet grass roots from the priest.

Then, like little mountain kings, they would follow the guard team on a patrol around the mountain; there was never a moment of rest.

The tribe was good to the cubs, and since life was better than before, they were allowed to do as they pleased.

Lin Qiu, now leading this string of tails, walked past the shed in front of the cave, intending to check on the red birds and sheep-beasts behind the mountain.

After walking only a few steps, he felt a chill on his head.

Lin Qiu looked up and saw light faintly filtering through the roof of the shed.

Another drop of water fell. He stepped aside, and the water landed right on Lang Sheng's forehead.

The little gray wolf touched his forehead, his round eyes looking blankly as he said, "Qiuqiu, it's raining."

Lin Qiu curled his lips: "Call me Uncle Qiu."

Lang Sheng: "Qiuqiu, it's raining inside the shed too, awoo."

Cubs had their own persistence. Lin Qiu sighed helplessly, "The wind is so strong during the rainy season, and it's so damp and humid, so of course the shed roof rots quickly."

"Qiu, then should we change it?"

A head poked out from behind the low wall, its neck stretched long, like a turtle poking its head out of the water to breathe.

The ground inside the shed was damp, and walking back and forth made it a bit dirty, so Lang Mo and the others had all sat outside.

Lin Qiu: "If we can change it, let's change it."

As soon as he finished speaking, seven more heads poked out from behind the low wall. They were all from the guard team, looking like a family of gophers, perfectly uniform.

Lang Xi: "Qiu! If we change it now, will we have to change it again during the snow season?"

Lin Qiu: "Most likely."

The shed had been built sturdily and was even reinforced before the rainy season, yet it hadn't been long before it ended up like this. Here, the snow was thick during the snow season, so it might collapse under the weight. Even if it didn't collapse, in such changeable weather, the lifespan of a hay roof was at most one year.

Lang Mo looked at the few chubby fingers barely resting on the low wall, stretched out a claw to press on them, and felt it wouldn't work.

He thought it over, his eyes suddenly lighting up, and his neck stretched even longer than before. He said: "Then that brick you mentioned—would we not have to change that?"

Lin Qiu said: "To use bricks, we'd need to make roof tiles, but it would definitely be sturdier than a grass shed."

Lang Mo patted the cub's little paw and said: "Alright! Let's do that!"

The cubs tried hard to stand on tiptoe, their round eyes peeking over the low wall, then pulled their paws back, quickly swiped at Lang Mo, and giggled as they pulled them back.

The few adult beastmen and the cubs started playing just like that.

*

The cave had poor ventilation, and since the red birds and sheep-beasts had been kept inside for so long, no matter how much they cleaned, there was still a smell on them.

Now that the rainy season was over, Lin Qiu transferred them directly to the shed on the west side.

A few patches of light fell on him, and when Lin Qiu looked up, he found that the roof of this shed was even more dilapidated, with the grass blown away.

As the weather became cooler, burning bricks was indeed more appropriate.

With the experience of making pottery, it was much easier to burn bricks.

Lin Qiu first told Lang Mo and the others how to build a brick kiln and how to make brick molds, leaving the rest for them to figure out.

The tribe couldn't build a large brick kiln yet, so they would first try using the two existing clay kilns for pottery.

The bricks were molded using wooden frames, a task left to Lang Qi.

After one rainy season, the tribe now had three looms, and there were plenty of spindles. Coupled with enough tables and stools for the beastmen, Lang Qi was now free and happy to have Lang Mo come to him.

Lin Qiu finished discussing this with Lang Mo halfway through the morning, took his little tail of cubs for a stroll around the tribe, and stopped when he reached the cave where the looms were kept.

The tribe was short on linen. After a rainy season, the beastmen had busily woven a few more bolts, but it still wasn't enough.

Having seen the benefits of linen, Lang An and the others would sit at the looms whenever they were free, and the second batch of linen thread collected during the rainy season was almost used up.

"Qiu, did you come down from the priest's cave?" Lang An asked, skillfully throwing the shuttle while still finding time to speak.

Lin Qiu: "I'm resting today."

He entered the cave, found a stool to sit on, and helped the beastmen spin thread. The few cubs following him poked their heads in to look around, saw nothing fun, and immediately ran off, swinging their thick, short legs.

Lang An smiled, saying gently, "The King and the others probably won't be back until tonight."

"Mm." Lin Qiu wasn't here to ask about him, anyway.

Lang An: "Then what shall we eat later?"

Lin Qiu turned the handle, thinking of the fish he had eaten over and over again; honestly, he was a bit sick of it.

No matter how you cooked fish, it was still fish.

Although there were various wild vegetables as side dishes, the beastmen couldn't live without meat, and two out of their three daily meals were fish.

The tribe didn't have enough other meat during the rainy season, so naturally, there was no dried meat left.

Lin Qiu sighed: "Fish."

The few sub-beastmen couldn't help but sigh as well, their hands losing strength.

"There's little prey, so it's good enough to be full." They comforted themselves, but they were becoming increasingly unsatisfied.

Seeing that Lin Qiu didn't have any new cooking methods, Lang An quickly said: "Let's not talk about that, eating fish is fine. Qiu, the linen grass in the tribe is almost used up again..."

Lin Qiu: "It's almost time to harvest the third crop. I'm thinking of getting some seeds back so we can grow them ourselves in the future."

The wild linen outside grew too scattered, and without fertilizer or watering, it grew entirely on its own.

Not only was it difficult to harvest, but it also grew unevenly.

Although linen was good, the beastmen were rough; a pair of shorts made of linen could be torn if one wasn't careful, and that was even with the linen fibers being tough enough.

In the future, they would need even more linen grass, so it would be better to grow it themselves.

After hearing what Lin Qiu had to say, Lang An and the others agreed it was a good idea. The land near the Wolf Tribe was flat; once cleared, it could be planted, not to mention they had bird droppings for fertilizer.

chapters.source_text:
“明天我们去割麻。”狼贝一听说麻没了，立即应下来。
今天几个队伍都回来得晚，也零零散散带回来些猎物，都是小型的。
奔波一天，大部分兽人吃过晚饭都睡着了。大山洞里呼噜声混杂，只几个小队的队长还围着狼岩坐着，商量事儿。
狼岩：“明天黑羽兽人就会过来。”
林楸困顿地打个哈欠，头发散开覆盖双肩，如墨倾倒。他额头抵着狼岩肩膀，有些睁不开眼。
“直接来狼山吗？”林楸含糊问。
狼岩：“先在大泽那边待一段时间，收麻跟蛮草的事儿依旧交给他们做。”
狼贝闻言，道：“那我们还是采集。”
“这次他们想送两个小兽人过来。”狼火看靠在狼岩身上的林楸快睡熟了，忍不住放低声音，“是当初偷盐的羽涯，还有他们的祭司羽乐。”
狼岩：“能干活儿就行。”
“王，我们想继续烧砖。”狼莫也插一句道。
狼岩看了眼肩上毛绒绒的脑袋，绷着身子没动。他身上现在肉稍稍比以前厚，除了火气重，靠着当垫子稳当又舒服。
狼岩：“楸的主意？”
狼莫：“差不多，我们想着棚子坏太快修起来麻烦，试试用砖瓦做。”
兽人们不知道砖瓦是什么，但楸说的，听着就靠谱。
狼岩：“那就去做吧。”
“狼石，狼山的巡逻最近抓紧些。”
狼石点头，全程就这一句话：“知道了，王。”
又说了会儿尾巴草的事以及明天捕猎的事，狼岩便叫兽人们各自回去睡觉。
晨光熹微，兽人们都起了。
林楸迷蒙地跟着坐起来，见草窝边上站着个高大的黑影。
狼岩弓着背，正往身上裹着兽皮裙。大家捕猎就穿兽皮裙乱糟蹋，对麻布做的衣服却小心护着。
林楸见那收紧的蜂腰下，屁股蛋儿一闪而过，立即转过头去。
狼岩手一顿，回头见林楸也醒了，给了他个后脑勺。
“可以再睡会儿。”
“去南边？”
“嗯。”
林楸昨晚没听到他们今天去捕猎的这一截，打个哈欠爬起来，声音带着初醒来的黏软，道：“我也去。”
狼岩收紧兽皮裙，腰腹肌肉一块一块的，臂膀宽阔，长发全绑在身后，一双眼睛在黑沉的山洞中也格外的亮。
比起林楸白腻的肤色，他麦色的皮肤充满野性。
看到林楸走到草窝边缘，他伸出手。
林楸只当他扶一把，却不想这兽人直接胳膊绕他腰上一整圈，直接将他提了下来。
林楸忙撑着他肩膀，道：“你答应了？”
“嗯。”狼岩的胳膊滚烫，他又没穿上衣，林楸双脚踩实地面后见他还不放手，红着耳朵忍不住拍了他两下。
“可以松开了。”
狼岩：“好。”
林楸吐息，飞快披上衣裳，穿好草鞋，先他一步出去。
也不知道是不是雨季待在一块儿的时间长了，狼岩越发照顾他，从吃饭喝水，到洗衣铺窝，全被他默默包揽过去。
林楸虽说适应良好，但有时候被旁的兽人挤眉弄眼看久了，也绷不住脸。
林楸跑得快，瞌睡早醒了。
狼岩落在后头，看着他往前疾走，眼如静潭深邃平静。相处越久，他养兽人的习惯也慢慢回来了。
他乐在其中。
吃过早饭，狩猎队再一次往南去。
林楸许久没跑，跟着狼岩跑了一段就气喘吁吁。
他看了眼时刻跟着自己步伐的大黑狼，忍不住道：“我觉得，我需要歇一会儿。”
狼岩眼里闪过笑意，慢慢停下来，身子微曲。
林楸飞快裹好衣服，往狼岩背上爬，手脚挂在他两侧，软绵绵的随着狼岩起身晃悠。
“抱紧。”
林楸听话地收紧胳膊腿儿。
他脸压在狼毛上，喘了会儿才道：“我觉得我应该好好练习一下奔跑，不然以后被敌人追，跑都跑不过。”
狼岩：“不会。”
林楸：“怎么不会。”他现在呼吸肺还疼呢。
狼岩眼睛暗色浓重，“我不会让你被敌人追。”
林楸脸整个压在狼毛里，不吭声了。
他发现狼岩有点惯着他。
狩猎一队、三队先去南边捕猎，顺带把做饭的狼雨跟狼虹带去，还有那些能用得到的工具。
二队由狼火带领，照旧先去西部接了黑羽部落的兽人过来。
他们应该碰不上。
林楸此行是为看麻草。
麻草又长得快差不多人高，有些长得快的已经挂起珠串似的果实，但还是绿色，采收不得。
林楸估摸着时间，差不多得等到尾巴草成熟，这些果实才能采收。
这次除了狩猎二队，其他队伍都在。人手足够，林楸领着狼冰的采集队收割一些，怕部落里断了麻草。
狩猎队则分散去，寻找藏在林中的呦呦兽。
狼金带着小狼狩猎队，里头多了个豹休，一群小狼在林子里找呦呦兽。
时而跑，时而停，狼金作为小狼狩猎队里的领头，已经能凭借脚印跟粪便，分辨猎物的踪迹。
呦呦兽分散，捕猎队自然也分散。
狼金带头，走着走着，不知不觉就听不到其他兽人的动静了。
四周是差不多的树木，雨季草木疯长，只看得到小狼们过来时，微微倾倒的痕迹。
前方不远处，一头呦呦兽出现，狼金压着身旁的豹休，掩藏起来。
其余小狼默契地趴了下来。
狼耳高竖，狼眼直勾勾地盯着那头肥壮的呦呦兽。
这年头也不知怎么回事儿，植物长得格外茂密，猎物虽少，但一个个吃得也肥壮。就他们这些兽人遭了难，一个个瘦弱不堪。
狼金下巴戳着草叶，隐藏气息。
他跟豹休小声道：“咱们今天肉管够。”
豹休是黑豹，身上斑纹不怎么清晰。对比身旁的小狼，尾巴长，耳朵圆，两圆滚滚的眼睛看着有些傻呆呆的。
雨季在狼部落里感受到了什么叫富裕，现在早被磨平了刺儿，因着感激，也跟在队伍里为狼部落尽心尽力。
这不代表他忘记了仇恨，他还小，只等成年，便会离去。
“母兽。”豹休道。
狼金刚一动，那边呦呦兽后头树枝挡住的地方，走出来个小呦呦兽。
“哎！”
“哎！！！白追了这么久。”后面小狼跟着颓坐在地上，一屁股压塌一片草。
兽人一有动静，前方呦呦兽受惊，一个蹿步跳跃，就消失在了林中。
狼金：“继续找吧。”
小狼蔫巴，耳朵都垂下来了。豹休跟在他身边，不习惯见小狼这个样子。
狼金一直傻乐呵，没心没肺的。要不是狼金带着，豹休不知道多久才会融入狼部落。豹休已经将他划入自己朋友的范围当中。
他举起爪子，戳了戳狼金。
“想不想吃好吃的？”
狼金并一众小狼脑袋点得飞起，眼冒金光。
豹休：“先捕猎，我刚刚看见了，咱们等会儿去找。”
*
狼冰带着小狼采集队，刚跟着林楸一起收割了十几捆麻草，就继续采集草药去了。
林楸将麻草用带来的麻绳捆好，狼岩随手一拎，将麻草堆在一起。
林楸：“你不去捕猎？”
狼岩：“用不着。”
呦呦兽不像其他兽群，需要兽人围堵。去的兽人越多，越容易受惊。
兽人又不是离了他不行。
等到林楸将这边的麻草收拾完，狩猎跟采集队陆陆续续回来。
两个狩猎队都带着一头成年呦呦兽，采集队藤筐里也尽是果子跟植物根茎，草叶还是少些。
虽说雨季就这么过了，但热度不会一下退去，这会儿正是下午最热的时候，兽人们放下猎物往地上一坐，躺开休息去。
林楸直起身，胳膊上带着被野草割出来的红痕。
他视线往兽人堆里一扫，戳了下身旁闷头干活的狼岩道：“还有一队小狼没回来。”
狼岩：“再等会儿。”
他们没有接近大泽，出来只跑了半个上午。还有一点时间。
又一会儿，狼游起身，带上两个兽人出去找小狼。
林楸：“不会丢了吧。”
“丢不了。”狼岩说。
时间差不多了，兽人们陆续起来，该搬猎物的搬猎物，该背麻草的背麻草。
林子里，狼游呼唤小狼的声音飘过来，林楸屏息静听，似有回应。
他松了口气，也往树后头钻，脱掉衣服变做兽形。
“嗷嗷嗷嗷嗷！！！”
一声狼叫传来，放松的兽人立即警惕。大家整齐划一，脑袋全都转向东南方向。
狼游飞速赶回来，脸上跟抹了锅底灰似的，“王……”
“王！！！豹休被嗡嗡虫咬了！！！”小狼尖锐的声音先一步传来。
狼群里一阵骚乱。
狼岩飞速跟小狼汇合，林楸紧紧跟上去，就看见个脑袋肿大的黑豹被小狼们围着，从林子里钻出来。
豹休被几十双狼眼盯着，吓了一跳。
他眼皮肿得圆眼睛成了眯缝眼，嘴巴也挨了几下，说话都得抽抽两下。
他支支吾吾，眼睛透着老实豹的憨傻，道：“怎、怎么了吗？”
……
“嗷嗷嗷嗷嗷！”寂静过后，狼群一瞬间混乱。
叫声惊起飞鸟，引得还没赶过来的狩猎二队跟黑羽部落齐齐警惕起来，加快速度往南边跑。
“王！他被嗡嗡虫咬了！他被嗡嗡虫咬了！”狼群一下爆发惊叫，兽人急得站不住，你踩我，我撞你，还有的直接撞树上。
被嗡嗡虫咬到可是要死的！
这群小狼怎么就一会儿不见，就去招惹嗡嗡虫了！
狼岩太阳穴抽了两下，眼神沉得吓狼，飞快道：“乔，带两个兽人送他回去！其他小狼被咬的全跟上，没被咬的留下 。”
狼乔叫上几个兽人扛起豹休就跑。
“你坚持住，我们带你去找祭司！”
“嗷嗷嗷！”小狼哭，“都怪我们！”
豹休挣扎，“我没……”
“别动！”狼乔低吼。几个狼兽人速度更快。
嗡嗡虫可是连弯角兽都能咬死的！
“他说带我们找好吃的，谁知道是去吃嗡嗡虫的巢穴。嗷嗷嗷嗷！！都是我们的错！”小狼一边哭，一边跑，手里空空荡荡了，哪里有什么巢。
狼岩脸上没什么表情，声音微沉道：“回去。”
chapters.title: 第93章
chapters.translated_text:
"We'll go harvest hemp tomorrow." As soon as Lang Bei heard that the hemp was running low, he agreed immediately.

All the teams returned late today, and they only brought back a scattering of small prey.

After a day of rushing about, most of the beastmen fell asleep after dinner. The large cave was filled with a chorus of snoring, with only the squad leaders sitting around Lang Yan, discussing matters.

Lang Yan: "The Black Feather beastmen will arrive tomorrow."

Lin Qiu yawned with fatigue, his hair falling over his shoulders like spilled ink. He rested his forehead against Lang Yan's shoulder, his eyes struggling to stay open.

"Are they coming straight to Wolf Mountain?" Lin Qiu asked vaguely.

Lang Yan: "They will stay by the Great Marsh for a while first. The work of collecting hemp and wild grass will still be left to them."

Upon hearing this, Lang Bei said, "Then we will continue gathering."

"This time, they want to send two young beastmen over." Lang Huo, seeing Lin Qiu leaning on Lang Yan and drifting off to sleep, couldn't help but lower his voice. "It's Yu Ya, who stole the salt back then, and their priest, Yu Le."

Lang Yan: "As long as they can work, it's fine."

"King, we want to continue firing bricks," Lang Mo added.

Lang Yan glanced at the fluffy head on his shoulder and remained tense and still. He had put on a little more weight recently, and besides being a bit hot-tempered, he made a steady and comfortable cushion.

Lang Yan: "Qiu's idea?"

Lang Mo: "Pretty much. We thought the sheds break too easily and are a hassle to repair, so we want to try using bricks and tiles."

The beastmen didn't know what bricks and tiles were, but if Qiu said it, it sounded reliable.

Lang Yan: "Then go ahead and do it."

"Lang Shi, tighten the patrols around Wolf Mountain."

Lang Shi nodded, his only words throughout being: "Understood, King."

After discussing the tail grass and tomorrow's hunting plans, Lang Yan told the beastmen to go back and sleep.

At the first light of dawn, the beastmen all rose.

Lin Qiu sat up in a daze and saw a tall, dark shadow standing by the grass nest.

Lang Yan was hunched over, wrapping a beast-skin skirt around his waist. Everyone wore beast-skin skirts for hunting to avoid ruining their clothes, but they protected the hemp cloth garments with great care.

Lin Qiu saw a flash of firm buttocks beneath the cinched waist and immediately turned his head away.

Lang Yan’s hands paused. He turned back to see Lin Qiu had also woken up, presenting him with the back of his head.

"You can sleep a bit longer."

"Going to the south?"

"Yes."

Lin Qiu hadn't heard the part about them going hunting today last night. He yawned and climbed up, his voice soft and sticky from just waking up. "I'm going too."

Lang Yan tightened his beast-skin skirt, revealing muscles on his waist and abdomen, his shoulders broad, his long hair tied behind him. His eyes were exceptionally bright even in the dim cave.

Compared to Lin Qiu's fair, smooth skin, his wheat-colored skin was full of wildness.

Seeing Lin Qiu walk to the edge of the grass nest, he reached out his hand.

Lin Qiu thought he was just helping him up, but the beastman wrapped an arm around his waist and lifted him straight down.

Lin Qiu hurriedly braced himself against his shoulders and said, "You agreed?"

"Yes." Lang Yan’s arm was scorching hot, and since he wasn't wearing a top, Lin Qiu felt his ears turn red and couldn't help but pat him twice after his feet touched the ground.

"You can let go now."

Lang Yan: "Okay."

Lin Qiu exhaled, quickly threw on his clothes, put on his grass sandals, and stepped out ahead of him.

He didn't know if it was because they had spent so much time together during the rainy season, but Lang Yan was taking care of him more and more, silently taking over everything from eating and drinking to washing clothes and laying out the nest.

Although Lin Qiu had adapted well, he sometimes couldn't keep a straight face when other beastmen gave him knowing looks.

Lin Qiu ran fast, his sleepiness long gone.

Lang Yan followed behind, watching him stride forward, his eyes as deep and calm as a still pool. The longer they spent together, the more his habit of "raising" a beastman slowly returned.

He enjoyed it.

After breakfast, the hunting team headed south once again.

Lin Qiu hadn't run in a long time, and after following Lang Yan for a stretch, he was already panting.

He glanced at the large black wolf keeping pace with him and couldn't help but say, "I think I need to rest for a while."

A flash of amusement crossed Lang Yan's eyes. He slowed to a stop and crouched slightly.

Lin Qiu quickly wrapped his clothes tight and climbed onto Lang Yan's back, hanging his hands and feet on either side, swaying softly as Lang Yan stood up.

"Hold on tight."

Lin Qiu obediently tightened his arms and legs.

He pressed his face into the wolf fur and panted for a moment before saying, "I think I should practice running properly, otherwise, if I'm chased by enemies in the future, I won't even be able to outrun them."

Lang Yan: "You won't be."

Lin Qiu: "Why wouldn't I be?" His lungs still hurt from breathing.

Lang Yan's eyes darkened. "I won't let you be chased by enemies."

Lin Qiu pressed his face entirely into the wolf fur and said nothing more.

He realized that Lang Yan was a bit too indulgent with him.

Hunting Teams One and Three went south first to hunt, taking along Lang Yu and Lang Hong, who were in charge of cooking, as well as the necessary tools.

Team Two, led by Lang Huo, went west as usual to pick up the Black Feather tribe beastmen.

They shouldn't run into each other.

Lin Qiu's trip was to check on the hemp grass.

The hemp had grown almost to human height; some of the faster-growing ones already had bead-like fruits, but they were still green and not ready for harvest.

Lin Qiu estimated the time; it would likely be when the tail grass matured that these fruits could be harvested.

This time, except for Hunting Team Two, all other teams were present. With enough manpower, Lin Qiu led Lang Bing’s gathering team to harvest some, fearing the tribe would run out of hemp.

The hunting teams dispersed to search for the Youyou beasts hidden in the forest.

Lang Jin led the young wolf hunting team, which now included Bao Xiu, and the group of young wolves searched the forest for Youyou beasts.

Running and stopping by turns, Lang Jin, as the leader of the young wolf hunting team, could already distinguish the tracks of prey based on footprints and droppings.

The Youyou beasts were scattered, so the hunting teams naturally dispersed as well.

Lang Jin led the way, and as they walked, they unknowingly lost track of the other beastmen.

All around were similar trees; the rainy season caused vegetation to grow wildly, and one could only see the slight traces of where the young wolves had passed.

Not far ahead, a Youyou beast appeared. Lang Jin pressed down on Bao Xiu beside him, hiding.

The rest of the young wolves lay down in tacit understanding.

Wolf ears stood high, wolf eyes staring straight at the plump Youyou beast.

Who knew what was going on these days; plants grew exceptionally lush, and although prey was scarce, each one was fat and sturdy. It was only the beastmen who had suffered, becoming thin and weak.

Lang Jin poked his chin into the grass, hiding his scent.

He whispered to Bao Xiu, "We'll have plenty of meat today."

Bao Xiu was a black panther, his spots not very distinct. Compared to the young wolves beside him, he had a long tail, round ears, and two round eyes that looked a bit silly.

During the rainy season, he had experienced what it meant to be wealthy in the Wolf Tribe. His thorns had long been smoothed away, and out of gratitude, he worked hard for the Wolf Tribe as part of the team.

This didn't mean he had forgotten his hatred; he was still young, and he would leave once he came of age.

"Mother beast," Bao Xiu said.

Just as Lang Jin moved, a small Youyou beast walked out from behind a tree that had been blocking their view.

"Hey!"

"Hey!!! All that chasing for nothing." The young wolves behind him slumped to the ground, their weight flattening a patch of grass.

As soon as the beastmen made a sound, the Youyou beast ahead was startled, leaped away, and disappeared into the forest.

Lang Jin: "Let's keep looking."

The young wolves were dejected, their ears drooping. Bao Xiu, who was beside him, wasn't used to seeing the young wolves like this.

Lang Jin was always foolishly happy and carefree. If it weren't for Lang Jin leading him, Bao Xiu didn't know how long it would have taken to integrate into the Wolf Tribe. Bao Xiu had already categorized him as a friend.

He raised a paw and poked Lang Jin.

"Want to eat something good?"

Lang Jin and the group of young wolves nodded vigorously, their eyes glowing.

Bao Xiu: "Let's hunt first. I saw it just now; we'll go find it later."

*

Lang Bing led the young wolf gathering team, having just harvested a dozen bundles of hemp with Lin Qiu, and went off to gather herbs.

Lin Qiu tied the hemp with the hemp rope they brought, and Lang Yan picked them up and piled them together.

Lin Qiu: "Aren't you going to hunt?"

Lang Yan: "No need."

Youyou beasts were not like other herds that required beastmen to surround them. The more beastmen that went, the easier they were to startle.

And the beastmen weren't incapable without him.

By the time Lin Qiu finished tidying up the hemp, the hunting and gathering teams returned one after another.

Both hunting teams brought back an adult Youyou beast, and the gathering team's baskets were full of fruits and plant roots, though there were fewer leaves.

Although the rainy season was passing, the heat wouldn't fade immediately. It was the hottest time of the afternoon, so the beastmen put down their prey, sat on the ground, and lay down to rest.

Lin Qiu straightened up, his arms marked with red scratches from the wild grass.

He scanned the pile of beastmen and poked Lang Yan, who was working silently beside him. "There's one group of young wolves that hasn't returned."

Lang Yan: "Wait a little longer."

They hadn't approached the Great Marsh and had only been out for half the morning. There was still some time.

After a while, Lang You stood up and took two beastmen to go find the young wolves.

Lin Qiu: "They wouldn't be lost, would they?"

"They won't be lost," Lang Yan said.

Time was up, and the beastmen rose one after another, some to carry the prey, others to shoulder the hemp.

In the forest, the sound of Lang You calling for the young wolves drifted over. Lin Qiu held his breath and listened; there seemed to be a response.

He breathed a sigh of relief and also slipped behind a tree to take off his clothes and transform into his beast form.

"Awooooo!!!"

A wolf howl came, and the relaxed beastmen immediately became alert. Everyone turned in unison, their heads facing the southeast.

Lang You rushed back, his face looking like it had been smeared with soot. "King..."

"King!!! Bao Xiu was bitten by buzz-bugs!!!" The young wolf's sharp voice came first.

A commotion broke out in the wolf pack.

Lang Yan quickly converged with the young wolves. Lin Qiu followed closely and saw a black panther with a swollen head being surrounded by the young wolves as they emerged from the forest.

Bao Xiu was startled by the dozens of wolf eyes staring at him.

His eyelids were so swollen that his round eyes had become slits, and his mouth had also been bitten a few times, making him twitch whenever he tried to speak.

He stammered, his eyes showing the simple-mindedness of an honest panther. "W-what's wrong?"

...

"Awooooo!" After the silence, the wolf pack fell into instant chaos.

The howling startled the birds, causing the Hunting Team Two and the Black Feather tribe, who hadn't arrived yet, to become alert and speed up their run toward the south.

"King! He was bitten by buzz-bugs! He was bitten by buzz-bugs!" The wolf pack erupted in screams. The beastmen were so anxious they couldn't stand still; they stepped on each other, bumped into each other, and some even crashed straight into trees.

Being bitten by buzz-bugs was fatal!

How could these young wolves have gone and provoked buzz-bugs in just a short while!

Lang Yan’s temples throbbed, his eyes darkening to a terrifying degree. He said quickly, "Qiao, take two beastmen and send him back! All the young wolves who were bitten follow, the ones who weren't stay behind."

Lang Qiao called a few beastmen, hoisted Bao Xiu up, and ran.

"Hold on, we're taking you to the priest!"

"Awoooo!" The young wolves cried, "It's all our fault!"

Bao Xiu struggled, "I didn't..."

"Don't move!" Lang Qiao growled. The few wolf beastmen moved even faster.

Buzz-bugs could even kill a curved-horn beast!

"He said he would take us to find something good to eat; who knew it was to eat the buzz-bugs' nest. Awooooo!!! It's all our fault!" The young wolves cried while running, their hands empty—where was any nest?

Lang Yan had no expression on his face, his voice low as he said, "Go back."

chapters.title: 第94章
chapters.translated_text:
The second hunting team escorted the Black Feather orcs all the way, following the sound they had heard earlier.

When they reached the forest, they only found the traces where the orcs had been lying down.

Catching the scent of the Wolf King, Lang Huo temporarily suppressed his anxiety and first led the Black Feather orcs toward the Great Marsh.

Above the dense forest canopy, Yu Shan and Yu Qian led the team, followed closely by the young orcs Yu Ya and Yu Le.

Yu Ya flapped his wings, hovering mid-air, and said somewhat tiredly, "Uncle Shan, what are they doing? Why aren't they moving anymore?"

As he finished speaking, the red-furred wolf below raised its head, let out a bark, and headed straight south.

The detour had already cost them time, but although Lang Huo was worried about what had just happened, knowing Lang Yan was there, he temporarily set his mind at ease.

The team of wolf orcs continued southward, with the Black Feather orcs following behind.

Yu Ya: "Uncle Shan, wouldn't it be better if we just flew straight across? You guys came here last time anyway. It's much faster than following this pack of wolf orcs."

Yu Shan said in a low voice, his words carried away by the wind, "This is their territory, talk less."

Yu Ya tightly closed his beak and moved closer to Yu Le, who was struggling a bit on the side.

"Le, how did you end up coming along?"

Yu Le glanced at him. Having flown for so long, his voice was a bit weak, "Grandpa told me to come."

"Alright." Up ahead, Yu Qian separated the two youngsters.

This Yu Ya had been chattering nonstop the entire journey. Well, the tribe now had fishing nets and pottery pots, and during the rainy season, even when they didn't catch prey most of the time, they could still eat fish, ensuring their food supply never ran out—otherwise, where would he get so much energy?

The route was lined with trees, no different from the environment in their own territory.

The Black Feather orcs flew stubbornly in silence, and after some unknown time, they only saw a boundless Great Marsh unfolding before their eyes.

Yu Shan slowed his pace, looked at the two sheds whose roofs had been blown off, slowly folded his wings, and landed smoothly.

The orcs behind followed closely, and the two young orcs obediently stood behind their leaders, Yu Shan and Yu Qian.

Underneath the repaired shed, Lang Yu and Lang Hong, who originally helped them cook, smiled and greeted them, "We meet again."

Yu Shan: "We meet again."

Seeing that Lang Yu and the others had already prepared the meal, Lang Huo sat down to eat with them as well.

Having run for a whole day, they were long since hungry to the point of weak limbs and feet.

Thinking of the roar from earlier, Lang Huo inched closer to Lang Yu and Lang Hong, who were eating in the corner, and asked, "Yu, what happened in the forest this afternoon?"

Holding his pottery bowl, Lang Yu ate for a long time without the contents decreasing much. Thinking of the Black Panther who had been bitten and injured by the buzzing bugs, he didn't much feel like eating either.

"Bao Xiu got bitten by buzzing bugs."

Lang Huo's hand tightened, and the bowl almost slipped from his grip. "Is it serious? What about the little wolf?"

He knew Bao Xiu had always been acting alongside the little wolf; with Bao Xiu bitten, there was no guarantee the little wolf...

"The little wolf is fine. Bao Xiu... looks like he was bitten pretty badly, but he can still talk, and we don't know how he is right now. Lang乔 and the others have already sent him back to find the Priest."

Lang Huo's heart sank to the bottom.

The Priest had repeatedly warned and instructed the orcs not to go near the buzzing bugs' nests, yet something had still happened now.

He could only pray that the Priest could save him, or... that Qiu could think of a way.

Lang Huo was somewhat restless. "We still have to stay here for a few days, so there's no way to find out what's going on."

Lang Yu pointed at the dilapidated shed overhead and said, "Let's deal with this side first. The sheds need to be repaired, and we need to arrange who does what work. There are quite a few new Black Feather orcs this time. You guys... lead them along first, and once they're familiar with things, you can go back."

Lang Huo was here with the purpose of keeping an eye on things as well, but he couldn't say that out loud.

Amidst the crowd of Black Feather orcs, the orcs were gobbling down their food hastily. Of the two young orcs, one almost buried his head into the bowl, shoveling food in large mouthfuls. The other was refined and dainty, like a cub that would never grow up, eating bite by tiny bite, which made the watching orcs anxious.

Yu Ya finished his food in one breath and wiped his mouth.

Smacking his lips twice, he squatted back down among his fellow orcs and looked around. It was just a forest, a large lake, and a few extra mud-and-wood sheds—no different from their side at all.

What else could they even do here?

Yu Ya stared at the large lake; could it be for them to catch fish?

He nudged Yu Le with his arm, causing the pottery bowl held by the thin-cheeked yet fair young orc to sway a few times, almost spilling the soup.

"Le."

"Mhm." Yu Le gave a muffled response, hugging his bowl and shuffling closer to Yu Qian. He didn't want to talk to this heavy-handed orc.

In the past, he didn't play with Yu Ya and the others either, having nothing to say.

Yet Yu Ya failed to notice the young orc's avoidance and leaned closer to Yu Le. "Le, stay closer to me. We're the only two young orcs, let's play together from now on."

Yu Le was almost squeezed into the corner. Yu Shan looked back and hauled the chattering Yu Ya aside.

"What playing, what playing? You're here to work."

Yu Shan estimated it would still take a few dozen sun-cycles before they could go to the Wolf Mountain side to harvest the tail-grass they mentioned, and only then would it be time for these two young orcs to learn.

Since they had just arrived, they had to put on a good performance, otherwise the wolf orcs would think they brought the young orcs here just for a free ride.

The Black Feather orcs were well-behaved; as soon as they finished eating, they hurried to repair the shed.

The floor of the shed looked as though it had been flooded, dried out to a layer of dust, with moss growing in the corners.

The Black Feather orcs repaired their own living quarters themselves. Mindful that they would start working tomorrow and certainly have no free time later, Yu Shan worked through the night to assign some orcs to clean the inside of the shed, while others gathered dry grass and branches to patch the roof.

With the chieftain away, Yu Shan was the leader, and everyone listened to him.

Yu Ya followed at Yu Shan's heels, grabbing grass with his claws and flying up to the roof to deliver it whenever he was told to pass some.

Yu Le followed behind Yu Qian, his eyes moist and listless.

He was still worrying about what his grandpa would do after he left.

Yu Qian was busy spreading the bedding nest. Seeing the young orc looking dazed, he couldn't help gently massaging the boy's hair. The strands were soft, yet somewhat withered and yellowish.

He asked gently, "Are you not used to it?"

Yu Le shook his head, his tears trembling on the verge of falling.

Yu Qian sighed softly, gathered the young orc into his arms, and said in a soft voice, "Don't worry, we are here. There are also tribal orcs watching over the chieftain's side, everything will be fine."

"Mhm!" Feeling the faint scent coming from the sub-orc, Yu Le couldn't hold back his tears as they fell, sobbing as he spoke.

"Be a good boy. We're here to work, and also to learn skills. The wolf orcs are pretty decent, we aren't afraid."

……

"Not afraid?!" The old priest gripped his walking stick, waving it near Bao Xiu's side. "Say that again—what is it you're not afraid of?!"

Bao Xiu pinned his ears back, lying flat on the ground with his swollen head buried under his paws.

"I'm really, really not afraid. I've raided buzzing bug nests before too; as long as you get bitten less, you, you're not afraid..."

The priest raised his walking stick, ready to strike. Lang An, who was lingering nearby, immediately grabbed the stick and urged anxiously, "Priest, don't get angry. Let's first see how to... treat this!"

They had all seen with their own eyes the horned beasts killed by buzzing bug bites.

"N-no need, it just looks scary to the orcs, if I rest and recover..."

The priest shot him a look as sharp as a keen blade. Bao Xiu covered his eyes with his paws, burying his entire body on the ground without daring to utter another sound.

A table and several long benches had also been placed in the priest's cave. Lang Yan and Lin Qiu sat on one side, while Lang Qiao and the others who had escorted Bao Xiu back also remained in the cave without leaving.

Their hunting grounds were still some distance away from Wolf Mountain. The orcs had run back with all their might, terrified that Bao Xiu might pass out along the way.

Seeing that he could still speak coherently now, they were somewhat terrified, fearing that the young orc might roll his eyes and pass away from a moment of carelessness.

An atmosphere of unease permeated the cave, and the adult orcs were somewhat restless.

Lang Jin shuffled over, rubbing against his companion, and sprawled out beside Bao Xiu.

With his paw blocking the side of his face, thinking the adult orcs couldn't see, he whispered to Bao Xiu, "Are you... really okay?"

Bao Xiu managed a smile at him, only to wince in pain and bare his teeth.

Nearby, Lang Qiao grabbed Lang Jin by the neck, dragging him away from Bao Xiu.

"We haven't settled accounts with you yet, behave yourself."

Lang Jin rolled his eyes, casting a stealthy glance at Lang Yan, who had been sitting quietly in the cave all along. His scalp tightened and his mouth twitched twice; the moment Lang Yan looked over, he immediately looked up at the ceiling.

Lang Yan's eyes were pitch black.

The buzzing bugs were huge and somewhat venomous. However, orcs had strong enough physiques, and since Bao Xiu had been fine for this long, he should be alright.

How could the priest possibly have medicine to treat buzzing bug bites? They didn't even dare go near these creatures, and even thought the lumps on the orcs' faces were bites from the buzzing bugs rather than stings from their tails.

After much deliberation, he could only provide some herbal medicine to reduce swelling and dispel venom.

Lin Qiu was also helpless, but taking advantage of the time the priest was busy mixing medicine, he hurriedly said, "Wang, while there is still light, we need to pull out the tail stingers from his wounds and clean the wounds first."

"Tail stingers?" Breaking free from Lang Qiao, Lang Jin squatted down in front of Bao Xiu to inspect closely.

With the pitch-black fur, how could anyone see anything? He reached out to rummage through Bao Xiu's fur and accidentally poked a wound, causing Bao Xiu to twitch in pain and tears to burst from his eyes.

Startled, Lang Jin quickly withdrew his paws and muttered, "Why grow fur so black?"

Bao Xiu's wound was both painful and itchy. His paws couldn't help scratching the ground as he still expressed regret, "It's a pity I didn't shake it down."

"You're still thinking about that!" Hearing Lin Qiu's words, Lang Qiao moved the little panther a bit further toward the cave entrance, pinched his ears, and stared with narrowed pupils for a long time until he finally spotted something.

"Go, ask the priest for the tweezers." With his amber eyes fixed on the wound, Lang Qiao nudged the little wolf with his foot.

The two little wolves immediately went to ask the priest for the tweezers, watching wide-eyed as their Uncle Qiao extracted a nail-length stinger from Bao Xiu's nose.

Extremely thin.

"Do buzzing bugs' mouths grow this long?"

"Qiu already said this is a tail stinger, so it definitely belongs on the tail."

Having found the first one, Lang Qiao successively discovered even more from Bao Xiu's body. Looking at the things on the leaf, a few little wolves suddenly came to a realization and said, "So buzzing bugs bite people with their bottoms!"

"Are you done yet?" The priest's voice came from inside.

Lang Qiao: "There should be more."

As he spoke, Lang An and several other sub-orcs came out, and while asking Bao Xiu, they carefully parted his fur to search diligently.

Bao Xiu was tightly surrounded by the wolf orcs.

With his swollen, slit-like eyes looking this way and that, his nose suddenly felt sour and tears welled up in the corners of his eyes.

He let out a sob, causing the hands of several wolf orcs to pause as if facing a formidable enemy.

"Don't, don't die on us!"

Not daring to cry, Bao Xiu said in a muffled voice, "I-I won't die. I've raided buzzing bug nests with Priest Rong before, they're really delicious."

Lang An: "It hurts like hell is more like it. Don't move, everyone hurry up and search."

However, with Bao Xiu saying this, everyone felt somewhat reassured.

As long as he wouldn't die, that was fine.

Bao Xiu remained lying flat like that, his vision blocked. A well-behaved little black panther, docile and obedient, his prickly defenses were now completely gone.

After several orcs squinted and searched for quite a while until their eyes ached, deeming it about enough, they applied medicine to the young orc.

With his entire head plastered in herbal medicine and reeking strongly of it, the little wolves were so choked by the smell that they didn't dare get close again.

As darkness fell, most of the orcs in the cave left.

Lang An and a few others went to cook, and Lang Qiao also grabbed the little wolves and left, leaving only the old priest, Lang Yan, Lin Qiu, and the soundly sleeping little panther sprawled on the ground inside the cave.

Leaning his shoulder against Lang Yan, Lin Qiu said in a low voice, "What I said—it won't be a big problem, right?"

Lang Yan gripped his wrist, pulling him up to his feet. "Don't think about it."

Knowing that Lin Qiu was still dwelling on that honey, seeing how even a thick-skinned and tough little black panther had ended up like this, one could only imagine what would happen to the delicate Lin Qiu.

Lin Qiu flicked his wrist, realizing his action was somewhat childish. He paused, tightened his handsome face, and followed Lang Yan down the mountain.

Cooking smoke began to rise in front of Wolf Mountain.

While Lang Mo's team was busy playing with mud, Lang Shi led Lang Mu to catch and slaughter a youyou beast.

By the time darkness fell completely, Lang Mo returned from the western cave, drenched in water and carrying a faint muddy scent.

Everyone had been busy digging soil today and hadn't done any other work.

Lang Mo had taken a bath in the river, shaking his damp hair as he rushed directly in front of Lin Qiu.

"Qiu! Is there ice to eat today?"

This was a habit the orcs had developed during the rainy season: they liked to make ice using clean water, then turn it into shaved ice topped with jam and various diced fruits. Afterward, they would scoop up a huge spoonful with a spoon and pop it straight into their mouths—sweet, icy, and full of fruity fragrance...

Lang Mo swallowed his saliva, his round eyes bright as he looked expectantly at Lin Qiu.

Having nothing to do at the moment, Lin Qiu was sitting on the low wall beneath the shed, leaning against Lang Yan. The two orcs enjoyed the breeze while keeping an eye on the cubs frolicking about.

When Lang Mo shuffled over, his desire to eat was completely undisguised.

Licking the drool from the corner of his mouth, he simply waited for Lin Qiu to nod.

Lin Qiu looked at Lang Yan.

Lang Yan lazily replied, "Mhm."

"Thank you, Wang!" Lang Mo's team almost jumped up.

Watching them hurriedly enter the cave, Lin Qiu reminded them, "Don't be greedy and eat too much, it's not like the rainy season anymore!"

"Got it!" The orcs had already run far away, their voices coming back blurred, showing just how impatient they were.

Accompanied by the smell of cooking smoke and firewood, the orcs successively washed their own pottery bowls and gathered beneath the shed.

The dim yellow full moon shone as the clouds dispersed, casting a brightness so clear it felt as though lamps had been lit.

The whitish soup in the pots boiled, bubbling up with round, large bubbles. Each pot was filled to the brim, with chunks of meat and bone piled so high they formed a peak.

Several basins of cold tossed wild vegetables were also placed on the stove.

The meat soup was scalding hot, and since the weather was still somewhat warm, the orcs didn't feel like eating everything hot all at once.

Howling sounds echoed, and the orcs inside the cave also emerged.

Everyone lined up to dish out their food. Lang Jin, who had been gossiping with Lang冰 and Lang Rong who were queuing behind him about what happened outside today, suddenly remembered that Bao Xiu hadn't come downstairs from the cave and simply scooped up a bowl to take up to him.

Lang冰 and Lang Rong followed closely behind him, one habitually helping to carry the chopsticks, and the other holding a spoon.

Upon ascending to the priest's cave, a fire was lit inside, and Bao Xiu was still lying flat on the animal skins spread across the ground.

The priest didn't allow him to move; he needed to be observed for the entire night, so he had to sleep here.

Upon hearing movement, he opened his eyes just a slit—looking as good as not opening them at all.

Lang Jin chuckled and placed the pottery bowl right in front of him.

"Eat up, it's youyou beast."

Bao Xiu's eyelids twitched, and the dried layer of herbal paste cracked into pieces, shedding a few flakes.

Lang冰 and Lang Rong sat surrounding him, each holding a large pottery bowl in their hands, looking at him with a mix of curiosity.

Sniffing, Bao Xiu propped himself up with his paws.

Looking gratefully at the three little wolves before him, he said, "Don't worry, once I recover, I'll get buzzing bug nests for you to eat again. They really are delicious."

Lang冰: "...... You should heal your injuries first."

Lang Jin nodded, a faint gleam in his eyes, "Mn, let's wait until your injuries are healed."
chapters.source_text:
狩猎二队接了黑羽兽人一路奔袭，寻着此前听见声音的地方而来。
到了林子，只发现兽人们卧趴过的痕迹。
嗅到有狼王的味道，狼火暂且按下心中焦急，先把黑羽兽人带去大泽那边。
密密匝匝的林木上空，羽山跟羽千带队，后头最先跟着小兽人羽涯跟羽乐。
羽涯挥动翅膀，滞在半空，有些疲累道：“阿山叔，他们在干什么？怎么不走了？”
话落，底下毛色带红的狼抬头看了眼，叫了声，又直直往南边去。
斜插过来已经耽搁了时间，狼火虽然操心刚刚的事儿，但知道有狼岩在，暂且放下心。
狼兽人队伍继续向着南边去，黑羽兽人则跟上。
羽涯：“阿山叔，我们直接飞过去不就好了，反正你们上次来过。比跟着这群狼兽人快多了。”
羽山低声，话随着风传到后头，“这是人家地盘，少说话。”
羽涯闭紧鸟喙，靠近一旁有些吃力的羽乐。
“乐，你怎么跟来了？”
羽乐看他一眼，飞了这么久，声音有些虚弱：“阿爷叫我来的。”
“好了。”前头羽千隔开两个小的。
这羽涯一路上说个不停，也是部落有了渔网跟陶锅，雨季大部分时候没捕到猎物还能吃鱼，食物没断过，不然哪有精力。
沿途都是树木，与自家领地的环境没什么两样。
黑羽兽人闷头飞，不知多久后，只看着眼前一片望不见尽头的大泽。
羽山速度放缓，看着那两处被吹飞了顶的棚子，慢慢收拢翅膀，丝滑落下。
后头兽人紧跟着，两个小兽人乖乖站在领头的羽山跟羽千后头。
那修好的一个棚子底下，原本帮他们做饭的狼雨跟狼虹笑着跟他们打招呼：“又见面了。”
羽山：“又见面了。”
狼火见狼雨他们已经把饭做好了，也一起坐下来吃。
他们跑了一天，早饿得手脚绵软。
狼火想着刚刚那叫声，挪着靠近角落里吃饭的狼雨跟狼虹，问：“雨，下午林子里出了什么事？”
狼雨捧着陶碗，吃了许久碗里没下去多少，想到被嗡嗡虫咬伤的黑豹，他也没多少胃口。
“豹休让嗡嗡虫给咬了。”
狼火手一紧，碗差点从手中跑出去，“严不严重？小狼呢？”
他知道豹休一直跟着小狼行动，豹休被咬，难保小狼……
“小狼没事，豹休……看着咬得不算轻，但还能说话，现在也不知道怎么样了。狼乔他们已经送回去找祭司了。”
狼火一颗心沉到底。
祭司千叮咛万嘱咐，不要兽人们靠近嗡嗡虫的巢穴，现在还是出事儿了。
只祈祷，祭司能救，或者……楸能想想办法。
狼火有些焦躁，“我们还要在这边待几天，想知道情况也没办法。”
狼雨指了指顶上破败的棚子道：“先忙这边吧，棚子要修补，干什么活要安排。这次新来的黑羽兽人不少，你们……先带一带，熟悉了再回去。”
狼火在这里，目的也是盯着点儿，不过这话不能明说。
黑羽兽人堆里，兽人们呼呼啦啦赶着吃饭。两个小兽人，一个脑袋快埋进碗里，大口大口刨食。一个斯斯文文，跟养不大的幼崽似的，吃个食儿都一点一点的，看得兽人心急。
羽涯一口气吃完，抹了一把嘴。
吧唧两下，再蹲在自家兽人堆里，四处看看。不就是林子，大湖，还多了几个泥巴木头建造的棚子，跟他们那边没什么两样。
他们来这儿还能做什么？
羽涯盯着那片大湖，难不成给他们捕鱼的？
他胳膊碰了碰羽乐，面颊偏瘦，但白净的小兽人捧着的陶碗晃荡几下，汤水差点撒出来。
“乐。”
“唔。”羽乐囫囵应了声，抱着碗往羽千身边挪了挪。他不想跟这个下手没轻没重的兽人说话。
以前他也不跟羽涯他们玩儿，没什么话说。
羽涯偏看不出小兽人的回避，还往羽乐那边靠了靠，“乐，你离我近点儿。就咱们两个是小兽人，以后咱俩一起玩儿。”
羽乐都快被他挤到角落去了，羽山回头看一眼，拎着说个不停的羽涯往边上放。
“玩儿什么玩儿，你是来干活儿的。”
羽山估摸着还要等几十个太阳日才能去狼山那边收他们说的尾巴草，到时候才是这两个小兽人学习的时候。
现在刚来，必须得好好表现，不然狼兽人以为他们是带小兽人来白吃白喝的。
黑羽兽人安分，吃完饭赶紧修补棚子。
棚子地面像被水淹过，晒干了一层灰，边边角角还长了青苔。
黑羽兽人自己住的自己修，羽山惦记着明天开始干活了，后头肯定没空，这会儿连夜安排兽人一部分清理棚子里面，一部分找干草树枝来修补棚顶。
族长不在，羽山就是领队，大伙儿都听他的。
羽涯跟在羽山屁股后头，让递草就用爪子抓着飞上棚顶送过去。
羽乐则跟在羽千后头，眼睛湿漉漉，无精打采。
他还惦记着他走之后，他阿爷怎么办。
羽千正在铺窝，看小兽人呆呆的，忍不住轻轻揉了揉他的头发。发丝柔软，还有些枯黄。
他温柔道：“是不是不习惯？”
羽乐摇头，眼泪摇摇欲坠。
羽千轻轻一叹，拢着小兽人靠在怀里，轻声道：“放心，有我们在。族长那边也有部落的兽人看着，没事儿的。”
“嗯！”羽乐感受到亚兽人身上的淡淡香味，憋不住眼泪掉下来，哽咽着道。
“乖，咱们是来干活儿的，也是来学本领的。狼兽人还算好，咱不怕。”
……
“不怕？！”老祭司抓着拐杖，悬在豹休身侧，“你再说一遍你不怕什么？！”
豹休耳朵后撇，趴在地上，肿胀的脑袋埋在爪子下。
“真的不、不怕，我以前也掏过嗡嗡虫的窝，只要被咬得少，就、就不怕……”
祭司抄起拐杖就要打，围在旁边的狼安立马抓住拐杖，急道：“祭司，别气，先看看他这……怎么治吧！”
他们可是亲眼看见被嗡嗡虫咬死的弯角兽的。
“不、不用，就是看着吓兽人，养一养……”
祭司一个眼神甩过来，利刀子似的。豹休爪子捂眼，整个埋在地上一声不敢吭了。
祭司山洞也放了一张桌子，几条长凳，狼岩跟林楸坐在一侧，送豹休回来的狼乔几个也守在洞中没走。
他们狩猎的地方离狼山还是有点距离，兽人们尽全力跑回来，就怕路上豹休厥过去。
现在看他还能好好说话，有些心惊胆战，生怕一不小心，小兽人白眼一翻就没了。
洞里弥漫着不安的气息，成年兽人们都有些焦躁。
狼金挪着，跟同伴磨蹭着，趴在豹休身边。
他爪子挡在脸侧，还以为成年兽人看不见，小声问豹休：“你、真没事儿？”
豹休冲着他一笑，又疼得龇牙。
旁边的狼乔一把薅着狼金的脖子，拽着他远离豹休。
“你的账还没跟你算呢，安分点。”
狼金眼珠子一转，悄悄看了一眼山洞里一直静坐的狼岩。他头皮发紧，嘴巴动了两下，在狼岩看来时，立马往天上看去。
狼岩眼里漆黑。
嗡嗡虫很大，有些毒。但兽人体格够强，豹休这么久没问题，应当就还好。
祭司哪有什么治疗被嗡嗡虫咬伤的药，他们都不敢靠近这东西，甚至以为兽人脸上的包是嗡嗡虫咬的，而不是尾巴蜇的。
思来想去，只能给些消肿解毒的草药。
林楸也无可奈何，不过趁着祭司忙着配药，赶紧道：“王，趁着还有光，要把他身上伤口的尾针夹出来，伤口先清理干净。”
“尾针？”狼金挣脱狼乔，蹲在豹休面前细看。
黢黑的毛，哪里看得出什么东西。他伸手往豹休毛毛里翻，一下戳到伤处，疼得豹休一个抽搐，眼泪都飙出来了。
狼金吓得赶紧收爪子，嘀咕：“长这么黑干什么？”
豹休伤口又疼又痒，爪子忍不住抓地，还在遗憾，“可惜没摇下来。”
“还想着呢！”狼乔听了林楸的话，将小豹子往洞外面挪了挪，捏着他耳朵，瞳孔缩紧看了许久，总算叫他看见个东西。
“去，找祭司要夹子。”狼乔琥珀色的眼睛不离那伤处，脚下踢了踢小狼。
两小狼立马找祭司要来夹子，眼睁睁看着他们乔叔从豹休的鼻子上夹出来一个指甲盖长的针。
极细。
“嗡嗡虫的嘴有这么长？”
“楸都说了，这是尾针，那肯定是尾巴上的。”
狼乔找了第一个，后头又接二连三地从豹休身上找出来更多。几个小狼看着叶片上的东西，恍然大悟道：“原来嗡嗡虫是用屁股咬人！”
“好了没有？”里头，祭司问道。
狼乔：“应该还有。”
话落，狼安几个亚兽人又出来，一边问豹休，一边小心翼翼翻着他毛毛，认真找。
豹休被狼兽人围了个严实。
他肿胀的眯缝眼左看右看，竟是鼻子一酸，眼角蓄起泪来。
他抽噎一下，几个狼兽人手一顿，如临大敌。
“可别、别死了！”
豹休不敢哭，声音嗡嗡的道：“不、不会死的，我以前跟着荣祭司也掏过嗡嗡虫的窝，很好吃的。”
狼安：“好疼还差不多，别动，大伙儿赶紧找。”
不过豹休这一说，大家心里有了底。
不会死就好。
豹休就这么趴着，视线被挡住。乖乖的一头小黑豹子，温顺听话，身上的刺儿这会儿彻底散了个干净。
几个兽人眯着眼睛找了好一会儿，都看得眼酸，差不多了，才给小兽人上药。
豹休一脑袋上糊上草药，满身药味儿，几个小狼被呛得都不敢再靠近。
天色暗了，洞内兽人走了大半。
狼安几个去做饭，狼乔也抓着小狼走了，洞内只剩下老祭司，狼岩，林楸，还有趴地上睡熟的小豹子。
林楸肩膀挨着狼岩，低声道：“我说的，不会有大问题吧。”
狼岩抓着他手腕，带着他站起来，“别想。”
知道林楸还惦记着那什么蜂蜜，单看皮糙肉厚的小黑豹都成这样了，更别提细皮嫩肉的林楸。
林楸晃了下手腕，察觉到有些幼稚，一滞，绷起俊秀的脸跟着狼岩下山。
狼山前冒起了炊烟。
狼莫小队忙着玩儿泥巴，狼石便带着狼木抓了一头呦呦兽杀了。
等到天色黑透，狼莫带着一身水汽跟点点泥腥味儿，从西边山洞回来。
今日大伙儿忙着刨土，没干其他活儿。
狼莫在河里洗了个澡，甩着湿润的头发，一口气冲到林楸面前。
“楸！今天有冰吃吗？”
兽人雨季里养成的习惯，喜欢用干净的水制冰，再做成冰沙，放上果酱、切碎的各种果丁。然后用勺子舀一大勺，往嘴里一塞，甜蜜冰凉，满口果香气……
狼莫咽了咽口水，圆眼晶亮，期待地看着林楸。
林楸这会儿没事儿，在棚子底下的矮墙上坐着，边上靠着狼岩，两个兽人吹着风，顺带看着四处撒欢儿的幼崽。
狼莫杵到跟前，想吃的欲望遮都遮不住。
他舔着嘴角的哈喇子，只等林楸点头。
林楸看向狼岩。
狼岩懒声：“嗯。”
“谢谢王！”狼莫小队差点蹦起来。
林楸看着他们急急忙忙进洞，提醒道：“别贪多，现在不比雨季！”
“知道了！”兽人已经跑远，声音模糊传来，可见多急。
伴着炊烟与柴火的味道，兽人们陆陆续续洗干净自己的陶碗，汇聚到棚子底下。
明月昏黄，云雾散开，竟透亮得仿佛点了灯。
锅里炖得发白的汤沸腾，鼓起圆圆的大泡，每个锅里都填得满满当当的，连肉带骨头的肉块堆得冒尖。
灶台上还放着几盆凉拌的野菜。
肉汤烫嘴，天气还有些热，兽人们也不乐意一下都吃热的。
狼嚎声响起，山洞里的兽人也都出来。
大伙儿排着队打饭，狼金正跟身后排队的狼冰、狼溶嘀嘀咕咕说完今天在外面的事，忽然想起山洞里豹休没下来，干脆也给他打了一碗带上去。
狼冰跟狼溶跟在他后头，一个顺手帮忙拿了筷子，一个抓着勺子。
上到祭司山洞，里头点着火，地上铺着的兽皮上，豹休还在上面趴着。
祭司不允许他挪动，今晚得观察一番，所以他得在这边睡着。
一听到动静，他睁开眼，就那么一条缝，看着也跟没睁眼似的。
狼金嘿嘿一笑，将陶碗往他面前一放。
“吃，呦呦兽哦。”
豹休眼皮抖了抖，干掉的草药糊糊裂成块，扑簌掉下来一些。
狼冰跟狼溶围坐在他跟前，每个兽人手里都捧着个大陶碗，有些好奇地看着他。
豹休吸着鼻子，爪子撑着起来。
他感激地看着面前三个小狼，道：“你们放心，等我好了，我再给你们弄嗡嗡虫巢吃，真的很好吃。”
狼冰：“……你先养好伤再说。”
狼金点点头，眼里冒着幽光，“嗯，养好伤再说。”

豹休这伤一养五天，好得彻彻底底，豹脸也恢复了圆润。
不过经次嗡嗡虫一刺，怎么看都比以前憨傻几分，尤其那极圆的眼睛，怎么看怎么都不聪明。
豹休伤好得差不多，狼火也带着队伍从大泽那边回来。
他们只带了几车鸟粪，麻线这些黑羽兽人收割后泡在水里，现在还没处理好。
一回到狼山，刚趴地上没躺上一会儿，就叫狼莫叫去帮忙给砖块脱模。
一小队二十多个兽人，几下就把百来块砖弄出来了。
狼火看着那方方正正的泥巴块儿，瞧着狼生带着幼崽从身边跑过去，忍不住拎着幼崽，抓着他爪子往那泥块儿上一按。
“诶！干什么呢！”狼莫吼道。
胖墩墩的狼崽子双眼无辜地被拎着，爪子收起，爪垫带着泥巴。
狼火一本正经道：“这小崽子往泥巴上踩呢，我帮你抓。”
幼崽艰难争辩：“嗷嗷嗷嗷，不是我嗷。”
狼火顺手捏住幼崽嘴筒子，“他说他错了。”
狼火：“小心点儿，好不容易弄出来的。”
这已经是第三次脱模了，前头几次不是泥巴软了，就是泥硬了，或者裂开，这砖瞧着简单，可做起来也有门道。
楸又不知道这些，还得他们自己摸索。
狼莫把这些看得仅次于食物。
这边弄完，差不多该吃午饭。
吃饭哪个兽人有狼莫积极，他先一步跑出去，自己端了陶碗吃。等到狼火慢悠悠晃回去，狼莫已经吃完，手里端着一碗冰沙。
那碗冰沙占据了他半个小盆似的陶碗。
狼火：“哪来的？”
他四处看了眼，没见着灶台上有，狼安他们也没做。
狼莫贼兮兮冲他一笑，“当然是我自己做的。”
狼火：“楸不是说不让吃。”
狼莫轻咳两声，得意道：“你忘了，我之前救豹休，可有十次选择食物的机会。”
狼火哥俩好的抱住他肩膀，“那你还剩几次，送我一次呗。”
狼莫：“最后一次。”
狼火一把将他甩开，“我刚刚给你帮了忙，你就这么敷衍我？”
狼莫：“真的是最后一次，前头几次，我这几天都用完了。”
他小小声抗议，“本来楸都不让我再吃的。”
狼火：“哼。”
狼莫看了看自己碗里，冰化得快，他递出去，“要不，分你一半。”
狼火看着那果酱混合着冰沙，大半化开，乱糟糟的，“算了。”
他嫌弃。
狼莫赶紧护着碗，“这可是你自己说的啊。”
狼火：“哼！”
东部大陆天气变化快，雨季结束后几天，下了几场小雨，温度也降了一点下来。
白天出太阳还有些热，但夜晚逐渐凉爽。
现在已经不用放冰盆，兽人们晚上依旧能睡得好了。
狼莫一口闷掉剩下的冰沙，满脸红润地去溪边洗碗。现在大雨少，溪水也慢慢干净了。
兽人们不去溪里捕鱼，现在竟也隐隐看得见藏在水草里的小鱼小虾。
幼崽最喜欢来这一处，抓着楸给他们做的小网兜，在溪水里捞。
捞好放罐子里，放上些溪石、浮萍，自个儿养着，竟也叫他们养得活。
吃过饭，兽人们蹲在溪边，叼着块秃毛的牙刷刷牙。
幼崽蹲在一侧，由成年兽人教着，也龇牙刷得有模有样。
有的兽人洗过澡，抓着兽皮或者麻布短裤搓洗，弄完了，才懒洋洋地甩着两条长腿儿，惬意地任由晚风拂过还滴着水的头发，回山洞里睡觉去。
半夜过，火堆熄灭，洞里黑得伸手不见五指。
林楸翻过身，嗅着淡淡的驱蚊的草药味道，梦中隐隐听到低低的痛呼。
“嗷呜，嗷呜……”哀哀切切，林楸微微皱眉。
“哼！好痛嗷……”
边上狼岩翻身，林楸挣扎着醒了，确认听到了兽人呼疼，一个翻身坐起来。
他眼睛还没睁开，狼岩按着他肩膀，“继续睡。”
“哪里还能睡得着。”林楸反过来抓着他手，带着自己起来，“谁在叫？”
狼岩见兽人们已经燃起火来，狼莫趴在草窝里，捂着肚子打滚。他道：“狼莫，看着吃坏了肚子。”
山洞里，兽人们围着狼莫，低低地说着话。
每个兽人脸上都写满担忧，见狼岩跟林楸靠近，立刻让开位置。
“王，莫肚子疼。”
“他跟我们吃的都一样，难不成背着我们吃其他东西了？”
狼岩：“送祭司那去。”
大晚上的，狼西跟旁边的兽人扛起狼莫，赶紧送到祭司山洞。兽人们不放心，都跟着过去。
走了一半，狼岩回头看一眼道：“明天要狩猎采集的，都回去。”
一下离开大半兽人，全都听话得很。
祭司山洞。
老祭司被连夜叫起来，听到狼莫支支吾吾将最近几天天天两顿冰沙的事儿一说，忍不住梆梆拍了狼莫脑门几下。
“尽给我找事儿！”
狼岩看狼莫疼得脸发白，劝着老祭司先配草药。
林楸蹲在狼莫跟前，兽人哼哼唧唧，试图抓着林楸的衣摆哭诉一下，叫狼岩瞧见，一爪子拍开。
“不要乱动。”
“我……呕！”
林楸下意识要退开，但蹲着只能一屁股往地上坐，狼岩手臂环住他肩膀，勾住腿弯往后一抱，离狼莫离得远远的。
老祭司急声道：“赶紧找东西接着，别吐我山洞。”
林楸拍了下狼岩胸口，“放我下来。”
狼岩示意狼石，抓着狼莫先去洞外吐。
狼安道：“我给他烧点水。”他匆匆下去，走了一半，被祭司叫住。
“药拿去熬了。”
草药裹在大叶片里抛下来，狼安抓住，往棚子底下走。
大山洞洞口蹲着人，见狼安回来，十几双狼眼睛发亮。
他们小声问：“安，莫怎么样了？”
狼安：“没大事，祭司说他吃多了冰。”
兽人听罢，摇摇脑袋，回窝里睡觉去了。
让他得意，现在吃出问题来了吧。
狼莫折腾一阵，又吐又拉，林楸怕他拉虚脱了，赶紧下去帮狼安看着药。待药汤一好，放水盆里凉一下，马上抓着狼莫给灌下去。
不过一会儿，又给他吐出来。
狼安皱眉，抓着狼莫道：“再吐，以后什么也别吃。”
狼莫泪眼汪汪。
“嗷呜……”
林楸再端来一碗，狼莫捏着鼻子慢慢喝。
几个兽人守着他。
祭司也没睡，直看着他不再吐了，圈着肚子哼哼唧唧打瞌睡，这才道：“我看没问题了，你们也都回去，我守着。”
林楸：“我明天没事儿……”
祭司：“不学了？”
林楸：“那我回去睡去了。”
狼安还想说什么，祭司摆手，道：“我觉少，我守着，都回。”
没人拗得过祭司，只能听话回了。
折腾半晚，林楸后半夜睡得迷迷糊糊，天一亮就起来了。
他下意识寻着狼莫草窝看，狼岩往侧边挪了一步，挡住林楸视线。
林楸慢慢抬头，眼里还有些困顿。
狼岩：“他还没从祭司山洞回来，不过肚子没那么疼了。”
林楸：“草药能治就好。”
昨晚出了这点事，也没耽搁兽人们今日狩猎采集。
洞内的兽人这会儿只剩零星，狼果赶着幼崽，叫他们都往外头去。
走着走着，忽然一个幼崽停下不动。
林楸正纳闷，狼岩疾步上前，抓着幼崽从幼崽堆里挪开。下一瞬，怀里就抱着个大胖娃娃。
林楸一惊，“又变了！”
狼果赶紧叫幼崽分开一些，“王，这一批幼崽，雪季前能变大半。可好像没有听说哪个亚兽人怀崽了。”
狼岩：“没伴侣，让他们怎么怀。”
不止狼部落的情况，大部分部落都是亚兽人跟雌性兽人少，雄兽人多。
“总有些有伴侣。”狼果道。
狼岩：“明年应该有。”
现在日子比以前好一点，兽人们应该愿意生。
简单交流过，狼岩看着怀里懵懵的白胖幼崽，道：“叫什么名字？”
幼崽一愣，笑弯了眼睛，侧头来蹭狼岩。甜滋滋的，跟裹了糖霜的糯米团子似的。
林楸轻声：“是个亚兽人崽崽？”
幼崽张开手，冲着林楸，学着狼生的叫法道：“楸楸。”
“王问你叫什么呢？”林楸脸上浮上笑意。
幼崽摇头，奶声奶气：“不嗷，知道。”
林楸笑容一僵。
狼王习以为常，道：“不是所有幼崽都有名字，要是他们的阿父阿爸不在了，那就没兽人取名。”
“那他……”林楸看着怀里的小崽崽，有些怜惜。
“嗯。”狼岩淡淡道。
楸没来之前，狼部落每天都有兽人饿死，这并不是夸张。有的兽人为了省出口粮给幼崽吃饱一点，本就少的食物，自己甚至只能吃几口维持生命。
好在部落都是将幼崽一起养，他们的亲兽人都忙着采集狩猎，几乎没有跟在自己亲兽人后头长大的。
他们一般对同伴比对生养他们的兽人更亲。
在食物缺乏的兽神大陆，这样反倒是对他们好。
亲缘关系浅薄，同伴之间才是互相扶持，合作的亲密关系。大家一起长大，培养默契，能更有利于一同捕猎，养活自己。
林楸看着笑容甜甜的幼崽，忍不住别开头，心里一酸。
脸颊上温软，幼崽却不懂。
他乖乖地将脸颊贴过来，手也紧紧抱着林楸的脖子。
“楸楸。”
林楸的眼神更加温柔，额头抵着幼崽额头，轻声道：“那我们给你取个名字，好不好？”
幼崽靠在林楸身上，又弯了弯眼。
林楸看向狼岩，“你是狼王，你取。”
狼岩：“狼壮。”
林楸嫌弃，“人家是亚兽人，这个好难听。”
“长得壮实一点不好吗？”
狼果在一边悄声道：“咱部落还有直接叫狼丑的呢。”
林楸：“再想。”
狼岩戳了戳幼崽的脸颊，软鼓鼓的，一下凹陷下去。他也不哭不闹，反而抓着狼岩的手，往嘴巴里塞。
林楸一下挡住，眼神催促狼岩。
狼岩：“狼圆。”
“圆滚滚的。”
林楸摸摸幼崽小脸，“这个好，但不是圆滚滚，是圆满。咱们以后就叫狼圆。”
狼圆是个小黑狼，但生得像汤圆。
这样一想，名字正合适。
chapters.translated_text:
Leopard Xiu spent five days recuperating, recovering completely, and his leopard face regained its roundness.

However, after being stung by the buzzing insects, he looked a bit more foolish than before, especially with those extremely round eyes that didn't look smart no matter how you looked at them.

Just as Leopard Xiu was mostly recovered, Wolf Huo returned with the team from the Great Marsh.

They only brought back a few carts of bird droppings; the hemp fibers harvested by the Black Feather orcs were still soaking in water and hadn't been processed yet.

As soon as they returned to Wolf Mountain and lay on the ground for a moment, they were called by Wolf Mo to help demold the bricks.

A small team of over twenty orcs quickly produced about a hundred bricks.

Wolf Huo looked at those square mud blocks, and seeing Wolf Sheng running past with a cub, he couldn't help but pick up the cub and press its paw onto a mud block.

"Hey! What are you doing!" Wolf Mo roared.

The chubby wolf cub was held up with an innocent look, its claws retracted, its paw pads covered in mud.

Wolf Huo said solemnly, "This little cub was stepping on the mud, I'm helping you catch it."

The cub struggled to argue, "Ao ao ao ao, it wasn't me, ao."

Wolf Huo casually pinched the cub's snout, "He says he was wrong."

Wolf Huo: "Be careful, these were hard to make."

This was already the third time they had demolded; the previous attempts either had mud that was too soft, too hard, or cracked. These bricks looked simple, but there was a knack to making them.

Qiu didn't know these things, so they had to figure it out themselves.

Wolf Mo valued these only second to food.

Once they finished here, it was almost time for lunch.

No orc was as enthusiastic about eating as Wolf Mo; he ran out first and served himself in a pottery bowl. By the time Wolf Huo wandered back slowly, Wolf Mo had already finished and was holding a bowl of shaved ice.

That bowl of shaved ice took up half of his small basin-like pottery bowl.

Wolf Huo: "Where did that come from?"

He looked around and didn't see any on the stove, and Wolf An and the others hadn't made any.

Wolf Mo gave him a sly smile, "Of course, I made it myself."

Wolf Huo: "Didn't Qiu say not to eat it?"

Wolf Mo coughed twice and said proudly, "You forgot, I had ten chances to choose food when I saved Leopard Xiu."

Wolf Huo hugged his shoulders like a brother, "Then how many do you have left? Give me one."

Wolf Mo: "It's the last one."

Wolf Huo shoved him away, "I just helped you, and you're being this stingy with me?"

Wolf Mo: "It really is the last one, I used up the previous ones over the last few days."

He protested in a small voice, "Qiu wasn't even going to let me eat any more."

Wolf Huo: "Hmph."

Wolf Mo looked at his bowl; the ice was melting fast, so he handed it out, "How about I share half with you?"

Wolf Huo looked at the jam mixed with shaved ice, mostly melted and messy, "Forget it."

He was disgusted.

Wolf Mo quickly protected his bowl, "You said that yourself."

Wolf Huo: "Hmph!"

The weather in the Eastern Continent changed quickly. A few days after the rainy season ended, there were a few light showers, and the temperature dropped a bit.

It was still a bit hot when the sun was out during the day, but the nights were gradually becoming cool.

Now there was no need for ice basins, and the orcs could sleep well at night again.

Wolf Mo gulped down the remaining shaved ice and went to the creek to wash his bowl, his face flushed. With less heavy rain now, the creek water was slowly becoming clean.

The orcs didn't go fishing in the creek, and now one could faintly see small fish and shrimp hiding in the water weeds.

The cubs loved coming here, catching fish in the creek with small nets Qiu had made for them.

They would put them in jars with creek stones and duckweed, raising them themselves, and surprisingly, they managed to keep them alive.

After eating, the orcs squatted by the creek, brushing their teeth with pieces of worn-out toothbrushes.

The cubs squatted to one side, taught by the adult orcs, also baring their teeth and brushing properly.

Some orcs, after bathing, scrubbed their animal skins or hemp shorts, and once finished, lazily swung their long legs, contentedly letting the evening breeze blow through their dripping hair as they headed back to the cave to sleep.

After midnight, the fire went out, and the cave was pitch black.

Lin Qiu turned over, smelling the faint scent of mosquito-repelling herbs, and heard low groans in his dream.

"Aowu, aowu..." mournful and pitiful, Lin Qiu frowned slightly.

"Hmph! So painful, ao..."

Beside him, Wolf Yan turned over. Lin Qiu struggled to wake up, confirmed he heard an orc in pain, and sat up.

Before he even opened his eyes, Wolf Yan pressed his shoulder, "Keep sleeping."

"How can I sleep now?" Lin Qiu grabbed his hand instead, pulling himself up, "Who is crying out?"

Seeing that the orcs had already lit a fire and Wolf Mo was rolling on the grass mat clutching his stomach, Wolf Yan said, "It's Wolf Mo, looks like he ate something bad."

In the cave, the orcs surrounded Wolf Mo, speaking in low voices.

Every orc's face was filled with worry, and seeing Wolf Yan and Lin Qiu approach, they immediately made room.

"King, Mo's stomach hurts."

"He ate the same things as us, could he have eaten something else behind our backs?"

Wolf Yan: "Take him to the Priest."

In the middle of the night, Wolf Xi and the nearby orcs carried Wolf Mo and rushed him to the Priest's cave. The orcs were worried and all followed.

Halfway there, Wolf Yan looked back and said, "Those who have to hunt and forage tomorrow, go back."

Most of the orcs left immediately, all very obedient.

The Priest's cave.

The old Priest was called up in the middle of the night, and upon hearing Wolf Mo stutter about eating two bowls of shaved ice every day for the past few days, he couldn't help but smack Wolf Mo on the forehead a few times.

"Always causing me trouble!"

Seeing Wolf Mo's face turn pale from pain, Wolf Yan urged the old Priest to prepare the herbs first.

Lin Qiu squatted in front of Wolf Mo, and the orc whimpered, trying to grab Lin Qiu's hem to complain, but Wolf Yan saw it and swatted his hand away.

"Don't move around."

"I... Ugh!"

Lin Qiu instinctively wanted to back away, but since he was squatting, he could only sit on the ground. Wolf Yan wrapped his arm around his shoulders, hooked his legs, and carried him back, keeping him far away from Wolf Mo.

The old Priest said urgently, "Quickly find something to catch it, don't vomit in my cave."

Lin Qiu patted Wolf Yan's chest, "Put me down."

Wolf Yan signaled Wolf Shi to grab Wolf Mo and take him outside the cave to vomit.

Wolf An said, "I'll boil some water for him." He hurried down, but was stopped by the Priest halfway.

"Take the medicine and boil it."

The herbs were wrapped in large leaves and tossed down. Wolf An caught them and walked toward the shed.

People were squatting at the entrance of the large cave, and seeing Wolf An return, a dozen pairs of wolf eyes lit up.

They asked in low voices, "An, how is Mo?"

Wolf An: "Nothing major, the Priest said he ate too much ice."

Upon hearing this, the orcs shook their heads and went back to their nests to sleep.

Let him be smug; now he's eaten himself into trouble.

After Wolf Mo struggled for a while, vomiting and having diarrhea, Lin Qiu was afraid he would become dehydrated, so he hurried down to help Wolf An watch the medicine. Once the decoction was ready, he cooled it in a water basin and immediately grabbed Wolf Mo to feed it to him.

But after a while, he vomited it back up.

Wolf An frowned, grabbing Wolf Mo, "If you vomit again, don't eat anything ever again."

Wolf Mo was teary-eyed.

"Aowu..."

Lin Qiu brought another bowl, and Wolf Mo pinched his nose and drank it slowly.

Several orcs guarded him.

The Priest didn't sleep either, watching until he stopped vomiting and was curled up clutching his stomach, dozing off, before saying, "I think it's fine now, you all go back, I'll watch him."

Lin Qiu: "I have nothing to do tomorrow..."

Priest: "Not studying anymore?"

Lin Qiu: "Then I'll go back to sleep."

Wolf An wanted to say something, but the Priest waved his hand, "I don't need much sleep, I'll watch him, everyone go back."

No one could argue with the Priest, so they had to obey and go back.

After a restless night, Lin Qiu slept groggily for the second half of the night and got up as soon as the sky brightened.

He instinctively looked toward Wolf Mo's grass nest, but Wolf Yan moved to the side, blocking Lin Qiu's view.

Lin Qiu slowly looked up, his eyes still sleepy.

Wolf Yan: "He hasn't returned from the Priest's cave yet, but his stomach doesn't hurt as much."

Lin Qiu: "As long as the herbs can cure it."

The incident last night didn't delay the orcs' hunting and foraging today.

There were only a few orcs left in the cave now, and Wolf Guo hurried the cubs, telling them all to go outside.

As they were walking, suddenly a cub stopped and didn't move.

Lin Qiu was wondering why, when Wolf Yan stepped forward quickly, grabbing the cub and moving it away from the pile of cubs. The next moment, he was holding a big, chubby baby in his arms.

Lin Qiu was startled, "It changed again!"

Wolf Guo quickly told the cubs to separate a bit, "King, this batch of cubs will be able to transform by the snow season. But it seems I haven't heard of any sub-beastman being pregnant."

Wolf Yan: "Without mates, how can they be pregnant."

It wasn't just the Wolf Tribe's situation; most tribes had few sub-beastmen and female orcs, and many male orcs.

"There are always some with mates," Wolf Guo said.

Wolf Yan: "There should be some next year."

Life was a bit better now than before, so the orcs should be willing to have children.

After a brief exchange, Wolf Yan looked at the dazed, white, chubby cub in his arms and said, "What's your name?"

The cub was stunned, eyes curving into smiles, and leaned over to nuzzle Wolf Yan. It was sweet, like a sticky rice ball coated in sugar frosting.

Lin Qiu whispered, "Is it a sub-beastman cub?"

The cub opened its arms toward Lin Qiu, imitating Wolf Sheng's way of calling, "Qiu Qiu."

"The King is asking what your name is," a smile appeared on Lin Qiu's face.

The cub shook its head, in a milky voice: "Don't, know."

Lin Qiu's smile stiffened.

The Wolf King was used to it, saying, "Not all cubs have names. If their father or dad is gone, then there's no orc to name them."

"Then he..." Lin Qiu looked at the little cub in his arms, feeling some pity.

"Hmm," Wolf Yan said faintly.

Before Qiu came, orcs starved to death in the Wolf Tribe every day; this was not an exaggeration. Some orcs, in order to save their rations so the cubs could eat a bit more, would only eat a few bites themselves to sustain life, even when food was already scarce.

Fortunately, the tribe raised the cubs together, and their biological parents were busy foraging and hunting, so almost none of them grew up following their own biological parents.

They were generally closer to their companions than to the orcs who gave birth to them.

In the food-scarce Beast God Continent, this was actually better for them.

Kinship ties were shallow; it was the companions who relied on each other and had intimate cooperative relationships. Growing up together and building rapport was more beneficial for hunting together and feeding themselves.

Lin Qiu looked at the cub with the sweet smile and couldn't help but turn his head away, his heart aching.

The cub didn't understand, feeling the warmth on its cheek.

It obediently pressed its cheek against him, its hands tightly hugging Lin Qiu's neck.

"Qiu Qiu."

Lin Qiu's eyes became even gentler, his forehead touching the cub's forehead, and he whispered, "Then let's give you a name, shall we?"

The cub leaned against Lin Qiu and curved its eyes again.

Lin Qiu looked at Wolf Yan, "You are the Wolf King, you name him."

Wolf Yan: "Wolf Zhuang (Sturdy)."

Lin Qiu was disgusted, "He's a sub-beastman, that sounds so ugly."

"Isn't it good to grow up sturdy?"

Wolf Guo said quietly from the side, "Our tribe even has one directly named Wolf Chou (Ugly)."

Lin Qiu: "Think of another one."

Wolf Yan poked the cub's cheek; it was soft and chubby, sinking in. It didn't cry or fuss, but instead grabbed Wolf Yan's hand and stuffed it into its mouth.

Lin Qiu blocked it immediately, his eyes urging Wolf Yan.

Wolf Yan: "Wolf Yuan (Round)."

"Round and chubby."

Lin Qiu touched the cub's little face, "This is good, but not round and chubby, it's 'Yuanman' (perfection/fulfillment). From now on, we'll call him Wolf Yuan."

Wolf Yuan was a little black wolf, but he was born looking like a tangyuan (sweet dumpling).

Thinking of it this way, the name was just right.
chapters.title: 第95章

chapters.source_text:
林楸抱了会儿幼崽，就让他跟着小伙伴玩儿去了。
狼生来接他，带着几个两三岁会变人形的小狼，抓着狼圆的手一下就跑了。
小家伙适应良好，柔软的头发被风吹得散乱，面上看不出阿父阿爸不在的难受，反倒是融入同伴中的开心。
林楸心里像有弯钩拉拽，呼吸都泛着疼。
“这些幼崽里，多少……是家庭完整的？”
狼岩：“两个。”
林楸声音艰涩：“哪两个？”
“狼贝的幼崽狼生，还有个没变人形的黑狼幼崽。像狼圆这种双方都不在的只有两个，其他有阿父或者阿爸。”
林楸眉头拧得死紧。
狼岩指腹触及他眉心，压了压，林楸心里绷着的那股气儿被他弄得散开。
狼岩收回手，道：“兽神大陆，只有强壮的兽人才能活下来。我们跟野兽没什么两样。”
林楸沉默几息，却道：“不，不一样。”
林楸眼里像蹿起一簇小火苗，“我们会种植，会自己制造自己想要的东西。现在捕猎是难以养活部落，但是我们可以自己养动物，自己种粮食。”
林楸定定看着狼岩，顷刻间有了决定，“我打算养咩咩兽。”
“红鸟呢？”
“养。”
“只要养得够多，即便外面没有猎物了，但我们依旧有足够的食物。”
狼岩笑容放大，面带鼓励，“那就去做吧。”
兽人们已经看到了林楸养红鸟的成果，匀出一点口粮用来发展养殖，相信兽人们也会支持的。
*
几个狩猎队休息一晚，赶早出去捕猎。
这次依旧是往南边，兽人们追着呦呦兽，一路从南部跑到东南。
这一头呦呦兽狼火小队追着，跑着跑着前面忽然出现个黑麻麻的东西。泥做的，圆滚滚，胖得跟陶罐一样。
有点眼熟……狼火紧着追猎物，一下没想起来。
兽人们下意识跳过去。
结果不知哪个兽人没看准，一脚踩下去。
狼火瞳孔一缩，想起来了。
他大喝：“跑！”
狼兽人不知道发生了什么，听到狼火这么着急，下意识铆足了劲儿跑。
一群巨狼，更是直接超过了前头的呦呦兽。
兽人顺手挥爪，抓住脖子上冒血的呦呦兽继续跑，一边可惜道：“嗷嗷嗷！没了没了，血旺没了！”
跑到距离足够，狼火扑地，爪子放在脑袋上躲着。
其他兽人也跟着学，就这么撅着屁股，埋着脑袋趴了许久……渐渐有兽人耐不住，窸窸窣窣往狼火身边挪动。
兽人埋头，忐忑道：“火，咱、咱们跑什么？”
狼火：“藏起来！”
“嗷！”兽人脸扑地，一动不敢动。
又许久，狼火才坐起来。
他环顾一圈，没找到威胁的东西，反倒是那个踩到嗡嗡虫巢穴的兽人正抓着脚丫子，龇着牙，一脸难受地试图将爪子上黏糊糊的东西擦干净。
可那味儿不知怎么，香甜十足。
狼火眼睁睁看着兽人爪子上举着一点黑褐色的东西，牵了丝儿，看着是要往嘴里塞。
狼火喝道：“狼丑！你干什么！”
狼丑吓得一哆嗦，爪子松掉，但那东西还挂着丝儿在手上晃荡。
兽人们离他两米远，嫌弃不已。
“你居然想吃脚丫子踩过的……”现在部落有楸，兽人们也跟着他讲究，吃饭前洗手，睡觉前刷牙，脏东西不往嘴里放，更何况脚下踩着的。
狼丑一看，面红耳赤，急忙解释道：“我没、我没想吃！”
“你明明都往嘴巴里塞了！我们又不瞎。”
“就是！我们又不瞎。”
“我不是吃，我闻一下。”
“你还闻！！！”
闹腾一番，狼丑辩解不清，满腔郁闷地脚丫子使劲儿在枯叶上蹭了蹭。
偏生那甜香格外诱人，兽人们动动鼻子，“哪儿来的味道？”
“好香啊……”
鼻子耸动，找着找着，全往狼丑那边去。直到看到他沾满草叶的脚丫子，兽人们滚了滚喉咙。
狼丑惊恐：“你们要吃我脚！”
“呕！！！你别乱说！”兽人们叫得比他还大声。
狼火显然也嗅到了味道，他看看被兽人们围拢的狼丑，忽然道：“咱悄悄回去看看。”
“看什么？”
“嗡嗡虫巢穴。”
“嗡嗡虫巢穴！刚刚那是嗡嗡虫！！！”狼脸惊恐，身子直立。
狼火：“去不去？”
“去！”
“呵。”狼火还不知道他们的德行。
他们眼里只有吃的东西。
不过鉴于之前豹休被嗡嗡虫蜇的事儿，兽人们万分小心。
沾了嗡嗡虫巢味道的狼丑留下，狼火点了几个跑得最快的兽人，用树叶裹住脸，只留下一个呼吸孔跟两个眼睛。
“走！”
狼火想到那香甜的味道，竟然比甜草还诱人，像雪季过后漫山遍野开满的花。
想着，狼火咽了咽口水。
又想起那香味是从狼丑臭脚丫子上传来的，脸一绿，立马屏息。
兽人们谨慎地沿着刚刚发现的巢穴走。
走着走着，狼火低声道：“几天前，豹休是不是就在这儿被咬的？”
边上几个狼兽人心有余悸，点点脑袋。
“那巢应该是从树上掉下来，过来的时候，听到响没？”
嗡嗡虫一般一大群聚集在一起，飞动起来的时候，翅膀发出密集的嗡嗡声，这是他们名字的由来。
边上族人想想，摇头。
“没感觉到动静。”
“没注意。”
“不知道。”
狼火眼里透着十足的谨慎，他不会为了一口吃的送命，但要是受点伤不致死……他非常愿意尝试。
兽人们压低脚步声，慢慢前进。
跑到这边花了十五分钟，回去就花了快半小时。
直到逼近嗡嗡虫巢穴，兽人们看着地上那个被踩碎的东西，鼻子动了动，眼睛一亮。
兽人激动地小声道：“火！没错，就是这个！”
狼火隔着树叶，竖起狼耳听着周围的动静，没敢妄动。正慢慢靠近，忽然听到远处其他狩猎队的呼喊，狼火脚下一软，差点跪下去。
其他狼兽人更是左脚踩着右脚，一下扑过去。
狼火闭眼，跟另外的兽人抓着他两条腿就要跑。
那倒霉蛋却鼻尖刚好凑到巢口，眼睛瓦亮。
“嗷嗷嗷嗷嗷嗷！！！”他激动地叫。
兽人以为他被蜇了，铆足了劲儿地跑。
兽人嚷嚷：“不是！不是！里面没动静，嗡嗡虫飞走了！”
他胸口擦着树叶，得亏有狼毛护着，不然全是血丝。
那边呼喊兽人的动静停了，像听到这边的声音，赶紧赶过来。后头等待的狼丑他们也听见了，生怕晚了就吃不上，拼了命地跑。
一时间，东西两边兽人汇合，一起停在了嗡嗡虫巢前。
狼游、狼乔看着地上那东西，吓得刚要跑，叫狼火喝住。
“嗡嗡虫搬家了。”
兽人才停下。
就这么一会儿，前头的兽人都闻到了味道。几个队长一对视，立即想到楸说过的蜂蜜。
各自眼里闪过遗憾……可惜被看见了，不然能偷偷吃一点。
狼游拍板，道：“带回去！”
兽人们扛着一头猎物，一个硕大的被踩了一下的嗡嗡虫巢，兴冲冲地往回跑。
“楸！楸！看看我们带什么回来……嗷！”
兽人肩膀上扛着的嗡嗡虫巢穴显眼极了。
老祭司这会儿坐在棚子里，正好把狼莫的草药拿下来，就眼睁睁看着这群兽人抓着嗡嗡虫巢靠近。
他甚至来不及看里面有没有嗡嗡虫，抡起拐杖就打。
打得兽人们嗷呜叫着跳脚，又不敢往远了跑，最后可怜兮兮地嚎着，叫能拉住祭司的兽人来帮忙。
带回来好东西，还没得夸呢，就被祭司打得萎靡。
豹休和一群小狼知道那东西是什么，暂且不动，先悄悄观察了一下这些成年狼兽人有没有被蜇。
见他们脸上完好，立马冲过去，亲亲热热地帮忙。
“火叔，我们来，我们来。”
狼乔手抵着小狼崽子的脑门，龇牙咧嘴，“想都别想。”
楸听到动静，这会儿才从山洞里走出来。见他们肩膀上扛着陶罐似的，还正疑惑，走近一看，不是陶罐，而是硕大的一个蜂巢！
跟那几十米树上挂着的马蜂窝似的，看着还要大些。
林楸：“你们没事吧。”
兽人哭唧唧，老祭司下了重手，但兽人一边躲着一边扯着嗓子叫，实际上没挨到多少。
但他们委屈！
“楸，你看看，这个是不是你要的蜂蜜。”
林楸不敢接。
他看老祭司铁青的脸，赶紧道：“你们哪儿来的，没受伤吧。”
“没！这个掉地上了，我们打猎的时候，狼丑不小心踩了一脚。我们才发现的。”
林楸看了眼祭司，见老兽人脸色缓和，这才笑着将蜂巢接过来。
“没受伤就好。”
老祭司：“哼！下次别磨磨唧唧，先解释清楚。”
狼火并一众狩猎队兽人瘪嘴，小声道：“那不是你没等我们说就打。”
老祭司耳朵没那么灵敏，没听见，但不代表他看不懂兽人眼神。
他也不走，就站在原地，也想看看楸说的这好吃的蜂蜜是个什么东西。
老祭司正了正神色，他不馋，只是看看这个有没有药用价值。
chapters.translated_text:
After holding the cub for a while, Lin Qiu let him go off to play with his little friends.

Lang Sheng came to pick him up, bringing along a few two- or three-year-old wolf cubs who could already shift into human form, and grabbed Lang Yuan by the hand before running off.

The little one adapted well; his soft hair was tousled by the wind, and there was no sign of sadness on his face about his father and papa being away—instead, he looked happy to be integrated with his companions.

It felt as if a hook were tugging at Lin Qiu’s heart, and even his breathing felt painful.

"Among these cubs, how many... have complete families?"

Lang Yan replied, "Two."

Lin Qiu’s voice was strained: "Which two?"

"Lang Bei’s cub, Lang Sheng, and a black wolf cub who hasn't shifted into human form yet. There are only two like Lang Yuan whose parents are both gone; the others have either a father or a papa."

Lin Qiu’s brows knitted tightly together.

Lang Yan pressed his thumb against the center of Lin Qiu’s brow, and the tension Lin Qiu had been holding onto dissipated under his touch.

Lang Yan withdrew his hand and said, "On the Beast God Continent, only the strong orcs survive. We are no different from wild beasts."

Lin Qiu was silent for a few moments, then said, "No, that's not the same."

A spark seemed to ignite in Lin Qiu’s eyes. "We can farm, and we can manufacture the things we need ourselves. Hunting alone is hard to sustain the tribe, but we can raise animals and grow our own food."

Lin Qiu looked steadily at Lang Yan, having made a decision in an instant. "I plan to raise Miemie beasts."

"What about the red birds?"

"Raise them too."

"As long as we raise enough of them, even if there is no prey outside, we will still have enough food."

Lang Yan’s smile widened, his expression encouraging. "Then go ahead and do it."

The orcs had already seen the results of Lin Qiu raising red birds; he believed the orcs would support setting aside a portion of their rations to develop animal husbandry.

*

Several hunting teams rested for the night and set out early to hunt.

This time, they headed south again, the orcs chasing the Youyou beasts all the way from the south to the southeast.

As the Langhuo team was chasing one particular Youyou beast, a dark, round object suddenly appeared in front of them. It was made of mud, round and plump, looking just like a pottery jar.

It looked a bit familiar... Langhuo was focused on the prey and didn't immediately recall what it was.

The orcs instinctively jumped over it.

As it turned out, one of the orcs didn't look closely and stepped right on it.

Langhuo’s pupils shrank; he remembered.

He shouted, "Run!"

The wolf orcs didn't know what had happened, but hearing Langhuo’s urgency, they instinctively put all their strength into running.

The pack of giant wolves even overtook the Youyou beast in front.

An orc casually swiped his claws, grabbed the bleeding Youyou beast by the neck, and kept running, lamenting, "Awoo! It’s gone, it’s gone! The blood curd is gone!"

Once they were at a safe distance, Langhuo dove to the ground, covering his head with his claws.

The other orcs followed suit, burying their heads and sticking their butts in the air for a long time... Gradually, some orcs couldn't stand it anymore and rustled over toward Langhuo.

An orc kept his head buried and asked nervously, "Huo, w-why are we running?"

Langhuo: "Hide!"

"Awoo!" The orc pressed his face into the dirt, not daring to move.

After a long while, Langhuo finally sat up.

He looked around and found no sign of danger. Instead, the orc who had stepped on the buzzing-insect nest was grabbing his foot, baring his teeth, and trying to wipe the sticky substance off his claws in discomfort.

But for some reason, the smell was incredibly sweet.

Langhuo watched as the orc held up a bit of the dark brown substance on his claw, which was trailing a string, looking as if he were about to put it in his mouth.

Langhuo barked, "Lang Chou! What are you doing!"

Lang Chou jumped in fright, his claw loosening, but the substance still dangled from his hand.

The other orcs stayed two meters away, looking disgusted.

"You actually wanted to eat something your foot stepped on..." Now that the tribe had Qiu, the orcs followed his lead in being particular—washing hands before eating, brushing teeth before sleeping, and not putting dirty things in their mouths, let alone something they had stepped on.

Lang Chou turned bright red and hurriedly explained, "I d-didn't! I didn't want to eat it!"

"You were clearly putting it in your mouth! We aren't blind."

"Exactly! We aren't blind."

"I wasn't eating it, I was just smelling it."

"You were smelling it too!!!"

After a bit of a commotion, Lang Chou couldn't clear his name and, full of frustration, vigorously rubbed his foot against the dry leaves.

Yet the sweet scent was exceptionally alluring, and the orcs twitched their noses. "Where is that smell coming from?"

"It smells so good..."

Sniffing and searching, they all ended up around Lang Chou. When they saw his grass-stained foot, the orcs gulped.

Lang Chou cried in terror, "You want to eat my foot!"

"Ugh!!! Don't talk nonsense!" The orcs shouted even louder than him.

Langhuo clearly smelled it too. He looked at Lang Chou surrounded by the orcs and suddenly said, "Let’s go back quietly and take a look."

"Look at what?"

"The buzzing-insect nest."

"The buzzing-insect nest! That was a buzzing-insect nest just now!!!" Their wolf faces were full of terror, their bodies standing rigid.

Langhuo: "Are we going or not?"

"Going!"

"Heh." Langhuo knew their true nature.

They only had eyes for food.

However, given what happened to Bao Xiu when he was stung by the buzzing insects, the orcs were extremely cautious.

They left Lang Chou, who was covered in the scent of the nest, behind. Langhuo picked a few of the fastest orcs and wrapped their faces in leaves, leaving only a breathing hole and two eye slits.

"Let's go!"

Langhuo thought of that sweet scent; it was even more alluring than sweet grass, like the flowers that bloomed all over the mountains after the snow season.

Thinking of this, Langhuo swallowed his saliva.

Then he remembered that the scent came from Lang Chou’s stinky foot, and his face turned green as he immediately held his breath.

The orcs cautiously followed the path to the nest they had just discovered.

As they walked, Langhuo whispered, "A few days ago, wasn't it right here that Bao Xiu got bitten?"

The wolf orcs nearby nodded, still feeling a lingering fear.

"The nest must have fallen from the tree. Did you hear any noise when we came over?"

Buzzing insects usually gathered in large groups, and when they flew, their wings made a dense buzzing sound, which was how they got their name.

The tribesmen nearby thought about it and shook their heads.

"Didn't feel any movement."

"Didn't notice."

"Don't know."

Langhuo’s eyes were full of caution. He wouldn't risk his life for a bite of food, but if it meant getting a non-lethal injury... he was very willing to try.

The orcs lowered their footsteps and moved forward slowly.

It had taken fifteen minutes to run there, but it took nearly half an hour to go back.

As they approached the buzzing-insect nest, the orcs looked at the crushed object on the ground, twitched their noses, and their eyes lit up.

An orc whispered excitedly, "Huo! That’s right, this is it!"

Langhuo listened to the surroundings through the leaves with his wolf ears, not daring to act rashly. Just as he was slowly approaching, he suddenly heard the shouts of other hunting teams in the distance, and Langhuo’s legs went weak, almost causing him to kneel.

The other wolf orcs tripped over their own feet and lunged forward.

Langhuo closed his eyes, and the other orcs grabbed his legs, ready to run.

But that unlucky fellow’s nose happened to be right at the opening of the nest, his eyes shining bright.

"Awoo awoo awoo awoo awoo!!!" he shouted excitedly.

The orcs thought he had been stung and ran with all their might.

The orc shouted, "No! No! There’s no movement inside, the buzzing insects have flown away!"

His chest was scraped by the leaves; it was a good thing he had wolf fur to protect him, otherwise, he would be covered in bloody scratches.

The shouting from the other side stopped, as if they had heard the noise here and were rushing over. Lang Chou and the others who were waiting behind heard it too, and fearing they wouldn't get to eat if they were late, they ran for their lives.

In an instant, the orcs from the east and west converged and stopped together in front of the buzzing-insect nest.

Lang You and Lang Qiao looked at the thing on the ground and were so scared they were about to run, but Langhuo stopped them.

"The buzzing insects have moved."

The orcs stopped.

In just this short time, the orcs in front had all smelled the scent. The captains exchanged glances, immediately thinking of the honey Qiu had mentioned.

Regret flashed in their eyes... it was a pity they had been seen, otherwise, they could have eaten a little bit in secret.

Lang You made the call: "Bring it back!"

The orcs carried the prey and the massive, stepped-on buzzing-insect nest, running back excitedly.

"Qiu! Qiu! Look what we brought back... Awoo!"

The buzzing-insect nest on the orc’s shoulder was extremely conspicuous.

The old priest was sitting in the shed at that moment, just putting away Lang Mo’s herbs, and watched as this group of orcs approached with the buzzing-insect nest.

He didn't even have time to check if there were any buzzing insects inside before he swung his staff and started hitting them.

The orcs yelped and jumped, not daring to run too far, and finally wailed pitifully, calling for an orc who could hold the priest back to help.
